latestRelease.notes:
# Highlights

*710 PRs from 212 contributors.*

**New models in this release** (see the [cookbook](https://docs.sglang.io/cookbook) for all supported models):

| Model | Type | PRs | Cookbook |
|---|---|---|---|
| Muse Glimmer | Autoregressive (Multimodal) | [#34262](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/34262) | [link](https://docs.sglang.io/cookbook/autoregressive/Meta/MuseGlimmer) |
| Intern-S2-Mobius | Autoregressive | [#33691](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33691) | [link](https://docs.sglang.io/cookbook/autoregressive/InternLM/Intern-S2-Mobius) |
| SANA-Video | Diffusion | [#32921](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32921) | [link](https://docs.sglang.io/cookbook/diffusion/SANA-Video/SANA-Video) |
| LingBot-Video-MoE | Diffusion | [#32341](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32341) | [link](https://docs.sglang.io/cookbook/diffusion/LingBot-Video/LingBot-Video-MoE) |
| LTX-2.5 | Diffusion | [#34471](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/34471) | [link](https://docs.sglang.io/cookbook/diffusion/LTX/LTX2.5) |
| Cosmos3 Edge & Distilled | Diffusion | [#31590](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/31590) | [link](https://docs.sglang.io/cookbook/diffusion/Cosmos/Cosmos3) |
| LongCat-Image | Diffusion | [#23274](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/23274) | |

Plus cookbook recipes for the [Qwen3.8 family](https://docs.sglang.io/cookbook/autoregressive/Qwen/Qwen3.8), [Ling-3.0](https://docs.sglang.io/cookbook/autoregressive/InclusionAI/Ling-3.0-flash), [Nemotron 3.5 Lightning](https://docs.sglang.io/cookbook/autoregressive/NVIDIA/Nemotron3.5-Lightning), [Dots3-Note](https://docs.sglang.io/cookbook/autoregressive/RedNote/Dots3-Note), and DeepSeek-V4-Pro-0813 ([#34809](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/34809)).

**Overlapped checkpoint staging at startup**: Checkpoint pages now stage from storage while CUDA graphs capture. Qwen3-32B on H100 starts **8.6-11.7% faster** than serial with prefetch, and **2.38x faster (35.6s vs 84.8s)** than the plain default. Opt in with `--startup-weight-load-mode overlap` ([#32017](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32017)).

**TP LMHead with All-to-All**: The TP LMHead's allgather + scatter becomes a single all-to-all for pure-DP dp-attention. On DeepSeek-V4-Pro B200 decode, LMHead time drops **320us to 169us** and TPOT improves 36.97ms to 35.67ms ([#32313](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32313)).

**FlashInfer MNNVL for pure allreduce**: Non-fused allreduce sites now reuse the FlashInfer MNNVL workspace instead of falling back to NCCL. DeepSeek-V4-Flash TP4 decode on Blackwell gains **up to +6.9% at small batches**. Auto-enabled for DeepSeek-V3/V3.2/V4; elsewhere `--enable-flashinfer-pure-allreduce` ([#30700](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/30700)).

**One compiled-kernel cache directory**: Triton, FlashInfer, Inductor, DeepGEMM, and CUDA driver caches all move under `SGLANG_CACHE_DIR`. The first launch after upgrading recompiles once; see Breaking Changes ([#32434](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32434)).

**Dependencies**: torch 2.13.0 with triton 3.7.1 ([#28836](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/28836)), flashinfer 0.6.17 ([#33997](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33997)), CuTeDSL 4.6.2, fixing an FA4 startup regression on Blackwell ([#34372](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/34372)), DeepEP now installed from released `sgl-deep-ep` wheels ([#33932](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33932)), and sgl-kernel 0.4.6.post1 ([#33842](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33842)).

## Breaking Changes & Upgrade Notes

* **The CUDA PyTorch stack moves to torch 2.13.0**, with triton 3.7.1, torchvision 0.28.0, and torchcodec 0.15.0 (torchaudio stays at 2.11.0); AOT kernels are rebuilt for Torch 2.13 and the XPU backend follows: [#28836](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/28836), [#33841](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33841), [#31751](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/31751)
* **Every compiled-kernel cache moves under `SGLANG_CACHE_DIR`**, so the first launch after upgrading recompiles once. Copy or symlink the old directories if you pre-warm or volume-mount them (`deep_gemm` and `flashinfer` are the expensive ones): `~/.triton` to `{SGLANG_CACHE_DIR}/triton`, `~/.cache/flashinfer` to `{SGLANG_CACHE_DIR}/.cache/flashinfer`, `~/.cache/deep_gemm` to `{SGLANG_CACHE_DIR}/deep_gemm`, `/tmp/torchinductor_$USER` to `{SGLANG_CACHE_DIR}/inductor`, `~/.nv/ComputeCache` to `{SGLANG_CACHE_DIR}/nv`. Setting any of `TRITON_CACHE_DIR`, `FLASHINFER_WORKSPACE_BASE`, `SGLANG_DG_CACHE_DIR`, `TORCHINDUCTOR_CACHE_DIR`, or `CUDA_CACHE_PATH` keeps that one where it is: [#32434](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32434)
* **The torchao integration is removed** (`--torchao-config` had raised ImportError for every accepted value since the torchao pin moved to 0.17.0): [#34304](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/34304)
* **DeepEP now installs from released `sgl-deep-ep` wheels** instead of building from source: [#33932](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33932)
* **MoE deferred finalize is on by default** on the NVFP4 + `flashinfer_trtllm` path with an unfused, non-TP1 shared expert (the DeepSeek-V3 family); set `SGLANG_ENABLE_MOE_DEFERRED_FINALIZE=False` to fall back: [#33618](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33618)
* **Unified-cache out-of-window SWA slot freeing is on by default** for the unified radix cache; set `SGLANG_OPT_UNIFIED_CACHE_FREE_OUT_OF_WINDOW_SLOTS=False` to restore the old behavior: [#34653](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/34653)
* **Remote media downloads are bounded to 64 MiB by default**, with redirect validation and opt-in exact-hostname allowlisting for image, video, and audio URLs: [#34892](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/34892)
* **The DSV4 fused MHC post+pre path is on by default**, including on SM12x: [#35214](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/35214), [#34019](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/34019)
* **torch.compile becomes opt-in for diffusion speed mode**: [#34173](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/34173)
* **22 unmaintained benchmarks are removed**: [#34520](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/34520)

signals.title: [PP + HiCache] HiCache Consistency Fix Plan
signals.text: # PP HiCache Consistency for Disaggregated Prefill — PR Plan ## Background ### Motivation In agentic and long-context reasoning scenarios, requests frequently share long prefixes (system prompts, tool definitions, multi-turn history) that can span tens of thousands of tokens. Recomputing these shared prefixes for every request is prohibitively expensive. SGLang's **HiCache** addresses this with a 3-level KV cache hierarchy — **L1** (GPU device memory) → **L2** (CPU host memory) → **L3** (external distributed storage, e.g. Mooncake) — enabling prefix reuse across requests and even across restarts via persistent storage. Meanwhile, large models (e.g. DeepSeek-V3 with 60 layers) require **Pipeline Parallelism (PP)** to split layers across multiple GPU groups, combined with **disaggregated prefill** where prefill and decode run on separate server pools. This PP + HiCache + disaggregated prefill stack is critical for production agentic workloads: it maximizes both throughput (via disaggregation) and cache hit rates (via L3 persistence) on large models. However, combining PP with L3 storage introduces a class of consistency bugs that do not exist in simpler configurations. Understanding why requires examining the cache hierarchy level by level. ### Why L3 Storage Breaks PP Consistency In PP mode, each rank runs an independent scheduler with its own radix tree. The key question is: why does adding L3 cause divergence when L1 and L2 alone do not? **L1-only + PP (no HiCache)**: Both ranks receive the same requests in the same order via P2P. `match_prefix` operates on the device radix tree, which is fully deterministic — insert and evict are driven by the same batch picks, and all operations are synchronous within each scheduler cycle. **No divergence possible.** **L1 + L2 + PP (HiCache without storage)**: Adding the host cache introduces `write-through` (GPU→CPU backup) and `load-back` (CPU→GPU restore). These are still **synchronous** operations within each cycle — `writing_check()` and `loading_check()` are called at deterministic points in the event loop, and the host tree mutations they produce are driven by the same batch sequence. ~~**No divergence possible.**~~ There is a small probability of matched_host mismatch!!! **L1 + L2 + L3 + PP (HiCache with storage)**: Adding L3 storage introduces the **prefetch thread** — an asynchronous background thread that queries external storage independently on each rank. This is where consistency breaks: 1. **Async completion timing**: PP0 and PP1's prefetch threads may complete at different wall-clock times. When PP0's prefetch finishes first, it inserts nodes into its host tree immediately, while PP1's tree has not yet been updated. The next `match_prefix` on each rank sees different host tree states → different `host_hit_length` → different `prefix_indices`. 2. **Anchor divergence**: The L3 query uses a hash chain starting from an anchor node in the host tree. If PP0 has already inserted nodes from a previous prefetch (giving it `host_hit=896`), its anchor and token range differ from PP1's (which has `host_hit=0`). The two ranks compute **completely different hash chains** for the same request → fetch different (or wrong) data from storage. 3. **Eviction divergence from wall-clock LRU**: Even after fixing async finalization (making PP1 event-driven), the eviction layer itself can diverge. LRU eviction uses `last_access_time = time.monotonic()`, which differs by microseconds between ranks → different victim node selection → different GPU→CPU demotion → different host memory pressure → different `evictable_host_leaves` candidate sets. In production (PP2 + NSA + disagg prefill), this caused: PP0 finalized a prefetch → inserted host node → immediately triggered `evict_host` (memory pressure) → evicted the node. PP1 replayed the same finalize event one cycle later → inserted the node → no eviction pressure → node remained. Result: PP0 `matched_host=0`, PP1 `matched_host=17664` → shape mismatch crash. 4. **Amplification cascade**: Once the host tree diverges (even by one node), all subsequent operations compound the difference — different eviction decisions, different write-through timing, different prefetch anchors for the next request — until a shape mismatch crash occurs. In essence: **L1 and L2 operations are synchronous and deterministic within each cycle, but L3 prefetch is asynchronous and state-dependent. The async completion timing, state-dependent query parameters, and wall-clock-dependent eviction ordering create a feedback loop where small divergences amplify into crashes.** ## Solution Architecture thanks @stepinto ### Three Communication Channels (Three Edge Types) ① PG1 — green bidirectional (between prefetch_thread) - Uses prefetch_sync_groups, gloo (CPU) backend, members = TP+CP+PP - Handles `#1` : global MIN over storage_hit_count - Bidirectional arrow = a truly symmetric all_reduce; all ranks participate equally and obtain the same hit count ② PG2 — purple bidirectional (between prefetch_sync_thread) - Uses prefetch_sync_groups2, also gloo, members = TP+CP+PP - Handles `#2`: global MIN over completed_tokens - Likewise a symmetric all_reduce ③ Scheduler-thread _all_reduce — directional (between Scheduler loops, PP0→PP1→PP2) - Handles `#3`/ `#4`/ `#5`/ `#6` (terminate MAX, qsize MIN, finish MIN) - Different mechanism: first reduces within the local stage's TP/CP group via GLOO, then uses _pp_sync point-to-point to overwrite downstream ranks with PP0's result - Directional arrow = not a symmetric reduce, but PP0 single-point decision + downstream broadcast ### Why Split It This Finely (Key Design Intent) 1. PG1 and PG2 have identical members, yet two sets are created — because `#1` and `#2` run on two different background threads. The same gloo communicator cannot be used for concurrent all_reduce from two threads (it would corrupt/deadlock), so each gets its own set. 2. Background uses gloo, while the scheduler-thread set mixes NCCL+P2P — gloo is CPU communication, isolated from the scheduler thread's CUDA collectives, preventing background all_reduce from blocking GPU computation. 3. The two categories have different semantics: - ①② are symmetric global MIN — pulling each rank's progress into alignment (whoever is slowest wins) - ③ is PP0 directional broadcast — termination timing / drain counts decided uniformly by the leader ## Work In Progress - [X] need cp sync https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/20460 - [x] https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/27285 FIx L2 - [ ] https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/27010 Fix L3 - [x] https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/29106 - [x] https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/25887 - [x] https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/29258 - [x] https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/30476 - [x] https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/28379 - [x] https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/31869 - [ ] A important debugging feature by @stepinto god : https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/34406 - [ ] https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/34815 Special thanks to @ShangmingCai @hzh0425 @stepinto for their guidance on the HiCache architecture, PP synchronization design, and code review throughout this effort. CC @merrymercy @hnyls2002 @xiezhq-hermann @Fridge003 @stepinto

signals.title: [RFC][Refactor] `mem_cache` pool / allocator restructure
signals.text: > **Roadmap v2.** Rewritten against `sglang/main` @ 2026-08-20; the original body is > in this issue's edit history. Hardware backends (`hardware_backend/npu/`, > `hardware_backend/mlx/`) are **out of scope** and are not covered by any item or > guard below. --- ## 1. TL;DR Reorganize `mem_cache/` from "a few catch-all files plus cross-feature pollution" into per-family one-module-per-family packages: - `allocator.py` → `allocator/` package — **done**, keep it closed - `memory_pool_host.py` → `pool_host/` package — **in progress**, 3 items left - `memory_pool.py` + 6 sibling files → `pool/` package — **not started**, and it is the only part of `mem_cache/` still actively getting worse - Untangle DSv4 ↔ HiSparse class misplacement - Naming rule: **remove role affixes that don't differentiate** - Add `mem_cache/README.md` (type × scope) index - Land a CI guard so the layout cannot regress once a target directory exists --- ## 2. Why v2: what changed since the RFC was opened The RFC was opened 2026-05-15. Three months of data: | File | 2026-05-15 | 2026-08-20 | Δ | |---|---|---|---| | `memory_pool.py` | 2257 lines / 11 classes | **5042 lines / 17 classes** | **+123%** | | `memory_pool_host.py` | 2105 lines / 8 classes | **1517 lines / 6 classes** | −28% | The layer that got a target directory shrank. The layer that did not got 2.8k lines and 6 new classes dumped into it: `PageMajorMHATokenToKVPool`, `MHATokenToKVPoolMXFP8`, `MHATokenToKOnlyPool`, `MiniMaxSparseKVPool`, `DSATokenToKVPool`, plus `KVWriteLoc` / `KvBufferDesc`. Two consequences drive v2: 1. **`pool/` moves from last to first.** It is the only remaining catch-all and the only one still growing. 2. **A directory alone is not a rule.** #29678 (2026-07-01) added `multi_ended_allocator.py` (2559 lines, 3 allocator classes) at top level *two months after* `allocator/` existed. Section 8 adds the guard. Additional drift the original body does not reflect: - `unified_cache_components/` was moved to `unified_cache/components/` in 60d6914f1 (2026-07-28), but the `_component` suffix was kept. The naming rule was silently dropped; the tree in the old §3.2 is contradicted by a landed PR. - `NSATokenToKVPool` → `DSATokenToKVPool`; `NSAIndexerPoolHost` → `DSAIndexerPoolHost`. All `nsa` names in the old tree are stale. - `allocator/mamba.py` holds `MambaSlotAllocator`, not `MambaTokenToKVPoolAllocator`. - `allocator/swa.py` gained `PureSWATokenToKVPoolAllocator` — filed correctly, which is the evidence that the rule works once the directory exists. - New, entirely uncovered by the old roadmap: `unified_memory_pool.py` (1691), `multi_ended_allocator.py` (2559), `kv_cache_configurator.py` (2190), `mamba_checkpoint_pool.py`, `index_key_cache.py`, `dsa_cache_layer_split.py`, `mamba_slot_fused.py`, `kv_vmm_backing.py`, `layout/`, `buffer_mode/`, `allocation.py`, `allocation_sizing.py`, `embedding_store.py`. --- ## 3. Rules for every PR under this issue 1. Title must carry the `[mem_cache][N/N]` prefix and state whether it is a **Mechanical Move**. 2. Mechanical Moves must satisfy the `mechanical-refactor-verify` skill. 3. Preserve git blame as far as possible; `git blame -C -C` is the accepted fallback. 4. **No compatibility shims.** Each move updates all importers in the same PR. This is the established precedent — `allocator.py` was deleted outright, not left as a re-export. `memory_pool.py` currently has 98 importers; they get updated, not forwarded. 5. Every PR must shrink the guard allowlist (§8) by exactly the classes it moved. 6. Adequate test coverage, and detailed review — no exceptions for "trivial" moves. --- ## 4. Naming rules 1. **Drop role affixes that do not differentiate.** If every file in a directory shares the role the directory already names, the affix carries no information: `pool_host/mha.py`, not `pool_host/mha_pool_host.py`. Keep `_backend` / `_controller` style only where same-directory siblings have *different* roles. 2. **A family is a module, and a module may be a file or a package.** One file per family is the default; a family over ~1500 lines becomes a package (`pool/deepseek_v4/` already does this, and `pool/mha/` must — see §5). 3. `Allocator` is overloaded and the two meanings must not be merged: - **slot allocator** — a `BaseTokenToKVPoolAllocator` subclass, answers "which slots are free". These belong in `allocator/`. - **host tensor allocator** — `HostTensorAllocator` and its subclasses (`ShmHostTensorAllocator`, `MooncakeHostTensorAllocator`, `UMBPHostTensorAllocator`), answers "give me pinned host memory". These stay in `pool_host/common.py` and `storage/`, and are **not** in scope for `allocator/`. --- ## 5. Target tree ``` mem_cache/ ├── README.md # (type × scope) index │ ├── allocator/ # slot indexing — CLOSED except for the two items in §6.1 │ ├── __init__.py │ ├── base.py # BaseTokenToKVPoolAllocator (abc only) │ ├── token.py # TokenToKVPoolAllocator (page_size=1) │ ├── paged.py # PagedTokenToKVPoolAllocator │ ├── mamba.py # MambaSlotAllocator │ ├── swa.py # SWATokenToKVPoolAllocator │ │ # PureSWATokenToKVPoolAllocator │ ├── hisparse.py # HiSparseTokenToKVPoolAllocator │ │ # DeepSeekV4HiSparseTokenToKVPoolAllocator │ └── multi_ended.py # MultiEndedAllocator │ # UnifiedMambaTokenToKVPoolAllocator │ # UnifiedSWATokenToKVPoolAllocator │ ├── pool/ # device physical storage │ ├── __init__.py │ ├── base.py # KVCache + BaseSWAKVPool + KVWriteLoc + KvBufferDesc │ ├── req_to_token.py # ReqToTokenPool + HybridReqToTokenPool │ ├── mha/ # 6 classes / ~1900 lines → package │ │ ├── __init__.py │ │ ├── base.py # MHATokenToKVPool │ │ ├── noop.py # NoOpMHATokenToKVPool │ │ ├── fp4.py # MHATokenToKVPoolFP4 │ │ ├── mxfp8.py # MHATokenToKVPoolMXFP8 │ │ ├── page_major.py # PageMajorMHATokenToKVPool │ │ └── k_only.py # MHATokenToKOnlyPool │ ├── mla.py # MLATokenToKVPool + MLATokenToKVPoolFP4 │ ├── dsa.py # DSATokenToKVPool + HiSparseDSATokenToKVPool │ │ # + LayerSplitDSATokenToKVPool │ │ # + IndexKeyCache + LayerSplitIndexKeyCache │ ├── mamba.py # MambaPool + MambaCheckpointPool + Int8CheckpointStore │ ├── hybrid.py # HybridLinearKVPool │ ├── swa.py # SWAKVPool │ ├── hisparse.py # HiSparseC4DevicePool │ ├── minimax.py # MiniMaxSparseKVPool │ ├── unified/ # shared-arena variants (see §9 D1) │ │ ├── __init__.py │ │ ├── arena.py # UnifiedKVPool + SubPoolSpec + MHA/MLA/Mamba specs │ │ ├── mha.py # UnifiedMHATokenToKVPool │ │ ├── mla.py # UnifiedMLATokenToKVPool │ │ ├── mamba.py # UnifiedMambaPool + UnifiedMambaSlotAllocator │ │ ├── swa.py # UnifiedSWAKVPool │ │ └── hybrid.py # UnifiedHybridReqToTokenPool + UnifiedHybridLinearKVPool │ └── deepseek_v4/ │ ├── __init__.py │ ├── composite.py # DeepSeekV4TokenToKVPool + DeepSeekV4UnifiedKVPool │ ├── single.py # DeepSeekV4SingleKVPool │ ├── indexer.py # DeepSeekV4IndexerPool │ └── compress_state.py # KVAndScore + CompressStatePool │ ├── pool_host/ # host-side mirrors for supported device pools │ ├── __init__.py │ ├── base.py # HostKVCache (abc) + synchronized decorator │ ├── common.py # HostTensorAllocator + ShmHostTensorAllocator + helpers │ ├── mha.py # MHATokenToKVPoolHost + MHATokenToKOnlyPoolHost │ │ # + AsymmetricMHATokenToKVPoolHost │ ├── mla.py # MLATokenToKVPoolHost │ ├── dsa.py # DSAIndexerPoolHost │ ├── mamba.py # MambaPoolHost │ ├── hisparse.py # HiSparseHostPoolMixin │ ├── group.py # PoolEntry + HostPoolGroup + LogicalHostPool │ └── deepseek_v4.py # DeepSeekV4PagedHostPool + DeepSeekV4StateHostPool │ ├── hybrid_cache/ # multi-pool orchestrator │ ├── controller.py # HybridCacheController │ └── pool_assembler.py # HybridPoolAssembler │ ├── unified_cache/components/ │ ├── __init__.py │ ├── base.py # TreeComponent (abc) + shared enums │ ├── full.py # FullComponent │ ├── mamba.py # MambaComponent │ └── swa.py # SWAComponent │ ├── allocation.py # scheduler-facing allocation policy (unchanged) ├── layout/ # cross-cutting memory layout helpers (unchanged) ├── buffer_mode/, storage/, sparsity/ # (unchanged) └── ... tree-layer files # (unchanged, #20415 territory) ``` Deleted when their last class moves out: `memory_pool.py`, `memory_pool_host.py`, `deepseek_v4_memory_pool.py`, `deepseek_v4_compress_state.py`, `swa_memory_pool.py`, `base_swa_memory_pool.py`, `hisparse_memory_pool.py`, `unified_memory_pool.py`, `multi_ended_allocator.py`, `mamba_checkpoint_pool.py`, `dsa_cache_layer_split.py`, `index_key_cache.py`. --- ## 6. Roadmap ### 6.1 `mem_cache/allocator/` — nearly done - [x] [Mechanical Move] split `allocator.py` into `allocator/` subpackage — #26675 - [x] [Mechanical Move] `SWATokenToKVPoolAllocator` — #26676 - [x] [Mechanical Move] HiSparse allocators — #26678 - [x] [Modify] Mamba allocator — #27256 - [ ] [Mechanical Move] `MultiEndedAllocator` → `allocator/multi_ended.py` (2559 lines / 3 classes — split into 3 PRs: `MultiEndedAllocator`, `UnifiedMambaTokenToKVPoolAllocator`, `UnifiedSWATokenToKVPoolAllocator`) - [ ] [Guard] land §8 with `allocator/` at zero allowlist entries ### 6.2 `mem_cache/pool_host/` — 3 items left - [x] [Mechanical Move] base subpackage (`__init__` + `base` + `hisparse` + `common`) — #27273 - [x] [Mechanical Move] `MHATokenToKVPoolHost` — #30249 - [x] [Mechanical Move] `MLATokenToKVPoolHost` — #30616 - [x] [Mechanical Move] `MambaPoolHost` — #31180 - [x] [Mechanical Move] `DSAIndexerPoolHost` → `pool_host/dsa.py` — #35306 *(in review)* - [ ] [Mechanical Move] `DeepSeekV4PagedHostPool` + `DeepSeekV4StateHostPool` → `pool_host/deepseek_v4.py` - [ ] [Mechanical Move] `PoolEntry` + `HostPoolGroup` + `LogicalHostPool` → `pool_host/group.py`, delete `memory_pool_host.py` - [ ] [Guard] extend §8 to `pool_host/` at zero allowlist entries ### 6.3 `mem_cache/pool/` — **promoted to top priority, not started** Order matters: `base.py` first so every later PR has a target for its base class, then leaves before composites. - [x] [Mechanical Move] create `pool/` + `base.py` — `KVCache`, `BaseSWAKVPool` (from `base_swa_memory_pool.py`), `KVWriteLoc`, `KvBufferDesc`, `unwrap_write_loc` — #35647. The `_set_kv_buffer_*` helpers stay put: the moved region references none of them, so moving them would only widen the diff. - [ ] [Mechanical Move] `ReqToTokenPool` + `HybridReqToTokenPool` → `pool/req_to_token.py` - [ ] [Mechanical Move] `pool/mha/` package — one PR for `base.py` (`MHATokenToKVPool`, 1112 lines), then one PR per variant group: `noop` + `k_only`, `fp4` + `mxfp8`, `page_major` - [ ] [Mechanical Move] `MLATokenToKVPool` + `MLATokenToKVPoolFP4` → `pool/mla.py` - [ ] [Mechanical Move] `DSATokenToKVPool` + `HiSparseDSATokenToKVPool` → `pool/dsa.py`, delete `hisparse_memory_pool.py` - [ ] [Mechanical Move] `IndexKeyCache` → `pool/dsa.py`, delete `index_key_cache.py` *(same module as its sole owner `DSATokenToKVPool`, which removes the `TYPE_CHECKING` import cycle between the two)* - [ ] [Mechanical Move] `LayerSplitDSATokenToKVPool` + `LayerSplitIndexKeyCache` → `pool/dsa.py`, delete `dsa_cache_layer_split.py` - [ ] [Mechanical Move] `MambaPool` → `pool/mamba.py`; fold in `MambaCheckpointPool` + `Int8CheckpointStore`, delete `mamba_checkpoint_pool.py` - [ ] [Mechanical Move] `SWAKVPool` → `pool/swa.py`, delete `swa_memory_pool.py` - [ ] [Modify] `HybridLinearKVPool` → `pool/hybrid.py` (rename to `HybridKVPool` — the only non-mechanical item here, needs its own discussion) - [ ] [Mechanical Move] `MiniMaxSparseKVPool` → `pool/minimax.py` - [ ] [Mechanical Move] `HiSparseC4DevicePool` → `pool/hisparse.py` *(untangles the DSv4 ↔ HiSparse misplacement in `deepseek_v4_memory_pool.py`)* - [ ] [Mechanical Move] `pool/deepseek_v4/` — `single.py`, `indexer.py`, `composite.py`, `compress_state.py`; delete `deepseek_v4_memory_pool.py` and `deepseek_v4_compress_state.py` - [ ] [Mechanical Move] `pool/unified/` (see §9 D1); delete `unified_memory_pool.py` - [ ] Delete `memory_pool.py` - [ ] [Guard] extend §8 to `pool/` at zero allowlist entries ### 6.4 Naming cleanups - [ ] [Mechanical Move] `hybrid_cache/hybrid_cache_controller.py` → `controller.py` - [ ] [Mechanical Move] `hybrid_cache/hybrid_pool_assembler.py` → `pool_assembler.py` - [x] [Mechanical Move] `unified_cache/components/{full,mamba,swa}_component.py` → `{full,mamba,swa}.py`; `tree_component.py` → `base.py` — #35644 *(this was missed by #32484, which moved the directory but kept the suffixes)* ### 6.5 Documentation and guard - [x] `mem_cache/README.md` — layer map, placement-by-base-class, §4 naming rules, §7 dependency invariants — #35643. Deliberately coarse: a per-class inventory would need updating by every remaining move, and it already has a rot-proof home in §8's shrink-only pins. - [x] `test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_mem_cache_layout_ratchet.py` (§8) — R1 (allocator + pool_host), R2, R3, R4 — #35638 (draft, stacked on #35306) - [ ] `.claude/skills/mem-cache-layout/SKILL.md` + trigger line in `.claude/rules/modify-component-must-read.md` - [ ] enable R1 for the `pool` role once `mem_cache/pool/` exists (first item of §6.3) --- ## 7. Layering and dependency invariants ``` scheduler / model_runner / attention backend │ ▼ ┌──────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ allocation.py │ per-batch allocation policy └──────────────────────────────────────────┘ │ ▼ ┌──────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ hybrid_cache/ │ multi-pool router └──────────────────────────────────────────┘ │ ▼ ┌──────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ allocator/ │ "give me N slots" └──────────────────────────────────────────┘ │ holds a reference to ↓ ▼ ┌────────────────────────┐ ┌──────────────────────────┐ │ pool/ (device, L1) │ ─ hicache ►│ pool_host/ (host, L2) │ └────────────────────────┘ offload └──────────────────────────┘ │ ▼ ┌──────────────────────────┐ │ storage/ (L3) │ └──────────────────────────┘ construction layer (cuts across all of the above, not a tier): kv_cache_configurator.py, kv_cache_builder.py, cache_init_params.py, allocation_sizing.py, kv_cache_dtype.py, kv_vmm_backing.py, hybrid_cache/pool_assembler.py ``` | Module | Cares about | In → Out | |---|---|---| | `allocation.py` | per-batch allocation policy | `batch` → `out_cache_loc` | | `hybrid_cache/` | per-layer routing across pools | `layer_id` → pool | | `allocator/` | which slots are free | `need_size` → `indices` | | `pool/` | physical KV / SSM state layout | `(layer_id, indices) ↔ tensor` | | `pool_host/` | host mirror + H2D/D2H | `device_indices ↔ host_indices` | **Dependency invariants** (machine-checkable, enforced by §8): - `pool/` must not import `allocator/`, `hybrid_cache/`, or `allocation.py`. - `pool_host/` must not import `allocator/` or `hybrid_cache/`. - `allocator/` may import `pool/` (it holds the pool it allocates into); the reverse is forbidden. - Nothing under `pool/`, `pool_host/`, or `allocator/` may import the construction layer. Construction depends on them, never the other way round. The original RFC declared per-layer responsibilities but no dependency direction. Without an enforced direction, the split only relocates files — the layers stop being layers the first time a pool reaches back up into an allocator. --- ## 8. Guard: `test_mem_cache_layout_ratchet.py` A directory is not a rule (see §2). The guard is a ratchet test in `test/registered/unit/mem_cache/`, modelled on the existing `test/registered/unit/test_module_state_ratchet.py` and registered into `base-a-test-cpu`. Four pins, each shrink-only, each covering one way the layout regressed after the restructure was agreed. ### R1 — a class lives where its base class says **Role is decided by base class, never by class name** — `HostTensorAllocator` is named `Allocator` but hands out pinned host memory, not KV slots (§4.3). Because inheritance crosses modules, the test builds a class graph over `mem_cache/` and takes its transitive closure. Class names do collide (three modules define `TreeNode`), so ancestry is unioned across same-named definitions: over-approximating turns a collision into a review conversation, where dropping all but one definition would turn it into a silent miss. | Transitive base | Required home | |---|---| | `BaseTokenToKVPoolAllocator` | `mem_cache/allocator/` | | `HostKVCache` | `mem_cache/pool_host/` | | `KVCache`, `BaseSWAKVPool`, `ReqToTokenPool`, `MambaPool` | `mem_cache/pool/` *(deferred)* | `_LEGACY_HOMES` pins the five classes still misfiled today (3 allocators in `multi_ended_allocator.py`, 2 host pools in `memory_pool_host.py`). **The pool role is enforced only once `mem_cache/pool/` exists.** An error telling someone to file a class into a package nobody has created is a trap, not a rule. R3 covers the device pools in the meantime; when the first `pool/` PR lands, `pool` joins the enforced roles and its 29 classes move from R3's pin into `_LEGACY_HOMES`. ### R2 — no new top-level modules `_TOP_LEVEL_MODULES` freezes the 40 `mem_cache/*.py` files that exist today. A new top-level module must go into a package, or grow the pin in the same PR — which forces the "why is this not in a package?" conversation into review instead of leaving it to be noticed three months later. ### R3 — modules slated for deletion only shrink R1 and R2 both miss the most damaging case: a class appended to a module that already exists. That is exactly how `memory_pool.py` gained `PageMajorMHATokenToKVPool`, `MHATokenToKVPoolMXFP8`, `MHATokenToKOnlyPool`, `MiniMaxSparseKVPool` and `DSATokenToKVPool` after the split was agreed. `_SHRINKING_MODULES` pins the class list of every module §5 marks for deletion. It needs no target package to exist, so it is what stands in for the pool role until R1 takes over. ### R4 — layers don't import upwards Asserts the §7 dependency invariants over the import graph. It passes on `main` today, so it locks in a property the code already has rather than demanding new work. ### Mechanics - Pins hold today's state, so the test is green on landing and never blocks unrelated work. - A violation that is not pinned → fail, with an error naming the correct target file and linking this roadmap. - **Every pin also fails when it rots**: a class that has moved, a module that is gone, a file that no longer exists. This makes every move PR shrink a pin (Rule 5 in §3) and turns the pins into the migration's progress ledger. - Scope is `python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/` only. `hardware_backend/` is explicitly excluded — its NPU/MLX pools and allocators are a separate device axis and are not governed by this issue. Each of the six failure paths (four violations, two rot cases) was verified to fire by injecting the violation into a scratch copy of the tree; a guard nobody has seen go red is not a guard. A skill (`.claude/skills/mem-cache-layout/SKILL.md`) covers the same rules for coding agents, but is *not* the guard: human PRs never read `.claude/skills/`. The ratchet blocks; the skill only teaches. --- ## 9. Resolved design decisions **D1 — `Unified*` shared-arena classes stay cohesive.** `unified_memory_pool.py` and `multi_ended_allocator.py` (both from #29678) are `Unified*` variants of every family, but they are coupled to a shared `UnifiedKVPool` arena rather than to their own families. Folding each into its family file would spread one concern across six files. They keep their cohesion in `pool/unified/` and `allocator/multi_ended.py`, as §5 shows. `pool/unified/` is the one place where the one-module-per-family rule (§4.2) is deliberately overridden by a one-module-per-arena split. **D2 — the construction layer is a follow-up issue, not part of this one.** `kv_cache_configurator.py` (2190) + `kv_cache_builder.py` + `cache_init_params.py` + `allocation_sizing.py` + `kv_cache_dtype.py` + `kv_vmm_backing.py` + `hybrid_cache/pool_assembler.py` (1960) is ~5.5k lines with no home in the tier diagram. §7 recognizes it as a cross-cutting layer; §5 deliberately leaves the files where they are. `mem_cache/build/` gets planned as its own issue **after §6.3 lands** — moving construction and storage in the same window would churn the same importers twice and make every Mechanical Move proof harder to review. **D3 — `IndexKeyCache` goes into `pool/dsa.py`, with no new base class.** Its only two importers are `DSATokenToKVPool` and `LayerSplitIndexKeyCache`, both of which land in `pool/dsa.py`; it holds a `self.pool` back-reference and reads ten pool attributes, so today the two sides only avoid an import cycle via `TYPE_CHECKING` and a string annotation. Same module removes the cycle. Its whole API (`move`, `get_buffer`, `store_quantized`, `cpu_copy`, `load_cpu_copy`, `state_buf_infos`) is the storage contract, and `DSATokenToKVPool` forwards to it one line at a time — it is simply DSA's second device buffer. It is **not** given a `KVCache` base just so the guard can classify it: inventing an abstraction to satisfy a linter is the wrong direction. Rule 2 of §8 covers it instead, by pinning the top-level module list.

signals.title: [Bug] Logprob mismatch between Prefill and Decode (Exactly at Index 96) when using FP8 KV Cache on H100
signals.text: ### Checklist - [x] I searched related issues but found no solution. - [ ] The bug persists in the latest version. - [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback. - [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed. - [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Describe the bug ### Issue Description I observed a strange numerical inconsistency in token logprobs between the generation phase (decode) and the prefill phase (when evaluating the full sequence at once) in `sglang`. Specifically, the logprobs match perfectly at the beginning, but start to diverge at a fixed position during the output generation—typically at absolute token index **96** with both English and Chinese prompts. Here are some key insights from my test: * **FP8 Dependency:** This issue **only** occurs when the server is launched with `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3`. If I remove this flag, the logprobs match perfectly between prefill and decode. * **Model & GPU Agnostic:** The mismatch occurs across different models (e.g., `Qwen3-14B-FP8` and `MiniMax-2.5`) and persists on both single-GPU and multi-GPU configurations. This indicates a systematic issue related to FP8 quantization/kernels rather than a specific model weight anomaly. * **The Magic Index Shift:** For a standard prompt, the divergence starts exactly at index 96. In almost all test cases, regardless of how I modify the prompt length, the logprobs between prefill and decode match perfectly and identically for the first 95 tokens, and the divergence always starts exactly at absolute token index 96. There is only one specific edge-case prompt (e.g., changing the phrase to "tell me a long long story") where the divergence boundary nudged to 97. In all other prompt variations, it firmly locks at 96. I am hoping someone can help reproduce this on different hardware setups/versions, or shed some light on why **96/97** acts as the boundary for this strange inconsistency. ### Reproduction ### Server Launch Command ```bash NCCL_DEBUG=INFO CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=4 python3 -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path test/models/Qwen3-14B-FP8 \ --host 0.0.0.0 \ --port 30000 \ --trust-remote-code \ --attention-backend fa3 \ --moe-runner-backend cutlass \ --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 \ --enable-deterministic-inference \ --disable-cuda-graph ``` --- ### Reproduction Script ```python import requests from transformers import AutoTokenizer import matplotlib.font_manager as fm import matplotlib.pyplot as plt model_path = "test/models/Qwen3-14B-FP8" tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model_path) prompt_text = "tell me a story" prompt_text = "讲个故事" prompt = tokenizer.apply_chat_template( conversation=[{"role": "user", "content": prompt_text}], add_generation_prompt=True, ) if isinstance(prompt, dict): prompt_tokens = prompt.get("input_ids") elif not isinstance(prompt, list): prompt_tokens = getattr(prompt, "input_ids") else: prompt_tokens = prompt sglang_url = "http://0.0.0.0:30000/generate" sglang_response = requests.post(sglang_url, json={ "input_ids": prompt_tokens, "return_logprob": True, "logprob_start_len": 0, "sampling_params": { "max_new_tokens": 100, "temperature": 0.0, } }) sglang_response.raise_for_status() sglang_response_json = sglang_response.json() print(sglang_response_json["text"]) input_token_logprobs = sglang_response_json["meta_info"]["input_token_logprobs"] output_token_logprobs = sglang_response_json["meta_info"]["output_token_logprobs"] token_logprobs = input_token_logprobs + output_token_logprobs output_ids = sglang_response_json["output_ids"] full_tokens = prompt_tokens + output_ids gateway_response = requests.post(sglang_url, json={ "input_ids": full_tokens, "return_logprob": True, "logprob_start_len": 0, "sampling_params": { "max_new_tokens": 0, "temperature": 0.0, } }) gateway_response.raise_for_status() gateway_response_json = gateway_response.json() gtw_input_token_logprobs = gateway_response_json["meta_info"]["input_token_logprobs"] gtw_output_token_logprobs = gateway_response_json["meta_info"]["output_token_logprobs"] gtw_token_logprobs = gtw_input_token_logprobs + gtw_output_token_logprobs lp_diff = [ (sg_lp[0] - gtw_lp[0]) for sg_lp, gtw_lp in zip(token_logprobs[1:], gtw_token_logprobs[1:]) ] plt.plot(lp_diff) for i in range(len(lp_diff)): if lp_diff[i] > 0.0: print(i, lp_diff[i]) ``` --- ### Output Logs & Mismatch Details When printing out the non-zero differences (`lp_diff > 0.0`), the mismatch highlights as follows: ```text 96 0.25577104091644287 98 0.21361911296844482 100 0.003986746072769165 102 6.913955076015554e-06 103 0.13288164138793945 104 0.061341941356658936 105 0.2093631476163864 106 0.3519784212112427 109 0.0005509540205821395 ``` ### Request for Collaboration If anyone is running an H100 or similar Ada/Hopper architecture with FP8 KV cache enabled, could you please verify if you see similar logprob drifts? Any pointers toward Triton kernels, FlashAttention alignment boundaries, or allocation chunk sizes that explain this `96` token threshold would be highly appreciated. ### Environment Python: 3.10.20 (main, Mar 11 2026, 17:46:40) [GCC 14.3.0] CUDA available: True GPU 0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7: NVIDIA H100 80GB HBM3 GPU 0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7 Compute Capability: 9.0 CUDA_HOME: /usr/local/cuda NVCC: Cuda compilation tools, release 12.9, V12.9.86 CUDA Driver Version: 570.195.03 PyTorch: 2.9.1+cu128 sglang: 0.5.10rc0 sglang-kernel: 0.4.0 flashinfer_python: 0.6.6 flashinfer_cubin: 0.6.6 flashinfer_jit_cache: Module packaging: 26.0 psutil: 7.2.2 pydantic: 2.13.4 python-multipart: 0.0.28 pyzmq: 27.1.0 uvicorn: 0.47.0 uvloop: 0.22.1 vllm: Module Not Found xgrammar: 0.1.32 openai: 2.6.1 tiktoken: 0.13.0 anthropic: signals.title: [Bug] flashinfer_trtllm MoE runner corrupts MiniMax-M2.7-NVFP4 output and asserts on DeepSeek-V4-Flash on B200
signals.text:
### Checklist - [x] I searched related issues but found no solution (see Related issues section below for adjacent reports). - [x] Reproduces on SGLang `v0.5.12` and `v0.5.12.post1` (current stable release at draft time); `dev` / `nightly-dev` not tested. - [x] Environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are included below. - [x] This is a bug report, not a general question. - [x] Posted in English. ### Summary On 8x NVIDIA B200 (SM100), the `flashinfer_trtllm` MoE runner shows two failure modes across the two MoE checkpoints I tested in SGLang `v0.5.12` and `v0.5.12.post1`: 1. **`nvidia/MiniMax-M2.7-NVFP4`**: the server starts successfully and returns HTTP 200, but generation is deterministic replacement-character-heavy corrupted text at `temperature=0`. This reproduces across the localization sweep below: FP4 GEMM backend, prompt shape, max_tokens, SGLang version, and both TP=8 and TP=1. 2. **`deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash`**: the server crashes at first forward pass with an `AssertionError` at `flashinfer_trtllm.py:686`. For comparison, the launch command shown on the NVIDIA model card for `nvidia/MiniMax-M2.7-NVFP4` uses `--moe-runner-backend flashinfer_cutlass`. On the same hardware, image, weights, and probes, that path produces clean expected output for M2.7-NVFP4, including `"What is 2+2?"` → `"4"` and 0% non-ASCII ratio across all four probes. The M2.7 failure narrows to the `flashinfer_trtllm` MoE runner path; I did not capture a server-side trace pinpointing the specific fused function reached on M2.7. The V4-Flash crash reaches the FP8 fused-experts path at `flashinfer_trtllm.py:686` (`fused_experts_none_to_flashinfer_trtllm_fp8`) per the stack trace below. **Maintainer note:** - **Scope:** I filed this as one issue because both failures occur through the `flashinfer_trtllm` MoE runner module. I have not verified that they share a root cause. I can split into separate issues if triage prefers. - **Terminology:** `flashinfer_trtllm` here refers to FlashInfer's TRT-LLM-derived MoE kernel path used through SGLang dispatch, not standalone TensorRT-LLM. ### Environment | Field | Value | | --- | --- | | Hardware | 8x NVIDIA B200 SXM (SM100) | | Driver | 580.126.09 | | CUDA in container | 13.0.1 (NVCC 13.0.88) | | Image | `lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.12.post1` | | Image digest | `sha256:b9079f568489b6620b580c2658e68e24791f02a212c4de23b8b5d42661de4b11` | | Image label | `ai.sglang.image.tag=lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.12.post1` | | SGLang commit | `5a15cde858ea09b77116212a39356f2fc51b8584` (per image labels) | | SGLang version (in-container) | `0.5.12.post1` | | FlashInfer | `0.6.11.post1` | | PyTorch | `2.11.0+cu130` (wheel built against CUDA 13.0; runs on container CUDA 13.0.1) | | Triton | `3.6.0` | | ModelOpt | `0.44.0` | | Transformers | `5.6.0` | | Python | `3.12` | | HF revision: `nvidia/MiniMax-M2.7-NVFP4` | `e79701cb1f9dce8fe5395b9ed2b20170beebecde` (uploaded 2026-04-24) | | HF revision: `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash` | `6976c7ff1b30a1b2cb7805021b8ba4684041f136` (uploaded 2026-05-06) | Also confirmed with base `lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.12` (the original V4 day-0 build before the `.post1` patch). Both versions exhibit the same failure mode (output reproduces under the base tag; see Cross-version evidence table below for the caveat that I captured `pip freeze` only inside the `.post1` container). This is not a `.post1`-only regression. > Note for maintainers: per FlashInfer release notes, DeepSeek-V4 sparse MLA TRTLLM-GEN kernels (PR flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#3269) landed in FlashInfer `v0.6.12rc1` (2026-05-22), which post-dates the FlashInfer `0.6.11.post1` shipped inside `lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.12.post1`. This may be relevant to Failure Mode 2 (V4-Flash assertion). I have not yet tested with FlashInfer `0.6.12+` and can do so on request.
python3 -m sglang.check_env output (captured inside lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.12.post1 on the test node) ``` ========== == CUDA == ========== CUDA Version 13.0.1 Python: 3.12.3 (main, Mar 23 2026, 19:04:32) [GCC 13.3.0] CUDA available: True GPU 0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7: NVIDIA B200 GPU 0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7 Compute Capability: 10.0 CUDA_HOME: /usr/local/cuda NVCC: Cuda compilation tools, release 13.0, V13.0.88 CUDA Driver Version: 580.126.09 PyTorch: 2.11.0+cu130 sglang: 0.5.12.post1 sglang-kernel: 0.4.2.post2 flashinfer_python: 0.6.11.post1 flashinfer_cubin: 0.6.11.post1 flashinfer_jit_cache: 0.6.11.post1+cu130 triton: 3.6.0 transformers: 5.6.0 torchao: 0.17.0+cu130 numpy: 2.3.5 aiohttp: 3.13.5 fastapi: 0.136.1 huggingface_hub: 1.16.1 interegular: 0.3.3 modelscope: 1.37.1 orjson: 3.11.9 outlines: 0.1.11 packaging: 26.2 psutil: 7.2.2 pydantic: 2.13.4 python-multipart: 0.0.29 pyzmq: 27.1.0 uvicorn: 0.47.0 uvloop: 0.22.1 vllm: Module Not Found xgrammar: 0.2.0 openai: 2.6.1 tiktoken: 0.13.0 anthropic: 0.104.1 litellm: Module Not Found torchcodec: 0.11.1+cu130 NVIDIA Topology: GPU0 GPU1 GPU2 GPU3 GPU4 GPU5 GPU6 GPU7 CPU Affinity NUMA Affinity GPU NUMA ID GPU0 X NV18 NV18 NV18 NV18 NV18 NV18 NV18 0-79 0 N/A GPU1 NV18 X NV18 NV18 NV18 NV18 NV18 NV18 0-79 0 N/A GPU2 NV18 NV18 X NV18 NV18 NV18 NV18 NV18 0-79 0 N/A GPU3 NV18 NV18 NV18 X NV18 NV18 NV18 NV18 0-79 0 N/A GPU4 NV18 NV18 NV18 NV18 X NV18 NV18 NV18 80-159 1 N/A GPU5 NV18 NV18 NV18 NV18 NV18 X NV18 NV18 80-159 1 N/A GPU6 NV18 NV18 NV18 NV18 NV18 NV18 X NV18 80-159 1 N/A GPU7 NV18 NV18 NV18 NV18 NV18 NV18 NV18 X 80-159 1 N/A Hypervisor vendor:: KVM ulimit soft: 1024 ```
### Failure Mode 1: M2.7-NVFP4 produces deterministic mojibake **Reproduction.** Launch: ```bash docker run --rm --gpus all --ipc=host --network=host --shm-size=32g \ --ulimit nofile=1048576:1048576 --ulimit memlock=-1 --ulimit stack=67108864 \ -v /path/to/m27-nvfp4:/models/m27-nvfp4:ro \ -e HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 \ lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.12.post1 \ python3 -m sglang.launch_server \ --model /models/m27-nvfp4 \ --served-model-name nvidia/MiniMax-M2.7-NVFP4 \ --tensor-parallel-size 8 \ --quantization modelopt_fp4 \ --trust-remote-code \ --reasoning-parser minimax-append-think \ --tool-call-parser minimax-m2 \ --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_trtllm \ --fp4-gemm-backend cutlass \ --attention-backend flashinfer \ --host 127.0.0.1 --port 30000 ``` Probe (temperature=0): ```bash curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:30000/v1/chat/completions \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"model":"nvidia/MiniMax-M2.7-NVFP4","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"What is 2+2? Reply with the number only."}],"temperature":0,"max_tokens":64}' \ | python3 -c 'import json,sys; print(repr(json.load(sys.stdin)["choices"][0]["message"]["content"]))' ``` **Expected**: clean answer content. With the `flashinfer_cutlass` MoE path, this probe returns `'... 4'`. **Observed** with `flashinfer_trtllm` MoE: `'�s000,�s,�s�l�l�s�l�l�s�l�n�s�l�s�l�s�l�i�s�l�i�s�l�i�s�l�i�s�l�'`. The output is deterministic across repeated `temperature=0` invocations and has a high non-ASCII/replacement-character ratio. **Localization sweep.** Failure reproduces under every combination I tested across these five axes: | Axis | Variants tested | All mojibake? | | --- | --- | --- | | FP4 GEMM backend | `auto`, `cutlass`, `flashinfer_cutedsl` | yes | | Prompt content / shape | 4 probes (2+2 short, 2+2 long max_tokens, reasoning, chat-shape long-context) | yes | | Prompt max_tokens | 64, 256, 512 | yes | | SGLang version | `v0.5.12`, `v0.5.12.post1` (byte-identical outputs) | yes | | Tensor parallelism | TP=8, TP=1 (single B200) | yes (TP=1 produces denser corruption than TP=8; see following table) | Sample per-probe statistics from the `cutlass` FP4 + `flashinfer_trtllm` MoE configuration at TP=8: | Probe | Probe description | max_tokens | Non-ASCII chars (code points) | Total chars (code points) | Non-ASCII ratio | | --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | | p1 | "What is 2+2?" | 64 | 30 | 71 | 42.25% | | p2 | Same prompt | 256 | 121 | 276 | 43.84% | | p3 | Reasoning ("trains meeting") | 256 | 203 | 279 | 72.76% | | p4 | Chat-shape long-context | 512 | 178 | 791 | 22.50% | Same probes at TP=1 (single B200), same model, same backend flags except `--tensor-parallel-size 1`: | Probe | Non-ASCII ratio (TP=1) | Non-ASCII ratio (TP=8) | | --- | ---: | ---: | | p1 | **88.73%** | 42.25% | | p2 | **96.96%** | 43.84% | | p3 | **96.20%** | 72.76% | | p4 | **75.72%** | 22.50% | TP=1 produces replacement-char-heavy output more densely than TP=8 across every probe. The failure reproduces on a single rank, so TP-distributed expert dispatch and all-to-all are not required to trigger it. This narrows the M2.7 repro to the single-rank `flashinfer_trtllm` runner/kernel path. **Cross-version evidence.** Identical config (`cutlass` FP4 + `flashinfer_trtllm` MoE), same hardware, same probes, only the SGLang image differs: | Image | Image digest | p1 first 200 chars | p2-p4 | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.12.post1` | `sha256:b9079f568489b6620b580c2658e68e24791f02a212c4de23b8b5d42661de4b11` | `�s000,�s,�s�l�l�s�l�l�s�l�n�s�l�s�l�s�l�i�s�l�i...` | replacement-char-heavy | | `lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.12` | `sha256:79d577610f5022e66b5bb618d434b23ab7121fc9f96d5dba3ee046d5eecfd4df` | byte-identical to row above | byte-identical | `v0.5.12.post1` is the post-release patch of the base `v0.5.12` release that introduced day-0 DeepSeek-V4 support. I observe the same output under the base tag; the in-container `pip freeze` was captured only for `.post1`, so I report this as "same output reproduces on base `v0.5.12`" rather than "byte-identical package set." This is not a `.post1`-only regression. **Reference comparison.** "Reference" throughout this draft means the NVIDIA model-card-recommended launch command (`--moe-runner-backend flashinfer_cutlass`); see . Same hardware, same image, same weights, same probes, only swapping `--moe-runner-backend flashinfer_trtllm` (the bug repro) back to `--moe-runner-backend flashinfer_cutlass`: | Probe | Non-ASCII ratio (`flashinfer_cutlass` MoE) | | --- | ---: | | p1 | 0% (cleanly returns "4") | | p2-p4 | 0% (clean prose) | ### Failure Mode 2: V4-Flash crashes at first forward pass Same image, same hardware, weights at `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash`. Launch command: ```bash docker run --rm --gpus all --ipc=host --network=host --shm-size=32g \ --ulimit nofile=1048576:1048576 --ulimit memlock=-1 --ulimit stack=67108864 \ -v /path/to/v4-flash:/models/v4-flash:ro \ -e HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 \ lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.12.post1 \ python3 -m sglang.launch_server \ --model /models/v4-flash \ --served-model-name deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash \ --tensor-parallel-size 8 \ --trust-remote-code \ --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_trtllm \ --attention-backend flashinfer \ --host 127.0.0.1 --port 30000 ``` This launch differs from Failure Mode 1 only in: model path and served-model-name swapped to V4-Flash; M2.7-specific `--reasoning-parser minimax-append-think`, `--tool-call-parser minimax-m2`, and `--quantization modelopt_fp4 --fp4-gemm-backend cutlass` flags dropped. V4-Flash carries its quantization in the model config. The server crashes during initial forward pass: ``` File "/sgl-workspace/sglang/python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/fused_moe_triton/layer.py", line 1062, in forward return self.forward_impl(hidden_states, topk_output) File "/sgl-workspace/sglang/python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/fused_moe_triton/layer.py", line 1072, in forward_impl combine_input = self.run_moe_core( File "/sgl-workspace/sglang/python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/fp8.py", line 1874, in apply return self.runner.run(dispatch_output, quant_info) File "/sgl-workspace/sglang/python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/runner.py", line 100, in run return self.fused_func(dispatch_output, quant_info, self.config) File "/sgl-workspace/sglang/python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/flashinfer_trtllm.py", line 1116, in fused_experts_none_to_flashinfer_trtllm return fused_experts_none_to_flashinfer_trtllm_fp8( File "/sgl-workspace/sglang/python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/flashinfer_trtllm.py", line 686, in fused_experts_none_to_flashinfer_trtllm_fp8 assert TopKOutputChecker.format_is_bypassed(topk_output) AssertionError ``` The same `flashinfer_trtllm.py` module that produces corrupted output on M2.7 fails an explicit format check on V4-Flash. The assertion suggests the FP8 fused path is receiving a `topk_output` format that does not satisfy `TopKOutputChecker.format_is_bypassed(topk_output)`. ### Localization summary The tested failures localize to the **`flashinfer_trtllm` MoE runner path**: - V4-Flash reaches the FP8 fused-experts code at `flashinfer_trtllm.py:686`. - M2.7 returns corrupted text through the same runner path, though I did not capture a trace identifying the exact fused function reached. The M2.7 sweep makes these less likely as primary triggers: - FP4 GEMM backend: varied `auto`, `cutlass`, and `flashinfer_cutedsl`; all reproduced. - Prompt content / shape: four probes reproduced. - Tensor parallelism: reproduced at both TP=8 and TP=1 (TP=1 produces denser corruption than TP=8 across all four probes; the bug is not TP-distribution-specific). - SGLang image: reproduced under both `v0.5.12` and `v0.5.12.post1`. - Weight loading / basic scheduler path: the `flashinfer_cutlass` MoE path on the same image, hardware, weights, and probes produced clean output. ### What this issue does NOT validate Untested axes (all orthogonal; I can run any on request): - FlashInfer `0.6.12rc1` or newer (only `0.6.11.post1` tested, as bundled in `lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.12.post1`). - SGLang `dev` / `nightly-dev` tags. - Different SM (only B200/SM100 tested; H100/H200 not tested). - Different attention backend (only `flashinfer` tested; `fa3`/`fa4`/`trtllm_mha`/`flashmla` not tested). - DeepEP / expert-parallelism enabled. - Speculative decoding enabled. - KV cache dtype other than default. - `--disable-flashinfer-autotune` (per the SGLang cookbook for DeepSeek-V4; not tested here). - Other NVFP4 MoE checkpoints beyond `nvidia/MiniMax-M2.7-NVFP4` and `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash`. - Direct FlashInfer-only repro (I observe the failure through SGLang's dispatch into FlashInfer). ### Repro artifacts Run directories on the test node, by purpose: - M2.7 isolation sweep manifest + per-probe smoke responses (A1 / X1 / TW configs at chat 2K/512 Poisson 4 rps): `track1-prepost-moe-isolation-20260525T180536Z/` - Cross-version probe artifacts (M2.7 on `v0.5.12.post1` + base `v0.5.12`, 4 probes per image, full analysis.txt): `mojibake-probe-20260525T182412Z/` - Localization probe artifacts (V4-Flash full crash log + M2.7 TP=1 single-rank probes): `localization-probes-20260525T184624Z/` - Reference (`flashinfer_cutlass` MoE) baseline + 3-run regimes: `track1-m27-reference-20260525T155755Z/` and `track1-reference-regimes-20260525T044957Z/` - Inside-container `pip freeze` (full 335-line capture from `lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.12.post1`): `env-capture-20260525T191232Z/env.txt` Available inline on request: full V4-Flash traceback, complete `pip freeze`, per-probe response JSONs, M2.7 server logs around the bad-output requests, raw response bytes (hex) for byte-level inspection. I can post a gist with any subset the maintainer wants to inspect. ### Potential next checks - Test whether FlashInfer `0.6.12rc1` or newer changes either failure mode. I can run this if useful. - Open a parallel issue in `flashinfer-ai/flashinfer` if maintainers believe the root cause is upstream of SGLang dispatch. - Consider replacing the V4-Flash assertion with a clearer error or fallback path if this topk format is currently unsupported by the FP8 `flashinfer_trtllm` path. ### Related issues Adjacent reports surfaced during issue search. I did not find an exact duplicate; these appear adjacent on the axes called out per bullet (let triage decide on duplication). None of them include an applicable fix or workaround for the failure modes reported here. Included for triage context in case they share a root cause or a tracking owner. - #19971 — `MiniMax-M2.5 FP8 produces garbage output on B200 with default trtllm gemm backend`. Same hardware (B200), same model family (M2 series), same "garbage output" symptom, different quantization (FP8 vs NVFP4) and different layer (trtllm GEMM vs trtllm MoE). May indicate a pattern in trtllm-derived kernels on B200 for this family. - #18989 (closed) — `[Bug] deepseek 3.2 nvfp4 moe-runner-backend=flashinfer_trtllm illegal memory access`. Same MoE runner, different NVFP4 MoE checkpoint, different failure mode (illegal memory access vs mojibake/assertion). Same kernel family. - #24502 — `[Bug] flashinfer_trtllm MoE runner has no DeepEP fused func registered — blocks EP+NVFP4 on Blackwell`. Same MoE runner, Blackwell-specific structural gap on a different code path. - #20022 — `[Tracking] Minimax-M2.5 (G)B200 Functional Support and Optimizations`. Cross-linking for the M2-family Blackwell tracking owners. Reporter context: independent benchmarking work on Nebius B200 hardware.

signals.title: [Bug] DeepSeek-V4-Pro Multi-Node PP2 TP8 Fails with AssertionError: Hidden size mismatch in Triton MoE Kernel
signals.text: ### Checklist - [x] I searched related issues but found no solution. - [x] The bug persists in the latest version. - [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback. - [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed. - [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Describe the bug ### **Title** [Bug] DeepSeek-V4-Pro Multi-Node PP2 TP8 Fails with `AssertionError: Hidden size mismatch` in Triton MoE Kernel --- ### **Type** Bug Report / Performance Scaling --- ### **Description** When deploying **DeepSeek-V4-Pro** (FP8 weights) on a multi-node high-performance cluster (2 nodes, 16x H100 80GB GPUs) using `pipeline-parallel-size=2` and `tensor-parallel-size=8`, SGLang crashes during the forward pass. Interestingly, the exact same `PP=2, TP=8` layout works successfully under vLLM, but SGLang throws an `AssertionError: Hidden size mismatch` inside its Triton MoE core (`fused_experts_impl`). Even after passing `--disable-cuda-graph`, the error persists, shifting from the CUDA Graph capture phase directly into the first request execution (`forward_extend` event loop). It seems that the PP proxy tensors or layer-slicing logic passes incorrect hidden dimension shapes into the `fused_moe` Triton kernel when PP > 1. Given that SGLang is highly optimized for DeepSeek architectures, enabling reliable multi-node PP scaling for DeepSeek-V4-Pro is crucial for large-scale enterprise clusters where cross-node tensor parallelism faces bandwidth constraints. --- ### **Environment** * **SGLang Version:** `v0.5.12.post1` (Official Docker Image: `lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.12.post1`) * **Hardware:** 2x Nodes, each with 8x NVIDIA H100 PCIe/SXM5 80GB (Total 16 GPUs) * **Interconnect:** High-bandwidth RoCE/InfiniBand (mlx5 HCAs mapped via `NCCL_IB_HCA`) * **CUDA Version:** 13.0.1 (Inside container) * **PyTorch Version:** 2.x (Bundled with container) --- ### **Steps to Reproduce** #### **Node 0 (Rank 0, Master IP: 192.168.180.132)** ```bash export HEAD_IP="192.168.180.132" docker run --rm --gpus all --network host \ --privileged --ipc=host \ --shm-size 128g \ --hostname gnho032 \ --add-host "gnho032:192.168.180.132" \ --add-host "gnho033:192.168.180.133" \ -v /storage/hpc/chendongshuo/.cache/huggingface:/root/.cache/huggingface \ -v /storage/hpc/chendongshuo/LLMs/DeepSeek-V4-Pro:/model/DeepSeek-V4-Pro \ -e NCCL_IB_HCA=mlx5_0,mlx5_2,mlx5_4,mlx5_6,mlx5_8 \ lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.12.post1 \ python3 -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path /model/DeepSeek-V4-Pro \ --trust-remote-code \ --served-model-name deepseek_pro \ --tensor-parallel-size 8 \ --pipeline-parallel-size 2 \ --nnodes 2 \ --node-rank 0 \ --dist-init-addr ${HEAD_IP}:5000 \ --host 0.0.0.0 \ --port 8000 \ --mem-fraction-static 0.90 \ --context-length 1000000 \ --chunked-prefill-size 4096 \ --max-running-requests 256 \ --tool-call-parser deepseekv4 \ --reasoning-parser deepseek-v4 \ --enable-cache-report ``` #### **Node 1 (Rank 1)** *(Same as Node 0, but running with `--node-rank 1`)* --- ### **Crash Traceback / Log Output** When running **with CUDA Graph enabled**, it fails during CUDA Graph capture: ```text [2026-06-03 03:21:28 PP0 TP0] Scheduler hit an exception: Traceback (most recent call last): ... File "/sgl-workspace/sglang/python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_v2.py", line 728, in forward return self.forward_normal_dual_stream( ... ) File "/sgl-workspace/sglang/python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_v2.py", line 784, in forward_normal_dual_stream final_hidden_states = self.experts(hidden_states, topk_output) ... File "/sgl-workspace/sglang/python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/triton_utils/fused_moe.py", line 121, in inplace_fused_experts fused_experts_impl( ... ) File "/sgl-workspace/sglang/python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/triton_utils/fused_moe.py", line 828, in fused_experts_impl assert hidden_states.shape[1] == w1.shape[2] - padded_size AssertionError: Hidden size mismatch ``` When running **with `--disable-cuda-graph**`, it bypasses the warmup but crashes instantly during the first extended forward pass (`forward_extend`) in the event loop: ```text [2026-06-03 03:35:10 PP0 TP2] Scheduler hit an exception: Traceback (most recent call last): File "/sgl-workspace/sglang/python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py", line 4041, in run_scheduler_process scheduler.run_event_loop() ... File "/sgl-workspace/sglang/python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler_pp_mixin.py", line 1175, in _pp_launch_batch result = self.run_batch(self.cur_batch, pp_proxy_tensors) ... File "/sgl-workspace/sglang/python/sglang/srt/model_executor/model_runner.py", line 3458, in _forward_raw ret, can_run_graph = self.forward_extend( ... ) ... File "/sgl-workspace/sglang/python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/triton_utils/fused_moe.py", line 828, in fused_experts_impl hidden_states.shape[1] == w1.shape[2] - padded_size AssertionError: Hidden size mismatch ``` --- ### **Expected Behavior** The model should initialize the pipeline-parallel groups correctly and complete the forward passes without dimension assertions inside the Triton MoE kernels, matching the multi-node PP capabilities found in other frameworks like vLLM. ### Reproduction 。 ### Environment 。

signals.title: [Bug] main-cann8.5.0-910b image fails to import torch_npu due to torch / torch_npu ABI mismatch
signals.text: ### Checklist - [x] I searched related issues but found no solution. - [x] The bug persists in the latest version. - [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback. - [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed. - [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Describe the bug When using the official/community SGLang NPU image: `swr.cn-southwest-2.myhuaweicloud.com/base_image/dockerhub/lmsysorg/sglang:main-cann8.5.0-910b` `sglang serve` fails immediately during startup while importing `torch`. The container has an incompatible PyTorch / torch_npu combination: - `torch`: `2.12.0` - `torch_npu`: `2.8.0.post2` Importing `torch` triggers torch backend auto-loading, which attempts to load `torch_npu`, but `libtorch_npu.so` fails with an undefined symbol: `_ZNK3c1010TensorImpl20is_contiguous_customENS_12MemoryFormatE` Detail error log: ``` File "/usr/local/python3.11.14/lib/python3.11/site-packages/torch_npu/utils/__init__.py", line 4, in from torch_npu import _C ImportError: /usr/local/python3.11.14/lib/python3.11/site-packages/torch_npu/lib/libtorch_npu.so: undefined symbol: _ZNK3c1010TensorImpl20is_contiguous_customENS_12MemoryFormatE The above exception was the direct cause of the following exception: Traceback (most recent call last): File "/usr/local/python3.11.14/bin/sglang", line 3, in from sglang.cli.main import main File "/sgl-workspace/sglang/python/sglang/__init__.py", line 29, in from sglang.srt.utils.hf_transformers_patches import apply_all as _apply_hf_patches File "/sgl-workspace/sglang/python/sglang/srt/utils/__init__.py", line 2, in from sglang.srt.utils.common import * File "/sgl-workspace/sglang/python/sglang/srt/utils/common.py", line 82, in import torch File "/usr/local/python3.11.14/lib/python3.11/site-packages/torch/__init__.py", line 3042, in _import_device_backends() File "/usr/local/python3.11.14/lib/python3.11/site-packages/torch/__init__.py", line 2999, in _import_device_backends raise RuntimeError( RuntimeError: Failed to load the backend extension: torch_npu. You can disable extension auto-loading with TORCH_DEVICE_BACKEND_AUTOLOAD=0. ``` This looks like the `main-cann8.5.0-910b` image was built with mismatched `torch` and `torch_npu` wheels. ### Reproduction 1. Pull the image: ```bash docker pull --platform linux/arm64 \ swr.cn-southwest-2.myhuaweicloud.com/base_image/dockerhub/lmsysorg/sglang:main-cann8.5.0-910b ``` 2. Start a container on Ascend 910B / 910B3. 3. Run: ```bash sglang serve \ --model-path /nas/disk1/Qwen-Image-2512 \ --port 8080 \ --log-level debug \ --host 0.0.0.0 ``` ### Environment - Image: `swr.cn-southwest-2.myhuaweicloud.com/base_image/dockerhub/lmsysorg/sglang:main-cann8.5.0-910b` - Platform: `linux/arm64` - Device: Ascend 910B3 - `npu-smi`: `25.5.0` - Python: `/usr/local/python3.11.14/bin/python` - Python version: `3.11.14` - CANN path in `sys.path`: - `/usr/local/Ascend/cann-8.5.0/python/site-packages` - `/usr/local/Ascend/ascend-toolkit/latest/python/site-packages` - `torch`: `2.12.0` - `torch_npu`: `2.8.0.post2` - Model: `/nas/disk1/Qwen-Image-2512`

signals.title: [Bug] EAGLE speculative decoding crashes with Mooncake L3 HiCache in standalone client mode (v0.5.13 regression)
signals.text: ### Checklist - [x] I searched related issues but found no solution. - [x] The bug persists in the latest version. - [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback. - [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed. - [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Describe the bug SGLang v0.5.13 introduced a new code path `maybe_register_hicache_draft()` that registers the EAGLE DRAFT KV pool with the Mooncake storage backend. When using Mooncake in **Mode B (standalone real client + dummy client)**, this registration fails because the DRAFT host pool buffer is allocated outside the Mooncake real client's shared memory segment. `register_buffer()` returns -1, causing a `RuntimeError` that crashes all scheduler processes during startup. This is a **regression from v0.5.12**, where the same EAGLE + Mooncake L3 configuration works without issue. In v0.5.12, the DRAFT KV pool is registered successfully ("HiCache draft KV registered: MHATokenToKVPool") and the server starts normally. The crash occurs at: ``` scheduler.py → kv_cache_builder.maybe_register_hicache_draft() → cache_controller.set_draft_kv_pool(pool, draft_host_pool) → cache_controller._maybe_register_draft_with_storage() → mooncake_store.register_mem_host_pool_v2(host_pool, PoolName.DRAFT) → mooncake_store.register_buffer(host_pool.kv_buffer) → store.register_buffer(ptr, size) # returns -1 → raise RuntimeError("Failed to register buffer to Mooncake Store, error code: -1") ``` The root cause is that in Mode B, SGLang runs as a DummyClient. The DRAFT host pool is allocated by SGLang's own allocator, which is not in the Mooncake real client's shared memory segment. The Mooncake `register_buffer()` API correctly rejects buffers outside its shared memory segment, but v0.5.13 unconditionally attempts this registration for the DRAFT pool. ### Reproduction ### Environment setup 1. Start Mooncake master with offload enabled: ```bash mooncake_master \ --rpc_port 50051 \ --http_metadata_server_port 8080 \ --eviction_high_watermark_ratio 0.7 \ --metrics_port 9003 \ --enable_offload \ --logtostderr \ --enable_metric_reporting \ --enable_http_metadata_server ``` 2. Start Mooncake standalone real client with SSD offload: ```bash MOONCAKE_OFFLOAD_FILE_STORAGE_PATH=/kv-cache-volume \ MOONCAKE_OFFLOAD_STORAGE_BACKEND_DESCRIPTOR=bucket_storage_backend \ MOONCAKE_OFFLOAD_BUCKET_MAX_TOTAL_SIZE=2199023255552 \ MOONCAKE_OFFLOAD_BUCKET_EVICTION_POLICY=lru \ MOONCAKE_OFFLOAD_LOCAL_BUFFER_SIZE_BYTES=51539607552 \ mooncake_client \ --master_server_address 127.0.0.1:50051 \ --host 127.0.0.1 \ --port 50052 \ --protocol rdma \ --device_names '' \ --metadata_server P2PHANDSHAKE \ --global_segment_size 256GB \ --threads 8 \ --enable_offload \ --logtostderr ``` 3. [2026-06-22 02:10:13] kill_process_tree called: parent_pid=1839, include_parent=True, pid=1839 ``` Full traceback: ``` File "/sgl-workspace/sglang/python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py", line 4046, in run_scheduler_process scheduler = Scheduler( File "/sgl-workspace/sglang/python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py", line 490, in __init__ kv_cache_builder.maybe_register_hicache_draft( File "/sgl-workspace/sglang/python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/kv_cache_builder.py", line 127, in maybe_register_hicache_draft tree_cache.cache_controller.set_draft_kv_pool(pool, draft_host_pool) File "/sgl-workspace/sglang/python/sglang/srt/managers/cache_controller.py", line 871, in set_draft_kv_pool self._maybe_register_draft_with_storage() File "/sgl-workspace/sglang/python/sglang/srt/managers/cache_controller.py", line 890, in _maybe_register_draft_with_storage self.storage_backend.register_mem_host_pool_v2( File "/sgl-workspace/sglang/python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/storage/mooncake_store/mooncake_store.py", line 637, in register_mem_host_pool_v2 super().register_buffer(host_pool.kv_buffer) File "/sgl-workspace/sglang/python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/storage/mooncake_store/mooncake_store.py", line 297, in register_buffer raise RuntimeError( RuntimeError: Failed to register buffer to Mooncake Store, error code: -1 ``` ### Success output (v0.5.12, same configuration) ``` [2026-06-22 02:36:38 TP0] HiCache draft KV registered: MHATokenToKVPool (host 3404288 slots) [2026-06-22 02:36:38 TP1] HiCache draft KV registered: MHATokenToKVPool (host 3404288 slots) ... signals.title: [Bug] DeepSeek-v4-pro on a multi-node H20 cluster with tp != dp hang
signals.text: ### Checklist - [x] I searched related issues but found no solution. - [x] The bug persists in the latest version. - [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback. - [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed. - [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Describe the bug When running DeepSeek-V4-Pro-FP8 on a multi-node H20 cluster with --tp 32 --ep 32 --dp 4 --enable-dp-attention + --moe-a2a-backend deepep, two issues accur **Issue 1 — Hang on all-reduce due to wrong communication group in DP attention** With DP attention enabled, some DP ranks receive empty batches and fast return, while others still enter the attention output projection (wo_b) and trigger an all-reduce. ``` DP0 / TP0-3: has tokens -> enters wo_b -> calls all-reduce -> blocks waiting for all ranks DP1 / TP4-7: empty batch -> fast return -> never calls this all-reduce ``` If wo_b uses the global TP group all-reduce, the collective becomes an 8-rank barrier where only 4 ranks show up. The empty-batch ranks skip it → permanent hang. Root cause: - the DeepSeek-V4 attention output linear layer defaults to a global TP all-reduce; under DP attention it must use the attention TP group (intra-DP-group) all-reduce instead. Relevant code: - python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_v4.py:462 (MQALayer.__init__) - python/sglang/srt/layers/linear.py:1543 (RowParallelLinear.forward) --- **Issue 2 — DeepEP bootstrap communication failure on multi-node H20** During DeepEP buffer creation, the NCCL/NVSHMEM bootstrap stage receives messages of unexpected length, causing startup/communication failure. Root cause: - on CU13 + flashinfer, the code may enable the MNNVL fabric path (use_fabric=True) via is_mnnvl_fabric_supported(). - MNNVL fabric is the cross-pod NVLink GPU-to-GPU memory path for GB200/GB300 NVL systems and must not be used on H20. Relevant code: - python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/token_dispatcher/deepep.py:237-258 (DeepEPBuffer.get_deepep_buffer) ### Reproduction ```bash export SGLANG_ENABLE_TP_MEMORY_INBALANCE_CHECK=0 export signals.title: [AMD] kv_canary verify_real_kv_hash intermittently fires in PD full-real-data path on ROCm
signals.text: ## Summary On ROCm (gfx942 / rocm700, `linux-mi325-2gpu-sglang`), the mock-model PD full-real-data canary test intermittently trips a `verify_real_kv_hash` kv_canary violation on the **decode** side, crashing the scheduler (in `--kv-canary raise` mode → decode `rc=-9` → 500s → job exit 137). Surfaced while onboarding `mock_model/test_e2e_pd.py` to AMD CI in #28850. The `TestPdTransferChecksumFullRealData` class (server args `--kv-canary-real-data all --kv-canary-sweep-interval 1`) is now gated off on AMD via `@unittest.skipIf(is_hip(), ...)`; the baseline `TestPdTransferCanaryClean` stays enabled. This issue tracks re-enabling the full-real-data leg on AMD. ## Evidence From PR Test Extra (AMD) run [27976339910](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/27976339910), job `extra-a-test-2-gpu-large-amd`: ``` disaggregation/decode.py:1807 event_loop_overlap_disagg_decode -> run_batch -> model_runner.forward -> kv_canary/runner/canary_manager.py _post_ops_outside_graph -> violation_manager.step() RuntimeError: kv_canary violation: launch_tag=TAIL_K_FULL fail_reason=verify_real_kv_hash slot_idx=61390 position=6092 stored_token=2005 expected_token=-1 stored_chain_hash=0x551075b2a7b94875 expected_aux=0x551075b2a7b94875 total_violations=256 [FIXTURE FAIL-FAST] decode (pid=...) exited rc=-9; aborting. ``` Key observations: - Servers started healthy (`available_gpu_mem=52.28 GB`, `max_total_num_tokens=3626179`) — not an OOM. - Violations are on a contiguous run of transferred-prefix slots near the prompt boundary (positions ~6092+), on the decode side `TAIL_K_FULL` verify. - The **chain hash matches** (`stored_chain_hash == expected_aux`); only the **real KV content hash** mismatches (`fail_reason=verify_real_kv_hash`). - Intermittent: the same test passed on a prior commit and on the rocm720 lane. ## Hypotheses 1. Intermittent PD KV-transfer nondeterminism on ROCm (prefill-written KV bytes differ from decode-read KV for some transferred slots). 2. Canary real-KV-hash sensitivity to ROCm/aiter bf16 nondeterminism in the PD path. ## Repro Dispatch `pr-test-amd-extra.yml` (default mi325 lane) and run `extra-a-test-2-gpu-large-amd`, or run `mock_model/test_e2e_pd.py::TestPdTransferChecksumFullRealData` on a 2-GPU MI325 host. It reproduces intermittently.
