signals.title: [Bug][kimi-k3] Long-context [PAD] (id 163839) storms + DSPARK inf/nan asserts — NaN-contaminated logits; released kimi-k3 image predates #32477; pad not stopped/filtered; allowed_special="all" makes [PAD] injectable
signals.text: ## Summary Serving **Kimi-K3** on the `kimi-k3` branch with DSPARK speculative decoding, we observe two recurring production failure modes that we believe share one root cause (transient **NaN contamination of logits**, consistent with the write-side bug fixed by #32477 — which is **not in any released `kimi-k3` image**): - **A. Mid-generation `[PAD]` token storms** — the model suddenly starts emitting the pad token (**id 163839**) as literal `[PAD]` text mid-response (in either the think channel or the content channel) and never stops until `max_tokens` or client disconnect. Worst single stream we captured: **17,256 `[PAD]` occurrences, ~2 MB of SSE, 664 s of decode**. - **B. DSPARK CUDA assert crashes** — sporadic full-engine aborts with `probability tensor contains either inf, nan or element < 0` (TensorCompare.cu assert) raised from the DSPARK prefill/draft path, killing all TP ranks (auto-recovers after reload). Both are bursty, correlate with **long contexts (≈90k–237k tokens)**, and are invisible in short-context testing. ## Environment - Branch: `kimi-k3` @ `f37baeb52f` source (image lineage `lmsysorg/sglang:kimi-k3-c6ad1f26-20260729`), SGLang 0.5.16, torch 2.11.0+cu130, CUDA 13.0 - Single node, 8× Blackwell-class GPUs (SM10x), TP=8 - Launch (per the Kimi-K3 cookbook, unified recipe): `--tp-size 8 --context-length 1000000 --disable-custom-all-reduce --enable-symm-mem --reasoning-parser kimi_k3 --tool-call-parser kimi_k3 --speculative-algorithm DSPARK --speculative-draft-model-path <RadixArk/Kimi-K3-DSpark> --speculative-dspark-block-size 7 --enable-linear-replayssm-spec --mamba-full-memory-ratio 0.1 --mem-fraction-static 0.93 --enable-hierarchical-cache --hicache-ratio 6 --hicache-mem-layout page_first --hicache-io-backend kernel --hicache-write-policy write_back --trust-remote-code` - Weights: official MXFP4 checkpoint (`moonshotai/Kimi-K3`), draft `RadixArk/Kimi-K3-DSpark` ## Symptom A in detail — `[PAD]` storms Observed at gateway level over a 48 h window under real agentic traffic (large system prompts, 10–80 tools, 25k–240k-token contexts): **140 storm events in 11 bursts**, hours of complete quiet in between. Channel split: ~70% inside the think channel (`reasoning_content` / thinking deltas), ~30% in visible content. Typical stream shape (chat completions, abridged): ``` data: {"choices":[{"delta":{"reasoning_content":" evaluating the"}}]} data: {"choices":[{"delta":{"reasoning_content":" user's"}}]} data: {"choices":[{"delta":{"reasoning_content":"[PAD]"}}]} data: {"choices":[{"delta":{"reasoning_content":"[PAD][PAD]"}}]} data: {"choices":[{"delta":{"reasoning_content":"[PAD][PAD][PAD][PAD]..."}}]} # unbounded until max_tokens / disconnect ``` During a storm the engine's own decode logs show **`accept len: 1.00, accept rate: 0.00` for hundreds of consecutive DSPARK batches** — the draft model cannot predict the degenerate distribution, so throughput collapses to non-speculative while burning until `max_tokens` (with `max_tokens=128000` agent requests this is expensive). Impact on agent harnesses is severe: the turn produces thinking + garbage and no tool call / no content, the harness re-prompts, the poisoned long context storms again → retry loop, each cycle re-prefilling ~100k+ tokens. ## Symptom B in detail — DSPARK assert ``` /pytorch/aten/src/ATen/native/cuda/TensorCompare.cu:109: _assert_async_cuda_kernel: Assertion `probability tensor contains either `inf`, `nan` or element < 0` failed. ... terminate called after throwing an instance of 'c10::AcceleratorError' ``` Raised under the DSPARK worker prefill path under long-context load; whole TP group dies (SIGQUIT cascade). ~1 event/day/8-GPU node at our traffic. `python/sglang/srt/speculative/dspark_components/dspark_draft.py` already anticipates exactly this ("an all-NaN row would otherwise make multinomial raise"), so NaN reaching sampling is a known-possible state. ## Why we believe these are the same bug — mechanism chain 1. **#32477 describes the write-side defect**: CUDA-graph padding rows carry undefined K/V yet target the reserved padding slot 0; page-table padding points at that page; a partially valid tile loads the page before masking → `0 × NaN` contaminates attention output. That lands NaN in logits *transiently, depending on batch composition* — matching our "mid-response, one bad step, then normal again" signature. 2. **NaN logits in sampling are UB** — `sanitize_nan_logits()`'s own docstring: NaN logits "can come back as **out-of-vocab token ids**". The guard is **default-off** (`SGLANG_SANITIZE_NAN_LOGITS=False`). 3. **`[PAD]` = id 163839 = `vocab_size − 1`** — precisely the boundary index a corrupted argmax/top-k walk lands on. (Related precedent: #32396 fixed NaN mis-selection in the EAGLE fused top-k=1 kernel; the AITER greedy path has a comparable guard for all-NaN rows returning `vocab_size`.) 4. The same NaN reaching DSPARK's `torch.multinomial` produces Symptom B. Two exits, one defect. **Cross-validation from production:** we cherry-picked `ee678910f7` (#32477) onto `f37baeb52f` and rolled it out worker-by-worker today. During the partial-rollout window, **every further storm landed on not-yet-patched workers; patched workers have recorded zero storms so far** (early data, hours; we will update this issue with 48 h A/B numbers against the 140-events/48 h baseline). ## Two aggravating factors independent of the root cause **(a) `[PAD]` is not a stop token and is not filtered.** K3's `generation_config.json` only sets `eos_token_id: 163586`; pad 163839 is not in stop ids, and the serving layer must run `skip_special_tokens=False` (the XTML think markers need to survive detokenization). Net effect: one degenerate sample doesn't self-terminate — it streams literal `[PAD]` text to clients unboundedly. A single mis-sampled token becomes a 128k-token incident. **(b) `allowed_special="all"` makes special tokens injectable from user text.** The checkpoint tokenizer (`tokenization_kimi.py`) encodes with `allowed_special="all"`, so a user message *containing the literal string* `[PAD]` tokenizes to the real pad id 163839 (verified). Untrusted input can therefore seed real special tokens into the context — and because storm output that reaches conversation history is replayed on the next turn, there is also a self-contamination loop (later turns imitate the degenerate pattern). ## Suggested actions 1. **Publish a new `kimi-k3` image containing #32477** (current latest `kimi-k3-c6ad1f26-20260729` predates it; the branch HEAD already has it via the main merges). For long-context K3 + DSPARK this appears to be correctness-critical, not just hygiene. 2. **Treat pad as a hard stop / filter for K3 serving**: add 163839 to default stop ids for `kimi_k3` (or drop pad tokens in the detokenizer even when `skip_special_tokens=False`). Either bounds the blast radius of any future sampling corruption to one token. 3. **Consider defaulting `SGLANG_SANITIZE_NAN_LOGITS=1`** (or at least recommending it in the K3 cookbook) — with the caveat that for a *fully*-NaN row it converts the failure into a uniform-random sample; a cheap boundary-id guard in the sampling kernels (like #32396 did for EAGLE) may be the better structural fix. 4. **Reconsider `allowed_special="all"` for untrusted chat text** (encode user content with special-token strings escaped), keeping structural tokens injectable only by the chat encoder itself. Happy to provide additional stream captures, decode-log excerpts, or run instrumented builds — and we'll report the post-#32477 A/B numbers here either way.

signals.title: [Roadmap]Fast Engine Recovery: Weight Cache Daemon
signals.text: # [Roadmap] Fast Engine Recovery: Weight Cache Daemon @liusy58 @QiuMike @alexnails Phase 1 landed in #27139 — a per-rank daemon holds post-quantized weights and serves them over CUDA IPC; weight load drops from ~306–327s to <1s on Qwen3-235B FP8 ([blog](https://www.lmsys.org/blog/2026-08-21-sglang-fast-recovery)). This issue tracks the next steps. Contributions and feedback are welcome. Related: #27052 (Fast Recovery framework), #27310 (GPU Memory Service / VMM) Goals: <10s cold restart and <1s warm standby switch; broaden model & quant coverage; make the cache outlive the daemon; make resident weights usable beyond the one GPU they sit on. Where Phase 1 stands: TP + PP, single-node and multi-node launch (each node spawns its share of ranks and joins one dist group), zero-copy IPC per GPU, unquantized + block-wise FP8. Not yet: cross-node daemon coordination / failover, DP & EP shard keying, spec-decoding draft models, weight update / sleep-wake, cache surviving daemon death. ## Model & quantization coverage - [ ] parity harness — disk-load vs daemon-load `state_dict` diff (names / shape / dtype / stride / byte hash) + short GSM8K gate; required evidence for every new allowlist entry - [ ] carry post-processing metadata in the manifest (final shape/stride, layout tag, whitelisted module attrs) instead of reproducing `process_weights_after_loading` on a meta-init model — this is what blocks most quant methods today - [ ] quant methods: per-tensor fp8 / w8a8 int8 / mxfp8 / nvfp4 / compressed-tensors / awq / gptq-marlin #32398 - [ ] archs: MoE (DeepSeek V3/V4, Ling, Kimi K3) / hybrid linear attention / multimodal (vision tower + projector) / LoRA base weights - [ ] MTP & EAGLE draft models (per-rank draft daemon), removing the `--speculative-algorithm` rejection in `server_args.py` #32744 - [ ] generic post-map rebuild hook to replace the hardcoded `_rebuild_stale_views`; make tied storages, param→buffer flips and non-persistent buffers explicit in the manifest - [ ] publish the support matrix in docs; unsupported combinations keep hard-erroring (no silent wrong numerics) ## Transport: CUDA VMM shareable handles (#27310 §4.2) - [ ] `vmm_fd` backend (skeleton already in `weight_cache/transport.py`): `cuMemCreate` + FD handles over `SCM_RIGHTS`, VA reservation on import, `torch_ipc` stays the fallback, `--weight-cache-transport {auto,torch_ipc,vmm_fd}` #33279 ## Weight update without reload - [ ] epoch handoff on stable VAs: readers unmap → writer commits → readers remap at the same VAs, so captured CUDA graphs stay valid - [ ] daemon as the weight delivery agent for trainer pushes (NCCL/RDMA); un-gate the `update_weights_*` rejections in `weight_updater.py` - [ ] colocated RL: engine itself takes the writer role, same protocol, no daemon in the loop ## Multi-instance & cross-GPU sharing - [ ] key the cache by physical GPU UUID + config fingerprint (plus optional `--weight-cache-namespace`) under a configurable runtime dir. Today the socket is `/tmp/sglang_weight_cache_rank{global_rank}.sock`, so 2× tp=4 on one 8-GPU node collide and rank 0 of the second instance attaches to the GPU 0 daemon - [ ] discovery: replace static socket paths with a lightweight registry (file-based dir, optionally etcd) so an engine rank selects a daemon by `CacheConfig` match rather than by process rank, and locates daemons across nodes without a manual `--weight-cache-socket` - [ ] `--weight-cache-peer-copy` — when no daemon holds the shard on the local GPU, `cudaMemcpyPeerAsync` it from a peer-GPU daemon (NVLink-domain check, chunked on a low-priority stream, bandwidth cap so a serving neighbour is not disturbed). 1× memory per instance, sub-second over NVLink vs ~300s from disk - [ ] preference order local zero-copy > peer copy > disk, reported per rank - [ ] fleet fill: a daemon fills itself from a peer daemon instead of disk (P2P on-node, NCCL/RDMA cross-node), so a fleet cold start pays one disk read per shard group — the real bottleneck for 1T+ models on shared FS; align with the checkpoint-engine broadcast path - [ ] out of scope for now: resharding across TP/EP topologies (tp=4 daemon → tp=8 engine) ## Multi-node, DP & EP - [ ] primary–secondary daemon coordination for multi-node TP (e.g. TP=16 = 2 nodes × 8 GPUs): primary orchestrates daemon startup, cross-node NCCL process-group formation and readiness signalling; secondaries load their local shards in parallel and serve IPC handles to engines on their own node. Basic multi-node launch already works via `--nnodes/--node-rank/--dist-init-method`; what is missing is the cluster state machine - [ ] cross-node daemon lifecycle: primary tracks which secondaries are alive, triggers coordinated restarts, signals engines on a dead secondary's node to fall back to disk; promote a secondary when the primary dies - [ ] DP support: every DP rank on a GPU maps the same daemon's handles, so a model is read from disk and quantized exactly once per GPU regardless of DP degree (today each DP rank disk-loads independently). This is about supporting SGLang's DP deployment model, not cross-GPU sharing - [ ] EP support: expert shards differ per EP rank, so cache and key them by `ep_rank`; handle partial expert loading when a rank owns a subset of experts - [ ] `CacheConfig`: add `ep_rank`, `dp_rank` and `node_rank` for correct shard identification under EP and multi-node (`dp_size`/`ep_size` are already there) ## Ops & reliability - [ ] `daemon status` command + Prometheus metrics (resident bytes, attached clients, load time, hit / mismatch / fallback), and an engine endpoint reporting how each rank got its weights - [ ] runtime dir with owner-only permissions + `SO_PEERCRED` check before handing out handles (no world-writable `/tmp` sockets) - [ ] `protocol_version` in the handshake with a documented skew policy (the env stamp already covers torch / arch skew) - [ ] `--weight-cache-max-bytes`, refcount-aware eviction, admission check against `gpu_memory_utilization` - [ ] systemd unit + k8s DaemonSet recipes; document container requirements for cross-container IPC - [ ] CI: CPU unit tests, 1-GPU daemon→client restart e2e with accuracy, 2-GPU TP e2e, nightly multi-node, restart-latency regression gate - [ ] docs page: three modes, support matrix, ops runbook, failure semantics - [ ] reclaim on daemon restart (Phase 6): the daemon holds no heavy logic and is robust by construction, but if it exits for an external reason its clients still hold the GPU memory alive through IPC refcounts — a restarted daemon should re-adopt that memory from a live client's references instead of reloading from disk ## Rest of the startup path - [ ] Phase 2 — CUDA graph serialization: persist captured graphs to shared memory or disk and replay instead of recapturing; needs pool-offset translation for address relocation, which is why it depends on the stable VAs above. ~34.9s (~9% of startup) → <3s - [ ] Phase 3 — kernel warmup: persist DeepGEMM JIT-compiled kernels across restarts, parallelize warmup across batch sizes. ~23.1s → <2s - [ ] Phase 4 — server & distributed init: lazy tokenizer init, config caching, NCCL session reuse. ~22s → <5s - [ ] KV cache alloc + warmup ~3.9s → <1.5s (KV reuse, skip warmup requests on restart) - [ ] standby orchestration: health / promotion, request draining and KV handoff, scheduler-level pause/resume for priority co-serving ## Open questions - [ ] manifest schema + versioning: SGLang-owned, stored by the memory owner as an opaque blob — what compatibility window across SGLang versions? - [ ] backend selection UX: server arg, TMS-side registration, or both? - [ ] peer copy: automatic whenever a peer daemon exists, or always explicit opt-in? default bandwidth cap next to a serving instance? ## KV Restore?

signals.title: [Bug] [XPU] Qwen3.5 GDN + speculative decode: causal_conv1d_update_xpu() got an unexpected keyword argument 'intermediate_conv_window'
signals.text: ### Checklist - [x] I searched related issues but found no solution. - [x] The bug persists in the latest version. - [ ] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback. - [ ] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed. - [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Describe the bug On --device xpu, any speculative-decoding run on a hybrid GDN/linear-attention model (Qwen3.5) crashes in the target-verify path during the server's own warmup generation, before any user request. gdn_backend.py:43-48 binds the XPU kernel as-is: elif is_xpu(): from sgl_kernel import causal_conv1d_fn_xpu, causal_conv1d_update_xpu causal_conv1d_update = causal_conv1d_update_xpu but the is_target_verify branch at gdn_backend.py:539 calls it with five spec-only kwargs that the XPU op schema does not have — intermediate_conv_window, intermediate_state_indices, retrieve_next_token, retrieve_next_sibling, retrieve_parent_token. The XPU signature stops at conv_state_indices / pad_slot_id. File "python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/linear/gdn_backend.py", line 539, in forward_extend mixed_qkv_processed = causal_conv1d_update( TypeError: causal_conv1d_update_xpu() got an unexpected keyword argument 'intermediate_conv_window' The scheduler dies, and the client then reports a downstream ConnectionError (secondary noise). Non-spec decode on the same model/backend is unaffected — only TARGET_VERIFY takes this branch. The NPU and CPU bindings a few lines below (gdn_backend.py:49-60) are wired the same way and look exposed to the identical gap; unverified. Issue is induce #31250 fix. ### Reproduction With simple below steps able to reproduce issue ``` python -m sglang.benchmark.one_batch_server \ --model-path Qwen/Qwen3.5-9B --trust-remote-code \ --device xpu --tp-size 4 \ --mem-fraction-static 0.8 --disable-radix-cache --chunked-prefill-size -1 \ --max-total-tokens 8192 --max-prefill-tokens 4096 --max-running-requests 1 \ --batch-size 1 --input-len 512 --output-len 8 \ --speculative-algorithm NEXTN TypeError: causal_conv1d_update_xpu() got an unexpected keyword argument 'intermediate_conv_window' ``` Note : #34712 is required to reproduce the above error using shell command. ### Environment Intel Environment - sglang : 0.5.18.dev364+g667e18d99 torch : 2.12.0+xpu | cuda: None | hip: None | xpu: 20250302 python : 3.12.13 | Linux-6.14.0-37-generic-x86_64-with-glibc2.41 device : 8 x Intel(R) Arc(TM) Pro B60 Graphics driver : 1.14.36300+8 | mem GB: 22.7

signals.title: [Feature] Router GEMM should keep fp32 output under deterministic inference (DeepSeek V3/V4)
signals.text: ### Checklist - [x] If this is not a feature request but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed. - [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Motivation The DeepSeek router GEMM should output fp32 under deterministic inference too. Today it falls back to bf16, and that is not needed for batch invariance. `python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_v2.py:512`: ```python if get_exec().deterministic.enable_deterministic_inference: return F.linear(hidden_states, self.weight, None) # -> bf16 logits ``` Every other branch in the same function returns fp32: `dsv3_router_gemm(out_dtype=torch.float32)`, `linear_bf16_fp32`, and the prefill-CP path. **fp32 output does not break batch invariance.** Batch invariance is about reduction order, not output dtype. Deterministic `F.linear` runs `matmul_kernel_persistent`, which accumulates in fp32 and already has an fp32 store branch (`batch_invariant_ops.py:167`) that is never reached. It is the same kernel with the same reduction; only the final store differs. The branch is unreachable because `_matmul_persistent_triton` allocates output as the input dtype (`batch_invariant_ops.py:185`). Same for the JIT `dsv3_router_gemm` kernel, where `kOutFloat` only changes `cast<OutT>(final_sum)`. **Impact.** Router logits feed `noaux_tc` top-k over 256/384 experts with an fp32 correction bias. bf16 has 8 mantissa bits, so adjacent expert scores often sit within one ULP and rounding can change which experts are selected — a different answer, not a small numeric difference. **Related bug.** `_mm_dtype_compat` (`batch_invariant_ops.py:967`), registered for `aten::mm.dtype`, does `matmul_persistent(...).to(out_dtype)`, i.e. fp32 -> bf16 -> fp32. Callers asking for fp32 get bf16 values. ### Proposed change 1. Add `out_dtype` (or a preallocated `output`) to `matmul_persistent` / `_matmul_persistent_triton` so the existing fp32 store branch is reachable. Tiling and accumulation order are unchanged. 2. Use it in `_mm_dtype_compat` instead of `.to(out_dtype)`. 3. In `DeepseekV2MoEGate.forward`, request fp32 out from the batch-invariant matmul instead of returning bare `F.linear`. 4. Keep one kernel for all M under deterministic mode — the normal path switches kernels at `max_router_gemm_tokens` (4 on SM100/103, else 16), and a token-count-dependent switch is batch-variant on its own. 5. `_matmul_persistent_deepgemm` allocates `out` as `a.dtype` for `deep_gemm.bf16_gemm_nn`; either find an fp32-out entry point or route fp32 requests to Triton. Cost should be negligible — the GEMM is `[M, 7168] x [7168, 256]` and this only changes the store dtype. ### Related resources - `python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_v2.py:512` - `python/sglang/srt/batch_invariant_ops/batch_invariant_ops.py:167,185,275,967` - `python/sglang/kernels/jit/csrc/gemm/dsv3_router_gemm.cuh` — `kOutFloat` - #12095 — added the `F.linear` fallback

signals.title: [Tracking] Host allocator: page-aligned allocation with host-side bookkeeping
signals.text: ## Motivation The KV allocator keeps its source of truth on device. Freeing KV therefore reads device state back -- `torch.unique(free_index // page_size)` with a data-dependent output shape, and on the SWA side the `full_to_swa_index_mapping` gather plus its `> 0` liveness filter -- each forcing a stream synchronization on the scheduler's stream. Under the overlap scheduler these syncs queue behind the WAR barrier, so the CPU parks until the in-flight forward drains. On workloads where requests finish every step (e.g. PD decode), this is a measurable throughput loss. None of that information needs a device read: it is host-known at allocation time. Target design (validated end-to-end by the #31335 spike): - Allocation is planned host-side in whole pages; each request tracks a page-ceiled allocated extent (`req.kv.kv_allocated_len`) with a single writer. - `free()` receives whole pages by construction -- no dedup, no liveness filter, no data-dependent shapes. `torch.unique` survives only behind a legacy API for truly scattered index sets. - Device tables (`req_to_token`, `full_to_swa_index_mapping`, `free_pages`) become write-only projections consumed by kernels; the scheduler never reads them back. ## Prior work **Landed** - #29427 / #29429 / #29432 -- `req.kv` container: owned-KV lifecycle and bookkeeping coupled to real allocations - #32701 -- free KV pages by segment in the paged allocator without a device sync (non-SWA) - #33475 / #34067 -- free-group batching and aliasing fix (hardening the deferred-free machinery the sync-free path relies on) - #35265 -- page-align the DFLASH decode KV reservation (toward the invariant: every writer keeps `kv_allocated_len` page-aligned) - #35286 -- assert the page-aligned SWA evict floor at PD decode prealloc (I2: SWA liveness boundary invariant) - #35382 -- share the page-aligned decode alloc lens between EAGLE and DFLASH (dedup; the watermark loop becomes the single writer of kv_allocated_len) **Closed** - #31335 (with CI companion #31194) -- the original spike validating the full shape - #25500 -- early PoC: unify page allocation estimation on `kv_allocated_len` - #33907 / #34783 -- SWA free without a device sync via segment liveness contracts; closing in favor of the host-bookkeeping approach (the `swa_alive_from` contract only holds on the chunk-cache path; page-aligned extents remove the need for it) ## In flight - #35396 -- assert the page-aligned SWA evict floor on the second PD decode prealloc path, and drop the fixture that mocked an unaligned tail length - #35401 -- write the `req_to_token` page tail so a row stays valid over every page the allocator handed out; widen the row headroom to `page_size - 1` for every paged config. Prerequisite for page-ceiling `kv_allocated_len`: without it, anything slicing a row by a page-ceiled length reads the previous occupant's indices - #35592 -- decide SWA slot liveness on the host and drop the `> 0` filter in `free_swa`. Callers now declare whether a range's SWA peers are still live, from state they already keep (`node.swa_tombstone`, `req.kv.swa_evicted_seqlen`, the unified tree's `cd.value is None`); `free_full` completes the pool-specific pair so `free(x) == free_full(x) + free_swa(x)` holds for every allocator. Stacked on #35773 this makes the per-decode-step window eviction (`free_swa_out_of_window_slots`) sync-free outright at `page_size == 1`; measured on its own it moves nothing, because the mapping clear syncs independently of the filter. Paged configs still hit the `torch.unique` in `_expand_to_full_pages`, which needs the page-representative read to go with it -- blocked only by HiCache LOAD_BACK, which re-pairs a page-aligned full chunk with an arbitrarily offset SWA chunk - #35773 -- clear `full_to_swa_index_mapping` with `index_fill_` instead of a scalar assignment. The `= 0` form takes the zero from host memory, so the write is a blocking H2D copy ordered behind everything already queued on the stream -- a second sync in the same free path, independent of the `> 0` filter. Four call sites: `free_swa`, the PD decode prealloc path (`alloc_extend_swa_tail`), and tombstone recovery in both the legacy and the unified tree

signals.title: [Bug] PrefillDelayer can enter a persistent mixed-state feedback loop and collapse prefill progress under DP Attention + chunked prefill
signals.text: ### Checklist - [x] I searched related issues / PRs and did not find one matching this exact failure mode. - [x] The issue is reproducible across repeated runs with the same server/client configuration. - [x] Requests complete successfully; this is primarily a scheduler / performance-stability issue rather than a model-correctness failure. - [x] I compared the behavior against `PrefillDelayer` disabled and inspected the relevant scheduler / delayer source code. - [x] I collected per-DP-rank scheduler metrics and prefill-progress counters. --- ## Summary Under a long-prefill workload with: - DeepSeek-V4-Pro - TP=8 - DP=8 - DP Attention enabled - chunked prefill enabled - PrefillDelayer enabled - one 8-GPU node an identical server configuration and deterministic workload can enter two qualitatively different runtime regimes: ### Healthy synchronized state - Input throughput: ~94.6–94.8k tok/s - DP ranks progress through prefill nearly in lockstep - `PrefillDelayer` converges to sustained `all / no_wait` - average running requests is ~8.5 ### Pathological LOW state - Input throughput: ~62–79k tok/s - within the first ~5 s of the formal workload, DP-rank prefill progress diverges by an integer number of effective prefill chunks - the first observed spread is typically exactly **16384 tokens**, i.e. one effective per-rank chunk - `PrefillDelayer` remains dominated by `mixed / delay` - average running requests collapses to ~0.15 - residual / under-filled prefill batches increase sharply This is not explained by persistent per-rank request-count imbalance. In one representative LOW run, the first 30 s admitted exactly the same number of sequences on all 8 DP ranks, yet rank-level prefill progress had already diverged by one full chunk within 5 s. Disabling `PrefillDelayer` does **not** recover the healthy state. Instead, the system enters a third regime with lower but more continuous concurrency: - throughput: ~48–68k tok/s - avg running requests: ~4.7–5.9 - residual batches: ~11–14% Therefore the LOW state with PrefillDelayer enabled is not equivalent to "PrefillDelayer disabled". It appears to be a distinct scheduler regime in which the delayer participates in suppressing prefill progress. The exact upstream trigger is still being localized. I am opening this issue because the observed `mixed/delay` feedback loop appears different from the already-known `all/slot_condition` starvation fixed in #29898. --- ## Environment ```text SGLang version : 0.5.14 commit : 49e384ce9d304648e9959666ecb8ce8cd98d0deb git log -1 : 49e384c [Cherry-pick to release/v0.5.14] Revert Gemma4 modelopt fp4 MoE backend change (#28347) (#29246) git describe : v0.5.14 remote : https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang.git local patches : no tracked-file modifications ``` The earlier scheduler-debug instrumentation was fully reverted before the measurements described here. The remaining untracked files were only local backup files / an empty accidental file; tracked scheduler source matched the clean release tree. Hardware / topology: ```text 1 node 8 × NVIDIA B30Z TP = 8 DP = 8 DP Attention = enabled MoE A2A backend = MegaMoE ``` Relevant server configuration: ```bash --tp 8 --dp 8 --enable-dp-attention --enable-prefill-delayer --chunked-prefill-size 131072 ``` With DP Attention, the effective per-rank prefill chunk is: ```text 131072 / 8 = 16384 tokens ``` Relevant MegaMoE cap: ```bash SGLANG_OPT_DEEPGEMM_MEGA_MOE_NUM_MAX_TOKENS_PER_RANK=16512 ``` Workload: ```text input length : 60000 output length : 1 max concurrency : 16 num prompts : 160 ignore_eos : true seed : 1 ``` The 60k prompt is therefore processed approximately as: ```text 16384 + 16384 + 16384 + remainder ``` The client workload is burst-style; no request-rate throttling or intentional staggering is used in the baseline. --- ## Reproduction behavior Representative post-reboot runs: | Run | Input TPS | Median TTFT | avg running | avg queue | residual batches | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | good | 94,634 | 9.66 s | 8.13 | 0.16 | 11.96% | | LOW | 72,923 | 12.38 s | 0.17 | 0.84 | 27.17% | | LOW | 62,379 | 13.81 s | 0.12 | 0.85 | 29.03% | | good | 94,690 | 9.65 s | 8.37 | 0.17 | 9.52% | | mid | 82,688 | 9.68 s | 5.90 | 0.29 | 12.81% | | LOW | 78,571 | 10.45 s | 0.24 | 0.84 | 28.41% | The healthy-state throughput is extremely stable (~94.6k tok/s, sub-percent variation), while LOW runs have a qualitatively different scheduler signature rather than ordinary run-to-run noise. A host reboot did not eliminate the problem. --- ## Observation 1: LOW starts as a rank-level prefill-progress divergence Using the per-rank counter: ```text sglang:realtime_tokens_total{dp_rank="...", mode="prefill_compute"} ``` I computed: ```text progress_spread(t) = max_i(prefill_tokens_i(t)) - min_i(prefill_tokens_i(t)) ``` Results: | Run | TPS | spread@5s | spread@10s | spread@15s | spread@20s | spread@30s | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | good | 94,634 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | | good | 94,690 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | | mid | 82,688 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | | LOW | 72,923 | 16k | 22k | 27k | 11k | 16k | | LOW | 62,379 | 16k | 16k | 60k | 60k | 60k | | LOW | 78,571 | 16k | 22k | 27k | 0 | 0 | The important feature is that the first LOW-state divergence is quantized at approximately: ```text 16384 tokens ``` which is exactly one effective prefill chunk. `realtime_tokens_total` is incremented from `report_prefill_stats()` after a prefill batch result is processed, so this metric represents completed/reported prefill progress. It does **not** by itself prove whether the original cause was scheduler suppression or slower GPU execution. ### Metric-cadence validation I separately validated the observable cadence of `realtime_tokens_total` using 0.2 s scrapes during a smaller N32/C16 run with the same 16k effective chunk. Across all ranks: ```text jump interval p50 = 1.397 s jump interval p95 = 1.535 s min interval = 0.401 s ``` Jump-size distribution: ```text 16384 ×112 (one full chunk) 11264 ×8 (tail chunks) 256 ×3 (small startup fragments) 32768 ×0 (no two-chunk merge observed) ``` Thus the progress-spread observation is not an artifact of multiple 16k completions being collapsed into one scrape sample in this validation run. --- ## Observation 2: persistent request-count imbalance is not required for LOW I counted per-rank `#new-seq` admissions during the first 30 s of the formal workload. | Run | r0 | r1 | r2 | r3 | r4 | r5 | r6 | r7 | range | CV | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | good | 26 | 26 | 26 | 26 | 26 | 27 | 26 | 26 | 1 | 1.4% | | good | 26 | 25 | 25 | 25 | 25 | 25 | 25 | 26 | 1 | 1.8% | | mid | 27 | 26 | 26 | 26 | 26 | 26 | 26 | 26 | 1 | 1.4% | | LOW | 18 | 18 | 18 | 18 | 18 | 18 | 18 | 18 | **0** | **0.0%** | | LOW | 18 | 18 | 18 | 18 | 17 | 17 | 18 | 18 | 1 | 2.6% | | LOW | 14 | 15 | 10 | 14 | 10 | 14 | 13 | 14 | 5 | 14.8% | The strongest case is the 72.9k TPS LOW run: ```text 18 18 18 18 18 18 18 18 ``` All eight ranks admitted exactly the same number of sequences during the first 30 s, yet prefill progress had already diverged by one 16k chunk at 5 s. Therefore persistent per-rank request-count imbalance is not a necessary condition for entering the LOW state. Sub-second request-arrival / dispatch timing skew is **not** ruled out by this measurement. Also, `#new-seq` is scheduler admission into a prefill batch, not a direct counter of the initial DataParallelController request dispatch. --- ## Observation 3: PrefillDelayer state strongly separates healthy and LOW runs From: ```text sglang:prefill_delayer_outcomes_total ``` healthy runs eventually converge to sustained: ```text input_estimation="all" output_reason="no_wait" ``` while LOW runs remain dominated by: ```text input_estimation="mixed" output_reason="delay" ``` In healthy runs, after an initial transient, `mixed/delay` can disappear for long intervals and all 8 ranks repeatedly observe an immediately releasable state. In LOW runs, `mixed/delay` remains persistent and the scheduler never establishes the same synchronized regime. I use: ```text all_no_wait / (all_no_wait + mixed_delay) ``` only as a diagnostic state index, not as a literal request-release probability, because `mixed/delay` may be counted repeatedly across multiple scheduler passes during one waiting episode. The observed behavior is best described as synchronization / phase-locking-like behavior; I am not claiming a formal oscillator model. --- ## Observation 4: LOW is not equivalent to disabling PrefillDelayer I ran a separate six-run experiment with the same 16k effective chunk but with PrefillDelayer disabled. | Run | Input TPS | avg running | residual batches | median TTFT | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 1 | 67,658 | 5.65 | 11.78% | 12.62 s | | 2 | 48,536 | 4.73 | 12.01% | 15.11 s | | 3 | 53,299 | 5.26 | 11.18% | 15.43 s | | 4 | 64,174 | 5.36 | 12.24% | 13.29 s | | 5 | 55,500 | 4.69 | 14.04% | 15.70 s | | 6 | 64,715 | 5.90 | 12.02% | 13.10 s | Mean throughput: ```text 58,980 tok/s CV = 12.88% ``` The important mechanism difference is: ```text PrefillDelayer ON, healthy : avg running ≈ 8.5 PrefillDelayer ON, deep LOW: avg running ≈ 0.15 PrefillDelayer OFF : avg running ≈ 4.7–5.9 ``` Thus the ON-LOW state is not simply the delayer becoming ineffective and behaving like OFF. The delayer-enabled LOW regime suppresses running concurrency far more aggressively than the OFF regime. This OFF experiment was not interleaved with the ON runs, so I do **not** use it to estimate relative state-entry probabilities. I also do not claim six samples prove a statistically unimodal OFF distribution. The robust observation is the mechanism-signature difference above. --- ## Observation 5: staggered arrivals make the failure worse As a diagnostic experiment, I changed the formal client traffic from a burst to: ```text 2 requests/s, fixed interval ``` while keeping concurrency=16. This was intentionally stopped after the direction was clearly harmful. Representative results: ```text burst: 94,630 tok/s ramp : 53,449 tok/s burst: 64,016 tok/s ramp : LOW again ``` The ramp sends approximately one new request every 0.5 s. With DP=8 this naturally exposes only a subset of ranks to new work at a time, increasing the probability that the delayer observes a `mixed` state. This is not presented as a production benchmark because the arrival process itself changed. It is included because the behavior is consistent with the delayer being highly sensitive to cross-rank arrival phase. Related newer work such as #35191 independently discusses trickle arrivals and persistent fragmented prefills, although that PR operates on a newer optional queue-trigger path that is not enabled in this configuration. --- ## Local source comparison against later upstream fixes I compared this exact `v0.5.14` tree against several later PrefillDelayer / scheduler fixes. ### 1. #29898 — missing locally The local `PrefillDelayer` has a bounded delay in the `mixed` branch: ```python prev_delayed_count = prev_state.delayed_count if prev_state else 0 if prev_delayed_count < self._max_delay_passes - 1: ... output_reason="delay" else: ... output_reason="wait_timeout" ``` but its `all` branch can still delay indefinitely when `slot_condition` or `queue_condition` remains true: ```python if slot_condition or queue_condition: ... next_state = next_state.bump_delayed_count() return _NegotiateOutput( output_allow=False, output_reason="delay", ... ) ``` with no equivalent `max_delay_passes` bound. This confirms that the local tree predates #29898. However, I do **not** claim #29898 is the direct cause here: in the collected workload, `all/delay` was not observed; the pathological state is dominated by `mixed/delay`. Its relevance is that upstream has independently confirmed that PrefillDelayer feedback can cause prefill starvation and running-batch collapse. --- ### 2. #31835 — current reproduction hits the older negotiation placement The local `schedule_policy.py` contains two paths: ```text add_one_req_ignore_eos() -> negotiation after budget/admission checks add_one_req() -> negotiation at the beginning of the function ``` The dispatch condition is: ```python if req.sampling_params.ignore_eos and getattr(self.tree_cache, "disable", True): return self.add_one_req_ignore_eos(req) ``` This reproduction has: ```text ignore_eos = true radix cache enabled -> tree_cache.disable = false ``` so the condition is false and the workload falls through to `add_one_req()`. In the local tree, `add_one_req()` begins with: ```python if (self.prefill_delayer_single_pass is not None) and ( not self.prefill_delayer_single_pass.negotiate_should_allow_prefill( local_prefillable=True, running_batch=self.running_batch.batch_size(), max_prefill_bs=self.max_prefill_bs, max_running_requests=self.max_running_requests, waiting_queue_len=self.waiting_queue_len, ) ): return AddReqResult.OTHER ``` before later request / chunk / admission checks. Therefore, on the actual reproduction path, `local_prefillable=True` is sampled before all subsequent admission checks. The alternate `add_one_req_ignore_eos()` path samples after budget checks, so the two paths have different semantics. This is directly relevant to interpretation of `all/mixed`: `local_prefillable` is a scheduler-side estimate whose meaning depends on where it is sampled, not a direct GPU-readiness signal. That said, I do **not** currently think this semantic issue alone explains the LOW state. In the failing workload, KV/SWA pressure is very low (observed full-pool usage ~0.55%, SWA usage ~2.74%), so most post-negotiation admission checks are unlikely to fail. The placement issue is therefore real in this path but not yet demonstrated to be the active trigger. --- ### 3. #30295 — key chunked-request double-count shape is still present The local scheduler already contains an early guard: ```python if ( self.get_num_allocatable_reqs(running_bs) <= 0 and self.chunked_req is None ... ): ``` but the later waiting-queue loop still contains: ```python if len(adder.can_run_list) >= self.get_num_allocatable_reqs(running_bs): self.running_batch.batch_is_full = True ``` while `add_chunked_req(...)` adds the in-flight chunked request to `self.can_run_list`, and `get_num_allocatable_reqs()` uses: ```python min( pp_max_micro_batch_size - running_bs, req_to_token_pool.available_size(), ) ``` where the in-flight request's slot is already reflected in `available_size()`. This preserves the shape of the later double-count fixed by #30295. I do not think this alone explains the reported collapse: #30295 causes a stable one-slot loss, whereas the LOW state here collapses avg running from approximately 8.5 to approximately 0.15. It may still be an adjacent bug or amplification factor. --- ### 4. #24768 — present locally, but current configuration uses CPU/Gloo negotiation The local tree contains the NCCL/device-group option for PrefillDelayer synchronization. With the current settings: ```text disable_overlap_schedule = false SGLANG_NCCL_ALL_GATHER_IN_OVERLAP_SCHEDULER_SYNC_BATCH = false ``` PrefillDelayer uses the CPU/Gloo negotiation path. Enabling the NCCL synchronization path in this MegaMoE configuration was not stable in my environment and led to an NVLink/barrier timeout, so it is not currently usable as a workaround. If the failure is ultimately localized to scheduler/readiness coordination, this cross-DP negotiation path is one area I plan to investigate further. --- ### 5. #35191 — not directly active, but relevant to the dynamics This newer work describes a separate PrefillDelayer problem where trickle arrivals can keep the observed batching target small and sustain fragmented prefills. The optional queue-trigger feature involved there is not enabled in this workload (`queue_min_ratio` unset), so this is not a direct code-path match. It is nevertheless consistent with the observation here that staggered arrivals strongly destabilize synchronized prefill behavior. --- ## Current interpretation The strongest evidence currently supports this descriptive sequence: ```text formal workload begins ↓ DP ranks initially receive approximately balanced request counts ↓ within the first few seconds, per-rank prefill progress diverges by an integer prefill-chunk amount ↓ PrefillDelayer repeatedly observes mixed states ↓ mixed/delay persists ↓ under-filled / residual batches increase ↓ running concurrency collapses ↓ LOW throughput state becomes self-sustaining ``` One causal distinction is still unresolved: ### Hypothesis B — execution-duration divergence One or more ranks receive comparable forward work but their GPU forward takes longer: ```text same/similar forward opportunity ↓ one rank completes later ↓ prefill progress diverges ↓ Delayer subsequently observes mixed ``` ### Hypothesis C — scheduler/readiness suppression The scheduler / delayer gives some ranks fewer forward opportunities: ```text scheduler readiness / negotiation diverges ↓ Delayer suppresses some prefill admissions ↓ those ranks do less forward work ↓ prefill progress diverges ``` I am instrumenting: ```text sglang:realtime_tokens_total{dp_rank,mode="prefill_compute"} ``` together with: ```text sglang:forward_execution_seconds_total{dp_rank,category} ``` using `SGLANG_ENABLE_METRICS_DEVICE_TIMER=1`. The DeviceTimer implementation uses CUDA events plus non-blocking `end_event.query()` rather than `synchronize()`, but I am first validating that enabling the timer itself does not perturb this timing-sensitive synchronization state. The intended discriminator is **not** event timestamp ordering, because Delayer negotiation necessarily precedes forward completion in the source code. Instead, the discriminator is the per-rank relationship between: ```text Δprefill_progress and Δcompleted_forward_execution_time ``` over a short window after the first rank-level progress divergence. Roughly: ```text ΔP lower and ΔF proportionally lower → rank likely completed less forward work → supports scheduler/readiness-side cause ΔP lower but ΔF similar or higher → rank spent comparable/more GPU time for less progress → supports execution-duration-side cause ``` This follow-up work is ongoing and is not required for the observations reported above. --- ## Why I think this deserves a separate issue I could not find an upstream issue matching all of these properties together: ```text DP Attention + PrefillDelayer + chunked long-prefill workload + same deterministic configuration + healthy ~94.8k state vs persistent LOW state + LOW dominated by mixed/delay + avg running collapsing near zero + rank progress diverging by exactly one effective prefill chunk + request-count admission remaining balanced in at least one LOW reproduction ``` #29898 is the closest known failure family, but it is specifically an `all / slot_condition` liveness bug. The behavior reported here appears to be a different `mixed`-branch feedback failure mode. --- ## Questions for maintainers 1. Is a persistent `mixed/delay` loop with very low `num_running_reqs` an expected / known failure mode of PrefillDelayer? 2. Are there known cases where the cross-DP `local_prefillable` negotiation can remain phase-shifted even when request counts are balanced across DP ranks? 3. Is there a known interaction between chunked prefill, an in-flight `chunked_req`, `can_run_list`, `batch_is_full`, and PrefillDelayer state that can create a self-reinforcing mixed state? 4. Would you expect #29898 / #31835 / #30295 to materially change this workload even though the observed state is primarily `mixed/delay` rather than `all/delay`? 5. Is there a recommended way to trace the first divergence between per-rank PrefillDelayer negotiation, prefill admission, and model-forward execution without materially perturbing scheduler timing? --- ## Additional data available I retained: - per-run server logs - per-rank Prefill batch logs - `#new-seq` / `#new-token` traces - 0.2 s Prometheus cadence captures - per-rank `realtime_tokens_total` - PrefillDelayer outcome counters - queue/running-request counters - host/GPU telemetry - good-state and LOW-state profiling artifacts I can provide a reduced reproduction package or additional per-rank timelines if useful.

signals.title: [Bug] Qwen3.6/Qwen3.8 multimodal mRoPE positions are passed to a 1D fused QK RMSNorm+RoPE CUDA kernel
signals.text: ### Checklist - [x] I searched related issues but found no solution. - [x] The bug persists in the latest version. - [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback. - [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed. - [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Describe the bug ## Summary On NVIDIA CUDA, the Qwen3.5-family full-attention implementation unconditionally selects `fused_qk_gemma_rmsnorm_rope_gate` when `attn_output_gate=True`. The fused kernel accepts only one-dimensional token positions (`positions: [T]`) and loads one scalar with: ```python pos = tl.load(positions_ptr + token).to(tl.int64) ``` However, Qwen3.6-27B and Qwen3.8-27B are multimodal Qwen3.5-family checkpoints. Their image/video prefill path supplies contiguous mRoPE positions with shape `(3, T)`, representing temporal, height, and width positions. Passing contiguous `(3, T)` positions to the current kernel makes it read only the first (temporal) row. Height and width positions are not applied to their assigned rotary dimensions. This silently changes Q/K for visual tokens and can degrade image understanding and GUI coordinate grounding. The same defect is present in SGLang v0.5.16, v0.5.17, and current `main`. ## Affected checkpoints | Checkpoint | Immutable revision | Architecture/config | Affected by this bug | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `Qwen/Qwen3.6-27B` | [`6a9e13bd6fc8f0983b9b99948120bc37f49c13e9`](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.6-27B/blob/6a9e13bd6fc8f0983b9b99948120bc37f49c13e9/config.json) | Multimodal `Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration`, interleaved mRoPE | Yes | | `Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B` | [`1d4bf0f2ff6012fd82039f2fa52739d0dd7c60c0`](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B/blob/1d4bf0f2ff6012fd82039f2fa52739d0dd7c60c0/config.json) | Multimodal `Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration`, interleaved mRoPE | Yes | | `Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B-FP8` | [`017b9c7af6b5689d5dd426a76e0bc077eb5ca20a`](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B-FP8/blob/017b9c7af6b5689d5dd426a76e0bc077eb5ca20a/config.json) | Same multimodal architecture and mRoPE config | Yes | | `Qwen/Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B` | [`207bd685a7e3696cfaff12ded7c6a7ea0f88c996`](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B/blob/207bd685a7e3696cfaff12ded7c6a7ea0f88c996/config.json) | Text-only `Qwen3_5MoeForCausalLM`, no `mrope_section` | No, not this specific bug | The affected 27B configs contain: ```json { "architectures": ["Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration"], "language_model_only": false, "text_config": { "attn_output_gate": true, "head_dim": 256, "partial_rotary_factor": 0.25, "rope_parameters": { "mrope_interleaved": true, "mrope_section": [11, 11, 10], "rope_theta": 10000000, "rope_type": "default" } } } ``` SGLang registers `Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration` through the same `qwen3_5.py` implementation that contains the fused CUDA dispatch: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/63d783bbe0955237ec41f9ddabf7235ddf04673c/python/sglang/srt/models/qwen3_5.py#L2354-L2366 ## SGLang versions reviewed | Version | Commit | | --- | --- | | v0.5.11 reference path | [`612785ffdcaf35552f1ed433a981d596ca9fe900`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/commit/612785ffdcaf35552f1ed433a981d596ca9fe900) | | v0.5.16 | [`fdebc938f7f4d16fe6b9f55dcd9a767cf0899ea1`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/commit/fdebc938f7f4d16fe6b9f55dcd9a767cf0899ea1) | | v0.5.17 | [`29481685462732237d80d86076d6563e1f658102`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/commit/29481685462732237d80d86076d6563e1f658102) | | latest `main` reviewed on 2026-08-18 | [`63d783bbe0955237ec41f9ddabf7235ddf04673c`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/commit/63d783bbe0955237ec41f9ddabf7235ddf04673c) | The kernel file has the same Git blob ID in v0.5.16, v0.5.17, and the reviewed `main`: ```text 56d442098c02fa289414fecf0958638dd7906d5b ``` ## Source-level reproduction ### 1. The multimodal processor constructs three-axis positions `QwenVLImageProcessor.compute_mrope_positions()` calls `MRotaryEmbedding.get_rope_index()`: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/63d783bbe0955237ec41f9ddabf7235ddf04673c/python/sglang/srt/multimodal/processors/qwen_vl.py#L451-L471 `ForwardBatch` documents the result as `[3, total_seq_len]` and concatenates it along dimension 1 before moving it to the model device: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/63d783bbe0955237ec41f9ddabf7235ddf04673c/python/sglang/srt/model_executor/forward_batch_info.py#L1128-L1132 https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/63d783bbe0955237ec41f9ddabf7235ddf04673c/python/sglang/srt/model_executor/forward_batch_info.py#L1212-L1253 For image/video tokens, the temporal, height, and width rows are different. For ordinary text prefill/decode they are normally equal, which is why text-only accuracy tests may not expose the bug. ### 2. The VLM passes `(3, T)` positions into the language model The Qwen3-VL wrapper replaces normal positions with `forward_batch.mrope_positions` and asserts `(3, seq_len)` for multimodal prefill: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/63d783bbe0955237ec41f9ddabf7235ddf04673c/python/sglang/srt/models/qwen3_vl.py#L1423-L1453 ### 3. CUDA dispatch has no shape or mRoPE guard Current `main` uses the fused path whenever CUDA and the attention output gate are enabled: ```python if _is_cuda and self.attn_output_gate: q, k, v, gate = self.forward_prepare_cuda_fused( positions=positions, hidden_states=hidden_states, ) ``` https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/63d783bbe0955237ec41f9ddabf7235ddf04673c/python/sglang/srt/models/qwen3_5.py#L1147-L1163 There is no check for `positions.ndim`, `MRotaryEmbedding`, `mrope_section`, or `mrope_interleaved`. ### 4. The selected kernel is strictly one-dimensional The wrapper documents `positions: [T]`, and the Triton kernel loads only `positions_ptr + token`: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/63d783bbe0955237ec41f9ddabf7235ddf04673c/python/sglang/kernels/ops/attention/fused_qk_rmsnorm_rope_gate.py#L107-L114 https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/63d783bbe0955237ec41f9ddabf7235ddf04673c/python/sglang/kernels/ops/attention/fused_qk_rmsnorm_rope_gate.py#L131-L153 The kernel receives no positions row stride, mRoPE section sizes, or interleaving metadata. For a contiguous `(3, T)` tensor, `positions_ptr + token` addresses only row 0. ## Minimal runtime assertion On an NVIDIA CUDA machine, add this temporary assertion at the beginning of `forward_prepare_cuda_fused`: ```diff def forward_prepare_cuda_fused(self, positions, hidden_states): + assert positions.ndim == 1, ( + f"1D fused RoPE received shape={tuple(positions.shape)}, " + f"stride={positions.stride()}, rotary={type(self.rotary_emb).__name__}" + ) ``` Then launch either multimodal checkpoint and send one image request: ```bash python -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B \ --host 0.0.0.0 \ --port 30000 ``` Expected result with current code: image prefill reaches the assertion with a shape equivalent to `(3, T)`. Removing the assertion silently feeds that tensor to the one-dimensional kernel. The same assertion can be reproduced with `Qwen/Qwen3.6-27B`. ## Why existing validation missed it The fused CUDA path was introduced by PR #28320: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/28320 That PR changed two production files and did not add a fused-vs-native tensor correctness test. Its reported accuracy validation used a text Qwen3.5 checkpoint and AIME26. Text positions have equal T/H/W rows, so reading only the first row is accidentally equivalent for that control case. ## Expected behavior For two-dimensional mRoPE positions, Q/K must use the configured temporal, height, and width positions according to `mrope_section` and `mrope_interleaved`, matching `MRotaryEmbedding`. The one-dimensional fused kernel must not be called with a two-dimensional tensor unless it is explicitly extended to implement the same mRoPE semantics. ## Actual behavior On NVIDIA CUDA with `attn_output_gate=True`, `(3, T)` positions are passed to a `[T]` kernel. Only temporal positions are read, so H/W rotary dimensions are incorrect during image/video prefill. ## Suggested minimal correctness fix Use the fused path only for its documented one-dimensional input contract: ```diff -if _is_cuda and self.attn_output_gate: +if _is_cuda and self.attn_output_gate and positions.ndim == 1: q, k, v, gate = self.forward_prepare_cuda_fused(...) else: q, k, v, gate = self.forward_prepare_native(...) ``` Also fail fast in the fused wrapper: ```python if positions.ndim != 1: raise ValueError( f"fused_qk_gemma_rmsnorm_rope_gate only supports [T] positions, " f"got {tuple(positions.shape)}" ) ``` This is a conservative fix. In the current mRoPE scheduler, Qwen3.6/Qwen3.8 text and decode positions may also be represented as `(3, T)` with equal rows, so this guard can reduce fusion coverage for those models. Correctness should take priority; a follow-up optimization can safely pass `positions[0]` in paths where equal rows are guaranteed without performing a synchronizing GPU comparison. The complete performance fix is to extend the fused kernel to accept `(3, T)` positions plus the row stride, `mrope_section`, and interleaving mode. ## Tests requested Please add a CUDA fused-vs-native test using identical Q/K, norm weights, and RoPE cache: | Case | Positions | Expected result | | --- | --- | --- | | Text control | `[T]` | Fused and native close within dtype tolerance | | Equal-axis control | `(3, T)`, all rows equal | Either safely reduce to row 0 or use the native path | | Real mRoPE | `(3, T)`, T/H/W differ | Must bypass the 1D kernel or match `MRotaryEmbedding` numerically | An end-to-end image grounding regression test would also be useful, but the tensor-level contract test should be sufficient to prevent this silent correctness bug from recurring. ## Scope and current evidence The source-level shape/semantic mismatch is deterministic and independently reproducible. It confirms a correctness defect in the CUDA path and confirms that Qwen3.8-27B shares the affected configuration and implementation path. I do not include a controlled end-to-end CUDA grounding A/B in this report yet. Therefore, this issue does not claim that this kernel explains every observed visual benchmark regression; it claims the narrower, directly provable bug that genuine three-axis mRoPE positions are silently processed as one-dimensional positions. ### Reproduction ``` python -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path Qwen/Qwen3.6-27B \ --port 8000 \ --tp-size 8 \ --mem-fraction-static 0.8 \ --reasoning-parser qwen3 ``` ### Environment I use the 0.5.16+cu129 docker. ``` Python: 3.12.3 (main, Jun 19 2026, 12:46:00) [GCC 13.3.0] CUDA available: True GPU 0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7: NVIDIA H100 80GB HBM3 GPU 0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7 Compute Capability: 9.0 CUDA_HOME: /usr/local/cuda NVCC: Cuda compilation tools, release 12.9, V12.9.86 CUDA Driver Version: 535.129.03 PyTorch: 2.11.0+cu129 sglang: 0.5.16 sglang-kernel: 0.4.5+cu129 flashinfer_python: 0.6.14 flashinfer_cubin: 0.6.14 flashinfer_jit_cache: 0.6.14+cu129 triton: 3.6.0 transformers: 5.12.1 torchao: 0.17.0+cu129 numpy: 2.4.4 aiohttp: 3.14.3 signals.title: [Bug] Anthropic endpoint: tool_reference parts in tool_result break chat templates without deferred-reference support (HTTP 500)
signals.text: ## Describe the bug The Anthropic-compatible endpoint (`/v1/messages`) converts `tool_reference` blocks found inside `tool_result` content into structured parts `{"type": "tool_reference", "name": ...}` (deferred tool loading, #22702). That part type is only understood by chat templates that implement deferred-reference expansion (GLM family). For any other model, the template hits the unknown item type and the whole request fails with HTTP 500: ``` jinja2.exceptions.TemplateError: Unexpected item type in content. ... [ts] Anthropic error response api_error (exception=ValueError): Internal server error ``` With Claude Code this is especially disruptive: once a session uses deferred tool loading (ToolSearch) and a `tool_reference` block enters the conversation history, **every subsequent request in that session fails** — the history carries the block forward, so retries cannot recover and only clearing/compacting the context fixes it. We observed ~26 consecutive 500s on a single session until it was abandoned. ## Reproduction Server: SGLang 0.5.17 (same code on `main`), any model whose chat template does not handle `tool_reference` (reproduced with the stock Qwen3.8-27B template): ```bash curl -s http://127.0.0.1:30000/v1/messages \ -H 'content-type: application/json' -H 'x-api-key: dummy' -d '{ "model": "qwen3.8-27b", "max_tokens": 16, "stream": false, "tools": [{"name": "DemoTool", "description": "demo", "input_schema": {"type": "object", "properties": {}}}], "messages": [ {"role": "user", "content": "list the deferred tools"}, {"role": "assistant", "content": [ {"type": "tool_use", "id": "toolu_1", "name": "ToolSearch", "input": {"query": "select:Foo"}} ]}, {"role": "user", "content": [ {"type": "tool_result", "tool_use_id": "toolu_1", "content": [ {"type": "text", "text": "Found 1 tool:"}, {"type": "tool_reference", "tool_name": "DemoTool"} ]} ]}, {"role": "user", "content": "now use it"} ] }' ``` Actual: `HTTP 500 {"type":"error","error":{"type":"api_error","message":"Internal server error"}}` with `TemplateError: Unexpected item type in content` in the server log. Same request with the `tool_reference` item removed: `HTTP 200`. (A `thinking` block in assistant history does not trigger this; the minimal trigger is the `tool_reference` item in a `tool_result` content list.) ## Root cause `python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/anthropic/serving.py`, `_convert_to_chat_completion_request` → `_convert_tool_result_content`: ```python elif item_type == "tool_reference": ref_name = item.get("tool_name") or item.get("name") if ref_name: tool_content_parts.append( {"type": "tool_reference", "name": ref_name} ) ``` The structured part is emitted unconditionally. Templates without deferred-reference expansion (e.g. Qwen's `render_content` macro, which only accepts `text`/`image`/`video` items) raise `TemplateError`, which is surfaced as a 500. Suggested fix: detect whether the loaded chat template handles `tool_reference` (e.g. substring check on the template source, mirroring how the unit tests fake `tokenizer_manager.tokenizer.chat_template`) and, when it does not, degrade the reference to a text part such as `[tool reference: <name>]` so history echoes keep working for all models while GLM behavior is preserved. A PR implementing this is coming. ## Environment ``` Python: 3.12.12 | packaged by conda-forge CUDA available: True GPU: 8x NVIDIA H100 80GB HBM3 (CC 9.0), Driver 580.95.05, CUDA 12.9 PyTorch: 2.11.0+cu130 sglang: 0.5.17 sglang-kernel: 0.4.5 flashinfer_python: 0.6.15.post1 triton: 3.6.0 transformers: 5.12.1 numpy: 2.3.5 fastapi: 0.141.1 pydantic: 2.14.0b1 anthropic: 0.125.0 ``` Full `python3 -m sglang.check_env` output: ``` Python: 3.12.12 | packaged by conda-forge | (main, Oct 22 2025, 23:25:55) [GCC 14.3.0] CUDA available: True GPU 0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7: NVIDIA H100 80GB HBM3 GPU signals.title: [Bug] A global --attention-backend kills the server when a non-DiT component does not declare it (MiniMax-H3 audio_vae)
signals.text: ### Checklist - [x] I searched related issues but found no solution. - [x] The bug persists in the latest version. - [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback. - [x] Please use English. ### Describe the bug Passing a global `--attention-backend` that the *DiT* supports takes the whole server down if any **non-DiT** component's attention layer does not declare that backend — even when the layer declares a `default_attention_backend` for exactly this case. With MiniMax-H3 and `--attention-backend sage_attn`: ``` ValueError: Attention backend 'sage_attn' is not supported by this attention layer; supported backends: ['fa', 'torch_sdpa'] ... Failed to load customized audio_vae ... Rank 0 scheduler is dead ``` The audio VAE's attention layer is constructed with both a supported set and a default: `python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/models/vaes/minimax_h3_audio_vae/audio_vae.py:60-70` ```python supported_attention_backends={AttentionBackendEnum.FA, AttentionBackendEnum.TORCH_SDPA}, default_attention_backend=AttentionBackendEnum.TORCH_SDPA, ``` `get_attn_backend()` does have a fallback path, but it is gated on the selection not being explicit (`selector.py:188-201`): ```python selection_is_explicit = isinstance(server_args, ServerArgs) and server_args.is_arg_explicitly_set("attention_backend") ... elif not selection_is_explicit: allowed_fallback_reason = "platform default fallback" ``` A `--attention-backend` on the command line is explicit, so `allowed_fallback_reason` stays `None`, `candidate_backends` holds only the requested backend, and `selector.py:233-241` turns it into the hard `ValueError` above. Not honouring an explicit request silently is reasonable; the problem is that a *global* flag is treated as an explicit request **for every component**, including ones that cannot possibly satisfy it and that ship a declared default for that situation. Practical consequence: any global sparse/fp8 attention backend requires the operator to know the full component list up front and repeat it, and getting it wrong is a dead server rather than a warning. On MiniMax-H3 all three non-DiT components (`text_encoder`, `audio_vae`, `video_vae`) have to be exempted, and the set has grown between nightlies, so a config that worked on an earlier image fails on a later one with an error that points at the VAE rather than at the flag. ### Reproduction ```bash sglang serve --model-path <MiniMax-H3> --model-variant fl2va \ --num-gpus 1 --attention-backend sage_attn ``` Startup fails as above. Works with the components enumerated: ```bash --attention-backend sage_attn \ --component-attention-backends text_encoder=torch_sdpa,audio_vae=torch_sdpa,video_vae=torch_sdpa ``` ### Environment One RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition (sm_120), CUDA 13, `lmsysorg/sglang` nightly. The code path is unchanged on current `main` (read at `a49560ce50`), so this is not specific to that GPU or image — any global backend a non-DiT component doesn't declare reproduces it. ### Suggested direction Any of these would work; the first is the smallest: 1. Treat `--attention-backend` as explicit only for components that declare support, and fall back to the layer's `default_attention_backend` elsewhere with a `logger.warning` naming the component. This keeps "don't silently downgrade what the user asked for" for the DiT, where the request is meaningful. 2. Keep failing closed, but make the message actionable: name the component being loaded and print the `--component-attention-backends component=torch_sdpa` line that fixes it. Happy to send a PR for either once maintainers pick one.

signals.title: [Bug] Qwen3-VL vision features diverge from Transformers/vLLM in v0.5.17 on fine-grained grounding
signals.text: ### Checklist - [x] I searched related issues but found no solution. - [x] The bug persists in the latest version. - [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback. - [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed. - [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Describe the bug ### Summary On the latest release, SGLang v0.5.17 (commit `29481685462732237d80d86076d6563e1f658102`), we observe a large accuracy discrepancy for fine-grained visual grounding with two Qwen3-VL-family checkpoints: `Tencent/UI-Mate-27B` and `Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B`. We replayed the same captured prompt contents and image bytes through SGLang, Hugging Face Transformers, and vLLM under greedy decoding (`temperature=0.0`, `top_p=1.0`). Only the engine changed. Transformers and vLLM agree closely, while SGLang produces systematically incorrect click coordinates. | Model | Engine | Dtype | Half-row hits | Median absolute y error / row pitch | |---|---|---:|---:|---:| | UI-Mate-27B | SGLang 0.5.17 | BF16 | 0/20 | 0.9748 | | UI-Mate-27B | Transformers | BF16 | 20/20 | 0.0636 | | UI-Mate-27B | vLLM (official-style TP2) | BF16 | 20/20 | 0.0649 | | Qwen3.8-27B | SGLang 0.5.17 | BF16 | 1/20 | 4.5964 | | Qwen3.8-27B | Transformers | BF16 | 20/20 | 0.0481 | | Qwen3.8-27B | vLLM | BF16 | 20/20 | 0.0559 | The criterion is whether the first click falls within half of one rendered row pitch. All arms use the same 20 fixed first-step inputs. This is intentionally a narrow fine-grained grounding test; we are not claiming that all Qwen3-VL tasks fail in SGLang. ### Evidence localizing the discrepancy For an aligned Qwen3.8 seed: - `input_ids` are identical between the Transformers replay and SGLang (same shape and hash). - `image_grid_thw` is identical: `[[1, 62, 100]]`. - The processor output shape is identical: `pixel_values=[6200, 1536]`, float32. - The default SGLang GPU processor differs slightly from the CPU processor (max absolute pixel delta `2/255`, mean absolute delta `1.56e-6`). Disabling the fast image processor remains 1/20, so this small preprocessing delta is not sufficient to explain the failure. - Text token embeddings before multimodal replacement are exactly equal elementwise in our probe. - Immediately after the vision merge, image-token relative L2 difference is approximately `0.0401`. - After the first GDN layer and the first full-attention layer, the relative L2 difference remains approximately `0.036`. This suggests the discrepancy is already present in the vision output and is then propagated by the language model. With an exact Transformers-generated prefix forced into both engines, both choose the same first action token and, after a prefix ending in `"y":`, the same leading coordinate digit with probability effectively 1. This argues against an action parser problem or a fixed coordinate-output-head bias. ### Controlled SGLang ablations (Qwen3.8 BF16, same 20 inputs) | Change from baseline | Half-row hits | Median error / row pitch | |---|---:|---:| | Baseline | 1/20 | 4.5964 | | Disable fast image processor | 1/20 | 4.5068 | | Disable prefill CUDA graph | 1/20 | 4.5516 | | Multimodal attention FA3 -> SDPA | 1/20 | 3.5061 | | Enable precise embedding interpolation | 1/20 | 4.5964 | | Compatibility-adapted v0.5.6.post2 `qwen3_vl.py` vision path | 0/20 | 4.5964 | ### Related issue This may be related to #19513, which reported incorrect Qwen3-VL vision output in older SGLang releases. However, we do not assume the same root cause: unlike that report, a compatibility-adapted v0.5.6.post2 vision-file rollback did **not** recover accuracy on our current v0.5.17 / Transformers 5.12 stack. We would appreciate guidance on the best supported way to compare the vision-encoder output against the Transformers reference, or on any known correctness flags/patches for this model family. ### Reproduction ### Minimal replay (Qwen3.8-27B, seed 8001) The attachment `qwen_seed8001_greedy_payload.json.txt` is a self-contained OpenAI chat-completions payload. It contains the exact prompt and the screenshot as a data URL. Compared with the captured benchmark request, only three fields were normalized: model ID → `Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B`, `temperature` → `0.0`, and `top_p` → `1.0`. The message contents and image bytes are unchanged. Start SGLang: ```bash python3 -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B \ --host 0.0.0.0 --port 30000 \ --tp-size 1 \ --dtype bfloat16 \ --trust-remote-code \ --context-length 131072 \ --chunked-prefill-size 4096 \ --reasoning-parser qwen3 ``` Download the attachment and replay it: ```python import json import requests payload = json.load(open("qwen_seed8001_greedy_payload.json.txt")) response = requests.post( "http://127.0.0.1:30000/v1/chat/completions", json=payload, timeout=600, ) response.raise_for_status() message = response.json()["choices"][0]["message"] print(message.get("reasoning_content")) print(message.get("content")) ``` Oracle row center for this screenshot: `y=277.1328125` in the declared 1000x1000 output space. Half-row acceptance interval: `[260.39453125, 293.87109375]`. Observed final actions under greedy decoding: ```text SGLang 0.5.17 BF16: {"type":"click","x":150,"y":125,"button":"left"} Transformers BF16: {"type":"click","x":150,"y":276,"button":"left"} vLLM BF16: {"type":"click","x":144,"y":275,"button":"left"} ``` Prompt-token counts are identical for this Qwen replay (2639). The same 20-input discrepancy was independently reproduced with UI-Mate-27B using its official-style vLLM TP2 serving configuration. SHA-256 of the proposed attachment: `d74eb21f628f4f9d172b916c2ec31e54162a954f15cc2f4bd0226ca3517287c2`. [qwen_seed8001_greedy_payload.json.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31285951/qwen_seed8001_greedy_payload.json.txt) ### Environment ```text Python: 3.12.3 (main, Jun 19 2026, 12:46:00) [GCC 13.3.0] CUDA available: True GPU 0,1,2,3: NVIDIA H200 NVL GPU 0,1,2,3 Compute Capability: 9.0 CUDA_HOME: /usr/local/cuda NVCC: Cuda compilation tools, release 12.9, V12.9.86 CUDA Driver Version: 580.105.08 PyTorch: 2.11.0+cu129 sglang: 0.5.17 sglang-kernel: 0.4.5+cu129 flashinfer_python: 0.6.15.post1 flashinfer_cubin: 0.6.15.post1 flashinfer_jit_cache: 0.6.15.post1+cu129 triton: 3.6.0 transformers: 5.12.1 torchao: 0.17.0+cu129 numpy: 2.4.4 aiohttp: 3.14.3 fastapi: 0.141.1 huggingface_hub: 1.27.0 interegular: 0.3.3 modelscope: 1.39.1 orjson: 3.11.9 outlines: 0.1.11 packaging: 26.3 psutil: 7.2.2 pydantic: 2.13.4 python-multipart: 0.0.32 pyzmq: 27.1.0 uvicorn: 0.52.1 uvloop: 0.22.1 vllm: Module Not Found xgrammar: 0.2.1 openai: 2.6.1 tiktoken: 0.13.0 anthropic: 0.121.0 litellm: Module Not Found torchcodec: 0.11.1+cu129 NVIDIA topology: GPU0 GPU1 GPU2 GPU3 NIC0 NIC1 CPU_Affinity NUMA GPU0 X NV6 NV6 NV6 SYS SYS 0-31,64-95 0 GPU1 NV6 X NV6 NV6 SYS SYS 0-31,64-95 0 GPU2 NV6 NV6 X NV6 SYS SYS 32-63,96-127 1 GPU3 NV6 NV6 NV6 X SYS SYS 32-63,96-127 1 ulimit soft: 131072 ``` SGLang source commit: `29481685462732237d80d86076d6563e1f658102` Container image: `sglang-0.5.17-cu129.sif` Primary SGLang launch settings: BF16, TP1 for Qwen3.8; BF16, TP2 for UI-Mate; FA3 default attention backend; chunked prefill size 4096. Exact Qwen command is included in Reproduction.

signals.title: [MoonEP] Kimi-K3 production integration roadmap
signals.text: ## Motivation Track MoonEP integration for Kimi-K3 as a small set of independently reviewable changes under the broader Kimi-K3 roadmap in #32607. MoonEP uses static-shape dispatch/combine plus dynamic redundant experts and remote expert prefetch to balance expert-parallel traffic. The first completion boundary is a reproducible Kimi-K3 MXFP4 configuration; broader runtime and model capabilities can follow independently. Related roadmap: vllm-project/vllm#52095. ## Current implementation - [x] **BF16/eager integration seam and correctness path** — #33249 Distinct `moonep` backend, dispatch/combine contracts, static buffer facade, BF16 expert layout and runner, FusedMoE wiring, and distributed validation harness. - [x] **Synthetic BF16 correctness validation** 8x H100 SXM; all eight ranks passed with zero numerical error. - [ ] **Kimi-K3 MXFP4 symmetric-memory + DeepGEMM path** — #34874 Author-validated end to end on 4x GB200, TP16/EP16, but still needs rebase, CI, and upstream dependency pinning. The merged BF16 path remains intentionally diagnostic: eager-only, replicated/global BF16 weights, and a correctness-first expert loop. ## Roadmap ### Productionization - [ ] **Land and pin the compatible MoonEP dependency** Merge or supersede MoonshotAI/MoonEP#32, then provide an exact commit, wheel, or container build. The integration must not depend on an undocumented development checkout. - [ ] **Rebase and land #34874** Rebase onto the latest `moonep`, isolate the MXFP4/DeepGEMM/symmetric-memory delta, fix pre-commit, and run the required SGLang CPU/GPU CI. - [ ] **Close correctness and support-contract gaps** @charliechenye Remove silent rank-0 fallback; keep padded routes out of planner statistics; reject unsupported bias; and fail fast for unsupported overlap/CUDA-graph combinations. - [ ] **Add focused automated coverage** Cover symmetric-pool row mapping and lifecycle, MXFP4 weight/scale residency, remote-prefetch remapping, MoonEP-to-DeepGEMM pre/post-permute, empty/padded groups, route weights, and capacity boundaries. - [ ] **Add a real Kimi-K3 integration test** Instantiate the actual `FusedMoE`/MXFP4 loading path without import stubs and exercise dispatch → prefetch → DeepGEMM → combine. Keep the BF16 harness as a component test. - [ ] **Run reproducible acceptance validation** Record exact SGLang/MoonEP/DeepGEMM revisions, image and launch command, topology, TP/EP, memory, correctness, prefill/decode coverage, capacity failures, and stability. - [ ] **Benchmark against DeepEP** Compare identical Kimi-K3 MXFP4 configurations across decode/small-batch and larger-batch workloads. Report TTFT, ITL, throughput, memory, and dispatch/planning/prefetch/GEMM/combine breakdown against a pre-agreed success threshold. - [ ] **Package and document the supported configuration** Provide installation, hardware/fabric prerequisite checks, launch recipe, support matrix, and troubleshooting guidance. ### Follow-up capabilities Each capability should be independently designed, benchmarked, and reviewed. They should not block the first narrow Kimi-K3 production configuration unless explicitly moved into its acceptance contract. - [ ] **Async communication and scheduler overlap** Use MoonEP's communication stream and `async_finish=True` event chain across dispatch, prefetch, compute, and combine. Define buffer/plan ownership for multiple in-flight batches, then integrate SBO/TBO rather than inheriting DeepEP overlap semantics accidentally. - [ ] **CUDA graph support and static-capacity classes** Capture stable prefill/decode capacity buckets, eliminate capture-time allocations and host synchronization, and guarantee rank-consistent bucket selection. Capacity policy should minimize padding without permitting collective disagreement. - [ ] **Zero-copy dispatch and combine** Integrate MoonEP's zero-copy controls with SGLang-owned static buffers so dispatch/combine can avoid avoidable allocation and copies. Coordinate this with CUDA graphs and output-buffer ownership. - [ ] **Quantized communication and additional expert formats** MXFP4 expert weights are the first target, but dispatched activations are still BF16. Scope FP8/other communication formats and additional expert-weight formats such as FP8 or NVFP4, including scale layout and remote-prefetch contracts. - [ ] **Tuned expert compute and kernel fusion** Tune the DeepGEMM contiguous grouped path over MoonEP `cu_seqlens`; evaluate Hopper and Blackwell separately. Consider fusing activation quantization, route-weight application, skipped-row zeroing, and other adapter work only when profiling identifies a meaningful boundary. - [ ] **EPLB and expert-placement interaction** MoonEP's dynamic redundant experts and SGLang EPLB both alter where expert work executes. Define compose-or-exclude semantics, placement-versioning, and how plans/prefetch row mappings react to expert relocation. - [ ] **General EP groups and topology support** Remove Kimi-K3's current EP=TP/TP-group assumptions where practical. Cover independent EP groups, multi-node NVLink fabric/IMEX domains, mixed DP+EP, and topology-aware capability probing. - [ ] **Serving-mode compatibility** Validate pipeline parallelism, PD disaggregation, speculative decoding/MTP, overlap scheduling, and memory-saver/offload behavior. Each combination needs an explicit support contract rather than inheriting generic MoE behavior. - [ ] **Broader model semantics** Support or explicitly reject fused/shared experts, expert bias, alternative gated activations, different gate/up layouts, router top-k values, and non-Kimi expert shapes. Promote MoonEP from a Kimi-K3 path to a generic backend only after these semantics are separated from model-specific assumptions. - [ ] **Resource lifecycle, observability, and autotuning** Integrate buffer and symmetric-pool teardown with model reload and runtime reset. Expose capacity utilization, padding, duplicated experts, prefetch volume/bandwidth, and per-stage timing; use those signals to tune capacity buckets, prefetch slots, and communication SMs. ## Initial completion boundary The Kimi-K3 productionization item is complete when: - the compatible MoonEP dependency and #34874-equivalent integration are merged and reproducibly installable; - focused tests and required SGLang CI pass; - unsupported configurations fail early; - Kimi-K3 validation is reproducible from recorded revisions and commands; and - MoonEP is compared with DeepEP against an agreed performance threshold. Follow-up capabilities remain open roadmap items and may graduate into their own tracking issues as designs and owners become clear.
