signals.title: RFC: Re-layer Draft SWA into Committed Sidecar KV and Verify Scratch
signals.text: ### Checklist - [ ] If this is not a feature request but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed. - [ ] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Summary This RFC proposes splitting draft Sliding Window Attention (SWA) KV in speculative decoding, such as DSV4 DSpark, into two explicitly modeled components: ```text Draft SWA ├── committed sidecar KV: content-scoped and reusable └── verify temporary: step-scoped scratch, never entering cache ``` Today, draft SWA is implicitly managed through the draft worker KV pool and coupled to target KV pool sizing. Its committed and in-flight states are not represented separately. This causes two problems: 1. Committed draft KV lacks explicit cache semantics. 2. Draft SWA memory is estimated as if draft layers had the same average structure as target layers. The proposal introduces: - A content-scoped draft SWA sidecar aligned with the target prefix cache. - Step-scoped scratch for speculative verification. - SWA-only draft memory accounting. - Correct stage-count derivation. - Radix cache, PD, and HiCache integration. - A draft-only compatibility path for `unified_kv`. This proposal does not change model numerics. It changes memory ownership, cache lifecycle, physical layout, and pool sizing. ## 2. Motivation ### 2.1 Memory ownership should follow data semantics Device memory in SGLang can be classified by ownership and lifetime: ```text Model-scoped: model weights and persistent model buffers Content-scoped: committed KV, Mamba checkpoints, compressed pages Request-scoped: active recurrent state and request-local runtime state Step-scoped: verification intermediates, logits, and temporary workspaces ``` The important distinction is: ```text Running / intermediate / in-flight state -> request-scoped or step-scoped Committed / reusable artifact -> content-scoped ``` Draft SWA currently mixes these two categories. ### 2.2 Semantics of committed draft SWA Taking DSV4 DSpark as an example, canonical draft KV is derived from injected target hidden states: ```text target hidden states -> canonical draft KV ``` For an already committed prefix: ```text same prefix + same target/draft weights -> same canonical draft KV ``` Therefore, committed draft SWA is a reusable artifact: ```text committed draft SWA = content-scoped sidecar KV ``` Its lifecycle should follow the committed target prefix rather than the lifetime of a request slot. ### 2.3 Semantics of verify temporary During speculative verification, temporary draft KV may represent tokens that are later rejected. Before acceptance is known, that data is not part of the committed sequence: ```text in-flight draft KV != committed prefix artifact ``` Verify temporary should therefore be: ```text step-scoped scratch ``` It must not become radix-visible, transferable, or reusable until the corresponding tokens have been accepted and canonical committed KV has been produced. ## 3. Problems with the Current Design ### 3.1 Committed draft SWA is not explicitly modeled The problem is not the target KV cache. The problem is that draft SWA is implicitly folded into the existing draft worker pool and target budget logic. There is no independent abstraction expressing: ```text this draft KV belongs to committed prefix content ``` Consequently: 1. Cache ownership is unclear. 2. Committed and speculative data share lifecycle assumptions. 3. Prefix reuse is difficult to express. 4. PD and HiCache integration is indirect. 5. Pool sizing is coupled to target-layer averages. ### 3.2 Draft SWA memory accounting is inaccurate The current DSV4 pool configurator approximately scales the target cost as follows: ```text bytes_per_full_token *= (target_layers + draft_layers) / target_layers ``` This treats each draft layer as one target average layer. However, DSV4 DSpark draft layers are SWA-only: ```text draft layer does not include C4 draft layer does not include C128 draft layer does not include the C4 indexer draft layer does not include C4/C128 compression state ``` Charging a draft layer as a target average layer therefore overestimates draft KV memory and reduces usable target KV capacity. A more accurate semantic term is: ```text draft_swa_committed_bytes_per_full_token = swa_full_tokens_ratio * draft_swa_bytes_per_token * draft_swa_stage_count ``` The physical `draft_swa_bytes_per_token` must come from the active backend layout: ```text paged backend: packed/padded SWA page bytes unified backend: unified row stride and storage dtype ``` Verify scratch is a separate fixed workspace term: ```text draft_swa_scratch_bytes = max_concurrent_requests * verify_scratch_width * scratch_bytes_per_row * draft_swa_stage_count ``` This separates content capacity from fixed speculative workspace. ### 3.3 DSpark stage count is ambiguous A DSpark bundle may expose: ```text num_nextn_predict_layers = 1 dspark_target_layer_ids = [40, 41, 42] ``` Although the model has one logical next-token prediction layer, the runtime captures and injects multiple target stages. The draft SWA sidecar stage count must therefore come from the actual capture/injection stages: ```text draft_swa_stage_count = len(dspark_target_layer_ids) ``` It must not be inferred only from `num_nextn_predict_layers`. ### 3.4 Rejected data can outlive its semantic scope A request-scoped ring may physically retain rejected draft rows until they are overwritten. Physical retention alone is acceptable for scratch, but those rows must never be interpreted as: - Committed KV. - Radix-cache content. - PD-transferable state. - HiCache-offloadable state. The current representation does not make this boundary explicit. ## 4. Relationship to `unified_kv` ### 4.1 Different architectural dimensions This RFC and `unified_kv` address different concerns. `unified_kv` primarily defines an execution-oriented physical layout: ```text request slot -> fixed SWA ring -> position modulo ring size ``` Its strengths include: - Predictable addresses. - Contiguous memory. - Low metadata overhead. - Efficient unified SWA/C4/C128 kernels. - Request-slot-oriented hot-path execution. The draft sidecar proposal defines ownership and cache lifecycle: ```text committed prefix artifact -> content-scoped sidecar in-flight verify state -> step-scoped scratch ``` The distinction is: ```text unified_kv: execution-oriented physical layout draft SWA sidecar: content-oriented ownership and lifecycle ``` ### 4.2 This RFC does not redesign target `unified_kv` The proposal does not convert target unified SWA into a content-addressed layout. The following target structures remain unchanged: ```text target unified SWA ring target C4/C128 layout target compression state target unified attention kernels target request-slot addressing ``` Compatibility is implemented as a draft-only extension. ### 4.3 Draft-only unified layout A compatible draft unified pool can use: ```text [ committed draft SWA rows ][ verify scratch rows ] ``` The draft attention metadata combines two address sources: ```text committed prefix: radix/content mapping -> committed sidecar rows current speculative step: request/step mapping -> scratch rows ``` The buffer can remain contiguous and compatible with a unified attention interface while preserving separate semantic lifecycles. ### 4.4 Transfer semantics under `unified_kv` Target and draft state may use different transfer semantics: ```text target unified SWA: request-scoped SWA_RING state draft committed sidecar: content-scoped SWA page state draft verify scratch: never transferred ``` This preserves the original target unified design while making committed draft SWA independently reusable. ## 5. Proposed Design ### 5.1 Overall structure ```text Draft SWA ├── committed sidecar KV │ ├── content-scoped │ ├── radix-visible │ ├── reusable │ └── transferable └── verify temporary ├── step-scoped ├── allocator-independent ├── radix-invisible └── non-transferable ``` This follows the same principle used by Mamba and compressed KV artifacts: ```text runtime temporary data is not shared only committed artifacts enter the cache ``` ### 5.2 Committed sidecar KV Committed sidecar KV represents canonical draft SWA KV belonging to an accepted prefix. Its properties are: 1. Content-scoped. 2. Determined by prefix content and model weights. 3. Reusable on radix-cache hits. 4. Coupled to target prefix lifecycle. 5. Eligible for PD transfer. 6. Eligible for HiCache offload/loadback. 7. Evicted consistently with the corresponding target prefix. It can be understood as: ```text the draft-side sidecar of the target prefix cache ``` The sidecar may use a separate pool or an additional physical region, but it must have explicit coverage and lifecycle semantics. ### 5.3 Verify temporary Verify temporary contains draft KV and attention inputs needed only by the active speculative step. Its properties are: 1. Step-scoped. 2. Never radix-visible. 3. Excluded from HiCache. 4. Excluded from PD transfer. 5. Excluded from long-lived allocator state. 6. Reusable as workspace after the step. 7. Incapable of producing cache artifacts for rejected tokens. Possible physical representations include: ```text temporary tensor workspace buffer step-local scratch range ``` It must not be treated as a long-lived committed request cache. ### 5.4 Accept-path data flow The numerically safe baseline is: ```text draft proposal / verify -> generate step-local temporary KV -> run verify attention -> compute accept/reject accepted -> derive canonical draft KV from target hidden states -> write canonical KV into committed sidecar -> mark sidecar coverage as committed rejected -> discard temporary KV ``` The invariant is: ```text only canonical, committed draft KV enters the sidecar ``` ### 5.5 Promotion optimization Promotion is valid only when verify temporary already contains the canonical target-hidden-derived KV representation: ```text canonical verify scratch -> select accepted rows -> promote/copy accepted rows into sidecar ``` Proposal KV produced from draft mask/noise hidden states is not necessarily numerically equivalent to canonical committed KV. Therefore: ```text proposal scratch must not be promoted directly ``` The first implementation should prefer direct canonical materialization. Promotion can be introduced later after numerical equivalence is demonstrated. ### 5.6 Prefix-cache-hit behavior When both target and draft sidecar coverage hit: ```text target committed KV hit draft committed sidecar KV hit -> reuse both directly ``` When target KV hits but draft sidecar coverage is missing: ```text target committed KV hit draft sidecar miss -> recompute/backfill draft sidecar ``` For SWA, the fallback should preserve the reusable prefix and recompute only the required trailing window where possible: ```text reuse prefix before trailing SWA window recompute trailing window commit reconstructed sidecar coverage ``` This fallback should be observable and should not become the normal path. ### 5.7 Eviction and consistency Sidecar coverage must never outlive its corresponding target prefix. The required invariant is: ```text valid draft sidecar coverage implies valid corresponding target prefix coverage ``` Insert, split, eviction, backup, and loadback must update sidecar coverage consistently. A stale sidecar must never be paired with a newly allocated target prefix using the same physical slots. ## 6. Backend Layouts ### 6.1 Paged backend The paged layout can use: ```text committed sidecar pages: indexed through content/SWA mapping verify scratch pages: indexed through request slot and step offset ``` Only committed pages are exposed to radix cache, PD, and HiCache. ### 6.2 `unified_kv` backend The target unified layout remains unchanged. The draft unified pool adds: ```text committed content-addressed rows verify scratch rows ``` The draft attention index stream is assembled from: ```text content indices for committed prefix scratch indices for current verify step ``` No target C4/C128 or target ring redesign is required. ### 6.3 Backend-independent semantics Physical layouts may differ, but all backends must satisfy: ```text committed rows: content-scoped and transferable scratch rows: step-scoped and non-transferable ``` Backend-specific row stride, padding, and dtype must be reflected in memory accounting. ## 7. Implementation Plan ### 7.1 Accounting fix Replace target-average-layer scaling with explicit draft SWA terms: ```text committed sidecar bytes per full token fixed verify scratch bytes ``` This step changes pool sizing only. ### 7.2 Stage-count correctness Derive `draft_swa_stage_count` from actual target capture/injection stages, such as `dspark_target_layer_ids`. ### 7.3 Sidecar abstraction Introduce an explicit draft SWA sidecar component with: - Content coverage. - Target-prefix coupling. - Insert, split, and eviction lifecycle. - Backup and loadback lifecycle. - Radix visibility. ### 7.4 Verify scratch separation Route speculative proposal and verify KV through step-local scratch. Scratch addresses must not be inserted into request-to-token mappings or radix nodes. ### 7.5 Accept path Materialize canonical accepted draft KV directly into committed sidecar rows. Rejected rows produce no sidecar coverage. ### 7.6 Prefix-hit and fallback path Reuse sidecar KV on a complete hit. On a target-hit/sidecar-miss case, recompute only the required trailing SWA region where possible. ### 7.7 PD and HiCache integration Expose committed sidecar pages as transferable state. Explicitly exclude verify scratch from all transfer descriptors. ### 7.8 `unified_kv` adapter Add a draft-only unified sidecar/scratch layout and mixed index generation. Do not modify the target unified ring or compressed-state kernels. ### 7.9 Rollout Gate the new layout behind a server argument during rollout. Unsupported backends must reject explicit enablement rather than silently falling back to incompatible semantics. ## 8. Compatibility and Risks ### 8.1 Numerical compatibility The design should not change model numerics. Canonical committed KV must continue to come from the target-hidden injection path unless a promotion path has proven numerical equivalence. ### 8.2 Cache consistency Sidecar and target prefix eviction must remain coupled. Incorrect coverage updates could pair stale sidecar KV with unrelated target content. ### 8.3 Fallback overhead A frequent sidecar-miss fallback would erase reuse benefits. The implementation should record sidecar hit rate and trailing-recompute frequency. ### 8.4 Accept-path overhead Extra materialization or copies may offset memory benefits. The baseline should use one canonical projection and direct committed scatter. Promotion should only be added when it reduces measured critical-path cost. ### 8.5 Backend complexity Paged and unified backends use different physical layouts. The abstraction must standardize semantics without forcing target unified kernels into the paged cache model. ### 8.6 Memory accounting drift Backend row padding, dtype, and page stride must be included in physical sizing. Semantic token counts alone are insufficient for exact allocation. ## 9. Validation Plan ### 9.1 Correctness Verify output parity and speculative accept-rate parity against main. ### 9.2 Cache-artifact invariant Confirm that: ```text rejected draft tokens produce no radix artifact verify scratch is unreachable after the step only accepted canonical KV gains sidecar coverage ``` ### 9.3 Accounting Compare calculated draft memory against allocated and measured memory. Expected results: - Lower draft over-reservation. - Larger usable target KV pool. - Fixed scratch overhead independent of cached token count. ### 9.4 Prefix reuse Measure: - Sidecar hit rate. - Target-hit/sidecar-miss rate. - Trailing-window recompute frequency. - Amount of reused committed draft KV. ### 9.5 PD and HiCache Verify that committed sidecar KV survives: - Prefill/decode transfer. - Offload. - Loadback. - Eviction and reallocation. Verify that scratch rows are never transferred. ### 9.6 `unified_kv` Validate that: - Target unified behavior is unchanged. - Draft committed rows use content indices. - Verify rows use scratch indices. - Mixed index streams produce numerical parity. - Target `SWA_RING` and draft `SWA` transfer states coexist correctly. ### 9.7 Performance Measure: - Per-step scratch overhead. - Canonical commit cost. - Optional promotion cost. - Attention metadata construction. - Prefix-hit latency. - End-to-end throughput and latency. ## 10. Alternatives Considered ### 10.1 Keep draft SWA request-scoped This preserves the current implementation shape but prevents committed draft KV from becoming a reusable prefix artifact. ### 10.2 Recompute draft SWA on every prefix hit This avoids sidecar memory but makes fallback the default and repeatedly pays the target-hidden projection cost. ### 10.3 Keep verify data in a long-lived request ring This simplifies addressing but retains rejected state longer than necessary and blurs committed versus in-flight ownership. ### 10.4 Convert target unified SWA to content-addressed storage This would unnecessarily redesign the target unified hot path and is outside the scope of this RFC. The preferred approach is a draft-only unified extension. ### 10.5 Promote proposal scratch directly This is invalid unless proposal scratch is numerically identical to canonical target-hidden-derived KV. The proposal does not assume this equivalence. ### Related resources _No response_

signals.title: [Bug] Qwen3.5 MTP weights silently dropped on compressed-tensors checkpoints (accept len pinned at 1.0)
signals.text: ### Checklist - [x] I searched related issues but found no solution. - [x] The bug persists in the latest version. - [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback. - [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed. - [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Describe the bug **This is the compressed-tensors counterpart of #23113.** That issue added a `quark` branch to `_mtp_quant_config()` in `python/sglang/srt/models/qwen3_5_mtp.py`; `compressed_tensors` still has no branch, and fails the same way. Serving a Qwen3.5-family model from a **compressed-tensors** checkpoint (AutoRound / llm-compressor) with MTP speculative decoding produces **`accept len: 1.000` exactly** — zero drafted tokens ever accepted — with zero variance across every prompt, seed and depth. Throughput collapses, since the full draft cost is paid for nothing: 30.7 tok/s at depth 8 against 248 tok/s for a working speculative path on the same server, model and prompts. **Root cause.** Such checkpoints list the MTP linears in `quantization_config.ignore` **individually**: ``` mtp.fc mtp.layers.0.self_attn.q_proj mtp.layers.0.mlp.gate_proj mtp.layers.0.self_attn.k_proj mtp.layers.0.mlp.up_proj mtp.layers.0.self_attn.v_proj mtp.layers.0.mlp.down_proj mtp.layers.0.self_attn.o_proj ``` but SGLang constructs them **fused**, as `qkv_proj` and `gate_up_proj`. The fused names match no `ignore` entry, so exactly those two linears are built quantized while the unfused ones correctly fall back to unquantized. Dumping the constructed module's parameters: ``` model.layers.0.qkv_proj.weight_packed (7168, 640) <- quantized model.layers.0.mlp.gate_up_proj.weight_packed (17408, 640) <- quantized model.layers.0.o_proj.weight (5120, 3072) <- correct model.layers.0.mlp.down_proj.weight (5120, 8704) <- correct ``` Every `mtp.*` tensor in the checkpoint is plain bf16 (15 tensors, none with `_scale`, none packed), so the five stacked ones find no matching parameter and are dropped in `load_weights()` by `logger.warning_once`: ``` Parameter model.layers.0.q_proj.weight not found in params_dict, skip loading Parameter model.layers.0.k_proj.weight not found in params_dict, skip loading Parameter model.layers.0.v_proj.weight not found in params_dict, skip loading Parameter model.layers.0.mlp.gate_proj.weight not found in params_dict, skip loading Parameter model.layers.0.mlp.up_proj.weight not found in params_dict, skip loading ``` The MTP attention and MLP therefore run **randomly initialized**. Because `o_proj` and `down_proj` load correctly, the module is only partly broken, weight loading reports success, and `warning_once` deduplicates the five lines into a single easily-missed warning. This is not a verification-side problem: the failure is identical under a greedy request and under `--speculative-use-rejection-sampling`, while a non-MTP speculative control on the same server, model and prompts reads `accept len` 5.43. ### Proposed fix Give `compressed_tensors` the same treatment as `quark`, in `_mtp_quant_config()`: ```python if quant_config and quant_config.get_name() == "compressed_tensors": ignore = getattr(quant_config, "ignore", None) or [] if any(isinstance(layer, str) and layer.startswith("mtp.") for layer in ignore): return None ``` Verified on the setup below — the fused parameters become plain `.weight` at full shape, `not found in params_dict` goes from 10 hits (5 tensors x 2 TP ranks) to 0, and acceptance comes alive: | | accept len | decode tok/s | |---|---:|---:| | before, `--speculative-num-draft-tokens 4` | 1.000 | 44.1 | | before, `--speculative-num-draft-tokens 8` | 1.000 | 30.7 | | **after, 4** | **3.262** | **141.7** | | **after, 8** | **5.132** | **153.1** | (mean over three prompt types, 2 seeds each, `--max-num-seqs 1`.) I am happy to open a PR with this if the approach looks right. A more general alternative would be to make the fused-name gate (`should_ignore_layer(..., fused_mapping=...)`) resolve MTP prefixes, but the narrow branch matches what #23113 already established for quark. ### Reproduction Any Qwen3.5-family compressed-tensors checkpoint whose `quantization_config.ignore` lists `mtp.*` layers. Used here: `Qwen3.8-27B-W4A16-AutoRound` (`quant_method: compressed-tensors`, `format: pack-quantized`), served on 2x RTX 3090: ```bash python3 -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path <qwen3.5-family-compressed-tensors-checkpoint> \ --tp-size 2 --dtype bfloat16 --trust-remote-code \ --context-length 98304 --mem-fraction-static 0.84 \ --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 --sampling-defaults model \ --speculative-algorithm EAGLE \ --speculative-draft-model-path <same checkpoint> \ --speculative-num-steps 3 --speculative-eagle-topk 1 \ --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4 ``` Send any request and watch the scheduler log: ``` Decode batch, ... accept len: 1.00, accept rate: 0.00, ... ``` `accept len` is pinned at exactly 1.00 for every batch. Grepping the boot log for `not found in params_dict` shows the five skipped MTP tensors. ### Environment ``` Python: 3.10.12 (main, Jun 22 2026, 18:55:27) [GCC 11.4.0] CUDA available: True GPU 0,1: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3090 GPU 0,1 Compute Capability: 8.6 CUDA_HOME: /usr/local/cuda NVCC: Cuda compilation tools, release 13.3, V13.3.73 CUDA Driver Version: 595.84 PyTorch: 2.13.0+cu130 sglang: 0.0.0.dev16855+g5f1283959 sglang-kernel: 0.4.6.post1+cu130 flashinfer_python: 0.6.17 flashinfer_cubin: 0.6.17 flashinfer_jit_cache: 0.6.17+cu130 triton: 3.7.1 transformers: 5.12.1 torchao: 0.17.0 numpy: 2.2.6 aiohttp: 3.14.3 fastapi: 0.141.1 huggingface_hub: 1.27.0 interegular: 0.3.3 modelscope: 1.39.1 orjson: 3.12.0 outlines: 0.1.11 packaging: 26.3 psutil: 7.2.2 pydantic: 2.13.4 python-multipart: 0.0.32 pyzmq: 27.1.0 uvicorn: 0.52.3 uvloop: 0.22.1 vllm: Module Not Found xgrammar: 0.2.1 openai: 2.6.1 tiktoken: 0.13.0 anthropic: 0.122.0 litellm: Module Not Found torchcodec: 0.15.0+cu130 NVIDIA Topology: [4mGPU0 GPU1 CPU Affinity NUMA Affinity GPU NUMA ID[0m ```

signals.title: [Feature] Enhanced KV Cache Observability: Full-Lifecycle Metrics and Diagnostics
signals.text: ### Checklist - [ ] If this is not a feature request but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed. - [ ] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Motivation ### Summary This proposal aims to build a **full-lifecycle observability framework** for SGLang's KV Cache (L1 GPU → L2 Host → L3 Storage/Mooncake). Currently, when the KV cache hit rate drops in production, operators lack the end-to-end visibility to quickly pinpoint the root cause. This feature will transform the KV Cache from a "black box" into a fully observable system. ### Motivation The KV Cache is critical for SGLang's performance, especially in multi-turn对话 and prefix caching scenarios. However, diagnosing cache hit rate degradation remains challenging due to: 1. **Limited cross-layer visibility**: No metrics to track transfer success/failure between L1, L2, and L3. 2. **Insufficient failure classification**: Cannot distinguish between "data not present" (capacity/eviction) and "data present but read failed" (transfer/error). 3. **Lack of request-level tracing**: No structured logs with `rid` to trace a single request across the entire cache hierarchy. ### Current Observability Status SGLang already exposes useful metrics via `--enable-metrics`: | Metric | Description | |--------|-------------| | `sglang:cached_tokens_total{source}` | Cache hits by source (device/host/storage) | | `sglang:cache_hit_tokens_l{1,2,3}_total` | Per-layer hit token counts | | `sglang:cache_hit_rate` | Overall cache hit rate | | `sglang:evicted_tokens_total` | L1 (device) eviction count | **However**, these metrics answer *"how many tokens were cached"* but not *"why caching failed"*. ### Proposed Solution - New Prometheus Metrics: Propose new metrics like hicache_transfer_fail_total, hicache_storage_hit_total, and hicache_storage_miss_total to track cross-layer transfer success rates and L3 hit/miss counts. - Structured Logging: Suggest a unified log format (e.g., [HICACHE] rid=<rid> event=<event> ...) to enable request-level tracing across the entire cache hierarchy. ### Expected Benefits This will transform the KV cache from a 'black box' into a fully observable system, significantly reducing Mean Time To Resolution (MTTR) for performance issues and enabling data-driven capacity planning. ### Related resources _No response_

signals.title: [Bug] Using hicache in the main branch of deepseekv4-flash will result in illegal memory access.
signals.text: ### Checklist - [x] I searched related issues but found no solution. - [x] The bug persists in the latest version. - [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback. - [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed. - [x] Please use English. However, we encountered illegal memory access issues. Commit ID: 880ab72f34ead8f39544c7c7e08edbd443964a1f。 ### Reproduction The hardware we are using is B200. server command is： sglang serve \ --trust-remote-code \ --model-path /models/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 \ --tp 2 \ --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_mxfp4 \ --speculative-algorithm DSPARK \ --chunked-prefill-size 16384 \ --max-prefill-tokens 16384 \ --cuda-graph-backend-prefill breakable \ --cuda-graph-max-bs-prefill 8192 \ --enable-deepseek-v4-fp4-indexer \ --max-running-requests 256 \ --swa-full-tokens-ratio 0.1 \ --mem-fraction-static 0.75 \ --detokenizer-worker-num 8 \ --tokenizer-worker-num 8 \ --reasoning-parser deepseek-v4 \ --tool-call-parser deepseekv4 \ --enable-hierarchical-cache \ --hicache-ratio 4 \ ### Environment B200

signals.title: [Bug] EAGLE speculative decoding (native Qwen3.5/3.8 MTP) hangs in tree_speculative_sampling_target_only on Ampere (2x A2, TP=2, 100% GPU util / low power)
signals.text: ### Environment - SGLang 0.5.17 (sglang-venv), flashinfer 0.6.15.post1 - 2x NVIDIA A2 (16GB each, sm_86 / Ampere), CUDA 13.3, NCCL 2.28.9 - TP=2, --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e5m2, --mem-fraction-static 0.90 ### Model - Qwen3.8-27B AWQ 4-bit VLM (arch qwen3_5 + qwen3_5_vision, hybrid GDN/mamba) ### Server config (native in-checkpoint MTP, no draft-model-path) --speculative-algorithm EAGLE --speculative-num-steps 3 --speculative-eagle-topk 1 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4 --mamba-ssm-dtype bfloat16 --mm-feature-transport cpu --disable-prefill-cuda-graph --cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 2 --sampling-backend pytorch --reasoning-parser qwen3 --max-total-tokens 153600 --context-length 153600 ### Symptom Startup succeeds: KV cache 81272 tokens, draft decode/extend + target verify CUDA graphs captured. A short request completes (200 OK). A longer request that reaches EAGLE verify makes **both TP ranks spin at 100% GPU utilization with very low power draw (~25W)** and the server hangs indefinitely (health returns 200 until the scheduler watchdog kills the process at 300s). ### py-spy stack (both scheduler ranks) tree_speculative_sampling_target_only (sgl_kernel/speculative.py:36) eagle_sample (eagle_utils.py:806) run_eagle_verify (eagle_worker_common.py:588) verify (eagle_worker_v2.py:1496) ### Notes - flashinfer sampling kernel JIT compilation requires curand.h which was missing from the image (built from nvidia-cu13 pip package headers); after supplying it the compile succeeds and sampling.so is cached, but the tree sampling kernel still hangs at runtime. - Same config without speculative decoding runs fine (~17.5 tok/s decode, 81K KV). ### Related #31478 (eagle: broadcast finalized verify decision across TP ranks) #33549 (100% util / low power decode hang) #29347 (EAGLE + CUDA graph deadlock)

signals.title: [Bug] Grammar token sync initializes a singleton NCCL group under DP attention
signals.text: ### Checklist - [x] I searched related issues. This is a focused follow-up to #8400 with a confirmed singleton-group cause. - [x] The behavior is present on current `main`. - [x] A minimal configuration and environment are included below. - [x] This report is in English. ### Describe the bug `Sampler._sync_token_ids_across_tp()` calls `torch.distributed.all_reduce()` directly whenever grammar sampling is active (or `SYNC_TOKEN_IDS_ACROSS_TP=1`). With DP attention enabled, the sampler selects `attn_tp_group`. A valid configuration can have: ```text tp_size=8 attention_dp_size=8 attention_cp_size=1 attention_tp_size = 8 / 8 / 1 = 1 ``` The sampler still submits a token-ID all-reduce to this singleton group. The operation is mathematically an identity, but the first call lazily initializes a one-rank NCCL communicator. On our topology NCCL 2.28.9 allocated a 512 MiB NET shared P2P pool during that initialization: ```text ncclCommInitRankConfig ... rank 0 nranks 1 ... Init START P2P Chunksize set to 524288 transport/net.cc:656 Cuda Alloc Size 536870912 64 coll channels ... 64 p2p channels, 64 p2p channels per peer ncclCommInitRankConfig ... rank 0 nranks 1 ... Init COMPLETE AllReduce ... count 1 ... [nranks=1] ``` When serving-time GPU memory is constrained, communicator initialization fails with: ```text sampler.py::_sync_token_ids_across_tp torch.distributed.all_reduce ncclUnhandledCudaError Failed to CUDA calloc 536870912 bytes ``` This is not a 512 MiB token tensor. The NCCL allocation is `64 channels * 16 shared steps * 512 KiB`. The corresponding NCCL behavior is reported in NVIDIA/nccl#2363. SGLang's `GroupCoordinator.all_reduce()` already returns locally when `world_size == 1`, but this sampler path bypasses `GroupCoordinator` because it needs `ReduceOp.MIN`. ### Reproduction Start a server with DP attention where attention TP size is one: ```bash python -m sglang.launch_server \ --tp-size 8 \ --dp-size 8 \ --enable-dp-attention \ --grammar-backend xgrammar \ ... ``` Then send a request with constrained decoding, for example `response_format.type=json_schema`. Ordinary requests do not take this sampler branch when `SYNC_TOKEN_IDS_ACROSS_TP` is unset. For allocation visibility: ```bash NCCL_DEBUG=INFO NCCL_DEBUG_SUBSYS=INIT,GRAPH,COLL,ALLOC ``` A short JSON-schema request is sufficient to initialize the singleton communicator. It does not require a long prompt or high KV-cache usage. ### Expected behavior Skip token-ID synchronization when the selected sampler sync group has `world_size <= 1`. The communicator membership is fixed, so this cannot suppress a later multi-rank collective; a real multi-rank operation necessarily uses a different process group. The minimal change should preserve the existing `ReduceOp.MIN` behavior for groups with `world_size > 1`. ### Environment - SGLang current `main` (base SHA `26579d893e4a7405fcee43479cd0afbe8291d0af`) - PyTorch 2.11.0 + CUDA 13.0 - NCCL 2.28.9 - 8x NVIDIA B300, single node - `tp_size=8`, `dp_size=8`, `attention_cp_size=1`, DP attention enabled - xgrammar backend; request uses JSON-schema constrained decoding Related history: #8400 reported the same grammar-sampler allocation failure signature. #13947 previously guarded TP synchronization by group size but was later reverted by #16845 as part of a broader sampler change.

signals.title: # Breakable CUDA graph: per-layer break dominates GDN prefill time on hybrid models (Qwen3.5/3.6)
signals.text: [upstream-issue.md](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31301114/upstream-issue.md)
signals.author: ljy6j13

signals.title: # Breakable CUDA graph: per-layer break dominates GDN prefill time on hybrid models (Qwen3.5/3.6)
signals.text: ## Summary On a hybrid linear-attention model (30 `linear_attention` + 10 `full_attention` layers), prefill spends ~50% of the step wall clock with the GPU idle. The idle is not kernel launch cost inside the layer — it is the per-layer graph break that `breakable` CUDA graph backend inserts at every attention boundary. Evidence: switching the GDN prefill kernel from Triton (5 kernels/layer) to FlashInfer (1 fused CUTLASS kernel/layer) removes 4 of 5 kernel launches per layer and changes end-to-end throughput by **0%**. The idle time per layer is unchanged at ~590 µs. This makes kernel-level fusion a dead end for this architecture, and points at the break mechanism itself as the thing to fix. ## Environment - SGLang `v0.5.16` (issue reproduced against `main` @ `17313cf4b2` source read) - Model: Qwen3.5-MoE architecture (`Qwen3_5MoeForConditionalGeneration`), 35B-A3B, FP8 - `num_hidden_layers: 40` → `layer_types`: 30 `linear_attention` + 10 `full_attention` (`full_attention_interval: 4`) - `linear_key_head_dim: 128`, `linear_value_head_dim: 128`, `mamba_ssm_dtype: float32` - MoE: `num_experts: 256`, `num_experts_per_tok: 8`, `moe_intermediate_size: 512` - Hardware: single H200 (SM90, 132 SMs) per node - Deployment: PD-disaggregated, 1 prefill node + 1 decode node, Mooncake over NVLink; also reproduced on a non-disaggregated (mixed) single-node deploy - `flashinfer` 0.6.14 - Speculative decoding: EAGLE, `--speculative-num-steps 2` Prefill node args (relevant subset): ``` --max-running-requests 256 --context-length 4096 --chunked-prefill-size 4096 --max-prefill-tokens 4096 --quantization fp8 --max-mamba-cache-size 256 --mem-fraction-static 0.85 --speculative-algorithm EAGLE --speculative-num-steps 2 --speculative-eagle-topk 1 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 3 --disaggregation-mode prefill ``` CUDA graph config resolves to `backend=breakable`, `num_tokens=[4, 8, 12, ..., 4096]`. ## Reproduction Capture a torch profiler trace on the prefill node under steady load, then classify each GPU kernel as graph-covered vs eager-launched by following `args.correlation` from the kernel to its CPU-side launch API (`cudaGraphLaunch` vs `cudaLaunchKernel` / `cuLaunchKernelEx`), and attribute the gap before each kernel to that kernel. ## Measurements ### Baseline: Triton GDN prefill kernel Dispatcher log: ``` GDN kernel dispatcher: decode=TritonGDNKernel, extend=TritonGDNKernel, verify=TritonGDNKernel ``` GDN kernels inside one prefill step — **10 kernels per linear_attention layer**: ``` x60 l2norm_fwd_kernel x30 _causal_conv1d_fwd_kernel x30 fused_qkv_split_gdn_prefill_kernel x30 fused_gdn_gating_kernel x30 chunk_local_cumsum_scalar_kernel x30 chunk_gated_delta_rule_fwd_kkt_solve_kernel x30 recompute_w_u_fwd_kernel x30 chunk_gated_delta_rule_fwd_kernel_h_blockdim64 x30 chunk_fwd_kernel_o ``` (300 GDN kernel launches, 2.77 ms of self time, in a 53 ms step.) Graph coverage for that step: ``` kernel total 1981 18.27 ms graph-covered 1440 (72.7%) 14.77 ms eager-launched 541 (27.3%) 3.51 ms <- but introduces 32.75 ms idle (61.3% of window) ``` Top idle contributors are all GDN, each appearing x30 or x60 (once per `linear_attention` layer): ``` idle self count kernel 7.37ms 0.07ms x60 l2norm_fwd_kernel 3.90ms 0.96ms x30 chunk_gated_delta_rule_fwd_kernel_h_blockdim64 3.30ms 0.07ms x30 chunk_local_cumsum_scalar_kernel 3.18ms 0.61ms x30 chunk_gated_delta_rule_fwd_kkt_solve_kernel 2.32ms 0.05ms x30 fused_gdn_gating_kernel 2.18ms 0.30ms x30 recompute_w_u_fwd_kernel 1.94ms 0.41ms x30 chunk_fwd_kernel_o ``` Note `l2norm_fwd_kernel`: **0.07 ms of self time gates 7.37 ms of idle.** ### After: FlashInfer GDN prefill kernel Set `--linear-attn-prefill-backend flashinfer` (SM90 + `linear_*_head_dim=128` + fp32 SSM state, so this is the validated domain per `flashinfer_gdn_prefill_default`). Dispatcher log confirms it took effect: ``` Linear attention kernel backend: decode=triton, prefill=flashinfer FlashInfer GDN kernels loaded successfully GDN kernel dispatcher: decode=TritonGDNKernel, extend=FlashInferGDNKernel, verify=FlashInferGDNKernel ``` GDN kernels inside one prefill step — the five `chunk_*` Triton kernels are gone, replaced by a single fused CUTLASS kernel: ``` x30 kernel_cutlass_kernel_flashinfergdn_kernelsdelta_rule_dsl... x60 l2norm_fwd_kernel x30 _causal_conv1d_fwd_kernel x30 fused_qkv_split_gdn_prefill_kernel x30 fused_gdn_gating_kernel ``` **5 kernels/layer instead of 10.** The fusion worked exactly as intended. Graph coverage for `step[EXTEND bs=15 toks=1319]` (60.6 ms): ``` kernel total 1919 28.65 ms graph-covered 1262 (65.8%) 22.08 ms eager-launched 657 (34.2%) 6.58 ms total idle 30.09 ms (49.6% of window) ``` The fused kernel alone: ``` 17.75ms idle / 1.61ms self / x30 ``` **592 µs of idle per layer, gating a kernel that runs for 54 µs.** An 11:1 idle-to-work ratio. ### End-to-end: no change Same benchmark, same dataset (~87 input / ~26 output tokens per request — a short-request translation workload), 1P1D, EAGLE mtp2: | Concurrency | req/s Δ | total tok/s Δ | mean TTFT Δ | |---|---|---|---| | 32 | −2.0% | −2.0% | +6.5% | | 64 | −1.2% | −1.1% | +3.1% | | 128 | +1.0% | +0.8% | −3.5% | | 256 | +1.5% | +1.6% | −7.3% | Within noise. Removing 4 of 5 kernel launches per layer, across 30 layers, changed nothing. ## Analysis `RadixLinearAttention.forward` routes to the break-marked variant when running under the breakable backend (`python/sglang/srt/layers/radix_linear_attention.py`): ```python bcg_unified_linear_attention_with_output = eager_on_graph(True)( unified_linear_attention_with_output ) ``` `eager_on_graph`'s wrapper (`python/sglang/srt/model_executor/runner_backend_utils/breakable_cuda_graph/breakable_cuda_graph.py`) ends the current segment, optionally barriers, runs the body eagerly, and begins a new segment. So every `linear_attention` layer forces one break. `cudaGraphLaunch` count in the trace is 41 per step = 30 linear + 10 full + 1 tail, matching exactly. The cost that does *not* go away when kernels are fused is what happens around each break: segment teardown/setup plus the host-side tensor preparation that runs eagerly between segments. CPU-side counters in the same window: ``` aten::empty x397 1.56 ms aten::empty_strided x201 0.86 ms aten::index_put_ x31 0.79 ms ``` Explicit sync points are negligible and are *not* the cause (`aten::item` x4 / 0.08 ms, `cudaStreamSynchronize` x12 / 0.06 ms) — 0.14 ms against 30 ms of idle. The controlled comparison is the key result: **the number of kernels inside the break changed 5x, the idle per break did not move.** That isolates the cost to the break itself rather than to launch overhead. For a 40-layer hybrid model this is 40 breaks per prefill step. Architectures with a high linear-attention layer count pay this proportionally — and the trend in hybrid models is toward more linear layers, not fewer. ## Impact The fixed per-step cost is ~30 ms regardless of batch size, so it is amortized only by batching. On short-request workloads (translation, chat) where prefill steps are frequent and small, this dominates: - `step[EXTEND bs=2 toks=70]`: 50.9 ms wall, 9.89 ms GPU busy → **19.4% util** - `step[EXTEND bs=15 toks=1319]`: 60.6 ms wall, 28.65 ms GPU busy → **47% util** The larger batch is better purely because the same fixed cost is spread over more tokens. ## Questions 1. Is the per-layer break required for `linear_attention`, or is it inherited from the shared attention break marker? Unlike full attention, GDN prefill does not appear to need per-layer metadata recomputed outside the graph — the SSM state indices are known at capture time for a given shape tier. 2. Could the host-side tensor preparation (`aten::empty` / `empty_strided` observed x600 per step) be hoisted out of the break, so the break carries only the kernel call? 3. Is there a path to capturing the `linear_attention` layers into the graph entirely on this architecture — i.e. a reason `full` backend rejects hybrid models beyond the GQA check that disables the enumerated prefill graph? Happy to run further experiments and share traces — we have a reproducible setup and both Triton and FlashInfer traces on hand.

signals.title: [Playground] Verified cell: Qwen3.8-27B / dgx-spark / nvfp4 / DFLASH2 / single
signals.text: > Hand-authored rather than playground-prefilled: the DGX Spark DFlash2 cells on the [Qwen3.8-27B cookbook page](https://docs.sglang.io/cookbook/autoregressive/Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B) carry the "Final Verification In Progress" badge, and this combination has been running as the production default on a real GB10 since 2026-08-20, from a public, digest-pinned deployment repo with a frozen benchmark battery. Offering the data for the verification pass. Everything below was measured on one ASUS Ascent GX10 (GB10, 128 GB unified, stock DGX OS); full methodology and raw numbers: [BENCHMARKS.md](https://github.com/hasso5703/dgx-spark-qwen38/blob/main/BENCHMARKS.md). ### Cookbook model Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B (autoregressive) ### Combination dgx-spark / default / nvfp4 / dflash (DFLASH2) / single ### Proposed cell snippet ```javascript { match: { hw: "dgx-spark", variant: "default", quant: "nvfp4", nodes: "single" }, verified: true, env: [], // The DFLASH2 spec selector adds, as today: // --speculative-algorithm DFLASH // --speculative-draft-model-path incoai/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2 // --speculative-num-draft-tokens 8 // We additionally run --speculative-draft-model-quantization unquant and pin the // draft revision (z-lab/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2 @ 50307d4c, byte-identical to incoai, see notes). flags: ["--trust-remote-code", "--model-path {{MODEL_NAME}}", "--mem-fraction-static 0.50", "--attention-backend flashinfer", "--chunked-prefill-size 8192", "--disable-prefill-cuda-graph", "--cuda-graph-max-bs 8", "--disable-flashinfer-autotune", "--mamba-radix-cache-strategy extra_buffer", "--mamba-ssm-dtype bfloat16", "--max-mamba-cache-size 96", "--max-running-requests 8", "--enable-torch-compile", "--torch-compile-max-bs 4", "--num-continuous-decode-steps 2", "--sleep-on-idle", "--reasoning-parser qwen3", "--tool-call-parser qwen3_coder", "--host {{HOST_IP}}", "--port {{PORT}}"] } ``` No `--kv-cache-dtype` flag: the RadixArk NVFP4 checkpoint self-declares fp8 KV, so keeping the current cell's explicit `fp8_e4m3` is equivalent. ### Existing cell at this match (for diff) ```javascript { match: { hw: "dgx-spark", variant: "default", quant: "nvfp4", nodes: "single" }, verified: true, verificationStatus: sel => sel.spec === "dflash" ? "in-progress" : "verified", env: [], flags: ["--trust-remote-code", "--model-path {{MODEL_NAME}}", "--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3", "--mem-fraction-static 0.85", "--attention-backend flashinfer", "--chunked-prefill-size 2048", "--reasoning-parser qwen3", "--tool-call-parser qwen3_coder", "--host {{HOST_IP}}", "--port {{PORT}}"] } ``` ### SGLang version No public build ships DFLASH2 yet, so the serving image is the pinned base `lmsysorg/sglang@sha256:febfb971c735...` (= `qwen38-27b`, 2026-08-15) plus five sha256-verified files: PR #35371 exactly as merged (`c14312a`), with the quantized-lm_head candidate path carrying #35496's contiguous-mask fix at both sites. Build recipe and manifest: [dflash2/](https://github.com/hasso5703/dgx-spark-qwen38/tree/main/dflash2). Same DFlash2 code paths as the `1cf2b8c` source build the cookbook install note pins. The repo repins to an official image the day one ships DFLASH2. ### Benchmark result Speed (greedy, deterministic stack, batch-1 decode unless noted): - Single stream vs the previous DSpark default, same box, same night: code DE 39.4 vs 25.4 tok/s, reasoning FR 43.5 vs 30.5, free prose FR 20.2 vs 14.0, math word problems at parity. `bench.sh` greedy median 50.0 tok/s on the instrument that measured 36-40 for DSpark. - Concurrency: 135-148 tok/s aggregate at c8; 258 tok/s at c32 (`--max-running-requests 32`), still climbing at c32. - Draft token count: K sweep on this box confirms 8 optimal, 9 collapses (credit [r0b0tlab](https://github.com/r0b0tlab/qwen38-27b-nvfp4-sm121-sglang)). - Acceptance is strongly content-dependent (code and math high, free prose lower); the full per-content table is in BENCHMARKS.md. Quality ("The losslessness study" in BENCHMARKS.md): with `--disable-flashinfer-autotune` the server is deterministic enough that quality evals reproduce to the point across seeds. GSM8K n=200: 188/200 vs 188/200, exact parity with DSpark. IFEval n=200: split within noise in both directions. tool-eval-bench (69 scenarios, two seeds): 93/93 DSpark vs 91/91 DFlash2; the stable 2-point deficit traces to floating-point near-tie flips, not drafter quality: at temperature 0 both drafters diverge from the pure autoregressive ground truth on 10/10 prompts, equally early, because block verification changes reduction orders. Verdict: no measurable real-quality loss on GB10. ### Notes / caveats GB10-specific observations, offered for the cell and its warnings: 1. `--disable-flashinfer-autotune` matters twice on GB10. Without it the identical config does not perform identically across boots: c8 aggregate ranged 92-111 tok/s and verify-heavy single-stream cells swung up to +-15 % (the on-disk autotune cache is read but a different draw can still land). Disabling costs ~2 % average throughput, makes both perf and quality benchmarks reproducible, and boots ~2 min faster. 2. `--mem-fraction-static 0.85` (current cell) deserves a warning on unified memory. FlashInfer autotune bursts and CUDA graph capture allocate outside SGLang's accounting; on this box, four consecutive native launches at fractions 0.60-0.85 (autotune enabled) each drove host RAM to zero, and one froze the machine (SSH dead, physical power cycle). We have not re-tested 0.85 with autotune disabled; 0.50 is the value with a week of production and a full install-cycle audit behind it, and it still serves 262144 context, 8 concurrent streams and 96 bf16 GDN state slots. Note `docker --memory` does not contain CUDA unified allocations, so the fraction is the only real guard on this platform. 3. Chunked prefill: 4096 measured ~16 % worse at c8 than 8192 on this box (2048, the current cell value, untested here). 4. `--cuda-graph-max-bs 8`: +6.5 % at c8 vs graphs capped lower (batches 5-8 otherwise run eager). 5. `--sleep-on-idle` is worth shipping in the Spark cell: without it the scheduler busy-spins at ~101 % of a core when idle. Measured: 12.1 W to 10.5 W module power, wake-up TTFT unchanged (0.23-0.24 s after 60 s and 300 s idle). Several GB10 owners hit this in the wild ([NVIDIA forum thread](https://forums.developer.nvidia.com/t/380257), [MiaAI-Lab issue #4](https://github.com/MiaAI-Lab/Qwen3.8-27B-SGLang-DGX-Spark/issues/4)). 6. Draft checkpoint identity: `incoai/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2` and `z-lab/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2` are byte-identical as of today (same `config.json` and `model.safetensors` blobs on the Hub), so either path attests the same weights. We pin z-lab @ `50307d4c`. 7. An FP8-target variant (same drafter) measured 108 tok/s at c8 here: a fallback if NVFP4-target quality is ever questioned. Reproduction: `curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hasso5703/dgx-spark-qwen38/main/get.sh | bash` installs the pinned stack end to end (or `./install.sh --no-service && ./run.sh` for a disposable foreground run). The frozen battery is `./bench-matrix.sh` and works against any OpenAI-compatible endpoint. Happy to run any additional protocol on this box for the verification pass. Credits: DFlash2 by z-lab / inco.ai (#35371); quantized-lm_head path by [MiaAI-Lab](https://github.com/MiaAI-Lab/Qwen3.8-27B-SGLang-DGX-Spark) (now upstream via #35496); K sweep by r0b0tlab. ### Attestation - [x] I ran this exact command on the listed hardware. (Production systemd service since 2026-08-20; the unit template renders to exactly this launch line, plus deployment extras that do not touch the engine path: `--served-model-name`, a chat template, an API key.) - [x] The server reached READY and answered a cURL request successfully. (Health and a real generation smoke on every install; 437-token canary passing.) - [x] Output looked correct on at least one prompt. (Deterministic quality battery, plus the GSM8K / IFEval / tool-eval runs above.)

signals.title: [Bug] /health handler's timeout path doesn't cancel the scheduler-side request, causing orphaned health-check requests  to pile up and crash paged-prefill batching
signals.text: ### Checklist - [x] I searched related issues but found no solution. - [ ] The bug persists in the latest version. - [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback. - [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed. - [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Describe the bug `GET /health` (`health_generate` in `sglang/srt/entrypoints/http_server.py`) dispatches a real 1-token `generate_request()` to the scheduler process, then waits up to `SGLANG_HEALTH_CHECK_TIMEOUT` (default 20s) for `tokenizer_manager.last_receive_tstamp` to advance: ```python task = asyncio.create_task(gen()) tic = time.time() while time.time() < tic + HEALTH_CHECK_TIMEOUT: await asyncio.sleep(1) if tokenizer_manager.last_receive_tstamp > tic: task.cancel() return Response(200) task.cancel() logger.error("Health check failed. Server couldn't get a response from detokenizer for last ...") return Response(503) ``` On timeout, `task.cancel()` only cancels the **local `asyncio.Task`** inside the HTTP-server process. The underlying generate request had already been forwarded to the **scheduler**, a separate process communicating over ZMQ/IPC — cancelling the local awaiting coroutine does not retract or abort the request there. If the scheduler is even briefly slow (GPU hiccup, batching contention, etc.), the request keeps running/queued server-side after the HTTP layer has already given up on it and returned 503. Because `HEALTH_CHECK_TIMEOUT` (20s) commonly equals or is close to the polling interval used by external health-checkers (e.g. Docker's default `HEALTHCHECK interval`), a single transient scheduler slowdown causes **every subsequent poll to add a brand-new independent 1-token request on top of ones the HTTP layer already abandoned**, rather than waiting for the backlog to clear. Over a multi-minute stall this produces several orphaned single-token `input_ids=[0]` requests all still resident in the scheduler simultaneously. We hit this in production: a transient scheduler stall (`last_heartbeat` frozen for ~2 minutes, confirmed via three consecutive `Health check failed ... last_heartbeat time: <frozen ts>` log lines 30s apart) let ~5 of these orphaned health-check requests accumulate, and when the scheduler eventually tried to batch them together it hit a shape-mismatch crash in the paged-prefill path: ``` ValueError: q.shape[0] (1) does not match qo_indptr[-1] (5). For paged prefill, q must have shape [total_tokens, num_heads, head_dim] where total_tokens = qo_indptr[-1]. ``` (`qo_indptr[-1]=5` lines up with the number of orphaned health-check requests that would have piled up in that stall window.) This is running Qwen3.5/Qwen3.8-style hybrid attention with `--speculative-algo NEXTN`, similar model/config class to #34239, and that crash then also left the passed-through GPU in an `NV_ERR_RESET_REQUIRED` state requiring a full VM power cycle to clear (separate GPU-driver-side issue, not filing here, just noting the blast radius). Regardless of whether the shape-mismatch crash itself is viewed as a separate bug (may well be, see #34239), the `/health` handler's failure-to-actually-cancel-server-side is a real, independent correctness gap worth fixing on its own: a health check that "fails" should not leave its probe request alive in the system. ### Reproduction ### Reproduction 1. Serve any generation model with `sglang.launch_server`. 2. Point a poller at `GET /health` with an interval at/near `SGLANG_HEALTH_CHECK_TIMEOUT` (default 20s) — e.g. Docker `HEALTHCHECK --interval=20s`. 3. Induce a transient scheduler slowdown for the request dispatched by one `/health` poll (e.g. artificially delay `generate_request`/the scheduler's batch loop, or trigger any other rare slow-path in the target model). 4. Observe: the HTTP layer times out and returns 503 after 20s, but the dispatched request remains resident in the scheduler (visible via internal batch/queue metrics, or by the request eventually completing/interfering with later batches after the HTTP layer has already discarded it). 5. Each subsequent 20s poll adds another independent request without waiting for the previous one(s) to actually clear scheduler-side. ### Suggested fix - On timeout, actually propagate cancellation to the scheduler (e.g. send an explicit abort/cancel message for `rid`, not just cancel the local `asyncio.Task` and pop local state), so a "failed" health check doesn't leave a live request behind. - Alternatively/additionally: dedupe or rate-limit concurrent in-flight health-check-generated requests (e.g. skip dispatching a new one if a prior health-check `rid` is still outstanding), so pollers with an interval ≤ `HEALTH_CHECK_TIMEOUT` cannot compound a backlog. ### Environment SGLang: `0.5.15.post1` FlashInfer: `0.6.12` Torch: `2.11.0+cu130` GPU: 1× NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (passthrough VM) Model: `Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B-FP8`, `--speculative-algo NEXTN --speculative-num-steps 3 --speculative-eagle-topk 1 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4 --context-length 262144`

signals.title: EncoderScheduler dispatches requests after request timeout
signals.text:
## Problem

The encoder scheduler cancels a timed-out request future, but leaves the corresponding PendingRequest in pending_queue. When the batch worker later dequeues it, the request is still broadcast to tensor-parallel workers and passed to the encoder even though its caller has already timed out.

## Reproduction

With EncoderScheduler running, block the first batch_encode call, submit a second request, and let the second request exceed SGLANG_ENCODER_REQ_TIMEOUT. The second future is cancelled, but the worker still dispatches that request after the first batch completes.

## Expected behavior

A request whose waiting future has been cancelled or completed should be removed from dispatchable work before broadcast and encoder execution.

## Fix

The accompanying branch filters completed futures before dispatch, re-checks after acquiring the dispatch lock, and skips completed per-request work. It adds a CPU-only regression test.

## Environment

This is a Python/backend scheduling issue and does not require GPU hardware to reproduce at the scheduler seam.
signals.author: hsusul

signals.title: [Bug] `uv pip install sglang` with uv < 0.12 silently installs 0.5.9 (6 months old)
signals.text: ### What happened I hit this yesterday: served Qwen3.8-27B-FP8 with `--tp 2` and got fluent but wrong output (e.g. trivial math answered incorrectly, no crash or NaN). Debugged the model first, then realized the actual problem: `uv pip install sglang` had installed **0.5.9** (2026-02-23) instead of 0.5.17. 0.5.9 predates the qwen3_5 dense TP>1 fix (#19070) — a dropped down_proj all-reduce — which explains the wrong output. ### Root cause - `flash-attn-4`, a mandatory dependency of every release since 0.5.10, has only pre-release versions on PyPI (4.0.0b5…b27). - uv < 0.12.0 does not honor pre-release specifiers in transitive dependency metadata (changed in astral-sh/uv#19993). It treats every sglang ≥ 0.5.10 as unsatisfiable and silently backtracks to 0.5.9 — the newest release without the flash-attn-4 dependency. No error, no warning. Repro (resolution only, any OS): ``` $ echo sglang | uv pip compile - --python-platform x86_64-manylinux_2_34 --python-version 3.12 # uv 0.11.x -> sglang==0.5.9 # uv 0.12.x -> sglang==0.5.17 ``` Pinning makes the mechanism visible, since the resolver can no longer backtrack: ``` $ echo 'sglang==0.5.10.post1' | uv pip compile - # uv 0.11.x × No solution found ... Because only flash-attn-4<4.0.0b4 is available and sglang==0.5.10.post1 depends on flash-attn-4>=4.0.0b4 ... hint: ... pre-releases weren't enabled (try: `--prerelease=allow`) ``` ### Docs inconsistency `uv pip install --prerelease=allow sglang` works (the install guide has the flag), but many docs pages use the plain command — e.g. https://lmsysorg.mintlify.app/cookbook/autoregressive/Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B#install-sglang (`docs/cookbook/autoregressive/Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B.mdx`), and about 12 cookbook pages total. Anyone following those pages (or typing the obvious command) with an older uv gets 0.5.9 silently. pip, uv ≥ 0.12, and the Docker images are unaffected. ### Possibly the same issue in the tracker - #24029 — qwen3-vl "output does not match the image at all": four users on 0.5.9; one environment paste (2026-05-25, when 0.5.12 was current) shows `sglang 0.5.9`, `torch 2.9.1` (0.5.9's exact pin), and `uv 0.11.16`. Resolved as "upgrade to >=0.5.12 is OK", without anyone asking why they were on 0.5.9. - Open issues filed months after newer releases existed, with an env of 0.5.9 and 0.5.9's torch pin: #34111 #34112 #34113 #33283 #25670. Not asserting these are all this — but the fingerprint matches a resolver-driven 0.5.9 install. One forward-looking note: `cuda-tile==1.6.0rc5` on current main (not yet in any release) is the same pattern — the first release shipping it will again be unresolvable for uv < 0.12 users, who would then silently stay on 0.5.17.

signals.title: Fix: Synchronize random token dropping in DeepSeek Janus Pro to prevent TP divergence
signals.text: ## Motivation This PR fixes a bug identified in Issue #14039 The original implementation used `torch.randn` without a synchronized generator, causing different TP ranks to drop different tokens during inference. This leads to state divergence and incorrect results in distributed settings. ## Modifications - Modified `python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_janus_pro.py`: - Added logic to broadcast a random seed from rank 0 to all other ranks when `torch.distributed` is initialized. - Used `torch.Generator` with the synchronized seed to generate the noise tensor. ## Accuracy Tests - This fix ensures consistency across tensor parallel ranks, preventing state divergence. It restores correctness in distributed inference scenarios. ## Benchmarking and Profiling - Minimal performance impact. The overhead of broadcasting a single seed scalar is negligible compared to the inference latency. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). signals.title: [npu] support features of qwen3_next; fixup accuracy bugs in qwen3_next
signals.text: ## Motivation - NPU supports features of qwen3_next(pd disaggregation, mtp, npugraph, fused operator, w8a8 quantizaton); - fixup accuracy bugs in qwen3_next on NPU This PR needs to run togather with the modification of https://github.com/sgl-project/sgl-kernel-npu/pull/259. And one should install latest CANN/PTA packages which include our new torch_npu kernels. ## Modifications This pull request significantly advances the NPU (Ascend) compatibility and performance for the Qwen3_next model within the SGLang framework. It integrates crucial NPU-specific optimizations and features, such as disaggregation and fused operators, while also rectifying known accuracy problems. The changes span across attention mechanisms, quantization processes, and general device management, aiming to provide a more robust and efficient experience on Ascend hardware. #### Highlights - NPU Feature Support: Introduced comprehensive NPU (Ascend) support for Qwen3_next model features, including disaggregation, multi-token prefill (MTP), NPU graph integration, fused operators, and W8A8 quantization. - Accuracy Bug Fixes: Addressed and resolved accuracy issues identified in the Qwen3_next model when running on NPU hardware. - Attention Backend Enhancements: Implemented a new AscendGDNAttnBackend for Mamba kernel attention on NPU, refining the handling of sequence lengths and cache locations for improved performance and correctness. - Quantization Improvements: Updated the W8A8 quantization logic to better support dynamic quantization on NPU and introduced a new utility script (convert_model_qwen3_next.py) for INT8 quantization of Qwen3_next models. - Device Agnostic Operations: Refactored cache management and memory pool initialization to be device-agnostic, moving away from hardcoded 'cuda' references to torch.get_device_module(). - New AscendC Fused Operator Integration: Added integration of the AscendC fused operator torch_npu.npu_recurrent_gated_delta_rule, which can be enabled by setting the ENABLE_ASCENDC_FUSION_GDN environment variable. ## Accuracy Tests ```[shell] export HCCL_OP_EXPANSION_MODE=AIV export DEEP_NORMAL_MODE_USE_INT8_QUANT=1 export ASCEND_USE_FIA=1 export SGLANG_ENABLE_OVERLAP_PLAN_STREAM=1 export SGLANG_ENABLE_SPEC_V2=1 export ENABLE_ASCENDC_FUSION_GDN=1 export MODEL_PATH=Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B-Instruct-A8W8 python -m sglang.launch_server --model-path ${MODEL_PATH} --trust-remote-code \ --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000 --nnodes 1 --node-rank 0 \ --attention-backend ascend --device npu --quantization modelslim \ --max-running-requests 16 \ --context-length 102400 --chunked-prefill-size 71680 --max-prefill-tokens 102400 \ --tp-size 8 \ --mem-fraction-static 0.7 --max-total-tokens 1126400 \ --moe-a2a-backend deepep --deepep-mode auto \ --disable-overlap-schedule --disable-radix-cache \ --speculative-algorithm NEXTN --speculative-num-steps 1 --speculative-eagle-topk 1 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 2 ``` ```[shell] python few_shot_gsm8k.py --data-path test.jsonl.txt --parallel 16 --num-question 200 --num-shots 5 --port 8000 --temperature 0 # Accuracy: 0.945 # Invaild: 0.000 # Latency: 389.107s # Output throughput: 83.327 token/s ``` ## Benchmarking and Profiling After enabling the aforementioned AscendC fused operator, the performance metrics are as follows: By configuring startup command: ```[shell] python -m sglang.launch_server --model-path ${MODEL_PATH} --trust-remote-code \ --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000 --nnodes 1 --node-rank 0 \ --attention-backend ascend --device npu \ --max-running-requests 96 --context-length 8192 --disable-radix-cache \ --chunked-prefill-size 327680 --max-prefill-tokens 4000 \ --tp-size 16 --enable-dp-attention --dp-size 4 --enable-dp-lm-head --mem-fraction-static 0.7 \ --moe-a2a-backend deepep --deepep-mode auto \ --cuda-graph-bs 24 \ --max-total-tokens 229504 ``` ```[shell] python -m sglang.bench_serving --base-url http://7.150.8.78:8000 --dataset-path /data/h00910141/ShareGPT_V3_unfiltered_cleaned_split.json --dataset-name=random --random-range-ratio 1 --random-input 3500 --random-output 1500 --max-concurrency 24 --num-prompts 24 ``` ### baseline tpot: 53.05ms, ttft: 6500ms ### pr tpot: 44.30ms, ttft: 6363ms ## signals.title: [diffusion] model: optimize Qwen2.5-VL ViT and text encoder
signals.text: ## Summary Replace HuggingFace's `Qwen2_5_VisionTransformerPretrainedModel` with a custom `Qwen2_5_VisionTransformer` for Qwen2.5-VL ViT, and extend `torch.compile` to cover the text encoder (ViT + LLM encode). **Custom ViT (`qwen2_5vl.py`):** - Unified attention backend (`flash_attention_2` / `sdpa` / `eager`) with automatic fallback: uses `flash_attn_varlen_func` when available, falls back to SDPA with `.contiguous()` fix for AMD MIOpen precision issue - `VisionRotaryEmbeddingWithCache`: pre-computed frequency cache, defers cos/sin to indexing time - `@lru_cache` on `_get_rope_by_thw`: caches window index + RoPE per (t, h, w) grid - Fused `gate_up_proj` via `MergedColumnParallelLinear` in ViT MLP - `RMSNorm` (with platform-specific fused kernels) replaces `Qwen2RMSNorm` - `torch.compile` compatibility: removed `pin_memory` in `_invert_permutation`, use `torch.tensor_split` instead of `torch.split` **AMD GPU precision fix:** - Root cause: HF's SDPA path passes non-contiguous tensors (from `torch.split`) to `F.scaled_dot_product_attention`, causing incorrect results in MIOpen backend. Single-layer error is small but accumulates exponentially through 32 ViT layers (cosine_sim drops to ~0.55). - Fix: SDPA path applies `.contiguous()` on qkv slices; FlashAttention varlen path is unaffected (uses contiguous `[seq, heads, dim]` format natively). ## Profiling ### Without `torch.compile` ### With `torch.compile` ## Test Plan - [x] Unit test: custom ViT vs HF ViT numerical consistency (3 cases, atol=1e-5) - [x] End-to-end: 40-step image generation produces correct output - [x] Profiling traces generated for both compile/no-compile modes

signals.title: Fix GLM4 MoE Lite CompressedTensors serving and transformers version checks
signals.text: ## Summary This PR fixes `Glm4MoeLiteForCausalLM` serving failures for CompressedTensors checkpoints (e.g. `GLM-4.7-Flash-REAP-23B-A3B-AWQ-4bit`) in SGLang, while keeping regular AWQ behavior intact. It also fixes an incorrect Transformers downgrade warning for GLM-4.7/GLM4 MoE Lite models. ## Problem SGLang could serve `/ssd512g/models/GLM-4.7-Flash-AWQ`, but failed on `/ssd512g/models/GLM-4.7-Flash-REAP-23B-A3B-AWQ-4bit` with: ``` AttributeError: 'ReplicatedLinear' object has no attribute 'weight' ``` Additionally, SGLang printed a misleading warning suggesting `transformers==4.57.1` for `glm4_moe_lite` even though this architecture requires Transformers >=5. ## Root cause 1. MLA attention init and backend dispatch assumed `.weight` exists on fused projection modules. CompressedTensors wrappers can expose packed weights without a dense `.weight`. 2. Fused module names (`fused_qkv_a_proj_with_mqa`, `gate_up_proj`) were not fully mapped to unfused names for ignore/scheme matching in quantized checkpoints. 3. `kv_b_proj` post-load path did not dequantize CT WNA16 packed tensors for MLA `w_kc`/`w_vc` generation. 4. Shared-experts fusion could be enabled even when shared experts are explicitly marked ignored/non-quantized in checkpoint config, causing bad weight routing. 5. `glm4_moe_lite` was missing from TF>=5 model checks, causing wrong downgrade guidance. ## Changes - Add robust `.weight` guards in MLA path selection and init: - `python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_v2.py` - `python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_common/attention_backend_handler.py` - Add CT WNA16 dequant helper and use it for `kv_b_proj` post-load processing: - `python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_common/deepseek_weight_loader.py` - Add packed fused-module mapping for ignore/scheme compatibility: - `python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_v2.py` - `python/sglang/srt/models/glm4_moe_lite.py` - `python/sglang/srt/models/glm4_moe.py` - Disable shared-experts fusion when checkpoint marks shared experts ignored/non-quantized: - `python/sglang/srt/models/glm4_moe_lite.py` - `python/sglang/srt/models/glm4_moe.py` - Handle GLM q_a/kv_a fused `weight_shape` metadata correctly for CT fusion path: - `python/sglang/srt/models/glm4_moe_lite.py` - Treat `glm4_moe_lite` as TF>=5-required architecture in version verification: - `python/sglang/srt/configs/model_config.py` ## Validation ### Unit tests Added targeted tests and verified all pass: ``` 12 passed ``` New tests: - `test/registered/core/test_model_config_transformers_version.py` - `test/registered/core/test_deepseek_attention_backend_handler.py` - `test/registered/core/test_deepseek_weight_loader.py` - `test/registered/core/test_deepseek_packed_modules_mapping.py` - `test/registered/core/test_glm4_moe_lite_shared_experts_fusion.py` - `test/registered/core/test_glm4_moe_shared_experts_fusion.py` ### Runtime validation (single-node, 2x3090) - REAP model now boots successfully on SGLang (port 8088). - Confirmed runtime log includes: - `Using CompressedTensorsWNA16MarlinMoEMethod` - shared-experts fusion auto-disabled due to ignored shared experts - Actual inference works and returns correct answers (not blank/repeating output after fix). - Compared against AWQ baseline server (port 8089), both produce valid outputs with expected latency/throughput range. ## Notes - For OpenAI chat endpoint with `reasoning_parser=glm45`, responses can go to `reasoning_content` by default. Validation used `chat_template_kwargs.enable_thinking=false` when comparing final answer content.

Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation <!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. --> As described in #19386 , with this pr, sub-batch preparation is not coupled with TBO, and multiple sub-batches (>2) are possible. ## Modifications <!-- Detail the changes made in this pull request. --> (1) use "xbo" instead of "tbo" as prefix of related variables, e.g., rename `tbo_children` to `xbo_children` (2) replace `split_seq_index: int` to `split_seq_indices: list[int]` These will not break TBO, and provide better compatibility for multi-microbatch overlap scenarios. For example, only index splitting algorithm and execution strategy are needed for a 3-batch overlap method implementation. Ideally, the batch preparation framework could also be reused like `CudaGraphRunnerPlugin`, `DPAttentionPreparer`. But to achieve this, more TBO codes need to be refactored. signals.title: [AMD] Port tree speculative sampling kernel to HIP
signals.text: ## Motivation Tree speculative sampling (used by EAGLE and n-gram speculative decoding) currently relies on FlashInfer's CUDA implementation, which is unavailable on ROCm. This means speculative decoding is silently disabled on AMD GPUs -- `TREE_SPEC_KERNEL_AVAILABLE` was hardcoded to `_is_cuda` only. This PR adds a standalone HIP kernel so that speculative decoding works on MI300X. ## Modifications The core change is a new file `sgl-kernel/csrc/speculative/speculative_sampling_hip.cu` containing a HIP-native implementation of `TreeSpecSamplingTargetOnlyKernel`. The kernel is written from scratch against `hipcub` rather than trying to port FlashInfer's CUB-based implementation, since FlashInfer itself has no HIP support. The algorithm is identical to the CUDA path: 1. Tree traversal with threshold-based accept/reject (same branching logic and threshold parameters as the CUDA kernel). 2. Final-token sampling via CDF inversion over `relu(target_probs - draft_probs)`, using `hipcub::BlockReduce` for the normalization sum and `hipcub::BlockScan` for the inclusive prefix sum. `atomicMin` on shared memory resolves the sampled index when multiple threads cross the threshold simultaneously. The shared memory layout uses a union of `BlockReduce::TempStorage` and `BlockScan::TempStorage` (same pattern as FlashInfer's kernel) to keep shared memory usage minimal. On the Python side, `spec_utils.py` now sets `TREE_SPEC_KERNEL_AVAILABLE = _is_cuda or _is_hip`, and provides PyTorch fallback implementations of `top_k_renorm_prob` and `top_p_renorm_prob` for HIP (these are normally FlashInfer functions that don't exist on ROCm). The fallbacks are simple -- `torch.topk` + mask + renormalize for top-k, and `torch.sort` + cumsum + mask for top-p. They're correct but not performance-critical since they run once per verification step on a (batch_size, vocab_size) tensor. The conditional imports in `eagle_info.py`, `eagle_info_v2.py`, and `ngram_info.py` now have an `elif is_hip()` branch that pulls `tree_speculative_sampling_target_only` from `sgl_kernel` and aliases the fallback renormalization functions. The CUDA path is untouched. Build system changes: added the new `.cu` file to `setup_rocm.py`'s source list and registered the op in `common_extension_rocm.cc` with the same `m.def`/`m.impl` signature as the CUDA registration. Unit tests in `test/registered/spec/utils/test_tree_speculative_sampling.py` cover the kernel with threshold=(1,1) and threshold=(0,0) cases, plus the `top_k_renorm_prob_fallback` and `top_p_renorm_prob_fallback` with both scalar and per-batch tensor inputs. Registered for both CUDA and AMD CI, following the same pattern as `test_build_eagle_tree.py`. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

signals.text: ## Motivation Migrate `moe_sum` kernel to JIT compilation (#17865). ## Modifications Under `python/sglang/jit_kernel/`: - `csrc/moe/moe_sum.cuh` — CUDA kernel (ported from `sgl-kernel/csrc/moe/moe_sum.cu`) - `moe_sum.py` — Python wrapper - `tests/test_moe_sum.py` — Unit tests (JIT vs AOT vs PyTorch) - `benchmark/bench_moe_sum.py` — Benchmark (JIT vs AOT vs PyTorch) And - `python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/gguf.py` — Switch import to JIT ## Accuracy Tests Pass all tests defined in `python/sglang/jit_kernel/tests/test_moe_sum.py` ## Benchmarking and Profiling ``` GPU: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5060 Laptop GPU Driver: 580.126.20 | CUDA: 12.8 | PyTorch: 2.9.1+cu128 Script: python/sglang/jit_kernel/benchmark/bench_moe_sum.py moe-sum-performance (unit: us): M × topk × K JIT AOT PyTorch AOT->JIT 1 × 2 × 512 0.81 0.82 1.62 -1.2% 16 × 4 × 1024 1.15 1.11 1.79 +3.6% 64 × 2 × 4096 4.60 4.61 7.80 -0.2% 64 × 4 × 4096 7.67 8.09 7.92 -5.2% 256 × 3 × 4096 24.02 23.06 29.08 +4.2% 1024 × 2 × 4096 65.33 68.74 104.65 -5.0% 1024 × 4 × 4096 270.00 267.61 287.28 +0.9% ``` JIT and AOT performance are essentially the same. Both are faster than torch.sum for most sizes. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

signals.title: [Diffuser] Fix duplicate is_neox_style check in _apply_rotary_emb
signals.text: ## Motivation Fix https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/19747 In `_apply_rotary_emb()`, line 30 checks `if is_neox_style:` inside an outer `if is_neox_style:` block (line 27). The inner check is always True, making the `else` branch (interleaved splitting via `x[..., ::2]`) dead code. For comparison, the LLM side implementation in `srt/layers/rotary_embedding/utils.py` correctly uses a single `if is_neox_style:` check to decide between chunk and interleaved splitting. ## Modifications Replace `if is_neox_style:` on line 30 with `if not interleaved:`. This makes the interleaved splitting path reachable when `is_neox_style=True` and `interleaved=True` are both passed. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review Process 1.
