signals.title: [AMD] Enable unified-KV HiSparse on ROCm for DeepSeek-V4
signals.text: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation <!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. --> On ROCm, HiSparse currently runs only on the **separate-KV** DeepSeek-V4 path (`SGLANG_HACK_FLASHMLA_BACKEND=triton`, packed FP8 KV layout), enabled by #26639. The **unified-KV** backend (`SGLANG_HACK_FLASHMLA_BACKEND=unified_kv_triton`) — where compressed C4 KV lives in the unified pool's `rows[swa_pages:]` and the HiSparse hot buffer is a bf16 view into that region backed by a linear host cold pool — was blocked by a temporary startup guard. This PR enables unified-KV + HiSparse on ROCm end-to-end, and adds JIT/unit/eval coverage. ## Modifications <!-- Detail the changes made in this pull request. --> - Enable unified-KV HiSparse on ROCm (`hisparse_coordinator.py`, `deepseek_v4_memory_pool.py`, `compressor_v2.py`, `arg_groups/hisparse_hook.py`, `srt/mem_cache/allocator/hisparse.py`): remove the temporary guard that blocked unified_kv_triton + HiSparse, wire the unified C4 device pool / linear host cold pool, and fix the compressed-C4 remap to account for the pre-applied swa_pages offset. - Enable dsv4 paged HiSparse JIT kernel tests on ROCm (`test/registered/kernels/ops/kvcache/test_hisparse.py`). - Honor the C4 shrink factor on the unified path (`deepseek_v4_memory_pool.py`, `mem_cache/allocator/hisparse.py`): upstream `pool_configurator` already folds `host_to_device_ratio = S` into `bytes_per_full_token` as a `1/(4S)` C4 term and raises `max_total_num_tokens` accordingly, but the unified pool ignored it. This sizes the on-device C4 region to the shrunk budget via `c4_compress_pages`, and stops `available_size()` / `full_available_size()` from clamping capacity to the device C4 pool — on the unified path the cold remainder is host-resident, so the bound is the logical full-token pool. Net effect: freed VRAM actually reaches `full_token`. Separate-KV / CUDA behaviour is unchanged. - Unit tests for the unified-KV HiSparse pool (`test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_hisparse_unified_pool.py`): host-mirror geometry, view aliasing of the unified compressed region, c4-only layer views, alloc/free mapping, oversubscribe and that c4_compress_pages actually shrinks the device C4 region while the c128 layers are untouched. - Eval tests (`.../mi35x/..._unified_eval_mi35x.py` and `..._unified_dp_eval_mi35x.py`): GSM8K accuracy + a ~19k-token long-context swap-path retrieval test, on TP8 and on TP8+DP-attention. **Highlight — the NVIDIA CUDA forward path is unchanged.** All modifications are confined to ROCm-only branches: `_is_hip` guards and HiSparse/unified-KV-gated code. (The JIT test change only removes `skipif(is_hip())` markers, so those tests now also run on ROCm; CUDA behavior is unaffected.) To enable this feature, you can pass e.g. ``` --enable-hisparse \ --hisparse-config '{"top_k": 1024, "device_buffer_size": 2048, "host_to_device_ratio": 4}' ``` in the server launch configs. ## Accuracy Tests <!-- If this pull request affects model outputs (e.g., changes to the kernel or model forward code), provide accuracy test results. --> GSM8K few-shot accuracy alone does **not** validate the host↔device swap path. With `device_buffer_size=2048` (compressed-token budget) and GSM8K prompts of ~1k–1.7k tokens (~250–425 compressed after the 4x C4 ratio), every request stays on the fast path (`host_len <= device_buffer_size` → preloaded to the device hot buffer), so decode is all device-resident hits and the **cold→hot swap-in (miss-copy) kernel is never exercised**. GSM8K therefore validates: sparse top-k selection numerics, unified-KV pool wiring/aliasing, the compressor write path, and HIP-graph decode stability — but **not** swap correctness. **Note:** a nonzero #cpu token in the decode log during GSM8K is the authoritative host backup of compressed C4 (every request is backed up to host), not decode-time swap-in. The swap-in (miss-copy) path is gated per-request by `host_len > device_buffer_size`; GSM8K's per-request footprint (~250–425 compressed) stays below `device_buffer_size=2048`, so it runs entirely on the preloaded hot path. Swap correctness is established by, in increasing scope: 1. **JIT kernel tests** (`test/registered/kernels/ops/kvcache/test_hisparse.py`): `test_dsv4_swap_in_reads_paged_host_layout`, `*_miss_copy_layout`, and the LRU/miss cases check the swap-in kernel byte-for-byte against a reference. 2. **End-to-end long-context swap test** (`test_b_long_context_swap`): a ~19k token prompt (~4750 compressed > 2048) forces a host cold pool and a swap-in on every decode step; a passcode buried in the long context can only be retrieved if cold→hot copies land correctly. This is the authoritative end-to-end swap oracle. **Accuracy of record:** The numbers reported here **(TP8 0.953 / TP8 DP8 0.949)** were reproduced locally on `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro`. ## Tests reproduction guidance ### JIT kernel (11 passed) ``` HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 python -m pytest test/registered/kernels/ops/kvcache/test_hisparse.py -v ``` These now also run on ROCm (the `skipif(is_hip())` markers were removed). The swap-in kernel cases (`test_dsv4_swap_in_reads_paged_host_layout`, `*_miss_copy_layout`, LRU/miss) compare the host→device cold-copy byte-for-byte against a reference, so a pass proves the swap-in kernel is numerically correct. ### unit test (6 passed) ``` HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 python -m pytest test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_hisparse_unified_pool.py -v ``` Validates the unified-KV pool: host-mirror geometry, the bf16 view aliasing into `rows[swa_pages:]`, C4-only layer views, alloc/free index mapping, and oversubscribe handling. ### e2e test (2 passed each) ``` python -m pytest -s -v test/registered/amd/accuracy/mi35x/test_deepseek_v4_pro_fp4_hisparse_unified_eval_mi35x.py python -m pytest -s -v test/registered/amd/accuracy/mi35x/test_deepseek_v4_pro_fp4_hisparse_unified_dp_eval_mi35x.py ``` Each file runs two methods. **What proves the feature is live:** **(a) Server startup** — the unified-KV HiSparse host cold pool is allocated, and the config is applied: ```text ... enable_hisparse=True, hisparse_config='{"top_k": 1024, "device_buffer_size": 2048, "host_to_device_ratio": 2}' ... Allocating 31.35 GB host memory for V4 paged pool 'dsv4_hisparse_c4' ... ``` The `dsv4_hisparse_c4` host pool only exists on the HiSparse path; its presence with `unified_kv_triton` confirms the unified hot/cold wiring is taken. **(b) `test_a_gsm8k`** — accuracy / sparse-selection guard. Expect the method to **PASS** with GSM8K accuracy ≈ 0.95 (assertion gate `> 0.91`). **(c) `test_b_long_context_swap`** — the swap-path guard, and the **authoritative evidence that host↔device swap works**. A ~19k-token prompt with a passcode buried at the top is sent; expect the method to **PASS** with the passcode echoed back: ```text long_context_swap completion='7G-ZULU-4419' ``` The corresponding server decode line is the smoking gun — a single long request whose compressed C4 footprint far exceeds `device_buffer_size=2048`: ```text Decode batch, #running-req: 1,, ..., #gpu token: 2049, gpu token usage: 0.00, #cpu token: 9566, cpu token usage: 0.01, cuda graph: True, ... ``` - `#gpu token: 2049` ≈ `device_buffer_size` (2048) → the device hot buffer is capped at the configured budget. - `#cpu token: 9566` (> 0) → the remaining cold C4 tokens live in the host pool and are streamed in on every decode step. - The passcode can only be retrieved if those cold→hot swap-ins land correctly, so a PASS proves end-to-end swap correctness (the DP file shows the same behavior under `--dp 8 --enable-dp-attention`). ## Speed Tests and Profiling <!-- If this pull request impacts inference speed, provide benchmarking and profiling results. --> This is a **capacity** feature, not a latency one, and it is worth being explicit about the trade rather than reporting a throughput number that misses the point. `host_to_device_ratio = S` shrinks the GPU-resident C4 region to `1/S` of the budget and mirrors the remainder on the host. Upstream `_get_bytes_per_full_token` already carries the resulting `1/(4S)` C4 term, so the freed VRAM shows up directly as a larger `max_total_num_tokens`. #32368 measures 12.90M → 17.56M (+36%) on the same 1P1D topology. The cost is decode-step latency: the swap-in runs on the main stream between the indexer and attention of every C4 layer. It is latency/occupancy-bound, not bandwidth-bound — `LaunchKernel` uses `grid = batch size`, so a per-rank decode batch of ~20 leaves ~9% occupancy on 256 CUs, which is why #32368's `device_buffer_size` sweep (2048 → 16384, ~8x fewer bytes moved) made decode monotonically *worse*. The levers are multi-CTA sharding (#31341) and side-stream overlap (#28523), neither of which is in this PR's scope. When to turn this on: HiSparse trades decode latency for token capacity, so it is a loss whenever the KV working set of your concurrent requests already fits in VRAM — you pay the swap-in cost and get nothing back. It pays off only past the point where the non-HiSparse configuration can no longer admit the load, at which point the comparison is not "slower" but "runs at all". ## CI coverage PR-CI: - `test/registered/kernels/ops/kvcache/test_hisparse.py` (HiSparse JIT kernels; HIP skip removed so it now runs on ROCm) - `test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_hisparse_unified_pool.py` (unified-KV C4 device pool) These give per-PR coverage of the unified-KV + HiSparse pool/kernel paths. Nightly e2e (8-GPU TP8 / TP8 DP8, `nightly=True`): - `nightly-amd-8-gpu-mi35x-deepseek-v4-pro-hisparse-unified` - `nightly-amd-8-gpu-mi35x-deepseek-v4-pro-hisparse-unified-dp` These two suites are registered but **not yet wired into any workflow**, so they do not run on PR or on the nightly schedule yet. Following the precedent of the unified-KV PR #27380, the PR-CI/nightly wiring is tracked in the AMD CI coverage issue #27521 (cc @bingxche @yctseng0211). I will add them to the issue list then. ## Checklist - [✔] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [✔] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [✔] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [✔] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process). 2. signals.title: [FEAT][SpecDecode] Add DP attention support for DFLASH speculative decoding
signals.text: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation DFLASH speculative decoding previously rejected `--enable-dp-attention` at startup. This blocks deployments that combine DFLASH with data-parallel attention (e.g. `--tensor-parallel-size 4 --dp-size 2 --enable-dp-attention`), which is a common setup for large MoE models like GLM-5. EAGLE3 already supports DP attention by running each draft worker inside the attention TP group (`attn_tp_group`). DFLASH should follow the same pattern, but it has additional constraints: it materializes target hidden states directly into the draft KV cache (instead of re-running a draft extend forward), and it performs draft greedy sampling over the target `lm_head`. These paths need explicit alignment with DP/EP padding, CUDA graph capture modes, and full-TP target verify collectives. <!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. --> ## Modifications ### `speculative_hook.py` - Remove the guard that blocked DFLASH + `enable_dp_attention`. - Auto-enable `enable_dp_lm_head` when DFLASH runs with DP attention, so draft greedy sampling's vocab-parallel `all_gather` stays within the attention TP group (matching `lm_head` sharding). Without this, a global-TP `all_gather` mixes tokens across DP groups and deadlocks when a peer DP group is IDLE. ### `dflash_worker_v2.py` **Draft worker initialization (mirrors EAGLE3 + dp_attention)** - Disable `dp_attention` on the draft server args (draft is dense; keeps KV row count aligned with `out_cache_loc`). - Create the draft worker inside `draft_tp_context(get_attention_tp_group())` so KV head partitioning matches `token_to_kv_pool.row_dim` (both use `attn_tp_size`). - Wrap draft `init_attention_backends`, `init_cuda_graphs`, and runtime draft forward + greedy sampling in `draft_tp_context`. **Prefill / extend path** - Early-return for non-extend DP ranks when `is_extend_in_batch=True` is broadcast globally but the local rank is IDLE/DECODE (avoids missing `extend_lens` / `prefix_lens`). - Trim trailing EP padding rows from target `hidden_states` before writing into draft KV when `moe_ep_size > 1` (fixes `cache_loc` vs `target_hidden` length mismatch on non-aligned token counts). **Decode path** - IDLE DP ranks participate in target verify (full-TP collective) with `capture_hidden_mode=FULL` to match active ranks. A `NULL` mode mismatch triggers a CUDA graph recapture whose internal barrier active ranks never enter, causing deadlock. - Move `_greedy_sample_from_vocab_parallel_head` inside `draft_tp_context` so its `all_gather` uses the attention TP group. <!-- Detail the changes made in this pull request. --> ## Test ### Environment * GPU: H100 * 4 * Model: `Qwen3.5-35B-A3B` * Draft model: `Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-DFlash` * Dataset: `human-eval` ### Launch Command ```bash CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1,2,3 python -m sglang.launch_server \ --served-model-name qwen35-dflash-dp \ --model-path /models/Qwen/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B/ \ --port 30001 \ --host 0.0.0.0 \ --trust-remote-code \ --tensor-parallel-size 4 \ --dp-size 2 \ --ep-size 4 \ --enable-dp-attention \ --page-size 64 \ --mem-fraction-static 0.85 \ --speculative-algorithm DFLASH \ --speculative-draft-model-path /aicp-models/z-lab/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-DFlash/ \ --speculative-num-draft-tokens 7 ``` ### Results | case_id | batch | num_prompts | output_throughput | mean_TPOT | | -------------------------------------- | ----: | ----------: | ----------------: | --------: | | `30ab57f3-7369-11f1-b936-62ed488933d3` | 4 | 16 | 507.83 | 6.82 | | `30ab57f3-7369-11f1-b936-62ed488933d3` | 16 | 48 | 1138.79 | 10.43 | | `30ab57f3-7369-11f1-b936-62ed488933d3` | 32 | 96 | 1385.22 | 15.41 | | `30ab57f3-7369-11f1-b936-62ed488933d3` | 48 | 144 | 1651.44 | 22.54 | | `f5bd91a4-7366-11f1-8ef7-62ed488933d3` | 4 | 16 | 690.96 | 3.74 | | `f5bd91a4-7366-11f1-8ef7-62ed488933d3` | 16 | 48 | 1246.92 | 9.21 | | `f5bd91a4-7366-11f1-8ef7-62ed488933d3` | 32 | 96 | 1615.66 | 14.74 | | `f5bd91a4-7366-11f1-8ef7-62ed488933d3` | 48 | 144 | 2681.93 | 11.54 | ### Acceptance Test | Config | dp_rank | accept_length | | --------------- | ------: | ------------: | | TP4 DP2 | 0 | 4.5927 | | TP4 DP2 | 1 | 4.7341 | | TP4 DP2 average | - signals.title: fix(mem_cache): emit BlockRemoved on session radix cache release
signals.text: ## Problem `RadixCache.release_radix_session` (the path that runs when a session is closed under `--enable-session-radix-cache`) frees KV blocks and deletes radix leaves, but — unlike the regular eviction path — it never emits `BlockRemoved` events. The regular `evict` path emits one `BlockRemoved` per freed node: ```python # python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/radix_cache.py, RadixCache.evict self.token_to_kv_pool_allocator.free(x.value) ... self._delete_leaf(x) ... self._record_remove_event(x) # <-- emits BlockRemoved ``` but `release_radix_session` only did the `free` + `_delete_leaf`, skipping the event: ```python # python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/session_radix_cache.py parent = node.parent self.token_to_kv_pool_allocator.free(node.value) self._delete_leaf(node) # (no _record_remove_event — BlockRemoved never emitted) freed += 1 ``` As a result, KV-aware routers consuming the event queue (e.g. dynamo) keep stale entries for blocks that a session release has already freed, so they may route future requests to freed/invalid KV. ## Fix Mirror the eviction path: call `self._record_remove_event(node)` for each freed node. `_record_remove_event` is a no-op when `enable_kv_cache_events` is false (guarded inside `KVCacheEventMixin`), so configurations that don't enable KV cache events are completely unaffected. Only `RadixCache` (and its subclass `HiRadixCache`) use `SessionRadixCacheMixin`, and both already inherit `KVCacheEventMixin`, so the call is always available. ## Tests New registered CPU unit test `test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_session_radix_blockremoved_event.py` (no server, no GPU): - `test_release_emits_blockremoved_for_freed_node` — single-session release emits one `BlockRemoved` per freed node. - `test_shared_prefix_emits_only_for_unique_tail` — two sessions sharing a prefix; releasing one emits a `BlockRemoved` only for the freed tail, the shared prefix (still held) is untouched. - `test_release_with_last_holder_frees_shared_leaf` — same content held by two sessions is freed (and emits) only on the last close. - `test_events_disabled_release_is_noop_for_queue` — with `enable_kv_cache_events=False`, release still works and the queue stays empty. All 4 tests fail on `main` (no `BlockRemoved` emitted) and pass with this fix. The existing `test/manual/core/test_session_radix_cache.py` (8 tests, asserts the freeing/shared-prefix/last-holder semantics) still passes — the fix adds event emission without changing what gets freed. ## Checklist - [x] Code is tested with CPU unit tests (no GPU required) - [x] `black`, `isort`, `codespell`, `ruff (F401/F821/UP037)` clean - [x] No behavioral change to what `release_radix_session` frees — only adds the previously-missing event <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: **Missing `run-ci` label** -- add it to run CI tests.<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: **Blocked** -- `run-ci` is required first.<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:heavy_minus_sign: **No AMD PR run found for this commit**.<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [AMD][Spec] Fix aiter GQA packing + split-KV routing in NEXTN spec attention (verify & draft_extend)
signals.text: ## Motivation On ROCm/gfx950 with the `aiter` attention backend, NEXTN speculative decoding for GQA MoE models **loses to non-spec past ~40K context** and degrades further as context grows — even though `accept_length` stays healthy (~2.4–3.4). Profiling (torch trace) shows no scheduling bubble (GPU 95–99% busy); the only thing that scales badly with context is attention. Root cause is two independent kernel-routing pathologies in the aiter backend: | Phase | Symptom | Mechanism | |---|---|---| | `target_verify` | verify decode-attn 14→587 ms (42×) at long ctx; trace signature `num_query_heads_16 / num_queries_per_kv_1` | **GQA amortization loss.** K/V for one local KV head was `.expand()`-ed to `tp_q_head_num`, so `unified_attention` computed `num_queries_per_kv = num_query_heads // num_kv_heads = 1` → full MHA tiling (~7× KV traffic). | | `draft_extend` (EAGLE-v2 KV catch-up) | ~773 ms residual @88K after the verify fix | **Occupancy starvation.** It fell through to `mha_batch_prefill_func` (prefill FMHA, no split-KV). Short Q (accepted tokens) → ~1 Q-tile → ~0.2% HBM BW, ~400× over the memory floor. | Fixing both makes spec decoding **win 1.35–1.76× across 1.4K–88K context** (crossover eliminated). ## Modifications - **verify** (`aiter_backend.py`): drop the stride-0 `.expand()` in the unified `target_verify` path; pass the true single KV head (exactly like `forward_decode`) so `unified_attention` derives `num_queries_per_kv = tp_q_head_num` and packs all Q heads against one KV load. `num_queries_per_kv` is the GQA group, not queries-per-tile. Rides the existing `SGLANG_AITER_UNIFIED_VERIFY`. - **draft_extend** (`aiter_backend.py`): route `draft_extend_v2` through `unified_attention` (GQA-packed **and** split-KV — the same kernel `target_verify` uses), with a 2D `block_table` built from the spec metadata and `seqused_k` from `kv_indptr` diffs. Gated behind a new `SGLANG_AITER_UNIFIED_DRAFT_EXTEND` (`EnvBool(True)` in `environ.py`), independent of the verify flag so it can be bisected/disabled alone. - **test** (`test/manual/test_aiter_unified_draft_extend_env.py`): guards the new flag's registration and default. Files: `python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/aiter_backend.py`, `python/sglang/srt/environ.py`, `test/manual/test_aiter_unified_draft_extend_env.py`. Split into 2 commits (verify fix; draft_extend fix + env flag + test). ## Accuracy Tests Vehicle: `amd/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-MoE-MXFP4` (GQA 32 q : 2 kv, head_dim 256), 2× MI350X/gfx950, ROCm 7.2.4, TP=2, `--attention-backend aiter`, NEXTN/EAGLE spec (num-steps 3, eagle-topk 1, draft-tokens 4). Server launch (all-fixes; MXFP4 spec shown — for FP8 use `--model-path Qwen/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8`, for no-spec drop the `--speculative-*` flags): ```bash SGLANG_USE_AITER=1 SGLANG_USE_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN=1 \ SGLANG_AITER_UNIFIED_VERIFY=1 SGLANG_AITER_UNIFIED_DRAFT_EXTEND=1 \ python -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path amd/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-MoE-MXFP4 --trust-remote-code \ --tp-size 2 --attention-backend aiter --linear-attn-backend triton \ --speculative-algorithm EAGLE --speculative-num-steps 3 \ --speculative-eagle-topk 1 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4 \ --page-size 64 --mem-fraction-static 0.95 \ --max-running-requests 40 --disable-radix-cache \ --host 127.0.0.1 --port 30000 ``` `SGLANG_AITER_UNIFIED_VERIFY` gates FIX 1, `SGLANG_AITER_UNIFIED_DRAFT_EXTEND` gates FIX 2 (both default on — set either to `0` to A/B). `--disable-radix-cache` sidesteps an unrelated pre-existing crash in the mamba radix cache eviction under concurrent distinct-prompt load, and is not required by the fixes. - **verify fix** changes tiling only, not the math → output identical, `accept_length` unchanged. - **draft_extend fix**: - conc-1 logit-diff of the old (FMHA) vs new (unified) draft_extend kernel = **0.000e+00** (bit-identical). - controlled accept A/B on identical inputs → **no regression** (new ≥ old). - stress: conc=8, heterogeneous 2K–61K ctx, CUDA-graph replay → clean, 0 crash/NaN/truncation, batched `accept 2.73`, coherent outputs. - Spec is lossless by construction: the target verify (identical in both arms) guarantees output = target-greedy regardless of the draft. - **gsm8k (end-to-end, spec-on, 512 questions, temp 0, max_tokens 8192):** **0.971**, **0% invalid** — the fixed spec pipeline produces correct answers; a broken verify/draft path would collapse this. - Note: batched temp-0 decode is nondeterministic run-to-run on this stack (batch composition varies FP-reduction order → argmax flips), so an exact output-hash A/B is not a valid batch>1 correctness gate — the signals above are. The kernel path requires ROCm/gfx950, so it is not exercised by the CPU unit test; the above is the accuracy evidence. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Same vehicle as above. | Metric | Before | After | |---|---|---| | verify attn (long ctx @88k) | 272 ms | 104 ms (2.6×) | | draft_extend attn @88K | ~773 ms | ~5 ms | | TPOT @88K | 13.8 ms | 6.8 ms | | spec vs non-spec, 1.4K–88K | loses past ~40K | **wins 1.35–1.76×** | - verify: trace `num_queries_per_kv` restored 1 → 16 (GQA group), killing the ~7× KV-traffic amplification. - draft_extend: `unified_attention`'s split-KV (`num_segments`) restores occupancy at short Q, moving the kernel from ~0.2% HBM BW to near the memory floor. - Residual after both fixes is the verify-MoE ceiling (unified-attn 417 ms + MoE GEMM 559 ms), not the draft path. ### High-batch: spec vs no-spec, both weight quants (all-fixes, ~1.7K ctx, 256 out tok, mem-frac 0.95) The fixes are in the attention path, independent of MoE weight quantization — confirmed by measuring both MXFP4 and FP8. Spec stays a net win through moderate batch on both (per-token TPOT, p50 ms): | conc | MXFP4 spec / nospec | speedup | FP8 spec / nospec | speedup | |---|---|---|---|---| | 4 | 6.5 / 9.6 | **1.48×** | 6.5 / 10.3 | **1.58×** | | 8 | 7.7 / 11.4 | **1.48×** | 8.3 / 11.9 | **1.43×** | | 16 | 10.3 / 13.8 | **1.34×** | 10.8 / 14.8 | **1.37×** | Spec wins 1.34–1.58× per token across conc 4–16 on both quants; FP8 benefits slightly more (its no-spec decode baseline is slower, so removing forward passes helps more). The win narrows with batch — textbook spec-decode behavior. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). (black 26.1.0, isort 7.0.0 `profile=black`, ruff 0.15.1 — all clean) - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). (`test/manual/test_aiter_unified_draft_extend_env.py`; kernel path needs gfx950, see Accuracy/Speed above) - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). (N/A — expert env flag, documented inline in `environ.py`) - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32463656503](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32463656503)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32463656506](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32463656506)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32463656517](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32463656517)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [AMD]DSV4 Fix KV pool sizing for the unified_kv backend
signals.text: ## Motivation The DSV4 `unified_kv` backend has a different physical KV layout than the fp8 path, but `DSV4PoolConfigurator` sized both identically. Under `unified_kv` this over-allocates memory (and can OOM), because: - KV is stored in **bf16 over the full latent** (`attn_head_dim * 2` bytes), not the fp8(nope) + bf16(rope) + scale 584-byte cell. - SWA and the c4/c128 compress-states are **fixed per-request rings** (`num_req_slots * ring_size`), independent of `full_token`, so they must be fixed biases rather than per-token terms. ## Modifications All changes are gated on the same `is_unified_kv_triton()` / `_unified_kv` switch the pool itself uses, so sizing and allocation cannot drift apart. **No behavior change on the non-unified (fp8) path.** ### Pool sizing (`pool_configurator.py`) - Use bf16 full-latent bytes for the per-token coeff on the unified path (`_get_bytes_per_full_token`). - Exclude SWA from the per-token coeff and account for it as a fixed bias (`_fixed_swa_bytes`), inflated for the speculative draft worker the same way as the coeff. - Move the **c4 compress-state (attn + indexer)** off the per-token coeff and size it as a request-scoped fixed bias (`_fixed_c4_state_bytes` / `_unified_c4_state_pool_size`), finalized once `max_running_requests` is known — mirroring the c128 state pool. Subtract it from the token budget and log `c4_state_fixed`. - Factor the `max_running_requests`-per-worker resolution into a shared helper (`_resolve_max_running_requests_per_worker`) reused by the c128 state, SWA ring, and c4 state fixed-byte terms. - Log the SWA ring and c4-state fixed biases alongside the existing c128 fixed bias. ### Memory pool (`deepseek_v4_memory_pool.py`) - Clamp `c4_state_pool_size` up to `num_req_slots * c4_ring_size` as a safety net (mirrors the c128 clamp). ### SWA idle accounting on the unified ring - `model_runner`: reconcile `swa_max_total_num_tokens` down to the allocator ring capacity (`swa_available_size`) so the idle pool-leak invariant matches the fixed per-request SWA ring (gated on unified_kv; no real buffer is resized). - `invariant_checker`: skip the SWA token-pool leak invariant on the unified ring — its `available` is non-binding and cached radix prefixes report a spurious `swa_evictable`, so `available + evictable + protected == total` does not hold; ring slots are still covered by the `req_to_token` leak check. - `pool_stats_observer`: zero `swa_evictable` on the unified ring so `swa_num_used` / `swa_token_usage` stay coherent (cached prefixes hold no ring slot). ### Review-fix follow-ups - Detect unified-KV via the canonical `get_kvcache()._unified_kv` (the previous `getattr(alloc, "_unified", ...)` was always `False` on the wrapped allocators — thanks @amd-danli103). Applied consistently in `invariant_checker`, `pool_stats_observer`, and `schedule_batch`. - Unwrap `logical_attn_allocator` in the `_check_kv_page_invariants` sub-allocator probe so the DSV4-HiSparse wrapper reaches its inner full/swa allocators. - `schedule_policy`: align the `add_one_req` SWA admission gate (`>=` -> `>`) with `add_one_req_ignore_eos` so an exact-fit request is admitted. ## Accuracy / Validation Validated on **DeepSeek-V4-Pro, `unified_kv` + EAGLE MTP (speculative), TP8 / DP8, ROCm**. <details> <summary>Server launch command</summary> ```bash export SGLANG_DEFAULT_THINKING=1 export SGLANG_DSV4_REASONING_EFFORT=max export SGLANG_OPT_DEEPGEMM_HC_PRENORM=false export SGLANG_USE_AITER=1 export SGLANG_USE_ROCM700A=1 export SGLANG_OPT_USE_FUSED_COMPRESS=true export SGLANG_HACK_FLASHMLA_BACKEND=unified_kv_triton export SGLANG_OPT_FP8_WO_A_GEMM=false export SGLANG_OPT_USE_JIT_INDEXER_METADATA=false export SGLANG_OPT_USE_TOPK_V2=false export SGLANG_OPT_USE_AITER_INDEXER=true export SGLANG_OPT_USE_TILELANG_INDEXER=false export SGLANG_OPT_USE_TILELANG_MHC_PRE=false export SGLANG_OPT_USE_TILELANG_MHC_POST=false export SGLANG_FP8_PAGED_MQA_LOGITS_TORCH=1 export SGLANG_OPT_USE_FUSED_COMPRESS_TRITON=true export SGLANG_OPT_USE_MULTI_STREAM_OVERLAP=false export SGLANG_ROCM_USE_MULTI_STREAM=false export AITER_BF16_FP8_MOE_BOUND=0 export SGLANG_OPT_FP4_MOE_K_ALIGN=128 export SGLANG_DSV4_INDEXER_K_CACHE_PRESHUFFLE=1 export SGLANG_EAGER_INPUT_NO_COPY=false signals.title: [Intel][XPU][LoRA] Enable LoRA on Intel XPU
signals.text: Enable the LoRA functionality on XPU (in addition to CUDA/ROCm), and enable the corresponding unit tests. Source changes: - backends (triton/chunked/torch): use torch.device(self.device) instead of a hard-coded "cuda". - lora_moe_runners: route XPU to the pure-torch _naive_moe_lora_align_block_size fallback. - rotary_embedding base.py / mrope.py: guard the XPU-only sgl_kernel imports (fused_qk_rope_with_cos_sin_cache_inplace, multimodal_rotary_embedding). - lora_overlap_loader: use self.device_module.current_stream() instead of torch.cuda.current_stream(). ### Supported and Verified following Features - Core dense LoRA (triton + csgmv backends) - cuda-graph + LoRA - Multi-LoRA - MoE-LoRA - Dynamic Load/ Unload - Pinned Adapters - LoRA with Overlap Loading - LoRA with Radix Cache - LoRA with TP - Eviction (LRU/FIFO) - Embedding with LoRA Test changes: - Device-agnostic device selection via get_device() and register_xpu_ci across the kernel/unit and small-model LoRA tests. <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation - Intel XPU is a first-class inference target: SGLang already supports XPU for base model inference; LoRA fine-tuned models are widely used in production and should be deployable on XPU without requiring a separate code path or falling back to the generic Transformers backbone. - Hard-coded "cuda" strings are silent correctness bugs on XPU: Several hot paths (init_cuda_graph_batch_info, lora_overlap_loader) referenced torch.cuda directly, causing device mismatches or runtime errors when the active device is an Intel XPU, even though the surrounding logic was otherwise device-agnostic. - CI coverage prevents regressions across backends: Without device-agnostic test infrastructure (get_device(), register_xpu_ci, ROUGE-L tolerance on XPU), XPU-specific breakage in LoRA paths would go undetected until a user report, making the XPU support effectively untested and unreliable. ## Modifications - Wrote a combined feature-level LoRA test suite validating Dynamic Load/Unload, Pinned Adapters, Radix Cache with LoRA, Embedding with LoRA, Multi-LoRA, and MoE-LoRA both individually and in combination across all three attention backends (csgmv, triton, and torch-native) to catch feature interaction bugs across devices and backend configurations - Replaced torch.cuda.current_stream() with self.device_module.current_stream() in lora_overlap_loader to prevent runtime errors on XPU using the existing device module abstraction - Added get_device() helper and register_xpu_ci for device-agnostic device selection across kernel and unit tests so the same test suite runs on both CUDA and XPU ## Accuracy Tests ## Speed Tests and Profiling <!-- If this pull request impacts inference speed, provide benchmarking and profiling results. --> ## Checklist - signals.title: [Feature] Add MiniCPM-SALA support
signals.text: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation Add native serving support for MiniCPM-SALA checkpoints, which interleave MiniCPM sparse softmax-attention layers with constant-decay Lightning linear-attention layers. The implementation integrates the model with SGLang's existing attention, linear-attention, CUDA graph, and memory-pool infrastructure. It also replaces the serving-time dependency on the original out-of-tree block-table extension with SGLang JIT kernels. ## Modifications - Add `MiniCPMHybridConfig` and register both `MiniCPMForCausalLM` and `MiniCPMSALAForCausalLM`. - Normalize mixer aliases and repeat mixer patterns to the configured layer count. - Parse both flattened and legacy nested sparse-attention configuration. - Describe Lightning state using the existing `Mamba2CacheParams` and linear-attention model registry. - Extend the MiniCPM model with SALA mixer support. - Add Lightning QKV projection, optional Q/K normalization, RoPE, output normalization and gating, configurable attention scaling, and checkpoint-compatible weight loading. - Reuse the in-tree Lightning backend and `seg_la` kernels instead of introducing a model-specific linear-attention backend or external dependency. - Generalize the shared Lightning backend to read the linear KV-head count, layerwise decay mode, and per-layer attention scale from the model config. - Add `minicpm_flashattn` and `minicpm_flashinfer` sparse-attention backends. - Compose with `FlashAttentionBackend` for dense metadata and CUDA graph state. - Keep FlashInfer support as a composed decode path rather than duplicating its wrapper management. - Select FA4 automatically on supported Blackwell GPUs. - Support dense/sparse prefill and decode, CUDA graph capture/replay, K1/K2 key compression, sparse top-k selection, and optional fused TileLang kernels. - Add JIT-compiled CUDA block-table kernels. - Use v2 for prefill and v3 for the optimized decode layout, with automatic v2 fallback for unsupported v3 shapes. - Cache compiled modules by top-k, head-group count, and block size. - Attach the MiniCPM compressed cache to the existing `ReqToTokenPool`. - Reserve and account for K1/K2 capacity without introducing a model-specific pool subclass. - Route extend/decode allocation, rollback, request release, streaming-session cleanup, allocator reset, and pool statistics through generic no-op auxiliary-cache hooks. - Add MiniCPM model overrides and developer controls. - Default sparse SALA models to `minicpm_flashattn`, or `minicpm_flashinfer` on supported Blackwell GPUs. - Disable radix caching only for configs that actually contain sparse or Lightning layers. - Reject unsupported sparse-attention PD disaggregation early. - Add `SGLANG_MINICPM_FUSE_TOPK`, `SGLANG_MINICPM_SPLIT_STAGE1`, `SGLANG_MINICPM_DENSE_AS_SPARSE`, and `SGLANG_MINICPM_FORCE_DENSE` environment switches. - Add CPU and CUDA coverage for configuration defaults, model overrides, Lightning dispatch, compressed-cache lifecycle, sparse metadata, block-table kernels, and compression kernels. ## Accuracy Tests The following CPU regression suite passes on the final rebased branch: ```text 112 passed, 8 subtests passed ``` It covers: - MiniCPM config parsing, mixer selection, Lightning cache shape, scaling, and idle batches. - Sparse metadata construction, CUDA graph padding, and dense/sparse batch accounting. - K1/K2 allocation boundaries, reuse, rollback, cleanup, and streaming-session release. - Backend defaults, force-dense remapping, radix-cache gating, and unsupported PD disaggregation. CUDA correctness tests are included for: - v2/v3 block-table outputs against a PyTorch reference. - Sparse key compression against a PyTorch reference. End-to-end checkpoint output accuracy has not yet been recorded on the final rebased branch and should be added before merge. ## Speed Tests and Profiling `test/registered/kernels/benchmark/bench_get_block_table.py` benchmarks the v2 prefill and v3 decode block-table kernels across token counts. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. signals.title: [Refactor] New EPD
signals.text: ## Motivation The EPD encoder had grown into a single 4464-line `python/sglang/srt/disaggregation/encode_server.py` that owned the FastAPI application, the DP launcher, the request scheduler, CPU preprocessing, the GPU forward, and both transfer backends at the same time. That coupling caused three concrete problems: **1. Duplicated orchestration.** HTTP non-DP and DP workers each maintained their own copy of encode scheduling, batch/direct branching, backend detection, metadata publication, embedding staging, send scheduling, error handling, resource release and metrics updates. On top of that: - single-request and batch encode had two separate implementations; - Mooncake, ZMQ-to-scheduler and ZMQ-to-tokenizer each carried near-identical send logic; - `send` and `release` were tightly coupled, and embedding cleanup was scattered across the normal, error and timeout branches. **2. Unsafe resource lifetimes.** Because `send` implicitly released embeddings and cleanup lived in several places, concurrent encode / send / release had no ordering guarantee: a release racing an in-flight forward could tear down state that a pending send still needed, and a failed encode could leave a `send` waiting forever. **3. No layer to build on.** There was no protocol-neutral home for scheduling, so gRPC could not reuse the HTTP backend topology, and neither the CPU preprocessing nor the HTTP layer could be replaced by a Rust implementation. This PR restructures the encoder into a package with explicit layers and unifies everything after `receive` into a single pipeline, while keeping the external HTTP/gRPC surface unchanged. ## Modifications ## 2. One inference lifecycle for every path Everything after `receive` now follows a single chain, identically for HTTP non-DP and for DP workers: ``` receive (protocol-specific entry point) → execute_encode_pipeline → MMEncoder.encode / batch_encode → acquire encode ref → preprocess → publish metadata → model forward → stage embedding → release encode ref → delivery.send → release_request ``` - `encode()` becomes a batch-of-one call into `batch_encode()`, so there is no second encode implementation. `EncoderScheduler` only decides *whether* requests coalesce into a batch. - `execute_encode_pipeline()` owns metrics and tracing, direct-vs-batched dispatch, metadata publication, the `MMEncoder` call, final metadata sync, the ZMQ synchronous send or the Mooncake metadata response, and resource release on the normal, error and timeout paths. - `ReqState` holds the whole per-request lifecycle: `embedding_data`, `embedding_ready`, `active_encodes`, `active_sends`, `release_requested`, `preserve_metadata_on_release`, `lifecycle_condition`, driven by `_acquire_encode_ref()` / `_release_encode_ref()`. The resulting guarantees: - a release issued during encode cannot delete request state early; - a release waits until `active_sends == 0`; - once a release is requested, new sends are rejected; - a shared embedding is freed only after all destinations have finished; - a failed encode still stages the error, so a waiting `send` can never block forever. - `EncoderDelivery` isolates the backend differences. The previous `ZmqSchedulerDelivery` and `ZmqTokenizerDelivery` collapse into one `ZmqDelivery` parameterized by `cleanup_receive_state`; `self.transfer_backend` / `self.use_mooncake` are cached on `MMEncoder` instead of re-reading `server_args.encoder_transfer_backend` all over the code. - `embedding_to_send.pop()`, `discard_embedding()`, handler-`finally` cleanup, the Mooncake callback cleanup and the ZMQ rendezvous cleanup all collapse into `release_request()`. - Mooncake marks an embedding ready **only after the CUDA stream is synchronized**, so an RDMA read can no longer observe a GPU buffer whose write has not landed. Global-cache embeddings keep their existing per-send registration semantics. ### 3. Metadata is published right after preprocess Every backend publishes embedding shape, dtype and size as soon as preprocessing completes — before the forward runs. At that point `ReqState.embedding_data` holds a metadata placeholder; the real embedding is staged and validated afterwards, which is what sets `embedding_ready`. For Mooncake non-DP this lets the receiver call `/scheduler_receive_meta_data`, then allocate and register its landing buffer **in parallel with the encoder forward**; the RDMA transfer itself still waits for `embedding_ready`. ZMQ publishes the same metadata today, but has no early consumer yet. ### 4. Preprocessing metadata consolidated `EncoderPreprocessResult` returns `mm_inputs`, `grid_thw` and `token_counts` together. Grid normalization and patch/token counting move out of `MMEncoder` into `EncoderPreprocessor`, so `process_mm_items` parses the grid exactly once and the direct, cache, Mooncake and batch paths reuse the same result. `slice_embedding` and `_encode_missing` no longer recompute token counts from the grid. ### 5. Receiver: one embedding pool for both backends - `EmbeddingPool` absorbs `MooncakeEmbeddingPool` and gains `try_stage` / `release_on_gc`. When `SGLANG_EMBEDDING_POOL_SIZE_MB` is set explicitly, `zmq_to_scheduler` also keeps received embeddings resident in the GPU pool: zero-copy per-modality views, slot lifetime bound to `mm_inputs` garbage collection, and a `PENDING` retry when the pool is full. **Default behaviour is unchanged** — the 4096 MB default still applies to Mooncake only. - RDMA buffer release becomes an ownership transfer to the receiving thread, which removes an up-to-1800 s `join` block on the scheduler main thread. - `WaitingMMRequestBase` (ABC) unifies `recv_embedding`; the backend differences shrink to three abstract methods — `send_encode_request`, `_extract_embedding_from_buffer`, `_prepare_embedding_buffer`. Seven separate failure paths merge into `_fail_and_release`, and the classes are renamed off "Image" into the `Zmq` / `Grpc` / `RDMA` families. - Dead code on the `zmq_to_tokenizer` path is removed. ## EPD performance results ### Common workload - 4 random 1080p JPEG images per request - Random input length 1024, output length 64 - Temperature 0, request rate `inf` - Radix cache and MM global cache disabled - Paired values below are `main/new_epd` ## Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct ### Test setup - One 8×H20 node - Encoder TP1 on GPU 0–1; Language TP1 on GPU 2 - Encoder/Language memory fraction: 0.60 - `single`: client concurrency 1, scheduler max batch 1, 8 requests per round - `batch`: client concurrency 4, scheduler max batch 4, 16 requests per round - Each case used 2 warmup requests followed by 3 measured rounds - Results are the median of the 3 rounds - `zmq_to_scheduler` used a 4096 MB embedding pool ### Results | Encoder DP | Path | Backend | Throughput (req/s) | Median TTFT (ms) | Median TPOT (ms) | |---:|---|---|---:|---:|---:| | 1 | single | Tokenizer | 0.288/0.294 | 3058/2976 | 6.774/6.783 | | 1 | single | Scheduler | 0.293/0.362 | 2990/2331 | 6.786/6.775 | | 1 | single | Mooncake | 0.368/0.403 | 2280/2047 | 6.783/6.778 | | 1 | batch | Tokenizer | 0.447/0.448 | 7095/7076 | 19.498/19.452 | | 1 | batch | Scheduler | 0.436/0.519 | 7476/5945 | 19.439/18.077 | | 1 | batch | Mooncake | 0.525/0.566 | 5860/5352 | 19.421/19.429 | | 2 | single | Tokenizer | 0.282/0.297 | 3122/2934 | 6.780/6.776 | | 2 | single | Scheduler* | 0.334/0.362 | 2556/2343 | 6.777/6.776 | | 2 | single | Mooncake | 0.366/0.402 | 2299/2058 | 6.784/6.779 | | 2 | batch | Tokenizer | 0.488/0.487 | 6369/6367 | 28.541/28.516 | | 2 | batch | Scheduler* | 0.478/0.582 | 6708/5121 | 26.301/27.547 | | 2 | batch | Mooncake | 0.591/0.636 | 4975/4574 | 28.569/26.525 | \* For DP2 Scheduler, main used two independent TP1/DP1 Encoders, while new_epd used one internal TP1/DP2 Encoder. ## Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8 ### Test setup - Two 8×H20 nodes - Language TP8 and Encoder deployed on separate nodes - Encoder/Language memory fraction: 0.70 - `DP4`: one TP1/DP4 Encoder process and one Encoder URL - `4×DP1`: four independent TP1/DP1 Encoders and four Encoder URLs - Concurrency 1: 16 warmup and 16 measured requests - Concurrency 8/32: 32 warmup and 64 measured requests - Results below use the second measured round - Scheduler embedding pool: 4096 MB ### Configurations | Client concurrency / scheduler max batch | Encoder layout | Encoder URLs | |---|---|---:| | 1/1 | DP1 | 1 | | 8/8 | DP4 | 1 | | 8/8 | 4×DP1 | 4 | | 32/8 | DP4 | 1 | | 32/8 | 4×DP1 | 4 | | 32/32 | 4×DP1 | 4 | ### Results | Concurrency / max batch | Layout | Backend | Throughput (req/s) | Median TTFT (ms) | Median TPOT (ms) | |---|---|---|---:|---:|---:| | 1/1 | DP1 | Tokenizer | 0.555/0.532 | 1438/1444 | 5.227/5.521 | | 1/1 | DP1 | Scheduler | 0.536/0.554 | 1470/1388 | 5.287/5.357 | | 1/1 | DP1 | Mooncake | 0.579/0.634 | 1315/1216 | 5.550/5.468 | | 8/8 | DP4 | Tokenizer | 1.487/1.495 | 4179/4183 | 18.838/18.889 | | 8/8 | DP4 | Scheduler | —/1.543 | —/3864 | —/19.014 | | 8/8 | DP4 | Mooncake | —/1.761 | —/3339 | —/19.010 | | 8/8 | 4×DP1 | Tokenizer | 1.568/1.651 | 3398/2815 | 18.652/33.909 | | 8/8 | 4×DP1 | Scheduler | 1.358/1.464 | 4323/4158 | 19.737/19.054 | | 8/8 | 4×DP1 | Mooncake | 1.865/1.910 | 2965/2718 | 20.067/18.725 | | 32/8 | DP4 | Tokenizer | 1.605/1.687 | 12621/11471 | 85.097/97.416 | | 32/8 | DP4 | Scheduler | —/1.585 | —/13857 | —/96.598 | | 32/8 | DP4 | Mooncake | —/2.246 | —/7814 | —/95.164 | | 32/8 | 4×DP1 | Tokenizer | 1.683/1.603 | 11529/12062 | 112.268/122.776 | | 32/8 | 4×DP1 | Scheduler | 1.341/1.389 | 16667/13518 | 108.282/108.752 | | 32/8 | 4×DP1 | Mooncake | 2.126/2.310 | 8433/7584 | 109.113/95.207 | | 32/32 | 4×DP1 | Tokenizer | 1.625/1.656 | 12093/11577 | 96.304/93.734 | | 32/32 | 4×DP1 | Scheduler | 1.551/1.607 | 12602/13285 | 115.445/96.704 | | 32/32 | 4×DP1 | Mooncake | 2.101/2.112 | 8615/8826 | 100.019/69.134 | `—` denotes an unsupported main DP4 combination. ### Known limitations in `main` - `main` does not support the `zmq_to_scheduler` path with Encoder DP enabled. - On the Mooncake path, enabling Encoder DP while running the Language service with TP greater than 1 causes request routing and embedding-lifecycle errors. These combinations were therefore not included as valid `main/new_epd` performance pairs. ## Accuracy Tests ## Speed Tests and Profiling ## Checklist - [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. signals.title: Fix dp-attention + speculative decoding crashes in flashinfer MLA backend
signals.text: ## Motivation Running MLA models (e.g. DeepSeek-R1) with `--enable-dp-attention` together with NEXTN/EAGLE speculative decoding on the flashinfer backend crashes during CUDA graph capture / prefill. Plain dp-attention (no spec) and plain spec (no dp-attention) each work; only the combination breaks. Verified fixed on 4-node A100*8 **tp32 / dp4 / ep32** DeepSeek-R1-0528-bf16. ## Root causes Two independent upstream changes exposed latent invariant violations in the MLA backend: 1. **PR #20978** ("pad max-num-requests in decode cuda graph") made the max capture batch size round **up** to a multiple of `attn_tp_size` under dp-attention. That padded bs can now exceed the `req_to_token_pool.size` bound the MLA backend used to size its cuda-graph indptr buffers in `__init__`, so the `[: bs + 1]` slices silently truncated and flashinfer's `plan()` failed with an indptr size mismatch. 2. **The flashinfer version bump** (current requires 0.6.14) added a strict ragged-prefill check `q.shape[0] == qo_indptr[-1]`. Under dp-attention the per-rank input `q` is padded, but the per-request `seq_lens` are not, so `qo_indptr[-1]` (real tokens) falls short of `q.shape[0]` (padded) and the ragged wrapper rejects the extra rows. This addresses the same issue as PR https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/21452, except that PR only fixes the problem in flashinfer_backend.py for PCG and does not handle flashinfer_mla_backend.py. Note this strict check has two independent victims under dp-attention: the paged/ragged prefill updater (FlashInferMLAIndicesUpdaterPrefill, addressed by Change 3), and the chunked-prefix MHA path (FlashInferMhaChunkKVRunner, addressed by Change 4). The latter only triggers on prefill with a non-empty prefix (radix-cache hits), so it stays dormant until requests re-prefill cached prefixes — most reliably under memory pressure when the scheduler retracts and replays requests. A single DP group hitting it raises ValueError and deadlocks the other groups inside EP collectives until the scheduler watchdog fires (300s), so it surfaces as a watchdog timeout rather than a clean error. ## Changes All in `python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/flashinfer_mla_backend.py`. **1. `FlashInferMLAMultiStepDraftBackend.init_cuda_graph_state` — grow shared indptr buffers to the capture bound** Grow the shared `kv_indptr` / `q_indptr_decode` to `max_bs * topk + 1` when the padded capture bs exceeds the `__init__` bound, and pass them into each child backend via new `kv_indptr_buf` / `q_indptr_decode_buf` params. Fixes root cause 1. **2. `FlashInferMLAAttnBackend.init_cuda_graph_state` — accept & rebind the shared buffers** Add `kv_indptr_buf` / `q_indptr_decode_buf` params. When provided, rebind both `self.kv_indptr` / `self.q_indptr_decode` **and** the decode indices updater's cached references (`self.indices_updater_decode.kv_indptr` / `.q_indptr`) — the updater caches those references at construction, so rebinding only `self` would leave a stale, too-small buffer. **3. Prefill indices updater — dummy padding request for ragged prefill under dp-attention** - `FlashInferMLAAttnBackend.init_forward_metadata`: compute `padded_num_tokens = extend_num_tokens` and `real_num_tokens = sum(extend_seq_lens_cpu)` (both host-side ints, guarded on `*_cpu is not None`), pass them through. - `FlashInferMLAIndicesUpdaterPrefill.update` / `call_begin_forward`: thread the two params through; in the non-spec ragged branch, when `padded_num_tokens > real_num_tokens`, append one dummy request to `qo_indptr` / `kv_indptr` / `kv_indices` covering the padding tokens (dummy kv entries point at slot 0 so its softmax stays finite). This satisfies the strict `q.shape[0] == qo_indptr[-1]` check without touching the causal masks of real requests, mirroring the piecewise-cuda-graph padding pattern in `flashinfer_backend.py` (see #26016). Fixes root cause 2. - The spec branch (`spec_info is not None`) needs no dummy request: those callers (target-verify) all set `use_ragged=False` and feed the paged wrapper, which has no `q.shape == qo_indptr[-1]` check. **4. FlashInferMhaChunkKVRunner — handle dp-attention padding in the chunked-prefix MHA path** This runner builds its own qo_indptr from the real per-request extend lens in update_wrapper() and never passes through call_begin_forward, so the dummy-request fix in Change 3 does not reach it. A dummy request is also not usable here: the chunk wrappers are ragged and a dummy could only be given an empty kv range, producing lse = -inf rows that then feed merge_state_v2. Instead, plan the wrappers with the real token count and record it (self.real_num_tokens, set only when extend_num_tokens > sum(extend_seq_lens_cpu), both host-side ints guarded on *_cpu is not None). In forward(), slice q down to real_num_tokens before the ragged run, then zero-pad the output (and lse, when returned) back up to the padded length. Zeros stay finite through merge_state_v2, and the padding rows are discarded downstream anyway. k/v need no slicing — flashinfer only checks q.shape[0] and never indexes past kv_indptr. Fixes root cause 2 on the chunked-prefix path. ## Verification - 4-node tp32/dp4/ep32 DeepSeek-R1-0528-bf16 + EAGLE (NEXTN, steps 2 / topk 1 / draft-tokens 3): server starts, CUDA graph capture + decode replay + spec decode all pass (`cuda graph: True, accept len ~2.3`). - Single / 8-way concurrent generation, and `repetition_penalty` / `frequency_penalty` / `presence_penalty` sampling all return correctly with no server-side errors. - gsm8k accuracy regression: **96.2%** (0% invalid, 1319 questions, 5-shot, thinking on) — on par with the 95.8% baseline, no regression. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #29495522440](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/29495522440)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #29495521900](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/29495521900)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [P/D disagg] Support DSV4 decode radix on ROCm unified KV
signals.text: ## Motivation #27770 added the supported device-only decode radix path for hybrid-SWA models on `UnifiedRadixCache`, but deliberately kept DeepSeek-V4 disabled. On ROCm, DeepSeek-V4 normally runs with: ```bash SGLANG_HACK_FLASHMLA_BACKEND=unified_kv_triton ``` That layout uses the same FULL+SWA unified radix structure and paged SWA-tail allocator, while DSV4 compressed KV/indexer/state transfer is already carried by the existing PD state payloads. Keeping the blanket DSV4 rejection forces redundant full-prefix transfer on every turn. This PR was rewritten on top of #27770. It no longer carries the competing FULL-only matcher or the old broad allocator-capability implementation. ## Scope Enable decode-side radix reuse only when all of the following hold: - the selected cache is actually `UnifiedRadixCache`; - the model uses paged SWA-tail allocation; - DSV4 is using the ROCm unified-KV layout; - the radix component set is exactly FULL+SWA; - hierarchical cache, SWA-compress, Mamba/SSM, HiSparse, fake transfer, and speculative decoding remain rejected by the existing guards. NPU C128, MTP/DSpark, and SWA+HiCache are intentionally out of scope. ## Implementation - Validate the cache implementation selected at runtime instead of requiring the legacy `SGLANG_ENABLE_UNIFIED_RADIX_TREE=1` environment gate. - Reuse #27770's insertion-margin and prefix-cap design so the complete SWA window is transferred into the fresh delta. - Preserve `skip_lock_node_ids` together with `swa_uuid_for_lock` across admission and early SWA-lock release. - If locking a radix hit makes admission fail, release it, refresh the pool budget, reset the request to the root/miss state, and retry once as a miss. This prevents a stable hit/reject loop from head-of-line blocking the decode queue. - Add focused compatibility, page/window geometry, lock ownership, and admission-liveness tests. ## Validation - `pre-commit run --files ...` — passed for all six changed files. - `test_decode_radix_lock_ref.py -v` — 13 passed. - `test_swa_decode_radix_cache.py -v` — 8 passed. - `test_decode_queue_cleanup.py -v` — 8 passed. - `test_unified_radix_cache_unittest.py` — passed. - AgentX 1P1D MI355X pressure run, job `26395`: TP8/DP1/EP1, concurrency 48, 3600-second profiling, latest `v0.5.17-rocm724-mi35x-20260820` image (`sha256:420f3f2d...c4fcf67f`). SLURM completed `0:0`; AIPerf `submission_valid=true`; 1,779 valid requests, 0 errors; final server prefix-cache hit 86.0%; no KV-full/SWA exhaustion/cache assertion/GPU memory fault. The E2E run exercised inputs up to 729,704 tokens and reached 79% decode FULL-KV usage plus 75% pre-allocation usage. Raw artifacts are under `/apps/InferenceX_CI/slurm_job-26395/`. ## Checklist - [x] Rebased onto current `main` after #27770. - [x] Removed the obsolete competing implementation. - [x] Added focused unit coverage. - [x] Ran formatting and local regression tests. - [x] Run current-head DSV4 1P1D cache-hit and pressure-stability validation. - [ ] Run maintainer Base/Extra/ROCm CI. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32463171838](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32463171838)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32463171607](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32463171607)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32463171709](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32463171709)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: feat(mem_cache): semantic KV cache reuse via a pluggable fuzzy-match radix backend
signals.text: ## Motivation Exact prefix matching cannot reuse KV across prompts that share meaning but not leading tokens: paraphrased questions over the same document, RAG prompts with reordered context, multi-user workloads hitting the same knowledge base. This PR adds opt-in **semantic KV cache reuse** following the `|exact|fuzzy|miss|` prompt decomposition from the fuzzy prefix matching design discussion (Draft_Prefix_Matching.md, @ibifrost): when the radix tree covers only a prefix, a pluggable `FuzzyMatchProvider` may nominate donor KV from a previously finished request, which is copied into recipient-owned slots with RoPE position correction before the forward pass. Design goals, per maintainer guidance (@hzh0425): keep the default path untouched, register the feature as a radix-cache backend, keep `model_runner` changes minimal. ## Modifications - **New `FuzzyRadixCache(RadixCache)`** registered as radix-cache backend `fuzzy_match` (flexkv pattern). All fuzzy behavior lives in the backend: provider match on exact-miss, donor validation + pinning (lock refs via a TreeNode-id registry), realization-slot pre-allocation with clean exact-only fallback, donor registration on request finish. - **Core `RadixCache`/`BasePrefixCache` changes = two seams:** `MatchResult.fuzzy_matched_len` (new trailing field) and a no-op `_on_finished_insert` hook between the finished-request insert and duplicate-slot freeing. - **`FuzzyKVRealizer`** collaborator does pre-forward donor-KV realization (V copy; K reverse-RoPE at donor positions + apply at target positions; per-layer zero-out mask). `model_runner.py` gains only orchestration: a gated `maybe_init_fuzzy_kv_realizer()` and one delegate call in `_forward_raw` beside the deferred-mamba hook (outside CUDA-graph capture/replay, covers all extend branches). - **`ReverseRotaryEmbedding` / `get_reverse_rope` / `reverse_rotary_emb`** additions to `layers/rotary_embedding` (native path; no CUDA kernel exists for the reverse direction). - **`SemanticEmbedding` provider** (default): implemented by the [`semblend`](https://github.com/WorldFlowAI/semblend) package ([PyPI](https://pypi.org/project/semblend/), Apache-2.0), installed via the new extra `pip install "sglang[fuzzy-semantic]"`. SemBlend is an open-source library for semantic KV-cache donor discovery and reuse planning: it embeds prompts (MiniLM ONNX), maintains the donor index, aligns donor and recipient token chunks (N:M), scores reuse quality against configurable gates, and emits the reuse plan — donor span, positions, and the per-layer mask — that this PR's realization path consumes. Keeping that pipeline in a package keeps SGLang's tree free of the embedding/ANN stack while the reuse-planning algorithms iterate. Lazy import + hard version gate at startup with an actionable error. The `FuzzyMatchProvider` interface is public so custom providers can plug in. - **Observability:** prefill batch log shows `#fuzzy-token: N` when fuzzy reuse fired (previously realized reuse showed as `#cached-token: 0`). - **Config surface:** selecting the backend enables the feature; five `--fuzzy-*` flags (provider, threshold, min-reuse-ratio, min-match-length, model-arch). Provider-internal tuning stays in config defaults. - **Docs:** end-to-end call chain with explicit lock/alloc/RoPE ownership in `python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/fuzzy_match/README.md` (requested in review of the experimental branch). - **Tests:** 21 CPU unit tests (`test_fuzzy_match_providers.py`, `test_fuzzy_radix_cache.py`), semblend faked via sys.modules — no new CI dependency. Cover pool-accounting failure modes: stale-donor and kv-length-mismatch fallbacks (leak-checked), donor pin/release lifecycle, donor-registration ordering vs duplicate freeing, node-registry maintenance, registry selection + unsupported-config rejection, and concurrent recipients pinning one donor. Not supported yet: MLA pools, EAGLE, multi-region reuse, hierarchical-cache interaction. ## Follow-on work This PR deliberately ships the minimal `|exact|fuzzy|miss|` pattern — one contiguous fuzzy span re-anchored at the exact-prefix boundary — because it reuses the existing inference pipeline with no structural changes. Planned follow-ups, in rough order: - **Multi-segment / multi-region reuse** (`|exact|miss|fuzzy|miss|fuzzy|...`), the realistic shape of RAG and multi-document workloads: the scheduler builds a segmented prefill plan of fresh spans plus donor-KV spans, and the attention backend consumes it via FlashInfer's `VariableBlockSparseAttentionWrapper` (per the design discussion, a better fit than `custom_mask`). Early prototypes on 64K multi-donor prompts show mean 7.65x TTFT speedup versus cold prefill with good quality — worth its own RFC once this foundation lands. - **True per-layer recompute** for masked layers (the current `layer_recompute_mask` is a zero-out signal); recompute is the cleaner long-term answer for quality. - **Donor-registration budgeting** (rate/dedup limits on donor indexing) to shrink the remaining enabled-but-idle overhead on dense short-request workloads. - **MLA-pool support** in the realization path. - **Hierarchical-cache (HiCache) interaction** — fuzzy donors resident in host tiers. ## Accuracy Tests All runs on THIS branch (A10G, Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct-AWQ, fresh server per configuration, 2026-07-13). - **GSM8K few-shot (n=1000), fuzzy on vs off:** baseline accuracy 0.862 (invalid 0.001) vs fuzzy-on **0.865** (invalid 0.001) — no degradation (delta within batching noise). The provider's gates produced **zero fuzzy fires across all 1000 questions** (short, semantically dissimilar prompts never meet the reuse-ratio gate; the few-shot prefix hits the exact radix path), and zero pool leaks. This is the negative control: enabling the backend does not perturb workloads without semantic overlap. - **Warm-vs-cold A/B at 8K/16K** (cnn_dailymail + wikihow clusters, at **default flags**). ROUGE-L / token-F1 compare the warm (reused) answer against the cold answer for the same prompt; the measurement scale: identical-prompt reruns without any reuse score ~0.88/0.90 (batching-noise floor), exact-prefix radix reuse scores 0.94/0.96. | Overlap type | cache frac | cold→warm TTFT | ROUGE-L | token-F1 | |---|---|---|---|---| | exact (control) | — (radix) | 3264→44ms | 0.941 | 0.955 | | partial_60 | 0.88 | 3254→646ms (5.0x) | 0.547 | 0.587 | | partial_80 | 0.58 | 3257→1700ms (1.9x) | 0.449 | 0.490 | | paraphrase | 0.76 | 3262→1034ms (3.2x) | 0.478 | 0.525 | | diverse (negative) | 0.00 | 3262→3318ms (no fire) | 0.878 | 0.898 | A sweep at looser settings (threshold 0.50, min-match 1) produced the same hit rates and the same drift — on genuinely similar pairs the threshold does not change what a hit does, it changes which pairs hit (on GSM8K, defaults fire on 1 in 1000 requests; the diverse control never fires). Read: a fuzzy hit trades TTFT for output drift beyond the rerun-noise floor — reuse is quality-gated but **not lossless**; answers remain on-topic and grounded (samples in the raw results), and per-layer recompute (follow-on) is the path to closing the gap. Zero pool-consistency failures across all sweeps and both GSM8K runs. Experimental-branch reference @16K (n=1): PPL(warm)/PPL(cold) 0.9587. - Statement of semantics: reuse is quality-gated but not lossless; the layer mask is a zero-out signal, not per-layer recompute. ## Speed Tests and Profiling - **Reuse speedup (this branch, e2e smoke):** paraphrase variant realized 104/119 donor tokens with RoPE correction; only 15 tokens prefilled. Experimental-branch reference at 16K: cold TTFT 4548ms → warm 230ms (19.8x); donor registration runs off the hot path (async embed). [OPTIONAL: re-measure 16K TTFT pair on this branch] - **No-hit overhead (GSM8K n=1000, parallel 32, default flags):** 1249 → 1164 tok/s output throughput (~7%) and 127.3 → 136.8s wall on a worst-case-dense workload (a thousand short requests, every one indexed as a donor). The synchronous per-miss lookup cost is bounded by `fuzzy_min_suffix_tokens` (default 256): suffixes too short to amortize a semantic lookup never pay for one. The residual is the asynchronous donor-registration embedding, which amortizes on long-context workloads (fewer, larger requests); donor-registration budgeting is listed as follow-on. Without the suffix gate the same workload measured ~10-11%. The feature is opt-in per deployment. ## Reproduction ```bash pip install "sglang[fuzzy-semantic]" python -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct-AWQ \ --radix-cache-backend fuzzy_match \ --fuzzy-model-arch qwen2.5-7b \ --mem-fraction-static 0.70 2>&1 | tee server.log # paired paraphrase prompts -> look for: # "fuzzy match success", "[FUZZY] Realized", "#fuzzy-token:" grep -c "pool memory leak detected" server.log # expect 0 ``` ## Checklist / credits - Design + `FuzzyMatchProvider` framework: @ibifrost (Draft_Prefix_Matching.md); backend-registry direction: @hzh0425. Co-authored-by: Chenxin Wu <ibifrostki@gmail.com> Big thanks to @ibifrost and @hzh0425 for all of the hard work/advice/reviewing over the past several months. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32513043966](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32513043966)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32513043826](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32513043826)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32513043948](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32513043948)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: Fix hybrid decode CUDA graph WAR event timing
signals.text:
## Summary Hybrid linear-attention (Mambaish) decode graphs continue reading shared recurrent state during CUDA graph replay. Publish the WAR read-done event after replay so the overlap scheduler cannot overwrite that state while the graph is still consuming it. ### Before ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant R as Decode graph runner participant G as GPU stream participant S as Overlap scheduler R->>G: Load shared Mamba state R->>G: Record read-done event R->>G: Replay CUDA graph S->>G: Wait for read-done G-->>S: Event completes before replay S->>G: Reuse / overwrite shared state Note over G: Replay is still reading the state
Race, hang, or invalid output ``` ### After ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant R as Decode graph runner participant G as GPU stream participant S as Overlap scheduler R->>G: Load shared Mamba state R->>G: Replay CUDA graph R->>G: Record read-done event S->>G: Wait for read-done G-->>S: Event completes after replay S->>G: Safely reuse / overwrite shared state ``` --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :x: [Run #32523278032](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32523278032) Latest PR Test (Extra): :x: [Run #32523277790](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32523277790) Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): :heavy_minus_sign: **No AMD PR run found for this commit**.

signals.title: [Intel][XPU] Add NUMA node binding support for Intel XPU
signals.text: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation `numa_utils` (the `SGLANG_NUMA_BIND_V2` launcher path that binds each GPU worker's CPU/memory to the GPU's local NUMA node) only supported CUDA — it discovered the GPU→NUMA mapping via NVML. Intel XPU has no NVML, so NUMA binding was silently skipped, leaving XPU workers unbound on multi-socket hosts and paying cross-socket memory-access penalties. This extends the existing NUMA-bind-v2 path to Intel XPU so XPU deployments get the same automatic CPU/memory affinity as CUDA. CUDA behavior is unchanged. ## Modifications `python/sglang/srt/utils/numa_utils.py`: - Admit XPU in the availability gate: `_is_numa_available` now checks `(_is_cuda or _is_xpu)`. - Query the GPU→NUMA mapping from **sysfs PCI topology** for XPU (`_query_numa_node_for_xpu` / `_list_xpu_pci_addresses`) instead of NVML — reads `/sys/bus/pci/devices/*/numa_node`, filtering to Intel display controllers (vendor `0x8086`, PCI class `0x03xx`), sorted by BDF to match PyTorch XPU's device order. Runs purely from sysfs in the launcher parent, mirroring why the CUDA path uses NVML there (no XPU-runtime init needed). - Honor `ZE_AFFINITY_MASK` (the XPU analogue of `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES`) so a logical device index maps to the correct physical GPU; falls back to unmasked order for composite/unparseable masks. - Report `ZE_AFFINITY_MASK` (instead of `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES` / NVML index) in the numactl debug string. - All XPU logic is behind `_is_xpu` branches; the CUDA path is untouched. Tests: - New `test/registered/xpu/test_numa_utils_xpu.py` (`register_xpu_ci` + `register_cpu_ci`; mock-based, no XPU hardware required) covering the XPU availability gate, Intel-GPU sysfs filtering/sorting, `ZE_AFFINITY_MASK` logical→physical remap, `numa_node == -1 → []`, out-of-range and no-GPU handling, and `_query_numa_node_for_gpu` delegation to the XPU path. - `test/registered/utils/test_numa_utils.py`: pinned `_is_xpu=False` on the two CUDA/CPU cases that exercise the real `_is_numa_available` / pynvml path, so they stay hermetic when the file runs on an XPU host. Verified on an 8× Intel Arc Pro B60 host: the sysfs enumeration matched `torch.xpu.device_count()`, produced a coherent 4-NUMA-node mapping, and `ZE_AFFINITY_MASK` remapping resolved correctly. NUMA unit tests pass (48 passed, 2 skipped). > **Known assumption:** the sysfs BDF sort is assumed to match PyTorch XPU's device order (the standard Level Zero convention). This could not be cross-checked directly on the test host (torch XPU exposes no PCI BDF, and `sycl-ls`/`xpu-smi` were unavailable), though the resulting NUMA mapping was coherent. ## Accuracy Tests N/A — this only affects launcher-side CPU/memory affinity (process placement), not the kernel or model forward path, so it cannot change model outputs. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not included. NUMA binding is a locality optimization whose benefit is host- and topology-dependent (magnitude scales with cross-socket memory traffic on the specific machine), and it is opt-in via `SGLANG_NUMA_BIND_V2`. With the flag unset, behavior is unchanged; the CUDA path is untouched, so there is no regression risk to the default path. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. signals.title: [Feat][Multimodal] Add ViT patch-based admission control for multimodal requests
signals.text: ## Motivation **Note**: Given that PR https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/31788 has not yet been merged, this PR incorporates fixes for sequence length. Multimodal requests may contain images with significantly different resolutions and aspect ratios. Limiting only the number of images or the original pixel count is inflexible and does not accurately represent ViT memory consumption. A request containing many small images may be safe, while another request containing only a few large images may cause an NPU out-of-memory error. This PR introduces admission control based on the actual ViT patch count after image resizing and alignment. It allows mixed-resolution requests to be scheduled according to their real visual workload and prevents oversized requests or prefill batches from entering ViT forward. ## Modifications - Compute the raw ViT patch count of each image from `image_grid_thw` after image preprocessing. - Propagate image patch counts from the tokenizer manager to the scheduler. - Add `--max-mm-patch-tokens-per-request` to reject requests whose total visual patch count exceeds the configured per-request limit. - Add `--max-prefill-mm-patch-tokens` to limit the total visual patch count admitted into a single prefill batch. - Keep requests that exceed the current prefill budget in the waiting queue instead of rejecting them. - Leave text-only requests and decode scheduling unchanged. - Add unit tests covering: - Mixed image grids. - PyTorch tensor and NumPy inputs. - Patch-count calculation. - Multimodal-input merging. ## Test ### Test Environment | Item | Configuration | |---|---| | Hardware | Ascend 910B3 / Atlas A2 | | Model | Qwen3.6-35B-A3B | | Tensor parallel size | 2 | | Static memory fraction | 0.75 | | Per-request patch budget | 220,000 | | Prefill-batch patch budget | 220,000 | ### Boundary Tests | Image resolution | Raw patches per image | Maximum successful images | One additional image | |---|---:|---:|---| | 512×512 | 1,024 | 214 | HTTP 400 | | 1280×720 | 3,520 | 62 | HTTP 400 | | 1920×1080 | 8,160 | 26 | HTTP 400 | | 2560×1440 | 14,400 | 15 | HTTP 400 | | 3840×2160 | 32,640 | 6 | HTTP 400 | All maximum values and their corresponding `maximum + 1` cases were verified using real requests. ### Extreme-Input Tests | Test case | Result | |---|---| | One 12000×12000 image | Succeeded | | 500 32×32 images in one request | Succeeded | | One 12000×12000 image plus 500 small images | Succeeded | | Four large images requiring 259,584 patches | Rejected with HTTP 400 before ViT forward | | Four concurrent requests with one different large image each | 4/4 succeeded | | 24 concurrent requests with 500 small images per request | 24/24 succeeded without OOM | ### High-Concurrency Mixed-Shape Test ```text Concurrent requests: 24 Images per request: 35 Different shapes per request: 35 Total images: 840 ``` Results: | Metric | Result | |---|---:| | Successful requests | 24/24 | | Failed requests | 0 | | HTTP 400 | 0 | | HTTP 500 | 0 | | NPU OOM | 0 | | Scheduler exceptions | 0 | | Health check after test | HTTP 200 | | Average latency | 143.33 seconds | | Minimum latency | 141.49 seconds | | Maximum latency | 155.68 seconds | HBM usage: | NPU | Before test | Peak | After test |
