signals.title: feat(load-reporter): add push-based engine load reporting
signals.text:
## Motivation Load-aware routing needs one authoritative view of scheduler load across data-parallel ranks. Polling every Worker from every Router adds fan-out, creates inconsistent views, and churns connections. This PR adds the Worker-side reporter: a push channel built on the scheduler's existing snapshot publication. One shared pull per fire is broadcast to every registered Router over long-lived bidirectional gRPC streams. Router-side ingestion, discovery, retries, and the Prefill throughput extension are intentionally split into follow-up PRs so each layer can be reviewed independently. > The push channel controls *delivery*, not *snapshot age*. End-to-end > freshness stays bounded by the scheduler's snapshot publication interval; > see [Freshness](#freshness). ## Modifications ### Architecture ```mermaid flowchart LR Scheduler["Scheduler
published per-DP-rank load snapshots"] Source["Per-mode snapshot source
manager get_loads / Router SHM reader"] Fire["Single fire loop
one pull per fire + rank-set validation"] Builder["LoadReport builder
HEALTHY / STALE / UNREACHABLE"] Service["Worker gRPC service
--load-reporter-port"] Router["Routers dial in
drive Monitor streams"] Scheduler --> Source --> Fire --> Builder --> Service --> Router ``` ### Protocol and configuration - The Worker hosts `sglang.router.loadmonitor.v1.LoadMonitorService.Monitor(stream RouterFrame) returns (stream WorkerFrame)` on a fixed, opt-in `--load-reporter-port`; each external Router dials in and drives its own stream (`register` → ack → bounded first fire → periodic reports). Stable field numbers and enum values are preserved. - `RouterFrame` = `register | update_config | keep_alive | stop`, with `register` required first; `WorkerFrame` = `registered | report | error`. Re-registering the same `router_id` replaces its old session; different `router_id`s coexist. - Package `grpcio` and `protobuf` through the optional `load-reporter` extra across all supported Python wheel variants. - Reporting stays opt-in so normal SGLang installations gain no mandatory runtime dependencies. ### Reporter runtime — one timer, one pull, broadcast - A single fire-loop task owns the only timer; sessions are passive bookkeeping (deadline, lease, capacity-1 queue) and own no task or timer. - Each fire performs exactly one bounded snapshot pull (`get_loads()`, 1 s budget). The same budget covers one retry when the expected DP-rank set changes mid-pull. - One report per pull, validated and built from that attempt only: `HEALTHY`, `STALE`, or `UNREACHABLE` (empty ranks + `last_error`). There is no persistent store and no cross-report merge, so a slow or stale rank is never replaced with historical data. - The fire broadcasts the same report to every session whose deadline fired; sessions registered before the next fire share its pull for their initial report. - Each session has a capacity-1 latest-wins queue, lease TTL with keep-alive renewal, mid-stream config updates, registration-anchored deadlines, and idempotent shutdown. - Pull, transport, and shutdown failures never propagate into the inference request path. ### Freshness End-to-end snapshot freshness is bounded by the scheduler's snapshot publication path (`load_snapshot_publish_interval`), not by the gRPC delivery cadence. The report interval controls how often a report is sent, not how old the snapshot inside it is — a poll at the same cadence observes data of the same age. What the push stream adds over polling is delivery, not freshness: a negotiated per-Router cadence, connection reuse, one-pull multi-Router fan-out, leases, and bounded backpressure. ### Tokenizer integration - Single-tokenizer HTTP and native gRPC start one reporter runtime in the FastAPI lifespan (native gRPC reuses the same process and listener). - Multi-tokenizer mode: `MultiTokenizerRouter` is the sole runtime owner; HTTP workers open no streams, and elastic scale changes update the expected DP-rank set (observed by the next fire). - Standalone SMG gRPC starts the reporter at request-manager readiness; older servicers without the readiness hook fail loudly when the reporter is enabled. - The embedded offline Engine API does not own the reporter; cleanup runs in the HTTP-server lifespan, the SMG gRPC-server finally path, and `MultiTokenizerRouter.close()`. ### Tests and documentation - Unit/integration coverage (CPU, real in-process `grpc.aio`): proto contract, fire loop (shared pull deadlines, broadcast to due sessions, per-session lease gating, rank-set-change retry sharing one budget, registration-anchored cadence, stale/error reports, re-registration, shutdown), snapshot validation and report-builder contracts, snapshot sources, service handshake and error frames, composition-root lifecycle, and standalone SMG wiring. - Negative invariants: request dispatch/completion/abort never trigger a pull; topology updates never pull immediately. - Registered GPU E2E tests with a real `grpc.aio` fake Router cover single-owner, multi-owner, and standalone SMG reporting. - Documentation covers the wire contract, serving-mode matrix, fire-loop schedule, freshness model, network/deployment assumptions, and shutdown behavior. ### Design advantages - **Zero request-path coupling:** dispatch, completion, and abort have no edge into the reporting graph; there is no per-request overhead. - **Efficient fan-out:** one pull per fire shared by all due sessions, persistent bidi streams, no Router-side polling fan-out or connection churn. - **Topology-safe:** reports preserve per-DP-rank detail; rank-set changes are validated and retried within the same fire budget. - **Resilient:** per-attempt status semantics, session replacement, leases, latest-wins backpressure, and bounded shutdown prevent stale tasks from accumulating. - **Extensible:** a stable protocol and a single validation entry point provide a clean foundation for the separately reviewed Router monitor and future metrics. ## Accuracy Tests N/A for model accuracy. This PR does not change model forward code, kernels, sampling, or generated outputs. Functional validation: - Registered CPU tests cover the protocol contract, fire-loop scheduling/broadcast, snapshot validation, report builder, service behavior, lifecycle, and standalone SMG wiring. - Registered GPU E2E tests drive a real `grpc.aio` fake Router against single-owner, multi-owner, and standalone SMG modes. - Generated protobuf/gRPC bindings import successfully and expose the expected `sglang.router.loadmonitor.v1` service. ## Speed Tests and Profiling N/A for inference throughput benchmarking. This is an opt-in control-plane feature and does not modify model execution. The reporter adds no request-path overhead: there are no hooks on the dispatch/completion paths, and sampling/network I/O runs in the single background fire task. No inference-speed improvement is claimed. Reporter cadence and freshness are exercised functionally by the registered tests; no new micro-benchmarks are claimed in this revision. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process). 2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers. 3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so. - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci`. 4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR. --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :x: [Run #32481593988](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32481593988) Latest PR Test (Extra): :x: [Run #32481593583](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32481593583) Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): :hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32481593848](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32481593848)

signals.title: [AMD] DeepSeek-V4: add aiter fused mHC post+pre with cross-layer boundary dispatch
signals.text: ## Summary Add a HIP/aiter fused `mhc_post` + next-layer `mhc_pre` path for DeepSeek-V4 on gfx95, dispatched across the attention/MoE boundary alongside the existing TileLang and Triton fused paths. On MI355X (gfx950) this is a **+0.8%–1.8% output-throughput win across concurrency 4–64 with accuracy preserved**. ## What changed - **`python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_common/amd/deepseek_v4_fused_mhc.py`** - `try_aiter_fused_mhc_post_pre()`: wraps `aiter.ops.mhc.mhc_fused_post_pre`. The aiter kernel self-gates fused-vs-unfused per arch/token-count, so no token threshold is duplicated here; import/runtime failures fall back and warn once. - `try_mhc_fused_post_pre_boundary()`: aiter → Triton dispatch. The two kernels expect opposite fn orientations (Triton transposed, aiter native). - `is_cross_layer_mhc_fusion_enabled()` / `_is_production_mhc_enabled()`: enable cross-layer fusion when either the TileLang path or the aiter gfx95 path is available. `_is_fused_mhc_post_pre_enabled()` is consolidated here (previously duplicated in `deepseek_v4.py`). - **`python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_v4.py`**: route the attn-side, FFN-side, and `op_mhc_post_attn_pre_mlp` boundaries through `_apply_mhc_post_pre_boundary()`, falling back to the unfused `hc_post` + `hc_pre` sequence when no fused kernel fires. In the operation/batch-overlap path (DP attention) `state` is a `_StateDict` (attribute access, no `__getitem__`), so read it via `state.<field>`. - **`test/registered/unit/models/test_deepseek_v4_amd_fused_mhc.py`**: gating/dispatch unit tests plus a gfx95-gated numerical test asserting `next_residual` (bit-exact) and `layer_input`/`post_mix` (bf16 tolerance) vs the unfused reference. ## Validation Model: `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro`. Hardware: MI355X (gfx950), TP4. Image: `rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.15.post1-rocm720-mi35x-20260724`. Baseline = image tree; Patched = image tree + this patch (only 2 model files differ). Env: `SGLANG_USE_AITER=1 AITER_BF16_FP8_MOE_BOUND=0 SGLANG_HACK_FLASHMLA_BACKEND=unified_kv_triton`. ### Unit test ``` $ python3 -m pytest test/registered/unit/models/test_deepseek_v4_amd_fused_mhc.py -q 8 passed ``` ### Accuracy (GSM8K, 1319 questions × 3 runs) | run | baseline | patched | |----:|:--------:|:-------:| | 1 | 0.942 | 0.947 | | 2 | 0.943 | 0.943 | | 3 | 0.937 | 0.944 | | **avg** | **0.941** | **0.945** | Invalid = 0.000 for all runs. Accuracy preserved (within run-to-run noise). ### Performance (ISL=8192, OSL=1024, output token throughput) | concurrency | baseline (tok/s) | patched (tok/s) | Δ | baseline TPOT (ms) | patched TPOT (ms) | |------------:|:----------------:|:---------------:|:-----:|:---:|:---:| | 4 | 216.38 | 219.66 | **+1.5%** | 17.507 | 17.242 | | 8 | 367.65 | 372.98 | **+1.4%** | 20.715 | 20.423 | | 16 | 568.64 | 579.04 | **+1.8%** | 26.460 | 25.960 | | 32 | 792.79 | 800.70 | **+1.0%** | 38.165 | 37.808 | | 64 | 1033.97 | 1042.04 | **+0.8%** | 58.854 | 58.412 | ### Commands used ```bash # Accuracy python3 benchmark/gsm8k/bench_sglang.py --num-questions 2000 --parallel 1200 # Performance (per concurrency C in 4 8 16 32 64) python3 benchmark_serving.py --model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro --backend sglang \ --dataset-name random --random-input-len 8192 --random-output-len 1024 \ --random-range-ratio 0.8 --num-prompts $((C*10)) --max-concurrency C --ignore-eos ``` ## Test plan / Checklist - [x] New unit test `test_deepseek_v4_amd_fused_mhc.py` passes (8 passed; gfx95 numerical). - [x] GSM8K accuracy preserved vs baseline (0.945 vs 0.941, invalid 0.000). - [x] Output throughput improves +0.8%–1.8% at concurrency 4–64 (TP4, 8k/1k), TPOT reduced. - [x] Falls back to unfused hc_post + hc_pre when no fused kernel fires (non-gfx95 / import failure). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32543411208](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32543411208)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32543410908](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32543410908)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32543411025](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32543411025)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [Spec] Windowed draft-decode attention for built-in EAGLE / MTP drafts
signals.text: # [Spec] Windowed draft-decode attention for built-in EAGLE / MTP drafts ## Motivation In [arXiv:2607.21535](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.21535) we show that a built-in MTP draft head's full-attention KV read grows with the prefix until it dominates the decode step, and that restricting the *draft's* attention to a sink plus recent window cuts the per-decode-step cost by +28% to +44% at 1M context across three architecture families at near-unchanged acceptance, with the target still verifying every token at full attention. The same idea motivated `--speculative-draft-window-size` in #24664, but that flag reaches the drafter through the model file (`llama_eagle3.py` sets `sliding_window_size` per layer) and the backend's per-layer SWA path, so it applies to `LlamaForCausalLMEagle3` checkpoints. This PR applies the window one level down, in the shared draft-decode index builder, so the built-in EAGLE / MTP (NEXTN) draft-decode path gets it on the Triton and FlashInfer draft backends with no model-file change and no second attention wrapper — the draft simply gets a shorter KV list. Only the windowing mechanism is upstreamed here; the paper's ring-buffer reclaim of the unread draft KV is possible follow-up work. ## Modifications 1. `generate_draft_decode_kv_indices` gains `window_size` and `sink_size` `tl.constexpr` params, both defaulting to `0`. With `window_size > 0` a draft-decode step gathers `[first sink_size tokens] + [most recent window_size tokens]` instead of the whole prefix, then appends the draft tree tokens unwindowed as before. `window_size == 0` collapses every added op to the identity, so the default path and the kernel's other callers (AITER, MLA) are unchanged. 2. `--speculative-draft-window-size` is now also honored by the built-in EAGLE / MTP draft-decode path on the Triton and FlashInfer draft backends. `spec_utils.resolve_draft_decode_window()` is the single mapping from server args to `(window_size, sink_size)`; both `*MultiStepDraftBackend`s call it once in `__init__`. 3. New `--speculative-draft-sink-size` for the attention sink, since a pure recent window drops the initial tokens attention reliably parks on. The window keeps DFLASH's unit and anchor — KV entries, counted back from the end of the prefix — so a step reads `min(seq_len, window + sink)` prefix entries, which at the default `sink=0` is `min(seq_len, window)`, the same expression as `_compute_compact_draft_seq_lens`, with no `-1`. Tree tokens are never capped, so the existing `window_size >= num_draft_tokens` check still holds. 4. A draft model with a sliding window of its own keeps it, and this windowing stays off. That covers an MTP head with SWA in its config and a `LlamaForCausalLMEagle3` drafter, whose window comes from this same flag. One KV list is shared by every draft layer, so the index builder cannot express a per-layer window, and a checkpoint's own window should win over a server flag either way. We warn only when the resulting window differs from the requested one, so the EAGLE-3 case stays quiet. CUDA graphs are safe: the per-request kept length rides in `kv_indptr`, exactly like the variable-seqlen path the graph already replays. Same launch grid, no host sync, no dynamic shapes. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Qwen3.6-35B-A3B bf16, one B200, `trtllm_mha` target, EAGLE `steps=6 topk=1 draft_tokens=7`, `W=4032 S=64` (4096 prefix entries per draft step), batch 1, RULER `niah_multiquery_enum`, 512 output tokens. `window` vs `native` on the same draft backend; the target is identical in every arm. `T_iter` is per-iteration wall time — the mechanism, without acceptance mixed in — and TPOT is `T_iter / AL`. | context | draft backend | TPOT native → window | speedup | T_iter native → window | AL native → window | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | 32K | triton | 3.895 → 3.068 ms | 1.27× | 12.67 → 10.05 ms (−21%) | 3.25 → 3.28 | | 64K | triton | 4.414 → 3.264 ms | 1.35× | 19.06 → 13.48 ms (−29%) | 4.32 → 4.13 | | 128K | triton | 7.047 → 4.568 ms | 1.54× | 31.65 → 20.02 ms (−37%) | 4.49 → 4.38 | | 256K | triton | 10.448 → 6.093 ms | 1.71× | 57.35 → 33.45 ms (−42%) | 5.49 → 5.49 | | 32K | flashinfer | 2.199 → 2.142 ms | 1.03× | 7.20 → 7.01 ms (−3%) | 3.28 → 3.28 | | 64K | flashinfer | 1.728 → 1.738 ms | 0.99× | 7.46 → 7.18 ms (−4%) | 4.32 → 4.13 | | 128K | flashinfer | 1.799 → 1.696 ms | 1.06× | 8.08 → 7.44 ms (−8%) | 4.49 → 4.38 | | 256K | flashinfer | 1.735 → 1.499 ms | 1.16× | 9.36 → 8.05 ms (−14%) | 5.39 → 5.37 | Dense (no speculation) TPOT at those four contexts, for reference: 2.997 / 3.158 / 3.320 / 3.698 ms. - `T_iter` drops at every point on both backends and the drop grows with context, which is the mechanism doing what it should: the draft's read is capped while native's grows. - TPOT also depends on acceptance, so the 64K FlashInfer point is a wash — a 4% per-iteration saving against a 4% acceptance dip. The window is a clear win on FlashInfer from ~128K up and at every point on Triton, whose full-prefix draft read is far more expensive to begin with. - Acceptance never beats native in this sweep. It does past 512K in the paper, but that needs RoPE extension beyond this checkpoint's 256K native context, so we leave it out of the PR's numbers. ## Testing `test/registered/unit/spec/test_draft_decode_window.py` — 13 tests / 28 subtests, 16 s on one GPU. Every expectation comes from a closed-form oracle over `seq_lens`, never from the kernel's own packing, so a bug can't be mirrored on both sides. - `window_size == 0` reproduces the full-KV read plan, offsets and gathered slots, for single- and multi-request batches at `topk` 1 and 2. This is the off-by-default regression guard. - Windowed `kv_indptr` lengths are `min(seq_len, sink + window) + tree`, and the gather really is `[sink] + [recent] + [tree]`, parametrized past 256K/512K/1M. - Tree drafts (`topk > 1`): each `(request, branch)` slot gets its own windowed base list plus its own branch at the oracle offset. Covered at `page_size == 1` and on the `page_size > 1 and topk > 1` paged branch, where tree tokens are read from the uncapped prefix end but written at the capped offset. - `resolve_draft_decode_window`, including the own-window opt-out and exactly when it warns, plus a CPU-only guard that both draft backends resolve through it. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/development_guide_using_docker.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/development_guide_using_docker.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/development_guide_using_docker.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/development_guide_using_docker.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/development_guide_using_docker.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32447503124](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32447503124)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32447503030](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32447503030)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32447503169](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32447503169)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [Feature] Realtime ASR: bounded long audio with encoder-window caching
signals.text: ## Summary This PR adds an experimental, opt-in realtime ASR path for long audio items. It bounds the acoustic work submitted by each update, reuses completed audio encoder windows through SGLang's existing multimodal cache, and publishes decoder progress through the existing append-only transcription delta event. The current realtime path re-submits all audio accumulated for an item every 2 seconds. This preserves full acoustic context, but both prefill and memory grow with the session. On long items, per-update latency eventually dominates realtime playback. For Qwen3-ASR-0.6B, the opt-in path works as follows: 1. Keep the existing cumulative path through the first 60 seconds. 2. On the first update after 60 seconds, establish a one-way handoff from the cumulative transcript to encoder-window continuation. 3. Keep at most eight complete model-native 8-second audio windows plus the current incomplete tail in each later request. 4. Reuse complete-window embeddings through the existing MM cache; always recompute the mutable tail. 5. Carry older semantic context in a bounded, confirmed transcript prefix and generate only the new suffix. 6. Stream decoder progress through the existing `conversation.item.input_audio_transcription.delta` event. No client schema or new event type is added. The default remains cumulative. Encoder windowing is currently enabled only for an explicitly declared English session on a local single-GPU runtime. Unsupported models and languages keep the cumulative path. Enabling encoder windowing with an incompatible distributed or disaggregated topology fails during server startup instead of silently changing the requested strategy. ## Relationship to RFC #22474 This PR builds on [RFC #22474](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/22474) rather than defining a second realtime ASR protocol. - **M1 transport and lifecycle are reused unchanged.** M1 landed in #22848 and introduced `WS /v1/realtime`, `session.update`, incremental PCM append, commit/clear, multi-item sessions, and the existing delta/completed/error event envelopes. This PR does not add a client event, response type, or replacement-transcript protocol. - **This PR implements the measured long-audio part of M2.** The RFC identifies repeated processing of accumulated audio as the main long-session cost and calls for profiling before cache changes. The results below show that the cumulative path becomes impractical for long items, so the opt-in path bounds acoustic context and reuses completed encoder windows through the existing MM embedding cache. - **It also implements the RFC's M3 direction within each backend request.** Generation runs with streaming enabled, but the endpoint publishes only append-safe progress through the existing `transcription.delta` event. This is stable delta streaming, not a new one-event-per-token wire contract. The implementation deliberately narrows the RFC's earlier cache discussion. The RFC's M2 sketch focused first on RadixCache feasibility and listed generic bidirectional encoder-output caching as out of scope. Radix prefix reuse alone cannot avoid re-encoding a growing audio item. This PR permits encoder reuse only when the multimodal processor declares independently encodable window geometry; otherwise the realtime item remains on the cumulative path. The RFC's architectural boundary is preserved: the realtime layer owns the WebSocket/session lifecycle, adapters and processors declare model capability, and the existing MM scheduler/cache performs best-effort reuse. This PR does not introduce an engine-level realtime session, scheduler-owned ASR state, or persistent per-session GPU state. ## Request flow ```mermaid flowchart TD A[Client appends PCM] --> B[2-second inference boundary] B --> C{Received audio over 60 seconds?} C -- No --> D[Submit audio from 0 to current end] D --> E[Cumulative transcript reconciliation] C -- Yes, first handoff --> F[Submit full audio once] F --> G[Create bounded confirmed-text prefix] C -- Yes, steady state --> H[Choose 8-second-aligned rolling range] G --> H H --> I[Up to 8 complete windows plus mutable tail] I --> J[Complete windows: existing MM embedding cache] I --> K[Mutable tail: encode, do not retain] J --> L[Decoder prefix plus new suffix generation] K --> L E --> M[Reconcile decoder updates] L --> M M --> N[Emit only append-safe delta text] N --> O[Existing transcription.delta event] O --> P[Advance absolute PCM cursors and compact old audio] ``` The first windowed request intentionally includes the full handoff audio. Once the handoff succeeds, steady-state requests retain no more than 64 seconds of complete encoder windows plus an incomplete tail shorter than 8 seconds. For example, a steady-state request near 130 seconds looks like this: ```text Older audio represented by confirmed text | v text: [bounded decoder prefix] audio: [w0][w1] ... [w7][tail] encoder: [cache hits / misses][encode] decoder: [prefix] + [rolling acoustic context] -> new suffix only wire: -> append-only stable deltas ``` ## Encoder-window reuse Qwen3-ASR declares its independent encoder geometry in the multimodal processor. For Qwen3-ASR-0.6B, one complete window is 8 seconds and produces 104 encoder tokens. The generic audio-window builder: - extracts complete windows independently from the mutable tail; - expands one audio placeholder into per-window token ranges; - hashes the exact feature, attention mask, modality, and token geometry; - marks complete windows as cacheable; - marks the mutable tail `use_embedding_cache=False`; and - provides an explicit encoder batch key for variable-width audio features. A cache miss or eviction simply re-encodes the window. Cache reuse is therefore a performance optimization, not persistent session state and not a correctness dependency. The cache is model-owned only through declarative capability data: ```text Transcription adapter -> activation threshold, language gate, text-prefix limits Multimodal processor -> independently encodable window geometry Generic audio-window builder -> feature extraction, MM items, identity, cacheability Existing MM scheduler/cache -> lookup, miss batching, embedding assembly ``` There is no ASR-specific scheduler session, cache service, GPU lease, or model forward API. ## Append-only decoder streaming Each backend ASR request now uses `stream=True` when the realtime endpoint provides a callback. Partial decoder text is stripped of model-specific output markers, reconciled against cumulative or windowed transcript state, and sent only when it extends the text already published for that request. This is decoder-token-driven stable delta streaming, not a guarantee of one WebSocket event per tokenizer token. Local Agreement and suffix holdback may release several tokens together. If a completed decode revises a prefix that was already emitted, the request fails closed rather than sending a conflicting append-only transcript. No client changes are required. The wire protocol remains: ```text conversation.item.input_audio_transcription.delta conversation.item.input_audio_transcription.completed ``` ## Enablement ```bash python -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path Qwen/Qwen3-ASR-0.6B \ --enable-asr-encoder-window \ --asr-max-buffer-seconds 1800 ``` The client uses the existing realtime transcription session format and must declare a supported language before sending audio: ```json { "type": "session.update", "session": { "audio": { "input": { "format": {"type": "audio/pcm", "rate": 16000}, "transcription": { "model": "qwen3-asr", "language": "en" }, "noise_reduction": null, "turn_detection": null } } } } ``` `--asr-max-buffer-seconds` is the total accepted duration of one client item. Resident PCM is independently compacted after the encoder-window handoff. ## Alternatives evaluated Before selecting this implementation, four approaches were run under the same controlled setup: Qwen3-ASR-0.6B, one RTX 4090, Triton attention, identical native audio, 16 kHz mono PCM16 WebSocket input, and 2-second flood-mode appends. Processing time is measured from the first send to the completed event; it measures server work rather than realtime playback. "Word error" is the normalized edit distance from the published reference; lower is better. | Approach | Long-audio behavior | Result | Decision | |---|---|---|---| | Cumulative | Re-submit all received audio every 2 seconds | 178.5 seconds of audio took 153.240 seconds; 291.1 seconds did not finish within 300 seconds | Keep as the unchanged default for normal items | | PCM tail slicing | Submit a bounded PCM tail plus 2-second overlap | 178.5 seconds took 109.735 seconds with 39.81% word error; longer cases did not finish | Rejected: bounded audio alone did not bound decoder-prefix work or preserve quality | | Encoder-aligned rolling context | Reuse complete windows and continue from confirmed text | Completed 291/593/908/1687-second inputs in 16.947/31.721/51.097/90.195 seconds | Selected: fastest completed long-stream approach and no client protocol change | | Independent segment finals | Finalize disjoint segments without a cross-segment prefix | Completed the same inputs in 18.804/35.343/55.127/98.233 seconds | Not selected: slower and requires replaceable snapshot semantics | The long-input comparison was: | Input | Cumulative | PCM slicing | Encoder windows | Independent segments | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:| | LongLibriHeavy 178.5 s | 153.240 s, 12.04% error | 109.735 s, 39.81% | 9.911 s, 11.30% | 11.586 s, 11.30% | | TED Al Gore 291.1 s | >300 s, incomplete | >300 s, incomplete | 16.947 s, 3.87% | 18.804 s, 4.66% | | LongLibriHeavy 592.6 s | >405 s, incomplete | >397 s, incomplete | 31.721 s, 7.95% | 35.343 s, 7.74% | | TED Craig Venter 907.8 s | >405 s, incomplete | >405 s, incomplete | 51.097 s, 4.50% | 55.127 s, 4.75% | | Earnings22 EXCOF 1686.7 s | >397 s, incomplete | >397 s, incomplete | 90.195 s, 12.80% | 98.233 s, 10.55% | ## Current-head GPU validation Environment: - Commit: `135eb6cf66` - GPU: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090, 24,564 MiB - Model: `Qwen/Qwen3-ASR-0.6B`, snapshot `5eb144179a02acc5e5ba31e748d22b0cf3e303b0` - Attention backend: Triton - Python 3.12.13, PyTorch 2.9.1+cu128, Transformers 5.8.1 - 16 kHz mono PCM16 WebSocket input, 2-second appends - `--mem-fraction-static 0.75`, 100 MiB MM cache, 1800-second item cap All reported accuracy and performance cases below are complete, unmodified published source rows or source files. No reported audio was concatenated, cropped, padded, or silence-extended. For every successful WebSocket case: ```text concatenate(all transcription.delta text) == completed transcript snapshot events == 0 ``` Selected native-audio results on the current head: | Input | Duration | Server processing time | Reference word error | Result vs pre-streaming encoder-window path | |---|---:|---:|---:|---| | Qwen English demo | 15.1 s | 0.814 s | no published reference | Byte-identical | | LongLibriHeavy | 75.0 s | 4.245 s | 11.02% | Same normalized output and error rate | | LongLibriHeavy | 93.4 s | 4.899 s; fresh rerun 5.222 s | 7.98%; rerun 7.45% | One-word first-run variation; rerun matched baseline | | TED Al Gore | 291.1 s | 16.837 s | 3.87% | Normalized-exact | | TED Barry Schwartz | 1104.6 s | 58.373 s; rerun 58.485 s | 2.39% both runs | Normalized-exact, full opening and ending | | Earnings22 EXCOF | 1686.7 s | 88.901 s; rerun 88.367 s | 12.80% both runs | Full opening and ending; 0.20-0.22% run-to-run text variation | The 28-minute Earnings22 run issued 844 backend requests. Of 888,608 prompt tokens, 511,624 were cache hits (57.6%); uncached prompt work was 376,984 tokens. The server remained healthy after every request. ### Paced streaming receipt The 15.05-second Qwen demo was also sent at realtime pace instead of flood mode: - 8 backend ASR requests; - 37 existing `transcription.delta` events; - 0 snapshot events; - the joined deltas were byte-identical to the completed transcript; and - the first six deltas arrived between 2.171 and 2.208 seconds after the run began, while 4 seconds of audio had been sent. This confirms that output is emitted while one backend decode is still running, while preserving the endpoint's append-only transcript contract. ## Public audio sources - Qwen English demo: <https://qianwen-res.oss-cn-beijing.aliyuncs.com/Qwen3-ASR-Repo/asr_en.wav> - LongLibriHeavy: <https://huggingface.co/datasets/inesc-id/longlibriheavy> - TED-LIUM long form: <https://huggingface.co/datasets/distil-whisper/tedlium-long-form> - Earnings22: <https://huggingface.co/datasets/distil-whisper/earnings22> The benchmark manifest records dataset revisions, row ids, decoded-audio SHA256, wire-PCM SHA256, duration, sample rate, and reference text. Every result reported above uses one native source row or source file without local audio construction. ## Implementation | Area | Responsibility | |---|---| | `realtime/asr_processor.py` | Selects cumulative/windowed requests, reconciles decoder updates, advances absolute cursors, and compacts PCM | | `realtime/audio_buffer.py` | Maintains the per-item absolute PCM timeline | | `realtime/decoder_suffix.py` | Reconciles bounded decoder-prefix continuations without fuzzy deletion | | `realtime/session.py` | Owns WebSocket lifecycle and emits existing append-only events | | `streaming_asr.py` | Runs backend streaming generation and model-specific partial-output processing | | Transcription adapter | Declares activation, supported languages, decoder-prefix limits, and streaming postprocessing | | `audio_encoder_windowing.py` | Builds complete-window and mutable-tail multimodal items | | Base/Qwen multimodal processors | Provide generic construction plus model-config-derived window geometry | | `MultimodalDataItem` / `mm_schedule.py` | Support opt-in cacheability and producer-declared compatible miss batching | | `server_args.py` | Adds the off-by-default `--enable-asr-encoder-window` switch and rejects incompatible runtime topologies during startup | ## Validation ```text 37 focused CPU tests passed 20 parameterized subtests passed py_compile passed git diff --check passed Ruff format check passed PR-file pre-commit hooks passed (black-jupyter skipped; no notebooks changed) GPU: 15-1687-second unmodified native-audio regression complete TED-LIUM and Earnings22 long-form recordings 1105- and 1687-second long-form reruns realtime-paced decoder-streaming trace ``` ## Limits - Encoder windowing is experimental, off by default, English-only for Qwen3-ASR, and currently limited to a local single-GPU runtime. Enabling it on an incompatible topology fails at startup. - Operators must raise `--asr-max-buffer-seconds` above 60 seconds for the strategy to activate. - Stable deltas are driven by backend token streaming, but Local Agreement may group tokens. This is not raw one-event-per-token passthrough. - `finish_reason=length`, irreconcilable streamed-prefix revisions, and unsafe no-word-boundary continuation fail closed. - No timestamps, forced aligner, model-native streaming state, distributed encoder cache, or scheduler-owned ASR session is introduced. - Validation is bounded to Qwen3-ASR-0.6B on one RTX 4090 and does not establish universal multilingual quality or production capacity. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: **Missing `run-ci` label** -- add it to run CI tests.<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: **Blocked** -- `run-ci` is required first.<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:heavy_minus_sign: **No AMD PR run found for this commit**.<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: Rust Tree Core with Full/SWA/Mamba Components
signals.text: ## Motivation UnifiedTreeCoreInterface support in Rust (focus on FULL component-only in this PR for early review feedbacks) ## Motivation The Unified Radix Cache was split so the tree state machine lives behind `UnifiedTreeCoreInterface`, selected by `SGLANG_UNIFIED_RADIX_TREE_CORE_BACKEND` (default `python`). This PR adds a Rust implementation of that interface as an in-tree backend registered under `rust`, covering the Full attention component. The tree core does the per-request radix walks, lock bookkeeping, and eviction scans on the scheduler's critical path; moving it to Rust takes that work off the GIL and smooths tail latency, while cache orchestration (pools, controller, action application) stays in Python. **Review guide**: the PR is two commits. The first seeds the three main Rust files with their python counterparts commented out; the second replaces them with the Rust implementation, so its diff reads as the python-to-rust translation side by side. Files without a direct python counterpart arrive as new files in the second commit. ## Modifications ### `rust/mem-cache/` — the tree core crate **Tree state machine** - `src/unified_tree_core.rs` — match/insert walks (resumable inserts with action barriers), lock APIs, device/host eviction walks, tombstone-chain deletion, HiCache backup/load-back/prefetch specs, and the sanity checker. - `src/node.rs` — the tree node: per-(component × tier) value slots and child edges keyed `(namespace, page key)`, mirroring `RadixKey.child_key`. - `src/node_arena.rs` — node storage: freelist-recycled slots behind monotonic never-recycled `NodeId` handles, with a single root serving every namespace. - `src/value.rs` — the `NodeId`/`NodeIdx_` handle types and per-slot value state. **Keys and hashing** - `src/key.rs` — the child-key trait over unigram (`Vec<i64>`) and bigram/EAGLE (`(i64, i64)`) page keys. - `src/hash.rs` — per-page SHA-256 hash chains, bit-identical to the python/native hasher. **Eviction machinery** - `src/unified_lru_list.rs` — intrusive per-slot LRU lists with lock-aware walkers. - `src/evictable_node_set.rs` — O(1) evictable-leaf sets (swap-remove vector plus a slot lookup table). - `src/eviction_strategy.rs` — LRU/FIFO/FILO priority keys for the eviction heap. **Components** - `src/components/mod.rs` — the `TreeComponent` trait the per-attention components implement, plus shared dispatch helpers. - `src/components/full.rs` — the Full attention component: lock walks, eviction, and transfer commits. Only the `[Full]` set is enabled; SWA and Mamba follow later. - `src/component_type.rs` — the `ComponentType` boundary enum (`FULL`/`SWA`/`MAMBA` values shared with python). **Boundary** - `src/python_bindings.rs` — the PyO3 binding exposing unigram and bigram tree cores; component sets other than `[Full]` are rejected with a clear error. - `src/events.rs` — KV cache events (`BlockStored`/`BlockRemoved`/`AllBlocksCleared`) for cache-aware routing. - `src/error.rs` — typed tree-core errors. **Crate scaffolding** - `Cargo.toml` / `README.md` / `src/lib.rs` — standalone crate (links libtorch via `tch`; PyO3 behind a default feature, so `cargo test` runs `--no-default-features`), docs, and module wiring. - `src/tests/` — the unit suite mirroring `src/` one file per module (566 tests, including a randomized multi-namespace op-sequence fuzz with per-step sanity checks). ### `python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/rust_tree_core/` — the backend package - `__init__.py` — registers the `rust` backend factory; the extension import stays inside the factory so unselected installs pay nothing. - `adapter.py` — `RustUnifiedTreeCore`, satisfying `UnifiedTreeCoreInterface` over the binding (tagged-tuple action/transfer marshaling at the boundary). - `extension.py` — build-and-load shim: compiles the crate with cargo on first use, deriving libtorch and the Python headers from the running interpreter's torch install, and rpaths torch/lib into the cdylib. ### Wiring and tests - `python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/unified_cache/tree_core_registry.py` — `SGLANG_UNIFIED_RADIX_TREE_CORE_BACKEND=rust` lazy-registers the in-tree backend on first lookup (no import-order dependence). - `test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_rust_tree_core.py` — end-to-end smoke through the compiled extension: registry resolution, insert/match round trip, lock accounting, and namespace isolation; module-skips when cargo is absent. ## Verification - `cargo test --no-default-features`: 566 passed. - Smoke suite: 4 passed end-to-end, including the first-use cargo build path. ## Perf Measurement & Accuracy TBD ## Review and Merge Process 1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process). 2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers. 3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so. - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci` 4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32459402669](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32459402669)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32459402289](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32459402289)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32459402548](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32459402548)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [AMD] Enable gfx1250 Support
signals.text: ## Motivation AMD gfx1250 is a new GPU architecture that differs substantially from the existing gfx95x and gfx942 targets SGLang already supports. Several components require gfx1250-specific paths due to architectural differences: - **No MFMA/WMMA FP4 scale instructions** (`V_WMMA_SCALE_F32_32X16X128_F4`): the existing CK/ASM `fused_moe` and fp4 dense GEMM paths produce garbage or crash. - **Triton `tl.dot(fp8, fp8)` miscompiles** for contraction dim ≥ 128 on gfx1250 (verified correct at K=64, broken at K≥128), requiring bf16 upcasting in the MLA attention Triton kernels. - **`llvm.amdgcn.raw.buffer.*` buffer instructions are absent** on RDNA4 (gfx12): the `quick_all_reduce` kernel would fail to compile. - **aiter CK-backed kernels (rope, QK RMSNorm, etc.) do not build** against the gfx1250 ROCm 7.15 image's composable_kernel. - **TileLang CK-backed buffer addressing does not compile** on gfx1250, blocking the Sinkhorn/MHC path. - **`num_stages > 1` Triton pipelines miscompile** on gfx1250, causing NaN in block-FP8 matmuls. - **ROCm SDK is pip-installed** (not at `/opt/rocm`) on this new image, requiring build and runtime path fixups for AITER, TileLang, MORI, and SGLang itself. This PR brings up gfx1250 support for DSv4, DSR1, and GPT-OSS-120B models with MXFP4/FP8 quantization. ## Modifications ### Infrastructure & Docker (`docker/rocm.Dockerfile`, `scripts/ci/amd/amd_ci_install_dependency.sh`, `python/pyproject_other.toml`) - Added a new `gfx1250-rocm7_15` Docker build stage starting from `ubuntu:24.04` with pip-installed ROCm 7.15 SDK, PyTorch 2.11, and Triton 3.7. Includes path and symlink workarounds for a pip-based (non-`/opt/rocm`) ROCm SDK. - Added `GPU_ARCH_LIST_ARG` build-arg and made `PYTORCH_ROCM_ARCH` configurable; per-arch `TRITON_COMMIT_DEFAULT` env vars. - Added gfx1250-specific AITER build path (`ENABLE_CK=0`, pip `--no-build-isolation`) and MORI build path using `CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH` for the ROCm SDK. - Added gfx1250-aware TileLang `ROCM_PATH` override during CMake build. - Updated Triton rebuild logic to preserve the installed version string (workaround for ROCm 7.15 / [rocm-systems#7643](https://github.com/ROCm/rocm-systems/issues/7643)). - Renamed `SETUPTOOLS_SCM_PRETEND_VERSION` → `SGLANG_VERSION` to avoid leaking SGLang's nightly version into AITER's version. - Added `compressed-tensors==0.16.0` pin to `runtime_common` (supports torch ≥ 2.10) and dropped the old per-`srt_hip` `==0.15.0` pin. - CI install script: ROCm-version-aware AITER rebuild (`pip --no-build-isolation` for ROCm ≥ 7.15), MORI `CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH` fix, and MORI commit extraction validation. ### Core utility (`python/sglang/srt/utils/common.py`) - Added `is_gfx1250_supported()` (cached) to detect AMD RDNA4 by `gcnArchName`. - Extended `mxfp_supported()` to include `"gfx1250"`. ### sgl-kernel (`sgl-kernel/setup_rocm.py`, `sgl-kernel/csrc/allreduce/quick_all_reduce_base.h`) - Added `gfx1250` to the allowed arch list in `setup_rocm.py`; gfx1250 shares the `E4M3` FP8 type and the 128KB dynamic smem budget with gfx950. - Guarded `llvm.amdgcn.raw.buffer.load/store.v4i32` declarations behind `#if !defined(__gfx1250__)`, providing stub no-ops for RDNA4 where those intrinsics don't exist. ### Attention kernels (`python/sglang/kernels/ops/attention/`) - **`decode_attention.py`**: Do not downcast `q` to `fp8` before the QK dot; instead upcast K to `q`'s dtype (`bf16`) for the dot product, avoiding the gfx1250 fp8 dot bug at K≥128. Also keep softmax weights `p` in fp32 for the P·V accumulation (recovers GSM8K accuracy ~0.82 → ~0.92 on gfx1250 R1). - **`extend_attention.py`**: Same fp8 upcast fix and fp32 P·V fix for the prefill extend/unified kernels. - **`dsv4/unified_kv_kernels/paged_decode.py`**: On gfx1250, dispatch DSv4 sparse decode attention to `aiter.ops.triton.attention.pa_decode_sparse.pa_decode_sparse` (the triton path) instead of the custom Triton implementation. - **`dsv4/unified_kv_kernels/paged_prefill.py`**: Disable the OPUS (gfx950 ASM) prefill path on gfx1250. ### MoE gate JIT kernel (`python/sglang/kernels/jit/csrc/moe/moe_fused_gate.cuh`) - Widened `__shfl_down_sync` mask from `0xFFFFFFFF` to a 64-bit `0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFULL` on gfx1250 (which requires a 64-bit sync mask), while staying 32-bit on all other arches. ### Layernorm (`python/sglang/kernels/ops/layernorm/mhc.py`, `python/sglang/srt/layers/layernorm.py`) - On gfx1250, use aiter's Triton RMSNorm and `rmsnorm2d_fwd_with_add` instead of the CK-backed aiter equivalents (which do not build). - Added pure-torch (`_hc_split_sinkhorn_torch`) and Triton (`_hc_split_sinkhorn_triton`) implementations of the Sinkhorn MHC kernel, dispatched on gfx1250 since TileLang's CK-backed addressing does not compile there. ### Quantization – FP8 (`python/sglang/kernels/ops/quantization/fp8_kernel.py`, `python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/fp8.py`, `python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/fp8_utils.py`) - **`fp8_kernel.py`**: Added `_w8a8_block_fp8_matmul_gfx1250`, a gfx1250-specific block-FP8 matmul that: (1) upcasts fp8 operands to bf16 before `tl.dot`, (2) uses only `num_stages=1` (no SW pipelining), and (3) avoids modulo-wrap index tricks that miscompile on gfx1250. Selected automatically when `_is_gfx1250` is set. - **`fp8_utils.py`**: Force `_use_aiter = False` on gfx1250 (CK/MFMA-dependent aiter quant/GEMM kernels cannot run), directing gfx1250 to the pure-Triton block-FP8 path. Extended `triton_w8a8_block_fp8_linear` to accept pre-quantized `(input, input_scale)` from gfx1250's fused quant ops (skipping re-quantization). - **`fp8.py`**: On gfx1250, use `moe_shuffle_scale` (n32k4 layout) instead of the gfx950 `shuffle_scale` (e8m0 layout) for FP8 MoE weight scales. Respect the `AITER_FORCE_A8W4` flag to select the triton a8w4 kernel shuffle layout. ### Quantization – MXFP4 Quark schemes (`python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/quark/schemes/`) - **`quark_w4a4_mxfp4.py`**: On gfx1250 with `AITER_FORCE_A8W4=1`, dequantize FP4 weights to bf16 at load time (since no dense fp4 GEMM is available) and run a plain bf16 linear forward. Includes a pure-Python MXFP4 e2m1 → bf16 dequantization LUT. - **`quark_w4a4_mxfp4_moe.py`**: On gfx1250, use `moe_shuffle_scale` (n32k4 layout) for W4A4 MoE weight scales (instead of `e8m0_shuffle`). Shuffle weights with the (16,16) aiter layout when `AITER_FORCE_A8W4` is set. - **`quark_w4a8_mxfp4_moe.py`**: Added a dedicated gfx1250 W4A8 MoE path (`_use_gfx1250_w4a8`): bypasses the aiter CK/ASM fused_moe entirely; uses aiter's triton `moe_gemm_a8w4` kernel with a contraction-major, gate/up-interleaved, unshuffled weight layout. Weight preparation (`_process_weights_gfx1250`) and forward (`aiter_w4a8_gfx1250_forward` in new file `aiter_mxfp4_w4a8_moe.py`) are implemented separately from the gfx950 path. ### New file: `python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/fused_moe_triton/aiter_mxfp4_w4a8_moe.py` - Implements MXFP4 W4A8 GPT-OSS MoE forward for gfx1250 via `moe_gemm_a8w4`: routing, manual activation gather (in-kernel TDM gather disabled on gfx1250), static-FP8 downcast, two-GEMM (gate_up + down) execution with fused SwiGLU, and scatter back to token order. ### RoPE (`python/sglang/srt/layers/rotary_embedding/factory.py`) - Fall back from aiter's CK rope kernels to SGLang's native rope on gfx1250 (aiter rope does not build on this arch). ### Communicator / fused quant (`python/sglang/srt/layers/communicator.py`) - On gfx1250, use `fused_rms_fp8_group_quant` (triton, group_size=hidden_size = per-token) instead of aiter's CK `rmsnorm_quant` / `add_rmsnorm_quant` kernels. ### Sampler (`python/sglang/srt/layers/sampler.py`) - Disable aiter's greedy sample kernel on gfx1250 (not supported), falling back to `torch.argmax`. ### Capture mode (`python/sglang/srt/model_executor/runner_utils/capture_mode.py`) - Disable `torch.compile` during CUDA graph capture on gfx1250 (compilation + capture together triggers issues on this arch). ### MLA attention (`python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_common/attention_forward_methods/forward_mla.py`, new `triton_qk_rmsnorm.py`) - On gfx1250 (`AITER_FORCE_A8W4=1`), substitute the aiter `fused_qk_rmsnorm` (CK-backed, doesn't build) with a self-contained Triton RMSNorm or pure-torch fallback from the new `triton_qk_rmsnorm.py`. - Fixed the RoPE skip condition to check membership in `FORWARD_ABSORB_CORE_ATTENTION_BACKENDS` (not a string equality check), preventing an incorrect empty-K bug on non-aiter backends. ### DSv4 decoder layer (`python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_v4.py`, `deepseek_common/utils.py`, `amd/deepseek_v4_fused_mhc.py`) - Extended all `_is_gfx95_supported` guards that gate MXFP4 fused quant, MQA q/k-norm, post-attention layernorm fused rmsnorm, and the fused MHC post/pre path to also include `_is_gfx1250_supported`. - On gfx1250, the fused MHC path is enabled by `SGLANG_OPT_FUSE_MHC_POST_PRE` alone (no TileLang dependency), and the aiter Triton `try_fused_hc_post_pre` is used at all token batch sizes (no M-threshold cap, since there is no TileLang fallback). - gfx1250 does not skip the post-layernorm step after the Triton MHC kernel (since `norm_fused=False` for the aiter path). ### C4 attention indexer (`python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/dsv4/indexer.py`) - Added `_use_torch_fn` guard so the `SGLANG_FP8_PAGED_MQA_LOGITS_TORCH` env var correctly prevents the 1D c4sl unsqueeze on gfx1250. ### Server args (`python/sglang/srt/server_args.py`) - Track `_mem_fraction_static_set_by_user`: when the user explicitly sets `--mem-fraction-static`, skip the automatic 0.85 scaling for `aiter` backend with long contexts (instead, emit a warning so the user knows what is happening). ## Accuracy Tests Passed E2E accuracy tests of DSv4, DSR1, and GPT-OSS-120B. GPT-OSS-120B > AITER_FORCE_A8W4=1 ENABLE_CK=0 SGLANG_USE_AITER=1 SGLANG_USE_AITER_MOE_GU_ITLV=1 SGLANG_USE_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN=1 python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model-path /dockerx/model/gpt-oss-120b-w-mxfp4-a-fp8/ --trust-remote-code --tp 1 --prefill-attention-backend triton --decode-attention-backend aiter --max-running-requests 1024 --mem-fraction-static 0.9 --disable-radix-cache --page-size 64 DSR1 > ENABLE_CK=0 SGLANG_USE_AITER=1 AITER_FORCE_A8W4=1 AITER_GROUPED_FORCE_SPLIT_K1=1 SGLANG_MOE_SHUFFLE_GFX1250=1 ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_QUANTIZATION=NONE SGLANG_AITER_FP8_PREFILL_ATTN=0 SGLANG_AITER_MLA_PERSIST=0 SGLANG_INT4_WEIGHT=0 SGLANG_MOE_PADDING=1 SGLANG_SET_CPU_AFFINITY=1 SGLANG_ROCM_FUSED_DECODE_MLA=0 SGLANG_USE_ROCM700A=1 AITER_GROUPED_CONTIGUOUS_TOKEN_THRESHOLD=16 python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model-path /dockerx/model/DeepSeek-R1-0528-MXFP4 --tensor-parallel-size 1 --trust-remote-code --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000 --mem-fraction-static 0.90 --chunked-prefill-size 16384 --attention-backend triton --max-running-requests 128 --kv-cache-dtype auto --page-size 64 DSv4-Flash > SGLANG_DEFAULT_THINKING=1 AITER_GROUPED_CONTIGUOUS_TOKEN_THRESHOLD=16 SGLANG_DSV4_REASONING_EFFORT=max SGLANG_USE_ROCM700A=0 SGLANG_HACK_FLASHMLA_BACKEND=unified_kv_triton AITER_BF16_FP8_MOE_BOUND=0 AITER_FORCE_A8W4=1 SGLANG_USE_AITER_MOE_GU_ITLV=0 SGLANG_OPT_FUSE_MHC_POST_PRE=0 ENABLE_CK=0 SGLANG_USE_AITER=1 AITER_GROUPED_FORCE_SPLIT_K1=1 python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model-path /dockerx/model/DeepSeek-V4-Flash --trust-remote-code --tp 1 --attention-backend dsv4 --page-size 256 --mem-fraction-static 0.60 --swa-full-tokens-ratio 0.15 --disable-shared-experts-fusion --tool-call-parser deepseekv4 --reasoning-parser deepseek-v4 --chunked-prefill-size 8192 --cuda-graph-max-bs 256 --max-running-requests 256 --disable-radix-cache --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 ## signals.title: [CPU] Fix NUMA/core binding for DP ranks
signals.text: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation <!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. --> Before this PR, `ModelRunner.init_threads_binding` picked the NUMA node / core group for a worker using `tp_rank`. Under DP, DP rank 0 and DP rank 1 both resolve to tp_rank=0 and get bound to the same NUMA node/cores instead of being spread across the machine. This PR fixes this incorrect binding. ## Modifications <!-- Detail the changes made in this pull request. --> 1. `init_threads_binding` now takes `numa_index` (the worker's global device id) and `world_size = dp_size * tp_size * pp_size`, instead of `tp_rank` and `tp_size`, so every rank across every DP replica maps to a distinct NUMA node / core group. Removed the `world_size == len(threads_bind_list)` equality assert for the explicit `SGLANG_CPU_OMP_THREADS_BIND` path, replacing it with only the per-rank bounds check. This permits the router-mode case (local `world_size=1`, multi-group bind string) while still catching a bind list that's too short. 2. `test/registered/cpu/test_subblock_sparse_attention.py`, added in https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/34680, fails in Xeon CPU CI with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'imageio'`: importing it pulls in `sglang.multimodal_gen`, which needs `diffusers/imageio/addict` from the diffusion extra. Install `.[diffusion]` instead of `.` in `docker/xeon.Dockerfile` — the extra is already declared in `python/pyproject_cpu.toml`. Note this grows the CI image. ## Accuracy Tests <!-- If this pull request affects model outputs (e.g., changes to the kernel or model forward code), provide accuracy test results. --> ## Speed Tests and Profiling <!-- If this pull request impacts inference speed, provide benchmarking and profiling results. --> ## Checklist - [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. signals.title: [NVIDIA][comm] Merge EP+MoE-TP post-experts all-reduces into one _TP reduction
signals.text: ## Problem statement With `--tp-size 4 --ep-size 2`, the post-experts reduction requires two all-reduces over orthogonal groups (`_MOE_EP` then `_MOE_TP`). The allreduce fusion gate was skipping *both* once `fuse_mlp_allreduce` was published, then Observed as GSM8k accuracy 0.012 on `nvidia/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-NVFP4` with silently returning under-reduced activations with no error. Observed as GSM8k accuracy 0.012 on `nvidia/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-NVFP4` with the fused residual+LN kernel reduced over only `_MOE_EP` (2 of 4 peers) — silently returning under-reduced activations with no error ## Motivation Under hybrid MoE EP+TP (`moe_ep_size > 1` **and** `moe_tp_size > 1`), allreduce fusion silently produces under-reduced activations. There is no error — the model just returns garbage. Reproduced on `main`, 4×GB200: ```bash python -m sglang.launch_server --model-path Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B \ --tp-size 4 --ep-size 2 --host 0.0.0.0 --port 30000 ``` ```bash curl -X POST http://localhost:30000/v1/chat/completions \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{ "model": "Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B", "messages": [ { "role": "user", "content": "Where is capital city of France? Answer in one short word." } ], "chat_template_kwargs": { "enable_thinking": false }, "max_tokens": 8, "temperature": 0 }' ``` The completion is garbage unless `--enforce-disable-flashinfer-allreduce-fusion` is passed. `--ep-size 4` and `--ep-size 1` are both fine. ### Root cause With `--tp-size 4 --ep-size 2`, the post-experts reduction spans **two** disjoint groups (`Qwen3MoeSparseMoeBlock.forward_normal`): ``` moe_expert_parallel_all_reduce -> _MOE_EP moe_tensor_model_parallel_all_reduce -> _MOE_TP ``` `_MOE_EP × _MOE_TP` is an orthogonal decomposition of the TP world (`moe_tp_size = tp_size // moe_ep_size // moe_dp_size`), so both reductions are needed to cover all 4 ranks. When the decoder publishes `fuse_mlp_allreduce`, `should_skip_post_experts_all_reduce()` skips **both** of them — it keys off `should_skip_mlp_all_reduce()`, which does not distinguish the EP path from the TP path. The reduction is then supposed to be absorbed by the next layer's fused residual+RMSNorm, but that kernel reduces over a **single** group: the MoE fusion workspace, which `ensure_workspace_initialized()` rendezvouses on `_MOE_EP` when `moe_ep_size > 1`. Net effect: the MoE output is reduced over 2 of the 4 required ranks. `--ep-size 4` (`moe_tp_size == 1`) and `--ep-size 1` (`moe_ep_size == 1`) are unaffected, because there a single group already covers every peer. This is pre-existing on `main` and independent of any in-flight FlashInfer work. It was surfaced while reviewing #30700 (thanks @mmangkad for the hybrid EP+TP question that led here). ### Graph illustration ## Why hybrid EP+TP specifically With `--tp-size 4 --ep-size 2`, `moe_tp_size = 4 // 2 // 1 = 2`, and the MoE output needs reducing over two orthogonal subgroups that together tile the TP world: ``` rank: 0 1 2 3 ep_rank: 0 0 1 1 <- which expert shard it holds tp_rank: 0 1 0 1 <- which FFN shard it holds _MOE_EP: {0,2} {1,3} _MOE_TP: {0,1} {2,3} ``` output needs reducing over two orthogonal subgroups that together tile the TP world: ``` rank: 0 1 2 3 ep_rank: 0 0 1 1 <- which expert shard it holds tp_rank: 0 1 0 1 <- which FFN shard it holds _MOE_EP: {0,2} {1,3} _MOE_TP: {0,1} {2,3} ``` Either reduction alone covers 2 of the 4 ranks; both are required. ``` layer N (MoE output) | layer N+1 ----------------------------------------------|------------------------ main experts --> [EP skipped] [TP skipped] -----|--> fused AR + RMSNorm | workspace group = _MOE_EP | sums {0,2} only -> WRONG this PR experts --> AR(_MOE_EP) --> AR(_MOE_TP) ----|--> RMSNorm {0,2} {0,1} | all 4 ranks summed -> ok ``` Publishing `fuse_mlp_allreduce` makes `should_skip_post_experts_all_reduce()` drop **both** reductions, because it keys off that flag without distinguishing the EP path from the TP path. The next layer's fused residual+LN then reduces over a single group — the MoE fusion workspace, which `ensure_workspace_initialized()` rendezvouses on `_MOE_EP` when `moe_ep_size > 1`. Half the peers never contribute, and the result is wrong without any error. No other configuration breaks, because no other configuration has two distinct subgroups: ``` ep_size=1 -> moe_tp_size == tp_size, _MOE_TP *is* _TP (parallel_state.py:2483) ep_size=4 -> moe_ep_size == tp_size, _MOE_EP *is* _TP (parallel_state.py:2454) ep_size=2 -> neither aliases _TP -> the only broken case ## Modifications `LayerCommunicator.should_fuse_mlp_allreduce_with_next_layer()` now returns `False` when `moe_ep_size > 1 and moe_tp_size > 1`. Fusion is only valid when one group covers every peer of the reduction, which is not the case here. Both post-experts all-reduces then run inline as usual. The guard sits before the backend-specific checks, so it covers the aiter fusion branch too — that path reduces over a single group for the same reason. Attention-side fusion is untouched: it uses the attention-TP workspace (`use_attn_tp_group=True`) whose group spans the full TP world, and it is gated on `apply_flashinfer_allreduce_fusion` alone, not on `fuse_mlp_allreduce`. New unit test `test/registered/unit/layers/test_layer_communicator_fusion_gate.py` (CPU, 3 cases): hybrid EP+TP must not fuse; pure-TP and pure-EP must still fuse. The hybrid case fails on pre-fix code and passes on the fix; the other two guard against the gate degrading to always-off. After fix: ``` {"id":"0dc05777d22f4efdbbba2ba896d4d196","object":"chat.completion","created":1785440815,"model":"nvidia/Qwen3-Coder-480B-A35B-Instruct-NVFP4","choices":[{"index":0,"message":{"role":"assistant","content":"Paris","reasoning_content":null,"tool_calls":null},"logprobs":null,"finish_reason":"stop","matched_stop":151645}],"usage":{"prompt_tokens":25,"total_tokens":27,"completion_tokens":2,"prompt_tokens_details":null,"reasoning_tokens":0},"metadata":{"weight_version":"default"}} ``` ## Accuracy Tests - `--tp-size 4 --ep-size 2` on 4×GB200 with Qwen3-30B-A3B: garbage before, correct completions after, **without** `--enforce-disable-flashinfer-allreduce-fusion`. - `--ep-size 4` and `--ep-size 1` re-checked for no regression. - `python -m pytest test/registered/unit/layers/test_layer_communicator_fusion_gate.py` — 3 passed. signals.title: [MLX] Upgrade to Torch 2.13/MLX 0.32+ and redesign the Torch-MLX tensor bridge
signals.text: ## Motivation MLX 0.32 can import Torch MPS allocations directly, while Torch 2.13 changes the runtime and DLPack edge cases that the Apple Silicon integration must support. The existing bridge stages MPS tensors through CPU memory, obscures borrowed-versus-owned lifetimes, and pays payload-sized copies. Separately, diffusion's `SGLANG_USE_MLX` norm override is not selected by normal MPS `CustomOp` dispatch; forcing those norms through Torch-MLX crossings is slower end to end. This PR upgrades the `srt_mps` runtime, fails fast on unsupported Torch/MLX pairs, separates owned copies from scoped zero-copy borrows, and removes the unreachable diffusion-only MLX fallback. It does not replace the existing SRT MLX runner; the stacked [yeahdongcn/sglang#7](https://github.com/yeahdongcn/sglang/pull/7) consumes these bridge primitives while redesigning that backend. ## Modifications - Update `srt_mps` in `python/pyproject_other.toml` to Torch 2.13.0, MLX >= 0.32.0, TorchVision 0.28.0, TorchAudio 2.11.0, and TorchCodec 0.15.0. The versions stay directly in `srt_mps`, matching the existing extra layout; `all_mps` inherits them through `srt_mps`. MLX keeps a 0.32.0 minimum but has no upper bound; startup accepts newer stable MLX releases. TorchAudio 2.11 remains intentional and was validated with the tested Torch 2.13 MPS stack. CPU and standalone `diffusion_mps` dependency lists are unchanged. - Move the SRT MLX version/device validation to the earliest model-independent `ServerArgs` bootstrap. With `SGLANG_USE_MLX=1`, SGLang requires stable Torch 2.13.x and stable MLX >= 0.32.0. Older MLX, Torch outside 2.13.x, and rc/dev builds fail before model path resolution/downloads and before the dummy-model short circuit. With the flag unset, importing SGLang still does not import MLX. - Redesign `tensor_bridge.py` around explicit ownership and batching: - `torch_to_mlx` creates and materializes MLX-owned storage when the result must outlive its Torch source. - `MlxTensorView` and `borrow_torch_tensors` provide persistent and batched zero-copy MPS borrows while retaining every Torch storage owner. - `mlx_call` and `mlx_call_multi` validate the target before work, fence Torch producers once, keep all borrowed inputs alive through lazy evaluation, evaluate ordinary multi-output results at one shared `mx.eval` boundary, batch the additional materialization boundary required by negative-stride outputs, and export them through DLPack. - `mlx_to_torch` uses evaluated DLPack views for MPS and explicit CPU views. Positive-stride layouts, including CPU float64, remain zero-copy. Negative-stride MLX views are materialized because Torch 2.13's DLPack importer otherwise aborts the process instead of raising a Python exception; unsupported CPU dtypes fail instead of silently narrowing. This PR intentionally owns these shared Torch-MLX bridge primitives. The stacked MPS redesign in [yeahdongcn/sglang#7](https://github.com/yeahdongcn/sglang/pull/7) consumes them for Torch-owned model weights and provider outputs, while its provider-specific invalidation callbacks and phase timing stay in that PR. - Remove `mps_fallback.py`, route diffusion MPS kernels to native Torch fallbacks, and use `F.layer_norm`/`F.rms_norm` instead of the old manual decomposition. The shared fallback remains compatible with both the default Torch 2.11 and CPU-backend Torch 2.12 stacks. RMSNorm preserves the optional-bias and input-dtype contracts even with fp32 parameters. The removed rotary and scale/shift entries were already aliases to Torch implementations; only the norm entries had MLX-specific implementations. - Remove diffusion's `SGLANG_USE_MLX` runtime handling and clarify in the existing documentation that the variable applies only to SRT serving. SRT keeps its existing `SGLANG_USE_MLX=1` opt-in. - Add Torch 2.13-compatible Triton import-stub symbols used by Inductor on MPS. - Rebase the branch onto upstream `main` at `978244d67148`; update VAE and Transformer component loaders to the upstream unified residency API so MPS layerwise offload remains valid after the upstream loader refactor. The diffusion MLX norm path is intentionally dropped after tracing and measurement. `CustomOp.dispatch_forward()` routes MPS to `forward_native`, so the legacy MLX override is unreachable in the normal production graph. Sana instrumentation confirmed zero legacy entrypoint calls, and forcing all 58 norms per DiT forward through MLX was slower end to end. Isolated large fp32 LayerNorm microbenchmarks sometimes favored MLX by a few percent, but the result was not robust across the common fp16/bf16 cases and did not justify repeated framework crossings. A future fully MLX-resident diffusion path can be evaluated separately. ## Accuracy Tests - `PATH="$PWD/sglang-metal/bin:$PATH" SGLANG_USE_MLX=1 HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 ./sglang-metal/bin/python test/run_suite.py --hw mlx --suite stage-a-unit-test-mlx` - **21/21 registered test files passed locally** on Apple M1 at PR head `c1f34a81d1`, including bridge, startup runtime gate, Triton-stub, and diffusion fallback coverage. - The focused bridge/runtime/diffusion-loader bundle passed **121 tests plus 36 subtests** after the rebase. - All four new test files are registered in `stage-a-unit-test-mlx`. `test_diffusion_torch_fallback.py` is additionally registered in `base-a-test-cpu`, `base-b-test-cpu`, and `base-b-test-cpu-arm64`. - The same six fallback UTs passed **6/6** in isolated Torch 2.11.0 and 2.12.0 CPU environments, including fp16/bf16 inputs with fp32 parameters. - Runtime tests verify Torch 2.12/2.14, MLX 0.31, and Torch/MLX rc/dev builds are rejected, while stable Torch 2.13 patch releases and stable MLX releases from 0.32.0 onward (including future minor versions) are accepted. Incompatible versions abort `ServerArgs` creation even for `model_path="dummy"`; missing MLX, unavailable PyTorch MPS, and unavailable MLX Metal each produce actionable startup errors. The disabled path constructs `ServerArgs` without importing MLX. - Bridge ownership checks cover owned/scoped/persistent lifetimes, source mutation and deletion, single-fence batched borrows, shared-eval multi-output calls, bfloat16/non-contiguous views, CPU float64 and unsupported dtypes, autograd detachment, invalid-target fail-fast behavior, and negative-stride materialization in an abort-safe subprocess. - SRT serving smoke with local `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B`: both `SGLANG_USE_MLX=1` and the no-env Torch-MPS path returned **200** from `/health` and `/generate`. For prompt `The capital of France is` with greedy 8-token decoding, both paths returned identical output token IDs `[12095, 13, 576, 6722, 315, 9625, 374, 1083]` and text `Paris. The capital of France is also`. - Sana 600M, prompt `A small red cube on a plain white background`, seed 42, 256x256, 4 steps: native Torch output and the hypothetical all-MLX norm output remained visually consistent (PSNR 41.95 dB; max pixel delta 50). The final `mlx_call` image was byte-identical to the earlier explicit- keepalive MLX image. The ordinary Sana path recorded 58 Torch norm calls per DiT forward and zero legacy norm-fallback entrypoint calls. After the rebase, a native Torch-MPS Sana smoke with the same 256x256/4-step configuration produced a valid RGB PNG in 24.87s with 6.33GB peak memory. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Environment: Apple M1, macOS 26.5.2, Torch 2.13.0, MLX 0.32.0. All timings include the required producer/consumer synchronization. The operation table reports end-to-end norm-call timings, including bridge/export and synchronization, rather than raw kernel-only timings. It is one representative median-after-warmup run; an independent rerun preserved the common-Sana ordering but flipped whether large-fp32 MLX was slightly ahead or behind. | Case | Torch native | MLX owned copy | MLX scoped borrow | |---|---:|---:|---:| | Sana RMSNorm `(1,300,1152)` fp32 | 230 us | 676 us | 259 us | | Sana LayerNorm `(1,256,1152)` bf16 | 254 us | 913 us | 324 us | | Flux LayerNorm `(1,4096,3072)` fp32 | 2508 us | 4763 us | 2441 us | Bridge A/B directly calls the final `mlx_call(lambda a: a, tensor)` API against the pre-change CPU-staging implementation at the branch merge base (Apple M1, Torch 2.13.0, MLX 0.32.0). The table reports the range of per-batch p50 values across three independent batches; each batch used 5 warmups and 20 measured samples with producer/consumer synchronization: | Logical tensor | dtype / payload | Old CPU-staging p50 range | Final `mlx_call` p50 range | Minimum paired speedup | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:| | `(4096,4096)` | fp32 / 64 MiB | 32.134-57.424 ms | 0.0410-0.0871 ms | 368.8x | | `(4096,4096)` | bf16 / 32 MiB | 10.301-34.715 ms | 0.0293-0.0418 ms | 351.2x | | `(4096,8192)` | bf16 / 64 MiB | 16.896-22.184 ms | 0.0407-0.0617 ms | 273.7x | The old MPS round-trip staged payload through CPU/NumPy in both directions. The final `mlx_call` path aliases the Metal allocation through DLPack, removing the payload-sized copies; the synchronized wrapper/barrier cost was 29-87 us across these repeats. The same-shape bf16 case is 32 MiB because each element uses two bytes; the final row adds a true 64 MiB bf16 payload. This zero-copy result applies to the scoped-borrow API, not to an MLX array that must own its storage after the call. For that ownership contract, the 64 MiB fp32 materialized copy is about 4.08 ms versus about 60 us for a scoped borrow. This is why the API separates owned and borrowed semantics instead of exposing an unchecked `copy=False` default. Final-API Sana 4-step E2E forced-MLX experiment using `mlx_call` for all 58 norms per DiT forward (clean paired repeat): | Metric | Torch native | MLX scoped borrow | MLX penalty | |---|---:|---:|---:| | Denoising step median | 720.18 ms | 1170.40 ms | +62.5% | | DiT forward median | 375.06 ms | 581.92 ms | +55.2% | | Steady DiT median (drop first 2) | 353.42 ms | 581.92 ms | +64.7% | A second same-configuration measurement had higher Torch variance and a smaller penalty (+20.6% step, +21.9% DiT), but MLX was slower in both runs. ## Checklist - [x] Formatted with repository pre-commit hooks. - [x] Added and ran registered unit tests. - [x] Registered the shared diffusion fallback in CPU CI. - [x] Updated Apple Metal and diffusion documentation. - [x] Included accuracy and speed evidence above. - [x] CPU dependency pins remain unchanged. ## Review and Merge Process This is a draft for review of the ownership contract and the diffusion path decision. Please review the Torch/MLX lifetime semantics first; CI should run the MLX, CPU, JIT-kernel, and multimodal-generation change paths before promotion. In particular, the draft-gated MLX, Xeon CPU, and ARM64 CPU jobs must complete before this PR is marked ready. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32544631916](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32544631916)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32544631670](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32544631670)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32544631820](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32544631820)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->
