Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation The Triton GDN prefill path normalizes Q and K with two separate `l2norm_fwd` launches. Qwen3.5 GDN uses equal Q/K head layouts, so both normalizations can be computed in one Triton launch. This change reduces GDN prefill launch overhead on AMD GPUs while preserving the existing two-kernel implementation as the fallback. <!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. --> ## Modifications - Add `fused_l2norm_qk` to normalize compatible Q/K tensors in one Triton launch. - Preserve runtime token-count behavior with `do_not_specialize` to avoid recompilation by sequence length. - Enable automatic fused routing only when: - the platform is AMD; - execution is in the GDN `chunk_gated_delta_rule` path; - Q/K are GPU BF16/FP32 tensors with identical shape and contiguous layout. - Preserve two existing `l2norm_fwd` calls for: - non-AMD platforms; - asymmetric Q/K row layouts; - non-contiguous or otherwise incompatible tensors. - unbenchmarked head dimensions larger than 512; - the launch-bound `head_dim=512, rows<32` corner. - Add AMD/CUDA correctness tests, explicit fused/fallback dispatch tests, and a focused benchmark. No KDA, Mamba, full-attention, CuTe DSL, FlashInfer, CPU, NPU, or XPU path is changed. <!-- Detail the changes made in this pull request. --> ## Accuracy Tests ```bash PYTHONPATH=python python3 -m pytest -q \ test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/test_fused_gdn_l2norm.py \ test/registered/attention/test_chunk_gated_delta_rule.py ``` <!-- If this pull request affects model outputs (e.g., changes to the kernel or model forward code), provide accuracy test results. --> ## Speed Tests and Profiling Representative equal-head Qwen3.5 GDN shapes (`head_dim=128`): | Tokens | Local heads | Fused (us) | Separate (us) | Latency reduction | |---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 16 | 2 | 3.34 | 5.32 | 37.2% | | 16 | 8 | 3.41 | 5.30 | 35.7% | | 257 | 8 | 4.87 | 6.50 | 25.1% | | 1024 | 2 | 4.94 | 6.49 | 23.9% | | 1024 | 8 | 10.73 | 13.35 | 19.6% | | 1024 | 16 | 17.67 | 21.02 | 16.0% | Across the tested Qwen3.5 equal-head `D=128` cases, fused normalization reduced median latency by approximately **16–38%**. Expanded BF16 sweep: - tokens: 1–16384; - local heads: 1–64; - head dimensions: 64/128/256/512; - 135 total shape combinations. | Head dim | Auto-enabled shapes | Minimum speedup | Median speedup | Maximum speedup | |---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 64 | 27 | 1.13× | 1.19× | 1.48× | | 128 | 63 | 1.11× | 1.15× | 1.48× | | 256 | 27 | 1.06× | 1.14× | 1.52× | | 512 (`rows>=32`) | 14 | 1.03× | 1.09× | 1.14× | | Model | Parallelism | Scenario | ISL | OSL | Concurrency | Requests per cycle | Metric | Paired mean improvement | |---|---:|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|---:| | 27B | TP1 | Short-prefill online latency | 256 | 8 | 1 | 64 | Mean TTFT | +0.79% | | 27B | TP1 | Long-prefill online latency | 8192 | 8 | 1 | 32 | Mean TTFT | +0.016% | | 27B | TP1 | Concurrent serving throughput | 4096 | 128 | 64 | 64 | Input throughput | +0.19% | | 397B | TP8 | Short-prefill online latency | 256 | 8 | 1 | 64 | Mean TTFT | +0.99% | | 397B | TP8 | Long-prefill online latency | 8192 | 8 | 1 | 64 | Mean TTFT | +0.048% | | 397B | TP8 | Concurrent serving throughput | 4096 | 128 | 64 | 64 | Input throughput | +0.013% | <!-- If this pull request impacts inference speed, provide benchmarking and profiling results. --> ## Checklist - signals.title: [XPU] Add CustomOp.forward_xpu fallback to forward_native
signals.text: dispatch_forward() routes the xpu platform to self.forward_xpu, but the base class never defined it. Since dispatch_forward() runs in __init__, any subclass without its own override raises AttributeError at construction, breaking model loading on Intel GPUs: AttributeError: 'LayerNorm' object has no attribute 'forward_xpu' Route xpu to forward_native, matching the existing forward_tpu/npu/oot fallbacks. No dispatch branch is modified, so CUDA/ROCm/NPU/MUSA/CPU behavior is unchanged. ## Motivation Fixes #33292 . CustomOp.dispatch_forward() maps the detected platform to a forward_<backend> method and caches it in __init__. Every backend has a base-class fallback — hip/cpu/musa → forward_cuda, tpu/oot/npu → forward_native — so a subclass only needs forward_native to work everywhere. The xpu branch (custom_op.py:83-84) was the sole exception: it returns self.forward_xpu, which was never defined. Because dispatch_forward() is called from __init__ (custom_op.py:27), this fails at construction, so it breaks model loading rather than inference: >>> from sglang.multimodal_gen.runtime.layers.layernorm import LayerNorm >>> LayerNorm(hidden_size=64) AttributeError: 'LayerNorm' object has no attribute 'forward_xpu' Five shipped subclasses relied on the missing method — LayerNorm (layernorm.py:329), RMSNormNoWeight (layernorm.py:316), GeluAndMul (activation.py:75), FusedLayerNormScaleShiftGateSelect01 (fused_scale_shift_gate.py:20), FusedResidualLayerNormScaleShiftGateSelect01 (fused_scale_shift_gate.py:85). All implement forward_native. Eight other subclasses define their own forward_xpu, which is why this went unnoticed. Present since #12484 (7bc1dae095). ## Modifications Just introduced forward_xpu in python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/layers/custom_op.py. Verified after the patch that all six branches dispatch_forward() can return resolve to a base-class method. ## Accuracy Tests This PR does not touch kernels or model forward code, so outputs are unchanged on any platform that was already binding correctly (CUDA/NPU single-GPU). ## Speed Tests and Profiling No kernel or scheduling changes, so there is no expected throughput change on platforms that were already binding correctly. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32488284480](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32488284480)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32488284296](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32488284296)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32488284549](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32488284549)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [fa] Make the FlashAttention backend extensible by subclasses
signals.text: ## Motivation `FlashAttentionBackend` is hard to specialize without copying it. Three things a subclass may need are not exposed today, leaving only the options of duplicating the backend or patching module globals: the logsumexp the kernel already computes, per-layer control of split-KV, and the choice of FA4 build. This adds a seam for each. All three are no-ops for current behavior. ## Modifications **`return_lse` on `forward_extend` / `forward_decode`.** The kernel already computes the logsumexp for the cascade merge and the backend discards it, and the forwards accept neither `return_lse` nor `**kwargs`, so a caller that needs the softmax normalizer has no way to get it. With `return_lse=True` they return `(output, lse)`, `lse` shaped `[total_q, num_heads]` (the varlen kernel emits it head-major). `_check_return_lse` raises on the combinations the paged path cannot serve — non-FA4, MLA, `fa_skip_kv_cache`, cross-attention, context parallelism, local and cascade attention — instead of returning a quietly wrong tensor. Defaults to `False`. **`_resolve_num_splits(layer, forward_batch, is_swa_layer)`.** Split-KV was read from `self.num_splits` at 13 kernel arguments, making it one value for the whole run. It is now resolved once per forward and threaded through, so a subclass can vary it per layer or per batch — for example forcing `1` on sliding-window layers, which degenerate when split. The base implementation returns `self.num_splits`. Since FA3's `scheduler_metadata` is precomputed from `self.num_splits`, the existing `sched_meta` gate also requires `num_splits == self.num_splits` so a subclass cannot reuse a schedule built for a different count; always true for the base class. **Kernel entry points as class attributes.** `flash_attn_with_kvcache` and `flash_attn_varlen_func` are bound on the class and the 15 invocations go through `self._flash_attn_*`, so a subclass can substitute a different FA4 build. ## Accuracy Tests Two cases added to `test/registered/attention/unittests/dense/test_fa4.py`, self-contained so the shared dense kit is untouched: - `test_return_lse` — calls the forwards directly, since `return_lse` is a backend-level contract and the `RadixAttention` dispatcher's custom-op schema cannot carry it, then checks the output and the LSE against a causal fp32 reference for MHA extend and GQA decode, plus the `[total_q, num_heads]` shape. - `test_return_lse_rejects_unsupported_paths` — the guarded paths raise, and the check is a no-op when the LSE is not requested. Both pass on a GB300 with no skips. Perturbing the returned LSE by a constant fails `test_return_lse` on 100% of elements, confirming the comparison is load-bearing. Not covered: windowed layers, because the dense harness leaves `attention_chunk_size` unset, so a `sliding_window_size` case is skipped for `fa4` before it asserts anything. The FA3 `sched_meta` gate was also not exercised, as the FA3 dense suite skips on that hardware; it is inert for the base class, whose hook returns `self.num_splits`. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not applicable. No behavior changes for existing callers: `return_lse` defaults to `False`, `_resolve_num_splits` returns `self.num_splits`, the `_flash_attn_*` attributes are bound to the same functions the module already imported, and the new `sched_meta` condition is always true unless a subclass varies the split count. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: **Missing `run-ci` label** -- add it to run CI tests.<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: **Blocked** -- `run-ci` is required first.<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:heavy_minus_sign: **No AMD PR run found for this commit**.<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [Diffusion][Refactor] Refactor and unify RoPE execution for DiT models using RotaryEmbedding based on CustomOp
signals.text:
## Motivation Currently, DiT models across SGLang call various ad-hoc functions to apply Rotary Position Embeddings. The choice of function depends on the target hardware device, argument types, and model-specific configurations. Furthermore, internal branches within these functions often perform device type checks again, leading to code fragmentation and duplication. To clean up and unify this behavior, this PR leverages SGLang's existing `CustomOp` mechanism to enhance the core `RotaryEmbedding` class located in `sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/layers/rotary_embedding/base.py`. This abstraction allows models to invoke RoPE through a single, unified interface without writing device-specific handling inside model code, significantly simplifying codebase maintainability and cross-platform execution. ## Modifications This PR is a continuation of [PR #31453](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/31453). Modified 9 key files to implement unified RoPE dispatch and propagate complex frequencies: ### 1. `python/sglang/multimodal_gen/configs/pipeline_configs/qwen_image.py` - Updated `get_freqs_cis()` to return both standard `cos_sin_cache` tuples (`freqs_cis`) and pre-calculated complex frequency tuples (`freqs_complex`). - Propagated `freqs_complex` through `_prepare_cond_kwargs` and pipeline stages. - Added Sequence Parallelism sharding for `img_complex` via `shard_rotary_emb_for_sp()`, enabling pre-computed complex frequencies to be passed directly to the Qwen Image DiT model. ### 2. `python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/layers/rotary_embedding/base.py` - Implemented `forward_npu`, `forward_cuda`, and `forward_native` backend methods inside the `RotaryEmbedding`. - Extended signatures to flexibly accept any RoPE inputs: `complex_freqs`, `cos`/`sin`, or 2D `cos_sin_cache`. - Integrated unified dispatching across lower-level implementations: - `_apply_rotary_emb_complex` (for complex multiplication). - `_apply_rotary_emb` (for standard PyTorch RoPE). - `apply_flashinfer_rope_qk_inplace` (for optimized CUDA execution). - Standardized tensor dimension expectations: `query` and `key` as 4D `[batch, seq_len, num_heads, head_size]`, `complex_freqs` as 3D `[num_tokens, 1, head_size // 2]`, and `cos`/`sin` as 2D `[num_tokens, head_size // 2]`. - Fixed a batch-broadcast bug: raw cos/sin DiT-style calls previously flattened [batch,seq,...] to [batch*seq,...] incorrectly for batch_size > 1. - Added an NPU fast path via torch_npu.npu_rotary_mul for is_neox_style=True, and a complex-multiply derivation path for is_neox_style=False on NPU/native, where no fused kernel exists otherwise. ### 3. `python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/layers/layernorm.py` - Added optional `freqs_complex` parameter to `apply_qk_norm_rope` and `apply_qk_norm_with_optional_rope`. - Replaced FlashInfer calls in the fallback path with the unified `RotaryEmbedding`. - Preserved the existing CUDA fused QK-Norm + RoPE kernel (`fused_inplace_qknorm_rope`) to ensure zero performance regression on CUDA. - Added a module-level _QK_NORM_ROPE_DICT cache keyed by (head_dim, is_neox) to avoid reconstructing RotaryEmbedding on every call. ### 4. `python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/models/dits/mova_video_dit.py` - Refactored `SelfAttention.forward` to implement the usage of `RotaryEmbedding`. ### 5. `python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/models/dits/qwen_image.py` - Updated `QwenImageCrossAttention` to extract `freqs_complex` from `cross_attention_kwargs`. - Passed `img_complex` and `txt_complex` into `apply_qk_norm_with_optional_rope`, enabling Qwen Image DiT cross-attention layers to leverage complex RoPE. ### 6. `python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/models/dits/glm_image.py` - Updated `GlmImageAttention` with `RotaryEmbedding` class usage. - Replaced the `_apply_rotary_emb` and `apply_flashinfer_rope_qk_inplace` functions with `self.rotary_emb()` call . ### 7. `python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/models/dits/flux.py` - Updated `FluxAttention` with `complex_freqs` computing and forwarding them into `apply_qk_norm_with_optional_rope`. ### 8. `python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/models/dits/flux_2.py` - Updated `Flux2Attention` with `complex_freqs` computing and forwarding them into `apply_qk_norm_with_optional_rope`. ### 9. `python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/models/dits/joy_image.py` - Updated `MMDoubleStreamBlock` with `complex_freqs` computing and forwarding them into `apply_qk_norm_with_optional_rope`. ## Tests The changes were tested on openmoss/MOVA-360p, GLM-Image, black-forest-labs/FLUX.1-dev, unsloth/FLUX.2-dev, jd-opensource/JoyAI-Image-Edit-Diffusers, nv-community/Cosmos3-Super-Text2Image and MusePublic/Qwen-image models.
Accuracy test, speed tests and profiling for Mova ### Mova video generation (the same as before changes): https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/396ce85d-df45-432a-a7bf-6d87b1fdb6ee ### 1. SGLang Server Launch Command ```bash sglang serve --model-path $(pwd)/mova_video_360p --pipeline-class-name MOVAPipeline --num-gpus 4 --ring-degree 1 --ulysses-degree 4 --performance-mode memory --dit-layerwise-offload --dit-offload-prefetch-size 0.1 --text-encoder-cpu-offload true --vae-cpu-offload true --enable-torch-compile --warmup-mode server --vae-tiling --vae-sp ``` ### 2. signals.title: [Model] Support Ling-3.0-flash (BailingMoeV3)
signals.text: ## Motivation Day-0 support for [inclusionAI/Ling-3.0-flash](https://huggingface.co/inclusionAI/Ling-3.0-flash) (`BailingMoeV3ForCausalLM`, `model_type=bailing_hybrid`): a hybrid MoE architecture interleaving KDA linear attention (with a safe-gate lower bound) and MLA, with MTP (NEXTN) and DSPARK speculative decoding support. ## Modifications - `BailingMoeV3ForCausalLM` model (`bailing_hybrid` config): KDA + MLA hybrid layers, 512-expert MoE, and MTP (NEXTN). - DSPARK support for the KDA hybrid path: graph-folded draft proposal, fused KDA chain-verify kernel, and DSA token-to-KV pool sizing. - KDA safe gate propagation through the Triton decode/target-verify kernels and their call sites, matching fused verification. - `ling3` reasoning and tool-call parsers. - BF16, FP8, compressed-tensors INT4, and native MXFP4 checkpoint support on Hopper and Blackwell. - Exactness, fusion-gate, quantization, and parser tests. ## Validation All serving runs kept decode CUDA Graph enabled and used the default graph sizing. No run used `--disable-cuda-graph` or `--cuda-graph-max-bs-decode`. ### Quantized checkpoints Full GSM8K uses 1,319 questions. Performance uses 80 exact-length random requests at ISL/OSL 8192/1024 with concurrency 1 and 16; throughput includes input and output tokens per second per GPU. | GPU | format | GSM8K | stop rate | throughput/GPU (c1 / c16) | P50 TTFT ms (c1 / c16) | P50 TPOT ms (c1 / c16) | default graph range | |---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | H200 | INT4 | 95.30% | 100% | 1,159 / 7,184 | 205.96 / 1,891.74 | 3.68 / 8.16 | through batch 218 | | H200 | MXFP4 | 96.29% | 100% | 709 / 5,215 | 305.23 / 2,725.52 | 6.05 / 11.17 | through batch 227 | | B200 | INT4 | 96.74% | 99.70% | 482 / 1,344 | 641.41 / 6,202.62 | 8.72 / 48.01 | through batch 305 | | B200 | MXFP4 | 96.29% | 99.62% | 785 / 7,933 | 127.97 / 1,117.16 | 5.60 / 7.98 | through batch 314 | INT4 selects Marlin on H200 and the graph-compatible Triton WNA16 path on B200. MXFP4 routed experts use the native FlashInfer runner on both GPUs. The B200 MXFP4 checkpoint also contains block-FP8 dense/shared projections, which use the Triton FP8 GEMM backend to avoid an unsupported FlashInfer FP8 tactic without converting the routed experts. BF16 and FP8 were rerun on H200 and B200 after the quantization changes. All four combinations served with CUDA Graph enabled, completed generation, and passed the 20-example GSM8K regression gate with 100% stop rate. ### Speculative decoding Ling-3.0-flash BF16, 4x B200 TP4, `temperature=1.0 / top_p=0.95`, thinking on, full GSM8K, `max_tokens=8192`: | spec decoding | score | stop rate | error rate | |---|---:|---:|---:| | DSPARK | 96.66% | 99.77% | 0.00% | | MTP (NEXTN) | 96.44% | 99.62% | 0.00% | Non-stop finishes are long reasoning outputs reaching `max_tokens`, not repetition loops. ## Checklist - [x] Format code with pre-commit. - [x] Add unit tests and register them in CI. - [x] Validate serving correctness, stop rate, and accuracy on H200 and B200. - [x] Publish deployment recipes and benchmark results in #34363. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32359477855](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32359477855)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32359477828](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32359477828)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32359477784](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32359477784)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [AMD] Add Work-Centric (Lean) Attention: a persistent-CTA decode kernel for long-context serving
signals.text: ## Motivation The standard flash-decode ("SplitK") attention kernel parallelizes decode by splitting each sequence's KV cache into chunks and assigning chunks to GPU compute units (CUs). While effective at short context, it leaves performance on the table in two common serving regimes: - **Long-context, low-batch** — std's grid is `batch × head-tiles × num_splits` with a fixed split count, so a single (or few) long sequence cannot generate enough KV-split work to fill all CUs: many CUs sit idle while the few launched programs each grind through a long serial KV loop, and decode-step latency grows **roughly linearly** with context, making the workload occupancy-starved, not bandwidth-bound. As context windows reach 64K–128K+, attention dominates the decode step here. - **Ragged batches** — with mixed sequence lengths, SplitK cannot rebalance a long request's work onto the CUs freed by short requests, so a few stragglers set the step latency. **Work-Centric Attention (WCA / "Lean")** launches a fixed persistent grid sized to the device CU count and derives its KV-tile schedule on-device from `kv_indptr`, cooperatively splitting long sequences across CTAs (work-stealing) so no CU idles. Decode-attention latency stays **nearly flat** as context grows (1.06–1.30× E2E throughput even on uniform batches) and absorbs raggedness for free (up to 1.52× throughput, 3.62× lower ITL). Lean is numerically identical to the standard kernel and ships behind a conservative auto-gate that enables it only where it wins — including by default under CUDA graphs — so existing workloads are unaffected. Validated on **AMD MI355X (gfx950)** across GQA (Qwen2.5-7B, Llama-3.1-8B) and MLA (DeepSeek-R1-MXFP4, TP=4, fp8 KV). Also re-validated on **AMD MI300X (gfx942)** at the same 1×CU grid across GQA (Qwen2.5-7B, Llama-3.1-8B) and MLA (proxied with DeepSeek-V2-Lite, fp8 KV, since fp4/MXFP4 GEMM is gfx950-only). ## Modifications A minimal, mostly-additive change (6 files, ~+1540 lines) on the ROCm/Triton backend. Almost all of it is new code; the only edits to existing paths are the `forward_decode` dispatch hook and the `decode_attention_fwd` signature. The standard decode path is untouched when Lean is inactive. | File | Change | |------|--------| | `python/sglang/kernels/ops/attention/decode_attention.py` (+822) | The Lean kernel (`_lean_attention_decode_kernel`) and its launch/dispatch helpers. `decode_attention_fwd` gains an `enable_lean` parameter and early dispatch to Lean. Supports bf16/fp16 and **fp8** KV (fold `k_scale` into `sm_scale`, cast `q → K.dtype` for the fp8×fp8 MMA, dequantize rope-split `kpe`, apply `v_scale`), and both contiguous and **paged** KV (`kv_loc // page_size` / `% page_size` addressing). Auto-gate: `lean_decode_seqlen_gate` (eager) and `lean_capture_policy` (CUDA-graph capture). | | `test/registered/kernels/test_lean_attention.py` (+440) | CI gating test on the MI35x AMD per-commit suite (`stage-b-test-1-gpu-small-amd-mi35x`): parity vs standard SplitK for bf16 (cos > 0.999), fp8 (cos > 0.99), and paged KV (cos > 0.999), plus gate/policy logic. | | `python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/triton_backend.py` (+119) | Resolve `enable_lean_attention` in `forward_decode` (explicit override → auto-gate → kill-switch); allocate the Lean scratch buffers (Mp/Lp/Op/locks) for the eager and CUDA-graph paths. | | `benchmark/lean_kernel_sweep.py` (+150) | Kernel-level Lean-vs-standard (SplitK) sweep: both GQA head configs × full batch/context grid, per-call latency, speedup, cosine parity, and eager-gate decision; writes a CSV. | | `python/sglang/srt/server_args.py` (+4) | `--enable-lean-attention` flag (`Optional[bool]`, default `None` = auto-gate). | | `python/sglang/srt/environ.py` (+11) | Two env vars: `SGLANG_DISABLE_LEAN_ATTENTION` kill-switch (force the standard kernel) and `SGLANG_FORCE_LEAN_GRID_CU_MULT` (persistent-grid size multiplier, default `1.0` = one CTA per CU; a knob for grid A/B without a rebuild). | **Design:** - **Persistent grid.** Launches `total_programs = device CU count` CTAs — one CTA per CU (rounded to whole XCDs under the ROCm XCD remap). One CTA per CU maximizes the KV work-tiles handled per CTA, so each CTA's cross-CTA combine/atomic reduction amortizes more useful work; oversubscribing (e.g. 2 CTAs/CU) halves tiles-per-CTA and inflates that reduction, regressing high-batch decode (measured on MI300X/gfx942 and confirmed on MI355X/gfx950). The grid is independent of batch×heads×splits, so it is CUDA-graph capturable and a single captured grid replays across batch sizes. - **On-device work-stealing.** Each CTA computes its slice of the global KV-tile work list from `kv_indptr`; long sequences are cooperatively split across CTAs. The schedule is derived from `kv_indptr` **at replay**, so a captured graph adapts to the real per-step sequence lengths and raggedness — no host sync, no per-step relaunch. - **Auto-gate.** The default (`None`) resolves to a concrete decision before launch; explicit `True`/`False` overrides it. Because Lean is a win only in specific regimes, the gate operates in two modes: - *Eager decode*, where real `seq_lens` are known: `lean_decode_seqlen_gate` keys a length threshold on query-head parallelism (`tiles = ceil(num_q_heads / min(16, kv_group))`, i.e. how well the standard kernel already fills the CUs), relaxed as batch grows. - *CUDA-graph capture*, where per-step lengths are not yet known: `lean_capture_policy` makes the bake decision from capture-time-known signals (`batch`, `tiles`, `is_mla`) — bake GQA/MHA at `batch ≥ 16`, MLA at `batch ≥ 8`, and never for heavy TP shards (`tiles < 4`). Lean's fixed grid then adapts to the actual lengths at replay. - **Shape/dtype coverage.** MHA, GQA, and MLA (rope-split `qk_head_dim != v_head_dim`); bf16/fp16/fp8 KV; contiguous and paged KV. Falls back to the standard kernel for unimplemented features (logit capping, attention sinks, xAI temperature, score modification), so results are never silently wrong. **Usage:** - Default (`None`): auto-gate — Lean turns on automatically where it wins (including by default under CUDA graphs). No flag needed. - Force on: `--enable-lean-attention` (with `--attention-backend triton`). - Force off: `--enable-lean-attention=False`, or `SGLANG_DISABLE_LEAN_ATTENTION=1`. ## Accuracy Tests **Test configuration:** | | | |---|---| | **Hardware** | 1× AMD Instinct MI355X (256 CUs, gfx950, 288 GB HBM3E) | | **Software** | ROCm 7.2.0, PyTorch 2.9.1+rocm7.2.0, Triton 3.7.0 (AMD wheel) | | **Models (head shapes)** | Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct (GQA 28Q/4KV, D=128) · Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct (GQA 32Q/8KV, D=128) | | **Method** | Isolated decode-attention call; compare Lean vs standard SplitK output over three KV formats — bf16, fp8 (e4m3, per-tensor scales), and paged (4-D buffer, scattered slots) | | **Metric** | Cosine similarity of the two output tensors | **Command** (the registered CI gating test): ```bash python3 -m pytest test/registered/kernels/test_lean_attention.py -v # Per shape: standard = decode_attention_fwd(..., enable_lean=False) # lean = decode_attention_fwd(..., enable_lean=True, lean_Mp/Lp/Op/locks=...) # cos = F.cosine_similarity(o_lean.flatten().float(), o_std.flatten().float(), dim=0) ``` **Results.** Lean matches the standard kernel across every tested configuration: | KV format | Configs | Result | |-----------|:-------:|:-------| | bf16/fp16 | 59 cells (2 models × 6 batches × 5 contexts, less Llama b32×128K) | **cosine = 1.0000** (bit-identical) | | fp8 e4m3 (per-tensor scale) | 2 models × {b1,b8} × {8K,32K} | **cosine > 0.99** (fp8 quantization noise only) | | paged (4-D, scattered slots) | 2 models × page_size {16, 64} | **cosine > 0.999** | Every measured configuration is bit-identical in bf16 (the one unmeasured cell, Llama batch-32 × 128K, exceeds the microbenchmark's single contiguous KV tensor — it is a harness limit, not a kernel result). The committed CI gating test (`test_lean_attention.py`) reproduces the bf16, fp8, and paged parity checks on the MI35x per-commit suite. Because output is numerically equivalent, downstream generation quality is unchanged. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Unless noted otherwise, the tables below are on **1× MI355X** (gfx950); the dedicated **MI300X (gfx942)** subsection re-runs the same suites on that arch. Both: ROCm 7.2.0, PyTorch2.9.1+rocm7.2.0, **Triton 3.7.0** (AMD wheel; the production ROCm wheel — the stock rocm7.2 image's Triton 3.5.1 inverts the crossover and must not be used for Lean benchmarking). The **baseline is the Triton backend's own standard decode kernel, not AITER**: both arms use `--attention-backend triton` and dispatch through the same `decode_attention_fwd`, differing only in the `enable_lean` branch, so this is a clean Lean-vs-standard A/B. ### Kernel-level (isolated decode attention, speedup = standard ÷ lean) Direct kernel call, fp16, random Q/K/V, `page_size=1`; batch ∈ {1,2,4,8,16,32} × context ∈ {8K,16K,32K,64K,128K}. **Command:** `SGLANG_FORCE_LEAN_GRID_CU_MULT=1.0 python3 benchmark/lean_kernel_sweep.py` **Qwen2.5-7B (28Q/4KV):** | batch | 8K | 16K | 32K | 64K | 128K | |------:|---:|----:|----:|----:|-----:| | 1 | 0.46× | 0.92× | **1.86×** | **3.30×** | **5.33×** | | 8 | 0.59× | **1.04×** | **1.28×** | **1.59×** | **1.95×** | | 32 | **1.78×** | **1.99×** | **2.21×** | **1.74×** | **1.77×** | **Llama-3.1-8B (32Q/8KV):** | batch | 8K | 16K | 32K | 64K | 128K | |------:|---:|----:|----:|----:|-----:| | 1 | 0.79× | **1.47×** | **2.41×** | **3.56×** | **5.92×** | | 8 | **1.46×** | **1.82×** | **1.97×** | **2.18×** | **1.71×** | | 32 | **2.13×** | **2.29×** | **1.74×** | **1.73×** | — | **Bold** = Lean is faster at the kernel level (speedup ≥ 1×). Peak **5.33× (Qwen) / 5.92× (Llama)** at batch=1 / 128K; speedup grows superlinearly with context (SplitK's idle-CU penalty scales with length, Lean's stays flat) and the crossover falls with batch. The production auto-gate turns Lean on around the **end-to-end** break-even (later than the isolated-kernel crossover), so it enables the long-context / larger-batch cells and keeps the standard kernel for short-context low-batch. (The batch-32 × 128K Llama cell exceeds the microbenchmark's single contiguous KV tensor and is not measured; real serving uses a paged KV pool and is unaffected — see the E2E tables.) ### End-to-end serving — GQA Full-model serving, closed-loop / fixed-batch (`num-prompts == max-concurrency == reqs`, `--request-rate inf`), CUDA graphs on (`--cuda-graph-bs 1 2 4 8 16 32`), `--seed 42` (both arms see the identical batch). `--random-range-ratio r` samples per-request prompt **and** output lengths in `[r·ctx, ctx]`, so `ratio < 1` = ragged. Rows include batch 1 to show the low-batch long-context win and the auto-gate's enabled region (GQA `batch ≥ 16`); below b16 the standard kernel runs by default. The win grows with raggedness (lower ratio) and context: peak **1.52× throughput** (Llama b32/16K r0.1) and **3.62× / 2.91× lower median / p99 ITL** (Llama b32/65K r0.1). **Uniform batches are also faster at every size** (1.06–1.30× throughput, 1.28–1.93× lower ITL) — e.g. b1 uniform 65K: Qwen 1.27× tps / 1.63× ITL, Llama 1.24× / 1.59×; b32 uniform 65K: Qwen 1.07× / 1.66×, Llama 1.16× / 1.93×. **Command** (per arm; identical `--seed 42`): ```bash # Server — baseline prepends `SGLANG_DISABLE_LEAN_ATTENTION=1`; Lean is the default (no flag) or `--enable-lean-attention`: python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model-path Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct \ --attention-backend triton --disable-radix-cache --context-length 73728 \ --mem-fraction-static 0.85 --cuda-graph-bs 1 2 4 8 16 32 --port 30000 # Client — per (B, ctx, ratio): python3 -m sglang.bench_serving --backend sglang --model Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct \ --dataset-name random --random-input-len <ctx> --random-output-len 512 \ --random-range-ratio <1.0|0.5|0.1> --num-prompts <B> --max-concurrency <B> --seed 42 ``` ### End-to-end serving — MLA (DeepSeek-R1-MXFP4, TP=4, fp8 KV) Same closed-loop methodology, `--tp-size 4 --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3`. Rows include batch 1 to show the gate boundary and where Lean helps vs regresses. At **batch 1 it regresses** (0.83× tps, 0.60× ITL), confirming the gate is correct — MLA's splitK is faster at low batch, so the auto-gate keeps it off there. **Command:** ```bash python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model-path <deepseek-r1-mxfp4> --tp-size 4 \ --trust-remote-code --attention-backend triton --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 \ --disable-radix-cache --mem-fraction-static 0.8 --context-length 163840 --port 9000 python3 -m sglang.bench_serving --backend sglang --model <deepseek-r1-mxfp4> --dataset-name random \ --random-input-len <ctx> --random-output-len 512 --random-range-ratio <1.0|0.5|0.1> \ --num-prompts <B> --max-concurrency <B> --seed 42 ``` ### Default path (auto-gate, no flag) The tables above are Lean-vs-baseline in the region the auto-gate enables. Confirming the **default** path (no `--enable-lean-attention`) reproduces them under CUDA graphs — 3 arms, Qwen GQA, 64K, ragged `ratio 0.1`, `--seed 42`: `auto` (no flag) tracks `forced` where the capture policy bakes Lean (b≥16) and stays at the standard kernel below the threshold: | batch | baseline tok/s | auto tok/s | forced tok/s | auto tracks | |------:|---------------:|-----------:|-------------:|:------------| | 8 | 79.55 | 79.53 | 88.83 | baseline (Lean off, b<16) | | 16 | 92.67 | **103.76** | 107.53 | forced (Lean on) | | 32 | 96.28 | **112.77** | 115.07 | forced (Lean on) | So the throughput/latency gains are delivered by default, with no configuration change. (At b8 the `forced` arm is already faster than baseline — 88.83 vs 79.55, ITL 1.98× — so the b≥16 GQA capture threshold is deliberately conservative and leaves some b8 headroom on the table; tightening it is future work.) ### MI300X (gfx942, 304 CUs) All tests: **1× AMD Instinct MI300X** (304 CUs, gfx942, 192 GB HBM3), ROCm 7.2.0, PyTorch2.9.1+rocm7.2.0, **Triton 3.7.0** (AMD wheel), CUDA graphs on, `--seed 42`, identical harnesses, commands, and auto-gate as above. Parity is arch-independent and passes unchanged (bf16 cos 1.0000, fp8 >0.99, paged >0.999). 1.71 | | Llama-3.1-8B | 32 | 0.5 | 32 | 45749 | 32K–65K | 385 | 12313 | 1.12 | 1.65 | 1.32 | | Llama-3.1-8B | 32 | 0.1 | 32 | 34369 | 6K–65K | 288 | 9226 | **1.14** | **2.14** | **1.83** | At `1×CU` the enabled region wins across the board on MI300X — including uniform batches (neutral-to-positive throughput, better tail latency). Peak **1.14× throughput** and **2.14× / 1.83× lower median / p99 ITL** (Llama b32×64K ragged). The MI355X auto-gate thresholds transfer unchanged. #### End-to-end serving — MLA (proxy: DeepSeek-V2-Lite, fp8 KV) `amd/DeepSeek-R1-MXFP4` **cannot run on MI300X**: fp4/MXFP4 matmul is a CDNA4 (gfx950) feature — gfx942 has no fp4 GEMM (0 `AFP4WFP4` configs; `aiter` marks the OCP fp4 dtypes "gfx950+"). MLA is therefore proxied on MI300X with **DeepSeek-V2-Lite** (16B MoE, MLA, fp8 KV, TP=1), same ragged sweep. ⚠️ V2-Lite has 16 query heads vs R1's 128, so its low-batch CU-saturation differs — this transfers to the R1 MLA gate only *qualitatively*. | B | ratio | ctx | tps× | ITL× | p99× | |--:|------:|----:|-----:|-----:|-----:| | 8 | 1.0 | 65K | 1.04 | 1.12 | 1.12 | | 8 | 0.5 | 65K | 0.99 | 1.16 | 1.12 | | 8 | 0.1 | 65K | 0.94 | 1.09 | 0.90 | | 16 | 1.0 | 65K | 1.07 | 1.29 | 1.28 | | 16 | 0.5 | 65K | **1.09** | **1.50** | **1.48** | | 16 | 0.1 | 65K | 1.06 | 1.37 | 1.70 | | 32 | 1.0 | 65K | 1.08 | 1.36 | 1.36 | | 32 | 0.5 | 65K | **1.14** | **1.75** | **1.74** | | 32 | 0.1 | 65K | 1.12 | 1.67 | 1.55 | b1 loses (0.31–0.42× — Lean's fixed grid is pure overhead at V2-Lite's 16-head batch-1 decode); b8 is borderline (~parity to 1.04×); **b16/b32 win** (up to 1.14× tps, 1.75× ITL). The clean-win region on this proxy is **b ≥ 16** (b8 borderline). Note this differs from R1 on MI355X, where the 128-head decode makes batch 1 a *win* at 1×CU — so the exact `is_mla` batch threshold is a function of head count and should be set from the R1 calibration, not this proxy. (b1 rows omitted from the table.) ## Conclusion Lean Attention is a flat-latency, work-stealing decode kernel for long-context and ragged serving on ROCm — up to **~5.9× at the kernel level**, **1.52× end-to-end throughput** and up to **3.6× lower median / 2.9× lower p99 ITL** on GQA, and **1.13× tps / 2.41× lower ITL** on MLA at batch ≥ 8 — at zero accuracy cost (bit-identical bf16; fp8/paged parity within quantization noise). It supports MHA/GQA/MLA, bf16/fp16/fp8 KV, and contiguous or paged KV, and runs behind a conservative, CUDA-graph-aware auto-gate that turns it on only where it wins (delivering the gains on the default path) and leaves the standard kernel in place everywhere else — so there is no regression risk. **Reproduce:** kernel sweep — `SGLANG_FORCE_LEAN_GRID_CU_MULT=1.0 python3 benchmark/lean_kernel_sweep.py`; CI parity (bf16/fp8/paged) — `pytest test/registered/kernels/test_lean_attention.py`; end-to-end — the `sglang.launch_server` + `sglang.bench_serving` commands in each subsection above. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32543424146](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32543424146)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32543423922](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32543423922)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32543424154](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32543424154)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [Spec] Fix Dspark and Dflash state divergence across TP rank
signals.text: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation Related to: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/33289 To fix https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/33289 bug, upgrade NCCL to the newest version (2.30.7). When TP > 1, Dspark makes serveral sampling decisions on reach rank: 1. The draft Markov chain samples proposal tokens step by step (with in-graph philox noise introduced since https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33298) 2. Target verify derives `correct_len` / `bonus` / `cap_trim_lens` 3. Prefill samples `next_token_ids` In order to maintain the speedup, SGLang skips cross-rank sync of sampled tokens by default (I found the comment here: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/python/sglang/srt/layers/sampler.py#L496). So nothing forces these values to agree. Once one rank commits a different token or accept length, sequence lengths and KV state drift apart and a later collective deadlocks (demonstrated by fault injection in the Accuracy Tests section below). ## Modifications Broadcast rank 0's sampling decisions before they affect state. The idea follows the existing `verify_lens` handling in `dspark_planner.py` and the EAGLE proposals in https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/29003 and https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/31478: 1. Broadcast every Markov proposal token in **both** eager and graph-folded sampling. Sync only at the end of a draft block is too late because each step depends on the previous token. 2. Broadcast `correct_len`, `bonus`, and `cap_trim_lens` in the eager verify path and the captured verify epilogue, before finalization, token output, or KV commit. Separate `all_reduce(MIN)` calls could combine fields from different ranks. 3. Broadcast prefill `next_token_ids` before entering the draft path. `DsparkTpSync` in `dspark_tp.py` (newly added file) uses the TP group's PyNCCL communicator. Process-group collectives cannot be captured in CUDA graphs, and using the model's existing TP communicator preserves collective ordering across eager and captured execution. With DP attention, it uses `attn_tp_group`, matching `verify_lens_broadcast_group` in original `dspark_planner.py`. TP=1 is a no-op. The reason why I don't match RNG seeds is because ranks can still diverge if they consume different numbers of random values, and it does not cover non-RNG differences. In addition, for TP > 1, this add `gamma + 3` broadcasts of a `[bs]` tensor per decode step, all within the captured graphs. ## Accuracy Tests All tests below on following configs: - 2 DGX Sparks - TP=2 - DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 with 131k context - Decode CUDA graphs and folded sampling enabled - Add https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33407 code. It fixes an unrelated bug for SM12x sparse-MLA topk dispatch crash at boot. Dspark + DeepSeek V4 Flash cannot start on DGX Sparks without it. - **NCCL 2.30.7** for SGLang's PyNCCL communicator via `SGLANG_NCCL_SO_PATH` (torch's bundled 2.28.9 wedges this workload's graph/eager mix with or without this patch; a separate problem from this fix) For accuracy test, we run`python3 -m sglang.test.few_shot_gsm8k --num-questions 200` (temp=0): accuracy 0.965, invalid 0.000. This is expected since there's no mathematical changes. To demonstrate the failure mode this patch addresses, we fault-injected a rank-local accept divergence into both builds: rank 1 lowers every accept length by one (`correct_len = torch.clamp(correct_len - 1, min=0)`, NCCL 2.30.7 in both _runs). **_Note: the fault reproduction code has been removed before submitting PR._** Without the fix, the server deadlocks before finishing startup warmup. With the fix, the same injection is harmless: rank 0's broadcast overwrites the divergent values, the server boots, and a temp=0 request returns the expected output. As a stability check on the fix itself (its broadcasts run inside the captured decode graphs), I sent 42 sequential chat requests with `ignore_eos=true` and `max_tokens=512` (30 at temp=1, then 12 at temp=0) and probed `/health_generate` after every request with a 180s client timeout, so a stuck collective surfaces as a failed request instead of a silent hang. As the result, all 42 returned HTTP 200 with `finish_reason=length`. 21504 tokens generated in total and mean acc_len during the temp=1 run was 2.86 (block_size=4). Same for temp=0, neither of them occur any error. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Test on 24 natural prompts, 256 output tokens, concurrency=1, temp=1, same setup as above: | Requests | Output throughput | TTFT mean/median/P90 (ms) | TPOT mean/median/P90 (ms) | |---|---|---|---| | 24 | 31.9 tok/s | 157.6 / 153.7 / 178.6 | 30.8 / 31.7 / 35.5 | Comparing with pre-fix TP baseline is impossible because it cannot survive under such load. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process). 4. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers. 5. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so. - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci` 6. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32537602162](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32537602162)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32537602058](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32537602058)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32537602063](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32537602063)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [Weight Cache] Support static DP/EP layouts
signals.text: ## Motivation Weight-cache daemons and engines must construct identical model-parallel layouts before CUDA IPC can safely map a cached MoE shard. The existing daemon launcher rejected `dp_size > 1`, preventing static DP/EP deployments from using the daemon-backed weight cache. This change adds static DP/EP layout support to the CUDA IPC weight-cache path. It is the implementation foundation for the DP/EP roadmap in #33522. ## Modifications - Propagate static DP/EP, MoE DP, attention DP, MoE A2A, and DeepEP-mode configuration from the engine into weight-cache daemons. - Initialize daemon-side model-parallel and MoE state with the same static layout as the engine. - Extend `CacheConfig` with MoE DP/EP shard identity and layout fields, so daemon/client compatibility validation rejects incompatible shards. - Fix static Mooncake EP dispatch to use an all-active rank mask when Elastic EP state is absent. - Route Qwen3 MoE through the existing DeepEP-class backend predicate so Mooncake uses the EP execution path. - Add CPU coverage for MoE shard-rank calculation, extended cache fingerprints, and daemon DeepEP-mode forwarding. The implementation supports static layouts. Dynamic expert placement, EPLB, redundant experts, and recovery lifecycle ownership remain roadmap work. ## Accuracy Tests - `PYTHONPATH=python python -m pytest -q test/registered/unit/model_loader/test_weight_cache_protocol.py` - `29 passed` - Eight-GPU Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP8 daemon IPC serving with `TP=DP=EP=8`, Mooncake low-latency A2A, DP attention, and DP LM head. - 8 daemons exported IPC handles. - 8 schedulers logged `Loaded model via IPC`. - A deterministic completion generated `Paris` for `The capital of France is`. ## Speed Tests and Profiling N/A. This change establishes static DP/EP correctness and does not claim a new performance result. ## Checklist - [x] Format modified Python files with Black; CI will run the repository pre-commit hooks. - [x] Add unit tests according to [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:no_entry_sign: [Run #32106334235](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32106334235)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32466696787](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32466696787)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32106333996](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32106333996)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [3/N] elastic-ep: Recapture decode CUDA graphs after scale-up
signals.text: ## Summary This PR follows [PR #30553](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/30553) and adds FULL decode CUDA graph recapture after runtime Elastic EP scale-up. Primary and joiner ranks rebuild their graphs for the expanded topology before the new EP size is committed. The existing scale-up API and EPLB lifecycle are unchanged. ## Changes - Defer initial decode graph capture on joining ranks until they enter the expanded world. - Finish the current sampling step, release the old graph state, and rebuild decode graphs with the expanded Mooncake WORLD and NIXL rank mask. - Require primary and joiner ranks to resolve the same graph mode and capture configuration before recapture. - Reuse SGLang's existing FULL decode graph initializer and synchronize all ranks before committing the scale operation. - Add graph-stable FA3 MLA metadata for the validated DeepSeek path. - Reject execution modes that do not use the supported decode finalization path. ## Configuration Launch primary and joiner groups with the same resolved graph settings: ```text --cuda-graph-backend-decode full --cuda-graph-backend-prefill disabled --cuda-graph-bs-decode 1 2 4 8 16 ``` The scale request and status API are inherited from the base scale-up PR. ## Known Limitations - Only FULL decode graph recapture is supported. Prefill and piecewise graph recapture are outside this PR. - Primary and joiner groups must use the same resolved CUDA graph configuration and effective capture sizes. - Recapture is synchronous. Configuring more decode batch sizes increases the scale-finalization pause. - The validated DeepSeek MLA path requires FlashAttention 3. - Speculative decoding, embedding, diffusion, encoder-only execution, forward hooks, and PDMux split-prefill are not supported with Elastic EP recapture. - The topology, scale-direction, and post-scale recovery limitations of the base scale-up PR still apply. ## Test Plan The manual Elastic EP tests cover direct, single-rank, mixed-cohort, and repeated scale-up: - `TestElasticScaleUp4To5CudaGraph` - `TestElasticScaleUp4To6CudaGraph` - `TestElasticScaleUp4To8CudaGraph` - `TestElasticScaleUp4To5To6CudaGraph` Each test captures decode batch sizes `1 2 4 8 16` and checks post-scale generation, routed joiner traffic, input logprobs, and GSM8K correctness. ```bash CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7 \ python -m pytest -v -s \ test/manual/ep/test_elastic_scale.py::TestElasticScaleUp4To5To6CudaGraph::test_scale_up_on_demand ``` The repeated 4-to-5-to-6 and direct 4-to-6 validations passed with all five decode graph sizes captured on every participating rank. ## References - [PR #30553](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/30553) - EPLB after scale-up - [PR #30164](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/30164) - runtime EP scale-up - [[RFC] Elastic EP Scale](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/22788) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32138752782](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32138752782)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32138752466](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32138752466)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32138752639](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32138752639)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: fix(bcg): preserve Qwen3-VL DeepStack inputs during replay
signals.text: ## Motivation Prefill breakable CUDA graph (BCG) replay should preserve the same model semantics as eager execution. Qwen3-VL passes intermediate visual features through `input_deepstack_embeds` and adds them at selected language-model layers. However, BCG did not copy this request-specific tensor into a stable graph input slot. As a result, normal BCG execution behaved like an explicit zero-DeepStack run rather than eager execution. Requests still completed successfully, making this a silent correctness issue. ## Reproduction Environment: - Model: `Qwen/Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct` - Revision: `0c351dd01ed87e9c1b53cbc748cba10e6187ff3b` - GPU: NVIDIA H200 - Dtype: BF16 - Decoding: greedy, `max_new_tokens=20` - Input: deterministic RGB vertical-stripe image The GPU test harness temporarily enabled Qwen3-VL for BCG testing. The experiment compares four arms: 1. `eager_normal` 2. `eager_zero_deepstack` 3. `bcg_normal` 4. `bcg_zero_deepstack` The zero-DeepStack arms replace `input_deepstack_embeds` with zeros immediately before the language-model forward call. Each result is formatted as: ```text (common_prefix_length, all_token_ids_equal, maximum_absolute_logprob_difference) ``` | Comparison | Before fix | After fix | |---|---:|---:| | `bcg_normal` vs `eager_normal` | `(7, False, 1.154)` | `(15, True, 0.071)` | | `bcg_normal` vs `bcg_zero_deepstack` | `(20, True, 0.000)` | `(7, False, 1.148)` | | `bcg_zero_deepstack` vs `eager_zero_deepstack` | `(20, True, 0.066)` | `(20, True, 0.066)` | | `eager_zero_deepstack` vs `eager_normal` | `(7, False, 1.138)` | `unchanged` | Before the fix, `bcg_normal` was identical to `bcg_zero_deepstack` and diverged from `eager_normal`. After the fix, `bcg_normal` matches `eager_normal` at the token level and correctly diverges from `bcg_zero_deepstack`. The zero-DeepStack control remains unchanged. Instrumentation also confirmed that `input_deepstack_embeds` was present and non-zero at the language-model entry before replay. The RGB image is used only as a deterministic semantic-equivalence test, not as a visual-quality benchmark. Note on text-only numerics: the slot buffer changes the captured-graph layout, so text-only completions under BCG shift slightly relative to eager (divergence around char 78 in hardware testing, with the slot verified zero throughout). This is the same class as ordinary BCG-vs-eager drift, but anyone diffing text outputs across this PR should expect it. ## Modifications - Add an explicit `supports_bcg_deepstack_replay` capability to Qwen3-VL. - Add an optional stable `input_deepstack_embeds` buffer and graph slot. - Allocate the slot only for multimodal models that opt in and have a non-zero DeepStack width. - Pass the stable slot during BCG capture so the DeepStack additions are included in the graph. - Copy the request-specific DeepStack tensor into the slot before replay. - Clear missing and padded regions to prevent stale data from previous requests. - Fail closed when a non-empty DeepStack tensor does not fit the captured slot, instead of replaying with a zeroed slot. - Add Qwen3-VL and Qwen3-VL MoE to the breakable prefill CUDA graph allowlist. - Add unit tests for capability gating, buffer allocation, slot registration, allowlist membership, and the per-replay slot lifecycle. Absence (`None` or an empty tensor) clears the slot silently; a non-empty tensor with a mismatched shape, dtype, or device raises rather than silently downgrading the request to zero-DeepStack semantics. The `RuntimeError` fires inside the replayed forward, so if the guard ever trips it takes down the scheduler rather than failing a single request. That is the intended trade for an unreachable contract violation, where the alternative is serving a silently wrong answer. Eager fallback is not available at this site: `input_deepstack_embeds` is only materialized inside `model.forward` (via `general_mm_embed_routine` → `separate_deepstack_embeds`), already past `_prepare_forward_metadata_for_replay` and inside the replay context, so there is no pre-commit validation point. `input_embeds` cannot be reused because DeepStack has a different shape and is consumed at selected intermediate language-model layers. `supports_bcg_deepstack_replay` is inherited by every subclass of `Qwen3VLForConditionalGeneration`: Qwen3.5, Qwen3.5-MoE, InternS1-Pro, InternS2-Mobius, InternS2-Preview, and the Qwen3-Omni MoE Thinker. This is deliberate. Those archs consume DeepStack through the same code path, so any checkpoint of theirs that ships non-empty `deepstack_visual_indexes` is covered without further change. Released checkpoints for those archs currently ship empty indexes, so the replay path is a no-op for them today. `MuseGlimmerForConditionalGeneration` is on the BCG allowlist but derives from a different base and does not consume DeepStack at all, so it is unaffected. Qwen3-VL and Qwen3-VL MoE now get prefill graphs by default. This changes replay-vs-eager numerics to the new baseline, and anyone who previously forced breakable prefill was silently running zero-DeepStack and should see grounding improve. ## Accuracy Tests ```bash pytest \ test/registered/unit/model_executor/test_deepstack_replay_slot.py \ test/registered/unit/model_executor/test_cuda_graph_buffer_registry.py \ test/registered/unit/model_executor/test_prefill_cuda_graph_runner.py \ test/registered/unit/model_executor/test_prefill_cuda_graph_runner_helpers.py ``` Result: ```text 55 passed, 24 warnings, 13 subtests passed in 10.70s ``` This includes 8 new tests and 47 existing adjacent tests. Allowlist membership is covered separately in `test/registered/unit/server_args/test_server_args.py`. The GPU four-arm validation results are shown in the Reproduction section. ## Speed Tests and Profiling This is a correctness fix, not a speed optimization. Models that do not activate DeepStack replay do not allocate the new buffer or perform the replay copy. For Qwen3-VL-8B with `max_num_tokens=8192`, `hidden_size=4096`, three DeepStack embeddings, and BF16, the maximum additional buffer is: ```text 8192 × 4096 × 3 × 2 bytes = 192 MiB ``` No replay-latency benchmark was performed. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [[Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit)](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [[Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests)](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [[Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations)](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). No user-facing API or configuration change. - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [[Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy)](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [[Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed)](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). Accuracy results and memory overhead are reported above; latency was not benchmarked. - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [[guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance)](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:no_entry_sign: [Run #32215734301](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32215734301)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32215734179](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32215734179)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32215734273](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32215734273)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [observability] Attribute additional phases in the startup breakdown
signals.text: ## Motivation `startup_time` only reports durations that are explicitly plumbed up to the scheduler. On Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP8, the two largest startup phases aren't among them and show up only as slack inside `scheduler_e2e`: | Phase | Duration | Share of `scheduler_e2e` | | --- | --- | --- | | `flashinfer_autotune` (B200) | 41.5s | 36% | | `deepgemm_jit` (H100) | 65.4s | 29% | Both run deep inside kernel wrappers and library init, where plumbing a timer up to the scheduler would change signatures across several unrelated layers. ## Modifications - New `observability/startup_phase_registry.py`, a process-global registry. `startup_phase("name")` times a block at any call depth; `startup_phase_prefix("draft_")` re-attributes an enclosed scope. Phases may overlap, so they don't sum to time-to-ready. - The registry is frozen once at scheduler-ready. Work recorded after the freeze (DeepGEMM JIT compiles on first use, including during warmup) drains into a new counter, `sglang:post_startup_time_seconds_total`, so the cold-start gauges keep meaning "time to ready" instead of drifting upward. - `build_scheduler_startup_time` merges the frozen phases in. `aggregate_scheduler_startup_times` and `emit_startup_time` now iterate whatever keys are present instead of a fixed list, so new phases reach `/get_server_info` and `/metrics` with no further changes. - New `sglang:engine_startup_duration_seconds` histogram, observed once at ready, for percentiles across restarts that a gauge can't express. - Instrumented DeepGEMM JIT, FlashInfer autotune, and torch distributed init. `ModelRunner` gets a decorator that applies the `draft_` prefix on draft runners, so a draft model's phases are attributed separately from the target's. - Removed `startup_func_log_and_timer.py` and its test. Its `sglang:startup_latency_breakdown_seconds_max` gauge had no production callers, so it was never populated on a real server. Existing `startup_time` fields are unchanged, and nothing is added to the forward or scheduling path. That gauge removal is the only non-additive part. ## Accuracy Tests Not applicable; this records durations and emits metrics, and touches neither the forward nor the scheduling path. ## Speed Tests and Profiling No serving-path cost: phases are recorded only during startup, the registry is frozen at scheduler-ready, and work after the freeze drains into a counter rather than reopening it. The startup durations it attributes are in the table above. ## Test Plan - Observability unit tests, including 11 covering freeze idempotence, drain-exactly-once, and prefix nesting. - Server runs scraping `/metrics`: H100 TP=2 (`deepgemm_jit` at 65.4s, `distributed_init` at 14.2s), H100 with an EAGLE3 draft (`draft_distributed_init` attributed separately from `distributed_init`), and B200 with FlashInfer CUTLASS FP8 (`flashinfer_autotune`). Each asserts that the cold-start gauges are unchanged by later traffic and that the histogram is observed exactly once. - Changed-file pre-commit hooks. ## Checklist - [x] Format the code with pre-commit. - [x] Add unit tests. - [x] Documentation is unaffected: `production_metrics.mdx` covers a subset (29 of 143 metrics) and no startup metrics. - [x] Accuracy and speed benchmarks are not applicable; the startup durations are in the table above. - [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32540234837](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32540234837)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32540234711](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32540234711)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32540234888](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32540234888)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: Avoid materializing GDN QKV tensors during target verification
signals.text: ## Summary This PR removes redundant Q/K/V materialization from compatible GDN speculative target-verification paths. `causal_conv1d_update` already produces packed QKV. Previously, every GDN layer launched `fused_qkv_split_gdn_prefill_kernel` to copy that output into three contiguous tensors before Triton target verification. Triton accepts explicit token strides, so it can consume zero-copy `torch.split`/`view` tensors instead. The optimization is route-aware: - Triton and ReplaySSM target verification use strided Q/K/V views. - Prefill, FlashInfer, CuTeDSL, and other routes requiring contiguous inputs retain materialization. - Model arithmetic, recurrent-state updates, speculative acceptance, logits, and sampling are unchanged. This eliminates one memory-copy kernel launch per GDN layer on every compatible target-verification pass. ## Profile evidence Matched H200 CPU/GPU traces using Qwen3.5-4B, ReplaySSM, and NEXTN T=3: | Target-verification metric | Baseline | Patch | Change | |---|---:|---:|---:| | QKV-split launches/pass | 24 | 0 | **-100%** | | QKV-split GPU time/pass | 56.946 us | 0 | **-56.946 us** | | CUDA-graph kernels | 452 | 428 | **-24** | | CUDA-graph span | 8,132.684 us | 8,040.898 us | **-91.786 us / -1.129%** | The graph-span reduction's approximate 95% interval was **79.732-103.841 us**. ## Standardized GSM8K benchmark 3 alternating baseline/QKV pairs ran on the same H200 with fresh servers, seed 0, empty prefix cache, and a 30-second cooldown. The benchmark used its defaults: 200 questions, five shots, 512 maximum output tokens, temperature 0, and parallelism 64. ### Pair 1 | Metric | Baseline | Patch | Change | |---|---:|---:|---:| | Output throughput | 6,433.642 tok/s | 6,762.467 tok/s | **+5.111%** | | Latency | 5.379 s | 5.145 s | **-4.350%** | | Engine TPOT | 9.7374 ms | 9.4735 ms | **-2.710%** | ### Pair 2 | Metric | Baseline | Patch | Change | |---|---:|---:|---:| | Output throughput | 6,202.258 tok/s | 6,366.221 tok/s | **+2.644%** | | Latency | 5.470 s | 5.401 s | **-1.261%** | | Engine TPOT | 10.2534 ms | 9.7761 ms | **-4.655%** | ### Pair 3 | Metric | Baseline | Patch | Change | |---|---:|---:|---:| | Output throughput | 6,496.073 tok/s | 6,669.102 tok/s | **+2.664%** | | Latency | 5.270 s | 5.134 s | **-2.581%** | | Engine TPOT | 9.3372 ms | 9.4393 ms | **+1.093%** | ### Three-pair aggregate | Metric | Baseline | Patch | Change | |---|---:|---:|---:| | Output throughput | 6,377.324 tok/s | 6,599.263 tok/s | **+3.480%** | | Latency | 5.373 s | 5.227 s | **-2.723%** | | Engine TPOT | 9.7760 ms | 9.5630 ms | **-2.179%** | | Accuracy | 87.667% | 87.500% | -0.167 pp | ## Reproduction Server: ```bash CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 \ PYTHONPATH=<sglang-source>/python \ sglang serve /path/Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B/ \ --port 30000 \ --dtype bfloat16 \ --language-only \ --limit-mm-data-per-request '{"image":0,"video":0,"audio":0}' \ --context-length 32768 \ --mem-fraction-static 0.8 \ --max-running-requests 64 \ --linear-attn-decode-backend triton \ --random-seed 0 \ --speculative-algorithm NEXTN \ --speculative-draft-model-path /path/Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B/ \ --speculative-num-steps 3 \ --speculative-eagle-topk 1 \ --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4 \ --enable-linear-replayssm-spec ``` Benchmark: ```bash python benchmark/gsm8k/bench_sglang.py \ --data-path /data/gsm8k/test.jsonl ``` Dataset SHA-256: ```text 3730d312f6e3440559ace48831e51066acaca737f6eabec99bccb9e4b3c39d14 ``` ## Validation - Exact target-verification output and recurrent-state parity. - ReplaySSM ring/fold parity and routing coverage. - Contiguous-input behavior retained for unsupported routes. - 31 affected H200 tests passed, covering 46 parameterized cases. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32532484205](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32532484205)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32532484040](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32532484040)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32532485372](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32532485372)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->
