signals.title: [Router] Add bounded consistent hashing with an absolute load gap
signals.text: Recommended review order: 1. Core policy and spill condition 2. HTTP active-load lifetime 3. Config and Python binding 4. Tests and documentation Fixes #33625 Supersedes #33791 This follow-up continues #33791 with permission from @waizuichougou. The original implementation commits are preserved with their authorship. Permission: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33791#issuecomment-5211652164 ## Summary - Keep `bounded_consistent_hashing` as an independent opt-in policy; strict `consistent_hashing` is completely unchanged. - Add the policy-specific configurable `min_load_gap`, measured in active requests. - Allow bounded spill only for an explicit `X-SMG-Routing-Key`, and only when both the absolute and relative load thresholds are exceeded. - Keep `X-SMG-Target-Worker` and implicit keys from `Authorization`, `X-Forwarded-For`, and `Cookie` strict. - In non-IGW mode, route over a cached aggregate ring containing both Regular and HTTP workers. - Rebuild that ring only when membership changes; the request hot path does not construct a ring. - Retain the preferred worker when no eligible spill candidate qualifies. - Track active load for the full streaming and non-streaming request lifecycle. ## Why existing policies do not cover this case This policy addresses a narrower contract than the existing alternatives: - `manual` with `assignment_mode=min_load` assigns a new routing key to the least-loaded worker and then stores that assignment in gateway-local mutable state. Separate gateway replicas cannot independently derive the same assignment without shared state. - `prefix_hash` hashes token prefixes and applies a ratio-only load factor. The regular Model Gateway HTTP path does not supply tokens, and its affinity key is not `X-SMG-Routing-Key`. - `cache_aware` detects fleet-wide max/min imbalance and switches to shortest-queue routing. It does not preserve deterministic routing-key placement or ring-order failover. - PR #31170 applies bounded affinity among native intra-instance DP ranks. It cannot select among independent backend workers behind Model Gateway. - Strict `consistent_hashing` remains unchanged for deployments where affinity is a correctness requirement rather than a cache-locality preference. ## Threshold rationale and limitations The two threshold terms intentionally use different references: - `preferred_load - min_healthy_load > min_load_gap` requires that moving the request can reduce active load by a meaningful absolute amount. - `preferred_load > mean_healthy_load * max_load_skew` requires that the preferred worker is an outlier relative to the healthy fleet. Using the minimum as the ratio denominator would be unstable whenever an idle worker has load zero. The parameter names are kept distinct from cache-aware `balance_abs_threshold` / `balance_rel_threshold` because the compared workers, selection behavior, and policy scope differ. Naming can be adjusted if the Model Gateway maintainers prefer a shared configuration vocabulary. **Limitations.** The load signal is local to each gateway process, so multiple gateway replicas may make different best-effort spill decisions. A spill also sacrifices worker-local KV locality and may require a cold prefill on the selected worker. This policy is therefore intended for cache-locality optimization only and must not be used when backend-local session state makes affinity a correctness requirement. ## Spill condition ```text preferred_load.saturating_sub(min_healthy_load) > min_load_gap && preferred_load > mean_healthy_load * max_load_skew ``` Both comparisons are strict. ## Two-worker HTTP A/B and default status The two-worker HTTP A/B comprised 5 repetitions, 20 cells, 400 groups, and 3,200 streaming requests. | Policy | Throughput vs strict | Mean TTFT | Placement | Spill | | ------ | -------------------------------: | ---------: | --------: | ----: | | strict | baseline | 3087.04 ms | 8:0 | N/A | | gap=1 | +2.330%, CI [1.016110, 1.035140] | 2684.51 ms | 6:2 | 25% | | gap=2 | +2.376%, CI [1.016512, 1.035208] | 2688.84 ms | 6:2 | 25% | | gap=4 | +2.099%, CI [1.012597, 1.031751] | 2694.72 ms | 6:2 | 25% | - All 3,200/3,200 requests returned HTTP 200 with matching output and no counter leakage. - Bounded routing changed the frozen eight-sibling placement from 8:0 to 6:2 and reduced mean TTFT by about 13%. - The cached-token fraction fell from 75.546% under strict routing to about 56.95%, while prefill compute increased by about 76%. - This explicitly trades cache reuse and prefill work for better load balance and latency. - Direct paired confidence intervals among gaps 1, 2, and 4 could not establish that any of the three settings differs from either of the others; all three converged to the same 25% spill and 6:2 placement. - The benchmark supports the bounded mechanism, but it does not support a claim that `min_load_gap=2` is optimal. The value 2 remains only a conservative, configurable middle default for this opt-in policy. The GPU A/B ran at SHA `10a3b95f510584174d8b8c661c7974b97d72291a`. The subsequent commits `75b73b0c5adc8c92b648caf984cd0cb28ab42877` and `356299712d1bc649efed655dc610838096b80d3a` contain only documentation/comment clarification and Black formatting; neither changes runtime semantics. ## Production signal and limitation hassellof reported successful affinity and a 3/2/1/2 placement during a storm drill: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/33625#issuecomment-5209076175 That drill did not record any diverts. It therefore did not exercise the gateway spill branch and is not a complete validation of spillover behavior. ## Validation - `cargo fmt --all -- --check` - `cargo check --locked --all-targets` - Bounded-policy Rust tests: 18 passed - Full Rust library: 414 passed - Load guard: 8 passed - Production Router→HTTP regression: 5 independent runs passed - Python: - 31 passed, 1 expected skip - 21 passed, 1 expected skip - 79 passed - Exact-SHA GPU A/B: 3,200/3,200 passed - Lint, Router, SMG benchmark, and current Base/platform CI passed - Any Draft-gated Extra workflow state reflects workflow gating or permissions, not a code failure - `git diff --check` - `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD` <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32352882706](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32352882706)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32352882467](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32352882467)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:heavy_minus_sign: **No AMD PR run found for this commit**.<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [Feature] Optimize AR and DiT overlap for GLM-Image dynamic batching
signals.text: ## Motivation This PR adds AR/DiT overlap to accelerate GLM-Image generation. This reduces the 10-prompt, concurrency-4 benchmark duration from about 223.79 to 182.39s, an **end-to-end improvement of roughly 18.4%.** By default, the overlap mode is disabled, so the existing execution behavior is unchanged: `--ar-dit-overlap-mode off` Users can explicitly enable it with: `--ar-dit-overlap-mode on`. When enabled, the scheduler can prefetch AR outputs for the next compatible request batch while the current DiT requests are being executed sequentially. This helps keep the DiT device fed in 1-AR / 1-DiT separated deployments and reduces idle time under higher concurrency. GLM-Image supports AR/DiT separation with external AR serving and native grouped requests. The original execution pattern is: ```text AR(batch N) -> DiT(req 1) -> DiT(req 2) -> ... -> DiT(req N) -> next AR(batch) ``` This batches the AR stage correctly, but the **next AR batch is only dispatched after all DiT requests in the current batch finish.** In a 1 AR + 1 DiT deployment, DiT runs sequentially on one device and becomes the throughput bottleneck. If AR is not prefetched while DiT is running, the DiT device has to wait for the next AR batch, creating pipeline bubbles. This PR changes the execution pattern to overlap external AR prefetch with sequential DiT execution: ``` AR(batch N) -> DiT(req 1), while prefetching next AR batch -> DiT(req 2) -> ... -> consume prefetched requests ``` The goal is to keep the DiT device fed with prepared AR tokens and reduce idle time in the separated AR/DiT deployment. # Modifications - Add an explicit supports_async_ar_prefetch() pipeline capability. - Enable async AR prefetch only for GLM-Image with an external SRT encoder URL. - Add a GLM-Image-specific async AR prefetch path instead of using the generic grouped pipeline executor from a background thread. - Prefetch AR tokens on CPU while sequential DiT execution is running. - Prefer already-prefetched requests before falling back to normal dynamic dispatch. - Add unit coverage for grouped and single-request GLM-Image external AR prefetch paths. # Accuracy Tests | model | LongText-Bench ZH | |---|---:| | GLM-Image (Official) | 0.9788 | | GLM-Image (AR & Dit Overlap) | **0.9803** | And run unit test: ``` PYTHONPATH=python python3 python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_glm_image_ar.py ``` Result: ``` Passed ``` # Speed Tests and Profiling Server start command ``` export HCCL_IF_BASE_PORT=25000 export HCCL_HOST_SOCKET_PORT_RANGE="25000-25199" export HCCL_NPU_SOCKET_PORT_RANGE="25200-25399" export ASCEND_RT_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 sglang serve \ --model-path /nas/disk1/GLM-Image/vision_language_encoder/ \ --tokenizer-path /nas/disk1/GLM-Image/processor/ \ --port 8764 \ --host 0.0.0.0 \ --base-gpu-id 0 \ --tp-size 1 \ --enable-multimodal \ --cuda-graph-max-bs 8 \ --device npu \ --attention-backend ascend \ --disable-fast-image-processor export SGLANG_CACHE_DIT_FN=2 export SGLANG_CACHE_DIT_BN=1 export SGLANG_CACHE_DIT_WARMUP=4 export SGLANG_CACHE_DIT_RDT=0.4 export SGLANG_CACHE_DIT_MC=4 export SGLANG_CACHE_DIT_TAYLORSEER=true export SGLANG_CACHE_DIT_TS_ORDER=2 export SGLANG_CACHE_DIT_ENABLED=true export HCCL_IF_BASE_PORT=26000 export HCCL_HOST_SOCKET_PORT_RANGE="26000-26199" export HCCL_NPU_SOCKET_PORT_RANGE="26200-26399" export ASCEND_RT_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1 sglang serve \ --model-path /nas/disk1/GLM-Image/ \ --base-gpu-id 0 \ --num-gpus 1 \ --srt-encoder-url http://127.0.0.1:8764 \ --srt-encoder-timeout 100 \ --port 8898 \ --batching-mode dynamic \ --batching-max-size 4 \ --batching-delay-ms 100 \ --enable-batching-metrics \ --ar-dit-overlap-mode on \ --host 0.0.0.0 ``` Before this PR ``` Benchmark duration: 223.79s Max request concurrency: 4 Successful requests: 10/10 ``` After this PR: ``` Benchmark duration (s): 182.39 Max request concurrency: 4 Successful requests: 10/10 ``` ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with signals.title: fix: load Gemma-4 vision tower unquantized under compressed-tensors
signals.text: ### What Addresses the Marlin shape-selection failure reported in #28018. `google/gemma-4-31B-it-qat-w4a16-ct` ignores every vision-tower linear, but its clip wrapper makes those `ignore` entries end in `.linear`. SGLang keeps that suffix on the unfused clippable linears; the fused `qkv_proj` / `gate_up_proj` do not, so those two per block miss the match and get quantized. `gate_up_proj` is `2 * 4304 = 8608`, not divisible by Marlin's `min_thread_n = 64`, so load dies in `gptq_marlin_repack`. So drop the compressed-tensors config for the vision tower, with a `warning_once`. Other quant methods are untouched: the NVFP4 checkpoint already excludes `model.vision_tower*` by glob, and I have nothing justifying de-quantizing online fp8/awq/gptq. Second point: `CompressedTensorsWNA16` and `GPTQMarlinLinearKernel` both dropped the return value of `check_marlin_supports_shape`, which never raises, so bad shapes hit the kernel instead of the actionable `min_thread_n = 64` error. Both now use `verify_marlin_supports_shape`, like `awq_marlin`. I left the repack kernel alone. ### Tests CPU unit tests, each confirmed to fail when its own fix alone is reverted: one builds the vision-tower modules against a two-layer replica of the checkpoint config and asserts `UnquantizedLinearMethod`; two assert `n=8608` raises `ValueError` on each Marlin path. End to end on one GB10, same command both sides: main dies in `gptq_marlin_repack` (`size_n = 8608` vs `tile_n_size = 64`); patched loads the checkpoint and answers a request. Output quality not asserted; TP>1 and image input untested. Happy to normalize `.linear` generically in compressed-tensors instead, if you prefer. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #31200478757](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31200478757)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31200478387](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31200478387)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: Add Agentic-Aware Tail-Optimized LRU eviction to the unified radix cache
signals.text: ## Motivation Tail-Optimized LRU (T-LRU, [NeurIPS 25](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.15152)) keeps only as much of a conversation cached as its next prefill needs to stay under a TTFT SLO budget, and frees the rest of the tail before falling back to recency order, so newer requests can be admitted. On agentic traces the tail is what a plain LRU protects at the expense of every other conversation's tail latency by up to 43%. The policy is opt-in and off by default; `lru` remains the default and its code path is unchanged. ## Modifications ``` --radix-eviction-policy tlru --tlru-threshold N # xi, in tokens --tlru-next-prompt-estimate M # Q_hat, in tokens ``` Concretely: a conversation or agentic turn with history length `L` whose next prompt is expected to add `Q_hat` tokens only needs `L + Q_hat - xi` tokens resident to keep its next prefill inside a TTFT budget `xi`. Everything past that point is "TEL-safe" — evicting it cannot worsen tail latency, because the recompute it causes still fits the budget. T-LRU frees those tokens first (phase 1) and continues in plain recency order once they run out (phase 2). Implemented as a priority function rather than a second eviction pass: a TEL-safe node reports as infinitely old, so the existing device and host eviction drivers produce both of the paper's phases unchanged. ```python budget = max(node.convo_length + self.next_prompt_estimate - self.threshold, 0) cached_without_this_node = node.depth - len(node.key) tel_safe = cached_without_this_node >= budget return (-1 if tel_safe else 0, node.last_access_time) ``` The conversation's history length (`convo_length`) is tracked as a monotone high-water mark separate from its resident depth, maintained on insert and split. Deriving it from what is still cached would leave a trimmed conversation over budget on every later pass and walk it down to nothing instead of stopping after `xi - Q_hat` tokens. Thresholds are expressed in tokens, unlike the paper's blocks (multiply the paper's values by `page_size` to convert), and startup rejects the two configurations that would silently reduce the policy to LRU (`xi <= Q_hat`, and use without the unified radix tree). **Choosing `xi` and `Q_hat`.** Only the difference `delta = xi - Q_hat` reaches the policy (the protected budget is `max(L - delta, 0)`), so the two are stated separately only because each is independently interpretable. `xi` is the tolerated recompute cost in tokens: pick a TTFT budget in seconds and divide by `alpha`, the measured per-uncached-token prefill cost of the system under test (~64 us/token here), giving `xi = 14592` — p5 of the trace's context-length distribution. `Q_hat` is the expected next-prompt size, taken from the trace's per-turn prompt-growth distribution rather than guessed: `2304`, its p60 (median growth is 1,731). Both are workload-relative token counts, so porting them to a new workload means re-deriving: re-measure `alpha` and re-apply the SLO, or match the freed share `F(delta) = sum(min(delta, ctx_i)) / sum(ctx_i)` (7.4% of served context at our setting) and solve for the new `delta`. Files touched (325 insertions, 7 deletions): | file | change | | --- | --- | | `mem_cache/evict_policy.py` | `TLRUStrategy` | | `mem_cache/unified_radix_cache.py` | `convo_length` bookkeeping on insert/split | | `mem_cache/cache_init_params.py`, `kv_cache_builder.py`, `utils.py` | plumb the two params | | `srt/server_args.py` | flags, choices, validation | | `test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_tlru_eviction_policy.py` | 9 unit tests | ## Accuracy Tests No change to model forward computation or kernels: the policy only reorders which cached prefixes are evicted, and an evicted prefix is recomputed exactly on its next request, so model outputs are unchanged by construction. The default `lru` path is untouched when the flag is not set. Policy behaviour is covered by 9 CPU-only unit tests (`test_tlru_eviction_policy.py`, no GPU required): - frees exactly the tail budget on a fresh conversation, and stops there - conversations under the threshold are entirely free - phase 1 spreads across conversations, then falls back to LRU - degenerates to exact LRU when `Q_hat` reaches `xi` - an oversized tail node is protected rather than partially freed - a compacted branch keeps its shared prefix protected - budget clamps at zero; priorities stay finite and orderable ## Speed Tests and Profiling Measured on DeepSeek-V4-Pro FP4, 4x B300, TP4/EP4/DP-attention, HiCache DRAM ratio 4, on the SemiAnalysis agentic trace via aiperf, 3,600 s measured after 600 s cache-pressure warmup, `xi=14592` / `Q_hat=2304`. C=32: 5 LRU / 12 T-LRU runs; C=40: 4 LRU / 5 T-LRU. **Methodology.** The client seed is pinned, so both arms replay identical trajectories; requests are matched across arms on `(conversation_id, turn_index)` and compared as a paired sample (~6,000+ matched requests per concurrency), which removes workload variance. Comparisons use the middle 80% of each run's measured window (opening/closing 10% trimmed from both arms alike) to exclude the residual warm-up transient and client-drain. And the trace is using [semianalysisai/cc-traces-weka-062126](https://huggingface.co/datasets/semianalysisai/cc-traces-weka-062126) on HuggingFace: 9,843 real Claude Code sessions (98,827 turns) captured by WEKA's kv-cache-tester. The actual generator code lives in the aiperf fork inside [InferenceX](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX), checked out at dd237099. **Paired quantile deltas, T-LRU vs LRU on identical requests (lower is better):** C=32: | metric | p50 | p75 | p90 | p95 | p99 | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | TTFT | -3.2%| -5.3% | -4.7% | -6.9% | -8.6% | | ITL | +2.2%* | -0.7% | -8.7% | -17.2% | -43.9% | C=40: | metric | p50 | p75 | p90 | p95 | p99 | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | TTFT | +5.1% | +2.4% | +2.1% | -4.3% | -13.6% | | ITL | +0.2% | +0.8% | -0.6% | -2.7% | -11.0% | The shape matches the mechanism: the decode tail is where retention pays off, and the effect grows monotonically toward the tail at C=32 (ITL -8.7% at p90 to -43.9% at p99), alongside TTFT body improvements. The cost is small and in the body: ITL p50 +2.2% at C=32 and TTFT p50 +5.1% at C=40 (both corroborated by run-level exact rank tests). **Throughput** (arm-level medians, higher is better) is unchanged — every delta is inside its replicate spread. The policy reshapes the latency distribution without moving aggregate throughput or the prefix hit rate. | C | metric | LRU | T-LRU | delta | replicate spread | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 32 | tok/s/GPU | 28,580 | 28,228 | -1.2% | 12.2% | | 32 | tok/s/user | 23.45 | 22.89 | -2.4% | 4.9% | | 32 | GPU prefix hit | 96.04% | 96.07% | +0.04 pp | 0.5 pp | | 40 | tok/s/GPU | 30,117 | 30,558 | +1.5% | 8.0% | | 40 | tok/s/user | 20.06 | 19.72 | -1.7% | 9.8% | | 40 | GPU prefix hit | 95.70% | 95.79% | +0.09 pp | 0.3 pp | Note: this configuration is well-provisioned (working set ~0.28x of KV capacity, 96% prefix hit rate vs a 97.7% ceiling), so these numbers are a lower bound on what a cache-pressured deployment shows; and `xi`/`Q_hat` are workload-relative token counts — copying our values onto a different context distribution will not reproduce this behaviour (only `xi - Q_hat` reaches the policy). **Write-back study.** There is a nuance in the analogy to a CPU cache: in a CPU, SRAM caches are *write-back* to DRAM; here, DRAM itself is the second-level cache (backing GPU HBM), and it runs write-back in an "allocate on eviction" sense. That is: a KV page gets its DRAM copy only at the moment it is demoted out of HBM, never proactively. Thus, the *write-back rate* is exactly the *eviction rate*. **Measured write-back and load-back rates** (median per run, 3,600 s window, from run counters): | arm | C | written back to DRAM | rate | load-back from DRAM | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | LRU | 32 | 30.0M tokens | ~8.3k tok/s 10 MB/s | 0.7M tok (~0.2 MB/s) | | LRU | 40 | 38.9M tokens | ~10.8k tok/s 13 MB/s | 3.3M tok (~1.1 MB/s) | | T-LRU | 32 | 48.1M tokens | ~13.4k tok/s 16 MB/s | 17.4M tok (~5.7 MB/s) | | T-LRU | 40 | 58.3M tokens | ~16.2k tok/s 19 MB/s | 22.8M tok (~7.5 MB/s) | Implied size is ~1.2 KB per token, consistent with MLA's compressed KV — this model is unusually cheap to demote. **Two main readings** 1. *Average bandwidth is trivial*. 10–20 MB/s sustained against an HBM↔DRAM link measured in hundreds of GB/s is negligible — write-back traffic is not a bandwidth concern here, even with T-LRU's 1.6× amplification (visible directly: e.g., T-LRU writes 48M vs LRU's 30M at C=32, and the ~17M difference is its load-back volume). Any latency cost from the demotion path arises from the moment copies happen — bursty, under memory pressure, on the eviction path while a prefill waits — not from the total data moved. 2. *The tier is write-heavy and read-light under LRU* (e.g., 30M written vs 0.7M read back at C=32, a 43:1 ratio). This is exactly when write-back is the right policy: write-through would have pre-copied everything for almost no read benefit. T-LRU narrows the ratio to ~3:1 by design — it deliberately evicts things that come back. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :no_entry_sign: [Run #32332104119](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32332104119) Latest PR Test (Extra): :no_entry_sign: [Run #32332103851](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32332103851) Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): :x: [Run #32332103948](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32332103948)

signals.title: Improve M3 performance on MI350
signals.text: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation Improve M3 performance on MI350. <!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. --> ## Modifications MI350X (gfx950) decode/prefill optimizations for MiniMax-M3 and M3-VL. Measured on TP8 / MXFP8 / 80k context: **1144 -> ~2035 tok/s decode** (13.98 -> 15.72 ms/step at the higher batch), GSM8K unchanged (88.55% before and after at the same budget; 95.3-95.7% at a 2048-token budget). ### MXFP8 / dense GEMM - AITER FlyDSL MXFP8 MoE support: pre-shuffled gate/up weights, E8M0 scales, OAI-SwiGLU activation handling, and fused shared-expert execution. - `--fp8-gemm-backend bf16`: dequantize MXFP8 weights once at load and run BF16 hipBLASLt linear. - `SGLANG_FORCE_MXFP8_BLOCK_CONVERT_DENSE=1`: convert *dense* weights to block-FP8 `[128,128]` at load while MoE stays on the native per-1x32 MX path (the block-scale MoE kernel does not support SwiGLU-OAI). ~+35% prefill. - `SGLANG_OPT_MXFP8_DENSE_PTPC_DECODE_M` (default 128): rowwise-FP8 (ptpc) dense fast path for skinny-M decode, falling back to the block-FP8 GEMM above it. The old cap of 8 silently disabled both this path and the quant fusions below at bs16; raising it was +14.2%. - Allows `--moe-runner-backend aiter` for MXFP8 on gfx950, and errors early if `SGLANG_USE_AITER=1` is not set. ### Fusions - Per-token FP8 quantization fused into the Gemma fused-add-RMSNorm Triton kernel, so the ptpc decode GEMM consumes `(fp8, scale)` directly. Uses an explicitly rounded `1/448` reciprocal (Triton `/` lowers to a fast reciprocal on ROCm, which cost 1 ULP vs AITER). - MoE all-reduce fused into the next layer's norm + qkv quant (`forward_with_allreduce_fusion_quant_per_token`), opt-in per model via `enable_fused_ar_quant_per_token` so it cannot fire for unrelated AITER GemmaRMSNorm models. - Shared-expert append folded into the Triton fused MoE gate (`nfse` handling fixed - the previous path double-appended the shared expert and dropped a routed one). - Shared-expert compute overlapped onto an alternate stream when the routed path forces fusion off. - Small-batch MoE sorting + MXFP8 quant kernel (`moe_sorting_small`), replacing a two-kernel path at decode shapes. ### Router GEMV - New Triton split-K router GEMV (`kernels/ops/gemm/router_gemv.py`) with in-kernel split-K fixup (no separate zero-init launch), per-M-bucket configs (BK 512, BN by batch), and the gate weight read once per decode batch. ~+2.8% then +5.5% on top. ### Sparse attention (ATOM port) - Gluon-based paged sparse prefill (`minimax_sparse_ops/atom_prefill.py`), default on via `SGLANG_OPT_USE_ATOM_PREFILL`, with Triton fallback for unsupported shapes and a scratch-size cap that falls back rather than OOMs. - Score-only index kernel at every page size: the per-page slot addressing is now a `PER_PAGE_SLOTS` constexpr chosen from `block_size_k // page_size`, instead of gating the whole (~1.6x) kernel behind `page_size >= 16`. - Index top-k shared across every N sparse layers, `SGLANG_MINIMAX_M3_INDEX_TOPK_FREQ` (default 2, ROCm only, never under two-batch overlap) - it changes which KV blocks skip layers attend, so it is an accuracy knob. - Decode top-k written straight into the reuse buffer; per-forward caches keyed on the owning `ForwardBatch` so they are TBO-safe. - JIT radix top-k unblocked under CUDA graphs (`kMaxNumBlocks` 4096 -> 16384). ### Dense decode attention - ROCm decode-attention KV tile 32 -> 64 tokens and a software-pipelined KV loop (`num_stages` 2) for `Lk <= 128`: 690 -> 285 us/launch, ~+7% e2e. - Decode `kv_indices` build parallelized across sequence spans. - Skips redundant sparse KV-cache writes when fusion already populated the cache, and top-k id sanitization when EP is off. ### Defaults and memory accounting - On ROCm gfx950, `--prefill-attention-backend` defaults to `aiter` (ck-tile fmha) while decode stays on Triton. Decode on the AITER backend costs ~3 points on AIME25, so it is not defaulted. - Replaced the blanket `mem_fraction_static *= 0.85` for the AITER backend at `context_len > 8192` with an exact charge: the paged-decode split workspace is fp32 and linear in context length (~4 GiB at 128k) and is allocated after the KV pool, so `KVCacheConfigurator` now re-solves the budget once with the measured size (`aiter_attn_workspace_bytes`) subtracted. The old flat haircut over-reserved ~28 GB. - MiniMax-M3-VL gets the same ROCm shared-expert support; EP/DeepEP guards preserved. ### Launch recipes ### Higher-accuracy dense path Keeps dense weights on the native MXFP8 path with the original per-1×32 scales. ``` SGLANG_USE_AITER=1 \ sglang serve \ --trust-remote-code \ --model-path /persistent/models/MiniMax-M3-MXFP8 \ --reasoning-parser auto \ --tool-call-parser auto \ --tp 8 \ --quantization mxfp8 \ --moe-runner-backend aiter \ --fp8-gemm-backend bf16 \ --enable-aiter-allreduce-fusion \ --attention-backend triton \ --prefill-attention-backend aiter \ --dtype bfloat16 \ --chunked-prefill-size 32768 \ --mem-fraction-static 0.80 \ --host 0.0.0.0 \ --port 30000 ``` ### Fast decode path Converts dense weights to block-FP8 at load and selects the automatic block-FP8/PTPC dispatch. MoE remains on native MXFP8. ``` SGLANG_USE_AITER=1 \ SGLANG_FORCE_MXFP8_BLOCK_CONVERT_DENSE=1 \ sglang serve \ --trust-remote-code \ --model-path /persistent/models/MiniMax-M3-MXFP8 \ --reasoning-parser auto \ --tool-call-parser auto \ --tp 8 \ --quantization mxfp8 \ --moe-runner-backend aiter \ --fp8-gemm-backend auto \ --enable-aiter-allreduce-fusion \ --attention-backend triton \ --prefill-attention-backend aiter \ --dtype bfloat16 \ --chunked-prefill-size 32768 \ --mem-fraction-static 0.80 \ --host 0.0.0.0 \ --port 30000 ``` ## Accuracy Tests baseline ``` == gsm8k == 1319 examples (single-shot) | 227.1s | 1485 tok/s | 337K tokens * score = 88.55% stop_rate = 89.61% truncated_rate = 10.39% [warn: hitting max_tokens] error_rate = 0.00% ``` this pr ``` == gsm8k == 1319 examples (single-shot) | 119.9s | 2862 tok/s | 343K tokens * score = 88.55% stop_rate = 89.69% truncated_rate = 10.31% [warn: hitting max_tokens] error_rate = 0.00% ``` <!-- If this pull request affects model outputs (e.g., changes to the kernel or model forward code), provide accuracy test results. --> ## Speed Tests and Profiling MI350X, TP8, MXFP8 MiniMax-M3. ### Dense-path configurations (bs1 / il8192) | Configuration | Decode | Prefill | | |---|---:|---:|---| | Native MXFP8 dense, `--fp8-gemm-backend bf16` (higher-accuracy dense) | 131 tok/s | 22.1k tok/s | reference | | Dense block-convert only (`SGLANG_FORCE_MXFP8_BLOCK_CONVERT_DENSE=1`) | 92.5 tok/s | 29.9k tok/s | **+35% prefill, -30% decode** — the CK a8w8 blockscale kernel is a prefill kernel, ~2.5x worse than bf16 hipBLASLt at M=1 | | Block-convert + PTPC decode fast path + the rest of this PR (fast decode) | 169 tok/s | ~46k tok/s | **+29% decode, +2.1x prefill** vs the first row | The two rows the launch recipes above expose are rows 1 and 3; row 2 is why the skinny-M PTPC path exists at all. ### Concurrency sweep (TP8) | CC | baseline tok/s/user | baseline tok/s/GPU | high accuracy tok/s/user | high accuracy tok/s/GPU | |---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 1 | 49.8 | 6.2 | 131.1 | 16.4 | | 2 | 48.9 | 12.2 | 126.0 | 31.5 | | 4 | 47.9 | 23.9 | 120.5 | 60.3 | | 8 | 46.5 | 46.5 | 112.4 | 112.5 | | 16 | 42.0 | 83.9 | 92.9 | 186.1 | | 32 | 36.8 | 147.3 | 73.9 | 296.0 | | 64 | 30.9 | 247.3 | 57.1 | 457.3 | | 128 | - | - | 41.7 | 667.0 | | 256 | - | - | 29.0 | 929.9 | ### Long-context decode (bs16-32 / il80000) 1144 -> 2035 tok/s (13.98 -> 15.72 ms/step at bs32) across the MXFP8 decode-M cap (+14.2%), the router GEMV M-keyed configs (+5.5%), the fmoe atomic reduce pick (+4.3%), the dense decode-attention tile+pipelining (+3.6% and +7.2%), and the ATOM sparse port. ## Checklist - [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process). 2. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32509460767](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32509460767)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32509460240](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32509460240)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32509460649](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32509460649)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [Fix] Account resident weight memory in KV sizing
signals.text: ## Motivation The IPC weight-cache daemon keeps model weights resident before the engine starts, so `ModelRunner` samples its pre-load free-memory baseline after those weights have already reduced free memory. Without correcting that baseline, KV sizing reserves headroom from only the remaining free memory and can over-allocate the KV cache. The correction must be rank-local before the distributed `MIN`: adding preloaded weight memory after ranks have already reduced their baselines is incorrect when rank footprints differ. Target KV sizing also happens after draft loading, so target, multi-runner, and future speculative draft weights must be aggregated before sizing. ## Modifications - Add a generic rank-local `BaseModelLoader.preloaded_weights_bytes` contract, defaulting to zero, and validate loader-provided values before use. - Aggregate preloaded bytes across target, multi-runner, and speculative draft workers. The current built-in IPC weight cache plus speculative decoding combination remains explicitly rejected because draft-model daemon support is not implemented yet, but the accounting path is ready for it. - Immediately before target KV-pool allocation, compute `MIN(local pre-load baseline + local preloaded weight bytes)` and update `pre_model_load_memory`, so initial sizing and post-capture resizing use the same corrected value. - Measure the daemon's process-local PyTorch allocator growth during model loading and return it through the IPC protocol as `preloaded_weights_bytes`. ## Accuracy Tests Ran a real persistent-daemon restart A/B with `Qwen/Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct` in BF16 at TP=1 on an 80 GB GPU. The standalone daemon retained 63,004 MiB of GPU memory while two independent engine clients were started sequentially against the same daemon. | Result | Without this fix | With this fix | |---|---:|---:| | Client pre-load available memory | 17.23 GB | 17.23 GB | | Reported preloaded weights | Not available | 65,546,485,760 bytes (61.045 GiB) | | KV cache tokens | 63,434 | 38,430 | | K + V allocation | 15.48 GB | 9.38 GB | | Memory before decode graph capture | 0.88 GB | 4.37 GB | | First client start | CUDA OOM during graph capture | Healthy; inference succeeded | | Second client start | Same CUDA OOM | Healthy; inference succeeded | Without the correction, both starts selected the same oversized KV cache and failed during decode CUDA graph capture while the daemon remained alive. With the correction, both starts completed graph capture, reached health, and served a completion against the same persistent daemon. This validates the final implementation and reproduces the accounting defect as a deterministic startup failure with a model whose resident weights occupy more than half of GPU memory. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not benchmarked. The steady-state inference path is unchanged. Startup adds two process-local allocator reads and one existing-world-group reduction before KV-pool allocation. ## Validation - Large-model persistent-daemon restart A/B passed as described above - Python syntax checks passed for all changed production files - Ruff error checks passed for all changed production files - Full Ruff checks passed for the central accounting and IPC modules - Diff whitespace checks passed ## Checklist - [x] Format code according to the repository hooks. - [x] Validate the exact final implementation with a persistent GPU daemon and two engine starts. - [ ] Update documentation — not applicable; no user-facing option or workflow changed. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32452400522](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32452400522)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32452400294](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32452400294)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32452400361](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32452400361)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [dLLM] Support DiffusionGemma serving
signals.text: ## Motivation The DiffusionGemma cookbook documents this model, but SGLang rejects it as unknown. This PR adds native text and image serving. It uses the shared dLLM and FDFO paths from [#27551](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/27551) and [#27877](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/27877). Fixes [#29904](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/29904) ## Changes - Add the DiffusionGemma model, image processor, weight loader, and Gemma4Renoise sampler - Run causal prompt prefill before each 256 token output block - Reuse request slots and KV cache across FDFO rounds - Add the required attention masks and TP1, TP2, and TP4 weight loading - Reject unsupported settings before model execution - Add focused model, scheduler, sampler, request, and CPU MoE tests ## Tests - 265 unit tests and 50 subtests passed - Full pre-commit passed on all 25 changed files - All 1,047 checkpoint tensors loaded at TP1, TP2, and TP4 - Real text and image serving passed on H200 - FDFO, synchronous decoding, long prompts, and exact output lengths passed - Unsupported request fields returned HTTP 400 before model execution ## Performance Four concurrent requests each generated 256 tokens with eight denoising rounds. Two warmups were discarded. Each result is the median of 15 trials. | Runtime | TP2 median | TP4 median | | --- | --- | --- | | SGLang | 0.621 s | 0.634 s | | vLLM 0.26.0 | 0.507 s | 0.496 s | These fixed work results check basic performance and do not claim a speed lead. ## Limits - Image requests require Triton on GPU - PP, CP, quantized loading, and untied embeddings are not supported - CUDA graphs, chunked prefill, and radix caching are disabled - This PR does not change MPS or DP placement ## Checklist - [x] Tests added and passing - [x] Pre-commit passing - [x] Accuracy and speed results included - [x] The existing cookbook already documents the launch command <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32530744663](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32530744663)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32530744539](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32530744539)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32530744541](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32530744541)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: perf(unified-memory): batch lazy-compaction mapping lookup
signals.text: ## Motivation Unified-memory lazy compaction reads `physical_to_virtual[src].item()` for every relocated survivor. Each scalar read synchronizes the GPU and CPU, making compaction a major bottleneck under memory pressure. Batching these lookups improved unified-memory throughput by 20.4% to 128.2% across Qwen3.5-0.8B, 4B, and 9B in eviction-heavy benchmarks. ## Modifications - Gather all survivor virtual IDs with one indexed tensor operation per move batch. - Keep the invalid-mapping assertion with one check per batch. - Add a regression test that rejects per-row mapping reads and verifies the virtual/physical mappings and relocated cache data. ## Accuracy Tests | Test | Result | |---|---:| | Complete allocator test file | **66 passed** | | Eviction/replay parity | **80/80 exact matches** | | Test-only diff applied to upstream base | **1 failed** (expected) | | New regression test with this patch | **1 passed** | The parity test compared output IDs, logprob token IDs, and logprob values between upstream unified memory and this patch after eviction. Maximum logprob difference was 0.0. <details> <summary>Test commands</summary> ```bash PYTHONPATH=python:test python -m pytest -q \ test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_multi_ended_allocator.py \ -k lazy_flush_gathers_survivor_mappings_as_one_batch PYTHONPATH=python:test python -m pytest -q \ test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_multi_ended_allocator.py ``` To reproduce the failure, apply only the test-file diff to the upstream base. The regression test fails at the per-row mapping lookup; it passes after the production-file diff is applied. </details> ## Speed Tests and Profiling ### Environment - GPU: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5090, 32,607 MiB; driver 610.62 - Models: `Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B`, `Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B`, and `Qwen/Qwen3.5-9B`, bfloat16 The three variants differ only as follows: | Configuration | Source revision | Server option | |---|---|---| | Static memory | `52afe87a08c6` (upstream base) | `--enable-unified-memory` disabled | | Unified memory (upstream) | `52afe87a08c6` | `--enable-unified-memory` | | Unified memory + batched mapping (this PR) | this PR | `--enable-unified-memory` | Each run used 80 prefix groups, four measured rounds, 1,024 input tokens, four output tokens, concurrency 16, and two priming passes. A fresh server was used for every variant and repetition. Results are medians of three runs. <details> <summary>Reproduction commands and workload</summary> ### Server Create isolated source trees for the exact revisions: ```bash git fetch upstream main git worktree add ../sglang-upstream-base \ 52afe87a08c6aa049c52f9507b4f0ca26cecb562 git fetch https://github.com/seokwoosong/sglang.git \ perf/unified-compaction-batch-mapping git worktree add ../sglang-unified-batched-mapping \ 66535cef39775b13a589668fc1429d57e8f8ff03 ``` Use `../sglang-upstream-base` for Static memory and Unified memory (upstream). Use `../sglang-unified-batched-mapping` for Unified memory + batched mapping (this PR). Start a fresh server for every variant, memory fraction, and repetition. ```bash PYTHONPATH=<SOURCE_TREE>/python python -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path <MODEL> \ --host 127.0.0.1 --port 30000 --tp 1 --dtype bfloat16 \ --page-size 1 \ --attention-backend triton \ --linear-attn-backend triton \ --mamba-backend triton \ --mamba-radix-cache-strategy extra_buffer \ --max-total-tokens 60000 \ --max-running-requests 16 \ --chunked-prefill-size 4096 \ --context-length 65536 \ --cuda-graph-backend-decode disabled \ --cuda-graph-backend-prefill disabled \ --enable-metrics \ --mem-fraction-static <MEMORY_FRACTION> \ [--enable-unified-memory] ``` Stop the server after each run so that every measurement starts from a fresh allocator and radix cache. Use these model-specific memory fractions: | Model | Memory fractions | |---|---| | `Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B` | 0.30, 0.15 | | `Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B` | 0.55, 0.40 | | `Qwen/Qwen3.5-9B` | 0.85, 0.75 | Each pair above leaves a valid cache pool and still causes L1 eviction. ### Workload reproduction The workload is deterministic and uses token IDs directly through `/generate`: 1. Initialize `random.Random(42)`. 2. Create 80 groups. Each group has a 972-token shared prefix (`int(1024 * 0.95)`) consisting of token `1000 + group_id`, followed by 971 values from `rng.randrange(2000, 200000)`. 3. Prime the radix cache twice. In each pass, submit every prefix sequentially with `temperature=0`, `max_new_tokens=1`, and `ignore_eos=true`. 4. Build four measured rounds. In each round, visit groups in reverse order (`79` through `0`) and append 52 new values from `rng.randrange(2000, 200000)` to the group's prefix. This produces 320 measured requests of exactly 1,024 input tokens each. 5. Submit all measured requests through the streaming `/generate` endpoint, limiting in-flight requests with `asyncio.Semaphore(16)`. Use `temperature=0`, `max_new_tokens=4`, and `ignore_eos=true`. 6. Measure wall-clock time immediately around the 320-request `asyncio.gather()`. Compute total token throughput as `sum(prompt_tokens + completion_tokens) / measured_seconds` using the token counts returned by the server. 7. Read `/metrics` immediately before and after the measured phase. Reject the run if a request failed or if `sglang:evicted_tokens_total` did not increase. Run three repetitions at each memory fraction. Rotate server order to reduce thermal and order bias: - repetition 1: Static memory, Unified memory (upstream), Unified memory + batched mapping - repetition 2: Unified memory (upstream), Unified memory + batched mapping, Static memory - repetition 3: Unified memory + batched mapping, Static memory, Unified memory (upstream) Report the median of the three runs. Across the three models, the matrix contains 54 clean runs and 17,280 measured requests in total. </details> ### Results | Model | GPU memory fraction | Static memory | Unified memory (upstream) | This PR | Improvement | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | Qwen3.5-0.8B | 0.30 | 88,366 tok/s | 50,938 tok/s | 97,612 tok/s | +91.6% | | Qwen3.5-0.8B | 0.15 | 82,397 tok/s | 31,320 tok/s | 71,467 tok/s | +128.2% | | Qwen3.5-4B | 0.55 | 19,253 tok/s | 13,501 tok/s | 18,404 tok/s | +36.3% | | Qwen3.5-4B | 0.40 | 17,390 tok/s | 12,311 tok/s | 16,961 tok/s | +37.8% | | Qwen3.5-9B | 0.85 | 10,650 tok/s | 8,612 tok/s | 10,372 tok/s | +20.4% | | Qwen3.5-9B | 0.75 | 10,155 tok/s | 8,276 tok/s | 10,226 tok/s | +23.6% | All 54 runs and 17,280 measured requests passed. L1 eviction occurred in every run. Upstream unified memory and this PR evicted exactly the same number of tokens in every repetition for five of the six rows; 0.8B/0.30 is an end-to-end comparison with scheduling-dependent eviction. The maximum throughput range across the three repetitions of any 4B or 9B variant was 1.04%. ### Profiler At 0.8B/0.15, both traces contained the same 51 `_flush` calls and 18 move-batch commits: | Metric inside `_flush` | Upstream | This PR | Change | |---|---:|---:|---:| | `aten::item` calls | 32,646 | 18 | -99.9% | | `_flush` CPU duration | 1,060.4 ms | 68.0 ms | -93.6% | The remaining 18 scalar reads are the intentional invalid-mapping check, once per committed move batch. <details> <summary>Profiler reproduction</summary> Use memory fraction 0.15 and the same priming procedure, but run one measured round (80 requests). Immediately before the measured phase, start the built-in profiler: ```bash curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:30000/start_profile \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{ "output_dir": "/tmp/sglang-compaction-profile", "num_steps": 64, "activities": ["CPU", "GPU"], "with_stack": false, "record_shapes": false }' ``` Count `aten::item` events whose timestamps and thread IDs fall inside a `MultiEndedAlloc._flush` event, and sum the durations of those `_flush` events. </details> ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). No user-facing documentation change is required. - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32537957236](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32537957236)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32537957041](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32537957041)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32537957144](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32537957144)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [AMD] [Spec] Enable stochastic tree verification on ROCm
signals.text: ## Motivation ROCm EAGLE verification currently routes every HIP request through greedy `argmax`, even when `temperature`, `top_p`, or `top_k` request stochastic sampling. ROCm also lacks the CUDA target-only tree-sampling kernel and its top-k/top-p renormalization operators. While validating a portable tree verifier with GLM-5.2-FP8, EAGLE top-k > 1 exposed a second blocker: DSA’s page-64 index cache received physical token-slot IDs but indexed them as page rows: ```python index_k[tgt_loc_flat] = index_k[src_loc_flat] ``` On MI355X this failed during draft cache preparation, before target verification: ```text HSA_STATUS_ERROR_EXCEPTION: An HSAIL operation resulted in a hardware exception (0x1016) torch.AcceleratorError: HIP error: unspecified launch failure ``` Both the stochastic verifier and page-aware DSA relocation are required for a complete ROCm top-k > 1 tree path. ## Modifications ### Target-only tree verification - `python/sglang/kernels/ops/speculative/tree_sampling.py` - Add the Triton target-only stochastic tree verifier and residual bonus-token sampling. - `python/sglang/kernels/ops/speculative/__init__.py` - Register the Triton tree-sampling operator for CUDA and HIP. - `python/sglang/srt/speculative/eagle_utils.py` - Route non-greedy HIP EAGLE requests to the Triton tree verifier; preserve chain rejection sampling and greedy dispatch. - `python/sglang/srt/speculative/dflash_utils.py` - Enable the same target-only Triton verifier for DFLASH on HIP. - `python/sglang/srt/speculative/spec_utils.py` - Advertise tree-kernel availability on HIP. ### Portable probability renormalization - `python/sglang/kernels/ops/sampling/renorm.py` - Add exact threshold-based top-k/top-p pivots, tie handling, and full-sort overflow fallback. - `python/sglang/kernels/ops/sampling/renorm_triton.py` - Fuse pivot application, masked reduction, and normalization for HIP. - `python/sglang/kernels/ops/sampling/__init__.py` - Select CUDA AOT, HIP Triton, or portable Torch implementations through the kernel registry. - `python/sglang/srt/layers/sampler.py` - Reuse the portable top-p semantics in the Torch sampler path. ### Page-aware DSA tree relocation - `python/sglang/kernels/ops/attention/dsa/index_buf_accessor.py` - Add overlap-safe gather/scatter kernels that move each token’s 128-byte FP8 index key and 4-byte FP32 scale by `(page, offset)`. - Preserve AITer’s 16x16 preshuffled K layout and CUDA’s row-major layout. - `python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/index_key_cache.py` - Replace token-slot-as-page-row indexing with logical K/scale relocation. - `python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/dsa_cache_layer_split.py` - Remove the duplicated broken override so layer-sharded caches inherit the corrected implementation. ### Tests - `test/registered/kernels/ops/speculative/test_tree_speculative_sampling_triton.py` - `test/registered/kernels/ops/speculative/test_spec_verify_distribution.py` - `test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/test_dsa_index_cache_move.py` ## Accuracy Tests ### MI355X unit tests on final PR commit ```text TestTreeSpeculativeSamplingTriton.test_matches_torch_oracle TestTreeSpeculativeSamplingTriton.test_seeded_inputs_are_repeatable TestTreeSpeculativeSamplingTriton.test_dflash_sampling_integration_matches_oracle TestTreeSpeculativeSamplingTriton.test_branched_tree_preserves_target_distribution TestTreeSpeculativeSamplingTriton.test_matches_cuda_aot_oracle [skipped on ROCm] TestSpecSamplingDispatch.test_hip_target_only_uses_triton_tree TestSpecSamplingDispatch.test_rejection_sampling_uses_triton_chain TestSpecVerifyDistribution.test_chain_sampler_preserves_target_distribution TestSpecVerifyDistribution.test_greedy_verify_collapses_to_argmax TestPortableSpecRenorm.test_top_k_scalar_and_per_row TestPortableSpecRenorm.test_top_p_per_row_and_zero_mass TestDSAIndexCacheMove.test_cross_page_overlap_and_identity TestDSAIndexCacheMove.test_empty_move TestDSAIndexCacheMove.test_layer_split_skips_non_owned_buffers TestDSAIndexCacheMove.test_page64_tree_prefix_tail_duplication ``` | Test file | Result | |---|---:| | `test_tree_speculative_sampling_triton.py` | 4 passed, 1 CUDA-only skip | | `test_spec_verify_distribution.py` | 5 passed, 1 sgl-kernel-only skip | | `test_dsa_index_cache_move.py` | 4 passed | | Pre-commit, all 15 changed files | Passed | CUDA-only registered renormalization oracles: ```text TestSpecRenormFallbacks.test_top_k_fallback_matches_kernel TestSpecRenormFallbacks.test_top_p_fallback_matches_kernel ``` ### GLM-5.2-FP8 customer workload Apex Shortlist problem 4, gold answer `2618`, `n=8`, `temperature=1.0`, `top_p=0.95`, `max_tokens=131072`, EAGLE top-k 2 / 5 steps / 6 draft tokens. | Platform | Correct | Stop | Length | Completion tokens | Server exceptions | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | MI355X, TP8 | 7/8 | 8 | 0 | 317,649 | 0 | | GB300, TP4 | 7/8 | 8 | 0 | 357,376 | 0 | MI355X top-k 3 stress: 27,681 completion tokens, 0 server exceptions. ## Speed Tests and Profiling No valid end-to-end before/after comparison exists: the previous HIP path silently executed greedy verification instead of the requested stochastic algorithm, and DSA top-k > 1 page-64 serving crashed before completion. Kernel optimization will follow separately. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). (No semantically valid baseline exists.) - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process). 2. signals.title: [Kimi K3] Rework skipped-think fix as opt-in force_nonempty_content with streaming coverage
signals.text: Stacked on top of #33995. Keeps @yhyang201's original commit `d11868d7d9` in history and supersedes it with a rework. ## Problem K3 sometimes closes its think channel before producing any answer (EOS inside think), so responses come back with `reasoning_content` but empty `content`. #33995 fixed the non-stream path by treating marker-less output as content, which has two leaks: - **Truncated reasoning becomes content**: a `max_tokens` cut also produces zero think markers, so truncated thinking gets misclassified as the answer. - **Streaming stays broken**: the branch only exists in `detect_and_parse`; `parse_streaming_increment` starts in `force_reasoning=True` and streams the raw payload as `reasoning_text`, so `stream=True` still returns `content=""`. ## What this PR does Reworks the fix as an opt-in, K3-native `force_nonempty_content`: - `KimiK3Detector.__init__` accepts `force_nonempty_content` so the existing `chat_template_kwargs` plumbing in `ReasoningParser` works (previously `TypeError`). - `detect_and_parse` reclassifies only on positive evidence: `RESPONSE_CLOSE` or `MESSAGE_CLOSE` present and zero think markers (full or partial). Bare marker-free text (truncated reasoning) stays reasoning. - Streaming **never holds chunks back**. A hold-back would starve SSE during long thinking runs (no delta until the channel decision) and trip client idle timeouts (observed: ~300 s client-side `terminated` while the server is still decoding). Instead, undecided prethink text streams as `reasoning_content` in real time, and `finish()` re-emits the cleaned payload as `content` once the response/message close proves skipped-think — mirroring the base class's `finish()` re-emit of accumulated reasoning. - The `finish()` re-emit is gated on `_in_reasoning`, i.e. it only fires when no channel decision ever happened mid-stream. Without the gate, answers that already streamed as `content` (`RESPONSE_OPEN` expressible, or `force_reasoning=False`) would be emitted a second time. - Under `stream_reasoning=False`, reasoning buffered past a mid-stream cut (e.g. `max_tokens`) still flushes: the non-fnc path delegates to the base `finish()`, and the fnc path flushes the buffer as `reasoning_text` itself, because the base implementation would reclassify it as `content` under fnc — the leak this flag exists to prevent. Clients therefore see: live `reasoning_content` while the model thinks → final `content` delta carrying the actual answer for skipped-think runs; long thinking runs stream uninterrupted end to end. No behavior change for `force_nonempty_content=False`; all existing K3 parser tests unchanged. ## Tests - `test_fnc_non_stream_skipped_think_vs_truncated_reasoning` — non-stream skipped-think vs truncated reasoning under `force_nonempty_content=True`. - `test_fnc_streaming_skipped_think_answer` — real-time reasoning deltas + finish() content re-emit, across chunk sizes 1/5/13. - `test_fnc_streaming_truncated_reasoning_stays_reasoning` — no close evidence → stays reasoning. - `test_fnc_streaming_long_think_streams_without_close` — 20k chars of marker-free thinking streams every chunk live; no hold-back. - `test_fnc_streaming_response_open_not_reemitted` / `test_fnc_streaming_force_reasoning_off_not_reemitted` — answer streams exactly once; the finish() re-emit never duplicates it. - `test_stream_reasoning_off_truncation_flushes_reasoning` — truncated reasoning flushes as reasoning, fnc on and off. - `test_fnc_stream_reasoning_off_skipped_think_reemits_content` — skipped-think re-emit still works when nothing streamed live. The duplication and flush-regression tests fail on the pre-gate code (verified by stashing the fix); everything passes after it. ``` $ pytest test/registered/unit/parser/test_kimik3_reasoning_parser.py test/registered/unit/parser/test_reasoning_parser.py 138 passed ``` ## Validation (BEAM 1M) Full [BEAM](https://github.com/MoonshotAI/Kimi-Vendor-Verifier/tree/main/beam) 1M run (700 long multi-turn questions near 1M context) on a 2-node 8×GB300 devbox, `moonshotai/Kimi-K3` TP8, `--default-chat-template-kwargs '{"force_nonempty_content": true}'`: | | empty content | overall (LLM-judged) | |---|---|---| | flag on (n=700) | **0.71%** (5/700) | 0.333 | | flag off (n=700) | **17.57%** (123/700) | 0.288 | - Empty-answer breakdown by failure mode: with the flag on, only **1/700 (0.14%)** is the skipped-think mode (finish=stop, empty content); the other 4 are finish=length at the 32k-token cap mid-reasoning, which no parser-side fix can address. With the flag off, **116/700 (16.6%)** are the skipped-think mode — the fix eliminates two orders of magnitude of them (16.6% → 0.14%). - A/B improvement is consistent across two independent judges (kimi-k3 self-judge +0.042, deepseek-v4-flash +0.045, full 700-question arms); the control arm's judged score (0.274/0.288 across judges) matches the externally reported 0.264 for this endpoint, so the eval setup lines up with theirs. Judge caveat: no official judge endpoint available, so absolute scores carry a judge-identity caveat; the empty-rate claim does not depend on the judge. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32437096484](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32437096484)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32437096359](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32437096359)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32437096508](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32437096508)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [AMD] Port CP V2 to the DeepSeek-V4 HIP backend
signals.text: Enables DeepSeek-V4 CP-v2 on ROCm by aligning the HIP metadata and KV-cache paths with the CP-v2 layout. ## Motivation [#33532](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33532) enabled DeepSeek-V4 CP-v2 in the CUDA backend, but the HIP backend still built metadata for the unsplit layout. Enabling CP-v2 on ROCm therefore produced inconsistent query metadata and cache-write locations. ## Changes - Port the CP-v2 metadata contract to the HIP backend: query metadata uses the padded CP layout, while cache-write locations remain in global logical-token order. - Pass `forward_batch` and the logical token count through prefill metadata construction, then reindex rank-local fields. - Skip the legacy CP-v1 model hook when CP-v2 is active. - Pad round-robin query metadata to each rank's physical row count. - For the non-unified fused QK/RoPE path, defer the SWA write until after the CP gather and reuse the already transformed KV. No attention kernel changes are required. ## Validation On 8×MI355X with DeepSeek-V4-Flash-DSpark, TP8, GSM8K (200 questions): - No CP: accuracy `0.950`, invalid `0.000`. - CP8 / CP-v1: accuracy `0.955`, invalid `0.000`. - CP8 / CP-v2: accuracy `0.950`, invalid `0.000`. The accuracy run used `unified_kv_triton`. A focused unit test separately covers the non-unified fused-store path and verifies that transformed KV is reused rather than computed twice (`1 passed`). `pre-commit` also passes on all changed files. cc @kkHuang-amd @HaiShaw @1am9trash <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32458806486](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32458806486)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32458806343](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32458806343)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32458806335](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32458806335)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [RL, Spec] DFlash: top-p mask capture
signals.text: ## Relationship to existing work #27408 introduced sampling-mask output support. #35205 restored the finite-`top_k` requirement and bounded support packing for sampling masks. #33459 added the DFlash SpecV2 logprob path. This PR extends that machinery to the DFlash family, with worker-specific adapters for DFlash and DSpark, while preserving the finite-`top_k` contract from #35205. ## Motivation Sampling masks let RL trainers reconstruct the inference policy more accurately and reduce rollout/training policy mismatch. This change makes that metadata available when using DFlash or DSpark speculative decoding. ## Modifications - Add a shared speculative sampling-mask capture/output contract used by DFlash and DSpark. - Capture masks and selected-token logprobs from the final adjusted target policy, including grammar, penalties, logit bias, and custom logit processors. - Keep speculative acceptance logic method-specific. - Align metadata with committed `out_tokens` and `commit_lens`, letting the existing result-processing path trim it alongside generated tokens. - Support DSpark compact/ragged verification after logits are restored to strided layout. - Reconstruct target policy per row for mixed-greedy DSpark batches; greedy rows emit singleton masks with logprob 0. - Pack only finite top-k support before device-to-host transfer. - Reject sampling-mask requests with unbounded top-k, `min_p`, simulated acceptance, or unsupported speculative methods. - For DFlash, additionally require non-greedy verification support and exact acceptance thresholds, and prevent incompatible runtime threshold changes while mask requests are active. - Do not enable sampling-mask capture for EAGLE, NGRAM, or other speculative methods. ## Tests - Added DFlash end-to-end coverage in the existing DFlash suite. - Added one DSpark end-to-end test covering a mixed greedy/sampling batch. - Ran focused formatting, lint, compilation, and diff checks. ## Performance considerations Capture remains opt-in. Support is bounded by finite top-k and packed before device-to-host transfer. DSpark performs opt-in target-policy recomputation after verification, so mask capture adds additional probability reconstruction work; this does not affect requests that do not request masks. ## Accuracy Tests Targeted final implementation: - 4/4 DFlash sampling-mask unit tests passed in Modal: - tensor-backed deferred materialization; - filtered target probabilities and selected-token logprobs; - greedy singleton masks; - whole-request rejection on support overflow. - Added registered DFlash server coverage asserting: - seven generated tokens produce seven masks and seven logprobs; - every sampled token belongs to its corresponding support. - Full Qwen3.6 NVFP4+DFlash B200 run: - 98,304 measured output tokens; - 49,152 requested masks returned, with no missing masks; - maximum observed top-p support was 5,306; a repeat reached 7,476; - completed without generation or mask-alignment errors. This feature only returns metadata and is not intended to change sampling decisions, so no downstream task-accuracy benchmark was run. ## Speed Tests and Profiling One B200 with: - nvidia/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-NVFP4; - modal-labs/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-DFlash; - DFlash block size 8, FA4 draft attention; - 32 concurrent requests, 512 generated tokens each; - warmup followed by six alternating mask/no-mask rounds. Results: - Without masks: 4,163.78 tok/s median - With masks: 4,160.45 tok/s median - Ratio: 0.9992, or approximately −0.08% The difference was within run-to-run noise. A complete repeat also showed no slowdown. ## Checklist - [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process). 2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers. 3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so. - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci` 4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32516412185](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32516412185)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32516411856](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32516411856)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32516412360](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32516412360)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [AMD][DCP] Skip unused QuickAllReduce allocation for DCP groups
signals.text: ## Motivation On ROCm, `GroupCoordinator` currently initializes QuickAllReduce whenever custom all-reduce is enabled. That is useful for TP, but current DCP communication paths do not dispatch to QuickAllReduce: - `ag_rs`: all-gather plus reduce-scatter for MLA, or an FP32 all-reduce for MHA. - `a2a` / `fi_a2a`: all-to-all. In a Kimi-K3 TP8/DCP8 profile on MI350X, constructing the DCP QuickAllReduce communicator reserved 4.002 GiB per GPU. Across 1,152 recorded rank-0 DCP collective dispatches, QuickAllReduce was selected zero times. TP QuickAllReduce remains useful and must stay enabled. Related to #29736. ## Modifications - Add an optional `use_quick_allreduce` control to `GroupCoordinator` and `init_model_parallel_group`. - Preserve the existing behavior by default: the new option inherits `use_custom_allreduce` when unspecified. - Disable QuickAllReduce only for the DCP group. - Keep the AITER custom-all-reduce and PyNccl setup unchanged. - Add a unit test that verifies DCP opts out while TP retains the default behavior. ## Accuracy Tests This does not change model math or the collective selected by current DCP paths. The targeted construction test passes: ``` 1 passed, 5 deselected ``` ## Speed Tests and Profiling This PR targets static memory rather than latency. Measured DCP communicator initialization on MI350X: | Component | Reserved per GPU | | --- | ---: | | PyNccl | 1.883 GiB | | AITER custom all-reduce | 3.002 GiB | | QuickAllReduce | 4.002 GiB | QuickAllReduce had zero selections in the recorded DCP dispatches, so this change reclaims the 4.002 GiB DCP allocation without removing TP QuickAllReduce. ## Checklist - [x] Ran pre-commit on the changed files. - [x] Added a focused unit test. - [x] No documentation change is required; the default API behavior is preserved. - [x] No model kernel or output math is changed. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32466886861](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32466886861)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32466886581](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32466886581)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32466886845](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32466886845)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->
