signals.title: [kernel] One rmsnorm kernel for every hidden size, tuned from Python
signals.text: > Generated by Claude. ## Motivation Three rmsnorm kernels (`rmsnorm.cuh`, `fused_add_rmsnorm.cuh`, `rmsnorm_hf.cuh`) with three hand-written dispatches covered a fraction of the hidden sizes SGLang serves. `_is_supported_rmsnorm_hidden_size` admitted only multiples of 256 (512 above 8192); fused-add only multiples of 16 up to 8192. **1536, 2304, 2560 — Qwen3-1.7B, Qwen3-30B, Gemma — all fell back to `forward_native`.** The HF-semantics variant was a separate file only because the flag could not be threaded through, and reaching it cost a `.contiguous()` copy. ## Modifications **One kernel.** `kFusedAdd` and `kCastXBeforeOutMul` become template flags. A tile may over-cover its row: `in_bound` predicates the surplus lanes and folds away entirely when the row divides the tile, so **any even hidden size up to 16384** works. The launcher takes an arbitrary row stride and checks alignment at runtime, which drops the `.contiguous()`. **Schedule moves to Python.** `(vec_size, num_threads, copy_mode)` are the trailing template arguments; C++ only validates them. Retuning now costs one JIT compile per configuration instead of invalidating every module built from the file. Parameterizing by thread count rather than unroll makes padded tiles expressible, and they sometimes win — 5120 gains 17% at batch 1 from a tile that idles 17% of its lanes. **Weight staging (`CopyMode`)**, the one new idea, is taken from [flashinfer's CuTe DSL rmsnorm](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/blob/v0.6.15.post1/flashinfer/norm/kernels/rmsnorm.py) — credited in the file header. RMSNorm reads its row twice, so something must survive the reduction; flashinfer parks the *input* tile in smem to keep it out of registers. Applying the same trick to the *weight* tile frees `kUnroll` vectors of register file: | config | unroll | registers | cp.async | TMA | |---|---|---|---|---| | rmsnorm 12288, 256t | 6 | 87 | **64** | **64** | | rmsnorm 16384, 128t | 16 | 254 | 154 | 168 | | fused_add 12288, 256t | 6 | 102 | **64** | **63** | 12288/256t crossing 64 registers doubles occupancy, 2 → 4 blocks/SM. `cp.async` fills the tile on SM80+; a single `cp.async.bulk` under `elect.sync` on SM90+. ## Accuracy Tests - `test_rmsnorm.py` + `test_fused_add_rmsnorm.py`: **2587 passed** - A correctness matrix over both kernels x bf16/fp16 x both semantics x padded and exact tiles x warp and CTA traits x block sizes from 16 to 1024: **2160 comparisons, 0 over tolerance**, and all three copy modes **bit-identical** to each other (1296 tensor pairs via `torch.equal`) - `sm_80` and `sm_90` cross-compiles of every schedule the Python side emits; TMA is correctly rejected below sm90 (`Feature 'elect' requires .target sm_90`) - End to end on B200: **Qwen3-8B gsm8k 0.927** (300 examples, TMA path live at dim=4096), Qwen3-0.6B 0.635 ## Benchmarking and Profiling B200, bf16, vs the best configuration found by an exhaustive sweep of the previous kernel: | dim | bs=1024 | bs=4096 | bs=8192 | |---|---|---|---| | 4096 | 0.97x | **1.04x** | 1.01x | | 8192 | **1.08x** | **1.04x** | **1.03x** | | 12288 | **1.03x** | **1.05x** | **1.03x** | | 16384 | 1.01x | **1.07x** | **1.04x** | 16384 at batch 8192 lands at 83.9 us, **matching flashinfer for the first time** (previously 3.6% behind). Small batches keep the existing lead — 3072 is 1.78x flashinfer at batch 4. Staging is worth 1.29x (cp.async) / 1.31x (TMA) over the register path at dim=12288, batch 8192, and nothing below unroll 4. The win is proportional to **unroll**, not to hidden size: 16384's best shapes use many threads and low unroll, so they gain least. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Code Formatting with Pre-Commit](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-formatting-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests as outlined in the [Running Unit Tests](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#running-unit-tests-adding-to-ci). - [x] Update documentation / docstrings / example tutorials as needed, according to [Writing Documentation](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#writing-documentation-running-docs-ci). - [x] Provide throughput / latency benchmark results and accuracy evaluation results as needed, according to [Benchmark and Profiling](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/benchmark_and_profiling.html) and [Accuracy Results](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/accuracy_evaluation.html). - [x] For reviewers: If you haven't made any contributions to this PR and are only assisting with merging the main branch, please remove yourself as a co-author when merging the PR. - [x] Please feel free to join our Slack channel at https://slack.sglang.ai to discuss your PR. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32512737979](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32512737979)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32512737666](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32512737666)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32512737905](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32512737905)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [LoRA] Add the sgl_lora MoE execution engine with JSON config resolution
signals.text: ## Motivation MoE (expert-weight) LoRA serving in SGLang currently runs through the experimental TRT-LLM path (`--moe-runner-backend experimental_sgl_trtllm` + virtual experts). That path has structural limits: - **Blackwell-only**: the trtllm-gen kernels require SM100/120, so there is no expert-LoRA path at all on Hopper (H200). - **Virtual-expert routing scales with `max_loras_per_batch × num_experts`**, so multi-adapter serving degrades sharply as slot capacity grows. - **No prefill CUDA graphs with LoRA**, and no support for shared-outer adapter factors (gate_up A / down B shared across experts, `expert_dim=1` — the native format of some recent MoE adapters). This PR adds `sgl_lora`: a self-contained MoE-LoRA execution engine selected with `--lora-execution-engine sgl_lora`, built from an exhaustive kernel/fusion/overlap sweep on GB300, B200, and H200 across three models (Qwen3.5-35B-A3B, Qwen3.5-397B, Inkling-Small; per-expert and shared-outer adapters, ranks 8–64). ## Modifications - **Engine** (`python/sglang/srt/lora/sgl_lora/`): masked expert-major decode path and route-major serial prefill path; per-expert and shared-outer factor layouts; two base-GEMM providers (DeepGEMM, CuTeDSL); side-stream overlap windows for the shared-decode path; capacity-flat routing (cost scales with *active* adapters, not slot capacity). - **JSON config resolution** (`sgl_lora/configs/{gb300,h200,default}.json`): every kernel-family/fusion/overlap/tile decision is data, resolved per (layout, activation, phase, batch shape) through ordered first-match scenario rows with fail-closed validation — a malformed row, unknown plan field, or unknown predicate key aborts startup instead of serving a wrong plan. `SGLANG_SGL_LORA_CONFIG_DIR` points at an override config root (arch JSONs at top level, M-bucketed base-GEMM tile tables under `gemm/`). Every shipped row carries real-model sweep provenance; unknown architectures fall to a conservative serial fallback (`default.json`). - **Prefill CUDA graphs with MoE LoRA** (breakable backend), including graph-stable LoRA workspaces. - **Dense-module gate**: adapter targets are pruned to weight-backed modules at registration, and per-module effective ranks let mixed multi-adapter batches skip dense-LoRA work for adapters that carry no weights for a module (the shared dense kernels in `kernels/ops/gemm` stay byte-identical to upstream — the gate enters as a batch-info view). - **Onboarding tuner** (`benchmark/kernels/lora_moe/tune_lora_config.py`): `--check` (CI-gateable coverage report), `--emit-seed` (serve a new geometry immediately), `--sweep` (e2e-tunes the two geometry-sensitive axes; writes winners back into the seed). - Guards: expert LoRA + DP-attention / elastic-EP / EPLB fail closed at startup (the DP-attention token-axis limitation exists silently in the legacy path today). Scope: bf16 serving path. fp8/nvfp4 qlora support is planned as a follow-up in this PR (the tuner carries a `TODO(quant)` and the config resolver already fails closed on future `quant` predicate keys). Structure note: the first commit is the engine; subsequent commits are review-round changes and will be squashed before undrafting. Two orthogonal fixes found during this work ship separately: `fix/chunked-sgmv-cache-key` (csgmv compile-cache key omits codegen parameters) and `fix/swa-kvpool-v-head-dim` (SWAKVPool lacks `get_v_head_dim`, crashing hybrid-SWA models on the triton attention backend). ## Accuracy Tests - `test/registered/unit/lora/`: 248 passed / 6 skipped (H200), including config-resolution pins, kernel numerics vs an fp32 oracle, byte-identity pins for the decode kernel policy, and prefill graph-vs-eager bit-exactness. - Greedy-decode correctness on real adapters vs the legacy triton reference: per-token logprob deltas at the measured bf16 noise floor (per-expert and shared-outer, all three campaign models). ## Speed Tests and Profiling Protocol: `bench_one_batch_server`, input 4096 / output 1024, bs 1/8/16/32, `max_loras_per_batch=4` distinct adapters, medians after first-pass discard. Baseline = experimental TRT-LLM LoRA path at its best posture (incl. prefill graphs where it can use them). - **Qwen3.5-35B (GB300, TP4)**: prefill +15–19%, decode parity. - **Qwen3.5-397B (B200, TP8)**: prefill +23%, decode −1.2%…+4.5% across bs. - **Inkling-Small (GB300)**: decode +0.5%…+11.9% with the model's shared/routed-expert parallelism active on both engines; prefill +2–5%. - **H200 (fa4 posture)**: the TRT engine cannot run (SM100/120-only kernels); vs the only runnable incumbent (legacy virtual experts on triton fused_moe): decode +1.7%…+19.7%, prefill +1.0–1.5% at bs≥8 (−13% at bs1). - **Prefill CUDA graphs**: 2.5–3.0× prefill throughput vs eager at equal chunking (the incumbent disables prefill graphs under LoRA). - **Multi-adapter**: routing cost is capacity-flat; with 4 distinct adapters/ranks resident, +15–24% prefill and +2–17% decode vs the incumbent. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: **Missing `run-ci` label** -- add it to run CI tests.<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: **Blocked** -- `run-ci` is required first.<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:heavy_minus_sign: **No AMD PR run found for this commit**.<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [HiSparse] Fix copy_cache_planned_kernel grid sizing for prefetch replay
signals.text: ## Motivation `copy_cache_planned_kernel` (introduced in #34329, HiSparse shared-index/IndexShare prefetch) replays a shared-index anchor's recorded miss plan into each skip layer's device buffer on a side stream. It launches with a small, batch-size-independent grid (`num_blocks=4`) and round-robins all requests' misses across that fixed set of warps. This works well at low batch size / low miss counts (the kernel's comment cites a 183us -> 29us H200 microbenchmark at bs=100 with 2 misses/req), but the total (request, miss) work grows with batch size while the grid does not. As batch size and per-request miss counts increase, the copy kernel's own wall time grows faster than the compute it's supposed to overlap. Because skip layers block on an event recorded after this kernel finishes, the anchor's compute stream ends up waiting on it — the prefetch's win shrinks and, past a few dozen concurrent requests, inverts into a regression relative to disabling prefetch entirely. ## Modifications Switch the grid to one block per request (`num_blocks=num_reqs`), the same convention `load_cache_to_device_buffer_kernel` already uses for the anchor's own swap-in. Each block now only handles its own request's miss list (round-robin across the block's warps), instead of a global round-robin over a fixed warp count. Parallelism now scales with the batch instead of sitting behind a fixed grid size. Files changed: - `python/sglang/kernels/jit/csrc/hisparse.cuh`: `copy_cache_planned_kernel` rewritten to one-block-per-request scheduling. - `python/sglang/srt/managers/hisparse_coordinator.py`: `_run_copy_only_kernel` passes `num_blocks=num_reqs` instead of a fixed constant. This trades away one property of the old design — a single request with an unusually large miss burst could previously draw on every warp in the grid — for parallelism that scales unconditionally with batch size. In practice this tradeoff favors the new design: all blocks launch concurrently well within the GPU's SM count, and requests sharing an anchor group go through the same top-k selection / LRU eviction logic, so large per-request miss skew is uncommon. ## Accuracy Tests No output change expected: the kernel still reads the same `miss_src`/`miss_dst`/`miss_counts` plan recorded by the anchor and performs the same per-item copy; only the block/warp assignment changed. Added a unit test to `test/registered/kernels/ops/kvcache/test_hisparse.py` (`test_copy_cache_planned_replays_per_request_with_varying_miss_counts`) that directly exercises `copy_cache_planned_mla` with `num_blocks=num_reqs` on a 3-request batch with varying miss counts (1, 1, 0), verifying each request's miss bytes land only in its own destination slots. Ran the full `test_hisparse.py` + `test_hisparse_prefetch.py` suite on the target hardware (14 passed, 8 skipped — skips are ROCm-only cases on this CUDA box). Also ran smoke tests (single request, greedy decoding, `temperature=0`) before each benchmark run below to confirm end-to-end output correctness under the real PD-disaggregated deployment. ## Speed Tests and Profiling 8x RTX PRO 6000 (SM120), GLM-5.2-nvfp4, TP8, PD disaggregated decode, DSA attention backend with `flashinfer_sparse_mla`, fp8_e4m3 KV cache, `top_k=2048`， 32k input，4k output. Decode steady-state gen throughput (tok/s) at fixed batch size: | BS | sync swap-in (prefetch off) | prefetch, old grid=4 | prefetch, this PR | vs sync | vs old grid=4 | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | 1 | 44.84 | 45.42 | 50.09 | +11.7% | +10.3% | | 2 | 79.00 | 69.34 | 89.46 | +13.2% | +29.0% | | 4 | 145.08 | 103.48 | 166.10 | +14.5% | +60.5% | | 8 | 269.87 | 150.95 | 318.79 | +18.1% | +111.2% | | 16 | 392.70 | 188.11 | 462.51 | +17.8% | +145.8% | | 32 | 558.33 | 218.37 | 633.26 | +13.4% | +190.0% | | 54 | 700.74 | 223.35 | 772.35 | +10.2% | +245.8% | With the old fixed grid, enabling prefetch is already a regression vs. disabling it starting around BS=2, and the regression grows with scale (-68% at BS=54). With this fix, prefetch is a consistent 10-18% win over synchronous swap-in across the entire batch-size range tested, with no batch-size-dependent falloff — matching the intent of #34329. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. signals.title: [NPU] [Diffusion] Fix critical Ascend NPU Diffusion regression/bugs & restore 2-NPU CI testcase
signals.text: ## Motivation Restore Ascend/NPU packed Ring Attention, 2-NPU diffusion CI suite, fix NPU correctness, runtime, and CI regressions exposed by recent Ring, SRT-CLIP, residency, and MOVA changes. After [#35004](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/35004), diffusion can import SRT CLIP code and execute SRT `init_npu_backend()`. Importing `torch_npu.contrib.transfer_to_npu` inside a native NPU diffusion process globally rewrites CUDA-facing APIs/device arguments and can alter runtime feature detection and kernel selection. `allow_internal_format=True` is also known to regress unquantized diffusion performance; the earlier Wan regression in [#20533](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/20533), fixed by [#20684](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/20684), increased `DecodingStage` from **6.1889 s to 11.76 s (+90.0%, 1.90x slower)**. The packed-attention implementation is extracted from the Ascend work in [#33569](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33569). ## Modifications - **Packed varlen / Ring Attention.** [#33327](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33327) extended Qwen to tail-padded Ring and fixed `u=1, r>1` replicated-token semantics, exposing the shared packed `flash_attn_varlen_func` path on NPU. Add an Ascend implementation backed by `npu_fused_infer_attention_score` (`TND`) with independent Q/K packed lengths, boundary validation, empty/non-contiguous handling, LSE normalization, and `AscendFlashAttnImpl.forward_varlen`. Unsupported FlashAttention options fail explicitly. - **Diffusion NPU runtime isolation.** Keep the SRT CUDA-compatibility layer out of diffusion: when `sglang.multimodal_gen` is loaded, do not import `torch_npu.contrib.transfer_to_npu` and do not enable `torch_npu.npu.config.allow_internal_format`. Preserve the existing `torch.cuda.is_available=False` re-mock on the SRT path after `transfer_to_npu`. `jit_compile=False` remains unchanged. - **MOVA 2-NPU correctness.** [#31453](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/31453) left a contiguous-layout assumption after attention. Multi-NPU attention may return a non-contiguous tensor, so use `reshape()` instead of `view()`. - **Host-memory accounting.** [#35641](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/35641) introduced storage-based module sizing for host-memory budgeting. Skip tensors whose storage access raises `RuntimeError` instead of failing memory planning; add focused unit coverage. - **NPU CI / GT.** - Restore the 2-NPU diffusion suite on `linux-aarch64-a3-800t-16`. - Split both 1-NPU and 2-NPU suites into two partitions. - Run GT generation on the A3-800T runner families. - Make GT jobs check out the requested `workflow_dispatch` ref. - Retry transient HTTP/image-decoding failures while downloading GT. - Update the NPU GT revision to `8e3d717e65fb87339c2974382a092a731669f884`. - **NPU dependencies.** Pin `sgl-kernel-npu` to `2026.8.13` and install the packaged `attentions` wheel in NPU CI/Docker; update release Docker pins accordingly. - **Performance baselines.** Refresh affected FLUX.2 text-encoding, ERNIE timestep-preparation, and LTX-2 connector/decoding baselines plus partition-duration estimates for the current A3-800T / auto-residency environment. Related residency policy: [#34615](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/34615). These are CI baseline updates, not algorithmic speedups. ## Accuracy Tests - NPU diffusion GT was regenerated successfully after the Ring semantic changes and A3-800T CI migration: [Generate Diffusion CI Ground Truth #32478548704](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32478548704). - Qwen Ring keeps the corrected semantics from #33327; no consistency thresholds are relaxed. - Runtime isolation changes backend initialization/dispatch only; #20684 reported no accuracy impact from disabling the problematic internal-format behavior. - The restored 2-NPU suite exercises the packed Ring path. - Invalid-storage host-memory handling has dedicated unit coverage. ## Speed Tests and Profiling The runtime fix prevents diffusion from inheriting SRT's global CUDA-compatibility monkey patches and `allow_internal_format=True`. ## Checklist - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32500914758](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32500914758)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32500914325](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32500914325)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32500914802](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32500914802)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [SM12x] b12x MXFP4 MoE: align with vLLM's pin, share the arena, run W4A8
signals.text: Updates the DSv4-Flash b12x MXFP4 expert backend so sglang runs the same MoE kernels the official vLLM DGX Spark image runs. This supersedes the earlier revision of this PR: same backend, but on the op-registry generation of b12x, with one shared scratch arena, and with the activation-quantized recipe on by default. Branch: `b12x-moe-sm12x` (force-push of the reviewed content; four commits). ## Why The official vLLM DGX Spark image (`eugr/spark-vllm-b12x`, nightly-20260815) ships b12x built from `local-inference-lab/b12x` master at `b4d6c7593`, which is the op-registry re-architecture (`Caps -> plan -> bind -> run`, `b12x.moe.fused_moe`). The previous revision of this backend targeted the 0.15.3 `b12x.integration.tp_moe` API, so the two stacks were running different kernels and any comparison between them was measuring two things at once. ## What changed **1. Migrate the MoE backend to the op-registry generation.** `prepare_b12x_fp4_moe_weights` splits into `plan_weights` + `prepare_weights`; format / layout / activation move onto the weight plan; `Caps` takes `weight_plan=experts.plan` instead of the per-tensor fields; `bind` takes `experts=` instead of 12 tensor kwargs, plus the W4A16 contract flags vLLM sets (`input_scales_static=True`, `unit_scale_contract=True`). `w13_layout` stays `up_gate` — sglang stores fused W13 as `[up; gate]`, and vLLM's `"w31"` reflects its own `[gate; up]` storage; copying that value would be a silent correctness bug. The compile-cache variable is renamed with the generation (`B12X_CUTE_COMPILE_CACHE_DIR` -> `B12X_COMPILE_CACHE_DIR`); the old name is not merely ignored, it is folded into the compile-cache key and fragments it. The generation guard becomes structural rather than a version string, because the wheel version stayed `1.2.3` across the re-architecture and cannot distinguish generations. **2. The pin is two commits past the vLLM image tree.** Both hops fix b12x code paths that sglang stages and vLLM's recipe never touches, which is why the image runs without them: - `5c8318009` — *Fix route-packed W4A16 top-k scaling* (b12x #219). At `b4d6c7593` the route-packed W4A16 epilogue references `metadata_row`, which is never defined when `mul_topk_weights` is compile-time enabled. Our FC2 applies top-k weights in-kernel, so it fails to compile. vLLM never stages that path (direct small-M kernels, router weight applied on the input). - `85d3681b` — *preallocate W4A16 route histograms for CUDA graph capture* (b12x #150). At `5c8318009` the non-trellis W4A16 arena spec list omits the route-packing histogram, so `bind` maps no view for it and the eager `torch.empty` fallback is refused under capture (`expert_counts is not initialized for CUDA graph capture`). vLLM sidesteps this by making b12x MoE a piecewise-graph boundary; sglang captures the full model graph and needs the histogram in the arena. Both landed upstream the same evening as the image tree. Every other commit in the interval is comm / PCIe-DCP-only and inert here. **3. One scratch plan and one arena, shared across expert layers.** Per-layer `torch.empty` resurrected the arena-duplication bug the 0.15.3 line already fixed once: 46 expert layers x ~250 MB left no room for the KV cache at `--mem-fraction-static=0.75` — the server refused to boot, and the minimum viable fraction was 0.829. Every expert layer presents identical caps, so one plan and one arena serve them all, which is also what vLLM's shared workspace manager does. Sharing is safe because `bind` is a pure view mapping over the arena: it holds no per-layer state, and the weight-plan identity check it performs passes across layers because `MoEWeightPreparationPlan` is a tensor-free frozen dataclass with value equality. Both live in `get_resources().buffers` behind a caps fingerprint, and layers are prepared at load time, before any capture, so the allocation never moves an address a captured graph baked. **4. W4A8 by default — this flips the numerics of this backend.** The vLLM image does not run the MoE as W4A16: its recipe sets `B12X_MOE_FORCE_A8=1`, selecting `quant_mode=w4a8_mx`, where activations are quantized to MXFP8-E4M3 in-kernel and served by the micro / dynamic kernel families that carry all of b12x's GB10 tuning. The W4A16 monolith is 945 us/launch at M=6 against their tuned dynamic path, and their kernel is trace-confirmed as `MoEDynamicKernelSilu`, which is structurally w4a8-only. W4A8 picks implementation (micro vs dynamic) and tile regime from the live token count, so the launcher plans per call, vLLM-style. That is affordable because b12x planning on this recipe is host-only and allocation-free, and under full-graph capture it runs once per bucket at capture time — replay is pure GPU. The shared arena is sized once over the whole count ladder via `required_nbytes`. `unit_scale_contract` stays W4A16-only per b12x's own gating; `input_scales_static` holds for both. **Accuracy evidence for the default flip.** DSv4-Flash on 2x DGX Spark, GSM8K with no simulated accept length, three runs: **0.980 / 0.975 / 0.965**. Speculative accept length holds at **4.02** — no degradation attributable to the activation quantization. To go back: `SGLANG_B12X_MOE_QUANT_MODE=w4a16` restores the frozen-plan bf16-activation path unchanged. **5. Shaping (no behavior change).** - New `python/sglang/srt/utils/b12x.py` holds the pin, the install hint, the generation guard and the compile-cache plumbing. sglang runs b12x from more than one place, and each caller was about to grow its own copy; one home means a pin move is one edit and the guard cannot drift between backends. - The compile-cache write becomes `setdefault`, so an explicitly configured `B12X_COMPILE_CACHE_DIR` is honoured instead of overwritten at import. - The generation guard also checks the op-registry entry points (`Caps`, `plan`, `plan_weights`, `prepare_weights`, `run`), so a partial match fails at startup with the install hint instead of as an `AttributeError` deep in weight loading. ## Environment variables | Name | Default | Meaning | |---|---|---| | `SGLANG_B12X_MOE_QUANT_MODE` | `w4a8_mx` | b12x quant mode, passed through verbatim. `w4a16` restores the previous path. Replaces the boolean sketch (`SGLANG_B12X_MOE_A8`) — the knob is the string b12x actually takes, and the set of modes is b12x's to grow. | | `SGLANG_B12X_ENABLE_WARMUP` | `True` | Compile every planned token count at load time, before capture. Renamed from `SGLANG_B12X_WARMUP` for the `ENABLE_` verb; the old name never shipped, so there is no alias. | | `SGLANG_B12X_MAX_TOKENS` | `4096` | Upper bound on tokens in one MoE call; sizes the arena. Track `--chunked-prefill-size` if that is raised. | | `SGLANG_B12X_CACHE_DIR` | `<sglang cache>/b12x` | Forwarded to `B12X_COMPILE_CACHE_DIR`. | ## Install ``` pip install --no-deps "b12x @ https://github.com/local-inference-lab/b12x/archive/85d3681bb2c3749e4e94e121d5d829c7ec6f0b9f.tar.gz" ``` `--no-deps` is required: b12x's metadata pulls a newer torch and breaks the rest of the image. ## Scope SM120 / SM121 only, and only reachable when the b12x MoE method is selected — no other target's code path is touched. Earlier b12x generations (0.15.x, the PyPI 1.2.x wheels) are rejected at startup rather than producing different numerics silently. ## Test plan - 2x DGX Spark (GB10, sm_121), DeepSeek-V4-Flash, TP=2: server boots at `--mem-fraction-static=0.75` (the arena fix), full-model CUDA graph capture completes (the `85d3681b` hop), GSM8K as above. - `SGLANG_B12X_MOE_QUANT_MODE=w4a16` exercises the frozen-plan path. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32513702094](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32513702094)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32513701772](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32513701772)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32513702106](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32513702106)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [Diffusion] Add MiniMax H3 cube sparse attention
signals.text: ## Summary - add a FlexAttention-based cube sparse attention backend for MiniMax H3's 3D visual streams - wire H3 packed-sequence metadata and denoise-step sparsity schedules into the native pipeline - keep text, audio, standalone reference images, and the text-only token refiner on dense attention - document the component-scoped command and add numerical, CUDA, admission, and parallelism coverage ## Behavior Select the backend only for the H3 transformer: ```bash --component-attention-backends transformer=cube_sparse_attn \ --attention-backend-config '{"local_cube_size":[4,4,4],"topk_ratio_list":[1.0,1.0,0.8,0.7,0.6,0.5,0.5]}' ``` A ratio of `1.0` uses H3's native FlashAttention path. Ratios below `1.0` use approximate cube sparsity. Ring parallelism is rejected because its attention exchange does not compose with this backend; Ulysses remains supported. ## Recommended `attention-backend-config` For `num_inference_steps=50` (49 denoise updates), use: ```json { "local_cube_size": [4, 4, 4], "topk_ratio_list": [ 1.0, 1.0, 0.55, 0.45, 0.35, 0.35, 0.30, 0.25, 0.25, 0.20, 0.20, 0.20, 0.15, 0.15, 0.15, 0.10, 0.10, 0.10, 0.10, 0.05, 0.05, 0.05, 0.05, 0.05, 0.05, 0.05, 0.05, 0.05, 0.05, 0.05, 0.05, 0.05, 0.05, 0.05, 0.05, 0.05, 0.05, 0.05, 0.05, 0.05, 0.05, 0.05, 0.05, 0.05, 0.05, 0.05, 0.05, 0.05, 0.05 ] } ``` Pass this JSON through `--attention-backend-config` alongside the component-scoped backend selection above. ## Implementation Note The Cube sparse attention backend in this PR is a reference implementation built with PyTorch FlexAttention. For higher performance on supported NVIDIA hardware, future work may explore replacing it with cuDNN Frontend's Block Sparse Attention ([cudnn-frontend/python/cudnn/block_sparse_attention at main · NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/tree/main/python/cudnn/block_sparse_attention)) operator. Broader hardware support and backend-specific optimizations are left to future community contributions. ## Performance On 2×H100 with the 1344×768, 4-second, 8-step TP2 workload: - dense FlashAttention denoise: 16.51s - aggressive all-`0.05` sparse schedule: 13.32s (19.3% faster) - mixed `[1.0, 1.0, 0.8, 0.7, 0.6, 0.5, 0.5]` schedule: 19.67s The mixed schedule is slower on this short sequence because FlexAttention routing overhead outweighs the sparse-kernel savings, so the feature remains opt-in and the cookbook calls out the tradeoff. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32444805483](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32444805483)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32444805371](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32444805371)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32444805340](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32444805340)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [Perf] Fuse prefill norm/act quantization for NVFP4 W4A4 hybrid models (Qwen3.5 family)
signals.text: > Rebased onto `main` after #34859 merged: the SiLU+FP4-quant base fusion landed with the model support, so this PR's net diff contains the three remaining changes (attention-layer SiLU coverage, post-LN+FP4-quant, and gated-norm+FP8-quant). ## Motivation For Qwen3.5-family hybrid (GDN + attention) models served with a mixed ModelOpt NVFP4(W4A4)+FP8 checkpoint, prefill spends a measurable share of GPU time in standalone norm / activation / quantization glue kernels: every projection input is normalized, written to HBM in bf16, then re-read and quantized by a separate kernel. Kernel-level tracing against vLLM 0.27.1 on the same model showed the GEMM/attention/GDN families at parity while SGLang lost time in this glue (vLLM fuses norm+quant and act+quant via torch.compile). This PR removes the extra round-trips with three targeted fusions (all bit-equivalent up to FP4/FP8 rounding ties, each with a kill switch): 1. **SiLU+mul + NVFP4 quant** for dense MLPs: replaces `act_and_mul` + the standalone per-block FP4 quantize with FlashInfer's `silu_and_mul_scaled_nvfp4_experts_quantize` (single-group form), handing `down_proj` a prequantized `(fp4, swizzled_scale)` tuple through the existing `_accepts_prequantized_fp4` path. Enabled for both GDN-layer and attention-layer MLPs. 2. **Post-attention GemmaRMSNorm + NVFP4 quant**: FlashInfer `add_rmsnorm_fp4quant` fuses the residual-add, the norm, and the `gate_up` input quant into one kernel. Gemma's `(1 + w)` scaling is folded into a precomputed weight; the swizzled block-scale is exposed as the 2D `(m_padded, K/16)` view so the cuDNN mm_fp4 backend's shape validation also passes. 3. **GDN gated RMSNorm + static-FP8 quant**: adds an fp8-store epilogue to the `fla` `layernorm_gated` Triton kernel (skips the bf16 intermediate write entirely) and teaches `ModelOptFp8LinearMethod` to accept a prequantized `(fp8, scale)` tuple for `out_proj` (explicit opt-in attribute, mirroring the fp4 path). Kill switches: `SGLANG_DISABLE_SILU_FP4_QUANT_FUSION=1`, `SGLANG_DISABLE_POST_LN_FP4_QUANT_FUSION=1`, `SGLANG_DISABLE_GATED_NORM_FP8_QUANT_FUSION=1`. The fusions auto-enable only when the touched projections use the matching ModelOpt linear method (NVFP4 W4A4 for 1-2, per-tensor static FP8 for 3), so other checkpoints and quant modes keep their current control flow. ## Benchmark Re-benchmarked on 2026-08-20 against the current PR base and head. Both lanes ran back-to-back on the same otherwise-idle physical GPU with the same container, model snapshot, server flags, prompt seed, and client command. ### Environment and revisions | Item | Value | |---|---| | GPU | NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition (SM120), physical GPU 2 | | Driver | 580.159.03 | | Container | `lmsysorg/sglang:qwen38` | | PyTorch / CUDA | `2.13.0+cu130` / CUDA 13.0 | | FlashInfer | 0.6.18 | | Model | `RadixArk/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4` | | Model snapshot | `554ebba9b5f1b79dc11246341960360e6ef05ef4` | | main/base | `a4ffb996db3e823708a53637f851e2677d4455a8` | | PR head | `a3facf77a9bf07464d87299d21dede0837df8e9d` | | merge base | `a4ffb996db3e823708a53637f851e2677d4455a8` | Because the merge base equals the tested main revision, this comparison isolates the PR's net diff. ### Commands The commands below were run inside the existing `sglang_bbuf` container. For the main lane, `SGLANG_TREE=/work/pr34934-rebench-main`; for the PR lane, `SGLANG_TREE=/work/pr34934-rebench-head`. Server: ```bash SGLANG_TREE=/work/pr34934-rebench-head CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=2 \ PYTHONPATH="${SGLANG_TREE}/python" \ python -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path RadixArk/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4 \ --host 0.0.0.0 \ --port 31002 \ --tp-size 1 \ --chunked-prefill-size 8192 \ --max-prefill-tokens 8192 \ --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 \ --mamba-ssm-dtype bfloat16 \ --disable-radix-cache ``` Benchmark client: ```bash SGLANG_TREE=/work/pr34934-rebench-head LANE=pr ROUND=1 CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES= \ PYTHONPATH="${SGLANG_TREE}/python" \ python -m sglang.bench_serving \ --backend sglang \ --host 127.0.0.1 \ --port 31002 \ --dataset-name random \ --model RadixArk/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4 \ --random-input-len 8192 \ --random-output-len 1024 \ --random-range-ratio 1 \ --num-prompts 5 \ --request-rate inf \ --max-concurrency 1 \ --seed 1234 \ --warmup-requests 1 \ --disable-tqdm \ --output-details \ --output-file "/work/pr34934-rebench-artifacts/${LANE}-round-${ROUND}.jsonl" ``` For each revision, one complete five-request run was discarded as a pre-run, then the recorded command was run three times (five requests per round, 15 measured requests per revision). Every invocation also ran the client's one built-in warmup request. GPU 2 had 0 MiB allocated before the first server was started and after the final server was stopped. ### Per-round results | Revision | Round | Mean TTFT (ms) | Median TTFT (ms) | Output tok/s | Median ITL (ms) | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | main | 1 | 655.48 | 642.42 | 64.66 | 14.94 | | main | 2 | 655.66 | 649.62 | 64.22 | 14.96 | | main | 3 | 653.87 | 638.01 | 64.41 | 14.96 | | PR | 1 | 638.52 | 626.78 | 64.32 | 14.95 | | PR | 2 | 640.99 | 627.77 | 64.42 | 14.95 | | PR | 3 | 640.33 | 628.54 | 64.53 | 14.95 | ### Aggregate result TTFT aggregates all 15 per-request observations. Output throughput is total generated tokens divided by total benchmark duration across the three recorded rounds. | Metric | main | main + this PR | Delta | |---|---:|---:|---:| | Mean TTFT | 655.00 ms | **639.95 ms** | **-15.06 ms (-2.30%)** | | Median TTFT | 642.42 ms | **627.77 ms** | **-14.65 ms (-2.28%)** | | Output throughput | 64.43 tok/s | 64.42 tok/s | -0.02% | | Median ITL | 14.957 ms | 14.949 ms | -0.008 ms | For the paired TTFT observations, the mean gain was 15.06 ms and the approximate 95% confidence interval was 10.79-19.32 ms. The current result supports a stable ~2.3% prefill TTFT improvement; decode throughput and ITL are unchanged within run-to-run noise. Startup logs confirmed that the optimized paths were active for the expected layers: - post-LN + FP4 quant: 64 layers - SiLU + FP4 quant: 64 layers - gated RMSNorm + FP8 quant: 48 GDN layers Both server logs were checked for traceback, CUDA error, OOM, and exception signatures; none were found. ### Correctness validation Correctness was not rerun as part of the 2026-08-20 performance pass. The earlier full GSM8K validation (1319 examples) reported: | Configuration | Score | |---|---:| | fusions off | 0.9635 | | fusions on | 0.9658 | The fused kernels were also previously checked for identical residual propagation relative to `fused_add_rmsnorm`. ### Data provenance The performance tables above come from the current PR head and its exact merge base, using three saved `bench_serving --output-details` JSONL results per lane. They replace the older 5-request/FlashInfer-0.6.17 table, which was measured against an earlier base and was not reproducible as a current-main/current-PR comparison. The previous H200 FP8-dynamic table was removed because these W4A4-specific fusions are inactive for that checkpoint and therefore it did not measure this PR's performance effect. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Code Formatting with Pre-Commit](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-formatting-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests as outlined in the [Running Unit Tests](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#running-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation / docstrings / example tutorials as needed, according to [Writing Documentation](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#writing-documentation). - [x] Provide throughput / latency benchmark results and accuracy evaluation results as needed, according to [Benchmark and Profiling](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/benchmark_and_profiling.html) and [Accuracy Results](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#accuracy-results). - [x] For reviewers: If you haven't made any contributions to this PR and are only assisting with merging the main branch, please remove yourself as a co-author when merging. - [x] Please feel free to join our Slack channel at https://slack.sglang.ai to discuss your PR. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32368351888](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32368351888)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32368351907](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32368351907)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32368351823](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32368351823)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: perf: overlap Qwen shared expert with DeepEP routed experts
signals.text: ## Motivation For Qwen MoE models using CUDA and DeepEP, the shared expert currently runs on the default stream before the routed-expert path. This serializes two independent computations and leaves an available alternate stream unused. This PR adds an opt-in path that overlaps the Qwen shared expert with routed-expert/DeepEP execution. ## Modifications - Add `SGLANG_QWEN_DEEPEP_SHARED_OVERLAP` (default: `false`). - When enabled on CUDA, enqueue the shared expert on `alt_stream`, execute the routed-expert path on the current stream, and wait on an event immediately before accumulating the shared output. - When breakable CUDA graph is active, skip this optimization and retain the existing serial shared-expert path; cross-segment overlap across the eager DeepEP break is out of scope. - Document the new environment variable. ## Accuracy Tests The accuracy evidence below was collected on predecessor `38f714d28e1fa01ae5b1ce38ce576373b8293722`, based on upstream main `0c072235f44fce4b89e594c2d3348e4f48e774b8`, with a clean source tree. Current head `76815b3766deb3a3c9aceef1cb346093f691d976` differs only by making breakable CUDA graph use the pre-existing serial fallback instead of an alternate-stream path with an immediate wait; the non-breakable overlap implementation measured below is unchanged. Configuration: `nvidia/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-NVFP4`, 8x GB300, FP4 weights, FP8 KV cache, TP8/DP8/EP8, NEXTN draft length 6, DeepEP low-latency mode, 200 GSM8K examples, 5 shots, temperature 0.6, top-p 0.95, and top-k 20. The run used natural NEXTN acceptance. | Metric | Result | Gate | |---|---:|---:| | GSM8K score | **0.990** (200/200) | >= 0.95 | | Request-weighted mean accepted length | **4.6102** (1,379 decode-log rows; request weight 11,625) | > 3.3 | | Evaluation latency | 95.646 s | -- | | Evaluation output throughput | 5,621.1 token/s | -- | All eight ranks completed target verify CUDA graph capture, followed by draft decode and draft extend graph capture. The job completed successfully with exit code 0. Breakable CUDA graph is now intentionally excluded from this optimization, and no performance gain is claimed for that fallback. ## Speed Tests and Profiling The performance A/B exercised the same overlap mechanism on the benchmark stack before this upstream-main port. The upstream-main commit listed in the accuracy section was validated separately through CUDA graph capture and GSM8K. The end-to-end A/B comparison used the same configuration and differed only in the job name and `SGLANG_QWEN_DEEPEP_SHARED_OVERLAP=true`. Configuration: `nvidia/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-NVFP4`, 24x GB300 disaggregated serving (four TP4/DP4/EP4 prefill replicas and one TP8/DP8/EP8 decode replica), FP4 weights, FP8 KV cache, NEXTN draft length 6, concurrency 896, fixed accepted length 4.8, and a 3,600-second AgentX replay. | AIPerf metric | Disabled | Enabled | Delta | |---|---:|---:|---:| | Total token throughput | 2,649,331.82 token/s | 2,705,912.48 token/s | **+2.14%** | | Output token throughput | 25,466.20 token/s | 26,000.99 token/s | **+2.10%** | | Request throughput | 27.980 request/s | 28.516 request/s | **+1.91%** | | Mean inter-token latency | 18.220 ms | 17.623 ms | **-3.28%** | | Theoretical prefix-cache hit | 95.433% | 95.452% | +0.020 pp | These are end-to-end AIPerf results without profiler instrumentation. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). The GPU-only stream path is covered by the end-to-end graph-capture and accuracy tests above. - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process). 2. signals.title: [AMD] DSv4: fuse the qk-norm-rope pair on the MTP target-verify path
signals.text: ## Summary On the DeepSeek-V4 unified-KV path, the fused qk-norm-rope kernel is wired to decode only. MTP **target-verify** falls back to running the same work as two separate launches per layer — `sglang::fused_q_norm_rope` for q and `sglang::fused_norm_rope` for kv — which is 122 launches per verify step across the 61 target layers. This PR routes target-verify through the same fused kernel, **with the cache store left off**. The store half deliberately does not move. Decode is a 1-source consumer: the ring holds everything, so writing it before attention is required. Target-verify is **2-source** — attention reads history from the ring and takes the current chunk as `k`/`v` so the draft tokens stay causally masked against one another. Writing the current chunk into the ring ahead of attention makes those tokens indistinguishable from history, and every draft position then attends to all of them regardless of order. Fusing the store as well drops GSM8K from 0.950 to 0.027 while looking like a ~7% throughput win, because it skips exactly the work correctness depends on. Only the norm+RoPE half is sound, and that is what this PR fuses. ## Modifications - **`python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_v4.py`** (`MQALayer._forward_prepare`) - `do_fused_store` now also admits `is_target_verify()` when the new gate is on. The kernel is token-indexed (`q`, `kv` and `positions` are all length M), so a verify batch carrying several draft tokens per request is a shape it already handles. - On that path the kernel is called with `swa_cache`/`swa_loc` left as `None`, so it performs q-norm+RoPE and kv-norm+RoPE and stores nothing. `get_unified_swa_loc` is not called at all — it exists solely to address a store this path no longer performs. - `kv` is returned instead of being set to `None`, so the caller's existing contract drives the rest unchanged: `attn_k = kv` gives attention the real current-chunk source, and `save_kv_cache = kv is not None` makes the backend write the ring after attention, exactly as the unfused path did. - `kv` is materialised with `.contiguous()` first: it is a strided slice of `qkv_a`, and the ring store requires a contiguous buffer. The unfused path pays the identical copy inside `_compute_kv_bf16`, so this is parity, not added overhead. - **`python/sglang/srt/environ.py`** — new `SGLANG_OPT_FUSED_QK_NORM_ROPE_VERIFY` (default on). Set to 0 to fall back to the unfused chain on the verify path. Decode, prefill and the non-unified paths are untouched. ### Kernel-level evidence Per target-verify forward, from graphs-off traces segmented by the 61 `DeepseekV4DecoderLayer` frames (TP8, 8k/1k, conc 16, rank 0). `fused_q_norm_rope` and `fused_norm_rope` both go to zero and one `_fused_qk_norm_rope_store_kernel` replaces them; no other kernel is added. | layer type | launches/fwd (base → patched) | GPU us/fwd excl. collective | |---|---|---| | CSA (30 layers) | 1920.0 → 1800.0 | 15779 → 15488 (−1.8%) | | HCA (31 layers) | 1526.8 → 1410.5 | 12385 → 12014 (−3.0%) | "excl. collective" is the number to read: `cross_device_reduce` blocks until the slowest rank arrives, so its duration tracks inter-rank skew rather than work this change moves. ## Accuracy Model `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro`, MI355X (gfx950), TP8. GSM8K, full 1319 questions, 5-shot, greedy. | run | accuracy | invalid | |---|---|---| | baseline (gate 0) | 0.950 | 0.000 | | patched (gate 1) | 0.949 | 0.000 | | patched (gate 1, repeat) | 0.945 | 0.000 | Note this is measured **without** `SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_LEN`. The throughput harness pins acceptance to the golden AL, which fabricates which draft tokens are accepted — fine for speed, but it would bypass the accept/reject path this change touches. Acceptance here is whatever the draft model earns. ```bash export SGLANG_HACK_FLASHMLA_BACKEND=unified_kv_triton export SGLANG_ENABLE_UNIFIED_RADIX_TREE=1 export SGLANG_OPT_UNIFIED_CACHE_FREE_OUT_OF_WINDOW_SLOTS=1 export AITER_BF16_FP8_MOE_BOUND=0 export SGLANG_DEFAULT_THINKING=1 SGLANG_DSV4_REASONING_EFFORT=high # flip this between 0 (baseline) and 1 (patched) export SGLANG_OPT_FUSED_QK_NORM_ROPE_VERIFY=1 python3 -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro \ --served-model-name deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro \ --host 0.0.0.0 --port 31710 --trust-remote-code \ --tensor-parallel-size 8 \ --attention-backend dsv4 \ --page-size 256 --swa-full-tokens-ratio 0.10 \ --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 \ --disable-shared-experts-fusion \ --tool-call-parser deepseekv4 --reasoning-parser deepseek-v4 \ --chunked-prefill-size 8192 --mem-fraction-static 0.85 \ --max-running-requests 32 --cuda-graph-max-bs 32 \ --speculative-algorithm EAGLE --speculative-num-steps 3 \ --speculative-eagle-topk 1 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4 python3 benchmark/gsm8k/bench_sglang.py \ --backend srt --host http://127.0.0.1 --port 31710 \ --num-questions 1319 --num-shots 5 \ --max-new-tokens 1024 --temperature 0.0 --parallel 32 ``` ## Performance Same model and hardware. 8k input / 1k output, TP8, steady state (10 waves through a `--max-concurrency` gate). Each cell is the mean of 2 repeats run in `off, on, on, off` order per concurrency, so a monotonic drift over the block shifts both arms equally instead of being credited to the patch. Repeated all-gates-off runs on this node put the noise floor at 0.25% (1σ). | concurrency | output tok/s (base → patched) | uplift | mean TPOT ms | accept len | |---|---|---|---|---| | 4 | 332.43 → 341.07 | **+2.60%** | 11.37 → 11.06 | 2.499 → 2.498 | | 8 | 543.73 → 555.57 | **+2.18%** | 13.75 → 13.46 | 2.499 → 2.469 | | 16 | 839.00 → 857.32 | **+2.18%** | 17.98 → 17.57 | 2.499 → 2.507 | | 32 | 1167.14 → 1186.66 | **+1.67%** | 25.79 → 25.34 | 2.482 → 2.508 | Acceptance length is flat across arms, so the uplift is kernel time and not a shift in speculation behaviour. ```bash # same server launch as above, with SGLANG_OPT_FUSED_QK_NORM_ROPE_VERIFY # flipped 0/1 between arms, plus the throughput harness env: export SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_LEN=2.49 export SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_METHOD=match-expected export SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_TOKEN_MODE=real-draft-token # CONC in {4, 8, 16, 32}; --max-running-requests/--cuda-graph-max-bs = 2*CONC # capped at 32 on both arms (this image cannot capture a decode graph at bs 48). CONC=16 python3 -m sglang.bench_serving --backend sglang \ --host 127.0.0.1 --port 31710 --model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro \ --dataset-name random --random-input-len 8192 --random-output-len 1024 \ --random-range-ratio 0.8 --num-prompts $((CONC * 10)) \ --max-concurrency $CONC ``` `bench_serving` ignores EOS by default here (it only offers `--disable-ignore-eos`), so every request runs to exactly 1024 output tokens and neither arm can win by generating less. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:no_entry_sign: [Run #32377716380](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32377716380)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32377716823](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32377716823)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32377716407](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32377716407)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [Fix] Pack device-pointer tables as uint64 to avoid 64-bit address overflow
signals.text: ## Motivation Fixes #35047. Several kernels pass base addresses to the device in a side table and bitcast each entry back to a pointer (`tl.load(meta_ptr + i).to(tl.pointer_type(...))` in Triton, `reinterpret_cast` in the host-side `gemm_ar` op). Those tables were built with `dtype=torch.int64`, which cannot hold an address `>= 2**63`: `torch.tensor()` unpacks Python ints through `long long`, so the build raises ``` ValueError: Overflow when unpacking long long ``` on the host, before any kernel is launched. Intel XPU (Level Zero / SYCL USM) device addresses have the top bit set, e.g. `0xffff85abd4e00000`, so every Mamba/GDN model hits this in conv-state scatter and `MambaPool` slot maintenance. CUDA/HIP VAs stay in the low canonical half, which is the only reason `int64` looks lossless there. ## Modifications - New `sglang.kernels.ops.memory.ptr_table.make_ptr_table(rows, device)`: builds the table as `uint64` (the only dtype that accepts a full 64-bit address) and `view`s it back to `int64`. `view` moves no bits, so kernels and C++ ops keep their existing signed element type — no kernel-side change, and `gemm_ar.cuh::set_bases`' `with_dtype<int64_t>()` check still holds. Companion columns (strides, element counts, block offsets) are non-negative, so their bits are unchanged too. - Route the three table builders through it: `_conv_multi_build_meta` (`mamba_state_scatter_triton.py`), `build_conv_slot_descriptor` (`mem_cache/mamba_slot_fused.py`), and `gemm_ar.init`'s `uc_bases`. ## Tests - `test/registered/kernels/ops/memory/test_ptr_table.py` (new, CPU suite): covers the full `[0, 2**64)` address range, and asserts both call sites' tables round-trip a spoofed top-bit-set `data_ptr()` while leaving companion columns identical to a real-address build. It spoofs the address because a backend whose VAs stay `< 2**47` can never catch this regression — the guard has to run on any runner. - `test/registered/layers/mamba/test_mamba_slot_fused.py` and `test/registered/unit/layers/test_mamba_state_scatter_triton.py` now select the accelerator via `get_device()` instead of hardcoding CUDA, and register on the XPU suite. Added coverage for `fused_conv_window_scatter_multi` (single-type, multi-type, and with the second/track index set), which had no test on any backend and is the kernel most exposed to the packing. Verified on 8x Intel Arc Pro B60 (torch 2.12.0+xpu): the new cases fail with the reported `ValueError` when `make_ptr_table` is reverted to `int64`, and all 15 pass with the fix (2 CUDA-only skips). `isort`/`black`/`ruff` and the repo's registered-test lint checks are clean. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32488679853](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32488679853)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32488679707](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32488679707)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32488679657](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32488679657)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.text: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation This is a follow-up to #30392, which introduced the `EmbeddingStore` abstraction for the multimodal embedding cache. Currently, `--enable-mm-global-cache` always initializes Mooncake and creates a fixed 4 GiB pinned CPU pool on every encoder TP rank. This prevents using the CPU pool independently as an L2 cache and duplicates cache resources across TP ranks. The encoder server's cache flow is currently owned by rank 0: rank 0 performs cache lookup, prefetch, assembly, and insertion, while the other ranks only participate in the TP encoding flow and cache-mask broadcasts. Although `EmbeddingCacheController` exposes `all_rank_get`, the encoder server does not currently drive cache loading and reads on every rank. Therefore, this PR keeps the supported rank-0 flow and allocates the cache pool and optional storage backend only on rank 0. | Configuration | Cache hierarchy | | --- | --- | | Cache flag unset | Embedding cache disabled | | `--enable-mm-global-cache` | CPU host pool only (L2) | | `--enable-mm-global-cache --mm-global-cache-backend mooncake` | CPU host pool + Mooncake (L2 + L3) | ## Modifications - Make the remote embedding store optional, so the cache defaults to L2 only. - Add `--mm-global-cache-size-gb` to configure the CPU pool per encoder TP group. - Create the cache controller, pinned pool, backend, and IO thread only on TP rank 0. - Reuse the existing TP CPU group for cache-mask broadcasts and `all_rank_get` synchronization instead of creating a separate process group. ## Accuracy Tests ## Speed Tests and Profiling ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. signals.title: [DSA] Route the ragged prefill top-k to the v2 kernel
signals.text: > Generated by Claude. **Stacked on #35041.** GitHub cannot use that PR's branch as a base here (its head lives in the fork, and a cross-fork PR's base must be a branch of the base repo), so this targets `main` and carries #35041's commit underneath. **Review only the second commit** (`[DSA] Route the ragged prefill top-k to the v2 kernel`); the diff collapses to it once #35041 merges and this is rebased. ## Motivation The extend-shaped `RAGGED` transform is the last DSA top-k path still served by the legacy sgl-kernel kernel (`topk_transform_prefill_ragged_kernel`), even though it is the cheapest one to serve. The DeepGEMM contiguous-KV indexer emits columns that are already absolute positions in the batch's flattened KV, so unlike the paged path there is no page table to gather through -- the entire transform is a per-row add. That is exactly v2's raw-index mode (added in #35041) plus a bias. ## What this does - **`TopKProblem` gains a `bias` field (default 0)** that `emit` adds to every selected index. Every pre-existing construction site omits it, so the compiler constant-folds the add away — see the SASS check below. - **`topk_ragged_kernel`** selects inside `[row_starts[b], row_starts[b] + seq_lens[b])` and emits `position + out_offsets[b]`. One block per row, and **no cluster path**: the cluster split exists to spread one very long row across blocks, which only pays off for the few-row decode shapes; prefill has thousands of rows. - **Unaligned window starts.** The window start is an arbitrary token offset, so the read base is rounded down to a 4-float boundary and the ≤ 3 columns that pulls in are masked to `-FLT_MAX` in place. They are a preceding request's columns *of the same row* — real finite scores that would otherwise win the selection. The row belongs to this block alone and the score buffer is dead after the top-k, so the write races with nothing. It lands after the PDL wait (the indexer rounds its own KV base down to 4 as well and would otherwise overwrite the mask) and is published by the `__syncthreads()` that every `forward()` already runs before it reads any score. - Rows with `seq_len <= topk` keep a trivial path that never reads the scores, so alignment never arises there. It cannot reuse `trivial_transform`, whose `-1` padding would pick up the bias. - `dsa_topk_backend` routes the RAGGED branch to it; prefill-CP (`batch_idx_list is not None`) stays on the legacy kernel, since its `topk_indices_offset` is built from `cu_seqlens_q` rather than the KV bases. ## The existing kernels are untouched Built the JIT module before and after and diffed the SASS per function (`cuobjdump -sass`, 12 kernels / 56648 instructions): | kernel | result | |---|---| | `topk_main_kernel` × {level 0..3} × {INDICES, PAGE_TABLE} | byte-identical | | `topk_small_batch_kernel` × {INDICES, PAGE_TABLE} | byte-identical | | `topk_plan` | byte-identical | | `topk_persistent_cluster_kernel` | same instruction count (2808); `+1 IMAD.MOV.U32 / -1 NOP` | `cuobjdump -res-usage` is identical field for field on all 12 (`REG:32 STACK LOCAL:0 SHARED CONSTANT`). The new kernel itself is `REG:32 STACK:0 SHARED:20224 LOCAL:0`, no spill. To keep it that way, the ragged bias must be set through its own construction path — assigning a runtime bias in `TopKPagedParams::problem()` would put a real `IADD` in every mode's `emit`. ## Tests `test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/test_topk_v2.py`: **278 passed** (234 existing + 44 new). The new cases cover every `row_start % 4` residue against each template band (trivial / Register2 / Register4 / Streaming), mixed lengths in one launch, the selection boundaries (`seq == k`, `k+1`, 8192/8193, 16385), long context, `row_starts=None`, and an offset distinct from `row_starts`. Everything outside a window is filled with a score that beats every in-window value, so a leak shows up as a wrong selection; each case also asserts that nothing outside the masked head was written. Also checked, unchanged from the base branch: `test_dsa_indexer.py` (same pass/fail set) and `test/registered/attention/unittests/dsa/test_dsa.py` (3 pre-existing `impl='trtllm'` hardware-gate failures, per `KNOWN_FAILURES.md §B`). And the v2 output matches the legacy kernel exactly when driven through `DSATopKBackend`, across aligned/unaligned starts and both the trivial and radix paths. ## Benchmark `bench_topk.py` gains a ragged benchmark alongside the paged one (this also un-shadows `benchmark_paged`, which a duplicate function name had replaced with a body-less stub). signals.title: [AMD] [Kimi-K3] Fuse the KDA input projection into a single GEMM on ROCm
signals.text: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation - KDA input projection on ROCm runs as two GEMMs per layer: a wide `[q, k, v, g]` projection (6144 rows/rank @ TP8) and a tiny `[f_a | b]` tail (128 + 12 rows/rank). - The tail is arithmetically negligible but still costs a full kernel launch and a second activation read every decode step. - Decode is bandwidth bound, so merging into one `N = 6288` GEMM makes the extra output columns nearly free and removes the second launch. - On gfx950 (`H = 7168`, TP8) the merged GEMM costs 0.55–0.73x the split pair for `M ≤ 64`, staying ahead up to a few hundred tokens; beyond that the untuned `N = 6288` shape loses to the tuned `N = 6144` one — so fusion is threshold-gated, not unconditional. - The `kimi_k3.py` comment warning that folding degrades kernel selection still holds for large-`M` prefill; this change reverses it only below the threshold, on ROCm, leaving the generic path untouched. ## Modifications - Merge the `[q, k, v, g]` and `[f_a | b]` projections into a single `N = 6288` GEMM (`_merge_kda_inproj_weights_hip`), gated by `SGLANG_ROCM_K3_FUSE_KDA_INPROJ` and a decode token-count threshold (a few hundred tokens). - Prefill (~1000-token chunks) and the generic, non-ROCm path are untouched. ## Accuracy Tests This is a layout-only change — same weights and values, reached through views — so parity is expected. **Full GSM8K** — n=1319, 5-shot, 8x MI355X TP8, Triton attention backend, fusion on by default: ``` python3 -m sglang.test.few_shot_gsm8k \ --num-questions 1319 \ --parallel 256 \ --num-shots 5 \ --max-new-tokens 512 \ --host http://127.0.0.1 \ --port 30001 ``` | Run | Accuracy | Invalid | |---|---:|---:| | 1 | 0.952 | 0.001 | | 2 | 0.951 | 0.001 | Both runs fall inside the documented 0.947–0.958 band (well above the 0.90 tripwire), consistent within noise. **Unit test:** `test/registered/amd/test_kimi_k3_kda_inproj_fusion.py` — 3 tests passed, 6 subtests passed. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Kimi K3: ISL 8192, OSL 1024, TP 8, MI355X * 8 ### Throughput/GPU | Conc | Split | Fused | Δ | |---:|---:|---:|---:| | 2 | 131.94 | 132.11 | +0.14% | | 4 | 218.34 | 219.80 | +0.67% | | 8 | 362.23 | 364.64 | +0.67% | | 16 | 550.69 | 561.43 | +1.95% | | 32 | 764.92 | 781.20 | +2.13% | ### Median ITL | Conc | Split | Fused | Δ | |---:|---:|---:|---:| | 2 | 16.15 | 16.13 | -0.15% | | 4 | 18.73 | 18.54 | -0.99% | | 8 | 20.91 | 20.70 | -1.03% | | 16 | 24.57 | 23.98 | -2.42% | | 32 | 30.75 | 29.94 | -2.62% | ### Median TTFT | Conc | Split | Fused | Δ | |---:|---:|---:|---:| | 2 | 913.08 | 912.99 | -0.01% | | 4 | 1556.02 | 1552.53 | -0.22% | | 8 | 2640.40 | 2451.79 | -7.14% | | 16 | 4791.64 | 4781.60 | -0.21% | | 32 | 8944.96 | 9081.63 | +1.53% | ### Median TPOT | Conc | Split | Fused | Δ | |---:|---:|---:|---:| | 2 | 16.15 | 16.13 | -0.14% | | 4 | 19.14 | 18.96 | -0.94% | | 8 | 22.34 | 22.12 | -0.98% | | 16 | 28.12 | 27.48 | -2.28% | | 32 | 38.48 | 37.54 | -2.44% | ## Checklist - signals.title: dsv4: merge c4 prefill compress+write into a single launch
signals.text: ## Summary Under prefill / `target_verify`, the ratio=4 (indexer) compress path launches two independent kernels back-to-back: - `flash_c4_prefill` — compress epilogue (compact output, one row per plan) - `write_c4_prefill` — ring-buffer staging write The **decode** path already fuses these inline (`flash_c4_decode`). This PR does the same for **prefill** by grid-concatenating the two domains into a single launch: blocks `[0, num_c_blocks)` run the compress epilogue, the trailing blocks run the write, dispatched on `blockIdx.x`. Both sub-kernels use the same 128-thread block and have **no cross-block data dependency** (compress reads prior-step overlap; write stages the current tokens for future steps), so no grid-wide sync is required. Implementation notes: - The compress and write bodies are factored into `__device__` impls addressed by an explicit `block_idx`. The standalone `__global__` wrappers (`flash_c4_prefill`, `write_c4_prefill`) are preserved for backward compatibility. - New `flash_c4_prefill_merged` kernel + `run_prefill_merged` launcher, exposed as `module.prefill_merged`. - **Opt-in** via `SGLANG_OPT_MERGE_COMPRESS_WRITE` (default **off**). Decode and the c128 path are unchanged. ## Validation - CG-OFF trace (DeepSeek-V4, MTP/EAGLE, TP8+DP-attn, MI355X) confirms the merged kernel fires and `write_c4_prefill` no longer appears (compress region 2 -> 1 launch for the ratio=4 path); c128 path untouched. - Output correctness verified end-to-end; 0 errors. ## Benchmark (conc=32, CG ON, 320 prompts, no warmup, ISL 8192 / OSL 1024, EAGLE 1/1/2) | metric | baseline (split) | merged (this PR) | Δ | |---|---:|---:|---:| | output throughput (tok/s) | 843.8 | 857.0 | +1.6% | | input throughput (tok/s) | 6617.4 | 6721.2 | +1.6% | | latency p50 (s) | 39.23 | 38.46 | -2.0% | | latency p90 (s) | 47.04 | 45.15 | -4.0% | | wall (s) | 388.4 | 382.4 | -1.5% | Since it is gated off by default, there is no behavior change unless `SGLANG_OPT_MERGE_COMPRESS_WRITE=1` is set. ## Test plan - [ ] Enable `SGLANG_OPT_MERGE_COMPRESS_WRITE=1` and confirm decode + prefill correctness on the ratio=4 indexer path. - [ ] Confirm compress-region launch count drops by one on the prefill path via profiler trace. Made with [Cursor](https://cursor.com) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32050079152](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32050079152)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32050078881](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32050078881)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [Bugfix] Chunk DSV4 indexer logits to bound transient memory
signals.text: ## Motivation Fixes #35201. The DSV4 sparse indexer materializes a `[query_rows, max_c4_seq_len]` fp32 logits tensor per layer per forward pass — allocated inside DeepGEMM's `fp8_paged_mqa_logits` (`csrc/apis/attention.hpp`, `torch::empty`) before the kernel launches. It grows linearly with accumulated context and **no part of sglang's memory budgeting accounts for it**, so long-context prefill OOMs deterministically, on every rank at once (the indexer is replicated, not TP-sharded). Repro on 4×H100 TP4, `DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731`, `--chunked-prefill-size 4096 --mem-fraction-static 0.9`: a single 800K-token request dies with ``` indexer.py forward_c4_indexer → deep_gemm fp8_paged_mqa_logits → CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 1.42 GiB ``` which is exactly `4096 rows × align(ceil(372K/4/256)·64, 256) cols × 4 B` — the chunk covering ~372K of the 800K prompt. At the default `--chunked-prefill-size 8192` the non-paged path allocates ~2× that and walls proportionally earlier. Lowering `mem_fraction_static` only moves the wall, since the requirement grows without bound in context length. ## Modifications Slice logits + top-k over query rows under a free-memory budget — the same shape `dsa_indexer.py` already uses for its `fp8_mqa_logits` allocation: - `_mqa_logits_chunk_rows()` returns a slice size when `query_rows × aligned_row_bytes` exceeds the budget, else `None` (single-call path, unchanged behavior). - The paged branch loops slices: per-slice `q`/`weights`/`c4_seq_lens`/`page_table`, per-slice DeepGEMM schedule metadata, per-slice top-k written into the matching rows of `c4_sparse_page_indices`. `max_c4_seq_len` stays full-width — logits columns are absolute c4 positions. Peak transient memory becomes the budget instead of `chunk_tokens × context`. - `_get_nonpaged_indexer_plan()` declines prefills whose logits would exceed the same budget, so they fall through to the chunked paged path (that path materializes its logits in one call with no slicing available). - Knob: `SGLANG_DSV4_MQA_LOGITS_FREE_MEM_FRACTION` (default 0.2), capped at 0.3 × total, mirroring the DSA indexer. Top-k is row-independent, so slicing preserves results exactly. **One deliberate difference from the DSA precedent:** the budget is measured per call, not cached. The free remainder shrinks as the KV pool fills, and a cached budget sampled while the server was idle sizes slices that no longer fit — during development this reproduced as 1020 MiB slices against 831 MiB free, i.e. the same OOM one level down. A static pre-check (64 MiB) keeps normal batches off that path entirely, so steady-state serving pays no `mem_get_info` sync. Happy to align the DSA path the same way in a follow-up if maintainers agree it has the same latent issue. ## Accuracy Test Row-slicing equivalence is the correctness-relevant property, covered by `test/registered/attention/test_dsv4_indexer_row_slice.py` (CPU-only, no GPU needed): chunked vs unchunked top-k output is bit-identical across chunk sizes 1/7/16/36/37 on random logits, plus budget-arithmetic tests pinned to the observed 1.42 GiB case and the DeepGEMM 256-column row alignment. 4 passed. End-to-end on 4×H100 TP4 with `DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731` (v0.5.17 image + this patch overlaid), greedy, cache flushed between probes: | prompt | before | after | |---|---|---| | 71,349 tok | OK | OK — **byte-identical output** | | 399,732 tok | OK (32.9 s) | OK (33.2 s) | | 799,550 tok | **OOM, all 4 ranks die** | **OK, 95.4 s**, 0 restarts, 0.76 GiB free | ## Benchmark and Profiling Result No steady-state throughput change is expected or observed: the static pre-check keeps sub-64 MiB allocations (all normal batches) on the original single-call path, byte-identical. The 71K and 400K probes above are within run-to-run noise of the unpatched server (4.8→4.9 s, 32.9→33.2 s). Chunking engages only where the alternative is a crash. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Code Formatting with Pre-Commit](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/development_guide_using_docker.html#code-formatting-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests as outlined in the [Running Unit Tests](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/development_guide_using_docker.html#running-unit-tests-adding-tests). - [x] Update documentation / docstrings / example tutorials as needed, according to [Writing Documentation](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/development_guide_using_docker.html#writing-documentations). - [x] Provide throughput / latency benchmark results and accuracy evaluation results as needed, according to [Benchmark and Profiling](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/benchmark_and_profiling.html). - [x] For reviewers: please read the [Reviewer Guidelines](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/docs/developer_guide/reviewer_guidelines.md). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32113606642](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32113606642)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32113606448](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32113606448)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: fix(sgl-model-gateway): parse prefilled Qwen3 reasoning
signals.text: ## Motivation Fixes #35148. When `qwen3` reasoning parsing is configured only in `sgl-model-gateway`, Qwen3.8 responses can contain a prefilled reasoning segment from the chat template. The gateway parser starts in the wrong state, so the reasoning is returned in `content` and `reasoning_content` remains null instead of separating the thinking and final answer. ## Modifications - Upgrade `reasoning-parser` from `1.0.0` to `1.3.0`. - Initialize the non-streaming parser per request, including reset and prefilled-thinking state. - Initialize each streaming parser per choice with the tokenizer's `ThinkingToggle`, `ThinkingKeyName`, and `think_in_prefill` settings. - Respect explicit `enable_thinking` / `thinking` request overrides. - Add unit regressions for Qwen3.8 prefilled `</think>` parsing in streaming and non-streaming paths. ## Accuracy Tests Added parser unit tests covering: - Qwen3 prefilled reasoning in the non-streaming path. - Qwen3 prefilled reasoning and closing `</think>` transition in the streaming path. - Thinking-toggle defaults and request-key resolution. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not applicable. This is a reasoning-parser correctness fix and does not change an inference kernel or performance-critical model computation. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32102419923](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32102419923)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32102419296](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32102419296)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->
