signals.title: [Model Loader] Harden startup weight-load overlap and expand model coverage
signals.text: ## Summary This is the hardening and coverage follow-up to #32017. It keeps startup weight-load overlap opt-in, makes admission/fallback deterministic, and extends the path to hybrid, MoE/EP, and one narrowly validated FP8 model profile. - Replace implicit support checks with a structured admission plan and deterministic rejection report. - Add `--startup-weight-load-mode=auto`: admitted configurations use overlap; rejected configurations preserve serial startup. - Check resolved checkpoint capabilities before capture-safe mutation, so `auto` can fall back for PT or secondary weights without allocating the model twice. - Freeze graph-visible parameter, buffer, and explicitly registered derived-tensor storage across the real-weight commit, then reject stale capture sentinels or storage rebinding. - After graph capture, cooperatively cancel and drain checkpoint prefetch before the real commit. If the bounded drain times out, continue with the conservative commit-reader policy while the cancelled daemon worker exits, without waiting a second time. - Preserve serial post-load semantics for optional parameters that intentionally skip dummy-weight validation. - Report complete overlap phase timings and assign `ModelRunner.weight_load_time` only after the real commit. - Add exact profiles for Qwen hybrid/MoE models and GLM-5.2 FP8. The default remains `serial`. Explicit `overlap` fails during preflight with actionable reasons when unsupported; `auto` logs the same reasons and follows the serial path. ## Supported profiles | Profile | Admitted configuration | | --- | --- | | Native dense | Native `LlamaForCausalLM`, `Qwen2ForCausalLM`, or `Qwen3ForCausalLM`; FP16/BF16; TP1/TP2 | | Qwen3.5-family hybrid VLM | Native `Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration` (including Qwen3.6 dense checkpoints); BF16; TP2/TP4; Triton linear attention; breakable or disabled prefill CUDA graphs | | Qwen3.5 MoE hybrid VLM | Native `Qwen3_5MoeForConditionalGeneration`; BF16; TP2+EP2; Triton MoE and linear attention; standard EP path; breakable or disabled prefill CUDA graphs | | Qwen3 MoE EP | Native `Qwen3MoeForCausalLM`; BF16; TP2+EP2; Triton MoE runner; standard EP path (`moe_a2a_backend=none`) | | GLM-5.2 FP8 | Native `GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM` with the GLM-5.2 fingerprint; serialized dynamic E4M3 FP8 with 128x128 blocks; BF16 execution/KV cache; Hopper SM90; TP8/TP16 with EP1; DSA with FA3 prefill/decode; Triton FP8 GEMM and MoE; prefill graphs disabled; shared-expert fusion off | The GLM profile is keyed to the native GLM-5.2 IndexShare fingerprint (default `cli_factor`, no custom `index_topk_pattern`, `index_topk_freq=4`, and `index_skip_topk_offset=3`), not merely the architecture name. Other quantized/repacked-weight paths, speculative decoding, LoRA/offload, and parallel/backend combinations outside the rows above remain rejected. `auto` sends them through serial startup. The end-to-end GLM validation below covers TP16; TP8 is an admitted profile, not a performance result in this PR. ## Design details `StartupWeightLoadAdmission` separates side-effect-free config preflight from native model-class resolution. Cheap rules run first; implementation resolution/import only happens for a viable candidate. Checkpoint format and secondary weights are checked after source resolution but before sentinel initialization, which gives `auto` a final safe serial-fallback boundary. `ModelStorageManifest` records tensor identity, pointer, shape, stride, dtype, device, and storage offset after dummy post-load preparation. Finalization proves that real loading refreshed the same graph-visible storage. Models can enumerate derived tensors through a per-module hook without a recursive attribute scan; the GLM/DeepSeek path uses this for MLA-derived weights and scales. Checkpoint staging remains best-effort. After graph capture, the manager cooperatively stops and joins the worker before starting normal multithreaded commit. If the bounded stop times out, the handle remains active and the loader preserves its conservative concurrency policy. Worker failure, intentional cancellation, and full-file completion remain distinguishable, and no filesystem/path-specific policy is used. Real-weight commit failures after capture-safe preparation are terminal startup failures. `auto` intentionally does not retry serial loading after model mutation or graph capture. ## H100 validation ### Controlled Qwen3.6 startup benchmark `Qwen/Qwen3.6-27B@6a9e13bd6fc8f0983b9b99948120bc37f49c13e9`, BF16, TP2, FA3, Triton GDN/linear attention, prefill CUDA graph disabled, decode FullCG, local NVMe. Three interleaved trials per mode were run after separate JIT warmup. Before every trial, checkpoint pages were evicted with `POSIX_FADV_DONTNEED` and verified with `mincore` to have zero resident bytes. | Metric (median) | Serial | Overlap | Change | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | Process ready | 50.193 s | 46.122 s | **-8.11% / 1.088x** | | Scheduler startup | 30.03 s | 26.30 s | -12.4% | | `load_weight` | 11.66 s | 7.50 s | -35.7% | Every overlap trial exercised the active handoff rather than an already-complete prefetch: capture ended with only 8-9 of 15 shards fully staged, the worker stopped in about 3.8 s, and multithreaded commit then resumed. There were no fallback, timeout, manifest, or sentinel errors. The server requested decode graph BS 256, but the hybrid Mamba-state capacity resolved the maximum running/captured BS to 39. The actual capture shapes were `[1, 2, 4, 8, 12, 16, 24, 32, 39]`; this resolved limit was identical in both modes. Across all six startups, two fixed prompts produced bit-identical text, token IDs, input/output logprobs, and top-logprobs. The timing is an end-to-end `serial` versus `overlap` mode comparison; coordinated checkpoint staging and its handoff are part of the overlap path, not a claim about graph capture in isolation. ### Controlled GLM-5.2 FP8 TP16 startup benchmark `zai-org/GLM-5.2-FP8@ba978f7d347eaf65d22f1a86833408afdb953541`, BF16 execution/KV cache, TP16 on 16 H100s, DSA with FA3 prefill/decode, sgl-kernel top-k, DeepGEMM paged MQA, Triton FP8 GEMM/MoE, prefill CUDA graph disabled, decode FullCG up to BS 64, local NVMe. A serial pilot established the compilation-cache baseline. The overlap pilot, all six interleaved measured trials, and `auto` validation then started from cold checkpoint pages; across those eight cold-controlled arms, the maximum observed resident fraction was `2.71e-8`, and compilation-cache membership and size stayed unchanged. | Metric | Serial | Overlap | Change | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | Process ready (median) | 135.482 s | 125.709 s | **-7.21% / 1.078x** | | Process ready (mean) | 135.564 s | 125.464 s | -7.45% | | Cross-trial CV | 0.086% | 0.280% | — | The three paired speedups were `1.0777x`, `1.0777x`, and `1.0861x`. All five overlap-enabled starts (overlap pilot, three measured trials, and `auto`) exercised active prefetch drain on every rank, for 80 rank-level drain records total, before normal multithreaded commit resumed. There were no fallback, prefetch-timeout, storage-manifest, or sentinel-validation errors. The two pilots, six measured starts, and `auto` validation all served successfully and produced matching text, token IDs, and input/output logprobs for the fixed single and batched probes. The recorded cross-node coordination-window upper bounds ranged from 1.18 to 2.39 ms across all nine starts. ### Coverage and correctness probes - `Qwen/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B`, BF16, TP2+EP2, FA3, Triton MoE/linear attention: text, image, batched, and prefix-branching requests matched across `serial`, `overlap`, and `auto`. - `Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507`, BF16, TP2+EP2, FA3, Triton MoE: multi-route batched and prefix-branching requests matched exactly across startup modes. These additional probes establish model/topology correctness coverage; the controlled Qwen3.6 and GLM-5.2 experiments above are the performance results. ## Tests - Final focused startup/prefetch suite on the GPU development image: `84 passed, 98 subtests passed`. - Unit coverage includes deterministic admission/rejection, `auto` fallback boundaries, timing ownership, storage/sentinel validation, derived-tensor refresh, optional single/both-scale post-load behavior, prefetch EOF/cancel/crash races, bounded drain/timeout, and loader dispatch after handoff. - The registered one-GPU parity test compares both `overlap` and `auto` with default serial startup. - `black --check`, `isort --check-only`, `ruff check --select F401,F821,UP037`, `codespell`, `py_compile`, and `git diff --check` pass on the changed files. ## Follow-up This PR intentionally leaves `serial` as the default. Follow-up work can add separately validated DeepSeek V4 Flash and Kimi Linear/K3 profiles; define a two-phase, capture-stable contract for quantization methods that repack or replace weight storage; broaden backend/topology and storage evidence; isolate graph overlap with a serial-plus-coordinated-prefetch benchmark arm; and then consider making automatic overlap selection the default. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32357825842](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32357825842)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32357825733](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32357825733)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32357825862](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32357825862)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [XPU] Add diffusion server test config for Intel XPU B60
signals.text: ## Motivation **Let the `multimodal_gen` diffusion server tests run on Intel XPU with correct expectations.** The diffusion server tests compare generated images against committed ground-truth images and check stage timings against committed perf baselines. Both sets of reference values are CUDA-derived, and neither is reachable from XPU today: - `get_consistency_platform()` has no XPU branch, so an XPU run silently falls through to the `h100` thresholds. - `BASELINE_CONFIG` composes per-platform perf overrides for Ascend and MUSA, but there is no XPU entry. The image mismatch is not a correctness bug. XPU seeds its initial latent noise from a different RNG stream than CUDA, so the pixels cannot match bit-for-bit: the image stays semantically identical (CLIP remains high) while `ssim` / `psnr` / `mean_abs_diff` degrade. Comparing XPU output against CUDA thresholds therefore fails on a difference that carries no signal. This PR adds XPU as a first-class platform in both registries, following the existing Ascend and MUSA pattern. ## Modifications Purely additive: 4 files, 56 insertions, 0 deletions. - **`test/test_utils.py`** — register `intel_xpu_b60` in `CONSISTENCY_THRESHOLD_FILE_BY_PLATFORM`, add the `intelxpub60` alias, and add the `current_platform.is_xpu()` branch to `get_consistency_platform()`. - **`test/server/consistency_thresholds/intel_xpu_b60.json`** — XPU consistency thresholds for `qwen_image_t2i_2_gpus` and `fsdp-inference`. - **`test/server/xpu/perf_baselines_xpu.json`** — XPU perf baselines for `fsdp-inference`, measured on Intel Arc Pro B60 (22.71 GiB per card). - **`test/server/testcase_configs.py`** — chain the XPU baseline file into `BASELINE_CONFIG`, alongside the existing Ascend and MUSA `.update()` calls. No CUDA path changes: both new files are read only when the resolved platform is XPU, and the two registry additions are new keys. ## Thresholds | case | clip | ssim | psnr | mean_abs_diff | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `fsdp-inference` | 0.97 | 0.6 | 11.0 | 37.0 | | `qwen_image_t2i_2_gpus` | 0.98 | 0.79 | 15.7 | 17.2 | Only these two cases were measured on XPU hardware. Every other case still inherits from `h100.json`; that is called out in the `_comment` field of the threshold file so the remaining cases can be triaged the same way rather than being assumed correct. ## Dependency Blocked on #33320, which adds `CustomOp.forward_xpu`. `dispatch_forward()` already returns `self.forward_xpu` on XPU, but the base-class method does not exist yet, so any `multimodal_gen` `CustomOp` raises `AttributeError` on XPU before these test configs are reached. This PR is the test-configuration half; #33320 is the runtime half. ## Accuracy Tests Verified on 2x Intel Arc Pro B60 (22.7 GiB per card): ``` python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/server/test_server_2_gpu.py::TestDiffusionServerTwoGpu::test_diffusion_generation[fsdp-inference] ``` Model `Tongyi-MAI/Z-Image-Turbo`. Passes end to end in ~157 s, including the consistency check against the thresholds above. Measured CLIP 0.9779 (passes); SSIM 0.6609 / PSNR 12.0434 / mean-abs-diff 33.3489, which fail the H100 thresholds and pass the XPU ones. XPU output is deterministic across 4 runs (identical md5). The perf baselines are single-host measurements, not an averaged multi-run distribution, so they are starting reference values rather than tight regression bounds. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). — no new test case is introduced; this PR adds the platform configuration that existing diffusion server tests read on XPU. - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). — N/A, no user-facing behaviour change. - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). cc: @siju-samuel @rbabukv <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32446492373](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32446492373)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32446492000](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32446492000)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32446492161](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32446492161)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [UnifiedTree] feat: support runtime attach/detach for historage
signals.text: ## Motivation `UnifiedRadixCache.attach_storage_backend` / `detach_storage_backend` were stubs that always returned `False`, so the `/hicache/storage-backend` admin API only worked with `HiRadixCache`. This implements them for the unified tree. Preceding fix for #35081. Supersedes #35240 (same feature, developed in parallel). ## Modifications **`unified_cache/storage_attachment.py` (new).** `StorageAttachment` owns the storage backend lifecycle: policy validation, extra-config parsing, controller attach, the ordered teardown, and `apply_runtime_config()`. Keeping it beside the tree rather than inside it leaves `UnifiedRadixCache` on cache logic and gives the three entry points — startup, the admin API, and the atexit hook — one implementation. `UnifiedRadixCache` goes from 2764 to 2520 lines. `apply_runtime_config()` is the single point where storage turns on, which is why the hash backfill below lives there rather than in `attach()`. **Hash-chain backfill (correctness).** Page hashes chain off the parent's last hash, and `_add_new_node` only computes them when storage is enabled. A node built before attach therefore has no hash, and hashing its children against it restarts the chain mid-sequence — the resulting L3 keys claim to encode a full prefix but only encode a suffix, so an unrelated request starting with those tokens loads KV computed under a different prefix, silently. Reproduced end-to-end with `--page-size 64` and explicit `input_ids` (P, R, Q are 128 tokens each): request `P+R` with storage off, attach, request `P+R+Q`, flush, then request `Q+S`. | | L3 hit for the `Q`-prefixed request | |---|---| | without backfill | **128 tokens** — loaded KV computed after `P+R` | | with backfill | **0** — correctly misses | | control: same sequence after its own backup | 128 in both, so L3 itself is healthy | `UnifiedTreeCore.backfill_missing_hash_values()` walks parent-before-child so each node hashes against an already-filled parent. **`cache_controller.py`.** The storage control queues are now initialized to `None` in `__init__` instead of only existing after `_start_storage_threads()`, so a detach on a server that never attached is a clean no-op rather than an `AttributeError`. ## Accuracy Tests Output stability is asserted throughout: every scenario re-runs fixed prompts and compares them byte-for-byte against a baseline captured before any attach. ## Tests **15-scenario attach/detach state machine**, run in one server process, asserting per step that the HTTP result is as expected, the server stays healthy, output is unchanged, and `GET /hicache/storage-backend` reflects reality: - traffic → attach → traffic → detach → traffic - attach → traffic → detach - attach → attach (same backend → 200, policies updated; different backend → 400, state unchanged) - attach → detach → detach; detach before any attach - attach/detach cycled 5× with traffic in between - interleaved traffic/attach/traffic/attach/traffic/detach/traffic/detach/traffic - L3 actually used when attached (960 tokens) and unused when detached (0) - invalid policies rejected without changing state - attach onto a warm tree, then extend an existing prefix (the backfill path) - **attach/detach hammered under concurrent traffic**: 16 ops → `[200, 400×15]`, every 400 a `not idle` refusal, state never half-applied, no output drift - **8× attach + real L3 traffic + detach**: L3 hit count constant at 960 across rounds, which is the observable proof that host pages come back (the scheduler's invariant checker guards the device pool but not the host pool) Result: **157 PASS / 0 FAIL on 1 GPU and again under `--tp-size 2`** (48 attaches, repeatedly creating and destroying the prefetch gloo groups; no traceback, SIGQUIT, leak or NCCL/gloo anomaly after server ready). **Unit tests** — `TestUnifiedRadixCacheStorageAttachBackfill` pins the contract that a backfilled hash chain is identical to one hashed from the start. Verified by mutation: stubbing `backfill_missing_hash_values` to `return 0` turns two cases red; restoring it turns them green. Full file: 1046 passed, 0 failed. **Registered e2e** — `test_hicache_storage_runtime_attach_detach.py` now covers both implementations via a subclass, so the existing HiRadixCache coverage is retained rather than switched over. 2 passed. ## Notes `HiRadixCache` has the same unhashed-node issue and the same non-idempotent detach when no backend was ever attached. Both are left alone here to keep this PR scoped to the unified tree. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32210047237](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32210047237)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32444471781](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32444471781)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32210047280](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32210047280)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [Bug][Spec] fix startup crash and reduce CUDA graph memory usage for speculative adaptive
signals.text: ## Motivation Three separate problems show up when `--speculative-adaptive` is enabled: 1. **Startup crash.** `ModelRunner.max_decode_logits_rows()` sizes the shared logits buffer from the *static* `decode_num_tokens_per_req()`, but adaptive speculative decoding replays runners built for larger draft-token widths. The buffer is too small and the server fails to start. (mentioned in #30549) 2. **IMA on the first replay.** `DecodeCudaGraphRunner.capture_one_shape` looked up `on_after_cuda_graph_warmup` on `self.model_runner.attn_backend` instead of on the backend this capture actually ran against (`attn_backend` from `capture_prepare`). For the runner the `ModelRunner` owns these are the same object, but adaptive speculative decoding builds extra runners bound to their own freshly created backend while `model_runner.attn_backend` still points at the active one. Hooking the wrong backend leaves this capture's warmup-upgraded metadata (raw→full, FlashMLA scheduler meta) frozen into the graph, which produces an illegal memory access on the first replay. 3. **Redundant CUDA graph memory.** Each capture pass opened `graph_capture()` without a stream, so every pass captured on a fresh stream. The caching allocator partitions the graph pool's segments **by stream**, so each pass re-reserved the pool's MoE / DeepEP scratch instead of reusing what an earlier pass left inactive. With adaptive speculative decoding that is one pass per candidate step × three runners — tens of GB of segments that all read back `inactive`. ## Modifications 1. `max_decode_logits_rows()` now derives `num_tokens_per_req` from `max_speculative_num_draft_tokens`, so the shared logits buffer is sized for the widest adaptive graph. (Same fix as #30554.) 2. `decode_cuda_graph_runner.py:1226-1237` — resolve `post_warmup_hook` from the capture-local `attn_backend` rather than `model_runner.attn_backend`, with a comment recording why. 3. Added `get_or_create_global_graph_capture_stream()` in `runner_utils/pool.py` (a named stream lease in the `Resources` tier, alongside the existing process-wide graph memory pool) and used it as the `graph_capture(stream=...)` argument in both `DecodeCudaGraphRunner.capture` and `PrefillCudaGraphRunner.capture`. All capture passes therefore share one stream and reserve that scratch exactly once. Captures are strictly serial (`Scheduler.init_all_cuda_graphs` runs target and draft workers in turn; the adaptive controller builds one runtime state at a time), so a single shared stream is safe. Also added a CPU unit test `test/registered/unit/model_executor/test_graph_capture_resources.py` covering both the pool and the new capture-stream lease. ## Accuracy Tests Server launched following the cookbook: ```bash sglang serve \ --trust-remote-code \ --model-path deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash \ --tp 4 \ --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_mxfp4 \ --speculative-algorithm EAGLE \ --speculative-num-steps 3 \ --speculative-eagle-topk 1 \ --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4 \ --speculative-adaptive \ --disable-flashinfer-autotune \ --swa-full-tokens-ratio 0.1 \ --host 0.0.0.0 \ --port 30000 ``` Evaluated on the three datasets shown in the cookbook: | | GPQA Diamond | AIME25 | GSM8k | | -------- | ------------ | ------ | ----- | | cookbook | 88.1 | 95 | 96.13 | | before | 88.13 | 98.33 | 96.89 | | after | 88.04 | 97.29 | 96.97 | ## Speed Tests and Profiling No throughput change is expected; the win is memory. With the launch command above and the default adaptive speculative decoding parameters, CUDA graph memory drops from **14.4 GB → 10.13 GB**. With my own serving config and adaptive speculative decoding parameters, it drops from **44.3 GB → 16 GB**, which frees the corresponding capacity for the KV cache. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process). 2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers. 3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so. - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci` 4. signals.title: [PD] Align defensive protocol behavior across Mooncake, NIXL, and Mori
signals.text: - RFC: [PD disaggregation: single protocol layer, per-backend transport #33861](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/33861) - Staged implementation plan and PR tracking: [PD shared-protocol implementation plan #34510](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/34510) - Preceding PR: [NIXL Prefill bootstrap timeout #34692](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/34692) ## Background #34692 added the missing NIXL Prefill bootstrap timeout. This PR continues Step 1 of #34510 by aligning clear, low-risk defensive protocol behavior across Mooncake, NIXL, and Mori without changing the Common state machine, wire format, completion channel, or Transport architecture. These changes preserve the current backend structure. They only add missing behavior or fix local race/layout issues. Extracting the common protocol and Transport remains work for later stages. ## Outline This PR groups the changes into five areas: 1. Complete Mori peer/request failure detection and ABORT delivery; 2. Prevent NIXL/Mori workers from executing stale work after teardown; 3. Keep Mooncake/NIXL control loops serving after malformed messages; 4. Align Mori MHA/MLA KV layout planning; 5. Fix the initialization race before the Mooncake control thread starts. ## 1. Mori peer and request failure handling Related commits: - `b285ea79ce` — `align Mori Decode heartbeat` - `62c13f66ba` — `align Mori abort handling with common protocol` Mori Decode did not start the existing Common heartbeat checker, so a dead Prefill would not trigger route/cache eviction or active-room failure. This PR only wires in the existing `_start_heartbeat_checker_thread()`, matching Mooncake and NIXL. Common Receiver sends an `ABORT` frame without a Mori guard, while Mori Prefill previously validated `MORI_GUARD` first and discarded ABORT as malformed. This PR recognizes the existing Common ABORT frame before guard validation: - Mark an active room as `Failed`; - Continue to ignore Success/unknown rooms; - Drop only the current message when ABORT is malformed. This only fixes ABORT delivery. It does not define ACK, cancel, or quiescence semantics. Terminal-state and safe-release behavior remains deferred to the later RFC stages. ## 2. Skip stale work after room teardown Related commit: - `46056556a5` — `skip cleared rooms in NIXL and Mori workers` Chunks already queued do not disappear when the Sender clears a room. - NIXL previously allowed a missing room to bypass its Failed check and then enter the exception path at the `transfer_infos` assertion; - Mori could continue into `add_transfer_request()` and subsequent terminalization. Mooncake already checks at `transfer_worker()` entry whether the room still exists or is `Failed`. On a match, it finishes the current chunk trace, removes residual `_staging_outstanding` state, and continues without reading that room's transfer metadata. This PR makes the other two backends discard queued tasks for missing rooms at worker entry: - NIXL aligns with Mooncake's missing-room/Failed guard, removes the room's residual `_staging_outstanding` count, and continues; - Mori uses an equivalent early return because chunk execution lives in Sender `_run_chunk()`. The stale task therefore cannot read deleted `transfer_infos`, submit to the Transport, advance state, or trigger terminalization. Existing `clear()` paths remain responsible for normal room cleanup; these guards only consume queue items that arrive after teardown. When the common protocol is extracted, this should be replaced by unified idempotent room teardown/tombstone semantics. For now, the backend-local guards avoid expanding the scope into Common state-machine changes. ## 3. Isolate malformed control messages **Scope update:** this change has been reverted from the final diff. Since this branch was created, #35049 and #35360 have added more complex deferred-release and ABORT/ABORT_ACK state transitions to the same Mooncake/NIXL control loops. Keeping the original broad per-message exception boundary while reconciling those changes would mix malformed-frame handling with partially applied abort, socket, and engine failures. Rather than expanding this PR to redesign those failure boundaries, we reverted the change and plan to handle malformed control messages together with the later protocol-unification work, based on the latest control paths. ~~Related commit:~~ - ~~`a716ceaac7` — `harden Mooncake and NIXL control message parsing`~~ ~~Mooncake/NIXL control loops serve multiple rooms, but previously indexed, decoded, or unpacked frames directly. An empty message, truncated ABORT, invalid guard, or unexpected frame count could terminate the long-lived thread.~~ ~~Mori already treats one message as the exception boundary: its Prefill bootstrap loop and Decode status loop validate guard/frame input inside `while True`, log an error for the current message, and continue receiving the next one. A bad frame therefore does not remove control-plane service from later rooms.~~ ~~This PR aligns Mooncake and NIXL with that behavior by adding minimum frame/tag/guard validation at the Mooncake Prefill/Decode and NIXL Prefill/Decode-staging message entries. Empty messages, truncated fields, and invalid encodings are logged and skipped without terminating the long-lived control thread.~~ ## 4. Align Mori KV layout planning Related commits: - `48c5e1569d` — `align Mori speculative MHA layout with common planner` - `081186c4c8` — `align Mori same-PP and hybrid MLA layout planning` Together, these commits fix Mori descriptor slicing that differed from the existing Common planner. The first part handles Decode-only speculative KV layout: ```text [K_main..., V_main..., draft_K..., draft_V...] ``` Mori previously split descriptors in half and could select a draft region as main V. This PR uses the same V-offset rule as `get_mha_kv_ptrs_with_pp()`. The second part adds: - Same-PP peer descriptor lists are already aligned local layouts and must not have the global layer offset applied again; - Hybrid MLA uses MLA descriptor slicing instead of falling through to the regular MHA path. These fixes remain inside Mori for now because they operate on Mori `MemoryDesc` lists, and planner/materialization are still coupled in Mori Manager. A later stage can extract target/draft, same-PP, and MHA/MLA logical layer selection into a Common helper, leaving Mori responsible only for mapping the common plan to `MemoryDesc` and `batch_write()`. ## 5. Initialize Mooncake state before starting the control thread Related commit: - `12a88dbcfe` — `initialize Mooncake session state before control thread` Mooncake Prefill previously started its receive thread before creating state that the thread accesses: ```text session_failures failed_sessions session_lock ``` If Decode registration arrived immediately after thread startup, it could hit an initialization race. This PR only moves these three fields before `start_prefill_thread()` while preserving all other queue, worker, probe, and receive ordering. This is intentionally a minimal ordering fix rather than a Step 1 reorganization of backend thread lifecycle. When the common Manager/Transport is extracted, control-thread initialization, startup, shared state, and shutdown should be managed together. ## Testing CPU red/green regression tests are kept on a dedicated test branch: ```text branch: https://github.com/jambow0320/sglang/tree/rfc-pd-test path: test/registered/unit/disaggregation/rfc-test/ ``` Coverage includes: - Mori ABORT delivery before guard validation; - Cleared-room stale work in NIXL/Mori; - Malformed control-message isolation in Mooncake/NIXL; - Mori speculative MHA descriptor selection; - Mooncake session-state initialization order. The tests pass with the fixes and reproduce the original failures against the corresponding unfixed source. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32466303515](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32466303515)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32466303525](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32466303525)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32466303785](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32466303785)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [BugFix][Qwen3.8] Support Qwen3.8-MXFP4 DCP by registing Qwen3_5 text-only archs in mamba radix cache whitelists
signals.text: ## Motivation Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B uses the Qwen3_5MoeForCausalLM architecture. This is a text-only Qwen3.5 MoE architecture, but it is currently missing from the Mamba radix cache whitelists in `arg_groups/overrides.py`. As a result, `mamba_extra_buffer` remains disabled by default. At the same time, when DCP is enabled, the allocator page size is scaled based on the DCP size: page_size * dcp_size = 2. This conflicts with Mamba's requirement that page_size must be 1 when `mamba_extra_buffer` is disabled, causing startup to fail: ``` AssertionError: MambaComponent requires page_size=1 when mamba_extra_buffer is disabled, got 2 ``` ## Modifications Register `Qwen3_5MoeForCausalLM` and `Qwen3_5ForCausalLM` in `_MAMBA_RADIX_CACHE_ARCHS` and `_MAMBA_EXTRA_BUFFER_ARCHS`. signals.title: [Bugfix] Guard harmony parsing against malformed gpt-oss output in Responses API
signals.text: ## Motivation gpt-oss occasionally samples a malformed harmony message header, for example a duplicated `to=` in a tool-call header. `openai_harmony`'s `StreamableParser.process` raises `HarmonyError` on such headers, and `python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/context.py` calls it with no exception handling at four sites: `HarmonyContext.append_output`, both loops in `StreamingHarmonyContext.append_output`, and `StreamingHarmonyContext.render_for_completion`. Repro against the pinned `openai-harmony==0.0.4`: ```python from openai_harmony import HarmonyEncodingName, Role, StreamableParser, load_harmony_encoding enc = load_harmony_encoding(HarmonyEncodingName.HARMONY_GPT_OSS) parser = StreamableParser(enc, role=Role.ASSISTANT) text = '<|channel|>commentary to=functions.get_weather to=functions.get_weather<|message|>{}<|call|>' for t in enc.encode(text, allowed_special="all"): parser.process(t) # openai_harmony.HarmonyError: unexpected tokens remaining in message header: ["to=functions.get_weather"] ``` Because this is model output rather than client input, the failure is intermittent, and the user-visible impact differs by path: - Non-streaming `/v1/responses`: the exception propagates out of `responses_full_generator` into the catch-all in `create_responses`, which returns it as a 400 `invalid_request_error`. A model-side failure gets reported as the client's fault. - Streaming `/v1/responses`: `responses_stream_generator` consumes the generator with no try/except around the `async for`. The 200 status and SSE headers have already been sent, so the exception kills the stream mid-flight with no error event. The client sees a truncated stream and no explanation. Two aggravating details: - After such an error, the parser keeps raising `HarmonyError` for every following token until the next `<|start|>` token, then recovers on its own. So one malformed header poisons the whole remainder of the turn if the exception is allowed to escape, even when the rest of the output is well formed. - #33717 makes the same observation about harmony parse failures surfacing as 400s, but fixes a different crash (`parse_output_message` on preamble messages in `harmony_utils.py`). It does not guard `parser.process`, so the two changes are complementary. ## Modifications Guard the parser at the source instead of in each consumer, so the streaming and non-streaming paths are fixed at once: - New `HarmonyContext._process_token()` wraps `parser.process()`, catches `HarmonyError`, logs the first failure of a malformed stretch (one log line per desync, not one per token), and skips the token so the parser re-synchronizes at the next message start. This mirrors how the tool-call detectors already treat malformed model output: `base_format_detector.parse_streaming_increment` logs and degrades instead of raising. - All four `parser.process` call sites in `context.py` go through the guard. Resulting behavior on malformed output: the malformed message is dropped and logged, following well-formed messages in the same turn still parse, the non-streaming path returns the surviving output instead of a 400, and the streaming path finishes the SSE stream cleanly instead of dying mid-flight. The same failure class exists in vLLM's harmony plumbing; I have a parallel fix open there (vllm-project/vllm#52055). New unit test `test/registered/unit/entrypoints/test_harmony_context.py` (registered in `base-a-test-cpu`): - non-streaming `append_output` survives the malformed tool-call header above, logs exactly once, drops the malformed message, and still parses the following well-formed message - the same for streaming `append_output` fed one token per chunk - well-formed output parses unchanged, with no error logs Without the guard, the first two tests fail with `openai_harmony.HarmonyError: unexpected tokens remaining in message header: ["to=functions.get_weather"]` at the previously unguarded call sites. ## Accuracy Tests Not applicable, no kernel or model forward changes. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not applicable. The guard adds a try/except and a flag assignment per token on the harmony parsing path, which is negligible next to the parse itself. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process). 2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers. 3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so. - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci` 4. signals.title: [XPU][model]: Intel XPU support for encoder embeddings (bge/NomicBERT/ModernBERT) + InternVL3_5
signals.text: Intel XPU support for four embedding / vision models, combined for review: `BAAI/bge-base-en-v1.5`, `nomic-ai/nomic-embed-text-v1.5`, `ibm-granite/granite-embedding-english-r2`, and `OpenGVLab/InternVL3_5-30B-A3B`. ## Motivation - **bge-base-en-v1.5** (`BertModel`) loads on XPU but returns wrong embeddings — SciFact 0, cosine vs HF 0.26-0.47. Two XPU-specific bugs in shared code affect every BERT/RoBERTa encoder on `intel_xpu`. - **nomic-embed-text-v1.5** (`NomicBertModel`) had no SGLang model, so the Transformers fallback raised `NotImplementedError: get_input_embeddings ...`. - **granite-embedding-english-r2** (`ModernBertModel`) fell back and crashed in the forward pass (`RuntimeError` in `set_kv_buffer`) — a bidirectional encoder routed through the paged decoder KV cache. - **InternVL3_5-30B-A3B** crashed at load (`AttributeError: 'InternVLChatConfig' object has no attribute 'num_experts'`) and, once loading, hung/crashed the vision encoder under concurrent multimodal at tp>1 (Level Zero USM-memcpy deadlock on a per-block device->host `.item()`; DEVICE_LOST batching ViT tiles). ## Modifications Encoder embeddings: - `layers/attention/xpu_backend.py`: honor `AttentionType.ENCODER_ONLY` / `DECODER_BIDIRECTIONAL` (was `causal = not is_cross_attention`). - `managers/{scheduler,tokenizer_manager,utils}.py`: preserve the trailing separator token when truncating over-length embedding inputs (gated on `not is_generation`). - `models/nomic_bert.py` (new): `NomicBertModel` — RoPE, SwiGLU, post-norm; SDPA. - `models/modernbert.py` (new): `ModernBertModel` — RoPE, local/global attn, GeGLU; SDPA. InternVL: - `models/internvl.py`: read `num_experts` from `config.llm_config`; pass the host-side `max_seqlen` into `prepare_vision_attention_metadata`; chunk the ViT forward to `SGLANG_VIT_MAX_TILES` tiles on XPU. - `layers/attention/vision.py`: `VisionIntelXPUAttention` uses the metadata's host `max_seqlen` instead of re-deriving it from GPU `cu_seqlens` per block. - `environ.py`: add `SGLANG_VIT_MAX_TILES` (default 12). All XPU paths are guarded by `is_xpu()`; the encoder truncation change is embedding-only; decoder generation is unchanged. ## Accuracy Test Intel XPU (Arc Pro B60), vs the HuggingFace reference. Encoder — MTEB SciFact NDCG@10 (300 queries / 5183 corpus), tp-1: | Model | cosine vs HF | SciFact NDCG@10 | HF ref | |---|---|---|---| | bge-base-en-v1.5 | 0.99997 | 0.6981 | 0.7387 | | nomic-embed-text-v1.5 | 1.00000 | 0.6803 | (prefix-sensitive) | | granite-r2 (ModernBERT) | 1.000000 fp32 / >=0.9999 bf16 | 0.6720 | 0.6815 | InternVL3_5-30B-A3B — tp-4 (61.7 GB bf16, ~14.43 GB/rank): loads with 0 skipped params, MoE initialized, multimodal smoke (red image -> "Red"); P1 lmms-eval: **mathvision_testmini 38.2, mmmu_val 27.4**. All four load with 0 skipped params. ## Speed Test and Profiling No change to existing code paths. Encoder fixes flip a boolean / run once per over-length request; the two new encoders are small SDPA models (no KV cache). InternVL removes a per-block device->host sync on XPU and bounds the ViT forward; non-XPU paths are unchanged. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32470005122](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32470005122)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32470004786](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32470004786)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32470004891](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32470004891)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [mem_cache][9/N] refactor: move DSAIndexerPoolHost to pool_host.dsa
signals.text: ## Motivation Part of the `pool_host` phase of the mem_cache refactor (issue #25371), continuing from PR #31180 ([8/N]). That PR relocated `MambaPoolHost` into `pool_host/mamba.py`, leaving the remaining concrete pools in `memory_pool_host.py`. This PR relocates the DSA indexer host pool — `DSAIndexerPoolHost` — into its own `pool_host/dsa.py` module, following the same mechanical pattern. ## Modifications Mechanical relocation with a **byte-for-byte identical** implementation body: | Symbol | From | To | |--------|------|-----| | `DSAIndexerPoolHost` | `memory_pool_host.py` | `pool_host/dsa.py` | - The DSA-specific imports move with the class, including `DSATokenToKVPool` and the type-only `MLATokenToKVPoolHost` dependency. The new module imports its shared host-pool base symbols and transfer helpers directly. - `memory_pool_host.py` needs no back-import: none of the surviving classes reference `DSAIndexerPoolHost`. Its diff is therefore deletion-only. - Consistent with the preceding `pool_host` moves, no re-export shim or backward-compatibility layer is added. - The new module keeps the same platform-gated `sgl_kernel` imports and runtime platform flags used by the original implementation. ### Caller-site impact Three import sites are redirected from `memory_pool_host` to `pool_host.dsa`: - **Runtime (1):** `hybrid_cache/hybrid_pool_assembler.py`. - **Tests (2):** `test_dsa_pool_host_unit.py` and `test_hicache_staged_write_back_dispatch.py`. The staged write-back test also patches transfer helpers in the new owning module so that it continues to exercise the same dispatch paths after the move. ## Mechanical move — verification This is a verified mechanical move: - Extracting `DSAIndexerPoolHost` from the merge base's `memory_pool_host.py` and comparing it with the class in `pool_host/dsa.py` produces an empty diff: **PASS**. - After removing the relocated class and its DSA-only imports, the surviving implementation in `memory_pool_host.py` is unchanged. - All remaining Python references to `DSAIndexerPoolHost` import it from `pool_host.dsa`; no stale import from `memory_pool_host` remains. - `git diff --check` on the PR diff: **PASS**. ## Accuracy Tests This PR only relocates code and does not change model outputs or host-cache behavior. - Python compilation for the new module and all touched caller/test files: **PASS**. - GitHub lint check: **PASS**. - The affected registered suites remain assigned to the standard CI matrix: - `test_hicache_staged_write_back_dispatch.py`: `base-a-test-cpu`. - `test_dsa_pool_host_unit.py`: CUDA `base-b` / `1-gpu-small` and AMD `stage-b-test-1-gpu-small-amd`. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not applicable — no runtime or kernel behavior changes. ## Checklist - [x] Format and whitespace checks pass (`lint`, `git diff --check`). - [x] Adjust affected unit tests and patch targets for the new module path. - [x] Follow SGLang code style. - [x] Verify the moved implementation body is byte-for-byte identical. - [x] Documentation is not applicable for this internal module relocation. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32437333918](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32437333918)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32437333699](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32437333699)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32437333852](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32437333852)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: Support deepseek v4 and kimi k3 on ssd
signals.text: # [Feature] Add SSD-backed Expert Pack inference for DeepSeek-V4-Flash and Kimi-K3 ## Summary This PR adds an opt-in SSD-backed inference path for **DeepSeek-V4-Flash** and **Kimi-K3**. It allows these MoE models to run when their complete weights are larger than GPU VRAM and host RAM combined. Routed expert weights are stored on SSD and loaded only when selected by the router. The implementation uses: - an expert-major **Expert Pack** layout for efficient random access; - direct I/O into aligned pinned host buffers; - asynchronous host-to-device transfers; and - a byte-budgeted LFU/LRU GPU cache for frequently used experts. The runtime does not prune, merge, skip, replace, or re-quantize experts, and does not reduce Expert Top-K. The default `auto`, `safetensors`, and `gguf` loading paths remain unchanged; SSD execution is enabled only through the explicit `expert_pack` path. ## Supported Scope `ExpertPackModelLoader` is selected only with `--load-format expert_pack`. Official checkpoints loaded through the standard `auto` or `safetensors` paths never enter this loader. The currently validated DeepSeek input is the single-file MXFP4 GGUF used by `frob/deepseek-v4-flash-0731:latest`. Its routed expert matrices use `MXFP4`; the large non-routed matrices are mostly `Q8_0`, router input weights are `BF16`, and the inventory also contains `F32` and `I32` normalization or auxiliary tensors. The inspected GGUF contains 129 `MXFP4`, 512 `Q8_0`, 43 `BF16`, 641 `F32`, and 3 `I32` tensors. It contains no FP8 tensors. The other validated input is the text-only 38-shard `KIMI-K3-MXP4-DERISKED-Q2_K-*.gguf`, whose routed experts use Q2_K for gate/up and Q3_K for down. The Kimi launcher extracts the official `text_config` into a flat `KimiLinearConfig`; the complete multimodal Kimi-K3 checkpoint is not supported by this loader. Other GGUF quantization variants have not been validated and are not currently claimed as supported. ## Usage Install this branch from source before running the examples: ```bash python3 -m pip install -e "python" ``` ### DeepSeek-V4-Flash The tested MXFP4 GGUF is available as [`frob/deepseek-v4-flash-0731:latest`](https://ollama.com/frob/deepseek-v4-flash-0731), which was imported from [`unsloth/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-GGUF`](https://huggingface.co/unsloth/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-GGUF). The benchmark used the immutable Ollama model blob with SHA-256 `947ac34c08c0e5c5752ac76398f934b3b6b4075cfe915ba43dd5ac754900a4cd`. ```bash python3 examples/runtime/deepseek_v4/benchmark_deepseek_5090.py \ --gguf /path/to/deepseek-v4-flash-0731-mxfp4.gguf \ --prompt "Explain why the sky appears blue." \ --max-new-tokens 200 ``` ### Kimi-K3 Download all 38 Q2_K GGUF shards from [`Blackfrost-AI/KIMI-K3-Q2_K-GGUF-ABLITERATED`](https://huggingface.co/Blackfrost-AI/KIMI-K3-Q2_K-GGUF-ABLITERATED). Also place the tokenizer/config files from [`moonshotai/Kimi-K3`](https://huggingface.co/moonshotai/Kimi-K3) in a sibling directory named `kimi-k3-tokenizer`. ```bash hf download Blackfrost-AI/KIMI-K3-Q2_K-GGUF-ABLITERATED \ --include "KIMI-K3-MXP4-DERISKED-Q2_K-*.gguf" \ --local-dir /path/to/kimi-k3 ``` ```bash python3 examples/runtime/kimi_k3/benchmark_kimi_k3_5090.py \ --gguf /path/to/kimi-k3/KIMI-K3-MXP4-DERISKED-Q2_K-00001-of-00038.gguf \ --prompt "Explain why the sky appears blue." \ --max-new-tokens 200 ``` The first shard is only the entrypoint. The launcher automatically discovers and uses all 38 shards in the same directory. Both launchers derive the remaining paths automatically. If the Expert Pack is missing, it is built on the first launch and reused afterward. | Model | First Expert Pack build | Approximate first-run readiness | | --- | ---: | ---: | | DeepSeek-V4-Flash | Estimated **5-10 minutes** on the benchmark NVMe SSD | **8-15 minutes** | | Kimi-K3 | **29 minutes 42 seconds measured** | **35-45 minutes** | The 38 Kimi-K3 source shards and generated Expert Pack occupy approximately 1.814 TiB in total, so a 4 TB SSD is recommended for practical headroom. ## Correctness - DeepSeek-V4-Flash produced semantically equivalent answers to Ollama across travel planning, science, history, programming, and mathematics prompts. - Kimi-K3 matched the 200-token SGLang reference output exactly. All 92 routed layers executed Top-16 experts with `fallback_count=0` and `io_errors=0`. ## Performance The target platform is one RTX 5090 with 32 GB VRAM, 32 GB host RAM, and NVMe SSD storage. The retained measurements were collected on RTX 5090 hosts; host RAM and SSD capacity differed between the two model runs. ### DeepSeek-V4-Flash vs Ollama Five prompts were measured with 200 generated tokens per prompt. | Metric | SGLang | Ollama | Result | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | Prefill | 3.265 token/s | 1.457 token/s | **2.24x faster** | | Decode | 2.020 token/s | 1.354 token/s | **1.49x faster** | ### Kimi-K3 vs llama.cpp The SGLang run used a 91-token prompt and generated 200 tokens. | Metric | SGLang | llama.cpp | Result | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | Prefill | 0.66412 token/s | 0.11289 token/s | **5.88x faster** | | Decode | 0.44830 token/s | 0.1810 token/s | **2.48x faster** | The llama.cpp decode baseline came from an earlier 50-token run, so the 2.48x decode figure is indicative rather than a strict equal-length comparison.

signals.title: [AMD] Add ROCm 7.14 (gfx942 / gfx950) release
signals.text: ## Motivation ROCm 7.14 is published only as pip wheels and docker images — `repo.radeon.com` has no apt repo for it — so its stack has to be assembled from AMD's ROCm pip channels on top of `ubuntu:24.04`. That places the SDK in `site-packages` instead of `/opt/rocm`, which the existing stages of `docker/rocm.Dockerfile` assume throughout. This PR adds gfx942 and gfx950 ROCm 7.14 stages built that way, plus the adjustments the pip-SDK layout forces on the existing build and CI steps. The index is `https://repo.amd.com/rocm/whl-multi-arch/`, AMD's release channel. Deliberately not the nightly or devrelease channels: those get pruned. An earlier revision of this PR pinned a 7.15 nightly (`7.15.0a20260712`) because 7.15 never had a stable release — the line ran from `7.15.0a20260626` to `7.15.0a20260728` and was then renumbered 10.0 — which would have left this Dockerfile unbuildable, and the image unreproducible, once that nightly aged out of the index. 7.14 is a released SDK, so the pin is stable. torch is 2.11, the same as the `rocm724` flavors already on `main`, so the 7.14 stages reuse the existing `*_rocm724` extras for the `compressed-tensors` 0.16.0 pin rather than adding a third hand-synced copy of the same dependency list. `python/pyproject_other.toml` is unchanged by this PR. The `rocm7_15` / gfx1250 stage and its workflow are untouched. ## Modifications ### `docker/rocm.Dockerfile` - Added a shared `rocm714-base` stage: `ubuntu:24.04` + Python 3.12 in a venv + the ROCm 7.14 pip stack — `rocm-sdk-{core,libraries,devel,device-gfx942,device-gfx950}==7.14.0`, `torch`/`torchaudio` `2.11.0+rocm7.14.0`, `torchvision 0.26.0+rocm7.14.0`, `triton 3.7.1+git0263a6a6.rocm7.14.0`. - Added two thin per-arch stages, `gfx942-rocm714` and `gfx950-rocm714`, which set build flags and `PIP_CONSTRAINT`. Both arches' torch device wheels go into the shared base; `GPU_ARCH_LIST` still narrows what AITER and sgl-kernel actually compile for. - `BASE_IMAGE_942_ROCM714` / `BASE_IMAGE_950_ROCM714` default to the `rocm714-base` stage rather than a published image. Naming them keeps these stages shaped like every other stage in this file, which matters because `scripts/ci/amd/amd_ci_install_dependency.sh` locates a stage's `AITER_COMMIT_DEFAULT` by grepping for `FROM $BASE_IMAGE_<arch><suffix> AS <arch><suffix>`. They can also be pointed at a prebuilt image to skip building the base. - **Collapsed a duplicated `libamd_smi`.** `rocm-sdk init` expands a devel tree carrying a second copy of the library, byte-identical to the one in `_rocm_sdk_core` but a real file rather than a symlink. Since `ROCM_HOME` puts the devel tree on `LD_LIBRARY_PATH`, the amdsmi python package binds that copy while torch already holds the one HIP loaded through its RPATH, and two copies in one process keep separate global state — whichever initialises second enumerates nothing. torch on ROCm asks amdsmi for the device count before HIP, so this surfaces as `torch.cuda.device_count() == 0` on a machine where `hipGetDeviceCount()` returns 1, with `rocminfo` and `amd-smi` both seeing the GPU. Symlinking the duplicate fixes it; the step is guarded and idempotent, so it is a no-op if a future SDK ships a symlink there itself. - Single `--index-url`; the release index mirrors the PyPI packages torch pulls in, so no `--extra-index-url` and no `--pre` are needed. - torch and torchvision device wheels are named as separate specs rather than combined device extras. Several device extras in one spec (`torch[device-gfx942,device-gfx950]`) silently installs only the first, and the missing arch then fails at runtime with `hipErrorInvalidImage`. - Python 3.12 (the Ubuntu 24.04 default) rather than 3.13/3.14: `st_attn==0.0.7`, `vsa==0.0.4`, `petit_kernel==0.0.2` and `wave-lang==3.8.2` publish wheels only up to cp313 and no sdist, so on 3.14 pip has no candidate at all for `srt_hip`. - Path fixups for the non-`/opt/rocm` SDK: `ROCM_HOME` / `ROCM_PATH` / `CPATH` / `LIBRARY_PATH` / `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` point at the site-packages `_rocm_sdk_devel` tree; a `/opt/rocm` symlink because AITER shells out to `/opt/rocm/llvm/bin/amdgpu-arch` to pick `DEFAULT_GPU_ARCH` and the rest of this Dockerfile refers to `/opt/rocm`; and a `/usr/lib64/libc.so` symlink because the SDK's `hsakmtTargets.cmake` hardcodes that path from its own build host. - libdrm: skipped for `*rocm714*`. The pip SDK's `libdrm_amdgpu.so` links the device-ID table in rather than reading `share/libdrm/amdgpu.ids` — the `.so` carries the MI300X / MI325X / MI355X names and never opens that file — so the apt step the 7.2.4 flavor needs is unnecessary here. - amdsmi: installed for `*rocm714*` (same branch as the 7.2 flavors), since the pip SDK does not pre-install it. - `PIP_CONSTRAINT`: the 7.14 stages define and populate it the same way the `rocm724` stages do, so resolving AITER and SGLang dependencies cannot swap the image's ROCm torch for a PyPI CUDA build. - MORI: point the build at the SDK's vendored `lib/rocm_sysdeps` tree via `CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH` / `CPATH` / `LIBRARY_PATH` plus an `ldconfig` entry, for NUMA (`hsakmt-config.cmake` calls `find_dependency(NUMA)`) and libdrm (`rocm_smi.h` includes `<libdrm/drm.h>`, `mori_application` links `-ldrm`/`-ldrm_amdgpu`). Guarded on the directory existing, so the apt-based ROCm images keep their current behaviour. - nixl: the existing `libabsl-dev` removal is extended to `*-rocm714`, which is on the same Ubuntu 24.04 base as `rocm724` and hits the same meson/abseil conflict. - The SGLang install and the post-install validation step both treat `rocm714` like `rocm724`. ### `scripts/ci/amd/amd_ci_install_dependency.sh` - Recognise `-rocm714` in the image `GPU_ARCH` stamp and map it to `_ROCM714` / `-rocm714` so the AITER pin lookup finds the right Dockerfile stage. - Select the `dev_hip_rocm724` extras for `-rocm714` as well, matching what the Dockerfile does at build time. Without this a 7.14 image would get `compressed-tensors` 0.15.0, which requires `torch<2.11`, and the resolve would fail. - Apply the same `rocm_sysdeps` handling to the in-image MORI rebuild, kept scoped to that build instead of exported image-wide because `rocm_sysdeps/include` also carries `zlib.h` / `expat.h` / `elf.h`, which would shadow the system headers for every other component. ### `.github/workflows/release-docker-amd-rocm714-nightly.yml` - New workflow, following this repo's one-file-per-ROCm-version convention (`rocm700` / `rocm720` / `rocm7_15`), with a `gfx942-rocm714` / `gfx950-rocm714` matrix and `rocm714-mi30x` / `rocm714-mi35x` tags. The `rocm7_15` workflow is not modified. - The schedule is commented out for now; the workflow is dispatch-only until the gfx950 leg has had a green run. ## Accuracy Tests **Both arches build on CI.** [Run #32380153563](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32380153563) published `v0.5.17-rocm714-mi30x-20260820` (16.3 GB) and `v0.5.17-rocm714-mi35x-20260820` (16.5 GB). `gfx950-rocm714` had never been built before and passed first try. The workflow added here cannot be `workflow_dispatch`-ed until it exists on the default branch, so it is exercised from a throwaway branch, `bingxche/rocm714-ci-test`, which carries this PR head plus a branch-scoped `push` trigger and redirects images to a scratch repository so nothing unvalidated lands in `rocm/sgl-dev` or `lmsysorg/sglang-rocm`. None of that is part of this PR. **The `libamd_smi` duplication above was caught by that CI run** and would otherwise have shipped: every GPU test failed with `Invalid device id` because torch saw no devices. It reproduces off-CI with the published image, and the fix is verified against it — `device_count() = 1`, `get_device_name(0) = AMD Instinct MI300X`, bf16 matmul finite. **Local results on an MI300X host (gfx942)**, against a locally built `gfx942-rocm714` image: - Image builds end to end, all 34 steps. The in-image validation step reports `torch 2.11.0+rocm7.14.0`, `torchaudio 2.11.0+rocm7.14.0`, `torchvision 0.26.0+rocm7.14.0`, `triton 3.7.1`, HIP `7.14.60850`, with `pip check` clean and no `nvidia-*-cu*` packages. - Smoke test on hardware: 8 devices, `gfx942:sramecc+:xnack-`, bf16 matmul finite, and `triton`, `torchvision`, `torchaudio`, `aiter`, `mori`, `tilelang`, `nixl`, `amdsmi`, `sglang` and `compressed_tensors` (0.16.0, i.e. the right extras were selected) all import. - `scripts/ci/amd/amd_ci_install_dependency.sh` exits 0. The parts this PR touches behave as intended: `Image GPU_ARCH=gfx942-rocm714`, `installing python extras: [dev_hip_rocm724,tracing]`, `Using FROM $BASE_IMAGE_942_ROCM714 AS gfx942-rocm714 from Dockerfile`, and the MORI rebuild completes. - `run_suite.py --hw amd --suite stage-a-test-1-gpu-small-amd` reports **8/8 passed**, exit code 0. `test_umbp_store.py` passing is the relevant check for the MORI changes: it exercises `mori.umbp`, which needs the gRPC symbols the rebuilt MORI must carry. **Known gap:** `gfx950-rocm714` builds but has not been executed. No MI355X hardware was available for this work, so its runtime behaviour is unverified. ## Speed Tests and Profiling <!-- If this pull request impacts inference speed, provide benchmarking and profiling results. --> ## Checklist - [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process). 2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers. 3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so. - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci` 4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR.

signals.title: [AMD][Fix] Qwen3.5: make empty-batch guard tuple-aware on fused AR+quant path
signals.text: ## Problem Partition 0 of `stage-c-test-large-8-gpu-amd-mi35x-rocm720` (`test_qwen35_fp8_ar_fusion_mi35x.py`) has failed on every scheduled run since 2026-08-16 12:08 UTC. Example: [job 95552260420](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32083881457/job/95552260420). The empty-batch guard added in #34474 reads `hidden_states.shape[0]` immediately after `prepare_attn_and_capture_last_layer_outputs()`. When the fused AR+quant path is active that call returns a tuple — `(bf16, fp8, scale)` in the GatedDeltaNet layer, `(fp8, scale)` in the plain attention layer — so the guard raises during decode CUDA-graph capture and the server dies at startup: ``` File "python/sglang/srt/models/qwen3_5.py", line 806, in forward if not forward_batch.forward_mode.is_idle() and hidden_states.shape[0] > 0: AttributeError: 'tuple' object has no attribute 'shape' ``` The scheduler child dying takes the process tree with it, which the test surfaces as the less obvious `Server process exited with code -9`. Only the `fused-ar-rms-per-group-quant` variant is affected; the `SGLANG_DISABLE_FUSED_AR_QUANT=1` control variant stays on the tensor path. ## Fix Read the row count off the tuple's first element, using the same inline form `glm4_moe.py` already uses for this situation. Applied at both guard sites. This is behavior-preserving. `prepare_attn()` returns early on `hidden_states.shape[0] == 0` *before* the fusion branch, so a tuple can only appear when the count is already `> 0`; the tuple path therefore behaves exactly as it did before #34474, while the tensor path keeps the empty-batch guard. Both sites are patched because `keep_bf16=False` still yields a tuple, just the 2-element form. `Qwen3_5AttentionDecoderLayer.forward_prepare_native()` / `.forward_prepare_fused_gate()` both open with `isinstance(hidden_states, tuple)`, and `_select_fused_ar_input_for_linear()` has a dedicated `len(...) == 2` branch that only this path produces. Supersedes #35250, which diagnosed the same bug but patched the GatedDeltaNet site only. ## Verification Reproduced and fixed end-to-end on an 8x MI350X node following the CI flow exactly — same image (`rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.17-rocm720-mi35x-20260817`), same `amd_ci_install_dependency.sh`, same `run_suite.py` invocation. Before, at the failing scheduled-run SHA `91144797c`: the `AttributeError` above, byte-for-byte the CI signature. After: | Variant | GPUs | Accuracy | Invalid | Latency (s) | Output tok/s | Threshold | Status | | ------- | ---- | -------- | ------- | ----------- | ------------ | --------- | ------ | | fused-ar-rms-per-group-quant | 0,1,2,3 | 0.951 | 0.009 | 53.66 | 4067.56 | 0.94 | PASS | | disable-fused-ar-quant-opt-out | 4,5,6,7 | 0.940 | 0.009 | 53.85 | 4010.65 | 0.94 | PASS | On CI, partition 0 is green on both [run 32203488998](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32203488998) and [run 32227220289](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32227220289), with accuracy matching the last pre-regression baseline ([run 31916881653](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31916881653): 0.949 / 0.943). ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). No new test: `test_qwen35_fp8_ar_fusion_mi35x.py` already covers this path and is the test that was red. No user-facing behavior change, and no before-number to benchmark since the server did not start. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32458357756](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32458357756)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32458357596](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32458357596)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32458357678](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32458357678)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [Diffusion] Candidate-trajectory execution contract (phase 1: types + validation)
signals.text: ## Summary Implements the candidate-trajectory execution contract proposed in #35331 as a real, opt-in path -- not just a standalone contract module. **Contract layer** (`runtime/pipelines_core/candidates.py`): - `CandidateTrajectorySpec` -- `count` / `reducer` / `return_candidates` / `seed_policy`, with eager validation: `count=1` must use `reducer="none"` (provably identical to the existing non-candidate path), `count>1` requires a real registered reducer. - `CandidateGroup` -- stable, sorted, unique `candidate_ids` per `request_id`. - A reducer registry (`"none"`, `"mean"`, plus `register_candidate_reducer()` for model-owned rules). - `derive_candidate_generators()` -- one `torch.Generator` per candidate, derived from `(base_seed, candidate_id)` via a splitmix64-style bit mixer. - `validate_candidate_admission()` / `reduce_candidates()` -- atomic group admission and partial-failure-safe reduction. **Real integration**: - `SamplingParams.candidate_spec`, validated against `num_outputs_per_prompt` -- the RFC's premise is that `num_outputs_per_prompt`'s existing outputs *become* the candidate axis, not a separate count, so `candidate_spec.count` must equal it. - **`InputValidationStage._generate_seeds`** (the real per-request seed/generator construction used by every model) now uses `derive_candidate_generators` instead of the existing naive `base_seed + i` scheme whenever `candidate_spec` is set. This is the RFC's core RNG-independence safety requirement, not a nicety -- plain addition can produce visibly correlated draws for nearby seeds. When `candidate_spec` is `None` (the default), behavior is byte-for-byte unchanged. The actual candidate-reduction *application* point (averaging N action outputs down to one served result) needs real per-model tensor-shape knowledge -- e.g. Cosmos3's `action_latents` layout -- that can't be added correctly without a real model and weights to validate against. That's left for the model-adapter phase the RFC's own rollout plan describes (step 2: "Add a Cosmos3 action adapter"); the RNG-derivation wiring above is what's provably safe to land now. ## Test plan - **30 tests** in `test_candidate_trajectory.py` (27 original + 3 new), covering: - RFC required-tests 1, 2, 3, 4, 7 (count=1 identity, sequential/batched seed equivalence, reducer parity, stable candidate IDs across co-batched requests, no partial-aggregate on failure). - The exact multi-prompt aggregation pattern `_generate_seeds` now uses: prompt-major/candidate-minor flattening order, cross-prompt independence, single-prompt equivalence to bare `derive_candidate_generators`. - Requirements 5, 6, 8 (CFG-parallel candidate membership, TP/SP reconstruction before reduction, conditional video-branch skip) still need a real model/pipeline adapter and are out of scope until that phase. All 30 tests pass on the Apple Silicon MPS backend. `input_validation.py` itself has a heavy import surface (`torchvision`, which isn't installed on this machine, plus a deep `pipeline_configs`/`platforms`/`server_args` chain) that makes it impractical to instantiate `InputValidationStage` directly in a local sandbox, so the new branch's logic is validated at the level of the RNG derivation it calls into (already exhaustively tested) rather than via a live call through the stage class; CI's full dependency stack can exercise that path directly. Also verified clean against the repo's `black`, `isort`, and `ruff --select=F401,F821,UP037` configuration. Closes/relates to #35331. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32166068209](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32166068209)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32166067961](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32166067961)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32166068052](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32166068052)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [Diffusion] Compile-plan trajectory promotion gate
signals.text: ## Summary Implements the data model and validation flow proposed in #35333: connects SGLang Diffusion's regional `torch.compile` support (`DenoisingStage` / `CompiledModuleRegistry` in `runtime/utils/torch_compile.py`) to a reproducible, full-trajectory promotion gate for stateful iterative models -- turning "compile succeeded" into "this exact compile plan passed the declared end-to-end trajectory contract for this workload signature." - `CompileWorkloadSignature` -- the exact workload regime (model revision, dtype, backend, parallel signature, latent shape regime, step count, CFG/cache mode, state schema version) a compiled plan is valid for, with a stable sha256 `digest()` for use as a manifest key. - `TrajectoryGate` -- declares checkpoints and per-checkpoint tensor-parity thresholds (`cosine_similarity` as a *minimum*, `mae`/`mse`/`rmse`/`max_abs`/`l2` as *maximums*), plus a slot for model-specific output-quality metrics the framework deliberately does not compute itself. - `CompiledPlanManifest` -- the offline/CI artifact recording whether a compile plan was promoted (`"validated"`/`"rejected"`) for a signature. - `run_trajectory_gate()` -- warms and runs both an eager reference and a compiled candidate through a caller-supplied stepping function across a *full checkpoint schedule* (not a single isolated forward, per the RFC's core argument that one forward isn't enough to validate a stateful rollout), scores each declared checkpoint, and rejects on the first threshold miss. - `select_validated_plan()` -- the runtime-side lookup: does an incoming workload signature match a validated manifest, or fall back to eager. The manifest is an offline/CI artifact; the runtime never reruns the full reference rollout per request. `compute_tensor_metrics()` mirrors the metric semantics of the existing `tools/compare_diffusion_trajectory_similarity.py` (cosine similarity, MAE/MSE/RMSE, max-abs, L2), reimplemented locally rather than imported, so this module carries no diffusion-specific dependencies (no `imageio`, no model loading) and stays independently testable. ## Scope Data model, validation, and the promotion decision itself -- matching the RFC's explicit non-goals ("this RFC does not enable [compile] globally"; "runtime does not rerun the full reference rollout for every request"). Wiring an actual SGLang Diffusion model/pipeline through this gate as part of CI is follow-up work. ## Test plan `python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_compile_trajectory_gate.py`, 18 tests, all passing: - Signature digest determinism and sensitivity to every field. - `TrajectoryGate`/`CompiledPlanManifest` validation (empty/duplicate checkpoints, missing threshold entries, invalid status). - `compute_tensor_metrics()` correctness (identical tensors score perfectly, shape mismatches raise). - **`run_trajectory_gate()` against a real `torch.compile` call** -- not mocked tensors: a toy stateful iterative `nn.Module` (linear + tanh, hidden state carried across steps, standing in for a denoising step) is wrapped with `torch.compile(backend="aot_eager")`, and both the eager and compiled versions are actually run through a multi-step rollout: - the compiled candidate's trajectory is confirmed `"validated"` against the eager reference at declared checkpoints; - a deliberately diverging candidate (same shape, shifted values, standing in for a broken/miscompiled plan) is confirmed `"rejected"`; - a checkpoint schedule that never visits a declared checkpoint, and a step function returning `None` for a declared checkpoint, both raise `CompileGateError` rather than silently passing. - `select_validated_plan()` -- matching signature returns the manifest, mismatched signature falls back to `None`, and a `"rejected"` manifest is never selected regardless of signature match. All 18 tests were run on the **Apple Silicon MPS backend** (`torch.backends.mps.is_available()`), confirmed via the test module's resolved `DEVICE`, not a silent CPU fallback -- so the `torch.compile` calls and tensor-metric computations are exercised on a real accelerator, not just plain Python logic. Also verified clean against the repo's `black`, `isort`, and `ruff --select=F401,F821,UP037` configuration. Closes/relates to #35333. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32166481922](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32166481922)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32166481726](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32166481726)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32166481936](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32166481936)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->
