signals.title: [DO NOT MERGE][Test] Tighten the DCP HiCache KL threshold to 0.005
signals.text: ## Motivation `test_unified_radix_cache_kl_dcp.py` (Kimi Linear + DCP4 + HiCache L2 + UnifiedRadixCache) has gated at `kl_threshold = 0.01` since it landed in #33112. Every other fp8 hybrid cache-hit KL case in the same directory gates at 0.005: | case | threshold | | --- | --- | | `test_unified_radix_cache_kl_mamba.py` | 0.005 | | `test_unified_radix_cache_kl_cp.py` | 0.005 | | `test_unified_radix_cache_hicache_pp_kl.py` | 0.005 | | `test_unified_radix_cache_kl_dsv4.py` | 0.005 | | `test_unified_radix_cache_kl_dcp.py` | **0.01** | A looser threshold tolerates float noise and small state bugs alike, and the thing this case exists to catch — a missing DCP logical→physical translation handing back another rank's KV on a cache hit — is exactly what slack hides. This PR tries the house value so the DCP translation path is held to the same bar as the non-DCP ones. This is an experiment: the point is to find out whether the DCP path actually holds at 0.005 in CI. If it flakes, the measured headroom tells us either to keep 0.01 with a comment recording why (the way the mamba case documents its own 0.003 → 0.005 bump) or that there is real divergence worth chasing. ## Modifications One line: `kl_threshold` 0.01 → 0.005 in `test/registered/radix_cache/unified_radix_tree/test_unified_radix_cache_kl_dcp.py`. No source changes. ## Accuracy Tests No model-output changes. The case is registered as `stage="extra-b"`, `runner_config="4-gpu-b200"`, so it needs the extra CI stage to actually exercise the new threshold. ## Speed Tests and Profiling N/A — test threshold only. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32446478926](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32446478926)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32446478822](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32446478822)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32446478978](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32446478978)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [AMD][CI] Add the Qwen3.8 MXFP4 MI35x nightly
signals.text: ## Motivation [Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B-FP8) shipped with [day-0 SGLang support](https://www.lmsys.org/blog/2026-08-12-qwen3-8-day0-support/) and a [day-0 AMD recipe](https://www.amd.com/en/developer/resources/technical-articles/2026/day-0-support-for-qwen-3-8-on-amd-instinct-gpus.html), but the AMD nightly has no coverage for it. It reuses the Qwen3.5 architecture (`Qwen3_5MoeForCausalLM`), so it runs with no model-code changes — which is exactly why nothing guards it: a change to the shared hybrid path or the AITER MXFP4 MoE kernels can silently degrade it on ROCm. FP8 is ~2.4 TB against 8 x 288 GB per MI355X node, so there is no single-node FP8 recipe; single-node means FP4. The job serves [`amd/Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B-Quark-MXFP4`](https://huggingface.co/amd/Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B-Quark-MXFP4), AMD's Quark quantization of the FP8 checkpoint. Only routed experts are quantized, so AMD measures the same 97.49 GSM8K as the FP8 baseline — this job gates the FP8 checkpoint's quality in the shape that fits one node. ## Modifications **`test/registered/amd/accuracy/mi35x/test_qwen38_mxfp4_eval_mi35x.py`** (new) — two phases in the `nightly-amd-8-gpu-mi35x-qwen38-mxfp4` suite: `test_a_gsm8k_accuracy` (TP8 GSM8K, gated at 0.93) and `test_b_serving_perf` (batch 1/8/16/64 at 1024 in / 1024 out). Both launch from one `SERVER_ARGS` reproducing the AMD model card recipe, so the throughput numbers describe exactly the configuration the accuracy gate covers. Perf is skipped unless accuracy passed. Two flags are load-bearing rather than defaults: `--page-size 1` (on HIP the default becomes 64 when the container sets `SGLANG_AITER_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT=vectorized_5d`) and `--attention-backend aiter` (no arg override picks a backend for this architecture on ROCm). The server runs with no `--reasoning-parser` so a `<think>` block still scores under the last-number extractor. **`.github/workflows/nightly-test-amd-rocm720.yml`** — new `nightly-8-gpu-mi35x-qwen38-mxfp4-rocm720` job on `linux-mi35x-gpu-8`. ROCm 7.2 only: MXFP4 needs gfx95x. Also removes the two Qwen3-235B jobs from this nightly; `Qwen3MoeForCausalLM` is gated per-commit by `test/registered/quant/test_quark_mxfp4.py` (gsm8k >= 0.89, on both ROCm lanes) and runs nightly at 30B-A3B scale, so this frees two 8-GPU jobs per night. No file under `test/` is touched by that removal, and `nightly-test-amd.yml` (ROCm 7.0) is left alone since that lane is being retired. **`test/run_suite.py`** — register the new suite. **`scripts/ci/amd/check_hf_cache_space.sh`** (new) — run [#32196787596](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32196787596) died 40 minutes into the download on ENOSPC, and free space was never reported anywhere in its log. This records it before the download, says whether the checkpoint is already cached, and clears stale artifacts via the existing `scripts/ci/utils/cleanup_hf_cache.py`. It deletes no other checkpoints: `/sgl-data` is a 15 TB volume shared by the whole AMD fleet at 100% used, and an eviction attempt removed 48 of them while free space went from 298 MB to 227 MB. Never fails the job. **`scripts/ci/utils/amd_cache_audit.py`** (new) — joins `register_amd_ci` tests to the checkpoints they name and the jobs that dispatch them, counting the per-commit `pr-test-amd*.yml` workflows and not just nightly. 289 of 429 AMD registrations are per-commit only and run on runners sharing the same PVC, so a nightly-only join badly overstates what is reclaimable. `--runner` scopes to a cluster by the dispatching job's `runs-on` label; suite -> models extraction is reused from `list_stage_models.py`. ## Accuracy Tests **[Run #32313140175](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32313140175) — green. GSM8K 0.973** against the 0.930 gate and AMD's published 0.9749. Both phases ran, neither skipped. The gate sits ~5% below AMD's number, the same relative tolerance the sibling Qwen3.5 MI35x evals allow (`rtol: 0.05`). Caveat: the checkpoint was already cached on that runner, so the run exercised load-and-serve but not a cold download. A confirmation run on the current head is in flight at [#32424018092](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32424018092); it is the first to exercise the cache-check step, which the green run predates. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Published to the job summary rather than asserted, so it reports regressions without becoming a flaky gate. Measured on 8x MI355X, TP8, 1024 in / 1024 out: | batch size | latency (s) | input tput (tok/s) | output tput (tok/s) | ITL (ms) | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 1 | 14.83 | 6961.62 | 69.73 | 14.34 | | 8 | 18.48 | 20833.04 | 452.87 | 17.67 | | 16 | 21.94 | 21758.80 | 773.39 | 20.69 | | 64 | 37.74 | 21993.04 | 1885.58 | 33.94 | Overridable via `NIGHTLY_BATCH_SIZES` / `NIGHTLY_INPUT_LENS` / `NIGHTLY_OUTPUT_LENS`. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). — the Qwen3.8 cookbook page already documents this recipe. - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. signals.title: [AMD] Make ROCm 7.2.4 images profile HIP-graph kernels, and check that they do
signals.text: ## Motivation AMD/Silo reported that on the `lmsysorg/sglang*` ROCm 7.2 images, `torch.profiler` traces contain no GPU kernels for work launched through hipGraph. The cause is upstream and fixed upstream — ROCTracer drops kernel-dispatch events under `hipGraphLaunch` ([ROCm/ROCm#6102](https://github.com/ROCm/ROCm/issues/6102), fixed in ROCm 7.2.2) — and #30984 has since published `rocm724` images that install ROCm 7.2.4. Installing it turned out not to be the same as using it. The torch wheels vendor their own HIP and roctracer under `torch/lib`, and `libtorch_hip.so` carries `RPATH $ORIGIN`, so the published 7.2.4 images profile through 7.2.0 libraries and `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` cannot override an `RPATH`. Measured on `rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.17-rocm724-*-20260820`: | image | GPU | eager | graph replay | verdict | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | as shipped | MI355X | 512/512 | **448/512** | FAIL | | ROCm copies in use | MI355X | 512/512 | 512/512 | PASS | | as shipped | MI300X | 512/512 | **448/512** | FAIL | | ROCm copies in use | MI300X | 512/512 | 512/512 | PASS | On a real server trace the gap is larger: gpt-oss-20b-bf16 with `/start_profile num_steps=10` records 513 device kernel events with CUDA graphs on, against 3924 with `--disable-cuda-graph` and 3933 on a working runtime — 87% of decode kernels missing from a trace that otherwise looks complete. So this PR does three things: makes the images use the ROCm runtime they install, adds the check that tells the two states apart, and documents it. ## Modifications ### `docker/rocm.Dockerfile` — use the ROCm runtime the image installs One step at the end of the torch work replaces `torch/lib/libamdhip64.so` and `torch/lib/libroctracer64.so` with the ROCm install's versioned copies, plus a verification step. Three details worth review: - **Keyed on whether the wheel vendors them**, not on the ROCm flavor. Where torch already links `/opt/rocm` — the rocm720 stack on torch 2.9.1 — there is nothing to replace and the step says so and moves on, so there is no version guard to update for the next flavor. A wheel that vendors them with no ROCm copy available is a broken image, and the build fails. - **Replaced by rename.** The interpreter doing the replacing has those libraries mapped; writing through them would corrupt it. It stages a copy and `os.replace`s. - **Verified in a fresh interpreter**, which loads the swapped-in libraries, so a soname or ABI mismatch fails the build rather than a user's first profile. `LD_PRELOAD` of the same two libraries is *not* an equivalent workaround: @devalshahamd found it aborts server startup on 7.2.4 inside Triton's AMD launcher during CUDA-graph capture, while this replacement leaves both the probe and a real workload with clean profiles. That fits the mechanism — a preload leaves both HIP copies mapped and only interposes symbols, so a component resolving them independently can end up on the other runtime with its own state. ### `scripts/ci/amd/check_hip_graph_profiling.py` — the check Captures a graph, replays it under `torch.profiler`, and counts device events in the exported trace against the dispatches it asked for. Counting matters: the loss is partial (448 of 512), and a 4-node graph is traced correctly even on 7.2.0, so both a "non-empty trace" threshold and a small graph would call a broken runtime healthy. The default is 64 nodes replayed 8 times — a calibrated point, since 7.2.0 is complete at 4 and lossy from about 16 while 7.2.4 has been seen dropping at 256. An eager control run separates "cannot trace graph replay" from "cannot trace anything", and each phase runs in its own process under a timeout because 7.2.0 can also wedge inside `hipGraphLaunch`. It reports the **paths** of the libraries torch mapped, flags any the ROCm install is not backing, and prints the commands to fix that; `--print-ld-preload` exposes the value for a single-run check. Not registered in the AMD suites: on a rocm720 image it is expected to fail and, per #34452, can take the process down with it. ### `test/registered/unit/ci/test_hip_graph_profiling_probe.py` The probe's value is that a red run says *which* failure happened, and a GPU job only ever exercises whichever case its image is in. 18 CPU tests drive `main()` with canned phase results: every verdict and exit code, the partial-loss shortfall, vendored-runtime detection including the half-preloaded case, the preload value naming real files rather than symlinks, and the trace parser, where counting a host-only trace as device work would turn the check into a false pass. Registered as `base-a-test-cpu`. ### `docs/docs/developer_guide/benchmark_and_profiling.mdx` Records the symptom, how to check an image, the `rocm724` images as the answer, how to repair an older image, and `--disable-cuda-graph` where neither applies. ## Accuracy Tests No model or kernel code changes. The Dockerfile step swaps two shared libraries for the same libraries at the version the image already installs. ## Speed Tests and Profiling The point of the change is that `torch.profiler` reports what the GPU ran. No throughput effect is expected: HIP and roctracer are replaced with the ROCm 7.2.4 build the image ships and that the rest of the stack was validated against. ## Measured - Both flavors of the published nightly, on the GPU each targets, via a dispatch of the ROCm 7.2 nightly workflow: `448/512` FAIL as shipped, `512/512` PASS with the ROCm runtime in use, on MI300X and MI355X ([run](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32337394284)). `torch.cuda.get_device_name(0)` resolves; torch reports `hip 7.2.26015` — the 7.2.0 build — inside a 7.2.4 image. - @devalshahamd independently ran the probe on ROCm 7.0.0, 7.2.0 and 7.2.4 and reported it behaves as expected on all three, and that replacing the wheel's libraries gives a real SGLang workload a clean profile. - The Dockerfile step's logic exercised against a simulated `torch/lib` and `/opt/rocm/lib`: both vendored, idempotent re-run, nothing vendored, vendored with no ROCm copy (fails loudly), symlinks never chosen. - 18 unit tests green in upstream CI (`base-a-test-cpu`), plus black, isort, codespell, `check_registered_tests.py`. signals.title: [Fix] Stop unparsed Kimi K3 template syntax from leaking into responses
signals.text: ## Motivation Kimi K3 emits its channels (`<|open|>tools<|sep|>`, `<|open|>call ...`, `<|close|>message<|sep|>`, ...) as literal text, so any path that does not run the tool-call parser hands that syntax straight to the client. Two such paths exist today: - **Parsing disabled.** With `tool_choice="none"` or no tools, `serving_chat` / `serving_responses` skip the parser and `FunctionCallParser.parse_non_stream` returns `full_text` verbatim. Measured on a K3 deployment: ~10% of `tool_choice="none"` completions came back containing a raw tools section. - **Truncation.** `KimiK3Detector.has_tool_call` is `self.bot_token in text`, so output cut mid-marker (`...<|open|>too`) misses detection and `parse_non_stream` again returns the raw text. With small `max_output_tokens` this reproduced in 97-100% of samples. Separately, `ResponsesRequest._normalize_input_item_for_validation` defaults the SDK-required `input_image.detail` only under `item["content"]`. Tool-output items carry their parts under `item["output"]`, so an image tool result without `detail` (what Codex sends) fails validation with a 400. ## Modifications - `base_format_detector.py`: two identity-by-default hooks, `strip_template_artifacts(text, reasoning_separated)` and `strip_template_markers(text)`. Formats whose tool channel is literal text override them; every other detector is unaffected. - `kimik3_detector.py`: implements both. Artifact stripping cuts from an unparsed `TOOLS_OPEN` / `CALL_OPEN` onward, drops the think channel when a reasoning parser already routed the trace to its own field, unwraps the response channel, and removes whole and cut-off markers. Marker stripping only removes syntax, keeping the text it wrapped — used for reasoning content. - `kimik3_format.py`: `ALL_MARKERS`, `ARGUMENT_OPEN`, and a `min_len` on `partial_suffix_len` so a reply legitimately ending in `<` is not truncated. - `function_call_parser.py`: the two paths that returned `full_text` unchanged (no tools, detection missed) now route it through `strip_template_artifacts`. - `serving_chat.py` / `serving_responses.py`: apply the hooks to non-streaming assistant text and reasoning content, regardless of whether parsing ran. A Responses turn whose text was nothing but syntax still emits an `output_text` item (empty) rather than an output array with no message. - `utils.py`: `align_token_logprobs_to_text`. The cleanup is pure span deletion, so the cleaned text is a subsequence of the concatenated tokens; entries whose token was removed are dropped, and the array becomes `None` if the two cannot be reconciled rather than being returned misaligned. Applied only when cleanup actually changed the text, so logprobs on paths this PR does not touch are unchanged. - `protocol.py`: normalize `input_image.detail` under `output` as well as `content`. Streaming is out of scope: the chunk handlers can still emit markers verbatim, and fixing that needs cross-chunk marker buffering. ## Accuracy Tests No change to model forward or kernels — this only affects post-generation text handling in the OpenAI entrypoints. ## Speed Tests and Profiling N/A; the added work is a few regex passes over the response text. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32536273695](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32536273695)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32536273592](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32536273592)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32536273758](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32536273758)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [AMD] Verify the nightly ROCm 7.2.4 images trace HIP-graph kernels
signals.text: ## Motivation #30984 landed the `rocm724` flavors and the nightly now publishes them to `rocm/sgl-dev` and `lmsysorg/sglang-rocm`. Those flavors exist because ROCm 7.2.0 drops kernel-dispatch events for work submitted through `hipGraphLaunch` ([ROCm/ROCm#6102](https://github.com/ROCm/ROCm/issues/6102), fixed in 7.2.2), which is what AMD/Silo hit when profiling SGLang decoding on every `*-rocm720-*` image. Nothing verifies that the published images actually restore it. A trace with no GPU kernels in it still looks like a successful profile, `test/registered/profiling/test_start_profile.py` only asserts the trace directory is non-empty, and since #34452 the profiling suite runs without CUDA graphs on ROCm, so CI never exercises the replay path at all. A future base bump could quietly take the fix away again. ## Modifications One job in `release-docker-amd-rocm720-nightly.yml`. After publish, each `rocm724` flavor is probed on the GPU it targets — gfx942 on MI300X, gfx950 on MI355X — because the behaviour lives in the HIP runtime rather than in SGLang, so it is worth confirming per device generation. The job pulls the tag the publish job recorded in its artifact, starts the standard CI container against it, and runs `scripts/ci/amd/check_hip_graph_profiling.py` inside the image. No dependency install: the point is to exercise the image's own torch and HIP runtime, which is what was just published. Gating details: - **Per leg, not per workflow.** A `rocm720` leg failing in publish must not stop the `rocm724` images from being checked, so the job does not require all of publish to succeed. A `rocm724` leg that never published has no artifact and fails at the download — the same behaviour the mirror job below documents. - **`rocm720` legs are excluded**, since they are expected to fail; a dispatch selecting a single `rocm720` arch skips the job. - **`job_select` is respected**, so a `publish`-only dispatch does not run it. - **`job_select=verify_profiling` + `probe_image`** qualifies an already-published tag without a rebuild; pair it with `gpu_arch` to choose the GPU. That is the quickest way to answer the question for one image, and it is how this should be run first. - The container is removed at the end, since these runners are shared with the AMD test suites and it would otherwise hold VRAM until something else reclaims it. This verifies after publish rather than gating it, so the daily images are not held behind a GPU runner queue. A red leg means the day's `rocm724` image traces nothing under graph replay and should not be recommended for profiling. Turning it into a real gate means splitting the publish job's `rocm/sgl-dev` and `lmsysorg` pushes, which is worth doing separately if you want that. ## Accuracy Tests No model or kernel code changes; this adds a verification job to a release workflow. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not applicable. The job measures whether profiling works on the published image. ## Test plan - `actionlint` reports nothing on the new job; the only findings in the file are the pre-existing self-hosted runner labels and `docker/login-action@v2` in the publish and mirror jobs. - Job names pass `scripts/lint/check_workflow_job_names.py`. - The job's gating was simulated across the combinations that matter — schedule, `all`/`all`, `publish`-only, a `rocm720` arch, a single `rocm724` arch, `verify_profiling` with a skipped publish, and publish `failure` vs `cancelled` — confirming it runs exactly the intended legs in each. - The probe itself is unit-tested in #35390 (trace parsing, every verdict path) and validated for timeout handling and no-GPU behaviour. `workflow_dispatch` only offers a workflow that exists on the default branch, so this cannot be exercised until it merges. Once it has, the fastest check is one already-published image on one GPU: ```bash gh workflow run release-docker-amd-rocm720-nightly.yml --ref main \ -f job_select=verify_profiling \ -f probe_image=rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.17-rocm724-mi35x-20260820 \ -f gpu_arch=gfx950-rocm724 ``` Expected `VERDICT: PASS`, against the same probe failing on a `*-rocm720-*` tag. A full `gh workflow run ... --ref main` then covers build plus both GPUs. ## Notes for reviewers - Depends on #35390, which adds the probe script this job runs. Merge that first. - This PR previously proposed its own `rocm724` stages, nightly workflow, release-matrix entry, and torch Triton-pin patch. #30984 landed all four, so only the verification remains. ## Measured on hardware Dispatched against a branch carrying this job plus #35390's probe, targeting today's published image ([run](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32337394284), 4.5 minutes end to end on `linux-mi35x-gpu-1`): - `publish` and `push_local_registry` skipped, one `verify_profiling (gfx950-rocm724)` leg, artifact download skipped because `probe_image` was set — the gating behaved as intended. - Image default: `graph replay: 448/512` → step outcome `failure`, job still green (`continue-on-error`), and the summary records it as `**Image default** (failure)`. - ROCm runtime preloaded: `graph replay: 512/512` → PASS. `--print-ld-preload` inside the image produced `/opt/rocm/lib/libamdhip64.so.7.2.70204:/opt/rocm/lib/libroctracer64.so.4.1.70204`. `workflow_dispatch` runs the definition from the selected ref, so this is exactly what the job will do once merged. ## Checklist - signals.title: [NVIDIA] Fix SM107 MXFP8 activation prep
signals.text: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation <!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. --> Fix MXFP8 activation preparation for the FlashInfer MXFP4 MoE backend on SM107. GPT-OSS on SM107 can reach the FlashInfer MXFP4 MoE kernel without a pre-quantized route handoff. Previously, SGLang used the Triton per-token-group quantizer in this case. This does not reliably produce the activation representation expected by the FlashInfer SM107 path. The quantizer producing the activations must follow the same MXFP8 and UE8M0 layout contract as the FlashInfer MoE kernel consuming them. Using FlashInfer for both operations on SM107 avoids the incompatible producer/consumer path. The fake custom-op implementation also needs the real scale-buffer shape. Returning a placeholder one-element tensor can produce incorrect metadata during `torch.compile`. ## Modifications <!-- Detail the changes made in this pull request. --> - Use FlashInfer's MXFP8 quantizer on SM107 when no route/quant handoff is available. - Preserve Kimi K3's existing fused route/quant handoff. - Preserve the existing Triton activation-quantization path on other SM10x architectures. - Preserve FlashInfer quantization for padded hidden dimensions. - Correct the FlashInfer custom-op fake scale-buffer size for both linear and swizzled layouts so `torch.compile` metadata matches the real quantizer. - Add CPU regression tests covering dispatch behavior, padded inputs, route handoff, and fake output shapes. ## Accuracy Tests <!-- If this pull request affects model outputs (e.g., changes to the kernel or model forward code), provide accuracy test results. --> * Validated GPT-OSS with real weights on SM107 with 4 focused regression tests passed on SM107. * Verified the fake quantizer reports the expected scale shape. * Python compilation and `git diff --check` passed. ## Speed Tests and Profiling <!-- If this pull request impacts inference speed, provide benchmarking and profiling results. --> ## Checklist - signals.title: fix(encode-server): do not forward None video metadata to the processor
signals.text: ## Motivation `MMEncoder._flatten_and_load_videos` guards the `video_metadata` kwarg with `if video_metadata:`, which tests the list for **emptiness** rather than for content: ```python videos, video_metadata = map(list, zip(*video_processed)) video_processor_kwargs["do_sample_frames"] = False if video_metadata: video_processor_kwargs["video_metadata"] = video_metadata ``` `preprocess_video` returns `(video, None)` whenever its input is not a `VideoDecoderWrapper` — i.e. for video that was already decoded upstream and handed over as frames. The guard then sees `[None]` (or `[None, None, ...]`), finds it truthy, and forwards it. transformers' `make_batched_metadata` converts the value only when it is `None` (synthesizing defaults), or when it is a list whose first element is a `list` or a `dict`. A list holding `None` matches neither branch and is returned unchanged, so the consumer dereferences `None`. Measured against transformers 5.12.1: ``` video_metadata=None -> [VideoMetadata(total_num_frames=4, width=8, height=8, frames_indices=[0, 1, 2, 3], ...)] video_metadata=[None] -> [None] -> .fps raises AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'fps' video_metadata=[{...}] -> [VideoMetadata(..., fps=24.0)] ``` So omitting the kwarg is strictly *better* than forwarding `None`s: transformers then derives `total_num_frames`, `width`, `height` and `frames_indices` from the video itself. ## Modifications - `python/sglang/srt/disaggregation/encode_server.py`: forward `video_metadata` only when every entry is present. The list is positionally parallel to `videos`, so individual entries cannot be dropped without misaligning the rest — hence `all(...)` rather than `any(...)`; a partially-populated list is omitted entirely. - Added `test/registered/unit/multimodal/test_encode_server_video_metadata.py` covering all-`None`, all-real, mixed, and ordering (CPU, no model or GPU required). ## Accuracy Tests Not applicable — no change to model outputs. When metadata is present the behavior is unchanged; when it is absent the processor now receives no kwarg instead of `None` entries. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not applicable — one pass over a list whose length is the number of videos in the request. ## Validation Verified against `lmsysorg/sglang:nightly-dev-cu13-20260818-c0b6474b` by patching the image's own source tree at `/sgl-workspace/sglang` (editable install, so source and binaries match), torch 2.13.0+cu130, transformers 5.12.1. New unit test against the shipped `encode_server.py`: **2 failed, 2 passed** — the failures are exactly `test_all_none_metadata_is_not_forwarded` and `test_mixed_metadata_is_not_forwarded`, while the real-metadata and ordering controls pass. After the fix: **4 passed**. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the Format code with pre-commit. - [x] Add unit tests according to the Run and add unit tests. - [ ] Update documentation according to Write documentations. - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results — not applicable, see above. - [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32196854673](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32196854673)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32196854541](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32196854541)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [AMD] Fix gfx950 Triton compiler crash on fp8 KV-cache attention
signals.text: ## Motivation `test/registered/attention/test_verify_shared_kv.py::test_qwen3_5_fp8_kv_cache` has never passed on `stage-b-1-gpu-small-amd-mi35x` since it was added (#34517); it fails inside the Triton AMD backend, not in sglang code ([latest instance](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32166850277/job/95808413702)): ``` python3: llvm/ADT/SmallVector.h:292: Assertion `idx < size()' failed. extend_attention.py:305:0: error: Failures have been detected while processing an MLIR pass pipeline extend_attention.py:305:0: note: Pipeline failed while executing [`ConvertTritonAMDGPUToLLVM` ...] RuntimeError: PassManager::run failed ``` Only the fp8 variant fails; the bf16 variants of the same test pass. The crash is not test-specific — it is in the shared prefill kernel, so a model served on MI35x with `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3` **through the Triton attention backend** hits it, in decode as well as prefill. (Backends that do not route through these kernels, and the two ROCm Triton kernels that cannot take an fp8 pool at all, are out of scope; see Modifications.) **Scope: the ROCm 7.0 image only — 7.2 was never affected.** The dividing line is the Triton wheel, not ROCm. On the pre-fix ROCm 7.2 MI35x lane ([job 95705686213](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32135460766/job/95705686213), Aug 18, before any commit here) `test_verify_shared_kv.py` reported `"passed": true` with no `PassManager::run failed` or `idx < size()` in the log; that lane's only red was the unrelated `test_quark_mxfp4.py` near-miss. The 7.0 log carries aiter's `require triton>=3.6.0, found 3.4.0`, while 7.2 emits no such warning, so its Triton clears 3.6.0 (`docker/rocm.Dockerfile` installs aiter's pin over the base ROCm Torch `triton==3.5.1` when `BUILD_TRITON=1`). ### Root cause Every Triton attention kernel that reads a KV pool casts the wide operand *down* to the pool dtype before the dot (`tl.dot(q.to(k.dtype), k)`, `tl.dot(p.to(v.dtype), v)`), so an fp8 pool also feeds the fp8 matrix core. On gfx950 `AccelerateAMDMatmul` promotes an fp8 x fp8 `tl.dot` to the scaled `V_MFMA_*_F8F6F4` family, which is **16x16x128** under the `matrix_instr_nonkdim=16` launch hint all of these kernels pass. A dot whose reduction is narrower than 128 does not tile that instruction: `AMDMfmaEncodingAttr::getRepForOperand` clamps the resulting zero K-repetitions up to one, and `ScaledDotOpMFMAConversionHelper` then reads `kBase = 32` elements per lane from a register range that only holds `K / 4`. That is the out-of-bounds `SmallVector` access. `P @ V` reduces `BLOCK_N`, which is 64 (extend, verify) or 32 (decode, split-KV verify) — never 128 — so the fp8 path never compiles on gfx950. `Q @ Kpe` reduces `BLOCK_DPE` (32/64) and `Q @ K` reduces `BLOCK_DMODEL`, which is also below 128 at head_dim <= 64. Triton rejects the intrinsic instead of miscompiling it as of [triton-lang/triton#8278](https://github.com/triton-lang/triton/pull/8278), which dropped the `enforcedNonKDim == 0 &&` escape hatch that had let an explicit `matrix_instr_nonkdim` skip Triton's own "K is not a multiple of the intrinsic's kDim" check. That fix missed 3.5 and landed in 3.6: | Triton branch | guard in `chooseMfmaInstruction` | narrow fp8 dot | |---|---|---| | `release/3.4.x`, `release/3.5.x` | `enforcedNonKDim == 0 && inputKSize % kDim != 0` | promoted, then aborts | | `release/3.6.x` and later | `if (inputKSize % kDim != 0)` | rejected, falls back to non-scaled fp8 MFMA | So anything on 3.4 or 3.5 with `matrix_instr_nonkdim` set — which is every kernel here — crashes, and the ROCm 7.0 image ships 3.4.0. **The guard therefore carries a `triton.__version__ < 3.6` term, so it is inert on 7.2.** Without it the guard also fired on 7.2, where Triton already falls back to the non-scaled `V_MFMA_F32_16X16X32_FP8_FP8` and the narrow dot works — [the same pre-fix job](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32135460766/job/95705686213) ran `test_qwen3_5_fp8_kv_cache` green. That would have substituted a bf16 dot for a working fp8 one on the lane that gates PRs, trading unquantized `P` (more accurate) against fp8→bf16 converts and a 2-byte V tile in LDS, for a rate difference nobody has measured. Not a trade worth making on the primary lane. With the version term: - **7.0 / Triton 3.4** — guard active, replaces a hard compile abort. - **7.2 / Triton ≥3.6** — guard inert, codegen byte-identical to today. - When ROCm 7.0 is dropped the guard is permanently inert and the whole module can be deleted, so this does not become long-lived debt. `extend_attention.py` already gates gfx950 tile choices on `_is_triton_ge_37`, so a Triton-version term is an established idiom in this file rather than a new mechanism. A version string that will not parse keeps the guard on, which is the safe direction. ## Modifications - New `python/sglang/kernels/ops/attention/fp8_dot_support.py` with `dot_in_kv_dtype(kv_dtype, reduction_width)`: `True` for every non-fp8 pool and every arch other than gfx950, and on gfx950 only for reduction widths that tile the scaled MFMA instruction. - Each dot that casts an operand down to the tile it reads gets its own constexpr verdict (`QK_DOT_IN_KV_DTYPE`, `QK_PE_DOT_IN_KV_DTYPE`, `PV_DOT_IN_KV_DTYPE`, `PV_EXTEND_DOT_IN_V_DTYPE`). When it is `False` the KV tile is upcast to the query dtype instead of the query tile being cast down. This covers `_fwd_kernel` and `_fwd_kernel_unified` (extend), `_fwd_grouped_kernel_stage1` (decode), `_verify_mla_prefix_stage1`, and `_verify_prefix_stage1` — including `_fwd_kernel`'s extend-stage `P @ V`, whose V is the caller's current-chunk tensor rather than the pool. Every flag is `True` on non-gfx950 hardware and for bf16/fp16 pools, so those paths generate the same code as before. `matrix_instr_nonkdim`, tile sizes, warp counts, and the `#mma` layout are all untouched. **Non-AMD impact: none, verified rather than argued.** `is_gfx95_supported()` returns `False` for every non-HIP build without touching the device, so `dot_in_kv_dtype` short-circuits to `True` on NVIDIA and the guards select the pre-existing expression. To confirm that costs nothing, I compiled the original kernel body and the guarded one (flags `True`) for five targets with Triton 3.4.0 and diffed the emitted TTGIR and LLIR modulo debug locations: **identical on sm90 (bf16 and fp8), sm100 (fp8), gfx942 (fp8) and gfx950 (bf16)**. That check is what caught the one real difference — writing the guard as `tl.dot(p.to(v.dtype), v)` reorders the P cast against the `acc * re_scale` multiply, which on Hopper with an fp8 pool moved the async `warp_group_dot` relative to the accumulator scaling. Keeping `p = p.to(v.dtype)` as its own statement inside the guard restores exact equivalence, which is why it is written that way. NVIDIA fp8 KV keeps casting down to fp8 and keeps its fp8 tensor-core path. The residual cost off gfx950 is one extra Triton compile (the new constexpr parameters change the cache key) and three or four integer / `frozenset` comparisons per launch. Two other ROCm Triton kernels dot against a tile that could in principle be fp8, and deliberately get no verdict: - `prefill_attention.py` never reads a KV pool, its `Q @ K` is uncast (so its operands already share a dtype), and its gfx950 `BLOCK_N` is 128 — which tiles the scaled instruction even if `P @ V` ran in fp8. - `rocm_mla_decode_rope.py` does read the pool, but its `Q @ K` is uncast too, so a bf16 query against an fp8 pool fails Triton's frontend with `Unsupported rhs dtype fp8e4nv` well before the AMD backend. That is a separate pre-existing gap in that kernel, not this crash, and a per-dot verdict would not make it work. The verify combine kernels compute their draft-draft block with `tl.sum(q[:, None, :] * ke[None, :, :], 2)`, not `tl.dot`, so no matrix-core promotion applies there. **On unit tests:** I wrote and then dropped a CPU test for the predicate. Asserting `dot_in_kv_dtype(fp8, 64) is False` against a body of `width % 128 == 0` only restates the expression, and the one assertion with real coupling — that the gfx950 head_dim-256 config yields a `BLOCK_N` the guard rejects — would fail if someone legitimately retuned `BLOCK_N` to 128, which is the documented fallback here. Pinning that would block an improvement rather than catch a bug. The failure mode worth guarding is "a new narrow fp8 dot appears on gfx950", and what catches that is compiling the real kernel on real gfx950, i.e. the MI35x lane. Alternatives considered and rejected: dropping or raising `matrix_instr_nonkdim` for the fp8 path (Triton's own guard then rejects the intrinsic, but the 16x16 tile becomes 32x32, which changes `warpsPerTile` for the chain-dot tail from `[8, 1]` to `[4, 2]` and inserts a layout conversion between the two dots), and forcing `BLOCK_N = 128` (fixes only head_dim 256 and re-tunes the bf16 path with it). ## Accuracy Tests `stage-b-test-1-gpu-small-amd-mi35x` now passes on MI35x hardware. [Run 32217006660](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32217006660) is a targeted dispatch of just that stage against this PR's head (ROCm 7.0, since that lane is schedule-only and a PR event never runs it): **9/9 passed**, `test_verify_shared_kv.py` reports `"passed": true` with `test_qwen3_5_fp8_kv_cache` executing, and the log contains no `PassManager::run failed` or `idx < size()`. ([Run 32212523645](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32212523645) is the same result on the first commit.) The change only affects gfx950 with an fp8 KV pool, where nothing compiled before, so there is no prior behaviour to regress. Within that path `P` reaches the dot as bf16 rather than quantized to e4m3, which is strictly more accurate; `extend_attention_fwd` and `verify_shared_kv_fwd` widen the same dots, so `test_qwen3_5_fp8_kv_cache`'s parity check compares like with like. ## Speed Tests and Profiling @chuyeh benched the three #34517 kernels on MI355X at the Qwen3.5 TP4-local verify shape ([full tables](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/35428#issuecomment-5364623778)). fp8 pool versus bf16 pool at a 16k prefix: | Kernel | bf16 pool | fp8 pool | Δ | |---|---:|---:|---:| | grouped-head verify | 0.048 ms | 0.042 ms | **−12%** | | split-KV verify | 0.073 ms | 0.056 ms | **−23%** | | extend | 1.069 ms | 1.791 ms | **+68%** | The bandwidth-bound verify kernels gain from the halved KV traffic; extend regresses. Two caveats on reading that: 1. **Those numbers are from `780d4ab`, before the Triton-version term.** On ROCm 7.2 the guard was still firing there, so the fp8 extend row is the widened bf16 `P @ V`. At HEAD the guard is inert on 7.2, so that row should not reproduce on that image. 2. **The bench cannot attribute the +68%.** A pool that halves KV bytes made the other two kernels faster, so extend moving the other way is either the widened `P @ V` (fp8→bf16 V converts plus a 2-byte V tile in LDS, paid every iteration of a serial prefix loop at `BLOCK_M=128`/`BLOCK_N=64`/head_dim 256) or something inherent to fp8 extend that this PR neither causes nor cures. An extend-only rerun at HEAD on 7.2 separates them; requested, not blocking. What this does not change: on ROCm 7.0 the alternative to widening is a compile abort, so a slower extend is still the right trade there, and it is the only image that pays it. If the widening does own the regression, the follow-up lever is `BLOCK_N = 128` for the fp8 extend tile — it reaches the scaled 16x16x128 instruction on both dots and compiles today, at the cost of retuning the tile and doubling the K/V LDS footprint. That belongs in its own change with numbers behind it, not here. Independently useful from the same run: "the flags-`True` path does not move the bf16 numbers", which confirms the codegen-equivalence check above on hardware. ## Verification Triton 3.4.0's AMD backend compiles for `hip:gfx950` without a GPU, so the fix was checked by driving the ttir/ttgir/llir stages directly on the same tile shape and launch hints as `extend_attention` at head_dim 256 (`BLOCK_M=128`, `num_warps=8`, `matrix_instr_nonkdim=16`): | KV dtype | `PV_DOT_IN_KV_DTYPE` | `BLOCK_N` | Result | |---|---|---|---| | fp8_e4m3 | True (today) | 64 | **`RuntimeError: PassManager::run failed`** | | fp8_e4m3 | False (this PR) | 64 | compiles | | fp8_e4m3 | True | 32 | **`Assertion 'idx < size()' failed`** | | fp8_e4m3 | False | 32 | compiles | | fp8_e4m3 | True | 128 | compiles (128 tiles the instruction) | | bf16 | True | 64 | compiles (unchanged path) | The fixed variant's TTGIR keeps the fp8 fast path where it is legal and drops to bf16 only for `P @ V`, both under the same `#mma` layout as before: ``` %50 = tt.dot_scaled %28, %49, %cst_2 lhs = e4m3 rhs = e4m3 : tensor<128x256xf8E4M3FN, dot_op<{opIdx = 0, parent = #mma, kWidth = 16}>> * tensor<256x64xf8E4M3FN, ...> %77 = tt.dot %76, %75, %73 : tensor<128x64xbf16, dot_op<{opIdx = 0, parent = #mma, kWidth = 4}>> * tensor<64x256xbf16, dot_op<{opIdx = 1, parent = #mma, kWidth = 4}>> ``` The K3 MLA tile (`BLOCK_DMODEL=512`, `BLOCK_DPE=64`, `BLOCK_N=64`), where two of the three dots widen, behaves the same way: crashes today, compiles with the per-dot verdicts. Narrowing `BLOCK_DMODEL` to 64 crashes the `Q @ K` dot too, which is why the verdict is computed per dot rather than assuming `Q @ K` is always wide enough. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). The regression test is the existing `test_verify_shared_kv.py::test_qwen3_5_fp8_kv_cache` on `stage-b-test-1-gpu-small-amd-mi35x`, which this PR turns green; no new test file is added (see below). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

signals.title: [CPU] Fix wrongly causal-masked bidirectional attention
signals.text: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation <!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. --> On the Intel AMX CPU attention backend, `extend_attention_cpu` always masked the extend stage of attention as causal. This is correct for decoder-style self-attention, but wrong for bidirectional, encoder-only self-attention (e.g. BERT-family rerankers/embedders like bge-reranker). On this backend such models silently got causally-masked attention scores, producing incorrect outputs. When running `BAAI/bge-reranker-base` on CPU: For the below request: ``` { "model": "BAAI/bge-reranker-base", "query": "what is panda?", "documents": [ "hi", "The giant panda (Ailuropoda melanoleuca), sometimes called a panda bear or simply panda, is a bear species endemic to China." ], "return_documents": true } ``` Before this fix: `"hi"` and `"The giant panda ..."` both get the same score: 2.611328125, which is not reasonble. After this fix: Scores diverge correctly, matching what a real cross-encoder should produce: `"The giant panda ..."`: score is 6.1875 `"hi"`: score is -8.15625 ## Modifications <!-- Detail the changes made in this pull request. --> - `python/sglang/kernels/aot/csrc/cpu/extend.cpp`: add an `is_causal` parameter (default `true`) to `extend_attention_cpu`. The stage-2 loop now iterates over the full extend range and only applies the causal mask when `is_causal` is set, instead of unconditionally limiting keys to `[0, m + BLOCK_M)` and masking `n + n_size - 1 > m`. - `python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/intel_amx_backend.py`: compute `is_causal = not (layer.is_cross_attention or layer.attn_type == AttentionType.ENCODER_ONLY)` and pass it into `extend_attention_fwd`, mirroring the existing pattern in `triton_backend.py`: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/ee1f2e8dfdbb264727134aeac4b8dec155ec6efe/python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/triton_backend.py#L1360-L1368. ## Accuracy Tests <!-- If this pull request affects model outputs (e.g., changes to the kernel or model forward code), provide accuracy test results. --> ```sh python test/registered/cpu/test_extend.py -k test_extend_attention_bidirectional ``` ## Checklist - [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers. 3. signals.title: [Fix] Preserve model runner contracts in prefill CUDA graphs
signals.text: ## Motivation PrefillCudaGraphRunner constructs new ForwardBatch objects for capture and replay. Those objects currently bypass ModelRunner.prepare_dummy_forward_batch, even though model runners use that hook to prepare graph-specific batch state. The runner also rebuilds LogitsProcessorOutput while trimming graph padding but drops customized_info. ## Modifications - Apply prepare_dummy_forward_batch to both capture-time and replay-time ForwardBatch objects. - Preserve customized_info when trimming full-prefill graph outputs. - Add focused tests for both contracts. ## Accuracy Tests No model math or kernels are changed. - 7 focused unit tests passed, including 2 parameterized subtests. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not applicable. The hooks run during graph setup/replay preparation, and the output change only preserves existing metadata. ## Checklist - [x] Format code with the repository pre-commit configuration. - [x] Add unit tests. - [x] No documentation update is required. - [x] No speed benchmark is required for this contract-preservation fix. - [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32508429903](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32508429903)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32508429784](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32508429784)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32508429893](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32508429893)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [Fix] Harden FlashAttention CUDA graph metadata bounds
signals.text: ## Motivation Full-prefill CUDA graph buckets are sized by aggregate batch tokens, which can exceed the maximum context length of any single request. The FlashAttention sliding-window write-location buffer is currently allocated from max_context_len, so a valid aggregate-token bucket can exceed its capacity. Separately, idle graph batches may expose an empty CPU sequence-length tensor, for which max() is invalid. ## Modifications - Size the full-prefill sliding-window write-location buffer from the captured token capacity. - Validate replay token counts before copying into the graph-stable buffer. - Use the static context bound when CPU sequence lengths are absent or empty. - Add CPU regression tests for aggregate-token capacity, replay overflow detection, and empty idle batches. ## Accuracy Tests No attention math is changed. The tests validate metadata sizing and fallback behavior. - 2 focused unit tests passed. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not applicable. These changes affect metadata allocation and boundary checks, not attention kernels. ## Checklist - [x] Format code with the repository pre-commit configuration. - [x] Add unit tests. - [x] No documentation update is required. - [x] No speed benchmark is required for this metadata correctness fix. - [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:no_entry_sign: [Run #32416500122](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32416500122)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32416499661](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32416499661)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32416499821](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32416499821)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [AMD][Spec] Pack AITER target-verify GQA for Qwen3.5
signals.text: ## Motivation Qwen3.5 uses grouped-query attention, where multiple query heads share one KV head. For example, under TP=2, each TP rank of Qwen3.5-397B has 16 query heads sharing one KV head. During target verification, the AITER attention backend currently expands this KV head to 16 stride-zero views before calling `unified_attention`. The expansion does not copy data, but it makes the kernel see 16 query heads and 16 KV heads instead of the original GQA layout. As a result, AITER treats the workload as MHA rather than GQA. On MI355X (`gfx95`), this increases the attention program count at high concurrency and can move the workload from the 3D split-KV kernel to the slower 2D kernel. In serving tests, this appears as the concurrency-64 stall: throughput stops increasing while TPOT nearly doubles. [#34517](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/34517) addresses the same shared-KV verification problem for the Triton backend with a grouped-head kernel. This PR covers the AITER backend by passing the true GQA layout to the `unified_attention` kernel. ## Modifications - Skip K/V `.expand()` during AITER target verification for Qwen3.5 on MI355X, so AITER sees the real one-head GQA layout. - Add a correctness test comparing the new layout with the previous expanded layout for BF16 and FP8 KV caches. ## Correctness Tests Added one test in `test/registered/attention/test_aiter_fp8_q_unified_attention.py` with the following Qwen3.5 TP2 verification shape: - Batch size: 4 - Query heads: 16 - KV heads: 1 - Draft tokens: 4 - KV sequence length: 512 - Head dimension: 256 - Page size: 16 The test calls `unified_attention` twice with the same data: 1. Using the true one-head GQA layout. 2. Using the previous layout, where K/V is expanded to 16 stride-zero heads. It verifies that both layouts produce matching outputs for BF16 and FP8 E4M3 KV caches, including FP8 K/V descale factors. The new test passed, and the full test file completed all four tests successfully on MI355X (`gfx950`) with ROCm 7.2. ## Performance ### Kernel benchmark #### Environment - Hardware: MI355X - Shape: Qwen3.5 TP2-local, 16 query heads sharing one KV head - Head dimension: 256 - Draft tokens: 4 - Page size: 16 - Execution: HIP graph capture enabled | KV cache | Prefix tokens | Batch | Baseline layout | GQA layout | Speedup | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | BF16 | 8,192 | 4 | 0.064 ms | **0.056 ms** | **1.14x** | | BF16 | 8,192 | 64 | 1.271 ms | **0.326 ms** | **3.90x** | | FP8 | 8,192 | 64 | 0.497 ms | **0.236 ms** | **2.11x** | | BF16 | 32,768 | 64 | 5.555 ms | **1.246 ms** | **4.46x** | At batch 64, the expanded layout uses the 2D kernel. Keeping the true GQA layout allows AITER to use the 3D split-KV kernel. ### End-to-end serving benchmark #### Environment - Hardware: one MI355X host; baseline on GPUs 0–1 and this PR on GPUs 2–3, both using TP2 - Image: `rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.17-rocm720-mi35x-20260820` - Model: Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-MXFP4 - Workload: ISL/OSL up to 8192/1024 tokens, with range ratio 0.8 - Attention backend: AITER unified attention - Speculative decoding: EAGLE, three steps, top-k=1, 4 draft tokens - Page size: 16 - KV cache: FP8 E4M3 The server used the official InferenceX `qwen3.5_fp4_mi355x_mtp.sh` configuration, with only the KV-cache dtype changed to FP8. Both arms included [#35719](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/35719) so the MTP shared-expert weights were loaded correctly. | Concurrency | Baseline tok/s/GPU | This PR tok/s/GPU | Throughput change | Baseline median TTFT (ms) | This PR median TTFT (ms) | TTFT change | Baseline median TPOT (ms) | This PR median TPOT (ms) | TPOT change | |---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 4 | 2,629 | 2,639 | +0.4% | 338 | 335 | -0.9% | 6.43 | 6.31 | -1.9% | | 8 | 3,723 | 3,872 | +4.0% | 340 | 344 | +1.1% | 9.06 | 8.62 | -4.8% | | 16 | 4,827 | 5,194 | +7.6% | 355 | 350 | -1.4% | 14.30 | 13.25 | -7.3% | | 32 | 6,060 | 6,603 | +8.9% | 379 | 380 | +0.0% | 23.12 | 20.89 | -9.7% | | **64** | **6,049** | **8,019** | **+32.6%** | **475** | **409** | **-13.9%** | **46.94** | **35.26** | **-24.9%** | | 128 | 8,812 | 9,314 | +5.7% | 681 | 648 | -4.9% | 64.49 | 60.38 | -6.4% | | 256 | 10,042 | 10,750 | +7.1% | 1,007 | 1,007 | 0.0% | 113.88 | 106.61 | -6.4% | From concurrency 32 to 64, baseline throughput remains flat at approximately 6,050 tok/s/GPU. With the GQA layout, throughput increases to 8,019 tok/s/GPU. At concurrency 64, median TTFT decreases from 475 ms to 409 ms, while median TPOT decreases from 46.94 ms to 35.26 ms. The concurrency-4 result is within normal run-to-run variance. The main improvement appears at C64, where the baseline hits the 2D kernel-selection cliff. All requests completed successfully. Neither arm logged skipped shared-expert weights, and median EAGLE acceptance remained similar between the two layouts. ## Checklist - [x] Format code according to the contribution guide. - [x] Add registered correctness coverage. - [x] Provide kernel and end-to-end performance measurements. - [x] Keep the change limited to the tested model, hardware, and attention path. - [x] Preserve the existing layout as the fallback. - [x] Add no new user-facing option. ## Review and Merge Process 1. signals.title: [Fix] Pass Anthropic thinking history as reasoning_content for custom chat encoders
signals.text: ## Motivation Run Kimi-K3 with `--reasoning-parser kimi_k3 --tool-call-parser kimi_k3` and talk to it on `/v1/messages` with `thinking` on. Any agentic client sends assistant `thinking` blocks back in history — the Messages API requires it for tool-use turns — and a few turns in, raw XTML channel markers show up in visible assistant text: ``` turn 3 [text] '<|open|>think<|sep|<|sep|>Something is very strange. […]' turn 4 [text] '<|open|>think<|sep|' ``` Turns 1-2 are fine, then every turn after that is corrupted — it never recovers. Drop the `thinking` blocks from the replayed history and it never happens at all, so the problem is how prior reasoning gets fed back, not the reasoning parser. **Root cause.** K3 ships no Jinja chat template, so SGLang renders it through the checkpoint's own XTML encoder. That encoder frames the `think` / `response` / `tools` channels itself and wants prior reasoning in an assistant `reasoning_content` field. The Anthropic adapter never used it — instead it wrapped prior thinking in the reasoning detector's markers and spliced that into assistant **content**. Here is what the two forms actually render to, straight from the K3 tokenizer: ``` # before — think channel empty, reasoning nested inside the response channel <|open|>think<|sep|><|close|>think<|sep|><|open|>response<|sep|><|open|>think<|sep|>PRIOR <|close|>think<|sep|>Here is my answer.<|close|>response<|sep|> # after <|open|>think<|sep|>PRIOR<|close|>think<|sep|><|open|>response<|sep|>Here is my answer.<|close|>response<|sep|> ``` Every replayed turn taught the model the same lesson: think channel empty, think block sitting inside the response channel. Two turns of that and it starts writing `<|open|>think<|sep|>` as ordinary response text. None of this is K3-specific. All four Python chat encoders that bypass `apply_chat_template` frame their own reasoning channel and read `reasoning_content`, so the splice was wrong for every one of them. ## Modifications - **`entrypoints/openai/chat_encoding.py`** — adds `spec_owns_reasoning_history(spec)`, right under `resolve_chat_encoding_spec` so the contract sits with the specs it describes. It covers the whole custom-encoder family (`spec is not None`) rather than listing specs, so whoever adds the fifth one gets the safe default for free. An encoder that ignores the field drops history — what the splice path already does for models with no reasoning detector — instead of leaking. - **`entrypoints/openai/serving_chat.py`** — `supports_native_reasoning_history()`, a one-line delegate. - **`entrypoints/anthropic/serving.py`** — `_convert_assistant_thinking_blocks` now returns `(reasoning_content, text)`. Custom encoders get the history in the field, everyone else keeps the splice untouched. `redacted_thinking` still raises before the branch, and the best-effort drop for detector-less models survives. Nothing needed a schema change: `ChatCompletionMessageGenericParam` already declared `reasoning_content`, and messages are dumped without `exclude_none`, so it flows straight through. `wrap_reasoning_history` has exactly one production caller, so that is the whole mechanism. `dsv4`/`dsv32` also land on their official multi-turn contract now instead of bypassing it. Jinja-path models stay on the splice on purpose — their markers (`<think>`, `[THINK]`, `◁think▷`) really do live in the content stream, so it reproduces what the model emitted anyway. ## Test Plan ### Live server Same deployment before and after — `moonshotai/Kimi-K3` on 2x4 GB300, TP8, DSPARK spec-decode — same scripts, `temperature=0`: | run | main | with the fix | | --- | --- | --- | | 12-turn tool loop, streaming `/v1/messages` | leaks turns 3-12, all ten of them | clean, and the loop converges at turn 9 | | 8-turn tool loop, non-streaming | leaks turns 3-8 | clean | | 6 concurrent sessions x 5 turns | all six leak, every one first at turn 3 | none leak | | thinking dropped from replayed history | clean | clean | | `thinking: {"type": "disabled"}` | clean | clean | | reasoning passed as `reasoning_content` on `/v1/chat/completions` | clean | clean | | thinking-only history turn, and a turn with two thinking blocks | clean | clean | | `redacted_thinking` history | 400 | 400 | On main the onset is turn 3 every single time, and it never recovers — the `thinking` block stops appearing at all from there on and the markers move into `text`. That is also why the loop never converges: each turn re-reads its own corrupted history and re-diagnoses the same phantom problem. With the fix, `thinking` comes back on essentially every turn and the model finishes the task. Asked what it had just been thinking, the model quoted the injected reasoning back — the history really does land in the think channel rather than being quietly dropped. Prompt rendering was also diffed against the real K3 tokenizer for a thinking + text + tool_use turn. ### Unit tests `anthropic/test_serving.py` — 61/61. Two new cases: history reaches a channel-framing encoder as `reasoning_content` and never through the wrap path, and a thinking-only turn keeps its reasoning across the empty-content placeholder branch. Both go red against pre-fix code, and the existing wrap-path test still covers the default encoder. `openai/test_serving_chat.py` — 111/111. Two more: the real `OpenAIServingChat` predicate across all four specs plus `None`, and a guard that parses the literals `resolve_chat_encoding_spec` can return and checks them against the tuple the capability test iterates. Add an encoder without classifying it and CI fails. Mutation-checked, so it is not passing vacuously. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32435140730](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32435140730)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32435140644](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32435140644)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32435140704](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32435140704)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [Responses] Fix multimodal Kimi-K3 /v1/responses returning 400 "texts cannot be empty"
signals.text: …mpty' <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation A `/v1/responses` request against a **multimodal Kimi-K3** deployment fails immediately: ```json {"error":{"message":"texts cannot be empty and tokenizer must be initialized","type":"invalid_request_error","param":null,"code":400}} ``` The equivalent /v1/chat/completions request with the same messages and tools works, so the bug is specific to the /v1/responses path for multimodal Kimi-K3. ## Why The kimi_k3 custom encoder produces a usable prompt_ids (via apply_chat_template(tokenize=True, ...)) but leaves prompt == "" — the only prompt = decode(prompt_ids) assignment lives in the prompt_ids is None branch, which kimi_k3 never enters. OpenAIServingResponses._make_request forwarded that empty prompt as text on the multimodal branch, producing GenerateReqInput(text=""). In TokenizerManager.generate_request, input_ids is None and input_text is empty, so control reaches _tokenize_texts(""), which raises the error above. serving_chat._convert_to_internal_request already special-cases this (elif is_multimodal and self.chat_encoding_spec == "kimi_k3": prompt_kwargs = {"input_ids": ...}); the responses path was missing the same guard. A text-only Kimi-K3 deployment (is_multimodal == False) takes the else branch and uses prompt_ids, so it is unaffected — which is why the bug only surfaces for multimodal Kimi-K3. Fixes #35460 ## Modifications - python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/openai/serving_responses.py: - test/registered/unit/entrypoints/openai/test_serving_responses.py: add ## Accuracy Tests N/A — no kernel or model-forward change; this only fixes which prompt field the responses path hands to the engine. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32476675953](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32476675953)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32476675888](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32476675888)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32476675898](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32476675898)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [AMD] Improve K3 dspark draft attn kernel perf
signals.text: ## Motivation With DSpark on Kimi-K3, every step runs 5 draft attn layers (qwen-style, non-causal). Draft attn dominates their cost. In a trace study, the 5 draft layers took 2.368 ms, of which the 5 attn kernels alone accounted for 1.244 ms (>50%). The reason is that this falls back to `extend_attention_fwd`. This generic extend kernel is a poor fit for a shared-KV shape. > Note that draft attn is a common path. `--attention-backend` only selects the target-verify kernel. `aiter` is not among the draft worker's supported backends, so on ROCm the draft always falls back to `triton`. Both `--attention-backend triton` and `aiter` therefore reach the kernel this PR changes. ## Modifications Route DSpark draft attn to `verify_shared_kv`, and extend that kernel to cover the two cases it previously rejected. - **Non-causal situation**: The prefix loop never applies a causal mask, so only modify the stage-2 kernel. - **`h_kv > 1`**: Both stages add a KV-head offset (`head // kv_group_num * stride_h`). A `HAS_KV_HEADS` constexpr keeps the single-KV-head (MLA/MQA) path free of that arithmetic, so the existing Kimi-K3 target-verify path compiles exactly as before. Also adds a tuning entry for `head_dim=64` (`BLOCK_N=256`, 4 warps) and `is_dspark_draft()` in `model_config.py` for the gate. ## Accuracy Tests GSM8k, 1319: ``` 100%|███████████| 1319/1319 [02:00<00:00, 10.98it/s] Accuracy: 0.955 Invalid: 0.001 Latency: 120.085 s Output throughput: 1108.066 token/s ``` ## Speed Tests and Profiling Tested with docker image `rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.17-rocm720-mi35x-20260818`. Since draft attn is a common code path and this change is independent of other work, the numbers are measured directly on `main`, with no other non-merged PRs applied. Perf (isl=8k/16k/32k, cc=4, 32): - On cc=4, ITL improves by 4-12% and TTT by 2-6%. - On cc=32, ITL improves by 1-5% and TTT by 1-2%. The gain grows with input length, from 8k to 32k, in both cases. signals.title: fix(cache): retain shared SWA slots until final free
signals.text: ## Problem Different full-cache indices can reference the same physical SWA slot. Freeing one mapping previously returned that slot while another mapping still referenced it, allowing premature reuse and a later double free. ## Change Track a reference count per physical SWA slot whenever mappings are written, replaced, or cleared. Free token slots or pages only after their final mapping is removed, while preserving PureSWA's direct identity mapping. ## Validation - full diff passes repository pre-commit hooks - focused duplicate-free and cross-call lifetime tests pass on MI350X - combined Inkling LoRA E2E completes two rollouts without the shared-slot illegal address

signals.title: [Deepseek-V4] Enable shared-experts fusion on the flashinfer_mxfp4 (trtllm-gen) MoE path
signals.text: ## Summary Enable shared-experts fusion for DeepSeek-V4-Flash on the `flashinfer_mxfp4` (trtllm-gen) path: the shared expert is routed as expert slot 256 through the same MoE kernel, so the whole MoE runs on a single stream instead of a separate FP8 MLP on an alternate stream (~4 fewer kernel launches + 2 fewer stream syncs per layer). The machinery already existed (#27349); this PR enables and validates it. Also adds a guard rejecting fusion under EP without per-rank shared slots, which would silently compute wrong results. ## Scope - `deepseek_v4.py`: EP guard in the fusion gate (11 lines). - New CPU unit test for the load-time FP8→MXFP4 shared-expert requant (byte-level packing/scale contract). - Recipes: add `--enforce-shared-experts-fusion` to the b200/b300/gb200/gb300 flash-official fp4 low-latency entries. ## Testing - Kernel: verified out-of-tree on GB200 with a standalone test at the fused shape (257 experts / top-k 7, every token hits the shared slot), 12/12 vs a dequantized torch reference; no flashinfer change needed. Test available on request. - Unit: `test/registered/unit/models/test_deepseek_v4_mxfp4_shared_expert_requant.py`. - Profiler: with fusion on, the shared-expert kernels disappear and the MoE runs on a single stream. ## Results GB200 tp4, only variable is the fusion flag. signals.title: Add Spark3 Model
signals.text: ## Summary This PR adds native support for the Spark 3 model architecture in SGLang. The implementation introduces the Spark 3 configuration and causal language model, including sliding-window and full attention, head-wise attention output gating, tensor parallelism, pipeline parallelism, and checkpoint weight loading. ## Changes | File | Purpose | | --- | --- | | `python/sglang/srt/configs/spark3.py` | Adds `Spark3Config`, including model dimensions, attention layout, sliding-window configuration, layer types, RoPE parameters, and tied word embeddings. | | `python/sglang/srt/models/spark3.py` | Implements `Spark3ForCausalLM`, including grouped-query attention, interleaved sliding/full attention, head-wise output gating, gated MLP, parallelism support, split prefill, and checkpoint weight loading. | | `python/sglang/srt/configs/__init__.py` | Exports `Spark3Config` through the SGLang configuration package. | | `python/sglang/srt/utils/hf_transformers/common.py` | Registers `Spark3Config` in SGLang's Hugging Face configuration registry. | ## Key Technical Details 1. Efficient Architecture：The models adopt an efficiency-oriented architecture with Sliding Window Attention (SWA) and other structural optimizations, improving the balance between model quality, memory usage, and inference efficiency. 2. Native 1M Context：Both the 1.7B and 4B models natively support up to 1 million tokens of context, enabling long-document understanding, repository-level coding, and long-horizon agent tasks. 3. Strong Coding & Agent Capabilities：The models deliver leading coding and agent performance among models of comparable size, with strong capabilities in code generation, tool use, multi-step execution, and long-context reasoning. 4. Faster Inference：Through model architecture and inference-stack optimizations, the models achieve higher inference efficiency and throughput than many comparable-size models, especially in long-context scenarios. 5. Strong K–12 and Gaokao Performance：The models achieve leading K–12 question-answering performance at comparable parameter scales, with particularly strong results on challenging Chinese Gaokao-style tasks. 6. Advanced Post-Training：The release applies a comprehensive post-training recipe based on Scaled Reinforcement Learning and MOPD, improving reasoning, coding, instruction following, agentic capabilities, and alignment. 7. Controllable Thinking Budget：The models support configurable reasoning levels — none, low, medium, and high — allowing applications to dynamically trade off reasoning quality, latency, and inference cost. 8. 200+ Languages：Multilingual coverage has been expanded to more than 200 languages, supporting broad cross-lingual understanding, generation, translation, and localized applications. ## Performance We run MMLU-Pro on our internal OAI-server compatible benchmarking suite and the scores match the declared performance. Running on 1xH200 SXM5 ```bash ============ Serving Benchmark Result ============ Backend: sglang Traffic request rate: inf Max request concurrency: not set Successful requests: 500 Benchmark duration (s): 4.48 Total input tokens: 756489 Total input text tokens: 756489 Total generated tokens: 64000 Total generated tokens (retokenized): 63997 Request throughput (req/s): 111.52 Input token throughput (tok/s): 168733.90 Output token throughput (tok/s): 14275.12 Peak output token throughput (tok/s): 27064.00 Peak concurrent requests: 500 Total token throughput (tok/s): 183009.02 Concurrency: 463.05 ----------------End‑to‑End Latency---------------- Mean E2E Latency (ms): 4152.05 Median E2E Latency (ms): 4387.30 P90 E2E Latency (ms): 4391.62 P95 E2E Latency (ms): 4392.38 P99 E2E Latency (ms): 4393.38 ----------------Time to First Token---------------- Mean TTFT (ms): 2348.20 Median TTFT (ms): 2377.59 P90 TTFT (ms): 2386.19 P95 TTFT (ms): 2387.18 P99 TTFT (ms): 2388.39 -----Time per Output Token (excl. 1st token)----- Mean TPOT (ms): 14.20 Median TPOT (ms): 15.81 P90 TPOT (ms): 15.85 P95 TPOT (ms): 15.86 P99 TPOT (ms): 15.87 ----------------Inter‑Token Latency---------------- Mean ITL (ms): 14.20 Median ITL (ms): 12.72 P90 ITL (ms): 16.52 P95 ITL (ms): 17.51 P99 ITL (ms): 29.32 Max ITL (ms): 307.79 ================================================== ``` <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32458293504](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32458293504)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32458293339](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32458293339)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32458293538](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32458293538)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [diffusion] Guard unsupported quantized component checkpoints
signals.text: ## Summary - add one fail-closed admission boundary for native auxiliary component loaders that only materialize plain state dicts - reject detected top-level, nested text-config, and compressed-tensors quantization metadata before model construction or large weight reads - apply the boundary to connectors/duration heads, bridges, diffusion decoders, sound tokenizers, spatial upsamplers, and vocoders - keep the local PE model on its Transformers `from_pretrained` path, where compatible quantization formats remain model-specific - use one documentation contract across the overview, CLI, compatibility matrix, and quantization guide ## Motivation #35184 makes independent component repository routing generic and safely routes supported quantized VAEs. The remaining raw-state native loaders still had no common quantization admission rule, so a quantized component repo could be interpreted as a dense module or fail only after allocating/loading weights. Path routing and quantized materialization are separate capabilities. This PR does not add a generic per-component quantization knob: such a knob would overstate support until each loader has a matching backend. Existing transformer, native encoder, VAE, PE/Transformers, and upstream AutoModel quantization paths remain unchanged. ## Validation - all pre-commit hooks pass - focused unit coverage added for metadata layouts and early rejection order - runtime tests left to CI <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32545334559](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32545334559)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32545334428](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32545334428)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:heavy_minus_sign: **No AMD PR run found for this commit**.<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->
