signals.title: Fix replicated (TP1) shared expert being summed by collectives that skip the MoE all-reduce
signals.text: Prevents replicated TP1 shared-expert outputs from being over-counted when the default `moe_a2a_backend=none` path replaces or defers the MoE post-expert reduction. ## Motivation `moe_a2a_backend` selects the MoE communication implementation; it does not enable or disable expert parallelism. `none` is the default non-A2A path, while `ep_size` controls EP separately. On the affected path, CP or DP may replace the MoE-internal all-reduce with a downstream SUM. Routed-expert outputs are per-rank partials and must be summed, but a TP1 shared-expert output is already complete and replicated on every rank. Before this fix, each rank passed `R_r + S` into the downstream SUM: `Σ(R_r + S) = ΣR_r + group_size × S` The correct result is: `ΣR_r + S` The reproduced DeepSeek-V4 configurations were: - `TP8 + CP8 + EP1`, `moe_a2a_backend=none` - `TP8 + DP8 + EP1`, `moe_a2a_backend=none` - `TP8 + CP8 + EP8`, `moe_a2a_backend=none` In the EP1 arms, EP is disabled and the routed MoE is tensor-parallel across eight ranks. In the EP8 arm, the routed MoE uses `moe_ep_size=8` and `moe_tp_size=1`. `CP8` and `DP8` describe the attention parallelism over the same eight-rank group. The invariant is not specific to EP1. A matched EP8 run reproduced the same failure: before the fix, only `31/44` common self-stable lengths matched the non-CP reference with mean `|Δlogprob|=1.964223`; after the fix, all `53/53` matched with mean `|Δlogprob|=0.004218`. The fix does not depend on `ep_size`. Mori does not take the affected CP gather/reduce-scatter path. It uses `forward_deepep`, whose combine returns complete per-token outputs, and adds the replicated shared expert once after combine. Therefore Mori does not exhibit this specific double-count. ## Changes - Hoist the replicated shared expert out of DeepSeek-V4 CP and DP SUM collectives, including eager and TBO paths. - Add it once after the final reduce-scatter. - Apply the same CP and DP handling to the DeepSeek-V2 family and the Laguna DP reduce-scatter path. - Disable deferred MLP all-reduce fusion when the shared expert is replicated. - Add equal-chunk, variable reduce-scatter, empty-rank, and model wiring regression coverage. ## Validation MI355X token-exact checks against matched references: - DeepSeek-V4, `TP8 + CP8 + EP1`, `a2a=none`: `7/53`, mean `|Δlogprob|=2.834` before; `50/53`, `0.086` after. - DeepSeek-V4, `TP8 + DP8 + EP1`, `a2a=none`: `5/53`, `2.864` before; `45/53`, `0.068` after. - DeepSeek-V4, `TP8 + CP8 + EP8`, `a2a=none`: `31/44`, `1.964223` before on common self-stable lengths; `53/53`, `0.004218` after. - GLM-5.1, `TP8 + EP1`, `a2a=none`, deferred all-reduce: `0/53`, `2.591` before; `49/53`, `0.060` after. - `pre-commit` passes and the focused regression suite reports `12 passed`. No routed-expert kernel or A2A dispatcher is changed. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32468761511](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32468761511)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32468761047](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32468761047)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32468761137](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32468761137)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: Fix: omit null id/name in streaming tool call deltas
signals.text: ## Problem Streaming `tool_calls` continuation chunks currently emit explicit nulls: ```json // first chunk — OK {"tool_calls":[{"id":"call_abc","index":0,"type":"function","function":{"name":"get_weather","arguments":""}}]} // continuation chunks — id/name serialized as null {"tool_calls":[{"id":null,"index":0,"type":"function","function":{"name":null,"arguments":"{"city":"}}]} ``` `ToolCall`/`FunctionResponse` are built with `id=None`/`name=None` for argument-delta chunks (see `_process_tool_call_stream` and `_check_for_unstreamed_tool_args` in `serving_chat.py`), and `model_dump_json()` serializes `None` as JSON `null`. ## Why this is wrong The de-facto OpenAI streaming contract is that `id`/`function.name`/`type` appear **only in the first delta** of a tool call; continuation chunks carry just `index` and `function.arguments`: - OpenAI's own wire format omits these fields in continuation chunks (developers observe the fields are absent, not null: https://community.openai.com/t/streaming-with-tools-missing-tool-id-name/997791). The `null` values shown in parts of the docs are SDK object reprs, not wire JSON. - vLLM, the other major OpenAI-compatible server, omits unset delta fields via `model_dump_json(exclude_unset=True)` (https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/serving.py). - The OpenAI streaming reference marks `id`/`function.name` as optional (https://developers.openai.com/api/reference/resources/chat/subresources/completions/streaming-events), and the established convention is omission. ## Why it breaks clients Delta mergers that treat `null` as an explicit value (e.g. `x !== undefined`, the common OpenAI-SDK-style merge) overwrite the `id`/`function.name` streamed in the first chunk with `null`. The accumulated tool call then has an empty name, failing with errors like `unknown tool ""`. This was observed in production against a DeepSeek-V4 sglang deployment (`tool_call_parser=deepseekv4`), but the bug is in the generic OpenAI adapter and affects every `--tool-call-parser`. The same failure mode was reported against vLLM backends emitting nulls (https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/26412). Similar behavior is observed in https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/master/packages/llm/llm-deepseek/src/translate.ts#L160 ## Fix Add `model_serializer(mode="wrap")` to `ToolCall` and `FunctionResponse` that drops `None` `id`/`name`/`arguments` from the serialized output. This matches the existing `DeltaMessage` serializer pattern in the same file. Non-streaming responses are unaffected: `id`/`name`/`arguments` are always present there. ## Clarification Fix implemented by codex and reviewed by human ## Tests Added unit tests in `test/registered/unit/entrypoints/openai/test_protocol.py`: - continuation chunk: `id`/`name` omitted, `index`/`arguments` preserved - first chunk: `id`/`name`/`arguments` kept <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32457812428](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32457812428)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32457812350](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32457812350)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32457812421](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32457812421)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: feat: add Mooncake GPU-direct SpecForge capture
signals.text: ## Summary - capture auxiliary and final hidden states on GPU for per-request SpecForge requests - publish source buffers through Mooncake nvlink, nvlink_intra, or rdma transports - keep hidden-state payloads off host memory and return only GPU buffer descriptors - retain source buffers until consumer release acknowledgement, with pending-batch and resident-byte bounds - force MNNVL for NVL72, intra-node NVLink for H200-class nodes, and HCA for RDMA ## Hardware benchmark Run on 2026-08-21 UTC. The target host had 8x NVIDIA H200 (driver 580.105.08) split into two TP4 replicas. A second H200 host ran the consumer on one GPU. The target was Qwen3.8-27B-FP8 with DSpark taps `[5, 19, 33, 47, 61]`; capture used Mooncake RDMA and a 32 GiB resident cap per replica. The repository base does not expose the GPU-direct capture endpoint, so the same protocol cannot run there. The controlled comparison uses the first functional implementation (`dbfed03cd8d8`) as the baseline and PR head (`60e519391d59`) as the post-change target. SpecForge was fixed at `9ce0b698c98c`. Each reported value is the median of two completed 512-sample runs with `max_length=8192`, concurrency 64, lease 8, prompt prefetch 4, ingest batch 128, least-tokens replica routing, length-bucketed requests, and overlapped capture/materialization. | Metric | Baseline | PR head | Change | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | Capture throughput (samples/s) | 52.1199 | 67.2924 | +29.11% | | Active RDMA materialization (samples/s) | 108.8696 | 120.6860 | +10.85% | | Pipeline throughput (samples/s) | 48.6419 | 61.9381 | +27.33% | | Pipeline elapsed (s) | 10.5319 | 8.2663 | -21.51% | | Durable cleanup (s) | 0.9571 | 0.0056 | -99.41% | Every completed run produced and removed all 512 samples, transferred 40,503,867,376 bytes, and reported zero host payload bytes. After each PR-head run, both control endpoints reported `resident_samples=0`, `resident_bytes=0`, `reserved_bytes=0`, `published_samples == released_samples`, and the full 32 GiB arena free. The 1024-sample stress case was excluded from throughput statistics: this benchmark retains every sample until its final durable acknowledgement, so two 32 GiB replicas cannot hold the full retained set. Both baseline and head reached the configured per-replica resident cap and returned `GPU-direct capture residency ... exceeds 34359738368 bytes`. signals.title: [model-gateway] Add opt-in `fips` feature using the AWS-LC FIPS module
signals.text: ## Motivation Some deployments (government and other regulated environments) require all cryptography to come from a FIPS 140-3 validated module. This PR adds an opt-in `fips` cargo feature to sgl-model-gateway so those users can build a compliant gateway. Default builds are not affected. ## Modifications Behind the new `fips` feature (off by default): - rustls uses the AWS-LC FIPS provider instead of ring for all TLS (HTTPS server and the reqwest/kube outbound clients; tonic is built without TLS features and does no TLS itself). - JWT verification uses the jsonwebtoken AWS-LC backend. - The wasm module SHA-256 hash uses AWS-LC. - `aws-lc-fips-sys` uses a normal caret requirement (`0.14`) so builds pick up the latest AWS-LC FIPS release (currently 0.14.1, bundling AWS-LC FIPS 4.1.0). AWS-LC FIPS is a CMVP-validated module lineage (see [certificate #5314](https://csrc.nist.gov/projects/cryptographic-module-validation-program/certificate/5314) for the 3.x static module). The exact module version in any given build can be read from the binary with `strings <binary> | grep "AWS-LC FIPS"`. Deployments that need a version literally listed on an issued certificate can pin, for example `=0.13.11` (AWS-LC FIPS 3.1.0, the exact version on #5314). - At startup the gateway asserts the installed rustls provider is FIPS and that the AWS-LC JWT provider was installed. If not, it fails to start. - The Python and Go bindings expose the same `fips` feature. Changes that apply to all builds: - New `src/crypto.rs` with `ensure_crypto_provider_installed()`, which replaces the two previous ad-hoc `ring::default_provider().install_default()` call sites, and a `Sha256Hasher` wrapper used for wasm module hashing. Default builds keep ring and RustCrypto sha2. - `jsonwebtoken` upgraded 9.3 to 10.4 and `smg-auth` 1.0.0 to 1.2.2. jsonwebtoken 9 was hardwired to ring; version 10 has pluggable backends. Default builds use its `rust_crypto` backend. Not changed: blake3/xxhash (used for cache-aware routing and consistent hashing, not security relevant) and the openssl dependency (test cert generation and the optional `vendored-openssl` feature only). Build note: `--features fips` (and therefore `--all-features`, used by `make lint` and the rust CI lint job) needs cmake and Go to compile AWS-LC. The CI lint job passes since GitHub runners include both. <details> <summary>FIPS verification evidence</summary> - The fips binary embeds the AWS-LC FIPS module version string (checked with `strings`, currently `AWS-LC FIPS 4.1.0`); the default binary does not. - The fips binary starts cleanly and serves `/liveness` and `/health`. - TLS handshake against the fips build negotiates TLS 1.3 `TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384`. Forcing `TLS_CHACHA20_POLY1305_SHA256` (not FIPS approved) fails against the fips build and succeeds against the default build, showing the provider swap is active. - Known residual: ring and the jsonwebtoken RustCrypto backend remain linked (cargo features are additive) but are never selected at runtime, which the startup assertions enforce. smg-auth internally uses RustCrypto sha2 for API key fingerprinting; that code only runs when control plane API keys are configured. </details> ## Accuracy Tests N/A, no model or inference code touched. ## Speed Tests and Profiling N/A, default builds keep the same crypto stack. The fips path only affects opt-in builds. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). (`cargo test --test security_tests` passes 48/48 with and without `--features fips`, covering JWT auth, API keys, and mTLS. `cargo clippy --all-targets` is clean in both modes.) - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). (N/A, no model or inference code touched.) - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process). 2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers. 3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so. - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci` 4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32446211701](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32446211701)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32446211379](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32446211379)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:heavy_minus_sign: **No AMD PR run found for this commit**.<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: Support NemotronH_Omni_Reasoning_V3 in SGLang
signals.text: ## Motivation The new Nemotron checkpoint uses the `NemotronH_Omni_Reasoning_V3` architecture, which SGLang does not currently recognize. It falls back to the generic Transformers implementation, and the embedded MTP and quantized vision weights do not load correctly. ## Modifications - Register `NemotronH_Omni_Reasoning_V3` as a multimodal model using the existing Nano Nemotron VL implementation. - Reuse the existing Nemotron-H runtime and Mamba configuration. - Unwrap the language model config for embedded MTP and handle the checkpoint's `language_model.` weight prefix. - Load and apply the vision projector's final LayerNorm. - Support the alternate RADIO weight layout used by the quantized checkpoints, including split Q/K/V weights. - Add tests Most of this reuses the existing Nemotron-H and Nano Nemotron VL paths. ## Accuracy Tests ## Speed Tests and Profiling This PR is mainly adding model support. Runtime tests included CUDA graphs and speculative decoding to make sure those paths work. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). signals.title: [AMD] Enable moe_a2a_backend=mori for DeepSeek-V4 prefill context parallelism
signals.text: Enables DeepSeek-V4 prefill context parallelism to use Mori for MoE all-to-all. ## Motivation DeepSeek-V4 prefill context parallelism rejected `moe_a2a_backend=mori`, although Mori already uses the same rank-local EP dispatch/combine path as DeepEP. ## Changes - Add `mori` to the DeepSeek-V4 CP validation whitelist. - Add `is_mori()` to the matching model-side backend gate. No dispatcher, collective, or compute kernel is changed. ## Why this is safe DeepSeek-V4 CP fixes `DP=1` and `CP=TP`; Mori resolution also fixes `EP=TP`. Each rank sends its local CP token shard through `forward_deepep`, and Mori combine returns complete outputs in source-rank order. The Mori path does not run the CP gather/reduce-scatter used by `a2a=none`, so its replicated shared expert is added once and is not affected by [#35535](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/35535). Short batches that cannot be CP-split fall back to replicated prefill, so Mori capacity must still cover `chunked_prefill_size`. ## Validation On 8×MI355X with DeepSeek-V4-Pro-DSpark, TP8/CP8, compared with matched non-CP Mori runs: - Short sweep: `40/40` stable first-token matches, mean top-1 logprob delta `-0.015`. - 4K–16K sweep: `14/14` deterministic lengths matched; one length was self-unstable and one hit the existing CP-v1 GPU fault. - `pre-commit`, syntax checks, and a Mori CP validation smoke test pass. CP+Mori TBO remains disabled. Generic Mori dynamic-capacity limits and the existing CP-v1 one-token-per-rank GPU fault are outside this PR. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32460650488](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32460650488)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32460650102](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32460650102)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32460650220](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32460650220)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [NPU] Adapt DFlash2 speculative decoding to Ascend NPUs
signals.text: ## Motivation DFlash2 (#35371) landed on main as the successor to DFlash: a block-diffusion drafter with local grouped convolutions and a candidate selector, currently CUDA-only. First-generation DFlash drafts already run on Ascend NPUs (#23122, #31739), but the DFlash2 checkpoints cannot serve on NPU yet, and I found no existing issue/PR tracking this. This PR adapts the DFlash2 verify path so it can serve on Ascend NPUs (and any Triton-free environment), while keeping the CUDA path byte-for-byte identical. ## Changes - **Triton import guards** (`triton_compat.py`, new): kernel modules in `kernels/ops/speculative/` imported triton unconditionally, which broke module import on Triton-free Ascend images. The new compat shim degrades `@triton.jit` to a stub that raises only on *launch*, so non-CUDA devices can import the DFlash/DSpark modules and dispatch to torch fallbacks. This is generic: any environment without triton benefits, CUDA is untouched. - **Torch chain speculative-sampling fallback** (`chain_speculative_sampling_torch` in `reject_sampling.py`): buffer-for- buffer mirror of `speculative_sampling_classic_kernel` (same `coin * q < p` accept rule, same residual `max(p - q, 0)` final sampling, NaN draft entries treated as 0, same `predicts`/`accept_index`/`accept_token_num` layouts). Used by DSpark on NPU and covered by unit tests on CPU. - **Device dispatch** (`dspark_accept.py`): `_accept_sampling_core` now routes through `inputs_on_cuda(candidates)` — triton kernel on CUDA (unchanged), torch fallback elsewhere (NPU/CPU). Also routed the `@triton.jit` helper kernels in this module through the compat shim. - **NPU verify fix** (`dflash_worker_v2.py`): `skip_attn_backend_init` is now `None if _is_npu else True`. The CUDA `prepare_for_verify` pre-plans (load_batch / init_forward_metadata); the NPU branch deliberately leaves planning to the forward path, so marking metadata ready here crashed the NPU graph runner (`raw_num_token` never initialized). - **NPU greedy verify alignment** (`dflash_worker_v2.py`): on NPU, skip the selector full-vocab sampling verify (`_selector_sampling_accept` and the chain-sampling branch) and take the argmax greedy verify instead, matching what EAGLE/first-gen DFLASH already do unconditionally on NPU. The full-vocab path scatters a dense [bs, gamma, vocab] buffer whose cost does not shrink with the verify window; on the 200K-vocab Qwen3.8 it dominates the step. CUDA behavior unchanged. - **Docs**: Qwen3.8-27B cookbook — DFlash2 drafter recipe and NPU support status. ## Tests - New unit tests (`test/registered/unit/spec/test_chain_speculative_sampling.py`, registered in `base-a-test-cpu`): analytic accept/reject/bonus cases, NaN handling, batch independence, statistical losslessness (20k samples, TV < 0.02), triton-compat helpers, and a CUDA parity check that runs the torch and triton kernels on identical buffers (`@skipIf` no CUDA). - Verified end-to-end on Ascend 910C (target `Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B`, draft `z-lab/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2`, tp=2): server starts, DFlash2 selector draft loads, both NPU graph captures succeed (incl. the in-graph sampler RNG), and requests pass, before and after the greedy-verify change. ## Plan status - [x] P0: pure-torch chain speculative-sampling verify + device dispatch + CPU unit tests against the Triton reference - [x] P0.5: guard the triton imports so Triton-free environments import the DFlash modules - [x] P1: validate NPU (aclgraph) capture of the DFlash2 selector draft sampler (done on 910C; `SGLANG_DFLASH_EAGER_DRAFT_SAMPLER=1` remains the escape hatch) - [x] P1: e2e greedy + sampling correctness on Ascend (server starts, requests pass) - [x] P2: performance investigation — moved to a follow-up PR. Profiling (temporary phase-timing instrumentation + torch-profiler traces, run locally and not part of this PR)showed the original suspects (vocab-wide `torch.topk` in the selector, dense chain sampling) are not the bottleneck: the selector top-k costs ~0.04 ms/step and DFLASH matches NEXTN kernel-for-kernel. The decode step is bounded by a shared TP2 per-layer allreduce floor (~43 collectives/step) of the target model verify. Optimization directions (accept-length tuning, verify-prep host-path reduction) will be pursued separately. ## Accuracy Tests Settings follow #23122/#16818 except hardware and models. - hardware: Ascend 910C (tp=2) - target_model: `Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B` (bf16 weights, `--mamba-ssm-dtype bfloat16 --mamba-scheduler-strategy extra_buffer`) - draft_model: `Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2` (`--speculative-num-draft-tokens 8`) - dataset: `gsm8k`, zero-shot, greedy (`temperature=0.0, top_p=1.0, top_k=1`) - max_new_tokens: `2048`; 128 samples per concurrency level - attention_backend: `ascend` ### Baseline accuracy | Concurrency | 1 | 2 | 4 | 8 | 16 | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Accuracy | 0.820 | 0.836 | 0.836 | 0.828 | 0.820 | ### DFLASH accuracy | Concurrency | 1 | 2 | 4 | 8 | 16 | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Accuracy | 0.820 | 0.836 | 0.836 | 0.820 | 0.836 | ### DFLASH acceptance length (block size 8; scheduler log accept len, ### windowed mean per decode-log interval) | Concurrency | 1 | 2 | 4 | 8 | 16 | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Accept len | 5.8 | 5.8 | 5.8 | 5.8 | 5.8 | Accept length is stable across concurrency levels (observed window means 4.85-6.20, batch sizes 1-17); log-reported accept rate ≈ 0.68. ## Benchmarking ### Baseline output tok/s | Concurrency | 1 | 2 | 4 | 8 | 16 | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | tok/s | 32.7 | 60.1 | 109.4 | 177.4 | 259.3 | ### DFLASH output tok/s | Concurrency | 1 | 2 | 4 | 8 | 16 | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | tok/s | 103.6 | 160.3 | 236.5 | 345.2 | 542.2 | ### Speedup (DFLASH / baseline) | Concurrency | 1 | 2 | 4 | 8 | 16 | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Speedup | 3.16 | 2.67 | 2.16 | 1.95 | 2.09 | <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32465960380](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32465960380)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32465960247](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32465960247)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32465960249](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32465960249)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [Feature] Add DeepEPv2 (ElasticBuffer) MoE A2A backend
signals.text: > Reland of #29525, which was reverted in #35568. > > The revert was caused by one line in the new e2e test: it registered itself to > `runner_config="deepep-8-gpu-h200"`, a runner config that does not exist. > `run_suite.py` validates every registered test's suite before collecting any > of them, so that single bad name aborted unrelated lanes as well -- the ARM CPU > and NPU suites both failed with `Tests registered to invalid suites`. It is > fixed here in a separate commit on top of a clean revert-of-the-revert, so the > restored change can be diffed against the original merge. Running the tests as > single files never goes through `run_suite.py`, which is why local runs stayed > green; `python3 test/run_suite.py --hw cpu --suite base-b-test-cpu-arm64` > reproduces it in one command and now passes. ## Motivation DeepEP v2's `ElasticBuffer` is an NCCL-symmetric-memory all-to-all engine with a fixed per-rank capacity. Fixed capacity means static communication shapes, which makes the MoE decode path CUDA-graph capturable under any topology — including multi-node, where legacy `low_latency` is not available as a graphable path. This PR adds it as a standalone backend `deepep_v2` alongside `deepep`; only expert-parallel dispatch/combine is replaced. Validated on Hopper (H20, H200) and Blackwell (B200 `sm_100`, B300 `sm_103`). ## Modifications - **`layers/moe/token_dispatcher/deepep_v2.py`** (new): the dispatcher. `--deepep-v2-mode direct|hybrid` selects the ElasticBuffer topology — **not** the legacy `normal/low_latency` split. Layout is chosen per batch by inference phase, not by comm mode: decode uses the expanded layout + masked GEMM (static shapes, graph-capturable, available under `hybrid` too), extend/prefill uses the contiguous layout. Single-shot `dispatch()/combine()` with a strict handle lifecycle; the guards run before the DeepEP import check so the module imports cleanly without DeepEP installed. - **`kernels/ops/moe/ep_moe_kernels.py`**: masked-slab repack kernels. A fixed per-expert worker pool keeps the grid static (graph-safe); top-k weights are folded in-kernel; the scale copy takes the source pack-dim stride, which is what makes Blackwell's packed-UE8M0 (column-major) layout correct alongside Hopper's row-major fp32. - **`layers/moe/moe_runner/deep_gemm.py`**: the FP8 adapter (masked decode / contiguous prefill, consuming DeepEP's 128-aligned psum directly as group offsets). `deep_gemm` is the only supported runner: deepep_v2 dispatches FP8 activations plus scales, and no other a2a backend targets a different runner family either. `--moe-runner-backend` is checked at startup, but the runner is chosen per layer by the quant method and several hard-select Triton regardless, so `MoeRunner` rejects the mismatch too — otherwise such a model would reach the permute registry and die on a bare assert after the weights are loaded. - **`layers/moe/ep_moe/layer.py`**: `get_moe_impl_class` resolves `deepep_v2` to `DeepEPMoE` like every other a2a backend — this is what makes the UE8M0 load-time weight requant apply on Blackwell. - **`server_args.py`, `arg_groups/overrides.py`**: the new flags; `ep_size` and `disable_shared_experts_fusion` are declared through the a2a passes, and the runner is validated against `resolved_view(...)` so a model declaration that restores an unsupported runner fails fast. Boot-time capacity check for the chunked-prefill budget. TBO/SBO and enforced shared-expert fusion are rejected at startup. - **`state_capturer/routed_experts.py`**: classify deepep_v2 as a scattered-a2a backend; otherwise `dp_rank > 0` reads unwritten buffer rows under `--enable-return-routed-experts`. - **No CI/Docker changes**: `sgl-deep-ep==0.1.1` already provides `ElasticBuffer`, so CI can exercise this backend as-is; it stays inert for every other configuration, fails fast when DeepEP is missing, and its unit tests need only Triton. - **Tests**: `test_deepep_v2_masked_slab.py` covers the masked-slab repack round-trip -- bf16/fp8, empty experts, the `max_m` boundary, overflow fail-fast, a production packed-UE8M0 scale, and CUDA-graph capture/replay -- and needs only Triton. `test_routed_experts_scattered_a2a.py` pins the capturer's backend classification. `test_routed_experts_dp_readback.py` is the only multi-GPU one: it runs DP>1 with dummy weights over a single 24-expert layer, because `dp_rank 0` sits at buffer offset 0 and looks correct even when the classification is wrong, so nothing below DP>1 can catch that regression; it also covers legacy `deepep` on the same path. Happy to drop or move any of these if they are not worth the coverage. ## Usage DeepEP v2 needs NCCL symmetric memory, which SGLang turns off by default (`NCCL_CUMEM_ENABLE` is set to `int(enable_symm_mem)` when the variable is unset), so an otherwise correct launch fails with `nccl.cu:104: Communicator does not support symmetric memory!`. Pass `NCCL_CUMEM_ENABLE=1` (used for every benchmark here) or `--enable-symm-mem`, which also works but additionally enables NVLS and a 4 GB symmetric-memory prealloc. `SGLANG_DEEPEP_V2_NUM_MAX_DISPATCH_TOKENS_PER_RANK` is the fixed per-rank buffer capacity. It must cover the per-rank chunk (`--chunked-prefill-size / dp_size` under DP attention), and that chunk must be a multiple of `page_size` — with `page_size=256, dp_size=8` the smallest usable pair is capacity 256 with `--chunked-prefill-size 2048`. Smaller capacity is better for decode; prefill servers size it to their chunk budget and add `--disable-cuda-graph`. No extra install step: the pinned `sgl-deep-ep==0.1.1` ships `ElasticBuffer` (`deep_ep 2.1.0`), so this backend runs on a stock environment. Re-validated on H20 x8 against that wheel with no source build and no code change -- `direct` GSM8K 0.970 / MMLU 0.890, `hybrid` 0.970 / 0.886, three-question gate passing in both modes. Earlier development used a DeepEP source build at `d4f41e4`; the packaged API is a superset of what the dispatcher calls. Multi-node: add `--deepep-v2-mode hybrid --enable-dp-lm-head --nnodes 2 --node-rank {0,1}`. Blackwell with a BF16 `wo_a` checkpoint: `SGLANG_OPT_FP8_WO_A_GEMM=0`. ## Accuracy Tests DeepSeek-V4-Flash-FP8, `--tp 8 --dp 8 --ep 8 --enable-dp-attention`, `deep_gemm`, kv fp8. | | deepep_v2 `direct` | deepep_v2 `hybrid` | deepep | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | H20 x8 — MMLU (500) | 0.888 | 0.890 | 0.888 | | H20 x8 — GSM8K (100) | 0.980 | 0.980 | 0.970 | | B200 x8 — MMLU (500) | 0.886 | 0.884 | — | | B200 x8 — GSM8K (100) | 0.950 | 0.970 | — | MMLU at 500 examples has a ~1.4pp standard error at this accuracy, which is wider than every gap in the table; repeat runs of one configuration spanned 0.884-0.896. These numbers show the absence of a systematic shift against the same-node `deepep` baseline, not a ranking. The three-question gate passes on every configuration above. Unit tests (CI, no DeepEP required): masked-slab repack including a production packed-UE8M0 scale and CUDA-graph capture/replay, handle-lifecycle guards, server-args resolution, capturer classification, plus a DP>1 routed-experts readback e2e. The three-question gate also passes on the multi-node configuration below. Earlier validation on the same dispatch path: needle retrieval across chunk boundaries and 8-way concurrent requests 24/24; prefill/decode disaggregation functional. ## Speed Tests | | deepep_v2 | deepep | delta | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | H20 x8 decode | 4,339 tok/s | 4,379 | -0.9% | | H20 x8 prefill | 22,353 in_tok/s | 21,651 | +3.2% | | B200 x8 decode | 8,429 tok/s | 8,675 | -2.8% | | B200 x8 prefill | 32,447 in_tok/s | 31,533 | +2.9% | Each backend pair was measured back-to-back on the same node, on torch 2.13 / sglang-kernel 0.4.6.post1, with the prefill cells interleaved so drift cannot bias one side. H20 prefill averages 4 samples per cell (sd 95 and 72), B200 prefill 2 per cell (sd 132 and 57); decode is one cell per side. Decode reproduces well across nodes -- deepep_v2 measured 8,385 / 8,403 / 8,429 tok/s on three different B200 nodes -- but the `deepep` side moved more, so the decode delta has landed between -0.9% and -2.8% across runs; read it as "a low single-digit percentage behind" rather than a precise figure. Prefill has been consistently ahead by roughly 3%. Multi-node (2x H20x8, TP16/EP16/DP16, `hybrid`, same protocol): **4,610 tok/s** decode with the masked-GEMM + CUDA-graph path over RDMA — a graphable cross-node decode path legacy `low_latency` does not provide — and **20,688 in_tok/s** prefill (two samples: 20,322 / 21,054). There is no same-fabric deepep baseline for this pair: DeepEP's NVSHMEM data plane does not complete across nodes on this RoCE setup, reproduced with DeepEP's own `test_internode.py` outside SGLang. Reproduction (5 rounds per boot, mean of the last 3; prefill flushes the radix cache before each round): ```bash # common: NCCL_CUMEM_ENABLE=1, SGLANG_DEEPEP_V2_NUM_SMS=20, capacity 1024 # deepep_v2: --moe-a2a-backend deepep_v2 --deepep-v2-mode direct # deepep : --moe-a2a-backend deepep --deepep-mode low_latency|normal --deepep-dispatcher-output-dtype fp8 # (with SGLANG_DEEPEP_NUM_MAX_DISPATCH_TOKENS_PER_RANK=1024) NCCL_CUMEM_ENABLE=1 SGLANG_DEEPEP_V2_NUM_SMS=20 \ SGLANG_DEEPEP_V2_NUM_MAX_DISPATCH_TOKENS_PER_RANK=1024 \ python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model-path $MODEL --trust-remote-code \ --tp-size 8 --dp-size 8 --ep-size 8 --enable-dp-attention --context-length 4096 \ --chunked-prefill-size 8192 --moe-runner-backend deep_gemm --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 \ --host 127.0.0.1 --port 30000 $BACKEND_FLAGS \ --mem-fraction-static 0.70 --cuda-graph-max-bs 128 # decode # --mem-fraction-static 0.80 --disable-cuda-graph --disable-piecewise-cuda-graph # prefill # decode python3 -m sglang.bench_serving --backend sglang --port 30000 --dataset-name random \ --num-prompts 128 --random-input-len 1 --random-output-len 1024 --random-range-ratio 1 --max-concurrency 128 # prefill (curl -s localhost:30000/flush_cache before each round) python3 -m sglang.bench_serving --backend sglang --port 30000 --dataset-name random \ --num-prompts 64 --random-input-len 1024 --random-output-len 1 --random-range-ratio 1 --max-concurrency 16 ``` ## Checklist - [x] Format code with pre-commit. - [x] Add unit tests. - [ ] Update documentation (separate follow-up PR). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmarks (above). - [x] Code style. ### Notes for reviewers - Prerequisites: none beyond the current pins -- `sgl-deep-ep==0.1.1` provides `ElasticBuffer`. NCCL symmetric memory must be on (see Usage). - Follow-ups: TBO/SBO comm-compute overlap (a PoC showed the naive two-phase split cannot overlap because `ElasticBuffer.dispatch` is host-blocking; it needs a `return_recv_hook`-style split in DeepEP), adapters for other MoE runners, documentation. signals.title: [mem_cache] docs: add a layer map and placement rules
signals.text: ## Motivation Part of #25371. `mem_cache/` has 40 top-level modules plus 10 subpackages and no index. Answering "is this class an allocator or a pool?" or "may `pool_host/` import `allocator/`?" currently means reading the RFC or grepping. ## Modifications Adds `python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/README.md`: - **Layers** -- the stack from `allocation.py` down through `allocator/`, `pool/`, `pool_host/`, `storage/`, with each layer's in/out contract. Names prefix-cache trees and the construction layer (`kv_cache_configurator.py`, `kv_cache_builder.py`, `cache_init_params.py`, `allocation_sizing.py`, `kv_cache_dtype.py`, `kv_vmm_backing.py`, `hybrid_cache/hybrid_pool_assembler.py`) as sitting outside that stack rather than in it. - **Where does my class go?** -- home by base class, not by name, plus the `Allocator`-means-two-things distinction (`BaseTokenToKVPoolAllocator` hands out KV slots and lives in `allocator/`; `HostTensorAllocator` hands out pinned host memory and does not). - **Conventions** -- the naming rule, family-as-package, and the dependency-direction invariants. Documentation only; no code changes. **Deliberately coarse.** An earlier draft carried a per-family x per-layer matrix naming the module that holds each class today. That inventory would need updating by every one of the ~20 remaining moves under #25371, and it already has a home that cannot rot: the shrink-only pins in the layout ratchet (#35638), which fail the build when a pinned class moves. Duplicating it here would just give the same fact a second home to drift from. The README documents the rules, which are stable; for "where does class X live today", `git grep` is the answer, and the README says so. ## Accuracy Test Not applicable -- documentation only. ## Benchmark and Profiling Results Not applicable -- documentation only. ## Checklist - signals.title: fix: detect cross-node multimodal transport by nnodes
signals.text: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation `determine_tensor_transport_mode()` currently treats a non-empty `dist_init_addr` as evidence that the deployment spans multiple nodes. However, `dist_init_addr` is a process-group rendezvous endpoint rather than a topology signal. Single-node multi-GPU TP deployments may also set it to bootstrap the TP process group. The inverse is also possible: in Ray multi-node TP/PP, the generated rendezvous address is injected into scheduler-actor copies of `ServerArgs`, while the `TokenizerManager` can retain the original `dist_init_addr=None`. External launchers using an `env://` rendezvous can produce the same state. Requiring both `nnodes > 1` and a non-empty address would therefore let the tokenizer select node-local CUDA IPC/SHM while schedulers select the default transport. The original false positive selects the `"default"` transport on a single node, causing `wrap_shm_features()` to become a no-op. Large multimodal pixel tensors are then pickled and broadcast through Gloo for every request. In an affected five-image document workload, this resulted in 2.2–6.5 GB transfers and 18–33 seconds spent in `recv_requests`. `nnodes` directly represents whether the deployment is multi-node and is therefore the appropriate source of truth. ## Modifications - Determine cross-node topology using `server_args.nnodes > 1`, independently of `server_args.dist_init_addr`. - Move `TensorTransportMode` and `determine_tensor_transport_mode()` into the existing `sglang.srt.multimodal.transport` package as the shared implementation. - Update the tokenizer manager, disaggregated encoder receiver, native Rust multimodal path, and `mm_utils` to use the shared helper. - Remove the duplicated implementations and the reverse lazy import from `mm_utils` to `tokenizer_manager`. - Add a truth-table regression test covering all four combinations of single-node/multi-node topology and present/absent rendezvous address. ## Accuracy Tests Not applicable. This change only affects multimodal tensor transport selection and does not modify model computation or outputs. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Before this fix, the affected five-image document workload observed 2.2–6.5 GB of pickled/Gloo-broadcast data and 18–33 seconds per `recv_requests` call. This change restores the existing shared-memory transport path for single-node multi-GPU TP deployments. No standalone post-change benchmark was run in the local development environment. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Documentation is not required because this is an internal transport-selection fix with no user-facing API change. - [x] This change has no model accuracy impact. - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. signals.title: [NPU] Support DSpark compact verify graph and folded verify epilogue
signals.text: ## Motivation DSpark on the Ascend DSV4 backend currently falls back to a uniform verify window or eager-side post-processing for parts of speculative decoding. This leaves two sources of avoidable overhead: 1. the target model verifies the full draft window even when the SPS policy selects a shorter per-request verify length; 2. accept/finalize and hidden/KV commit remain outside the target verify graph. This PR enables the compact DSpark path on NPU, adds token-tiered graph replay for ragged target verify, and folds the eligible verify epilogue into the graph. ## Modifications ### 1. DSpark compact verify on NPU - Build packed/ragged verify windows from per-request verify lengths selected by the DSpark planner. - Add NPU-safe compact row mapping, verify-ID gathering, cache-location handling, and compact-to-strided scatter. - Construct DSV4 SWA, sparse-attention, C4/C128 compressor, position, state, and page-table metadata from the live compact layout. - Preserve eager fallback when the selected attention backend does not support ragged verify graphs. ### 2. Compact target-verify graph - Advertise ragged verify graph support for the DSV4 Ascend backend. - Select target-verify graphs by compact token tier while retaining fixed graph-owned buffers. - Refresh query indptr, sequence lengths, cache/page tables, compressor locations/state, and sparse indices before replay. - Add an NPU-local bucketed-layout cache so the Ascend and DSV4 metadata consumers reuse the same derived layout. - Use the safe last-location Triton path for DSV4 NPU allocation metadata. ### 3. Verify epilogue graph - Add a DSV4 NPU-specific target-verify tail hook that uses the committed/live prefix lengths from DSV4 metadata. - Fold greedy accept/finalize and eligible hidden/KV commit into the compact target-verify graph. - Keep sampling, grammar-constrained decoding, logits adjustments, and other ineligible cases on the existing eager epilogue path. - Keep the adaptation NPU/DSV4-specific so the existing CUDA behavior remains unchanged. ## Accuracy Tests - GPQA-Diamond accuracy: **0.91** with DSpark on Ascend NPU. - The compact path preserves the target-model verification result; it changes the number of draft tokens verified and where graph-safe post-processing executes. ## Speed Tests and Profiling No standalone performance number is included in this PR. The expected gain comes from reducing target-verify tokens according to the SPS-selected compact lengths and removing eligible verify epilogue launches from the host path. ## Validation - Python syntax compilation passed for all Python files changed by this PR. - Added scheduler coverage for exact eager token counts when the backend does not support ragged verify graphs. ## Checklist - [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy). - [ ] Provide speed benchmark results according to [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32468745273](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32468745273)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32468745123](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32468745123)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32468745271](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32468745271)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [diffusion] docs+skill: which components to stream under layerwise offload
signals.text: Documents what belongs in `--layerwise-offload-components`, and corrects four things the first version of this PR got wrong about it. ## Motivation The docs never said what belongs in the component list, so it reads like a memory dial to turn all the way up. The rule is cost per pass, not component size: streaming pays one host-to-device transfer of a component's weights per pass over that component, overlapped with that pass's compute. Four things decide whether that is cheap, and the first version of this PR had three of them backwards: 1. **Count passes from the code.** A "one-shot" component need not be one pass. H3's `_decode_temporal_streaming` re-runs the whole video decoder per temporal chunk, so streaming its 36 blocks pays 36 transfers per chunk. 2. **There are three placements, not two.** A component can be declared streamed and still hold its blocks (`--layerwise-resident-layers video_vae=36`), which transfers them once instead of per pass and releases the VRAM when the component finishes. Telling the reader to drop a one-shot component from the list instead keeps it resident for the whole process, which is the VRAM a 12-24 GB budget does not have. 3. **Host memory is one budget.** Pinning a one-shot component competes with the page cache that a streamed component's mapped weights read through, so per-component placement is not independent. 4. **Bytes are not the cost.** A pinned source transfers asynchronously; an unpinned or mapped source is synchronous whatever the call requests, because the driver stages it through its own buffer. It also read 132 ms of a 1.04 s step as 0.5%. The measured fact is that the sweep is flat because prefetch hides the transfer, not because the bytes are negligible, so the guidance is now to measure rather than to divide bytes by bandwidth and stop there. ## Modifications Four subsections in Section 1 of `sglang-diffusion-performance`, the mirrored guidance in `deployment_cookbook.mdx`, and an RTX 4090 entry in the H3 deployment config. ## Accuracy Tests Documentation only. Residency and prefetch are lossless: a residency sweep on Wan2.1-1.3B produced one SHA-256 across every setting. ## Speed Tests and Profiling MiniMax-H3 fl2va, 1x RTX 4090, 864x480 / 124 frames / 20 NFE, bf16, seed 1101. Video VAE, 36 blocks, decode only: | placement | decode | |---|---| | streamed | 150 s | | streamed, blocks resident | **13 s** | DiT denoise, same bytes per step, only the host-side source differs: | DiT weight source | denoise | per step | configuration | |---|---|---|---| | pinned host memory | **122.84 s** | 6.10 s | host uncapped, 116.7 GB pinned | | checkpoint mapping | 330.74 s | 17.4 s | host 32 GiB, allocator 23 GiB | | checkpoint mapping | 318.94-356.37 s | 16.8-18.7 s | host 32 GiB, allocator 12 GiB | The last row is one configuration measured twice; the 12% spread tracked host load on a shared machine, so smaller differences than that are unresolved here. For scale on the same card and shape, ComfyUI runs these unpruned bf16 weights at 6.58-6.59 s/step. Its `--fast-disk` mode holds 57.5 GiB of anonymous host memory instead of 116.5 GiB at the same 6.57-6.60 s/step, so the pinned path is at parity and the mapped path is a host-side tax rather than a GPU result. Prefetch depth is left unquantified on purpose: it is not monotonic and the direction depends on model, resolution and card, so the docs say sweep it. Related: #35813 (the alias fix these numbers depend on), #35812 (auto streams the DiT instead of OOMing on a 12 GB card). ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Code Formatting with Pre-Commit](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-formatting-with-pre-commit). - [x] Update documentation as needed, including docstrings or example tutorials. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32477627164](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32477627164)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32477626744](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32477626744)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32477627225](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32477627225)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [Fix] Forward an explicit CXX to nvcc via -ccbin in JIT builds
signals.text: ## Problem The JIT build resolves the host compiler from `CXX` (`toolchain.host_compiler_path()`) and uses it for the `.cpp` translation units and the link step — but never tells nvcc. nvcc ignores `CXX` entirely: it takes `-ccbin` or falls back to `gcc` from `PATH`. So on a machine whose default gcc is newer than the CUDA toolkit's nvcc supports, every JIT kernel build fails: ``` host_config.h:132: #error -- unsupported GNU version! gcc versions later than 12 are not supported! ``` even when the user explicitly set `CXX=/usr/bin/g++-12` to fix exactly that. Repro on such a machine (CUDA 12.x nvcc + default gcc 13): ```python import os os.environ["CXX"] = "/usr/bin/g++-12" from sglang.kernels.jit.utils.compile import toolchain print(toolchain.host_compiler_path()) # /usr/bin/g++-12 (.cpp units + link) print(toolchain.base_cuda_flags()) # ['-Xcompiler', '-fPIC'] <- no -ccbin ``` The generated `build.ninja` compiles `.cpp` with `$cxx` (g++-12) while the `compile_cuda` rule lets nvcc pick `gcc` (13) for all host code inside `.cu` units. ## Fix `base_cuda_flags()` appends `-ccbin $CXX` when `CXX` is set explicitly (resolved through the `@cache_once`-cached `explicit_host_compiler()`, so both call sites see one value). When `CXX` is unset the flags are unchanged — nvcc's own default (`gcc` from PATH) is preserved, since forwarding the `"c++"` fallback would silently change the default host compiler. The HIP branch is untouched (hipcc takes no `-ccbin`). The build key follows automatically: it is taken over the generated `build.ninja` text (which now embeds the flag) and `_environment_fingerprint` already fingerprints `host_compiler_path()`, so a changed `CXX` re-keys the build instead of reusing stale binaries. Verified end to end on an RTX 3080 / CUDA 12.0 / default gcc 13 machine: with the JIT cache cleared, `CXX=/usr/bin/gcc-12 python3 -m sglang.launch_server ...` now compiles all JIT kernels and serves traffic. Before the fix the same command failed every `.cu` build with the error above, and the only workaround was to also set `NVCC_CCBIN` — a variable this code path never reads. signals.title: [AMD][CI] Name the ROCm Image That Actually Ran in AMD Job Names
signals.text: Follow-up to #35602 and #35603. ## Summary This PR changes the job names shown in GitHub Actions for five AMD test workflows and updates the AMD CI monitor to follow those names. GPU tests now use: ```text <test> (<selected ROCm version>, <runner>[, <part>]) ``` Within these five test workflows, jobs that only wait, start another workflow, or collect results use neutral names. The ROCm 7.0 workflows stay separate from the workflows that handle ROCm 7.2.0/7.2.4. ## Before / After — directly changed workflows The examples below show the rule applied to every GPU job in each workflow. | Workflow | Before | After | | --- | --- | --- | | `PR Test ROCm 7.0 (AMD)` — 16 direct GPU job definitions | `stage-c-test-large-8-gpu-amd (linux-mi300-8gpu-sglang, 3)` | `stage-c-test-large-8-gpu-amd (rocm700, linux-mi300-8gpu-sglang, 3)` | | `PR Test ROCm 7.2 (AMD)` — 18 direct GPU job definitions | `stage-c-test-large-8-gpu-amd-rocm720 (...)`, even when the workflow used ROCm 7.2.4 | `stage-c-test-large-8-gpu-amd (rocm724, ...)` by default, or `(rocm720, ...)` when 7.2.0 is selected | | `PR Test Extra (AMD)` — 3 GPU job definitions | Default ROCm 7.2.4 was hidden: `extra-a-test-1-gpu-small-amd (...)`; other versions were put in the test name: `...-rocm700 (...)` | `extra-a-test-1-gpu-small-amd (rocm724, ...)`, `(rocm720, ...)`, or `(rocm700, ...)` | | `Nightly Test (AMD ROCm 7.0)` — 43 GPU jobs | `nightly-test-1-gpu-unit` | `nightly-test-1-gpu-unit (rocm700, linux-mi300-1gpu-sglang)` | | `Nightly Test (AMD ROCm 7.2)` — 47 GPU job definitions; a full nightly using both versions creates 94 jobs | `nightly-test-1-gpu-unit-rocm720 (rocm724)` or `(rocm720)` | `nightly-test-1-gpu-unit (rocm724, linux-mi300-1gpu-sglang)` or `(rocm720, linux-mi300-1gpu-sglang)` | | ROCm 7.2 PR helper jobs | `call-pr-test-amd-extra-rocm720`, `wait-for-stage-a-amd-rocm720`, `wait-for-stage-b-amd-rocm720`, `pr-test-amd-rocm720-finish` | `call-pr-test-amd-extra`, `wait-for-stage-a-amd`, `wait-for-stage-b-amd`, `pr-test-amd-finish` | | `AMD CI Job Monitor` | Looked for the old names, mixed ROCm 7.2.0 and 7.2.4 nightly results, and created empty reports for wait jobs | Looks for the new names, reports each nightly ROCm version and runner separately, skips wait jobs, and stops with an error if name parsing fails | The ROCm 7.2 nightly setup step also changes from the fixed `Setup docker (ROCm 7.2)` to `Setup docker (rocm724)` or `Setup docker (rocm720)`. The ROCm 7.0 and 7.2 PR workflows now share the same neutral wait/caller/finish labels; the workflow title still tells the two runs apart. ## Before / After — workflows that call these workflows These three files are not edited, but their child jobs inherit the new names: | Caller workflow | Before | After | | --- | --- | --- | | `AMD AITER Scout` — all four AMD PR/nightly paths | `call-nightly-amd-rocm720 / nightly-test-1-gpu-unit-rocm720 (rocm724)` | `call-nightly-amd-rocm720 / nightly-test-1-gpu-unit (rocm724, linux-mi300-1gpu-sglang)` | | `Release Branch Cut` — AMD PR and nightly paths | `run-pr-tests-amd / stage-a-test-1-gpu-small-amd-rocm720 (...)` | `run-pr-tests-amd / stage-a-test-1-gpu-small-amd (rocm724, ...)` | | `Bot Bump SGLang Version` — AMD nightly path | `run-nightly-tests-amd / nightly-test-1-gpu-unit-rocm720 (rocm724)` | `run-nightly-tests-amd / nightly-test-1-gpu-unit (rocm724, linux-mi300-1gpu-sglang)` | The AITER Scout outer prefixes `call-pr-test-amd-rocm720 /` and `call-nightly-amd-rocm720 /` are unchanged; only their child names become accurate. ## Unchanged AMD workflows These AMD workflow files keep the same job names and behavior: - `nightly-amd-mi355x-disagg.yml` - `nightly-test-amd-miles-rocm720.yml` - `release-docker-amd-miles-rocm700-nightly.yml` - `release-docker-amd-miles-rocm720-nightly.yml` - `release-docker-amd-nightly.yml` - `release-docker-amd-rocm720-nightly.yml` - `release-docker-amd-rocm7_15-nightly.yml` - `release-docker-amd.yml` PR States is also unchanged. ## What happens after merge - AMD GPU test execution is unchanged: the same tests run on the same machines, with the same images, commands, triggers, and schedules. The visible names and monitor grouping change. - Behind-the-scenes job IDs stay the same, so job dependencies and manual job selection keep working. - The merge checks named `lint` and `pr-test-finish` keep the same names. - GitHub starts new history under the new names. Any outside script or dashboard that searches for an old full name must be updated. - The AMD CI monitor's ROCm 7.2 Extra row may be blank until the first scheduled/full Extra run after merge, because older runs have the old caller name. - The name uses the selected `rocm_version`; it does not try to infer ROCm from a custom `AMD_CI_IMAGE` tag. - A job skipped very early may show the name formula instead of the finished name. signals.title: [Unified Cache][Draft POC]: Add optional external-cache linker mode to Unified Radix Cache
signals.text: ## Motivation Unified Radix Cache manages heterogeneous model states, including full-attention KV, SWA KV, and model-specific sidecars. On GB platforms, **deployments may need to aggregate larger memory regions into a shared Global Memory pool**. This requires an efficient way for Unified Radix Cache to access remote memory directly without overhead on the inference critical path. This PR adds an optional external-cache linker mode. It allows the tree to access a Global Memory pool through backends such as Mooncake or UMBP .. while retaining ownership of allocation, insertion, component consistency, and cache-node lifetime. The existing hierarchical cache path remains unchanged. The linker is an opt-in alternative for deployments that need a larger shared memory pool while preserving inference performance. ## Modifications This PR is currently at the proof-of-concept stage and will be split into several smaller, focused PRs: - [ ] Introduce the external linker interface and common linker wrapper - [ ] Integrate external linker support into `UnifiedRadixCache` - [ ] Add direct linker implementations for Mooncake、UMBP - [ ] Expand correctness, compatibility, and performance testing - [ ] Support prefetch - [ ] Support other implementations ## Speed Tests and Profiling The optional Mooncake linker was benchmarked against the existing L3 Mooncake path on 8 * H200 GPUs. Lower TTFT is better. A positive percentage means that the linker is faster. signals.title: fix(anthropic): preserve deferred ToolSearch on generic templates
signals.text: ## Motivation Fixes #35692. The Anthropic endpoint receives `tool_reference` blocks from Claude Code ToolSearch results. SGLang previously forwarded those blocks as structured message content unconditionally. Templates without native deferred-tool support, including the stock Qwen3.8-27B template, reject that content type and return HTTP 500. Because the reference remains in conversation history, every later request in the session also fails. A text-only fallback prevents the crash but loses ToolSearch semantics if all deferred schemas remain visible from the first turn. This revision preserves discovery gating for templates that cannot expand references themselves. ## Behavior - Templates with native deferred loading, such as GLM, still receive the complete tool catalog and structured `tool_reference` parts. Their template performs filtering and inline schema expansion. - Generic templates receive only non-deferred tools initially. - When conversation history contains a `tool_reference`, the matching deferred tool is added to the current request's normal tool list and the history block is rendered as a text marker. - Unreferenced deferred tools remain hidden, and a forced deferred `tool_choice` is rejected until that tool has been discovered. Generic templates cannot preserve Anthropic's exact inline-placement and prompt-cache behavior, but they now preserve the functional contract: a deferred tool becomes callable only after ToolSearch discovers it. ## Implementation - Extract deterministic capability detection and routing into `anthropic/tool_reference.py`. - Parse the Jinja AST and require executable references to both `tool_reference` and `defer_loading`; comments or templates that merely print a reference marker do not count as native expansion support. - Collect referenced tool names while converting message history. - Strip deferred-loading metadata before forwarding an unlocked tool to a generic template. - Keep the existing native structured-reference path unchanged. ## Tests Added focused CPU regression coverage for: - Jinja capability detection, including dict-valued templates and false-positive guards. - Hiding deferred tools before discovery. - Unlocking only referenced tools. - Qwen-style strict content rendering without `Unexpected item type in content`. - Unknown references and forced `tool_choice` behavior. - Preservation of the native GLM path. Local verification: - `test_tool_reference.py`: 11/11 passed. - Existing `test_serving.py`: 61/61 passed. - Ruff, Black, isort, and `git diff --check`: passed. - The stock Qwen3.8-27B template rendered successfully: initial tools were `[ToolSearch]`; after a Bash reference they were `[ToolSearch, Bash]`; unreferenced Read remained hidden. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32475052912](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32475052912)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32475052775](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32475052775)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32475052943](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32475052943)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [Feature] Support for same GPU native DP replicas with optional CUDA MPS
signals.text: ## Motivation Phase 1 for <https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/35648>. But It will work great for one shot models that don't need to save KV cache, like prefill embedding only models. This change adds `--same-gpu-replicas N` for running `N` native SGLang data-parallel replicas on one physical GPU through one public server endpoint. This is still useful for cases where only one query needs to be answered without need for shared kv. For example: ```bash --same-gpu-replicas 2 ``` resolves to: ```bash --dp-size 2 --gpu-id-step 0 ``` CUDA MPS is optional and remains externally managed. SGLang runs with normal CUDA scheduling when MPS is unavailable and logs a CUDA startup warning when `nvidia-cuda-mps-control` is not installed. ## Modifications - Add `--same-gpu-replicas N` for guarded same-GPU native DP. - Validate the supported topology: TP=1, PP=1, single node, no DP attention, disaggregation, elastic scaling, or Ray, and explicit `--max-total-tokens`. - Launch same-GPU replicas sequentially to reduce startup memory contention. - Keep one public SGLang endpoint; the native DP controller routes requests across private scheduler/model replicas. - Log whether the NVIDIA MPS control utility is available when same-GPU replicas run on CUDA. - Add unit coverage for flag resolution, the legacy alias, conflicts, and topology validation. - Tested using custom `bench_same_gpu_mps` script for endpoint throughput and latency benchmarking. ## Accuracy tests N/A. This change modifies replica placement and request routing; it does not change model-forward or kernel numerics. ## Speed tests and profiling Hardware: RTX 4070 Ti 12 GB Model: `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B` Workload: 100 requests, concurrency 6, four warmup requests, and 128 output tokens per request. CUDA MPS was unavailable in this WSL environment, so these results compare normal CUDA scheduling with one versus two same-GPU replicas. | Configuration | Completion throughput | p50 latency | p90 latency | p99 latency | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 1 replica | 279.7 tok/s | 2.093 s | 3.949 s | 4.157 s | | 2 same-GPU replicas | 538.9 tok/s | 1.176 s | 1.228 s | 4.930 s | Two same-GPU replicas improved aggregate completion throughput by **92.7%** and reduced p50 latency by **43.8%**. The p99 result should be validated with repeated runs. ### Embedding model Hardware: RTX 4070 Ti 12 GB Model: `Qwen/Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B` Workload: 100 embedding requests, concurrency 6, four warmup requests, and one input per request (20 prompt tokens per input). CUDA MPS was unavailable in this WSL environment, so these results compare normal CUDA scheduling with one versus two same-GPU replicas. | Configuration | Embedding throughput | p50 latency | p90 latency | p99 latency | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 1 replica | 127.0 embeddings/s | 0.043 s | 0.062 s | 0.071 s | | 2 same-GPU replicas | 133.2 embeddings/s | 0.043 s | 0.057 s | 0.071 s | | 3 same-GPU replicas | 152.7 embeddings/s | 0.034 s | 0.065 s | 0.111 s | Three same-GPU replicas improved aggregate embedding throughput by **20.2%** over one replica and reduced p50 latency by **20.0%**. However, p99 latency increased to 0.111 s, so validate the tail-latency trade-off with repeated runs and longer or batched inputs. ### CUDA MPS validation CUDA MPS is optional and must be started outside SGLang. ```bash export CUDA_MPS_PIPE_DIRECTORY=/tmp/sglang-mps-pipe export CUDA_MPS_LOG_DIRECTORY=/tmp/sglang-mps-log mkdir -p "$CUDA_MPS_PIPE_DIRECTORY" "$CUDA_MPS_LOG_DIRECTORY" nvidia-cuda-mps-control -d ``` Launch SGLang with two same-GPU replicas: ```bash python -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B \ --same-gpu-replicas 2 \ --mem-fraction-static 0.35 \ --max-total-tokens 1024 \ --max-running-requests 4 \ --disable-cuda-graph ``` Verify that both scheduler processes attached to the MPS server: ```bash MPS_SERVER_PID=$( printf 'get_server_list\n' | nvidia-cuda-mps-control | awk 'NF {print $1; exit}' ) printf 'get_client_list %s\n' "$MPS_SERVER_PID" | nvidia-cuda-mps-control ps -eo pid,ppid,args | grep '[s]glang::scheduler' ``` The two scheduler PIDs must appear in the MPS client list. ## Checklist - [x] Add unit tests. - [x] Add a manual benchmark utility. - [ ] Run NVIDIA CUDA MPS attachment and benchmark validation on native Linux. - [ ] Run formatting and full relevant CI. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32481003421](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32481003421)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32481002895](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32481002895)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32481003083](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32481003083)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: perf: cut device syncs and redundant launches from decode scheduling
signals.text: On a PD-disaggregated decode node there is a ~4ms GPU bubble between two forwards. nsys shows the scheduler thread blocked in cudaStreamSynchronize, 8-12ms each. All of those syncs sit on schedule_stream, and _apply_war_barrier fences that stream behind the in-flight forward, so anything that needs a value back on the host waits out a whole forward; the remaining host work (MLP-sync all_gather plus launch prep) then lands in the window before the next forward. Each sync point is removed in turn: 1. Preallocation (DecodePreallocQueue.pop_preallocated) - torch.tensor([...], device=...) becomes a pinned staging buffer plus a non_blocking copy. A pageable H2D goes through memcpy_and_sync in aten, i.e. cudaMemcpyAsync + cudaStreamSynchronize; the pinned copy is still ordered before the allocator kernel that reads it, so semantics are unchanged. Shared helper: pinned_int64_pair() in allocator/base.py. - Same three blocking H2D in SWATokenToKVPoolAllocator.alloc_extend_swa_tail (swa_seq_lens / swa_last_loc / mapping[...] = 0); the last one now writes a cached device scalar. - The page/state indices sent to the prefill node were read back with .cpu() at admission time. They are now registered as device tensors and read back by flush_pending_metadata() after the next forward has been launched, on a separate stream (gated on an event, pinned async D2H, record_stream). The writes stay on schedule_stream so WAR ordering is unchanged. 2. KV release on request completion free() dedups page ids with torch.unique, and free_swa() additionally reads the mapping back (unique plus a > 0 mask) to discover which pages carry SWA state. Both shapes are data-dependent, hence the sync. The caller can name the range instead: - PagedTokenToKVPoolAllocator.free_page_reps(): release by one representative token per page. - SWATokenToKVPoolAllocator.free_full_segment() / free_swa_segment() / free_swa_page_reps(): the mapping preserves a token's offset within its page (both pools advance on the same seq_lens), so one token every page_size positions from a page-aligned start hits each SWA page exactly once. - SWAChunkCache.cache_finished_req releases the two pools separately: the full pool from cache_protected_len, the SWA pool only from swa_evicted_seqlen, since window eviction already released what came before. _release_overallocated_kv_indices and the window eviction in free_swa_out_of_window_slots go through the same segment API. Composite allocators keep falling back to free(): radix cache nodes are not guaranteed to still be SWA-mapped, so the positional derivation does not hold for them. The aliased-pool allocator (PureSWATokenToKVPoolAllocator, where full_attn_allocator IS swa_attn_allocator) also falls back, otherwise the split release would free the same slots twice. 3. Batched window eviction (maybe_evict_swa) Calling the release per request put O(batch_size) calls on the scheduler thread right before the launch, ~90us each. The whole batch's out-of-window ranges are now gathered in one indexed read. That single call is then made sync-free by gathering one token per page (step=page_size) and releasing through free_swa_page_reps(), so eviction costs one op and no sync. 4. NVTX NVTX ranges for the scheduler's hot regions, and real NVTX step spans for ModelRunner.forward and the multi-layer draft-extend replay path (previously only torch record_function, invisible in nsys). 5. C128 state reset on admission (clear_c128_req_state) With the syncs gone, this region was still bimodal: 0.05ms without an admission, 5-8ms with one. The cost had become launch count -- one fill_ plus one zero_ per C128 pool, ~40 launches per admitted request, and a kernel launch on this ARM host is ~17us. The written constants are fixed, so the first call bakes a template and every later call issues a single _foreach_copy_ over contiguous slices: 40 kernels collapse to 1. The template is built with the same ops as the old path, so the bytes written are bitwise identical even where -inf saturates in the pool dtype. Both C128 layouts are covered; mismatched pool shape/dtype/ring_size falls back to the per-pool loop. Measured on a 4-rank decode node (per-rank per-iteration means): - cudaStreamSynchronize in pop_preallocated: 263 calls / 2518ms -> 0 - prebuilt batch assembly: 1.16 -> 0.22 ms/iter, p90 6.68 -> 1.64ms - get_next_batch_to_run: 10.74 -> 8.31 ms/iter - iteration rate: 35.1 -> 39.3 iter/s per rank (+13%) - clear_c128_req_state microbenchmark: 40 -> 1 kernels, 0.721 -> 0.078 ms - batched sync-free eviction removed 901 syncs / 2761ms per 14.2s window, 85% of the time spent in the eviction region Page conservation for the positional release was validated with SGLANG_DEBUG_MEMORY_POOL=1 over ~10k decode steps (its assertions are host-visible syncs, so that flag must not be mixed into a perf run), plus equivalence tests against the unique-based path for the strided gather and for free_swa_page_reps. The batched out-of-window free in maybe_evict_swa originates from an internal patch by a teammate; a Co-authored-by trailer will be added before merge. <!-- Thank you for your contribution! signals.title: [Runtime] Don't override CUDA_MODULE_LOADING
signals.text: ## Motivation `_set_envs_and_config()` currently assigns `CUDA_MODULE_LOADING=AUTO` before launching workers. This silently replaces a deployment's explicit `DEFAULT`, `EAGER`, or `LAZY` choice with an undocumented value whose behavior is not part of NVIDIA's compatibility contract. SGLang has no corresponding CLI option or runtime invariant that requires overriding this CUDA control plane. This matters when a deployment intentionally uses eager loading to move first-use module initialization out of the request path, accepting additional startup time and memory for more predictable request latency. Today that setting is overwritten before local multiprocessing scheduler workers are spawned. ## NVIDIA CUDA contract The NVIDIA CUDA Programming Guide documents [`CUDA_MODULE_LOADING`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-programming-guide/05-appendices/environment-variables.html#cuda-module-loading) with these possible values: > `DEFAULT`: Default behavior, equivalent to `LAZY`. > `LAZY`: The loading of specific kernels is delayed until a CUDA function handle ... is extracted. > `EAGER`: Fully loads CUDA modules and kernels at program initialization. `AUTO` is not a documented value. NVIDIA's [Lazy Loading guide](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-programming-guide/04-special-topics/lazy-loading.html) states: > As of CUDA 12.3 lazy loading is enabled by default on all platforms, but can be controlled via the `CUDA_MODULE_LOADING` environment variable. Its change history also records the version boundary: lazy loading was introduced but disabled by default in CUDA 11.7, became the Linux default in CUDA 12.2, and became the Windows default in CUDA 12.3. Therefore, an unset variable follows the installed CUDA/PyTorch stack rather than a version-independent SGLang policy. ## Change Don't assign `CUDA_MODULE_LOADING` in `_set_envs_and_config()`. - User-provided `DEFAULT`, `EAGER`, or `LAZY` values are no longer overwritten before local multiprocessing workers are spawned. - When the variable is absent, module-loading behavior is left to the installed CUDA/PyTorch stack. Current published Linux CUDA 12.9 and CUDA 13.0 images default to lazy loading; older or custom environments may differ. - Ray deployments should provide this variable through the cluster or job runtime environment when deterministic propagation to remote actors is required. - This PR does not add an SGLang CLI flag or change `CUDA_DEVICE_MAX_CONNECTIONS`. ## Validation - `pre-commit run --files python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/engine.py` - `git diff --check` - On a CUDA 13 environment, `cuModuleGetLoadingMode()` reported `LAZY` for unset, `DEFAULT`, `LAZY`, `AUTO`, and an arbitrary unknown value, and `EAGER` for `EAGER`. The `AUTO` result is an observation for that environment, not a documented compatibility guarantee. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32469777290](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32469777290)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32469777211](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32469777211)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32469777364](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32469777364)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: fix: manually register kv_b_proj to attn_mha so mla models can round-…
signals.text: ## Motivation address #35702. MLA models now cannot be saved then loaded with `ShardedModelLoader`. The error we get is : ``` File "python/sglang/srt/model_loader/loader.py", line 1796, in load_model param_data = state_dict[key].data ~~~~~~~~~~^^^^^ KeyError: 'model.layers.22.self_attn.attn_mha.kv_b_proj.weight' ``` and the reason is: 1. `DeepseekV2AttentionMLA.__init__` sets `self.attn_mha.kv_b_proj = None` and `forward_prepare` fills it in on first use. Assigning an `nn.Module` goes through `nn.Module.__setattr__`, which **registers `kv_b_proj` as a submodule of `attn_mha`** — so after one forward the same weight appears in `model.state_dict()` under two names sharing one storage. 2. `ShardedStateLoader.save_model` dumps `_filter_subtensors(model.state_dict())`, which dedups tensors sharing storage and keeps the lexicographically smaller key. `...attn_mha.kv_b_proj.weight` sorts before `...kv_b_proj.weight`, so the canonical name is dropped from the checkpoint. 3. On load, `load_model` iterates the checkpoint's keys and indexes a **fresh** model's state dict, which has never forwarded and therefore has no `attn_mha.kv_b_proj` — `KeyError`. ## Modifications We mannually register `kv_b_proj` as attribute of `self.attn_mha` without making it a module. This means, it will not be present in `model.state_dict()` and will not cause the eviction of our beloved `self.kv_b_proj`. ## Accuracy Tests Using DeepSeek-V2-Lite on GH200 node. ``` python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model-path '${model}' \ --trust-remote-code --attention-backend triton \ --host 127.0.0.1 --port ${PORT} python3 -m sglang.test.run_eval --host 127.0.0.1 --port ${PORT} \ --eval-name gsm8k --api completion --num-examples 200 ``` results: ``` Total latency: 21.807 s Score: 0.320 Output throughput: 1987.862 token/s [METRIC] gsm8k_score=0.32 labels={"model": "/iopsstor/scratch/cscs/yboughizane/.cache/huggingface/hub/models--deepseek-ai--DeepSeek-V2-Lite/snapshots/604d5664dddd88a0433dbae533b7fe9472482de0", "eval": "gsm8k"} [METRIC] gsm8k_latency=21.806841063982574 labels={"model": "/iopsstor/scratch/cscs/yboughizane/.cache/huggingface/hub/models--deepseek-ai--DeepSeek-V2-Lite/snapshots/604d5664dddd88a0433dbae533b7fe9472482de0", "eval": "gsm8k"} ``` ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not applicable, this PR does not involve performance-related changes. ## Validation The repro script from #35702 does not fail anymore. ## Checklist -
