signals.title: Support mxfp8 KV cache in PD transfer
signals.text: ## Motivation MXFP8 KV refused PD disaggregation outright: `get_contiguous_buf_infos` raised `KV transfer / disaggregation is unsupported for MXFP8 KV cache (scale buffers are not exposed)`. This exposes them, so a hybrid attention + linear-attention model serves PD with `--kv-cache-dtype mxfp8`. The scales do not go on the KV lists. Four call sites derive geometry from their length -- `len(kv_data_ptrs) // layer_num` in `setup_state_kv_args`, `len(kv_item_lens) // 2` in the staging handler, the layer range in `prefill.py`, and per-token bytes in `common/conn.py` -- so appending buffers there would silently skew all of them. They ride the multi-component state channel instead, which already carries KV-adjacent buffers for `SWA_RING`, `C128_STATE` and `MINIMAX_INDEX_K`. Two components rather than one, because a SWA pool nests two MXFP8 pools and their scales need different index payloads: the full-attention scales follow the whole sequence, the sliding-window scales follow the window through `translate_loc_from_full_to_swa`. One component cannot carry both. `item_lens` splits on the layout: the interleaved buffer (the `page_size == 128` path) puts pages on the leading axis so one row is one page, while the flat buffer is per slot and a page spans `page_size` rows. Removing the refusal surfaced a second gap: this pool overrides `_create_buffers` wholesale, and the base class only builds `_kv_buffer_descs` at the end of the method it replaced, so the inherited accessor hit an `AttributeError`. The descriptors are now built there too. `set_kv_buffer_prefix_valid` still refuses -- its callers are the DSpark and DFlash speculative paths, which PD does not reach. A hybrid model also needs #35689, now on main: without it the empty mamba temporal buffer fails the batch registration before any of this runs. ## Accuracy Single-node PD, one prefill and one decode role, TP=2 each, mooncake over IB, hierarchical cache on the prefill role, `--kv-cache-dtype mxfp8`. `sgl-eval` aime26, thinking on, `max_tokens=131072`: ``` score = 0.9333 error_rate = 0.00% stop_rate = 0.9667 truncated_rate = 0.0333 total_completion_tokens = 822323 ``` One of the two misses is `finish_reason=length` with no answer extracted, so 28/29 of the samples that finished are correct -- level with the 0.9667 the same setup reads on bf16 KV, where nothing truncated. MXFP8 spends about 7% more completion tokens (822k against 768k), which is what pushes one problem into the cap. A prompt whose prefix is well past the sliding window answers correctly and repeatably. Pointing the window component at the whole-sequence payload instead degenerates it to empty or truncated completions, which is what confirms the window scales are read rather than incidentally correct. The flat layout has no hardware coverage here -- fa4 pins `page_size` to 128, so only the interleaved branch runs -- and is covered by the unit test. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32437324281](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32437324281)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32437324240](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32437324240)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32437324245](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32437324245)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [AMD] Fix Qwen3.5 MTP dropping fused shared-expert weights
signals.text: ## Motivation Since #33889, Qwen3.5 MXFP4 with MTP speculative decoding on MI355X lost about 12% throughput. The cause is that the MTP draft model is loaded without its shared-expert weights. **What fusion does to the weight layout.** When a Qwen3.5 MoE layer fuses its shared expert, it deliberately does not build a separate `shared_expert` module — the shared expert becomes one more routed expert, living in slot `num_experts`. Any loader for such a layer therefore has to route `mlp.shared_expert.*` into that slot. `qwen3_5.py` does exactly that; `qwen3_5_mtp.py` never learned to. **Why the target model is unaffected.** In this checkpoint the target's routed experts are MXFP4 while its shared expert stays bf16. Fusing them would push a higher-precision tensor through the quantized routed-expert path, so `can_fuse_shared_expert()` refuses. The target therefore always takes the unfused path, keeps its `shared_expert` module, and loads normally — the gap in the MTP loader is invisible from here. **Why the draft model is affected, and only recently.** The MTP module is excluded from quantization in full: all 1536 `mtp.*` routed-expert tensors and its shared expert alike. The draft is thus uniformly bf16, nothing is mixed-precision, and fusing it is perfectly valid — the gate correctly says yes. It simply never had the chance before. Until #33889, the target's Quark config installed a single process-wide `disable_shared_experts_fusion` override, which switched fusion off for every runner, draft included. #33889 made that decision per-runner, so the draft started fusing for the first time and immediately ran into the loader gap. **Why nobody noticed.** With fusion on there is no `shared_expert` module to load into, and the expert mapping only covers slots `0 .. num_experts-1`, so each `mlp.shared_expert.{gate,up,down}_proj.weight` matches nothing and ends at `logger.warning_once("Parameter ... not found in params_dict, skip loading")` — three tensors per TP rank, one suppressed log line, no error. The draft then runs with an uninitialized shared expert. Since a speculative draft cannot corrupt verified output, accuracy is unaffected; the damage appears only as a fall in accept rate, from 0.65 to 0.51, and hence in throughput. This PR teaches the MTP loader to place those weights into the fused slot, so the draft that #33889 legitimately enabled actually receives them. ## Modifications `python/sglang/srt/models/qwen3_5_mtp.py`, mirroring `qwen3_5.py`: - Size the expert mapping as `num_experts + num_fused_shared_experts` so slot `num_experts` has an entry. The fusion count is read from the constructed modules, because `num_fused_shared_experts` is set on `Qwen3_5MoeForConditionalGeneration` and the MTP wraps a `Qwen3_5ForCausalLM`, which does not carry it. - Rewrite `mlp.shared_expert.` to `mlp.experts.{num_experts}.` before the mapping loops. Both are keyed on the model's actual fusion state rather than on a platform check. When nothing fuses, `num_fused_shared_experts` is `0`, the mapping size is unchanged and the rewrite never fires, so this is a no-op for every non-fusing configuration. Not covered: the fused-checkpoint variant (a single `experts.gate_up_proj` tensor). `qwen3_5.py` handles that with a dedicated branch that chunks the tensor into `w1`/`w3`; the MTP loader's `load_fused_expert_weights` indexes per expert id and cannot serve a single shared-expert tensor. Adding that path untested seemed worse than leaving it, since no checkpoint on hand exercises it. ## Accuracy Tests No accuracy change is expected: only the draft model changes, and a speculative draft cannot alter verified output. The visible effect is the accept rate. Measured over ~100 decode-batch samples per point. | conc | accept_len before | after | accept_rate before | after | |---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 4 | 2.5278 | 2.9533 | 0.5097 | 0.6509 | | 8 | 2.5507 | 2.9374 | 0.5168 | 0.6457 | | 16 | 2.5144 | 2.9508 | 0.5054 | 0.6501 | Skipped weights during load go from 3 per TP rank to 0. ## Speed Tests and Profiling ### Summary at conc=4 | Config | Total Throughput | Median E2E (ms) | Median TTFT (ms) | Median TPOT (ms) | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:| | `eda0ddc260d4` (last good) | 5365.74 | 5992.71 | 326.84 | 6.25 | | `b61a06921e` (#33889) | 4716.15 | 6662.60 | 322.72 | 7.05 | | `b61a06921e` + PR #35719 | 5429.77 | 5912.64 | 326.93 | 6.11 | The third row was obtained by switching shared-expert fusion off on `b61a06921e`, which removes the unloaded-shared-expert condition from the draft; this PR removes the same condition by loading the fused weights instead of dropping them. ### Full sweep MI355X, `amd/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-MXFP4`, TP=2, EAGLE MTP (3 steps / topk 1 / 4 draft tokens), page-size 16, `fp8_e4m3` KV, `--attention-backend aiter`, ISL=8192 / OSL=1024, `num_prompts = 10 x conc`, server relaunched per concurrency with `--max-running-requests = conc`. Server flags follow `benchmarks/single_node/fixed_seq_len/qwen3.5_fp4_mi355x_mtp.sh`. Before and after were run back to back on the same GPU pair, both at `7f8f030000`. | conc | Total Throughput before | after | Delta | Median E2E (ms) before | after | Median TTFT (ms) before | after | Median TPOT (ms) before | after | |---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 4 | 4746.11 | 5417.31 | **+14.14%** | 6726.7 | 5969.1 | 333.3 | 336.7 | 7.07 | 6.22 | | 8 | 6835.64 | 7626.54 | **+11.57%** | 9243.7 | 8370.3 | 336.4 | 335.9 | 9.67 | 8.82 | | 16 | 9011.82 | 10141.08 | **+12.53%** | 13997.8 | 12840.5 | 346.1 | 361.6 | 14.86 | 13.48 | The gain is decode-side, as expected from an accept-rate change: TTFT is flat, TPOT improves by 9–12%. This restores the configuration to its previously published InferenceX level. The last sweep on image `lmsysorg/sglang-rocm:v0.5.16-rocm720-mi35x-20260730` recorded 582.84 / 852.30 / 1130.14 output tok/s at conc 4 / 8 / 16; with this patch the same setup measures 602.47 / 857.12 / 1123.38. Bisecting `accept len` over the 759 commits between that image's sglang and `63d783bbe0` lands on #33889, with a clean split (2.84–2.92 before, 2.50–2.57 after, no intermediate values). ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32499687037](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32499687037)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32499686918](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32499686918)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32499686928](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32499686928)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [BugFix][DP] Prevent health checks from perturbing user request routing
signals.text: ## Motivation Generation health checks (`HEALTH_CHECK_*`) are intentionally skipped by the scheduler while normal inference is already making progress. Under DP serving, however, the request passes through `DataParallelController` before that scheduler-side skip. With `round_robin`, a generation health request currently advances the same dispatch state used by user requests. For load-aware methods, it can also participate in the user load-budget refresh/update path. This means a health request that is later discarded can still perturb user-request ownership across DP ranks. In a long-prefill DP-Attention workload, this produced a reproducible scheduling failure chain: ```text generation health request -> user LB state is mutated -> per-rank user ownership becomes uneven -> some DP ranks become idle while peers continue prefill -> PrefillDelayer sees persistent mixed states / timeout -> effective concurrency and throughput drop ``` The root-cause investigation is tracked in #35241. ## Modifications This PR isolates generation-health dispatch state from user load-balancing state in `DataParallelController`: - Detect generation health requests before normal user LB dispatch. - Use an independent round-robin counter for health requests. - Do not refresh or mutate the user `DPBudget` for health-only dispatches. - For batch generate, refresh the user load budget only when the batch contains a user request. - Preserve explicit `routed_dp_rank` behavior. - Preserve `FOLLOW_BOOTSTRAP_ROOM` semantics for PD/disaggregated serving, since that path uses request-specific routing rather than shared mutable user LB state. This PR does **not** change DP Attention, PrefillDelayer, scheduler busy-health skip behavior, or the health endpoint semantics. ## Regression Tests Added CPU unit coverage for: - independent user-RR and health-RR state; - health dispatch using only active workers; - explicit `routed_dp_rank` not advancing health RR state; - health dispatch bypassing user load-budget refresh; - health-only batch dispatch not refreshing user load state; - `FOLLOW_BOOTSTRAP_ROOM` health routing compatibility. ```text python3 -m pytest test/registered/unit/managers/test_data_parallel_controller.py -q 23 passed git diff --check clean pre-commit run --files \ python/sglang/srt/managers/data_parallel_controller.py \ test/registered/unit/managers/test_data_parallel_controller.py all passed ``` ## Runtime Validation Validated on 8x NVIDIA B300 with DeepSeek-V4-Pro, TP8/DP8, DP Attention, MegaMoE, PrefillDelayer, round-robin routing, 8k effective prefill chunk, C16/N160, 60k input / 1 output. The external watchdog continued issuing generation health checks during the patched runs. | Configuration | Input TPS | avg running | HEALTH at DPC | IDLE-while-EXTEND | Delayer timeout | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | Original + generation health ON (observed HIT) | 76,417 | 6.84 | 59 | 33 | 9 | | Original + generation health OFF | 94,720-94,974 | 8.55-8.76 | 0 | 0 | 0 | | Patched + generation health ON, 4/4 runs | 94,372-94,822 | 8.60-8.69 | 49-51 | 0 | 0 | All patched runs completed 160/160 requests with no fatal errors. Generation-health traffic remained present at DPC, while the user-ownership hole and associated concurrency collapse disappeared. This is a scoped validation for the tested failure family; it is not intended to claim that generation health is the cause of every low-throughput state. ## Scope The intended invariant is: > Generation health traffic must not mutate the load-balancing state used by user requests when it is routed through DP serving. This PR does not make round-robin load-aware and does not change the configured load-balancing policy. Related: #35241 <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32445999557](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32445999557)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32445998878](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32445998878)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32445999010](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32445999010)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [diffusion] Enable LongCat breakable CUDA graphs
signals.text: ## Summary - enable the existing diffusion breakable CUDA graph runner for `meituan-longcat/LongCat-Image` - keep LongCat's fixed 512-token DiT prompt shape unchanged so the generic BCG buckets do not capture unused expanded signatures - document the deployment command and refresh the checked-in diffusion performance/profile skills ## Why LongCat's native eager DiT trace is launch-heavy between attention calls. The existing BCG runner can capture those regions as 31 graph segments, but LongCat was not admitted by the model and pipeline allowlists. LongCat always sends the full 512-token prompt body to the DiT. A small model-specific pass-through padder therefore preserves one reusable signature for short and long raw prompts instead of applying generic prompt padding. ## Production-shape visual and end-to-end A/B (B300) Prompt from the checked-in LongCat diffusion benchmark preset: `A red panda reading a book beside a sunlit window.` Configuration: NVIDIA B300 SXM6 AC, native `--backend sglang`, BF16, 1 GPU, 1024x1024, 50 steps, guidance 4.5, seed 42, prompt rewrite disabled, `quality=lossless`, `--performance-mode manual`. ![LongCat main eager versus PR BCG](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/pr-media/diffusion-prs/35724/main-vs-pr.jpg) The main and PR PNGs are byte-exact (`sha256=6a44ff30a185993f50d23da660b3cbe42fb8fdf8ac1d0d612d0086f35c723372`). | Path | Saved-request e2e runs | Mean e2e | Mean denoise stage | | --- | --- | ---: | ---: | | main, eager | 7.422 / 7.421 / 7.445 s | 7.429 s | 7.109 s | | this PR, BCG | 7.178 / 7.174 / 7.175 s | 7.175 s | 6.261 s | That is a **3.42% end-to-end reduction** and an **11.93% denoise-stage reduction** on B300. signals.title: [Fix][GDN] Route DFlash/DSpark commits through ReplaySSM spec fold
signals.text: ## Motivation ReplaySSM speculative-state folding already supports GDN when speculative decoding commits through `commit_mamba_states_after_verify()`. DFlash and DSpark use a different path and call `HybridLinearAttnBackend.update_mamba_state_after_mtp_verify()` directly after target verification. Before this change, the direct commit path recognized ReplaySSM only for KDA. A GDN target therefore fell back to the regular intermediate-state scatter path, even though `--enable-linear-replayssm-spec` intentionally removes `intermediate_ssm`. The KV-cache configurator prevented this invalid path by rejecting every non-KDA DFlash/DSpark target. This PR routes the built-in GDN backend through the existing ReplaySSM fold implementation from #28695. It does not change the ReplaySSM kernels, model outputs, public flags, or the generic speculative-decoding commit path. ## Modifications - Resolve the direct ReplaySSM verify-commit handler when `HybridLinearAttnBackend` is initialized. - Select the KDA handler only when speculative folding is enabled, and select the GDN handler only for a concrete `GDNAttnBackend`. - Keep the existing intermediate-state scatter fallback for every other backend and for ReplaySSM-disabled execution. - Replace the pool-local KDA-only rejection with validation scoped to DFlash/DSpark target workers before memory-pool sizing. - Fail fast for unsupported direct-verify configurations: non-GDN/KDA targets, non-CUDA/ROCm devices, unified memory, and non-static ragged verification for GDN. KDA compact-ragged verification remains supported. - Add a focused CPU regression test for GDN/KDA handler selection, constructor wiring, direct commit dispatch, and configuration guards. ## Accuracy Tests The following focused and neighboring regression tests pass: | Test | Result | |---|---:| | New GDN direct-commit regression test | 3/3 passed | | GDN ReplaySSM speculative fold parity | 4/4 passed | | GDN/KDA ReplaySSM packed-decode parity | 6/6 passed | | GDN attention backend regression suite | 9/9 passed | | Mamba2 attention backend regression suite | 9/9 passed | | Hybrid FlashInfer metadata regression suite | 2/2 passed | | NGRAM/Mamba verify-update regression suite | 14/14 passed | | ReplaySSM ring accounting | 3/3 passed | The GPU tests were run on a single NVIDIA H20. The clean end-to-end A/B test used Qwen3.8-27B as the target, Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2 as the draft model, DFlash with one speculative step and eight draft tokens, TP=1, Triton attention backends, CUDA graphs disabled, five-shot GSM8K with 200 questions, parallelism 4, temperature 0, and top-p 1. The only server-side difference was `--enable-linear-replayssm-spec`. | Configuration | Accuracy | Invalid outputs | Exact output match | |---|---:|---:|---:| | Baseline | 194/200 (97.0%) | 0 | Reference | | ReplaySSM | 194/200 (97.0%) | 0 | 200/200 | ## Speed Tests and Profiling N/A. This PR fixes routing to the existing ReplaySSM implementation and does not change its kernels. The GSM8K run above is reported only as an accuracy test; its single-run wall-clock timing is intentionally not used as a performance claim. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). N/A: this PR adds no public flag or API and fixes an already documented GDN ReplaySSM path. - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. signals.title: [diffusion] park a layerwise component's non-layer weights between uses
signals.text: ## Motivation Layerwise offload streams a component's blocks and releases them when its use ends. Everything else the component owns — embeddings, projections, norms, heads — stays on the device for the whole request. That is right while it is the component being used, and pure cost afterwards. On a small card the stage that follows is the one that needs the room. MiniMax-H3 at 864x480 / 124 frames / 20 steps, one RTX 4090, host memory capped at 32 GiB. The VAE decode is half the request, because `decode_temporal` re-runs the whole decoder per temporal chunk — so under layerwise offload the VAE's 36 blocks are re-streamed every chunk: ``` [MiniMaxH3TextEncodingStage] finished in 0.50 s [MiniMaxH3DenoisingStage] finished in 141.20 s [MiniMaxH3DecodingStage] finished in 140.60 s <- as much as 20 denoise steps ``` Holding those blocks resident (`--layerwise-resident-layers video_vae=36`, #35688) is what makes the decode cheap — 23 s instead of 150 — and it needs 9 GB. With a hard 12 GiB allocator cap the decode then dies for want of 20 MiB: ``` CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 20.00 MiB. 12.00 GiB allowed; Of the allocated memory 11.86 GiB is allocated by PyTorch ``` Of that 11.86 GiB, the DiT is still holding 2.09 GB and the text encoder 1.40 GB that the decode never touches. `PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True` does not close the gap. ## Modifications `park_non_layer_weights()` moves the parameters no manager streams to the host and leaves a `(1,)` placeholder behind; `restore_non_layer_weights()` brings them back. `LayerwiseOffloadStrategy` calls them from `finish_use` and `prepare_for_use`, so a component gives up that memory exactly while it is not the one being used. Scope is deliberately narrow: - **Parameters only.** Buffers stay resident because layerwise offload keeps them on purpose — a shared RoPE cache is referenced by many layers. - **One host copy, made once.** Steady state is one transfer each way per use: about 0.35 s for H3's 3.5 GB, against the 130 s the resident VAE saves. - **Follows `--performance-mode memory`**, which already trades latency for footprint. Nothing changes under the other modes. - **MPS untouched.** It has its own subphase-scoped mechanism. ## Accuracy Tests Which device holds a weight; the weights themselves are unchanged. Three unit tests cover the mode gate, that streamed layer weights are never parked and buffers stay resident, and that parking is a no-op outside memory mode. `test_layerwise_offload.py` (with the checkpoint-mapping branch applied, since that is the configuration measured): 117 passed. ## Speed Tests and Profiling H3 `fl2va`, 864x480 / 124 frames / 20 steps, seed 1101, single RTX 4090, host memory capped at 32 GiB. The 12 GiB VRAM budget is **enforced** with `torch.cuda.set_per_process_memory_fraction`, not inferred from `nvidia-smi` — which reports the caching allocator's reserved pool and so overstates it. | configuration | denoise | decode | end to end | 12 GiB cap | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | default | 141 s | 150 s | 303 s | fits, but decode dominates | | `video_vae=36` | 158 s | 23 s | 192 s | OOM in decode | | `video_vae=36` + this change | 159 s | **13 s** | **177 s** | **fits** | Host memory is unchanged at 24.5 GiB. Denoise varies 141–159 s with load on this shared box; decode is the term this change is about and it is stable. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32500676246](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32500676246)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32500676017](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32500676017)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32500676321](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32500676321)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [kernel] Split the custom all-reduce communicator into push/pull planes
signals.text: > Generated by Claude. ## Motivation Every JIT collective in `csrc/distributed` and `csrc/kimi_k3/comm` took one flat `CommunicatorObj` that carried every buffer any of them might want: `2 * world_size` push slots, a pull workspace, per-block semaphores, a rank-local counter, and one of the three multicast addresses. Consequences: - The other two multicast addresses travelled out of band. `ws_mc_base` was an `int64_t` argument repeated at five call sites, always the same constant; `pull_sem_mc_ptr` went through a per-world-size Python dict populated by `register_comm()`, duplicated in three modules. - A push-only owner (the fused qk-norm instances in `minimax_m2`) had to allocate a placeholder 1 KB pull buffer plus one semaphore purely to satisfy the constructor. - Only `custom_all_reduce.cuh` ever read `pull_workspaces` / `pull_bytes` / `pull_mc_workspace`. The K3 pull kernels reduce in place on the caller's own symmetric input and borrow the plane just to barrier on, so half the object was dead weight for most callers. - `custom_all_reduce.cuh` defined helpers at `namespace sglang` scope and was `#include`d by three K3 files across directories, so renaming anything inside it silently broke downstream kernels. ## What changed Split the object by lifetime rather than by direction: | | contents | |---|---| | `sgl.distributed.PushPlane` | zero-filled symmetric push slots, rank-local phase counter, multicast base | | `sgl.distributed.PullPlane` | symmetric pull buffers + per-block semaphores, both multicast bases. Either half may be a 0-element tensor | | `sgl.distributed.Communicator` | the two planes (either optional) + the pull launch widths; what every kernel takes | Both *fixed* multicast addresses now live on the planes. That deletes the `ws_mc_base` parameter from five entry points and the `_PULL_SEM_MC_MAP` registry from three modules. The *per-call* multicast address — a slice of the caller's own symmetric buffer, so it changes every call — stays a plain `intptr_t`, which is what it should be. `PullPlane`'s optional halves replace the placeholder-buffer trick: `minimax_m2` now constructs `Communicator(push=..., pull=None)` and a kernel that needs a missing plane fails with a message instead of reading a dummy buffer. ### Shared vocabulary moved under `include/` - **`include/sgl_kernel/distributed/ptx.cuh`** collects the inline PTX the collectives share into `sglang::device::ptx`, which `mbarrier.cuh` and the two K3 files reopen. Removed: three identical copies of the multimem flag increment, three copies of the "multicast alias of a semaphore's flag" helper (now `Semaphore::mc_flag`), and the 16B access helpers that were defined at `namespace sglang` scope inside `custom_all_reduce.cuh`. `csrc/kimi_k3/comm/ptx_sys.cuh` is deleted. The five communication kernels now contain zero inline PTX. - **`Barrier` / `McBarrier`** (unicast fan-out and one-`multimem.red` variants of the same window protocol) and **`LamportTrait`** (the pos-zero marker) live next to the planes, so each protocol has one implementation instead of one per kernel. - The three `csrc` → `csrc` includes of `custom_all_reduce.cuh` are gone. What they actually used — `reduce_vec`, the marker traits — moved under `include/`. - `alloc_workspace_tensor` moved to `host::ffi`, so `utils.cuh` no longer depends on `ffi.h`. `tp_qknorm`'s 8B `ld.volatile` / `st.volatile` pair became `ld_relaxed_8B` / `st_relaxed_8B` at `.sys` scope (PTX defines volatile as relaxed at system scope, and the store is cross-GPU). Load scope measured identical at `.gpu`, so the `.gpu` load variant was dropped and the vocabulary has one scope. ## Verification (8×B200, SM100) **Correctness — 291 tests, all passing** | test | | |---|---| | `test_custom_all_reduce.py` (8 GPU) | 180 passed | | `test_ar_fusion.py` (8 GPU) | 58 passed | | `test_tp_qknorm.py` (8 GPU) | 42 passed | | `test_collectives.py` (8 GPU) | 5 passed | | `test_compute.py` | 6 passed | | `test_custom_all_reduce_v2_capability.py` | 4 passed | | `test_attn_residual.py` | 1 passed | All 11 affected JIT modules build; `fp8_blockwise_scaled_mm_sm120` verified with a direct SM120 nvcc compile. clangd reports zero diagnostics on every touched file except two pre-existing cutlass include-path gaps in `.clangd`. **Registers / spills** — `cuobjdump -res-usage`, this branch vs the merge base, kernels paired by hand where the refactor renamed them: - **No spills anywhere** (`STACK=0`, `LOCAL=0` for every kernel). - Unchanged or better everywhere except `1shot_push`: bf16 60→63, fp16 61→63, fp32 56→58. That kernel is 2.7–6.2 % *faster* — `LamportTrait`'s 4-byte-atom marker test replaces a per-bf16-half test, cutting its SASS from 512 to 344 instructions. - `2shot_pull` eager improves (bf16 53→51) and the multicast variants drop one register. **Performance** — kernel time only, measured by replaying a CUDA graph of 20 chained calls so host dispatch is excluded; three interleaved rounds per arm, per-arm spread under 1 %: | variant | delta vs merge base | |---|---| | `1shot_push` / eager (dispatched ≤ 768 KB) | **−2.7 % … −6.2 %** | | `2shot_pull` / multicast (dispatched > 768 KB) | −0.03 % … +0.39 % | | `1shot_pull` eager and multicast | −1.1 % … +0.6 % | | `2shot_pull` / eager | +0.5 % … +0.9 % | 33 points: median +0.32 %, worst +0.92 %. On the path the tuned SM100/world-8 config actually dispatches: median **−3.30 %**, worst +0.39 %. One note on how that number was reached. An earlier revision of this branch regressed `2shot_pull` eager by 7–18 %. Bisecting with self-contained reference kernels showed the params layout, the `Barrier` object and the `Impl` abstraction were all innocent — an exact transplant of the old body still regressed. The cause was the address form: folding the shard offset into the eight base pointers as a typed 32-bit vector index keeps the peer table on the uniform datapath (`UIMAD.WIDE` off a constant-bank base), whereas biasing `vid` per access, or using a 64-bit byte offset, makes all eight addresses thread-varying and costs ~12 registers per thread. Also, binding a params array address to a named local that stays live across the kernel breaks the same proof. Both are noted in comments at the point of use, since either one silently costs ~10 %. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32484511620](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32484511620)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32510836380](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32510836380)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32484511571](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32484511571)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [multimodal] Fix NVFP4 diffusion models on sm_120 (RTX PRO 6000 / RTX 50xx)
signals.text: ## Motivation NVFP4 diffusion checkpoints cannot be served on sm_120 GPUs (RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell / RTX 50xx). Two independent defects in the shared ModelOpt FP4 path are involved; neither is model-specific. **1. The default FP4 GEMM backend does not exist on sm_120.** `CudaPlatformBase.get_modelopt_flashinfer_fp4_backend()` defaults to `"trtllm"`, and `flashinfer.mm_fp4` rejects it there: ``` ValueError: mm_fp4 does not support backend 'trtllm' with capability 120 ``` so the first quantized linear aborts and no NVFP4 model runs at all. **2. The block-scale layout is chosen by a heuristic whose negative branch is unreachable.** In `ModelOptFp4LinearMethod.process_weights_after_loading()` the `trtllm` branch fetches its own shuffled scale layout and **returns**. Everything still executing below it is therefore a TMA-layout consumer (`cutlass`, `cudnn`, `auto`) — but the layout was instead selected by a module-name test: ```python uses_flux1_scale_layout = not getattr( self.quant_config, "checkpoint_uses_packed_qkv", False ) and getattr(layer, "prefix", "").startswith( ("transformer_blocks.", "single_transformer_blocks.") ) if flashinfer_backend is None or uses_flux1_scale_layout: ``` Any model whose blocks are not named with the FLUX.1 prefixes skips the swizzle and hands the kernel block scales in the wrong layout. This does not raise — it silently produces broken output. ## Modifications - `runtime/platforms/cuda.py`: default the FP4 GEMM backend to `"auto"` on sm_120 (which resolves to flashinfer's sm_12x NVFP4 kernel) and keep `"trtllm"` elsewhere. `SGLANG_DIFFUSION_FLASHINFER_FP4_GEMM_BACKEND` still overrides. Uses the pre-existing `is_sm120()`, so no other capability changes behaviour. - `runtime/layers/quantization/modelopt_quant.py`: apply the 128x4 TMA reshape unconditionally, and delete the unreachable heuristic. This also removes two defensive `getattr()`s and the now-redundant second `_get_fp4_gemm_op()` call. - `test/unit/test_modelopt_fp4_backend.py`: new unit test pinning the default-backend resolution (sm_120 vs other, all explicit env spellings, unknown value falls back to the platform default). ## Accuracy Tests Verified on one RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition (sm_120) with an NVFP4 MiniMax-H3 checkpoint: - before: startup fails on (1); forcing a backend past it renders grey noise, which is (2). - after: output is **bit-identical** (md5 of the produced mp4) to the previously env-forced workaround, with no environment variables set. Same seed, same request, three runs. `python -m pytest python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_modelopt_fp4_backend.py` — 4 passed. ## Speed Tests and Profiling No performance change is expected or measured: the same kernel is selected, and the scale reshape is a one-time weight-load step. Paired single-GPU runs before/after differ by 0.2%, inside this box's run-to-run floor. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). --- sm_120 also needs #35740 (MiniMax-H3 model-side quantized-scale fixes) for a working NVFP4 MiniMax-H3; the two are in different layers and independent, hence separate PRs. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32467781044](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32467781044)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32467780725](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32467780725)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32467780863](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32467780863)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [multimodal] MiniMax-H3: fix quantized qkv scales and missing-param policy
signals.text: ## Motivation Two MiniMax-H3 model-side defects that only appear on a quantized checkpoint (NVFP4 or fp8). **1. Per-output-row quantization metadata is not reordered with its rows.** MiniMax-H3 checkpoints store qkv grouped, so `_install_qkv_weight_loader()` permutes the fused qkv weight's output rows into `q|k|v` order via `_reorder_grouped_qkv_to_qkv()`. NVFP4 block scales and fp8 per-channel scales are indexed by that same output row, and they were loaded unpermuted — every scale ends up attached to the wrong row. The weights are correct; the dequantized values are not. The symptom is grey mush, with no error anywhere. **2. `_mark_missing_params_required()` overwrites each quant method's own missing-parameter policy.** A quant method declares in `create_weights()` what it can synthesize when a scale is absent from the checkpoint — weight-only NVFP4 has no `input_scale` and marks it `missing_param_init = "ones"`. H3 then blanket-stamps every parameter `"error"`, so the declaration is lost and the loader raises: ``` ValueError: Required checkpoint parameter '...input_scale' was not loaded ``` ## Modifications - New module-level helper `_install_qkv_row_reorder()` wraps a qkv parameter's weight loader (and its `rank_local_weight_transform`, needed by rank-local FSDP) with the same row permutation used for the weight. Applied to every `qkv_proj` parameter except the weight itself. The gate is the row count: a tensor whose leading dim is not the checkpoint's qkv row count is passed through untouched, which covers per-tensor scalars and swizzled block-scale layouts that are not row-indexed. It reads the **loaded checkpoint tensor**, not the local parameter, so it also holds under tensor parallelism, where the local parameter only owns its own shard of the rows. - `_mark_missing_params_required()` now only claims parameters that have no declared policy. - `test/unit/test_minimax_h3_qkv_scale_reorder.py`: new unit test covering both branches of the row-count gate (row-indexed metadata is permuted, swizzled and per-tensor metadata is not) on the wrapped loader and on `rank_local_weight_transform`. Depends on nothing else, but on sm_120 both this and #35739 are required to get a working NVFP4 MiniMax-H3 (the two fixes are in different layers, hence separate PRs). ## Accuracy Tests On one RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition (sm_120) with an NVFP4 MiniMax-H3 checkpoint: - (2) alone is a hard load failure. - With (2) fixed, (1) renders grey mush. - With both fixed, output is structurally the same as the bf16 checkpoint, and bit-identical across repeated runs at the same seed. The reorder is only reachable for a quantized checkpoint with per-row scales; a bf16 run has no parameters other than the weight on `qkv_proj`, so it is unaffected. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Weight-load-time only; no change to the forward path and none measured (paired runs within 0.2%). ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32467818110](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32467818110)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32467817775](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32467817775)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32467818267](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32467818267)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.text: MXFP4 checkpoints (GPT-OSS) could not run on XPU: `mxfp4` was registered only for cpu/cuda/gfx95, and `Mxfp4MoEMethod` had no XPU branch, so it fell through to a bf16 upcast needing `triton_kernels` and ~42 GB for GPT-OSS-20B. `moe_grouped_mm_nt_xe20_w4a16` consumes the checkpoint layout as-is (packed e2m1 + N-outer ue8m0 g32 scales, interleaved gate/up rows), so add the XPU dispatch, skip the upcast, and keep the layout unpadded. signals.title: [multimodal] MiniMax-H3: accept target.width/height as an exact canvas
signals.text: ## Motivation `target.short_edge` names a *policy* size and lets `adapt_shape_v1` choose the canvas. A caller that already knows the geometry it wants — a fixed delivery format, a UI preset — has to work backwards to a nominal short edge plus a ratio string that round to it, and gets no error when the guess is wrong: unknown `target` keys are silently ignored, so a request carrying `width`/`height` is admitted and rendered at whatever the ratio resolved to. (`conditions[i]` and the canonical request both reject unknown keys; `target` is the one place that does not.) Naming both axes is exact, because the ratio *is* the canvas: the resolver's nominal-times-ratio step reproduces it and the nearest-32 rounding is a no-op. So this needs no resolver or stage change — validation rewrites the pair into the `short_edge` + `aspect_ratio` it denotes, and the canonical request keeps its existing three-key projection. A test asserts the resolved shape is identical to the equivalent ratio request (the resolved shape does not carry the ratio string, so nothing downstream can tell them apart). ## Modifications - `request_validation.py`: `_normalize_exact_canvas()` rewrites `target.width`+`height` into `short_edge=min(w, h)` and `aspect_ratio="W:H"`. - refuses a canvas off the 32px grid or over `MINIMAX_H3_MAX_PIXELS` rather than rounding or scaling it — silently changing the requested geometry is worse than refusing it; - refuses naming both spellings, and half a pair; - an exact canvas is exempt from the finite-ratio allowlist: that allowlist constrains *ratio* requests to tested shapes, and a caller naming both axes has already chosen. - `configs/sample/minimax_h3.py`: add `width`/`height` to the `target` projection in `_validate()`, otherwise the offline path drops them before validation sees them. - signals.title: [diffusion] read the next mapped layer ahead instead of faulting on it
signals.text: ## Motivation A weight left on the checkpoint mapping (#35701) is copied to the device synchronously, so when the page cache has dropped its pages the read happens on the critical path: the copy stalls in a major fault while the GPU waits. On MiniMax-H3 that is 44 GiB of DiT weights walked once per denoise step against roughly 8 GiB of page cache, so most steps fault. It shows up as load sensitivity — the denoise stage tracks how contended the host's memory bandwidth is, because the faults are competing for it. Every alternative that buys overlap buys it with host memory this budget does not have: pinning cannot be done on a mapping at all, and staging copies are the thing the mapping exists to avoid. Readahead buys it with nothing. ## Modifications `MADV_WILLNEED` over the next layer's mapped range, issued when the current layer is staged. Asynchronous readahead: free when the pages are already resident, overlapped with the current layer's compute when they are not, and it commits no memory of its own. One call per layer rather than per weight — a layer's mapped tensors are slices of the same checkpoint shard, so advising min..max covers them together and keeps this to one syscall per prefetch. `madvise` is bound through `ctypes` once and left as `None` where libc does not offer it, so the advice is skipped rather than guarded at every call site. ## Accuracy Tests Which pages are resident when a copy runs; the bytes copied are identical. `test_layerwise_offload.py` on this branch: 55 passed. ## Speed Tests and Profiling H3 `fl2va`, 864x480 / 124 frames / 20 steps, seed 1101, single RTX 4090, 12 GiB VRAM cap enforced with `torch.cuda.set_per_process_memory_fraction`, host memory capped at 32 GiB, `--layerwise-resident-layers video_vae=36`. This box is shared and its load average swings between 80 and 220, which is exactly the axis this change is about, so the samples are reported with it: | | load | denoise | decode | end to end | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | without readahead | 87 | 144.65 s | 13.08 s | 161.44 s | | without readahead | 131 | 157.05 s | 13.21 s | 175.72 s | | without readahead | 152 | 146.68 s | 12.92 s | 163.25 s | | **with readahead** | **139** | **144.89 s** | 12.88 s | **161.50 s** | | **with readahead** | **217** | **144.82 s** | 12.76 s** | **161.34 s** | Without it, end to end swings 161–176 s with load. With it, load 139 and load 217 both land at 161.3–161.5 s: the load-sensitive term is gone, which is the point. The decode stage is unchanged, as expected — its weights are held resident for the stage rather than re-read. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). Stacked on #35701, which is what puts weights on a mapping in the first place. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32545220090](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32545220090)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32545220075](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32545220075)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32545220112](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32545220112)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [diffusion] Z-Image: autotune the shared transformer block at both token scales (H100 1024^2 denoise 13.58 -> 9.58 s, 1.42x)
signals.text: torch.compile on zimage-base gets 1.42x faster: steady-state denoise at 1024x1024 goes 13.575 s -> 9.577 s on one H100, from a single kernel. Z-Image reuses one transformer block for the context refiner (a few dozen caption tokens), the noise refiner (4096) and the unified stream (4128 at 1024x1024). The flash-attn call breaks the graph, so the block's attention compiles into a frame of its own that is entered with all three counts; automatic dynamic shapes make its token dim symbolic, and Inductor autotunes the fused-qkv GEMM once, against whichever count it traced first. The caption branch wins that race and the resulting BLOCK_M=32/BLOCK_N=32 config then runs the 4096- and 4128-token layers too. It is the only dynamic-shape Triton template the model selects, and it accounts for the entire difference above. The same gap appears in the comparison table in BBuf/how-to-optim-algorithm-in-cuda#21. Set inductor's multi_kernel_hints for this model, so the block is compiled once per hint and dispatched on the runtime shape and the token dim stays dynamic. The knob is a generic DiTConfig.torch_compile_inductor_config passthrough that is empty for every other model; inductor config is process-global and is read when a graph compiles, so it cannot be scoped to the torch.compile call, and `mode` rules out torch.compile(options=...). The root cause is the flash-attn graph break, which is what routes three very different token counts through one compiled frame. Removing it would help any DiT with mixed sequence lengths and is worth doing separately. Test Plan: Steady-state denoise on one H100, min of requests 2..8 (request 1 carries the compile), stock preset with no extra flags: ``` export CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 CI=1 SGLANG_DIFFUSION_SYNC_STAGE_PROFILING=1 \ FLASHINFER_DISABLE_VERSION_CHECK=1 B=python/sglang/multimodal_gen/.claude/skills/sglang-diffusion-benchmark-profile/scripts/bench_diffusion_denoise.py rm -rf ~/.cache/sgl_diffusion/torch_compile_cache python3 $B --model zimage-base --iterations 8 --label compile --output-dir /tmp/zb python3 $B --model zimage-base --iterations 8 --label eager --no-torch-compile --output-dir /tmp/zb ``` | arm | denoise | | |----------------------|----------|--------------| | torch.compile before | 13.575 s | | | torch.compile after | 9.577 s | 1.42x faster | | eager, for reference | 9.567 s | | First-request e2e goes 79.6 s -> 96.2 s, the cost of autotuning the block at two sizes instead of one. Verified from the generated code that the fused-qkv site is now autotuned at 32, 64, 4096 and 4128 rather than at 32 alone. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32493494360](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32493494360)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32493494260](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32493494260)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32493494399](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32493494399)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [Perf] Tune the W4AFP8 DeepEP low-latency requant launch geometry
signals.text: ## Motivation `fp8_per_token_to_per_tensor_quant_triton()` turns DeepEP low-latency's per-token-group fp8 payload into the per-tensor fp8 that the first CUTLASS W4A8 grouped GEMM consumes. It is a pure streaming pass — two bytes moved and two multiplies per element — but three properties of its launch shape cost more than the arithmetic does. **Access width.** A 1024-element tile over 8 warps is 4 B/thread, which is exactly where Triton stops vectorizing: the compiled kernel contained only `ld.global.b32` / `st.global.b32` on every part tested. 4 warps put 8 B/thread in flight and restore `v2.b32` accesses (2 warps reach `v4.b32`, but measured slower than 4). **Scale addressing.** Scales were indexed on the element axis (`(k_offsets // 128) * stride2`), so each 1024-lane load resolved to 8 distinct addresses read 128 times each. The dispatcher returns the last two scale dims column-major for TMA (`[E, M, hidden // 128]` with `stride1 == 1`), so those 8 addresses are `m` elements apart — a scattered gather, replicated per row, per tile. **Grid shape.** The m-grid was pinned to 32 programs per expert regardless of how many rows were live, so at low-latency decode row counts most programs only loaded `masked_m`, compared, and exited. This is by far the largest effect, and it grows with the local expert count: at 256 local experts and one row each, the kernel spent 35 µs to move 3 µs of data. ## Modifications `python/sglang/kernels/ops/moe/ep_moe_kernels.py` - Tile the payload as `[G_BLOCK_SIZE, 128]` — whole scale groups — instead of a flat run of elements. The per-group scale becomes one scalar load, the fast axis stays contiguous, and a partial `k` masks whole groups. (`K_BLOCK_SIZE` is renamed `G_BLOCK_SIZE` because the constexpr changed units: it counted hidden elements, it now counts 128-wide scale groups, so 8 groups is the old 1024 elements.) - Launch with 4 warps. - A 1024-element tile per program, widening to 2048 once there are >= 32 local experts, where the expert axis alone fills the machine. The tile is kept in *elements* and divided by the scale group width to get `G_BLOCK_SIZE`, because bytes-per-thread is the tuned quantity -- a different group width would otherwise silently halve or double the measured tile. It is also rounded down to the payload, so a small hidden size never runs a mostly-masked tile. - `requant_launch_geometry()` sizes the m-grid from `expected_rows`: one program per expected row, floored at 4, never above the historical 32, and additionally capped by the expert count while fewer than 64 rows per expert are live — past that the extra programs carry real work rather than early exits, and the cap costs a few percent. The estimate is rounded **down** to a power of two because `dispatch_a` already rounds up (it adds the expert count before dividing), so a uniform average of 8 rows arrives as 9 and must not launch 16 programs. The m-grid therefore only ever *shrinks*, which is why no measured cell regresses. - `expected_rows=None` keeps the previous **m-grid** for any other caller; note the tile width and warp count change regardless of that argument. `cutlass_w4a8_moe.py` / `w4afp8.py` — thread the dispatcher's `expected_m` (already computed host-side in `dispatch_a`, and constant for a captured CUDA graph) down to the requant. It is a launch hint only: correctness does not depend on it, and an expert that receives more rows than expected simply loops over more of them. Tests: the GPU unit test covers the geometry combinations (row estimates, 4/40/128 experts, row-major and column-major scales, uneven per-expert row counts); a CPU test pins the heuristic's contracts; and a new `base-b-kernel-benchmark` entry compares the shipped geometry against the previous one. ## Accuracy Tests Output is **bitwise identical to the merged kernel** on H100, H200 and B200 — every shape below at 0, 1, 3, 7, 64 and all padded rows live, both scale layouts, plus a skewed `masked_m` where every expert gets a different row count: ``` == bitwise equality vs main, high expert counts == ok k7168 E64 ok k7168 E128 ok k7168 E256 ok k3584 E112 ok k3584 E256 ok k3584 E512 ALL PASS ``` Unit tests: **48 passed** on H100, H200 and B200 — and across two toolchains, `torch 2.11.0+cu130` / `triton 3.6.0` and `torch 2.13.0+cu130` / `triton 3.7.1` (the newer pair matters because the access-width behaviour this PR exploits is Triton codegen, not hardware). That count includes the existing W4AFP8 dtype and post-reorder CPU tests. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Merged `main` vs this branch, DeepEP column-major scales, timed inside a CUDA graph, variants interleaved and order-swapped (the first variant measured reads ~10% fast on sub-2 µs shapes). `rows` is live rows per expert, and the row estimate passed in is what `dispatch_a` would report for that dispatch. **8 to 56 local experts** | shape | rows | H100 | H200 | B200 | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 7168, 8 experts | 8 / 32 | 1.03x / 1.11x | 1.08x / 1.10x | 0.98x / 1.18x | | | 512 / 1024 | 1.18x / 1.18x | 1.25x / 1.24x | 1.33x / **1.48x** | | 3584, 8 experts | 8 / 32 | 1.23x / 1.15x | 1.27x / 1.14x | 1.01x / 1.14x | | | 512 / 1024 | 1.15x / 1.06x | 1.28x / 1.07x | 1.22x / 1.24x | | 3584, 56 experts | 8 / 32 | **2.43x** / 1.85x | **2.51x** / 1.92x | **2.32x** / 2.00x | | | 128 / 256 | 1.30x / 1.21x | 1.52x / 1.39x | 1.74x / 1.84x | | 1152, 8 experts | 8 / 32 | 1.06x / 1.06x | 1.11x / 1.07x | 1.01x / 1.05x | | | 512 / 1024 | 1.18x / 1.19x | 1.19x / 1.20x | 1.16x / 1.19x | The single sub-1.00x cell is B200 at 8 rows: 1.84 vs 1.87 µs, a 0.03 µs tie. **64 to 512 local experts** — where the old fixed grid hurt most (`main` µs -> branch µs on H100): | shape | rows=1 | rows=8 | rows=32 | rows=128 | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 7168, 64 experts | 9.3 -> 1.9 (**4.9x**) | 9.6 -> 3.1 (3.1x) | 13.3 -> 7.3 (1.81x) | 53.2 -> 44.4 (1.20x) | | 7168, 128 experts | 18.1 -> 2.1 (**8.6x**) | 18.2 -> 4.5 (4.1x) | 33.5 -> 23.5 (1.42x) | 101.5 -> 84.0 (1.21x) | | 7168, 256 experts | 35.3 -> 3.3 (**10.6x**) | 35.8 -> 7.9 (4.6x) | 64.8 -> 44.5 (1.46x) | 195.2 -> 161.4 (1.21x) | | 3584, 112 experts | 9.5 -> 1.8 (5.2x) | 9.6 -> 2.8 (3.5x) | 13.5 -> 6.4 (2.10x) | 47.5 -> 38.7 (1.23x) | | 3584, 256 experts | 20.6 -> 2.2 (9.2x) | 20.7 -> 4.1 (5.0x) | 37.7 -> 22.6 (1.67x) | 102.2 -> 82.4 (1.24x) | | 3584, 512 experts | 40.3 -> 3.3 (**12.1x**) | 41.0 -> 8.2 (5.0x) | 73.7 -> 44.7 (1.65x) | — | H200 and B200 are the same shape and generally better at >= 32 rows: e.g. 3584 / 512 experts at 32 rows is 2.07x on H200 and 2.86x on B200, and 7168 / 256 experts at 128 rows is 1.39x / 1.87x. **Rounding the row estimate down rather than up** (both directions measured at the same shapes): | shape | true rows | H100 (triton 3.6 / 3.7.1) | H200 | B200 | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 7168, 8 experts | 4 | +12.1% / +0.3% | +12.5% | +12.3% | | 3584, 56 experts | 8 | +3.5% / +3.0% | +4.9% | +6.1% | | 3584, 128 experts | 4 | +7.4% / +8.0% | +8.1% | +8.9% | Positive means rounding up is slower. Triton 3.7.1 closes the 7168 case to a tie but never reverses the direction. The in-tree benchmark reproduces the low-expert-count end (H200, µs): ``` hidden num_experts m rows | tuned legacy-geometry 7168 8 1024 8 | 1.5698 2.2400 7168 8 1024 256 | 8.9140 11.0138 3584 56 256 8 | 2.3238 5.5467 3584 56 256 256 | 28.9774 39.4359 ``` Two things I would flag rather than hide. The heuristic was fitted from sweeps of `m_grid ∈ {1..64}` x `g_block ∈ {8, 16, 32}` over hidden sizes 1152/3584/7168, expert counts 8 to 512 and row counts 1 to 256, on all three parts; the shipped choice lands within ~0-5% of the per-cell optimum in the low-latency decode range, with a few ~8-12% outliers on sub-4 µs shapes at very high expert counts. And the *best* tile/warp pair is architecture-dependent at high expert counts — the parts disagree there — so the values here are the ones that win on all of them, and closing the remaining few percent would need autotuning rather than constants. Not covered: a multi-node end-to-end decode run. This is a kernel-level change with bitwise-equal output, so the risk is confined to performance, but the e2e number is still outstanding. H20 was not measured — it is not present in either of our GPU fleets. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). — no user-facing behaviour or flags change. - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32545378258](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32545378258)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32545378103](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32545378103)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32545378287](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32545378287)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [AMD][CI] Fix ROCm 7.0's dead apt index fail the MORI dependency install
signals.text: ## Motivation Fixes cluster **R387** from the Aug-20 AMD CI monitor report: all 27 jobs in [PR Test ROCm 7.0 (AMD) run 32399046576](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32399046576), plus the nightly-7.0 kimi-k26 job, died identically in "Install dependencies". The report filed this as pure infra needing an AMD artifactory restore. **It is also a code regression, it is specific to ROCm 7.0, and the code half is fixable here.** From the failing [job log](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32399046576/job/96522664507): ``` Err:13 http://compute-artifactory.amd.com/artifactory/list/rocm-osdb-22.04-deb compute-rocm-rel-7.0/38 amd64 Packages 404 Not Found [IP: 10.216.51.87 80] Fetched 48.0 MB in 3s (18.2 MB/s) E: Some index files failed to download. They have been ignored, or old ones used instead. ##[error]Process completed with exit code 100. ``` ### Where it came from The `apt-get update` is new. It was added on 2026-08-20 by c7478228dd (#30984, the ROCm 7.2.4 / Python 3.12 / torch 2.11 upgrade), inside a `docker exec ... bash -c` that runs under `set -euo pipefail`: ```bash git submodule update --init --recursive apt-get update apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends libgrpc++-dev 2>/dev/null || true ``` Every *other* change that PR made to this script is gated on the image flavor — the extras swap (`dev_hip` → `dev_hip_rocm724`), the AITER `torch.Stream` patch, and the AITER commit lookup all sit behind `IMAGE_STAGE_SUFFIX == "-rocm724"`. These two apt lines are the only ungated change in the PR, so a 7.2.4 fix also began running on ROCm 7.0. Before that commit the MORI reinstall did no apt work at all and was immune. ### Why only ROCm 7.0 Not because the code path is 7.0-specific — the identical path runs on 7.2.4 and passes. It is purely base-image lineage: | Flavor | Base image | `rocm-osdb` source | |---|---|---| | 7.0 | `rocm/sgl-dev:rocm7-vllm-20250904` (AMD-internal dev image) | **yes** | | 7.2.0 | `rocm/pytorch:rocm7.2_ubuntu22.04_py3.10_pytorch_release_2.9.1` | no | | 7.2.4 | `rocm/pytorch:rocm7.2.4_ubuntu24.04_py3.12_pytorch_release_2.10.0` | no | Only 7.0 builds on an AMD-internal image, which is what drags in `compute-artifactory.amd.com/.../rocm-osdb-22.04-deb`. The dead index name encodes it exactly: `compute-rocm-rel-7.0/38` is the internal ROCm 7.0 release channel, build 38. Confirmed against a real 7.2.4 job from the same day ([96420374950](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32367546070/job/96420375378)), which runs the same MORI reinstall and the same `apt-get update` and succeeds, fetching 40.1 MB cleanly. Its apt hosts are entirely public, with no `compute-artifactory.amd.com` entry. (7.2.0 is inferred from the same public lineage rather than observed — nothing currently runs it, since the PR gate defaults to `rocm724`.) ### Why the guard is not just about rocm-osdb That step reaches **six** external apt hosts: ``` http://compute-artifactory.amd.com ← the one that died https://apt.llvm.org https://archive.ubuntu.com https://packages.broadcom.com https://ppa.launchpadcontent.net https://repo.radeon.com ``` `apt-get update` returns non-zero if *any* index fails, so under `set -e` each of those six is a single point of failure for the whole AMD fleet — for a package that is optional. This is not hypothetical: R391, the cluster that turned the AMD docker build red the same day, was an `apt.llvm.org` GPG/curl failure, also on that list. Note too that apt itself treated the failure as recoverable — "They have been ignored, or old ones used instead" — and every index we actually use fetched fine. Nothing in this repo installs from `rocm-osdb`; it is inherited from the base image. ## Modifications `scripts/ci/amd/amd_ci_install_dependency.sh` only. Two changes, addressing the root cause and the blast radius separately: **1. Run the apt step only on `rocm724`.** Only that base actually lacks the package — its job log shows `libgrpc++-dev` "previously unselected", downloaded from `noble/universe` and unpacked. ROCm 7.0 and 7.2.0 built MORI without it for months before #30984, so there the apt round trip is pure risk, and 7.0 is precisely the image carrying the dead source. This restores pre-#30984 behaviour on 7.0/7.2.0 rather than merely tolerating the failure there. **2. Keep both apt steps non-fatal where they do run**, and log which one degraded: ```bash if [ '${IMAGE_STAGE_SUFFIX}' = '-rocm724' ]; then apt-get update || echo '[MORI] apt-get update reported errors; continuing with the indexes it did fetch' apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends libgrpc++-dev || echo '[MORI] libgrpc++-dev unavailable; building MORI without it' fi ``` The gate alone would fix the reported incident but leave 7.2.4 exposed to the other five hosts; the guard alone would tolerate a failure that 7.0 and 7.2.0 need not risk at all. Dropping `2>/dev/null` in favour of an explicit message keeps a degraded install visible instead of swallowing it. No retry logic is added: the image already sets `Acquire::Retries "5"` via `/etc/apt/apt.conf.d/80-net-hardening` (visible in the log as the repeated `Ign:13` attempts), and a 404 is not retryable. This was the only unguarded `apt-get update` left in the AMD CI path; every other one under `scripts/ci/` is already `|| true` or wrapped in a retry loop, matching `scripts/ci/cuda/ci_install_dependency.sh`. **`test/registered/unit/tools/test_amd_ci_install_dependency.py`** — a 45-line guard asserting that no `apt-get` call in this script can abort the run. It runs on `base-a-test-cpu` (no docker, no ROCm, no GPU) alongside the existing CI-tooling tests in `test/registered/unit/tools/`. It carries more weight than it looks, because **no pull-request-triggered workflow can catch this regression**. `pr-test-amd.yml` (ROCm 7.0) was demoted to a daily shadow in #34204 and now has only `schedule` / `workflow_dispatch` / `workflow_call` triggers — no `pull_request`. The PR gate is `pr-test-amd-rocm720.yml`, which defaults to `rocm724`. So the image carrying the dead index is never exercised pre-merge, and the static check is the only pre-merge signal on this invariant. ### Not addressed here Removing the `rocm-osdb` source from the ROCm 7.0 image itself would be the cleanest cleanup, but it needs a `docker/rocm.Dockerfile` change plus an image rebuild — and `release-docker-amd-nightly` is currently red (R391), so it could not ship now. It would also only remove one of the six hosts. Worth a separate PR once the image pipeline is healthy. ## Accuracy Tests Not applicable — CI dependency-install script and its test only; no runtime or model code touched. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not applicable. ## Verification The unit test fails against the pre-fix script, naming the offending line, and passes against the fix: ``` # against the pre-fix script AssertionError: Lists differ: ['apt-get update'] != [] # against this branch 1 passed ``` The flavor gate was verified by expanding it for each `IMAGE_STAGE_SUFFIX` value against a stub `apt-get` that exits 100, checking both whether apt ran and whether the MORI build after it is still reached: ``` PASS flavor='<7.0>' apt ran: no build reached: yes PASS flavor='-rocm720' apt ran: no build reached: yes PASS flavor='-rocm724' apt ran: yes build reached: yes ``` While developing the original guard I also replayed the incident end to end — a stub `apt-get` reproducing the 404 and exit 100, driving the apt lines extracted from the script inside the same `set -euo pipefail` context — confirming the MORI build is still reached both when `libgrpc++-dev` remains resolvable and when it does not, with no regression on the healthy path. Also run: the full `test/registered/unit/tools/` directory (12 passed), `run_suite.py` collection with `sanity_check=True` plus `validate_all_suites` over all registered files (clean; the new test resolves into `base-a-test-cpu`), `shellcheck -S warning` (no new findings — the only remaining warning is a pre-existing `SC2034`), `bash -n`, `black`, `isort`, `ruff`, `codespell`, and the `check-registered-tests` / `check-no-bare-pytest-main` lint hooks. **Note for reviewers:** this PR's own AMD CI cannot reproduce R387 — it runs 7.2.4, whose public base has no `rocm-osdb` source. In-situ validation needs the daily `pr-test-amd.yml` cron (17:30 UTC) or a manual `workflow_dispatch` of it. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). — n/a. - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). — n/a. - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process). 2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers. 3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32442764695](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32442764695)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32442764522](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32442764522)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32442764708](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32442764708)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->
