signals.title: [P/D disagg] Decode-side radix cache for DeepSeek-V4 (DSA compressed KV)
signals.text: ## Motivation Extend the decode-side radix cache for SWA hybrid models in P/D disaggregation to **DeepSeek-V4** (DSA compressed KV). DSV4 was previously rejected at startup; on CUDA the rejection is unnecessary: - The c4 / c4-indexer / c128 pools have **no allocator of their own** — their rows derive positionally from the virtual full-id space (`full_id // ratio`) and live/die with the FULL allocator's pages. The `[FULL, SWA]` unified-tree components therefore already keep every compressed pool coherent on prefix reuse (this is also why non-disaggregated radix caching already works for DSV4). - `page_size` 256 is a multiple of both 4 and 128, so a page-aligned prefix boundary is always a compressed-group boundary. - The existing SWA-tail prealloc machinery (prefix cap at the sliding-window start, extra-window retention, SWA lock-uuid protocol, dual-pool budgets) applies unchanged; DSV4 already runs it today without radix. The guard now keeps **NPU** (separate c4/c128 allocators + a tree-level C128 sidecar, not wired for the decode-radix lock path) and **HIP** (unified-kv SWA ring is per-request, not content-stable) rejected with explicit errors, and only opens the CUDA path. Also fixes a latent cache-hit-kit bug: a router's `/server_info` does not expose the backend page size, so the expected-cache computation ran with `page_size=1` (no alignment). The gpt-oss coverage survived only because `384 + 64` divides by 64 exactly. The kit now takes an explicit `page_size`, and the decode-radix mixin probes the decode server for it. ## Test - New `test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_kv_cache_builder_decode_radix_guards.py` (CPU): NPU/HIP rejections hold, CUDA passes. - `test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_decode_radix_lock_ref.py`: DSV4-geometry property test — with window 128 < page 256 the radix prefix cap stays page- and compress-group-aligned, keeps one full window before the insert boundary, and prompts ≤ 512 tokens reuse nothing. - New `test/registered/disaggregation/test_disaggregation_decode_radix_cache_swa_dsv4.py` (8-gpu-h200, extra-b): DeepSeek-V4-Flash-FP8, non-spec, mooncake; multi-turn cache-hit growth + two-pass GSM8K non-regression via the shared mixin (now parameterized). - CPU: guards + lock_ref + queue_cleanup + hisparse_allocator — 28 passed; unified radix cache suite — 1082 passed, 50 subtests. - End-to-end on 8xH20, 4P+4D, nixl, DeepSeek-V4-Flash (MXFP4), non-spec: - multi-turn cache hits `0 -> 1024 -> 2048` cached tokens per client across rounds, matching page-aligned expectations exactly, identical before and after GSM8K churn; - two-pass GSM8K (100 examples): **0.96 / 0.96, zero drop**, second pass faster (981 vs 950 tok/s); - idle full/swa usage returns to ~0; no asserts, no 503 aborts, no retractions. - End-to-end **cross-node** on 2x 8xH20 (dedicated prefill node + decode node, 8P+8D, tp=8 each, sglang-router), nixl, DeepSeek-V4-Flash (MXFP4), non-spec: - repeated 1201-token prompts through the router: `cached_tokens` `0 -> 1024` across passes (page-256 aligned), decode-side prefix reuse intact across nodes; - GSM8K sanity through the router: 50/50 correct, 0 truncations, 0 errors; - shared-prefix benchmark (`generated-shared-prefix`: 8 groups x 32 prompts, 8192-token shared system prompt, 128-token question, 256 output tokens; 256 requests, max-concurrency 32), decode radix ON vs OFF (flag removed, otherwise identical cluster): | metric | radix ON | baseline | delta | |---|---|---|---| | median TTFT | 1,226 ms | 1,919 ms | **-36%** | | mean TTFT | 2,589 ms | 2,969 ms | -13% | | P90 TTFT | 7,976 ms | 8,763 ms | -9% | | median E2E | 5,024 ms | 5,458 ms | -8% | | request throughput | 5.00 req/s | 4.84 req/s | +3.3% | | output throughput | 1,280 tok/s | 1,239 tok/s | +3.3% | - both runs 256/256 successful, zero errors/retractions. The throughput delta is modest because the workload is decode-dominated (256 output tokens per request); the cache removes the per-request cross-node KV transfer of the ~8.2k-token shared prefix, which lands in TTFT. The test cluster routes UCX over TCP (no cross-subnet RoCE on its fabric), which amplifies the transfer savings — on an RDMA fabric the absolute TTFT gap is expected to narrow, with the direction unchanged. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to the [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32484214033](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32484214033)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32484213817](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32484213817)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32484214002](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32484214002)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: refactor(disagg): remove unreferenced dead code
signals.text: ## Motivation Four symbols in `python/sglang/srt/disaggregation/` have no callers anywhere in the repo. They are not private helpers awaiting a caller — each one's live replacement or live sibling is sitting right next to it, which is what makes the deletion safe to reason about. The clearest case is `page_indices_to_cp_rank_page_indices`. It became dead in 1adb53f14 ("Fix CP page filtering by request-local position", #28718), which reimplemented its only caller `filter_kv_indices_for_cp_rank` on top of the new `_get_cp_rank_page_bounds` helper but left the old function behind. That means the CP correctness fix in #28718 was applied to code nothing calls. ## Modifications Pure deletion, 4 files, 0 insertions / 76 deletions. No behavior change. | Symbol | File | Why it is dead | |---|---|---| | `page_indices_to_cp_rank_page_indices` | `utils.py` | Orphaned by #28718; `_get_cp_rank_page_bounds` directly above it is the live replacement | | `KVArgs.ib_traffic_class` | `base/conn.py` | Bare annotation, never assigned or read. Its neighbor `ib_device` *is* live (set in `prefill.py`/`decode.py`, consumed by `mori/conn.py`) | | `get_transferred_rids` | `prefill.py` | Docstring claims "Used by PP", but no PP path references it. `scheduler_pp_mixin.py` calls `poll_and_all_reduce_attn_cp_tp_group` directly | | `StagingAllocator.get_round` | `common/staging_buffer.py` | Third of three accessors over the same tuple; `get_ptr`/`get_offset` have callers, this never did. The round is still reachable via `get_watermark()` | One note on `get_transferred_rids`: it calls `poll_and_all_reduce_attn_cp_tp_group`, which is a **collective**. An accidental caller reaching it on only some ranks would hang, so removing it is slightly safer than leaving it available. Deliberately **not** removed, though a plain grep also finds no callers — these are extension points, not dead code: - `EventPublisherFactory.register_publisher` (`kv_events.py`) — plugin registration hook; removing it would break out-of-tree publishers. - The empty `MooncakeKVBootstrapServer` / `MoriKVBootstrapServer` / `NixlKVBootstrapServer` and `AscendKV*` subclasses. - FastAPI route handlers in `encode_server.py` / `encode_receiver.py`, which are reached via their decorators. ## Accuracy Tests Not applicable — no model output, kernel, or forward path is touched. Every hunk is a deletion of code with no callers. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not applicable — no code on any execution path changed. ## Verification performed - No caller for any of the four across `.py` / `.md` / `.sh` / `.rs` in `python/`, `test/`, `docs/`, `sgl-router/`, `benchmark/`. - No import orphaned by the removals: `np` still has 6 uses in `utils.py`; `List[` 8 uses and `poll_and_all_reduce_attn_cp_tp_group` 6 uses in `prefill.py`. - `ruff 0.15.1 --select=F401,F821,UP037` (the pinned pre-commit config) passes, as do the pinned `black 26.1.0` and `isort 7.0.0`. Disaggregation integration tests were **not** run locally (they need multi-GPU hardware). For deletions of uncalled code, the reference sweep plus the F401/F821 pass is the substantive evidence; CI should confirm. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). — N/A: removal of code with no callers adds no testable behavior. - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). — N/A: none of these symbols are documented. - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results. — N/A, see above. - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32469085221](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32469085221)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32469085104](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32469085104)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32469085156](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32469085156)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [WIP] [Diffusion] Add configurable reference image resizing for MiniMax H3 Ref2VA
signals.text: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation <!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. --> MiniMax H3 Ref2VA currently resizes every reference image to a fixed 2048-pixel short edge, including upscaling smaller inputs. This behavior matches the original Diffusers preprocessing, but some distilled Ref2VA checkpoints use a different reference-image preprocessing policy during training. For example, ModelTC's MiniMax-H3-Turbo Ref2VA checkpoint recommends matching the reference-image pixel area to the target video canvas: https://github.com/ModelTC/Minimax-H3-Turbo#note-on-reference-image-resizing In addition to this, Comfy also offers two different resize modes: https://docs.comfy.org/tutorials/video/minimax/minimax-h3#prompting-tips-3 Using a different resize policy at inference time can result in: - a mismatch between training and inference preprocessing; - unnecessarily large reference-image token sequences; - increased memory usage from upscaling small reference images; - degraded Ref2VA conditioning quality. This PR adds configurable reference-image resizing for MiniMax H3 Ref2VA while preserving the existing SGLang behavior as the default. ## Modifications <!-- Detail the changes made in this pull request. --> ### Add `reference_resize_mode` Add a new MiniMax H3 sampling parameter: ```python reference_resize_mode: str = "diffusers" ``` Supported values: | Mode | Behavior | |---|---| | `match` | Match the reference-image pixel area to the resolved target canvas while preserving aspect ratio. Smaller references are not upscaled. | | `max` | Downscale only when the reference-image short edge exceeds 2048 pixels. | | `diffusers` | Always resize the reference-image short edge to 2048 pixels, including upscaling. | The default remains `diffusers` to preserve existing SGLang behavior. ### Propagate the parameter through all request paths The parameter is supported by: - offline `DiffGenerator` requests; - JSON `/v1/videos` requests; - multipart `/v1/videos` requests; - dynamic batching and disaggregated request transfer through `SamplingParams`. The HTTP video adapter only adds the parameter to lowered sampling kwargs when it was explicitly provided. This ensures omitted values continue to use the `diffusers` default. Example: ```json { "task": "ref2va", "reference_resize_mode": "match", "target": { "short_edge": 544, "aspect_ratio": "16:9", "duration_seconds": 5.0 } } ``` ### Resolve `match` against the final target canvas Reference-image geometry is resolved during pre-queue admission, after the target video canvas has been finalized. For `match`, the scale factor is: ```python scale = min(1.0, sqrt(target_area / reference_area)) ``` The resized dimensions: - preserve the reference-image aspect ratio; - are independently rounded to the nearest multiple of 32; - do not crop the source image; - do not upscale smaller reference images. This policy applies only to Ref2VA image references using the `image.reference_preserve` material chain. FL2VA first/last keyframes continue to use the existing `image.target_canvas` path and are unaffected. ### Misc For the default `diffusers` mode, the existing shape policy identifier is preserved: ```text reference_image_short_edge_v1 ``` The new modes use: ```text reference_image_match_v1 reference_image_max_v1 ``` This avoids breaking external logs, tests, or consumers that depend on the existing `shape_policy_version`. ## Accuracy Tests <!-- If this pull request affects model outputs (e.g., changes to the kernel or model forward code), provide accuracy test results. --> This PR changes only MiniMax-H3 Ref2VA reference-image preprocessing. It does not modify model weights, kernels, or forward-pass math. The default `diffusers` policy remains backward compatible: - Reference-image short edge remains 2048. - Upscaling behavior is unchanged. - `shape_policy_version` remains `reference_image_short_edge_v1`. The opt-in `match` and `max` policies intentionally change Ref2VA conditioning inputs. Added deterministic unit tests cover: - `match`: matches the target canvas pixel area while preserving aspect ratio. - `match`: does not upscale smaller reference images. - `max`: caps the reference short edge at 2048 without intentional upscaling. - `diffusers`: preserves the legacy 2048-short-edge behavior and metadata. - Mode normalization and invalid-mode rejection. - Invalid target-canvas rejection. - `/v1/videos` transport of `reference_resize_mode`. - Preservation of the default when the request omits the option. - Prequeue propagation of the selected mode and resolved target canvas. - Backward-compatible prequeue fallback to `diffusers`. Test command: ```bash PYTHONPATH="$PWD/python" python -m pytest -q \ python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_minimax_h3_admission.py \ python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_minimax_h3_media.py \ -k "reference_resize or reference_image_resize" ``` All tests have passed. No end-to-end visual-quality benchmark is required for the unchanged default diffusers path. Visual output changes are expected only when callers explicitly select `match` or `max`. ## Speed Tests and Profiling <!-- If this pull request impacts inference speed, provide benchmarking and profiling results. --> ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process). 2. signals.title: Add PD test for inkling with mxfp8 KV
signals.text: ## Motivation Inkling is the widest single-model exercise of the multi-component state transfer we have. One request carries the main KV list plus four state components, and with MXFP8 KV they cover three of the five index-payload builders: | Component | Index payload | | --- | --- | | `SWA` | window, translated into the SWA index space | | `MAMBA` | per-request ShortConv state slot | | `BLOCK_SCALE` | whole sequence, full KV index space | | `BLOCK_SCALE_SWA` | window, SWA index space | A model that ships one or two components leaves most of that dispatch untested. Nothing launched a PD pair for this one, so registration, per-component index payloads, and the page-granular slicing behind them had no end-to-end guard on the path where they interact -- which is where both of the last two defects in this area lived. MXFP8 KV needs SM100+, so the case is registered on a Blackwell runner. Only the MXFP8 configuration is covered. It is a superset of bf16 at the orchestration level -- same components, same transfer, same hierarchical prefill cache, plus the two scale components -- and bf16 PD is already exercised by the existing disaggregation tests, so a second case would spend another server pair on largely duplicated coverage. HiCache rides the prefill role only: the decode role forces chunk cache, and its radix opt-in is refused for sliding-window models. `start_prefill` / `start_decode` are overridden because the fixture pins `--tp 1`, the same reason `test_disaggregation_dsv4.py` overrides them. ## Verification Five local runs on 4xB200, one prefill and one decode role at TP=2 each, mooncake over IB: 400-491s, gsm8k 0.845-0.890. `est_time=600` covers all of them. The host cache is given an absolute size rather than the default ratio. The ratio scales with the device pool, which put the prefill role alone at ~103 GB of host memory across its ranks and got the pair OOM-killed on a runner; a fixed 8 GB keeps the tiering exercised and the footprint predictable. Reverting the MXFP8 scale exposure takes it red at server launch, so the case guards what it claims to: ``` NotImplementedError: KV transfer / disaggregation is unsupported for MXFP8 KV cache (scale buffers are not exposed). ```

signals.text: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation SGLang only has a single `--json-model-override-args`, and every place that reads the **draft** (speculative) checkpoint's HF config reuses it. There is no way to tweak only the draft model's config (layer count, rope settings, ...) — the same override also lands on the target model. For speculative setups, where the draft path equals the target path, the two cannot be distinguished at all. This PR adds a draft-only override arg; when it is not passed, behavior is identical to before. ## Modifications - New server arg `--speculative-draft-json-model-override-args` (`ServerArgs.speculative_draft_json_model_override_args`, `NS("spec")`, default `None`). Semantics when set are **replace**, not merge. - Docs: new row in the Speculative decoding table of `docs/docs/advanced_features/server_arguments.mdx`. ## Accuracy Tests Not applicable — no kernel or model forward change. signals.title: [NPU] Introduce minimal DeviceOperator for runtime layout adaptation
signals.text: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation Ascend generations may require different runtime representations for the same semantic data. Today, the MXFP MoE routing path directly normalizes the E8M0 scale layout in init_routing.py: npu_moe_init_routing_v2 (quant_mode=3) produces a flat [N, M] scale while the downstream A5 grouped-matmul path consumes the pair-split [N, M/2, 2] representation. This introduces a minimal DeviceOperator abstraction following #35709 and moves this runtime-visible layout adaptation out of the MoE feature code: <!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. --> ## Modifications - AscendDeviceGeneration + get_npu_device_generation(): centralized, cached generation detection (Ascend950 -> A5, else LEGACY; current device is probed, never a hardcoded device 0) - BaseDeviceOperator / A5DeviceOperator with the first contract, normalize_mxfp_scale_layout(); Base is identity (legacy representation = producer's native layout), A5 performs the existing pair-split - get_device_operator() lazy factory: importing the module never probes the device - init_routing.py: _normalize_mxfp_scale() removed; the MXFP8 branch now delegates to the DeviceOperator, keeping the quant decision (quant_mode == MXFP8_QUANT_MODE) in feature code The change is intentionally small: kernel/provider differences remain outside this abstraction. signals.title: refactor(disagg): collapse duplicated branches in get_kv_class
signals.text: ## Motivation `get_kv_class` in `python/sglang/srt/disaggregation/utils.py` dispatches to per-backend KV classes through five `elif` branches. Each branch repeated the same boilerplate: - `from sglang.srt.disaggregation.base import KVArgs` plus a `KVClassType.KVARGS: KVArgs` entry — every backend maps `KVARGS` to the *same* class, so this was duplicated five times for no reason. - `return class_mapping.get(class_type)` as the branch's last statement, five times. There was also a stale `from sglang.srt.disaggregation.fake import FakeKVReceiver, FakeKVSender` at the top of the function body. It is unused: the `FAKE` branch re-imports what it needs, so those two names were pulled in on *every* call regardless of backend and then never referenced. Plus five vestigial single-element parens, `KVClassType.RECEIVER: (MooncakeKVReceiver)`, which are just the bare name. ## Modifications 1 file, +14 / -22. Purely structural: - Hoists the shared `KVArgs` lookup into one early return at the top. - Removes the five per-branch `KVArgs` imports and `KVClassType.KVARGS` entries. - Moves the `ValueError` for an unknown backend into an `else`, so each branch only builds `class_mapping` and there is a single `return class_mapping.get(class_type)` at the end. - Drops the stale `fake` import and the five redundant parens. Two properties are deliberately preserved: **Per-backend imports stay explicit.** The regular naming would allow collapsing this to a `getattr(module, prefix + suffix)` table of about ten lines. That is intentionally *not* done — it would break `grep MooncakeKVSender` as a way to find this dispatch, and static analysis could no longer follow it. Each backend module is still imported lazily on its own branch only, so importing `utils` does not drag in mooncake/nixl/mori/ascend. **`FAKE` + `BOOTSTRAP_SERVER` -> `None`.** The fake backend's mapping has no `BOOTSTRAP_SERVER` key, so that combination returns `None` via `.get()`. `managers/disagg_service.py` calls `get_kv_class(..., BOOTSTRAP_SERVER)`, so this is load-bearing. A comment was added rather than "fixing" it into a raise. ## Accuracy Tests Not applicable — no model output, kernel, or forward path is touched. This is a class-lookup table. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not applicable. The function runs a handful of times at PD server startup, not on any per-request path. ## Verification performed Behavior equivalence was checked directly rather than by inspection. Both the pre- and post-change `get_kv_class` were extracted via AST, executed against stub backend modules, and compared across **all 26 `(TransferBackend, KVClassType)` combinations plus an unknown-backend case**. Every case returns the identical class, including: - `FAKE` + `BOOTSTRAP_SERVER` -> `None` - unknown backend -> `ValueError` Also: pinned `ruff 0.15.1 --select=F401,F821,UP037` (the pre-commit config) passes, plus pinned `black 26.1.0` and `isort 7.0.0`. F401 is the relevant check here since the change removes an import. Disaggregation integration tests were **not** run locally (they need multi-GPU hardware). Note this function is exercised on every PD server start via `prefill.py`, `decode.py`, and `disagg_service.py`, so any CI job that boots a PD pair covers it. Part of a small series of independent disaggregation cleanups. Related: #35838, #35843, #35844. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). — N/A: no behavior change; equivalence over all 26 dispatch combinations is documented above. - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). — N/A: internal dispatch helper, not documented. - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results. — N/A, see above. - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32470570755](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32470570755)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32470570273](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32470570273)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32470570385](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32470570385)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [DeepSeek-V4][DSpark] Handle zero-length CUDA graph padding in online C128 planner
signals.text: ## Motivation Fix online C128 compression for DeepSeek-V4 with DSpark compact ragged verification and CUDA graph enabled. The issue can be reproduced with: ```bash SGLANG_OPT_USE_ONLINE_COMPRESS=1 SGLANG_EXPERIMENTAL_ONLINE_C128_DSPARK=1 SGLANG_RAGGED_VERIFY_MODE=compact ``` DSpark compact verification uses ragged verify lengths. During CUDA graph replay, the request batch is padded to the selected graph bucket size. Rows that do not correspond to active requests are represented by: ```txt extend_len = 0 ``` These padded rows contain no query tokens and should not generate online C128 compression or state-pool write plans. Previously, _plan_prefill_partial required every row to satisfy: ```cpp 0 < extend_len && extend_len <= seq_len ``` As a result, the first CUDA graph replay containing padded DSpark rows failed with a RuntimeCheck. This was not normally observed in the Eagle/MTP path because its verification layout uses a fixed number of draft tokens for every request row. DSpark compact verification, however, has variable verify lengths and zero-length graph padding rows. Changes - Allow extend_len == 0 in the online C128 prefill planner. - Skip zero-length padded rows because they own no query tokens and must not produce PlanC, PlanW, or state-pool entries. - Preserve validation that extend_len must not exceed seq_len. - Add a detailed error message containing the invalid lengths and batch row index. This PR is bound to PR32035 and needs to be tested on PR32035.https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32035 <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32470841798](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32470841798)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32470841770](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32470841770)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32470841913](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32470841913)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [Diffusion][minimax-h3] Restrict MiniMax-H3 SubBlock sparsity to video queries
signals.text: ## Motivation MiniMax-H3 packs text, condition-image/video, target-video, and audio tokens into the same denoising sequence. The existing SubBlock path applies sparse attention to every query in that packed sequence, even though the sparsity policy is primarily intended for video queries. The audio latent sequence is substantially shorter than the video latent sequence and does not have the same spatial redundancy as video tokens. Applying the same 64-token block granularity and sparsity ratio to audio queries therefore produces a much coarser approximation: sparsifying a small number of audio query blocks affects a larger fraction of the generated audio. This makes short audio tracks particularly sensitive, especially near the end of a 5-second generation. Text, condition-image, audio, and mixed-modality query blocks do not benefit from the video-specific sparsity policy and may lose relevant K/V context when routed with the same top-k budget. This PR restricts sparse block selection to pure-video query blocks. Query blocks containing text, condition-image, audio, or mixed rows retain all K/V blocks and therefore execute dense attention inside the same BSA kernel. Reference-video and target-video rows remain eligible for sparse routing. ## Modifications - Track video-query provenance through MiniMax-H3 presentation, text encoding, packed-sequence preparation, and denoising. - Include target-video rows, reference-video latent rows, and Ref2VA Qwen video-placeholder rows in the video-query provenance. - Keep text, condition-image, audio, timestamp, vision-delimiter, and mixed-modality rows non-video. - Build a request-static query-block mask at the existing 64-token SubBlock granularity. - Classify each query block as: - sparse when all real rows in the block are video rows; - dense when the block contains any text, condition-image, audio, or mixed-modality row. - Keep mixed video/non-video boundary blocks dense so every non-video row retains exact attention. - Build one heterogeneous BSA block-index/count representation: - pure-video query blocks keep the router-selected top-k K/V blocks; - non-video and mixed query blocks keep all K/V blocks. - Execute the complete real packed document through one heterogeneous BSA call; the padding-only document keeps the existing dense fallback. - Use the existing per-query-block count interfaces: - SM90: `mask_block_cnt`; - SM100: `q2k_block_nums`. - Sort compact sparse prefixes before heterogeneous expansion only on SM90, where the kernel requires ordered active prefixes. - Preserve the router output order on SM100 and avoid an unnecessary GPU sort. - Avoid the additional dense FA call, video-Q gather, and dense/sparse output scatter required by the earlier two-attention prototype. - Preserve the existing SubBlock kernel contract: - 64-token query/key blocks; - SM90 SGLang CuTe-DSL kernel; - SM100 FlashInfer `bsa_attn_blk64_fwd`. - Resolve the effective MiniMax-H3 transformer backend through one H3-specific helper with selector-compatible precedence, and use the same resolution logic for admission, text metadata, and denoising metadata. - Preserve loader-scoped `transformer` component attention overrides across MiniMax-H3's lazy DiT attention initialization. - Allow configurations such as a global FA backend with `transformer=subblock_sparse_attn`. - Reject Ring parallelism unless the resolved MiniMax-H3 transformer backend is FA. - Gate video provenance and heterogeneous routing to MiniMax-H3 requests whose effective transformer backend is `subblock_sparse_attn`. - Keep non-SubBlock MiniMax-H3 execution and the behavior of all other diffusion models unchanged. - Add tests for: - video-query provenance; - pure-video and mixed query-block classification; - ragged final query blocks; - per-query-block dense/sparse counts; ## Accuracy Tests We evaluated one 5-second sample from each supported task: T2VA, FL2VA, and Ref2VA. All runs use 50 denoising steps, a 768-pixel short edge, 24 fps, and 8xH200 GPUs with SP/Ulysses degree 8. "Before" applies the SubBlock top-k budget to every query block. "After" applies the top-k budget only to pure-video query blocks, while non-video and mixed query blocks retain all K/V blocks. Each SubBlock output is compared with its matching lossless output. The Ref2VA before/after results use the exact same lossless reference. The final Ref2VA rerun was performed with the code from [#35481](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/35481) applied on top of this PR branch. ### Video quality SSIM `↑`: higher is better. | Task | SSIM before ↑ | SSIM after ↑ | Difference ↑ | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | T2VA | 0.751427 | 0.757598 | +0.006171 | | FL2VA | 0.790167 | 0.794569 | +0.004402 | | Ref2VA* | 0.940194 | 0.940913 | +0.000719 | SSIM is measured across all decoded frames using weighted YUV420 SSIM. The heterogeneous BSA implementation preserves visual quality across all three tasks. ### Full-track audio quality Correlation `↑`: higher is better. nMSE `↓`: lower is better. nMSE reduction `↑`: higher is better. | Task | Correlation before ↑ | Correlation after ↑ | nMSE before ↓ | nMSE after ↓ | nMSE reduction ↑ | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | | T2VA | 0.587379 | 0.685984 | 1.192913 | 0.536445 | 55.0% | | FL2VA | 0.752955 | 0.988301 | 1.087023 | 0.023919 | 97.8% | | Ref2VA* | 0.943636 | 0.992069 | 0.109817 | 0.015824 | 85.6% | ### Final-second audio quality Final one-second correlation `↑`: higher is better. Final one-second nMSE `↓`: lower is better. nMSE reduction `↑`: higher is better. | Task | Final 1s correlation before ↑ | Final 1s correlation after ↑ | Final 1s nMSE before ↓ | Final 1s nMSE after ↓ | nMSE reduction ↑ | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | | T2VA | 0.568423 | 0.815203 | 2.770409 | 0.341037 | 87.7% | | FL2VA | 0.878575 | 0.990173 | 0.762153 | 0.019796 | 97.4% | | Ref2VA* | 0.923841 | 0.991169 | 0.145545 | 0.017839 | 87.7% | Audio was decoded to 32 kHz stereo PCM. Correlation is the mean per-channel Pearson correlation after DC removal. nMSE is normalized by the lossless reference signal power. All compared audio tracks contain 165,888 decoded samples per channel. The best measured alignment offset is 0 ms in every comparison, so the improvements are not caused by duration changes, truncation, or codec-padding differences. The result is not expected to be audio-lossless. Video and audio remain coupled through the joint denoiser, so sparse video attention can still affect audio indirectly. This change removes the direct degradation caused by applying the video sparsity policy to non-video queries. \* Ref2VA was benchmarked with [#35481](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/35481) applied on top. ## Speed Tests and Profiling All values below are server-reported generation times after model startup. Latency `↓`: lower is better. Speedup `↑`: higher is better. SubBlock configuration: - `sparsity=0.75` - `n_q=4` - `n_k=4` - `skip_first_steps=10` - `skip_first_layers=0` - `min_seq_len=4096` ### Before: uniform sparse budget for all query blocks | Task | Lossless latency ↓ | SubBlock latency ↓ | Speedup ↑ | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | T2VA | 37.769s | 28.790s | 1.312x | | FL2VA | 41.282s | 31.113s | 1.327x | | Ref2VA | 133.510s | 91.470s | 1.460x | ### After: heterogeneous dense/sparse BSA | Task | Lossless latency ↓ | SubBlock latency ↓ | Speedup ↑ | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | T2VA | 37.552s | 28.782s | 1.305x | | FL2VA | 41.007s | 32.142s | 1.276x | | Ref2VA* | 133.510s | 92.020s | 1.451x | ### Heterogeneous-routing overhead Latency change `↓`: lower is better. | Task | SubBlock before ↓ | SubBlock after ↓ | Latency change ↓ | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | T2VA | 28.790s | 28.782s | -0.03% | | FL2VA | 31.113s | 32.142s | +3.3% | | Ref2VA* | 91.470s | 92.020s | +0.6% | The heterogeneous BSA implementation retains a 1.28-1.45x speedup over lossless execution. Compared with the previous uniform-sparsity implementation, the measured latency change ranges from -0.03% to +3.3%. Using one BSA call avoids the additional dense FA launch, video-Q gather, and output scatter of the earlier two-attention prototype. Non-video query blocks execute dense attention by setting their per-query-block count to the complete K/V block count, while pure-video blocks retain the router-selected top-k budget. For the measured T2VA sequence, block alignment keeps 152 of 590 key blocks for each pure-video query block, corresponding to an effective sparsity of 0.7424. \* The final Ref2VA rerun was benchmarked with [#35481](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/35481) applied on top. ## Checklist - [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. signals.title: [MUSA] add platform capability support and skip CUDA-only dtype fallback
signals.text: ## Summary - add in-tree MUSA SRT platform support with CUDA-compatible device ops - make platform auto-discovery select MUSA before CUDA when `torch.version.musa` is present and `torch.musa.is_available()` is true - skip the legacy CUDA sm80 BF16 dtype fallback on MUSA by gating it on `current_platform.is_cuda()` inside the model load flow - bump `srt_musa` dependency on `torchada` to `>=0.1.84` ## Motivation Refs #16565. MUSA support should be explicit at the platform/capability layer instead of reusing CUDA-only fallback logic. ## Verification Verified in a MUSA 4.3.5 / torch 2.9.0 environment with torchada `>=0.1.84` available from source. Inline checks confirmed: - `current_platform` resolves to `MusaSRTPlatform` - `current_platform.is_musa()` is `True` - `torch.musa.is_available()` is `True` - `torch.empty(1, device="cuda").device == musa:0` - `maybe_downgrade_dtype_for_legacy_gpu()` skips CUDA capability checks on non-CUDA platforms and still downgrades bf16 to float16 on legacy CUDA <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32476004882](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32476004882)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32476004703](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32476004703)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32476004818](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32476004818)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [diffusion] Allow Cache-DiT with DiT layerwise offload
signals.text: ## Summary DiT layerwise offload and Cache-DiT can run together. The old startup `ValueError` was an implementation accident, not a real mutex. On one 24GB 4090 D, MiniMax-H3 `fl2va` 1344×768 · 107 frames · **50 NFE** (`kitchen_int8` + FA, DiT+TE layerwise). Layerwise-only vs the same commit without this patch is within noise (**+0.1%**). Prefetch including last-layer wrap is unchanged. | Config | timed e2e | Denoise | vs FA | PSNR vs FA | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:| | Layerwise only | 721.2 s | 700.9 s | — | — | | + Cache-DiT `R=0.24` `W=2` `MC=16` | **173.2 s** | **153.9 s** | 4.16× | 15.90dB | | + `sage_attn` + same | **106.4 s** | **87.1 s** | 6.78× | 15.89dB | | + Cache-DiT `F1B2 W=8 R=0.08 MC=2` | **392.3 s** | **372.7 s** | 1.84× | **30.10dB** | Recommended quality setting: `Fn=1 Bn=2 W=8 R=0.08 MC=2` (30.1 dB, 1.84× vs FA). Spectrum PR [#35684](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/35684) `11/5/1.0` was **285.3 s / 27.4 dB** — faster, slightly lower PSNR. ## Why they conflicted **Layerwise**: most weights stay on CPU. The running layer is copied to GPU; the next layer is prefetched in the background. **Cache-DiT**: a step may skip middle blocks. DBCache always runs the first `Fn` blocks, then on a hit skips `Mn` and (optionally) runs the last `Bn` blocks. Skipped blocks are never `forward`ed.These axes are orthogonal. Skipping a block means *less* H2D, not more. Layerwise assumed every step walks `0..N-1` in order: 1. After layer `i`, prefetch `i+1`. 2. Near the tail, `% N` wraps to the next step's layer 0. A Cache-DiT hit is `0 ──skip 1–5──→ 6 → 7` (8-layer, `Fn=1,Bn=2`): ``` Layerwise assumed: 0 → 1 → 2 → 3 → 4 → 5 → 6 → 7 Cache-DiT actually: 0 ──────── skip 1–5 ──────── → 6 → 7 ``` Layer 1 is prefetched during layer 0 and never posts a release hook, or a wrap/release leaves `empty((1,))` on the next compute layer → **shape mismatch**. The old fix banned the combination at startup. Default `Bn=0`: a hit ends after layer 0. Layer 1 sits on GPU until the next step unless prepare drops it. ## What changed Trust only layers that actually ran. A full-stack step still prefetches as before (including last-layer wrap). - Jump: release the unused gap; sync-load the destination if needed. - Next step: `prepare` drops leftover prefetch (`Bn=0`). - Startup allows Cache-DiT + DiT layerwise. FSDP stays incompatible. No `Fn/Bn` plan is published. The first layer after a skip may sync-load one layer of PCIe. Default `Bn=0` has no Bn to load. | | Before | After | |---|---|---| | Full stack (layerwise only) | Sequential prefetch + wrap | Same | | Cache-DiT skip | Prefetch `i+1` / wrap → empty / crash | Drop the gap, sync-load dest | | Combined | Startup `ValueError` | Allowed | ## Tests ### MiniMax-H3 on 4090 D Protocol unless noted: 1344×768, 107 frames, `kitchen_int8` + FA, `--performance-mode memory`, `--layerwise-offload-components dit,text_encoder`. **Cache-DiT without DiT layerwise** OOM on 24GB (22.94 GiB used, +932 MiB). Same on baseline. Not a regression. **Scheme sweep** (same process, forced skip so DBCache actually jumps). 8 requested steps → 7 NFE; SCM rerun used 9 steps → 8 NFE because `cache_dit.steps_mask` only allows 4 or 6 when `total_steps < 8`. That limit is upstream Cache-DiT, not this patch. No shape-mismatch / empty weight crash on any scheme. | Scheme | Steps | Denoise | E2E | Peak | Result | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---| | Layerwise only | 8 | 97.6 s | 134.4 s | 21.1 GB | ok | | DBCache `F1B0` | 8 | 29.3 s | 47.9 s | 18.4 GB | ok | | DBCache `F1B2` | 8 | 32.0 s | 50.7 s | 18.1 GB | ok | | DBCache `F2B0` | 8 | 30.6 s | 49.4 s | 17.5 GB | ok | | `F1B0` + TaylorSeer O1 | 8 | 29.3 s | 47.8 s | 17.6 GB | ok | | `F1B0` + SCM `fast` | 9 | 71.2 s | 115.3 s | 22.9 GB | ok (5 compute / 3 cache) | | `F1B0` + SCM `medium` | 9 | 83.5 s | 102.4 s | 18.2 GB | ok (6 compute / 2 cache) | Do not stack Spectrum / TeaCache with Cache-DiT. Hooks cover whole-block `forward()` only. ## Example ```bash # Do not pass --quality (H3 generic Cache-DiT is disabled if quality is explicit). sglang generate \ --model-path MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3 \ --model-variant fl2va \ --quantization kitchen_int8 \ --attention-backend fa \ --performance-mode memory \ --layerwise-offload-components dit,text_encoder \ --dit-offload-prefetch-size 1 \ --dit-layerwise-resident-layers 0 \ --enable-cache-dit true \ --cache-dit-params '{"Fn_compute_blocks":1,"Bn_compute_blocks":2,"max_warmup_steps":8,"residual_diff_threshold":0.08,"max_continuous_cached_steps":2}' ``` Layerwise only video: https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b63a2a09-6b8e-46ab-bb00-441cce2830e0 Layerwise +cache-dit video: https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a78e5341-197e-468a-8931-19b811c7245d Need `comfy-kitchen` for `kitchen_int8`. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32475568019](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32475568019)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32475567844](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32475567844)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32475567908](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32475567908)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [diffusion] tolerate an MPS non-layer restore before anything was captured
signals.text: The MPS non-layer weight stores (`_mps_cpu_non_layer_parameters`, `_mps_cpu_buffers`) exist only after `_capture_mps_cpu_non_layer_weights` runs, but a residency strategy can drive a use interval before that — `restore_mps_cpu_non_layer_weights` then raises `AttributeError`, which surfaces out of the scheduler as a generic request failure instead of anything actionable. This gives the stores a class-level `None` default and makes the three consumers (`restore`/`materialize`/`release`) a no-op in that state. The no-op is the correct semantics rather than error-swallowing: nothing was captured, so there is nothing to restore or release, and after capture the attributes are always dicts. The added test drives all three methods on an unconfigured component with MPS stubbed on, and fails with the pre-change `AttributeError` when the guards are removed. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32478082492](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32478082492)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:no_entry_sign: [Run #32478082220](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32478082220)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32478082364](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32478082364)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [diffusion] keep a CPU-started VAE's weights on the checkpoint mapping
signals.text: The VAE loader copied every weight into pre-allocated parameters unless the platform was MPS (`assign=bool(cpu_offload_flag and current_platform.is_mps())`), so a component that starts on the CPU paid its full size in anonymous host memory even though the safetensors mapping already held the bytes. Anonymous pages are exactly what a small host is short of: the page cache can drop and re-fetch file-backed pages, but a copy it cannot. On MiniMax-H3 under a 32 GiB host envelope, the video VAE's copy cost 9.7 GB — measured on one RTX 4090 with identical flags, assigning the mapped tensors instead raises the host memory available at offload-configure time from **8.8 to 18.5 GiB**, which is budget the DiT's pinned prefetch can then actually spend. The load line now reports the placement: `Loaded video_vae: ... host mmap: 9.7` against the previous `host pageable: 9.7`. Assignment replaces a parameter rather than writing through it, so a checkpoint tensor whose dtype differs from its parameter's would silently change the module's dtype; `_match_checkpoint_dtypes` converts those first, which copies exactly the tensors that cannot stay on the mapping. MPS behavior is unchanged — it always assigned. Unit tests cover the dtype-matching helper (left alone / converted / extra key). Verified e2e on the box: the server reaches ready with the VAE on its mapping and no OOM lines. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32539898117](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32539898117)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32539897974](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32539897974)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32539898052](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32539898052)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: fix(kimi-k3): align reported cached tokens with prompt usage
signals.text: ## Motivation For Kimi K3, the reported `prompt_tokens` excludes the three-token assistant generation stub appended by the chat template. However, `cached_tokens` was still reported as the raw physical prefix-cache length. When the cached prefix overlaps the trailing generation stub, `cached_tokens` can exceed `prompt_tokens`. For example: ```text prompt_tokens = 6207 cached_tokens = 6208 ``` This violates the expected invariant that cached tokens are a subset of prompt tokens and can result in inconsistent cache-input accounting or billing. ## Modifications - Added K3-specific normalization for reported cached tokens. - For Kimi K3, reported cached tokens are calculated as: ```python min(raw_cached_tokens, reported_prompt_tokens) ``` This excludes only the portion of the trailing generation stub reached by the cached prefix. - Preserved the original `cached_tokens` value when the cached prefix does not reach the generation stub. - Preserved existing behavior for all non-K3 models. - Applied the normalization consistently to: - Non-streaming Chat Completions - Streaming final usage - Continuous streaming usage - Kept scheduler-side and KV-cache accounting unchanged. The change only affects the OpenAI-compatible usage response. - Added regression coverage for: - K3 cache hits overlapping the generation stub - K3 cache hits ending before the generation stub - Non-K3 cached-token reporting - K3 continuous streaming usage ## Accuracy Tests This change does not affect model inputs, model outputs, kernels, sampling, or model forward execution. It only normalizes usage metadata returned to API clients. The following behavior matrix was verified against the production reporting helpers: ```text Model Raw prompt/cache Reported prompt/cache Kimi K3 6210 / 6000 6207 / 6000 Kimi K3 6210 / 6208 6207 / 6207 Non-K3 6210 / 6208 6210 / 6208 DSV4 6210 / 6208 6210 / 6208 ``` Additional verification: - Python syntax validation passed for the modified implementation and test files. - `git diff --check` passed. - Regression unit tests were added. The unit-test file could not be executed in the local environment because the required `orjson` dependency was unavailable. The tests are expected to run in the standard SGLang CI environment. ## Speed Tests and Profiling No inference benchmark was performed because this change does not modify the inference path. The additional work is limited to the CPU response-serialization path and consists of: - One K3 model-type check - One integer `min()` operation It does not affect tokenization, prefix-cache lookup, scheduling, prefill, decode, KV transfer, or GPU execution. ## Checklist - [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). `pre-commit` was not run in the current local environment. - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). signals.title: model: restore Hunyuan-A13B q/k shape after per-head qk_norm (fix non-CUDA attention crash)
signals.text: ## Motivation Serving `tencent/Hunyuan-A13B-Instruct` (`HunYuanMoEV1ForCausalLM`, `use_qk_norm=True`) on non-CUDA backends (Intel XPU / triton) crashes in attention: ``` RuntimeError: mat1 and mat2 shapes cannot be multiplied (24x128 and 512x4096) ``` `HunYuanAttention.forward`'s `use_qk_norm` path reshapes q/k to `(tokens*heads, head_dim)` for the per-head RMSNorm but never restores the flat `(tokens, heads*head_dim)` shape that RadixAttention / `o_proj` expect. On CUDA the flashinfer backend recomputes the token count from batch metadata, so the mangled leading dim is masked; triton/XPU keys off `q.shape[0]`, so the bad shape reaches `o_proj` (per-rank `512 = 4 heads x 128` at tp-8) and the matmul fails. ## Modifications Restore the flat shape after the per-head norm by appending `.reshape(-1, self.q_size)` / `.reshape(-1, self.kv_size)`, matching the canonical `models/utils.py::apply_qk_norm` (which ends with `q = q_by_head.view(q.shape)`). Only the self-attn `use_qk_norm` path changes; the final tensor shape is identical to before on every backend, so CUDA behavior is unchanged. (The `cross`/CLA path has the same latent missing-restore, but `use_cla=False` for this model, so it is left untouched and flagged for a follow-up.) ## Accuracy Tests Intel XPU, tp-8, bf16 — model loads with 0 skipped params and the server stays healthy through the previously-crashing qk_norm path: - gsm8k 5-shot smoke: 10/10. - gsm8k raw completions (200 samples, max_gen_toks 8192): strict-match 73.5% / flexible-extract 79.5%. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32480991137](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32480991137)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32480990686](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32480990686)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32480990967](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32480990967)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [AMD] Implement DeepSeek V4 DCP on ROCm
signals.text: ## Motivation DeepSeek V4 accepted decode-context-parallel arguments on ROCm, but did not shard its KV and index state across DCP ranks. This PR implements DSV4 decode context parallelism for the ROCm unified-KV backend. ## What changed - Use global logical pages backed by owner-local physical KV pools. - Localize C4/C128 metadata and compressed writes, then gather local candidates for stable global top-k selection. - Build graph-safe decode and prefill index streams. - Merge rank-local attention outputs with natural-log LSE through the validated AG/RS backend. - Account for logical allocation-page geometry in scheduler admission and metrics while preserving the no-DCP unified-KV sink behavior. - Reject unsupported combinations, including A2A/fi_a2a, attention DP, disaggregation, DSA prefill CP, and DSV4 HiCache+DCP. ## Scope This PR is based directly on upstream main. It neither contains nor depends on #35043 or #35233; those stability PRs remain independent and mergeable in either order. DSV4 HiCache+DCP integration is deliberately excluded and will be submitted separately after this backend lands. The generic DCP+DSpark HiCache sizing fix is already upstream in #35221. ## Validation Validated against current `main` on 8x AMD Instinct MI355X: - TP8 no-DCP and TP8/DCP8 AG/RS produced the same 16 output IDs; DCP8 returned all 16 logprobs with zero retractions. - DCP8 pressure test: 8 concurrent 16K requests (131,072 input tokens) all returned HTTP 200 and completed by length with zero retractions; final health checks and service-log scan were clean. Full-model validation used standard NCCL collectives with `--disable-custom-all-reduce`, `SGLANG_USE_AITER_AG=0`, and `SGLANG_DP_USE_REDUCE_SCATTER=0`. AITER custom all-reduce and HiCache stability changes are not included. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32486203443](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32486203443)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32486203536](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32486203536)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32486203329](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32486203329)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [diffusion] refactor: hand out pinned host memory per layer
signals.text: The pin budget was asked once per component, all or nothing, so a DiT larger than the whole spendable budget pinned zero bytes. This asks per layer — a component too large to pin whole still pins the layers the budget covers — and spends the budget where it pays: streamed layers before resident ones (a resident layer transfers once per stage, a streamed one every step), and the stepped DiT before once-per-request encoders. Four defects found while getting there, each fixed with a test that fails when the fix is reverted: - **The same free memory was spent twice.** The copies-fit check ran before the pins it had just booked were allocated, so the live reading still counted those bytes as free — for a component between roughly 1× and 2× of available host memory, the old plan copied the whole checkpoint into memory that could not hold it. Everything the plan adds is now weighed as one sum. - **The plan was charged its gross allocations, not its net cost.** A store buffer that replaces an anonymous original — the fused-qkv share — is a wash: the original is freed when its parameter is rebound. Charging it as new made the plan give back pins the host could afford. The fit checks now weigh only the bytes copied off the checkpoint mapping. - **Pins that still do not fit are given back** from the tail of the pin order, which holds the least valuable ones, instead of over-committing. - **The benefit ranking silently degraded to bare bytes**: its step count was read off `pipeline_class_name`, an override that is normally unset, so a 45 GB once-per-request encoder could outrank the 20-step DiT. The pipeline is now resolved the way `build_pipeline` does (a cache hit by then). Measured on MiniMax-H3 fl2va, one RTX 4090, 12 GiB allocator cap, 32 GiB host envelope, with the VAE on its checkpoint mapping (#35862): the plan pins **13 of 50 DiT layers** and the run peaks at **20.4 GiB** of anonymous host memory — inside the envelope it planned for, reproduced across rounds. Stacked with the mapped-layer courier (#35882) this is the configuration that runs the lossless bf16 denoise at a median of 11.0–12.0 s/step, ahead of ComfyUI's 13.0 measured under the same 32 GiB convention on the same GPU in the same bandwidth window. Merge note: this PR and #35882 touch the same file; whichever lands second rebases (the resolution is mechanical — both sides add independent methods). 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32537578638](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32537578638)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32537578453](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32537578453)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32537578576](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32537578576)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [HiCache][PD] Fix write-through lock leak for retraction host pools
signals.text: ## Motivation #20049 fixed a pure-decode liveness bug where HiCache write-through acknowledgements were not processed and their radix-tree `lock_ref`s leaked. After #30511 consolidated HiCache event checks and removed the dedicated acknowledgement flush, a PD decode configuration with a retraction-only host pool fell outside the new event-drain gate. That configuration creates a host cache controller without `--enable-hierarchical-cache`, so it can issue write-through backups but did not poll their completion events. This is a configuration-coverage regression of the #20049 liveness invariant after #30511. ## Root cause When `cache_controller` exists, the decode radix cache enables HiCache write-through backups. Each backup calls `inc_lock_ref`, and only acknowledgement processing in `check_hicache_events()` performs the matching `dec_lock_ref`. The old decode drain gate used `enable_decode_hicache`, which additionally required `--enable-hierarchical-cache`. With a retraction-only host pool, write-through therefore remained enabled while acknowledgement draining remained disabled. In the reproduced stall there were 19 lock increments and 11 decrements, leaving 8 leaked locks and 33,536 protected tokens. The GPU was idle with active/running/waiting all at 0, but `evictable_size=0`; the retracted request could never pass its resume allocation gate, and restore was never called. ## Fix Poll HiCache events whenever the decode tree cache has an actual cache controller, matching the capability that enables write-through backups instead of relying on the `--enable-hierarchical-cache` CLI state. Deployments without a controller still skip the event drain. The focused regression test covers the retraction-only configuration with `enable_hierarchical_cache=false` and the old `enable_decode_hicache=false` gate, verifies that ranks with different local acknowledgement readiness make the same drain decision, and verifies that the no-controller path performs no drain. ## Validation - Pre-fix active-shared workload: 8/8 stalls. - Post-fix liveness gate: 21/21 PASS; legacy `length`: 10/10; candidate `backup-cost`: 10/10. - Restore lifecycle: 42/42 `restore_start` and 42/42 `restore_done`; all outputs byte-identical. - Latest `main` compatibility smoke: 3/3 PASS. Every run triggered a real memory-pressure retraction, completed 4/4 requests, restored on both TP ranks with no divergence or watchdog, matched outputs byte-for-byte, and cleaned all processes, ports, and GPU memory. - Focused regression: fails before the fix and passes after it (2 tests). - Related PD decode CPU tests: 32 passed. - HiCache CPU/GPU tests: 18 passed and 7 passed. - Unified radix-cache suite: 1,082 passed, 1,070 skipped. ## Related - Regression coverage for #20049 - Event-check consolidation in #30511 - Discovered while stress-testing #35717 <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32487573497](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32487573497)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32487573315](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32487573315)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32487573967](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32487573967)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [AMD] Skip full-vocab softmax in EAGLE topk==1 draft on ROCm
signals.text: ## Motivation With `--speculative-eagle-topk 1` the EAGLE draft tree degenerates to a single chain, so the returned `topk_p` is never consumed downstream and only the selected index matters. Softmax is monotonic and cannot move an argmax, so the full-vocab `torch.softmax` the draft loop computes is pure overhead. #26235 removed it, #26358 reverted it after DSv3.2-MTP GSM8K collapsed on ROCm, and #26397 relanded it behind `not _is_hip` — so CUDA gets the fast path and ROCm still pays for a softmax whose result it discards. On a profiled Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-MXFP4 MTP run (MI355X, TP2, IL8192/OL1024), the discarded softmax and its top-1 reduction are **11.4% of the entire MTP draft CUDA-graph**: | kernel | total (µs) | calls | per call (µs) | |---|---:|---:|---:| | `cunn_SoftMaxForwardGmem` | 95,312.3 | 1200 | 79.4 | | `at::native::reduce_kernel<512,1,…>` (`torch.max`) | 83,624.7 | 1200 | 69.7 | | **total** | **178,937.0** | | **149.1** | Prior attempts and why this differs: #26633 proposed deleting the `not _is_hip` gate outright; its CI went red and the author closed it with no review. #29800 is open but ships a monkey-patch script under `scripts/`, patches only the draft-extend site (not the draft-decode loop where the time actually goes), and relies on an fp32 cast — which cannot break ties, since widening from fp8 is lossless. ## Modifications **Purely additive: 159 insertions, 0 deletions, in 2 files.** The existing `elif self.topk == 1 and not _is_hip:` branch and its body are not modified, so CUDA and every non-ROCm platform are byte-for-byte unchanged — a new `elif` is layered after it. Given this code path was reverted once for an accuracy collapse, not perturbing the platform that currently works is worth more than de-duplicating the two branches. No new module-level state, no new helper functions, and no new env var: `SGLANG_USE_AITER` already gates aiter, and reverting this commit is the rollback lever. - `speculative/eagle_worker_v2.py`: bind `aiter.greedy_sample` once in `EagleDraftWorker.__init__` (env/platform config is init-static per the repo style rule), then add the ROCm branch inline at **both** call sites — the draft-decode loop, where the draft steps run and the measured time goes, and the draft-extend selection. #29800 patches only the latter. The branch body is 8 lines. - New unit test pinning the two aiter properties this depends on: the `hipcub::ArgMax` lowest-index tie-break, and correctness above the vocab floor. ```python elif self.topk == 1 and not _is_hip: ... # unchanged, not in the diff elif ( self.topk == 1 and self.aiter_greedy_sample is not None and logits_output.next_token_logits.shape[-1] > 1023 * 16 ): logits = logits_output.next_token_logits selected = torch.empty( logits.shape[0], dtype=torch.int32, device=logits.device ) self.aiter_greedy_sample(selected, logits) topk_index = selected.to(torch.int64).unsqueeze(-1) topk_p = torch.ones_like(topk_index, dtype=torch.float32) forward_batch.positions.add_(1) ``` Branch behavior, showing nothing can get slower — ROCm's only path today is the `else`: | case | before | after | |---|---|---| | CUDA, topk=1 | `not _is_hip` branch | same branch, not in the diff | | ROCm, aiter bound + vocab > 16368 | `else` softmax | **new branch** | | ROCm, no aiter or vocab ≤ 16368 | `else` softmax | `else` softmax (identical to today) | | topk > 1 / rejection sampling | unchanged | unchanged | ### aiter bug found while validating this `aiter::greedy_sample` returns **negative, out-of-range indices for vocab ≤ 16368**. Its kernel launches `BlockSize=1024 × VecSize=16`; a thread whose first offset `threadIdx.x * 16` already exceeds `N` skips the initial load, leaving `vec_pre` uninitialized, but still enters the tail with `key = threadIdx.x * 16 - 16385` — a negative key that can win the block reduction. That predicts breakage exactly for `N <= 1023 * 16 = 16368`, and bisecting the boundary on gfx950 / ROCm 7.2 reproduces it precisely: wrong (negative) indices up to `N = 16368`, correct from `N = 16369`. This is also the likely root cause of the out-of-range token ids already documented at `layers/sampler.py:53`. This PR guards around it; an aiter-side fix is being filed separately. ## Accuracy Tests GSM8K, 200 questions, 5-shot, same server config, MI355X TP2: | | accuracy | invalid | |---|---:|---:| | run 1 before / after | 0.930 / 0.940 | 0.000 | | run 2 before / after | 0.930 / 0.950 | 0.000 | No regression in either run. The gains are 2 and 4 questions out of 200 and should be read as noise, not as an improvement. One negative result worth recording: **the tie-break instability that motivated the #26397 gate does not reproduce in isolation on gfx950 / ROCm 7.2.** Across batch-shape padding, repeated calls, and fp8-quantized logits with ~2.6 tied cells per row at the maximum, `torch.argmax`, `softmax+fast_topk`, and `aiter greedy_sample` all returned identical, stable, lowest-index results. That matches what #26633 reported, so the reland's premise is unconfirmed rather than disproven. This PR does not rest on that question either way — it uses a kernel whose tie-break is contractual. ## Benchmarking and Profiling ### Profile: the kernels are gone Same server config, conc4, profiled before and after, parsed with `trace_module_analyzer`. Draft-graph kernels (`Module Types == "Layer"`): | kernel | before | after | |---|---|---| | `cunn_SoftMaxForwardGmem` | 95,312.3 µs × 1200 | **absent** | | `at::native::reduce_kernel<512,1,…>` | 83,624.7 µs × 1200 | **absent** | | `aiter::greedy_sample_kernel` | 127.7 µs × 7 *(final sampler only)* | 22,013.4 µs × 1221 | | **net on these kernels** | | **−157,051 µs** | | draft CUDA-graph total | 1,568,438.9 µs | 1,432,504.0 µs (**−8.7%**) | Per draft step the selection goes **149.1 µs → 18.0 µs (8.3×)**. ### End-to-end Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-MXFP4, MI355X TP2, IL8192/OL1024, EAGLE `num-steps 3 / topk 1 / draft-tokens 4`. Run 1 is on the pre-rebase base; run 2 is on the current base — both are independent server loads per side. **median TPOT** — the metric this change acts on, a median over thousands of decode tokens: | | conc4 | conc8 | conc16 | conc32 | conc64 | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | run 1 Δ | −1.14% | −1.28% | −1.23% | −0.37% | +0.46% | | run 2 Δ | −1.99% | −0.25% | −2.12% | −1.04% | −0.52% | | run 2 before (ms) | 4.88 | 6.92 | 10.57 | 16.66 | 28.02 | | run 2 after (ms) | 4.78 | 6.90 | 10.34 | 16.49 | 27.88 | **Negative in 9 of 10 measurements**, the exception being run 1's conc64 (+0.46%), which run 2 puts at −0.52%. **total throughput** — cannot resolve an effect this size and should not be read as a result: | | conc4 | conc8 | conc16 | conc32 | conc64 | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | run 1 Δ | +3.10% | +1.35% | +1.41% | +0.41% | +0.21% | | run 2 Δ | +0.39% | −0.04% | +1.43% | +1.01% | −0.15% | Run 1's conc4 read +3.10%, but a repeat at 2.5× the prompt count gave +0.60% and the *baseline itself* moved 5.9% between runs. At these request counts throughput is dominated by TTFT and scheduling jitter. Honest summary: **median TPOT −1% to −2% at conc4–32, ~−0.5% at conc64.** Not a 5%-class win. The saving is a near-fixed ~130 µs per draft step, so its relative value shrinks as the iteration grows with concurrency. It is a small, reproducible decode-latency improvement that deletes a full-vocab softmax whose output was being discarded. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review Process 1. signals.title: [FlashInfer] perf: Fuse FP4 MoE input quantization and shared-expert SwiGLU
signals.text: ## Motivation This PR depends on [FlashInfer PR #4640](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/4640) for `mm_bf16_swiglu`. FlashInfer's `void flashinfer::trtllm_mnnvl_allreduce::oneshotAllreduceFusionKernel` can fuse nvfp4 quantization within the AR+Norm kernel, saving a kernel launch before every MoE call. Although this seemed a flat flashinfer API usage, this exposed the issue highlighted [here](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/4640#issuecomment-5370216869); thus we need a workaround to make the integration e2e valuable perf wise. ## Modifications - Feed fused all-reduce + residual + RMSNorm FP4 outputs directly into the FlashInfer TRT-LLM MoE runner. - Use FlashInfer BF16 GEMM1 + SwiGLU for eligible shared experts during decode/target verification, with an M ≤ 64 gate and existing fallbacks. - Prepare the fused shared-expert weight layout after loading and add focused integration/eligibility tests. ## Performance GLM-5.2-NVFP4, TP4; random 1,024-token input and 1,024-token output; total requests = 16 × concurrency. Values are median TPOT in ms/token (lower is better). Baseline: `main@0e4a09480c`; feature: `2113186027`. Both runs used the FlashInfer 0.6.17 compatibility overlay through `f0f8760e`. | Concurrency | `main` | This PR | Improvement | | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | | 1 | 6.552 | 6.498 | +0.82% | | 2 | 7.044 | 6.950 | +1.33% | | 4 | 7.998 | 7.924 | +0.93% | | 8 | 9.598 | 9.474 | +1.30% | | 16 | 12.433 | 12.306 | +1.02% | | 32 | 15.861 | 15.649 | +1.34% | | 64 | 20.225 | 20.320 | -0.47% | In this single sweep, the feature improves median TPOT by 0.82–1.34% through concurrency 32 and regresses by 0.47% at concurrency 64. main: The down projection gemm on the shared path can't execute immediately after the activation, fortunately it doesn't spill after the down proj gemm on the routed path for bs=1 in most of the cases. PR: NVFP4 quantization call is gone and down proj gemm on shared path can execute immediately after the first fused gemm. --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :x: [Run #32497779839](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32497779839) Latest PR Test (Extra): :x: [Run #32497779063](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32497779063) Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): :x: [Run #32497779884](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32497779884)

signals.title: fix: shrink --hicache-size budget for SIDECAR draft host pool
signals.text: ## Motivation When `--hicache-size` is set (fixed GB budget for host-side KV cache) and a SIDECAR draft model is registered, the draft model also gets a host-side KV pool that must match the target's token count (for 1-to-1 index sharing in L2 transfers). However, the draft's per-token byte cost can be **larger** than the target's (e.g. quantized target + bf16 draft), causing the combined target+draft host memory allocation to **exceed** the user-specified `--hicache-size` budget. In practice this causes the server to OOM on startup. For example, with a quantized 27B target + bf16 1.5B draft at TP=4: - Target host pool: 7.60 GB/rank - Draft host pool: 9.50 GB/rank - **Total: 17.10 GB/rank** — far exceeding the 4 GB `--hicache-size` cap ## Modifications Add `_adjust_hicache_size_for_draft()` in `kv_cache_builder.py` which: 1. Computes the per-token byte cost of both target and draft device pools via `_device_pool_size_per_token()`, which derives the cost from pool geometry (head_dim, head_num, layer_num, dtype for MHA; kv_cache_dim, layer_num, dtype for MLA) rather than `get_kv_size_bytes()`, since the device pool may be in post-capture mode where buffers are not yet allocated. 2. Shrinks the budget by the factor `target_spt / (target_spt + draft_spt)` so the total (target + draft) stays within the user's `--hicache-size` cap. 3. Reduces both `hicache_size` and `hicache_ratio` (the latter needed because post-capture pools have zero allocated buffers, so sizing falls back to the ratio). 4. Runs before `create_tree_cache()` so the adjusted values flow into both the tree cache and the memory bag. The adjustment only applies in fixed-size (`hicache_size > 0`) mode; ratio mode already scales both pools proportionally. ## Accuracy Tests This change does not affect model outputs — it only adjusts host memory pool sizing. No accuracy impact. ## Speed Tests and Profiling This change does not impact inference speed. It only prevents OOM at startup when using speculative decoding with HiCache. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32497855405](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32497855405)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32497855075](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32497855075)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32497855339](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32497855339)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->
