signals.title: config: record resolution writes in a declaration stash
signals.text: ## Stack Part of a series that moves `ServerArgs` from "mutate the record at construction" to "resolve once, publish into config bags". Each PR stands alone (builds, passes its own tests); review bottom-up. | # | PR | base | |---|----|------| | 0 | #35904 | `main` | | 1 | #35905 | #35904 | | 2 | #35906 | #35905 | | 3 | #35907 | #35906 | | 4 | #35908 | #35907 | | 5 | #35909 | #35908 | | 6 | #35910 | #35909 | Whole-series CI vehicle (not for merge): #35917 ## Motivation Resolution used to write `ServerArgs` fields with bare assignments, so what a handler decided was indistinguishable from what the caller passed in. To project configuration bags from resolution output (later in this stack), every resolution write must be recorded, not just applied. ## Modifications - Every in-pipeline scalar write goes through a declaration (`self._declare(...)` on handlers, `declare_resolution(...)` in the hooks): the write is appended to a declaration stash on the record and applied to the field immediately, so successors that read the field directly see the same value as before. - The model-override registry entries and post-process passes declare through the same channel. - `declare_resolution`'s docstring states what routing a write through the stash changes: a declaration is replayed last, so an immediate writer that declares a field a deferred writer also decides now beats it. A resolver gating on such a field must read the resolving view, not the raw field. - Guards (all derivation-based, each verified by injection): - no converted field is assigned bare anywhere in the pipeline; - the stash agrees with the fields it declared; - the stash accounts for every change resolution made (resolve, diff against the raw snapshot, require a declaration for every changed leaf); - an immediate writer must not silently override a deferred writer's different value — the fixture matrix includes a shape that actually reaches that branch (`--enable-waterfill --moe-a2a-backend ascend_tp`). ## Verification - Declaration guard suite green at this commit; each guard reddens when its protected property is broken (verified by injecting the corresponding bug). - A/B: fully-resolved records across an 11-configuration matrix are field-for-field identical to the base revision. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32541509037](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32541509037)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32541508898](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32541508898)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32541509062](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32541509062)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: config: project the config bags from the resolution result
signals.text: ## Stack Part of a series that moves `ServerArgs` from "mutate the record at construction" to "resolve once, publish into config bags". Each PR stands alone (builds, passes its own tests); review bottom-up. | # | PR | base | |---|----|------| | 0 | #35904 | `main` | | 1 | #35905 | #35904 | | 2 | #35906 | #35905 | | 3 | #35907 | #35906 | | 4 | #35908 | #35907 | | 5 | #35909 | #35908 | | 6 | #35910 | #35909 | Whole-series CI vehicle (not for merge): #35917 ## Motivation The config bags were projected from whatever the record's fields held at publish time. With resolution writes now declared (previous PR), the projection can read the resolution *result* — the raw input plus the ordered declarations — which makes "what did the user ask for" and "what did resolution decide" separately answerable, and makes late writes visible to the projection. ## Modifications - `_build_config_bags` projects from `resolution_result(record, field)`: last declaration wins, else the raw-input snapshot, else the field. - Late resolution (LoRA normalization, auto parser detection — steps that need the launcher's validation stage) records through `declare_late_resolution`, so the bags describe the resolved value rather than the `auto` the CLI carried. - Out-of-tree platform hooks are wrapped by `declare_direct_writes`: their field rebinds are diffed and declared, so a plugin's defaults are not dropped by the projection. - First reader batch moves to the bags (speculative workers; runner/cache/expert components; scheduler and manager paths). `read_draft_checkpoint_gamma` reads the resolving view rather than a bag: it is called from inside resolution where no bag exists yet, and its caller swallows exceptions, so a bag read silently dropped the draft checkpoint's gamma. - Nested resolution decisions (e.g. `cuda_graph_config.decode.max_bs`, written through the declared object) are pinned end-to-end: a test resolves, publishes, and asserts the bag's graph config matches the record's, including leaves filled after the declaring step. ## Verification - Bag-leaf equivalence: 2826 comparisons between projected bags and the resolved record across the fixture matrix. - Pickle-to-child: a record that traveled by pickle projects the same bags as its parent. - Reader-vs-metadata cross-check over 1981 read sites; namespace accessor shadowing guard. - A/B: resolved end-state identical to base across the 11-configuration matrix. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32541510719](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32541510719)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32541510589](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32541510589)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32541510713](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32541510713)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: config: constructing a config no longer resolves it
signals.text: ## Stack Part of a series that moves `ServerArgs` from "mutate the record at construction" to "resolve once, publish into config bags". Each PR stands alone (builds, passes its own tests); review bottom-up. | # | PR | base | |---|----|------| | 0 | #35904 | `main` | | 1 | #35905 | #35904 | | 2 | #35906 | #35905 | | 3 | #35907 | #35906 | | 4 | #35908 | #35907 | | 5 | #35909 | #35908 | | 6 | #35910 | #35909 | Whole-series CI vehicle (not for merge): #35917 ## Motivation `__post_init__` ran the whole resolution pipeline, so every construction produced a resolved record — a fixture inspecting defaults, a config being validated, a record on its way to a subprocess that would resolve it again. That is the reason the record could not stay at what the caller asked for. Resolution is deterministic on the raw input but **not** repeatable on its own output: the DP-attention step derives the chunked prefill size from the chunked prefill size, so a second pass halves it again (8192 → 4096 → 2048, measured), and the schedule conservativeness is scaled again (0.3 → 0.09). **This is the only behavioral change in the stack**; everything before it is record-keeping and everything after is read redirection. ## Modifications - Construction is inert. `resolve_once()` is the single gate: it runs the pipeline unless the record has been through it, and marks the record on every exit (the mark also arms a read-only `__setattr__` — post-resolution changes go to the bags via `get_context().override`). - The launcher resolves the engine's record once; `publish` asks the gate on the way in and finds nothing left to do for a record that arrived resolved (e.g. by pickle, which carries the declarations). - Programs that build their own record resolve it before reading what resolution decides. Seven entries across the repository (the model gateway's launcher, benchmarks, examples) did not — e.g. the gateway sized its worker plan from a raw `dp_size`, so `--tp-size 4 --dwdp-size 4` launched one server instead of four, and a speculative benchmark forwarded `--mem-fraction-static None` to the server it spawns. All seven resolve now, and the census that found them is a test whose universe is the repository, not the package — keyed on the record's import source, because the diffusion runtime has a same-spelled `ServerArgs` with no resolution step. - A copy of a resolved record stays resolved: `ServerArgs.replace_resolved(source, **changes)` carries everything resolution left on the instance (raw snapshot, declaration stash, memoized `ModelConfig`, flags — enumerated from the instance, not listed) and appends the change as a declaration so the projection sees it. The Ray paths and the gateway's per-worker copy use it; a bare `dataclasses.replace` re-entered resolution on already-resolved values (measured on a 2-GPU Ray run: both scheduler actors ran with `chunked_prefill_size=2048` while the engine reported 4096). A derived pin forbids bare `dataclasses.replace` of a record outside the helper, with the helper's own call as the positive control. ## Verification - Gate refusal and reproducibility suites; the seam has exactly one pipeline caller and the gate's callers are pinned together with the rule they stand for (a non-mechanism caller must resolve a record it built itself from argv). - Ray smoke run (dp=2, tp=2, DP attention, 2 GPUs, real weights): generation OK, the DP-attention adjustment logged exactly once, zero read-only violations. - Blast radius of the read-only flag measured by flipping it early and running the unit suite; every affected fixture fixed to pass both before and after. - A/B: resolved end-state identical to base across the 11-configuration matrix. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32541511485](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32541511485)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32541511413](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32541511413)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32541511489](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32541511489)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.text: ## Stack Part of a series that moves `ServerArgs` from "mutate the record at construction" to "resolve once, publish into config bags". signals.title: Fix nullable GLM tool argument parsing
signals.text: ## Motivation The GLM-4.7/GLM-5 tool-call parser infers a schema type such as `["string", "null"]` as the primary type `string`. As a result, a model-emitted JSON `null` can be serialized as a string instead of remaining null. | Argument schema | Model output | Before | After | |---|---|---|---| | `{"type": ["string", "null"]}` | `null` | String (`"None"` complete, `"null"` streaming) | JSON `null` | | `{"type": ["string", "null"]}` | `value` | `"value"` | `"value"` | | `{"type": "string"}` | `null` | `"None"` complete, `"null"` streaming | `"null"` | ## Modifications - Preserve an unquoted `null` when the argument's JSON Schema explicitly permits it. - Delay serialization of nullable string values until the complete streaming value distinguishes JSON null from ordinary text. - Share argument-schema lookup between type inference and nullability checks. - Add registered CPU regression coverage for complete and fragmented incremental parsing. ## Accuracy Tests Not applicable; this changes tool-argument parsing rather than model generation. signals.title: [OpenAI] Drop empty assistant turns for mistral_common tokenizers
signals.text: A chat request containing an assistant message with empty content fails on Mistral models but works on every other model. mistral_common validates conversation structure and rejects the turn, so the request is refused; DeepSeek and other Jinja templates simply ignore it. Since the turn carries no information, this is an OpenAI-compatibility gap rather than a malformed request. `patch_mistral_common_tokenizer` now drops assistant turns that have neither content nor tool calls before handing the conversation to mistral_common. Turns with `tool_calls`, multimodal content, or real text are untouched, and a trailing assistant message is already consumed upstream as the `continue_final_message` prefix, so this cannot swallow a prefill. Reproduced and verified on one devbox with a Mistral model served from a local directory (so the tokenizer resolves to `MistralCommonBackend`), using the reported payload — `user` / `assistant("")` / `user`: - before #35215: HTTP 500 `Internal server error: Invalid assistant message` - with #35215: HTTP 400 `BadRequest` — honest, but still refused - with this change: HTTP 200 and a normal completion Normal multi-turn chat is unaffected. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32527397164](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32527397164)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32527396874](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32527396874)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32527397117](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32527397117)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: Keep the DeepSeek router GEMM in fp32 under deterministic inference
signals.text: ## Motivation Closes #34758. Under deterministic inference the DeepSeek router GEMM returns bf16 logits, while every other branch of `MoEGate.forward` returns fp32 (`dsv3_router_gemm(out_dtype=torch.float32)`, `linear_bf16_fp32`, the prefill-CP path). `noaux_tc` ranks 256/384 experts against an fp32 correction bias, and adjacent expert scores routinely sit within one bf16 ULP, so the narrower store changes which experts run — a different answer, not a small numeric difference. fp32 output does not cost batch invariance. Invariance is a property of the reduction order, and the store happens after the reduction is complete. ## Modifications The root cause is one missing degree of freedom: `matmul_persistent` could not express *accumulate fp32, store fp32* — the output dtype was implicitly `a.dtype`. Every symptom in the issue follows from that. **`batch_invariant_ops.py`** - `out_dtype` threaded through `matmul_persistent`, `_matmul_persistent_triton` and `_matmul_persistent_deepgemm`. - The Triton tile config stays keyed on the **input** dtype. This is load-bearing: the configs are not the same shape (`bfloat16 -> BLOCK_SIZE_K=64`, `float32 -> BLOCK_SIZE_K=32`), so keying on `out_dtype` - would halve the k-tile and silently run a different reduction than the non-deterministic path. Only the `torch.empty` moves. - DeepGEMM keeps its kernel instead of falling back to Triton. `bf16_gemm_nn` only stores bf16, but - bf16_gemm_nt` already takes an fp32 `out` (it is what `gemm_nt_bf16bf16f32` and `_BF16F32WarmupExecutor` use) and wants the `[N, K]` rhs that `matmul_persistent` has already checked is contiguous. Routing fp32 to Triton would have demoted the kernel on exactly the H200/B200 deterministic runs this is meant to help. - `_mm_dtype_compat` asks the kernel for `out_dtype` rather than casting afterwards, fixing the `fp32 -> bf16 -> fp32` round trip that handed `aten::mm.dtype` callers bf16 values. - Its two `.contiguous()` calls are dropped. For the router, `mat2` is `weight.t()`, so they were materializing a `[7168, 256]` copy every forward, every MoE layer, and disqualifying the DeepGEMM path on the way. Its sibling `mm_batch_invariant` never did this, and the kernel takes strided operands. **`deepseek_v2.py`** — the deterministic branch becomes `torch.mm(hidden_states, self.weight.t(), out_dtype=torch.float32)`. Going through the aten override rather than importing `matmul_persistent` keeps device dispatch intact. The issue's fourth point needs no work: this branch already returns above the `max_router_gemm_tokens` switch, so the token-count-dependent kernel choice was never reachable under deterministic mode. **`npu_batch_invariant_ops.py`** — `aten::mm.dtype` registered on NPU. It casts rather than widening (the NPU kernel stores its input dtype), so precision there is unchanged; without it `out_dtype=` would fall through to the stock NPU matmul and leave batch-invariant mode altogether. ## Accuracy Tests Measured on one GPU with the Triton backend, `[64, 7168] x [7168, 256]` shaped like the router GEMM. The reduction is untouched — the bf16 result is bit-identical to the fp32 result rounded: ``` bf16 store == round(fp32 store) True distinct values, bf16 / fp32 1958 / 16382 of 16384 max abs err vs fp64 bf16 9.800e-01 -> fp32 3.895e-03 (~250x) batch invariant for M in {1,2,4,5,16,17,64} exact ``` Expert-selection impact, holding the accumulator fixed and changing only the store, over `[4096, 7168] x [7168, 256]` with top-8 and an fp32 correction bias: | router logit std | tokens with a different expert set | |---|---| | 0.05 | 18 / 4096 | | 0.10 | 54 / 4096 | | 0.25 | 77 / 4096 | | 0.50 | 90 / 4096 | | 1.00 | 109 / 4096 | | 2.00 | 84 / 4096 | 0.4%–2.7% of tokens routed to a different expert set purely from the bf16 store. These are synthetic weights; a real DeepSeek-V3 comparison would be stronger and I do not have an 8xH200 to run it on. New tests in `test/registered/unit/batch_invariant_ops/test_matmul_out_dtype.py`, registered `base-b` / `1-gpu-large` rather than `1-gpu-small`: DeepGEMM is disabled on SM120, so only the H100 runner exercises the fp32 `bf16_gemm_nt` path. The file sets `_ENABLE_MM_COMPARISON_TEST`, and the operands satisfy the DeepGEMM gate, so CI diffs NT against Triton on every push. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not benchmarked. The GEMM is `[M, 7168] x [7168, 256]` and the kernel choice is unchanged on every backend, so the only cost is the wider store; the `.contiguous()` removal should be a small win on the deterministic path. ## Notes for reviewers Two things worth a closer look: 1. The `bf16_gemm_nt` fp32-out branch is reasoned from `gemm_nt_bf16bf16f32` and `_BF16F32WarmupExecutor`, not executed locally — no DeepGEMM on the hardware I have. The new test covers it on the first H100 CI run. 2. The `.contiguous()` removal in `_mm_dtype_compat` is the one change beyond the literal ask. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. signals.title: [CI vehicle] config: resolve once, publish into the config bags (whole series)
signals.text: ## Motivation **Review/CI vehicle — not for merge.** This PR carries the whole series at once so CI runs over the combined diff and the full change can be read in one place. The mergeable units are the stacked members below; land them bottom-up and close this one when the last member merges. | # | PR | base | |---|----|------| | 0 | #35904 | `main` | | 1 | #35905 | #35904 | | 2 | #35906 | #35905 | | 3 | #35907 | #35906 | | 4 | #35908 | #35907 | | 5 | #35909 | #35908 | | 6 | #35910 | #35909 | The series moves `ServerArgs` from "mutate the record at construction" toward "resolve once, publish the result into the config bags": resolution writes become declarations (#35905), the bags project from raw input plus declarations (#35906), construction stops resolving (#35907, the only behavioral change), borrowed-record reads follow the bags (#35908), and publish moves above the launcher's effective-configuration reads (#35910). #35904 fixes a pre-existing silent-override-drop independently; #35909 pins two orderings resolution relies on. The tip commit is an empty placeholder: the members share head SHAs with this branch's commits, and GitHub dedupes check suites by SHA — without a distinct tip this PR would show the members' runs instead of its own. ## Modifications Union of #35904–#35910; no changes beyond them (plus the empty tip commit). ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32541519842](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32541519842)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32541519693](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32541519693)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32541519853](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32541519853)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.text: ## Motivation DeepSeek V4 W4A4 MegaMoE currently requires users to set two SGLang-specific environment variables manually. retain warning-only deprecation entries that direct users to the server flag. - Update the B200 and context-parallel E2E launch commands. - Migrate the DeepSeek V4 cookbook, generated model snippets, playground behavior, and cookbook model template. - Add server-argument, deprecation, and cookbook-template regression tests. ## Accuracy Tests On `baizhou-dev-gb300`, the updated launch command passed all 9 tests in `TestDSV4FlashFP4B200W4A4MegaMoE`. - GSM8K score: 0.940 - Verified all four scheduler processes received `DG_USE_FP4_ACTS=1` and `DG_USE_MXF4_KIND=1`. - The launch command used only `--enable-w4a4-megamoe`; neither removed SGLang environment variable was present. - Focused unit tests for the new server argument and deprecated variables also passed. ## Speed Tests and Profiling - GB300 E2E output throughput: 301.08 token/s. - This PR changes configuration plumbing and does not change the MegaMoE kernel. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. signals.title: [Docs] Add --prerelease=allow to cookbook uv install commands
signals.text: ## Motivation Fixes the docs half of #35912. uv older than 0.12.0 does not honor pre-release specifiers found in **transitive** dependency metadata (changed in astral-sh/uv#19993, released in [uv 0.12.0](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/releases/tag/0.12.0) on 2026-07-28). `flash-attn-4`, a mandatory dependency of every release since 0.5.10, only publishes pre-releases on PyPI, so `uv pip install sglang` treats every release ≥ 0.5.10 as unsatisfiable and silently backtracks to **0.5.9** (2026-02-23) — no error, no warning. Users then hit bugs that were fixed months ago. `docs/docs/get-started/install.mdx` already carries `--prerelease=allow` (#29676), but the cookbook pages do not, so anyone following a model page — or typing the obvious command — still lands on 0.5.9. Two things make this worse than when #29676 landed: - `sglang==0.5.18` now also pins `cuda-tile==1.6.0rc5`, so **source and editable installs fail outright** on uv < 0.12.0 (the resolver cannot backtrack when the version is fixed), which is why the `-e python` commands need the flag too. - uv 0.12.0 is only a few weeks old, so most environments and images still ship 0.11.x. Measured with `uv pip compile` (`--python-platform x86_64-manylinux_2_34 --python-version 3.12`): | uv | default | `--prerelease=allow` | | --- | --- | --- | | 0.11.24 | **`sglang==0.5.9`** | `sglang==0.5.18` | | 0.12.5 | `sglang==0.5.18` | `sglang==0.5.18` | And with the version pinned so the resolver cannot backtrack (uv 0.11.24, default): ``` $ echo 'sglang==0.5.18' | uv pip compile - --python-platform x86_64-manylinux_2_34 × Because there is no version of cuda-tile==1.6.0rc5 and sglang==0.5.18 depends on cuda-tile==1.6.0rc5, we can conclude that sglang==0.5.18 cannot be used. hint: `cuda-tile` was requested with a pre-release marker ... (try: `--prerelease=allow`) ``` `pip`, uv ≥ 0.12.0, and the Docker images are unaffected. On new uv the flag is a harmless no-op. ## Modifications Docs only. - Added `--prerelease=allow` to **31 commands across 26 cookbook pages** — every command that installs SGLang, in all three forms: - PyPI: `uv pip install sglang`, `"sglang>=0.5.9"`, the pinned nightly in `Nemotron3-Nano.mdx` - git: `uv pip install 'git+https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang.git#subdirectory=python'` - source: `uv pip install -e python`, `-e "python[all]"` - Same fix in `.claude/skills/cookbook-add-model/templates/page.mdx.tmpl`, so new pages get it by default. - Added a two-sentence `<Note>` to `install.mdx` Method 1 explaining why the flag is there and that uv ≥ 0.12.0 does not need it. Deliberately left alone, verified as unaffected: - Commands that do not install SGLang: `lmms_eval` (Qwen3-VL), `natten` (LTX2.5), `".[s2pro]"` (S2-Pro — that is the separate `sglang-omni` repo). - The pages that already had the flag: the six diffusion pages and LongCat-2.0. - `hardware-platforms/tpu.mdx` (installs `sglang-jax`, a different repo), `hardware-platforms/cpu_server.mdx` (`cp pyproject_cpu.toml`), `hardware-platforms/apple_metal.mdx` and `sglang-diffusion/installation.mdx` (`mv pyproject_other.toml`) — neither `pyproject_cpu.toml` nor `pyproject_other.toml` contains `flash-attn-4`, `cuda-tile`, or any other pre-release pin. After this change, `git grep "uv pip install" -- docs` has no remaining SGLang install without the flag. ## Accuracy Tests N/A — documentation only. ## Speed Tests and Profiling N/A — documentation only. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). — N/A, docs only; `node docs/scripts/check_cookbook_configs.mjs` passes. - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results. — N/A, docs only. - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Follow-ups (not in this PR) #35912 also raises two non-docs items this PR does not address: a packaging/runtime guard so the silent downgrade cannot happen at all, and re-triaging the older issues whose environment fingerprint matches a resolver-driven 0.5.9 install (#24029, #34111, #34112, #34113, #33283, #25670). 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32534198341](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32534198341)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32534198151](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32534198151)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:heavy_minus_sign: **No AMD PR run found for this commit**.<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [Fix] Read the granite sinks dtype from the exec bag, not the legacy global shim
signals.text: ## Motivation #35794 (Granite SWA) added a `get_global_server_args()` read to `build_attention_sinks`, to pick the `sinks` dtype from the configured attention backend. That is the legacy process-global shim the runtime context replaced, and `test_legacy_global_ratchet.py` pins its call-sites at `1` — the shim definition itself. The ratchet has been **red on `main` at `2`** since that PR merged. This unblocks CI with no behaviour change. ## Modifications `granite.py` reads the same field off the `exec` config bag instead: ```diff -from sglang.srt.server_args import get_global_server_args +from sglang.srt.runtime_context import get_exec, get_parallel ... - attn_backend = get_global_server_args().attention_backend + attn_backend = get_exec().kernel.attention_backend ``` This is exactly what `gpt_oss.py` already does for the same decision, so the two now agree. Resolved values are identical: bfloat16 sinks, float32 under `trtllm_mha`. ### The rule being preserved is wrong — recorded, not fixed A `TODO(kpham-sgl)` next to the code says so, because it is not obvious from reading it: - **`trtllm_mha`'s kernel consumes float32 sinks; FA4 asserts bfloat16.** One parameter has one dtype, so a split launch (`--prefill-attention-backend fa4 --decode-attention-backend trtllm_mha`) cannot be served at all — whichever half is read, the other kernel gets the wrong dtype. - **A split-only launch leaves the base field unset**, so this read returns `None` and silently picks bfloat16. - **The checkpoint's own sinks dtype is unverified.** `default_weight_loader` asserts size, not dtype, and `copy_` casts silently — so a checkpoint shipping a different dtype is converted here with no error. The fix belongs at init, once the serving backend(s) are known — a per-phase sinks tensor, or the checkpoint dtype plus a cast in the one kernel that needs float32. That is deliberately **not** in this PR: it is a behaviour change and wants its own review, and the ratchet should not stay red waiting for it. #34917 covers the gpt-oss half of the same problem. ## Accuracy Tests No behaviour change — the two accessors return the same resolved field, verified directly under both configurations: | `--attention-backend` | sinks dtype | |---|---| | `fa3` | `torch.bfloat16` | | `trtllm_mha` | `torch.float32` | - `test_legacy_global_ratchet.py` — back to baseline `1`; red on `main` today at `2`. - `test_global_config_read_ratchet.py`, `test_split_attention_backend_decisions.py` — pass. (`test_inkling_selects_the_half_serving_the_forward` fails identically with this change reverted — missing CUDA-only `cutlass` in my local env — so it is not from this PR.) signals.title: [HiCache] Reject load-back specs that claim nodes pinned by an in-flight load-back
signals.text: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation With hierarchical caching on the unified radix tree, `commit_load_back` republishes Full device values before the H->D DMA acks. A second load-back anchor can then build a spec that claims just the still-host-only SWA window slice of a node pinned by the first, in-flight load-back, and trips the commit-time pin assert (`load_back_pending_id` held by a different anchor), crashing the scheduler. ## Modifications - `unified_tree_core.py` `build_load_back_spec`: reject any spec whose `nodes_to_load` (KV or per-component transfers) contains a node with a foreign `load_back_pending_id`; return an empty spec so the caller backs off and the request recomputes. The commit-time assert stays as a backstop. - `unified_radix_cache.py` `_load_back_transfers`: guard the skip threshold with `max(1, self.load_back_threshold)` so an entirely empty spec can never report success, even when `load_back_threshold <= 0`. - Add regression test `test_hicache_swa_load_back_rejects_foreign_pinned_window`: fails on the pinned-anchor assert before the fix, passes after. ## Accuracy Tests N/A — no change to model forward paths. The behavior change degrades a previously-crashing concurrent load-back overlap into a recompute. ## Speed Tests and Profiling N/A — the rejection branch only triggers on the overlap case that previously hit the assert. ## Original commits - `1c7d510789` ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32538734701](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32538734701)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:no_entry_sign: [Run #32538818136](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32538818136)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32538734821](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32538734821)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [HiCache] Clamp tombstoned SWA locs in UnifiedSWAKVPool translation
signals.text: ## Summary `UnifiedSWAKVPool.translate_loc_from_full_to_swa` returned the raw virtual-to-physical lookup, so a tombstoned v2p entry (`-1`) escaped to the caller as a negative slot id. With `page_size > 1` the page math turns it into a value in `[-ps, -1]` instead. Either way the caller ends up indexing the SWA KV buffer with a negative loc, which is an illegal access under captured cuda-graph replay. This clamps the translated locs to `0` before the `int32` cast, matching the existing tombstone-safety clamp in `MultiEndedAllocator.translate_kv_loc`: slot 0 is the reserved padding sink, so tombstoned reads/writes land there harmlessly instead of walking off the front of the buffer. Behavior for non-tombstoned entries is unchanged — physical locs are already non-negative, so the clamp is a no-op on them. The change is local to this method; no signature or caller changes. ## Test plan - `black --check` on the changed file: clean. - `python3 -m py_compile` on the changed file: clean. - Ported from an internal commit where the change was validated on a hierarchical-cache SWA serving setup; the GPU/cuda-graph reproduction was not re-run in this checkout (no suitable local environment), so it is left to CI. ## Original commits - `660518afe` <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32539420741](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32539420741)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32540700084](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32540700084)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32539420576](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32539420576)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [Fix] Prevent zombie requests after client disconnect: always dispatch AbortReq
signals.text: ## Problem Streaming clients that disconnect mid-generation (Esc in an agent UI, network drop, proxy timeout) leave **orphaned requests decoding on the scheduler until the request reaches its configured generation limit**, while TokenizerManager spams thousands of: ``` Received output for rid='...' but the state was deleted in TokenizerManager. ``` Observed on SGLang v0.5.17 while serving Qwen3.8-27B on AMD MI300X (ROCm): a single interrupted 4k-token request produced more than 5,000 error messages over several minutes and kept consuming GPU decode throughput as a zombie. ## Root cause 1. Client disconnect cancels the streaming response; `CancelledError`/`GeneratorExit` is raised inside `TokenizerManager.generate_request`. 2. Since #32588 (retained by its revert #34160), the cleanup runs under `except BaseException:` and immediately deletes `rid_to_state[rid]` via `_discard_pending_req_states`. 3. Two seconds later, the delayed `create_abort_task` fires `abort_request(rid)` - but its guard (`rid not in self.rid_to_state -> return`) silently drops the dispatch because the state was already deleted in step 2. 4. The scheduler never receives an `AbortReq` and keeps decoding; every streamed chunk then hits the missing-state error path. Regression chain: - #457 introduced the guard as pure idempotency: deletion + dispatch happened together inside `abort_request()`, so dispatch was never gated on state presence. - #28694 added the cleanup with `except Exception:` - deliberately not catching `CancelledError`, so disconnects were unaffected. - #32588 switched the cleanup to `except BaseException:`; the revert in #34160 kept that form. This made the cleanup fire on disconnect cancellation and turned the pre-existing guard into a dispatch blocker. ## Fix Two complementary changes in `python/sglang/srt/managers/tokenizer_manager.py`: - **A - `abort_request()`**: remove the `rid_to_state` presence guard. The scheduler owns the real request lifecycle; `rid_to_state` is only HTTP/stream-response bookkeeping and may legitimately be gone while a request still runs. Unknown rids are a safe no-op on the scheduler side: abort handling safely ignores requests that are no longer active, making duplicate dispatches harmless. This also restores manual `POST /abort_request` for already-orphaned rids. - **B - `generate_request()` cleanup**: replace the pop-only helper with `_abort_and_discard_pending_req_states`, which dispatches `AbortReq` **before** popping each still-pending state. Disconnect cleanup no longer depends on the delayed background task at all. ## Repro ```bash curl -sN localhost:30000/generate \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{"text":"long story...","sampling_params":{"max_new_tokens":4000},"stream":true}' & PID=$! sleep 8 && kill -9 "$PID" # client disconnect mid-decode ``` Before: thousands of `state was deleted` lines; `#running-req` stays elevated for minutes. After: <=2 backlog lines, decode stops within ~1 s. ## Verification | Test | Before | After | |---|---|---| | Streaming disconnect (mid-decode) | More than 5,000 error messages; zombie until generation limit | 2 backlog lines, stopped in ~1s | | `/abort_request` with orphaned rid | silently dropped (no-op) | dispatched, scheduler aborts | | `/abort_request` with bogus rid | dropped | safe no-op on scheduler | | Normal completion (stream/non-stream) | OK | OK | Tested on SGLang commit 5a46d657b7ea8de932266dc0a084d2217c78b168 (v0.5.17.dev, main @ 2026-08-21, ROCm build), with Qwen3.8-27B (BF16) on AMD MI300X (ROCm), TP=1, using FP8 E4M3 KV cache. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32541491057](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32541491057)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32541490987](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32541490987)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32541491040](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32541491040)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [diffusion] Fix unbounded A2A staging buffer growth across request sh…
signals.text: _a2a_staging_buffer keys by (role, shape, dtype, device), retaining one staging buffer per distinct request shape forever. Serving workloads with varied resolutions/durations accumulate these buffers without bound: on MiniMax-H3 ref2va (8x RTX 5090, ulysses=8) a memory snapshot showed 12.4 GiB held by these buffers after ~30 varied requests, ending in repeated CUDA OOM. torch.cuda.empty_cache() cannot reclaim them (module-level dict keeps references). Fix: key by (role, dtype, device) and grow a single flat buffer to the largest numel seen, viewing it to each request's shape. Reuse semantics are unchanged (a role's buffer is fully consumed before its next use); staging memory is now bounded by |roles| x largest request. <!-- Thank you for your contribution! signals.title: Warn when deterministic inference is combined with a quantized KV cache
signals.text: ## Motivation `--enable-deterministic-inference` combined with a quantized KV cache silently breaks the batch-invariance guarantee the feature exists to provide, and nothing tells the user: no warning, no guard, and no mention of KV cache dtype on the deterministic inference page. The docs state SGLang "achieves fully deterministic inference", list **"Reinforcement Learning: Ensures consistent logprobs across runs"** as the primary use case, and name the root cause of non-determinism as *"different batch sizes cause GPU kernels to split reduction operations differently"* — which is exactly the mechanism that still bites here. Measured on H100 NVL / SM90, **sglang 0.5.18**, `Qwen/Qwen3-8B` (bf16 weights, so KV dtype is the only variable), `--attention-backend fa3 --enable-deterministic-inference --disable-cuda-graph`, greedy, 224 new tokens: | `--kv-cache-dtype` | first divergent **absolute** index (prompt lens 4/3/12/31) | tokens differing | max Δlogprob | |---|---|---|---| | `fp8_e4m3` | **97, 97, 97, 97** | 118–138 of 224 | **0.4625** | | *(omitted)* | **None** | **0** | **0.0** | Prompt lengths 3→31 diverge at the same *absolute* position; the bf16 control is bitwise identical. That control also rules out an off-by-one in the comparison and shows deterministic inference does deliver batch invariance on this path for bf16. Reduced to the kernel, no model and no server: `forward_extend` (`flashattention_backend.py:1497`) and `forward_decode` (`:1988`) call the *same* `flash_attn_with_kvcache` against the same paged pool, differing only in query-row count. Over byte-identical fp8 KV: | kv_len | fp8_e4m3 max\|prefill−decode\| | bitwise equal | bf16 control | |---|---|---|---| | 88 / 94 / 95 / **96** | 0.0 | ✅ | ✅ 0.0 | | **97** | **3.906e-3** | ❌ | ✅ 0.0 | | 98 → 256 | ~1e-2 | ❌ | ✅ 0.0 | The sweep is **byte-identical at `num_splits` 0 and 1**, so SplitKV — the only thing deterministic inference pins here (`:319-323`) — is not the mechanism. The kernel's internal KV-block tiling is. Full analysis, the standalone repro script, and two hypotheses I checked and ruled out (`scheduler_metadata` asymmetry; asymmetric Q cast) are in [#25790](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/25790#issuecomment-5377092000). **This PR does not fix the divergence.** The FA3 kernel is fetched from `sgl-project/sgl-attn` (`CMakeLists.txt:82-87`, fp8 SM90 instantiations at `:443-445`), so the fix belongs there and is a two-repo change. This PR closes the "silent" half: users combining these flags get told. ## Modifications - **`arg_groups/overrides.py`** — new read-only post-process pass `_deterministic_quantized_kv_cache_warning`, next to the sibling deterministic guards. Fires when deterministic inference is on and `kv_cache_dtype` is one of `fp8_e4m3`, `fp8_e5m2`, `mxfp8`, `nvfp4`, `fp4_mx_block16`. - **`server_args.py`** — invoked at its legacy slot beside `_deterministic_sampling_backend` (registration alone does not run a pass). - **`docs/.../deterministic_inference.mdx`** — "Known Limitation: Quantized KV Cache" subsection under Supported Backends. - **`test/registered/unit/server_args/test_server_args.py`** — 3 CPU-only tests: warns for fp8 and declares nothing (so the pass cannot start rewriting the user's dtype); silent for `auto`/`bf16`/`bfloat16`; silent when deterministic inference is off. The last two are the negative branches — they are what catches the predicate degrading to always-true and warning every fp8 user. Deliberate choices, happy to change any of them: 1. **Warning, not an error or an override.** The combination is still reproducible run to run, which is enough for callers who only need that; it is prefill-vs-decode agreement that fails. Erroring would break working setups and silently rewriting the user's dtype seems worse than telling them. 2. **Gated on dtype, not backend.** I measured `fp8_e4m3` on **fa3** only. `flashinfer` and `triton` at fp8 are unmeasured, so I worded it as "does not guarantee" and named the measured configuration rather than narrowing the trigger and letting unmeasured paths stay silent. If you would rather scope it to fa3, say so and I will — it needs measurement I have not done. 3. **No registered KL test asserting the current fp8 numbers.** Pinning the buggy value is the loose-threshold trap that lets a real state bug hide. A near-zero assertion becomes correct once the kernel is fixed. **Known gap:** the guard reads the CLI value, so it does not catch a *checkpoint-derived* fp8 KV cache — `--kv-cache-dtype auto` with `hf_quant_config.json: {"kv_cache_quant_algo": "FP8"}` resolves to fp8 later in `mem_cache/kv_cache_dtype.py` while `server_args` still prints `auto` (same resolution path noted in #35291). Catching that needs the warning at resolution time, where the flag is not currently available. Left as a follow-up rather than shipping a config probe I cannot exercise without an NVFP4 checkpoint. ## Accuracy Tests No effect on model outputs — the pass declares nothing and only logs. The measurements above characterise pre-existing behaviour on unmodified `main`; the bf16 column is the control. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not applicable: one dtype-set membership test during argument resolution, no runtime path touched. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). — ran the pinned `black` 26.1.0, `isort` 7.0.0, `ruff` 0.15.1 (`F401,F821,UP037`) and `codespell` 2.4.1, plus the local `check_registered_tests.py` and `check_no_bare_pytest_main.py` hooks. All clean. - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results — see above; no output or speed impact. - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Environment ``` sglang 0.5.18 · torch 2.13.0+cu130 · CUDA 13.0 NVIDIA H100 NVL (95830 MiB) · driver 580.159.04 · SM90 ``` 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32544123492](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32544123492)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32544123322](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32544123322)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32544123554](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32544123554)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.text: ## Summary - route `--component-paths.<name> owner/repo/subfolder` through the existing component-path resolver - download only the selected Hub subfolder instead of treating the full slash-delimited value as a repo ID - document local directories, standalone Hub repos, and Hub component subfolders as the supported component override forms ## Motivation Many independently quantized encoders and VAEs are published as component subfolders inside a complete Diffusers repository. The loader-side resolver already supports that source form, but the composed-pipeline entry point called the generic whole-repo downloader first, so the request never reached it. ## Scope and churn No new CLI or resolver is introduced. signals.title: [diffusion] let `all` mean every layer in the layerwise placement flags
signals.text: `--layerwise-resident-layers video_vae=36` required the caller to know that this model's video VAE has 36 decoder blocks — a model internal — and the value boundary made it worse: a value below 1 is a fraction of the layers, so `1.0` resolved to **one layer**, and "every layer" had no spelling at all. `all` now parses to infinity and resolves to the component's own layer count at configure time, for both the resident and prefetch per-component maps: `--layerwise-resident-layers video_vae=all`. The cookbook's consumer recipes keep the explicit number for now and can move to `all` once this lands. The added test drives `configure_layerwise_offload_modules` with `dit=all` and asserts the manager holds exactly its own layer count; it fails with the parsing removed. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32544377169](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32544377169)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32544377611](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32544377611)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32544377002](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32544377002)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

Qwen3-32B on H100 starts **8.6-11.7% faster** than serial with prefetch, and **2.38x faster (35.6s vs 84.8s)** than the plain default. Opt in with `--startup-weight-load-mode overlap` ([#32017](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32017)). **TP LMHead with All-to-All**: The TP LMHead's allgather + scatter becomes a single all-to-all for pure-DP dp-attention. On DeepSeek-V4-Pro B200 decode, LMHead time drops **320us to 169us** and TPOT improves 36.97ms to 35.67ms ([#32313](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32313)). **FlashInfer MNNVL for pure allreduce**: Non-fused allreduce sites now reuse the FlashInfer MNNVL workspace instead of falling back to NCCL. signal.title: Add sampling observer auxiliary output hooks
signal.text: ## Motivation Some sampling-time integrations need to observe logits before grammar masking and attach structured per-token metadata to generated responses. Doing this currently requires coupling the integration directly to model-runner and scheduler internals. ## Modifications - Add an optional sampling observer interface around grammar masking and token sampling. - Carry observer-owned auxiliary tensors through asynchronous result copying and pipeline-parallel transport. - Consume committed-token metadata after scheduler output processing and expose accumulated values through the existing customized response metadata path. - Preserve the existing sampling path when no observer is configured. ## Accuracy Tests - `pytest -q test/registered/unit/managers/test_batch_result_processor_hidden_states.py test/registered/unit/managers/test_generation_auxiliary_output.py test/registered/unit/managers/test_output_streamer_customized_info.py test/registered/unit/sampling/test_sampling_batch_info.py` - 75 passed, 2 subtests passed - The tests include exact numerical-equivalence coverage for the observer-disabled logits path. ## Speed Tests and Profiling No standalone benchmark was run. When no observer is configured, the added path performs no auxiliary tensor computation or transfer. ## Checklist - [x] Format the code with the repository pre-commit hooks. - [x] Add registered unit tests for the new behavior. - [x] Document the extension contracts in the protocol docstrings. - [x] Verify numerical identity when the observer is disabled. - [x] Keep the change independent of model-specific implementations. ## Original commits - `60d0a82433` - `df3183df41` - `46e1b8eca2` - `2f598043c7` <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32492449054](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32492449054)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32492448997](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32492448997)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32492449051](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32492449051)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [Feature] Add MiniCPM-SALA support
signal.text: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation Add native serving support for MiniCPM-SALA checkpoints, which interleave MiniCPM sparse softmax-attention layers with constant-decay Lightning linear-attention layers. The implementation integrates the model with SGLang's existing attention, linear-attention, CUDA graph, and memory-pool infrastructure. It also replaces the serving-time dependency on the original out-of-tree block-table extension with SGLang JIT kernels. ## Modifications - Add `MiniCPMHybridConfig` and register both `MiniCPMForCausalLM` and `MiniCPMSALAForCausalLM`. - Normalize mixer aliases and repeat mixer patterns to the configured layer count. - Parse both flattened and legacy nested sparse-attention configuration. - Describe Lightning state using the existing `Mamba2CacheParams` and linear-attention model registry. - Extend the MiniCPM model with SALA mixer support. - Add Lightning QKV projection, optional Q/K normalization, RoPE, output normalization and gating, configurable attention scaling, and checkpoint-compatible weight loading. - Reuse the in-tree Lightning backend and `seg_la` kernels instead of introducing a model-specific linear-attention backend or external dependency. - Generalize the shared Lightning backend to read the linear KV-head count, layerwise decay mode, and per-layer attention scale from the model config. - Add `minicpm_flashattn` and `minicpm_flashinfer` sparse-attention backends. - Compose with `FlashAttentionBackend` for dense metadata and CUDA graph state. - Keep FlashInfer support as a composed decode path rather than duplicating its wrapper management. - Select FA4 automatically on supported Blackwell GPUs. - Support dense/sparse prefill and decode, CUDA graph capture/replay, K1/K2 key compression, sparse top-k selection, and optional fused TileLang kernels. - Add JIT-compiled CUDA block-table kernels. - Use v2 for prefill and v3 for the optimized decode layout, with automatic v2 fallback for unsupported v3 shapes. - Cache compiled modules by top-k, head-group count, and block size. - Attach the MiniCPM compressed cache to the existing `ReqToTokenPool`. - Reserve and account for K1/K2 capacity without introducing a model-specific pool subclass. - Route extend/decode allocation, rollback, request release, streaming-session cleanup, allocator reset, and pool statistics through generic no-op auxiliary-cache hooks. - Add MiniCPM model overrides and developer controls. - Default sparse SALA models to `minicpm_flashattn`, or `minicpm_flashinfer` on supported Blackwell GPUs. - Disable radix caching only for configs that actually contain sparse or Lightning layers. - Reject unsupported sparse-attention PD disaggregation early. - Add `SGLANG_MINICPM_FUSE_TOPK`, `SGLANG_MINICPM_SPLIT_STAGE1`, `SGLANG_MINICPM_DENSE_AS_SPARSE`, and `SGLANG_MINICPM_FORCE_DENSE` environment switches. - Add CPU and CUDA coverage for configuration defaults, model overrides, Lightning dispatch, compressed-cache lifecycle, sparse metadata, block-table kernels, and compression kernels. ## Accuracy Tests The following CPU regression suite passes on the final rebased branch: ```text 112 passed, 8 subtests passed ``` It covers: - MiniCPM config parsing, mixer selection, Lightning cache shape, scaling, and idle batches. - Sparse metadata construction, CUDA graph padding, and dense/sparse batch accounting. - K1/K2 allocation boundaries, reuse, rollback, cleanup, and streaming-session release. - Backend defaults, force-dense remapping, radix-cache gating, and unsupported PD disaggregation. signal.title: Support CPU offload for mxfp8 KV cache
signal.text: ## Motivation MXFP8 KV refused CPU offload, and a PD decode role reaches that path under pool pressure, so #35718 only holds while the decode pool has room: ``` decode SWA pool at 98% -> update_running_batch -> retract_decode -> release_req -> req.offload_kv_cache -> SWAKVPool.get_cpu_copy -> full_kv_pool.get_cpu_copy -> NotImplementedError: CPU offloading is unsupported for MXFP8 KV cache ``` The decode scheduler dies there, every later request fails, and gsm8k reads 0.12. Skipping the offload is not an alternative: retraction is backup-or-abort, and a request whose backup is skipped gets `FINISH_ABORT` rather than re-bootstrapped, which costs the same answers. The `host_pool` backup backend does not apply either, since it wants a HiCache pool on the decode role and the decode radix opt-in is refused for sliding-window models. Two places had to change. The pool now copies the block scales alongside K/V, reusing the interleave helpers it already has so the swizzle arithmetic stays in one place. And `SWAKVPool._filter_swa_cpu_copy`, which trims the SWA half row-wise before loading, assumed a chunk is exactly `[k, v]` and dropped the scales; it now follows whatever shape the sub-pool produced. ## Accuracy Single-node PD on 4xB200, one prefill and one decode role at TP=2 each, MXFP8 KV, `--max-total-tokens 65536` so retraction actually happens. gsm8k, 10-shot, 200 questions: ``` before score 0.12 Scheduler hit an exception (x2) after score 0.855 97 retractions, no exception ``` The score matters as much as the absence of the crash here: scales are stored by position within a page, retraction resumes a request at new slots, and misplacing them on the way back would dequantize against the wrong exponents without raising anything. 97 retract-and-resume cycles landing at 0.855 rules that out. Surfaced by the pair test in #35840. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32505813751](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32505813751)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32505813553](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32505813553)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32505813787](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32505813787)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->
signal.author: ispobock

signal.title: [AMD] Add ROCm 7.14 (gfx942 / gfx950) release
signal.text: ## Motivation ROCm 7.14 is published only as pip wheels and docker images — `repo.radeon.com` has no apt repo for it — so its stack has to be assembled from AMD's ROCm pip channels on top of `ubuntu:24.04`. That places the SDK in `site-packages` instead of `/opt/rocm`, which the existing stages of `docker/rocm.Dockerfile` assume throughout. This PR adds gfx942 and gfx950 ROCm 7.14 stages built that way, plus the adjustments the pip-SDK layout forces on the existing build and CI steps. The index is `https://repo.amd.com/rocm/whl-multi-arch/`, AMD's release channel. Deliberately not the nightly or devrelease channels: those get pruned. An earlier revision of this PR pinned a 7.15 nightly (`7.15.0a20260712`) because 7.15 never had a stable release — the line ran from `7.15.0a20260626` to `7.15.0a20260728` and was then renumbered 10.0 — which would have left this Dockerfile unbuildable, and the image unreproducible, once that nightly aged out of the index. 7.14 is a released SDK, so the pin is stable. torch is 2.11, the same as the `rocm724` flavors already on `main`, so the 7.14 stages reuse the existing `*_rocm724` extras for the `compressed-tensors` 0.16.0 pin rather than adding a third hand-synced copy of the same dependency list. `python/pyproject_other.toml` is unchanged by this PR. The `rocm7_15` / gfx1250 stage and its workflow are untouched. ## Modifications ### `docker/rocm.Dockerfile` - Added a shared `rocm714-base` stage: `ubuntu:24.04` + Python 3.12 in a venv + the ROCm 7.14 pip stack — `rocm-sdk-{core,libraries,devel,device-gfx942,device-gfx950}==7.14.0`, `torch`/`torchaudio` `2.11.0+rocm7.14.0`, `torchvision 0.26.0+rocm7.14.0`, `triton 3.7.1+git0263a6a6.rocm7.14.0`. - Added two thin per-arch stages, `gfx942-rocm714` and `gfx950-rocm714`, which set build flags and `PIP_CONSTRAINT`. Both arches' torch device wheels go into the shared base; `GPU_ARCH_LIST` still narrows what AITER and sgl-kernel actually compile for. - `BASE_IMAGE_942_ROCM714` / `BASE_IMAGE_950_ROCM714` default to the `rocm714-base` stage rather than a published image. Naming them keeps these stages shaped like every other stage in this file, which matters because `scripts/ci/amd/amd_ci_install_dependency.sh` locates a stage's `AITER_COMMIT_DEFAULT` by grepping for `FROM $BASE_IMAGE_<arch><suffix> AS <arch><suffix>`. They can also be pointed at a prebuilt image to skip building the base. - **Collapsed a duplicated `libamd_smi`.** `rocm-sdk init` expands a devel tree carrying a second copy of the library, byte-identical to the one in `_rocm_sdk_core` but a real file rather than a symlink. Since `ROCM_HOME` puts the devel tree on `LD_LIBRARY_PATH`, the amdsmi python package binds that copy while torch already holds the one HIP loaded through its RPATH, and two copies in one process keep separate global state — whichever initialises second enumerates nothing. torch on ROCm asks amdsmi for the device count before HIP, so this surfaces as `torch.cuda.device_count() == 0` on a machine where `hipGetDeviceCount()` returns 1, with `rocminfo` and `amd-smi` both seeing the GPU. Symlinking the duplicate fixes it; the step is guarded and idempotent, so it is a no-op if a future SDK ships a symlink there itself. - Single `--index-url`; the release index mirrors the PyPI packages torch pulls in, so no `--extra-index-url` and no `--pre` are needed. - torch and torchvision device wheels are named as separate specs rather than combined device extras. Several device extras in one spec (`torch[device-gfx942,device-gfx950]`) silently installs only the first, and the missing arch then fails at runtime with `hipErrorInvalidImage`. - Python 3.12 (the Ubuntu 24.04 default) rather than 3.13/3.14: `st_attn==0.0.7`, `vsa==0.0.4`, `petit_kernel==0.0.2` and `wave-lang==3.8.2` publish wheels only up to cp313 and no sdist, so on 3.14 pip has no candidate at all for `srt_hip`. - Path fixups for the non-`/opt/rocm` SDK: `ROCM_HOME` / `ROCM_PATH` / `CPATH` / `LIBRARY_PATH` / `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` point at the site-packages `_rocm_sdk_devel` tree; a `/opt/rocm` symlink because AITER shells out to `/opt/rocm/llvm/bin/amdgpu-arch` to pick `DEFAULT_GPU_ARCH` and the rest of this Dockerfile refers to `/opt/rocm`; and a `/usr/lib64/libc.so` symlink because the SDK's `hsakmtTargets.cmake` hardcodes that path from its own build host. - libdrm: skipped for `*rocm714*`. The pip SDK's `libdrm_amdgpu.so` links the device-ID table in rather than reading `share/libdrm/amdgpu.ids` — the `.so` carries the MI300X / MI325X / MI355X names and never opens that file — so the apt step the 7.2.4 flavor needs is unnecessary here. - amdsmi: installed for `*rocm714*` (same branch as the 7.2 flavors), since the pip SDK does not pre-install it. - `PIP_CONSTRAINT`: the 7.14 stages define and populate it the same way the `rocm724` stages do, so resolving AITER and SGLang dependencies cannot swap the image's ROCm torch for a PyPI CUDA build. - MORI: point the build at the SDK's vendored `lib/rocm_sysdeps` tree via `CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH` / `CPATH` / `LIBRARY_PATH` plus an `ldconfig` entry, for NUMA (`hsakmt-config.cmake` calls `find_dependency(NUMA)`) and libdrm (`rocm_smi.h` includes `<libdrm/drm.h>`, `mori_application` links `-ldrm`/`-ldrm_amdgpu`). Guarded on the directory existing, so the apt-based ROCm images keep their current behaviour. - nixl: the existing `libabsl-dev` removal is extended to `*-rocm714`, which is on the same Ubuntu 24.04 base as `rocm724` and hits the same meson/abseil conflict. - The SGLang install and the post-install validation step both treat `rocm714` like `rocm724`. ### `scripts/ci/amd/amd_ci_install_dependency.sh` - Recognise `-rocm714` in the image `GPU_ARCH` stamp and map it to `_ROCM714` / `-rocm714` so the AITER pin lookup finds the right Dockerfile stage. - Select the `dev_hip_rocm724` extras for `-rocm714` as well, matching what the Dockerfile does at build time. Without this a 7.14 image would get `compressed-tensors` 0.15.0, which requires `torch<2.11`, and the resolve would fail. - Apply the same `rocm_sysdeps` handling to the in-image MORI rebuild, kept scoped to that build instead of exported image-wide because `rocm_sysdeps/include` also carries `zlib.h` / `expat.h` / `elf.h`, which would shadow the system headers for every other component. ### `.github/workflows/release-docker-amd-rocm714-nightly.yml` - New workflow, following this repo's one-file-per-ROCm-version convention (`rocm700` / `rocm720` / `rocm7_15`), with a `gfx942-rocm714` / `gfx950-rocm714` matrix and `rocm714-mi30x` / `rocm714-mi35x` tags. The `rocm7_15` workflow is not modified. - The schedule is commented out for now; the workflow is dispatch-only until the gfx950 leg has had a green run. ## Accuracy Tests **Both arches build on CI.** [Run #32380153563](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32380153563) published `v0.5.17-rocm714-mi30x-20260820` (16.3 GB) and `v0.5.17-rocm714-mi35x-20260820` (16.5 GB). `gfx950-rocm714` had never been built before and passed first try. The workflow added here cannot be `workflow_dispatch`-ed until it exists on the default branch, so it is exercised from a throwaway branch, `bingxche/rocm714-ci-test`, which carries this PR head plus a branch-scoped `push` trigger and redirects images to a scratch repository so nothing unvalidated lands in `rocm/sgl-dev` or `lmsysorg/sglang-rocm`. None of that is part of this PR. **The `libamd_smi` duplication above was caught by that CI run** and would otherwise have shipped: every GPU test failed with `Invalid device id` because torch saw no devices. It reproduces off-CI with the published image, and the fix is verified against it — `device_count() = 1`, `get_device_name(0) = AMD Instinct MI300X`, bf16 matmul finite. **Local results on an MI300X host (gfx942)**, against a locally built `gfx942-rocm714` image: - Image builds end to end, all 34 steps. The in-image validation step reports `torch 2.11.0+rocm7.14.0`, `torchaudio 2.11.0+rocm7.14.0`, `torchvision 0.26.0+rocm7.14.0`, `triton 3.7.1`, HIP `7.14.60850`, with `pip check` clean and no `nvidia-*-cu*` packages. - Smoke test on hardware: 8 devices, `gfx942:sramecc+:xnack-`, bf16 matmul finite, and `triton`, `torchvision`, `torchaudio`, `aiter`, `mori`, `tilelang`, `nixl`, `amdsmi`, `sglang` and `compressed_tensors` (0.16.0, i.e. the right extras were selected) all import. - `scripts/ci/amd/amd_ci_install_dependency.sh` exits 0. The parts this PR touches behave as intended: `Image GPU_ARCH=gfx942-rocm714`, `installing python extras: [dev_hip_rocm724,tracing]`, `Using FROM $BASE_IMAGE_942_ROCM714 AS gfx942-rocm714 from Dockerfile`, and the MORI rebuild completes. - `run_suite.py --hw amd --suite stage-a-test-1-gpu-small-amd` reports **8/8 passed**, exit code 0. `test_umbp_store.py` passing is the relevant check for the MORI changes: it exercises `mori.umbp`, which needs the gRPC symbols the rebuilt MORI must carry. **Known gap:** `gfx950-rocm714` builds but has not been executed. No MI355X hardware was available for this work, so its runtime behaviour is unverified. ## Speed Tests and Profiling <!-- If this pull request impacts inference speed, provide benchmarking and profiling results. --> ## Checklist - [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. signal.title: [AMD] [Kimi-K3] Fuse the KDA input projection into a single GEMM on ROCm
signal.text: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation - KDA input projection on ROCm runs as two GEMMs per layer: a wide `[q, k, v, g]` projection (6144 rows/rank @ TP8) and a tiny `[f_a | b]` tail (128 + 12 rows/rank). - The tail is arithmetically negligible but still costs a full kernel launch and a second activation read every decode step. - Decode is bandwidth bound, so merging into one `N = 6288` GEMM makes the extra output columns nearly free and removes the second launch. - On gfx950 (`H = 7168`, TP8) the merged GEMM costs 0.55–0.73x the split pair for `M ≤ 64`, staying ahead up to a few hundred tokens; beyond that the untuned `N = 6288` shape loses to the tuned `N = 6144` one — so fusion is threshold-gated, not unconditional. - The `kimi_k3.py` comment warning that folding degrades kernel selection still holds for large-`M` prefill; this change reverses it only below the threshold, on ROCm, leaving the generic path untouched. ## Modifications - Merge the `[q, k, v, g]` and `[f_a | b]` projections into a single `N = 6288` GEMM (`_merge_kda_inproj_weights_hip`), gated by `SGLANG_ROCM_K3_FUSE_KDA_INPROJ` and a decode token-count threshold (a few hundred tokens). - Prefill (~1000-token chunks) and the generic, non-ROCm path are untouched. ## Accuracy Tests This is a layout-only change — same weights and values, reached through views — so parity is expected. **Full GSM8K** — n=1319, 5-shot, 8x MI355X TP8, Triton attention backend, fusion on by default: ``` python3 -m sglang.test.few_shot_gsm8k \ --num-questions 1319 \ --parallel 256 \ --num-shots 5 \ --max-new-tokens 512 \ --host http://127.0.0.1 \ --port 30001 ``` | Run | Accuracy | Invalid | |---|---:|---:| | 1 | 0.952 | 0.001 | | 2 | 0.951 | 0.001 | Both runs fall inside the documented 0.947–0.958 band (well above the 0.90 tripwire), consistent within noise. **Unit test:** `test/registered/amd/test_kimi_k3_kda_inproj_fusion.py` — 3 tests passed, 6 subtests passed. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Kimi K3: ISL 8192, OSL 1024, TP 8, MI355X * 8 ### Throughput/GPU | Conc | Split | Fused | Δ | |---:|---:|---:|---:| | 2 | 131.94 | 132.11 | +0.14% | | 4 | 218.34 | 219.80 | +0.67% | | 8 | 362.23 | 364.64 | +0.67% | | 16 | 550.69 | 561.43 | +1.95% | | 32 | 764.92 | 781.20 | +2.13% | ### Median ITL | Conc | Split | Fused | Δ | |---:|---:|---:|---:| | 2 | 16.15 | 16.13 | -0.15% | | 4 | 18.73 | 18.54 | -0.99% | | 8 | 20.91 | 20.70 | -1.03% | | 16 | 24.57 | 23.98 | -2.42% | | 32 | 30.75 | 29.94 | -2.62% | ### Median TTFT | Conc | Split | Fused | Δ | |---:|---:|---:|---:| | 2 | 913.08 | 912.99 | -0.01% | | 4 | 1556.02 | 1552.53 | -0.22% | | 8 | 2640.40 | 2451.79 | -7.14% | | 16 | 4791.64 | 4781.60 | -0.21% | | 32 | 8944.96 | 9081.63 | +1.53% | ### Median TPOT | Conc | Split | Fused | Δ | |---:|---:|---:|---:| | 2 | 16.15 | 16.13 | -0.14% | | 4 | 19.14 | 18.96 | -0.94% | | 8 | 22.34 | 22.12 | -0.98% | | 16 | 28.12 | 27.48 | -2.28% | | 32 | 38.48 | 37.54 | -2.44% | ## Checklist -
