signal.title: [diffusion] Guard unsupported quantized component checkpoints
signal.text: ## Summary - add one fail-closed admission boundary for native auxiliary component loaders that only materialize plain state dicts - reject detected top-level, nested text-config, and compressed-tensors quantization metadata before model construction or large weight reads - apply the boundary to connectors/duration heads, bridges, diffusion decoders, sound tokenizers, spatial upsamplers, and vocoders - keep the local PE model on its Transformers `from_pretrained` path, where compatible quantization formats remain model-specific - use one documentation contract across the overview, CLI, compatibility matrix, and quantization guide ## Motivation #35184 makes independent component repository routing generic and safely routes supported quantized VAEs. The remaining raw-state native loaders still had no common quantization admission rule, so a quantized component repo could be interpreted as a dense module or fail only after allocating/loading weights. Path routing and quantized materialization are separate capabilities. This PR does not add a generic per-component quantization knob: such a knob would overstate support until each loader has a matching backend. Existing transformer, native encoder, VAE, PE/Transformers, and upstream AutoModel quantization paths remain unchanged. ## Validation - all pre-commit hooks pass - focused unit coverage added for metadata layouts and early rejection order - runtime tests left to CI <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32545334559](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32545334559)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32545334428](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32545334428)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:heavy_minus_sign: **No AMD PR run found for this commit**.<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [Perf] Tune the W4AFP8 DeepEP low-latency requant launch geometry
signal.text: ## Motivation `fp8_per_token_to_per_tensor_quant_triton()` turns DeepEP low-latency's per-token-group fp8 payload into the per-tensor fp8 that the first CUTLASS W4A8 grouped GEMM consumes. It is a pure streaming pass — two bytes moved and two multiplies per element — but three properties of its launch shape cost more than the arithmetic does. **Access width.** A 1024-element tile over 8 warps is 4 B/thread, which is exactly where Triton stops vectorizing: the compiled kernel contained only `ld.global.b32` / `st.global.b32` on every part tested. 4 warps put 8 B/thread in flight and restore `v2.b32` accesses (2 warps reach `v4.b32`, but measured slower than 4). **Scale addressing.** Scales were indexed on the element axis (`(k_offsets // 128) * stride2`), so each 1024-lane load resolved to 8 distinct addresses read 128 times each. The dispatcher returns the last two scale dims column-major for TMA (`[E, M, hidden // 128]` with `stride1 == 1`), so those 8 addresses are `m` elements apart — a scattered gather, replicated per row, per tile. **Grid shape.** The m-grid was pinned to 32 programs per expert regardless of how many rows were live, so at low-latency decode row counts most programs only loaded `masked_m`, compared, and exited. This is by far the largest effect, and it grows with the local expert count: at 256 local experts and one row each, the kernel spent 35 µs to move 3 µs of data. ## Modifications `python/sglang/kernels/ops/moe/ep_moe_kernels.py` - Tile the payload as `[G_BLOCK_SIZE, 128]` — whole scale groups — instead of a flat run of elements. The per-group scale becomes one scalar load, the fast axis stays contiguous, and a partial `k` masks whole groups. (`K_BLOCK_SIZE` is renamed `G_BLOCK_SIZE` because the constexpr changed units: it counted hidden elements, it now counts 128-wide scale groups, so 8 groups is the old 1024 elements.) - Launch with 4 warps. - A 1024-element tile per program, widening to 2048 once there are >= 32 local experts, where the expert axis alone fills the machine. The tile is kept in *elements* and divided by the scale group width to get `G_BLOCK_SIZE`, because bytes-per-thread is the tuned quantity -- a different group width would otherwise silently halve or double the measured tile. It is also rounded down to the payload, so a small hidden size never runs a mostly-masked tile. - `requant_launch_geometry()` sizes the m-grid from `expected_rows`: one program per expected row, floored at 4, never above the historical 32, and additionally capped by the expert count while fewer than 64 rows per expert are live — past that the extra programs carry real work rather than early exits, and the cap costs a few percent. The estimate is rounded **down** to a power of two because `dispatch_a` already rounds up (it adds the expert count before dividing), so a uniform average of 8 rows arrives as 9 and must not launch 16 programs. The m-grid therefore only ever *shrinks*, which is why no measured cell regresses. - `expected_rows=None` keeps the previous **m-grid** for any other caller; note the tile width and warp count change regardless of that argument. `cutlass_w4a8_moe.py` / `w4afp8.py` — thread the dispatcher's `expected_m` (already computed host-side in `dispatch_a`, and constant for a captured CUDA graph) down to the requant. It is a launch hint only: correctness does not depend on it, and an expert that receives more rows than expected simply loops over more of them. Tests: the GPU unit test covers the geometry combinations (row estimates, 4/40/128 experts, row-major and column-major scales, uneven per-expert row counts); a CPU test pins the heuristic's contracts; and a new `base-b-kernel-benchmark` entry compares the shipped geometry against the previous one. ## Accuracy Tests Output is **bitwise identical to the merged kernel** on H100, H200 and B200 — every shape below at 0, 1, 3, 7, 64 and all padded rows live, both scale layouts, plus a skewed `masked_m` where every expert gets a different row count: ``` == bitwise equality vs main, high expert counts == ok k7168 E64 ok k7168 E128 ok k7168 E256 ok k3584 E112 ok k3584 E256 ok k3584 E512 ALL PASS ``` Unit tests: **48 passed** on H100, H200 and B200 — and across two toolchains, `torch 2.11.0+cu130` / `triton 3.6.0` and `torch 2.13.0+cu130` / `triton 3.7.1` (the newer pair matters because the access-width behaviour this PR exploits is Triton codegen, not hardware). That count includes the existing W4AFP8 dtype and post-reorder CPU tests. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Merged `main` vs this branch, DeepEP column-major scales, timed inside a CUDA graph, variants interleaved and order-swapped (the first variant measured reads ~10% fast on sub-2 µs shapes). `rows` is live rows per expert, and the row estimate passed in is what `dispatch_a` would report for that dispatch. **8 to 56 local experts** | shape | rows | H100 | H200 | B200 | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 7168, 8 experts | 8 / 32 | 1.03x / 1.11x | 1.08x / 1.10x | 0.98x / 1.18x | | | 512 / 1024 | 1.18x / 1.18x | 1.25x / 1.24x | 1.33x / **1.48x** | | 3584, 8 experts | 8 / 32 | 1.23x / 1.15x | 1.27x / 1.14x | 1.01x / 1.14x | | | 512 / 1024 | 1.15x / 1.06x | 1.28x / 1.07x | 1.22x / 1.24x | | 3584, 56 experts | 8 / 32 | **2.43x** / 1.85x | **2.51x** / 1.92x | **2.32x** / 2.00x | | | 128 / 256 | 1.30x / 1.21x | 1.52x / 1.39x | 1.74x / 1.84x | | 1152, 8 experts | 8 / 32 | 1.06x / 1.06x | 1.11x / 1.07x | 1.01x / 1.05x | | | 512 / 1024 | 1.18x / 1.19x | 1.19x / 1.20x | 1.16x / 1.19x | The single sub-1.00x cell is B200 at 8 rows: 1.84 vs 1.87 µs, a 0.03 µs tie. **64 to 512 local experts** — where the old fixed grid hurt most (`main` µs -> branch µs on H100): | shape | rows=1 | rows=8 | rows=32 | rows=128 | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 7168, 64 experts | 9.3 -> 1.9 (**4.9x**) | 9.6 -> 3.1 (3.1x) | 13.3 -> 7.3 (1.81x) | 53.2 -> 44.4 (1.20x) | | 7168, 128 experts | 18.1 -> 2.1 (**8.6x**) | 18.2 -> 4.5 (4.1x) | 33.5 -> 23.5 (1.42x) | 101.5 -> 84.0 (1.21x) | | 7168, 256 experts | 35.3 -> 3.3 (**10.6x**) | 35.8 -> 7.9 (4.6x) | 64.8 -> 44.5 (1.46x) | 195.2 -> 161.4 (1.21x) | | 3584, 112 experts | 9.5 -> 1.8 (5.2x) | 9.6 -> 2.8 (3.5x) | 13.5 -> 6.4 (2.10x) | 47.5 -> 38.7 (1.23x) | | 3584, 256 experts | 20.6 -> 2.2 (9.2x) | 20.7 -> 4.1 (5.0x) | 37.7 -> 22.6 (1.67x) | 102.2 -> 82.4 (1.24x) | | 3584, 512 experts | 40.3 -> 3.3 (**12.1x**) | 41.0 -> 8.2 (5.0x) | 73.7 -> 44.7 (1.65x) | — | H200 and B200 are the same shape and generally better at >= 32 rows: e.g. 3584 / 512 experts at 32 rows is 2.07x on H200 and 2.86x on B200, and 7168 / 256 experts at 128 rows is 1.39x / 1.87x. **Rounding the row estimate down rather than up** (both directions measured at the same shapes): | shape | true rows | H100 (triton 3.6 / 3.7.1) | H200 | B200 | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 7168, 8 experts | 4 | +12.1% / +0.3% | +12.5% | +12.3% | | 3584, 56 experts | 8 | +3.5% / +3.0% | +4.9% | +6.1% | | 3584, 128 experts | 4 | +7.4% / +8.0% | +8.1% | +8.9% | Positive means rounding up is slower. Triton 3.7.1 closes the 7168 case to a tie but never reverses the direction. The in-tree benchmark reproduces the low-expert-count end (H200, µs): ``` hidden num_experts m rows | tuned legacy-geometry 7168 8 1024 8 | 1.5698 2.2400 7168 8 1024 256 | 8.9140 11.0138 3584 56 256 8 | 2.3238 5.5467 3584 56 256 256 | 28.9774 39.4359 ``` Two things I would flag rather than hide. The heuristic was fitted from sweeps of `m_grid ∈ {1..64}` x `g_block ∈ {8, 16, 32}` over hidden sizes 1152/3584/7168, expert counts 8 to 512 and row counts 1 to 256, on all three parts; the shipped choice lands within ~0-5% of the per-cell optimum in the low-latency decode range, with a few ~8-12% outliers on sub-4 µs shapes at very high expert counts. And the *best* tile/warp pair is architecture-dependent at high expert counts — the parts disagree there — so the values here are the ones that win on all of them, and closing the remaining few percent would need autotuning rather than constants. Not covered: a multi-node end-to-end decode run. This is a kernel-level change with bitwise-equal output, so the risk is confined to performance, but the e2e number is still outstanding. H20 was not measured — it is not present in either of our GPU fleets. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). — no user-facing behaviour or flags change. - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32545378258](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32545378258)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32545378103](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32545378103)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32545378287](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32545378287)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [diffusion] read the next mapped layer ahead instead of faulting on it
signal.text: ## Motivation A weight left on the checkpoint mapping (#35701) is copied to the device synchronously, so when the page cache has dropped its pages the read happens on the critical path: the copy stalls in a major fault while the GPU waits. On MiniMax-H3 that is 44 GiB of DiT weights walked once per denoise step against roughly 8 GiB of page cache, so most steps fault. It shows up as load sensitivity — the denoise stage tracks how contended the host's memory bandwidth is, because the faults are competing for it. Every alternative that buys overlap buys it with host memory this budget does not have: pinning cannot be done on a mapping at all, and staging copies are the thing the mapping exists to avoid. Readahead buys it with nothing. ## Modifications `MADV_WILLNEED` over the next layer's mapped range, issued when the current layer is staged. Asynchronous readahead: free when the pages are already resident, overlapped with the current layer's compute when they are not, and it commits no memory of its own. One call per layer rather than per weight — a layer's mapped tensors are slices of the same checkpoint shard, so advising min..max covers them together and keeps this to one syscall per prefetch. `madvise` is bound through `ctypes` once and left as `None` where libc does not offer it, so the advice is skipped rather than guarded at every call site. ## Accuracy Tests Which pages are resident when a copy runs; the bytes copied are identical. `test_layerwise_offload.py` on this branch: 55 passed. ## Speed Tests and Profiling H3 `fl2va`, 864x480 / 124 frames / 20 steps, seed 1101, single RTX 4090, 12 GiB VRAM cap enforced with `torch.cuda.set_per_process_memory_fraction`, host memory capped at 32 GiB, `--layerwise-resident-layers video_vae=36`. This box is shared and its load average swings between 80 and 220, which is exactly the axis this change is about, so the samples are reported with it: | | load | denoise | decode | end to end | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | without readahead | 87 | 144.65 s | 13.08 s | 161.44 s | | without readahead | 131 | 157.05 s | 13.21 s | 175.72 s | | without readahead | 152 | 146.68 s | 12.92 s | 163.25 s | | **with readahead** | **139** | **144.89 s** | 12.88 s | **161.50 s** | | **with readahead** | **217** | **144.82 s** | 12.76 s** | **161.34 s** | Without it, end to end swings 161–176 s with load. With it, load 139 and load 217 both land at 161.3–161.5 s: the load-sensitive term is gone, which is the point. The decode stage is unchanged, as expected — its weights are held resident for the stage rather than re-read. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). signal.title: [Feature] PP Support PD + DSpark
signal.text: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation Fixes #32750. The existing PD + DSpark path works without Pipeline Parallelism because the prefill worker captures all required target hidden states, injects draft KV locally, and transfers target KV + draft KV to the decode worker. With PP enabled, the captured target hidden states are distributed across PP stages. Each stage only owns a subset of the features required by the DSpark context projection. Injecting draft KV independently on each stage is not equivalent to the non-PP computation because RMSNorm must be applied after the full context projection is accumulated. ## Design This PR keeps the existing PD data plane unchanged: ```text Prefill -> target KV + draft KV -> Decode ``` Hidden states are not transferred across the PD boundary. Each prefill PP stage computes its local pre-norm context contribution: ```text ctx_i = h_i @ W_i.T ``` The accumulated context is carried through PP proxy tensors: ```text ctx_acc = recv_ctx_acc + ctx_i ``` The last PP stage performs: ```text ctx_norm = RMSNorm(ctx_acc) K, V = KVProj(ctx_norm) ``` and writes draft KV into the prefill-side draft KV pool. This preserves the original non-PP computation: ```text concat(h1, ..., hk) @ W_fc.T == sum_i(h_i @ W_i.T) ``` while keeping the additional PP payload fixed at `[num_tokens, hidden_size]`. ## Changes ### PP-aware target capture - Capture only target layers owned by the current PP rank. - Carry local captures through `dspark_aux_hidden_states`. - See [`deepseek_v4.py`](https://github.com/bytedance-iaas/sglang/blob/fix/dspark-lifecycle-draft-kv-pool/python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_v4.py#L2455-L2467) and [`kimi_k3.py`](https://github.com/bytedance-iaas/sglang/blob/fix/dspark-lifecycle-draft-kv-pool/python/sglang/srt/models/kimi_k3.py#L2483-L2525). ### Fixed-size PP context accumulation - Each rank computes its local projection contribution. - `dspark_ctx_acc` remains `[num_tokens, hidden_size]` across PP hops. - Raw `dspark_aux_hidden_states` is removed after local projection. - RMSNorm is applied once on the final PP rank. - See [`dspark_worker_v2.py`](https://github.com/bytedance-iaas/sglang/blob/fix/dspark-lifecycle-draft-kv-pool/python/sglang/srt/speculative/dspark_components/dspark_worker_v2.py#L693-L726). ### DSV4 block-FP8 column slicing - Slice matching FP8 weight columns and scale blocks. - Support canonical FP8 scales and DeepGEMM packed UE8M0 scales. - Avoid repeated zero-padded full-K GEMMs for cross-rank target features. - See [`deepseek_v4_dspark.py`](https://github.com/bytedance-iaas/sglang/blob/fix/dspark-lifecycle-draft-kv-pool/python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_v4_dspark.py#L70-L147). Unsupported quantization backends retain the full-K fallback in [`project_target_hidden_partial()`](https://github.com/bytedance-iaas/sglang/blob/fix/dspark-lifecycle-draft-kv-pool/python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_v4_dspark.py#L803-L846). ### Single-owner fast path When all target layers belong to the final PP rank, that rank uses the existing full projection directly. Non-owner DSV4 ranks use lifecycle-only skeleton models: - No draft stages or heads. - No checkpoint weight loading. - No draft KV pool. - No planner, proposer, or injector. - Distributed lifecycle remains aligned across ranks. See [`dspark_config.py`](https://github.com/bytedance-iaas/sglang/blob/fix/dspark-lifecycle-draft-kv-pool/python/sglang/srt/speculative/dspark_components/dspark_config.py#L41-L73) and [`deepseek_v4_dspark.py`](https://github.com/bytedance-iaas/sglang/blob/fix/dspark-lifecycle-draft-kv-pool/python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_v4_dspark.py#L678-L708). ### Draft KV injection and transfer - Add projected-context KV injection on the final PP rank. - Apply normalization, WKV projection, KV normalization, and RoPE before writing draft SWA KV. - Assign target KV global layer IDs. - Use the `1_000_000+` namespace for draft KV entries. - Only the final PP rank transfers draft KV; every PP rank transfers its local target KV. See [`dspark_kv_inject.py`](https://github.com/bytedance-iaas/sglang/blob/fix/dspark-lifecycle-draft-kv-pool/python/sglang/srt/speculative/dspark_components/dspark_kv_inject.py#L77-L159), [`utils.py`](https://github.com/bytedance-iaas/sglang/blob/fix/dspark-lifecycle-draft-kv-pool/python/sglang/srt/disaggregation/utils.py#L965-L1001), and [`prefill.py`](https://github.com/bytedance-iaas/sglang/blob/fix/dspark-lifecycle-draft-kv-pool/python/sglang/srt/disaggregation/prefill.py#L197-L257). ### PP bootstrap and transfer consensus - Ordered intersection for successful bootstrap/transfer requests. - Ordered union for failures. - Any PP-rank failure becomes a global failure. - KV is not released until the local transfer reaches a terminal state. See [`scheduler_pp_mixin.py`](https://github.com/bytedance-iaas/sglang/blob/fix/dspark-lifecycle-draft-kv-pool/python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler_pp_mixin.py#L861-L914) and [`prefill.py`](https://github.com/bytedance-iaas/sglang/blob/fix/dspark-lifecycle-draft-kv-pool/python/sglang/srt/disaggregation/prefill.py#L857-L938). ## Supported Scope - Supported: `PP + DSPARK + PD prefill` - Unsupported: `PP + DSPARK decode` - Unsupported: `PP + DSPARK unified serving` - Unsupported: `DSPARK + context parallelism` ## Why `scheduler_pp_mixin.py` Is Modified The last PP stage performs additional work because it injects and transfers draft KV, while the other PP stages only transfer their local target KV. This creates asymmetric transfer completion times. The previous PP scheduler logic treated successful and failed transfers as one unordered set. It could also admit requests based only on `KVPoll.WaitingForInput`, before confirming that every PP stage had sufficient local metadata credits. Under sustained load, these behaviors could cause: - different PP stages to admit requests in different orders; - early KV release on stages that completed before the last PP stage; - inflight queue divergence after a transfer failure; - PP send/receive or proxy-tensor scheduling desynchronization. The scheduler changes make the control plane deterministic: - bootstrap readiness is probed without reserving resources; - request order is preserved during PP intersection and union; - transfer success requires intersection across all PP stages; - transfer failure is propagated as a union across all PP stages; - release occurs only after the last PP stage has completed both target KV and draft KV transfer; - DSpark draft input is reconstructed after PP output processing; - PP output tokens are moved to the batch device before creating the next draft state. The scheduler does not transfer hidden states or draft KV itself. Its role is to keep admission, completion, and release decisions consistent across PP stages despite the extra work performed by the last stage. ## fixes state-component matching This patch fixes state-component matching for PD transfer when PP ranks expose different state component layouts. Previously, state components were matched positionally: ```text prefill state[i] -> decode state[i] ``` That is not always valid for DSV4 under PP. Some state components are optional per PP stage. For example, `C128_STATE` only exists on PP ranks that own C128 layers. When the final PP rank sends draft SWA but does not own any C128 layer, the source and destination layouts can diverge: ```text Prefill final PP rank: state[0] = target SWA state[1] = draft SWA Decode rank: state[0] = target SWA state[1] = target C128_STATE state[2] = draft SWA ``` With positional matching, `prefill state[1]` would incorrectly map to `decode state[1]`, so draft SWA could be written into the target C128 state buffer. The fix is to include `state_types` in the decode registration metadata and match state components by `(StateType, occurrence)` instead of list index: ```text prefill SWA #1 -> decode SWA #1 prefill SWA #2 -> decode SWA #2 ``` This keeps the existing behavior when layouts are already aligned, while correctly handling missing optional components such as `C128_STATE`. The change is applied to both Mooncake and NIXL transfer paths. For mixed-version compatibility, if the peer does not provide `state_types`, the code falls back to the old positional mapping. This does not change the actual KV/state data layout or copy logic. It only changes how the destination state component is selected. ## Accuracy Tests ``` SGLANG_PP_LAYER_PARTITION="6,5,6,5,6,5,5,5" SGLANG_DISAGGREGATION_BOOTSTRAP_TIMEOUT=600 NCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME=eth0 --tool-call-parser deepseekv4 --disable-overlap-schedule --disable-piecewise-cuda-graph --disaggregation-transfer-backend mooncake --enable-metrics --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_mxfp4 --speculative-algo DSPARK --disaggregation-mode prefill --disaggregation-ib-device "mlx5_1,mlx5_2,mlx5_3,mlx5_4" --disable-flashinfer-autotune --disable-shared-experts-fusion SGLANG_DSV4_FP4_EXPERTS=1 SGLANG_JIT_DEEPGEMM_PRECOMPILE=1 SGLANG_OPT_DEEPGEMM_HC_PRENORM=1 SGLANG_OPT_USE_TILELANG_MHC_PRE=1 GLOO_SOCKET_IFNAME=eth0 NCCL_MIN_NCHANNELS=24 NCCL_IB_QPS_PER_CONNECTION=8 sglang serve signal.title: [diffusion] fix a refit KeyError on mapped weights, and stop claiming strides the reload discards
signal.text: Two defects in the metadata the mapped-weight store records, both found while verifying the one #35813 fixes. Stacked on #35813. ## Motivation **A refit of a mapped weight raises `KeyError: 'offset'`.** `update_cpu_weights` branches on `preserve_strides` but, unlike its three siblings (`prefetch_layer`, `sync_layer_to_cpu`, `iter_cpu_weights`), has no `mapped` guard. A mapped weight's metadata carries neither `offset` nor `numel`, and a fully mapped layer has no consolidated buffer at all, so the `else` branch reads keys that were never written. Reaching it needs only a Linux host whose checkpoint is larger than host memory — the configuration the mapped path exists for — plus a `weights_updater` refit. **A non-contiguous weight could stay mapped, and lose its layout in silence.** The mapped test ran before the contiguity test, and `MappedRegions.holds` is a storage-pointer test that says nothing about layout, so a strided view of a mapping took the mapped branch. Reload there allocates with `torch.empty(shape)` and copies: values survive, strides do not. The metadata recorded `stride` and hardcoded `preserve_strides: False`, so the one key that could have restored the layout was never read. No configuration in the tree reaches the second one today — `use_checkpoint_tensor_directly` is MPS-gated and the quantization passes that transpose weights all allocate anonymously, so the two sets are disjoint. What closes the gap is the size test the encoder loader already applies (`text_encoder_loader.py`: "On any host it becomes the only call once the checkpoint is larger than host memory"). Adopting it for a DiT is what would hand `fp8_scaled_mm` a row-major weight where its own comment calls column-major a correctness requirement — no shape mismatch, no error. ## Modifications - `update_cpu_weights`: a mapped weight's new values go into an owned CPU tensor that replaces the store entry. The mapping is a read-only view of the checkpoint, so it cannot be written back; owning the storage costs that weight's bytes in anonymous memory, on a configuration that chose mapping because host memory was short. - Require contiguity before a weight stays mapped, so a strided one falls through to the `torch.empty_strided` path that preserves its layout. - Drop the `stride` key from mapped metadata. Nothing read it. ## Accuracy Tests Two tests in `test_layerwise_offload.py`, both failing before this change on Linux (the second with the exact `KeyError: 'offset'`) and passing after; 55 passed in the file, no regressions. - a transposed view of a mapping is claimed by the strided path, keeps `stride() == (1, 8)`, and records `preserve_strides: True` - a refit of a mapped weight returns the name as updated, leaves the new values in the store, and leaves the checkpoint file byte-identical ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Code Formatting with Pre-Commit](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-formatting-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests as outlined in the [Running Unit Tests](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#running-unit-tests-adding-tests-to-ci). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32545065647](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32545065647)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32545065489](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32545065489)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32545065675](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32545065675)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [docs] Re-measure the Qwen3.8-27B RTX 5090, RTX PRO 6000 and DGX Spark grids on 1cf2b8c
signal.text: ## Motivation #35786 retuned the RTX 5090 DFLASH2 cells against commit `1cf2b8c` (#35496), leaving the card split across two builds. This unifies the RTX 5090 column on that commit — and, rather than tuning only the cells that were suspect, **re-runs every published RTX 5090, RTX PRO 6000 and DGX Spark cell end to end** so each pin on those two cards is a measurement rather than an inheritance. The NVFP4 cells were exercised with `RadixArk/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4-BF16-LMHead`, the dense-`lm_head` export that will replace the current NVFP4 repo. Its head adds ~3.2 GB of weights, which is what moves the 32 GB card's pins. ## Modifications RTX PRO 6000: **no changes** — all 48 cells serve at the published `0.85 / chunk 2048`. RTX 5090: | Cell | Published | This PR | |---|---|---| | no-speculation, all four | 0.90 | unchanged | | EAGLE float32 | 0.94 | unchanged | | EAGLE bfloat16 | 0.92 | **0.93** | | DSpark bfloat16 | 0.90 | **0.88** | | DFlash2 bfloat16 | 0.88 | **0.91 + `--chunked-prefill-size 1024`** | | DSpark float32, DFlash2 float32 | 0.92 / 0.895 | **greyed out** | - The DFlash2 bfloat16 cell is the only one on the page that needs a prefill chunk below the engine default; the overlay now emits it. - float32 is greyed for both draft-model picks on the 5090 only. EAGLE and no-speculation keep float32 — replayssm keeps EAGLE's state pool tiny and no-speculation loads no draft weights, so neither is squeezed. - Install accordion already pins `1cf2b8c` for the RTX 5090 column and the DFLASH2 cells (carried from the previous commit on this branch). DGX Spark: **base mem-fraction 0.85 → 0.80** on all three quant cells, and DFLASH2's `in-progress` badge comes off — the platform's full 48-cell grid is now verified on `1cf2b8c`. - The 0.80 pin is a host collision, not a VRAM wall: on 128 GB unified memory, 0.85 leaves ~8 GB for the OS — exactly DGX OS earlyoom's SIGTERM threshold (`-M 8388608`). The first long prefill or boot-time graph capture dips under it and the scheduler dies with `exit code -15` and no traceback. At 0.85, 15/48 cells were killed, each matching an earlyoom journal entry 1:1; which 15 is margin noise, biased toward bfloat16-SSM and the DSPARK/DFLASH2 high-ratio cells. At 0.80 every cell served on every attempt. ## Accuracy Tests N/A (docs only). ## Speed Tests and Profiling 112 cells across three platforms, all on `1cf2b8c`, ISL 8192 / OSL 1024, concurrency 1, 4 prompts, `--random-range-ratio 1.0`. A cell passes only on exit 0 with exactly 4 successful requests, 32,768 input and 4,096 generated tokens. **RTX PRO 6000 — 48/48 pass at the published pins**, across BF16 / FP8 / NVFP4 × none / EAGLE / DSpark / DFlash2 × both tiers × both state dtypes. Sample: NVFP4 + DFlash2 + High-Throughput + float32 → pool 203,670, 5.38 ms TPOT; BF16 + no-spec + Low-Latency + float32 → pool 271,433, 37.51 ms. **RTX 5090 — verified pins** | Cell | pin | KV pool | slots | TPOT | accept | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | no-spec bf16 LL | 0.90 | 82,422 | 42 | 14.40 ms | — | | EAGLE bf16 LL | 0.93 | 16,992 | 6 | 8.07 ms | 3.02 | | EAGLE fp32 LL | 0.94 | 15,746 | 5 | 8.50 ms | 2.90 | | DSpark bf16 LL | 0.88 | 17,954 | 5 | 7.41 ms | 2.59 | | DFlash2 bf16 LL | 0.91 + chunk 1024 | 13,506 | 5 | 4.92 ms | 4.29 | | DFlash2 bf16 HT | 0.91 + chunk 1024 | 15,330 | 4 | 4.92 ms | 4.29 | **Why the four float32 draft-model cells are greyed.** Each was walked from 0.86 to 0.96 at both prefill chunk sizes, then given balanced-ratio overrides up to 20. Below ~0.92 the state pool never reaches the tier's slot count; at or above it, prefill graph capture or the first request OOMs. DSpark float32 Low-Latency, for example: K=2 at 0.89, K=3 at 0.90, K=4 at 0.91–0.92 against the 5 the tier needs, and every mem-fraction that does reach 5 fails in capture or at runtime. Overrides moved DSpark past the pool wall only to hit the runtime wall, and never got DFlash2 float32 past the pool wall at all. **DGX Spark — 48/48 serve at 0.80** (boot-and-serve standard: the same workload and exact-token pass gate, but no TPOT/accept numbers taken, consistent with this platform's previous validation). Provenance: the full 48 were measured on #35496's branch head (`1bb02535`; its DFlash2 code is byte-identical to `1cf2b8c`), then every cell whose pin this PR changes — all 15 re-pinned cells — plus the tightest unchanged cell (BF16 + DFlash2 + Low-Latency + float32) was re-verified on the literal `1cf2b8c` (`dflash2-pin-1cf2b8c`) build: 16/16 serve at the shipped 0.80. DFLASH2: 12/12, selector folded into the draft CUDA graph. EAGLE: 12/12 — replayssm keeps its state pool at the no-spec size, so these are the grid's roomiest cells. NVFP4 exercised with the BF16-LMHead export like the SM120 pass; the packed-head export also served its four DFLASH2 cells on this platform in a separate 12-cell DFLASH2 pass. GB10 reproduction quirks (CDI-only docker GPU access, `nvidia-smi` memory `Not Supported`, BF16 ~10 min to READY) are in the updated Configuration Tips bullet. ## Note on timing The NVFP4 pins here describe the BF16-LMHead export. While `RadixArk/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4` still serves the packed-head weights, the NVFP4 cells on this page are a step ahead of the checkpoint — so this is best merged alongside that repo swap. The BF16 and FP8 cells, and the non-NVFP4 conclusions, are unaffected either way. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: **Missing `run-ci` label** -- add it to run CI tests.<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: **Blocked** -- `run-ci` is required first.<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:heavy_minus_sign: **No AMD PR run found for this commit**.<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.text: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation Ascend generations may require different runtime representations for the same semantic data. Today, the MXFP MoE routing path directly normalizes the E8M0 scale layout in init_routing.py: npu_moe_init_routing_v2 (quant_mode=3) produces a flat [N, M] scale while the downstream A5 grouped-matmul path consumes the pair-split [N, M/2, 2] representation. This introduces a minimal DeviceOperator abstraction following #35709 and moves this runtime-visible layout adaptation out of the MoE feature code: <!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. --> ## Modifications - AscendDeviceGeneration + get_npu_device_generation(): centralized, cached generation detection (Ascend950 -> A5, else LEGACY; current device is probed, never a hardcoded device 0) - BaseDeviceOperator / A5DeviceOperator with the first contract, normalize_mxfp_scale_layout(); Base is identity (legacy representation = producer's native layout), A5 performs the existing pair-split - get_device_operator() lazy factory: importing the module never probes the device - init_routing.py: _normalize_mxfp_scale() removed; the MXFP8 branch now delegates to the DeviceOperator, keeping the quant decision (quant_mode == MXFP8_QUANT_MODE) in feature code The change is intentionally small: kernel/provider differences remain outside this abstraction. signal.title: Fix buffer-mode HiCache load-back ownership races; add optional prefetch anchor lock
signal.text: # Fix buffer-mode HiCache load-back ownership races; add optional prefetch anchor lock ## Motivation In buffer-only host memory mode, `init_load_back` consumes a staged storage prefetch by allocating device slots, queueing a layer-gated H2D transfer, and then inserting the span into the radix tree. The insert is what adjudicates slot ownership — and it ran *after* the transfer was already in flight. If the tree gained an overlapping span while the fetch was held — a concurrent request publishing the same prefix between staging and consumption, or live full-KV sitting under an SWA tombstone (invisible to the unified match length but still deduped against by the insert walk) — the insert freed the very slots the in-flight copy targeted: a queued use-after-free. Reallocation of those slots produced silent KV corruption and downstream allocator faults. ## Changes 1. **Ownership pre-check (always on):** before launching the transfer, re-match against live tree state and require both the unified match length and `full_kv_hit_length` to equal the staged `matched_len`. This proves the insert can only add nodes, never dedup-free the incoming slots. Invalid holds drop with a warning and the request recomputes. 2. **Post-insert fail-stop:** if the post-insert canonical tree slice diverges from the incoming slots, raise instead of returning indices that a queued transfer no longer owns. 3. **Canonical ownership:** return the post-insert tree slice rather than the raw allocation. 4. **Optional anchor lock (env-gated, default off):** `SGLANG_ENABLE_HICACHE_BUFFER_ANCHOR_LOCK=1` pins the staged prefetch's device anchor from IO commit to consumption so eviction cannot invalidate the splice and waste the fetch. Locked tokens are capped at `SGLANG_HICACHE_BUFFER_ANCHOR_LOCK_CAP` × the device pool (default 0.5); over-cap holds launch unlocked, so queued holds can never make the pool unevictable. Locks are released idempotently at every consume/drop/abort exit, with a fail-loud accounting assert. ## Testing - Three regression tests covering the race class: sibling-published span (unified drift), full-KV overlap masked by an SWA tombstone (only `full_kv_hit_length` can see it), and the post-insert fail-stop. All three fail on the pre-fix code and pass with the fix. - Full `test_unified_radix_cache_unittest.py` passes. - Verified in an extended production-shaped soak on an internal deployment (buffer-only mode with a storage backend): the ownership checks drop conflicting holds cleanly under concurrent same-prefix traffic, the anchor lock eliminates eviction-caused prefetch waste in steady and moderate-churn regimes, and the lock accounting stayed exact across many engine restarts. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32542984646](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32542984646)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32542984592](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32542984592)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32542984583](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32542984583)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [MLX] Upgrade to Torch 2.13/MLX 0.32+ and redesign the Torch-MLX tensor bridge
signal.text: ## Motivation MLX 0.32 can import Torch MPS allocations directly, while Torch 2.13 changes the runtime and DLPack edge cases that the Apple Silicon integration must support. The existing bridge stages MPS tensors through CPU memory, obscures borrowed-versus-owned lifetimes, and pays payload-sized copies. Separately, diffusion's `SGLANG_USE_MLX` norm override is not selected by normal MPS `CustomOp` dispatch; forcing those norms through Torch-MLX crossings is slower end to end. This PR upgrades the `srt_mps` runtime, fails fast on unsupported Torch/MLX pairs, separates owned copies from scoped zero-copy borrows, and removes the unreachable diffusion-only MLX fallback. It does not replace the existing SRT MLX runner; the stacked [yeahdongcn/sglang#7](https://github.com/yeahdongcn/sglang/pull/7) consumes these bridge primitives while redesigning that backend. ## Modifications - Update `srt_mps` in `python/pyproject_other.toml` to Torch 2.13.0, MLX >= 0.32.0, TorchVision 0.28.0, TorchAudio 2.11.0, and TorchCodec 0.15.0. The versions stay directly in `srt_mps`, matching the existing extra layout; `all_mps` inherits them through `srt_mps`. MLX keeps a 0.32.0 minimum but has no upper bound; startup accepts newer stable MLX releases. TorchAudio 2.11 remains intentional and was validated with the tested Torch 2.13 MPS stack. CPU and standalone `diffusion_mps` dependency lists are unchanged. - Move the SRT MLX version/device validation to the earliest model-independent `ServerArgs` bootstrap. With `SGLANG_USE_MLX=1`, SGLang requires stable Torch 2.13.x and stable MLX >= 0.32.0. Older MLX, Torch outside 2.13.x, and rc/dev builds fail before model path resolution/downloads and before the dummy-model short circuit. With the flag unset, importing SGLang still does not import MLX. - Redesign `tensor_bridge.py` around explicit ownership and batching: - `torch_to_mlx` creates and materializes MLX-owned storage when the result must outlive its Torch source. - `MlxTensorView` and `borrow_torch_tensors` provide persistent and batched zero-copy MPS borrows while retaining every Torch storage owner. - `mlx_call` and `mlx_call_multi` validate the target before work, fence Torch producers once, keep all borrowed inputs alive through lazy evaluation, evaluate ordinary multi-output results at one shared `mx.eval` boundary, batch the additional materialization boundary required by negative-stride outputs, and export them through DLPack. - `mlx_to_torch` uses evaluated DLPack views for MPS and explicit CPU views. Positive-stride layouts, including CPU float64, remain zero-copy. Negative-stride MLX views are materialized because Torch 2.13's DLPack importer otherwise aborts the process instead of raising a Python exception; unsupported CPU dtypes fail instead of silently narrowing. This PR intentionally owns these shared Torch-MLX bridge primitives. The stacked MPS redesign in [yeahdongcn/sglang#7](https://github.com/yeahdongcn/sglang/pull/7) consumes them for Torch-owned model weights and provider outputs, while its provider-specific invalidation callbacks and phase timing stay in that PR. - Remove `mps_fallback.py`, route diffusion MPS kernels to native Torch fallbacks, and use `F.layer_norm`/`F.rms_norm` instead of the old manual decomposition. The shared fallback remains compatible with both the default Torch 2.11 and CPU-backend Torch 2.12 stacks. RMSNorm preserves the optional-bias and input-dtype contracts even with fp32 parameters. The removed rotary and scale/shift entries were already aliases to Torch implementations; only the norm entries had MLX-specific implementations. - Remove diffusion's `SGLANG_USE_MLX` runtime handling and clarify in the existing documentation that the variable applies only to SRT serving. SRT keeps its existing `SGLANG_USE_MLX=1` opt-in. - Add Torch 2.13-compatible Triton import-stub symbols used by Inductor on MPS. - Rebase the branch onto upstream `main` at `978244d67148`; update VAE and Transformer component loaders to the upstream unified residency API so MPS layerwise offload remains valid after the upstream loader refactor. The diffusion MLX norm path is intentionally dropped after tracing and measurement. `CustomOp.dispatch_forward()` routes MPS to `forward_native`, so the legacy MLX override is unreachable in the normal production graph. Sana instrumentation confirmed zero legacy entrypoint calls, and forcing all 58 norms per DiT forward through MLX was slower end to end. Isolated large fp32 LayerNorm microbenchmarks sometimes favored MLX by a few percent, but the result was not robust across the common fp16/bf16 cases and did not justify repeated framework crossings. A future fully MLX-resident diffusion path can be evaluated separately. ## Accuracy Tests - `PATH="$PWD/sglang-metal/bin:$PATH" SGLANG_USE_MLX=1 HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 ./sglang-metal/bin/python test/run_suite.py --hw mlx --suite stage-a-unit-test-mlx` - **21/21 registered test files passed locally** on Apple M1 at PR head `c1f34a81d1`, including bridge, startup runtime gate, Triton-stub, and diffusion fallback coverage. - The focused bridge/runtime/diffusion-loader bundle passed **121 tests plus 36 subtests** after the rebase. - All four new test files are registered in `stage-a-unit-test-mlx`. `test_diffusion_torch_fallback.py` is additionally registered in `base-a-test-cpu`, `base-b-test-cpu`, and `base-b-test-cpu-arm64`. - The same six fallback UTs passed **6/6** in isolated Torch 2.11.0 and 2.12.0 CPU environments, including fp16/bf16 inputs with fp32 parameters. - Runtime tests verify Torch 2.12/2.14, MLX 0.31, and Torch/MLX rc/dev builds are rejected, while stable Torch 2.13 patch releases and stable MLX releases from 0.32.0 onward (including future minor versions) are accepted. Incompatible versions abort `ServerArgs` creation even for `model_path="dummy"`; missing MLX, unavailable PyTorch MPS, and unavailable MLX Metal each produce actionable startup errors. The disabled path constructs `ServerArgs` without importing MLX. - Bridge ownership checks cover owned/scoped/persistent lifetimes, source mutation and deletion, single-fence batched borrows, shared-eval multi-output calls, bfloat16/non-contiguous views, CPU float64 and unsupported dtypes, autograd detachment, invalid-target fail-fast behavior, and negative-stride materialization in an abort-safe subprocess. - SRT serving smoke with local `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B`: both `SGLANG_USE_MLX=1` and the no-env Torch-MPS path returned **200** from `/health` and `/generate`. For prompt `The capital of France is` with greedy 8-token decoding, both paths returned identical output token IDs `[12095, 13, 576, 6722, 315, 9625, 374, 1083]` and text `Paris. The capital of France is also`. - Sana 600M, prompt `A small red cube on a plain white background`, seed 42, 256x256, 4 steps: native Torch output and the hypothetical all-MLX norm output remained visually consistent (PSNR 41.95 dB; max pixel delta 50). The final `mlx_call` image was byte-identical to the earlier explicit- keepalive MLX image. The ordinary Sana path recorded 58 Torch norm calls per DiT forward and zero legacy norm-fallback entrypoint calls. After the rebase, a native Torch-MPS Sana smoke with the same 256x256/4-step configuration produced a valid RGB PNG in 24.87s with 6.33GB peak memory. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Environment: Apple M1, macOS 26.5.2, Torch 2.13.0, MLX 0.32.0. All timings include the required producer/consumer synchronization. The operation table reports end-to-end norm-call timings, including bridge/export and synchronization, rather than raw kernel-only timings. It is one representative median-after-warmup run; an independent rerun preserved the common-Sana ordering but flipped whether large-fp32 MLX was slightly ahead or behind. | Case | Torch native | MLX owned copy | MLX scoped borrow | |---|---:|---:|---:| | Sana RMSNorm `(1,300,1152)` fp32 | 230 us | 676 us | 259 us | | Sana LayerNorm `(1,256,1152)` bf16 | 254 us | 913 us | 324 us | | Flux LayerNorm `(1,4096,3072)` fp32 | 2508 us | 4763 us | 2441 us | Bridge A/B directly calls the final `mlx_call(lambda a: a, tensor)` API against the pre-change CPU-staging implementation at the branch merge base (Apple M1, Torch 2.13.0, MLX 0.32.0). The table reports the range of per-batch p50 values across three independent batches; each batch used 5 warmups and 20 measured samples with producer/consumer synchronization: | Logical tensor | dtype / payload | Old CPU-staging p50 range | Final `mlx_call` p50 range | Minimum paired speedup | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:| | `(4096,4096)` | fp32 / 64 MiB | 32.134-57.424 ms | 0.0410-0.0871 ms | 368.8x | | `(4096,4096)` | bf16 / 32 MiB | 10.301-34.715 ms | 0.0293-0.0418 ms | 351.2x | | `(4096,8192)` | bf16 / 64 MiB | 16.896-22.184 ms | 0.0407-0.0617 ms | 273.7x | The old MPS round-trip staged payload through CPU/NumPy in both directions. The final `mlx_call` path aliases the Metal allocation through DLPack, removing the payload-sized copies; the synchronized wrapper/barrier cost was 29-87 us across these repeats. The same-shape bf16 case is 32 MiB because each element uses two bytes; the final row adds a true 64 MiB bf16 payload. This zero-copy result applies to the scoped-borrow API, not to an MLX array that must own its storage after the call. For that ownership contract, the 64 MiB fp32 materialized copy is about 4.08 ms versus about 60 us for a scoped borrow. This is why the API separates owned and borrowed semantics instead of exposing an unchecked `copy=False` default. Final-API Sana 4-step E2E forced-MLX experiment using `mlx_call` for all 58 norms per DiT forward (clean paired repeat): | Metric | Torch native | MLX scoped borrow | MLX penalty | |---|---:|---:|---:| | Denoising step median | 720.18 ms | 1170.40 ms | +62.5% | | DiT forward median | 375.06 ms | 581.92 ms | +55.2% | | Steady DiT median (drop first 2) | 353.42 ms | 581.92 ms | +64.7% | A second same-configuration measurement had higher Torch variance and a smaller penalty (+20.6% step, +21.9% DiT), but MLX was slower in both runs. ## Checklist - [x] Formatted with repository pre-commit hooks. - [x] Added and ran registered unit tests. - [x] Registered the shared diffusion fallback in CPU CI. - [x] Updated Apple Metal and diffusion documentation. - [x] Included accuracy and speed evidence above. - [x] CPU dependency pins remain unchanged. ## Review and Merge Process This is a draft for review of the ownership contract and the diffusion path decision. Please review the Torch/MLX lifetime semantics first; CI should run the MLX, CPU, JIT-kernel, and multimodal-generation change paths before promotion. In particular, the draft-gated MLX, Xeon CPU, and ARM64 CPU jobs must complete before this PR is marked ready. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32544631916](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32544631916)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32544631670](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32544631670)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32544631820](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32544631820)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [Diffusion][minimax-h3] Restrict MiniMax-H3 SubBlock sparsity to video queries
signal.text: ## Motivation MiniMax-H3 packs text, condition-image/video, target-video, and audio tokens into the same denoising sequence. The existing SubBlock path applies sparse attention to every query in that packed sequence, even though the sparsity policy is primarily intended for video queries. The audio latent sequence is substantially shorter than the video latent sequence and does not have the same spatial redundancy as video tokens. Applying the same 64-token block granularity and sparsity ratio to audio queries therefore produces a much coarser approximation: sparsifying a small number of audio query blocks affects a larger fraction of the generated audio. This makes short audio tracks particularly sensitive, especially near the end of a 5-second generation. Text, condition-image, audio, and mixed-modality query blocks do not benefit from the video-specific sparsity policy and may lose relevant K/V context when routed with the same top-k budget. This PR restricts sparse block selection to pure-video query blocks. Query blocks containing text, condition-image, audio, or mixed rows retain all K/V blocks and therefore execute dense attention inside the same BSA kernel. Reference-video and target-video rows remain eligible for sparse routing. ## Modifications - Track video-query provenance through MiniMax-H3 presentation, text encoding, packed-sequence preparation, and denoising. - Include target-video rows, reference-video latent rows, and Ref2VA Qwen video-placeholder rows in the video-query provenance. - Keep text, condition-image, audio, timestamp, vision-delimiter, and mixed-modality rows non-video. - Build a request-static query-block mask at the existing 64-token SubBlock granularity. - Classify each query block as: - sparse when all real rows in the block are video rows; - dense when the block contains any text, condition-image, audio, or mixed-modality row. - Keep mixed video/non-video boundary blocks dense so every non-video row retains exact attention. - Build one heterogeneous BSA block-index/count representation: - pure-video query blocks keep the router-selected top-k K/V blocks; - non-video and mixed query blocks keep all K/V blocks. - Execute the complete real packed document through one heterogeneous BSA call; the padding-only document keeps the existing dense fallback. - Use the existing per-query-block count interfaces: - SM90: `mask_block_cnt`; - SM100: `q2k_block_nums`. - Sort compact sparse prefixes before heterogeneous expansion only on SM90, where the kernel requires ordered active prefixes. - Preserve the router output order on SM100 and avoid an unnecessary GPU sort. - Avoid the additional dense FA call, video-Q gather, and dense/sparse output scatter required by the earlier two-attention prototype. - Preserve the existing SubBlock kernel contract: - 64-token query/key blocks; - SM90 SGLang CuTe-DSL kernel; - SM100 FlashInfer `bsa_attn_blk64_fwd`. - Resolve the effective MiniMax-H3 transformer backend through one H3-specific helper with selector-compatible precedence, and use the same resolution logic for admission, text metadata, and denoising metadata. - Preserve loader-scoped `transformer` component attention overrides across MiniMax-H3's lazy DiT attention initialization. - Allow configurations such as a global FA backend with `transformer=subblock_sparse_attn`. - Reject Ring parallelism unless the resolved MiniMax-H3 transformer backend is FA. - Gate video provenance and heterogeneous routing to MiniMax-H3 requests whose effective transformer backend is `subblock_sparse_attn`. - Keep non-SubBlock MiniMax-H3 execution and the behavior of all other diffusion models unchanged. - Add tests for: - video-query provenance; - pure-video and mixed query-block classification; - ragged final query blocks; - per-query-block dense/sparse counts; ## Accuracy Tests We evaluated one 5-second sample from each supported task: T2VA, FL2VA, and Ref2VA. All runs use 50 denoising steps, a 768-pixel short edge, 24 fps, and 8xH200 GPUs with SP/Ulysses degree 8. "Before" applies the SubBlock top-k budget to every query block. "After" applies the top-k budget only to pure-video query blocks, while non-video and mixed query blocks retain all K/V blocks. Each SubBlock output is compared with its matching lossless output. The Ref2VA before/after results use the exact same lossless reference. The final Ref2VA rerun was performed with the code from [#35481](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/35481) applied on top of this PR branch. ### Video quality SSIM `↑`: higher is better. | Task | SSIM before ↑ | SSIM after ↑ | Difference ↑ | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | T2VA | 0.751427 | 0.757598 | +0.006171 | | FL2VA | 0.790167 | 0.794569 | +0.004402 | | Ref2VA* | 0.940194 | 0.940913 | +0.000719 | SSIM is measured across all decoded frames using weighted YUV420 SSIM. The heterogeneous BSA implementation preserves visual quality across all three tasks. ### Full-track audio quality Correlation `↑`: higher is better. nMSE `↓`: lower is better. nMSE reduction `↑`: higher is better. | Task | Correlation before ↑ | Correlation after ↑ | nMSE before ↓ | nMSE after ↓ | nMSE reduction ↑ | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | | T2VA | 0.587379 | 0.685984 | 1.192913 | 0.536445 | 55.0% | | FL2VA | 0.752955 | 0.988301 | 1.087023 | 0.023919 | 97.8% | | Ref2VA* | 0.943636 | 0.992069 | 0.109817 | 0.015824 | 85.6% | ### Final-second audio quality Final one-second correlation `↑`: higher is better. Final one-second nMSE `↓`: lower is better. nMSE reduction `↑`: higher is better. | Task | Final 1s correlation before ↑ | Final 1s correlation after ↑ | Final 1s nMSE before ↓ | Final 1s nMSE after ↓ | nMSE reduction ↑ | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | | T2VA | 0.568423 | 0.815203 | 2.770409 | 0.341037 | 87.7% | | FL2VA | 0.878575 | 0.990173 | 0.762153 | 0.019796 | 97.4% | | Ref2VA* | 0.923841 | 0.991169 | 0.145545 | 0.017839 | 87.7% | Audio was decoded to 32 kHz stereo PCM. Correlation is the mean per-channel Pearson correlation after DC removal. nMSE is normalized by the lossless reference signal power. All compared audio tracks contain 165,888 decoded samples per channel. The best measured alignment offset is 0 ms in every comparison, so the improvements are not caused by duration changes, truncation, or codec-padding differences. The result is not expected to be audio-lossless. Video and audio remain coupled through the joint denoiser, so sparse video attention can still affect audio indirectly. This change removes the direct degradation caused by applying the video sparsity policy to non-video queries. \* Ref2VA was benchmarked with [#35481](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/35481) applied on top. ## Speed Tests and Profiling All values below are server-reported generation times after model startup. Latency `↓`: lower is better. Speedup `↑`: higher is better. SubBlock configuration: - `sparsity=0.75` - `n_q=4` - `n_k=4` - `skip_first_steps=10` - `skip_first_layers=0` - `min_seq_len=4096` ### Before: uniform sparse budget for all query blocks | Task | Lossless latency ↓ | SubBlock latency ↓ | Speedup ↑ | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | T2VA | 37.769s | 28.790s | 1.312x | | FL2VA | 41.282s | 31.113s | 1.327x | | Ref2VA | 133.510s | 91.470s | 1.460x | ### After: heterogeneous dense/sparse BSA | Task | Lossless latency ↓ | SubBlock latency ↓ | Speedup ↑ | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | T2VA | 37.552s | 28.782s | 1.305x | | FL2VA | 41.007s | 32.142s | 1.276x | | Ref2VA* | 133.510s | 92.020s | 1.451x | ### Heterogeneous-routing overhead Latency change `↓`: lower is better. | Task | SubBlock before ↓ | SubBlock after ↓ | Latency change ↓ | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | T2VA | 28.790s | 28.782s | -0.03% | | FL2VA | 31.113s | 32.142s | +3.3% | | Ref2VA* | 91.470s | 92.020s | +0.6% | The heterogeneous BSA implementation retains a 1.28-1.45x speedup over lossless execution. Compared with the previous uniform-sparsity implementation, the measured latency change ranges from -0.03% to +3.3%. Using one BSA call avoids the additional dense FA launch, video-Q gather, and output scatter of the earlier two-attention prototype. Non-video query blocks execute dense attention by setting their per-query-block count to the complete K/V block count, while pure-video blocks retain the router-selected top-k budget. signal.title: [diffusion] ship mapped layers through a courier thread
signal.text: A copy whose source is a checkpoint mapping is synchronous however it is requested — the driver stages unpinned memory through its own buffer — and the prefetch hooks run on the compute thread, so every mapped layer stalled the denoise step for its whole transfer. This adds a courier: a worker thread that stages a mapped layer's bytes into one of two pinned slots (a plain memcpy when the page cache holds them) and issues the device copy on its own stream, where it is genuinely asynchronous. Parameters are still rebound on the compute thread at collect time, so module state is never touched concurrently; blocking callers and any courier failure keep the direct synchronous path. Measured on MiniMax-H3 fl2va, one RTX 4090, 12 GiB allocator cap, 32 GiB host envelope, 864×480 / 124 frames / 20 NFE, interleaved same-window A/B: baseline 538.8 s of denoise (median 25.0 s/step) against 369.1 s (median 18.0) with the courier — 31% faster, and the effect grows with host memory-bandwidth contention, because that contention is exactly what the compute thread stops paying for. Output equivalence was checked at the video level: SSIM against a baseline run equals the baseline's own run-to-run SSIM (0.9941 = 0.9941), and the audio stream is bit-identical. Stacked with per-layer pinning (#35867) and the VAE staying on its mapping (#35862), the same budget runs the lossless bf16 denoise at a **median of 11.0–12.0 s/step across two interleaved rounds — ahead of ComfyUI's 13.0** measured under the same 32 GiB psutil convention on the same GPU in the same bandwidth window. Tests cover the ship/collect handshake, release_all draining an in-flight layer, and the fallback when the courier dies mid-flight; the first two fail with the courier disabled. Merge note: this PR and #35867 touch the same file; whichever lands second rebases (the resolution is mechanical — both sides add independent methods). 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32544255265](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32544255265)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32544255098](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32544255098)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32544255197](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32544255197)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [Fix] Prevent zombie requests after client disconnect: always dispatch AbortReq
signal.text: ## Problem Streaming clients that disconnect mid-generation (Esc in an agent UI, network drop, proxy timeout) leave **orphaned requests decoding on the scheduler until the request reaches its configured generation limit**, while TokenizerManager spams thousands of: ``` Received output for rid='...' but the state was deleted in TokenizerManager. ``` Observed on SGLang v0.5.17 while serving Qwen3.8-27B on AMD MI300X (ROCm): a single interrupted 4k-token request produced more than 5,000 error messages over several minutes and kept consuming GPU decode throughput as a zombie. ## Root cause 1. Client disconnect cancels the streaming response; `CancelledError`/`GeneratorExit` is raised inside `TokenizerManager.generate_request`. 2. Since #32588 (retained by its revert #34160), the cleanup runs under `except BaseException:` and immediately deletes `rid_to_state[rid]` via `_discard_pending_req_states`. 3. Two seconds later, the delayed `create_abort_task` fires `abort_request(rid)` - but its guard (`rid not in self.rid_to_state -> return`) silently drops the dispatch because the state was already deleted in step 2. 4. The scheduler never receives an `AbortReq` and keeps decoding; every streamed chunk then hits the missing-state error path. Regression chain: - #457 introduced the guard as pure idempotency: deletion + dispatch happened together inside `abort_request()`, so dispatch was never gated on state presence. - #28694 added the cleanup with `except Exception:` - deliberately not catching `CancelledError`, so disconnects were unaffected. - #32588 switched the cleanup to `except BaseException:`; the revert in #34160 kept that form. This made the cleanup fire on disconnect cancellation and turned the pre-existing guard into a dispatch blocker. ## Fix Two complementary changes in `python/sglang/srt/managers/tokenizer_manager.py`: - **A - `abort_request()`**: remove the `rid_to_state` presence guard. The scheduler owns the real request lifecycle; `rid_to_state` is only HTTP/stream-response bookkeeping and may legitimately be gone while a request still runs. Unknown rids are a safe no-op on the scheduler side: abort handling safely ignores requests that are no longer active, making duplicate dispatches harmless. This also restores manual `POST /abort_request` for already-orphaned rids. - **B - `generate_request()` cleanup**: replace the pop-only helper with `_abort_and_discard_pending_req_states`, which dispatches `AbortReq` **before** popping each still-pending state. Disconnect cleanup no longer depends on the delayed background task at all. ## Repro ```bash curl -sN localhost:30000/generate \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{"text":"long story...","sampling_params":{"max_new_tokens":4000},"stream":true}' & PID=$! sleep 8 && kill -9 "$PID" # client disconnect mid-decode ``` Before: thousands of `state was deleted` lines; `#running-req` stays elevated for minutes. After: <=2 backlog lines, decode stops within ~1 s. ## Verification | Test | Before | After | |---|---|---| | Streaming disconnect (mid-decode) | More than 5,000 error messages; zombie until generation limit | 2 backlog lines, stopped in ~1s | | `/abort_request` with orphaned rid | silently dropped (no-op) | dispatched, scheduler aborts | | `/abort_request` with bogus rid | dropped | safe no-op on scheduler | | Normal completion (stream/non-stream) | OK | OK | Tested on SGLang commit 5a46d657b7ea8de932266dc0a084d2217c78b168 (v0.5.17.dev, main @ 2026-08-21, ROCm build), with Qwen3.8-27B (BF16) on AMD MI300X (ROCm), TP=1, using FP8 E4M3 KV cache. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32541491057](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32541491057)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32541490987](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32541490987)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32541491040](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32541491040)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: Warn when deterministic inference is combined with a quantized KV cache
signal.text: ## Motivation `--enable-deterministic-inference` combined with a quantized KV cache silently breaks the batch-invariance guarantee the feature exists to provide, and nothing tells the user: no warning, no guard, and no mention of KV cache dtype on the deterministic inference page. The docs state SGLang "achieves fully deterministic inference", list **"Reinforcement Learning: Ensures consistent logprobs across runs"** as the primary use case, and name the root cause of non-determinism as *"different batch sizes cause GPU kernels to split reduction operations differently"* — which is exactly the mechanism that still bites here. Measured on H100 NVL / SM90, **sglang 0.5.18**, `Qwen/Qwen3-8B` (bf16 weights, so KV dtype is the only variable), `--attention-backend fa3 --enable-deterministic-inference --disable-cuda-graph`, greedy, 224 new tokens: | `--kv-cache-dtype` | first divergent **absolute** index (prompt lens 4/3/12/31) | tokens differing | max Δlogprob | |---|---|---|---| | `fp8_e4m3` | **97, 97, 97, 97** | 118–138 of 224 | **0.4625** | | *(omitted)* | **None** | **0** | **0.0** | Prompt lengths 3→31 diverge at the same *absolute* position; the bf16 control is bitwise identical. That control also rules out an off-by-one in the comparison and shows deterministic inference does deliver batch invariance on this path for bf16. Reduced to the kernel, no model and no server: `forward_extend` (`flashattention_backend.py:1497`) and `forward_decode` (`:1988`) call the *same* `flash_attn_with_kvcache` against the same paged pool, differing only in query-row count. Over byte-identical fp8 KV: | kv_len | fp8_e4m3 max\|prefill−decode\| | bitwise equal | bf16 control | |---|---|---|---| | 88 / 94 / 95 / **96** | 0.0 | ✅ | ✅ 0.0 | | **97** | **3.906e-3** | ❌ | ✅ 0.0 | | 98 → 256 | ~1e-2 | ❌ | ✅ 0.0 | The sweep is **byte-identical at `num_splits` 0 and 1**, so SplitKV — the only thing deterministic inference pins here (`:319-323`) — is not the mechanism. The kernel's internal KV-block tiling is. Full analysis, the standalone repro script, and two hypotheses I checked and ruled out (`scheduler_metadata` asymmetry; asymmetric Q cast) are in [#25790](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/25790#issuecomment-5377092000). **This PR does not fix the divergence.** The FA3 kernel is fetched from `sgl-project/sgl-attn` (`CMakeLists.txt:82-87`, fp8 SM90 instantiations at `:443-445`), so the fix belongs there and is a two-repo change. This PR closes the "silent" half: users combining these flags get told. ## Modifications - **`arg_groups/overrides.py`** — new read-only post-process pass `_deterministic_quantized_kv_cache_warning`, next to the sibling deterministic guards. Fires when deterministic inference is on and `kv_cache_dtype` is one of `fp8_e4m3`, `fp8_e5m2`, `mxfp8`, `nvfp4`, `fp4_mx_block16`. - **`server_args.py`** — invoked at its legacy slot beside `_deterministic_sampling_backend` (registration alone does not run a pass). - **`docs/.../deterministic_inference.mdx`** — "Known Limitation: Quantized KV Cache" subsection under Supported Backends. - **`test/registered/unit/server_args/test_server_args.py`** — 3 CPU-only tests: warns for fp8 and declares nothing (so the pass cannot start rewriting the user's dtype); silent for `auto`/`bf16`/`bfloat16`; silent when deterministic inference is off. The last two are the negative branches — they are what catches the predicate degrading to always-true and warning every fp8 user. Deliberate choices, happy to change any of them: 1. **Warning, not an error or an override.** The combination is still reproducible run to run, which is enough for callers who only need that; it is prefill-vs-decode agreement that fails. Erroring would break working setups and silently rewriting the user's dtype seems worse than telling them. 2. **Gated on dtype, not backend.** I measured `fp8_e4m3` on **fa3** only. `flashinfer` and `triton` at fp8 are unmeasured, so I worded it as "does not guarantee" and named the measured configuration rather than narrowing the trigger and letting unmeasured paths stay silent. If you would rather scope it to fa3, say so and I will — it needs measurement I have not done. 3. **No registered KL test asserting the current fp8 numbers.** Pinning the buggy value is the loose-threshold trap that lets a real state bug hide. A near-zero assertion becomes correct once the kernel is fixed. **Known gap:** the guard reads the CLI value, so it does not catch a *checkpoint-derived* fp8 KV cache — `--kv-cache-dtype auto` with `hf_quant_config.json: {"kv_cache_quant_algo": "FP8"}` resolves to fp8 later in `mem_cache/kv_cache_dtype.py` while `server_args` still prints `auto` (same resolution path noted in #35291). Catching that needs the warning at resolution time, where the flag is not currently available. Left as a follow-up rather than shipping a config probe I cannot exercise without an NVFP4 checkpoint. ## Accuracy Tests No effect on model outputs — the pass declares nothing and only logs. The measurements above characterise pre-existing behaviour on unmodified `main`; the bf16 column is the control. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not applicable: one dtype-set membership test during argument resolution, no runtime path touched. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). — ran the pinned `black` 26.1.0, `isort` 7.0.0, `ruff` 0.15.1 (`F401,F821,UP037`) and `codespell` 2.4.1, plus the local `check_registered_tests.py` and `check_no_bare_pytest_main.py` hooks. signal.title: [diffusion] refactor: hand out pinned host memory per layer
signal.text: The pin budget was asked once per component, all or nothing, so a DiT larger than the whole spendable budget pinned zero bytes. This asks per layer — a component too large to pin whole still pins the layers the budget covers — and spends the budget where it pays: streamed layers before resident ones (a resident layer transfers once per stage, a streamed one every step), and the stepped DiT before once-per-request encoders. Four defects found while getting there, each fixed with a test that fails when the fix is reverted: - **The same free memory was spent twice.** The copies-fit check ran before the pins it had just booked were allocated, so the live reading still counted those bytes as free — for a component between roughly 1× and 2× of available host memory, the old plan copied the whole checkpoint into memory that could not hold it. Everything the plan adds is now weighed as one sum. - **The plan was charged its gross allocations, not its net cost.** A store buffer that replaces an anonymous original — the fused-qkv share — is a wash: the original is freed when its parameter is rebound. Charging it as new made the plan give back pins the host could afford. The fit checks now weigh only the bytes copied off the checkpoint mapping. - **Pins that still do not fit are given back** from the tail of the pin order, which holds the least valuable ones, instead of over-committing. - **The benefit ranking silently degraded to bare bytes**: its step count was read off `pipeline_class_name`, an override that is normally unset, so a 45 GB once-per-request encoder could outrank the 20-step DiT. The pipeline is now resolved the way `build_pipeline` does (a cache hit by then). Measured on MiniMax-H3 fl2va, one RTX 4090, 12 GiB allocator cap, 32 GiB host envelope, with the VAE on its checkpoint mapping (#35862): the plan pins **13 of 50 DiT layers** and the run peaks at **20.4 GiB** of anonymous host memory — inside the envelope it planned for, reproduced across rounds. Stacked with the mapped-layer courier (#35882) this is the configuration that runs the lossless bf16 denoise at a median of 11.0–12.0 s/step, ahead of ComfyUI's 13.0 measured under the same 32 GiB convention on the same GPU in the same bandwidth window. Merge note: this PR and #35882 touch the same file; whichever lands second rebases (the resolution is mechanical — both sides add independent methods). 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32537578638](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32537578638)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32537578453](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32537578453)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32537578576](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32537578576)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Describe the bug ### Issue Description I observed a strange numerical inconsistency in token logprobs between the generation phase (decode) and the prefill phase (when evaluating the full sequence at once) in `sglang`. Specifically, the logprobs match perfectly at the beginning, but start to diverge at a fixed position during the output generation—typically at absolute token index **96** with both English and Chinese prompts. Here are some key insights from my test: * **FP8 Dependency:** This issue **only** occurs when the server is launched with `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3`. If I remove this flag, the logprobs match perfectly between prefill and decode. * **Model & GPU Agnostic:** The mismatch occurs across different models (e.g., `Qwen3-14B-FP8` and `MiniMax-2.5`) and persists on both single-GPU and multi-GPU configurations. This indicates a systematic issue related to FP8 quantization/kernels rather than a specific model weight anomaly. * **The Magic Index Shift:** For a standard prompt, the divergence starts exactly at index 96. In almost all test cases, regardless of how I modify the prompt length, the logprobs between prefill and decode match perfectly and identically for the first 95 tokens, and the divergence always starts exactly at absolute token index 96. There is only one specific edge-case prompt (e.g., changing the phrase to "tell me a long long story") where the divergence boundary nudged to 97. In all other prompt variations, it firmly locks at 96. I am hoping someone can help reproduce this on different hardware setups/versions, or shed some light on why **96/97** acts as the boundary for this strange inconsistency. ### Reproduction ### Server
