signal.title: Fix context-boundary max_new_tokens clipping
signal.text: ## TL;DR - **Bug:** requests accepted at the advertised context boundary can return two fewer tokens than requested. - **Cause:** a legacy output-token reserve introduced by #1748 remains in the scheduler even though exact-boundary requests are now valid (#22546) and page-aware KV admission is enforced separately (#25126). - **Fix:** use `max_req_len - input_len + 1`, while leaving the separate page-rounded global KV-admission bound unchanged. - **Safety:** generating `N` tokens forwards the prompt and only the first `N - 1` generated tokens; the final token is sampled and returned without another decode step. - **Validation:** focused scheduler tests, end-to-end boundary tests on Qwen3/Qwen3.5, speculative-decoding coverage, and an independent behavior cross-check against Mini-SGLang. ## Motivation Requests that fit the advertised context length are silently clipped by two tokens in the scheduler. With `--context-length 4096`, `ignore_eos=True`, and `max_new_tokens=16`: ```text input=4078, requested=16, actual=16 input=4079, requested=16, actual=15 input=4080, requested=16, actual=14 input=4081, requested=16, HTTP 400 ``` This reproduces on both Qwen3-0.6B and the hybrid GDN/linear-attention Qwen3.5-0.8B path, so it is not model-specific. SGLang's public validation permits requests whose total length is exactly the model context length: ```text input_len + max_new_tokens <= context_len ``` This boundary was explicitly adopted in #22546 after the same behavior was reported in discussion #16020. The scheduler uses a different internal length. In [`TPModelWorker.get_worker_info`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/604d3561b012816aa4cec2fb89c522f819f68af8/python/sglang/srt/managers/tp_worker.py#L514-L519), `max_req_len` is already defined as: ```python max_req_len = min( context_len - 1, effective_max_total_num_tokens * dcp_size - 1, ) ``` However, [`Scheduler.init_req_max_new_tokens`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/604d3561b012816aa4cec2fb89c522f819f68af8/python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py#L2140-L2148) applies the second subtraction: ```python max_req_len - input_len - 1 ``` The two commit-pinned assignments are therefore: 1. [`max_req_len = context_len - 1`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/604d3561b012816aa4cec2fb89c522f819f68af8/python/sglang/srt/managers/tp_worker.py#L513-L519) 2. [`max_new_tokens <= max_req_len - input_len - 1`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/604d3561b012816aa4cec2fb89c522f819f68af8/python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py#L2140-L2148) When the context-length bound is active, composing them gives `max_new_tokens <= context_len - input_len - 2`, explaining the two-token clipping. The second subtraction was originally an intentional conservative reserve from #1748; the historical context below explains why it is redundant under the current contract and page-aware admission logic. The execution invariant is that generating `N` output tokens forwards the prompt and only the first `N - 1` generated tokens. The final token is sampled and returned, but is never forwarded in another decode step. Therefore: ```text input_len + max_new_tokens - 1 <= max_req_len max_new_tokens <= max_req_len - input_len + 1 ``` EOS does not require a separate reserved slot: when sampled, it is itself one of the generated tokens. The page-rounded global KV admission bound remains a separate safety constraint. ## Modifications - Use `max_req_len - input_len + 1` for the per-request context bound. - Keep the page-rounded global KV admission bound added by #25126 unchanged. - Update the existing scheduler property tests to encode the forward-length invariant. - Add a focused regression for a request exactly at the public context boundary. The regression fails on the parent commit with `14 != 16` and passes with this change. After the change: ```text input=4078, requested=16, actual=16 input=4079, requested=16, actual=16 input=4080, requested=16, actual=16 input=4081, requested=16, HTTP 400 ``` ## Historical Context The extra scheduler subtraction was intentional when introduced by [#1748](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/1748) in October 2024. That PR described three conservative rules: leave one token when deriving `max_req_len` from capacity, leave five tokens for `max_req_input_len`, and leave one more token when adjusting `max_new_tokens`. At that time, the goal was prefill-OOM robustness, and admission used a simpler strict estimate based on `extend_input_len + max_new_tokens < rem_total_tokens`. Two later changes altered the contract and made the relevant safety check explicit: - [#22546](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/22546) changed public validation to allow `input_len + max_new_tokens == context_len`. It was approved by the maintainer who introduced #1748. - [#25126](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/25126) added the separate page-aware global KV bound `ceil_page(input_len) + max_new_tokens + page_size < max_total_num_tokens`, preventing requests that can never pass `PrefillAdder` admission from entering the waiting queue. The historical reserve therefore should not be treated as an accidental typo. Under the current contract, however, retaining it in the context bound silently clips valid requests even when the newer explicit KV-admission bound has sufficient capacity. This PR removes that now-redundant context reserve while preserving the page-aware KV safety constraint. ## Follow-up The `+1` conversion is necessary because `max_req_len` currently represents the maximum forwarded/KV-backed length, while the final sampled token is returned without another forward. A separate refactor could make this distinction explicit with names such as `max_forward_len` and `max_total_sequence_len`, then audit all consumers in the scheduler, attention metadata, speculative decoding, disaggregation, and memory pools. That broader semantic rename is intentionally out of scope here; this PR keeps the existing `max_req_len` contract and applies the localized conversion required to fix the boundary behavior. ## Mini-SGLang Cross-Check Mini-SGLang independently implements the same public context-boundary behavior. Its scheduler computes: ```python max_output_len = max_seq_len - input_len ``` Thus, for model context length `C`, input length `I`, and requested output length `O`, Mini-SGLang permits `O <= C - I`. See [Mini-SGLang scheduler intake](https://github.com/sgl-project/mini-sglang/blob/9a91cfafe754aa85daee49998176275667eb58f2/python/minisgl/scheduler/scheduler.py#L177-L188). This is consistent with its execution state. A request sets `max_device_len = input_len + output_len`, and each forward increments `device_len` before the next token is sampled. Consequently, generating `O` output tokens forwards the prompt plus only the first `O - 1` generated tokens; the final sampled token is returned without another forward. See [request state](https://github.com/sgl-project/mini-sglang/blob/9a91cfafe754aa85daee49998176275667eb58f2/python/minisgl/core.py#L38-L58) and [engine forward](https://github.com/sgl-project/mini-sglang/blob/9a91cfafe754aa85daee49998176275667eb58f2/python/minisgl/engine/engine.py#L190-L207). With core SGLang's `max_req_len = C - 1`, this PR's bound reduces to: ```text O <= max_req_len - I + 1 <= (C - 1) - I + 1 <= C - I ``` The patched core context bound therefore matches Mini-SGLang's behavior. This is independent corroboration of the forward-length invariant, not a substitute for core-specific tests covering page-rounded global KV admission, DCP, speculative-decoding reservations, and other production modes. ## Accuracy Tests This changes only scheduler length accounting, not model forward computation, logits, or sampling math. End-to-end validation used Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B on an RTX 3070 with the Triton attention backend. All accepted requests through total length 4096 returned the requested token count; total length 4097 remained rejected with HTTP 400. The exact boundary also passed with Qwen3.5 NEXTN/EAGLE speculative decoding, including its four reserved token slots; one token beyond it returned HTTP 400 and the server remained healthy. Focused unit results: ```text 9 passed, 542 subtests passed ``` ## Speed Tests and Profiling No hot inference path changes. The patch replaces one integer expression during request initialization, so no speed impact is expected. Local `pre-commit run --all-files` passed all Python formatting, lint, registered-test, and repository checks. Rust-only hooks could not run because this WSL environment does not have `cargo` or `rustup`; this PR does not modify Rust files. No user-facing documentation change is required; the scheduler comment now documents the corrected forward-length invariant. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. signal.title: [Roadmap]Fast Engine Recovery: Weight Cache Daemon
signal.text: # [Roadmap] Fast Engine Recovery: Weight Cache Daemon @liusy58 @QiuMike @alexnails Phase 1 landed in #27139 — a per-rank daemon holds post-quantized weights and serves them over CUDA IPC; weight load drops from ~306–327s to <1s on Qwen3-235B FP8 ([blog](https://www.lmsys.org/blog/2026-08-21-sglang-fast-recovery)). This issue tracks the next steps. Contributions and feedback are welcome. Related: #27052 (Fast Recovery framework), #27310 (GPU Memory Service / VMM) Goals: <10s cold restart and <1s warm standby switch; broaden model & quant coverage; make the cache outlive the daemon; make resident weights usable beyond the one GPU they sit on. Where Phase 1 stands: TP + PP, single-node and multi-node launch (each node spawns its share of ranks and joins one dist group), zero-copy IPC per GPU, unquantized + block-wise FP8. Not yet: cross-node daemon coordination / failover, DP & EP shard keying, spec-decoding draft models, weight update / sleep-wake, cache surviving daemon death. ## Model & quantization coverage - [ ] parity harness — disk-load vs daemon-load `state_dict` diff (names / shape / dtype / stride / byte hash) + short GSM8K gate; required evidence for every new allowlist entry - [ ] carry post-processing metadata in the manifest (final shape/stride, layout tag, whitelisted module attrs) instead of reproducing `process_weights_after_loading` on a meta-init model — this is what blocks most quant methods today - [ ] quant methods: per-tensor fp8 / w8a8 int8 / mxfp8 / nvfp4 / compressed-tensors / awq / gptq-marlin #32398 - [ ] archs: MoE (DeepSeek V3/V4, Ling, Kimi K3) / hybrid linear attention / multimodal (vision tower + projector) / LoRA base weights - [ ] MTP & EAGLE draft models (per-rank draft daemon), removing the `--speculative-algorithm` rejection in `server_args.py` #32744 - [ ] generic post-map rebuild hook to replace the hardcoded `_rebuild_stale_views`; make tied storages, param→buffer flips and non-persistent buffers explicit in the manifest - [ ] publish the support matrix in docs; unsupported combinations keep hard-erroring (no silent wrong numerics) ## Transport: CUDA VMM shareable handles (#27310 §4.2) - [ ] `vmm_fd` backend (skeleton already in `weight_cache/transport.py`): `cuMemCreate` + FD handles over `SCM_RIGHTS`, VA reservation on import, `torch_ipc` stays the fallback, `--weight-cache-transport {auto,torch_ipc,vmm_fd}` #33279 ## Weight update without reload - [ ] epoch handoff on stable VAs: readers unmap → writer commits → readers remap at the same VAs, so captured CUDA graphs stay valid - [ ] daemon as the weight delivery agent for trainer pushes (NCCL/RDMA); un-gate the `update_weights_*` rejections in `weight_updater.py` - [ ] colocated RL: engine itself takes the writer role, same protocol, no daemon in the loop ## Multi-instance & cross-GPU sharing - [ ] key the cache by physical GPU UUID + config fingerprint (plus optional `--weight-cache-namespace`) under a configurable runtime dir. Today the socket is `/tmp/sglang_weight_cache_rank{global_rank}.sock`, so 2× tp=4 on one 8-GPU node collide and rank 0 of the second instance attaches to the GPU 0 daemon - [ ] discovery: replace static socket paths with a lightweight registry (file-based dir, optionally etcd) so an engine rank selects a daemon by `CacheConfig` match rather than by process rank, and locates daemons across nodes without a manual `--weight-cache-socket` - [ ] `--weight-cache-peer-copy` — when no daemon holds the shard on the local GPU, `cudaMemcpyPeerAsync` it from a peer-GPU daemon (NVLink-domain check, chunked on a low-priority stream, bandwidth cap so a serving neighbour is not disturbed). 1× memory per instance, sub-second over NVLink vs ~300s from disk - [ ] preference order local zero-copy > peer copy > disk, reported per rank - [ ] fleet fill: a daemon fills itself from a peer daemon instead of disk (P2P on-node, NCCL/RDMA cross-node), so a fleet cold start pays one disk read per shard group — the real bottleneck for 1T+ models on shared FS; align with the checkpoint-engine broadcast path - [ ] out of scope for now: resharding across TP/EP topologies (tp=4 daemon → tp=8 engine) ## Multi-node, DP & EP - [ ] primary–secondary daemon coordination for multi-node TP (e.g. TP=16 = 2 nodes × 8 GPUs): primary orchestrates daemon startup, cross-node NCCL process-group formation and readiness signalling; secondaries load their local shards in parallel and serve IPC handles to engines on their own node. Basic multi-node launch already works via `--nnodes/--node-rank/--dist-init-method`; what is missing is the cluster state machine - [ ] cross-node daemon lifecycle: primary tracks which secondaries are alive, triggers coordinated restarts, signals engines on a dead secondary's node to fall back to disk; promote a secondary when the primary dies - [ ] DP support: every DP rank on a GPU maps the same daemon's handles, so a model is read from disk and quantized exactly once per GPU regardless of DP degree (today each DP rank disk-loads independently). This is about supporting SGLang's DP deployment model, not cross-GPU sharing - [ ] EP support: expert shards differ per EP rank, so cache and key them by `ep_rank`; handle partial expert loading when a rank owns a subset of experts - [ ] `CacheConfig`: add `ep_rank`, `dp_rank` and `node_rank` for correct shard identification under EP and multi-node (`dp_size`/`ep_size` are already there) ## Ops & reliability - [ ] `daemon status` command + Prometheus metrics (resident bytes, attached clients, load time, hit / mismatch / fallback), and an engine endpoint reporting how each rank got its weights - [ ] runtime dir with owner-only permissions + `SO_PEERCRED` check before handing out handles (no world-writable `/tmp` sockets) - [ ] `protocol_version` in the handshake with a documented skew policy (the env stamp already covers torch / arch skew) - [ ] `--weight-cache-max-bytes`, refcount-aware eviction, admission check against `gpu_memory_utilization` - [ ] systemd unit + k8s DaemonSet recipes; document container requirements for cross-container IPC - [ ] CI: CPU unit tests, 1-GPU daemon→client restart e2e with accuracy, 2-GPU TP e2e, nightly multi-node, restart-latency regression gate - [ ] docs page: three modes, support matrix, ops runbook, failure semantics - [ ] reclaim on daemon restart (Phase 6): the daemon holds no heavy logic and is robust by construction, but if it exits for an external reason its clients still hold the GPU memory alive through IPC refcounts — a restarted daemon should re-adopt that memory from a live client's references instead of reloading from disk ## Rest of the startup path - [ ] Phase 2 — CUDA graph serialization: persist captured graphs to shared memory or disk and replay instead of recapturing; needs pool-offset translation for address relocation, which is why it depends on the stable VAs above. ~34.9s (~9% of startup) → <3s - [ ] Phase 3 — kernel warmup: persist DeepGEMM JIT-compiled kernels across restarts, parallelize warmup across batch sizes. ~23.1s → <2s - [ ] Phase 4 — server & distributed init: lazy tokenizer init, config caching, NCCL session reuse. ~22s → <5s - [ ] KV cache alloc + warmup ~3.9s → <1.5s (KV reuse, skip warmup requests on restart) - [ ] standby orchestration: health / promotion, request draining and KV handoff, scheduler-level pause/resume for priority co-serving ## Open questions - [ ] manifest schema + versioning: SGLang-owned, stored by the memory owner as an opaque blob — what compatibility window across SGLang versions? - [ ] backend selection UX: server arg, TMS-side registration, or both? - [ ] peer copy: automatic whenever a peer daemon exists, or always explicit opt-in? default bandwidth cap next to a serving instance? ## KV Restore?

signal.title: config: pin two orderings resolution relies on
signal.text: ## Stack Part of a series that moves `ServerArgs` from "mutate the record at construction" to "resolve once, publish into config bags". Each PR stands alone (builds, passes its own tests); review bottom-up. | # | PR | base | |---|----|------| | 0 | #35904 | `main` | | 1 | #35905 | #35904 | | 2 | #35906 | #35905 | | 3 | #35907 | #35906 | | 4 | #35908 | #35907 | | 5 | #35909 | #35908 | | 6 | #35910 | #35909 | Whole-series CI vehicle (not for merge): #35917 ## Motivation Two orderings inside resolution hold today by accident, and nothing would notice them breaking. Tests only — no production change. ## Modifications - `ModelConfig` is built from resolved input: the pin derives both sides from source — the fields `ModelConfig.from_server_args` reads, and the pipeline step each is declared at — and fails if a field it reads is declared after the first build. Two documented exceptions are named and asserted with equality, not membership: - `is_embedding` is read for what the caller asked for (passed through, never stored) — resolution later overwrites the field with a different quantity sharing the name; - four fields the model-override registries decide *after* the handler builds and caches the configuration (`dtype`, `quantization`, `enable_multi_layer_eagle`, `disable_hybrid_swa_memory`). The build/collect positions are read from the one handler body that contains both, and the registry-declared set is imported from the chain ratchet's derivation rather than re-derived — a copy that drifts narrower would make the check quietly vacuous. A fifth field arriving in that position fails; so does fixing the ordering — either way someone has to look. - The chain-read ratchet unions all four declaration channels (handler keywords, live registries, pass returns, late resolution) with per-channel floors, so a channel whose derivation collapses fails loudly instead of narrowing the check. ## Verification - Both pins verified by injection: reversing the build/collect comparison reports exactly the four named fields; a shape reaching a stale field reddens the main assertion. - Guard suite and lint green at this boundary. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32541515150](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32541515150)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32541515080](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32541515080)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32541515157](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32541515157)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [diffusion] Fix unbounded A2A staging buffer growth across request sh…
signal.text: _a2a_staging_buffer keys by (role, shape, dtype, device), retaining one staging buffer per distinct request shape forever. Serving workloads with varied resolutions/durations accumulate these buffers without bound: on MiniMax-H3 ref2va (8x RTX 5090, ulysses=8) a memory snapshot showed 12.4 GiB held by these buffers after ~30 varied requests, ending in repeated CUDA OOM. torch.cuda.empty_cache() cannot reclaim them (module-level dict keeps references). Fix: key by (role, dtype, device) and grow a single flat buffer to the largest numel seen, viewing it to each request's shape. Reuse semantics are unchanged (a role's buffer is fully consumed before its next use); staging memory is now bounded by |roles| x largest request. <!-- Thank you for your contribution! signal.title: config: constructing a config no longer resolves it
signal.text: ## Stack Part of a series that moves `ServerArgs` from "mutate the record at construction" to "resolve once, publish into config bags". Each PR stands alone (builds, passes its own tests); review bottom-up. | # | PR | base | |---|----|------| | 0 | #35904 | `main` | | 1 | #35905 | #35904 | | 2 | #35906 | #35905 | | 3 | #35907 | #35906 | | 4 | #35908 | #35907 | | 5 | #35909 | #35908 | | 6 | #35910 | #35909 | Whole-series CI vehicle (not for merge): #35917 ## Motivation `__post_init__` ran the whole resolution pipeline, so every construction produced a resolved record — a fixture inspecting defaults, a config being validated, a record on its way to a subprocess that would resolve it again. That is the reason the record could not stay at what the caller asked for. Resolution is deterministic on the raw input but **not** repeatable on its own output: the DP-attention step derives the chunked prefill size from the chunked prefill size, so a second pass halves it again (8192 → 4096 → 2048, measured), and the schedule conservativeness is scaled again (0.3 → 0.09). **This is the only behavioral change in the stack**; everything before it is record-keeping and everything after is read redirection. ## Modifications - Construction is inert. `resolve_once()` is the single gate: it runs the pipeline unless the record has been through it, and marks the record on every exit (the mark also arms a read-only `__setattr__` — post-resolution changes go to the bags via `get_context().override`). - The launcher resolves the engine's record once; `publish` asks the gate on the way in and finds nothing left to do for a record that arrived resolved (e.g. by pickle, which carries the declarations). - Programs that build their own record resolve it before reading what resolution decides. Seven entries across the repository (the model gateway's launcher, benchmarks, examples) did not — e.g. the gateway sized its worker plan from a raw `dp_size`, so `--tp-size 4 --dwdp-size 4` launched one server instead of four, and a speculative benchmark forwarded `--mem-fraction-static None` to the server it spawns. All seven resolve now, and the census that found them is a test whose universe is the repository, not the package — keyed on the record's import source, because the diffusion runtime has a same-spelled `ServerArgs` with no resolution step. - A copy of a resolved record stays resolved: `ServerArgs.replace_resolved(source, **changes)` carries everything resolution left on the instance (raw snapshot, declaration stash, memoized `ModelConfig`, flags — enumerated from the instance, not listed) and appends the change as a declaration so the projection sees it. The Ray paths and the gateway's per-worker copy use it; a bare `dataclasses.replace` re-entered resolution on already-resolved values (measured on a 2-GPU Ray run: both scheduler actors ran with `chunked_prefill_size=2048` while the engine reported 4096). A derived pin forbids bare `dataclasses.replace` of a record outside the helper, with the helper's own call as the positive control. ## Verification - Gate refusal and reproducibility suites; the seam has exactly one pipeline caller and the gate's callers are pinned together with the rule they stand for (a non-mechanism caller must resolve a record it built itself from argv). - Ray smoke run (dp=2, tp=2, DP attention, 2 GPUs, real weights): generation OK, the DP-attention adjustment logged exactly once, zero read-only violations. - Blast radius of the read-only flag measured by flipping it early and running the unit suite; every affected fixture fixed to pass both before and after. - A/B: resolved end-state identical to base across the 11-configuration matrix. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32541511485](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32541511485)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32541511413](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32541511413)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32541511489](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32541511489)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: config: publish before the launcher reads effective configuration
signal.text: ## Stack Part of a series that moves `ServerArgs` from "mutate the record at construction" to "resolve once, publish into config bags". Each PR stands alone (builds, passes its own tests); review bottom-up. | # | PR | base | |---|----|------| | 0 | #35904 | `main` | | 1 | #35905 | #35904 | | 2 | #35906 | #35905 | | 3 | #35907 | #35906 | | 4 | #35908 | #35907 | | 5 | #35909 | #35908 | | 6 | #35910 | #35909 | Whole-series CI vehicle (not for merge): #35917 ## Motivation The launcher published last — after validating, allocating ports, and deciding whether to start the engine-info bootstrap server — so all of those read effective configuration off the record, which is exactly what the record should stop carrying. ## Modifications - Publish moves up to just below validation, the earliest it can go: auto-parser detection is resolution that needs a tokenizer and a chat template, and validation normalizes LoRA adapter paths through late resolution — both must write the record, and a published record is read-only. The launch order is: resolve → env → plugins → auto-parser → validate → **publish** → ports → spawn. Validation still throws before any subprocess spawns; the launcher creates them in three helpers, all called below both. - The data-parallel controller, the HTTP lifespan's gRPC-mode branch, and the launcher's per-TP-rank layout read the bags / configured sizes. - A guard walks the other direction — from everything resolution can reach (the pipeline's imports, every pass and provider in the live registries, by-value pass call sites) to any config-bag accessor — because a bag read inside resolution raises only on the branch that reaches it. Two such reads shipped and stayed green for everything except the configuration that triggers them; both are caught by the walk (verified by putting each back). Registered entries are derived from the live registries via `inspect`: a decorator-keyed scan saw 39 of 65 — most providers register through a helper. A source-order pin keeps the late resolvers above the publish. ## Verification - No-bag walk over all resolution-reachable entries; launcher source-order pin; validation-before-publish pin; configured-size call-site checks. - Full guard suite and lint green at the stack tip; GPU round (TP / spec / PD / PP on mock weights) and a 2-GPU Ray run green. - A/B: resolved end-state identical to base across the 11-configuration matrix. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32541517133](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32541517133)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32541516995](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32541516995)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32541517255](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32541517255)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.text: ## Stack Part of a series that moves `ServerArgs` from "mutate the record at construction" to "resolve once, publish into config bags". Each PR stands alone (builds, passes its own tests); review bottom-up. | # | PR | base | |---|----|------| | 0 | #35904 | `main` | | 1 | #35905 | #35904 | | 2 | #35906 | #35905 | | 3 | #35907 | #35906 | | 4 | #35908 | #35907 | | 5 | #35909 | #35908 | | 6 | #35910 | #35909 | Whole-series CI vehicle (not for merge): #35917 ## Motivation Components reached the startup record through whatever object happened to hold it — `model_runner.server_args.field`, `self.scheduler.server_args.field`. A reference lifted off another object carries no contract, and no read census counted that spelling: it had grown to 105 reads across 36 files unnoticed. Once the record stays at the user's raw input, these reads answer with the CLI default. ## Modifications - Every borrowed-record chain read of a resolution-written field moves to the config bags (weight loading, graph capture, pool configurator, forward-batch construction, KV pool runtime, disaggregation and elastic-EP paths, HTTP/gRPC surfaces, attention backends). - Reads that follow the *configured* topology rather than live process groups use the `configured_*()` accessors (a draft runner shares the target's process groups, so the live property would answer for the wrong runner). - Reads of raw input (host, ports, paths the caller chose) stay on the record — that is what the record is for. - The chain-read ratchet pins the converted set at zero: the written-field set is derived from four channels (handler keywords, the live override registries, post-process pass returns, late resolution), so a field that stops being resolution-written drops out of scope instead of pinning a stale name. ## Verification - Chain-read ratchet: zero borrowed chain reads of resolution-written fields at this commit (105/36 on base, same scanner). - Guard suite and lint green at this boundary; signal.title: config: project the config bags from the resolution result
signal.text: ## Stack Part of a series that moves `ServerArgs` from "mutate the record at construction" to "resolve once, publish into config bags". Each PR stands alone (builds, passes its own tests); review bottom-up. | # | PR | base | |---|----|------| | 0 | #35904 | `main` | | 1 | #35905 | #35904 | | 2 | #35906 | #35905 | | 3 | #35907 | #35906 | | 4 | #35908 | #35907 | | 5 | #35909 | #35908 | | 6 | #35910 | #35909 | Whole-series CI vehicle (not for merge): #35917 ## Motivation The config bags were projected from whatever the record's fields held at publish time. With resolution writes now declared (previous PR), the projection can read the resolution *result* — the raw input plus the ordered declarations — which makes "what did the user ask for" and "what did resolution decide" separately answerable, and makes late writes visible to the projection. ## Modifications - `_build_config_bags` projects from `resolution_result(record, field)`: last declaration wins, else the raw-input snapshot, else the field. - Late resolution (LoRA normalization, auto parser detection — steps that need the launcher's validation stage) records through `declare_late_resolution`, so the bags describe the resolved value rather than the `auto` the CLI carried. - Out-of-tree platform hooks are wrapped by `declare_direct_writes`: their field rebinds are diffed and declared, so a plugin's defaults are not dropped by the projection. - First reader batch moves to the bags (speculative workers; signal.title: config: record resolution writes in a declaration stash
signal.text: ## Stack Part of a series that moves `ServerArgs` from "mutate the record at construction" to "resolve once, publish into config bags". Each PR stands alone (builds, passes its own tests); review bottom-up. | # | PR | base | |---|----|------| | 0 | #35904 | `main` | | 1 | #35905 | #35904 | | 2 | #35906 | #35905 | | 3 | #35907 | #35906 | | 4 | #35908 | #35907 | | 5 | #35909 | #35908 | | 6 | #35910 | #35909 | Whole-series CI vehicle (not for merge): #35917 ## Motivation Resolution used to write `ServerArgs` fields with bare assignments, so what a handler decided was indistinguishable from what the caller passed in. To project configuration bags from resolution output (later in this stack), every resolution write must be recorded, not just applied. ## Modifications - Every in-pipeline scalar write goes through a declaration (`self._declare(...)` on handlers, `declare_resolution(...)` in the hooks): the write is appended to a declaration stash on the record and applied to the field immediately, so successors that read the field directly see the same value as before. - The model-override registry entries and post-process passes declare through the same channel. - `declare_resolution`'s docstring states what routing a write through the stash changes: a declaration is replayed last, so an immediate writer that declares a field a deferred writer also decides now beats it. A resolver gating on such a field must read the resolving view, not the raw field. - Guards (all derivation-based, each verified by injection): - no converted field is assigned bare anywhere in the pipeline; - the stash agrees with the fields it declared; - the stash accounts for every change resolution made (resolve, diff against the raw snapshot, require a declaration for every changed leaf); - an immediate writer must not silently override a deferred writer's different value — the fixture matrix includes a shape that actually reaches that branch (`--enable-waterfill --moe-a2a-backend ascend_tp`). ## Verification - Declaration guard suite green at this commit; each guard reddens when its protected property is broken (verified by injecting the corresponding bug). - A/B: fully-resolved records across an 11-configuration matrix are field-for-field identical to the base revision. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32541509037](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32541509037)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32541508898](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32541508898)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32541509062](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32541509062)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: Fix FlashInfer MHA one-shot DP-attention padding
signal.text: ## Motivation Fixes #30916 (the MHA one-shot leg; see "Relation to #30916" below). Under DP attention, every rank's input rows are padded beyond its real extend tokens — to the `attn_tp_size` multiple for reduce-scatter alignment, and to the global max token count when the prefill breakable CUDA graph forces MAX_LEN padding. The flashinfer ragged wrappers build `qo_indptr` from per-request extend lengths, so a padded rank violates their strict check and crashes the scheduler: ``` ValueError: q.shape[0] (4) does not match qo_indptr[-1] (1). For ragged prefill, q must have shape [total_tokens, num_heads, head_dim] where total_tokens = qo_indptr[-1]. ``` Two paths are affected: 1. **MHA_ONE_SHOT** with no cached prefix (reported in a comment on #30916; `tp=8, dp=2` → `attn_tp_size=4`, a one-token prefill pads Q to 4 rows against a 1-row indptr); 2. **absorbed MLA ragged prefill** — the same invariant violation on the MLA path, observed in production with `enable_dp_attention + tp8/dp2` and the prefill breakable CUDA graph enabled: MAX_LEN padding pads the shorter DP rank even when every request's extend length is individually aligned. ## Modification Single predicate, two consumers: - **`ForwardBatch.has_dp_padding_rows()`** (`forward_batch_deepseek_mha_mixin.py`): true when `sum(extend_seq_lens_cpu) != positions.shape[0]` — i.e. the rank's input has padding rows, covering both padding sources (attn_tp alignment and MAX_LEN). Fails closed: without host-side extend lengths (gpu_only batches) it reports padding so callers stay on the padding-tolerant paths. - **`attention_backend_handler.py`**: the flashinfer MHA one-shot dispatch keeps ONE_SHOT only on padding-free extends; a padded extend falls back to absorbed MLA. - **`flashinfer_mla_backend.py` `init_forward_metadata`**: `use_ragged` additionally requires no padding rows; a padded extend plans the **paged** prefill wrapper instead — the path DP attention already uses for extends with a radix-cache prefix, so it is the DP-padding-tolerant one. Backends inheriting `FlashInferMLAAttnBackend.init_forward_metadata` (flashmla, cutlass_mla, trtllm_mla fallback legs) inherit the gate. Captured prefill (tc_piecewise / breakable) already pins MLA + paged prefill ahead of these checks and is unchanged. ### Why a padding-row check, not per-request alignment An earlier draft of this PR gated ONE_SHOT on `extend_len % attn_tp_size == 0` for every request. Production showed that check is wrong in both directions: - **Too permissive** — MAX_LEN padding pads the whole rank even when every request is individually aligned (DP0=[4] vs DP1=[8] pads DP0 to 8 rows), so the guard passes and the wrapper still crashes. This is exactly the MLA-ragged crash above. - **Too restrictive** — a batch like extend=[2,2] at `attn_tp_size=4` is sum-aligned and padding-free; per-request alignment would reject it needlessly (the ragged wrapper natively handles variable per-request lengths). The ragged wrapper's own check only asserts `q.shape[0] == qo_indptr[-1]`, i.e. "no padding rows" — so that is the invariant the guard enforces. ### Design trade-off vs making ragged tolerate padding #30916 (still open) instead teaches the MLA ragged updater to *accept* padding by appending a dummy request covering the padding rows (and slices/zero-pads on the chunked-prefix runner). That keeps the ragged fast path on padded batches at the cost of metadata surgery. This PR takes the simpler correctness-first route: padded extends use the paged prefill path (already the production path under DP attention whenever a prefix exists). Cost: a DP rank whose padded length exceeds its real tokens runs paged instead of ragged prefill on eager (non-captured) extends — batches that previously crashed outright. When #30916 lands, this gate can be relaxed. ## Tests Hermetic dispatch tests (no GPU, no weights) in `test/registered/unit/models/test_deepseek_mla_dispatch.py`: - padded extend (1 real token, 4 rows) → MLA; - padding-free extend → MHA_ONE_SHOT retained; - per-request-aligned but MAX_LEN-padded extend (4 real tokens, 8 rows) → MLA (the case the per-request check misses); - predicate unit tests: rows-match → no padding; extra rows → padding; unknown extend lengths / missing positions → fail closed. Red-verified: neutralizing the predicate flips both padded cases to MHA_ONE_SHOT. The `use_ragged` gate in `flashinfer_mla_backend.py` is not covered by a hermetic test (the backend constructor needs a live model runner); it is validated by the production reproducer below. ## Verification `python3 -m pytest -q test/registered/unit/models/test_deepseek_mla_dispatch.py` — 13 passed. End-to-end (DeepSeek-V3.2-style MoE, `tp=8 dp=2` DP attention, flashinfer backend, prefill breakable CUDA graph enabled, PD disagg): before the fix, the prefill scheduler crashed with the exact `q.shape[0] (4) does not match qo_indptr[-1] (1)` error seconds after serving started, on the first DP-uneven batch (absorbed-MLA ragged path). With the fix, the same workload starts, serves warmup + uneven real traffic across both DP ranks (mixed cuda-graph and eager prefill batches), passes functional smoke checks with coherent outputs, and the decode side runs clean with no watchdog events. ## Relation to #30916 - Covers the **MHA one-shot no-prefix leg** reported in the #30916 comment, which that PR's Changes 3/4 do not reach. - Fixes the same MLA ragged-path invariant as #30916 Change 3, by avoidance (paged fallback) rather than dummy-request tolerance. No correctness conflict if both land; the gate here becomes redundant for the non-spec path once #30916 is in. - Does not touch the two buffer-sizing fixes in #30916 Changes 1/2 (spec decode cuda-graph buffers) — those remain needed independently. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32541097977](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32541097977)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32541097902](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32541097902)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32541098048](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32541098048)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: config: a defensive publish must not re-project over a live process
signal.text: ## Stack Part of a series that moves `ServerArgs` from "mutate the record at construction" to "resolve once, publish into config bags". Each PR stands alone (builds, passes its own tests); review bottom-up. | # | PR | base | |---|----|------| | 0 | #35904 | `main` | | 1 | #35905 | #35904 | | 2 | #35906 | #35905 | | 3 | #35907 | #35906 | | 4 | #35908 | #35907 | | 5 | #35909 | #35908 | | 6 | #35910 | #35909 | Whole-series CI vehicle (not for merge): #35917 ## Motivation `ModelRunner` and `TokenizerManager` publish the startup record in their constructors because either can be built standalone (a benchmark harness, the manual runner tests) with nothing published before it. Inside a real process the launcher has already published the same record, and publishing again re-projects the config bags: every `get_context().override(...)` taken between the two calls is discarded, and the provenance log with it. No process opens that window today — checked, not assumed: every `override(...)` site in the tree runs below the publish that precedes it. But the discard is silent, both constructors are reachable inside a live process, and nothing at the call site says which case it is. Any override placed in such a window from now on would be undone without a trace. ## Modifications - `ensure_published(server_args, *, role)`: a no-op when this record is already published under this role, a normal publish otherwise (empty slot, a different record, or a different role). `publish` keeps last-publish-wins — an engine rebuild must not inherit the previous engine's runtime scaling — and now logs the overrides a re-projection drops instead of dropping them quietly. - `ModelRunner`, `TokenizerManager`, and the in-process encoder ask for the end state through `ensure_published`. - The census of constructor publishes is derived from the code (`sglang.test.config_publishers`) and keyed by owning class: a constructor that owns the runtime it publishes uses `publish`; one that may run inside a live process uses `ensure_published`. The difference is invisible in the syntax, so a new publishing constructor fails the pin until it is classified. Independent of the rest of the stack: it fixes behavior that predates it. ## Verification - Behavioral tests for all four publish/ensure_published cases (same record+role, different record, different role, empty slot), plus the derived constructor census (adding an unclassified publishing constructor fails; verified by injection). - Full guard suite and lint green at this commit. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32537319855](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32537319855)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:no_entry_sign: [Run #32540484831](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32540484831)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32537319728](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32537319728)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [HiCache] Clamp tombstoned SWA locs in UnifiedSWAKVPool translation
signal.text: ## Summary `UnifiedSWAKVPool.translate_loc_from_full_to_swa` returned the raw virtual-to-physical lookup, so a tombstoned v2p entry (`-1`) escaped to the caller as a negative slot id. With `page_size > 1` the page math turns it into a value in `[-ps, -1]` instead. Either way the caller ends up indexing the SWA KV buffer with a negative loc, which is an illegal access under captured cuda-graph replay. This clamps the translated locs to `0` before the `int32` cast, matching the existing tombstone-safety clamp in `MultiEndedAllocator.translate_kv_loc`: slot 0 is the reserved padding sink, so tombstoned reads/writes land there harmlessly instead of walking off the front of the buffer. Behavior for non-tombstoned entries is unchanged — physical locs are already non-negative, so the clamp is a no-op on them. The change is local to this method; no signature or caller changes. ## Test plan - `black --check` on the changed file: clean. - `python3 -m py_compile` on the changed file: clean. - Ported from an internal commit where the change was validated on a hierarchical-cache SWA serving setup; the GPU/cuda-graph reproduction was not re-run in this checkout (no suitable local environment), so it is left to CI. ## Original commits - `660518afe` <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32539420741](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32539420741)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32540700084](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32540700084)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32539420576](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32539420576)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.author: gjsheu

signal.title: [PD] Fix NIXL P/D serving stall after prefill replacement
signal.text: ## Motivation Addresses the prefill-replacement stall in #33789. When a prefill is replaced behind a bootstrap address that stays reachable (typically a k8s Service), the decode never notices: its cached rank endpoints still point at the dead process, so every request after the swap dies on the waiting timeout until the decode is restarted. Reproduced on 2x RTX 3090 (Qwen2.5-0.5B, mini-lb, NIXL). With a direct address and the default 5 s heartbeat, stock recovers on its own, so the repro masks the heartbeat (`SGLANG_DISAGGREGATION_HEARTBEAT_INTERVAL=120`) and swaps the prefill inside the window: | phase | stock v0.5.16 | this PR | |---|---|---| | baseline request | pass | pass | | right after the swap | fails (expected: the first request is the detection signal) | fails (expected) | | after one heartbeat tick | stuck forever | pass | Same result on TP=2 (4x RTX 3090), and re-validated against v0.5.17. ## Modifications The bootstrap server returns a per-process instance id in a `X-SGLang-Disaggregation-Instance-ID` response header. A header rather than a JSON field because old decodes reject unknown topology keys. The decode caches the id it registered against and recovers on two paths: - Heartbeat: each tick probes `/health` on a fresh connection (a kept-alive socket would keep reaching the draining old process). A healthy answer with a different id evicts the cached connections and fails the in-flight rooms, so retries re-bootstrap against the new instance. - Failure backstop (NIXL): a request that fails on reused cached endpoints re-probes `/health`. A healthy answer with a different id gets the same treatment; an inconclusive probe (error, non-200, id missing) only invalidates the cache, so a slow-but-alive prefill is not mass-retried. Per-rank and dp-rank query responses are validated against the cached id too, since a kept-alive socket to a draining process could otherwise repopulate a fresh cache with dead endpoints. Every verdict is anchored to the topology snapshot captured before the network call that produced it, so a verdict racing a replacement plus recovery can never tear down a freshly recovered cache. The concurrency reasoning is in comments next to each gate. While testing this path I hit and fixed several adjacent bugs: connection eviction matched addresses by string prefix; unlocked reads and writes of the shared tables could kill the heartbeat thread (KeyError/RuntimeError); a concurrent `max()`-based status write could resurrect an already-failed room; failed rooms leaked staging counts, tracker entries, dp-rank deadlines and failure records; and the NIXL bootstrap thread died on any exception. Each fix has a regression test that was verified to fail on the pre-fix code. The second commit adds the same header to `rust/sglang-server` and pins its `/health` shallow when the bootstrap registry is mounted (the deep probe stays on `/health_generate`): the decode reads bootstrap `/health` with short timeouts, and the default 20 s generation probe would count as heartbeat misses and retire a healthy prefill. Happy to drop this commit and take Rust parity as a follow-up if preferred. The PD disaggregation guide gains a short section on replacement detection. Known limitations, kept out of scope on purpose: - The decode-replacement direction of #33789 is unchanged: replaced decodes still leave stale peer registrations on the prefill. - Decode-to-prefill registration stays a one-way ZMQ send, as today; a lost registration is not retried until the next eviction. - Replacements between two pre-instance-id prefills stay undetectable (nothing to compare), same as stock. ## Testing `test/registered/unit/disaggregation/` plus the priority-scheduling suite: 213 tests + 31 subtests, all bug-regression cases red-verified on pre-fix code. `cargo test -p sglang-server --lib` for the Rust side. E2E `test_disaggregation_nixl.py::test_role_replacements_reconnect` masks the heartbeat, replaces the prefill (SIGTERM before SIGKILL, matching how k8s replaces a pod) and asserts recovery; on stock code that assertion is the one that fails, matching the table above. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #31644233829](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31644233829)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31644233491](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31644233491)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [observability] Attribute additional phases in the startup breakdown
signal.text: ## Motivation `startup_time` only reports durations that are explicitly plumbed up to the scheduler. On Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP8, the two largest startup phases aren't among them and show up only as slack inside `scheduler_e2e`: | Phase | Duration | Share of `scheduler_e2e` | | --- | --- | --- | | `flashinfer_autotune` (B200) | 41.5s | 36% | | `deepgemm_jit` (H100) | 65.4s | 29% | Both run deep inside kernel wrappers and library init, where plumbing a timer up to the scheduler would change signatures across several unrelated layers. ## Modifications - New `observability/startup_phase_registry.py`, a process-global registry. `startup_phase("name")` times a block at any call depth; `startup_phase_prefix("draft_")` re-attributes an enclosed scope. Phases may overlap, so they don't sum to time-to-ready. - The registry is frozen once at scheduler-ready. Work recorded after the freeze (DeepGEMM JIT compiles on first use, including during warmup) drains into a new counter, `sglang:post_startup_time_seconds_total`, so the cold-start gauges keep meaning "time to ready" instead of drifting upward. - `build_scheduler_startup_time` merges the frozen phases in. `aggregate_scheduler_startup_times` and `emit_startup_time` now iterate whatever keys are present instead of a fixed list, so new phases reach `/get_server_info` and `/metrics` with no further changes. - New `sglang:engine_startup_duration_seconds` histogram, observed once at ready, for percentiles across restarts that a gauge can't express. - Instrumented DeepGEMM JIT, FlashInfer autotune, and torch distributed init. `ModelRunner` gets a decorator that applies the `draft_` prefix on draft runners, so a draft model's phases are attributed separately from the target's. - Removed `startup_func_log_and_timer.py` and its test. Its `sglang:startup_latency_breakdown_seconds_max` gauge had no production callers, so it was never populated on a real server. Existing `startup_time` fields are unchanged, and nothing is added to the forward or scheduling path. That gauge removal is the only non-additive part. ## Accuracy Tests Not applicable; this records durations and emits metrics, and touches neither the forward nor the scheduling path. ## Speed Tests and Profiling No serving-path cost: phases are recorded only during startup, the registry is frozen at scheduler-ready, and work after the freeze drains into a counter rather than reopening it. The startup durations it attributes are in the table above. ## Test Plan - Observability unit tests, including 11 covering freeze idempotence, drain-exactly-once, and prefix nesting. - Server runs scraping `/metrics`: H100 TP=2 (`deepgemm_jit` at 65.4s, `distributed_init` at 14.2s), H100 with an EAGLE3 draft (`draft_distributed_init` attributed separately from `distributed_init`), and B200 with FlashInfer CUTLASS FP8 (`flashinfer_autotune`). Each asserts that the cold-start gauges are unchanged by later traffic and that the histogram is observed exactly once. - Changed-file pre-commit hooks. ## Checklist - [x] Format the code with pre-commit. - [x] Add unit tests. - [x] Documentation is unaffected: `production_metrics.mdx` covers a subset (29 of 143 metrics) and no startup metrics. - [x] Accuracy and speed benchmarks are not applicable; the startup durations are in the table above. - [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32540234837](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32540234837)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32540234711](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32540234711)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32540234888](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32540234888)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [AMD] Optimize Kimi-K3 Triton MLA prefill on gfx950
signal.text: ## Motivation Kimi-K3 uses two attention representations during prefill at TP8 on MI355X: - Fresh/zero-prefix MHA: 12 heads with QK/V dimensions 192/128. - Cached-prefix absorbed MLA: 12 query heads, one KV head, and QK/V dimensions 576/512. Current Triton prefill leaves performance on the table for both shapes: 1. The exact K3 kernels use one pipeline stage and natural-exponential online softmax. 2. Absorbed 576/512 prefill processes one full 512-wide value accumulator, increasing register pressure. 3. FP8 cached-prefix P·V can underflow small softmax probabilities. 4. Aiter supports native FP8 zero-prefix prefill, but Triton lacks an equivalent opt-in path. ## Changes ### K3 prefill tuning - Use two pipeline stages for exact gfx950 K3 192/128 and N32 576/512 prefill kernels. - Fold `log2(e)` into the attention scale and use `exp2` for unmodified K3 logits. - Convert stored LSE back to natural-log units. - Preserve current compact ragged-grid scheduling and the generic Triton-3.7 fallback. ### 4×128 absorbed MLA kernel Add a dedicated split-dimension kernel for cached-prefix K3 MLA: ```text Q/K latent: 4 × 128 Q/K tail: 64 V/output: 4 × 128 ``` The kernel maintains one online-softmax state and four independent FP32 value accumulators before concatenating the normalized 128-wide outputs. Dispatch is restricted to: - gfx950; - 12 query heads and one KV head; - QK/V dimensions 576/512; - BF16 current Q/K/V and output; - BF16 cached prefix with unit scales, or opt-in FP8 cached prefix with supported descales; - causal attention; - page size 1; - contiguous last dimensions; - no custom mask, sliding window, logit cap, XAI temperature, sink, LSE, score modifier, auxiliary tensor, or skipped stage. Unsupported calls immediately use the existing generic kernel. ### FP8 prefill Add: ```bash SGLANG_TRITON_FP8_PREFILL_ATTN=1 ``` This is enabled by default. Set `SGLANG_TRITON_FP8_PREFILL_ATTN=0` to disable native FP8 prefill. On exact K3 gfx950 shapes: - Zero-prefix 192/128 Q/K/V are cast from BF16 to FP8 before launch, matching Aiter behavior. - Absorbed 576/512 prefill keeps current-chunk Q/K/V in BF16 while using the FP8 cached prefix. - Softmax probabilities are multiplied by `FP8_MAX` before FP8 P·V and the accumulator contribution is divided by the same factor. - Non-unit cached-prefix K/V descales are supported. The default-on path achieved 98% GSM8K accuracy in model-level validation. ## Performance MI355X measurements used a device warmup and HIP-graph replay. Against unmodified current main: | K3 prefill case | Current main | This change | Speedup | |---|---:|---:|---:| | Zero-prefix BF16, 8K | 0.726 ms | 0.415 ms | 1.75× | | Zero-prefix FP8, 8K, casts included | 0.726 ms | 0.420 ms | 1.73× | | Absorbed BF16, 8K prefix + 8K extend | 8.658 ms | 4.133 ms | 2.09× | | Absorbed FP8, 8K prefix + 8K extend | 6.770 ms | 3.687 ms | 1.84× | FP8 zero-prefix compared with the optimized BF16 path: | Length | BF16 | FP8, casts included | Result | |---:|---:|---:|---:| | 8K | 0.414 ms | 0.421 ms | No difference | | 16K | 1.500 ms | 1.400 ms | FP8 1.07× faster | | 32K | 6.255 ms | 5.145 ms | FP8 1.22× faster | The default-on policy intentionally follows Aiter and enables native FP8 at every length despite the small 8K crossover loss. ### End-to-end serving Throughput uplift is computed as the geometric mean of the per-concurrency ratios at concurrency 2, 4, 8, and 16. Kimi-K3 TP8, ISL/OSL 8192/1024: | Concurrency | Baseline tok/s | This change tok/s | Uplift | |---:|---:|---:|---:| | 2 | 874.18 | 879.54 | +0.6% | | 4 | 1529.69 | 1586.17 | +3.7% | | 8 | 2554.27 | 2586.82 | +1.3% | | 16 | 3892.75 | 3940.95 | +1.2% | | **Geomean** | — | — | **+1.70%** | Kimi-K3 TP8, ISL/OSL 68K/350: | Concurrency | Baseline tok/s | This change tok/s | Uplift | |---:|---:|---:|---:| | 2 | 6092.96 | 6910.34 | +13.4% | | 4 | 7060.28 | 8185.23 | +15.9% | | 8 | 7655.63 | 9017.19 | +17.8% | | 16 | 7973.53 | 9540.03 | +19.6% | | **Geomean** | — | — | **+16.67%** | The long-context gain is predominantly improved prefill/TTFT; median ITL is effectively unchanged in both comparisons. ## Numerics - BF16 absorbed split versus current-main generic output: relative L2 approximately `9.5e-5`. - FP8 absorbed split versus the corrected generic FP8 path: relative L2 approximately `6.6e-5`. - Zero-prefix FP8 versus BF16: relative L2 approximately 3.4-3.5%. - Kimi-K3 model-level GSM8K accuracy with FP8 prefill enabled: 98%. Additional long-context logits and workload validation remain recommended. ## Platform scope All specialized execution paths require gfx950 and exact K3 shapes. On NVIDIA and other AMD architectures: - the split-dimension dispatcher returns false; - FP8 Q/K/V casting is disabled; - FP8 probability scaling is disabled; - K3 `exp2` and two-stage specializations are disabled; - existing generic attention behavior remains active. ## Validation - Ruff 0.15.1 passed with the repository's configured rule selection. - Black 26.1.0 passed. - Isort 7.0.0 passed. - `git diff --check` passed. - Kimi-K3 GSM8K accuracy with FP8 prefill enabled: 98%. - Four focused K3 BF16/FP8 parity and dispatch tests pass on gfx950. - The focused kernel tests are registered in the per-PR `stage-b-test-1-gpu-small-amd-mi35x` suite. - Generic Triton-3.7 fallback tests passed after the final gfx950-only gate. signal.title: [Fix] Harden FlashAttention CUDA graph metadata bounds
signal.text: ## Motivation Full-prefill CUDA graph buckets are sized by aggregate batch tokens, which can exceed the maximum context length of any single request. The FlashAttention sliding-window write-location buffer is currently allocated from max_context_len, so a valid aggregate-token bucket can exceed its capacity. Separately, idle graph batches may expose an empty CPU sequence-length tensor, for which max() is invalid. ## Modifications - Size the full-prefill sliding-window write-location buffer from the captured token capacity. - Validate replay token counts before copying into the graph-stable buffer. - Use the static context bound when CPU sequence lengths are absent or empty. - Add CPU regression tests for aggregate-token capacity, replay overflow detection, and empty idle batches. ## Accuracy Tests No attention math is changed. The tests validate metadata sizing and fallback behavior. - 2 focused unit tests passed. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not applicable. These changes affect metadata allocation and boundary checks, not attention kernels. ## Checklist - [x] Format code with the repository pre-commit configuration. - [x] Add unit tests. - [x] No documentation update is required. - [x] No speed benchmark is required for this metadata correctness fix. - [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:no_entry_sign: [Run #32416500122](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32416500122)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32416499661](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32416499661)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32416499821](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32416499821)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [AMD] kv_canary verify_real_kv_hash intermittently fires in PD full-real-data path on ROCm
signal.text: ## Summary On ROCm (gfx942 / rocm700, `linux-mi325-2gpu-sglang`), the mock-model PD full-real-data canary test intermittently trips a `verify_real_kv_hash` kv_canary violation on the **decode** side, crashing the scheduler (in `--kv-canary raise` mode → decode `rc=-9` → 500s → job exit 137). Surfaced while onboarding `mock_model/test_e2e_pd.py` to AMD CI in #28850. The `TestPdTransferChecksumFullRealData` class (server args `--kv-canary-real-data all --kv-canary-sweep-interval 1`) is now gated off on AMD via `@unittest.skipIf(is_hip(), ...)`; the baseline `TestPdTransferCanaryClean` stays enabled. This issue tracks re-enabling the full-real-data leg on AMD. ## Evidence From PR Test Extra (AMD) run [27976339910](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/27976339910), job `extra-a-test-2-gpu-large-amd`: ``` disaggregation/decode.py:1807 event_loop_overlap_disagg_decode -> run_batch -> model_runner.forward -> kv_canary/runner/canary_manager.py _post_ops_outside_graph -> violation_manager.step() RuntimeError: kv_canary violation: launch_tag=TAIL_K_FULL fail_reason=verify_real_kv_hash slot_idx=61390 position=6092 stored_token=2005 expected_token=-1 stored_chain_hash=0x551075b2a7b94875 expected_aux=0x551075b2a7b94875 total_violations=256 [FIXTURE FAIL-FAST] decode (pid=...) exited rc=-9; aborting. ``` Key observations: - Servers started healthy (`available_gpu_mem=52.28 GB`, `max_total_num_tokens=3626179`) — not an OOM. - Violations are on a contiguous run of transferred-prefix slots near the prompt boundary (positions ~6092+), on the decode side `TAIL_K_FULL` verify. - The **chain hash matches** (`stored_chain_hash == expected_aux`); only the **real KV content hash** mismatches (`fail_reason=verify_real_kv_hash`). - Intermittent: the same test passed on a prior commit and on the rocm720 lane. ## Hypotheses 1. Intermittent PD KV-transfer nondeterminism on ROCm (prefill-written KV bytes differ from decode-read KV for some transferred slots). 2. Canary real-KV-hash sensitivity to ROCm/aiter bf16 nondeterminism in the PD path. ## Repro Dispatch `pr-test-amd-extra.yml` (default mi325 lane) and run `extra-a-test-2-gpu-large-amd`, or run `mock_model/test_e2e_pd.py::TestPdTransferChecksumFullRealData` on a 2-GPU MI325 host. It reproduces intermittently.

signal.title: [Bug] DeepSeek-V4-Pro Multi-Node PP2 TP8 Fails with AssertionError: Hidden size mismatch in Triton MoE Kernel
signal.text: ### Checklist - [x] I searched related issues but found no solution. - [x] The bug persists in the latest version. - [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback. - [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed. - [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Describe the bug ### **Title** [Bug] DeepSeek-V4-Pro Multi-Node PP2 TP8 Fails with `AssertionError: Hidden size mismatch` in Triton MoE Kernel --- ### **Type** Bug Report / Performance Scaling --- ### **Description** When deploying **DeepSeek-V4-Pro** (FP8 weights) on a multi-node high-performance cluster (2 nodes, 16x H100 80GB GPUs) using `pipeline-parallel-size=2` and `tensor-parallel-size=8`, SGLang crashes during the forward pass. Interestingly, the exact same `PP=2, TP=8` layout works successfully under vLLM, but SGLang throws an `AssertionError: Hidden size mismatch` inside its Triton MoE core (`fused_experts_impl`). Even after passing `--disable-cuda-graph`, the error persists, shifting from the CUDA Graph capture phase directly into the first request execution (`forward_extend` event loop). It seems that the PP proxy tensors or layer-slicing logic passes incorrect hidden dimension shapes into the `fused_moe` Triton kernel when PP > 1. Given that SGLang is highly optimized for DeepSeek architectures, enabling reliable multi-node PP scaling for DeepSeek-V4-Pro is crucial for large-scale enterprise clusters where cross-node tensor parallelism faces bandwidth constraints. --- ### **Environment** * **SGLang Version:** `v0.5.12.post1` (Official Docker Image: `lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.12.post1`) * **Hardware:** 2x Nodes, each with 8x NVIDIA H100 PCIe/SXM5 80GB (Total 16 GPUs) * **Interconnect:** High-bandwidth RoCE/InfiniBand (mlx5 HCAs mapped via `NCCL_IB_HCA`) * **CUDA Version:** 13.0.1 (Inside container) * **PyTorch Version:** 2.x (Bundled with container) --- ### **Steps to Reproduce** #### **Node 0 (Rank 0, Master IP: 192.168.180.132)** ```bash export HEAD_IP="192.168.180.132" docker run --rm --gpus all --network host \ --privileged --ipc=host \ --shm-size 128g \ --hostname gnho032 \ --add-host "gnho032:192.168.180.132" \ --add-host "gnho033:192.168.180.133" \ -v /storage/hpc/chendongshuo/.cache/huggingface:/root/.cache/huggingface \ -v /storage/hpc/chendongshuo/LLMs/DeepSeek-V4-Pro:/model/DeepSeek-V4-Pro \ -e NCCL_IB_HCA=mlx5_0,mlx5_2,mlx5_4,mlx5_6,mlx5_8 \ lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.12.post1 \ python3 -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path /model/DeepSeek-V4-Pro \ --trust-remote-code \ --served-model-name deepseek_pro \ --tensor-parallel-size 8 \ --pipeline-parallel-size 2 \ --nnodes 2 \ --node-rank 0 \ --dist-init-addr ${HEAD_IP}:5000 \ --host 0.0.0.0 \ --port 8000 \ --mem-fraction-static 0.90 \ --context-length 1000000 \ --chunked-prefill-size 4096 \ --max-running-requests 256 \ --tool-call-parser deepseekv4 \ --reasoning-parser deepseek-v4 \ --enable-cache-report ``` #### **Node 1 (Rank 1)** *(Same as Node 0, but running with `--node-rank 1`)* --- ### **Crash Traceback / Log Output** When running **with CUDA Graph enabled**, it fails during CUDA Graph capture: ```text [2026-06-03 03:21:28 PP0 TP0] Scheduler hit an exception: Traceback (most recent call last): ... File "/sgl-workspace/sglang/python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_v2.py", line 728, in forward return self.forward_normal_dual_stream( ... ) File "/sgl-workspace/sglang/python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_v2.py", line 784, in forward_normal_dual_stream final_hidden_states = self.experts(hidden_states, topk_output) ... File "/sgl-workspace/sglang/python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/triton_utils/fused_moe.py", line 121, in inplace_fused_experts fused_experts_impl( ... ) File "/sgl-workspace/sglang/python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/triton_utils/fused_moe.py", line 828, in fused_experts_impl assert hidden_states.shape[1] == w1.shape[2] - padded_size AssertionError: Hidden size mismatch ``` When running **with `--disable-cuda-graph**`, it bypasses the warmup but crashes instantly during the first extended forward pass (`forward_extend`) in the event loop: ```text [2026-06-03 03:35:10 PP0 TP2] Scheduler hit an exception: Traceback (most recent call last): File "/sgl-workspace/sglang/python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py", line 4041, in run_scheduler_process scheduler.run_event_loop() ... File "/sgl-workspace/sglang/python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler_pp_mixin.py", line 1175, in _pp_launch_batch result = self.run_batch(self.cur_batch, pp_proxy_tensors) ... File "/sgl-workspace/sglang/python/sglang/srt/model_executor/model_runner.py", line 3458, in _forward_raw ret, can_run_graph = self.forward_extend( ... ) ... File "/sgl-workspace/sglang/python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/triton_utils/fused_moe.py", line 828, in fused_experts_impl hidden_states.shape[1] == w1.shape[2] - padded_size AssertionError: Hidden size mismatch ``` --- ### **Expected Behavior** The model should initialize the pipeline-parallel groups correctly and complete the forward passes without dimension assertions inside the Triton MoE kernels, matching the multi-node PP capabilities found in other frameworks like vLLM. ### Reproduction 。 ### Environment 。

Otherwise, it will be closed. - [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Describe the bug When running DeepSeek-V4-Pro-FP8 on a multi-node H20 cluster with --tp 32 --ep 32 --dp 4 --enable-dp-attention + --moe-a2a-backend deepep, two issues accur **Issue 1 — Hang on all-reduce due to wrong communication group in DP attention** With DP attention enabled, some DP ranks receive empty batches and fast return, while others still enter the attention output projection (wo_b) and trigger an all-reduce. ``` DP0 / TP0-3: has tokens -> enters wo_b -> calls all-reduce -> blocks waiting for all ranks DP1 / TP4-7: empty batch -> fast return -> never calls this all-reduce ``` If wo_b uses the global TP group all-reduce, the collective becomes an 8-rank barrier where only 4 ranks show up. The empty-batch ranks skip it → permanent hang. Root cause: - the DeepSeek-V4 attention output linear layer defaults to a global TP all-reduce; under DP attention it must use the attention TP group (intra-DP-group) all-reduce instead. Relevant code: - python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_v4.py:462 (MQALayer.__init__) - python/sglang/srt/layers/linear.py:1543 (RowParallelLinear.forward) --- **Issue 2 — DeepEP bootstrap communication failure on multi-node H20** During DeepEP buffer creation, the NCCL/NVSHMEM bootstrap stage receives messages of unexpected length, causing startup/communication failure. Root cause: - on CU13 + flashinfer, the code may enable the MNNVL fabric path (use_fabric=True) via is_mnnvl_fabric_supported(). - MNNVL fabric is the cross-pod NVLink GPU-to-GPU memory path for GB200/GB300 NVL systems and must not be used on H20. Relevant code: - python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/token_dispatcher/deepep.py:237-258 (DeepEPBuffer.get_deepep_buffer) ### Reproduction ```bash export SGLANG_ENABLE_TP_MEMORY_INBALANCE_CHECK=0 export
