signal.title: [Fix] Forward an explicit CXX to nvcc via -ccbin in JIT builds
signal.text: ## Problem The JIT build resolves the host compiler from `CXX` (`toolchain.host_compiler_path()`) and uses it for the `.cpp` translation units and the link step — but never tells nvcc. nvcc ignores `CXX` entirely: it takes `-ccbin` or falls back to `gcc` from `PATH`. So on a machine whose default gcc is newer than the CUDA toolkit's nvcc supports, every JIT kernel build fails: ``` host_config.h:132: #error -- unsupported GNU version! gcc versions later than 12 are not supported! ``` even when the user explicitly set `CXX=/usr/bin/g++-12` to fix exactly that. Repro on such a machine (CUDA 12.x nvcc + default gcc 13): ```python import os os.environ["CXX"] = "/usr/bin/g++-12" from sglang.kernels.jit.utils.compile import toolchain print(toolchain.host_compiler_path()) # /usr/bin/g++-12 (.cpp units + link) print(toolchain.base_cuda_flags()) # ['-Xcompiler', '-fPIC'] <- no -ccbin ``` The generated `build.ninja` compiles `.cpp` with `$cxx` (g++-12) while the `compile_cuda` rule lets nvcc pick `gcc` (13) for all host code inside `.cu` units. ## Fix `base_cuda_flags()` appends `-ccbin $CXX` when `CXX` is set explicitly (resolved through the `@cache_once`-cached `explicit_host_compiler()`, so both call sites see one value). When `CXX` is unset the flags are unchanged — nvcc's own default (`gcc` from PATH) is preserved, since forwarding the `"c++"` fallback would silently change the default host compiler. The HIP branch is untouched (hipcc takes no `-ccbin`). The build key follows automatically: it is taken over the generated `build.ninja` text (which now embeds the flag) and `_environment_fingerprint` already fingerprints `host_compiler_path()`, so a changed `CXX` re-keys the build instead of reusing stale binaries. Verified end to end on an RTX 3080 / CUDA 12.0 / default gcc 13 machine: with the JIT cache cleared, `CXX=/usr/bin/gcc-12 python3 -m sglang.launch_server ...` now compiles all JIT kernels and serves traffic. Before the fix the same command failed every `.cu` build with the error above, and the only workaround was to also set `NVCC_CCBIN` — a variable this code path never reads. Per review, no unit test is attached: the behavior depends on a compiler the CI machine is not guaranteed to have, so the change ships without a test. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:warning: [Run #32535669810](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32535669810)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:warning: [Run #32535669745](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32535669745)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:warning: [Run #32535669764](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32535669764)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [Fix] Stop unparsed Kimi K3 template syntax from leaking into responses
signal.text: ## Motivation Kimi K3 emits its channels (`<|open|>tools<|sep|>`, `<|open|>call ...`, `<|close|>message<|sep|>`, ...) as literal text, so any path that does not run the tool-call parser hands that syntax straight to the client. Two such paths exist today: - **Parsing disabled.** With `tool_choice="none"` or no tools, `serving_chat` / `serving_responses` skip the parser and `FunctionCallParser.parse_non_stream` returns `full_text` verbatim. Measured on a K3 deployment: ~10% of `tool_choice="none"` completions came back containing a raw tools section. - **Truncation.** `KimiK3Detector.has_tool_call` is `self.bot_token in text`, so output cut mid-marker (`...<|open|>too`) misses detection and `parse_non_stream` again returns the raw text. With small `max_output_tokens` this reproduced in 97-100% of samples. Separately, `ResponsesRequest._normalize_input_item_for_validation` defaults the SDK-required `input_image.detail` only under `item["content"]`. Tool-output items carry their parts under `item["output"]`, so an image tool result without `detail` (what Codex sends) fails validation with a 400. ## Modifications - `base_format_detector.py`: two identity-by-default hooks, `strip_template_artifacts(text, reasoning_separated)` and `strip_template_markers(text)`. Formats whose tool channel is literal text override them; every other detector is unaffected. - `kimik3_detector.py`: implements both. Artifact stripping cuts from an unparsed `TOOLS_OPEN` / `CALL_OPEN` onward, drops the think channel when a reasoning parser already routed the trace to its own field, unwraps the response channel, and removes whole and cut-off markers. Marker stripping only removes syntax, keeping the text it wrapped — used for reasoning content. - `kimik3_format.py`: `ALL_MARKERS`, `ARGUMENT_OPEN`, and a `min_len` on `partial_suffix_len` so a reply legitimately ending in `<` is not truncated. - `function_call_parser.py`: the two paths that returned `full_text` unchanged (no tools, detection missed) now route it through `strip_template_artifacts`. - `serving_chat.py` / `serving_responses.py`: apply the hooks to non-streaming assistant text and reasoning content, regardless of whether parsing ran. A Responses turn whose text was nothing but syntax still emits an `output_text` item (empty) rather than an output array with no message. - `utils.py`: `align_token_logprobs_to_text`. The cleanup is pure span deletion, so the cleaned text is a subsequence of the concatenated tokens; entries whose token was removed are dropped, and the array becomes `None` if the two cannot be reconciled rather than being returned misaligned. Applied only when cleanup actually changed the text, so logprobs on paths this PR does not touch are unchanged. - `protocol.py`: normalize `input_image.detail` under `output` as well as `content`. Streaming is out of scope: the chunk handlers can still emit markers verbatim, and fixing that needs cross-chunk marker buffering. ## Accuracy Tests No change to model forward or kernels — this only affects post-generation text handling in the OpenAI entrypoints. ## Speed Tests and Profiling N/A; the added work is a few regex passes over the response text. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32536273695](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32536273695)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32536273592](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32536273592)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32536273758](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32536273758)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [AMD] Skip full-vocab softmax in EAGLE topk==1 draft on ROCm
signal.text: ## Motivation With `--speculative-eagle-topk 1` the EAGLE draft tree degenerates to a single chain, so the returned `topk_p` is never consumed downstream and only the selected index matters. Softmax is monotonic and cannot move an argmax, so the full-vocab `torch.softmax` the draft loop computes is pure overhead. #26235 removed it, #26358 reverted it after DSv3.2-MTP GSM8K collapsed on ROCm, and #26397 relanded it behind `not _is_hip` — so CUDA gets the fast path and ROCm still pays for a softmax whose result it discards. On a profiled Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-MXFP4 MTP run (MI355X, TP2, IL8192/OL1024), the discarded softmax and its top-1 reduction are **11.4% of the entire MTP draft CUDA-graph**: | kernel | total (µs) | calls | per call (µs) | |---|---:|---:|---:| | `cunn_SoftMaxForwardGmem` | 95,312.3 | 1200 | 79.4 | | `at::native::reduce_kernel<512,1,…>` (`torch.max`) | 83,624.7 | 1200 | 69.7 | | **total** | **178,937.0** | | **149.1** | Prior attempts and why this differs: #26633 proposed deleting the `not _is_hip` gate outright; its CI went red and the author closed it with no review. #29800 is open but ships a monkey-patch script under `scripts/`, patches only the draft-extend site (not the draft-decode loop where the time actually goes), and relies on an fp32 cast — which cannot break ties, since widening from fp8 is lossless. ## Modifications **Purely additive: 159 insertions, 0 deletions, in 2 files.** The existing `elif self.topk == 1 and not _is_hip:` branch and its body are not modified, so CUDA and every non-ROCm platform are byte-for-byte unchanged — a new `elif` is layered after it. Given this code path was reverted once for an accuracy collapse, not perturbing the platform that currently works is worth more than de-duplicating the two branches. No new module-level state, no new helper functions, and no new env var: `SGLANG_USE_AITER` already gates aiter, and reverting this commit is the rollback lever. - `speculative/eagle_worker_v2.py`: bind `aiter.greedy_sample` once in `EagleDraftWorker.__init__` (env/platform config is init-static per the repo style rule), then add the ROCm branch inline at **both** call sites — the draft-decode loop, where the draft steps run and the measured time goes, and the draft-extend selection. #29800 patches only the latter. The branch body is 8 lines. - New unit test pinning the two aiter properties this depends on: the `hipcub::ArgMax` lowest-index tie-break, and correctness above the vocab floor. ```python elif self.topk == 1 and not _is_hip: ... # unchanged, not in the diff elif ( self.topk == 1 and self.aiter_greedy_sample is not None and logits_output.next_token_logits.shape[-1] > 1023 * 16 ): logits = logits_output.next_token_logits selected = torch.empty( logits.shape[0], dtype=torch.int32, device=logits.device ) self.aiter_greedy_sample(selected, logits) topk_index = selected.to(torch.int64).unsqueeze(-1) topk_p = torch.ones_like(topk_index, dtype=torch.float32) forward_batch.positions.add_(1) ``` Branch behavior, showing nothing can get slower — ROCm's only path today is the `else`: | case | before | after | |---|---|---| | CUDA, topk=1 | `not _is_hip` branch | same branch, not in the diff | | ROCm, aiter bound + vocab > 16368 | `else` softmax | **new branch** | | ROCm, no aiter or vocab ≤ 16368 | `else` softmax | `else` softmax (identical to today) | | topk > 1 / rejection sampling | unchanged | unchanged | ### aiter bug found while validating this `aiter::greedy_sample` returns **negative, out-of-range indices for vocab ≤ 16368**. Its kernel launches `BlockSize=1024 × VecSize=16`; a thread whose first offset `threadIdx.x * 16` already exceeds `N` skips the initial load, leaving `vec_pre` uninitialized, but still enters the tail with `key = threadIdx.x * 16 - 16385` — a negative key that can win the block reduction. That predicts breakage exactly for `N <= 1023 * 16 = 16368`, and bisecting the boundary on gfx950 / ROCm 7.2 reproduces it precisely: wrong (negative) indices up to `N = 16368`, correct from `N = 16369`. This is also the likely root cause of the out-of-range token ids already documented at `layers/sampler.py:53`. This PR guards around it; an aiter-side fix is being filed separately. ## Accuracy Tests GSM8K, 200 questions, 5-shot, same server config, MI355X TP2: | | accuracy | invalid | |---|---:|---:| | run 1 before / after | 0.930 / 0.940 | 0.000 | | run 2 before / after | 0.930 / 0.950 | 0.000 | No regression in either run. The gains are 2 and 4 questions out of 200 and should be read as noise, not as an improvement. One negative result worth recording: **the tie-break instability that motivated the #26397 gate does not reproduce in isolation on gfx950 / ROCm 7.2.** Across batch-shape padding, repeated calls, and fp8-quantized logits with ~2.6 tied cells per row at the maximum, `torch.argmax`, `softmax+fast_topk`, and `aiter greedy_sample` all returned identical, stable, lowest-index results. That matches what #26633 reported, so the reland's premise is unconfirmed rather than disproven. This PR does not rest on that question either way — it uses a kernel whose tie-break is contractual. ## Benchmarking and Profiling ### Profile: the kernels are gone Same server config, conc4, profiled before and after, parsed with `trace_module_analyzer`. Draft-graph kernels (`Module Types == "Layer"`): | kernel | before | after | |---|---|---| | `cunn_SoftMaxForwardGmem` | 95,312.3 µs × 1200 | **absent** | | `at::native::reduce_kernel<512,1,…>` | 83,624.7 µs × 1200 | **absent** | | `aiter::greedy_sample_kernel` | 127.7 µs × 7 *(final sampler only)* | 22,013.4 µs × 1221 | | **net on these kernels** | | **−157,051 µs** | | draft CUDA-graph total | 1,568,438.9 µs | 1,432,504.0 µs (**−8.7%**) | Per draft step the selection goes **149.1 µs → 18.0 µs (8.3×)**. ### End-to-end Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-MXFP4, MI355X TP2, IL8192/OL1024, EAGLE `num-steps 3 / topk 1 / draft-tokens 4`. Run 1 is on the pre-rebase base; run 2 is on the current base — both are independent server loads per side. **median TPOT** — the metric this change acts on, a median over thousands of decode tokens: | | conc4 | conc8 | conc16 | conc32 | conc64 | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | run 1 Δ | −1.14% | −1.28% | −1.23% | −0.37% | +0.46% | | run 2 Δ | −1.99% | −0.25% | −2.12% | −1.04% | −0.52% | | run 2 before (ms) | 4.88 | 6.92 | 10.57 | 16.66 | 28.02 | | run 2 after (ms) | 4.78 | 6.90 | 10.34 | 16.49 | 27.88 | **Negative in 9 of 10 measurements**, the exception being run 1's conc64 (+0.46%), which run 2 puts at −0.52%. **total throughput** — cannot resolve an effect this size and should not be read as a result: | | conc4 | conc8 | conc16 | conc32 | conc64 | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | run 1 Δ | +3.10% | +1.35% | +1.41% | +0.41% | +0.21% | | run 2 Δ | +0.39% | −0.04% | +1.43% | +1.01% | −0.15% | Run 1's conc4 read +3.10%, but a repeat at 2.5× the prompt count gave +0.60% and the *baseline itself* moved 5.9% between runs. At these request counts throughput is dominated by TTFT and scheduling jitter. Honest summary: **median TPOT −1% to −2% at conc4–32, ~−0.5% at conc64.** Not a 5%-class win. The saving is a near-fixed ~130 µs per draft step, so its relative value shrinks as the iteration grows with concurrency. It is a small, reproducible decode-latency improvement that deletes a full-vocab softmax whose output was being discarded. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review Process 1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the PR flow. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process). 2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers. 3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so. - `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci`, `/tag-and-rerun-ci` 4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls to merge. cc @Qiaolin-Yu @michaelzhang-ai <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32502499374](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32502499374)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32502536281](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32502536281)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32502499391](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32502499391)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [Docs] Add --prerelease=allow to cookbook uv install commands
signal.text: ## Motivation Fixes the docs half of #35912. uv older than 0.12.0 does not honor pre-release specifiers found in **transitive** dependency metadata (changed in astral-sh/uv#19993, released in [uv 0.12.0](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/releases/tag/0.12.0) on 2026-07-28). `flash-attn-4`, a mandatory dependency of every release since 0.5.10, only publishes pre-releases on PyPI, so `uv pip install sglang` treats every release ≥ 0.5.10 as unsatisfiable and silently backtracks to **0.5.9** (2026-02-23) — no error, no warning. Users then hit bugs that were fixed months ago. `docs/docs/get-started/install.mdx` already carries `--prerelease=allow` (#29676), but the cookbook pages do not, so anyone following a model page — or typing the obvious command — still lands on 0.5.9. Two things make this worse than when #29676 landed: - `sglang==0.5.18` now also pins `cuda-tile==1.6.0rc5`, so **source and editable installs fail outright** on uv < 0.12.0 (the resolver cannot backtrack when the version is fixed), which is why the `-e python` commands need the flag too. - uv 0.12.0 is only a few weeks old, so most environments and images still ship 0.11.x. Measured with `uv pip compile` (`--python-platform x86_64-manylinux_2_34 --python-version 3.12`): | uv | default | `--prerelease=allow` | | --- | --- | --- | | 0.11.24 | **`sglang==0.5.9`** | `sglang==0.5.18` | | 0.12.5 | `sglang==0.5.18` | `sglang==0.5.18` | And with the version pinned so the resolver cannot backtrack (uv 0.11.24, default): ``` $ echo 'sglang==0.5.18' | uv pip compile - --python-platform x86_64-manylinux_2_34 × Because there is no version of cuda-tile==1.6.0rc5 and sglang==0.5.18 depends on cuda-tile==1.6.0rc5, we can conclude that sglang==0.5.18 cannot be used. hint: `cuda-tile` was requested with a pre-release marker ... (try: `--prerelease=allow`) ``` `pip`, uv ≥ 0.12.0, and the Docker images are unaffected. On new uv the flag is a harmless no-op. ## Modifications Docs only. - Added `--prerelease=allow` to **31 commands across 26 cookbook pages** — every command that installs SGLang, in all three forms: - PyPI: `uv pip install sglang`, `"sglang>=0.5.9"`, the pinned nightly in `Nemotron3-Nano.mdx` - git: `uv pip install 'git+https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang.git#subdirectory=python'` - source: `uv pip install -e python`, `-e "python[all]"` - Same fix in `.claude/skills/cookbook-add-model/templates/page.mdx.tmpl`, so new pages get it by default. - Added a two-sentence `<Note>` to `install.mdx` Method 1 explaining why the flag is there and that uv ≥ 0.12.0 does not need it. Deliberately left alone, verified as unaffected: - Commands that do not install SGLang: `lmms_eval` (Qwen3-VL), `natten` (LTX2.5), `".[s2pro]"` (S2-Pro — that is the separate `sglang-omni` repo). - The pages that already had the flag: the six diffusion pages and LongCat-2.0. - `hardware-platforms/tpu.mdx` (installs `sglang-jax`, a different repo), `hardware-platforms/cpu_server.mdx` (`cp pyproject_cpu.toml`), `hardware-platforms/apple_metal.mdx` and `sglang-diffusion/installation.mdx` (`mv pyproject_other.toml`) — neither `pyproject_cpu.toml` nor `pyproject_other.toml` contains `flash-attn-4`, `cuda-tile`, or any other pre-release pin. After this change, `git grep "uv pip install" -- docs` has no remaining SGLang install without the flag. ## Accuracy Tests N/A — documentation only. ## Speed Tests and Profiling N/A — documentation only. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). — N/A, docs only; `node docs/scripts/check_cookbook_configs.mjs` passes. - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results. — N/A, docs only. - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Follow-ups (not in this PR) #35912 also raises two non-docs items this PR does not address: a packaging/runtime guard so the silent downgrade cannot happen at all, and re-triaging the older issues whose environment fingerprint matches a resolver-driven 0.5.9 install (#24029, #34111, #34112, #34113, #33283, #25670). 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32534198341](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32534198341)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32534198151](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32534198151)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:heavy_minus_sign: **No AMD PR run found for this commit**.<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: perf: overlap Qwen shared expert with DeepEP routed experts
signal.text: ## Motivation For Qwen MoE models using CUDA and DeepEP, the shared expert currently runs on the default stream before the routed-expert path. This serializes two independent computations and leaves an available alternate stream unused. This PR adds an opt-in path that overlaps the Qwen shared expert with routed-expert/DeepEP execution. ## Modifications - Add `SGLANG_QWEN_DEEPEP_SHARED_OVERLAP` (default: `false`). - When enabled on CUDA, enqueue the shared expert on `alt_stream`, execute the routed-expert path on the current stream, and wait on an event immediately before accumulating the shared output. - When breakable CUDA graph is active, skip this optimization and retain the existing serial shared-expert path; cross-segment overlap across the eager DeepEP break is out of scope. - Document the new environment variable. ## Accuracy Tests The accuracy evidence below was collected on predecessor `38f714d28e1fa01ae5b1ce38ce576373b8293722`, based on upstream main `0c072235f44fce4b89e594c2d3348e4f48e774b8`, with a clean source tree. Current head `76815b3766deb3a3c9aceef1cb346093f691d976` differs only by making breakable CUDA graph use the pre-existing serial fallback instead of an alternate-stream path with an immediate wait; the non-breakable overlap implementation measured below is unchanged. Configuration: `nvidia/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-NVFP4`, 8x GB300, FP4 weights, FP8 KV cache, TP8/DP8/EP8, NEXTN draft length 6, DeepEP low-latency mode, 200 GSM8K examples, 5 shots, temperature 0.6, top-p 0.95, and top-k 20. The run used natural NEXTN acceptance. | Metric | Result | Gate | |---|---:|---:| | GSM8K score | **0.990** (200/200) | >= 0.95 | | Request-weighted mean accepted length | **4.6102** (1,379 decode-log rows; request weight 11,625) | > 3.3 | | Evaluation latency | 95.646 s | -- | | Evaluation output throughput | 5,621.1 token/s | -- | All eight ranks completed target verify CUDA graph capture, followed by draft decode and draft extend graph capture. The job completed successfully with exit code 0. Breakable CUDA graph is now intentionally excluded from this optimization, and no performance gain is claimed for that fallback. ## Speed Tests and Profiling The performance A/B exercised the same overlap mechanism on the benchmark stack before this upstream-main port. The upstream-main commit listed in the accuracy section was validated separately through CUDA graph capture and GSM8K. The end-to-end A/B comparison used the same configuration and differed only in the job name and `SGLANG_QWEN_DEEPEP_SHARED_OVERLAP=true`. Configuration: `nvidia/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-NVFP4`, 24x GB300 disaggregated serving (four TP4/DP4/EP4 prefill replicas and one TP8/DP8/EP8 decode replica), FP4 weights, FP8 KV cache, NEXTN draft length 6, concurrency 896, fixed accepted length 4.8, and a 3,600-second AgentX replay. | AIPerf metric | Disabled | Enabled | Delta | |---|---:|---:|---:| | Total token throughput | 2,649,331.82 token/s | 2,705,912.48 token/s | **+2.14%** | | Output token throughput | 25,466.20 token/s | 26,000.99 token/s | **+2.10%** | | Request throughput | 27.980 request/s | 28.516 request/s | **+1.91%** | | Mean inter-token latency | 18.220 ms | 17.623 ms | **-3.28%** | | Theoretical prefix-cache hit | 95.433% | 95.452% | +0.020 pp | These are end-to-end AIPerf results without profiler instrumentation. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). signal.title: feat(mem_cache): semantic KV cache reuse via a pluggable fuzzy-match radix backend
signal.text: ## Motivation Exact prefix matching cannot reuse KV across prompts that share meaning but not leading tokens: paraphrased questions over the same document, RAG prompts with reordered context, multi-user workloads hitting the same knowledge base. This PR adds opt-in **semantic KV cache reuse** following the `|exact|fuzzy|miss|` prompt decomposition from the fuzzy prefix matching design discussion (Draft_Prefix_Matching.md, @ibifrost): when the radix tree covers only a prefix, a pluggable `FuzzyMatchProvider` may nominate donor KV from a previously finished request, which is copied into recipient-owned slots with RoPE position correction before the forward pass. Design goals, per maintainer guidance (@hzh0425): keep the default path untouched, register the feature as a radix-cache backend, keep `model_runner` changes minimal. ## Modifications - **New `FuzzyRadixCache(RadixCache)`** registered as radix-cache backend `fuzzy_match` (flexkv pattern). All fuzzy behavior lives in the backend: provider match on exact-miss, donor validation + pinning (lock refs via a TreeNode-id registry), realization-slot pre-allocation with clean exact-only fallback, donor registration on request finish. - **Core `RadixCache`/`BasePrefixCache` changes = two seams:** `MatchResult.fuzzy_matched_len` (new trailing field) and a no-op `_on_finished_insert` hook between the finished-request insert and duplicate-slot freeing. - **`FuzzyKVRealizer`** collaborator does pre-forward donor-KV realization (V copy; K reverse-RoPE at donor positions + apply at target positions; per-layer zero-out mask). `model_runner.py` gains only orchestration: a gated `maybe_init_fuzzy_kv_realizer()` and one delegate call in `_forward_raw` beside the deferred-mamba hook (outside CUDA-graph capture/replay, covers all extend branches). - **`ReverseRotaryEmbedding` / `get_reverse_rope` / `reverse_rotary_emb`** additions to `layers/rotary_embedding` (native path; no CUDA kernel exists for the reverse direction). - **`SemanticEmbedding` provider** (default): implemented by the [`semblend`](https://github.com/WorldFlowAI/semblend) package ([PyPI](https://pypi.org/project/semblend/), Apache-2.0), installed via the new extra `pip install "sglang[fuzzy-semantic]"`. SemBlend is an open-source library for semantic KV-cache donor discovery and reuse planning: it embeds prompts (MiniLM ONNX), maintains the donor index, aligns donor and recipient token chunks (N:M), scores reuse quality against configurable gates, and emits the reuse plan — donor span, positions, and the per-layer mask — that this PR's realization path consumes. Keeping that pipeline in a package keeps SGLang's tree free of the embedding/ANN stack while the reuse-planning algorithms iterate. Lazy import + hard version gate at startup with an actionable error. The `FuzzyMatchProvider` interface is public so custom providers can plug in. - **Observability:** prefill batch log shows `#fuzzy-token: N` when fuzzy reuse fired (previously realized reuse showed as `#cached-token: 0`). - **Config surface:** selecting the backend enables the feature; five `--fuzzy-*` flags (provider, threshold, min-reuse-ratio, min-match-length, model-arch). Provider-internal tuning stays in config defaults. - **Docs:** end-to-end call chain with explicit lock/alloc/RoPE ownership in `python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/fuzzy_match/README.md` (requested in review of the experimental branch). - **Tests:** 21 CPU unit tests (`test_fuzzy_match_providers.py`, `test_fuzzy_radix_cache.py`), semblend faked via sys.modules — no new CI dependency. Cover pool-accounting failure modes: stale-donor and kv-length-mismatch fallbacks (leak-checked), donor pin/release lifecycle, donor-registration ordering vs duplicate freeing, node-registry maintenance, registry selection + unsupported-config rejection, and concurrent recipients pinning one donor. Not supported yet: MLA pools, EAGLE, multi-region reuse, hierarchical-cache interaction. ## Follow-on work This PR deliberately ships the minimal `|exact|fuzzy|miss|` pattern — one contiguous fuzzy span re-anchored at the exact-prefix boundary — because it reuses the existing inference pipeline with no structural changes. Planned follow-ups, in rough order: - **Multi-segment / multi-region reuse** (`|exact|miss|fuzzy|miss|fuzzy|...`), the realistic shape of RAG and multi-document workloads: the scheduler builds a segmented prefill plan of fresh spans plus donor-KV spans, and the attention backend consumes it via FlashInfer's `VariableBlockSparseAttentionWrapper` (per the design discussion, a better fit than `custom_mask`). Early prototypes on 64K multi-donor prompts show mean 7.65x TTFT speedup versus cold prefill with good quality — worth its own RFC once this foundation lands. - **True per-layer recompute** for masked layers (the current `layer_recompute_mask` is a zero-out signal); recompute is the cleaner long-term answer for quality. - **Donor-registration budgeting** (rate/dedup limits on donor indexing) to shrink the remaining enabled-but-idle overhead on dense short-request workloads. - **MLA-pool support** in the realization path. - **Hierarchical-cache (HiCache) interaction** — fuzzy donors resident in host tiers. ## Accuracy Tests All runs on THIS branch (A10G, Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct-AWQ, fresh server per configuration, 2026-07-13). - **GSM8K few-shot (n=1000), fuzzy on vs off:** baseline accuracy 0.862 (invalid 0.001) vs fuzzy-on **0.865** (invalid 0.001) — no degradation (delta within batching noise). The provider's gates produced **zero fuzzy fires across all 1000 questions** (short, semantically dissimilar prompts never meet the reuse-ratio gate; the few-shot prefix hits the exact radix path), and zero pool leaks. This is the negative control: enabling the backend does not perturb workloads without semantic overlap. - **Warm-vs-cold A/B at 8K/16K** (cnn_dailymail + wikihow clusters, at **default flags**). ROUGE-L / token-F1 compare the warm (reused) answer against the cold answer for the same prompt; the measurement scale: identical-prompt reruns without any reuse score ~0.88/0.90 (batching-noise floor), exact-prefix radix reuse scores 0.94/0.96. | Overlap type | cache frac | cold→warm TTFT | ROUGE-L | token-F1 | |---|---|---|---|---| | exact (control) | — (radix) | 3264→44ms | 0.941 | 0.955 | | partial_60 | 0.88 | 3254→646ms (5.0x) | 0.547 | 0.587 | | partial_80 | 0.58 | 3257→1700ms (1.9x) | 0.449 | 0.490 | | paraphrase | 0.76 | 3262→1034ms (3.2x) | 0.478 | 0.525 | | diverse (negative) | 0.00 | 3262→3318ms (no fire) | 0.878 | 0.898 | A sweep at looser settings (threshold 0.50, min-match 1) produced the same hit rates and the same drift — on genuinely similar pairs the threshold does not change what a hit does, it changes which pairs hit (on GSM8K, defaults fire on 1 in 1000 requests; the diverse control never fires). Read: a fuzzy hit trades TTFT for output drift beyond the rerun-noise floor — reuse is quality-gated but **not lossless**; answers remain on-topic and grounded (samples in the raw results), and per-layer recompute (follow-on) is the path to closing the gap. Zero pool-consistency failures across all sweeps and both GSM8K runs. Experimental-branch reference @16K (n=1): PPL(warm)/PPL(cold) 0.9587. - Statement of semantics: reuse is quality-gated but not lossless; the layer mask is a zero-out signal, not per-layer recompute. ## Speed Tests and Profiling - **Reuse speedup (this branch, e2e smoke):** paraphrase variant realized 104/119 donor tokens with RoPE correction; only 15 tokens prefilled. Experimental-branch reference at 16K: cold TTFT 4548ms → warm 230ms (19.8x); donor registration runs off the hot path (async embed). [OPTIONAL: re-measure 16K TTFT pair on this branch] - **No-hit overhead (GSM8K n=1000, parallel 32, default flags):** 1249 → 1164 tok/s output throughput (~7%) and 127.3 → 136.8s wall on a worst-case-dense workload (a thousand short requests, every one indexed as a donor). The synchronous per-miss lookup cost is bounded by `fuzzy_min_suffix_tokens` (default 256): suffixes too short to amortize a semantic lookup never pay for one. The residual is the asynchronous donor-registration embedding, which amortizes on long-context workloads (fewer, larger requests); donor-registration budgeting is listed as follow-on. Without the suffix gate the same workload measured ~10-11%. The feature is opt-in per deployment. ## Reproduction ```bash pip install "sglang[fuzzy-semantic]" python -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct-AWQ \ --radix-cache-backend fuzzy_match \ --fuzzy-model-arch qwen2.5-7b \ --mem-fraction-static 0.70 2>&1 | tee server.log # paired paraphrase prompts -> look for: # "fuzzy match success", "[FUZZY] Realized", "#fuzzy-token:" grep -c "pool memory leak detected" server.log # expect 0 ``` ## Checklist / credits - Design + `FuzzyMatchProvider` framework: @ibifrost (Draft_Prefix_Matching.md); backend-registry direction: @hzh0425. Co-authored-by: Chenxin Wu <ibifrostki@gmail.com> Big thanks to @ibifrost and @hzh0425 for all of the hard work/advice/reviewing over the past several months. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32513043966](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32513043966)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32513043826](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32513043826)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32513043948](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32513043948)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [Kimi K3] Exclude template-rendered response_format tokens from billed prompt_tokens
signal.text: ## Problem For Kimi K3, requests with `response_format` report inflated `usage.prompt_tokens`. A vendor conformance run measured **186 vs the reference API's 119** for the same request, breaking billing alignment with the official K3 API. Root cause: `_encode_messages` (kimi_k3 branch) passes `response_format` into the checkpoint's chat template, which renders the JSON schema plus wrapper instructions into the prompt. Those tokens land in `origin_input_ids` and are counted as prompt tokens. The grammar/constraint path adds zero prompt tokens — the inflation comes solely from the template render. ## What this PR does - In the kimi_k3 encoder, when `response_format` is present, render the template once more without the `response_format` kwarg and record the token-count delta on the request (`_response_format_prompt_tokens`). Measuring the diff is robust to whatever wrapper the checkpoint template adds — no hardcoded schema-length math. - `_reported_prompt_tokens` subtracts that count alongside the existing `_KIMI_K3_GENERATION_STUB_TOKENS` adjustment, so billed/reported prompt tokens match the reference API with and without `response_format`. Cost: one extra CPU-side template render per response_format request; no behavior change for other models or for requests without `response_format`. ## Tests `test_kimi_k3_response_format_tokens_not_billed` — mocks the two renders (186 with the schema block, 119 baseline), asserts the measured delta (67) is excluded from reported prompt tokens and that requests without `response_format` keep the existing stub-only adjustment. Also updated `test_kimi_k3_encoder_receives_wire_request_fields` for the extra baseline render. ``` $ pytest test/registered/unit/entrypoints/openai/test_serving_chat.py test/registered/unit/entrypoints/openai/test_protocol.py 155 passed ``` ## Known gap (pre-existing, not made worse by this PR) `/v1/responses` (`serving_responses.py`) reads `prompt_tokens` from meta_info directly and does not go through `_reported_prompt_tokens`, so neither this adjustment nor the existing 3-token generation-stub adjustment applies there. K3 vendor conformance is chat-completions-only, so this is out of scope here; flagging for a follow-up if Responses API billing parity is ever needed. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32439564964](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32439564964)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32439564942](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32439564942)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32439564948](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32439564948)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->
signal.author: JustinTong0323

signal.title: Keep the DeepSeek router GEMM in fp32 under deterministic inference
signal.text: ## Motivation Closes #34758. Under deterministic inference the DeepSeek router GEMM returns bf16 logits, while every other branch of `MoEGate.forward` returns fp32 (`dsv3_router_gemm(out_dtype=torch.float32)`, `linear_bf16_fp32`, the prefill-CP path). `noaux_tc` ranks 256/384 experts against an fp32 correction bias, and adjacent expert scores routinely sit within one bf16 ULP, so the narrower store changes which experts run — a different answer, not a small numeric difference. fp32 output does not cost batch invariance. Invariance is a property of the reduction order, and the store happens after the reduction is complete. ## Modifications The root cause is one missing degree of freedom: `matmul_persistent` could not express *accumulate fp32, store fp32* — the output dtype was implicitly `a.dtype`. Every symptom in the issue follows from that. **`batch_invariant_ops.py`** - `out_dtype` threaded through `matmul_persistent`, `_matmul_persistent_triton` and `_matmul_persistent_deepgemm`. - The Triton tile config stays keyed on the **input** dtype. This is load-bearing: the configs are not the same shape (`bfloat16 -> BLOCK_SIZE_K=64`, `float32 -> BLOCK_SIZE_K=32`), so keying on `out_dtype` - would halve the k-tile and silently run a different reduction than the non-deterministic path. Only the `torch.empty` moves. - DeepGEMM keeps its kernel instead of falling back to Triton. `bf16_gemm_nn` only stores bf16, but - bf16_gemm_nt` already takes an fp32 `out` (it is what `gemm_nt_bf16bf16f32` and `_BF16F32WarmupExecutor` use) and wants the `[N, K]` rhs that `matmul_persistent` has already checked is contiguous. Routing fp32 to Triton would have demoted the kernel on exactly the H200/B200 deterministic runs this is meant to help. - `_mm_dtype_compat` asks the kernel for `out_dtype` rather than casting afterwards, fixing the `fp32 -> bf16 -> fp32` round trip that handed `aten::mm.dtype` callers bf16 values. - Its two `.contiguous()` calls are dropped. For the router, `mat2` is `weight.t()`, so they were materializing a `[7168, 256]` copy every forward, every MoE layer, and disqualifying the DeepGEMM path on the way. Its sibling `mm_batch_invariant` never did this, and the kernel takes strided operands. **`deepseek_v2.py`** — the deterministic branch becomes `torch.mm(hidden_states, self.weight.t(), out_dtype=torch.float32)`. Going through the aten override rather than importing `matmul_persistent` keeps device dispatch intact. The issue's fourth point needs no work: this branch already returns above the `max_router_gemm_tokens` switch, so the token-count-dependent kernel choice was never reachable under deterministic mode. **`npu_batch_invariant_ops.py`** — `aten::mm.dtype` registered on NPU. It casts rather than widening (the NPU kernel stores its input dtype), so precision there is unchanged; without it `out_dtype=` would fall through to the stock NPU matmul and leave batch-invariant mode altogether. ## Accuracy Tests Measured on one GPU with the Triton backend, `[64, 7168] x [7168, 256]` shaped like the router GEMM. The reduction is untouched — the bf16 result is bit-identical to the fp32 result rounded: ``` bf16 store == round(fp32 store) True distinct values, bf16 / fp32 1958 / 16382 of 16384 max abs err vs fp64 bf16 9.800e-01 -> fp32 3.895e-03 (~250x) batch invariant for M in {1,2,4,5,16,17,64} exact ``` Expert-selection impact, holding the accumulator fixed and changing only the store, over `[4096, 7168] x [7168, 256]` with top-8 and an fp32 correction bias: | router logit std | tokens with a different expert set | |---|---| | 0.05 | 18 / 4096 | | 0.10 | 54 / 4096 | | 0.25 | 77 / 4096 | | 0.50 | 90 / 4096 | | 1.00 | 109 / 4096 | | 2.00 | 84 / 4096 | 0.4%–2.7% of tokens routed to a different expert set purely from the bf16 store. These are synthetic weights; a real DeepSeek-V3 comparison would be stronger and I do not have an 8xH200 to run it on. New tests in `test/registered/unit/batch_invariant_ops/test_matmul_out_dtype.py`, registered `base-b` / `1-gpu-large` rather than `1-gpu-small`: DeepGEMM is disabled on SM120, so only the H100 runner exercises the fp32 `bf16_gemm_nt` path. The file sets `_ENABLE_MM_COMPARISON_TEST`, and the operands satisfy the DeepGEMM gate, so CI diffs NT against Triton on every push. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not benchmarked. The GEMM is `[M, 7168] x [7168, 256]` and the kernel choice is unchanged on every backend, so the only cost is the wider store; the `.contiguous()` removal should be a small win on the deterministic path. ## Notes for reviewers Two things worth a closer look: 1. The `bf16_gemm_nt` fp32-out branch is reasoned from `gemm_nt_bf16bf16f32` and `_BF16F32WarmupExecutor`, not executed locally — no DeepGEMM on the hardware I have. The new test covers it on the first H100 CI run. 2. The `.contiguous()` removal in `_mm_dtype_compat` is the one change beyond the literal ask. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process). 2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers. 3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so. - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci` 4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32531503131](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32531503131)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32531503207](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32531503207)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32531503286](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32531503286)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: Avoid materializing GDN QKV tensors during target verification
signal.text: ## Summary This PR removes redundant Q/K/V materialization from compatible GDN speculative target-verification paths. `causal_conv1d_update` already produces packed QKV. Previously, every GDN layer launched `fused_qkv_split_gdn_prefill_kernel` to copy that output into three contiguous tensors before Triton target verification. Triton accepts explicit token strides, so it can consume zero-copy `torch.split`/`view` tensors instead. The optimization is route-aware: - Triton and ReplaySSM target verification use strided Q/K/V views. - Prefill, FlashInfer, CuTeDSL, and other routes requiring contiguous inputs retain materialization. - Model arithmetic, recurrent-state updates, speculative acceptance, logits, and sampling are unchanged. This eliminates one memory-copy kernel launch per GDN layer on every compatible target-verification pass. ## Profile evidence Matched H200 CPU/GPU traces using Qwen3.5-4B, ReplaySSM, and NEXTN T=3: | Target-verification metric | Baseline | Patch | Change | |---|---:|---:|---:| | QKV-split launches/pass | 24 | 0 | **-100%** | | QKV-split GPU time/pass | 56.946 us | 0 | **-56.946 us** | | CUDA-graph kernels | 452 | 428 | **-24** | | CUDA-graph span | 8,132.684 us | 8,040.898 us | **-91.786 us / -1.129%** | The graph-span reduction's approximate 95% interval was **79.732-103.841 us**. ## Standardized GSM8K benchmark 3 alternating baseline/QKV pairs ran on the same H200 with fresh servers, seed 0, empty prefix cache, and a 30-second cooldown. The benchmark used its defaults: 200 questions, five shots, 512 maximum output tokens, temperature 0, and parallelism 64. ### Pair 1 | Metric | Baseline | Patch | Change | |---|---:|---:|---:| | Output throughput | 6,433.642 tok/s | 6,762.467 tok/s | **+5.111%** | | Latency | 5.379 s | 5.145 s | **-4.350%** | | Engine TPOT | 9.7374 ms | 9.4735 ms | **-2.710%** | ### Pair 2 | Metric | Baseline | Patch | Change | |---|---:|---:|---:| | Output throughput | 6,202.258 tok/s | 6,366.221 tok/s | **+2.644%** | | Latency | 5.470 s | 5.401 s | **-1.261%** | | Engine TPOT | 10.2534 ms | 9.7761 ms | **-4.655%** | ### Pair 3 | Metric | Baseline | Patch | Change | |---|---:|---:|---:| | Output throughput | 6,496.073 tok/s | 6,669.102 tok/s | **+2.664%** | | Latency | 5.270 s | 5.134 s | **-2.581%** | | Engine TPOT | 9.3372 ms | 9.4393 ms | **+1.093%** | ### Three-pair aggregate | Metric | Baseline | Patch | Change | |---|---:|---:|---:| | Output throughput | 6,377.324 tok/s | 6,599.263 tok/s | **+3.480%** | | Latency | 5.373 s | 5.227 s | **-2.723%** | | Engine TPOT | 9.7760 ms | 9.5630 ms | **-2.179%** | | Accuracy | 87.667% | 87.500% | -0.167 pp | ## Reproduction Server: ```bash CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 \ PYTHONPATH=<sglang-source>/python \ sglang serve /path/Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B/ \ --port 30000 \ --dtype bfloat16 \ --language-only \ --limit-mm-data-per-request '{"image":0,"video":0,"audio":0}' \ --context-length 32768 \ --mem-fraction-static 0.8 \ --max-running-requests 64 \ --linear-attn-decode-backend triton \ --random-seed 0 \ --speculative-algorithm NEXTN \ --speculative-draft-model-path /path/Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B/ \ --speculative-num-steps 3 \ --speculative-eagle-topk 1 \ --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4 \ --enable-linear-replayssm-spec ``` Benchmark: ```bash python benchmark/gsm8k/bench_sglang.py \ --data-path /data/gsm8k/test.jsonl ``` Dataset SHA-256: ```text 3730d312f6e3440559ace48831e51066acaca737f6eabec99bccb9e4b3c39d14 ``` ## Validation - Exact target-verification output and recurrent-state parity. - ReplaySSM ring/fold parity and routing coverage. - Contiguous-input behavior retained for unsupported routes. - 31 affected H200 tests passed, covering 46 parameterized cases. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32532484205](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32532484205)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32532484040](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32532484040)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32532485372](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32532485372)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [Kimi K3] Rework skipped-think fix as opt-in force_nonempty_content with streaming coverage
signal.text: Stacked on top of #33995. Keeps @yhyang201's original commit `d11868d7d9` in history and supersedes it with a rework. ## Problem K3 sometimes closes its think channel before producing any answer (EOS inside think), so responses come back with `reasoning_content` but empty `content`. #33995 fixed the non-stream path by treating marker-less output as content, which has two leaks: - **Truncated reasoning becomes content**: a `max_tokens` cut also produces zero think markers, so truncated thinking gets misclassified as the answer. - **Streaming stays broken**: the branch only exists in `detect_and_parse`; `parse_streaming_increment` starts in `force_reasoning=True` and streams the raw payload as `reasoning_text`, so `stream=True` still returns `content=""`. ## What this PR does Reworks the fix as an opt-in, K3-native `force_nonempty_content`: - `KimiK3Detector.__init__` accepts `force_nonempty_content` so the existing `chat_template_kwargs` plumbing in `ReasoningParser` works (previously `TypeError`). - `detect_and_parse` reclassifies only on positive evidence: `RESPONSE_CLOSE` or `MESSAGE_CLOSE` present and zero think markers (full or partial). Bare marker-free text (truncated reasoning) stays reasoning. - Streaming **never holds chunks back**. A hold-back would starve SSE during long thinking runs (no delta until the channel decision) and trip client idle timeouts (observed: ~300 s client-side `terminated` while the server is still decoding). Instead, undecided prethink text streams as `reasoning_content` in real time, and `finish()` re-emits the cleaned payload as `content` once the response/message close proves skipped-think — mirroring the base class's `finish()` re-emit of accumulated reasoning. - The `finish()` re-emit is gated on `_in_reasoning`, i.e. it only fires when no channel decision ever happened mid-stream. Without the gate, answers that already streamed as `content` (`RESPONSE_OPEN` expressible, or `force_reasoning=False`) would be emitted a second time. - Under `stream_reasoning=False`, reasoning buffered past a mid-stream cut (e.g. `max_tokens`) still flushes: the non-fnc path delegates to the base `finish()`, and the fnc path flushes the buffer as `reasoning_text` itself, because the base implementation would reclassify it as `content` under fnc — the leak this flag exists to prevent. Clients therefore see: live `reasoning_content` while the model thinks → final `content` delta carrying the actual answer for skipped-think runs; long thinking runs stream uninterrupted end to end. No behavior change for `force_nonempty_content=False`; all existing K3 parser tests unchanged. ## Tests - `test_fnc_non_stream_skipped_think_vs_truncated_reasoning` — non-stream skipped-think vs truncated reasoning under `force_nonempty_content=True`. - `test_fnc_streaming_skipped_think_answer` — real-time reasoning deltas + finish() content re-emit, across chunk sizes 1/5/13. - `test_fnc_streaming_truncated_reasoning_stays_reasoning` — no close evidence → stays reasoning. - `test_fnc_streaming_long_think_streams_without_close` — 20k chars of marker-free thinking streams every chunk live; no hold-back. - `test_fnc_streaming_response_open_not_reemitted` / `test_fnc_streaming_force_reasoning_off_not_reemitted` — answer streams exactly once; the finish() re-emit never duplicates it. - `test_stream_reasoning_off_truncation_flushes_reasoning` — truncated reasoning flushes as reasoning, fnc on and off. - `test_fnc_stream_reasoning_off_skipped_think_reemits_content` — skipped-think re-emit still works when nothing streamed live. The duplication and flush-regression tests fail on the pre-gate code (verified by stashing the fix); everything passes after it. ``` $ pytest test/registered/unit/parser/test_kimik3_reasoning_parser.py test/registered/unit/parser/test_reasoning_parser.py 138 passed ``` ## Validation (BEAM 1M) Full [BEAM](https://github.com/MoonshotAI/Kimi-Vendor-Verifier/tree/main/beam) 1M run (700 long multi-turn questions near 1M context) on a 2-node 8×GB300 devbox, `moonshotai/Kimi-K3` TP8, `--default-chat-template-kwargs '{"force_nonempty_content": true}'`: | | empty content | overall (LLM-judged) | |---|---|---| | flag on (n=700) | **0.71%** (5/700) | 0.333 | | flag off (n=700) | **17.57%** (123/700) | 0.288 | - Empty-answer breakdown by failure mode: with the flag on, only **1/700 (0.14%)** is the skipped-think mode (finish=stop, empty content); the other 4 are finish=length at the 32k-token cap mid-reasoning, which no parser-side fix can address. With the flag off, **116/700 (16.6%)** are the skipped-think mode — the fix eliminates two orders of magnitude of them (16.6% → 0.14%). - A/B improvement is consistent across two independent judges (kimi-k3 self-judge +0.042, deepseek-v4-flash +0.045, full 700-question arms); the control arm's judged score (0.274/0.288 across judges) matches the externally reported 0.264 for this endpoint, so the eval setup lines up with theirs. Judge caveat: no official judge endpoint available, so absolute scores carry a judge-identity caveat; the empty-rate claim does not depend on the judge. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32437096484](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32437096484)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32437096359](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32437096359)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32437096508](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32437096508)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [sglang-miles] RDT/NIXL weight sync support for Ray scheduler actors
signal.text: ## What sglang-side support for **RDT (Ray Direct Transport / NIXL) weight sync** — lets the [miles](https://github.com/radixark/miles) trainer push RL weights to rollout engines via a zero-copy RDMA pull instead of NCCL broadcast. Paired with the miles-side PR (radixark/miles#1313), which has the perf write-up. ## Changes - **`ray/scheduler_actor.py`** — add `pull_weights()`, which uses `ray.experimental.set_target_for_ref` to RDMA pre-sharded weight buckets directly into the model's `param.data` buffers (no intermediate receive buffers / copies). - **`ray/engine.py` + `ray/data_parallel_controller.py`** — register `SchedulerActor`s as **detached** named actors with the http **port** baked into the name, so the trainer (a different Ray job) can discover them via `list_named_actors` even when several engines share a node; raise `max_concurrency` so a concurrent `pull_weights` is not starved while `run_event_loop` blocks; set `RAY_EXPERIMENTAL_NOSET_CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1` so the absolute GPU id from `get_accelerator_ids()` stays valid. - **`server_args.py`** — add `enable_engine_info_bootstrap` to start the engine-info bootstrap server and register per-rank parallelism config **without** the mooncake/verbs P2P transfer-engine seeding. - **`entrypoints/engine.py` + `model_executor/model_runner.py`** — honor `enable_engine_info_bootstrap`; make the P2P transfer-engine memory registration non-fatal so EFA/verbs clusters where it fails don't crash the scheduler (RDT only needs the parallelism config). - **`model_loader/loader.py`** — make `post_load_weights` public so the RDT path can invoke it. - **`pyproject.toml`** — require `ray>=2.55.1` (`ray.experimental.set_target_for_ref`). ## Notes Targeting the `sglang-miles` integration branch; rebased onto current `sglang-miles` (#28001, #29339). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32447564994](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32447564994)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32447564933](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32447564933)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:heavy_minus_sign: **No AMD PR run found for this commit**.<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [dLLM] Support DiffusionGemma serving
signal.text: ## Motivation The DiffusionGemma cookbook documents this model, but SGLang rejects it as unknown. This PR adds native text and image serving. It uses the shared dLLM and FDFO paths from [#27551](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/27551) and [#27877](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/27877). Fixes [#29904](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/29904) ## Changes - Add the DiffusionGemma model, image processor, weight loader, and Gemma4Renoise sampler - Run causal prompt prefill before each 256 token output block - Reuse request slots and KV cache across FDFO rounds - Add the required attention masks and TP1, TP2, and TP4 weight loading - Reject unsupported settings before model execution - Add focused model, scheduler, sampler, request, and CPU MoE tests ## Tests - 265 unit tests and 50 subtests passed - Full pre-commit passed on all 25 changed files - All 1,047 checkpoint tensors loaded at TP1, TP2, and TP4 - Real text and image serving passed on H200 - FDFO, synchronous decoding, long prompts, and exact output lengths passed - Unsupported request fields returned HTTP 400 before model execution ## Performance Four concurrent requests each generated 256 tokens with eight denoising rounds. Two warmups were discarded. Each result is the median of 15 trials. | Runtime | TP2 median | TP4 median | | --- | --- | --- | | SGLang | 0.621 s | 0.634 s | | vLLM 0.26.0 | 0.507 s | 0.496 s | These fixed work results check basic performance and do not claim a speed lead. ## Limits - Image requests require Triton on GPU - PP, CP, quantized loading, and untied embeddings are not supported - CUDA graphs, chunked prefill, and radix caching are disabled - This PR does not change MPS or DP placement ## Checklist - [x] Tests added and passing - [x] Pre-commit passing - [x] Accuracy and speed results included - [x] The existing cookbook already documents the launch command <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32530744663](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32530744663)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32530744539](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32530744539)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32530744541](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32530744541)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [RL, Spec] DFlash: top-p mask capture
signal.text: ## Relationship to existing work #27408 introduced sampling-mask output support. #35205 restored the finite-`top_k` requirement and bounded support packing for sampling masks. #33459 added the DFlash SpecV2 logprob path. This PR extends that machinery to the DFlash family, with worker-specific adapters for DFlash and DSpark, while preserving the finite-`top_k` contract from #35205. ## Motivation Sampling masks let RL trainers reconstruct the inference policy more accurately and reduce rollout/training policy mismatch. This change makes that metadata available when using DFlash or DSpark speculative decoding. ## Modifications - Add a shared speculative sampling-mask capture/output contract used by DFlash and DSpark. - Capture masks and selected-token logprobs from the final adjusted target policy, including grammar, penalties, logit bias, and custom logit processors. - Keep speculative acceptance logic method-specific. - Align metadata with committed `out_tokens` and `commit_lens`, letting the existing result-processing path trim it alongside generated tokens. - Support DSpark compact/ragged verification after logits are restored to strided layout. - Reconstruct target policy per row for mixed-greedy DSpark batches; greedy rows emit singleton masks with logprob 0. - Pack only finite top-k support before device-to-host transfer. - Reject sampling-mask requests with unbounded top-k, `min_p`, simulated acceptance, or unsupported speculative methods. - For DFlash, additionally require non-greedy verification support and exact acceptance thresholds, and prevent incompatible runtime threshold changes while mask requests are active. - Do not enable sampling-mask capture for EAGLE, NGRAM, or other speculative methods. ## Tests - Added DFlash end-to-end coverage in the existing DFlash suite. - Added one DSpark end-to-end test covering a mixed greedy/sampling batch. - Ran focused formatting, lint, compilation, and diff checks. ## Performance considerations Capture remains opt-in. Support is bounded by finite top-k and packed before device-to-host transfer. DSpark performs opt-in target-policy recomputation after verification, so mask capture adds additional probability reconstruction work; this does not affect requests that do not request masks. ## Accuracy Tests Targeted final implementation: - 4/4 DFlash sampling-mask unit tests passed in Modal: - tensor-backed deferred materialization; - filtered target probabilities and selected-token logprobs; - greedy singleton masks; - whole-request rejection on support overflow. - Added registered DFlash server coverage asserting: - seven generated tokens produce seven masks and seven logprobs; - every sampled token belongs to its corresponding support. - Full Qwen3.6 NVFP4+DFlash B200 run: - 98,304 measured output tokens; - 49,152 requested masks returned, with no missing masks; - maximum observed top-p support was 5,306; a repeat reached 7,476; - completed without generation or mask-alignment errors. This feature only returns metadata and is not intended to change sampling decisions, so no downstream task-accuracy benchmark was run. ## Speed Tests and Profiling One B200 with: - nvidia/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-NVFP4; - modal-labs/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-DFlash; - DFlash block size 8, FA4 draft attention; - 32 concurrent requests, 512 generated tokens each; - warmup followed by six alternating mask/no-mask rounds. Results: - Without masks: 4,163.78 tok/s median - With masks: 4,160.45 tok/s median - Ratio: 0.9992, or approximately −0.08% The difference was within run-to-run noise. A complete repeat also showed no slowdown. ## Checklist - [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. signal.title: fix(test): stabilize nightly precision regression
signal.text: ## Root cause [`test_nightly_precision_regression`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31501558607/job/94072436800) failed for `zai-org/GLM-5.2-FP8` with TP=8 for two independent harness reasons: 1. The test skipped the remote restore when a self-hosted runner already had `.pt` files under `/tmp/sglang_precision_baselines`. A stale baseline captured replicated layer-entry tensors after FlashInfer fusion failed to initialize, while the target contained TP-partial tensors. Treating both as partial produced the approximately 8x mismatch. The historical initialization failure is tracked by [FlashInfer #3676](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/issues/3676) and [SGLang #30875](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/30875), and was mitigated by [SGLang #30580](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/30580). 2. After a clean fused refresh, the comparator still observed rank-local BF16 buffers before fused all-reduce and residual RMSNorm. CPU-side reduction of those buffers is not the kernel's semantic output and drifted across runners. Current H200 runs initialize TRTLLM fusion on all eight ranks. This PR keeps fusion enabled and moves the comparison to `self_attn.inputs.hidden_states`, the replicated value consumed by attention after `prepare_attn()`. ## Fix - Always restore a signature-compatible remote baseline, atomically replace local tensors, and include the capture filters, TP size, and fusion backend in the signature. - Compare only the replicated post-fusion attention input. Keep layer-entry captures only as a per-layer/step/rank guard that rejects fusion fallback. - Make ordinary `/rerun-test` read-only. Add a maintainer-only, in-repo H200 refresh path: `/rerun-test --refresh-precision-baseline test/registered/debug_utils/test_nightly_precision_regression.py`. Serving runtime and all-reduce implementation code are unchanged. ## Verification - [Cross-runner Nightly comparator](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31862539092): passed all 33 post-fusion records with `max_rel_diff=0.0`. - [Cleanup-head baseline refresh](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31893911079): fusion initialized on all eight ranks and the guarded refresh passed. - [Cleanup-head read-only comparator](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31894139007): restored the refreshed baseline, passed a non-empty comparison, and did not publish. - All 42 baseline-store unit tests and changed-file pre-commit checks passed. ## Accuracy Tests No model-forward changes. The registered 8-GPU H200 test exercises the actual fused path. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not applicable; serving performance is unchanged. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32528141728](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32528141728)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32528141490](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32528141490)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32528141589](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32528141589)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [LoRA] Add the sgl_lora MoE execution engine with JSON config resolution
signal.text: ## Motivation MoE (expert-weight) LoRA serving in SGLang currently runs through the experimental TRT-LLM path (`--moe-runner-backend experimental_sgl_trtllm` + virtual experts). That path has structural limits: - **Blackwell-only**: the trtllm-gen kernels require SM100/120, so there is no expert-LoRA path at all on Hopper (H200). - **Virtual-expert routing scales with `max_loras_per_batch × num_experts`**, so multi-adapter serving degrades sharply as slot capacity grows. - **No prefill CUDA graphs with LoRA**, and no support for shared-outer adapter factors (gate_up A / down B shared across experts, `expert_dim=1` — the native format of some recent MoE adapters). This PR adds `sgl_lora`: a self-contained MoE-LoRA execution engine selected with `--lora-execution-engine sgl_lora`, built from an exhaustive kernel/fusion/overlap sweep on GB300, B200, and H200 across three models (Qwen3.5-35B-A3B, Qwen3.5-397B, Inkling-Small; per-expert and shared-outer adapters, ranks 8–64). ## Modifications - **Engine** (`python/sglang/srt/lora/sgl_lora/`): masked expert-major decode path and route-major serial prefill path; per-expert and shared-outer factor layouts; two base-GEMM providers (DeepGEMM, CuTeDSL); side-stream overlap windows for the shared-decode path; capacity-flat routing (cost scales with *active* adapters, not slot capacity). - **JSON config resolution** (`sgl_lora/configs/{gb300,h200,default}.json`): every kernel-family/fusion/overlap/tile decision is data, resolved per (layout, activation, phase, batch shape) through ordered first-match scenario rows with fail-closed validation — a malformed row, unknown plan field, or unknown predicate key aborts startup instead of serving a wrong plan. `SGLANG_SGL_LORA_CONFIG_DIR` points at an override config root (arch JSONs at top level, M-bucketed base-GEMM tile tables under `gemm/`). Every shipped row carries real-model sweep provenance; unknown architectures fall to a conservative serial fallback (`default.json`). - **Prefill CUDA graphs with MoE LoRA** (breakable backend), including graph-stable LoRA workspaces. - **Dense-module gate**: adapter targets are pruned to weight-backed modules at registration, and per-module effective ranks let mixed multi-adapter batches skip dense-LoRA work for adapters that carry no weights for a module (the shared dense kernels in `kernels/ops/gemm` stay byte-identical to upstream — the gate enters as a batch-info view). - **Onboarding tuner** (`benchmark/kernels/lora_moe/tune_lora_config.py`): `--check` (CI-gateable coverage report), `--emit-seed` (serve a new geometry immediately), `--sweep` (e2e-tunes the two geometry-sensitive axes; writes winners back into the seed). - Guards: expert LoRA + DP-attention / elastic-EP / EPLB fail closed at startup (the DP-attention token-axis limitation exists silently in the legacy path today). Scope: bf16 serving path. fp8/nvfp4 qlora support is planned as a follow-up in this PR (the tuner carries a `TODO(quant)` and the config resolver already fails closed on future `quant` predicate keys). Structure note: the first commit is the engine; subsequent commits are review-round changes and will be squashed before undrafting. Two orthogonal fixes found during this work ship separately: `fix/chunked-sgmv-cache-key` (csgmv compile-cache key omits codegen parameters) and `fix/swa-kvpool-v-head-dim` (SWAKVPool lacks `get_v_head_dim`, crashing hybrid-SWA models on the triton attention backend). ## Accuracy Tests - `test/registered/unit/lora/`: 248 passed / 6 skipped (H200), including config-resolution pins, kernel numerics vs an fp32 oracle, byte-identity pins for the decode kernel policy, and prefill graph-vs-eager bit-exactness. - Greedy-decode correctness on real adapters vs the legacy triton reference: per-token logprob deltas at the measured bf16 noise floor (per-expert and shared-outer, all three campaign models). ## Speed Tests and Profiling Protocol: `bench_one_batch_server`, input 4096 / output 1024, bs 1/8/16/32, `max_loras_per_batch=4` distinct adapters, medians after first-pass discard. Baseline = experimental TRT-LLM LoRA path at its best posture (incl. prefill graphs where it can use them). - **Qwen3.5-35B (GB300, TP4)**: prefill +15–19%, decode parity. - **Qwen3.5-397B (B200, TP8)**: prefill +23%, decode −1.2%…+4.5% across bs. - **Inkling-Small (GB300)**: decode +0.5%…+11.9% with the model's shared/routed-expert parallelism active on both engines; prefill +2–5%. - **H200 (fa4 posture)**: the TRT engine cannot run (SM100/120-only kernels); vs the only runnable incumbent (legacy virtual experts on triton fused_moe): decode +1.7%…+19.7%, prefill +1.0–1.5% at bs≥8 (−13% at bs1). - **Prefill CUDA graphs**: 2.5–3.0× prefill throughput vs eager at equal chunking (the incumbent disables prefill graphs under LoRA). - **Multi-adapter**: routing cost is capacity-flat; with 4 distinct adapters/ranks resident, +15–24% prefill and +2–17% decode vs the incumbent. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: **Missing `run-ci` label** -- add it to run CI tests.<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: **Blocked** -- `run-ci` is required first.<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:heavy_minus_sign: **No AMD PR run found for this commit**.<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->
