signal.title: [Spec][LoRA] Support multi-adapter LoRA with EAGLE/NEXTN/DFLASH/DSPARK speculative decoding
signal.text: ## Motivation #12903 enabled LoRA with NGRAM speculative decoding. This extends it to **EAGLE / NEXTN / EAGLE3, DFLASH and DSPARK with multiple adapters co-batched**, one of the LoRA items in #11762. Adapters apply to the target model only; one shared draft runs unadapted. Speculation stays lossless per adapter (verify samples from the adapted target), so only the accept rate is affected. Supersedes #28395, which strips LoRA from a per-draft `ServerArgs` copy — a mechanism that no longer exists now that per-runner values are constructor arguments. Thanks to @tengxiaoliu for the original approach and the MoE target-verify fix this builds on. ## Modifications **Draft runner is unadapted.** Every worker gets the same published `ServerArgs`, so `enable_lora` is `True` for the draft too; the exclusion is keyed on `is_draft_worker` in `maybe_init_lora_manager`. Otherwise the draft loads the target's adapters into a model with a different layer count and startup fails. `ModelRunner.lora_manager` is now always present (`None` when unset) and every LoRA path keys off it rather than the config, so a draft runner skips them by construction. **`TARGET_VERIFY` token counts.** It reports `is_extend()` but leaves `extend_seq_lens(_cpu)` as `None`, breaking three call sites: | Path | Failure | |---|---| | triton eager segments | `max(None)` (hit whenever `bs > max_bs_in_cuda_graph`) | | MoE `_add_moe_lora_info` | `sum(None)` | | csgmv `_determine_chunk_size` | `None` comparison, with `--max-lora-chunk-size > 16` | New `get_batch_token_counts` holds the forward-mode dispatch in one place; all three route through it. The triton graph path now asserts the verify width matches the captured `seg_lens` width instead of silently mis-segmenting adapters — that backend bakes `seg_lens` at capture time and never refreshes it, so a differing width would map adapters onto the wrong token rows. **MoE LoRA cuda-graph buffers** were sized in requests while verify capture feeds `bs * draft_token_num` tokens; the per-token buffers are now sized by verify width. This was also undersized for NGRAM + MoE LoRA. **Shared lm_head.** An MTP draft implementing `set_lm_head_from_target` shares the target's lm_head *module*; if LoRA-wrapped, draft forwards apply the target's deltas against batch metadata of a different shape. The draft now gets the unwrapped base layer, so lm_head adapters cost accept rate rather than correctness. Adapters carrying embedding weights warn as they load; rejecting them would rule out every MTP-capable base, whose public adapters all ship `unembed_tokens` under an `all-linear` config. **Validation.** The NGRAM-only rejection becomes `_check_lora_speculative_compatibility`: multi-adapter EAGLE/NEXTN/EAGLE3, DFLASH and DSPARK allowed on either kernel backend, rejecting `--speculative-adaptive` (the draft reads a static speculative config), the `experimental_sgl_trtllm` MoE runner (its TopK reads the LoRA config per forward), and `SGLANG_ENABLE_OVERLAP_PLAN_STREAM` (LoRA batch prep would run on the plan stream, unordered against in-flight forwards). ## Accuracy Tests Unit tests cover the argument matrix, the draft-runner gate, the `TARGET_VERIFY` segment math, and the embedding warning (`base-a-test-cpu`, plus one `1-gpu-small` file). The e2e test (`base-b-test-1-gpu-large`) asserts serving properties rather than output text, since greedy decoding is not bitwise reproducible across batch shapes here. Losslessness is verified out of band by `test/manual/lora/run_spec_lora_matrix.py`, comparing spec-on vs spec-off **per adapter** across solo, mixed-adapter, and wider-than-cuda-graph batches, after measuring the reproducibility floor so model nondeterminism is not read as failure. | Config | Result | |---|---| | NEXTN Qwen3.5-35B-A3B, `triton` | **PASS** — every reproducible pair matched | | NEXTN Qwen3.5-35B-A3B, `csgmv` | **PASS** — every reproducible pair matched | | DFLASH Llama-3.1-8B, `triton` | **PASS** — 0 comparisons skipped | | DFLASH Llama-3.1-8B, `csgmv` | **PASS** — 0 comparisons skipped | | DSPARK Inkling-Small (TP8) | **PASS** — 9 of 36 comparisons made | DFLASH is the strongest signal: Llama-3.1-8B is fully reproducible, so every comparison was made and matched on both kernel backends, with two adapters differing in rank (64 / 8) and module set. DSPARK is the weakest — Inkling-Small is nondeterministic on 9 of 12 (route, prompt) pairs — but it is the only leg exercising an adapter that wraps the target's lm_head. Adapter identity inside one verify batch was also checked directly, which text equality cannot do on a nondeterministic model: with three adapters whose trained behavior is to prefix every output word with their own name, one batch carrying base plus all three returned **16/16 requests wearing their own prefix and no foreign one**. Crossed verify segments would be plainly visible. Accept length is unchanged by that co-batching (≤0.6 SE against the same routes measured alone). Two bugs these runs caught that no unit test reached: a config-vs-manager gate crashing the spec server on every TP rank once `enable_lora` reads True on the draft, and drafts taking the target's lm_head / embed_tokens *module* then dereferencing base-layer attributes the LoRA wrapper does not forward. The second is why unwrapping happens at every acquisition point. Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507 + EAGLE3 was also run; its one divergent prompt diverges identically with **zero adapters loaded**, so it belongs to that model's topk>1 tree-verify path. `test/manual/lora/check_spec_baseline_divergence.py` is the control. ## Accept length Every route measured at the same decode depth (20-token cap, a shared prompt set, natural sampling), so no arm is averaged over a different number of verify steps. Each row is self-contained — the spec config differs per algorithm, so only base vs adapters within a row is comparable. With the public adapters each config already uses, 96 prompts per route (mean ± standard error; per-prompt spread is 0.23-1.09, so 16 prompts could not separate these): | Config | base | adapters | vs base | |---|---|---|---| | NEXTN Qwen3.5-35B-A3B (TP4) | 3.097 ± 0.034 | 3.208 ± 0.024 | +3.6%, t=2.7 | | DFLASH Llama-3.1-8B | 2.793 ± 0.061 | 2.708 ± 0.067, 2.669 ± 0.069 | −3.1% / −4.5%, t≤1.4 | | DSPARK Inkling-Small (TP8) | 2.919 ± 0.123 | 2.878 ± 0.119, 2.663 ± 0.097 | −1.4% / −8.8%, t≤1.6 | Only NEXTN separates from base at all, and it goes slightly *up*. DFLASH and DSPARK show nothing distinguishable, including between their two adapters (t=0.4 and t=1.4). So serving these adapters costs no meaningful accept length — none of them moves the output distribution much. That is the whole reason, and it does not generalize. Repeating it on Qwen3.5-35B-A3B (TP4, 4 draft tokens) with three private adapters that force a heavy shift — each prefixes every output word — at mixed rank, one carrying per-expert MoE and lm_head weights (n=16; every gap below is ≥3.9 SE): | route | NEXTN | DFLASH | EAGLE3 | |---|---|---|---| | base | **3.085** | 2.479 | 2.166 | | A (r16) | 2.468 (−20.0%) | 1.635 (−34.0%) | 1.231 (−43.2%) | | B (r32) | 2.507 (−18.7%) | 1.628 (−34.3%) | 1.289 (−40.5%) | | C (r32, +lm_head, MoE) | 2.132 (−30.9%) | 1.636 (−34.0%) | 1.285 (−40.7%) | First-draft-token acceptance, measured exactly by running a one-token draft chain so accept length minus 1 is the probability: | route | NEXTN | DFLASH | EAGLE3 | |---|---|---|---| | base | **0.921** | 0.705 | 0.611 | | A | 0.760 | 0.487 | 0.219 | | B | 0.826 | 0.473 | 0.257 | | C | 0.732 | 0.488 | 0.227 | So the shared-draft design costs accept rate in proportion to how far an adapter moves the output distribution, and self-drafting tolerates it best: NEXTN's own MTP layers lose 19-31%, while separately trained heads lose ~34% (DFLASH) and ~41% (EAGLE3) and give up most of it at the first proposal. Correctness is unaffected in every case — verify still samples from the adapted target. EAGLE3 numbers here are indicative only: they need a local fix to `set_eagle3_layers_to_capture` on this model (unrelated to LoRA, to be filed separately) and were run at `topk=1` for comparability rather than EAGLE3's usual tree verify. ## Benchmarking and Profiling 256 requests x 512 in / 128 out, adapters round-robin, Qwen3.5-35B-A3B + NEXTN, TP4 on 4xGB300. Output tok/s: | concurrency | base, no spec | base + spec | LoRA, no spec | **LoRA + spec** | |---|---|---|---|---| | 1 | 290.8 | 552.2 | 154.4 | **327.3** | | 8 | 1865.4 | 1985.9 | 942.5 | **758.0** | | 32 | 5788.8 | 4011.7 | 2975.4 | **1419.7** | Speculation with adapters gives 2.12x at c=1, falling below 1x by c=32 where speculation loses with or without LoRA. Serving adapters costs ~2-3x throughput independently of speculation. Two follow-ups found while testing, both **general LoRA issues rather than speculative-decoding ones**, so deliberately not gated here: LoRA + `--enable-two-batch-overlap` (TBO children are built by `filter_batch`, which slices `lora_ids` but never rebuilds the LoRA batch info) and LoRA + `--enable-lora-overlap-loading` (an adapter was observed silently not applied while a sibling applied correctly; reproduces with speculation off). ## Checklist - [x] Format code with pre-commit - [x] Add unit tests - [x] Provide accuracy and speed results <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:no_entry_sign: [Run #32329478822](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32329478822)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32329478643](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32329478643)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32329478825](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32329478825)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: Fix nullable GLM tool argument parsing
signal.text: ## Motivation The GLM-4.7/GLM-5 tool-call parser infers a schema type such as `["string", "null"]` as the primary type `string`. As a result, a model-emitted JSON `null` can be serialized as a string instead of remaining null. | Argument schema | Model output | Before | After | |---|---|---|---| | `{"type": ["string", "null"]}` | `null` | String (`"None"` complete, `"null"` streaming) | JSON `null` | | `{"type": ["string", "null"]}` | `value` | `"value"` | `"value"` | | `{"type": "string"}` | `null` | `"None"` complete, `"null"` streaming | `"null"` | ## Modifications - Preserve an unquoted `null` when the argument's JSON Schema explicitly permits it. - Delay serialization of nullable string values until the complete streaming value distinguishes JSON null from ordinary text. - Share argument-schema lookup between type inference and nullability checks. - Add registered CPU regression coverage for complete and fragmented incremental parsing. ## Accuracy Tests Not applicable; this changes tool-argument parsing rather than model generation. The registered CPU test covers nullable null, nullable string, and non-nullable literal-null behavior in complete and incremental parsing. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not applicable; this does not change model inference. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. signal.title: [OpenAI] Drop empty assistant turns for mistral_common tokenizers
signal.text: A chat request containing an assistant message with empty content fails on Mistral models but works on every other model. mistral_common validates conversation structure and rejects the turn, so the request is refused; DeepSeek and other Jinja templates simply ignore it. Since the turn carries no information, this is an OpenAI-compatibility gap rather than a malformed request. `patch_mistral_common_tokenizer` now drops assistant turns that have neither content nor tool calls before handing the conversation to mistral_common. Turns with `tool_calls`, multimodal content, or real text are untouched, and a trailing assistant message is already consumed upstream as the `continue_final_message` prefix, so this cannot swallow a prefill. Reproduced and verified on one devbox with a Mistral model served from a local directory (so the tokenizer resolves to `MistralCommonBackend`), using the reported payload — `user` / `assistant("")` / `user`: - before #35215: HTTP 500 `Internal server error: Invalid assistant message` - with #35215: HTTP 400 `BadRequest` — honest, but still refused - with this change: HTTP 200 and a normal completion Normal multi-turn chat is unaffected. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32527397164](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32527397164)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32527396874](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32527396874)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32527397117](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32527397117)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->
signal.author: alisonshao

signal.title: [kernel] Split the custom all-reduce communicator into push/pull planes
signal.text: > Generated by Claude. ## Motivation Every JIT collective in `csrc/distributed` and `csrc/kimi_k3/comm` took one flat `CommunicatorObj` that carried every buffer any of them might want: `2 * world_size` push slots, a pull workspace, per-block semaphores, a rank-local counter, and one of the three multicast addresses. Consequences: - The other two multicast addresses travelled out of band. `ws_mc_base` was an `int64_t` argument repeated at five call sites, always the same constant; `pull_sem_mc_ptr` went through a per-world-size Python dict populated by `register_comm()`, duplicated in three modules. - A push-only owner (the fused qk-norm instances in `minimax_m2`) had to allocate a placeholder 1 KB pull buffer plus one semaphore purely to satisfy the constructor. - Only `custom_all_reduce.cuh` ever read `pull_workspaces` / `pull_bytes` / `pull_mc_workspace`. The K3 pull kernels reduce in place on the caller's own symmetric input and borrow the plane just to barrier on, so half the object was dead weight for most callers. - `custom_all_reduce.cuh` defined helpers at `namespace sglang` scope and was `#include`d by three K3 files across directories, so renaming anything inside it silently broke downstream kernels. ## What changed Split the object by lifetime rather than by direction: | | contents | |---|---| | `sgl.distributed.PushPlane` | zero-filled symmetric push slots, rank-local phase counter, multicast base | | `sgl.distributed.PullPlane` | symmetric pull buffers + per-block semaphores, both multicast bases. Either half may be a 0-element tensor | | `sgl.distributed.Communicator` | the two planes (either optional) + the pull launch widths; what every kernel takes | Both *fixed* multicast addresses now live on the planes. That deletes the `ws_mc_base` parameter from five entry points and the `_PULL_SEM_MC_MAP` registry from three modules. The *per-call* multicast address — a slice of the caller's own symmetric buffer, so it changes every call — stays a plain `intptr_t`, which is what it should be. `PullPlane`'s optional halves replace the placeholder-buffer trick: `minimax_m2` now constructs `Communicator(push=..., pull=None)` and a kernel that needs a missing plane fails with a message instead of reading a dummy buffer. ### Shared vocabulary moved under `include/` - **`include/sgl_kernel/distributed/ptx.cuh`** collects the inline PTX the collectives share into `sglang::device::ptx`, which `mbarrier.cuh` and the two K3 files reopen. Removed: three identical copies of the multimem flag increment, three copies of the "multicast alias of a semaphore's flag" helper (now `Semaphore::mc_flag`), and the 16B access helpers that were defined at `namespace sglang` scope inside `custom_all_reduce.cuh`. `csrc/kimi_k3/comm/ptx_sys.cuh` is deleted. The five communication kernels now contain zero inline PTX. - **`Barrier` / `McBarrier`** (unicast fan-out and one-`multimem.red` variants of the same window protocol) and **`LamportTrait`** (the pos-zero marker) live next to the planes, so each protocol has one implementation instead of one per kernel. - The three `csrc` → `csrc` includes of `custom_all_reduce.cuh` are gone. What they actually used — `reduce_vec`, the marker traits — moved under `include/`. - `alloc_workspace_tensor` moved to `host::ffi`, so `utils.cuh` no longer depends on `ffi.h`. `tp_qknorm`'s 8B `ld.volatile` / `st.volatile` pair became `ld_relaxed_8B` / `st_relaxed_8B` at `.sys` scope (PTX defines volatile as relaxed at system scope, and the store is cross-GPU). Load scope measured identical at `.gpu`, so the `.gpu` load variant was dropped and the vocabulary has one scope. ## Verification (8×B200, SM100) **Correctness — 291 tests, all passing** | test | | |---|---| | `test_custom_all_reduce.py` (8 GPU) | 180 passed | | `test_ar_fusion.py` (8 GPU) | 58 passed | | `test_tp_qknorm.py` (8 GPU) | 42 passed | | `test_collectives.py` (8 GPU) | 5 passed | | `test_compute.py` | 6 passed | | `test_custom_all_reduce_v2_capability.py` | 4 passed | | `test_attn_residual.py` | 1 passed | All 11 affected JIT modules build; `fp8_blockwise_scaled_mm_sm120` verified with a direct SM120 nvcc compile. clangd reports zero diagnostics on every touched file except two pre-existing cutlass include-path gaps in `.clangd`. **Registers / spills** — `cuobjdump -res-usage`, this branch vs the merge base, kernels paired by hand where the refactor renamed them: - **No spills anywhere** (`STACK=0`, `LOCAL=0` for every kernel). - Unchanged or better everywhere except `1shot_push`: bf16 60→63, fp16 61→63, fp32 56→58. That kernel is 2.7–6.2 % *faster* — `LamportTrait`'s 4-byte-atom marker test replaces a per-bf16-half test, cutting its SASS from 512 to 344 instructions. - `2shot_pull` eager improves (bf16 53→51) and the multicast variants drop one register. **Performance** — kernel time only, measured by replaying a CUDA graph of 20 chained calls so host dispatch is excluded; three interleaved rounds per arm, per-arm spread under 1 %: | variant | delta vs merge base | |---|---| | `1shot_push` / eager (dispatched ≤ 768 KB) | **−2.7 % … −6.2 %** | | `2shot_pull` / multicast (dispatched > 768 KB) | −0.03 % … +0.39 % | | `1shot_pull` eager and multicast | −1.1 % … +0.6 % | | `2shot_pull` / eager | +0.5 % … +0.9 % | 33 points: median +0.32 %, worst +0.92 %. On the path the tuned SM100/world-8 config actually dispatches: median **−3.30 %**, worst +0.39 %. One note on how that number was reached. An earlier revision of this branch regressed `2shot_pull` eager by 7–18 %. Bisecting with self-contained reference kernels showed the params layout, the `Barrier` object and the `Impl` abstraction were all innocent — an exact transplant of the old body still regressed. The cause was the address form: folding the shard offset into the eight base pointers as a typed 32-bit vector index keeps the peer table on the uniform datapath (`UIMAD.WIDE` off a constant-bank base), whereas biasing `vid` per access, or using a 64-bit byte offset, makes all eight addresses thread-varying and costs ~12 registers per thread. Also, binding a params array address to a named local that stays live across the kernel breaks the same proof. Both are noted in comments at the point of use, since either one silently costs ~10 %. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32484511620](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32484511620)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32510836380](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32510836380)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32484511571](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32484511571)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [Runtime] Don't override CUDA_MODULE_LOADING
signal.text: ## Motivation `_set_envs_and_config()` currently assigns `CUDA_MODULE_LOADING=AUTO` before launching workers. This silently replaces a deployment's explicit `DEFAULT`, `EAGER`, or `LAZY` choice with an undocumented value whose behavior is not part of NVIDIA's compatibility contract. SGLang has no corresponding CLI option or runtime invariant that requires overriding this CUDA control plane. This matters when a deployment intentionally uses eager loading to move first-use module initialization out of the request path, accepting additional startup time and memory for more predictable request latency. Today that setting is overwritten before local multiprocessing scheduler workers are spawned. ## NVIDIA CUDA contract The NVIDIA CUDA Programming Guide documents [`CUDA_MODULE_LOADING`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-programming-guide/05-appendices/environment-variables.html#cuda-module-loading) with these possible values: > `DEFAULT`: Default behavior, equivalent to `LAZY`. > `LAZY`: The loading of specific kernels is delayed until a CUDA function handle ... is extracted. > `EAGER`: Fully loads CUDA modules and kernels at program initialization. `AUTO` is not a documented value. NVIDIA's [Lazy Loading guide](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-programming-guide/04-special-topics/lazy-loading.html) states: > As of CUDA 12.3 lazy loading is enabled by default on all platforms, but can be controlled via the `CUDA_MODULE_LOADING` environment variable. Its change history also records the version boundary: lazy loading was introduced but disabled by default in CUDA 11.7, became the Linux default in CUDA 12.2, and became the Windows default in CUDA 12.3. Therefore, an unset variable follows the installed CUDA/PyTorch stack rather than a version-independent SGLang policy. ## Change Don't assign `CUDA_MODULE_LOADING` in `_set_envs_and_config()`. - User-provided `DEFAULT`, `EAGER`, or `LAZY` values are no longer overwritten before local multiprocessing workers are spawned. - When the variable is absent, module-loading behavior is left to the installed CUDA/PyTorch stack. Current published Linux CUDA 12.9 and CUDA 13.0 images default to lazy loading; older or custom environments may differ. - Ray deployments should provide this variable through the cluster or job runtime environment when deterministic propagation to remote actors is required. - This PR does not add an SGLang CLI flag or change `CUDA_DEVICE_MAX_CONNECTIONS`. ## Validation - `pre-commit run --files python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/engine.py` - `git diff --check` - On a CUDA 13 environment, `cuModuleGetLoadingMode()` reported `LAZY` for unset, `DEFAULT`, `LAZY`, `AUTO`, and an arbitrary unknown value, and `EAGER` for `EAGER`. The `AUTO` result is an observation for that environment, not a documented compatibility guarantee. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32469777290](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32469777290)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32469777211](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32469777211)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32469777364](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32469777364)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: fix(mem_cache): emit BlockRemoved on session radix cache release
signal.text: ## Problem `RadixCache.release_radix_session` (the path that runs when a session is closed under `--enable-session-radix-cache`) frees KV blocks and deletes radix leaves, but — unlike the regular eviction path — it never emits `BlockRemoved` events. The regular `evict` path emits one `BlockRemoved` per freed node: ```python # python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/radix_cache.py, RadixCache.evict self.token_to_kv_pool_allocator.free(x.value) ... self._delete_leaf(x) ... self._record_remove_event(x) # <-- emits BlockRemoved ``` but `release_radix_session` only did the `free` + `_delete_leaf`, skipping the event: ```python # python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/session_radix_cache.py parent = node.parent self.token_to_kv_pool_allocator.free(node.value) self._delete_leaf(node) # (no _record_remove_event — BlockRemoved never emitted) freed += 1 ``` As a result, KV-aware routers consuming the event queue (e.g. dynamo) keep stale entries for blocks that a session release has already freed, so they may route future requests to freed/invalid KV. ## Fix Mirror the eviction path: call `self._record_remove_event(node)` for each freed node. `_record_remove_event` is a no-op when `enable_kv_cache_events` is false (guarded inside `KVCacheEventMixin`), so configurations that don't enable KV cache events are completely unaffected. Only `RadixCache` (and its subclass `HiRadixCache`) use `SessionRadixCacheMixin`, and both already inherit `KVCacheEventMixin`, so the call is always available. ## Tests New registered CPU unit test `test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_session_radix_blockremoved_event.py` (no server, no GPU): - `test_release_emits_blockremoved_for_freed_node` — single-session release emits one `BlockRemoved` per freed node. - `test_shared_prefix_emits_only_for_unique_tail` — two sessions sharing a prefix; releasing one emits a `BlockRemoved` only for the freed tail, the shared prefix (still held) is untouched. - `test_release_with_last_holder_frees_shared_leaf` — same content held by two sessions is freed (and emits) only on the last close. - `test_events_disabled_release_is_noop_for_queue` — with `enable_kv_cache_events=False`, release still works and the queue stays empty. All 4 tests fail on `main` (no `BlockRemoved` emitted) and pass with this fix. The existing `test/manual/core/test_session_radix_cache.py` (8 tests, asserts the freeing/shared-prefix/last-holder semantics) still passes — the fix adds event emission without changing what gets freed. ## Checklist - [x] Code is tested with CPU unit tests (no GPU required) - [x] `black`, `isort`, `codespell`, `ruff (F401/F821/UP037)` clean - [x] No behavioral change to what `release_radix_session` frees — only adds the previously-missing event <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: **Missing `run-ci` label** -- add it to run CI tests.<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: **Blocked** -- `run-ci` is required first.<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:heavy_minus_sign: **No AMD PR run found for this commit**.<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: fix(disagg): PD transfer-failure injection was silently inert
signal.text: ## Motivation PD transfer-failure injection has been silently inert. `_get_failure_prob()` in `python/sglang/srt/disaggregation/utils.py` guarded the canonical env read with a `try/except` and fell back to a legacy `DISAGGREGATION_TEST_FAILURE_PROB` name: ```python def _get_failure_prob() -> float: try: return float(envs.SGLANG_TEST_DISAGG_FAILURE_PROB.get()) except Exception: # fallback to legacy env var return float(os.getenv("DISAGGREGATION_TEST_FAILURE_PROB", "0")) ``` But `EnvField.get()` never raises. An unset variable returns the default (`0.0`), and even an unparseable value only warns and returns the default. So the `except` branch is unreachable and the legacy name was ignored outright — with `DISAGGREGATION_TEST_FAILURE_PROB=0.05` set, `_get_failure_prob()` returns `0.0`. Two registered CI tests set exactly that variable to exercise PD transfer-failure recovery, so **both have been running with zero failure injection and their retry-path assertions have been passing vacuously**: - `test/registered/disaggregation/test_disaggregation_basic.py` - `test/registered/amd/disaggregation/test_disaggregation_basic.py` ## Modifications 4 files, +13 / -17. `environ.py` is deliberately untouched. - Both failure tests now set the canonical `SGLANG_TEST_DISAGG_FAILURE_PROB` via `envs.<...>.override()` instead of mutating `os.environ`, per the env-var conventions. The override is entered before the servers launch so the subprocesses inherit it. - The legacy name is **dropped**, not preserved behind a deprecation alias. It is a test-only knob and it has never functioned, so nothing that works today can regress: no in-repo caller sets it after this change, and any out-of-tree user setting it was already silently getting `0.0`. - Dropping it removes the dead `try/except`, which leaves `_get_failure_prob` as a one-line wrapper over a descriptor read — so it is inlined into its single caller and deleted. `utils.py` loses its last use of `os` as a result. - Also drops the matching legacy `os.environ.pop` from the nixl test's defensive clear, which would otherwise be a no-op naming a variable the codebase no longer honors. After this change `DISAGGREGATION_TEST_FAILURE_PROB` appears nowhere in the repo. ## Accuracy Tests Not applicable — no model output, kernel, or forward path is touched. The affected code is a test-only failure-injection knob. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not applicable. The read gets marginally cheaper: one descriptor access inline, instead of a function call wrapping a `try/except` around the same access. ## Verification performed **The bug was reproduced against this PR's base commit.** With `DISAGGREGATION_TEST_FAILURE_PROB=0.05` and the pre-change `_get_failure_prob()`, the result is `0.0`. **The fix was then verified end-to-end** by executing the post-change `_poll_with_failure_injection` against 4000 pollers: | Case | Result | |---|---| | no env set | no injection | | legacy name set | no injection — unchanged, it was already broken | | `override(0.05)` (what the tests now do) | **4.78% injection** (191/4000) | | after the override context exits | injection stops | The third row is the one that matters: it confirms the tests' new idiom actually reaches the injection path and produces the intended ~5% failure rate, which is precisely what was not happening before. The second row confirms removing the legacy name changes nothing for anyone — it was a no-op before and is a no-op now. Also: pinned `ruff 0.15.1 --select=F401,F821,UP037` (the pre-commit config) passes, plus pinned `black 26.1.0` and `isort 7.0.0`. Import survival checked in each touched test file. The two PD tests themselves were **not** run locally — they need multi-GPU hardware. ## NOTE FOR REVIEWERS These two tests will now genuinely inject 5% transfer failures for the first time. If the transfer-recovery path has regressed during the period when injection was inert, they may start failing. **That would be a real pre-existing defect surfacing, not a regression introduced by this PR** — and arguably the point of fixing the injection. Part of a series of disaggregation cleanups; this is the only one that changes runtime behavior. Related: #35838, #35843, #35844, #35847, #35886. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). — the fix restores two existing CI tests that were passing vacuously; the measured-injection verification above covers the mechanism. - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). — N/A: test-only env var, not user documentation. - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results. — N/A, see above. - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32507426911](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32507426911)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32507426752](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32507426752)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32507426980](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32507426980)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [dLLM] Add JointThresholdInDel algorithm for insertion & deletion decoding
signal.text: ## Motivation This PR introduces the `JointThresholdInDel` algorithm, which extends `JointThreshold` with structural edit token support for diffusion LLMs. It enables the model to not only fill masks and refine tokens, but also **delete** positions (block shrinks) and **insert** new positions via SPLIT (block expands). This is essential for models trained with insertion and deletion capabilities (e.g., LLaDA2.2-flash with InDel training). ## Modifications ### New Algorithm: `JointThresholdInDel` - **DELETE token**: When the model predicts a DELETE token at a position, that position is removed from the block, remaining positions shift left, and the block is padded with mask tokens. - **SPLIT (insert) token**: When the model predicts a SPLIT token, the position expands into `[mask, current_token]`, allowing the model to insert new content. - **Original mask tracking (`is_orig_mask`)**: Distinguishes masks from the initial block vs. masks introduced by DELETE padding or SPLIT expansion, ensuring correct M2T scheduling. - **Anti-loop mechanism**: Detects repeated block states and deterministically injects diversity at the lowest-confidence position via `argmin`, preventing infinite loops caused by DELETE/SPLIT cycles. - **Bounded final cleanup**: When the post-edit budget is reached or the regular-update limit is exceeded, selects every remaining non-prompt mask and suppresses MASK, DELETE, and SPLIT. If token IDs change, one additional forward is performed before emitting the request so the KV cache matches the final block. - **Cumulative post-edit budget**: The consumed post-edit budget is not reset if an original mask reappears. This intentionally differs from the released reference decoder. - **FDFO compatible**: All iteration state is carried in the `states` dict, fully compatible with First-Done-First-Out scheduling. ### Config Changes Added `delete_token_id` and `split_token_id` to `DllmConfig`. `JointThresholdInDel` requires both IDs in checkpoint metadata or an explicit model override, and rejects unsupported or partial configurations at startup. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review Process 1. signal.title: [AMD] [Spec] Enable stochastic tree verification on ROCm
signal.text: ## Motivation ROCm EAGLE verification currently routes every HIP request through greedy `argmax`, even when `temperature`, `top_p`, or `top_k` request stochastic sampling. ROCm also lacks the CUDA target-only tree-sampling kernel and its top-k/top-p renormalization operators. While validating a portable tree verifier with GLM-5.2-FP8, EAGLE top-k > 1 exposed a second blocker: DSA’s page-64 index cache received physical token-slot IDs but indexed them as page rows: ```python index_k[tgt_loc_flat] = index_k[src_loc_flat] ``` On MI355X this failed during draft cache preparation, before target verification: ```text HSA_STATUS_ERROR_EXCEPTION: An HSAIL operation resulted in a hardware exception (0x1016) torch.AcceleratorError: HIP error: unspecified launch failure ``` Both the stochastic verifier and page-aware DSA relocation are required for a complete ROCm top-k > 1 tree path. ## Modifications ### Target-only tree verification - `python/sglang/kernels/ops/speculative/tree_sampling.py` - Add the Triton target-only stochastic tree verifier and residual bonus-token sampling. - `python/sglang/kernels/ops/speculative/__init__.py` - Register the Triton tree-sampling operator for CUDA and HIP. - `python/sglang/srt/speculative/eagle_utils.py` - Route non-greedy HIP EAGLE requests to the Triton tree verifier; preserve chain rejection sampling and greedy dispatch. - `python/sglang/srt/speculative/dflash_utils.py` - Enable the same target-only Triton verifier for DFLASH on HIP. - `python/sglang/srt/speculative/spec_utils.py` - Advertise tree-kernel availability on HIP. ### Portable probability renormalization - signal.title: Fix hybrid decode CUDA graph WAR event timing
signal.text:
## Summary Hybrid linear-attention (Mambaish) decode graphs continue reading shared recurrent state during CUDA graph replay. Publish the WAR read-done event after replay so the overlap scheduler cannot overwrite that state while the graph is still consuming it. ### Before ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant R as Decode graph runner participant G as GPU stream participant S as Overlap scheduler R->>G: Load shared Mamba state R->>G: Record read-done event R->>G: Replay CUDA graph S->>G: Wait for read-done G-->>S: Event completes before replay S->>G: Reuse / overwrite shared state Note over G: Replay is still reading the state
Race, hang, or invalid output ``` ### After ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant R as Decode graph runner participant G as GPU stream participant S as Overlap scheduler R->>G: Load shared Mamba state R->>G: Replay CUDA graph R->>G: Record read-done event S->>G: Wait for read-done G-->>S: Event completes after replay S->>G: Safely reuse / overwrite shared state ``` --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :x: [Run #32523278032](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32523278032) Latest PR Test (Extra): :x: [Run #32523277790](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32523277790) Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): :heavy_minus_sign: **No AMD PR run found for this commit**.

signal.author: sglang-bot

signal.title: [Bug] `uv pip install sglang` with uv < 0.12 silently installs 0.5.9 (6 months old)
signal.text: ### What happened I hit this yesterday: served Qwen3.8-27B-FP8 with `--tp 2` and got fluent but wrong output (e.g. trivial math answered incorrectly, no crash or NaN). Debugged the model first, then realized the actual problem: `uv pip install sglang` had installed **0.5.9** (2026-02-23) instead of 0.5.17. 0.5.9 predates the qwen3_5 dense TP>1 fix (#19070) — a dropped down_proj all-reduce — which explains the wrong output. ### Root cause - `flash-attn-4`, a mandatory dependency of every release since 0.5.10, has only pre-release versions on PyPI (4.0.0b5…b27). - uv < 0.12.0 does not honor pre-release specifiers in transitive dependency metadata (changed in astral-sh/uv#19993). It treats every sglang ≥ 0.5.10 as unsatisfiable and silently backtracks to 0.5.9 — the newest release without the flash-attn-4 dependency. No error, no warning. Repro (resolution only, any OS): ``` $ echo sglang | uv pip compile - --python-platform x86_64-manylinux_2_34 --python-version 3.12 # uv 0.11.x -> sglang==0.5.9 # uv 0.12.x -> sglang==0.5.17 ``` Pinning makes the mechanism visible, since the resolver can no longer backtrack: ``` $ echo 'sglang==0.5.10.post1' | uv pip compile - # uv 0.11.x × No solution found ... Because only flash-attn-4<4.0.0b4 is available and sglang==0.5.10.post1 depends on flash-attn-4>=4.0.0b4 ... hint: ... pre-releases weren't enabled (try: `--prerelease=allow`) ``` ### Docs inconsistency `uv pip install --prerelease=allow sglang` works (the install guide has the flag), but many docs pages use the plain command — e.g. https://lmsysorg.mintlify.app/cookbook/autoregressive/Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B#install-sglang (`docs/cookbook/autoregressive/Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B.mdx`), and about 12 cookbook pages total. Anyone following those pages (or typing the obvious command) with an older uv gets 0.5.9 silently. pip, uv ≥ 0.12, and the Docker images are unaffected. ### Possibly the same issue in the tracker - #24029 — qwen3-vl "output does not match the image at all": four users on 0.5.9; one environment paste (2026-05-25, when 0.5.12 was current) shows `sglang 0.5.9`, `torch 2.9.1` (0.5.9's exact pin), and `uv 0.11.16`. Resolved as "upgrade to >=0.5.12 is OK", without anyone asking why they were on 0.5.9. - Open issues filed months after newer releases existed, with an env of 0.5.9 and 0.5.9's torch pin: #34111 #34112 #34113 #33283 #25670. Not asserting these are all this — but the fingerprint matches a resolver-driven 0.5.9 install. One forward-looking note: `cuda-tile==1.6.0rc5` on current main (not yet in any release) is the same pattern — the first release shipping it will again be unresolvable for uv < 0.12 users, who would then silently stay on 0.5.17.

signal.title: Return the caller's embedding for Llama 4 precomputed image input
signal.text: ## Motivation A caller can skip the vision tower by passing an already-computed image embedding as image data, using the public precomputed-embedding input format. On Llama 4 that embedding was re-encoded instead of used. The multimodal processor stores the supplied embedding under the item's `feature` attribute and tags the item as precomputed. It leaves the older `precomputed_embeddings` attribute unset, and the scheduler's central bypass only short-circuits on that older attribute. The item therefore falls through to the model, and Llama 4's image-feature hook had no precomputed branch to catch it. **Before:** the embedding is run through the vision tower and projector. **After:** it is returned unchanged; the vision tower is never entered. This is the Llama 4 entry in #6483. #8156 moved Llama 4 onto generic processor handling but did not bridge the two attributes. ## Modifications The early return already used by the MiniCPM-V and MiniCPM-o models, unchanged: ```python if items and items[0].format == MultimodalInputFormat.PRECOMPUTED_EMBEDDING: result = torch.cat([item.feature for item in items]) return result.reshape(-1, result.shape[-1]) ``` As in both references the branch is chosen from the first item, so a single encode batch mixing precomputed and raw items is unsupported. That comes from the shared scheduler batching path, not from this change. ## Accuracy Tests The raw-pixel path is untouched. Restoring only the changed source file turns the new test red, showing the vision tower being entered: ``` $ SRC=python/sglang/srt/models/mllama4.py $ TEST=test/registered/unit/models/test_mllama4_precomputed_embedding.py $ git checkout origin/main -- $SRC && pytest $TEST E AssertionError: Lists differ: [tensor([[1., 1., ...]])] != [] # tower entered 3 failed, 1 passed $ git checkout HEAD -- $SRC && pytest $TEST 4 passed ``` Run on CPU; no GPU was available, so this is not a live generation. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

signal.title: [Spec] Fix target-only sampling CDF boundaries
signal.text: ## Motivation The target-only speculative sampling kernel uses coins from `[0, 1)` but selected a target CDF bucket with `coin <= cumulative_probability`. At the lower endpoint, that can accept a draft token with zero target probability. Exact interior CDF boundaries are also assigned to the preceding bucket instead of the next positive-mass bucket. Fixes #35771. ## Modifications - Use the half-open CDF condition `coin < cumulative_probability`. - Require positive target probability before either acceptance-threshold path can accept a draft. - Update the permissive zero-threshold test to preserve acceptance of all positive-mass drafts while rejecting impossible drafts. - Add native regression coverage for zero-mass drafts, exact CDF boundaries, and valid endpoint coins. ## Accuracy Tests - Built the modified `speculative_sampling.cu` with CUDA 13.0 for SM103 and ran `python/sglang/kernels/aot/tests/speculative/test_speculative_sampling.py` on B300: `7 passed`. - `pre-commit run --files python/sglang/kernels/aot/csrc/speculative/speculative_sampling.cuh python/sglang/kernels/aot/tests/speculative/test_speculative_sampling.py` ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not benchmarked. The hot-path change is one positive-mass predicate and a strict comparison; it adds no allocation, synchronization, or data movement. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). signal.title: [Unified Cache][Draft POC]: Add optional external-cache linker mode to Unified Radix Cache
signal.text: ## Motivation Unified Radix Cache manages heterogeneous model states, including full-attention KV, SWA KV, and model-specific sidecars. On GB platforms, **deployments may need to aggregate larger memory regions into a shared Global Memory pool**. This requires an efficient way for Unified Radix Cache to access remote memory directly without overhead on the inference critical path. This PR adds an optional external-cache linker mode. It allows the tree to access a Global Memory pool through backends such as Mooncake or UMBP .. while retaining ownership of allocation, insertion, component consistency, and cache-node lifetime. The existing hierarchical cache path remains unchanged. The linker is an opt-in alternative for deployments that need a larger shared memory pool while preserving inference performance. ## Modifications This PR is currently at the proof-of-concept stage and will be split into several smaller, focused PRs: - [ ] Introduce the external linker interface and common linker wrapper - [ ] Integrate external linker support into `UnifiedRadixCache` - [ ] Add direct linker implementations for Mooncake、UMBP - [ ] Expand correctness, compatibility, and performance testing - [ ] Support prefetch - [ ] Support other implementations ## Speed Tests and Profiling The optional Mooncake linker was benchmarked against the existing L3 Mooncake path on 8 * H200 GPUs. Lower TTFT is better. A positive percentage means that the linker is faster. signal.title: [Bugfix] Guard harmony parsing against malformed gpt-oss output in Responses API
signal.text: ## Motivation gpt-oss occasionally samples a malformed harmony message header, for example a duplicated `to=` in a tool-call header. `openai_harmony`'s `StreamableParser.process` raises `HarmonyError` on such headers, and `python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/context.py` calls it with no exception handling at four sites: `HarmonyContext.append_output`, both loops in `StreamingHarmonyContext.append_output`, and `StreamingHarmonyContext.render_for_completion`. Repro against the pinned `openai-harmony==0.0.4`: ```python from openai_harmony import HarmonyEncodingName, Role, StreamableParser, load_harmony_encoding enc = load_harmony_encoding(HarmonyEncodingName.HARMONY_GPT_OSS) parser = StreamableParser(enc, role=Role.ASSISTANT) text = '<|channel|>commentary to=functions.get_weather to=functions.get_weather<|message|>{}<|call|>' for t in enc.encode(text, allowed_special="all"): parser.process(t) # openai_harmony.HarmonyError: unexpected tokens remaining in message header: ["to=functions.get_weather"] ``` Because this is model output rather than client input, the failure is intermittent, and the user-visible impact differs by path: - Non-streaming `/v1/responses`: the exception propagates out of `responses_full_generator` into the catch-all in `create_responses`, which returns it as a 400 `invalid_request_error`. A model-side failure gets reported as the client's fault. - Streaming `/v1/responses`: `responses_stream_generator` consumes the generator with no try/except around the `async for`. The 200 status and SSE headers have already been sent, so the exception kills the stream mid-flight with no error event. The client sees a truncated stream and no explanation. Two aggravating details: - After such an error, the parser keeps raising `HarmonyError` for every following token until the next `<|start|>` token, then recovers on its own. So one malformed header poisons the whole remainder of the turn if the exception is allowed to escape, even when the rest of the output is well formed. - #33717 makes the same observation about harmony parse failures surfacing as 400s, but fixes a different crash (`parse_output_message` on preamble messages in `harmony_utils.py`). It does not guard `parser.process`, so the two changes are complementary. ## Modifications Guard the parser at the source instead of in each consumer, so the streaming and non-streaming paths are fixed at once: - New `HarmonyContext._process_token()` wraps `parser.process()`, catches `HarmonyError`, logs the first failure of a malformed stretch (one log line per desync, not one per token), and skips the token so the parser re-synchronizes at the next message start. This mirrors how the tool-call detectors already treat malformed model output: `base_format_detector.parse_streaming_increment` logs and degrades instead of raising. - All four `parser.process` call sites in `context.py` go through the guard. Resulting behavior on malformed output: the malformed message is dropped and logged, following well-formed messages in the same turn still parse, the non-streaming path returns the surviving output instead of a 400, and the streaming path finishes the SSE stream cleanly instead of dying mid-flight. The same failure class exists in vLLM's harmony plumbing; I have a parallel fix open there (vllm-project/vllm#52055). New unit test `test/registered/unit/entrypoints/test_harmony_context.py` (registered in `base-a-test-cpu`): - non-streaming `append_output` survives the malformed tool-call header above, logs exactly once, drops the malformed message, and still parses the following well-formed message - the same for streaming `append_output` fed one token per chunk - well-formed output parses unchanged, with no error logs Without the guard, the first two tests fail with `openai_harmony.HarmonyError: unexpected tokens remaining in message header: ["to=functions.get_weather"]` at the previously unguarded call sites. ## Accuracy Tests Not applicable, no kernel or model forward changes. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not applicable. The guard adds a try/except and a flag assignment per token on the harmony parsing path, which is negligible next to the parse itself. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. signal.title: fix(mlx): skip transformers resolution for KV cache
signal.text: ## Motivation MLX model startup currently reaches Transformers architecture resolution while building the KV cache. Models such as Hunyuan that rely on remote `auto_map` entries can fail there even though MLX loads them through `mlx_lm` and does not use the Transformers backend. Fixes #32521. ## Modifications - Short-circuit Transformers backend detection when the MLX backend is active. - Add a CPU regression test that makes architecture resolution fail if it is called and verifies KV cache construction still completes on the MLX path. ## Accuracy Tests Not applicable. This changes backend selection during startup and does not modify model outputs. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not applicable. The MLX path now avoids an unnecessary architecture-resolution call. ## Validation - Hunyuan config harness on macOS arm64 with Python 3.11, MLX 0.32.1, and mlx-lm 0.31.3. Current `main` raises the reported remote architecture error inside `build_kv_cache`. This branch completes the same function path with `SGLANG_USE_MLX=1`. No model weights were loaded. - The same harness with `SGLANG_USE_MLX=0` still calls the architecture resolver and raises the same error. - `python -m pytest -q test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_kv_cache_builder.py` passed. - Pre-commit passed for both changed files, including Black, isort, Ruff, codespell, AST, and registered-test validation. - Python bytecode compilation passed for both changed files. ## Checklist - [x] Format code according to the project pre-commit configuration. - [x] Add a registered CPU unit test. - [x] Documentation is not required for this internal startup fix. - [x] Accuracy and speed benchmarks are not applicable to this control-flow fix. - [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32494813999](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32494813999)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32494813613](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32494813613)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32494813990](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32494813990)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [Diffusion] Candidate-trajectory execution contract (phase 1: types + validation)
signal.text: ## Summary Implements the candidate-trajectory execution contract proposed in #35331 as a real, opt-in path -- not just a standalone contract module. **Contract layer** (`runtime/pipelines_core/candidates.py`): - `CandidateTrajectorySpec` -- `count` / `reducer` / `return_candidates` / `seed_policy`, with eager validation: `count=1` must use `reducer="none"` (provably identical to the existing non-candidate path), `count>1` requires a real registered reducer. - `CandidateGroup` -- stable, sorted, unique `candidate_ids` per `request_id`. - A reducer registry (`"none"`, `"mean"`, plus `register_candidate_reducer()` for model-owned rules). - `derive_candidate_generators()` -- one `torch.Generator` per candidate, derived from `(base_seed, candidate_id)` via a splitmix64-style bit mixer. - `validate_candidate_admission()` / `reduce_candidates()` -- atomic group admission and partial-failure-safe reduction. **Real integration**: - `SamplingParams.candidate_spec`, validated against `num_outputs_per_prompt` -- the RFC's premise is that `num_outputs_per_prompt`'s existing outputs *become* the candidate axis, not a separate count, so `candidate_spec.count` must equal it. - **`InputValidationStage._generate_seeds`** (the real per-request seed/generator construction used by every model) now uses `derive_candidate_generators` instead of the existing naive `base_seed + i` scheme whenever `candidate_spec` is set. This is the RFC's core RNG-independence safety requirement, not a nicety -- plain addition can produce visibly correlated draws for nearby seeds. When `candidate_spec` is `None` (the default), behavior is byte-for-byte unchanged. The actual candidate-reduction *application* point (averaging N action outputs down to one served result) needs real per-model tensor-shape knowledge -- e.g. Cosmos3's `action_latents` layout -- that can't be added correctly without a real model and weights to validate against. That's left for the model-adapter phase the RFC's own rollout plan describes (step 2: "Add a Cosmos3 action adapter"); the RNG-derivation wiring above is what's provably safe to land now. ## Test plan - **30 tests** in `test_candidate_trajectory.py` (27 original + 3 new), covering: - RFC required-tests 1, 2, 3, 4, 7 (count=1 identity, sequential/batched seed equivalence, reducer parity, stable candidate IDs across co-batched requests, no partial-aggregate on failure). - The exact multi-prompt aggregation pattern `_generate_seeds` now uses: prompt-major/candidate-minor flattening order, cross-prompt independence, single-prompt equivalence to bare `derive_candidate_generators`. - Requirements 5, 6, 8 (CFG-parallel candidate membership, TP/SP reconstruction before reduction, conditional video-branch skip) still need a real model/pipeline adapter and are out of scope until that phase. All 30 tests pass on the Apple Silicon MPS backend. `input_validation.py` itself has a heavy import surface (`torchvision`, which isn't installed on this machine, plus a deep `pipeline_configs`/`platforms`/`server_args` chain) that makes it impractical to instantiate `InputValidationStage` directly in a local sandbox, so the new branch's logic is validated at the level of the RNG derivation it calls into (already exhaustively tested) rather than via a live call through the stage class; CI's full dependency stack can exercise that path directly. Also verified clean against the repo's `black`, `isort`, and `ruff --select=F401,F821,UP037` configuration. Closes/relates to #35331. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32166068209](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32166068209)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32166067961](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32166067961)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32166068052](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32166068052)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->
signal.author: OnePunchMonk

signal.title: Remove many scheduler synchronization to enable overlap scheduler on agent workload
signal.text: ## Motivation DSV4 disaggregated sparse prefill still exposes scheduler-side CUDA synchronization and long host stalls across allocator cleanup, transfer-index preparation, HiCache write-back/load-back, and speculative-MoE execution. Under full GB300 load, Blackwell MegaMoE can additionally deadlock at its whole-grid software barrier when every SM is occupied. ## Changes ### HiCache - Dispatch unavoidable direct-I/O index readiness waits from a device-bound helper thread. - Batch unified write-back eviction transfers. - Keep Full-KV load-back ownership separate from auxiliary-pool locks. - Track readiness per evicted node and wait only for the nodes included in a transfer. ### Sparse-prefill and allocator cleanup - Preserve dense segment metadata and free paged SWA/HiSparse/unified mappings without data-dependent `torch.unique` discovery. - Remove scalar synchronization from unified SWA CPU-copy bookkeeping. - Build sparse-prefill metadata before replay and publish the shared-read boundary for EAGLE/DFLASH/DSpark paths. - Pin scheduler metadata before asynchronous H2D copies. ### Disaggregated transfer scheduling - Stage prefill and cached-prefix transfer indices asynchronously instead of converting them on the scheduler hot path. - Avoid blocking cached-prefix early sends. - Move request-scoped prefill DP-rank registration to a reusable background executor. ### Blackwell MegaMoE - Reserve two SMs by default for Blackwell MegaMoE so side-stream/NCCL work can drain while its clustered grid barrier is active. - Keep Hopper behavior unchanged and provide explicit total-SM/reserved-SM environment overrides. ## Validation - Real DSpark GSM8K validation completed all 1,319 samples without a MegaMoE grid-barrier timeout: flexible exact match **0.9659 ± 0.0050**, strict exact match **0.9666 ± 0.0049**. ### Throughput A/B The comparison used the same GB300 AgentX workload and serving configuration: 2xDEP8 prefill plus DEP12 decode (28 GPUs), concurrency 1152, a 300-second trace idle-gap cap, and a 2.1 HiCache ratio. Throughput below is total input plus output tokens per second per GPU. | Profiling elapsed | Main baseline (tok/s/GPU) | This PR (tok/s/GPU) | Improvement | | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | | 10 min | 61,456 | 80,017 | +30.2% | | 15 min | 72,798 | 94,354 | +29.6% | | 20 min | 79,832 | 102,993 | +29.0% | | 25 min | 83,970 | 106,639 | +27.0% | | 30 min | 85,584 | 111,173 | +29.9% | | 35 min | 87,442 | 109,768 | +25.5% | | 40 min | 86,425 | 109,912 | +27.2% | Note baseline crash at 40 min so only comparing up to this time. This crash is fixed in pr. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32493356544](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32493356544)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32493356067](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32493356067)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32493356372](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32493356372)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->
signal.author: weireweire

signal.title: [diffusion] vae: fix silently ignored --vae-tiling for Sana (AutoencoderDC)
signal.text: ### Motivation Fixes #34482. `--vae-tiling` was silently ignored for Sana models: the `AutoencoderDC` wrapper does not proxy `enable_tiling` to the inner diffusers model, so the call raised `AttributeError`, which (at the time this PR was opened) was swallowed by a bare `except` in `DecodingStage`. On 8GB GPUs this turns a would-be-successful generation into a fatal OOM after the full denoising loop has already run. See the issue for the root-cause chain. ### Modifications - `runtime/models/vaes/autoencoder_dc.py`: proxy `enable_tiling` / `disable_tiling` to the inner diffusers `AutoencoderDC`, which already implements them. `enable_tiling` is a no-op (with `warning_once`) when spatial-shard parallel decode is installed on this wrapper, since diffusers' `tiled_decode` running per-rank inside a height-sharded decoder breaks the halo exchange (mismatched collective rounds / wrong neighbours). - `configs/models/vaes/sana.py`, `configs/pipeline_configs/sana.py`: update the two comments that claimed DC-AE tiling is unsupported. - `test/unit/test_autoencoder_dc.py`: CPU-only unit test asserting the proxy forwards to the inner model and that the spatial-shard guard is a no-op. ### Scope / decisions - **Default unchanged.** `SanaPipelineConfig.vae_tiling` stays `False`; tiling is opt-in via `--vae-tiling`. DC-AE is a 32x-compression autoencoder and tile seam quality / the benefit of diffusers' default 512 tile have not been validated, so a default flip does not belong in a bugfix. - **`decoding.py` is no longer touched.** The v1 of this PR also replaced the bare `except` around `enable_tiling()` with a warning; main has since fixed that call site independently (specific `AttributeError` handling + warning), so that change is dropped here and the PR is now purely the wrapper-side fix. ### Test / Verification - Before: `sglang generate --model-path Efficient-Large-Model/Sana_600M_512px_diffusers --prompt "..." --save-output --vae-tiling` — fatal OOM in `DecodingStage` on RTX 4070 Laptop 8GB (3/3 runs). Note: with DC-AE's 32x compression, tiling only engages at ≥1024x1024 (512x512 gives a 16x16 latent == `tile_latent_min`). - After: same command (1024x1024) succeeds end-to-end; output image correct. This PR changes correctness (OOM → success), not performance; timings are not reported. - `pytest python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_autoencoder_dc.py` passes. - pre-commit clean.
signal.author: emmayang767

signal.title: [Diffusion] Compile-plan trajectory promotion gate
signal.text: ## Summary Implements the data model and validation flow proposed in #35333: connects SGLang Diffusion's regional `torch.compile` support (`DenoisingStage` / `CompiledModuleRegistry` in `runtime/utils/torch_compile.py`) to a reproducible, full-trajectory promotion gate for stateful iterative models -- turning "compile succeeded" into "this exact compile plan passed the declared end-to-end trajectory contract for this workload signature." - `CompileWorkloadSignature` -- the exact workload regime (model revision, dtype, backend, parallel signature, latent shape regime, step count, CFG/cache mode, state schema version) a compiled plan is valid for, with a stable sha256 `digest()` for use as a manifest key. - `TrajectoryGate` -- declares checkpoints and per-checkpoint tensor-parity thresholds (`cosine_similarity` as a *minimum*, `mae`/`mse`/`rmse`/`max_abs`/`l2` as *maximums*), plus a slot for model-specific output-quality metrics the framework deliberately does not compute itself. - `CompiledPlanManifest` -- the offline/CI artifact recording whether a compile plan was promoted (`"validated"`/`"rejected"`) for a signature. - `run_trajectory_gate()` -- warms and runs both an eager reference and a compiled candidate through a caller-supplied stepping function across a *full checkpoint schedule* (not a single isolated forward, per the RFC's core argument that one forward isn't enough to validate a stateful rollout), scores each declared checkpoint, and rejects on the first threshold miss. - `select_validated_plan()` -- the runtime-side lookup: does an incoming workload signature match a validated manifest, or fall back to eager. The manifest is an offline/CI artifact; the runtime never reruns the full reference rollout per request. `compute_tensor_metrics()` mirrors the metric semantics of the existing `tools/compare_diffusion_trajectory_similarity.py` (cosine similarity, MAE/MSE/RMSE, max-abs, L2), reimplemented locally rather than imported, so this module carries no diffusion-specific dependencies (no `imageio`, no model loading) and stays independently testable. ## Scope Data model, validation, and the promotion decision itself -- matching the RFC's explicit non-goals ("this RFC does not enable [compile] globally"; "runtime does not rerun the full reference rollout for every request"). Wiring an actual SGLang Diffusion model/pipeline through this gate as part of CI is follow-up work. ## Test plan `python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_compile_trajectory_gate.py`, 18 tests, all passing: - Signature digest determinism and sensitivity to every field. - `TrajectoryGate`/`CompiledPlanManifest` validation (empty/duplicate checkpoints, missing threshold entries, invalid status). - `compute_tensor_metrics()` correctness (identical tensors score perfectly, shape mismatches raise). - **`run_trajectory_gate()` against a real `torch.compile` call** -- not mocked tensors: a toy stateful iterative `nn.Module` (linear + tanh, hidden state carried across steps, standing in for a denoising step) is wrapped with `torch.compile(backend="aot_eager")`, and both the eager and compiled versions are actually run through a multi-step rollout: - the compiled candidate's trajectory is confirmed `"validated"` against the eager reference at declared checkpoints; - a deliberately diverging candidate (same shape, shifted values, standing in for a broken/miscompiled plan) is confirmed `"rejected"`; - a checkpoint schedule that never visits a declared checkpoint, and a step function returning `None` for a declared checkpoint, both raise `CompileGateError` rather than silently passing. - `select_validated_plan()` -- matching signature returns the manifest, mismatched signature falls back to `None`, and a `"rejected"` manifest is never selected regardless of signature match. All 18 tests were run on the **Apple Silicon MPS backend** (`torch.backends.mps.is_available()`), confirmed via the test module's resolved `DEVICE`, not a silent CPU fallback -- so the `torch.compile` calls and tensor-metric computations are exercised on a real accelerator, not just plain Python logic. Also verified clean against the repo's `black`, `isort`, and `ruff --select=F401,F821,UP037` configuration. Closes/relates to #35333. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32166481922](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32166481922)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32166481726](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32166481726)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32166481936](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32166481936)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [AMD][CI] Add the Qwen3.8 MXFP4 MI35x nightly
signal.text: ## Motivation [Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B-FP8) shipped with [day-0 SGLang support](https://www.lmsys.org/blog/2026-08-12-qwen3-8-day0-support/) and a [day-0 AMD recipe](https://www.amd.com/en/developer/resources/technical-articles/2026/day-0-support-for-qwen-3-8-on-amd-instinct-gpus.html), but the AMD nightly has no coverage for it. It reuses the Qwen3.5 architecture (`Qwen3_5MoeForCausalLM`), so it runs with no model-code changes — which is exactly why nothing guards it: a change to the shared hybrid path or the AITER MXFP4 MoE kernels can silently degrade it on ROCm. FP8 is ~2.4 TB against 8 x 288 GB per MI355X node, so there is no single-node FP8 recipe; single-node means FP4. The job serves [`amd/Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B-Quark-MXFP4`](https://huggingface.co/amd/Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B-Quark-MXFP4), AMD's Quark quantization of the FP8 checkpoint. Only routed experts are quantized, so AMD measures the same 97.49 GSM8K as the FP8 baseline — this job gates the FP8 checkpoint's quality in the shape that fits one node. ## Modifications **`test/registered/amd/accuracy/mi35x/test_qwen38_mxfp4_eval_mi35x.py`** (new) — two phases in the `nightly-amd-8-gpu-mi35x-qwen38-mxfp4` suite: `test_a_gsm8k_accuracy` (TP8 GSM8K, gated at 0.93) and `test_b_serving_perf` (batch 1/8/16/64 at 1024 in / 1024 out). Both launch from one `SERVER_ARGS` reproducing the AMD model card recipe, so the throughput numbers describe exactly the configuration the accuracy gate covers. Perf is skipped unless accuracy passed. Two flags are load-bearing rather than defaults: `--page-size 1` (on HIP the default becomes 64 when the container sets `SGLANG_AITER_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT=vectorized_5d`) and `--attention-backend aiter` (no arg override picks a backend for this architecture on ROCm). The server runs with no `--reasoning-parser` so a `<think>` block still scores under the last-number extractor. **`.github/workflows/nightly-test-amd-rocm720.yml`** — new `nightly-8-gpu-mi35x-qwen38-mxfp4-rocm720` job on `linux-mi35x-gpu-8`. ROCm 7.2 only: MXFP4 needs gfx95x. Also removes the two Qwen3-235B jobs from this nightly; `Qwen3MoeForCausalLM` is gated per-commit by `test/registered/quant/test_quark_mxfp4.py` (gsm8k >= 0.89, on both ROCm lanes) and runs nightly at 30B-A3B scale, so this frees two 8-GPU jobs per night. No file under `test/` is touched by that removal, and `nightly-test-amd.yml` (ROCm 7.0) is left alone since that lane is being retired. **`test/run_suite.py`** — register the new suite. **`scripts/ci/amd/check_hf_cache_space.sh`** (new) — run [#32196787596](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32196787596) died 40 minutes into the download on ENOSPC, and free space was never reported anywhere in its log. This records it before the download, says whether the checkpoint is already cached, and clears stale artifacts via the existing `scripts/ci/utils/cleanup_hf_cache.py`. It deletes no other checkpoints: `/sgl-data` is a 15 TB volume shared by the whole AMD fleet at 100% used, and an eviction attempt removed 48 of them while free space went from 298 MB to 227 MB. Never fails the job. **`scripts/ci/utils/amd_cache_audit.py`** (new) — joins `register_amd_ci` tests to the checkpoints they name and the jobs that dispatch them, counting the per-commit `pr-test-amd*.yml` workflows and not just nightly. 289 of 429 AMD registrations are per-commit only and run on runners sharing the same PVC, so a nightly-only join badly overstates what is reclaimable. `--runner` scopes to a cluster by the dispatching job's `runs-on` label; suite -> models extraction is reused from `list_stage_models.py`. ## Accuracy Tests **[Run #32313140175](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32313140175) — green. GSM8K 0.973** against the 0.930 gate and AMD's published 0.9749. Both phases ran, neither skipped. The gate sits ~5% below AMD's number, the same relative tolerance the sibling Qwen3.5 MI35x evals allow (`rtol: 0.05`). Caveat: the checkpoint was already cached on that runner, so the run exercised load-and-serve but not a cold download. A confirmation run on the current head is in flight at [#32424018092](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32424018092); it is the first to exercise the cache-check step, which the green run predates. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Published to the job summary rather than asserted, so it reports regressions without becoming a flaky gate. Measured on 8x MI355X, TP8, 1024 in / 1024 out: | batch size | latency (s) | input tput (tok/s) | output tput (tok/s) | ITL (ms) | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 1 | 14.83 | 6961.62 | 69.73 | 14.34 | | 8 | 18.48 | 20833.04 | 452.87 | 17.67 | | 16 | 21.94 | 21758.80 | 773.39 | 20.69 | | 64 | 37.74 | 21993.04 | 1885.58 | 33.94 | Overridable via `NIGHTLY_BATCH_SIZES` / `NIGHTLY_INPUT_LENS` / `NIGHTLY_OUTPUT_LENS`. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). — the Qwen3.8 cookbook page already documents this recipe. - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process). 2.
