signal.title: fix(cache): retain shared SWA slots until final free
signal.text: ## Problem Different full-cache indices can reference the same physical SWA slot. Freeing one mapping previously returned that slot while another mapping still referenced it, allowing premature reuse and a later double free. ## Change Track a reference count per physical SWA slot whenever mappings are written, replaced, or cleared. Free token slots or pages only after their final mapping is removed, while preserving PureSWA's direct identity mapping. ## Validation - full diff passes repository pre-commit hooks - focused duplicate-free and cross-call lifetime tests pass on MI350X - combined Inkling LoRA E2E completes two rollouts without the shared-slot illegal address

signal.title: Fix Prometheus name[] filtering for multiprocess metrics
signal.text: ## Motivation Closes #35752. Upper-layer schedulers and resource managers such as llm-d and AIBrix may request only selected SGLang metrics from `/metrics` using repeated `name[]` query parameters. In multiprocess mode, SGLang's Prometheus registry could omit `MultiProcessCollector` during restricted collection, causing filtered requests to return no SGLang samples even though unfiltered scrapes work. This PR preserves upstream `prometheus_client` name-based filtering behavior for SGLang multiprocess metrics. ## Modifications - Bump the minimum `prometheus-client` version from `0.20.0` to `0.25.0` across package variants. - Create the metrics registry with `CollectorRegistry(support_collectors_without_names=True)` so restricted registries can still include multiprocess collectors. - Add registered observability coverage for `/metrics?name[]=...` requests, verifying that only the requested SGLang metric names are returned. ## Accuracy Tests N/A. This change only affects Prometheus metrics exposition and does not affect model outputs. ## Speed Tests and Profiling N/A. signal.author: muchengl

signal.title: [Fix] Pass Anthropic thinking history as reasoning_content for custom chat encoders
signal.text: ## Motivation Run Kimi-K3 with `--reasoning-parser kimi_k3 --tool-call-parser kimi_k3` and talk to it on `/v1/messages` with `thinking` on. Any agentic client sends assistant `thinking` blocks back in history — the Messages API requires it for tool-use turns — and a few turns in, raw XTML channel markers show up in visible assistant text: ``` turn 3 [text] '<|open|>think<|sep|<|sep|>Something is very strange. […]' turn 4 [text] '<|open|>think<|sep|' ``` Turns 1-2 are fine, then every turn after that is corrupted — it never recovers. Drop the `thinking` blocks from the replayed history and it never happens at all, so the problem is how prior reasoning gets fed back, not the reasoning parser. **Root cause.** K3 ships no Jinja chat template, so SGLang renders it through the checkpoint's own XTML encoder. That encoder frames the `think` / `response` / `tools` channels itself and wants prior reasoning in an assistant `reasoning_content` field. The Anthropic adapter never used it — instead it wrapped prior thinking in the reasoning detector's markers and spliced that into assistant **content**. Here is what the two forms actually render to, straight from the K3 tokenizer: ``` # before — think channel empty, reasoning nested inside the response channel <|open|>think<|sep|><|close|>think<|sep|><|open|>response<|sep|><|open|>think<|sep|>PRIOR <|close|>think<|sep|>Here is my answer.<|close|>response<|sep|> # after <|open|>think<|sep|>PRIOR<|close|>think<|sep|><|open|>response<|sep|>Here is my answer.<|close|>response<|sep|> ``` Every replayed turn taught the model the same lesson: think channel empty, think block sitting inside the response channel. Two turns of that and it starts writing `<|open|>think<|sep|>` as ordinary response text. None of this is K3-specific. All four Python chat encoders that bypass `apply_chat_template` frame their own reasoning channel and read `reasoning_content`, so the splice was wrong for every one of them. ## Modifications - **`entrypoints/openai/chat_encoding.py`** — adds `spec_owns_reasoning_history(spec)`, right under `resolve_chat_encoding_spec` so the contract sits with the specs it describes. It covers the whole custom-encoder family (`spec is not None`) rather than listing specs, so whoever adds the fifth one gets the safe default for free. An encoder that ignores the field drops history — what the splice path already does for models with no reasoning detector — instead of leaking. - **`entrypoints/openai/serving_chat.py`** — `supports_native_reasoning_history()`, a one-line delegate. - **`entrypoints/anthropic/serving.py`** — `_convert_assistant_thinking_blocks` now returns `(reasoning_content, text)`. Custom encoders get the history in the field, everyone else keeps the splice untouched. `redacted_thinking` still raises before the branch, and the best-effort drop for detector-less models survives. Nothing needed a schema change: `ChatCompletionMessageGenericParam` already declared `reasoning_content`, and messages are dumped without `exclude_none`, so it flows straight through. `wrap_reasoning_history` has exactly one production caller, so that is the whole mechanism. `dsv4`/`dsv32` also land on their official multi-turn contract now instead of bypassing it. Jinja-path models stay on the splice on purpose — their markers (`<think>`, `[THINK]`, `◁think▷`) really do live in the content stream, so it reproduces what the model emitted anyway. ## Test Plan ### Live server Same deployment before and after — `moonshotai/Kimi-K3` on 2x4 GB300, TP8, DSPARK spec-decode — same scripts, `temperature=0`: | run | main | with the fix | | --- | --- | --- | | 12-turn tool loop, streaming `/v1/messages` | leaks turns 3-12, all ten of them | clean, and the loop converges at turn 9 | | 8-turn tool loop, non-streaming | leaks turns 3-8 | clean | | 6 concurrent sessions x 5 turns | all six leak, every one first at turn 3 | none leak | | thinking dropped from replayed history | clean | clean | | `thinking: {"type": "disabled"}` | clean | clean | | reasoning passed as `reasoning_content` on `/v1/chat/completions` | clean | clean | | thinking-only history turn, and a turn with two thinking blocks | clean | clean | | `redacted_thinking` history | 400 | 400 | On main the onset is turn 3 every single time, and it never recovers — the `thinking` block stops appearing at all from there on and the markers move into `text`. That is also why the loop never converges: each turn re-reads its own corrupted history and re-diagnoses the same phantom problem. With the fix, `thinking` comes back on essentially every turn and the model finishes the task. Asked what it had just been thinking, the model quoted the injected reasoning back — the history really does land in the think channel rather than being quietly dropped. Prompt rendering was also diffed against the real K3 tokenizer for a thinking + text + tool_use turn. ### Unit tests `anthropic/test_serving.py` — 61/61. Two new cases: history reaches a channel-framing encoder as `reasoning_content` and never through the wrap path, and a thinking-only turn keeps its reasoning across the empty-content placeholder branch. Both go red against pre-fix code, and the existing wrap-path test still covers the default encoder. `openai/test_serving_chat.py` — 111/111. Two more: the real `OpenAIServingChat` predicate across all four specs plus `None`, and a guard that parses the literals `resolve_chat_encoding_spec` can return and checks them against the tuple the capability test iterates. Add an encoder without classifying it and CI fails. Mutation-checked, so it is not passing vacuously. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32435140730](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32435140730)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32435140644](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32435140644)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32435140704](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32435140704)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->
signal.author: mmangkad

signal.title: fix(qwen3-omni/asr): support heterogeneous audio lengths in cross-request MM batches
signal.text: ## Motivation `_batch_encode_per_image_misses()` collects multimodal cache misses across multiple requests and calls the model embedding function once for the whole batch. Qwen3-Omni and Qwen3-ASR share the Qwen3-Omni audio encoder. Their `get_audio_feature()` paths assumed that every audio item in a cross-request batch shared the same padded time dimension: - audio features: `[batch, mel, time]` - attention masks: `[batch, time]` Audio preprocessing runs independently per request, so padding is only consistent *within* a request. Concurrent requests carrying different audio durations therefore produce shapes such as: - request 0 mask: `[1, 900]` - request 1 mask: `[1, 700]` Concatenating those tensors raises: ```text RuntimeError: Sizes of tensors must match except in dimension 0 ``` The failure happens before the audio tower is invoked. The exception is raised on every TP scheduler rank and terminates the server, affecting all in-flight requests. The older request-local embedding path did not normally expose this assumption. Cross-request ViT/MM cache-miss batching introduced by #24013 made heterogeneous request-local padding observable by the model adapters. Qwen3-ASR reuses `Qwen3OmniMoeAudioEncoder` and follows the same request-local padding path, so concurrent ASR requests were vulnerable to the same failure. Qwen3-Omni image and video inputs are not affected. Those modalities already use flattened variable-length patch features whose leading dimension can be concatenated safely; the incompatible request-local padding assumption exists only in the audio collation path. ### Failure before the fix Two concurrent requests containing 900-frame and 700-frame audio features reproduce the failure. Sanitized traceback — the same exception occurred on every TP rank: ```text Traceback (most recent call last): File ".../scheduler.py", in run_batch batch_result = self.model_worker.forward_batch_generation(...) File ".../model_runner.py", in forward output = self._forward_raw(...) File ".../qwen3_vl.py", in forward hidden_states = general_mm_embed_routine(...) File ".../mm_utils.py", in _get_chunked_prefill_embedding hash_to_embedding = _batch_encode_per_image_misses(...) File ".../mm_utils.py", in _batch_encode_per_image_misses all_miss_embedding = data_embedding_func(miss_items) File ".../qwen3_omni_moe.py", in get_audio_feature torch.cat([item.feature_attention_mask for item in items], dim=0) RuntimeError: Sizes of tensors must match except in dimension 0. Expected size 900 but got size 700 for tensor number 1 in the list. ``` After the exception, all scheduler ranks exited and the server process was terminated. ## Modifications In `python/sglang/srt/models/qwen3_omni_moe.py`: - Add `_pack_audio_features()`, an audio packing helper that validates: - features have shape `[batch, mel, time]`, - masks have shape `[batch, time]`, - feature and mask batch/time dimensions agree, - all items use the same mel dimension. - Preserve the existing vectorized fast path when all items share one time dimension. - For heterogeneous items: compact each sample with its own attention mask, concatenate only the valid frames, preserve request and sample order, and pass per-sample lengths to the audio tower. - Keep a single audio-tower invocation for the entire cross-request cache-miss batch — heterogeneous items do **not** fall back to per-item encoder calls, and the batch is never zero-padded to the longest request. In `python/sglang/srt/models/qwen3_asr.py`: - Reuse `_pack_audio_features()` for the standard masked processor path. - Preserve the existing no-mask fallback behavior. The shared audio-tower contract is unchanged: - `input_features`: `[mel, total_valid_frames]` - `feature_lens`: `[num_audio_samples]` ## Accuracy Tests Added CPU regression coverage in `test/registered/unit/models/test_qwen3_audio_packing.py` for: - heterogeneous 900/700-frame audio items, - packed shape `[mel, 1600]` and `feature_lens == [900, 700]`, - Qwen3-ASR input shaped `[2, mel, 900] + [1, mel, 700]`, packed as `[mel, 2500]` with `feature_lens == [900, 900, 700]`, - valid-frame content and request ordering, - parity with the previous implementation for equal-length inputs, - feature/mask rank, batch, time, and mel-dimension validation, - the complete `_batch_encode_per_image_misses()` path with two requests, asserting exactly one audio-tower invocation and correct per-request cache splitting after encoding. The cross-request regression tests exercise both the Qwen3-Omni and Qwen3-ASR `get_audio_feature()` implementations. Result: **9 passed**. The core shape failure is backend-independent and reproduces on CPU before the audio tower is called. Full after-fix GPU server-level Qwen3-Omni and Qwen3-ASR tests were not run locally. ## Speed Tests and Profiling The equal-shape fast path preserves the previous vectorized implementation. Per-item compaction is used only when request-local time dimensions differ. Local packing-only microbenchmark — macOS arm64, PyTorch 2.13.0, 1 thread, 128 mel bins, `torch.utils.benchmark.Timer`: | Input | Previous | Updated | Difference | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 2 equal items, 900 frames | 69.8 µs | 71.3 µs | +1.5 µs (+2.1%) | | 8 equal items, 900 frames | 272.3 µs | 277.8 µs | +5.5 µs (+2.0%) | | 2 heterogeneous items, 900/700 frames | shape error | 175.8 µs | now supported | | 8 heterogeneous items, 300–1000 frames | shape error | 593.9 µs | now supported | These measurements cover packing only and exclude audio-tower execution. No GPU end-to-end profiling was performed locally. ## Related - #24013 — PR introducing cross-request ViT/MM cache-miss batching. - #33408 — issue reporting a similar heterogeneous-shape failure in Unlimited-OCR image batching. - #33458 — model-specific PR addressing the Unlimited-OCR failure. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). (N/A: no public API or configuration change.) - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32511171696](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32511171696)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32511171440](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32511171440)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32511171583](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32511171583)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->
signal.author: sghhhh

signal.title: [Spec] Enable adaptive speculative decoding under DP attention
signal.text: ## Motivation `--speculative-adaptive` picks the speculative draft depth (`num_steps`) per batch at runtime. It is disabled whenever `--enable-dp-attention` is set: `adaptive_unsupported_reason()` bails out and the server falls back to static params. The guard is there for a reason. Under DP attention each rank picks its own `num_steps`, and `num_draft_tokens = num_steps + 1` sets the shape of the cross-rank MLP-sync `all_gather`. If ranks disagree, the collective shapes diverge and NCCL hangs. So adaptive is off exactly where it would help most: DP-attention deployments of large MoE models. This PR makes it work there. ## Modifications Agree on the tier across ranks using the MLP-sync `all_gather` that already runs, so there is no new collective: - `dp_attn.py`: each rank appends its desired `num_steps` to the sync vector (idle and non-adaptive ranks send a sentinel). The tier is the `min()` over the column. `min` is safe because every tier is prebuilt on every rank, and a rank only votes low when its batch is large, so no rank is ever pushed to do more draft work than it asked for. The result is written to the batch the worker forwards (`batch_to_gather`, which for a prebuilt batch is its inner idle batch, not `local_batch`). - `schedule_batch.py`: new field `adaptive_consensus_steps`. - `adaptive_runtime_state.py`: under DP the per-rank EMA keeps learning but stops activating on its own; the consensus drives activation. - `eagle_worker_v2.py`: honor `adaptive_consensus_steps` when set, otherwise route locally by batch size. - `adaptive_spec_params.py`: drop the `enable_dp_attention` guard. The other guards (multi_layer_eagle, TBO, pdmux) stay. `num_steps` only changes how many draft tokens are proposed per step. The verify step still decides what gets accepted, so the output is identical at any tier. Known limits: under skewed load `min` pins every rank to the lowest tier a neighbor wants, so a light rank can lose speculation it could afford. `candidate_steps` must stay at or below the boot `--speculative-num-steps`. `SGLANG_SCHEDULER_SKIP_ALL_GATHER=1` with real DP bypasses the consensus writeback. ## Accuracy Tests Output is unchanged by construction. The new test runs GSM8K through the adaptive plus DP path and checks the score holds. ## Speed Tests and Profiling This is an enablement change, not a speed change. What matters is that the consensus adds no overhead when the tier holds. Large MoE model, 4xH200, `--tp 4 --dp 2 --ep 4 --enable-dp-attention`, EAGLE `num_steps=3 topk=1 draft=4`, GSM8K, per-request `spec_accept_length`: | concurrency | config | accept_len | tok/s | |---|---|---|---| | 1 | fixed steps=3 | 3.25 | 116 | | 1 | adaptive | 3.24 | 116 | | 8 | fixed steps=3 | 3.24 | 548 | | 8 | adaptive | 3.25 | 548 | While the tier holds, adaptive matches fixed `num_steps` exactly. A shape-changing switch across ranks completes with no deadlock (covered by the new test, and by a 48-request run on the model above). Whether downshifting helps depends on the workload: it pays off when acceptance drops under load. GSM8K keeps acceptance high, so there is nothing to gain there, and a win on a low-acceptance workload is out of scope for this PR. ## Checklist - [x] Format code with pre-commit - [x] Add unit tests - [ ] Update documentation - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results - [x] Follow the SGLang code style

signal.title: [diffusion] tolerate an MPS non-layer restore before anything was captured
signal.text: The MPS non-layer weight stores (`_mps_cpu_non_layer_parameters`, `_mps_cpu_buffers`) exist only after `_capture_mps_cpu_non_layer_weights` runs, but a residency strategy can drive a use interval before that — `restore_mps_cpu_non_layer_weights` then raises `AttributeError`, which surfaces out of the scheduler as a generic request failure instead of anything actionable. This gives the stores a class-level `None` default and makes the three consumers (`restore`/`materialize`/`release`) a no-op in that state. The no-op is the correct semantics rather than error-swallowing: nothing was captured, so there is nothing to restore or release, and after capture the attributes are always dicts. The added test drives all three methods on an unconfigured component with MPS stubbed on, and fails with the pre-change `AttributeError` when the guards are removed. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32478082492](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32478082492)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:no_entry_sign: [Run #32478082220](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32478082220)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32478082364](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32478082364)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->
signal.author: mickqian

signal.title: fix(health): abort the timed-out /health probe scheduler-side
signal.text: ## Motivation Fixes #35884. `health_generate` sends a real one-token request to the scheduler, then gives up after `SGLANG_HEALTH_CHECK_TIMEOUT`. `task.cancel()` only cancels the local asyncio task — the request already went over IPC and keeps running scheduler-side. A poller at the timeout interval (Docker's default `HEALTHCHECK --interval=20s` against the default 20s) then adds a fresh probe every poll while the earlier ones are still resident. The reporter saw ~5 pile up during a 2-minute stall, and batching them crashed paged prefill with `q.shape[0] (1) does not match qo_indptr[-1] (5)`. Aborting isn't enough on its own. `is_health_check_generate_req` matches on the rid prefix and `AbortReq` inherits `rid` from `BaseReq`, so the abort for a probe is itself read as a probe and dropped by the busy-skip in `process_input_requests` — exactly when the scheduler is busy holding the orphan it should retract. ## Modifications - `entrypoints/http_server.py`: on timeout, abort the probe's rid before popping `rid_to_state`. - `managers/utils.py`: add `is_health_check_probe()`, which also requires a `TokenizedGenerateReqInput` / `TokenizedEmbeddingReqInput`. The rid-only predicate stays for its other two callers, which pass `Req` and `AbortReq` and want the looser match. - `managers/scheduler.py`: use it for the busy-skip. - `test/registered/unit/`: abort on timeout, no abort on success, and the `AbortReq` classification. Verified red before the fix (`AssertionError: 0 != 1` on the abort count). ## Accuracy Tests N/A — no kernel, model forward, or sampling changes. ## Speed Tests and Profiling N/A. The abort runs only on the timeout path, at most once per failed poll. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Notes - The success path deliberately doesn't abort — a server that answered completes its own probe, and a busy scheduler never admits one. Happy to make it symmetric if you'd rather. - Doesn't touch the paged-prefill shape mismatch itself, which may well be separate — see #34239. - The encoder health handler runs an in-process encode behind a dispatch lock, not IPC dispatch, so it's unaffected. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32510634068](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32510634068)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32510633962](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32510633962)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32510633973](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32510633973)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.author: polisettyvarma

signal.title: [dLLM] Cut per-step host overhead in the dLLM extend path
signal.text: ## Motivation dLLM inference disables the overlap scheduler (each denoise step has a hard input dependency on the previous step's result), so every bit of host time between steps is exposed directly as device idle. Profiling LLaDA2 at bs=128 on Ascend 910B3 showed three host-side costs on the per-step path, none of which needed to be there: 1. `AscendAttnBackend.init_forward_metadata` took two D2H syncs to obtain values the scheduler already holds on the host (`seq_lens_max`, `extend_seq_lens_cpu_int`). 2. `NPUGraphRunner` re-read `forward_batch.seq_lens.cpu()` before every replay, a blocking D2H behind whatever is queued on the stream, while the same host mirror was already available. 3. `_alloc_extend_loc_with_kv_reuse` (the dLLM FDFO retained-KV path) re-read each reuse row's retained block with its own slice + cast kernel, and pulled every scheduling scalar out of CPU tensors one element at a time. Both costs grow linearly with batch size. ## Modifications **`hardware_backend/npu/attention/ascend_backend.py`** — take `seq_lens_max` from `seq_lens_cpu` and build `extend_seq_lens_cpu_int` from `extend_seq_lens_cpu`. Gated on `forward_mode.is_dllm_extend()`, so the decode/prefill path is byte-identical. **`hardware_backend/npu/graph_runner/npu_graph_runner.py`** — use `forward_batch.seq_lens_cpu` when present, falling back to `.cpu()` when it is not. This one is **not** dLLM-gated and affects every non-DeepSeek-DSA/V4 model on this path, so it is worth stating why it is equivalent: `seq_lens_cpu` is already the authoritative host mirror here — the Ascend attention backend derives its own `seq_lens_cpu_int` from it for every forward mode, and likewise adds the draft width on target-verify. Reading the device tensor in the graph runner made the two components disagree on their source for the same forward; this aligns them. The `is_target_verify()` adjustment is unchanged, and the two former branches collapse into one because they now differ only by that addition. **`mem_cache/allocation.py`** — three changes inside `_alloc_extend_loc_with_kv_reuse`, which is reached only via `if batch.is_dllm()` in `alloc_for_extend`, so non-dLLM requests never enter it: - Add `_gather_reused_block_locs`: the retained blocks all share one length, so fetch them with a single flat index op instead of one slice + cast kernel per row. It replaces one kernel launch per row with a fixed index build + H2D, so it wins on wide batches and loses on narrow ones. The gate is the reuse-row count, re-evaluated every round, so a batch that shrinks falls back on its own — a small-batch latency deployment keeps the per-row path without configuring anything. The threshold defaults to the backend's measured break-even (8 on Ascend, where break-even is ~6) and is unset on backends where it has not been measured, so those keep today's behavior. `SGLANG_DLLM_BATCHED_GATHER_MIN_ROWS` overrides it: a row count to retune, or `-1` to disable the batched path outright for A/B and rollback. Rows of non-uniform block length keep the per-row path regardless. The resolved default is logged once at INFO. - Replace the per-element `int(cpu_tensor[i])` reads with one `.tolist()` per tensor. Unconditional: strictly less work at any batch size. At bs=128 the old code did roughly 770 of these, each allocating a temporary 0-dim tensor. - Hoist the `torch.tensor([-1], device=...)` filler out of the `last_loc` comprehension. Unconditional for the same reason. Every empty-prefix row was allocating its own identical device tensor; the list is consumed by `torch.cat`, which copies, so one shared tensor is equivalent. ### Configuration One new environment variable, `SGLANG_DLLM_BATCHED_GATHER_MIN_ROWS` (`EnvInt(None)` in `environ.py`), the minimum number of dLLM FDFO reuse rows at which the retained blocks are gathered in one flat index op. Nothing needs to be set for the intended behavior on either an Ascend or a non-Ascend deployment: | Value | Behavior | When to use | | --- | --- | --- | | unset (default) | Ascend: batch at 8+ reuse rows. Other backends: always per-row. | Normal serving, both latency and throughput. | | `N` (>= 0) | Batch at `N`+ reuse rows. | Enabling it on a backend after measuring its break-even, or retuning Ascend. | | `-1` | Never batch. | Production A/B and quick rollback. | ```bash # enable on a non-Ascend backend after measuring its break-even SGLANG_DLLM_BATCHED_GATHER_MIN_ROWS=8 python3 -m sglang.launch_server ... # roll back to the per-row path without redeploying SGLANG_DLLM_BATCHED_GATHER_MIN_ROWS=-1 python3 -m sglang.launch_server ... ``` The resolved default is logged once at INFO: ``` dLLM retained-block gather: batching enabled above 8 reuse rows (Ascend default). Override with SGLANG_DLLM_BATCHED_GATHER_MIN_ROWS. ``` ## Accuracy Tests No effect on model outputs — all three changes are host-side bookkeeping that produce the same values (the same slot indices, the same metadata) by different means. Verified with LLaDA2-mini on gsm8k (zero-shot, full 1319 samples): accuracy unchanged. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Measured on Ascend 910B3 at bs=128 (LLaDA2-mini, 32-token dLLM blocks), microbenchmarking each site against the code it replaces: | Site | Before | After | Saved | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | Retained-block gather (128 reuse rows x 32) | 5671 us | 309 us | **5.4 ms** | | ~770 scheduling scalar reads | 3849 us | 54 us | **3.3 ms** | | `init_forward_metadata` (idle stream) | 251 us | 83 us | 168 us | | Graph replay `seq_lens` (idle stream) | 44 us | 6 us | 38 us | The gather is the dominant one and the only part that changes complexity: the per-row path costs about 44 us per reuse row (one kernel launch each) and scales linearly, while the batched path is roughly constant at about 270 us. That constant is why it is row-gated rather than unconditional — below the break-even the per-row path is genuinely faster: | reuse rows | per-row | batched | | | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- | | 1 | 120 us | 305 us | per-row path taken | | 4 | 196 us | 269 us | per-row path taken | | 6 | 279 us | 271 us | break-even | | 8 | 362 us | 268 us | Ascend default threshold | | 32 | 1449 us | 277 us | | | 64 | 2762 us | 268 us | | | 128 | 5671 us | 309 us | | | 256 | 11466 us | 353 us | | The `last_loc` hoist is not in the table because its benefit depends on how many requests have an empty prefix: each such row was allocating a device tensor at about 70 us, so it saves that times the number of empty-prefix rows in the batch (up to 8.9 ms at bs=128 when every row is fresh, and nothing when every row has a cached prefix). On Ascend at bs=128 this removes about 8.7 ms per step out of the box, against a step time of about 98 ms. On a backend where the gather threshold is unset it removes about 3.5 ms (the scalar reads plus the two D2H syncs); the gather itself is one env var away once its break-even has been measured there. ## Unit Tests `test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_dllm_reused_block_gather.py` (CPU-only, no server) pins the flat index arithmetic in `_gather_reused_block_locs` against per-row slicing. Each case covers a way the gather can be heterogeneous across rows, which is where a "looks equivalent" rewrite goes wrong: distinct per-row start offsets, unsorted pool indices, and a block ending exactly at the row boundary. Changing `row * width` to `row * block_len` in the implementation fails all three. These are deliberately not a re-test of the happy path. `test_dllm_fdfo_kv_reuse.py` covers that already in principle, but its reuse rows all share one prefix length and ascending pool indices, so an implementation that broadcast row 0's offset across every row would still pass it. (It is also module-level skipped today, and its fixtures no longer match `alloc_for_extend` — un-skipping it raises `SimpleNamespace has no attribute out_cache_loc_dsv4` — so it is not currently guarding anything either way.) The two D2H changes have no new tests: they need an NPU, and their equivalence is structural (`seq_lens_cpu` is the mirror of `seq_lens`, which the same backend already relies on). ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. signal.title: [Bugfix] Preserve non-tool JSON responses in Llama32Detector and add exist_ok to qwen3_asr AutoConfig
signal.text: ## Motivation 1. In `Llama32Detector.detect_and_parse`, when a model generates a standard JSON object response (e.g. `{"answer": 42}`), `has_tool_call` detects the leading `{` and passes it to `detect_and_parse`. If the JSON does not contain tool names matching the request's registered tools, `parse_base_json` returns `calls = []`. However, `detect_and_parse` previously swallowed the input text and returned an empty string for `normal_text` instead of preserving the original content. 2. In `python/sglang/srt/configs/qwen3_asr.py`, `AutoConfig.register` was missing `exist_ok=True`, raising a `ValueError` when imported in environments where `qwen3_asr` is already registered. ## Proposed Changes - In `Llama32Detector.detect_and_parse`, if `calls` is empty after parsing actions, return `StreamingParseResult(normal_text=text, calls=[])` so non-tool JSON outputs are fully preserved. - Added `exist_ok=True` to `AutoConfig.register` in `qwen3_asr.py`. - Added unit test `test_non_tool_json_object_preserved` in `test/registered/unit/function_call/test_llama32_detector.py`. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32509850779](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32509850779)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32509850461](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32509850461)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32509850659](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32509850659)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: Improve M3 performance on MI350
signal.text: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation Improve M3 performance on MI350. <!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. --> ## Modifications MI350X (gfx950) decode/prefill optimizations for MiniMax-M3 and M3-VL. Measured on TP8 / MXFP8 / 80k context: **1144 -> ~2035 tok/s decode** (13.98 -> 15.72 ms/step at the higher batch), GSM8K unchanged (88.55% before and after at the same budget; 95.3-95.7% at a 2048-token budget). ### MXFP8 / dense GEMM - AITER FlyDSL MXFP8 MoE support: pre-shuffled gate/up weights, E8M0 scales, OAI-SwiGLU activation handling, and fused shared-expert execution. - `--fp8-gemm-backend bf16`: dequantize MXFP8 weights once at load and run BF16 hipBLASLt linear. - `SGLANG_FORCE_MXFP8_BLOCK_CONVERT_DENSE=1`: convert *dense* weights to block-FP8 `[128,128]` at load while MoE stays on the native per-1x32 MX path (the block-scale MoE kernel does not support SwiGLU-OAI). ~+35% prefill. - `SGLANG_OPT_MXFP8_DENSE_PTPC_DECODE_M` (default 128): rowwise-FP8 (ptpc) dense fast path for skinny-M decode, falling back to the block-FP8 GEMM above it. The old cap of 8 silently disabled both this path and the quant fusions below at bs16; raising it was +14.2%. - Allows `--moe-runner-backend aiter` for MXFP8 on gfx950, and errors early if `SGLANG_USE_AITER=1` is not set. ### Fusions - Per-token FP8 quantization fused into the Gemma fused-add-RMSNorm Triton kernel, so the ptpc decode GEMM consumes `(fp8, scale)` directly. Uses an explicitly rounded `1/448` reciprocal (Triton `/` lowers to a fast reciprocal on ROCm, which cost 1 ULP vs AITER). - MoE all-reduce fused into the next layer's norm + qkv quant (`forward_with_allreduce_fusion_quant_per_token`), opt-in per model via `enable_fused_ar_quant_per_token` so it cannot fire for unrelated AITER GemmaRMSNorm models. - Shared-expert append folded into the Triton fused MoE gate (`nfse` handling fixed - the previous path double-appended the shared expert and dropped a routed one). - Shared-expert compute overlapped onto an alternate stream when the routed path forces fusion off. - Small-batch MoE sorting + MXFP8 quant kernel (`moe_sorting_small`), replacing a two-kernel path at decode shapes. ### Router GEMV - New Triton split-K router GEMV (`kernels/ops/gemm/router_gemv.py`) with in-kernel split-K fixup (no separate zero-init launch), per-M-bucket configs (BK 512, BN by batch), and the gate weight read once per decode batch. ~+2.8% then +5.5% on top. ### Sparse attention (ATOM port) - Gluon-based paged sparse prefill (`minimax_sparse_ops/atom_prefill.py`), default on via `SGLANG_OPT_USE_ATOM_PREFILL`, with Triton fallback for unsupported shapes and a scratch-size cap that falls back rather than OOMs. - Score-only index kernel at every page size: the per-page slot addressing is now a `PER_PAGE_SLOTS` constexpr chosen from `block_size_k // page_size`, instead of gating the whole (~1.6x) kernel behind `page_size >= 16`. - Index top-k shared across every N sparse layers, `SGLANG_MINIMAX_M3_INDEX_TOPK_FREQ` (default 2, ROCm only, never under two-batch overlap) - it changes which KV blocks skip layers attend, so it is an accuracy knob. - Decode top-k written straight into the reuse buffer; per-forward caches keyed on the owning `ForwardBatch` so they are TBO-safe. - JIT radix top-k unblocked under CUDA graphs (`kMaxNumBlocks` 4096 -> 16384). ### Dense decode attention - ROCm decode-attention KV tile 32 -> 64 tokens and a software-pipelined KV loop (`num_stages` 2) for `Lk <= 128`: 690 -> 285 us/launch, ~+7% e2e. - Decode `kv_indices` build parallelized across sequence spans. - Skips redundant sparse KV-cache writes when fusion already populated the cache, and top-k id sanitization when EP is off. ### Defaults and memory accounting - On ROCm gfx950, `--prefill-attention-backend` defaults to `aiter` (ck-tile fmha) while decode stays on Triton. Decode on the AITER backend costs ~3 points on AIME25, so it is not defaulted. - Replaced the blanket `mem_fraction_static *= 0.85` for the AITER backend at `context_len > 8192` with an exact charge: the paged-decode split workspace is fp32 and linear in context length (~4 GiB at 128k) and is allocated after the KV pool, so `KVCacheConfigurator` now re-solves the budget once with the measured size (`aiter_attn_workspace_bytes`) subtracted. The old flat haircut over-reserved ~28 GB. - MiniMax-M3-VL gets the same ROCm shared-expert support; EP/DeepEP guards preserved. ### Launch recipes ### Higher-accuracy dense path Keeps dense weights on the native MXFP8 path with the original per-1×32 scales. ``` SGLANG_USE_AITER=1 \ sglang serve \ --trust-remote-code \ --model-path /persistent/models/MiniMax-M3-MXFP8 \ --reasoning-parser auto \ --tool-call-parser auto \ --tp 8 \ --quantization mxfp8 \ --moe-runner-backend aiter \ --fp8-gemm-backend bf16 \ --enable-aiter-allreduce-fusion \ --attention-backend triton \ --prefill-attention-backend aiter \ --dtype bfloat16 \ --chunked-prefill-size 32768 \ --mem-fraction-static 0.80 \ --host 0.0.0.0 \ --port 30000 ``` ### Fast decode path Converts dense weights to block-FP8 at load and selects the automatic block-FP8/PTPC dispatch. MoE remains on native MXFP8. ``` SGLANG_USE_AITER=1 \ SGLANG_FORCE_MXFP8_BLOCK_CONVERT_DENSE=1 \ sglang serve \ --trust-remote-code \ --model-path /persistent/models/MiniMax-M3-MXFP8 \ --reasoning-parser auto \ --tool-call-parser auto \ --tp 8 \ --quantization mxfp8 \ --moe-runner-backend aiter \ --fp8-gemm-backend auto \ --enable-aiter-allreduce-fusion \ --attention-backend triton \ --prefill-attention-backend aiter \ --dtype bfloat16 \ --chunked-prefill-size 32768 \ --mem-fraction-static 0.80 \ --host 0.0.0.0 \ --port 30000 ``` ## Accuracy Tests baseline ``` == gsm8k == 1319 examples (single-shot) | 227.1s | 1485 tok/s | 337K tokens * score = 88.55% stop_rate = 89.61% truncated_rate = 10.39% [warn: hitting max_tokens] error_rate = 0.00% ``` this pr ``` == gsm8k == 1319 examples (single-shot) | 119.9s | 2862 tok/s | 343K tokens * score = 88.55% stop_rate = 89.69% truncated_rate = 10.31% [warn: hitting max_tokens] error_rate = 0.00% ``` <!-- If this pull request affects model outputs (e.g., changes to the kernel or model forward code), provide accuracy test results. --> ## Speed Tests and Profiling MI350X, TP8, MXFP8 MiniMax-M3. ### Dense-path configurations (bs1 / il8192) | Configuration | Decode | Prefill | | |---|---:|---:|---| | Native MXFP8 dense, `--fp8-gemm-backend bf16` (higher-accuracy dense) | 131 tok/s | 22.1k tok/s | reference | | Dense block-convert only (`SGLANG_FORCE_MXFP8_BLOCK_CONVERT_DENSE=1`) | 92.5 tok/s | 29.9k tok/s | **+35% prefill, -30% decode** — the CK a8w8 blockscale kernel is a prefill kernel, ~2.5x worse than bf16 hipBLASLt at M=1 | | Block-convert + PTPC decode fast path + the rest of this PR (fast decode) | 169 tok/s | ~46k tok/s | **+29% decode, +2.1x prefill** vs the first row | The two rows the launch recipes above expose are rows 1 and 3; row 2 is why the skinny-M PTPC path exists at all. ### Concurrency sweep (TP8) | CC | baseline tok/s/user | baseline tok/s/GPU | high accuracy tok/s/user | high accuracy tok/s/GPU | |---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 1 | 49.8 | 6.2 | 131.1 | 16.4 | | 2 | 48.9 | 12.2 | 126.0 | 31.5 | | 4 | 47.9 | 23.9 | 120.5 | 60.3 | | 8 | 46.5 | 46.5 | 112.4 | 112.5 | | 16 | 42.0 | 83.9 | 92.9 | 186.1 | | 32 | 36.8 | 147.3 | 73.9 | 296.0 | | 64 | 30.9 | 247.3 | 57.1 | 457.3 | | 128 | - | - | 41.7 | 667.0 | | 256 | - | - | 29.0 | 929.9 | ### Long-context decode (bs16-32 / il80000) 1144 -> 2035 tok/s (13.98 -> 15.72 ms/step at bs32) across the MXFP8 decode-M cap (+14.2%), the router GEMV M-keyed configs (+5.5%), the fmoe atomic reduce pick (+4.3%), the dense decode-attention tile+pipelining (+3.6% and +7.2%), and the ATOM sparse port. ## Checklist - [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process). 2. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32509460767](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32509460767)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32509460240](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32509460240)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32509460649](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32509460649)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: Fix dp-attention + speculative decoding crashes in flashinfer MLA backend
signal.text: ## Motivation Running MLA models (e.g. DeepSeek-R1) with `--enable-dp-attention` together with NEXTN/EAGLE speculative decoding on the flashinfer backend crashes during CUDA graph capture / prefill. Plain dp-attention (no spec) and plain spec (no dp-attention) each work; only the combination breaks. Verified fixed on 4-node A100*8 **tp32 / dp4 / ep32** DeepSeek-R1-0528-bf16. ## Root causes Two independent upstream changes exposed latent invariant violations in the MLA backend: 1. **PR #20978** ("pad max-num-requests in decode cuda graph") made the max capture batch size round **up** to a multiple of `attn_tp_size` under dp-attention. That padded bs can now exceed the `req_to_token_pool.size` bound the MLA backend used to size its cuda-graph indptr buffers in `__init__`, so the `[: bs + 1]` slices silently truncated and flashinfer's `plan()` failed with an indptr size mismatch. 2. **The flashinfer version bump** (current requires 0.6.14) added a strict ragged-prefill check `q.shape[0] == qo_indptr[-1]`. Under dp-attention the per-rank input `q` is padded, but the per-request `seq_lens` are not, so `qo_indptr[-1]` (real tokens) falls short of `q.shape[0]` (padded) and the ragged wrapper rejects the extra rows. This addresses the same issue as PR https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/21452, except that PR only fixes the problem in flashinfer_backend.py for PCG and does not handle flashinfer_mla_backend.py. Note this strict check has two independent victims under dp-attention: the paged/ragged prefill updater (FlashInferMLAIndicesUpdaterPrefill, addressed by Change 3), and the chunked-prefix MHA path (FlashInferMhaChunkKVRunner, addressed by Change 4). The latter only triggers on prefill with a non-empty prefix (radix-cache hits), so it stays dormant until requests re-prefill cached prefixes — most reliably under memory pressure when the scheduler retracts and replays requests. A single DP group hitting it raises ValueError and deadlocks the other groups inside EP collectives until the scheduler watchdog fires (300s), so it surfaces as a watchdog timeout rather than a clean error. ## Changes All in `python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/flashinfer_mla_backend.py`. **1. `FlashInferMLAMultiStepDraftBackend.init_cuda_graph_state` — grow shared indptr buffers to the capture bound** Grow the shared `kv_indptr` / `q_indptr_decode` to `max_bs * topk + 1` when the padded capture bs exceeds the `__init__` bound, and pass them into each child backend via new `kv_indptr_buf` / `q_indptr_decode_buf` params. Fixes root cause 1. **2. `FlashInferMLAAttnBackend.init_cuda_graph_state` — accept & rebind the shared buffers** Add `kv_indptr_buf` / `q_indptr_decode_buf` params. When provided, rebind both `self.kv_indptr` / `self.q_indptr_decode` **and** the decode indices updater's cached references (`self.indices_updater_decode.kv_indptr` / `.q_indptr`) — the updater caches those references at construction, so rebinding only `self` would leave a stale, too-small buffer. **3. Prefill indices updater — dummy padding request for ragged prefill under dp-attention** - `FlashInferMLAAttnBackend.init_forward_metadata`: compute `padded_num_tokens = extend_num_tokens` and `real_num_tokens = sum(extend_seq_lens_cpu)` (both host-side ints, guarded on `*_cpu is not None`), pass them through. - `FlashInferMLAIndicesUpdaterPrefill.update` / `call_begin_forward`: thread the two params through; in the non-spec ragged branch, when `padded_num_tokens > real_num_tokens`, append one dummy request to `qo_indptr` / `kv_indptr` / `kv_indices` covering the padding tokens (dummy kv entries point at slot 0 so its softmax stays finite). This satisfies the strict `q.shape[0] == qo_indptr[-1]` check without touching the causal masks of real requests, mirroring the piecewise-cuda-graph padding pattern in `flashinfer_backend.py` (see #26016). Fixes root cause 2. - The spec branch (`spec_info is not None`) needs no dummy request: those callers (target-verify) all set `use_ragged=False` and feed the paged wrapper, which has no `q.shape == qo_indptr[-1]` check. **4. FlashInferMhaChunkKVRunner — handle dp-attention padding in the chunked-prefix MHA path** This runner builds its own qo_indptr from the real per-request extend lens in update_wrapper() and never passes through call_begin_forward, so the dummy-request fix in Change 3 does not reach it. A dummy request is also not usable here: the chunk wrappers are ragged and a dummy could only be given an empty kv range, producing lse = -inf rows that then feed merge_state_v2. Instead, plan the wrappers with the real token count and record it (self.real_num_tokens, set only when extend_num_tokens > sum(extend_seq_lens_cpu), both host-side ints guarded on *_cpu is not None). In forward(), slice q down to real_num_tokens before the ragged run, then zero-pad the output (and lse, when returned) back up to the padded length. Zeros stay finite through merge_state_v2, and the padding rows are discarded downstream anyway. k/v need no slicing — flashinfer only checks q.shape[0] and never indexes past kv_indptr. Fixes root cause 2 on the chunked-prefix path. ## Verification - 4-node tp32/dp4/ep32 DeepSeek-R1-0528-bf16 + EAGLE (NEXTN, steps 2 / topk 1 / draft-tokens 3): server starts, CUDA graph capture + decode replay + spec decode all pass (`cuda graph: True, accept len ~2.3`). - Single / 8-way concurrent generation, and `repetition_penalty` / `frequency_penalty` / `presence_penalty` sampling all return correctly with no server-side errors. - gsm8k accuracy regression: **96.2%** (0% invalid, 1319 questions, 5-shot, thinking on) — on par with the 95.8% baseline, no regression. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #29495522440](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/29495522440)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #29495521900](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/29495521900)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: fix(cpu): avoid GPU-only MoE top-k kernels on non-AMX CPUs

signal.title: [Model] Complete dots.note.omni support with native encoders, video preprocessing, and MTP decoding
signal.text: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation Merge dots.note.omni model ## Modifications This PR completes the SGLang integration of dots.note.omni, including: - Native in-process vision and audio encoders - Train-consistent native video preprocessing - Full-sharing MTP/NextN speculative decoding - DP/TP/EP execution support, including overlap scheduling - Correct KV-cache sizing for the hybrid sliding-window draft model ## How dots.note.omni differs from existing models dots.note.omni does not fit several assumptions made by existing multimodal and speculative-decoding paths. ### Multimodal architecture Unlike models that reuse standard Hugging Face vision/audio encoders, dots.note.omni uses: - A custom MoE vision transformer - A Whisper-derived audio encoder with a model-specific convolutional frontend and token-length calculation - Model-specific image and audio placeholder expansion - **A native video pipeline that jointly samples and interleaves frames, timestamps, and audio segments under a token budget** The video representation must match the training-time flattening algorithm. Applying a generic uniform-frame video processor changes the modality ordering, sampling strategy, and token allocation, which causes an inference/training mismatch. ### Language-model attention (**Introduce dots_hybrid_attn_backend**) The dots3 language model combines: - MLA - Full-attention and sliding-window layers with different attention geometry - Optional DSA indexing on full-attention layers - Head-wise or element-wise attention gates Therefore, its full-attention and SWA layers cannot always share the same attention path or KV-cache accounting. ### MTP structure the standard single-layer EAGLE/NextN execution path with an ordinary SWA-capacity, MLA-based draft layer. ## Model-specific changes ### Native vision and audio towers This PR migrates the dots.note.omni encoders into SGLang: - Adds the dots MoE ViT implementation - Adds the dots audio model and Whisper-derived speech encoder - Uses SGLang FA3 and fused MoE kernels - Loads encoder weights directly from the model directory - Removes runtime imports and compatibility shims for mm_encoder_server - Honors --language-only, allowing encoder/LLM disaggregation and text-only deployments without loading the multimodal towers ### Train-consistent video preprocessing This PR vendors the required dots video flattening pipeline and integrates it with the OpenAI chat API. The processor: - Accepts a native video_url - Decodes and processes remote video payloads entirely in memory - Uses the tokenizer loaded from the served model - Produces interleaved timestamp, image, and audio content matching training - Uses a deterministic seed derived from the video and question - Reserving the context budget for each video input - Falls back to visual-only processing if audio would exceed the configured token budget - Records per-request preprocessing latency The following request-scoped controls are added: | Field | Purpose | |-------|---------| | seq | Total sequence budget used by the video flattener | | audio_cap | Maximum fraction of the input budget assigned to audio | | audio_sr | Audio sample rate | | k_mode | Deterministic evaluation/sampling mode | These options are request-scoped because evaluation jobs with different context budgets may share one server. Current native-video limitations: - One video per request - A native video cannot currently be mixed with separate image or audio inputs in the same request ### Full-sharing MTP/NextN A dedicated Dot3NoteForCausalLMNextN draft model is added. For draft-model loading, the dots3 configuration is rewritten before attention shapes and KV-cache geometry are derived: - The draft architecture becomes Dot3NoteForCausalLMNextN - Exactly one recursively shared MTP layer is exposed - The layer uses the dots3 SWA attention geometry - A checkpoint-provided MTP embedding is retained when present - The target LM head is shared with the draft model Target verification and draft extension use the paged, absorbed SWA-MLA path. The expanded SWA-MHA path remains limited to prefill, where its logical-tail metadata is available. ## Shared SGLang changes and why they are needed The changes below are implemented in shared infrastructure because the underlying correctness conditions are not specific to one model name. ### 1. Hybrid SWA draft KV-cache accounting The existing hybrid pool configurator charged all EAGLE/NextN draft layers as full-attention layers. That is incorrect for dots3 because its shared draft layer is an ordinary SWA layer with: - SWA latent-vector geometry - SWA token capacity rather than full-attention capacity The speculative auxiliary configuration now records how many draft layers are SWA layers. The hybrid pool configurator separately accounts for: - Full-capacity full-attention draft layers - Ordinary SWA draft layers using the target SWA capacity - Full-capacity SWA-shaped draft layers, such as the existing Inkling case This prevents both under-allocation and unnecessary loss of target KV-cache capacity. The logic is generic for hybrid-SWA models using EAGLE-family draft models. ### 2. DP dummy-row normalization for overlap MTP With DP attention and overlap scheduling, an idle rank must still participate in MLP and attention collectives. SGLang creates dummy rows for this purpose. For speculative decoding, attention metadata may be planned before DP synchronization adds those rows. This previously left the following structures with inconsistent request dimensions: - GPU and CPU extend-length metadata - Prefix-length metadata - Draft cache locations - Positions and hidden states - Dense attention page tables - Draft logits returned to the speculative worker This PR normalizes speculative dummy rows before draft buffers are allocated, keeps the CPU and GPU metadata aligned, preserves the normalized output rows on idle ranks, and exposes a backend hook to refresh row-dependent attention metadata after DP padding. The backend hook defaults to a no-op. Only backends whose metadata can be safely rebuilt opt in, so pre-planned sparse/DSA schedules remain untouched. ### 3. Attention page-table normalization A shared helper is added to align a pre-planned page table with a DP-normalized batch. It truncates extra rows or appends zero-valued dummy rows. Both the dots hybrid backend and the FA3 SWA-MLA fallback use this helper. This avoids model-name checks and makes the invariant explicit at the attention-backend boundary. ### 4. FA3 SWA-MLA fallback dots3's MTP layer is both SWA-shaped and MLA-based. Target verification and draft extension already have a paged latent KV view, while the existing expanded SWA-MHA path is designed for prefill. FA3 therefore gains an absorbed SWA-MLA fallback that consumes the SWA page table and latent KV cache directly. This is exposed as a backend capability and selected by the model only when available. ### 5. OpenAI request and internal request plumbing The dots video controls and the unrendered user question are propagated through: - ChatCompletionRequest - OpenAI chat serving - GenerateReqInput - The dots multimodal processor The original question is required because the training-consistent adapter uses it for deterministic sampling and cache-key construction. It cannot reliably be recovered from the rendered chat prompt, which also contains template, role, and system tokens. The new fields retain defaults and are only consumed by the dots native-video path. ### 6. Encoder/LLM disaggregation validation Dot3NoteForCausalLM is added to the architectures allowed to use --encoder-only and --language-only. The model itself skips vision and audio tower construction in language-only mode. This avoids consuming memory needed by the language model and enables the standard encoder-disaggregation deployment pattern. ## Tests The PR adds coverage for the shared correctness changes: - The DSA K-only rotary path does not alias query and key inputs - Draft-extend dummy requests keep CPU and GPU length metadata aligned - Idle speculative batches retain normalized dummy logits and hidden states - Hybrid-SWA draft layers use SWA geometry and capacity during KV-cache sizing An EP8/TP8/DP8 launch script is also included for dots.note.omni with: - DeepEP - NEXTN speculative decoding - FA3 draft attention - Optional overlap scheduling - Optional language-only mode - Optional DSA and speculative-decoding switches ## Accuracy Tests <!-- If this pull request affects model outputs (e.g., changes to the kernel or model forward code), provide accuracy test results. --> ## Speed Tests and Profiling <!-- If this pull request impacts inference speed, provide benchmarking and profiling results. --> ## Checklist - [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. signal.title: [XPU][model]: Intel XPU support for encoder embeddings (bge/NomicBERT/ModernBERT) + InternVL3_5
signal.text: Intel XPU support for four embedding / vision models, combined for review: `BAAI/bge-base-en-v1.5`, `nomic-ai/nomic-embed-text-v1.5`, `ibm-granite/granite-embedding-english-r2`, and `OpenGVLab/InternVL3_5-30B-A3B`. ## Motivation - **bge-base-en-v1.5** (`BertModel`) loads on XPU but returns wrong embeddings — SciFact 0, cosine vs HF 0.26-0.47. Two XPU-specific bugs in shared code affect every BERT/RoBERTa encoder on `intel_xpu`. - **nomic-embed-text-v1.5** (`NomicBertModel`) had no SGLang model, so the Transformers fallback raised `NotImplementedError: get_input_embeddings ...`. - **granite-embedding-english-r2** (`ModernBertModel`) fell back and crashed in the forward pass (`RuntimeError` in `set_kv_buffer`) — a bidirectional encoder routed through the paged decoder KV cache. - **InternVL3_5-30B-A3B** crashed at load (`AttributeError: 'InternVLChatConfig' object has no attribute 'num_experts'`) and, once loading, hung/crashed the vision encoder under concurrent multimodal at tp>1 (Level Zero USM-memcpy deadlock on a per-block device->host `.item()`; DEVICE_LOST batching ViT tiles). ## Modifications Encoder embeddings: - `layers/attention/xpu_backend.py`: honor `AttentionType.ENCODER_ONLY` / `DECODER_BIDIRECTIONAL` (was `causal = not is_cross_attention`). - `managers/{scheduler,tokenizer_manager,utils}.py`: preserve the trailing separator token when truncating over-length embedding inputs (gated on `not is_generation`). - `models/nomic_bert.py` (new): `NomicBertModel` — RoPE, SwiGLU, post-norm; SDPA. - `models/modernbert.py` (new): `ModernBertModel` — RoPE, local/global attn, GeGLU; SDPA. InternVL: - `models/internvl.py`: read `num_experts` from `config.llm_config`; pass the host-side `max_seqlen` into `prepare_vision_attention_metadata`; chunk the ViT forward to `SGLANG_VIT_MAX_TILES` tiles on XPU. - `layers/attention/vision.py`: `VisionIntelXPUAttention` uses the metadata's host `max_seqlen` instead of re-deriving it from GPU `cu_seqlens` per block. - `environ.py`: add `SGLANG_VIT_MAX_TILES` (default 12). All XPU paths are guarded by `is_xpu()`; the encoder truncation change is embedding-only; decoder generation is unchanged. ## Accuracy Test Intel XPU (Arc Pro B60), vs the HuggingFace reference. Encoder — MTEB SciFact NDCG@10 (300 queries / 5183 corpus), tp-1: | Model | cosine vs HF | SciFact NDCG@10 | HF ref | |---|---|---|---| | bge-base-en-v1.5 | 0.99997 | 0.6981 | 0.7387 | | nomic-embed-text-v1.5 | 1.00000 | 0.6803 | (prefix-sensitive) | | granite-r2 (ModernBERT) | 1.000000 fp32 / >=0.9999 bf16 | 0.6720 | 0.6815 | InternVL3_5-30B-A3B — tp-4 (61.7 GB bf16, ~14.43 GB/rank): loads with 0 skipped params, MoE initialized, multimodal smoke (red image -> "Red"); P1 lmms-eval: **mathvision_testmini 38.2, mmmu_val 27.4**. All four load with 0 skipped params. ## Speed Test and Profiling No change to existing code paths. Encoder fixes flip a boolean / run once per over-length request; the two new encoders are small SDPA models (no KV cache). InternVL removes a per-block device->host sync on XPU and bounds the ViT forward; non-XPU paths are unchanged. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32470005122](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32470005122)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32470004786](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32470004786)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32470004891](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32470004891)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [LMCache] Register fused MLA KV buffer over multi-process
signal.text: ## Motivation The SGLang → LMCache multi-process (MP) offload path only handles MHA KV pools. For MLA models (DeepSeek V2/V3/R1, GLM), `LMCRadixCache` probed `k_buffer` / `v_buffer` via `getattr`, but `MLATokenToKVPool` fuses K and V into a single latent `kv_buffer` per layer and exposes no `k_buffer` — so enabling LMCache on an MLA model failed to register the KV cache correctly. This is the SGLang half of a two-repo change. The LMCache companion is LMCache/LMCache#4695, which teaches the LMCache MP daemon to accept the fused single-buffer (empty-V) layout that this PR sends. ## Modifications - `python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/storage/lmcache/lmc_radix_cache.py`: replace the `getattr(k_buffer/v_buffer)` private-buffer probing with a `_select_register_pools(kvcache)` helper that returns the `(k_pool, v_pool)` to register: - **MHA**: `(k_buffer, v_buffer)` — unchanged. - **MLA**: `(kv_buffer, [])` — register the fused latent buffer as K with an empty V pool; the LMCache daemon detects the single-buffer layout. - **DSA** (`DSATokenToKVPool`, a subclass of `MLATokenToKVPool`, so checked first): `NotImplementedError` — the separate indexer cache register path is a deliberate follow-up, not silently mis-registered. - `test/srt/mem_cache/test_select_register_pools.py`: unit tests covering the MHA / MLA / DSA selection (CPU-only, spec-mocked pools — no KV allocation). No change to model forward or kernels, so no accuracy/speed impact. ## Accuracy Tests N/A — offload-path plumbing only; does not touch model outputs. ## Speed Tests and Profiling N/A. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the Format code with pre-commit. - [x] Add unit tests according to the Run and add unit tests. - [ ] Update documentation. - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results. - [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32507760187](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32507760187)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32507760082](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32507760082)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32507760080](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32507760080)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: fix: skip timed out encoder requests
signal.text: ## Summary - skip timed-out encoder requests before worker broadcast and encoder execution - re-check request liveness after acquiring the encoder dispatch lock - add a CPU-only regression test for queued request timeout ## Motivation `EncoderScheduler.submit` cancels the request future when the per-request timeout expires, but the `PendingRequest` remains in the queue. A later batch can therefore still broadcast and execute work for a caller that has already timed out. This is especially harmful for encoder disaggregation because the late work can consume encoder capacity and produce late transfer-side effects. Fixes #35891 ## Tests - `PYTHONPYCACHEPREFIX=/tmp/sglang-pycache python3 -m py_compile python/sglang/srt/disaggregation/encode_server.py test/registered/unit/disaggregation/test_encoder_scheduler.py` - `git diff --check` - Focused pytest was attempted but collection is blocked in this environment because `triton` and `torch` are unavailable. - Ruff reports two pre-existing violations elsewhere in `encode_server.py`.
signal.author: hsusul

signal.title: EncoderScheduler dispatches requests after request timeout
signal.text:
## Problem

The encoder scheduler cancels a timed-out request future, but leaves the corresponding PendingRequest in pending_queue. When the batch worker later dequeues it, the request is still broadcast to tensor-parallel workers and passed to the encoder even though its caller has already timed out.

## Reproduction

With EncoderScheduler running, block the first batch_encode call, submit a second request, and let the second request exceed SGLANG_ENCODER_REQ_TIMEOUT. The second future is cancelled, but the worker still dispatches that request after the first batch completes.

## Expected behavior

A request whose waiting future has been cancelled or completed should be removed from dispatchable work before broadcast and encoder execution.

## Fix

The accompanying branch filters completed futures before dispatch, re-checks after acquiring the dispatch lock, and skips completed per-request work. It adds a CPU-only regression test.

## Environment

This is a Python/backend scheduling issue and does not require GPU hardware to reproduce at the scheduler seam.
signal.author: hsusul

signal.title: [NPU] [Diffusion] Fix critical Ascend NPU Diffusion regression/bugs & restore 2-NPU CI testcase
signal.text: ## Motivation Restore Ascend/NPU packed Ring Attention, 2-NPU diffusion CI suite, fix NPU correctness, runtime, and CI regressions exposed by recent Ring, SRT-CLIP, residency, and MOVA changes. After [#35004](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/35004), diffusion can import SRT CLIP code and execute SRT `init_npu_backend()`. Importing `torch_npu.contrib.transfer_to_npu` inside a native NPU diffusion process globally rewrites CUDA-facing APIs/device arguments and can alter runtime feature detection and kernel selection. `allow_internal_format=True` is also known to regress unquantized diffusion performance; the earlier Wan regression in [#20533](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/20533), fixed by [#20684](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/20684), increased `DecodingStage` from **6.1889 s to 11.76 s (+90.0%, 1.90x slower)**. The packed-attention implementation is extracted from the Ascend work in [#33569](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33569). ## Modifications - **Packed varlen / Ring Attention.** [#33327](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33327) extended Qwen to tail-padded Ring and fixed `u=1, r>1` replicated-token semantics, exposing the shared packed `flash_attn_varlen_func` path on NPU. Add an Ascend implementation backed by `npu_fused_infer_attention_score` (`TND`) with independent Q/K packed lengths, boundary validation, empty/non-contiguous handling, LSE normalization, and `AscendFlashAttnImpl.forward_varlen`. Unsupported FlashAttention options fail explicitly. - **Diffusion NPU runtime isolation.** Keep the SRT CUDA-compatibility layer out of diffusion: when `sglang.multimodal_gen` is loaded, do not import `torch_npu.contrib.transfer_to_npu` and do not enable `torch_npu.npu.config.allow_internal_format`. Preserve the existing `torch.cuda.is_available=False` re-mock on the SRT path after `transfer_to_npu`. `jit_compile=False` remains unchanged. - **MOVA 2-NPU correctness.** [#31453](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/31453) left a contiguous-layout assumption after attention. Multi-NPU attention may return a non-contiguous tensor, so use `reshape()` instead of `view()`. - **Host-memory accounting.** [#35641](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/35641) introduced storage-based module sizing for host-memory budgeting. Skip tensors whose storage access raises `RuntimeError` instead of failing memory planning; add focused unit coverage. - **NPU CI / GT.** - Restore the 2-NPU diffusion suite on `linux-aarch64-a3-800t-16`. - Split both 1-NPU and 2-NPU suites into two partitions. - Run GT generation on the A3-800T runner families. - Make GT jobs check out the requested `workflow_dispatch` ref. - Retry transient HTTP/image-decoding failures while downloading GT. - Update the NPU GT revision to `8e3d717e65fb87339c2974382a092a731669f884`. - **NPU dependencies.** Pin `sgl-kernel-npu` to `2026.8.13` and install the packaged `attentions` wheel in NPU CI/Docker; update release Docker pins accordingly. - **Performance baselines.** Refresh affected FLUX.2 text-encoding, ERNIE timestep-preparation, and LTX-2 connector/decoding baselines plus partition-duration estimates for the current A3-800T / auto-residency environment. Related residency policy: [#34615](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/34615). These are CI baseline updates, not algorithmic speedups. ## Accuracy Tests - NPU diffusion GT was regenerated successfully after the Ring semantic changes and A3-800T CI migration: [Generate Diffusion CI Ground Truth #32478548704](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32478548704). - Qwen Ring keeps the corrected semantics from #33327; no consistency thresholds are relaxed. - Runtime isolation changes backend initialization/dispatch only; #20684 reported no accuracy impact from disabling the problematic internal-format behavior. - The restored 2-NPU suite exercises the packed Ring path. - Invalid-storage host-memory handling has dedicated unit coverage. ## Speed Tests and Profiling The runtime fix prevents diffusion from inheriting SRT's global CUDA-compatibility monkey patches and `allow_internal_format=True`. ## Checklist - signal.title: [AMD][DCP] Skip unused QuickAllReduce allocation for DCP groups
signal.text: ## Motivation On ROCm, `GroupCoordinator` currently initializes QuickAllReduce whenever custom all-reduce is enabled. That is useful for TP, but current DCP communication paths do not dispatch to QuickAllReduce: - `ag_rs`: all-gather plus reduce-scatter for MLA, or an FP32 all-reduce for MHA. - `a2a` / `fi_a2a`: all-to-all. In a Kimi-K3 TP8/DCP8 profile on MI350X, constructing the DCP QuickAllReduce communicator reserved 4.002 GiB per GPU. Across 1,152 recorded rank-0 DCP collective dispatches, QuickAllReduce was selected zero times. TP QuickAllReduce remains useful and must stay enabled. Related to #29736. ## Modifications - Add an optional `use_quick_allreduce` control to `GroupCoordinator` and `init_model_parallel_group`. - Preserve the existing behavior by default: the new option inherits `use_custom_allreduce` when unspecified. - Disable QuickAllReduce only for the DCP group. - Keep the AITER custom-all-reduce and PyNccl setup unchanged. - Add a unit test that verifies DCP opts out while TP retains the default behavior. ## Accuracy Tests This does not change model math or the collective selected by current DCP paths. The targeted construction test passes: ``` 1 passed, 5 deselected ``` ## Speed Tests and Profiling This PR targets static memory rather than latency. Measured DCP communicator initialization on MI350X: | Component | Reserved per GPU | | --- | ---: | | PyNccl | 1.883 GiB | | AITER custom all-reduce | 3.002 GiB | | QuickAllReduce | 4.002 GiB | QuickAllReduce had zero selections in the recorded DCP dispatches, so this change reclaims the 4.002 GiB DCP allocation without removing TP QuickAllReduce. ## Checklist - [x] Ran pre-commit on the changed files. - [x] Added a focused unit test. - [x] No documentation change is required; the default API behavior is preserved. - [x] No model kernel or output math is changed. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32466886861](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32466886861)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32466886581](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32466886581)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32466886845](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32466886845)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->
