signal.title: Rust Tree Core with Full/SWA/Mamba Components
signal.text: ## Motivation UnifiedTreeCoreInterface support in Rust (focus on FULL component-only in this PR for early review feedbacks) ## Motivation The Unified Radix Cache was split so the tree state machine lives behind `UnifiedTreeCoreInterface`, selected by `SGLANG_UNIFIED_RADIX_TREE_CORE_BACKEND` (default `python`). This PR adds a Rust implementation of that interface as an in-tree backend registered under `rust`, covering the Full attention component. The tree core does the per-request radix walks, lock bookkeeping, and eviction scans on the scheduler's critical path; moving it to Rust takes that work off the GIL and smooths tail latency, while cache orchestration (pools, controller, action application) stays in Python. **Review guide**: the PR is two commits. The first seeds the three main Rust files with their python counterparts commented out; the second replaces them with the Rust implementation, so its diff reads as the python-to-rust translation side by side. Files without a direct python counterpart arrive as new files in the second commit. ## Modifications ### `rust/mem-cache/` — the tree core crate **Tree state machine** - `src/unified_tree_core.rs` — match/insert walks (resumable inserts with action barriers), lock APIs, device/host eviction walks, tombstone-chain deletion, HiCache backup/load-back/prefetch specs, and the sanity checker. - `src/node.rs` — the tree node: per-(component × tier) value slots and child edges keyed `(namespace, page key)`, mirroring `RadixKey.child_key`. - `src/node_arena.rs` — node storage: freelist-recycled slots behind monotonic never-recycled `NodeId` handles, with a single root serving every namespace. - `src/value.rs` — the `NodeId`/`NodeIdx_` handle types and per-slot value state. **Keys and hashing** - `src/key.rs` — the child-key trait over unigram (`Vec<i64>`) and bigram/EAGLE (`(i64, i64)`) page keys. - `src/hash.rs` — per-page SHA-256 hash chains, bit-identical to the python/native hasher. **Eviction machinery** - `src/unified_lru_list.rs` — intrusive per-slot LRU lists with lock-aware walkers. - `src/evictable_node_set.rs` — O(1) evictable-leaf sets (swap-remove vector plus a slot lookup table). - `src/eviction_strategy.rs` — LRU/FIFO/FILO priority keys for the eviction heap. **Components** - `src/components/mod.rs` — the `TreeComponent` trait the per-attention components implement, plus shared dispatch helpers. - `src/components/full.rs` — the Full attention component: lock walks, eviction, and transfer commits. Only the `[Full]` set is enabled; SWA and Mamba follow later. - `src/component_type.rs` — the `ComponentType` boundary enum (`FULL`/`SWA`/`MAMBA` values shared with python). **Boundary** - `src/python_bindings.rs` — the PyO3 binding exposing unigram and bigram tree cores; component sets other than `[Full]` are rejected with a clear error. - `src/events.rs` — KV cache events (`BlockStored`/`BlockRemoved`/`AllBlocksCleared`) for cache-aware routing. - `src/error.rs` — typed tree-core errors. **Crate scaffolding** - `Cargo.toml` / `README.md` / `src/lib.rs` — standalone crate (links libtorch via `tch`; PyO3 behind a default feature, so `cargo test` runs `--no-default-features`), docs, and module wiring. - `src/tests/` — the unit suite mirroring `src/` one file per module (566 tests, including a randomized multi-namespace op-sequence fuzz with per-step sanity checks). ### `python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/rust_tree_core/` — the backend package - `__init__.py` — registers the `rust` backend factory; the extension import stays inside the factory so unselected installs pay nothing. - `adapter.py` — `RustUnifiedTreeCore`, satisfying `UnifiedTreeCoreInterface` over the binding (tagged-tuple action/transfer marshaling at the boundary). - `extension.py` — build-and-load shim: compiles the crate with cargo on first use, deriving libtorch and the Python headers from the running interpreter's torch install, and rpaths torch/lib into the cdylib. ### Wiring and tests - `python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/unified_cache/tree_core_registry.py` — `SGLANG_UNIFIED_RADIX_TREE_CORE_BACKEND=rust` lazy-registers the in-tree backend on first lookup (no import-order dependence). - `test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_rust_tree_core.py` — end-to-end smoke through the compiled extension: registry resolution, insert/match round trip, lock accounting, and namespace isolation; module-skips when cargo is absent. ## Verification - `cargo test --no-default-features`: 566 passed. - Smoke suite: 4 passed end-to-end, including the first-use cargo build path. ## Perf Measurement & Accuracy TBD ## Review and Merge Process 1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process). 2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers. 3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so. - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci` 4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32459402669](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32459402669)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32459402289](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32459402289)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32459402548](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32459402548)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: WIP: [MiniMax-M3][AMD] Fix EAGLE3 TARGET_VERIFY extend_seq_lens
signal.text: **This is work in progress as output with EAGLE3 is garbled but at least server starts.** ## Motivation MiniMax-M3 EAGLE3 speculative decoding **crashes on AMD/ROCm** (and possibly CUDA GPU) because the model's sparse attention backend reconstructs missing `extend_seq_lens` metadata during EAGLE TARGET_VERIFY only when `self.is_npu` is true. A fix for Ascend NPU was introduced in [#32941](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32941); the same issue affects other GPUs, but the fix is only for NPU. ## Modifications A small modification in `python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/minimax_sparse_backend.py` extends the NPU fix to other architectures. With this patch, the server stays up and serves requests. ## Validation (local, WIP) - Hardware: 8× AMD MI350X (gfx950), ROCm 7.2.x - Target: `MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3-MXFP8` (`--quantization mxfp8`) - Draft: `Inferact/MiniMax-M3-EAGLE3` - Flags: `--speculative-algorithm EAGLE3`, `--disable-cuda-graph`, `--disable-radix-cache`, `--attention-backend aiter`, `--tp 8` - Unpatched `main`: crash on TARGET_VERIFY - With this patch: server stays up; completions succeed (EAGLE output quality still under investigation) ## Test plan - [ ] MiniMax-M3 + EAGLE3 on ROCm (MXFP8 and/or bf16) - [ ] Server survives `/health`, `/model_info`, and `/v1/completions` verify path - [ ] NPU regression: Ascend MiniMax-M3 EAGLE verify unchanged - [ ] Non-spec baseline unchanged ## Related - #32941 — NPU-only `_resolve_extend_meta` reconstruction - #28715 — MiniMax-M3 + `set_eagle3_layers_to_capture` Made with [Cursor](https://cursor.com) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32505348142](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32505348142)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32505348037](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32505348037)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32505348145](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32505348145)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: feat: add Mooncake GPU-direct SpecForge capture
signal.text: ## Summary - capture auxiliary and final hidden states on GPU for per-request SpecForge requests - publish source buffers through Mooncake nvlink, nvlink_intra, or rdma transports - keep hidden-state payloads off host memory and return only GPU buffer descriptors - retain source buffers until consumer release acknowledgement, with pending-batch and resident-byte bounds - force MNNVL for NVL72, intra-node NVLink for H200-class nodes, and HCA for RDMA ## Hardware benchmark Run on 2026-08-21 UTC. The target host had 8x NVIDIA H200 (driver 580.105.08) split into two TP4 replicas. A second H200 host ran the consumer on one GPU. The target was Qwen3.8-27B-FP8 with DSpark taps `[5, 19, 33, 47, 61]`; capture used Mooncake RDMA and a 32 GiB resident cap per replica. The repository base does not expose the GPU-direct capture endpoint, so the same protocol cannot run there. The controlled comparison uses the first functional implementation (`dbfed03cd8d8`) as the baseline and PR head (`60e519391d59`) as the post-change target. SpecForge was fixed at `9ce0b698c98c`. Each reported value is the median of two completed 512-sample runs with `max_length=8192`, concurrency 64, lease 8, prompt prefetch 4, ingest batch 128, least-tokens replica routing, length-bucketed requests, and overlapped capture/materialization. | Metric | Baseline | PR head | Change | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | Capture throughput (samples/s) | 52.1199 | 67.2924 | +29.11% | | Active RDMA materialization (samples/s) | 108.8696 | 120.6860 | +10.85% | | Pipeline throughput (samples/s) | 48.6419 | 61.9381 | +27.33% | | Pipeline elapsed (s) | 10.5319 | 8.2663 | -21.51% | | Durable cleanup (s) | 0.9571 | 0.0056 | -99.41% | Every completed run produced and removed all 512 samples, transferred 40,503,867,376 bytes, and reported zero host payload bytes. After each PR-head run, both control endpoints reported `resident_samples=0`, `resident_bytes=0`, `reserved_bytes=0`, `published_samples == released_samples`, and the full 32 GiB arena free. The 1024-sample stress case was excluded from throughput statistics: this benchmark retains every sample until its final durable acknowledgement, so two 32 GiB replicas cannot hold the full retained set. Both baseline and head reached the configured per-replica resident cap and returned `GPU-direct capture residency ... exceeds 34359738368 bytes`. Builds, unit tests, integration tests, and CI were not run as part of this hardware benchmark. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: **Missing `run-ci` label** -- add it to run CI tests.<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: **Blocked** -- `run-ci` is required first.<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:heavy_minus_sign: **No AMD PR run found for this commit**.<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [Feature] Realtime ASR: bounded long audio with encoder-window caching
signal.text: ## Summary This PR adds an experimental, opt-in realtime ASR path for long audio items. It bounds the acoustic work submitted by each update, reuses completed audio encoder windows through SGLang's existing multimodal cache, and publishes decoder progress through the existing append-only transcription delta event. The current realtime path re-submits all audio accumulated for an item every 2 seconds. This preserves full acoustic context, but both prefill and memory grow with the session. On long items, per-update latency eventually dominates realtime playback. For Qwen3-ASR-0.6B, the opt-in path works as follows: 1. Keep the existing cumulative path through the first 60 seconds. 2. On the first update after 60 seconds, establish a one-way handoff from the cumulative transcript to encoder-window continuation. 3. Keep at most eight complete model-native 8-second audio windows plus the current incomplete tail in each later request. 4. Reuse complete-window embeddings through the existing MM cache; always recompute the mutable tail. 5. Carry older semantic context in a bounded, confirmed transcript prefix and generate only the new suffix. 6. Stream decoder progress through the existing `conversation.item.input_audio_transcription.delta` event. No client schema or new event type is added. The default remains cumulative. Encoder windowing is currently enabled only for an explicitly declared English session on a local single-GPU runtime. Unsupported models and languages keep the cumulative path. Enabling encoder windowing with an incompatible distributed or disaggregated topology fails during server startup instead of silently changing the requested strategy. ## Relationship to RFC #22474 This PR builds on [RFC #22474](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/22474) rather than defining a second realtime ASR protocol. - **M1 transport and lifecycle are reused unchanged.** M1 landed in #22848 and introduced `WS /v1/realtime`, `session.update`, incremental PCM append, commit/clear, multi-item sessions, and the existing delta/completed/error event envelopes. This PR does not add a client event, response type, or replacement-transcript protocol. - **This PR implements the measured long-audio part of M2.** The RFC identifies repeated processing of accumulated audio as the main long-session cost and calls for profiling before cache changes. The results below show that the cumulative path becomes impractical for long items, so the opt-in path bounds acoustic context and reuses completed encoder windows through the existing MM embedding cache. - **It also implements the RFC's M3 direction within each backend request.** Generation runs with streaming enabled, but the endpoint publishes only append-safe progress through the existing `transcription.delta` event. This is stable delta streaming, not a new one-event-per-token wire contract. The implementation deliberately narrows the RFC's earlier cache discussion. The RFC's M2 sketch focused first on RadixCache feasibility and listed generic bidirectional encoder-output caching as out of scope. Radix prefix reuse alone cannot avoid re-encoding a growing audio item. This PR permits encoder reuse only when the multimodal processor declares independently encodable window geometry; otherwise the realtime item remains on the cumulative path. The RFC's architectural boundary is preserved: the realtime layer owns the WebSocket/session lifecycle, adapters and processors declare model capability, and the existing MM scheduler/cache performs best-effort reuse. This PR does not introduce an engine-level realtime session, scheduler-owned ASR state, or persistent per-session GPU state. ## Request flow ```mermaid flowchart TD A[Client appends PCM] --> B[2-second inference boundary] B --> C{Received audio over 60 seconds?} C -- No --> D[Submit audio from 0 to current end] D --> E[Cumulative transcript reconciliation] C -- Yes, first handoff --> F[Submit full audio once] F --> G[Create bounded confirmed-text prefix] C -- Yes, steady state --> H[Choose 8-second-aligned rolling range] G --> H H --> I[Up to 8 complete windows plus mutable tail] I --> J[Complete windows: existing MM embedding cache] I --> K[Mutable tail: encode, do not retain] J --> L[Decoder prefix plus new suffix generation] K --> L E --> M[Reconcile decoder updates] L --> M M --> N[Emit only append-safe delta text] N --> O[Existing transcription.delta event] O --> P[Advance absolute PCM cursors and compact old audio] ``` The first windowed request intentionally includes the full handoff audio. Once the handoff succeeds, steady-state requests retain no more than 64 seconds of complete encoder windows plus an incomplete tail shorter than 8 seconds. For example, a steady-state request near 130 seconds looks like this: ```text Older audio represented by confirmed text | v text: [bounded decoder prefix] audio: [w0][w1] ... [w7][tail] encoder: [cache hits / misses][encode] decoder: [prefix] + [rolling acoustic context] -> new suffix only wire: -> append-only stable deltas ``` ## Encoder-window reuse Qwen3-ASR declares its independent encoder geometry in the multimodal processor. For Qwen3-ASR-0.6B, one complete window is 8 seconds and produces 104 encoder tokens. The generic audio-window builder: - extracts complete windows independently from the mutable tail; - expands one audio placeholder into per-window token ranges; - hashes the exact feature, attention mask, modality, and token geometry; - marks complete windows as cacheable; - marks the mutable tail `use_embedding_cache=False`; and - provides an explicit encoder batch key for variable-width audio features. A cache miss or eviction simply re-encodes the window. Cache reuse is therefore a performance optimization, not persistent session state and not a correctness dependency. The cache is model-owned only through declarative capability data: ```text Transcription adapter -> activation threshold, language gate, text-prefix limits Multimodal processor -> independently encodable window geometry Generic audio-window builder -> feature extraction, MM items, identity, cacheability Existing MM scheduler/cache -> lookup, miss batching, embedding assembly ``` There is no ASR-specific scheduler session, cache service, GPU lease, or model forward API. ## Append-only decoder streaming Each backend ASR request now uses `stream=True` when the realtime endpoint provides a callback. Partial decoder text is stripped of model-specific output markers, reconciled against cumulative or windowed transcript state, and sent only when it extends the text already published for that request. This is decoder-token-driven stable delta streaming, not a guarantee of one WebSocket event per tokenizer token. Local Agreement and suffix holdback may release several tokens together. If a completed decode revises a prefix that was already emitted, the request fails closed rather than sending a conflicting append-only transcript. No client changes are required. The wire protocol remains: ```text conversation.item.input_audio_transcription.delta conversation.item.input_audio_transcription.completed ``` ## Enablement ```bash python -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path Qwen/Qwen3-ASR-0.6B \ --enable-asr-encoder-window \ --asr-max-buffer-seconds 1800 ``` The client uses the existing realtime transcription session format and must declare a supported language before sending audio: ```json { "type": "session.update", "session": { "audio": { "input": { "format": {"type": "audio/pcm", "rate": 16000}, "transcription": { "model": "qwen3-asr", "language": "en" }, "noise_reduction": null, "turn_detection": null } } } } ``` `--asr-max-buffer-seconds` is the total accepted duration of one client item. Resident PCM is independently compacted after the encoder-window handoff. ## Alternatives evaluated Before selecting this implementation, four approaches were run under the same controlled setup: Qwen3-ASR-0.6B, one RTX 4090, Triton attention, identical native audio, 16 kHz mono PCM16 WebSocket input, and 2-second flood-mode appends. Processing time is measured from the first send to the completed event; it measures server work rather than realtime playback. "Word error" is the normalized edit distance from the published reference; lower is better. | Approach | Long-audio behavior | Result | Decision | |---|---|---|---| | Cumulative | Re-submit all received audio every 2 seconds | 178.5 seconds of audio took 153.240 seconds; 291.1 seconds did not finish within 300 seconds | Keep as the unchanged default for normal items | | PCM tail slicing | Submit a bounded PCM tail plus 2-second overlap | 178.5 seconds took 109.735 seconds with 39.81% word error; longer cases did not finish | Rejected: bounded audio alone did not bound decoder-prefix work or preserve quality | | Encoder-aligned rolling context | Reuse complete windows and continue from confirmed text | Completed 291/593/908/1687-second inputs in 16.947/31.721/51.097/90.195 seconds | Selected: fastest completed long-stream approach and no client protocol change | | Independent segment finals | Finalize disjoint segments without a cross-segment prefix | Completed the same inputs in 18.804/35.343/55.127/98.233 seconds | Not selected: slower and requires replaceable snapshot semantics | The long-input comparison was: | Input | Cumulative | PCM slicing | Encoder windows | Independent segments | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:| | LongLibriHeavy 178.5 s | 153.240 s, 12.04% error | 109.735 s, 39.81% | 9.911 s, 11.30% | 11.586 s, 11.30% | | TED Al Gore 291.1 s | >300 s, incomplete | >300 s, incomplete | 16.947 s, 3.87% | 18.804 s, 4.66% | | LongLibriHeavy 592.6 s | >405 s, incomplete | >397 s, incomplete | 31.721 s, 7.95% | 35.343 s, 7.74% | | TED Craig Venter 907.8 s | >405 s, incomplete | >405 s, incomplete | 51.097 s, 4.50% | 55.127 s, 4.75% | | Earnings22 EXCOF 1686.7 s | >397 s, incomplete | >397 s, incomplete | 90.195 s, 12.80% | 98.233 s, 10.55% | ## Current-head GPU validation Environment: - Commit: `135eb6cf66` - GPU: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090, 24,564 MiB - Model: `Qwen/Qwen3-ASR-0.6B`, snapshot `5eb144179a02acc5e5ba31e748d22b0cf3e303b0` - Attention backend: Triton - Python 3.12.13, PyTorch 2.9.1+cu128, Transformers 5.8.1 - 16 kHz mono PCM16 WebSocket input, 2-second appends - `--mem-fraction-static 0.75`, 100 MiB MM cache, 1800-second item cap All reported accuracy and performance cases below are complete, unmodified published source rows or source files. No reported audio was concatenated, cropped, padded, or silence-extended. signal.title: [AMD][CI][Fix] Guard FP32 LM head mm(out_dtype) fast path on ROCm
signal.text: ## Motivation `test/registered/rl/test_fp32_lm_head.py` fails deterministically on the AMD `stage-b-test-1-gpu-small-amd` shard (`linux-mi300-1gpu-sglang`, partition 7): ``` RuntimeError: gemm input type at::BFloat16 and output type float is not supported for ROCm ``` The FP32 LM head fast path added in #32370 selects `torch.mm(..., out_dtype=torch.float32)` whenever `hidden_states.is_cuda`: ```python use_mm_out_dtype = ( hidden_states.is_cuda and hidden_states.dtype == lm_head.weight.dtype and hidden_states.dtype in (torch.float16, torch.bfloat16) ) ``` `is_cuda` is `True` on ROCm, but the mixed input/output GEMM is **not** available in the torch build the failing image ships. `rocm/sgl-dev:*-rocm700-*` is based on `rocm/sgl-dev:rocm7-vllm-20250904`, which pins torch `2.9.0a0+git7bcbafe` (upstream commit `7bcbafe`, 2025-08-04). In that source `at::cuda::blas::gemm<at::BFloat16, float>()` rejects unconditionally, before any backend dispatch: ```cpp template <> void gemm<at::BFloat16, float>(CUDABLAS_GEMM_ARGTYPES_AND_C_DTYPE(at::BFloat16, float)) { #ifdef USE_ROCM TORCH_CHECK(false, "gemm input type at::BFloat16 and output type float is not supported for ROCm"); #else ... #endif gemm_internal<at::BFloat16, float>(...); // unreachable on ROCm } ``` pytorch#161540 (`a8d6943d36c1`, 2025-09-02) removed these four unconditional checks — in v2.9.1 the same guard reads `#ifndef USE_ROCM` and only covers the CUDA compute-capability case. The `rocm720` images use `rocm/pytorch:rocm7.2_..._pytorch_release_2.9.1` and so include it. **The dividing line is torch source older than 2025-09-02, not the ROCm version** — `rocm700-mi35x` (gfx950) also ships the old torch, while `rocm720-mi30x` (gfx942) ships 2.9.1, so this does not track gfx942 vs gfx950 either. On newer torch there is a second, narrower raise site: the Composable Kernel branch inside `gemm_internal`. That one requires an explicit `torch.backends.cuda.preferred_blas_library("ck")` — `blasPreferredBackend()` only ever resolves to `Cublas` or `Cublaslt` from env, and SGLang never calls the setter — so it is not what CI hits. The two are distinguishable by message: the CK branch in `gemm_internal<at::BFloat16, float>` prints `at::Half` (an upstream copy-paste typo, still present in v2.9.1), whereas CI reports `at::BFloat16`, which only the unconditional check emits. The capability gate below is deliberately agnostic to *which* of these applies. It never probes with a real GEMM: an earlier revision of this PR did, and the hipBLASLt algorithm lookup cost ~700 ms on MI355X without amortizing into the first real LM head GEMM. This is pre-existing CI debt on `main`, not a regression from any in-flight PR; the same shard fails on scheduled `main` runs. ## Modifications **`python/sglang/srt/layers/logits_processor.py`** - Add `_supports_mm_fp32_out_dtype(device_type, dtype)` and make it a conjunct of `use_mm_out_dtype`, so an unsupported build falls back to the pre-existing explicit-FP32-cast `torch.matmul` path instead of raising. It decides from metadata, no GEMM: - **ROCm**: gate on `torch >= 2.9.0`, the first release containing pytorch#161540. - **CUDA**: BF16 additionally requires compute capability 8.0+, which torch enforces in the `#ifndef USE_ROCM` branch of the very same function. FP16 has no such restriction. The version comparison is prerelease-aware on purpose. The rocm700 image ships `2.9.0a0+git7bcbafe`, and `utils/common.py`'s existing `torch_release` tuple discards the alpha marker: | version string | `parse(...) >= parse("2.9.0")` | `.release >= (2,9,0)` | |---|---|---| | `2.8.0` | False ✅ | False ✅ | | `2.9.0a0+git7bcbafe` (**the failing image**) | **False ✅** | **True ❌** | | `2.9.0` | True ✅ | True ✅ | | `2.9.1+rocm7.2.0.git7e1940d4` | True ✅ | True ✅ | Using the `.release` tuple would leave the shard red. There is a regression test pinned to exactly this. Deliberately **not** a plain `is_hip()` gate. `torch.mm(out_dtype=...)` works fine on ROCm with a current torch (verified on gfx950 / ROCm 7.2), and disabling it there would give up #32370's optimization on hardware that supports it — measured at 5.3× (batch 8) to 8.6× (batch 256) for a 152064x4096 BF16 LM head, plus a 2.32 GiB transient FP32 weight copy per forward. A bare `is_hip` gate would also have missed the CUDA sm80 rule and simply relocated the crash to V100. **Coverage deliberately dropped**: the Composable Kernel BLAS backend rejects this op on *any* torch version, and the version gate does not catch it. Reaching CK requires an explicit `torch.backends.cuda.preferred_blas_library("ck")`; no env var selects it (`Context.h` maps `TORCH_BLAS_PREFER_{CU,HIP}BLASLT` to `Cublaslt` only) and SGLang never calls the setter. **`test/registered/rl/test_fp32_lm_head.py`** - Derive the expected op from the same helper rather than `torch.cuda.is_available()`, which encoded the wrong assumption. - Add `force_support` to `_run_case`, pinning the helper's answer so **both** selection branches are exercised on every runner, NVIDIA included. Without it the suite is tautological: it asserts against the same predicate production consults, so the assertion holds by construction and the fallback branch is only ever reached on a host that already lacks support. - Add `TestMMFP32OutDtypeGate` covering the version strings, the ROCm gate, the sm80 rule, and non-CUDA devices. Pure metadata, so it needs no GPU. ## Accuracy Tests No numerical change on any backend that was already working — where the gate returns `True` the emitted op is byte-identical to before. Where it returns `False` the code takes the explicit-FP32-cast path, which is the same path used before #32370 and which is strictly higher precision than the `bf16`-input GEMM it replaces (both accumulate to FP32; the fallback additionally upcasts the inputs). No accuracy run is attached because on the available hardware (MI355X, ROCm 7.2, hipBLASLt) the gate returns `True` and this PR is a no-op at runtime. ## Speed Tests and Profiling No steady-state delta, and no added device work anywhere: - The fused `mm(out_dtype=fp32)` path is preserved bit-for-bit on every build that implements it. - The gate issues **zero GEMMs**. `_TORCH_HAS_ROCM_MM_FP32_OUT` is a single `packaging.version.parse` at import. `_supports_mm_fp32_out_dtype` is `@lru_cache`d on `(device_type, dtype)`; on ROCm it only reads that bool, and `torch.cuda.get_device_capability()` is reached only on NVIDIA + BF16, once. - Per forward this is one cached-function call plus a tuple hash (sub-microsecond, host-side), and it is the **last** conjunct of a short-circuiting `and`, so it is not even evaluated unless the three cheap dtype/device checks already passed. - No CUDA-graph impact: the gate is Python, so it runs at capture time and never during replay. ### Unit tests `11 passed` (16 subtests) on MI355X / ROCm 7.2 / torch 2.9.1. The suite needs no GPU for the gate tests. Both branches of the selection are asserted on every runner via `force_support`, and the gate is asserted directly against the real-world version strings including the failing image's `2.9.0a0+git7bcbafe`. **Mutation checks** — the PR head is green. To show the new tests are not tautological, the fix was broken locally in two ways and reverted; each breakage is caught: | mutation applied locally, then reverted | caught by | |---|---| | drop `and _supports_mm_fp32_out_dtype(...)` from `use_mm_out_dtype` | `test_probe_unsupported_falls_back_to_explicit_fp32_matmul`, for both FP16 and BF16 — the fallback stops being selected and the ROCm raise comes back | | swap the prerelease-aware `parse()` for a `.release` tuple compare | `test_torch_version_compare_is_prerelease_aware`, on exactly `2.9.0a0+git7bcbafe` — the failing image's torch gets misread as `>= 2.9.0` | No pre-existing test reacts to the first mutation, which is why the original suite was blind to this regression. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process). 2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers. 3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so. 4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR. cc @ilyasher-harmonic (author of #32370) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32504804119](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32504804119)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32504803993](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32504803993)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32504804194](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32504804194)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [P/D disagg] Support DSV4 decode radix on ROCm unified KV
signal.text: ## Motivation #27770 added the supported device-only decode radix path for hybrid-SWA models on `UnifiedRadixCache`, but deliberately kept DeepSeek-V4 disabled. On ROCm, DeepSeek-V4 normally runs with: ```bash SGLANG_HACK_FLASHMLA_BACKEND=unified_kv_triton ``` That layout uses the same FULL+SWA unified radix structure and paged SWA-tail allocator, while DSV4 compressed KV/indexer/state transfer is already carried by the existing PD state payloads. Keeping the blanket DSV4 rejection forces redundant full-prefix transfer on every turn. This PR was rewritten on top of #27770. It no longer carries the competing FULL-only matcher or the old broad allocator-capability implementation. ## Scope Enable decode-side radix reuse only when all of the following hold: - the selected cache is actually `UnifiedRadixCache`; - the model uses paged SWA-tail allocation; - DSV4 is using the ROCm unified-KV layout; - the radix component set is exactly FULL+SWA; - hierarchical cache, SWA-compress, Mamba/SSM, HiSparse, fake transfer, and speculative decoding remain rejected by the existing guards. NPU C128, MTP/DSpark, and SWA+HiCache are intentionally out of scope. ## Implementation - Validate the cache implementation selected at runtime instead of requiring the legacy `SGLANG_ENABLE_UNIFIED_RADIX_TREE=1` environment gate. - Reuse #27770's insertion-margin and prefix-cap design so the complete SWA window is transferred into the fresh delta. - Preserve `skip_lock_node_ids` together with `swa_uuid_for_lock` across admission and early SWA-lock release. - If locking a radix hit makes admission fail, release it, refresh the pool budget, reset the request to the root/miss state, and retry once as a miss. This prevents a stable hit/reject loop from head-of-line blocking the decode queue. - Add focused compatibility, page/window geometry, lock ownership, and admission-liveness tests. ## Validation - `pre-commit run --files ...` — passed for all six changed files. - `test_decode_radix_lock_ref.py -v` — 13 passed. - `test_swa_decode_radix_cache.py -v` — 8 passed. - `test_decode_queue_cleanup.py -v` — 8 passed. - `test_unified_radix_cache_unittest.py` — passed. - AgentX 1P1D MI355X pressure run, job `26395`: TP8/DP1/EP1, concurrency 48, 3600-second profiling, latest `v0.5.17-rocm724-mi35x-20260820` image (`sha256:420f3f2d...c4fcf67f`). SLURM completed `0:0`; AIPerf `submission_valid=true`; 1,779 valid requests, 0 errors; final server prefix-cache hit 86.0%; no KV-full/SWA exhaustion/cache assertion/GPU memory fault. The E2E run exercised inputs up to 729,704 tokens and reached 79% decode FULL-KV usage plus 75% pre-allocation usage. Raw artifacts are under `/apps/InferenceX_CI/slurm_job-26395/`. ## Checklist - [x] Rebased onto current `main` after #27770. - [x] Removed the obsolete competing implementation. - [x] Added focused unit coverage. - [x] Ran formatting and local regression tests. - [x] Run current-head DSV4 1P1D cache-hit and pressure-stability validation. - [ ] Run maintainer Base/Extra/ROCm CI. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32463171838](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32463171838)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32463171607](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32463171607)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32463171709](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32463171709)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [sgl-router] Worker Snapshot Support for Recoverable KV Placement State in sgl-router
signal.text: ## Motivation KV-aware routing depends on an accurate view of the KV blocks available on each worker replica. Previously, sgl-router built this view only from live `BlockStored` and `BlockRemoved` events. If the Router started after the Worker cache had already been populated, or if the Router restarted and lost its in-memory index, the existing KV placement state could not be reconstructed. Missing or stale placement metadata does not affect inference correctness, but it reduces cache-aware routing quality and may lower the KV cache hit rate. This PR implements the snapshot bootstrap and full-recovery portion of #33394. Short-gap recovery through the replay endpoint remains separate follow-up work related to #32729. ## Modifications ### Worker-side snapshot provider - Add an optional `snapshot_endpoint` to the built-in ZMQ KV-event publisher. The endpoint is exposed independently for each routable DP or attention-DP replica using `base_port + dp_rank`. - Maintain an in-memory KV placement mirror inside the publisher thread. Sequence assignment, event application, and snapshot capture are serialized by the same thread, so the snapshot and its live-event barrier represent one consistent placement cut. - Include the replica lifecycle `epoch`, `replica_rank`, `barrier_seq`, `resume_seq`, `barrier_id`, and the active block records required to reconstruct parent relationships. - Stream large snapshots in chunks of up to 4096 records. The chunk size limits each ZMQ message, not the total snapshot size. - Scope the publisher epoch to one DP replica lifecycle, so restarting one DP rank does not invalidate the other ranks. - Keep the replay buffer complete after a sequence number is assigned even if live PUB delivery fails, and index the snapshot mirror by `block_hash` for direct removal. ### Discovery and compatibility - Advertise the optional snapshot host, base port, and protocol version through `/server_info`. An invalid or absent snapshot configuration does not hide an otherwise valid live KV-event publisher. - Append NUL-delimited epoch and snapshot-barrier metadata to the ZMQ topic frame only for snapshot-capable publishers. The sequence frame and event payload remain unchanged. - Preserve compatibility with existing ZMQ consumers because SUB filters are prefix-based. - Keep workers without a snapshot endpoint in the existing `LegacyBestEffort` live-only mode. ### Router-side recovery For each `(worker_url, dp_rank)` replica, sgl-router now: 1. subscribes to the live event stream; 2. fetches the replica snapshot while buffering live events; 3. waits for and validates the matching snapshot barrier; 4. verifies contiguous sequence numbers and applies post-snapshot updates; 5. replaces the replica placement state in the HashTree; and 6. marks the replica `READY`. One snapshot is fetched per independently routable DP or attention-DP replica, rather than per TP rank. Snapshot-capable replicas remain absent from the cache-aware placement tree until synchronization completes. Normal routing fallback remains available while a replica is synchronizing. A sequence gap, epoch change, publisher reset, decode failure, or invalid snapshot clears only the affected replica placement state and triggers a fresh synchronization. Snapshot retries use bounded buffering, cancellation-aware tasks, and exponential backoff. ### Code organization - Add `snapshot.rs` for the chunked snapshot wire protocol and validation. - Add `sync.rs` for bootstrap, barrier catch-up, replica state transitions, gap detection, and resynchronization. - Keep `index.rs` as the lifecycle facade for worker discovery, subscriber management, and snapshot task ownership. ## Accuracy Tests This PR does not change model execution, kernels, or generated outputs. The following tests passed: ```bash PYTHONPATH=python python3 -m pytest -q \ test/registered/unit/disaggregation/test_kv_events.py # 10 passed PYTHONPATH=python python3 -m pytest -q \ test/registered/unit/entrypoints/test_server_info.py # 17 passed cd experimental/sgl-router cargo test --lib policies::kv_events # 102 passed cargo test --test component # 41 passed ``` The snapshot recovery E2E test also passed with two Workers and one Router: - KV blocks populated before Router startup were recovered from snapshots. - Live KV events produced after the Router became ready were applied incrementally. - After restarting the Router, the placement view was rebuilt and the same cached prefixes continued to route to the expected Workers. The legacy compatibility E2E test also passed: Workers without a snapshot endpoint continued to use live-only indexing, and two Router instances converged to the expected prefix routing results. ## Speed Tests and Profiling No model throughput benchmark was run because this PR does not modify the inference or request-forwarding path. Snapshot capture uses the publisher in-memory placement mirror, and snapshot network transfer runs on a separate thread using bounded chunks. Normal live-event processing remains incremental. ## Checklist - [x] Format the code according to the repository pre-commit configuration. - [x] Add unit tests for snapshot capture, chunking, epoch isolation, protocol validation, recovery, failure handling, and legacy compatibility. - [x] Document the snapshot protocol and synchronization lifecycle in the implementation. - [x] Provide accuracy and speed-test applicability and E2E validation results. - [x] Follow the existing SGLang Python and Rust code organization and style. Related RFC: #33394 Related replay work: #32729 <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32504345673](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32504345673)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32504345455](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32504345455)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32504345984](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32504345984)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [AMD][Fix] Qwen3.5: make empty-batch guard tuple-aware on fused AR+quant path
signal.text: ## Problem Partition 0 of `stage-c-test-large-8-gpu-amd-mi35x-rocm720` (`test_qwen35_fp8_ar_fusion_mi35x.py`) has failed on every scheduled run since 2026-08-16 12:08 UTC. Example: [job 95552260420](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32083881457/job/95552260420). The empty-batch guard added in #34474 reads `hidden_states.shape[0]` immediately after `prepare_attn_and_capture_last_layer_outputs()`. When the fused AR+quant path is active that call returns a tuple — `(bf16, fp8, scale)` in the GatedDeltaNet layer, `(fp8, scale)` in the plain attention layer — so the guard raises during decode CUDA-graph capture and the server dies at startup: ``` File "python/sglang/srt/models/qwen3_5.py", line 806, in forward if not forward_batch.forward_mode.is_idle() and hidden_states.shape[0] > 0: AttributeError: 'tuple' object has no attribute 'shape' ``` The scheduler child dying takes the process tree with it, which the test surfaces as the less obvious `Server process exited with code -9`. Only the `fused-ar-rms-per-group-quant` variant is affected; the `SGLANG_DISABLE_FUSED_AR_QUANT=1` control variant stays on the tensor path. ## Fix Read the row count off the tuple's first element, using the same inline form `glm4_moe.py` already uses for this situation. Applied at both guard sites. This is behavior-preserving. `prepare_attn()` returns early on `hidden_states.shape[0] == 0` *before* the fusion branch, so a tuple can only appear when the count is already `> 0`; the tuple path therefore behaves exactly as it did before #34474, while the tensor path keeps the empty-batch guard. Both sites are patched because `keep_bf16=False` still yields a tuple, just the 2-element form. `Qwen3_5AttentionDecoderLayer.forward_prepare_native()` / `.forward_prepare_fused_gate()` both open with `isinstance(hidden_states, tuple)`, and `_select_fused_ar_input_for_linear()` has a dedicated `len(...) == 2` branch that only this path produces. Supersedes #35250, which diagnosed the same bug but patched the GatedDeltaNet site only. ## Verification Reproduced and fixed end-to-end on an 8x MI350X node following the CI flow exactly — same image (`rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.17-rocm720-mi35x-20260817`), same `amd_ci_install_dependency.sh`, same `run_suite.py` invocation. Before, at the failing scheduled-run SHA `91144797c`: the `AttributeError` above, byte-for-byte the CI signature. After: | Variant | GPUs | Accuracy | Invalid | Latency (s) | Output tok/s | Threshold | Status | | ------- | ---- | -------- | ------- | ----------- | ------------ | --------- | ------ | | fused-ar-rms-per-group-quant | 0,1,2,3 | 0.951 | 0.009 | 53.66 | 4067.56 | 0.94 | PASS | | disable-fused-ar-quant-opt-out | 4,5,6,7 | 0.940 | 0.009 | 53.85 | 4010.65 | 0.94 | PASS | On CI, partition 0 is green on both [run 32203488998](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32203488998) and [run 32227220289](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32227220289), with accuracy matching the last pre-regression baseline ([run 31916881653](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31916881653): 0.949 / 0.943). ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). No new test: `test_qwen35_fp8_ar_fusion_mi35x.py` already covers this path and is the test that was red. No user-facing behavior change, and no before-number to benchmark since the server did not start. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32458357756](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32458357756)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32458357596](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32458357596)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32458357678](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32458357678)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: Add Spark3 Model
signal.text: ## Summary This PR adds native support for the Spark 3 model architecture in SGLang. The implementation introduces the Spark 3 configuration and causal language model, including sliding-window and full attention, head-wise attention output gating, tensor parallelism, pipeline parallelism, and checkpoint weight loading. ## Changes | File | Purpose | | --- | --- | | `python/sglang/srt/configs/spark3.py` | Adds `Spark3Config`, including model dimensions, attention layout, sliding-window configuration, layer types, RoPE parameters, and tied word embeddings. | | `python/sglang/srt/models/spark3.py` | Implements `Spark3ForCausalLM`, including grouped-query attention, interleaved sliding/full attention, head-wise output gating, gated MLP, parallelism support, split prefill, and checkpoint weight loading. | | `python/sglang/srt/configs/__init__.py` | Exports `Spark3Config` through the SGLang configuration package. | | `python/sglang/srt/utils/hf_transformers/common.py` | Registers `Spark3Config` in SGLang's Hugging Face configuration registry. | ## Key Technical Details 1. Efficient Architecture：The models adopt an efficiency-oriented architecture with Sliding Window Attention (SWA) and other structural optimizations, improving the balance between model quality, memory usage, and inference efficiency. 2. Native 1M Context：Both the 1.7B and 4B models natively support up to 1 million tokens of context, enabling long-document understanding, repository-level coding, and long-horizon agent tasks. 3. Strong Coding & Agent Capabilities：The models deliver leading coding and agent performance among models of comparable size, with strong capabilities in code generation, tool use, multi-step execution, and long-context reasoning. 4. Faster Inference：Through model architecture and inference-stack optimizations, the models achieve higher inference efficiency and throughput than many comparable-size models, especially in long-context scenarios. 5. Strong K–12 and Gaokao Performance：The models achieve leading K–12 question-answering performance at comparable parameter scales, with particularly strong results on challenging Chinese Gaokao-style tasks. 6. Advanced Post-Training：The release applies a comprehensive post-training recipe based on Scaled Reinforcement Learning and MOPD, improving reasoning, coding, instruction following, agentic capabilities, and alignment. 7. Controllable Thinking Budget：The models support configurable reasoning levels — none, low, medium, and high — allowing applications to dynamically trade off reasoning quality, latency, and inference cost. 8. 200+ Languages：Multilingual coverage has been expanded to more than 200 languages, supporting broad cross-lingual understanding, generation, translation, and localized applications. ## Performance We run MMLU-Pro on our internal OAI-server compatible benchmarking suite and the scores match the declared performance. Running on 1xH200 SXM5 ```bash ============ Serving Benchmark Result ============ Backend: sglang Traffic request rate: inf Max request concurrency: not set Successful requests: 500 Benchmark duration (s): 4.48 Total input tokens: 756489 Total input text tokens: 756489 Total generated tokens: 64000 Total generated tokens (retokenized): 63997 Request throughput (req/s): 111.52 Input token throughput (tok/s): 168733.90 Output token throughput (tok/s): 14275.12 Peak output token throughput (tok/s): 27064.00 Peak concurrent requests: 500 Total token throughput (tok/s): 183009.02 Concurrency: 463.05 ----------------End‑to‑End Latency---------------- Mean E2E Latency (ms): 4152.05 Median E2E Latency (ms): 4387.30 P90 E2E Latency (ms): 4391.62 P95 E2E Latency (ms): 4392.38 P99 E2E Latency (ms): 4393.38 ----------------Time to First Token---------------- Mean TTFT (ms): 2348.20 Median TTFT (ms): 2377.59 P90 TTFT (ms): 2386.19 P95 TTFT (ms): 2387.18 P99 TTFT (ms): 2388.39 -----Time per Output Token (excl. 1st token)----- Mean TPOT (ms): 14.20 Median TPOT (ms): 15.81 P90 TPOT (ms): 15.85 P95 TPOT (ms): 15.86 P99 TPOT (ms): 15.87 ----------------Inter‑Token Latency---------------- Mean ITL (ms): 14.20 Median ITL (ms): 12.72 P90 ITL (ms): 16.52 P95 ITL (ms): 17.51 P99 ITL (ms): 29.32 Max ITL (ms): 307.79 ================================================== ``` <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32458293504](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32458293504)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32458293339](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32458293339)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32458293538](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32458293538)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [Bugfix] Fix Qwen3.5 MTP compressed-tensors ignore matching
signal.text: ## Motivation Fixes #35797. Compressed-tensors Qwen3.5 checkpoints list the individual MTP projections under `quantization_config.ignore`. `Qwen3_5ForCausalLMMTP` did not expose the target model's `packed_modules_mapping`, so the loader passed an empty fused mapping into the quantization config. As a result, `qkv_proj` and `gate_up_proj` could not inherit the ignore decisions of `q_proj`/`k_proj`/`v_proj` and `gate_proj`/`up_proj`. They were built with packed parameters even though the checkpoint stores plain BF16 weights, so those MTP weights were skipped during loading. ## Modification - Reuse `Qwen3_5ForCausalLM.packed_modules_mapping` on the MTP entry class. - Add CPU regression coverage showing that both fused projections inherit their component ignore entries. This preserves per-layer compressed-tensors semantics instead of disabling quantization for the entire MTP module. ## Tests - `test_shared_experts_fusion_gates.py`: 27/27 CPU tests passed. - `black --check` on both changed files. - `ruff check --select F401,F821,UP037` on both changed files. - `py_compile` on both changed files. - `git diff --check`. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32503315942](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32503315942)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32503315781](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32503315781)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32503315963](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32503315963)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [mem_cache] docs: add a layer map and placement rules
signal.text: ## Motivation Part of #25371. `mem_cache/` has 40 top-level modules plus 10 subpackages and no index. Answering "is this class an allocator or a pool?" or "may `pool_host/` import `allocator/`?" currently means reading the RFC or grepping. ## Modifications Adds `python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/README.md`: - **Layers** -- the stack from `allocation.py` down through `allocator/`, `pool/`, `pool_host/`, `storage/`, with each layer's in/out contract. Names prefix-cache trees and the construction layer (`kv_cache_configurator.py`, `kv_cache_builder.py`, `cache_init_params.py`, `allocation_sizing.py`, `kv_cache_dtype.py`, `kv_vmm_backing.py`, `hybrid_cache/hybrid_pool_assembler.py`) as sitting outside that stack rather than in it. - **Where does my class go?** -- home by base class, not by name, plus the `Allocator`-means-two-things distinction (`BaseTokenToKVPoolAllocator` hands out KV slots and lives in `allocator/`; `HostTensorAllocator` hands out pinned host memory and does not). - **Conventions** -- the naming rule, family-as-package, and the dependency-direction invariants. Documentation only; no code changes. **Deliberately coarse.** An earlier draft carried a per-family x per-layer matrix naming the module that holds each class today. That inventory would need updating by every one of the ~20 remaining moves under #25371, and it already has a home that cannot rot: the shrink-only pins in the layout ratchet (#35638), which fail the build when a pinned class moves. Duplicating it here would just give the same fact a second home to drift from. The README documents the rules, which are stable; for "where does class X live today", `git grep` is the answer, and the README says so. ## Accuracy Test Not applicable -- documentation only. ## Benchmark and Profiling Results Not applicable -- documentation only. ## Checklist - signal.title: Inference Support Mamba 2 and 1
signal.text: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation Add SGLang support for the **Mamba family of pure state-space models**, none of which could be served before — they crashed at startup or fell through to attention code paths they don't fit. This PR covers both generations: - **Mamba2 (SSD):** `mistralai/Mamba-Codestral-7B-v0.1` - **Mamba-1 (selective-scan):** `tiiuae/falcon-mamba-7b` / `-instruct`, `state-spaces/mamba-130m-hf`, and the raw `state-spaces/mamba-{130m,790m,2.8b}` checkpoints Root causes addressed: these configs have no `num_attention_heads`/`head_dim`, so shape derivation tripped before any weights loaded; the pure-SSM path routed through the paged decoder KV cache (an SSM keeps none); Mamba2 checkpoints use `backbone.*` names with no `max_position_embeddings`; and the raw state-spaces configs carry no `model_type`/`architectures`, so `AutoConfig` rejected them outright. ## Modifications - **New models:** `Mamba2ForCausalLM` (`models/mamba2.py`), `FalconMambaForCausalLM` (`models/falcon_mamba.py`), `MambaForCausalLM` (`models/mamba.py`) — pre-norm mixer decoder layers, no MLP; weight loaders remap `backbone.* → model.*`, `embeddings/embedding. → embed_tokens`, `norm_f → norm` (Mamba2 also `A_log → A`; Mamba-1 keeps `A_log`). - **New Mamba-1 mixer** (`layers/attention/mamba/mamba1.py`, `MambaMixer1`): causal conv over intermediate channels, `x_proj`/`dt_proj` selection, optional Falcon weightless RMSNorm on `B`/`C`/`dt`. Decode reuses `selective_state_update`; prefill uses a portable per-timestep selective scan (works off-CUDA, e.g. XPU). - **Reuse of the Mamba2 backend for Mamba-1:** express the full-rank Mamba-1 state on the Mamba2 head layout (`num_heads = intermediate_size`, `head_dim = 1`) via `Mamba2StateShape.create_mamba1`, so it rides the existing attention backend and memory pool unchanged. - **Config/wiring (gated, additive):** `AttentionArch.SSM`; `PURE_SSM_ARCHITECTURES` / `PURE_MAMBA1_ARCHITECTURES` with `_is_pure_mamba2` / `_is_pure_mamba1` flags; KV-less handling (`head_dim = 0`) in `model_config.py`; cache-param build in `hybrid_arch.py`; SSM backend selection in `attention_backend_setup.py`; forward-metadata guard in `eager_runner.py`. - **Raw-checkpoint support:** `_try_load_raw_mamba_config` pre-`AutoConfig` hook in `utils/hf_transformers/config.py` builds a `MambaConfig` from the minimal `d_model`/`n_layer`/`ssm_cfg` config. - **Conv dtype fix** for fp32 checkpoints (`SGLANG_MAMBA_CONV_DTYPE` mismatch); CPU unit test for Mamba2 weight remapping; docs entry. All changes are gated behind the SSM arch/flag; existing MLA/MHA models keep their original code paths. ## Accuracy Tests | Model | Task | Metric | SGLang (Intel XPU) | |---|---|---|---| | Mamba-Codestral-7B-v0.1 | gsm8k (1319, 5-shot, greedy) | flexible / strict | 0.4579 / 0.4488 | | falcon-mamba-7b | gsm8k (1319, 5-shot) | flexible / strict | 0.5140 / 0.5095 | | falcon-mamba-7b-instruct | gsm8k (1319, 5-shot, chat) | flexible / strict | 0.5883 / 0.5534 | | state-spaces/mamba-130m-hf | piqa (1000, 5-shot) | acc / acc_norm | 0.649 / 0.637 (≈ published 0.64) | | state-spaces/mamba-130m (raw) | hellaswag (limit-50, 5-shot) | acc / acc_norm | 0.34 / 0.48 | | state-spaces/mamba-790m, 2.8b (raw) | — | greedy generation | coherent | All models load with 0 real skipped params. Stock server commands run unchanged (raw checkpoints need `--tokenizer-path EleutherAI/gpt-neox-20b`, a deployment flag). ## Speed Tests and Profiling Adds new models with no change to existing code paths or their speed. Serving on Intel XPU (2× Arc Pro B60): Mamba-Codestral ~36 concurrent sequences / ~220 tok/s decode (tp-size 2); Falcon-Mamba ~42 / ~200 tok/s (tp-size 1). Pure SSM models report a zero-byte KV cache, so concurrency is bounded by `--max-total-tokens` / Mamba state-cache slots rather than KV memory. Mamba-1 prefill uses a per-token selective scan (no in-tree chunked-scan kernel yet), so prefill throughput is low — a Triton Mamba-1 scan kernel is the natural follow-up. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. signal.title: fix(parser): match model-specific rules before the mimo fallback
signal.text: ## Motivation Parser auto-detection returns the first rule that matches, so broad rules have to come last. The `mimo` rule matches on nothing more than a template setting `enable_thinking | default(false)`, which many chat templates do. It was ordered ahead of rules that key on model specific markers, so those templates resolve to `mimo`. On current main, a template that contains the marker and also sets that default resolves as: | Template contains | Expected | Detected on main | | --- | --- | --- | | `<mm:think>` | `minimax-m3` | `mimo` | | `<minimax:tool_call>` | `minimax` | `mimo` | | `Step-3.5` | `step3p5` | `mimo` | | `<steptml:invoke` | `step3` | `mimo` | | `<｜DSML｜tool_calls>` | `deepseek-v4` | `mimo` | | `<function=` and `<parameter=` | `qwen3_coder` (tool call) | `mimo` | The last row is the one that breaks output parsing, since the tool call parser itself is wrong. `test_specific_rules_precede_broad_fallbacks` already states that specific rules must run before broad ones, and already guards `poolside_v1` and `minicpm5` against `mimo`. This applies the same ordering to the remaining rules. ## Modifications - Move `mimo` after the marker based rules in `REASONING_PARSER_RULES` and `TOOL_CALL_PARSER_RULES`. Its position relative to `qwen`, `deepseek_v3` and `deepseek_r1` is unchanged, since those predicates cannot match at the same time as `mimo`. - Extend `test_specific_rules_precede_broad_fallbacks` with the missing ordering checks. - Add two tests that run detection on templates carrying both a marker and the `enable_thinking` default. Templates with no marker still resolve to `mimo`, so detection for MiMo itself is unchanged. Reproduction used minimal templates built from the marker plus the `enable_thinking` default, not a full vendor template. Tests: ``` pytest test/registered/unit/parser/test_template_manager.py 43 passed, 65 subtests passed ``` Reverting only the source change, with the new tests in place, fails 12 of them. ## Accuracy Tests Not applicable. This does not change kernels or model forward code. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not applicable. signal.title: [Bug] /health handler's timeout path doesn't cancel the scheduler-side request, causing orphaned health-check requests  to pile up and crash paged-prefill batching
signal.text: ### Checklist - [x] I searched related issues but found no solution. - [ ] The bug persists in the latest version. - [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback. - [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed. - [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Describe the bug `GET /health` (`health_generate` in `sglang/srt/entrypoints/http_server.py`) dispatches a real 1-token `generate_request()` to the scheduler process, then waits up to `SGLANG_HEALTH_CHECK_TIMEOUT` (default 20s) for `tokenizer_manager.last_receive_tstamp` to advance: ```python task = asyncio.create_task(gen()) tic = time.time() while time.time() < tic + HEALTH_CHECK_TIMEOUT: await asyncio.sleep(1) if tokenizer_manager.last_receive_tstamp > tic: task.cancel() return Response(200) task.cancel() logger.error("Health check failed. Server couldn't get a response from detokenizer for last ...") return Response(503) ``` On timeout, `task.cancel()` only cancels the **local `asyncio.Task`** inside the HTTP-server process. The underlying generate request had already been forwarded to the **scheduler**, a separate process communicating over ZMQ/IPC — cancelling the local awaiting coroutine does not retract or abort the request there. If the scheduler is even briefly slow (GPU hiccup, batching contention, etc.), the request keeps running/queued server-side after the HTTP layer has already given up on it and returned 503. Because `HEALTH_CHECK_TIMEOUT` (20s) commonly equals or is close to the polling interval used by external health-checkers (e.g. Docker's default `HEALTHCHECK interval`), a single transient scheduler slowdown causes **every subsequent poll to add a brand-new independent 1-token request on top of ones the HTTP layer already abandoned**, rather than waiting for the backlog to clear. Over a multi-minute stall this produces several orphaned single-token `input_ids=[0]` requests all still resident in the scheduler simultaneously. We hit this in production: a transient scheduler stall (`last_heartbeat` frozen for ~2 minutes, confirmed via three consecutive `Health check failed ... last_heartbeat time: <frozen ts>` log lines 30s apart) let ~5 of these orphaned health-check requests accumulate, and when the scheduler eventually tried to batch them together it hit a shape-mismatch crash in the paged-prefill path: ``` ValueError: q.shape[0] (1) does not match qo_indptr[-1] (5). For paged prefill, q must have shape [total_tokens, num_heads, head_dim] where total_tokens = qo_indptr[-1]. ``` (`qo_indptr[-1]=5` lines up with the number of orphaned health-check requests that would have piled up in that stall window.) This is running Qwen3.5/Qwen3.8-style hybrid attention with `--speculative-algo NEXTN`, similar model/config class to #34239, and that crash then also left the passed-through GPU in an `NV_ERR_RESET_REQUIRED` state requiring a full VM power cycle to clear (separate GPU-driver-side issue, not filing here, just noting the blast radius). Regardless of whether the shape-mismatch crash itself is viewed as a separate bug (may well be, see #34239), the `/health` handler's failure-to-actually-cancel-server-side is a real, independent correctness gap worth fixing on its own: a health check that "fails" should not leave its probe request alive in the system. ### Reproduction ### Reproduction 1. Serve any generation model with `sglang.launch_server`. 2. Point a poller at `GET /health` with an interval at/near `SGLANG_HEALTH_CHECK_TIMEOUT` (default 20s) — e.g. Docker `HEALTHCHECK --interval=20s`. 3. Induce a transient scheduler slowdown for the request dispatched by one `/health` poll (e.g. artificially delay `generate_request`/the scheduler's batch loop, or trigger any other rare slow-path in the target model). 4. Observe: the HTTP layer times out and returns 503 after 20s, but the dispatched request remains resident in the scheduler (visible via internal batch/queue metrics, or by the request eventually completing/interfering with later batches after the HTTP layer has already discarded it). 5. Each subsequent 20s poll adds another independent request without waiting for the previous one(s) to actually clear scheduler-side. ### Suggested fix - On timeout, actually propagate cancellation to the scheduler (e.g. send an explicit abort/cancel message for `rid`, not just cancel the local `asyncio.Task` and pop local state), so a "failed" health check doesn't leave a live request behind. - Alternatively/additionally: dedupe or rate-limit concurrent in-flight health-check-generated requests (e.g. skip dispatching a new one if a prior health-check `rid` is still outstanding), so pollers with an interval ≤ `HEALTH_CHECK_TIMEOUT` cannot compound a backlog. ### Environment SGLang: `0.5.15.post1` FlashInfer: `0.6.12` Torch: `2.11.0+cu130` GPU: 1× NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (passthrough VM) Model: `Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B-FP8`, `--speculative-algo NEXTN --speculative-num-steps 3 --speculative-eagle-topk 1 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4 --context-length 262144`

signal.title: [diffusion] docs: what a 12 GB + 32 GB budget buys for MiniMax-H3
signal.text: On consumer hardware the host is the binding constraint, not the card. The H3 page did not say so. ## Motivation H3 is about 108 GB of weights — 61.73 GB of DiT, 46.18 GB of text encoder. The existing recipes (one 24 GB card, two 32 GB cards) all assume a host that can hold them. No consumer configuration can, and where the shortfall lands decides the throughput. ## Modifications A section for **12 GB VRAM inside a 32 GB host**, with the two budgets separated because they buy different things: | | 12 GB VRAM + 32 GB host | VRAM budget only, host free | | --- | ---: | ---: | | Peak VRAM | ≤ 12 GiB | ≤ 12 GiB | | Host anonymous (must fit) | 24.5 GiB | 116.7 GB pinned | | Denoise, 864×480 / 124 frames / 20 NFE | 17.38 s/it | 6.10 s/it | Inside 32 GB the weights cannot be held, so roughly 49 GiB per step is re-read from the checkpoint mapping at about 3.4 GB/s. That is arithmetic, not a tuning gap — so the section says an NVMe is a requirement, not a recommendation. Two measurement notes, because getting them wrong wastes real time: - Count host memory as **anonymous** bytes (`RssAnon`). Page cache behind a file mapping is droppable, so `VmRSS` overstates what has to fit. - **Enforce** the VRAM budget with `torch.cuda.set_per_process_memory_fraction`. `nvidia-smi` reports the caching allocator's reserved pool and overstates the requirement. The ComfyUI comparison carries the budget on each side, because without that it misleads in both directions: on the same unpruned bf16 weights sglang denoises at 6.10 s/it against 6.58–6.59, but **both** need about 116 GB of host memory to get there. Inside 12 GB + 32 GB ComfyUI's own path uses `minimax_h3_fl2va_pruned_int8_convrot` and `qwen3vl_32b_minimax_h3_nvfp4_awq` — an int8 DiT and an NVFP4 text encoder against a pruned 40.2 GB file where the unpruned one is 66.3 GB. Different weights, so not like-for-like with the recipes on this page. ## Accuracy Tests Documentation only. Every number is from a measured run on one RTX 4090 at 864×480 / 124 frames / 20 NFE, bf16, seed 1101, cfg 1.0, euler_ancestral, sigma shift 12.0/3.0, VRAM enforced as above. The ComfyUI side used the Comfy-Org unpruned bf16 checkpoints with `--bf16-unet --bf16-text-enc` and no `TorchCompileModel` node. ## Speed Tests and Profiling The table is the result. No code changes. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32501047159](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32501047159)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32501046937](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32501046937)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:heavy_minus_sign: **No AMD PR run found for this commit**.<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [diffusion] park a layerwise component's non-layer weights between uses
signal.text: ## Motivation Layerwise offload streams a component's blocks and releases them when its use ends. Everything else the component owns — embeddings, projections, norms, heads — stays on the device for the whole request. That is right while it is the component being used, and pure cost afterwards. On a small card the stage that follows is the one that needs the room. MiniMax-H3 at 864x480 / 124 frames / 20 steps, one RTX 4090, host memory capped at 32 GiB. The VAE decode is half the request, because `decode_temporal` re-runs the whole decoder per temporal chunk — so under layerwise offload the VAE's 36 blocks are re-streamed every chunk: ``` [MiniMaxH3TextEncodingStage] finished in 0.50 s [MiniMaxH3DenoisingStage] finished in 141.20 s [MiniMaxH3DecodingStage] finished in 140.60 s <- as much as 20 denoise steps ``` Holding those blocks resident (`--layerwise-resident-layers video_vae=36`, #35688) is what makes the decode cheap — 23 s instead of 150 — and it needs 9 GB. With a hard 12 GiB allocator cap the decode then dies for want of 20 MiB: ``` CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 20.00 MiB. 12.00 GiB allowed; Of the allocated memory 11.86 GiB is allocated by PyTorch ``` Of that 11.86 GiB, the DiT is still holding 2.09 GB and the text encoder 1.40 GB that the decode never touches. `PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True` does not close the gap. ## Modifications `park_non_layer_weights()` moves the parameters no manager streams to the host and leaves a `(1,)` placeholder behind; `restore_non_layer_weights()` brings them back. `LayerwiseOffloadStrategy` calls them from `finish_use` and `prepare_for_use`, so a component gives up that memory exactly while it is not the one being used. Scope is deliberately narrow: - **Parameters only.** Buffers stay resident because layerwise offload keeps them on purpose — a shared RoPE cache is referenced by many layers. - **One host copy, made once.** Steady state is one transfer each way per use: about 0.35 s for H3's 3.5 GB, against the 130 s the resident VAE saves. - **Follows `--performance-mode memory`**, which already trades latency for footprint. Nothing changes under the other modes. - **MPS untouched.** It has its own subphase-scoped mechanism. ## Accuracy Tests Which device holds a weight; the weights themselves are unchanged. Three unit tests cover the mode gate, that streamed layer weights are never parked and buffers stay resident, and that parking is a no-op outside memory mode. `test_layerwise_offload.py` (with the checkpoint-mapping branch applied, since that is the configuration measured): 117 passed. ## Speed Tests and Profiling H3 `fl2va`, 864x480 / 124 frames / 20 steps, seed 1101, single RTX 4090, host memory capped at 32 GiB. The 12 GiB VRAM budget is **enforced** with `torch.cuda.set_per_process_memory_fraction`, not inferred from `nvidia-smi` — which reports the caching allocator's reserved pool and so overstates it. | configuration | denoise | decode | end to end | 12 GiB cap | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | default | 141 s | 150 s | 303 s | fits, but decode dominates | | `video_vae=36` | 158 s | 23 s | 192 s | OOM in decode | | `video_vae=36` + this change | 159 s | **13 s** | **177 s** | **fits** | Host memory is unchanged at 24.5 GiB. Denoise varies 141–159 s with load on this shared box; decode is the term this change is about and it is stable. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32500676246](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32500676246)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32500676017](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32500676017)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32500676321](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32500676321)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->
