signal.title: [AMD][CI] Name the ROCm Image That Actually Ran in AMD Job Names
signal.text: Follow-up to #35602 and #35603. ## Summary This PR changes the job names shown in GitHub Actions for five AMD test workflows and updates the AMD CI monitor to follow those names. GPU tests now use: ```text <test> (<selected ROCm version>, <runner>[, <part>]) ``` Within these five test workflows, jobs that only wait, start another workflow, or collect results use neutral names. The ROCm 7.0 workflows stay separate from the workflows that handle ROCm 7.2.0/7.2.4. ## Before / After — directly changed workflows The examples below show the rule applied to every GPU job in each workflow. | Workflow | Before | After | | --- | --- | --- | | `PR Test ROCm 7.0 (AMD)` — 16 direct GPU job definitions | `stage-c-test-large-8-gpu-amd (linux-mi300-8gpu-sglang, 3)` | `stage-c-test-large-8-gpu-amd (rocm700, linux-mi300-8gpu-sglang, 3)` | | `PR Test ROCm 7.2 (AMD)` — 18 direct GPU job definitions | `stage-c-test-large-8-gpu-amd-rocm720 (...)`, even when the workflow used ROCm 7.2.4 | `stage-c-test-large-8-gpu-amd (rocm724, ...)` by default, or `(rocm720, ...)` when 7.2.0 is selected | | `PR Test Extra (AMD)` — 3 GPU job definitions | Default ROCm 7.2.4 was hidden: `extra-a-test-1-gpu-small-amd (...)`; other versions were put in the test name: `...-rocm700 (...)` | `extra-a-test-1-gpu-small-amd (rocm724, ...)`, `(rocm720, ...)`, or `(rocm700, ...)` | | `Nightly Test (AMD ROCm 7.0)` — 43 GPU jobs | `nightly-test-1-gpu-unit` | `nightly-test-1-gpu-unit (rocm700, linux-mi300-1gpu-sglang)` | | `Nightly Test (AMD ROCm 7.2)` — 47 GPU job definitions; a full nightly using both versions creates 94 jobs | `nightly-test-1-gpu-unit-rocm720 (rocm724)` or `(rocm720)` | `nightly-test-1-gpu-unit (rocm724, linux-mi300-1gpu-sglang)` or `(rocm720, linux-mi300-1gpu-sglang)` | | ROCm 7.2 PR helper jobs | `call-pr-test-amd-extra-rocm720`, `wait-for-stage-a-amd-rocm720`, `wait-for-stage-b-amd-rocm720`, `pr-test-amd-rocm720-finish` | `call-pr-test-amd-extra`, `wait-for-stage-a-amd`, `wait-for-stage-b-amd`, `pr-test-amd-finish` | | `AMD CI Job Monitor` | Looked for the old names, mixed ROCm 7.2.0 and 7.2.4 nightly results, and created empty reports for wait jobs | Looks for the new names, reports each nightly ROCm version and runner separately, skips wait jobs, and stops with an error if name parsing fails | The ROCm 7.2 nightly setup step also changes from the fixed `Setup docker (ROCm 7.2)` to `Setup docker (rocm724)` or `Setup docker (rocm720)`. The ROCm 7.0 and 7.2 PR workflows now share the same neutral wait/caller/finish labels; the workflow title still tells the two runs apart. ## Before / After — workflows that call these workflows These three files are not edited, but their child jobs inherit the new names: | Caller workflow | Before | After | | --- | --- | --- | | `AMD AITER Scout` — all four AMD PR/nightly paths | `call-nightly-amd-rocm720 / nightly-test-1-gpu-unit-rocm720 (rocm724)` | `call-nightly-amd-rocm720 / nightly-test-1-gpu-unit (rocm724, linux-mi300-1gpu-sglang)` | | `Release Branch Cut` — AMD PR and nightly paths | `run-pr-tests-amd / stage-a-test-1-gpu-small-amd-rocm720 (...)` | `run-pr-tests-amd / stage-a-test-1-gpu-small-amd (rocm724, ...)` | | `Bot Bump SGLang Version` — AMD nightly path | `run-nightly-tests-amd / nightly-test-1-gpu-unit-rocm720 (rocm724)` | `run-nightly-tests-amd / nightly-test-1-gpu-unit (rocm724, linux-mi300-1gpu-sglang)` | The AITER Scout outer prefixes `call-pr-test-amd-rocm720 /` and `call-nightly-amd-rocm720 /` are unchanged; only their child names become accurate. ## Unchanged AMD workflows These AMD workflow files keep the same job names and behavior: - `nightly-amd-mi355x-disagg.yml` - `nightly-test-amd-miles-rocm720.yml` - `release-docker-amd-miles-rocm700-nightly.yml` - `release-docker-amd-miles-rocm720-nightly.yml` - `release-docker-amd-nightly.yml` - `release-docker-amd-rocm720-nightly.yml` - `release-docker-amd-rocm7_15-nightly.yml` - `release-docker-amd.yml` PR States is also unchanged. ## What happens after merge - AMD GPU test execution is unchanged: the same tests run on the same machines, with the same images, commands, triggers, and schedules. The visible names and monitor grouping change. - Behind-the-scenes job IDs stay the same, so job dependencies and manual job selection keep working. - The merge checks named `lint` and `pr-test-finish` keep the same names. - GitHub starts new history under the new names. Any outside script or dashboard that searches for an old full name must be updated. - The AMD CI monitor's ROCm 7.2 Extra row may be blank until the first scheduled/full Extra run after merge, because older runs have the old caller name. - The name uses the selected `rocm_version`; it does not try to infer ROCm from a custom `AMD_CI_IMAGE` tag. - A job skipped very early may show the name formula instead of the finished name. Jobs that actually run show the selected ROCm version and runner. ## Validation - [Final-head monitor check](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32497819201/job/96820327015) produced the expected monitor targets: PR 7.2 `19`, nightly 7.2 `94`, PR 7.0 `17`, nightly 7.0 `43`, and MI355X disaggregation `2`. - [Fresh PR run](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32497819499) shows the new helper names. - YAML parsing, monitor actionlint, workflow job-name lint, Python compilation, and `git diff --check` pass. ## Checklist - [x] Format code according to the contribution guide. - [ ] Add unit tests — N/A: CI configuration change. - [ ] Update documentation — N/A. - [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32497819615](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32497819615)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32497819328](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32497819328)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32497819499](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32497819499)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: fix(intel_amx): keep the metadata seq_lens in forward_extend/forward_…
signal.text: ## Motivation Two `IntelAMXAttnBackend` entry points unpack a precomputed `seq_lens` and then immediately overwrite it with `forward_batch.seq_lens`, discarding the value their own metadata builder had computed. **`forward_extend`:** ```python seq_lens, extend_seq_lens, extend_start_loc, tree_mask = self.extend_metadata _, max_extend_len = self.forward_metadata seq_lens = forward_batch.seq_lens # <-- discards the verify adjustment ``` In `TARGET_VERIFY` mode `_build_extend_metadata` deliberately returns `forward_batch.seq_lens + num_draft_tokens`, because a verify batch writes its draft KV into `[seq_lens, seq_lens + draft_token_num)` **without** bumping `seq_lens`. The overwrite hid every draft KV entry from `extend_attention_cpu`, so each draft token attended only to the committed prefix. The result was silently wrong attention output rather than a crash, which is why it showed up as accuracy and logprob failures. This is why `test/registered/cpu/test_spec_eagle_parity_cpu.py` is currently registered as `disabled="EAGLE3 numerical parity mismatches on CPU intel_amx"`. **`forward_decode`:** ```python if self.draft_decode_metadata is not None: req_to_token, seq_lens, req_pool_indices = self.draft_decode_metadata ... q = q.reshape(-1, layer.tp_q_head_num * layer.qk_head_dim) seq_lens = forward_batch.seq_lens # <-- discards the expanded lengths ``` `IntelAMXMultiStepDraftBackend.init_forward_metadata` hands each draft step an expanded triple sized `batch_size * topk`, and sizes `attn_logits` from that same `bs`: ```python bs = num_seqs * topk attn_logits = torch.zeros((bs, num_head, num_kv_splits, v_head_dim + 1), ...) seq_lens_expanded = seq_lens.repeat_interleave(topk) + step + 1 self.attn_backends[step].draft_decode_metadata = ( req_to_token_draft, seq_lens_expanded, req_pool_indices_expanded, ) ``` The overwrite kept the expanded `req_to_token` and `req_pool_indices` but paired them with the unexpanded lengths, so `decode_attention_cpu` derived `num_seqs` from the wrong tensor and aborted immediately: ``` RuntimeError: CHECK_EQ(attn_logits.size(0), num_seqs) failed. 4 vs 1 ``` That made every EAGLE `topk > 1` run on CPU fail at server startup. Both sites are the same mistake, in the same file, so they are fixed together. ## Modifications `python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/intel_amx_backend.py` — delete both overwriting assignments and keep the metadata values, with a comment at each site explaining the invariant. `test/registered/cpu/test_spec_eagle_parity_cpu.py` — drop the `disabled=` argument from `register_cpu_ci(...)`, re-enabling the greedy parity test that the `forward_extend` bug had disabled. `test/registered/unit/layers/attention/test_intel_amx_verify_seqlens.py` (new) — registered CPU unit test that stubs the kernel entry points and asserts the `seq_lens` tensor that actually reaches them, in four cases: a verify batch and an ordinary prefill batch through `forward_extend`, and a draft-decode batch and a plain decode batch through `forward_decode`. Each case fails on the pre-fix code and passes on the fix. ## Accuracy Tests Run on an Intel Xeon host (128 physical cores / 256 logical across 4 NUMA nodes) with `--device cpu --attention-backend intel_amx`, same container and same command line, baseline vs. patched. ### `forward_extend` Baseline: ``` 7 failed, 13 passed, 1 skipped, 14 errors in 1329.27s ``` Patched: ``` 18 passed, 1 skipped, 14 errors, 2 subtests passed in 929.51s ``` All 7 failures are fixed: | Test | Baseline failure | | --- | --- | | `test_spec_eagle_parity_cpu::test_parity_vs_reference` | `' a' != ' a city of romance, art, fashion, and cuisi[164 chars] has'` | | `test_spec_eagle_cpu::test_gsm8k` | `np.float64(0.015625) not greater than 0.2` | | `test_spec_eagle_cpu::test_logprob_match` | `np.float64(8.417016625404358) not less than 0.5` | | `test_spec_eagle_cpu::test_logprob_decode_match_prefill` | 2 SUBFAILED | | `test_spec_eagle_cpu::test_finish_stop_eos` | `Expected finish_reason: stop, but got: length` | | `test_spec_eagle_cpu::test_token_ids_logprob_ragged` | `RuntimeError: prefix len < 0!` | ### `forward_decode` The 14 errors above were all `test_spec_eagle_topk_cpu::TestEagleLlama2Topk4` `setUpClass` failures with the `4 vs 1` abort. With the `forward_decode` fix, `test/registered/cpu/test_spec_eagle_topk_cpu.py` runs clean: ``` 13 passed, 1 skipped, 2 subtests passed in 862.21s (0:14:22) ``` The file's registration comment (`Measured 830s all-green on a 40-core GNR socket`) records that this suite is expected to be all-green, which is what it now is. Its `disabled=` marker is left in place, because it is set for an unrelated reason (the gated `meta-llama/Llama-2-7b-chat-hf` weights), not for this crash. All 26 tests in `test_spec_kernels.py` pass in both runs, so the non-verify paths are unchanged. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not a performance change, but the suite got faster because the requests now accept drafts instead of falling back: 1329s -> 930s for the same suite. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the Format code with pre-commit. - [x] Add unit tests according to the Run and add unit tests. - [ ] Update documentation according to Write documentations. - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to Test the accuracy and Benchmark the speed. - [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32500674135](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32500674135)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32500673863](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32500673863)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32500674062](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32500674062)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [AMD] Drop redundant FP8 bpreshuffle scale transpose via fused AR kernel
signal.text: Dependent on https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/4478, merged but need aiter update. ## Motivation On gfx95 (MI35x, ROCm >= 7.2) the gfx95 bpreshuffle FP8 block-scale GEMM consumes the per-group activation scale in a **column-major** layout, whereas the fused all-reduce + RMSNorm + per-group-FP8-quant kernel emits it **row-major**. To bridge the two, the fused-quant path in `layernorm.py` currently runs an explicit post-kernel transpose (`materialize_bpreshuffle_fp8_scale`, i.e. `scale.t().contiguous().t()`) on every eligible layer. That `.contiguous()` launches an extra copy kernel per fused-quant call — pure overhead in the decode-latency-bound regime where the model is dominated by many small kernel launches. aiter's fused kernel already has a compile-time `TRANSPOSE_SCALE` template (ROCm/aiter#3652) that can write the scale directly in the column-major layout the bpreshuffle GEMM wants, at zero extra cost (it only changes the store-index math). This PR plumbs that flag through so the fused kernel emits the transposed scale itself, and drops the redundant post-kernel transpose on the fused-success paths. The emitted layout is byte-for-byte identical to what `materialize_bpreshuffle_fp8_scale` produced (column-major storage `(num_groups, M)` viewed as `(M, num_groups)`, stride `(1, M)`), so this is a numerics-preserving change. This is FP8-only. The MXFP4 path uses a different kernel (`custom_fused_ar_rms_mxfp4_quant`) and is untouched. **Dependency:** requires the paired aiter change that forwards `transpose_scale` through `custom_fused_ar_rms_per_group_quant` / `fused_ar_rms_per_group_quant` / the ops stub to the (already capable) C++ op, plus a bundled-aiter pin bump. Without it, the fused-kernel call falls back (the flag is ignored / raises and is caught), so this PR should land together with / after the aiter bump. ## Modifications - `python/sglang/srt/distributed/communication_op.py`: add a `transpose_scale` kwarg to `tensor_model_parallel_fused_allreduce_rmsnorm_quant_per_group` and forward it to the group coordinator. - `python/sglang/srt/distributed/parallel_state.py`: add `transpose_scale` to `GroupCoordinator.fused_allreduce_rmsnorm_quant_per_group` and forward it into the `ca_comm.custom_fused_ar_rms_per_group_quant` call. - `python/sglang/srt/layers/layernorm.py`: pass `transpose_scale=use_bpreshuffle` to both fused per-group-quant calls (the `keep_bf16=False` attention path and the `keep_bf16=True` GDN emit_bf16 path), and remove the now-redundant `materialize_bpreshuffle_fp8_scale` on the two fused-success return paths. - The two separate-per-group-quant **fallback** paths intentionally keep `materialize_bpreshuffle_fp8_scale`: `per_1x128_quant`'s own `transpose_scale` byte-shuffles the scale into a different physical arrangement, not the column-major layout this GEMM consumes. - The FP8 linear consumer (`aiter_w8a8_block_fp8_linear`) is unchanged: the scale layout reaching it is identical, and its own `materialize` call becomes an idempotent no-op (`.contiguous()` short-circuits on an already-column-major tensor). ## Accuracy Tests Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8, TP4 (MI35x), `--enable-aiter-allreduce-fusion`, gsm8k (1319 questions): | Metric | Reference (with transpose) | This PR (fused transpose_scale) | |---|---|---| | Accuracy | 0.947 | **0.955** | | Invalid | 0.008 | 0.008 | Within run-to-run noise (marginally higher) — the change is numerics-preserving. ## Benchmarking and Profiling **Kernel-level confirmation (conc4 profile, IL8192/OL1024, 8 steps):** the fused kernel template flipped `TRANSPOSE_SCALE` false→true (`allreduce_fusion_kernel_1stage_per_group<…Lb0ELb0E>` → `<…Lb0ELb1E>`, 354 calls; `local_device_load_rmsnorm_quant_per_group_naive` Lb0→Lb1, 59 calls). The removed transpose copy (`elementwise_kernel_manual_unroll<…nocast>`) dropped from **960 → 547 = −413**, exactly `354 + 59` (one `.contiguous()` per fused-quant call). Total GPU kernel launches: 11555 → 11142. **End-to-end (Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8, TP4, IL8192/OL1024, num_prompts = concurrency × 10):** | Concurrency | Output tok/s (before → after) | Δ throughput | Median TPOT ms (before → after) | Δ TPOT | |---|---|---|---|---| | 4 | 438.8 → 443.1 | +0.98% | 8.44 → 8.41 | −0.37% | | 8 | 744.7 → 754.0 | +1.25% | 9.67 → 9.54 | −1.30% | | 16 | 1058.3 → 1071.4 | +1.24% | 13.53 → 13.30 | −1.67% | | 32 | 1525.8 → 1536.3 | +0.69% | 18.05 → 17.97 | −0.42% | | 64 | 1960.7 → 1973.7 | +0.66% | 27.27 → 27.09 | −0.65% | | 128 | 2615.1 → 2621.7 | +0.25% | 38.42 → 38.38 | −0.09% | Output-throughput geomean **+0.84%**; decode TPOT consistently lower across the sweep. A small but clean, zero-risk reduction — the benefit is the removal of ~per-layer kernel launches in the decode path. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review Process 1. signal.title: [AMD] Add AITER HIP backend for packed GDN decode on gfx950
signal.text: ## Motivation SGLang currently uses the Triton GDN kernel for Qwen3.5 decode on ROCm. For the fixed packed BF16 contract on MI355X, the new AITER HIP kernel reduces decode latency by about 13–23% while keeping the existing one-launch packed data flow. This PR wires that kernel into SGLang as an explicit decode backend. Unsupported contracts continue to use Triton. ## Modifications - Add `--linear-attn-decode-backend hip` and `LinearAttnKernelBackend.HIP`; keep `hip` out of the shared/default and prefill backend choices, and reject it for non-GDN models during initialization. - Add `HipGDNKernel`, which calls AITER directly for the exact packed BF16 gfx950 contract. - Gate the AITER path with `is_gfx95_supported()` and fall back to Triton decode on other ROCm architectures. - Keep ReplaySSM and unsupported shapes, dtypes, strides, scales, or layouts on `TritonGDNKernel`. - Keep prefill/extend and verify paths on Triton. - Add unit tests for exact-contract dispatch, architecture and contract fallback, CLI scope, non-GDN rejection, ReplaySSM fallback, and prefill/verify dispatch. No QKV split/copy, state conversion, temporary tensor, or additional kernel launch is added to the supported decode path. The default backend is unchanged unless `hip` is selected. ## Accuracy Tests GSM8K, 5-shot, all 1319 questions, temperature 0, max new tokens 2048; Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-MXFP4, TP2, MI355X. Both servers used Triton prefill and BF16 Mamba state. | Backend | Accuracy | Correct | Invalid | |---|---:|---:|---:| | Triton | 92.6459% | 1222/1319 | 8/1319 | | AITER HIP | 92.3427% | 1218/1319 | 6/1319 | This single deterministic pair differs by four correct answers (`-0.3033` percentage points). It is reported as a draft result rather than an accuracy-parity claim; prediction-level diffing and/or repeated evaluation is required before marking the PR ready. Normalized output throughput was `+0.819%`; total latency is not compared because the two runs generated different token counts. ## Benchmarking and Profiling ### Kernel (exact AITER PR commit) AITER `test_common.perftest`: two warmup iterations followed by 101 profiled decode calls, with default input rotation and device-time averaging. The table reports the median of five fresh-process `avg us/iter` results. | BS | Triton BF16 | AITER HIP | Latency reduction | |---:|---:|---:|---:| | 32 | 18.174 us | **13.965 us** | **23.16%** | | 64 | 31.746 us | **24.764 us** | **21.99%** | | 128 | 56.940 us | **49.603 us** | **12.89%** | ### End-to-end Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-MXFP4, TP2, MI355X; random ISL/OSL 8192/1024, range ratio 0.8, request rate `inf`, prompts = concurrency x 10. Each point used a fresh server and an identical full-workload warmup. Only the decode backend changed; prefill remained Triton. | Concurrency | Triton output tok/s | AITER HIP output tok/s | Throughput | Median TPOT (Triton -> HIP) | |---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 4 | 362.097 | 367.788 | **+1.572%** | 10.334 -> 10.181 ms | | 8 | 589.844 | 609.401 | **+3.316%** | 12.785 -> 12.541 ms | | 16 | 858.537 | 873.679 | **+1.764%** | 17.984 -> 17.663 ms | | 32 | 1140.530 | 1166.321 | **+2.261%** | 27.119 -> 26.482 ms | | 64 | 1461.569 | 1486.747 | **+1.723%** | 43.125 -> 42.335 ms | | 128 | 1823.527 | 1859.667 | **+1.982%** | 69.714 -> 68.288 ms | Across the six points, the non-weighted mean improvement was `+2.103%` output throughput and `+1.901%` median TPOT. Median TTFT, TPOT, ITL, and E2E latency improved at every point. ## Checklist - [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32455071581](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32455071581)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32455071437](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32455071437)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32455071578](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32455071578)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: fix: detect cross-node multimodal transport by nnodes
signal.text: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation `determine_tensor_transport_mode()` currently treats a non-empty `dist_init_addr` as evidence that the deployment spans multiple nodes. However, `dist_init_addr` is a process-group rendezvous endpoint rather than a topology signal. Single-node multi-GPU TP deployments may also set it to bootstrap the TP process group. The inverse is also possible: in Ray multi-node TP/PP, the generated rendezvous address is injected into scheduler-actor copies of `ServerArgs`, while the `TokenizerManager` can retain the original `dist_init_addr=None`. External launchers using an `env://` rendezvous can produce the same state. Requiring both `nnodes > 1` and a non-empty address would therefore let the tokenizer select node-local CUDA IPC/SHM while schedulers select the default transport. The original false positive selects the `"default"` transport on a single node, causing `wrap_shm_features()` to become a no-op. Large multimodal pixel tensors are then pickled and broadcast through Gloo for every request. In an affected five-image document workload, this resulted in 2.2–6.5 GB transfers and 18–33 seconds spent in `recv_requests`. `nnodes` directly represents whether the deployment is multi-node and is therefore the appropriate source of truth. ## Modifications - Determine cross-node topology using `server_args.nnodes > 1`, independently of `server_args.dist_init_addr`. - Move `TensorTransportMode` and `determine_tensor_transport_mode()` into the existing `sglang.srt.multimodal.transport` package as the shared implementation. - Update the tokenizer manager, disaggregated encoder receiver, native Rust multimodal path, and `mm_utils` to use the shared helper. - Remove the duplicated implementations and the reverse lazy import from `mm_utils` to `tokenizer_manager`. - Add a truth-table regression test covering all four combinations of single-node/multi-node topology and present/absent rendezvous address. ## Accuracy Tests Not applicable. This change only affects multimodal tensor transport selection and does not modify model computation or outputs. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Before this fix, the affected five-image document workload observed 2.2–6.5 GB of pickled/Gloo-broadcast data and 18–33 seconds per `recv_requests` call. This change restores the existing shared-memory transport path for single-node multi-GPU TP deployments. No standalone post-change benchmark was run in the local development environment. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Documentation is not required because this is an internal transport-selection fix with no user-facing API change. - [x] This change has no model accuracy impact. - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process). 2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers. 3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so. - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci` 4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32499500809](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32499500809)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32499500686](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32499500686)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32499500763](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32499500763)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [PD] Align defensive protocol behavior across Mooncake, NIXL, and Mori
signal.text: - RFC: [PD disaggregation: single protocol layer, per-backend transport #33861](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/33861) - Staged implementation plan and PR tracking: [PD shared-protocol implementation plan #34510](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/34510) - Preceding PR: [NIXL Prefill bootstrap timeout #34692](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/34692) ## Background #34692 added the missing NIXL Prefill bootstrap timeout. This PR continues Step 1 of #34510 by aligning clear, low-risk defensive protocol behavior across Mooncake, NIXL, and Mori without changing the Common state machine, wire format, completion channel, or Transport architecture. These changes preserve the current backend structure. They only add missing behavior or fix local race/layout issues. Extracting the common protocol and Transport remains work for later stages. ## Outline This PR groups the changes into five areas: 1. Complete Mori peer/request failure detection and ABORT delivery; 2. Prevent NIXL/Mori workers from executing stale work after teardown; 3. Keep Mooncake/NIXL control loops serving after malformed messages; 4. Align Mori MHA/MLA KV layout planning; 5. Fix the initialization race before the Mooncake control thread starts. ## 1. Mori peer and request failure handling Related commits: - `b285ea79ce` — `align Mori Decode heartbeat` - `62c13f66ba` — `align Mori abort handling with common protocol` Mori Decode did not start the existing Common heartbeat checker, so a dead Prefill would not trigger route/cache eviction or active-room failure. This PR only wires in the existing `_start_heartbeat_checker_thread()`, matching Mooncake and NIXL. Common Receiver sends an `ABORT` frame without a Mori guard, while Mori Prefill previously validated `MORI_GUARD` first and discarded ABORT as malformed. This PR recognizes the existing Common ABORT frame before guard validation: - Mark an active room as `Failed`; - Continue to ignore Success/unknown rooms; - Drop only the current message when ABORT is malformed. This only fixes ABORT delivery. It does not define ACK, cancel, or quiescence semantics. Terminal-state and safe-release behavior remains deferred to the later RFC stages. ## 2. Skip stale work after room teardown Related commit: - `46056556a5` — `skip cleared rooms in NIXL and Mori workers` Chunks already queued do not disappear when the Sender clears a room. - NIXL previously allowed a missing room to bypass its Failed check and then enter the exception path at the `transfer_infos` assertion; - Mori could continue into `add_transfer_request()` and subsequent terminalization. Mooncake already checks at `transfer_worker()` entry whether the room still exists or is `Failed`. On a match, it finishes the current chunk trace, removes residual `_staging_outstanding` state, and continues without reading that room's transfer metadata. This PR makes the other two backends discard queued tasks for missing rooms at worker entry: - NIXL aligns with Mooncake's missing-room/Failed guard, removes the room's residual `_staging_outstanding` count, and continues; - Mori uses an equivalent early return because chunk execution lives in Sender `_run_chunk()`. The stale task therefore cannot read deleted `transfer_infos`, submit to the Transport, advance state, or trigger terminalization. Existing `clear()` paths remain responsible for normal room cleanup; these guards only consume queue items that arrive after teardown. When the common protocol is extracted, this should be replaced by unified idempotent room teardown/tombstone semantics. For now, the backend-local guards avoid expanding the scope into Common state-machine changes. ## 3. Isolate malformed control messages **Scope update:** this change has been reverted from the final diff. Since this branch was created, #35049 and #35360 have added more complex deferred-release and ABORT/ABORT_ACK state transitions to the same Mooncake/NIXL control loops. Keeping the original broad per-message exception boundary while reconciling those changes would mix malformed-frame handling with partially applied abort, socket, and engine failures. Rather than expanding this PR to redesign those failure boundaries, we reverted the change and plan to handle malformed control messages together with the later protocol-unification work, based on the latest control paths. ~~Related commit:~~ - ~~`a716ceaac7` — `harden Mooncake and NIXL control message parsing`~~ ~~Mooncake/NIXL control loops serve multiple rooms, but previously indexed, decoded, or unpacked frames directly. An empty message, truncated ABORT, invalid guard, or unexpected frame count could terminate the long-lived thread.~~ ~~Mori already treats one message as the exception boundary: its Prefill bootstrap loop and Decode status loop validate guard/frame input inside `while True`, log an error for the current message, and continue receiving the next one. A bad frame therefore does not remove control-plane service from later rooms.~~ ~~This PR aligns Mooncake and NIXL with that behavior by adding minimum frame/tag/guard validation at the Mooncake Prefill/Decode and NIXL Prefill/Decode-staging message entries. Empty messages, truncated fields, and invalid encodings are logged and skipped without terminating the long-lived control thread.~~ ## 4. Align Mori KV layout planning Related commits: - `48c5e1569d` — `align Mori speculative MHA layout with common planner` - `081186c4c8` — `align Mori same-PP and hybrid MLA layout planning` Together, these commits fix Mori descriptor slicing that differed from the existing Common planner. The first part handles Decode-only speculative KV layout: ```text [K_main..., V_main..., draft_K..., draft_V...] ``` Mori previously split descriptors in half and could select a draft region as main V. This PR uses the same V-offset rule as `get_mha_kv_ptrs_with_pp()`. The second part adds: - Same-PP peer descriptor lists are already aligned local layouts and must not have the global layer offset applied again; - Hybrid MLA uses MLA descriptor slicing instead of falling through to the regular MHA path. These fixes remain inside Mori for now because they operate on Mori `MemoryDesc` lists, and planner/materialization are still coupled in Mori Manager. A later stage can extract target/draft, same-PP, and MHA/MLA logical layer selection into a Common helper, leaving Mori responsible only for mapping the common plan to `MemoryDesc` and `batch_write()`. ## 5. Initialize Mooncake state before starting the control thread Related commit: - `12a88dbcfe` — `initialize Mooncake session state before control thread` Mooncake Prefill previously started its receive thread before creating state that the thread accesses: ```text session_failures failed_sessions session_lock ``` If Decode registration arrived immediately after thread startup, it could hit an initialization race. This PR only moves these three fields before `start_prefill_thread()` while preserving all other queue, worker, probe, and receive ordering. This is intentionally a minimal ordering fix rather than a Step 1 reorganization of backend thread lifecycle. When the common Manager/Transport is extracted, control-thread initialization, startup, shared state, and shutdown should be managed together. ## Testing CPU red/green regression tests are kept on a dedicated test branch: ```text branch: https://github.com/jambow0320/sglang/tree/rfc-pd-test path: test/registered/unit/disaggregation/rfc-test/ ``` Coverage includes: - Mori ABORT delivery before guard validation; - Cleared-room stale work in NIXL/Mori; - Malformed control-message isolation in Mooncake/NIXL; - Mori speculative MHA descriptor selection; - Mooncake session-state initialization order. The tests pass with the fixes and reproduce the original failures against the corresponding unfixed source. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32466303515](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32466303515)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32466303525](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32466303525)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32466303785](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32466303785)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [AMD] Fix Qwen3.5 MTP dropping fused shared-expert weights
signal.text: ## Motivation Since #33889, Qwen3.5 MXFP4 with MTP speculative decoding on MI355X lost about 12% throughput. The cause is that the MTP draft model is loaded without its shared-expert weights. **What fusion does to the weight layout.** When a Qwen3.5 MoE layer fuses its shared expert, it deliberately does not build a separate `shared_expert` module — the shared expert becomes one more routed expert, living in slot `num_experts`. Any loader for such a layer therefore has to route `mlp.shared_expert.*` into that slot. `qwen3_5.py` does exactly that; `qwen3_5_mtp.py` never learned to. **Why the target model is unaffected.** In this checkpoint the target's routed experts are MXFP4 while its shared expert stays bf16. Fusing them would push a higher-precision tensor through the quantized routed-expert path, so `can_fuse_shared_expert()` refuses. The target therefore always takes the unfused path, keeps its `shared_expert` module, and loads normally — the gap in the MTP loader is invisible from here. **Why the draft model is affected, and only recently.** The MTP module is excluded from quantization in full: all 1536 `mtp.*` routed-expert tensors and its shared expert alike. The draft is thus uniformly bf16, nothing is mixed-precision, and fusing it is perfectly valid — the gate correctly says yes. It simply never had the chance before. Until #33889, the target's Quark config installed a single process-wide `disable_shared_experts_fusion` override, which switched fusion off for every runner, draft included. #33889 made that decision per-runner, so the draft started fusing for the first time and immediately ran into the loader gap. **Why nobody noticed.** With fusion on there is no `shared_expert` module to load into, and the expert mapping only covers slots `0 .. num_experts-1`, so each `mlp.shared_expert.{gate,up,down}_proj.weight` matches nothing and ends at `logger.warning_once("Parameter ... not found in params_dict, skip loading")` — three tensors per TP rank, one suppressed log line, no error. The draft then runs with an uninitialized shared expert. Since a speculative draft cannot corrupt verified output, accuracy is unaffected; the damage appears only as a fall in accept rate, from 0.65 to 0.51, and hence in throughput. This PR teaches the MTP loader to place those weights into the fused slot, so the draft that #33889 legitimately enabled actually receives them. ## Modifications `python/sglang/srt/models/qwen3_5_mtp.py`, mirroring `qwen3_5.py`: - Size the expert mapping as `num_experts + num_fused_shared_experts` so slot `num_experts` has an entry. The fusion count is read from the constructed modules, because `num_fused_shared_experts` is set on `Qwen3_5MoeForConditionalGeneration` and the MTP wraps a `Qwen3_5ForCausalLM`, which does not carry it. - Rewrite `mlp.shared_expert.` to `mlp.experts.{num_experts}.` before the mapping loops. Both are keyed on the model's actual fusion state rather than on a platform check. When nothing fuses, `num_fused_shared_experts` is `0`, the mapping size is unchanged and the rewrite never fires, so this is a no-op for every non-fusing configuration. Not covered: the fused-checkpoint variant (a single `experts.gate_up_proj` tensor). `qwen3_5.py` handles that with a dedicated branch that chunks the tensor into `w1`/`w3`; the MTP loader's `load_fused_expert_weights` indexes per expert id and cannot serve a single shared-expert tensor. Adding that path untested seemed worse than leaving it, since no checkpoint on hand exercises it. ## Accuracy Tests No accuracy change is expected: only the draft model changes, and a speculative draft cannot alter verified output. The visible effect is the accept rate. Measured over ~100 decode-batch samples per point. | conc | accept_len before | after | accept_rate before | after | |---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 4 | 2.5278 | 2.9533 | 0.5097 | 0.6509 | | 8 | 2.5507 | 2.9374 | 0.5168 | 0.6457 | | 16 | 2.5144 | 2.9508 | 0.5054 | 0.6501 | Skipped weights during load go from 3 per TP rank to 0. ## Speed Tests and Profiling ### Summary at conc=4 | Config | Total Throughput | Median E2E (ms) | Median TTFT (ms) | Median TPOT (ms) | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:| | `eda0ddc260d4` (last good) | 5365.74 | 5992.71 | 326.84 | 6.25 | | `b61a06921e` (#33889) | 4716.15 | 6662.60 | 322.72 | 7.05 | | `b61a06921e` + PR #35719 | 5429.77 | 5912.64 | 326.93 | 6.11 | The third row was obtained by switching shared-expert fusion off on `b61a06921e`, which removes the unloaded-shared-expert condition from the draft; this PR removes the same condition by loading the fused weights instead of dropping them. ### Full sweep MI355X, `amd/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-MXFP4`, TP=2, EAGLE MTP (3 steps / topk 1 / 4 draft tokens), page-size 16, `fp8_e4m3` KV, `--attention-backend aiter`, ISL=8192 / OSL=1024, `num_prompts = 10 x conc`, server relaunched per concurrency with `--max-running-requests = conc`. Server flags follow `benchmarks/single_node/fixed_seq_len/qwen3.5_fp4_mi355x_mtp.sh`. Before and after were run back to back on the same GPU pair, both at `7f8f030000`. | conc | Total Throughput before | after | Delta | Median E2E (ms) before | after | Median TTFT (ms) before | after | Median TPOT (ms) before | after | |---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 4 | 4746.11 | 5417.31 | **+14.14%** | 6726.7 | 5969.1 | 333.3 | 336.7 | 7.07 | 6.22 | | 8 | 6835.64 | 7626.54 | **+11.57%** | 9243.7 | 8370.3 | 336.4 | 335.9 | 9.67 | 8.82 | | 16 | 9011.82 | 10141.08 | **+12.53%** | 13997.8 | 12840.5 | 346.1 | 361.6 | 14.86 | 13.48 | The gain is decode-side, as expected from an accept-rate change: TTFT is flat, TPOT improves by 9–12%. This restores the configuration to its previously published InferenceX level. The last sweep on image `lmsysorg/sglang-rocm:v0.5.16-rocm720-mi35x-20260730` recorded 582.84 / 852.30 / 1130.14 output tok/s at conc 4 / 8 / 16; with this patch the same setup measures 602.47 / 857.12 / 1123.38. Bisecting `accept len` over the 759 commits between that image's sglang and `63d783bbe0` lands on #33889, with a clean split (2.84–2.92 before, 2.50–2.57 after, no intermediate values). ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32499687037](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32499687037)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32499686918](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32499686918)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32499686928](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32499686928)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [AMD] Add HiCache KV offloading for Qwen3.5 MXFP4 MI355X cookbook
signal.text: ## Summary Add HiCache host-DRAM KV offloading support for the Qwen3.5-397B-A17B MXFP4 MI355X deployment, and bump the MI355X Docker image. ## Changes ### Deployment Generator (`qwen35-deployment.jsx`) - Add a **KV Offloading** UI toggle with two options: `Disabled` (default) and `HiCache`. - Only visible when MI355X + FP4 + 397B is selected. - When HiCache is enabled, emits: - `--enable-hierarchical-cache` - `--hicache-ratio 1.5` - `--hicache-write-policy write_through` - `--hicache-io-backend direct` - `--hicache-mem-layout page_first_direct` - These flags enable host-DRAM KV cache offloading, allowing higher concurrency beyond GPU-resident KV limits for agentic workloads. ### Cookbook Page (`Qwen3.5.mdx`) - Bump MI355X Docker image: `v0.5.15.post1-rocm720-mi35x-20260715` → `v0.5.17-rocm720-mi35x-20260818`. - Add HiCache KV offloading note in the deployment notes section. ## Motivation Aligned with [InferenceX #2693](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/pull/2693), which adds HiCache host-DRAM KV tier arms to the Qwen3.5 MXFP4 MI355X AgentX sweep (TP4 concurrency 40–64, TP2 concurrency 20–32 with HiCache). cc @yichiche

signal.title: fix(mem_cache): honor the pool device for speculative mamba caches
signal.text: ## Motivation `MambaPool` allocates its speculative-decoding scratch buffers with a hardcoded `device="cuda"`, while every sibling allocation in the same constructor honors the `device` argument. Any non-CUDA device that enables speculative decoding for a hybrid linear-attention model therefore fails during pool construction, before the first forward pass: ``` File "/work/python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/memory_pool.py", line 705, in __init__ intermediate_ssm_state_cache = torch.zeros(..., device="cuda") AssertionError: Torch not compiled with CUDA enabled ``` All three occurrences are inside the `speculative_num_draft_tokens is not None` branch, which is why the non-speculative path on CPU/NPU was never affected. One of them even sits under a comment that reads *"Original dense layout (NPU/CPU, or EAGLE tree verify)"* — the layout was already meant to serve non-CUDA devices, only the allocation device was not. ## Modifications `python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/memory_pool.py` — replace the three hardcoded `device="cuda"` literals with the pool's device: | Allocation | Before | After | Reachable on CPU/NPU today | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `intermediate_ssm_state_cache` | `device="cuda"` | `device=device` | Yes — this is the one that aborts | | `intermediate_conv_window_cache` | `device="cuda"` | `device=device` | Yes | | `_allocate_deduplicated_conv_window` (`phys`) | `device="cuda"` | `device=self.device` | No | The first two are in the dense layout that `conv_window_dedup_enabled()` selects for NPU/CPU, so they abort today. The third is in the deduplicated layout, which that same gate restricts to CUDA, so it is currently a no-op — fixed for consistency, so that relaxing the gate later does not reintroduce the bug in the one place it was missed. No behavior change on CUDA: `device` is `"cuda"` there. Adds `test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_mamba_pool_speculative_device.py` (registered CPU unit test) covering both intermediate layouts, since the deduplicated and dense paths allocate through separate code. The test patches the platform predicate to reach each layout, because neither is reachable from both sides on a single runner. ## Accuracy Tests No effect on model outputs — this only changes where the tensors are allocated. Verified on an Intel Xeon host (128 physical cores / 256 logical across 4 NUMA nodes) with `--device cpu --attention-backend intel_amx` and `Qwen3.5-9B`, which previously aborted during pool construction and now allocates cleanly: ``` Mamba Cache is allocated. max_mamba_cache_size: 17, conv_state size: 0.02GB, ssm_state size: 0.84GB intermediate_ssm_state_cache size: 4.50GB intermediate_conv_window_cache size: 0.11GB ``` (That run still stops later at a separate, unrelated gap — the CPU GDN kernels have no target-verify entry points yet. That is out of scope here and will be a follow-up PR; this change is a strict prerequisite for it.) ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not applicable — allocation-site change only, no change to any hot path. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the Format code with pre-commit. - [x] Add unit tests according to the Run and add unit tests. - [ ] Update documentation according to Write documentations. - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to Test the accuracy and Benchmark the speed. - [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32499595945](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32499595945)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32499595693](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32499595693)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32499596136](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32499596136)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [FlashInfer] perf: Fuse FP4 MoE input quantization and shared-expert SwiGLU
signal.text: ## Motivation This PR depends on [FlashInfer PR #4640](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/4640) for `mm_bf16_swiglu`. FlashInfer's `void flashinfer::trtllm_mnnvl_allreduce::oneshotAllreduceFusionKernel` can fuse nvfp4 quantization within the AR+Norm kernel, saving a kernel launch before every MoE call. Although this seemed a flat flashinfer API usage, this exposed the issue highlighted [here](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/4640#issuecomment-5370216869); thus we need a workaround to make the integration e2e valuable perf wise. ## Modifications - Feed fused all-reduce + residual + RMSNorm FP4 outputs directly into the FlashInfer TRT-LLM MoE runner. - Use FlashInfer BF16 GEMM1 + SwiGLU for eligible shared experts during decode/target verification, with an M ≤ 64 gate and existing fallbacks. - Prepare the fused shared-expert weight layout after loading and add focused integration/eligibility tests. ## Performance GLM-5.2-NVFP4, TP4; random 1,024-token input and 1,024-token output; total requests = 16 × concurrency. Values are median TPOT in ms/token (lower is better). Baseline: `main@0e4a09480c`; feature: `2113186027`. Both runs used the FlashInfer 0.6.17 compatibility overlay through `f0f8760e`. | Concurrency | `main` | This PR | Improvement | | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | | 1 | 6.552 | 6.498 | +0.82% | | 2 | 7.044 | 6.950 | +1.33% | | 4 | 7.998 | 7.924 | +0.93% | | 8 | 9.598 | 9.474 | +1.30% | | 16 | 12.433 | 12.306 | +1.02% | | 32 | 15.861 | 15.649 | +1.34% | | 64 | 20.225 | 20.320 | -0.47% | In this single sweep, the feature improves median TPOT by 0.82–1.34% through concurrency 32 and regresses by 0.47% at concurrency 64. main: The down projection gemm on the shared path can't execute immediately after the activation, fortunately it doesn't spill after the down proj gemm on the routed path for bs=1 in most of the cases. PR: NVFP4 quantization call is gone and down proj gemm on shared path can execute immediately after the first fused gemm. --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :x: [Run #32497779839](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32497779839) Latest PR Test (Extra): :x: [Run #32497779063](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32497779063) Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): :x: [Run #32497779884](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32497779884)

signal.title: [Deepseek-V4] Enable shared-experts fusion on the flashinfer_mxfp4 (trtllm-gen) MoE path
signal.text: ## Summary Enable shared-experts fusion for DeepSeek-V4-Flash on the `flashinfer_mxfp4` (trtllm-gen) path: the shared expert is routed as expert slot 256 through the same MoE kernel, so the whole MoE runs on a single stream instead of a separate FP8 MLP on an alternate stream (~4 fewer kernel launches + 2 fewer stream syncs per layer). The machinery already existed (#27349); this PR enables and validates it. Also adds a guard rejecting fusion under EP without per-rank shared slots, which would silently compute wrong results. ## Scope - `deepseek_v4.py`: EP guard in the fusion gate (11 lines). - New CPU unit test for the load-time FP8→MXFP4 shared-expert requant (byte-level packing/scale contract). - Recipes: add `--enforce-shared-experts-fusion` to the b200/b300/gb200/gb300 flash-official fp4 low-latency entries. ## Testing - Kernel: verified out-of-tree on GB200 with a standalone test at the fused shape (257 experts / top-k 7, every token hits the shared slot), 12/12 vs a dequantized torch reference; no flashinfer change needed. Test available on request. - Unit: `test/registered/unit/models/test_deepseek_v4_mxfp4_shared_expert_requant.py`. - Profiler: with fusion on, the shared-expert kernels disappear and the MoE runs on a single stream. ## Results GB200 tp4, only variable is the fusion flag. Accuracy: | Benchmark | baseline (off) | fused (on) | |---|---|---| | gsm8k 8-shot 1319q (3 runs) | 0.949 / 0.954 / 0.954 | 0.951 / 0.952 / 0.948 | | AIME25 pass@1[avg-of-16] (thinking, effort max) | 99.79% ± 0.83 | 99.17% ± 1.49 | | AIME25 pass@16 / majority@16 | 100% / 100% | 100% / 100% | Performance (bench_serving, random 1024in/512out): | QPS | Mean TTFT | Mean ITL | P99 ITL | Output tput | |---|---|---|---|---| | 1 | 240→208 ms (-13.4%) | 7.74→7.43 ms (-4.0%) | 24.0→20.3 ms (-15.4%) | flat | | 4 | 334→287 ms (-14.0%) | 22.8→20.3 ms (-10.8%) | 385→183 ms (-52.6%) | flat | | 8 | 494→390 ms (-21.0%) | flat | 946→675 ms (-28.6%) | +0.6% | Warmed gsm8k e2e +5-7%; bs1 decode median 6.94→6.83 ms. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32498573043](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32498573043)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32498572168](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32498572168)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32498572647](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32498572647)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: Restructure mem_cache auto-labels by layer
signal.text: ## Summary The `hicache` auto-label rule in `.github/labeler.yml` only matched files whose path contains the substring `hicache`. This misses the files that **define and own** HiCache: | File | What it owns | |---|---| | `python/sglang/srt/managers/cache_controller.py` | `class HiCacheController` | | `python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/hiradix_cache.py` | `class HiRadixCache(RadixCache)` | | `python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/memory_pool_host.py` | HiCache host memory pool | | `python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/storage/**` | HiCache storage backends (hf3fs / mooncake / nixl / eic / aibrix / simm) | | `python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/hybrid_cache/**` | Hybrid cache controller | | `test/registered/hicache/**` | HiCache test group | Of all files referencing `hicache` / `HiRadixCache` identifiers, ~50 core files in `python/sglang/srt/` were not labeled because their filename does not contain `hicache` — including the controller class definition itself. Add the territory paths plus a case-insensitive `**/*HiCache*` glob. ## Out of scope (intentional) Generic call-site files (`scheduler.py`, `server_args.py`, `model_runner.py`, `http_server.py`, observability mixins, disagg modules) are **not** added. signal.title: fix: shrink --hicache-size budget for SIDECAR draft host pool
signal.text: ## Motivation When `--hicache-size` is set (fixed GB budget for host-side KV cache) and a SIDECAR draft model is registered, the draft model also gets a host-side KV pool that must match the target's token count (for 1-to-1 index sharing in L2 transfers). However, the draft's per-token byte cost can be **larger** than the target's (e.g. quantized target + bf16 draft), causing the combined target+draft host memory allocation to **exceed** the user-specified `--hicache-size` budget. In practice this causes the server to OOM on startup. For example, with a quantized 27B target + bf16 1.5B draft at TP=4: - Target host pool: 7.60 GB/rank - Draft host pool: 9.50 GB/rank - **Total: 17.10 GB/rank** — far exceeding the 4 GB `--hicache-size` cap ## Modifications Add `_adjust_hicache_size_for_draft()` in `kv_cache_builder.py` which: 1. Computes the per-token byte cost of both target and draft device pools via `_device_pool_size_per_token()`, which derives the cost from pool geometry (head_dim, head_num, layer_num, dtype for MHA; kv_cache_dim, layer_num, dtype for MLA) rather than `get_kv_size_bytes()`, since the device pool may be in post-capture mode where buffers are not yet allocated. 2. Shrinks the budget by the factor `target_spt / (target_spt + draft_spt)` so the total (target + draft) stays within the user's `--hicache-size` cap. 3. Reduces both `hicache_size` and `hicache_ratio` (the latter needed because post-capture pools have zero allocated buffers, so sizing falls back to the ratio). 4. Runs before `create_tree_cache()` so the adjusted values flow into both the tree cache and the memory bag. The adjustment only applies in fixed-size (`hicache_size > 0`) mode; ratio mode already scales both pools proportionally. ## Accuracy Tests This change does not affect model outputs — it only adjusts host memory pool sizing. No accuracy impact. ## Speed Tests and Profiling This change does not impact inference speed. It only prevents OOM at startup when using speculative decoding with HiCache. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32497855405](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32497855405)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32497855075](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32497855075)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32497855339](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32497855339)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [P/D disagg] Decode-side radix cache for DeepSeek-V4 (DSA compressed KV)
signal.text: ## Motivation Extend the decode-side radix cache for SWA hybrid models in P/D disaggregation to **DeepSeek-V4** (DSA compressed KV). DSV4 was previously rejected at startup; on CUDA the rejection is unnecessary: - The c4 / c4-indexer / c128 pools have **no allocator of their own** — their rows derive positionally from the virtual full-id space (`full_id // ratio`) and live/die with the FULL allocator's pages. The `[FULL, SWA]` unified-tree components therefore already keep every compressed pool coherent on prefix reuse (this is also why non-disaggregated radix caching already works for DSV4). - `page_size` 256 is a multiple of both 4 and 128, so a page-aligned prefix boundary is always a compressed-group boundary. - The existing SWA-tail prealloc machinery (prefix cap at the sliding-window start, extra-window retention, SWA lock-uuid protocol, dual-pool budgets) applies unchanged; DSV4 already runs it today without radix. The guard now keeps **NPU** (separate c4/c128 allocators + a tree-level C128 sidecar, not wired for the decode-radix lock path) and **HIP** (unified-kv SWA ring is per-request, not content-stable) rejected with explicit errors, and only opens the CUDA path. Also fixes a latent cache-hit-kit bug: a router's `/server_info` does not expose the backend page size, so the expected-cache computation ran with `page_size=1` (no alignment). The gpt-oss coverage survived only because `384 + 64` divides by 64 exactly. The kit now takes an explicit `page_size`, and the decode-radix mixin probes the decode server for it. ## Test - New `test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_kv_cache_builder_decode_radix_guards.py` (CPU): NPU/HIP rejections hold, CUDA passes. - `test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_decode_radix_lock_ref.py`: DSV4-geometry property test — with window 128 < page 256 the radix prefix cap stays page- and compress-group-aligned, keeps one full window before the insert boundary, and prompts ≤ 512 tokens reuse nothing. - New `test/registered/disaggregation/test_disaggregation_decode_radix_cache_swa_dsv4.py` (8-gpu-h200, extra-b): DeepSeek-V4-Flash-FP8, non-spec, mooncake; multi-turn cache-hit growth + two-pass GSM8K non-regression via the shared mixin (now parameterized). - CPU: guards + lock_ref + queue_cleanup + hisparse_allocator — 28 passed; unified radix cache suite — 1082 passed, 50 subtests. - End-to-end on 8xH20, 4P+4D, nixl, DeepSeek-V4-Flash (MXFP4), non-spec: - multi-turn cache hits `0 -> 1024 -> 2048` cached tokens per client across rounds, matching page-aligned expectations exactly, identical before and after GSM8K churn; - two-pass GSM8K (100 examples): **0.96 / 0.96, zero drop**, second pass faster (981 vs 950 tok/s); - idle full/swa usage returns to ~0; no asserts, no 503 aborts, no retractions. - End-to-end **cross-node** on 2x 8xH20 (dedicated prefill node + decode node, 8P+8D, tp=8 each, sglang-router), nixl, DeepSeek-V4-Flash (MXFP4), non-spec: - repeated 1201-token prompts through the router: `cached_tokens` `0 -> 1024` across passes (page-256 aligned), decode-side prefix reuse intact across nodes; - GSM8K sanity through the router: 50/50 correct, 0 truncations, 0 errors; - shared-prefix benchmark (`generated-shared-prefix`: 8 groups x 32 prompts, 8192-token shared system prompt, 128-token question, 256 output tokens; 256 requests, max-concurrency 32), decode radix ON vs OFF (flag removed, otherwise identical cluster): | metric | radix ON | baseline | delta | |---|---|---|---| | median TTFT | 1,226 ms | 1,919 ms | **-36%** | | mean TTFT | 2,589 ms | 2,969 ms | -13% | | P90 TTFT | 7,976 ms | 8,763 ms | -9% | | median E2E | 5,024 ms | 5,458 ms | -8% | | request throughput | 5.00 req/s | 4.84 req/s | +3.3% | | output throughput | 1,280 tok/s | 1,239 tok/s | +3.3% | - both runs 256/256 successful, zero errors/retractions. The throughput delta is modest because the workload is decode-dominated (256 output tokens per request); the cache removes the per-request cross-node KV transfer of the ~8.2k-token shared prefix, which lands in TTFT. The test cluster routes UCX over TCP (no cross-subnet RoCE on its fabric), which amplifies the transfer savings — on an RDMA fabric the absolute TTFT gap is expected to narrow, with the direction unchanged. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to the [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32484214033](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32484214033)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32484213817](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32484213817)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32484214002](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32484214002)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [AMD] Fix Quark W4A4 MXFP4 MoE clamped-SwiGLU on the AITER path
signal.text: ## Motivation The Quark W4A4 MXFP4 scheme omits `swiglu_limit` when building `AiterMoeQuantInfo`, so MiniMax-M3's clamped-SiLU MoE (`gemm1_alpha`=1.702, `gemm1_clamp_limit`=7.0) never gets clamped in the AITER runner (`layers/moe/moe_runner/aiter.py`), producing garbage output. This PR fixes output quality for `amd/MiniMax-M3-MXFP4`. ## Modifications `python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/quark/schemes/quark_w4a4_mxfp4_moe.py` (mirrors `Mxfp4MoEMethod`): - `create_moe_runner`: for the AITER backend, translate `activation` to `"swiglu"` via `dataclasses.replace` when a clamp limit is set (`gemm1_clamp_limit`/`swiglu_limit > 0`). - `apply_weights`: forward `swiglu_limit = gemm1_clamp_limit or swiglu_limit or 0.0` onto `AiterMoeQuantInfo`. Both are **gated on a positive clamp limit**, so plain-SwiGLU Quark MXFP4 models (limit unset → 0.0) keep `activation="silu"` and `swiglu_limit=0.0` and are unchanged. Runtime note: to match MiniMax-M3's `interleaved=False` gate/up layout, launch with `SGLANG_USE_AITER_MOE_GU_ITLV=0` (SEPARATED gate_mode). This env is already handled upstream in the AITER runner; this PR only makes the runner reach that path. ## Accuracy Tests amd/MiniMax-M3-MXFP4, TP4, MI350x/MI355x. - Before this fix: MXFP4 output is incoherent (token-salad); - After this fix: coherent output; AIME25 ≈ 0.81–0.83 (n=10) vs 0.88 for the BF16 baseline. GSM8k test: { "gsm8k": { "name": "gsm8k", "alias": "gsm8k", "sample_len": 1319, "exact_match,strict-match": 0.9507202426080363, "exact_match_stderr,strict-match": 0.00596215065581247, "exact_match,flexible-extract": 0.9613343442001516, "exact_match_stderr,flexible-extract": 0.005310583162098061 } } evalscope:10 times AIME25 { "aime25/MiniMax-M3-MXFP4@aime25": 0.8367, "aime25/mean_acc": 0.8367, "aime25/default": 0.8367 } ## Benchmarking and Profiling The changed branch is taken only for clamped-SwiGLU checkpoints, and plain-SwiGLU Quark MXFP4 models run the identical code path as before (`activation="silu"`, `swiglu_limit=0.0`), so there is no hot-path change. Serving throughput of `amd/MiniMax-M3-MXFP4` with the fix applied (`SGLANG_USE_AITER`, `SGLANG_USE_AITER_MOE_GU_ITLV=0`), TP4 on MI350x: Config: `generated-shared-prefix`, concurrency 4 (unbounded request rate), 1024 in / 1024 out, 32 requests, 208 s. | Metric | Value | | --- | --- | | Requests completed | 32 | | Request throughput | 0.15 req/s | | Output throughput | **307 tok/s** | | Total throughput | 12,886 tok/s | | Input throughput | 12,579 tok/s | | Effective concurrency | 4.0 | Latency (median / p99): | Metric | Median | p99 | | --- | --- | --- | | E2E latency | 25.5 s | 29.0 s | | TTFT | 1.77 s | 5.86 s | | TPOT (per output token) | 11.9 ms | 12.2 ms | | ITL (inter-token) | 11.6 ms | 23.3 ms | ## Unit tests `test/registered/unit/layers/quantization/test_quark_w4a4_mxfp4_moe.py` (CPU-only): asserts the activation translation happens iff a clamp limit is set, and that `swiglu_limit` is forwarded (clamped) / stays 0.0 (unclamped). ## Checklist - [x] Format code with pre-commit (black 26.1.0, isort 7.0.0). - [x] Add unit tests. - [X] Provide accuracy/speed benchmark results (fill in exact numbers above). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance. ## Review and Merge Process 1. signal.title: Add PD test for inkling with mxfp8 KV
signal.text: ## Motivation Inkling is the widest single-model exercise of the multi-component state transfer we have. One request carries the main KV list plus four state components, and with MXFP8 KV they cover three of the five index-payload builders: | Component | Index payload | | --- | --- | | `SWA` | window, translated into the SWA index space | | `MAMBA` | per-request ShortConv state slot | | `BLOCK_SCALE` | whole sequence, full KV index space | | `BLOCK_SCALE_SWA` | window, SWA index space | A model that ships one or two components leaves most of that dispatch untested. Nothing launched a PD pair for this one, so registration, per-component index payloads, and the page-granular slicing behind them had no end-to-end guard on the path where they interact -- which is where both of the last two defects in this area lived. MXFP8 KV needs SM100+, so the case is registered on a Blackwell runner. Only the MXFP8 configuration is covered. It is a superset of bf16 at the orchestration level -- same components, same transfer, same hierarchical prefill cache, plus the two scale components -- and bf16 PD is already exercised by the existing disaggregation tests, so a second case would spend another server pair on largely duplicated coverage. HiCache rides the prefill role only: the decode role forces chunk cache, and its radix opt-in is refused for sliding-window models. `start_prefill` / `start_decode` are overridden because the fixture pins `--tp 1`, the same reason `test_disaggregation_dsv4.py` overrides them. ## Verification Five local runs on 4xB200, one prefill and one decode role at TP=2 each, mooncake over IB: 400-491s, gsm8k 0.845-0.890. `est_time=600` covers all of them. The host cache is given an absolute size rather than the default ratio. The ratio scales with the device pool, which put the prefill role alone at ~103 GB of host memory across its ranks and got the pair OOM-killed on a runner; a fixed 8 GB keeps the tiering exercised and the footprint predictable. Reverting the MXFP8 scale exposure takes it red at server launch, so the case guards what it claims to: ``` NotImplementedError: KV transfer / disaggregation is unsupported for MXFP8 KV cache (scale buffers are not exposed). ```

signal.title: [Feature] Router GEMM should keep fp32 output under deterministic inference (DeepSeek V3/V4)
signal.text: ### Checklist - [x] If this is not a feature request but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed. - [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Motivation The DeepSeek router GEMM should output fp32 under deterministic inference too. Today it falls back to bf16, and that is not needed for batch invariance. `python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_v2.py:512`: ```python if get_exec().deterministic.enable_deterministic_inference: return F.linear(hidden_states, self.weight, None) # -> bf16 logits ``` Every other branch in the same function returns fp32: `dsv3_router_gemm(out_dtype=torch.float32)`, `linear_bf16_fp32`, and the prefill-CP path. **fp32 output does not break batch invariance.** Batch invariance is about reduction order, not output dtype. Deterministic `F.linear` runs `matmul_kernel_persistent`, which accumulates in fp32 and already has an fp32 store branch (`batch_invariant_ops.py:167`) that is never reached. It is the same kernel with the same reduction; only the final store differs. The branch is unreachable because `_matmul_persistent_triton` allocates output as the input dtype (`batch_invariant_ops.py:185`). Same for the JIT `dsv3_router_gemm` kernel, where `kOutFloat` only changes `cast<OutT>(final_sum)`. **Impact.** Router logits feed `noaux_tc` top-k over 256/384 experts with an fp32 correction bias. bf16 has 8 mantissa bits, so adjacent expert scores often sit within one ULP and rounding can change which experts are selected — a different answer, not a small numeric difference. **Related bug.** `_mm_dtype_compat` (`batch_invariant_ops.py:967`), registered for `aten::mm.dtype`, does `matmul_persistent(...).to(out_dtype)`, i.e. fp32 -> bf16 -> fp32. Callers asking for fp32 get bf16 values. ### Proposed change 1. Add `out_dtype` (or a preallocated `output`) to `matmul_persistent` / `_matmul_persistent_triton` so the existing fp32 store branch is reachable. Tiling and accumulation order are unchanged. 2. Use it in `_mm_dtype_compat` instead of `.to(out_dtype)`. 3. In `DeepseekV2MoEGate.forward`, request fp32 out from the batch-invariant matmul instead of returning bare `F.linear`. 4. Keep one kernel for all M under deterministic mode — the normal path switches kernels at `max_router_gemm_tokens` (4 on SM100/103, else 16), and a token-count-dependent switch is batch-variant on its own. 5. `_matmul_persistent_deepgemm` allocates `out` as `a.dtype` for `deep_gemm.bf16_gemm_nn`; either find an fp32-out entry point or route fp32 requests to Triton. Cost should be negligible — the GEMM is `[M, 7168] x [7168, 256]` and this only changes the store dtype. ### Related resources - `python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_v2.py:512` - `python/sglang/srt/batch_invariant_ops/batch_invariant_ops.py:167,185,275,967` - `python/sglang/kernels/jit/csrc/gemm/dsv3_router_gemm.cuh` — `kOutFloat` - #12095 — added the `F.linear` fallback

signal.title: [Bug] A global --attention-backend kills the server when a non-DiT component does not declare it (MiniMax-H3 audio_vae)
signal.text: ### Checklist - [x] I searched related issues but found no solution. - [x] The bug persists in the latest version. - [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback. - [x] Please use English. ### Describe the bug Passing a global `--attention-backend` that the *DiT* supports takes the whole server down if any **non-DiT** component's attention layer does not declare that backend — even when the layer declares a `default_attention_backend` for exactly this case. With MiniMax-H3 and `--attention-backend sage_attn`: ``` ValueError: Attention backend 'sage_attn' is not supported by this attention layer; supported backends: ['fa', 'torch_sdpa'] ... Failed to load customized audio_vae ... Rank 0 scheduler is dead ``` The audio VAE's attention layer is constructed with both a supported set and a default: `python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/models/vaes/minimax_h3_audio_vae/audio_vae.py:60-70` ```python supported_attention_backends={AttentionBackendEnum.FA, AttentionBackendEnum.TORCH_SDPA}, default_attention_backend=AttentionBackendEnum.TORCH_SDPA, ``` `get_attn_backend()` does have a fallback path, but it is gated on the selection not being explicit (`selector.py:188-201`): ```python selection_is_explicit = isinstance(server_args, ServerArgs) and server_args.is_arg_explicitly_set("attention_backend") ... elif not selection_is_explicit: allowed_fallback_reason = "platform default fallback" ``` A `--attention-backend` on the command line is explicit, so `allowed_fallback_reason` stays `None`, `candidate_backends` holds only the requested backend, and `selector.py:233-241` turns it into the hard `ValueError` above. Not honouring an explicit request silently is reasonable; the problem is that a *global* flag is treated as an explicit request **for every component**, including ones that cannot possibly satisfy it and that ship a declared default for that situation. Practical consequence: any global sparse/fp8 attention backend requires the operator to know the full component list up front and repeat it, and getting it wrong is a dead server rather than a warning. On MiniMax-H3 all three non-DiT components (`text_encoder`, `audio_vae`, `video_vae`) have to be exempted, and the set has grown between nightlies, so a config that worked on an earlier image fails on a later one with an error that points at the VAE rather than at the flag. ### Reproduction ```bash sglang serve --model-path <MiniMax-H3> --model-variant fl2va \ --num-gpus 1 --attention-backend sage_attn ``` Startup fails as above. Works with the components enumerated: ```bash --attention-backend sage_attn \ --component-attention-backends text_encoder=torch_sdpa,audio_vae=torch_sdpa,video_vae=torch_sdpa ``` ### Environment One RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition (sm_120), CUDA 13, `lmsysorg/sglang` nightly. The code path is unchanged on current `main` (read at `a49560ce50`), so this is not specific to that GPU or image — any global backend a non-DiT component doesn't declare reproduces it. ### Suggested direction Any of these would work; the first is the smallest: 1. Treat `--attention-backend` as explicit only for components that declare support, and fall back to the layer's `default_attention_backend` elsewhere with a `logger.warning` naming the component. This keeps "don't silently downgrade what the user asked for" for the DiT, where the request is meaningful. 2. Keep failing closed, but make the message actionable: name the component being loaded and print the `--component-attention-backends component=torch_sdpa` line that fixes it. Happy to send a PR for either once maintainers pick one.

signal.text: ## Motivation `request_validation._validate_target` calls `warn_unverified_short_edge(short_edge)` unconditionally, so a stock request at the recommended short edge logs a warning that names the requested value as the verified one: ``` WARNING ... target.short_edge=768 is outside the verified configuration: 768 is the only short edge MiniMax publishes recipes and reference outputs for ... ``` `resolved_plan._validate_base_short_edge` already guards the same call with `if short_edge != MINIMAX_H3_BASE_SHORT_EDGE`.
