signal.title: [diffusion] Z-Image: autotune the shared transformer block at both token scales (H100 1024^2 denoise 13.58 -> 9.58 s, 1.42x)
signal.text: torch.compile on zimage-base gets 1.42x faster: steady-state denoise at 1024x1024 goes 13.575 s -> 9.577 s on one H100, from a single kernel. Z-Image reuses one transformer block for the context refiner (a few dozen caption tokens), the noise refiner (4096) and the unified stream (4128 at 1024x1024). The flash-attn call breaks the graph, so the block's attention compiles into a frame of its own that is entered with all three counts; automatic dynamic shapes make its token dim symbolic, and Inductor autotunes the fused-qkv GEMM once, against whichever count it traced first. The caption branch wins that race and the resulting BLOCK_M=32/BLOCK_N=32 config then runs the 4096- and 4128-token layers too. It is the only dynamic-shape Triton template the model selects, and it accounts for the entire difference above. The same gap appears in the comparison table in BBuf/how-to-optim-algorithm-in-cuda#21. Set inductor's multi_kernel_hints for this model, so the block is compiled once per hint and dispatched on the runtime shape and the token dim stays dynamic. The knob is a generic DiTConfig.torch_compile_inductor_config passthrough that is empty for every other model; inductor config is process-global and is read when a graph compiles, so it cannot be scoped to the torch.compile call, and `mode` rules out torch.compile(options=...). The root cause is the flash-attn graph break, which is what routes three very different token counts through one compiled frame. Removing it would help any DiT with mixed sequence lengths and is worth doing separately. Test Plan: Steady-state denoise on one H100, min of requests 2..8 (request 1 carries the compile), stock preset with no extra flags: ``` export CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 CI=1 SGLANG_DIFFUSION_SYNC_STAGE_PROFILING=1 \ FLASHINFER_DISABLE_VERSION_CHECK=1 B=python/sglang/multimodal_gen/.claude/skills/sglang-diffusion-benchmark-profile/scripts/bench_diffusion_denoise.py rm -rf ~/.cache/sgl_diffusion/torch_compile_cache python3 $B --model zimage-base --iterations 8 --label compile --output-dir /tmp/zb python3 $B --model zimage-base --iterations 8 --label eager --no-torch-compile --output-dir /tmp/zb ``` | arm | denoise | | |----------------------|----------|--------------| | torch.compile before | 13.575 s | | | torch.compile after | 9.577 s | 1.42x faster | | eager, for reference | 9.567 s | | First-request e2e goes 79.6 s -> 96.2 s, the cost of autotuning the block at two sizes instead of one. Verified from the generated code that the fused-qkv site is now autotuned at 32, 64, 4096 and 4128 rather than at 32 alone. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32493494360](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32493494360)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32493494260](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32493494260)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32493494399](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32493494399)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Describe the bug On --device xpu, any speculative-decoding run on a hybrid GDN/linear-attention model (Qwen3.5) crashes in the target-verify path during the server's own warmup generation, before any user request. gdn_backend.py:43-48 binds the XPU kernel as-is: elif is_xpu(): from sgl_kernel import causal_conv1d_fn_xpu, causal_conv1d_update_xpu causal_conv1d_update = causal_conv1d_update_xpu but the is_target_verify branch at gdn_backend.py:539 calls it with five spec-only kwargs that the XPU op schema does not have — intermediate_conv_window, intermediate_state_indices, retrieve_next_token, retrieve_next_sibling, retrieve_parent_token. File "python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/linear/gdn_backend.py", line 539, in forward_extend mixed_qkv_processed = causal_conv1d_update( TypeError: causal_conv1d_update_xpu() got an unexpected keyword argument 'intermediate_conv_window' The scheduler dies, and the client then reports a downstream ConnectionError (secondary noise). signal.title: [PD] Introduce runtime role switching between prefill and decode
signal.text: ## [PD] Introduce runtime prefill<->decode role switching (mori backend) ### Motivation SGLang's PD disaggregation currently **pins each instance's role (`prefill` / `decode`) at startup** with no way to change it at runtime — to re-balance the P:D ratio you must tear down and relaunch servers. This PR introduces **runtime P<->D role switching**: an operator/router can convert a prefill instance into a decode instance (or vice versa) live, without restarting the server or reloading weights. It lands as a first PoC on the **mori** transfer backend; the control plane is backend-agnostic. ### Design: in-place role flip Key enabler: **the token KV pool is role-independent** — prefill and decode allocate the same KV memory structure. Only the *role-specific* disaggregation structures differ (prefill: bootstrap queue + KV sender; decode: receiver/poll threads, bootstrap registration, role-specific queues/metadata buffers). A flip therefore does **not** reallocate the KV pool or touch model weights. It only tears down and rebuilds the small role-specific structures, then re-dispatches the scheduler event loop to the new role. Draining to idle before teardown is a correctness requirement (an in-flight decode request's KV is owned by an upstream prefill). ### API ``` POST /pd_role_switch {"new_role": "prefill" | "decode", "decode_cuda_graph_bs": [..]?} ``` Gated by `--enable-pd-role-switch` (default **off**, zero impact on existing PD). ### What's in this PR - **Control plane**: `--enable-pd-role-switch`; `PdRoleSwitchReqInput/Output`; `POST /pd_role_switch`; `handle_pd_role_switch` + teardown/rebuild in a dedicated `disaggregation/role_switch.py`; event-loop re-dispatch on flip. Hardened with an in-progress re-entrancy guard, a fail-fast "unhealthy" state on rebuild failure, and table-driven precondition checks. - **Decode CUDA graph on flip**: enable and capture the decode graph on the flip to decode; the captured batch sizes are queryable via `/get_server_info` and can be passed as `decode_cuda_graph_bs` for a size-matched capture; idempotent. - **Backend opt-in interface**: `BaseKVManager.supports_role_switch` + `teardown()`, so other transfer backends can support role switching (checked up-front in the reject path). - **mori & mooncake backends**: teardown/rebuild hooks for KV-transfer managers (worker threads poll-based so they observe the stop flag; sockets, zmq context, RDMA registrations and the IOEngine / transfer engine released). mooncake: @LLLL114 (Mooncake team). - **Radix / hicache compatibility**: release the prefix cache on flip; removes the previous `--disable-radix-cache` requirement (works with `--disaggregation-decode-enable-radix-cache`). - **Plumbing / invariants**: `disagg_service.py` (bootstrap started on role-switch instances), `tokenizer_control_mixin.py`, `model_runner_kv_cache_mixin.py` (role-agnostic pre-alloc), `invariant_checker.py` (leak check keyed on the pool, not the role). - **Unit tests** (CPU-only, mocked): `test/registered/unit/disaggregation/test_pd_role_switch.py`. ### Validation **Unit tests** — `test/registered/unit/disaggregation/test_pd_role_switch.py`: **17 passed** (control-plane contract, all reject branches, same-role no-op, successful-flip orchestration, serialization, teardown thread-leak, radix-on prefix-cache release). **E2E accuracy (original)** — DeepSeek-R1-0528-MXFP4, 1P1D on 2×MI355X, mori KV transfer, TP8 (pure-TP MoE), concurrency 128, GSM8K (1319, lm_eval flexible/strict): | stage | flexible-extract | strict-match | |-------|------------------|--------------| | baseline (P=node A, D=node B) | 0.9469 | 0.9462 | | after flip (roles swapped via /pd_role_switch) | 0.9462 | 0.9454 | | after flip back (reverted) | 0.9416 | 0.9447 | **Accuracy + performance with radix cache ON (new)** — Qwen3-32B (dense, TP=8, pure-TP), mori, 1P1D on 2×MI300X; 8k1k = random 8192/1024, 320 prompts, concurrency 32, warmup 64: | state | gsm8k | out tok/s | total tok/s | TTFT med | TPOT med | |-------|-------|-----------|-------------|----------|----------| | ① baseline | 0.840 | 2680 | 24119 | 649 ms | 10.62 ms | | ② flip | 0.850 | 2655 | 23895 | 633 ms | 10.77 ms | | ③ flip-back | 0.840 | 2641 | 23772 | 679 ms | 10.69 ms | **Leak stress (new)** — 25 round-trip cycles = **100 role switches**, run once with the radix cache OFF and once ON, metrics recorded per cycle. `flip_fails=0`; weight / kvcache / graph / GPU-free / thread-count stay flat across cycles 2–25 in both configs ⇒ no resource leak. | metric (radix OFF) | baseline | cycles 1–25 | |--------------------|----------|-------------| | kvcache / graph (GB) | 115.05 / 1.09 | constant | | gpu_free (MB) | P=53567 D=53488 | constant | | threads (lwp) | P=2127 D=2047 | constant | | metric (radix ON) | baseline | cycles 1–25 | |-------------------|----------|-------------| | kvcache / graph (GB) | 115.05 / 1.07 | constant | | gpu_free (MB) | P=50908 D=50748 | bit-for-bit constant | | threads (lwp) | P=2519 D=2224 | ±16, non-monotonic | ### Limitations / follow-ups - Only the **mori** backend's teardown/rebuild hooks are implemented; other backends opt in via `supports_role_switch` + `teardown()`. - Validated with pure-TP MoE (`--tp-size 8`, no EP / DP-attention / MoE a2a). With `--moe-a2a-backend mori`, the a2a dispatch buffer is sized per-role at startup and is not yet rebuilt on flip — a follow-up. - Flip is driven externally (operator/router); an automatic load-based flip policy is out of scope here. ### How to use ```bash # launch both instances with the flag (add --disaggregation-decode-enable-radix-cache to run with radix on) python3 -m sglang.launch_server ... --disaggregation-mode prefill --enable-pd-role-switch python3 -m sglang.launch_server ... --disaggregation-mode decode --enable-pd-role-switch # (optional) query a decode server's captured decode-graph batch sizes curl http://<decode>:8000/get_server_info # -> internal_states[].decode_cuda_graph_bs # after draining, flip (optionally pass decode_cuda_graph_bs for a size-matched capture) curl http://<inst>:8000/pd_role_switch -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"new_role":"decode"}' ``` Co-authored-by: huanglong <huanglong@linux.alibaba.com> <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32485782530](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32485782530)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32485782309](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32485782309)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32485782487](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32485782487)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [fa] Make the FlashAttention backend extensible by subclasses
signal.text: ## Motivation `FlashAttentionBackend` is hard to specialize without copying it. Three things a subclass may need are not exposed today, leaving only the options of duplicating the backend or patching module globals: the logsumexp the kernel already computes, per-layer control of split-KV, and the choice of FA4 build. This adds a seam for each. All three are no-ops for current behavior. ## Modifications **`return_lse` on `forward_extend` / `forward_decode`.** The kernel already computes the logsumexp for the cascade merge and the backend discards it, and the forwards accept neither `return_lse` nor `**kwargs`, so a caller that needs the softmax normalizer has no way to get it. With `return_lse=True` they return `(output, lse)`, `lse` shaped `[total_q, num_heads]` (the varlen kernel emits it head-major). `_check_return_lse` raises on the combinations the paged path cannot serve — non-FA4, MLA, `fa_skip_kv_cache`, cross-attention, context parallelism, local and cascade attention — instead of returning a quietly wrong tensor. Defaults to `False`. **`_resolve_num_splits(layer, forward_batch, is_swa_layer)`.** Split-KV was read from `self.num_splits` at 13 kernel arguments, making it one value for the whole run. It is now resolved once per forward and threaded through, so a subclass can vary it per layer or per batch — for example forcing `1` on sliding-window layers, which degenerate when split. The base implementation returns `self.num_splits`. Since FA3's `scheduler_metadata` is precomputed from `self.num_splits`, the existing `sched_meta` gate also requires `num_splits == self.num_splits` so a subclass cannot reuse a schedule built for a different count; always true for the base class. **Kernel entry points as class attributes.** `flash_attn_with_kvcache` and `flash_attn_varlen_func` are bound on the class and the 15 invocations go through `self._flash_attn_*`, so a subclass can substitute a different FA4 build. ## Accuracy Tests Two cases added to `test/registered/attention/unittests/dense/test_fa4.py`, self-contained so the shared dense kit is untouched: - `test_return_lse` — calls the forwards directly, since `return_lse` is a backend-level contract and the `RadixAttention` dispatcher's custom-op schema cannot carry it, then checks the output and the LSE against a causal fp32 reference for MHA extend and GQA decode, plus the `[total_q, num_heads]` shape. - `test_return_lse_rejects_unsupported_paths` — the guarded paths raise, and the check is a no-op when the LSE is not requested. Both pass on a GB300 with no skips. Perturbing the returned LSE by a constant fails `test_return_lse` on 100% of elements, confirming the comparison is load-bearing. Not covered: windowed layers, because the dense harness leaves `attention_chunk_size` unset, so a `sliding_window_size` case is skipped for `fa4` before it asserts anything. The FA3 `sched_meta` gate was also not exercised, as the FA3 dense suite skips on that hardware; it is inert for the base class, whose hook returns `self.num_splits`. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not applicable. signal.title: [dLLM] Fix KV leak on FDFO abort and cap the staging token-budget fallback at one block
signal.text: ## Motivation Two device-agnostic dLLM correctness fixes found while running LLaDA2 FDFO at large batch sizes. Both reproduce on any backend (no device-specific branches involved). ### Bug 1: KV leak when aborting FDFO requests with unresolved blocks `RadixCache.cache_finished_req` slices `req_to_token` by `len(origin_input_ids + output_ids)`, but an FDFO request's unresolved denoise block exists only in `dllm_incomplete_ids` — its committed KV slots lie **beyond** that length. The tail free never sees those slots, so every aborted incomplete request orphans one block of KV, and the pool never recovers. **How to reproduce** (radix cache on, i.e. default): ```bash # 1. Launch a dLLM server; strict idle check turns the leak warning into a hard error. # --dllm-algorithm is the only required dLLM flag (FDFO and radix cache are on by # default; the attention backend is auto-resolved per platform). SGLANG_ENABLE_STRICT_MEM_CHECK_DURING_IDLE=1 \ python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model inclusionAI/LLaDA2.0-mini --trust-remote-code \ --dllm-algorithm LowConfidence # 2. Send concurrent long generations and hard-disconnect the clients mid-generation # (client-side timeout closes the connection -> server aborts the request while # its current denoise block is still unresolved) python3 - <<'EOF' import concurrent.futures, requests def hit(i): try: requests.post("http://127.0.0.1:30000/generate", json={"text": "Write a very long story.", "sampling_params": {"max_new_tokens": 2048}}, timeout=5) except requests.exceptions.ReadTimeout: pass with concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor(128) as ex: list(ex.map(hit, range(128))) EOF # 3. Wait for the server to go idle ``` Before this PR: once the server goes idle, the invariant check fails (crash under strict mode, repeated warnings otherwise): ``` File ".../sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py", line 3662, in on_idle self.invariant_checker._report_leak("pool", "\n".join(messages)) File ".../sglang/srt/managers/scheduler_components/invariant_checker.py", line 428, in _report_leak raise_error_or_warn( ValueError: pool memory leak detected! [full] total=635008, available=32, evictable=634944, protected=0, session_held=0, uncached=0 ``` The accounting pins it down: `available + evictable + protected + session_held + uncached = 634976`, which is short of `total = 635008` by exactly **32 tokens = one denoise block** — this trace had one aborted incomplete request. The pool shrinks by one block per aborted incomplete request and never recovers (bisected with per-abort allocator accounting). After this PR: the idle check passes; the pool returns to full size after every abort wave. ### Bug 2: uncapped staging token-budget fallback crashes the denoise reshape `PrefillAdder._get_dllm_remain_tokens` falls back to `rem_dllm_tokens` when `rem_total_tokens` is exhausted. `rem_total_tokens` charges `max_new_tokens` upfront for every staging row on every scheduling round, so long-output workloads drive it negative long before the KV pool actually fills — the fallback is then the common path, and it is uncapped: a staging row can be granted more than `block_size` tokens (e.g. a mid-prompt prefill row's whole remaining prompt). That produces a variable-length row, which crashes the denoise algorithms' uniform-block reshape (`view(B, block_size)`). **How to reproduce**: ```bash # 1. Launch as above (strict-mode env not needed) python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model inclusionAI/LLaDA2.0-mini --trust-remote-code \ --dllm-algorithm LowConfidence # 2. Long-output workload at full batch (bench_serving defaults to port 30000, # matching the server default) python3 -m sglang.bench_serving --backend sglang --dataset-name random \ --num-prompts 512 --random-input-len 512 --random-output-len 2048 --random-range-ratio 1 ``` Before this PR: once `rem_total_tokens` goes negative (reliably within the run), the scheduler admits an over-sized staging row and the server crashes in the denoise step with `RuntimeError: shape '[B, 32]' is invalid for input of size N`. After this PR: a single staging grant is capped at one block, every row stays uniform, and the run completes. ## Modifications - `mem_cache/radix_cache.py`: slice `kv_indices` by `kv_len_to_handle` instead of `len(token_ids)`, matching the chunk-cache (radix-disabled) branch which already frees by KV length. For non-dLLM requests `kv_len_to_handle` never exceeds `len(token_ids)` (AR requests finish with `kv_committed_len < len(origin_input_ids + output_ids)`), so the slice is byte-identical and AR behavior is unchanged. - Note: the same slicing pattern exists in `mamba_radix_cache`, `swa_radix_cache`, `pure_swa_radix_cache`, `unified_radix_cache`, and `radix_cache_cpp`; those are unreachable by dLLM today (latent only) and are left as-is. - `managers/schedule_policy.py`: cap the fallback at `min(rem_dllm_tokens, dllm_block_size)` so a single staging grant can never exceed one block. The fallback itself is kept — removing it would stall in-flight denoise blocks once `rem_total_tokens` goes negative; it is only clamped. AR never reaches this function (`_get_dllm_remain_tokens` is only called on `dllm_config is not None` paths). ## Unit Tests Two CPU-only regression tests (`base-a-test-cpu`, no GPU/server), both verified **red on the pre-fix code and green on the fix**: - `test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_radix_cache_dllm_abort_free.py` — the aborted-FDFO case fails pre-fix with the unresolved block's KV slots unaccounted (`[] != [108..111]`), plus an AR-invariance case pinning the new kv-length slice byte-identical to the old behavior for autoregressive requests. - `test/registered/unit/managers/test_dllm_staging_token_budget.py` — the exhausted-budget fallback returns one block instead of the whole `rem_dllm_tokens` (pre-fix: `4096 != 32`), does not inflate a sub-block budget, and leaves the normal budget path unchanged. ## Accuracy Tests No effect on model outputs by construction (memory-reclaim / scheduling-budget only). Verified with LLaDA2-mini on gsm8k (zero-shot, full 1319 samples): accuracy unchanged before/after. ## Speed Tests and Profiling No measurable throughput change; both fixes are off the hot path (abort cleanup, and a clamp on an already-taken fallback branch). The repros above are the before/after evidence: the abort wave now passes the idle pool invariant check, and the 512-in/2048-out full-batch run completes instead of crashing. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. signal.title: refactor(disagg): collapse duplicated branches in get_kv_class
signal.text: ## Motivation `get_kv_class` in `python/sglang/srt/disaggregation/utils.py` dispatches to per-backend KV classes through five `elif` branches. Each branch repeated the same boilerplate: - `from sglang.srt.disaggregation.base import KVArgs` plus a `KVClassType.KVARGS: KVArgs` entry — every backend maps `KVARGS` to the *same* class, so this was duplicated five times for no reason. - `return class_mapping.get(class_type)` as the branch's last statement, five times. There was also a stale `from sglang.srt.disaggregation.fake import FakeKVReceiver, FakeKVSender` at the top of the function body. It is unused: the `FAKE` branch re-imports what it needs, so those two names were pulled in on *every* call regardless of backend and then never referenced. Plus five vestigial single-element parens, `KVClassType.RECEIVER: (MooncakeKVReceiver)`, which are just the bare name. ## Modifications 1 file, +14 / -22. Purely structural: - Hoists the shared `KVArgs` lookup into one early return at the top. - Removes the five per-branch `KVArgs` imports and `KVClassType.KVARGS` entries. - Moves the `ValueError` for an unknown backend into an `else`, so each branch only builds `class_mapping` and there is a single `return class_mapping.get(class_type)` at the end. - Drops the stale `fake` import and the five redundant parens. Two properties are deliberately preserved: **Per-backend imports stay explicit.** The regular naming would allow collapsing this to a `getattr(module, prefix + suffix)` table of about ten lines. That is intentionally *not* done — it would break `grep MooncakeKVSender` as a way to find this dispatch, and static analysis could no longer follow it. Each backend module is still imported lazily on its own branch only, so importing `utils` does not drag in mooncake/nixl/mori/ascend. **`FAKE` + `BOOTSTRAP_SERVER` -> `None`.** The fake backend's mapping has no `BOOTSTRAP_SERVER` key, so that combination returns `None` via `.get()`. `managers/disagg_service.py` calls `get_kv_class(..., BOOTSTRAP_SERVER)`, so this is load-bearing. A comment was added rather than "fixing" it into a raise. ## Accuracy Tests Not applicable — no model output, kernel, or forward path is touched. This is a class-lookup table. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not applicable. The function runs a handful of times at PD server startup, not on any per-request path. ## Verification performed Behavior equivalence was checked directly rather than by inspection. Both the pre- and post-change `get_kv_class` were extracted via AST, executed against stub backend modules, and compared across **all 26 `(TransferBackend, KVClassType)` combinations plus an unknown-backend case**. Every case returns the identical class, including: - `FAKE` + `BOOTSTRAP_SERVER` -> `None` - unknown backend -> `ValueError` Also: pinned `ruff 0.15.1 --select=F401,F821,UP037` (the pre-commit config) passes, plus pinned `black 26.1.0` and `isort 7.0.0`. F401 is the relevant check here since the change removes an import. Disaggregation integration tests were **not** run locally (they need multi-GPU hardware). Note this function is exercised on every PD server start via `prefill.py`, `decode.py`, and `disagg_service.py`, so any CI job that boots a PD pair covers it. Part of a small series of independent disaggregation cleanups. Related: #35838, #35843, #35844. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). — N/A: no behavior change; equivalence over all 26 dispatch combinations is documented above. - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). — N/A: internal dispatch helper, not documented. - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results. — N/A, see above. - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32470570755](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32470570755)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32470570273](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32470570273)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32470570385](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32470570385)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [multimodal] MiniMax-H3: fix quantized qkv scales and missing-param policy
signal.text: ## Motivation Two MiniMax-H3 model-side defects that only appear on a quantized checkpoint (NVFP4 or fp8). **1. Per-output-row quantization metadata is not reordered with its rows.** MiniMax-H3 checkpoints store qkv grouped, so `_install_qkv_weight_loader()` permutes the fused qkv weight's output rows into `q|k|v` order via `_reorder_grouped_qkv_to_qkv()`. NVFP4 block scales and fp8 per-channel scales are indexed by that same output row, and they were loaded unpermuted — every scale ends up attached to the wrong row. The weights are correct; the dequantized values are not. The symptom is grey mush, with no error anywhere. **2. `_mark_missing_params_required()` overwrites each quant method's own missing-parameter policy.** A quant method declares in `create_weights()` what it can synthesize when a scale is absent from the checkpoint — weight-only NVFP4 has no `input_scale` and marks it `missing_param_init = "ones"`. H3 then blanket-stamps every parameter `"error"`, so the declaration is lost and the loader raises: ``` ValueError: Required checkpoint parameter '...input_scale' was not loaded ``` ## Modifications - New module-level helper `_install_qkv_row_reorder()` wraps a qkv parameter's weight loader (and its `rank_local_weight_transform`, needed by rank-local FSDP) with the same row permutation used for the weight. Applied to every `qkv_proj` parameter except the weight itself. The gate is the row count: a tensor whose leading dim is not the checkpoint's qkv row count is passed through untouched, which covers per-tensor scalars and swizzled block-scale layouts that are not row-indexed. It reads the **loaded checkpoint tensor**, not the local parameter, so it also holds under tensor parallelism, where the local parameter only owns its own shard of the rows. - `_mark_missing_params_required()` now only claims parameters that have no declared policy. - `test/unit/test_minimax_h3_qkv_scale_reorder.py`: new unit test covering both branches of the row-count gate (row-indexed metadata is permuted, swizzled and per-tensor metadata is not) on the wrapped loader and on `rank_local_weight_transform`. Depends on nothing else, but on sm_120 both this and #35739 are required to get a working NVFP4 MiniMax-H3 (the two fixes are in different layers, hence separate PRs). ## Accuracy Tests On one RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition (sm_120) with an NVFP4 MiniMax-H3 checkpoint: - (2) alone is a hard load failure. - With (2) fixed, (1) renders grey mush. - With both fixed, output is structurally the same as the bf16 checkpoint, and bit-identical across repeated runs at the same seed. The reorder is only reachable for a quantized checkpoint with per-row scales; a bf16 run has no parameters other than the weight on `qkv_proj`, so it is unaffected. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Weight-load-time only; no change to the forward path and none measured (paired runs within 0.2%). ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32467818110](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32467818110)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32467817775](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32467817775)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32467818267](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32467818267)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: refactor(disagg): remove unreferenced dead code
signal.text: ## Motivation Four symbols in `python/sglang/srt/disaggregation/` have no callers anywhere in the repo. They are not private helpers awaiting a caller — each one's live replacement or live sibling is sitting right next to it, which is what makes the deletion safe to reason about. The clearest case is `page_indices_to_cp_rank_page_indices`. It became dead in 1adb53f14 ("Fix CP page filtering by request-local position", #28718), which reimplemented its only caller `filter_kv_indices_for_cp_rank` on top of the new `_get_cp_rank_page_bounds` helper but left the old function behind. That means the CP correctness fix in #28718 was applied to code nothing calls. ## Modifications Pure deletion, 4 files, 0 insertions / 76 deletions. No behavior change. | Symbol | File | Why it is dead | |---|---|---| | `page_indices_to_cp_rank_page_indices` | `utils.py` | Orphaned by #28718; `_get_cp_rank_page_bounds` directly above it is the live replacement | | `KVArgs.ib_traffic_class` | `base/conn.py` | Bare annotation, never assigned or read. Its neighbor `ib_device` *is* live (set in `prefill.py`/`decode.py`, consumed by `mori/conn.py`) | | `get_transferred_rids` | `prefill.py` | Docstring claims "Used by PP", but no PP path references it. `scheduler_pp_mixin.py` calls `poll_and_all_reduce_attn_cp_tp_group` directly | | `StagingAllocator.get_round` | `common/staging_buffer.py` | Third of three accessors over the same tuple; `get_ptr`/`get_offset` have callers, this never did. The round is still reachable via `get_watermark()` | One note on `get_transferred_rids`: it calls `poll_and_all_reduce_attn_cp_tp_group`, which is a **collective**. An accidental caller reaching it on only some ranks would hang, so removing it is slightly safer than leaving it available. Deliberately **not** removed, though a plain grep also finds no callers — these are extension points, not dead code: - `EventPublisherFactory.register_publisher` (`kv_events.py`) — plugin registration hook; removing it would break out-of-tree publishers. - The empty `MooncakeKVBootstrapServer` / `MoriKVBootstrapServer` / `NixlKVBootstrapServer` and `AscendKV*` subclasses. - FastAPI route handlers in `encode_server.py` / `encode_receiver.py`, which are reached via their decorators. ## Accuracy Tests Not applicable — no model output, kernel, or forward path is touched. signal.title: [AMD] Implement DeepSeek V4 DCP on ROCm
signal.text: ## Motivation DeepSeek V4 accepted decode-context-parallel arguments on ROCm, but did not shard its KV and index state across DCP ranks. This PR implements DSV4 decode context parallelism for the ROCm unified-KV backend. ## What changed - Use global logical pages backed by owner-local physical KV pools. - Localize C4/C128 metadata and compressed writes, then gather local candidates for stable global top-k selection. - Build graph-safe decode and prefill index streams. - Merge rank-local attention outputs with natural-log LSE through the validated AG/RS backend. - Account for logical allocation-page geometry in scheduler admission and metrics while preserving the no-DCP unified-KV sink behavior. - Reject unsupported combinations, including A2A/fi_a2a, attention DP, disaggregation, DSA prefill CP, and DSV4 HiCache+DCP. ## Scope This PR is based directly on upstream main. It neither contains nor depends on #35043 or #35233; those stability PRs remain independent and mergeable in either order. DSV4 HiCache+DCP integration is deliberately excluded and will be submitted separately after this backend lands. The generic DCP+DSpark HiCache sizing fix is already upstream in #35221. ## Validation Validated against current `main` on 8x AMD Instinct MI355X: - TP8 no-DCP and TP8/DCP8 AG/RS produced the same 16 output IDs; DCP8 returned all 16 logprobs with zero retractions. - DCP8 pressure test: 8 concurrent 16K requests (131,072 input tokens) all returned HTTP 200 and completed by length with zero retractions; final health checks and service-log scan were clean. Full-model validation used standard NCCL collectives with `--disable-custom-all-reduce`, `SGLANG_USE_AITER_AG=0`, and `SGLANG_DP_USE_REDUCE_SCATTER=0`. AITER custom all-reduce and HiCache stability changes are not included. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32486203443](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32486203443)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32486203536](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32486203536)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32486203329](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32486203329)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: feat(load-reporter): add push-based engine load reporting
signal.text:
## Motivation Load-aware routing needs one authoritative view of scheduler load across data-parallel ranks. Polling every Worker from every Router adds fan-out, creates inconsistent views, and churns connections. This PR adds the Worker-side reporter: a push channel built on the scheduler's existing snapshot publication. One shared pull per fire is broadcast to every registered Router over long-lived bidirectional gRPC streams. Router-side ingestion, discovery, retries, and the Prefill throughput extension are intentionally split into follow-up PRs so each layer can be reviewed independently. > The push channel controls *delivery*, not *snapshot age*. End-to-end > freshness stays bounded by the scheduler's snapshot publication interval; > see [Freshness](#freshness). ## Modifications ### Architecture ```mermaid flowchart LR Scheduler["Scheduler
published per-DP-rank load snapshots"] Source["Per-mode snapshot source
manager get_loads / Router SHM reader"] Fire["Single fire loop
one pull per fire + rank-set validation"] Builder["LoadReport builder
HEALTHY / STALE / UNREACHABLE"] Service["Worker gRPC service
--load-reporter-port"] Router["Routers dial in
drive Monitor streams"] Scheduler --> Source --> Fire --> Builder --> Service --> Router ``` ### Protocol and configuration - The Worker hosts `sglang.router.loadmonitor.v1.LoadMonitorService.Monitor(stream RouterFrame) returns (stream WorkerFrame)` on a fixed, opt-in `--load-reporter-port`; each external Router dials in and drives its own stream (`register` → ack → bounded first fire → periodic reports). Stable field numbers and enum values are preserved. - `RouterFrame` = `register | update_config | keep_alive | stop`, with `register` required first; `WorkerFrame` = `registered | report | error`. Re-registering the same `router_id` replaces its old session; different `router_id`s coexist. - Package `grpcio` and `protobuf` through the optional `load-reporter` extra across all supported Python wheel variants. - Reporting stays opt-in so normal SGLang installations gain no mandatory runtime dependencies. ### Reporter runtime — one timer, one pull, broadcast - A single fire-loop task owns the only timer; sessions are passive bookkeeping (deadline, lease, capacity-1 queue) and own no task or timer. - Each fire performs exactly one bounded snapshot pull (`get_loads()`, 1 s budget). The same budget covers one retry when the expected DP-rank set changes mid-pull. - One report per pull, validated and built from that attempt only: `HEALTHY`, `STALE`, or `UNREACHABLE` (empty ranks + `last_error`). There is no persistent store and no cross-report merge, so a slow or stale rank is never replaced with historical data. - The fire broadcasts the same report to every session whose deadline fired; sessions registered before the next fire share its pull for their initial report. - Each session has a capacity-1 latest-wins queue, lease TTL with keep-alive renewal, mid-stream config updates, registration-anchored deadlines, and idempotent shutdown. - Pull, transport, and shutdown failures never propagate into the inference request path. ### Freshness End-to-end snapshot freshness is bounded by the scheduler's snapshot publication path (`load_snapshot_publish_interval`), not by the gRPC delivery cadence. The report interval controls how often a report is sent, not how old the snapshot inside it is — a poll at the same cadence observes data of the same age. What the push stream adds over polling is delivery, not freshness: a negotiated per-Router cadence, connection reuse, one-pull multi-Router fan-out, leases, and bounded backpressure. ### Tokenizer integration - Single-tokenizer HTTP and native gRPC start one reporter runtime in the FastAPI lifespan (native gRPC reuses the same process and listener). - Multi-tokenizer mode: `MultiTokenizerRouter` is the sole runtime owner; HTTP workers open no streams, and elastic scale changes update the expected DP-rank set (observed by the next fire). - Standalone SMG gRPC starts the reporter at request-manager readiness; older servicers without the readiness hook fail loudly when the reporter is enabled. - The embedded offline Engine API does not own the reporter; cleanup runs in the HTTP-server lifespan, the SMG gRPC-server finally path, and `MultiTokenizerRouter.close()`. ### Tests and documentation - Unit/integration coverage (CPU, real in-process `grpc.aio`): proto contract, fire loop (shared pull deadlines, broadcast to due sessions, per-session lease gating, rank-set-change retry sharing one budget, registration-anchored cadence, stale/error reports, re-registration, shutdown), snapshot validation and report-builder contracts, snapshot sources, service handshake and error frames, composition-root lifecycle, and standalone SMG wiring. - Negative invariants: request dispatch/completion/abort never trigger a pull; topology updates never pull immediately. - Registered GPU E2E tests with a real `grpc.aio` fake Router cover single-owner, multi-owner, and standalone SMG reporting. - Documentation covers the wire contract, serving-mode matrix, fire-loop schedule, freshness model, network/deployment assumptions, and shutdown behavior. ### Design advantages - **Zero request-path coupling:** dispatch, completion, and abort have no edge into the reporting graph; there is no per-request overhead. - **Efficient fan-out:** one pull per fire shared by all due sessions, persistent bidi streams, no Router-side polling fan-out or connection churn. - **Topology-safe:** reports preserve per-DP-rank detail; rank-set changes are validated and retried within the same fire budget. - **Resilient:** per-attempt status semantics, session replacement, leases, latest-wins backpressure, and bounded shutdown prevent stale tasks from accumulating. - **Extensible:** a stable protocol and a single validation entry point provide a clean foundation for the separately reviewed Router monitor and future metrics. ## Accuracy Tests N/A for model accuracy. This PR does not change model forward code, kernels, sampling, or generated outputs. Functional validation: - Registered CPU tests cover the protocol contract, fire-loop scheduling/broadcast, snapshot validation, report builder, service behavior, lifecycle, and standalone SMG wiring. - Registered GPU E2E tests drive a real `grpc.aio` fake Router against single-owner, multi-owner, and standalone SMG modes. - Generated protobuf/gRPC bindings import successfully and expose the expected `sglang.router.loadmonitor.v1` service. ## Speed Tests and Profiling N/A for inference throughput benchmarking. This is an opt-in control-plane feature and does not modify model execution. The reporter adds no request-path overhead: there are no hooks on the dispatch/completion paths, and sampling/network I/O runs in the single background fire task. No inference-speed improvement is claimed. Reporter cadence and freshness are exercised functionally by the registered tests; no new micro-benchmarks are claimed in this revision. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process). 2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers. 3. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR. --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :x: [Run #32481593988](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32481593988) Latest PR Test (Extra): :x: [Run #32481593583](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32481593583) Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): :hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32481593848](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32481593848)

signal.title: [diffusion] let the auto policy select H3's DiT for layerwise offload
signal.text: H3 on a 12 GiB card with no flags fails to load. The DiT was never eligible for automatic offload. ## Motivation `_should_auto_enable_dit_layerwise_offload` gates on: ```python if args.performance_mode not in deployment_config.dit_layerwise_offload_modes: return False ``` `dit_layerwise_offload_modes` defaults to `()`, so for any model that does not declare it this is always true and the DiT is never selected — **in any mode**. Every Wan config declares `("memory",)`; H3 declared nothing, so auto picked `text_encoder, image_encoder, vae` and left the 61.73 GB DiT resident. `keep_resident_min_available_gb=120` is not the bug and behaves correctly: on a 12 GiB card that is far below the threshold, so `_filter_high_memory_resident_components` rightly does not filter. ## Modifications 1. **H3 declares `dit_layerwise_offload_modes=("auto", "memory")`.** 2. **New `auto_layerwise_resident_layers`** so a model can name the layer lists to hold on the device for a component the policy streams. H3 declares `video_vae=1.0`: `decode_temporal` re-runs the whole decoder per temporal chunk, so streaming its 36 blocks pays the transfer per chunk — 150 s of decode against 13 s held. Without this, auto selects a component and then picks its slowest path. 3. **A warning when a model's own threshold contradicts a resident DiT**, naming the missing declaration instead of leaving the allocator to report it. (3) is a warning, not an error: the threshold is about plenty, not fit, so a small model's DiT can legitimately be resident below it. ## Accuracy Tests Placement only; no weights or numerics change. One RTX 4090, allocator capped at 12 GiB via `set_per_process_memory_fraction`, launched with no flags beyond `--model-path` / `--model-variant`: | | components auto selected | OOM lines | result | | --- | --- | ---: | --- | | before | `text_encoder, image_encoder, vae` | 5 | load failed | | after | `dit, text_encoder, image_encoder, vae` | 0 | READY | Resulting placement matches what the explicit flags produce. ## Speed Tests and Profiling An availability fix — before it the configuration does not start. The decode figure behind (2), 864x480 / 124 frames: 150 s streamed against 13 s with the blocks held. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32485591398](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32485591398)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32485591182](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32485591182)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32485591400](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32485591400)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [Intel][XPU] Accept XPU in the shared test CLI --device choices
signal.text: add_common_sglang_args_and_parse hardcoded choices=["auto", "cuda", "rocm", "cpu"], so --device xpu was rejected even though ServerArgs accepts it. It also offered "rocm", which DeviceConfig always refuses: PyTorch drives AMD GPUs through the "cuda" device type. This change as part of #24922 ## Motivation Any test or benchmark using the shared CLI parser fails on Intel GPUs: argparse.ArgumentError: argument --device: invalid choice: 'xpu' (choose from auto, cuda, rocm, cpu) `add_common_sglang_args_and_parse` hardcoded `["auto", "cuda", "rocm", "cpu"]`, while the server's `SUPPORTED_DEVICES` is `["cuda", "xpu", "hpu", "cpu", "npu", "musa", "mps"]` — so the harness rejected five devices the server accepts. It also offered `"rocm"`, which is invalid everywhere: `DeviceConfig("rocm")` raises, since PyTorch has no `rocm` device type and `RocmSRTPlatform.device_type` is `"cuda"`. The old list offered an unusable value while rejecting every valid non-CUDA accelerator. Auto-detection itself was never broken (`ServerArgs.device=None` → `get_device()`, harness `"auto"` → `auto_config_device()`); the hardcoded `choices` was the only blocker. ## Modifications `python/sglang/test/test_utils.py` - `--device` uses `choices=["auto"] + SUPPORTED_DEVICES`, help text derived from the same list, so the harness can't drift from the server. - Dropped `"rocm"`; AMD GPUs use `--device cuda`, as they already did everywhere else. - Fixed two stale docstrings, including a `run_bench_one_batch` `Args: device:` block for a parameter the function never had. `test/registered/unit/test_common_sglang_args.py` (new) - Per-vendor classes (NVIDIA / AMD ROCm / Intel XPU / CPU) plus parser-wide contracts, following `unit/platforms/test_platform_interface.py`. - `register_cpu_ci(est_time=3, suite="base-a-test-cpu")` — parsing argv, reading class-level `device_type`, and building `DeviceConfig` need no accelerator, so all vendor paths are covered on CPU-only CI. No caller impact: all 26 callers checked, none reads `args.device`; `auto`/`cuda`/`cpu` still accepted; nothing in the repo ever passed `--device rocm`. Out of scope: `ServerArgs.device` and `server_arguments.mdx` still omit `mps` from their help strings — a separate doc inconsistency. ## Accuracy Tests Not applicable — CLI argument parsing only. No kernel, model forward, or sampling code is touched, and no signatures changed (docstrings only), so model outputs cannot change. ## Speed Tests and Profiling No inference-path impact — the change only affects CLI parsing at startup. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32488730983](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32488730983)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32488730260](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32488730260)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32488730711](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32488730711)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [Fix] Pack device-pointer tables as uint64 to avoid 64-bit address overflow
signal.text: ## Motivation Fixes #35047. Several kernels pass base addresses to the device in a side table and bitcast each entry back to a pointer (`tl.load(meta_ptr + i).to(tl.pointer_type(...))` in Triton, `reinterpret_cast` in the host-side `gemm_ar` op). Those tables were built with `dtype=torch.int64`, which cannot hold an address `>= 2**63`: `torch.tensor()` unpacks Python ints through `long long`, so the build raises ``` ValueError: Overflow when unpacking long long ``` on the host, before any kernel is launched. Intel XPU (Level Zero / SYCL USM) device addresses have the top bit set, e.g. `0xffff85abd4e00000`, so every Mamba/GDN model hits this in conv-state scatter and `MambaPool` slot maintenance. CUDA/HIP VAs stay in the low canonical half, which is the only reason `int64` looks lossless there. ## Modifications - New `sglang.kernels.ops.memory.ptr_table.make_ptr_table(rows, device)`: builds the table as `uint64` (the only dtype that accepts a full 64-bit address) and `view`s it back to `int64`. `view` moves no bits, so kernels and C++ ops keep their existing signed element type — no kernel-side change, and `gemm_ar.cuh::set_bases`' `with_dtype<int64_t>()` check still holds. Companion columns (strides, element counts, block offsets) are non-negative, so their bits are unchanged too. - Route the three table builders through it: `_conv_multi_build_meta` (`mamba_state_scatter_triton.py`), `build_conv_slot_descriptor` (`mem_cache/mamba_slot_fused.py`), and `gemm_ar.init`'s `uc_bases`. ## Tests - `test/registered/kernels/ops/memory/test_ptr_table.py` (new, CPU suite): covers the full `[0, 2**64)` address range, and asserts both call sites' tables round-trip a spoofed top-bit-set `data_ptr()` while leaving companion columns identical to a real-address build. It spoofs the address because a backend whose VAs stay `< 2**47` can never catch this regression — the guard has to run on any runner. - `test/registered/layers/mamba/test_mamba_slot_fused.py` and `test/registered/unit/layers/test_mamba_state_scatter_triton.py` now select the accelerator via `get_device()` instead of hardcoding CUDA, and register on the XPU suite. Added coverage for `fused_conv_window_scatter_multi` (single-type, multi-type, and with the second/track index set), which had no test on any backend and is the kernel most exposed to the packing. Verified on 8x Intel Arc Pro B60 (torch 2.12.0+xpu): the new cases fail with the reported `ValueError` when `make_ptr_table` is reverted to `int64`, and all 15 pass with the fix (2 CUDA-only skips). `isort`/`black`/`ruff` and the repo's registered-test lint checks are clean. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32488679853](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32488679853)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32488679707](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32488679707)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32488679657](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32488679657)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: fix(dsv4): avoid fused TopK v2 on Hopper
signal.text: ## Motivation DeepSeek-V4 decode can produce incomplete DSA TopK v2 output on Hopper when a small mixed batch crosses the 32K C4 cluster floor. In an 8x H200 TP8 deployment, this surfaced as a reproducible downstream CUDA illegal-memory access when one long request crossed raw token 131072 while seven short requests remained active. The failure is in the current fused small-batch DSMEM path, not in Marlin, Mooncake, FP8 KV cache, or the general persistent-cluster implementation. ## Root cause Calling `topk_transform_512_v2` directly on H200 with an identity page table gave the following result: ```text C4 seq_len: 32767 32768 32769 33000 2000 12000 16385 1000 unique/512 slots: 512 512 115 207 512 512 512 512 ``` For `batch_size <= 15`, the small-batch cluster floor is 32768. The two rows just above that floor enter `Cluster::forward` in `topk_small_batch_kernel` and return incomplete output on SM90. Register and streaming rows in the same launch are correct. Additional isolation: - Moving the PDL wait before the first `seq_lens` read did not repair the two failing rows. - The existing persistent-cluster path was correct: `batch=31, seq_len=65537` returned 512 unique valid indices for all 31 rows. - Disabling TopK v2 made the full workload stable, and restoring the original v2 dispatch reproduced the crash at the same C4 boundary. The direct kernel corruption is deterministic. The link from stale/duplicate TopK slots to the downstream sparse-attention illegal access is supported by the full-model boundary A/B. ## Changes - Keep the fused small-batch path on SM100+. - On Hopper, route the same shapes through the existing persistent-cluster plus main-kernel path. - Add a regression test with mixed row lengths immediately below, at, and above the 32768 small-batch cluster floor. Blackwell dispatch is unchanged. ## Validation Tested environment: ```text GPU: 8x NVIDIA H200 (SM90a) Model: DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 SGLang base: 7adf2f4a9a4389d1c021a2caf128cf7e2f4adb35 PyTorch: 2.11.0 CUDA toolkit: 13.1 TP: 8 KV cache: FP8 E4M3 MoE runner: Marlin Context length: 400000 Decode CUDA Graph: enabled ``` Results with the Hopper fallback: - Direct mixed-boundary kernel check: all 8 rows returned 512 unique indices, all in range. - Deterministic boundary reproducer (`1 x 130800 -> 10000` plus `7 x 2000 -> 10000`): all requests completed; 80,000 output tokens; no CUDA error. - Full stability gate (`40 x 200000 -> 40000`, concurrency 40): 40/40 requests completed; 8,000,000 input and 1,600,000 output tokens; 1566.01 output tok/s; HTTP health remained 200. - Persistent-path regression (`1 x 298933 -> 10000` plus `7 x 9731 -> 10000`): all requests completed, including the C4 `> 65536` row. - The same full stability gate with Mooncake HiCache write-through: 40/40 completed; actual Mooncake SSD read/write counters increased; no CUDA error. The deployed validation branch also contained a PDL-wait placement cleanup inside the fused kernel. A PDL-only A/B did not fix the corruption, and the fused kernel is not launched on SM90 after this dispatch change. This PR intentionally excludes that unrelated cleanup and contains only the minimal Hopper fallback. The tested `topk_v2.cuh` and regression-test base blobs are unchanged on current `main` as of 2026-08-06. ## Related work - #26788 introduced the current TopK v2 implementation. - #25574 / #25575 concern the pre-#26788 fused kernel and code that no longer exists. - #25785 adds a PDL trigger for the older implementation; it does not address this output corruption. - #31123 handles negative padded `seq_lens`, a different failure class. - #32910 fixes the CUDA 13 compiler crash when building this kernel, separate from the runtime correctness issue here. ## Checklist - [x] The change is scoped to the affected architecture and dispatch path. - [x] A focused regression test is included. - [x] `git diff --check` passes. - [x] Full-model correctness and long-running serving validation are reported above. - [ ] CI (this PR). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #31081928822](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31081928822)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31081928039](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31081928039)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [EAGLE] perf: Fuse speculative relay scatter
signal.text: ## Motivation During EAGLE speculative decoding with overlap scheduling, `FutureMap.stash` scatters the bonus token, top-k metadata, hidden states, and optional draft/DSA fields into request-pool-indexed buffers. The original path launches a cast followed by separate `index_put` kernels in the latency-sensitive transition between `draft_extend` and `draft`. These fields share the same destination row indices, so they can be written in one launch to reduce kernel-launch bubbles and host dispatch overhead. ## Modifications - Add a CUDA-only Triton `scatter_spec_extras` kernel that scatters all enabled relay fields with one launch and compile-time specialization for top-k, hidden-state, draft-probability, and DSA fields. - Use the fused path from `FutureMap.stash` after a compact shape, layout, device, and draft-dtype compatibility check, while preserving the original indexed assignments for non-CUDA backends and incompatible inputs. - Register the kernel in the unified kernel inventory with CUDA capability metadata. - Add CUDA tests covering a trace-derived GLM configuration, multiple field specializations, index layouts, empty batches, and native fallback for incompatible inputs. ## Accuracy GLM5.2 B200 ```bash sgl-eval run gsm8k \ --base-url http://localhost:30000/v1 \ --num-threads 32 --max-tokens 8192 ``` main: ```bash == gsm8k == 1319 examples (single-shot) | 312.9s | 3337 tok/s | 1.0M tokens * score = 94.92% stop_rate = 96.89% truncated_rate = 3.11% [warn: hitting max_tokens] error_rate = 0.00% ``` PR: ```bash == gsm8k == 1319 examples (single-shot) | 294.9s | 3683 tok/s | 1.1M tokens * score = 94.62% stop_rate = 96.59% truncated_rate = 3.41% [warn: hitting max_tokens] error_rate = 0.00% ``` ## Speeup main: PR: --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :x: [Run #30530319761](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/30530319761) Latest PR Test (Extra): :x: [Run #30530319567](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/30530319567)

signal.title: [XPU] Add CustomOp.forward_xpu fallback to forward_native
signal.text: dispatch_forward() routes the xpu platform to self.forward_xpu, but the base class never defined it. Since dispatch_forward() runs in __init__, any subclass without its own override raises AttributeError at construction, breaking model loading on Intel GPUs: AttributeError: 'LayerNorm' object has no attribute 'forward_xpu' Route xpu to forward_native, matching the existing forward_tpu/npu/oot fallbacks. No dispatch branch is modified, so CUDA/ROCm/NPU/MUSA/CPU behavior is unchanged. ## Motivation Fixes #33292 . CustomOp.dispatch_forward() maps the detected platform to a forward_<backend> method and caches it in __init__. Every backend has a base-class fallback — hip/cpu/musa → forward_cuda, tpu/oot/npu → forward_native — so a subclass only needs forward_native to work everywhere. The xpu branch (custom_op.py:83-84) was the sole exception: it returns self.forward_xpu, which was never defined. Because dispatch_forward() is called from __init__ (custom_op.py:27), this fails at construction, so it breaks model loading rather than inference: >>> from sglang.multimodal_gen.runtime.layers.layernorm import LayerNorm >>> LayerNorm(hidden_size=64) AttributeError: 'LayerNorm' object has no attribute 'forward_xpu' Five shipped subclasses relied on the missing method — LayerNorm (layernorm.py:329), RMSNormNoWeight (layernorm.py:316), GeluAndMul (activation.py:75), FusedLayerNormScaleShiftGateSelect01 (fused_scale_shift_gate.py:20), FusedResidualLayerNormScaleShiftGateSelect01 (fused_scale_shift_gate.py:85). All implement forward_native. Eight other subclasses define their own forward_xpu, which is why this went unnoticed. Present since #12484 (7bc1dae095). ## Modifications Just introduced forward_xpu in python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/layers/custom_op.py. Verified after the patch that all six branches dispatch_forward() can return resolve to a base-class method. ## Accuracy Tests This PR does not touch kernels or model forward code, so outputs are unchanged on any platform that was already binding correctly (CUDA/NPU single-GPU). ## Speed Tests and Profiling No kernel or scheduling changes, so there is no expected throughput change on platforms that were already binding correctly. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32488284480](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32488284480)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32488284296](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32488284296)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32488284549](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32488284549)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [Bugfix] Make DWDP cuda.bindings import non-fatal on non-CUDA platforms
signal.text: DWDP is CUDA/NVLink-only, but its modules are on the import chain reached during ModelRunner init on every platform. The unconditional top-level `from cuda.bindings import driver as cuda` in vmm.py and transport.py crashes startup on Intel XPU/CPU where cuda-python is absent, even though no cuda symbol is ever dereferenced there. Guard the import with try/except and fall back to `cuda = None`. Fixes #31995 ## Motivation PR #29778 (DWDP for MoE prefill) added unconditional top-level imports of from cuda.bindings import driver as cuda in dwdp/vmm.py and dwdp/transport.py. DWDP is a CUDA/NVLink-only feature, but these modules sit on an import chain that executes on every platform during ModelRunner init, independent of whether DWDP is enabled: model_runner.py:81 from sglang.srt.layers.moe.dwdp import DwdpManager └─ dwdp/__init__.py → dwdp_manager └─ dwdp_manager.py → layout, transport, weight_manager, ... └─ layout.py:11 from ...dwdp.vmm import align_down, align_up └─ vmm.py:11 from cuda.bindings import driver as cuda 💥 On platforms where the cuda-python package is absent (XPU, CPU, etc.), this raises ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'cuda' and aborts startup — even though not a single cuda symbol is dereferenced on those platforms. cuda-python>=13.0 is declared in pyproject.toml but is a CUDA-only dependency not installed in XPU/CPU environments. ## Modifications - python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/dwdp/vmm.py — wrap the cuda.bindings import in try/except ImportError, falling back to cuda = None. - python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/dwdp/transport.py — same guard. ## Accuracy Tests - No accuracy impact — change is import-guarding only, no runtime logic touched. - CUDA path unchanged: cuda.bindings still imports normally where the package is present. ## Speed Tests and Profiling - Not applicable — no runtime/hot-path code modified; the guard only affects module import on non-CUDA platforms. ## Checklist - [x] Format code with pre-commit run --all-files - [x] Verified import succeeds on XPU and remains functional on CUDA <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32488218123](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32488218123)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32488217826](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32488217826)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32488218084](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32488218084)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [HiCache][PD] Fix write-through lock leak for retraction host pools
signal.text: ## Motivation #20049 fixed a pure-decode liveness bug where HiCache write-through acknowledgements were not processed and their radix-tree `lock_ref`s leaked. After #30511 consolidated HiCache event checks and removed the dedicated acknowledgement flush, a PD decode configuration with a retraction-only host pool fell outside the new event-drain gate. That configuration creates a host cache controller without `--enable-hierarchical-cache`, so it can issue write-through backups but did not poll their completion events. This is a configuration-coverage regression of the #20049 liveness invariant after #30511. ## Root cause When `cache_controller` exists, the decode radix cache enables HiCache write-through backups. Each backup calls `inc_lock_ref`, and only acknowledgement processing in `check_hicache_events()` performs the matching `dec_lock_ref`. The old decode drain gate used `enable_decode_hicache`, which additionally required `--enable-hierarchical-cache`. With a retraction-only host pool, write-through therefore remained enabled while acknowledgement draining remained disabled. In the reproduced stall there were 19 lock increments and 11 decrements, leaving 8 leaked locks and 33,536 protected tokens. The GPU was idle with active/running/waiting all at 0, but `evictable_size=0`; the retracted request could never pass its resume allocation gate, and restore was never called. ## Fix Poll HiCache events whenever the decode tree cache has an actual cache controller, matching the capability that enables write-through backups instead of relying on the `--enable-hierarchical-cache` CLI state. Deployments without a controller still skip the event drain. The focused regression test covers the retraction-only configuration with `enable_hierarchical_cache=false` and the old `enable_decode_hicache=false` gate, verifies that ranks with different local acknowledgement readiness make the same drain decision, and verifies that the no-controller path performs no drain. ## Validation - Pre-fix active-shared workload: 8/8 stalls. - Post-fix liveness gate: 21/21 PASS; legacy `length`: 10/10; candidate `backup-cost`: 10/10. - Restore lifecycle: 42/42 `restore_start` and 42/42 `restore_done`; all outputs byte-identical. - Latest `main` compatibility smoke: 3/3 PASS. Every run triggered a real memory-pressure retraction, completed 4/4 requests, restored on both TP ranks with no divergence or watchdog, matched outputs byte-for-byte, and cleaned all processes, ports, and GPU memory. - Focused regression: fails before the fix and passes after it (2 tests). - Related PD decode CPU tests: 32 passed. - HiCache CPU/GPU tests: 18 passed and 7 passed. - Unified radix-cache suite: 1,082 passed, 1,070 skipped. ## Related - Regression coverage for #20049 - Event-check consolidation in #30511 - Discovered while stress-testing #35717 <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32487573497](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32487573497)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32487573315](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32487573315)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32487573967](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32487573967)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->
