signal.title: [diffusion] stop the mapped-weight store from holding the parameter itself
signal.text: Mapped layer weights were silently replaced by a broadcast placeholder. On main since #35701. ## Motivation `_initialize_layer_weights` stores the tensor it is about to overwrite: ```python local_weight = self._to_local_tensor(weight) # returns `weight` itself for a plain Parameter self._mapped_cpu_weights[layer_idx][name] = local_weight ... weight.data = self._get_shared_empty_tensor_for_target(weight, local_weight.dtype) ``` `Tensor.data = ...` swaps the object's storage in place, so the store is left holding the shared `torch.empty((1,))`. Reload then does `gpu_tensor.copy_(cpu_tensor)`, a one-element source **broadcasts**, and nothing raises. `iter_cpu_weights`, which offers the real weights for checksums, yields the same entries. Instrumented on MiniMax-H3 `fl2va`, 1x RTX 4090, host capped at 32 GiB: | | tensors | `numel == 1` | bytes in store | `_mapped_bytes` | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | | before, `blocks` | 450 | **450** | 0.000 GiB | 49.357 GiB | | before, `model.language_model.layers` | 550 | **550** | 0.000 GiB | 45.411 GiB | | after, `blocks` | 450 | 0 | **49.357 GiB** | 49.357 GiB | The counter was always right — it reads `local_weight` before the overwrite — which is why the logs looked fine. ## Modifications Store an independent tensor over the same mapped storage. No copy: the storage is shared, so #35701's point (these bytes are not duplicated in host memory) still holds. ## Accuracy Tests The existing tests could not catch this. `_FileBackedBlock` builds its parameter as `Parameter(mapped.reshape(8, 8))`, and `reshape` returns a fresh object — so `local_weight is weight` was false in tests and true in every real model. The new test asserts identity (`tensor is not parameters[name]`) rather than `numel`, because the aliasing is the defect and a particular `.data` assignment merely reveals it. Fails before, passes after. ## Speed Tests and Profiling The fix makes the 32 GiB configuration **slower**, because the earlier number never moved the weights. 864x480 / 124 frames / 20 NFE: | | denoise | | --- | ---: | | before (weights not transferred) | 142.00 s | | after (49.36 GiB moved per step) | 330.74 s | Anything measured on that path is void: the per-step GEMM/attention split, the synchronous-copy count, the resident-layer saturation point, the `torch.compile` comparison. The unconstrained-host path is unaffected — `host_copies_would_not_fit` is false there, so nothing is mapped and the weights take the normal pinned path. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32456602667](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32456602667)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:no_entry_sign: [Run #32456988315](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32456988315)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32456602643](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32456602643)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: feat(gemma4): make multimodal loading opt-in
signal.text: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation Gemma 4 multimodal models currently build their vision and audio components and load their weights even for text-only serving. This increases memory usage and model load time. It also causes SGLang to treat the model as multimodal and disable the prefill CUDA graph because breakable CUDA graphs are incompatible with multimodal models. This PR makes Gemma 4 multimodal loading opt-in with `--enable-multimodal`, matching Llama 4 and Gemma 3. > On a DGX Spark with TP1, text-only mode increased the default static memory fraction from `0.8115` to `0.8880` and reduced memory used by model weights. Together, these changes increased the KV cache capacity from 265,062 to 326,684 tokens, an increase of 61,622 tokens or 23.2%. ## Modifications - Default `gemma4_mm` and `gemma4_unified` to text-only mode. - Build and load vision and audio components only when `--enable-multimodal` is set. - Update Gemma 4 deployment documentation with the new default and flag. - Enable multimodal mode explicitly in the existing Gemma 4 MMMU eval configurations. ## Accuracy Tests Not applicable. This PR does not change model computation. The registered Gemma 4 MMMU eval configurations now pass `--enable-multimodal` explicitly and keep their existing thresholds. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not applicable. This PR only skips multimodal component construction and weight loading during text-only serving. signal.title: [Bugfix] Check paged KV capacity before kernel launch
signal.text: ## Summary - Check paged KV capacity before launching the extend/decode Triton allocator kernels. - Preserve the existing release-page merge behavior before the capacity check. - Add regression tests covering OOM, successful allocation, and release-page merging. ## Motivation The old implementation launched the allocation kernel and only then checked whether enough free pages were available. On an A100 with two free pages, a prefill or decode request requiring three pages returned `None` but still launched the kernel once. The kernel could read beyond the logical free-page list. This is reachable in normal serving when the KV cache is full and no more evictable pages are available. See issue #34399 for the reproducible online path and evidence. ## Validation ### Unit and allocator tests ```text 138 passed, 2 warnings, 33 subtests passed in 29.19s ``` The test command covered the new paged allocator regression tests, multi-ended allocator, paged free, SWA, HiSparse, DCP layout, KV page invariants, and decode bookkeeping tests. ### A100 validation With `NVIDIA A100-PCIE-40GB`, PyTorch `2.9.1+cu128`, and `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1`: ```text extend_oom= True kernel_launches= 0 free_unchanged= True decode_oom= True kernel_launches= 0 free_unchanged= True ``` The same unmodified-mainline inputs launched one kernel in each path. ### OOM-path microbenchmark After warming the successful kernel path, 100 synchronous prefill OOM calls measured: ```text main: 126.14 us/call patch: 59.37 us/call ``` This is a single local failure-path measurement, not an end-to-end throughput benchmark. Successful allocation behavior is unchanged. ## Scope This patch is intentionally limited to the paged allocator capacity-check ordering. It does not change the Triton kernel interface, page numbering, or normal successful allocation behavior. Fixes #34399 <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32484222870](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32484222870)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32484222812](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32484222812)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32484222848](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32484222848)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [Kimi] trtllm_mla: serve varlen absorbed MLA under both tc_piecewise and breakable prefill CUDA graphs (fixes #32655)
signal.text: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation Under a captured prefill CUDA graph (`tc_piecewise` **or** `breakable`) the DeepSeek/Kimi dispatcher returns `AttnForwardMethod.MLA` even for a genuine extend (`attention_backend_handler.py:151`). `TRTLLMMLABackend` has no varlen extend kernel, so it delegates the whole batch to the FlashInfer paged-MLA parent, which does: ```python # flashinfer_mla_backend.py:602 k_buf = self.token_to_kv_pool.get_key_buffer(layer.layer_id).to(q.dtype) ``` `get_key_buffer()` returns the **entire KV pool for that layer**, not the pages this request needs. Under `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3` with a bf16 query this converts the whole pool from FP8 to BF16 **per layer, per forward**. The cost is not a slow kernel — it is a full-pool memory copy before the kernel starts. This is #32655 (Kimi-K2.6-NVFP4, 4×GB300 TP4: TTFT 122.68 → 344.58 ms after #30889 put `KimiK25ForConditionalGeneration` on the piecewise allowlist). Kimi's default prefill graph mode is `breakable` (per #34245's precedence rule), and the same FlashInfer full-pool-dequant fallback fires there for exactly the same reason: measured on a clean base with no patch, default TTFT is 340.4 ms — within 1.7% of the original bug reproduction (346.46 ms). Fixing only the `tc_piecewise` path would leave the default path broken, so this PR serves the fast kernel under **both** graph modes. This PR leaves `server_args.py`'s routing untouched — Kimi still resolves to `breakable`, exactly as #34245 intended — and teaches `TRTLLMMLABackend` to serve the fast varlen-absorbed kernel under **either** `is_in_tc_piecewise_cuda_graph()` **or** `is_in_breakable_cuda_graph()`. Measured ~51.1 ms under `breakable` (6.7× vs the unpatched default), which is also faster than forcing `tc_piecewise` (~54.6 ms). flashinfer ≥ 0.6.15 exposes `cum_seq_lens_q` / `max_q_len` on `trtllm_batch_decode_with_kv_cache_mla`, so the trtllm-gen absorbed kernel can take a ragged `q` and read FP8 paged KV natively. The conversion disappears entirely, under both graph modes. ## Modifications **Backend (`trtllm_mla_backend.py`)** 1. `TRTLLMMLAPrefillMetadata` gains `block_kv_indices` / `seq_lens_k` / `max_seq_len_k`. Absorbed MLA reads paged KV, and the extend branch never built a block table — this is the substance of the patch. Reuses the existing `_create_block_kv_indices` / `_calc_padded_blocks`; **no new kernel**. 2. `_run_varlen_absorbed_kernel()` — absorbed MLA over a ragged `q`. Kept separate from `_run_decode_kernel()`, which serves the dense `[bs, draft_token_num]` verify layout. 3. `_call_trtllm_batch_decode_mla()` — shared flashinfer call layer for both hooks. 4. `supports_varlen_absorbed_mla` class attribute — same shape as the existing `supports_ragged_verify_graph` / `needs_cpu_seq_lens` capability flags. 5. `varlen_absorbed_mla_supported(kv_cache_dtype)` — module-level predicate for arch + KV-dtype eligibility. `ServerArgs` reads the same function, so the config decision cannot drift from what the kernel can do. 6. `forward_extend` gains the varlen branch, guarded by `layer.head_dim == kv_lora_rank + qk_rope_head_dim` so the MHA companion layer (`attn_mha`, head_dim 192) can never enter the absorbed kernel. 7. `use_varlen_absorbed` accepts either `is_in_tc_piecewise_cuda_graph()` or `is_in_breakable_cuda_graph()`. `fallback_to_flashinfer_impl = not use_varlen_absorbed and (...)` needed no change; it chains automatically. 8. `varlen_absorbed_mla_shape_ok()` — extends the shape gate to correctly cover `num_heads_q=96` wide-EP DP-attention configurations. **Opt-outs (`tokenspeed_mla_backend.py` / `cutedsl_mla_backend.py`)** — one line each. `TokenspeedMLABackend` inherits `backend == "trtllm-gen"` from `super().__init__()`, so a string gate cannot exclude it; without the flag its `_run_decode_kernel` override would `TypeError` on every TP rank during prefill graph capture. **`server_args.py`** — the pre-existing `tc_piecewise`-upgrade exclusion (`self._resolved_attention_backends()[0] != "trtllm_mla"`, which blanket-excluded any `trtllm_mla` config) is narrowed to `not self._trtllm_mla_lacks_varlen_absorbed()`, excluding only configs where the absorbed kernel is actually unavailable. This has no effect on Kimi's routing — #34245's `is_multimodal_breakable_cuda_graph_supported` check already short-circuits that branch for Kimi before reaching this condition — but it does affect any other piecewise-allowlisted, non-breakable-allowlisted model taking this upgrade path. **Why `major == 10` and not `is_blackwell_supported()`** — flashinfer's `trtllm_batch_decode_with_kv_cache_mla` (0.6.17) resolves `backend="auto"` to `"xqa"` on any device whose compute-capability major is not 10, including SM120/SM121, and the `xqa` backend raises if `cum_seq_lens_q`/`max_q_len` are set — which this kernel always sets. So SM12x hits a hard `ValueError`, not a silent fallback. `is_blackwell_supported()` (`cc[0] in [10, 12]`) would admit SM12x into that crash; `major == 10` mirrors flashinfer's own dispatch condition instead of trusting the string. **Tests** — `test_mla_varlen_absorbed_gate.py` (capability + config/runtime contract, incl. the wide-EP shape gate regression lock), `test_trtllm_mla_piecewise.py` / `test_trtllm_mla_breakable.py` (9+3 numerical cases across both graph fixtures + arch gate + negative routing), and two cases added to `test_multimodal_piecewise_cuda_graph.py`. All registered for CI on `4-gpu-b200` **and** `1-gpu-large` (the arch gate is `major == 10`; registering only `1-gpu-large` would skip everything, and `pr-test-finish` treats `skipped` as pass). ## Accuracy Tests **Kimi-K2.6-NVFP4, 4×GB300 TP4, fp8 KV — GSM8K full test set (1319 questions, 5-shot)** | context | prefill graph | stock | patched | |---|---|---|---| | 8192 | `breakable` (default) | 0.934 | 0.942 | | 2048 | `breakable` (default) | 0.939 | 0.944 | ## Speed Tests and Profiling ### Kimi-K2.6-NVFP4, 4×GB300 TP4 — the issue's own configuration 1k input / 1k output, `--max-concurrency 1`, 3 rounds. | arm | prefill graph | Mean TTFT (3 reps) | vs patched-default | |---|---|---|---| | stock + forced `tc_piecewise` (anchor) | `tc_piecewise` | 343.70 / 344.09 / 343.80 ms | 6.73× | | stock + default | `breakable` | 340.57 / 340.37 / 340.28 ms | 6.67× | | **patched + default (this PR)** | `breakable` | **50.93 / 51.18 / 51.10 ms** | baseline | | patched + forced `tc_piecewise` (regression check) | `tc_piecewise` | 54.61 / 54.71 / 54.58 ms | 6.29× | TPOT is identical across all four arms (5.04–5.06 ms) — decode is untouched, as expected since this PR only changes the prefill/extend path. ### Concurrency sweep — 8×B200 TP8, breakable (default) track Throughput-sensitive benchmark: one server per arm, sweeping concurrency without restart, `num-prompts = 5 × max-concurrency` per the steady-state rule. | conc | TTFT stock → patched (ms) | Δ TTFT | throughput stock → patched (tok/s) | Δ throughput | |---|---|---|---|---| | 1 | 295.69 → 44.50 | **−84.9%**, latency-bound | 207.97 → 219.33 | +5.5% | | 4 | 580.21 → 192.40 | **−66.8%** | 660.47 → 710.25 | +7.5% | | 16 | 555.96 → 314.13 | **−43.5%** | 1763.67 → 1813.97 | +2.9% | | 64 | 1079.23 → 822.12 | **−23.8%**, shrinks as load rises and prefill overlaps decode | 4139.92 → 4202.37 | +1.5% | Throughput does not regress at any point; this is a prefill-latency fix, so the TTFT win shrinks as the workload becomes more decode-bound at high concurrency, while throughput gains taper for the same reason. ### Reproduction ```bash # Same server command reproduces both arms — checkout main for the bug, this # branch for the fix; no flags differ between them. python3 -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path nvidia/Kimi-K2.6-NVFP4 --trust-remote-code \ --served-model-name kimi \ --tp 4 --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 --quantization modelopt_fp4 \ --attention-backend trtllm_mla \ --context-length 2048 --mem-fraction-static 0.9 \ --host 127.0.0.1 --port 31500 # client python3 -m sglang.benchmark.serving --backend sglang \ --host 127.0.0.1 --port 31500 --model kimi --tokenizer nvidia/Kimi-K2.6-NVFP4 \ --dataset-name random --random-input-len 1000 --random-output-len 1000 \ --random-range-ratio 1.0 --num-prompts 5 --max-concurrency 1 \ --request-rate inf --warmup-requests 1 --seed 42 --flush-cache ``` ## Checklist - [x] Format code with pre-commit - [x] Add unit tests (registered on `4-gpu-b200` and `1-gpu-large`, both `tc_piecewise` and `breakable` fixtures) - [x] Update documentation (`test/registered/attention/unittests/mla/README.md` capability matrix) - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results (both graph modes) - [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance ## Review and Merge Process 1. signal.title: [Perf][DSV4] add ag_gemm and moe_rs overlap kernels for dsv4 prefill
signal.text: ## 1. Motivation We implement communication-computation overlap for DeepSeek V4 Prefill CP by introducing two fused Triton kernels built on `torch.symmetric_memory`: 1. Fused AllGather + FP8 Quantization + GEMM: the CP AllGather is performed on a dedicated stream via Copy Engine (CE) P2P pulls (consuming no SMs), while a fused kernel on the compute stream performs on-the-fly FP8 quantization and shared expert `gate_up_proj` GEMM. The compute kernel poll signals to consume each chunk as soon as the CE delivers it, overlapping the AllGather with computation. 2. Fused MoE TopK-Reduce + Shared Expert Add + ReduceScatter: the routed expert output reduction, shared expert addition, and ReduceScatter send are fused into a single kernel, overlapping the ReduceScatter communication with the reduction computation. - Co-auther: @zxdukki ## 2. Modifications - **Environment Variable** - Add `SGLANG_OPT_USE_TORCH_SYMM_MEM_FUSED_KERNEL` (default `False`) to enable the fused kernels. - **New Triton Kernels (`symm_mem_kernels/`)** - Add allgather_gemm_symm_mem.py: triton kernel for CE-driven AllGather + on-the-fly FP8 quantization and GEMM with signal-based coordination across two streams. - Add moe_reduce_rs_symm_mem.py: fused MoE topk-reduce + shared expert addition + ReduceScatter in a single triton kernel. - **TorchSymmMemCommunicator (torch_symm_mem.py)** - Split `disabled` / `allreduce_disabled` so fused-kernel contexts work without multicast support. - Add lazy-init helpers to cache AG-GEMM and MoE-RS contexts. - Add CP-mode activation via `set_use_cp()` / `get_active_comm()`. - **Model & Layer (parallel_state.py, fused_moe.py, deepseek_v2/v4.py)** - Initialize `TorchSymmMemCommunicator` when the fused-kernel env var is enabled. - Add `no_topk_reduce` option to skip in-kernel reduction (deferred to the fused RS kernel). - Integrate `maybe_fused_ag_shared_experts` and `maybe_fused_shared_add_rs` into the MoE forward path. - Skip the standalone CP AllGather in `DeepseekV4DecoderLayer` when the fused path is active. ## 3. Evaluation ### 3.1. Experiment Setup - 3 nodes, with 8 × H20 GPUs and 4 dual-port 200Gbps NICs per node. DSV4 Flash uses 1 node with CP8-TP8 for prefill. DSV4 Pro uses 3 nodes with PP3-CP8-TP8 for prefill. - Input length 16k/32k/64k/128k, output length 1. ### 3.2. Performance Evaluation - DSV4 Flash mean TTFT: | Input Len | Baseline (ms) | Overlap (ms) | Speedup | | ---- | ---- | ---- | ---- | | 16k | 548.89 | 521.44 | 5.00% | | 32k | 1092.81 | 1034.50 | 5.33% | | 64k | 2200.69 | 2122.33 | 3.56% | | 128k | 4664.76 | 4500.17 | 3.53% | - DSV4 Pro mean TTFT: | Input Len | Baseline (ms) | Overlap (ms) | Speedup | | ---- | ---- | ---- | ---- | | 16k | 1066.37 | 1028.04 | 3.59% | | 32k | 1641.93 | 1586.49 | 3.37% | | 64k | 2832.55 | 2731.91 | 3.55% | | 128k | 5355.57 | 5173.78 | 3.39% | - Bench Script: ``` # (random-input-len, num-prompts) BENCH_CONFIGS=( "16384 300" "32768 150" "65536 100" "131072 50" ) for cfg in "${BENCH_CONFIGS[@]}"; do read -r INPUT_LEN NUM_PROMPTS <<< "$cfg" python -m sglang.bench_serving \ --backend sglang --host localhost --port 8288 \ --dataset-name random \ --dataset-path ./ShareGPT_V3_unfiltered_cleaned_split.json \ --num-prompts $NUM_PROMPTS --max-concurrency 1 \ --random-input-len $INPUT_LEN --random-output-len 1 \ --random-range-ratio 1.0 --request-rate inf done ``` ### 3.3. Profiling Here we take DSV4 Flash as an example to show profiling before and after optimization. - AllGather + FP8 Quantization + GEMM (476μs->309μs): - Baseline: - Overlap: - MoE TopK-Reduce + Shared Expert Add + ReduceScatter (415μs->235μs): - Baseline: - Overlap: ### 3.4. Accuracy Tests - DSV4 Flash: ``` # ----------------------- baseline ----------------------- # # python -m benchmark.gsm8k.bench_sglang --port 8288 --num-questions 1000 100%|██████████████████████████████████████| 1000/1000 [02:36<00:00, 6.37it/s] Accuracy: 0.950 Invalid: 0.000 Latency: 156.981 s Output throughput: 565.851 token/s # ----------------------- overlap ----------------------- # # python -m benchmark.gsm8k.bench_sglang --port 8288 --num-questions 1000 100%|██████████████████████████████████████| 1000/1000 [02:15<00:00, 7.39it/s] Accuracy: 0.956 Invalid: 0.000 Latency: 135.355 s Output throughput: 655.545 token/s ``` - DSV4 Pro: ``` # ----------------------- baseline ----------------------- # # python -m benchmark.gsm8k.bench_sglang --port 8288 --num-questions 1000 100%|██████████████████████████████████████| 1000/1000 [04:31<00:00, 3.69it/s] Accuracy: 0.957 Invalid: 0.000 Latency: 271.137 s Output throughput: 334.259 token/s # ----------------------- overlap ----------------------- # # python -m benchmark.gsm8k.bench_sglang --port 8288 --num-questions 1000 100%|██████████████████████████████████████| 1000/1000 [04:32<00:00, 3.67it/s] Accuracy: 0.957 Invalid: 0.000 Latency: 272.710 s Output throughput: 331.315 token/s ``` ### 3.5. Repro Script - DSV4 Flash (1 node with CP8-TP8 for prefill): ``` SGLANG_DSV4_FP4_EXPERTS=0 \ SGLANG_OPT_USE_JIT_INDEXER_METADATA=1 \ SGLANG_JIT_DEEPGEMM_PRECOMPILE=0 \ SGLANG_PP_SKIP_PURE_CHUNKED_OUTPUT_COMM=1 \ SGLANG_OPT_USE_TORCH_SYMM_MEM_FUSED_KERNEL=1 \ SGLANG_OPT_USE_ONLINE_COMPRESS=1 \ SGLANG_TORCH_PROFILER_DIR=./profile \ python -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path /home/models/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-FP8 \ --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8288 \ --trust-remote-code --enable-cache-report \ --log-level info --enable-metrics \ --page-size 64 --cuda-graph-max-bs 64 \ --max-running-requests 64 \ --mem-fraction-static 0.95 \ --tp-size 8 --pp-size 1 --nnodes 1 \ --node-rank 0 \ --dist-init-addr 192.168.0.1:25000 \ --enable-dsa-prefill-context-parallel \ --dsa-prefill-cp-mode round-robin-split \ --disable-radix-cache \ --tool-call-parser deepseekv4 \ --reasoning-parser deepseek-v4 ``` - DSV4 Pro (3 nodes with PP3-CP8-TP8 for prefill): ``` SGLANG_DSV4_FP4_EXPERTS=0 \ SGLANG_OPT_USE_JIT_INDEXER_METADATA=1 \ SGLANG_JIT_DEEPGEMM_PRECOMPILE=0 \ SGLANG_PP_SKIP_PURE_CHUNKED_OUTPUT_COMM=1 \ SGLANG_OPT_USE_TORCH_SYMM_MEM_FUSED_KERNEL=1 \ SGLANG_OPT_USE_ONLINE_COMPRESS=1 \ SGLANG_TORCH_PROFILER_DIR=./profile \ python -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path /home/models/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-FP8 \ --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8288 \ --trust-remote-code --enable-cache-report \ --log-level info --enable-metrics \ --page-size 64 --cuda-graph-max-bs 64 \ --max-running-requests 64 \ --mem-fraction-static 0.95 \ --tp-size 8 --pp-size 3 --nnodes 3 \ --node-rank ${NODE_ID} \ --dist-init-addr 192.168.0.1:25000 \ --enable-dsa-prefill-context-parallel \ --dsa-prefill-cp-mode round-robin-split \ --disable-radix-cache \ --tool-call-parser deepseekv4 \ --reasoning-parser deepseek-v4 ``` --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :x: [Run #32481815212](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32481815212) Latest PR Test (Extra): :x: [Run #32481815030](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32481815030) Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): :x: [Run #32481815151](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32481815151)

signal.title: fix(hicache): make device eviction sync-free
signal.text: ## Motivation HiRadixCache's device eviction hot path called `torch.unique(free_index // page_size)` to derive page ids. `torch.unique` on a CUDA tensor has a data-dependent output shape, forcing an implicit host/device sync on every eviction. Under multi-GPU TP this stalls the eviction path and can hang the scheduler. ## Changes 1. **Sync-free page derivation**: for page-aligned contiguous runs (guaranteed by `PagedTokenToKVPoolAllocator.alloc`), derive page ids with a fixed-shape strided slice `device_indices[::page_size] // page_size` instead of `torch.unique`. Non-paged or non-page-multiple inputs fall back to `allocator.free`. `TreeCache.page_size == allocator.page_size` is enforced in `kv_cache_builder` (incl. DCP where both equal `page_size * dcp_size`). 2. **Pending write-through guard**: skip device eviction for nodes whose host write-through DMA has not been acked yet, avoiding a use-after-free of KV slots still being read by the DMA (`record_stream` only protects the index tensor). Added a `_replace_pending_write_through_node` invariant assert (pending ⇒ backuped). 3. **Debug-only page-alignment assertions** (`SGLANG_DEBUG_MEMORY_POOL`) to pin the contiguity/alignment invariant without adding sync in production. ## Tests Added `test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_hicache_device_eviction_unit.py` (12 CPU-only unit tests) covering the release routing branches, fallback delegation, debug assertions, and the pending write-through guard on both eviction paths. All pass locally; `black --check` and `py_compile` clean. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32481909321](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32481909321)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32481909175](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32481909175)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32481909382](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32481909382)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [Feature] Support for same GPU native DP replicas with optional CUDA MPS
signal.text: ## Motivation Phase 1 for <https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/35648>. But It will work great for one shot models that don't need to save KV cache, like prefill embedding only models. This change adds `--same-gpu-replicas N` for running `N` native SGLang data-parallel replicas on one physical GPU through one public server endpoint. This is still useful for cases where only one query needs to be answered without need for shared kv. For example: ```bash --same-gpu-replicas 2 ``` resolves to: ```bash --dp-size 2 --gpu-id-step 0 ``` CUDA MPS is optional and remains externally managed. SGLang runs with normal CUDA scheduling when MPS is unavailable and logs a CUDA startup warning when `nvidia-cuda-mps-control` is not installed. ## Modifications - Add `--same-gpu-replicas N` for guarded same-GPU native DP. - Validate the supported topology: TP=1, PP=1, single node, no DP attention, disaggregation, elastic scaling, or Ray, and explicit `--max-total-tokens`. - Launch same-GPU replicas sequentially to reduce startup memory contention. - Keep one public SGLang endpoint; the native DP controller routes requests across private scheduler/model replicas. - Log whether the NVIDIA MPS control utility is available when same-GPU replicas run on CUDA. - Add unit coverage for flag resolution, the legacy alias, conflicts, and topology validation. - Tested using custom `bench_same_gpu_mps` script for endpoint throughput and latency benchmarking. ## Accuracy tests N/A. This change modifies replica placement and request routing; it does not change model-forward or kernel numerics. ## Speed tests and profiling Hardware: RTX 4070 Ti 12 GB Model: `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B` Workload: 100 requests, concurrency 6, four warmup requests, and 128 output tokens per request. CUDA MPS was unavailable in this WSL environment, so these results compare normal CUDA scheduling with one versus two same-GPU replicas. | Configuration | Completion throughput | p50 latency | p90 latency | p99 latency | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 1 replica | 279.7 tok/s | 2.093 s | 3.949 s | 4.157 s | | 2 same-GPU replicas | 538.9 tok/s | 1.176 s | 1.228 s | 4.930 s | Two same-GPU replicas improved aggregate completion throughput by **92.7%** and reduced p50 latency by **43.8%**. The p99 result should be validated with repeated runs. ### Embedding model Hardware: RTX 4070 Ti 12 GB Model: `Qwen/Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B` Workload: 100 embedding requests, concurrency 6, four warmup requests, and one input per request (20 prompt tokens per input). CUDA MPS was unavailable in this WSL environment, so these results compare normal CUDA scheduling with one versus two same-GPU replicas. | Configuration | Embedding throughput | p50 latency | p90 latency | p99 latency | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 1 replica | 127.0 embeddings/s | 0.043 s | 0.062 s | 0.071 s | | 2 same-GPU replicas | 133.2 embeddings/s | 0.043 s | 0.057 s | 0.071 s | | 3 same-GPU replicas | 152.7 embeddings/s | 0.034 s | 0.065 s | 0.111 s | Three same-GPU replicas improved aggregate embedding throughput by **20.2%** over one replica and reduced p50 latency by **20.0%**. However, p99 latency increased to 0.111 s, so validate the tail-latency trade-off with repeated runs and longer or batched inputs. ### CUDA MPS validation CUDA MPS is optional and must be started outside SGLang. ```bash export CUDA_MPS_PIPE_DIRECTORY=/tmp/sglang-mps-pipe export CUDA_MPS_LOG_DIRECTORY=/tmp/sglang-mps-log mkdir -p "$CUDA_MPS_PIPE_DIRECTORY" "$CUDA_MPS_LOG_DIRECTORY" nvidia-cuda-mps-control -d ``` Launch SGLang with two same-GPU replicas: ```bash python -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B \ --same-gpu-replicas 2 \ --mem-fraction-static 0.35 \ --max-total-tokens 1024 \ --max-running-requests 4 \ --disable-cuda-graph ``` Verify that both scheduler processes attached to the MPS server: ```bash MPS_SERVER_PID=$( printf 'get_server_list\n' | nvidia-cuda-mps-control | awk 'NF {print $1; exit}' ) printf 'get_client_list %s\n' "$MPS_SERVER_PID" | nvidia-cuda-mps-control ps -eo pid,ppid,args | grep '[s]glang::scheduler' ``` The two scheduler PIDs must appear in the MPS client list. ## Checklist - [x] Add unit tests. - [x] Add a manual benchmark utility. - [ ] Run NVIDIA CUDA MPS attachment and benchmark validation on native Linux. - [ ] Run formatting and full relevant CI. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32481003421](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32481003421)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32481002895](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32481002895)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32481003083](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32481003083)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: fix(kimi-k3): align reported cached tokens with prompt usage
signal.text: ## Motivation For Kimi K3, the reported `prompt_tokens` excludes the three-token assistant generation stub appended by the chat template. However, `cached_tokens` was still reported as the raw physical prefix-cache length. When the cached prefix overlaps the trailing generation stub, `cached_tokens` can exceed `prompt_tokens`. For example: ```text prompt_tokens = 6207 cached_tokens = 6208 ``` This violates the expected invariant that cached tokens are a subset of prompt tokens and can result in inconsistent cache-input accounting or billing. ## Modifications - Added K3-specific normalization for reported cached tokens. - For Kimi K3, reported cached tokens are calculated as: ```python min(raw_cached_tokens, reported_prompt_tokens) ``` This excludes only the portion of the trailing generation stub reached by the cached prefix. - Preserved the original `cached_tokens` value when the cached prefix does not reach the generation stub. - Preserved existing behavior for all non-K3 models. - Applied the normalization consistently to: - Non-streaming Chat Completions - Streaming final usage - Continuous streaming usage - Kept scheduler-side and KV-cache accounting unchanged. The change only affects the OpenAI-compatible usage response. - Added regression coverage for: - K3 cache hits overlapping the generation stub - K3 cache hits ending before the generation stub - Non-K3 cached-token reporting - K3 continuous streaming usage ## Accuracy Tests This change does not affect model inputs, model outputs, kernels, sampling, or model forward execution. It only normalizes usage metadata returned to API clients. The following behavior matrix was verified against the production reporting helpers: ```text Model Raw prompt/cache Reported prompt/cache Kimi K3 6210 / 6000 6207 / 6000 Kimi K3 6210 / 6208 6207 / 6207 Non-K3 6210 / 6208 6210 / 6208 DSV4 6210 / 6208 6210 / 6208 ``` Additional verification: - Python syntax validation passed for the modified implementation and test files. - `git diff --check` passed. - Regression unit tests were added. The unit-test file could not be executed in the local environment because the required `orjson` dependency was unavailable. The tests are expected to run in the standard SGLang CI environment. ## Speed Tests and Profiling No inference benchmark was performed because this change does not modify the inference path. The additional work is limited to the CPU response-serialization path and consists of: - One K3 model-type check - One integer `min()` operation It does not affect tokenization, prefix-cache lookup, scheduling, prefill, decode, KV transfer, or GPU execution. ## Checklist - [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). `pre-commit` was not run in the current local environment. - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). No documentation update is required because no public API, configuration, or user workflow is changed. - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). Not applicable to model accuracy or inference performance; validation details are provided above. - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process). 2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers. 3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so. - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci` 4. signal.author: KEVINTUAN12

signal.title: model: restore Hunyuan-A13B q/k shape after per-head qk_norm (fix non-CUDA attention crash)
signal.text: ## Motivation Serving `tencent/Hunyuan-A13B-Instruct` (`HunYuanMoEV1ForCausalLM`, `use_qk_norm=True`) on non-CUDA backends (Intel XPU / triton) crashes in attention: ``` RuntimeError: mat1 and mat2 shapes cannot be multiplied (24x128 and 512x4096) ``` `HunYuanAttention.forward`'s `use_qk_norm` path reshapes q/k to `(tokens*heads, head_dim)` for the per-head RMSNorm but never restores the flat `(tokens, heads*head_dim)` shape that RadixAttention / `o_proj` expect. On CUDA the flashinfer backend recomputes the token count from batch metadata, so the mangled leading dim is masked; triton/XPU keys off `q.shape[0]`, so the bad shape reaches `o_proj` (per-rank `512 = 4 heads x 128` at tp-8) and the matmul fails. ## Modifications Restore the flat shape after the per-head norm by appending `.reshape(-1, self.q_size)` / `.reshape(-1, self.kv_size)`, matching the canonical `models/utils.py::apply_qk_norm` (which ends with `q = q_by_head.view(q.shape)`). Only the self-attn `use_qk_norm` path changes; the final tensor shape is identical to before on every backend, so CUDA behavior is unchanged. (The `cross`/CLA path has the same latent missing-restore, but `use_cla=False` for this model, so it is left untouched and flagged for a follow-up.) ## Accuracy Tests Intel XPU, tp-8, bf16 — model loads with 0 skipped params and the server stays healthy through the previously-crashing qk_norm path: - gsm8k 5-shot smoke: 10/10. - gsm8k raw completions (200 samples, max_gen_toks 8192): strict-match 73.5% / flexible-extract 79.5%. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32480991137](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32480991137)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32480990686](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32480990686)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32480990967](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32480990967)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->
signal.author: desmond-intel

signal.title: [Fix] Spawn, don't fork, the benchmark server process
signal.text: `sglang.benchmark.*` launched the server with the platform-default start method (fork on Linux), but the parent already initializes the accelerator in ServerArgs.__post_init__ -- get_xpu_memory_capacity() calls torch.xpu.mem_get_info(), get_device_sm() calls torch.cuda.get_device_capability(). The forked child inherits a dead context and dies on its first device op: RuntimeError: Cannot re-initialize XPU in forked subprocess. launch_server() does force spawn, but only via _set_envs_and_config() once it is already running inside the child, which is too late. Use an explicit spawn context for the process itself. Latent on text-only CUDA runs, where the forked child touches the device only after handing off to spawned scheduler workers; reproducible on XPU and on any backend once the child does device work during warmup (e.g. a VLM processor's image.to(device)). Fixes #34709 <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation sglang.benchmark.* launches the server with the default start method (fork on Linux), but the parent already initialized the accelerator in ServerArgs.__post_init__ (XPU: torch.xpu.mem_get_info(); CUDA: torch.cuda.get_device_capability()). The forked child inherits a dead context and fails on its first device op: RuntimeError: Cannot re-initialize XPU in forked subprocess. launch_server() forces spawn, but only from inside the already-forked child (entrypoints/engine.py:1703) — too late. Latent on text-only CUDA (the child does no device work before spawning scheduler workers); fatal on XPU, and on any backend once the child touches the device during warmup (e.g. a VLM processor's image.to(device)). ## Modifications endpoint.py: launch_or_reuse_server() — create the server process with an explicit spawn context: proc = multiprocessing.get_context("spawn").Process(...) Payload is picklable; the child already expects spawn semantics. ## Accuracy Tests N/A — no kernel/model-forward change; outputs bit-identical. Verified on Nvidia GPU and Intel XPU backend environment. ## Speed Tests and Profiling No inference-path impact. Spawn adds a few seconds of one-time startup cost, outside every measurement window (benchmarks start only after server_is_up()). ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32479274666](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32479274666)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32479274544](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32479274544)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32479274733](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32479274733)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->
signal.author: dayanandav

signal.title: [Diffusion][Refactor] Refactor and unify RoPE execution for DiT models using RotaryEmbedding based on CustomOp
signal.text:
## Motivation Currently, DiT models across SGLang call various ad-hoc functions to apply Rotary Position Embeddings. The choice of function depends on the target hardware device, argument types, and model-specific configurations. Furthermore, internal branches within these functions often perform device type checks again, leading to code fragmentation and duplication. To clean up and unify this behavior, this PR leverages SGLang's existing `CustomOp` mechanism to enhance the core `RotaryEmbedding` class located in `sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/layers/rotary_embedding/base.py`. This abstraction allows models to invoke RoPE through a single, unified interface without writing device-specific handling inside model code, significantly simplifying codebase maintainability and cross-platform execution. ## Modifications This PR is a continuation of [PR #31453](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/31453). Modified 9 key files to implement unified RoPE dispatch and propagate complex frequencies: ### 1. `python/sglang/multimodal_gen/configs/pipeline_configs/qwen_image.py` - Updated `get_freqs_cis()` to return both standard `cos_sin_cache` tuples (`freqs_cis`) and pre-calculated complex frequency tuples (`freqs_complex`). - Propagated `freqs_complex` through `_prepare_cond_kwargs` and pipeline stages. - Added Sequence Parallelism sharding for `img_complex` via `shard_rotary_emb_for_sp()`, enabling pre-computed complex frequencies to be passed directly to the Qwen Image DiT model. ### 2. `python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/layers/rotary_embedding/base.py` - Implemented `forward_npu`, `forward_cuda`, and `forward_native` backend methods inside the `RotaryEmbedding`. - Extended signatures to flexibly accept any RoPE inputs: `complex_freqs`, `cos`/`sin`, or 2D `cos_sin_cache`. - Integrated unified dispatching across lower-level implementations: - `_apply_rotary_emb_complex` (for complex multiplication). - `_apply_rotary_emb` (for standard PyTorch RoPE). - `apply_flashinfer_rope_qk_inplace` (for optimized CUDA execution). - Standardized tensor dimension expectations: `query` and `key` as 4D `[batch, seq_len, num_heads, head_size]`, `complex_freqs` as 3D `[num_tokens, 1, head_size // 2]`, and `cos`/`sin` as 2D `[num_tokens, head_size // 2]`. - Fixed a batch-broadcast bug: raw cos/sin DiT-style calls previously flattened [batch,seq,...] to [batch*seq,...] incorrectly for batch_size > 1. - Added an NPU fast path via torch_npu.npu_rotary_mul for is_neox_style=True, and a complex-multiply derivation path for is_neox_style=False on NPU/native, where no fused kernel exists otherwise. ### 3. `python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/layers/layernorm.py` - Added optional `freqs_complex` parameter to `apply_qk_norm_rope` and `apply_qk_norm_with_optional_rope`. - Replaced FlashInfer calls in the fallback path with the unified `RotaryEmbedding`. - Preserved the existing CUDA fused QK-Norm + RoPE kernel (`fused_inplace_qknorm_rope`) to ensure zero performance regression on CUDA. - Added a module-level _QK_NORM_ROPE_DICT cache keyed by (head_dim, is_neox) to avoid reconstructing RotaryEmbedding on every call. ### 4. `python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/models/dits/mova_video_dit.py` - Refactored `SelfAttention.forward` to implement the usage of `RotaryEmbedding`. ### 5. `python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/models/dits/qwen_image.py` - Updated `QwenImageCrossAttention` to extract `freqs_complex` from `cross_attention_kwargs`. - Passed `img_complex` and `txt_complex` into `apply_qk_norm_with_optional_rope`, enabling Qwen Image DiT cross-attention layers to leverage complex RoPE. ### 6. `python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/models/dits/glm_image.py` - Updated `GlmImageAttention` with `RotaryEmbedding` class usage. - Replaced the `_apply_rotary_emb` and `apply_flashinfer_rope_qk_inplace` functions with `self.rotary_emb()` call . ### 7. `python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/models/dits/flux.py` - Updated `FluxAttention` with `complex_freqs` computing and forwarding them into `apply_qk_norm_with_optional_rope`. ### 8. `python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/models/dits/flux_2.py` - Updated `Flux2Attention` with `complex_freqs` computing and forwarding them into `apply_qk_norm_with_optional_rope`. ### 9. `python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/models/dits/joy_image.py` - Updated `MMDoubleStreamBlock` with `complex_freqs` computing and forwarding them into `apply_qk_norm_with_optional_rope`. ## Tests The changes were tested on openmoss/MOVA-360p, GLM-Image, black-forest-labs/FLUX.1-dev, unsloth/FLUX.2-dev, jd-opensource/JoyAI-Image-Edit-Diffusers, nv-community/Cosmos3-Super-Text2Image and MusePublic/Qwen-image models.
Accuracy test, speed tests and profiling for Mova ### Mova video generation (the same as before changes): https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/396ce85d-df45-432a-a7bf-6d87b1fdb6ee ### 1. SGLang Server Launch Command ```bash sglang serve --model-path $(pwd)/mova_video_360p --pipeline-class-name MOVAPipeline --num-gpus 4 --ring-degree 1 --ulysses-degree 4 --performance-mode memory --dit-layerwise-offload --dit-offload-prefetch-size 0.1 --text-encoder-cpu-offload true --vae-cpu-offload true --enable-torch-compile --warmup-mode server --vae-tiling --vae-sp ``` ### 2. Video Generation Request ```bash curl -X POST "http://localhost:30000/v1/videos" -F "prompt=A curious raccoon" -F "input_reference=@/.../images/raccoon.png" -F "size=640x352" -F "num_frames=49" -F "fps=24" -F "num_inference_steps=25" -F "guidance_scale=5.0" -o create_video.json ``` ### 3. Profiler Latency Results (Ascend NPU) The table below compares the detailed execution times of the rope functions on NPU before and after modifications: | Implementation | func_name | time(%) | total_time(us) | num_calls | Avg(us) | Min(us) | Max(us) | | :--- | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | | **Baseline** | apply_rotary_embedding_native | 100 | 13628501.78 | 2448 | 5567.1984 | 4108.45 | 12372.26 | | **Modified** | _apply_rotary_emb_complex | 100 | 9655076.15 | 2448 | 3944.0671 | 2750.82 | 8124 | | **Baseline** | apply_qk_norm_with_optional_rope | 100 | 23891794.86 | 1224 | 19519.4402 | 15016.6 | 39062.05 | | **Modified** | apply_qk_norm_with_optional_rope | 100 | 14707268.69 | 1224 | 12015.7424 | 8519.32 | 20765.84 | There the `apply_rotary_embedding_native` and `_apply_rotary_emb_complex` functions are imlementing the RoPE logic and the `apply_qk_norm_with_optional_rope` is the common place where they're being called. ### 5. signal.title: [Feature] Beam search support
signal.text: Beam search as a per-request feature: `sampling_params.beam_width = k` returns the top-`n` sequences. No server flag; beam and ordinary requests share the same batches and memory pools. ## Results `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B-Base`, 1x H200, `beam_width = 5000`. End-to-end latency (ms), mean / p50 / p90: | output tokens | sync | overlap | |---|---|---| | 3 | 244.6 / 158.0 / 469.0 | 259.1 / 176.6 / 470.4 | | 16 | 927.7 / 1028.8 / 1120.6 | 903.9 / 957.6 / 1361.7 | | 32 | 1690.7 / 1788.6 / 1827.3 | 1650.9 / 1716.8 / 2003.0 | | 64 | 3511.0 / 3554.1 / 3697.7 | 3303.3 / 3277.3 / 3506.5 | | 128 | 8087.3 / 8267.2 / 8655.6 | 7067.0 / 7164.5 / 7201.3 | `sglang:fwd_occupancy` median under saturated load is 43.7-50.1%, at 67-87% whole-device utilization. ## Repro ```bash python -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B-Base --port 30000 \ --dtype bfloat16 --attention-backend flashinfer \ --mem-fraction-static 0.4 --max-running-requests 20004 \ --context-length 4096 --random-seed 0 \ --disable-radix-cache --disable-chunked-prefix-cache # add --disable-overlap-schedule for the sync column ``` Drive concurrent `/generate` calls with `{"beam_width": 5000, "n": 5000}`, sweeping `max_new_tokens`. Per row, `(max_new_tokens, num_requests, qps, concurrency)`: `(3, 23, 0.8, 4)`, `(16, 10, 0.3, 2)`, `(32, 8, 0.25, 2)`, `(64, 6, 0.2, 2)`, `(128, 4, 0.15, 2)`. For the occupancy row, add `SGLANG_ENABLE_METRICS_DEVICE_TIMER=1`, `--enable-metrics --decode-log-interval 2`, and take the median of `sglang:fwd_occupancy`. `--decode-log-interval 1` reports `NaN`: the window resets every batch and never reaches the branch that computes the ratio. ## Verification - Unit tests (`beam_search`, managers, mem_cache): 2062 passed. - HF parity (`test/manual/beam_search/test_beam_parity.py`): sequence-set overlap 8/10 at `k = 10`. - Load (`test/manual/beam_search/test_beam_search_load.py`): mixed widths 2-100, 100 requests at 10 QPS, p50/p90/p99 = 53/58/175 ms; 3200-wide fan-out passes. - Beam mixed with ordinary penalized requests in the same batches: 36/36. - Sync and overlap agree digest-for-digest, with `SGLANG_ENABLE_STRICT_MEM_CHECK_DURING_BUSY=1` silent throughout. - Ordinary-path regression: `few_shot_gsm8k` 200q greedy 0.470 unchanged. ## Not supported yet Rejected at admission with an explicit error: speculative decoding, PD disaggregation, dp attention, pipeline parallelism, `page_size > 1`, hierarchical cache, SWA/mamba hybrid caches, hisparse, encoder-decoder, diffusion LLM, LoRA, sessions, constrained decoding, stop strings/regex, `min_new_tokens`, `return_logprob`, `return_hidden_states`, and sampling-mask/routed-experts returns. Beam requests are also excluded from mixed-chunk prefill batches. **Retraction.** A beam group cannot be retracted: its member rows alias the leader's prompt KV, so rolling back part of the group corrupts it. Under KV pressure ordinary requests are retracted first, and if that is not enough the whole group is aborted with HTTP 500 instead of being requeued. Admission reserves the group's `req_to_token` rows but still budgets decode KV at one token per step, so a large `beam_width` can reach this path under load. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32469224188](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32469224188)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32469223729](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32469223729)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32469224176](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32469224176)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: fix: handle list token-id logprob results
signal.text: ## Motivation In mixed batches, `next_token_token_ids_logprobs_val` can contain both: - tensors for requests that ask for token-ID logprobs; - list placeholders for requests that do not ask for token-ID logprobs. The current prefill and decode normalization paths call `.tolist()` on every entry. When an entry is already a list, this raises: ```text AttributeError: 'list' object has no attribute 'tolist' ``` Fixes #35705. ## Modifications - Use `torch.is_tensor()` to check each token-ID logprob result before calling `.tolist()`. - Preserve values that are already lists. - Apply the fix to both prefill and decode normalization paths. - Add focused CPU regression tests covering mixed list and tensor results in both paths. ## Accuracy Tests - Deployment validation against the reported failure scenario passed. - Added regression coverage for both prefill and decode result normalization. - This change does not modify model forward computation or numerical results. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not applicable. The change only adds a lightweight `torch.is_tensor()` check while normalizing token-ID logprob results. This path runs only when token-ID logprobs are requested, and no measurable performance impact is expected. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). signal.text: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation <!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. --> MiniMax H3 Ref2VA currently resizes every reference image to a fixed 2048-pixel short edge, including upscaling smaller inputs. This behavior matches the original Diffusers preprocessing, but some distilled Ref2VA checkpoints use a different reference-image preprocessing policy during training. For example, ModelTC's MiniMax-H3-Turbo Ref2VA checkpoint recommends matching the reference-image pixel area to the target video canvas: https://github.com/ModelTC/Minimax-H3-Turbo#note-on-reference-image-resizing In addition to this, Comfy also offers two different resize modes: https://docs.comfy.org/tutorials/video/minimax/minimax-h3#prompting-tips-3 Using a different resize policy at inference time can result in: - a mismatch between training and inference preprocessing; - unnecessarily large reference-image token sequences; - increased memory usage from upscaling small reference images; - degraded Ref2VA conditioning quality. This PR adds configurable reference-image resizing for MiniMax H3 Ref2VA while preserving the existing SGLang behavior as the default. ## Modifications <!-- Detail the changes made in this pull request. --> ### Add `reference_resize_mode` Add a new MiniMax H3 sampling parameter: ```python reference_resize_mode: str = "diffusers" ``` Supported values: | Mode | Behavior | |---|---| | `match` | Match the reference-image pixel area to the resolved target canvas while preserving aspect ratio. Smaller references are not upscaled. | | `max` | Downscale only when the reference-image short edge exceeds 2048 pixels. | | `diffusers` | Always resize the reference-image short edge to 2048 pixels, including upscaling. | The default remains `diffusers` to preserve existing SGLang behavior. ### Propagate the parameter through all request paths The parameter is supported by: - offline `DiffGenerator` requests; - JSON `/v1/videos` requests; - multipart `/v1/videos` requests; - dynamic batching and disaggregated request transfer through `SamplingParams`. The HTTP video adapter only adds the parameter to lowered sampling kwargs when it was explicitly provided. This ensures omitted values continue to use the `diffusers` default. Example: ```json { "task": "ref2va", "reference_resize_mode": "match", "target": { "short_edge": 544, "aspect_ratio": "16:9", "duration_seconds": 5.0 } } ``` ### Resolve `match` against the final target canvas Reference-image geometry is resolved during pre-queue admission, after the target video canvas has been finalized. For `match`, the scale factor is: ```python scale = min(1.0, sqrt(target_area / reference_area)) ``` The resized dimensions: - preserve the reference-image aspect ratio; - are independently rounded to the nearest multiple of 32; - do not crop the source image; - do not upscale smaller reference images. This policy applies only to Ref2VA image references using the `image.reference_preserve` material chain. FL2VA first/last keyframes continue to use the existing `image.target_canvas` path and are unaffected. ### Misc For the default `diffusers` mode, the existing shape policy identifier is preserved: ```text reference_image_short_edge_v1 ``` The new modes use: ```text reference_image_match_v1 reference_image_max_v1 ``` This avoids breaking external logs, tests, or consumers that depend on the existing `shape_policy_version`. ## Accuracy Tests <!-- If this pull request affects model outputs (e.g., changes to the kernel or model forward code), provide accuracy test results. --> This PR changes only MiniMax-H3 Ref2VA reference-image preprocessing. It does not modify model weights, kernels, or forward-pass math. The default `diffusers` policy remains backward compatible: - Reference-image short edge remains 2048. - Upscaling behavior is unchanged. - `shape_policy_version` remains `reference_image_short_edge_v1`. The opt-in `match` and `max` policies intentionally change Ref2VA conditioning inputs. Added deterministic unit tests cover: - `match`: matches the target canvas pixel area while preserving aspect ratio. - `match`: does not upscale smaller reference images. - `max`: caps the reference short edge at 2048 without intentional upscaling. - `diffusers`: preserves the legacy 2048-short-edge behavior and metadata. - Mode normalization and invalid-mode rejection. - Invalid target-canvas rejection. - `/v1/videos` transport of `reference_resize_mode`. - Preservation of the default when the request omits the option. - Prequeue propagation of the selected mode and resolved target canvas. - Backward-compatible prequeue fallback to `diffusers`. Test command: ```bash PYTHONPATH="$PWD/python" python -m pytest -q \ python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_minimax_h3_admission.py \ python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_minimax_h3_media.py \ -k "reference_resize or reference_image_resize" ``` All tests have passed. No end-to-end visual-quality benchmark is required for the unchanged default diffusers path. Visual output changes are expected only when callers explicitly select `match` or `max`. ## Speed Tests and Profiling <!-- If this pull request impacts inference speed, provide benchmarking and profiling results. --> ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process). 2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers. 3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so. - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci` 4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32480559906](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32480559906)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32480559740](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32480559740)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32480559859](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32480559859)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [AMD] Enable unified-KV HiSparse on ROCm for DeepSeek-V4
signal.text: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation <!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. --> On ROCm, HiSparse currently runs only on the **separate-KV** DeepSeek-V4 path (`SGLANG_HACK_FLASHMLA_BACKEND=triton`, packed FP8 KV layout), enabled by #26639. The **unified-KV** backend (`SGLANG_HACK_FLASHMLA_BACKEND=unified_kv_triton`) — where compressed C4 KV lives in the unified pool's `rows[swa_pages:]` and the HiSparse hot buffer is a bf16 view into that region backed by a linear host cold pool — was blocked by a temporary startup guard. This PR enables unified-KV + HiSparse on ROCm end-to-end, and adds JIT/unit/eval coverage. ## Modifications <!-- Detail the changes made in this pull request. --> - Enable unified-KV HiSparse on ROCm (`hisparse_coordinator.py`, `deepseek_v4_memory_pool.py`, `compressor_v2.py`, `arg_groups/hisparse_hook.py`, `srt/mem_cache/allocator/hisparse.py`): remove the temporary guard that blocked unified_kv_triton + HiSparse, wire the unified C4 device pool / linear host cold pool, and fix the compressed-C4 remap to account for the pre-applied swa_pages offset. - Enable dsv4 paged HiSparse JIT kernel tests on ROCm (`test/registered/kernels/ops/kvcache/test_hisparse.py`). - Honor the C4 shrink factor on the unified path (`deepseek_v4_memory_pool.py`, `mem_cache/allocator/hisparse.py`): upstream `pool_configurator` already folds `host_to_device_ratio = S` into `bytes_per_full_token` as a `1/(4S)` C4 term and raises `max_total_num_tokens` accordingly, but the unified pool ignored it. This sizes the on-device C4 region to the shrunk budget via `c4_compress_pages`, and stops `available_size()` / `full_available_size()` from clamping capacity to the device C4 pool — on the unified path the cold remainder is host-resident, so the bound is the logical full-token pool. Net effect: freed VRAM actually reaches `full_token`. Separate-KV / CUDA behaviour is unchanged. - Unit tests for the unified-KV HiSparse pool (`test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_hisparse_unified_pool.py`): host-mirror geometry, view aliasing of the unified compressed region, c4-only layer views, alloc/free mapping, oversubscribe and that c4_compress_pages actually shrinks the device C4 region while the c128 layers are untouched. - Eval tests (`.../mi35x/..._unified_eval_mi35x.py` and `..._unified_dp_eval_mi35x.py`): GSM8K accuracy + a ~19k-token long-context swap-path retrieval test, on TP8 and on TP8+DP-attention. **Highlight — the NVIDIA CUDA forward path is unchanged.** All modifications are confined to ROCm-only branches: `_is_hip` guards and HiSparse/unified-KV-gated code. (The JIT test change only removes `skipif(is_hip())` markers, so those tests now also run on ROCm; CUDA behavior is unaffected.) To enable this feature, you can pass e.g. ``` --enable-hisparse \ --hisparse-config '{"top_k": 1024, "device_buffer_size": 2048, "host_to_device_ratio": 4}' ``` in the server launch configs. ## Accuracy Tests <!-- If this pull request affects model outputs (e.g., changes to the kernel or model forward code), provide accuracy test results. --> GSM8K few-shot accuracy alone does **not** validate the host↔device swap path. With `device_buffer_size=2048` (compressed-token budget) and GSM8K prompts of ~1k–1.7k tokens (~250–425 compressed after the 4x C4 ratio), every request stays on the fast path (`host_len <= device_buffer_size` → preloaded to the device hot buffer), so decode is all device-resident hits and the **cold→hot swap-in (miss-copy) kernel is never exercised**. GSM8K therefore validates: sparse top-k selection numerics, unified-KV pool wiring/aliasing, the compressor write path, and HIP-graph decode stability — but **not** swap correctness. **Note:** a nonzero #cpu token in the decode log during GSM8K is the authoritative host backup of compressed C4 (every request is backed up to host), not decode-time swap-in. The swap-in (miss-copy) path is gated per-request by `host_len > device_buffer_size`; GSM8K's per-request footprint (~250–425 compressed) stays below `device_buffer_size=2048`, so it runs entirely on the preloaded hot path. Swap correctness is established by, in increasing scope: 1. **JIT kernel tests** (`test/registered/kernels/ops/kvcache/test_hisparse.py`): `test_dsv4_swap_in_reads_paged_host_layout`, `*_miss_copy_layout`, and the LRU/miss cases check the swap-in kernel byte-for-byte against a reference. 2. **End-to-end long-context swap test** (`test_b_long_context_swap`): a ~19k token prompt (~4750 compressed > 2048) forces a host cold pool and a swap-in on every decode step; a passcode buried in the long context can only be retrieved if cold→hot copies land correctly. This is the authoritative end-to-end swap oracle. **Accuracy of record:** The numbers reported here **(TP8 0.953 / TP8 DP8 0.949)** were reproduced locally on `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro`. ## Tests reproduction guidance ### JIT kernel (11 passed) ``` HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 python -m pytest test/registered/kernels/ops/kvcache/test_hisparse.py -v ``` These now also run on ROCm (the `skipif(is_hip())` markers were removed). The swap-in kernel cases (`test_dsv4_swap_in_reads_paged_host_layout`, `*_miss_copy_layout`, LRU/miss) compare the host→device cold-copy byte-for-byte against a reference, so a pass proves the swap-in kernel is numerically correct. ### unit test (6 passed) ``` HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 python -m pytest test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_hisparse_unified_pool.py -v ``` Validates the unified-KV pool: host-mirror geometry, the bf16 view aliasing into `rows[swa_pages:]`, C4-only layer views, alloc/free index mapping, and oversubscribe handling. ### e2e test (2 passed each) ``` python -m pytest -s -v test/registered/amd/accuracy/mi35x/test_deepseek_v4_pro_fp4_hisparse_unified_eval_mi35x.py python -m pytest -s -v test/registered/amd/accuracy/mi35x/test_deepseek_v4_pro_fp4_hisparse_unified_dp_eval_mi35x.py ``` Each file runs two methods. **What proves the feature is live:** **(a) Server startup** — the unified-KV HiSparse host cold pool is allocated, and the config is applied: ```text ... enable_hisparse=True, hisparse_config='{"top_k": 1024, "device_buffer_size": 2048, "host_to_device_ratio": 2}' ... Allocating 31.35 GB host memory for V4 paged pool 'dsv4_hisparse_c4' ... ``` The `dsv4_hisparse_c4` host pool only exists on the HiSparse path; its presence with `unified_kv_triton` confirms the unified hot/cold wiring is taken. **(b) `test_a_gsm8k`** — accuracy / sparse-selection guard. Expect the method to **PASS** with GSM8K accuracy ≈ 0.95 (assertion gate `> 0.91`). **(c) `test_b_long_context_swap`** — the swap-path guard, and the **authoritative evidence that host↔device swap works**. A ~19k-token prompt with a passcode buried at the top is sent; expect the method to **PASS** with the passcode echoed back: ```text long_context_swap completion='7G-ZULU-4419' ``` The corresponding server decode line is the smoking gun — a single long request whose compressed C4 footprint far exceeds `device_buffer_size=2048`: ```text Decode batch, #running-req: 1,, ..., #gpu token: 2049, gpu token usage: 0.00, #cpu token: 9566, cpu token usage: 0.01, cuda graph: True, ... ``` - `#gpu token: 2049` ≈ `device_buffer_size` (2048) → the device hot buffer is capped at the configured budget. - `#cpu token: 9566` (> 0) → the remaining cold C4 tokens live in the host pool and are streamed in on every decode step. - The passcode can only be retrieved if those cold→hot swap-ins land correctly, so a PASS proves end-to-end swap correctness (the DP file shows the same behavior under `--dp 8 --enable-dp-attention`). ## Speed Tests and Profiling <!-- If this pull request impacts inference speed, provide benchmarking and profiling results. --> This is a **capacity** feature, not a latency one, and it is worth being explicit about the trade rather than reporting a throughput number that misses the point. `host_to_device_ratio = S` shrinks the GPU-resident C4 region to `1/S` of the budget and mirrors the remainder on the host. Upstream `_get_bytes_per_full_token` already carries the resulting `1/(4S)` C4 term, so the freed VRAM shows up directly as a larger `max_total_num_tokens`. #32368 measures 12.90M → 17.56M (+36%) on the same 1P1D topology. The cost is decode-step latency: the swap-in runs on the main stream between the indexer and attention of every C4 layer. It is latency/occupancy-bound, not bandwidth-bound — `LaunchKernel` uses `grid = batch size`, so a per-rank decode batch of ~20 leaves ~9% occupancy on 256 CUs, which is why #32368's `device_buffer_size` sweep (2048 → 16384, ~8x fewer bytes moved) made decode monotonically *worse*. The levers are multi-CTA sharding (#31341) and side-stream overlap (#28523), neither of which is in this PR's scope. When to turn this on: HiSparse trades decode latency for token capacity, so it is a loss whenever the KV working set of your concurrent requests already fits in VRAM — you pay the swap-in cost and get nothing back. It pays off only past the point where the non-HiSparse configuration can no longer admit the load, at which point the comparison is not "slower" but "runs at all". ## CI coverage PR-CI: - `test/registered/kernels/ops/kvcache/test_hisparse.py` (HiSparse JIT kernels; HIP skip removed so it now runs on ROCm) - `test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_hisparse_unified_pool.py` (unified-KV C4 device pool) These give per-PR coverage of the unified-KV + HiSparse pool/kernel paths. Nightly e2e (8-GPU TP8 / TP8 DP8, `nightly=True`): - `nightly-amd-8-gpu-mi35x-deepseek-v4-pro-hisparse-unified` - `nightly-amd-8-gpu-mi35x-deepseek-v4-pro-hisparse-unified-dp` These two suites are registered but **not yet wired into any workflow**, so they do not run on PR or on the nightly schedule yet. Following the precedent of the unified-KV PR #27380, the PR-CI/nightly wiring is tracked in the AMD CI coverage issue #27521 (cc @bingxche @yctseng0211). I will add them to the issue list then. ## Checklist - [✔] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [✔] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [✔] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [✔] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process). 2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers. 3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so. - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci` 4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32474067894](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32474067894)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32474067330](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32474067330)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32474067909](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32474067909)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: Fix: remove hardcoded CUDA device placement in model files (#34552)
signal.text: Replace hardcoded .cuda() and .to("cuda") calls with device-aware placement to support XPU, NPU, HPU, and CPU backends. - llava.py, llavavid.py, yivl.py: place vision towers on the language model device. - gpt_oss.py: dequantize weights and move expert shards to the destination device. - phi4mm_audio.py: move streaming masks to xs_pad.device instead of forcing CUDA. Single-device CUDA behavior remains unchanged. Fixes #34552 ## Motivation `.cuda()` / `.to("cuda")` in model code ignores the resolved `--device`, so the legacy LLaVA models fail to start on XPU (and NPU/HPU/CPU): python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model-path lmms-lab/llava-onevision-qwen2-0.5b-ov --device xpu AssertionError: Torch not compiled with CUDA enabled Two more files carry the same pattern and are fixed alongside it. Fixes #34552. ## Modifications Derive the device from the tensor or module the result must match: - `llava.py`, `llavavid.py`, `yivl.py` — load the CLIP/SigLIP vision tower onto the language model's device. Fixes `Llava{Llama,Qwen,Mistral}ForCausalLM`, `LlavaVidForCausalLM`, `YiVLForCausalLM`. `LlavaForConditionalGeneration` overrides `load_weights` and was unaffected. - `gpt_oss.py` `_dequant_mlp_weight` — dequantize on `get_device()` instead of an unguarded `.cuda()`; also a startup crash on XPU for original-layout checkpoints. Result is still restored to `original_device`. - `gpt_oss.py` `_load_mxfp4_experts_weights` — move each shard to the destination param's device; the old `if _is_cuda` guard left non-CUDA backends slicing experts on CPU. - `phi4mm_audio.py` `forward_embeddings` — move the CPU-built streaming masks to `xs_pad.device`, matching `calculate_hs_mask` in the same class. Drops `xs_pad = xs_pad.cuda()`, which retargeted the input when it sat on a non-current CUDA index. Every replacement resolves to the same device `.cuda()` picked, so single-device CUDA behavior is unchanged. ## Accuracy Tests Device selection only; existing coverage should be green and unchanged: - `vlm/test_vision_openai_server_a.py::TestLlavaServer`, `vlm/test_vision_chunked_prefill.py`, `unit/models/test_llava.py` - `models_e2e/test_gpt_oss_sm120.py`, `models_e2e/test_gpt_oss_4gpu_mxfp4.py` - `npu/vlm_models/test_npu_phi4_multimodal_instruct.py`, `npu/llm_models/test_npu_phi_4_multimodal_llm.py` Not covered: `yivl.py` / `llavavid.py` (no registered test), the phi4mm audio encoder (NPU tests are image + text only), and the gpt_oss original-layout load. ## Speed Tests and Profiling No inference-path change — weight loading and one-time mask construction only. gpt-oss startup on XPU/NPU improves slightly (expert slicing no longer falls back to CPU); not benchmarked. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32479403443](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32479403443)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32479403136](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32479403136)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32479403328](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32479403328)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->
