signal.title: [diffusion] Accelerate SANA-Video linear attention in quality=high
signal.text: ## Summary - add a request-scoped SANA-Video linear-attention fast path for `quality=high` - keep BF16 inputs for the first linear-attention GEMM while requesting FP32 accumulation/output; keep the second GEMM in FP32 - preserve the original FP32-input chain bit-for-bit for the default `quality=lossless` - add CUDA guards, mount/unmount coverage, fused-kernel docs, and benchmark-skill guidance ## H200 results Native SGLang eager, BF16, 832x480, 17 frames, 50 steps, guidance 6.0, seed 42: | Path | Denoise latency | | --- | ---: | | main, `quality=high` | 243.8 / 244.7 ms/step | | this PR, `quality=high` | 231.7 / 232.6 ms/step | This is about a 5.0% denoise reduction with unchanged peak reserved memory. The production-shape attention microbenchmark improved from 0.7352 ms to 0.3898 ms (1.89x). All 17 decoded frames passed the repository video thresholds against main: - minimum SSIM: 0.9244 (threshold 0.92) - minimum PSNR: 31.33 dB (threshold 24 dB) - mean SSIM / PSNR: 0.9370 / 32.43 dB An additional 832x480, 81-frame, 8-step `quality=lossless` run produced the exact same MP4 SHA256 as the main eager baseline (`7167b9f4...`), confirming that the default path remains bit-exact. ## Cookbook production video and end-to-end A/B (B300) Prompt from `docs/cookbook/diffusion/SANA-Video/SANA-Video.mdx`: `A red tram moves slowly through a sunlit city square while pedestrians cross behind it. motion score: 30.` Configuration: NVIDIA B300 SXM6 AC, native `--backend sglang`, BF16, 1 GPU, 832x480, 81 frames at 16 FPS, 50 steps, guidance 6.0, seed 42, `quality=high`, `--performance-mode manual`. ![SANA-Video quality=high main versus PR, frames 0/40/80](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/pr-media/diffusion-prs/35728/contact-sheet.jpg) [Side-by-side production video](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/pr-media/diffusion-prs/35728/side-by-side.mp4) · [main video](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/pr-media/diffusion-prs/35728/main.mp4) · [PR video](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/pr-media/diffusion-prs/35728/pr.mp4) | Path | Saved-request e2e runs | Mean e2e | Mean denoise stage | | --- | --- | ---: | ---: | | main, `quality=high` | 53.397 / 53.411 / 53.399 s | 53.402 s | 50.713 s | | this PR, `quality=high` | 49.537 / 49.554 / 49.533 s | 49.542 s | 46.869 s | That is a **7.23% end-to-end reduction** and a **7.58% denoise-stage reduction** on B300. Across all 81 decoded frames, main versus PR measured mean/min SSIM **0.95467 / 0.94467** and mean/min PSNR **31.63 / 30.19 dB**. Request e2e starts immediately before `generate()` and ends after the MP4 exists and its SHA256 is recorded, so it includes text encoding, DiT, VAE decode, materialization, and video saving. Model loading and one benchmark warmup are excluded. Logs confirm that the quality-gated kernel mounted on the PR path and that both paths used the native backend with no diffusers fallback. After the complete SANA-Video model group, the task-owned B300 cache was deleted: 14,003,439,075 bytes and 5 weight files removed, with zero residual model-cache files verified. ## Validation - `pre-commit run --files ...` - H200: `test_sites.py::test_sana_video_linear_attention_quality_path_and_guards` plus `test_sana_video.py` (5 passed) - H200: final 50-step high-quality model run and 81-frame lossless regression The isolated SANA-Video cache was deleted after the model test group; the cleanup ledger confirms zero residual model-cache files and zero residual weight files. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32450207949](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32450207949)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32450207904](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32450207904)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32450208088](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32450208088)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [FIX] use DP attention group for MoonViT reductions
signal.text: ## Motivation Kimi-VL can deadlock on the first image request when DP attention is enabled with more than one DP group and `attn_tp_size > 1`, such as TP4/DP2. MoonViT shards its attention output projection and MLP output projection across the attention TP group, but these layers reduce through the global TP group. Only the DP group handling the image executes these collectives, so ranks enqueue different collective sequences. Fixes #34442. ## Modifications - Use the DP-attention TP group for the MoonViT attention output projection. - Use the DP-attention TP group for the MoonViT MLP output projection. - Add a unit test covering both reduction paths. ## Accuracy Tests The change only selects the communicator for existing reductions. The added unit test checks both projections. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not run. signal.title: [DeepSeek-V4][DSpark] Handle zero-length CUDA graph padding in online C128 planner
signal.text: ## Motivation Fix online C128 compression for DeepSeek-V4 with DSpark compact ragged verification and CUDA graph enabled. The issue can be reproduced with: ```bash SGLANG_OPT_USE_ONLINE_COMPRESS=1 SGLANG_EXPERIMENTAL_ONLINE_C128_DSPARK=1 SGLANG_RAGGED_VERIFY_MODE=compact ``` DSpark compact verification uses ragged verify lengths. During CUDA graph replay, the request batch is padded to the selected graph bucket size. Rows that do not correspond to active requests are represented by: ```txt extend_len = 0 ``` These padded rows contain no query tokens and should not generate online C128 compression or state-pool write plans. Previously, _plan_prefill_partial required every row to satisfy: ```cpp 0 < extend_len && extend_len <= seq_len ``` As a result, the first CUDA graph replay containing padded DSpark rows failed with a RuntimeCheck. This was not normally observed in the Eagle/MTP path because its verification layout uses a fixed number of draft tokens for every request row. DSpark compact verification, however, has variable verify lengths and zero-length graph padding rows. Changes - Allow extend_len == 0 in the online C128 prefill planner. - Skip zero-length padded rows because they own no query tokens and must not produce PlanC, PlanW, or state-pool entries. - Preserve validation that extend_len must not exceed seq_len. - Add a detailed error message containing the invalid lengths and batch row index. This PR is bound to PR32035 and needs to be tested on PR32035.https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32035 <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32470841798](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32470841798)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32470841770](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32470841770)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32470841913](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32470841913)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.text: ## Summary - enable the existing diffusion breakable CUDA graph runner for `meituan-longcat/LongCat-Image` - keep LongCat's fixed 512-token DiT prompt shape unchanged so the generic BCG buckets do not capture unused expanded signatures - document the deployment command and refresh the checked-in diffusion performance/profile skills ## Why LongCat's native eager DiT trace is launch-heavy between attention calls. The existing BCG runner can capture those regions as 31 graph segments, but LongCat was not admitted by the model and pipeline allowlists. LongCat always sends the full 512-token prompt body to the DiT. A small model-specific pass-through padder therefore preserves one reusable signature for short and long raw prompts instead of applying generic prompt padding. ## Production-shape visual and end-to-end A/B (B300) Prompt from the checked-in LongCat diffusion benchmark preset: `A red panda reading a book beside a sunlit window.` Configuration: NVIDIA B300 SXM6 AC, native `--backend sglang`, BF16, 1 GPU, 1024x1024, 50 steps, guidance 4.5, seed 42, prompt rewrite disabled, `quality=lossless`, `--performance-mode manual`. ![LongCat main eager versus PR BCG](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/pr-media/diffusion-prs/35724/main-vs-pr.jpg) The main and PR PNGs are byte-exact (`sha256=6a44ff30a185993f50d23da660b3cbe42fb8fdf8ac1d0d612d0086f35c723372`). | Path | Saved-request e2e runs | Mean e2e | Mean denoise stage | | --- | --- | ---: | ---: | | main, eager | 7.422 / 7.421 / 7.445 s | 7.429 s | 7.109 s | | this PR, BCG | 7.178 / 7.174 / 7.175 s | 7.175 s | 6.261 s | That is a **3.42% end-to-end reduction** and an **11.93% denoise-stage reduction** on B300. Request e2e starts immediately before `generate()` and ends after the output file exists and its SHA256 is recorded, so it includes prompt encoding, DiT, VAE decode, materialization, and PNG saving. Model loading, the one-time 16.43 s BCG capture, and one benchmark warmup are excluded. Logs confirm the native backend with no diffusers fallback. signal.title: feat(kv-events): Add component_types field to BlockStored for per-component placement tracking
signal.text: ## Motivation KV-aware routers consume `BlockStored` / `BlockRemoved` to track which blocks live on which tier. On hybrid models the unified radix tree keeps several independent KV components on one node — full attention, sliding window, mamba state — and evicts and restores them independently. A `BlockStored` today only says "this block is on GPU". That is ambiguous once SWA has been tombstoned off an internal node while its full KV stays resident: the router still believes the block is fully reusable and routes a request that then has to recompute the window. This adds an opt-in per-component placement dimension so a consumer can tell what is actually resident at a given medium, following the same shape as #18205 which added the `medium` field. ## Modifications Gated behind `--enable-kv-events-component-types`, off by default. 1. **Schema.** A trailing `Optional[list[str]]` on `BlockStored` plus the `KV_COMPONENT_FULL/SWA/MAMBA` wire names. `BlockRemoved` stays whole-block — a removal always means the base (full) component left the tier, so there is nothing partial to express. 2. **Plumbing.** The flag flows from `ServerArgs` through `CacheInitParams` into the cache builder, and is documented in the server arguments reference. The UMBP subscriber logs the component dimension but does not forward it; its external-KV API is keyed by `(hashes, tier)` only. 3. **Emission.** `KVCacheEventMixin` gains a `_component_types_for_page` hook defaulting to `None`; `UnifiedTreeCore` overrides it and reports residency off live tree state, anchoring the single per-leaf mamba state to the leaf's last page. 4. **Tests.** 20 unit tests in `TestUnifiedRadixCacheComponentPlacementEvents`, plus wire-layout tests in `test_kv_events.py`. Three ordering constraints shaped the implementation and are worth flagging for review: - *Gains defer, losses do not.* SWA and Mamba attach device values through barrier-applied actions (`SWARebuild`, `MambaEvictExcessPathStates`), so a node's component set is not final until those apply. Inserts collect nodes in `_InsertWalkState` and emit one snapshot per node in the TAIL step; evictions are final when the component is dropped and emit immediately. - *Emission is root-first.* SWA splits the fresh leaf at commit time, so nodes are noted in neither tree nor creation order. `_record_store_event` seeds a node's lazily computed hash chain off its parent's hash, so announcing a child first would publish it as a root block under a hash no other code path reproduces. - *Partial eviction restates, never removes.* When SWA or Mamba is tombstoned while full survives the block has not left the tier, so we restate the smaller component set. Whole-block teardowns (`_demote`, host-leaf eviction) keep emitting `BlockRemoved` and never restate. `commit_load_back` also moves its emit after every component restores, unioning each component's `nodes_to_load`; emitting on full's list alone reported a promoted block as full-only. ## Subscriber compatibility `BlockStored` is a msgspec `array_like` struct, so every field is always encoded positionally — an unset `component_types` is a trailing `nil`, not an omitted slot (pinned by `test_component_types_is_the_trailing_slot`). With the flag **off** that `nil` is exactly what a positional decoder reads for an absent optional, so subscribers are unaffected; verified against both in-tree decoders, sgl-router (which drains unknown trailing fields, `experimental/sgl-router/src/policies/kv_events/wire.rs:420`) and dynamo's kv-router. With the flag **on**, the slot holds a list. sgl-router still ignores it. dynamo's kv-router, however, shares one positional layout with vLLM in which that slot is `lora_name` (a string), so it rejects the whole event batch. This is exactly why the feature is opt-in, and enabling it against a dynamo subscriber is not supported today. Aligning the two representations — dynamo already models this as one event per KV-cache group tagged with `kv_cache_spec_kind` — is a larger cross-project change and deliberately out of scope here. Only component-aware caches honour the flag; the mixin hook returns `None` elsewhere, so `radix_cache`, `hiradix_cache`, `swa_radix_cache`, `mamba_radix_cache` and `hi_mamba_radix_cache` are untouched. ## Accuracy Tests Not applicable — observability only. This touches no kernel, no model forward path, and no cache eviction or placement decision; it changes what is reported about placement, never the placement itself. Unit tests run locally across page_size 1/4/16/64/128 and the FULL, FULL+SWA, FULL+MAMBA and FULL+SWA+MAMBA configurations (`test_unified_radix_cache_unittest.py`, `test_kv_events.py`, and the radix/hiradix/swa/mamba mem_cache units): 1113 passed, 1030 skipped (config-conditional), 140 subtests passed. `test_unified_radix_cache_unittest.py` is one of the 12 files currently deferred at module level by #31812 during the ServerArgs config-namespace migration, so those cases will not run in CI until that skip is lifted upstream; the run above was done locally with the module skip removed. The wire-layout tests live in `test_kv_events.py`, which is not deferred and does run in CI. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not applicable. With the flag off the added cost is one boolean check per store event. With it on, a per-page component scan bounded by the component count (at most 3) plus one ancestor walk per insert flush. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. signal.title: [Mooncake] Fix silent SSD offload corruption when TP/PP ranks share ssd_offload_path
signal.text: ## Motivation Each scheduler rank embeds its own `MooncakeDistributedStore` client, and `MooncakeStore.__init__ `passes all of them the same ssd_offload_path. Mooncake's SSD tier assumes one client per storage location, and a shared directory corrupts silently: - bucket ids are generated per process (`timestamp<<12` seed with a plain atomic increment, `mooncake-store/src/storage_backend.cpp`) - after a restart every client resumes from the same scanned max_bucket_id, making filename collisions deterministic - bucket files are opened with `O_CREAT|O_TRUNC`, so a collision truncates another rank's bucket and subsequent reads return wrong KV bytes with no error ## Modifications Give every rank a private subdirectory `ssd_offload_path/rank_<dp_rank>_<tp_rank>_<pp_rank>` (created before setup()). The suffix mirrors the per-rank key convention already used in this file (mha_suffix). When storage_config is None the path is used as-is, unchanged from today. The dp_rank component is required, not cosmetic: with dp-attention, `HiCacheController` reports the attention-group-local rank as tp_rank, which is 0 on every DP rank when attn_tp_size == 1 (e.g. tp8/dp8 DeepSeek), so tp_rank alone collapses all ranks onto one directory. We hit exactly this in a production deployment: 8 clients started in the same second shared one seed and truncated each other's buckets within minutes. `HiCacheStorageConfig` gains a `dp_rank` field (default 0) populated from the dp_rank the controller already computes. Note for existing SSD-offload deployments: previously offloaded buckets at the directory root are orphaned by the layout change (a one-time cache loss, recomputed on miss - not corruption). They can be deleted. ## Accuracy Tests N/A - no change to model outputs (client-side storage path handling only). ## Speed Tests and Profiling N/A - one os.makedirs at engine startup. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32459318185](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32459318185)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32459318138](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32459318138)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32459318314](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32459318314)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.author: yxxhero

signal.title: [NPU] Adapt DFlash2 speculative decoding to Ascend NPUs
signal.text: ## Motivation DFlash2 (#35371) landed on main as the successor to DFlash: a block-diffusion drafter with local grouped convolutions and a candidate selector, currently CUDA-only. First-generation DFlash drafts already run on Ascend NPUs (#23122, #31739), but the DFlash2 checkpoints cannot serve on NPU yet, and I found no existing issue/PR tracking this. This PR adapts the DFlash2 verify path so it can serve on Ascend NPUs (and any Triton-free environment), while keeping the CUDA path byte-for-byte identical. ## Changes - **Triton import guards** (`triton_compat.py`, new): kernel modules in `kernels/ops/speculative/` imported triton unconditionally, which broke module import on Triton-free Ascend images. The new compat shim degrades `@triton.jit` to a stub that raises only on *launch*, so non-CUDA devices can import the DFlash/DSpark modules and dispatch to torch fallbacks. This is generic: any environment without triton benefits, CUDA is untouched. - **Torch chain speculative-sampling fallback** (`chain_speculative_sampling_torch` in `reject_sampling.py`): buffer-for- buffer mirror of `speculative_sampling_classic_kernel` (same `coin * q < p` accept rule, same residual `max(p - q, 0)` final sampling, NaN draft entries treated as 0, same `predicts`/`accept_index`/`accept_token_num` layouts). Used by DSpark on NPU and covered by unit tests on CPU. - **Device dispatch** (`dspark_accept.py`): `_accept_sampling_core` now routes through `inputs_on_cuda(candidates)` — triton kernel on CUDA (unchanged), torch fallback elsewhere (NPU/CPU). Also routed the `@triton.jit` helper kernels in this module through the compat shim. - **NPU verify fix** (`dflash_worker_v2.py`): `skip_attn_backend_init` is now `None if _is_npu else True`. The CUDA `prepare_for_verify` pre-plans (load_batch / init_forward_metadata); the NPU branch deliberately leaves planning to the forward path, so marking metadata ready here crashed the NPU graph runner (`raw_num_token` never initialized). - **NPU greedy verify alignment** (`dflash_worker_v2.py`): on NPU, skip the selector full-vocab sampling verify (`_selector_sampling_accept` and the chain-sampling branch) and take the argmax greedy verify instead, matching what EAGLE/first-gen DFLASH already do unconditionally on NPU. The full-vocab path scatters a dense [bs, gamma, vocab] buffer whose cost does not shrink with the verify window; on the 200K-vocab Qwen3.8 it dominates the step. CUDA behavior unchanged. - **Docs**: Qwen3.8-27B cookbook — DFlash2 drafter recipe and NPU support status. ## Tests - New unit tests (`test/registered/unit/spec/test_chain_speculative_sampling.py`, registered in `base-a-test-cpu`): analytic accept/reject/bonus cases, NaN handling, batch independence, statistical losslessness (20k samples, TV < 0.02), triton-compat helpers, and a CUDA parity check that runs the torch and triton kernels on identical buffers (`@skipIf` no CUDA). - Verified end-to-end on Ascend 910C (target `Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B`, draft `z-lab/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2`, tp=2): server starts, DFlash2 selector draft loads, both NPU graph captures succeed (incl. the in-graph sampler RNG), and requests pass, before and after the greedy-verify change. ## Plan status - [x] P0: pure-torch chain speculative-sampling verify + device dispatch + CPU unit tests against the Triton reference - [x] P0.5: guard the triton imports so Triton-free environments import the DFlash modules - [x] P1: validate NPU (aclgraph) capture of the DFlash2 selector draft sampler (done on 910C; `SGLANG_DFLASH_EAGER_DRAFT_SAMPLER=1` remains the escape hatch) - [x] P1: e2e greedy + sampling correctness on Ascend (server starts, requests pass) - [x] P2: performance investigation — moved to a follow-up PR. Profiling (temporary phase-timing instrumentation + torch-profiler traces, run locally and not part of this PR)showed the original suspects (vocab-wide `torch.topk` in the selector, dense chain sampling) are not the bottleneck: the selector top-k costs ~0.04 ms/step and DFLASH matches NEXTN kernel-for-kernel. The decode step is bounded by a shared TP2 per-layer allreduce floor (~43 collectives/step) of the target model verify. Optimization directions (accept-length tuning, verify-prep host-path reduction) will be pursued separately. ## Accuracy Tests Settings follow #23122/#16818 except hardware and models. - hardware: Ascend 910C (tp=2) - target_model: `Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B` (bf16 weights, `--mamba-ssm-dtype bfloat16 --mamba-scheduler-strategy extra_buffer`) - draft_model: `Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2` (`--speculative-num-draft-tokens 8`) - dataset: `gsm8k`, zero-shot, greedy (`temperature=0.0, top_p=1.0, top_k=1`) - max_new_tokens: `2048`; 128 samples per concurrency level - attention_backend: `ascend` ### Baseline accuracy | Concurrency | 1 | 2 | 4 | 8 | 16 | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Accuracy | 0.820 | 0.836 | 0.836 | 0.828 | 0.820 | ### DFLASH accuracy | Concurrency | 1 | 2 | 4 | 8 | 16 | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Accuracy | 0.820 | 0.836 | 0.836 | 0.820 | 0.836 | ### DFLASH acceptance length (block size 8; scheduler log accept len, ### windowed mean per decode-log interval) | Concurrency | 1 | 2 | 4 | 8 | 16 | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Accept len | 5.8 | 5.8 | 5.8 | 5.8 | 5.8 | Accept length is stable across concurrency levels (observed window means 4.85-6.20, batch sizes 1-17); log-reported accept rate ≈ 0.68. ## Benchmarking ### Baseline output tok/s | Concurrency | 1 | 2 | 4 | 8 | 16 | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | tok/s | 32.7 | 60.1 | 109.4 | 177.4 | 259.3 | ### DFLASH output tok/s | Concurrency | 1 | 2 | 4 | 8 | 16 | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | tok/s | 103.6 | 160.3 | 236.5 | 345.2 | 542.2 | ### Speedup (DFLASH / baseline) | Concurrency | 1 | 2 | 4 | 8 | 16 | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Speedup | 3.16 | 2.67 | 2.16 | 1.95 | 2.09 | <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32465960380](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32465960380)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32465960247](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32465960247)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32465960249](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32465960249)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->
signal.author: syd520zy

signal.title: [Bugfix] Hold references to fire-and-forget tasks in disaggregation
signal.text: ## Motivation Five `asyncio.create_task()` calls in `srt/disaggregation` throw the returned task away. The event loop only keeps a **weak** reference to a running task, so one whose sole reference was the `create_task()` expression can be garbage collected before it finishes — [the asyncio docs call this out explicitly](https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-task.html#asyncio.create_task): > Important: Save a reference to the result of this function, to avoid a task disappearing mid-execution. The event loop only keeps weak references to tasks. A task that isn't referenced elsewhere may get garbage collected at any time, even before it's done. `MMEncoder` in `encode_server.py` already handles this correctly — `self.background_tasks` at line 346, used at 1060, 2022 and 2069. This PR applies that same pattern to the classes in the package that miss it. | site | task | what a collection costs | |---|---|---| | `encode_server.py:2929` `DPDispatcher.start` | `_result_listener` | dispatcher stops consuming worker results | | `encode_server.py:2930` | `_worker_watchdog` | dead ranks are never detected | | `encode_server.py:2931` | `_cleanup_stale_mappings` | stale mooncake mappings accumulate | | `common/conn.py:1721` `CommonKVBootstrapServer._run_server` | `_cleanup_expired_entries` | `room_to_dp_rank` grows without bound | | `encode_receiver.py:1668` `MMReceiverBase` | the encode dispatch | the encode never happens; the paired `_recv_mm_data` just times out | The first four are process-lifetime loops, which is the worst case for this bug — nothing else ever holds them. `encode_receiver.py` deserves a note: the code creates the encode task and then awaits `_recv_mm_data` on a socket, so the task is awaited *indirectly*, never through the task object. A local binding would only cover the happy path — if `wait_for` raises `TimeoutError` the frame unwinds while the encode may still be in flight — so this uses the same instance-level set as the rest. ## Modifications - `DPDispatcher`: add `self.background_tasks`, register the three loops from `start()`. - `CommonKVBootstrapServer`: add `self._background_tasks`, register the cleanup loop. - `MMReceiverBase`: add `self._background_tasks`, register the encode dispatch. Each uses `set.discard` in the done callback so a double-callback can't raise. No control flow, scheduling order or awaited behaviour changes — the tasks were fire-and-forget before and remain so; they simply can no longer be collected while still running. ## Accuracy Tests Not applicable — no kernel or model forward code is touched. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not applicable. The added work is one `set.add` per task and one `discard` on completion. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the pre-commit config — run with the pinned versions: ```console $ isort --check-only <changed files> # isort 7.0.0 $ black --check <changed files> # black 26.1.0 All done! ✨ 🍰 ✨ 3 files would be left unchanged. $ ruff check --select=F401,F821,UP037 <changed files> # ruff 0.15.1 All checks passed! ``` - [ ] Add unit tests — I did not add one, and would rather say why than leave the box quietly unticked: the failure mode is a garbage-collection race, so a test has to force a GC at a chosen moment and assert a task did *not* vanish, which is flaky by construction. All five call sites also need a live dispatcher / bootstrap server / receiver to reach. Happy to add one if you have a shape in mind. - [x] Update documentation — not applicable. - [ ] Accuracy and speed benchmarks — not applicable, see above. - [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance. Found with an AST scan for `create_task` / `ensure_future` results discarded as bare expression statements; after this change that scan reports zero remaining sites in `srt/disaggregation`. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #31452866731](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31452866731)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31452866525](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31452866525)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [Feature] Add DeepEPv2 (ElasticBuffer) MoE A2A backend
signal.text: > Reland of #29525, which was reverted in #35568. > > The revert was caused by one line in the new e2e test: it registered itself to > `runner_config="deepep-8-gpu-h200"`, a runner config that does not exist. > `run_suite.py` validates every registered test's suite before collecting any > of them, so that single bad name aborted unrelated lanes as well -- the ARM CPU > and NPU suites both failed with `Tests registered to invalid suites`. It is > fixed here in a separate commit on top of a clean revert-of-the-revert, so the > restored change can be diffed against the original merge. Running the tests as > single files never goes through `run_suite.py`, which is why local runs stayed > green; `python3 test/run_suite.py --hw cpu --suite base-b-test-cpu-arm64` > reproduces it in one command and now passes. ## Motivation DeepEP v2's `ElasticBuffer` is an NCCL-symmetric-memory all-to-all engine with a fixed per-rank capacity. Fixed capacity means static communication shapes, which makes the MoE decode path CUDA-graph capturable under any topology — including multi-node, where legacy `low_latency` is not available as a graphable path. This PR adds it as a standalone backend `deepep_v2` alongside `deepep`; only expert-parallel dispatch/combine is replaced. Validated on Hopper (H20, H200) and Blackwell (B200 `sm_100`, B300 `sm_103`). ## Modifications - **`layers/moe/token_dispatcher/deepep_v2.py`** (new): the dispatcher. `--deepep-v2-mode direct|hybrid` selects the ElasticBuffer topology — **not** the legacy `normal/low_latency` split. Layout is chosen per batch by inference phase, not by comm mode: decode uses the expanded layout + masked GEMM (static shapes, graph-capturable, available under `hybrid` too), extend/prefill uses the contiguous layout. Single-shot `dispatch()/combine()` with a strict handle lifecycle; the guards run before the DeepEP import check so the module imports cleanly without DeepEP installed. - **`kernels/ops/moe/ep_moe_kernels.py`**: masked-slab repack kernels. A fixed per-expert worker pool keeps the grid static (graph-safe); top-k weights are folded in-kernel; the scale copy takes the source pack-dim stride, which is what makes Blackwell's packed-UE8M0 (column-major) layout correct alongside Hopper's row-major fp32. - **`layers/moe/moe_runner/deep_gemm.py`**: the FP8 adapter (masked decode / contiguous prefill, consuming DeepEP's 128-aligned psum directly as group offsets). `deep_gemm` is the only supported runner: deepep_v2 dispatches FP8 activations plus scales, and no other a2a backend targets a different runner family either. `--moe-runner-backend` is checked at startup, but the runner is chosen per layer by the quant method and several hard-select Triton regardless, so `MoeRunner` rejects the mismatch too — otherwise such a model would reach the permute registry and die on a bare assert after the weights are loaded. - **`layers/moe/ep_moe/layer.py`**: `get_moe_impl_class` resolves `deepep_v2` to `DeepEPMoE` like every other a2a backend — this is what makes the UE8M0 load-time weight requant apply on Blackwell. - **`server_args.py`, `arg_groups/overrides.py`**: the new flags; `ep_size` and `disable_shared_experts_fusion` are declared through the a2a passes, and the runner is validated against `resolved_view(...)` so a model declaration that restores an unsupported runner fails fast. Boot-time capacity check for the chunked-prefill budget. TBO/SBO and enforced shared-expert fusion are rejected at startup. - **`state_capturer/routed_experts.py`**: classify deepep_v2 as a scattered-a2a backend; otherwise `dp_rank > 0` reads unwritten buffer rows under `--enable-return-routed-experts`. - **No CI/Docker changes**: `sgl-deep-ep==0.1.1` already provides `ElasticBuffer`, so CI can exercise this backend as-is; it stays inert for every other configuration, fails fast when DeepEP is missing, and its unit tests need only Triton. - **Tests**: `test_deepep_v2_masked_slab.py` covers the masked-slab repack round-trip -- bf16/fp8, empty experts, the `max_m` boundary, overflow fail-fast, a production packed-UE8M0 scale, and CUDA-graph capture/replay -- and needs only Triton. `test_routed_experts_scattered_a2a.py` pins the capturer's backend classification. `test_routed_experts_dp_readback.py` is the only multi-GPU one: it runs DP>1 with dummy weights over a single 24-expert layer, because `dp_rank 0` sits at buffer offset 0 and looks correct even when the classification is wrong, so nothing below DP>1 can catch that regression; it also covers legacy `deepep` on the same path. Happy to drop or move any of these if they are not worth the coverage. ## Usage DeepEP v2 needs NCCL symmetric memory, which SGLang turns off by default (`NCCL_CUMEM_ENABLE` is set to `int(enable_symm_mem)` when the variable is unset), so an otherwise correct launch fails with `nccl.cu:104: Communicator does not support symmetric memory!`. Pass `NCCL_CUMEM_ENABLE=1` (used for every benchmark here) or `--enable-symm-mem`, which also works but additionally enables NVLS and a 4 GB symmetric-memory prealloc. `SGLANG_DEEPEP_V2_NUM_MAX_DISPATCH_TOKENS_PER_RANK` is the fixed per-rank buffer capacity. It must cover the per-rank chunk (`--chunked-prefill-size / dp_size` under DP attention), and that chunk must be a multiple of `page_size` — with `page_size=256, dp_size=8` the smallest usable pair is capacity 256 with `--chunked-prefill-size 2048`. Smaller capacity is better for decode; prefill servers size it to their chunk budget and add `--disable-cuda-graph`. No extra install step: the pinned `sgl-deep-ep==0.1.1` ships `ElasticBuffer` (`deep_ep 2.1.0`), so this backend runs on a stock environment. Re-validated on H20 x8 against that wheel with no source build and no code change -- `direct` GSM8K 0.970 / MMLU 0.890, `hybrid` 0.970 / 0.886, three-question gate passing in both modes. Earlier development used a DeepEP source build at `d4f41e4`; the packaged API is a superset of what the dispatcher calls. Multi-node: add `--deepep-v2-mode hybrid --enable-dp-lm-head --nnodes 2 --node-rank {0,1}`. Blackwell with a BF16 `wo_a` checkpoint: `SGLANG_OPT_FP8_WO_A_GEMM=0`. ## Accuracy Tests DeepSeek-V4-Flash-FP8, `--tp 8 --dp 8 --ep 8 --enable-dp-attention`, `deep_gemm`, kv fp8. | | deepep_v2 `direct` | deepep_v2 `hybrid` | deepep | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | H20 x8 — MMLU (500) | 0.888 | 0.890 | 0.888 | | H20 x8 — GSM8K (100) | 0.980 | 0.980 | 0.970 | | B200 x8 — MMLU (500) | 0.886 | 0.884 | — | | B200 x8 — GSM8K (100) | 0.950 | 0.970 | — | MMLU at 500 examples has a ~1.4pp standard error at this accuracy, which is wider than every gap in the table; repeat runs of one configuration spanned 0.884-0.896. These numbers show the absence of a systematic shift against the same-node `deepep` baseline, not a ranking. The three-question gate passes on every configuration above. Unit tests (CI, no DeepEP required): masked-slab repack including a production packed-UE8M0 scale and CUDA-graph capture/replay, handle-lifecycle guards, server-args resolution, capturer classification, plus a DP>1 routed-experts readback e2e. The three-question gate also passes on the multi-node configuration below. Earlier validation on the same dispatch path: needle retrieval across chunk boundaries and 8-way concurrent requests 24/24; prefill/decode disaggregation functional. ## Speed Tests | | deepep_v2 | deepep | delta | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | H20 x8 decode | 4,339 tok/s | 4,379 | -0.9% | | H20 x8 prefill | 22,353 in_tok/s | 21,651 | +3.2% | | B200 x8 decode | 8,429 tok/s | 8,675 | -2.8% | | B200 x8 prefill | 32,447 in_tok/s | 31,533 | +2.9% | Each backend pair was measured back-to-back on the same node, on torch 2.13 / sglang-kernel 0.4.6.post1, with the prefill cells interleaved so drift cannot bias one side. H20 prefill averages 4 samples per cell (sd 95 and 72), B200 prefill 2 per cell (sd 132 and 57); decode is one cell per side. Decode reproduces well across nodes -- deepep_v2 measured 8,385 / 8,403 / 8,429 tok/s on three different B200 nodes -- but the `deepep` side moved more, so the decode delta has landed between -0.9% and -2.8% across runs; read it as "a low single-digit percentage behind" rather than a precise figure. Prefill has been consistently ahead by roughly 3%. Multi-node (2x H20x8, TP16/EP16/DP16, `hybrid`, same protocol): **4,610 tok/s** decode with the masked-GEMM + CUDA-graph path over RDMA — a graphable cross-node decode path legacy `low_latency` does not provide — and **20,688 in_tok/s** prefill (two samples: 20,322 / 21,054). There is no same-fabric deepep baseline for this pair: DeepEP's NVSHMEM data plane does not complete across nodes on this RoCE setup, reproduced with DeepEP's own `test_internode.py` outside SGLang. Reproduction (5 rounds per boot, mean of the last 3; prefill flushes the radix cache before each round): ```bash # common: NCCL_CUMEM_ENABLE=1, SGLANG_DEEPEP_V2_NUM_SMS=20, capacity 1024 # deepep_v2: --moe-a2a-backend deepep_v2 --deepep-v2-mode direct # deepep : --moe-a2a-backend deepep --deepep-mode low_latency|normal --deepep-dispatcher-output-dtype fp8 # (with SGLANG_DEEPEP_NUM_MAX_DISPATCH_TOKENS_PER_RANK=1024) NCCL_CUMEM_ENABLE=1 SGLANG_DEEPEP_V2_NUM_SMS=20 \ SGLANG_DEEPEP_V2_NUM_MAX_DISPATCH_TOKENS_PER_RANK=1024 \ python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model-path $MODEL --trust-remote-code \ --tp-size 8 --dp-size 8 --ep-size 8 --enable-dp-attention --context-length 4096 \ --chunked-prefill-size 8192 --moe-runner-backend deep_gemm --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 \ --host 127.0.0.1 --port 30000 $BACKEND_FLAGS \ --mem-fraction-static 0.70 --cuda-graph-max-bs 128 # decode # --mem-fraction-static 0.80 --disable-cuda-graph --disable-piecewise-cuda-graph # prefill # decode python3 -m sglang.bench_serving --backend sglang --port 30000 --dataset-name random \ --num-prompts 128 --random-input-len 1 --random-output-len 1024 --random-range-ratio 1 --max-concurrency 128 # prefill (curl -s localhost:30000/flush_cache before each round) python3 -m sglang.bench_serving --backend sglang --port 30000 --dataset-name random \ --num-prompts 64 --random-input-len 1024 --random-output-len 1 --random-range-ratio 1 --max-concurrency 16 ``` ## Checklist - [x] Format code with pre-commit. - [x] Add unit tests. - [ ] Update documentation (separate follow-up PR). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmarks (above). - [x] Code style. ### Notes for reviewers - Prerequisites: none beyond the current pins -- `sgl-deep-ep==0.1.1` provides `ElasticBuffer`. NCCL symmetric memory must be on (see Usage). - Follow-ups: TBO/SBO comm-compute overlap (a PoC showed the naive two-phase split cannot overlap because `ElasticBuffer.dispatch` is host-blocking; it needs a `return_recv_hook`-style split in DeepEP), adapters for other MoE runners, documentation. signal.title: Fix replicated (TP1) shared expert being summed by collectives that skip the MoE all-reduce
signal.text: Prevents replicated TP1 shared-expert outputs from being over-counted when the default `moe_a2a_backend=none` path replaces or defers the MoE post-expert reduction. ## Motivation `moe_a2a_backend` selects the MoE communication implementation; it does not enable or disable expert parallelism. `none` is the default non-A2A path, while `ep_size` controls EP separately. On the affected path, CP or DP may replace the MoE-internal all-reduce with a downstream SUM. Routed-expert outputs are per-rank partials and must be summed, but a TP1 shared-expert output is already complete and replicated on every rank. Before this fix, each rank passed `R_r + S` into the downstream SUM: `Σ(R_r + S) = ΣR_r + group_size × S` The correct result is: `ΣR_r + S` The reproduced DeepSeek-V4 configurations were: - `TP8 + CP8 + EP1`, `moe_a2a_backend=none` - `TP8 + DP8 + EP1`, `moe_a2a_backend=none` - `TP8 + CP8 + EP8`, `moe_a2a_backend=none` In the EP1 arms, EP is disabled and the routed MoE is tensor-parallel across eight ranks. In the EP8 arm, the routed MoE uses `moe_ep_size=8` and `moe_tp_size=1`. `CP8` and `DP8` describe the attention parallelism over the same eight-rank group. The invariant is not specific to EP1. A matched EP8 run reproduced the same failure: before the fix, only `31/44` common self-stable lengths matched the non-CP reference with mean `|Δlogprob|=1.964223`; after the fix, all `53/53` matched with mean `|Δlogprob|=0.004218`. The fix does not depend on `ep_size`. Mori does not take the affected CP gather/reduce-scatter path. It uses `forward_deepep`, whose combine returns complete per-token outputs, and adds the replicated shared expert once after combine. Therefore Mori does not exhibit this specific double-count. ## Changes - Hoist the replicated shared expert out of DeepSeek-V4 CP and DP SUM collectives, including eager and TBO paths. - Add it once after the final reduce-scatter. - Apply the same CP and DP handling to the DeepSeek-V2 family and the Laguna DP reduce-scatter path. - Disable deferred MLP all-reduce fusion when the shared expert is replicated. - Add equal-chunk, variable reduce-scatter, empty-rank, and model wiring regression coverage. ## Validation MI355X token-exact checks against matched references: - DeepSeek-V4, `TP8 + CP8 + EP1`, `a2a=none`: `7/53`, mean `|Δlogprob|=2.834` before; `50/53`, `0.086` after. - DeepSeek-V4, `TP8 + DP8 + EP1`, `a2a=none`: `5/53`, `2.864` before; `45/53`, `0.068` after. - DeepSeek-V4, `TP8 + CP8 + EP8`, `a2a=none`: `31/44`, `1.964223` before on common self-stable lengths; `53/53`, `0.004218` after. - GLM-5.1, `TP8 + EP1`, `a2a=none`, deferred all-reduce: `0/53`, `2.591` before; `49/53`, `0.060` after. - `pre-commit` passes and the focused regression suite reports `12 passed`. No routed-expert kernel or A2A dispatcher is changed. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32468761511](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32468761511)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32468761047](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32468761047)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32468761137](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32468761137)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [NPU] Support DSpark compact verify graph and folded verify epilogue
signal.text: ## Motivation DSpark on the Ascend DSV4 backend currently falls back to a uniform verify window or eager-side post-processing for parts of speculative decoding. This leaves two sources of avoidable overhead: 1. the target model verifies the full draft window even when the SPS policy selects a shorter per-request verify length; 2. accept/finalize and hidden/KV commit remain outside the target verify graph. This PR enables the compact DSpark path on NPU, adds token-tiered graph replay for ragged target verify, and folds the eligible verify epilogue into the graph. ## Modifications ### 1. DSpark compact verify on NPU - Build packed/ragged verify windows from per-request verify lengths selected by the DSpark planner. - Add NPU-safe compact row mapping, verify-ID gathering, cache-location handling, and compact-to-strided scatter. - Construct DSV4 SWA, sparse-attention, C4/C128 compressor, position, state, and page-table metadata from the live compact layout. - Preserve eager fallback when the selected attention backend does not support ragged verify graphs. ### 2. Compact target-verify graph - Advertise ragged verify graph support for the DSV4 Ascend backend. - Select target-verify graphs by compact token tier while retaining fixed graph-owned buffers. - Refresh query indptr, sequence lengths, cache/page tables, compressor locations/state, and sparse indices before replay. - Add an NPU-local bucketed-layout cache so the Ascend and DSV4 metadata consumers reuse the same derived layout. - Use the safe last-location Triton path for DSV4 NPU allocation metadata. ### 3. Verify epilogue graph - Add a DSV4 NPU-specific target-verify tail hook that uses the committed/live prefix lengths from DSV4 metadata. - Fold greedy accept/finalize and eligible hidden/KV commit into the compact target-verify graph. - Keep sampling, grammar-constrained decoding, logits adjustments, and other ineligible cases on the existing eager epilogue path. - Keep the adaptation NPU/DSV4-specific so the existing CUDA behavior remains unchanged. ## Accuracy Tests - GPQA-Diamond accuracy: **0.91** with DSpark on Ascend NPU. - The compact path preserves the target-model verification result; it changes the number of draft tokens verified and where graph-safe post-processing executes. ## Speed Tests and Profiling No standalone performance number is included in this PR. The expected gain comes from reducing target-verify tokens according to the SPS-selected compact lengths and removing eligible verify epilogue launches from the host path. ## Validation - Python syntax compilation passed for all Python files changed by this PR. - Added scheduler coverage for exact eager token counts when the backend does not support ragged verify graphs. ## Checklist - [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy). - [ ] Provide speed benchmark results according to [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32468745273](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32468745273)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32468745123](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32468745123)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32468745271](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32468745271)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: fix(encode-server): do not forward None video metadata to the processor
signal.text: ## Motivation `MMEncoder._flatten_and_load_videos` guards the `video_metadata` kwarg with `if video_metadata:`, which tests the list for **emptiness** rather than for content: ```python videos, video_metadata = map(list, zip(*video_processed)) video_processor_kwargs["do_sample_frames"] = False if video_metadata: video_processor_kwargs["video_metadata"] = video_metadata ``` `preprocess_video` returns `(video, None)` whenever its input is not a `VideoDecoderWrapper` — i.e. for video that was already decoded upstream and handed over as frames. The guard then sees `[None]` (or `[None, None, ...]`), finds it truthy, and forwards it. transformers' `make_batched_metadata` converts the value only when it is `None` (synthesizing defaults), or when it is a list whose first element is a `list` or a `dict`. A list holding `None` matches neither branch and is returned unchanged, so the consumer dereferences `None`. Measured against transformers 5.12.1: ``` video_metadata=None -> [VideoMetadata(total_num_frames=4, width=8, height=8, frames_indices=[0, 1, 2, 3], ...)] video_metadata=[None] -> [None] -> .fps raises AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'fps' video_metadata=[{...}] -> [VideoMetadata(..., fps=24.0)] ``` So omitting the kwarg is strictly *better* than forwarding `None`s: transformers then derives `total_num_frames`, `width`, `height` and `frames_indices` from the video itself. ## Modifications - `python/sglang/srt/disaggregation/encode_server.py`: forward `video_metadata` only when every entry is present. The list is positionally parallel to `videos`, so individual entries cannot be dropped without misaligning the rest — hence `all(...)` rather than `any(...)`; a partially-populated list is omitted entirely. - Added `test/registered/unit/multimodal/test_encode_server_video_metadata.py` covering all-`None`, all-real, mixed, and ordering (CPU, no model or GPU required). ## Accuracy Tests Not applicable — no change to model outputs. When metadata is present the behavior is unchanged; when it is absent the processor now receives no kwarg instead of `None` entries. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not applicable — one pass over a list whose length is the number of videos in the request. ## Validation Verified against `lmsysorg/sglang:nightly-dev-cu13-20260818-c0b6474b` by patching the image's own source tree at `/sgl-workspace/sglang` (editable install, so source and binaries match), torch 2.13.0+cu130, transformers 5.12.1. New unit test against the shipped `encode_server.py`: **2 failed, 2 passed** — the failures are exactly `test_all_none_metadata_is_not_forwarded` and `test_mixed_metadata_is_not_forwarded`, while the real-metadata and ordering controls pass. After the fix: **4 passed**. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the Format code with pre-commit. - [x] Add unit tests according to the Run and add unit tests. - [ ] Update documentation according to Write documentations. - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results — not applicable, see above. - [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32196854673](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32196854673)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32196854541](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32196854541)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [Spec][Args] Add --speculative-draft-json-model-override-args to override the draft model config independently of the target's
signal.text: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation SGLang only has a single `--json-model-override-args`, and every place that reads the **draft** (speculative) checkpoint's HF config reuses it. There is no way to tweak only the draft model's config (layer count, rope settings, ...) — the same override also lands on the target model. For speculative setups, where the draft path equals the target path, the two cannot be distinguished at all. This PR adds a draft-only override arg; when it is not passed, behavior is identical to before. ## Modifications - New server arg `--speculative-draft-json-model-override-args` (`ServerArgs.speculative_draft_json_model_override_args`, `NS("spec")`, default `None`). The `None` default is what distinguishes "not passed" from an explicit empty dict, and is the basis of the backward-compatibility guarantee. - New single-entry helper `draft_model_override_args_json(server_args=...)` in `configs/model_config.py`: returns the draft arg when set, otherwise falls back to `json_model_override_args`. Semantics when set are **replace**, not merge. - Docs: new row in the Speculative decoding table of `docs/docs/advanced_features/server_arguments.mdx`. ## Accuracy Tests Not applicable — no kernel or model forward change. With the new arg unset, every draft-side config read resolves to exactly the same value as before (covered by the unit tests below). ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not applicable — arg-resolution / config-construction only, no runtime path change. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. signal.title: [NPU] Add NpuSRTPlatform so current_platform resolves on Ascend
signal.text: ## Motivation The `platforms/` subsystem shipped `PlatformEnum.NPU` and the `npu -> hccl` distributed-backend mapping, but the concrete `platforms/npu.py` module and the corresponding fallback branch in `_resolve_platform` were never landed. On an Ascend 910B / A2 host with `torch_npu` installed and no `SGLANG_PLATFORM` set, `sglang.srt.platforms.current_platform` therefore fell back to the base `SRTPlatform` (device_type='cpu', backend='gloo') even though the full `hardware_backend/npu/` stack (ascend attention, NPUMHATokenToKVPool, NPUGraphRunner, ...) was present in the tree. Related RFC: #20372 ("Introduce hardware plugin system") explicitly calls for `platforms/npu.py`. ## Modifications This change fills that gap in-tree, matching the design intent already visible in `platforms/device_mixin.py` and mirroring `platforms/xpu.py`: ** New `python/sglang/srt/platforms/npu.py` ** (mirrors `platforms/xpu.py`): - `NpuDeviceMixin(DeviceMixin)` overriding the memory / device / seed helpers against `torch.npu.*`, with a lazy `_ensure_torch_npu()` guard so environments that don't have `torch_npu` installed never trigger a hard import at module load time. - `NpuSRTPlatform(NpuDeviceMixin, SRTPlatform)` overriding the NPU-specific policy bits: - `get_default_attention_backend()` ->`"ascend"`, - `get_dispatch_key_name()` -> `"npu"`, - `supports_fp8()` and `support_cuda_graph()` -> True, - `support_piecewise_cuda_graph()` -> False. - `get_torch_distributed_backend_str` is intentionally **not** overridden -- `_DEVICE_TO_DISTRIBUTED_BACKEND` in `device_mixin.py` already maps `"npu" -> "hccl"` (or `"zbal"` when `SGLANG_ZBAL_LOCAL_MEM_SIZE > 0`). - The `get_*_cls` factory methods are left at their base `NotImplementedError` defaults on purpose: in-tree NPU dispatch already flows through `if _is_npu:` guards in `kv_cache_configurator`, `cuda_graph_setup`, etc., and the factories are only consulted for out-of-tree platforms via `current_platform.is_out_of_tree()`. This matches how `CudaSRTPlatform` handles the same set of methods. ** `python/sglang/srt/platforms/__init__.py` **: - Import `NpuSRTPlatform`. - Add `_is_npu_available()`, which checks `hasattr(torch, "npu") and torch.npu.is_available()`. It deliberately does NOT call `sglang.srt.utils.common.is_npu`, because that helper raises when `torch_npu` is importable but no NPU is visible, and a boolean "available" probe must never raise. - Wire a fallback branch in `_resolve_platform` after the XPU branch and before the base fallback, and document the new arm in the discovery-flow docstring. ## Verification Verified on an 8x Ascend 910B2 host (torch 2.10, torch_npu 2.10.0, CANN 9.0.0). With no `SGLANG_PLATFORM` set and no plugin registered: ```python >>> from sglang.srt.platforms import current_platform >>> type(current_platform).__name__ 'NpuSRTPlatform' >>> current_platform.device_type, current_platform.is_npu() ('npu', True) >>> current_platform.get_torch_distributed_backend_str() 'hccl' >>> current_platform.get_default_attention_backend() 'ascend' >>> current_platform.get_device_name(0) 'Ascend910B2' >>> current_platform.get_device_total_memory(0) 65452113920 ``` CUDA / ROCm / XPU / CPU-opt-in fallback paths are unchanged. No existing in-tree file is modified besides platforms/__init__.py, so hardware_backend/npu/* and every is_npu() legacy call site continue to work exactly as before. ## Checklist - Format your code according to the https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/development_guide_using_docker.html#code-formatting-with-pre-commit. - Add unit tests as outlined in the https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/development_guide_using_docker.html#running-unit-tests-adding-to-ci — N/A for a device-registration patch; covered by manual verification above on real 910B2 hardware. - Update documentation as needed, including docstrings or example tutorials. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #31392979514](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31392979514)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31392978004](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31392978004)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [Diffusion] Align MiniMax H3 request RNG with reference
signal.text: ## Summary - use one request-local CPU generator for MiniMax H3 noise - preserve the reference draw order: visual conditions, target video tensor, then target audio rows - precompute condition noise before denoising instead of re-seeding per modality or condition - keep the existing H3-only scope so other diffusion consistency trajectories are unchanged ## Why The previous implementation independently re-seeded video, audio, and condition streams. For T2VA this made the target audio latent diverge immediately; because H3 jointly attends over video and audio rows, video output also drifted. The new contract follows the official Diffusers MiniMax H3 implementation from huggingface/diffusers#14355. ## Validation - focused MiniMax H3 numerical contract: 5 passed on H100 devbox - pre-commit: passed on the exact remote checkout - standard 2-GPU H100 E2E: 1 passed in 176.29s (47.50s generation, 22.5 GiB peak GPU memory) - official GT workflow: [run 31890047128](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31890047128) succeeded - ci-data GT commit: [81ca8f18](https://github.com/sgl-project/ci-data-diffusion/commit/81ca8f18d485df4e4bac9a5a40c5b4666f0fa57f) - NVIDIA PR CI: [run 31890556920](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31890556920) succeeded The GT follow-up is intentionally limited to the affected MiniMax H3 H100 T2VA frames. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32387986025](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32387986025)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32387985835](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32387985835)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32387986295](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32387986295)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->
signal.author: mickqian

signal.title: [multimodal] MiniMax-H3: accept target.width/height as an exact canvas
signal.text: ## Motivation `target.short_edge` names a *policy* size and lets `adapt_shape_v1` choose the canvas. A caller that already knows the geometry it wants — a fixed delivery format, a UI preset — has to work backwards to a nominal short edge plus a ratio string that round to it, and gets no error when the guess is wrong: unknown `target` keys are silently ignored, so a request carrying `width`/`height` is admitted and rendered at whatever the ratio resolved to. (`conditions[i]` and the canonical request both reject unknown keys; `target` is the one place that does not.) Naming both axes is exact, because the ratio *is* the canvas: the resolver's nominal-times-ratio step reproduces it and the nearest-32 rounding is a no-op. So this needs no resolver or stage change — validation rewrites the pair into the `short_edge` + `aspect_ratio` it denotes, and the canonical request keeps its existing three-key projection. A test asserts the resolved shape is identical to the equivalent ratio request (the resolved shape does not carry the ratio string, so nothing downstream can tell them apart). ## Modifications - `request_validation.py`: `_normalize_exact_canvas()` rewrites `target.width`+`height` into `short_edge=min(w, h)` and `aspect_ratio="W:H"`. - refuses a canvas off the 32px grid or over `MINIMAX_H3_MAX_PIXELS` rather than rounding or scaling it — silently changing the requested geometry is worse than refusing it; - refuses naming both spellings, and half a pair; - defers the inclusive 1:4..4:1 range and the grid to `minimax_h3_resolve_spatial_shape` (asks the resolver whether it reproduces the canvas) instead of restating those rules; - keeps the forced-`"auto"` task guard, since the rewrite ends in a concrete ratio; - an exact canvas is exempt from the finite-ratio allowlist: that allowlist constrains *ratio* requests to tested shapes, and a caller naming both axes has already chosen. - `configs/sample/minimax_h3.py`: add `width`/`height` to the `target` projection in `_validate()`, otherwise the offline path drops them before validation sees them. - `test/unit/test_minimax_h3_exact_target_canvas.py`: new, 16 cases (accepted canvas, plan geometry, equivalence with the ratio spelling, the pixel-budget edge, allowlist exemption, fl2va, and each rejection). ## Accuracy Tests No change for existing requests: `width`/`height` absent takes the same path as before. `pytest python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/ -k minimax` → 103 passed. ## Speed Tests and Profiling N/A (request validation only). ## Checklist - signal.title: [multimodal] Fix NVFP4 diffusion models on sm_120 (RTX PRO 6000 / RTX 50xx)
signal.text: ## Motivation NVFP4 diffusion checkpoints cannot be served on sm_120 GPUs (RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell / RTX 50xx). Two independent defects in the shared ModelOpt FP4 path are involved; neither is model-specific. **1. The default FP4 GEMM backend does not exist on sm_120.** `CudaPlatformBase.get_modelopt_flashinfer_fp4_backend()` defaults to `"trtllm"`, and `flashinfer.mm_fp4` rejects it there: ``` ValueError: mm_fp4 does not support backend 'trtllm' with capability 120 ``` so the first quantized linear aborts and no NVFP4 model runs at all. **2. The block-scale layout is chosen by a heuristic whose negative branch is unreachable.** In `ModelOptFp4LinearMethod.process_weights_after_loading()` the `trtllm` branch fetches its own shuffled scale layout and **returns**. Everything still executing below it is therefore a TMA-layout consumer (`cutlass`, `cudnn`, `auto`) — but the layout was instead selected by a module-name test: ```python uses_flux1_scale_layout = not getattr( self.quant_config, "checkpoint_uses_packed_qkv", False ) and getattr(layer, "prefix", "").startswith( ("transformer_blocks.", "single_transformer_blocks.") ) if flashinfer_backend is None or uses_flux1_scale_layout: ``` Any model whose blocks are not named with the FLUX.1 prefixes skips the swizzle and hands the kernel block scales in the wrong layout. This does not raise — it silently produces broken output. ## Modifications - `runtime/platforms/cuda.py`: default the FP4 GEMM backend to `"auto"` on sm_120 (which resolves to flashinfer's sm_12x NVFP4 kernel) and keep `"trtllm"` elsewhere. `SGLANG_DIFFUSION_FLASHINFER_FP4_GEMM_BACKEND` still overrides. Uses the pre-existing `is_sm120()`, so no other capability changes behaviour. - `runtime/layers/quantization/modelopt_quant.py`: apply the 128x4 TMA reshape unconditionally, and delete the unreachable heuristic. This also removes two defensive `getattr()`s and the now-redundant second `_get_fp4_gemm_op()` call. - `test/unit/test_modelopt_fp4_backend.py`: new unit test pinning the default-backend resolution (sm_120 vs other, all explicit env spellings, unknown value falls back to the platform default). ## Accuracy Tests Verified on one RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition (sm_120) with an NVFP4 MiniMax-H3 checkpoint: - before: startup fails on (1); forcing a backend past it renders grey noise, which is (2). - after: output is **bit-identical** (md5 of the produced mp4) to the previously env-forced workaround, with no environment variables set. Same seed, same request, three runs. `python -m pytest python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_modelopt_fp4_backend.py` — 4 passed. ## Speed Tests and Profiling No performance change is expected or measured: the same kernel is selected, and the scale reshape is a one-time weight-load step. Paired single-GPU runs before/after differ by 0.2%, inside this box's run-to-run floor. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). --- sm_120 also needs #35740 (MiniMax-H3 model-side quantized-scale fixes) for a working NVFP4 MiniMax-H3; the two are in different layers and independent, hence separate PRs. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32467781044](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32467781044)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32467780725](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32467780725)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32467780863](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32467780863)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [Bugfix] Reject non-positive prefill request limits
signal.text: ## Motivation Starting an engine with `prefill_max_requests=0` completes model setup, then the first `generate()` call blocks. Current `main` still accepts the value and passes it to the scheduler, where the first request fails the admission check because `0 >= 0`. Fail during argument resolution, before model startup. Fixes https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/23788. ## Modifications Reject non-positive `prefill_max_requests` values in the model-independent `ServerArgs` validation path. The parameterized CPU test covers `0` and `-1`. Valid positive values and the default `None` keep their existing behavior. ## Accuracy Tests Not applicable. This only validates configuration. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not applicable. Valid configurations use the same scheduler path. ## Checklist - [x] Format code. All applicable pre-commit hooks passed on both changed files. - [x] Add unit tests. See the raw test output below. - Documentation: not needed. The existing help already describes `None` as no limit. - Accuracy and speed benchmarks: not applicable. - [x] Follow the SGLang code style. The repository's touched-file pre-commit subset passed. <details> <summary>Red and green logs</summary> The linked issue records the live GPU repro: `generate()` did not return within 60 seconds. On current `upstream/main`, the model-independent argument path still accepted the invalid value: ```text $ TORCHDYNAMO_DISABLE=1 PYTHONPATH=python .venv/bin/python - <<'PY' from sglang.srt.server_args import ServerArgs args = ServerArgs(model_path="dummy", prefill_max_requests=0) print(f"resolution=accepted value={args.prefill_max_requests}") PY resolution=accepted value=0 ``` After the fix: ```text $ TORCHDYNAMO_DISABLE=1 PYTHONPATH=python .venv/bin/python test/registered/unit/server_args/test_server_args.py TestPrepareServerArgs Ran 6 tests in 0.053s OK $ TORCHDYNAMO_DISABLE=1 PYTHONPATH=python .venv/bin/python -c 'from sglang.srt.server_args import ServerArgs; ServerArgs(model_path="dummy", prefill_max_requests=0)' ValueError: --prefill-max-requests must be positive when set. ``` </details> ## Review and Merge Process Maintainer action: review and trigger repository CI. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32467757024](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32467757024)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32467756953](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32467756953)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32467757126](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32467757126)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->
