signal.title: feat(hicache): support Ascend Mamba states with FIA and async IO
signal.text: > This is the `qwen_optimize` counterpart of #32500. The original PR remains targeted at `main`. ## Motivation Qwen3.6 hybrid models require both Full KV and the matching Mamba state when a HiCache prefix is reused on Ascend. PR #32275 introduced the correct Torch-based Ascend host-transfer fallback for these Mamba state sidecars. This PR preserves that fallback and extends the integration in two areas found during Qwen3.6 NPU validation: 1. FIA exposes KV cache buffers as per-layer views, while Ascend HiCache's all-layer exchange path requires the original contiguous allocation. HiCache write-through can otherwise fail or hang when FIA is enabled. 2. The Torch Mamba transfer path materializes the layout before D2H/H2D. A native asynchronous transfer operator can avoid that overhead when the matching `sgl-kernel-npu` capability is installed. This PR therefore supersedes #32275 while preserving its commits and default behavior. ## Modifications ### Ascend Mamba State HiCache IO - Keep the synchronous Torch implementation as the default. - Add an optional runtime mode: ```bash SGLANG_NPU_HICACHE_MAMBA_IO=sync|async ``` - `sync`: existing Torch fallback (default); - `async`: require the native operator and fail fast at startup when it is unavailable. - Support conv and temporal state components, including conv-only models. - Accept physically dense transposed/NEXTN state payloads without requiring a logical contiguous layout. - Check native operator availability in SGLang before selecting the async path. - Keep tensor layout, dtype, pinned-memory, pitch, layer-range, and index validation in the native operator as the single transfer-safety boundary. - Dispatch the native path from the same component-level copy helpers used by the CUDA/ROCm implementation: per-layer PF->LF for Host-to-Device loads and all-layer LF->PF for Device-to-Host backups. Temporal and conv components retain their existing outer-loop structure instead of bypassing it through a monolithic Ascend-only fast path. - Preserve the helpers as `@staticmethod` functions with their original signatures. The H2D native entry consumes the current-layer Device view already passed as `dst`; no full `device_layers` argument or additional IO backend name is introduced. `kernel_ascend` remains the sole Ascend backend, with `sync|async` selecting its implementation. - Keep CUDA/ROCm HiCache paths unchanged. ### FIA + HiCache Compatibility - Retain contiguous all-layer Ascend K/V backing tensors. - Continue exposing per-layer views to FIA so graph capture does not retain the full tensor. - Let HiCache explicitly retrieve the contiguous backing tensors for `kernel_ascend` transfers. - Allocate the backing tensors inside the existing KV-cache memory-saver region so the allocation lifecycle remains unchanged. ### Tests - Add unit coverage for explicit sync/async selection, operator fail-fast, and conv-only states. - Cover component-level async dispatch and preservation of the synchronous Torch fallback. - Cover transposed dense layouts and invalid payload rejection in the native operator tests. - Extend staged write-back dispatch coverage for the Ascend Mamba path. ## Dependency The optional native path uses: - https://github.com/sgl-project/sgl-kernel-npu/pull/626 SGLang remains functional without that PR because `sync` is the default. Explicit `async` mode requires the matching native operator. ## Validation Latest component-level integration update (2026-08-12): - `python -m py_compile` passed for the modified SGLang files. - `git diff --check` passed. - The matching component-level native entries were loaded and exercised by the NPU microbenchmark reported in the kernel PR. - The current Codex environment does not expose an NPU, so the device-dependent unit file was not re-run here; the failure occurs during NPU availability detection before test collection. Earlier NPU unit and end-to-end results are retained below. The subsequent interface cleanup that preserves the static helper signatures passed Python compilation and `git diff --check`. Its current-layer Device-view entry still requires a fresh NPU build/unit/end-to-end run; the performance numbers below were collected before this interface-only cleanup and are not relabelled as a new measurement. - `test_npu_mamba_async_layout.py`: 4/4 passed. - `test_hicache_staged_write_back_dispatch.py`: 13 passed, 1 expected skip. - Native kernel tests: 9/9 passed on NPU. - Python compilation and `git diff --check` passed. Qwen3.6 AIME26 deterministic concurrent HiCache validation: - Round 1: cold build, 10 requests. - Round 2: 10/10 Device/L1 hits. - Round 3 after L1 pressure: all 10 requests hit cache (5 Device + 5 Host in the concurrent run). - Round 2 and Round 3 scores were both 1.0. Prewarmed 20-request, one-token-completion transfer A/B: - Torch fallback mean request latency: 641.15 ms. - Native async mean request latency: 505.01 ms. - Observed request-level speedup: 1.27x. Both variants recorded 20/20 Host/L2 hits. This transfer-heavy workload keeps generation to one token so that the host reload path is a material part of request latency. Repeated full end-to-end serving benchmark: - Five repeats per variant with rotated execution order. - Identical full-workload prewarming before measurement. - 16 prompts, 16K input tokens, 512 output tokens, concurrency 4. - `temperature=0`, fixed L1 capacity 486208, HiCache write-through with ratio 2. Mean results over five repeats: | Variant | Wall time | Mean TTFT | Mean TPOT | Mean E2E | Total TPS | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | | PR baseline | 70.930 s | 5243 ms | 10.948 ms | 10838 ms | 171.52 | | Adapted sync, FIA off | 70.878 s | 5111 ms | 11.144 ms | 10806 ms | 173.51 | | Adapted async, FIA off | 69.722 s | 5042 ms | 10.902 ms | 10612 ms | 175.75 | | FIA on, sync | 71.183 s | 5209 ms | 11.244 ms | 10955 ms | 171.20 | | FIA on, async | 71.836 s | 5384 ms | 10.802 ms | 10905 ms | 169.46 | Paired five-repeat comparisons: - The adapted synchronous path with FIA disabled is effectively neutral versus the clean PR baseline: wall-time difference +0.06%. - With FIA disabled, native async versus sync improves wall time by 1.60%, mean E2E by 1.77%, TTFT by 1.14%, TPOT by 2.14%, and throughput by 1.34%. - FIA is a compatibility path rather than a general performance optimization for this workload. The full FIA+async stack is 1.28% slower in wall time than the clean PR baseline, while TPOT improves by 1.33%. The isolated native operator benchmark is reported in the kernel PR. The gap between the isolated transfer and full serving gains is expected: Mamba state reload is only one part of long-context prefill and decode. ### Follow-up forced Host/L2 validation The five-variant comparison above is retained for completeness. A subsequent FIA-off A/B used stricter Host/L2 controls: - five repeats with alternating `sync -> async` / `async -> sync` order; - 16 prompts, 16K input tokens, 512 output tokens, concurrency 4; - PrefillDelayer disabled; - every measured variant/repeat recorded 16/16 pure Host hits, 261120 cached Host tokens, and zero Device hits. Mean Round-2 Host/L2 results: | Metric | Sync | Native async | Paired async improvement | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | Wall time | 29.868 s | 28.884 s | 3.30% (3.14% median) | | Mean TTFT | 669.44 ms | 589.07 ms | 11.95% (12.94% median) | | Mean TPOT | 12.796 ms | 12.342 ms | 3.56% (3.40% median) | | Mean E2E | 7208.36 ms | 6895.76 ms | 4.34% (3.65% median) | | Output throughput | 274.32 tok/s | 283.72 tok/s | 3.42% (3.24% median) | All five paired wall-time samples favored the native path, with improvements from 2.06% to 5.21%. Because this follow-up removes the PrefillDelayer scheduling confounder and validates every Host/L2 hit, it is the more reliable result for the FIA-off forced-Host-reload path. It does not replace the FIA-on compatibility comparison above. ### Ascend Profile analysis (diagnostic only) A separate single-run Ascend Profile compared the Torch fallback and native path with FIA enabled. It used 16 prompts, 16K input tokens, 512 output tokens, concurrency 4, and verified 16/16 pure Host/L2 hits in the measured round. This run is used for attribution only; profiler overhead and the single sample make it unsuitable as a replacement for the repeated serving results above. - The identifiable Torch fallback materialization path accounted for about 1.884 s of Host API self time (`index_select`, `copy_`, `index_copy_`, and `_to_copy`). - Its state-specific device gather/scatter work was about 598.8 ms, but 93.2% of it overlapped those Host API intervals, so it must not be added again to the 1.884 s. - The native `transfer_state_dim_exchange` path used about 42.9 ms of Host API time. Its H2D and D2H DMA tasks totaled about 18.84 ms. - The timeline observed no overlap between those DMA tasks and model compute (including FIA) in this workload. The Profile therefore attributes the gain primarily to the layout-aware direct copy, which removes the fallback gather, temporary materialization, H2D Tensor creation, and device scatter. `aclrtMemcpy2dAsync` provides stream-ordered nonblocking submission, but this measurement does not claim a compute-overlap gain. Even perfect overlap of all currently visible native DMA would save at most about 18.84 ms, or 0.06% of the 31.64 s profiled async wall time. ## Checklist - [x] Synchronous fallback remains the default. - [x] Existing CUDA/ROCm paths are unchanged. - [x] SGLang checks native operator availability before enabling `async`. - [x] Native operator owns all transfer layout and bounds validation. - [x] Explicit `async` mode fails fast instead of silently changing behavior. - [x] Unit and NPU kernel validation pass. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32464793144](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32464793144)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32464793031](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32464793031)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32464793118](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32464793118)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [AMD] Enable moe_a2a_backend=mori for DeepSeek-V4 prefill context parallelism
signal.text: Enables DeepSeek-V4 prefill context parallelism to use Mori for MoE all-to-all. ## Motivation DeepSeek-V4 prefill context parallelism rejected `moe_a2a_backend=mori`, although Mori already uses the same rank-local EP dispatch/combine path as DeepEP. ## Changes - Add `mori` to the DeepSeek-V4 CP validation whitelist. - Add `is_mori()` to the matching model-side backend gate. No dispatcher, collective, or compute kernel is changed. ## Why this is safe DeepSeek-V4 CP fixes `DP=1` and `CP=TP`; Mori resolution also fixes `EP=TP`. Each rank sends its local CP token shard through `forward_deepep`, and Mori combine returns complete outputs in source-rank order. The Mori path does not run the CP gather/reduce-scatter used by `a2a=none`, so its replicated shared expert is added once and is not affected by [#35535](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/35535). Short batches that cannot be CP-split fall back to replicated prefill, so Mori capacity must still cover `chunked_prefill_size`. ## Validation On 8×MI355X with DeepSeek-V4-Pro-DSpark, TP8/CP8, compared with matched non-CP Mori runs: - Short sweep: `40/40` stable first-token matches, mean top-1 logprob delta `-0.015`. - 4K–16K sweep: `14/14` deterministic lengths matched; one length was self-unstable and one hit the existing CP-v1 GPU fault. - `pre-commit`, syntax checks, and a Mori CP validation smoke test pass. CP+Mori TBO remains disabled. Generic Mori dynamic-capacity limits and the existing CP-v1 one-token-per-rank GPU fault are outside this PR. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32460650488](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32460650488)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32460650102](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32460650102)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32460650220](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32460650220)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: test: pin the int32 page-offset overflow in _page_split_kernel
signal.text: ## Motivation `_page_split_kernel` takes `page_idx` and `sub` from `tl.program_id(0)` (int32) and builds two byte offsets from them: ```python src_base = src_ptr + page_idx * src_stride0 dst_base = dst_ptr + (page_idx * RATIO + sub) * dst_stride0 ``` Both products are int32. Past 2**31 they wrap, and Triton sign-extends the result onto the 64-bit pointer, so the access lands about 2 GiB below the buffer: a silent write into a neighbouring allocation, or an illegal access if that page is unmapped. #34025 reported this and #34027 carries the fix. This adds the regression coverage to go with it, so the offset cannot quietly return to int32 in a later refactor. ## Modifications Adds `test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/test_page_split_int32_offset.py` on `base-b-kernel-unit` / `1-gpu-large`. The two offsets wrap at different pool sizes, so each gets its own test: - destination: dst page 57,359, reached once the pool holds 14,340 source pages (3,671,040 tokens/rank) - source: `page_idx` 14,340, at the shipped 149,760 B page stride Both strides are kernel parameters, so each test packs the axis it is not exercising. Only one buffer has to span 2**31 at a time, which holds peak at 4.13 GiB instead of ~8. The source test sets `src_stride0` to 2**27 so the wrap arrives at page 16 and its destination stays a few MB. Each large buffer sits above a canary region in the same allocation. A regression then writes into memory the test owns and trips an assertion, rather than raising an illegal access that would take the CUDA context down for everything else in the process. Masked page skipping, the alignment tail and the persistent-buffer contract are already covered by `TestTouchedPageSplit` in `test_flash_mla_backends.py`, through the production entry point. This file only covers the arithmetic past 2**31. Includes the one-line fix from #34027 so the test passes standalone. I will drop it and rebase if that lands first. ## Accuracy Tests RTX 5070 (SM120), torch 2.9.1+cu128 / triton 3.5.1. Peak 4.13 GiB, nothing retained between tests. - **Reverting the fix fails both tests**, 6 assertions, no illegal access. The canary catches the destination wrap; the source wrap reads canary bytes into the destination, where the signature check catches it. - **Mutation check.** Setting `data_src_off = 0` fails 53 assertions. Source pages carry a per-(page, sub) signature so that class of regression cannot hide behind a uniform fill. - **Boundary arithmetic, checked separately.** Replicating the offset expressions and widening after the multiply puts the int32 wrap at -2,147,446,336 (pid 57,359, destination) and -2,147,408,896 (pid 57,360, source). int64 matches exact arithmetic at every pid. - **Well past the boundary.** A 100,000-page run at the production stride, covering 42,641 wrapping destination programs and 10,660 wrapping source pages, is byte-exact throughout. ## Speed Tests and Profiling At 8,192 pages, where neither variant wraps: int32 4.818 ms, int64 4.797 ms (-0.43%, noise). One widened scalar op against ~37 KB of copy per program. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

signal.title: [MoonEP] Destroy communication buffers on runtime reset
signal.text: ## Motivation Part of #35783. MoonEP communication buffers own NVLink/VMM resources and already expose explicit destruction, but `reset_context()` currently drops the runtime resource store without invoking that cleanup. This draft makes reset/test teardown deterministic for the communication-buffer path already present on the `moonep` branch. This is intentionally the first narrow lifecycle PR. It does not cover the symmetric weight pool from #34874, observability, autotuning, model reload, production graceful shutdown, or GPU/multi-rank teardown validation. ## Modifications - Add a named finalizer registry to runtime `Resources`. - Run finalizers once in LIFO order during `reset_context()`. - Reject duplicate finalizer names. - Continue cleanup after individual failures, install fresh runtime resources, then raise an aggregate error chained from the first failure. - Register `MoonEPBuffer.destroy_all_buffers()` when the process-local MoonEP buffer state is first created. - Add unit coverage for finalizer ordering, uniqueness, failure handling, fresh reset state, and destruction of multiple MoonEP capacity buffers exactly once. ## Accuracy Tests Not applicable. This change does not alter model outputs or the dispatch/combine data path. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not applicable. Cleanup runs only from `reset_context()`; no inference hot path was changed. ## Tests - `test/registered/unit/test_runtime_context.py`: 72 passed, 35 subtests passed. GPU and multi-rank teardown validation has not been run for this draft. ## Checklist - [x] Format code according to the repository pre-commit configuration. - [x] Add focused unit tests. - [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance. - [ ] Documentation update — not applicable to this internal lifecycle seam. - [ ] Accuracy and speed benchmarks — not applicable to reset-only cleanup. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32463957071](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32463957071)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32463956581](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32463956581)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32463956855](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32463956855)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [Bug][kimi-k3] Long-context [PAD] (id 163839) storms + DSPARK inf/nan asserts — NaN-contaminated logits; released kimi-k3 image predates #32477; pad not stopped/filtered; allowed_special="all" makes [PAD] injectable
signal.text: ## Summary Serving **Kimi-K3** on the `kimi-k3` branch with DSPARK speculative decoding, we observe two recurring production failure modes that we believe share one root cause (transient **NaN contamination of logits**, consistent with the write-side bug fixed by #32477 — which is **not in any released `kimi-k3` image**): - **A. Mid-generation `[PAD]` token storms** — the model suddenly starts emitting the pad token (**id 163839**) as literal `[PAD]` text mid-response (in either the think channel or the content channel) and never stops until `max_tokens` or client disconnect. Worst single stream we captured: **17,256 `[PAD]` occurrences, ~2 MB of SSE, 664 s of decode**. - **B. DSPARK CUDA assert crashes** — sporadic full-engine aborts with `probability tensor contains either inf, nan or element < 0` (TensorCompare.cu assert) raised from the DSPARK prefill/draft path, killing all TP ranks (auto-recovers after reload). Both are bursty, correlate with **long contexts (≈90k–237k tokens)**, and are invisible in short-context testing. ## Environment - Branch: `kimi-k3` @ `f37baeb52f` source (image lineage `lmsysorg/sglang:kimi-k3-c6ad1f26-20260729`), SGLang 0.5.16, torch 2.11.0+cu130, CUDA 13.0 - Single node, 8× Blackwell-class GPUs (SM10x), TP=8 - Launch (per the Kimi-K3 cookbook, unified recipe): `--tp-size 8 --context-length 1000000 --disable-custom-all-reduce --enable-symm-mem --reasoning-parser kimi_k3 --tool-call-parser kimi_k3 --speculative-algorithm DSPARK --speculative-draft-model-path <RadixArk/Kimi-K3-DSpark> --speculative-dspark-block-size 7 --enable-linear-replayssm-spec --mamba-full-memory-ratio 0.1 --mem-fraction-static 0.93 --enable-hierarchical-cache --hicache-ratio 6 --hicache-mem-layout page_first --hicache-io-backend kernel --hicache-write-policy write_back --trust-remote-code` - Weights: official MXFP4 checkpoint (`moonshotai/Kimi-K3`), draft `RadixArk/Kimi-K3-DSpark` ## Symptom A in detail — `[PAD]` storms Observed at gateway level over a 48 h window under real agentic traffic (large system prompts, 10–80 tools, 25k–240k-token contexts): **140 storm events in 11 bursts**, hours of complete quiet in between. Channel split: ~70% inside the think channel (`reasoning_content` / thinking deltas), ~30% in visible content. Typical stream shape (chat completions, abridged): ``` data: {"choices":[{"delta":{"reasoning_content":" evaluating the"}}]} data: {"choices":[{"delta":{"reasoning_content":" user's"}}]} data: {"choices":[{"delta":{"reasoning_content":"[PAD]"}}]} data: {"choices":[{"delta":{"reasoning_content":"[PAD][PAD]"}}]} data: {"choices":[{"delta":{"reasoning_content":"[PAD][PAD][PAD][PAD]..."}}]} # unbounded until max_tokens / disconnect ``` During a storm the engine's own decode logs show **`accept len: 1.00, accept rate: 0.00` for hundreds of consecutive DSPARK batches** — the draft model cannot predict the degenerate distribution, so throughput collapses to non-speculative while burning until `max_tokens` (with `max_tokens=128000` agent requests this is expensive). Impact on agent harnesses is severe: the turn produces thinking + garbage and no tool call / no content, the harness re-prompts, the poisoned long context storms again → retry loop, each cycle re-prefilling ~100k+ tokens. ## Symptom B in detail — DSPARK assert ``` /pytorch/aten/src/ATen/native/cuda/TensorCompare.cu:109: _assert_async_cuda_kernel: Assertion `probability tensor contains either `inf`, `nan` or element < 0` failed. ... terminate called after throwing an instance of 'c10::AcceleratorError' ``` Raised under the DSPARK worker prefill path under long-context load; whole TP group dies (SIGQUIT cascade). ~1 event/day/8-GPU node at our traffic. `python/sglang/srt/speculative/dspark_components/dspark_draft.py` already anticipates exactly this ("an all-NaN row would otherwise make multinomial raise"), so NaN reaching sampling is a known-possible state. ## Why we believe these are the same bug — mechanism chain 1. **#32477 describes the write-side defect**: CUDA-graph padding rows carry undefined K/V yet target the reserved padding slot 0; page-table padding points at that page; a partially valid tile loads the page before masking → `0 × NaN` contaminates attention output. That lands NaN in logits *transiently, depending on batch composition* — matching our "mid-response, one bad step, then normal again" signature. 2. **NaN logits in sampling are UB** — `sanitize_nan_logits()`'s own docstring: NaN logits "can come back as **out-of-vocab token ids**". The guard is **default-off** (`SGLANG_SANITIZE_NAN_LOGITS=False`). 3. **`[PAD]` = id 163839 = `vocab_size − 1`** — precisely the boundary index a corrupted argmax/top-k walk lands on. (Related precedent: #32396 fixed NaN mis-selection in the EAGLE fused top-k=1 kernel; the AITER greedy path has a comparable guard for all-NaN rows returning `vocab_size`.) 4. The same NaN reaching DSPARK's `torch.multinomial` produces Symptom B. Two exits, one defect. **Cross-validation from production:** we cherry-picked `ee678910f7` (#32477) onto `f37baeb52f` and rolled it out worker-by-worker today. During the partial-rollout window, **every further storm landed on not-yet-patched workers; patched workers have recorded zero storms so far** (early data, hours; we will update this issue with 48 h A/B numbers against the 140-events/48 h baseline). ## Two aggravating factors independent of the root cause **(a) `[PAD]` is not a stop token and is not filtered.** K3's `generation_config.json` only sets `eos_token_id: 163586`; pad 163839 is not in stop ids, and the serving layer must run `skip_special_tokens=False` (the XTML think markers need to survive detokenization). Net effect: one degenerate sample doesn't self-terminate — it streams literal `[PAD]` text to clients unboundedly. A single mis-sampled token becomes a 128k-token incident. **(b) `allowed_special="all"` makes special tokens injectable from user text.** The checkpoint tokenizer (`tokenization_kimi.py`) encodes with `allowed_special="all"`, so a user message *containing the literal string* `[PAD]` tokenizes to the real pad id 163839 (verified). Untrusted input can therefore seed real special tokens into the context — and because storm output that reaches conversation history is replayed on the next turn, there is also a self-contamination loop (later turns imitate the degenerate pattern). ## Suggested actions 1. **Publish a new `kimi-k3` image containing #32477** (current latest `kimi-k3-c6ad1f26-20260729` predates it; the branch HEAD already has it via the main merges). For long-context K3 + DSPARK this appears to be correctness-critical, not just hygiene. 2. **Treat pad as a hard stop / filter for K3 serving**: add 163839 to default stop ids for `kimi_k3` (or drop pad tokens in the detokenizer even when `skip_special_tokens=False`). Either bounds the blast radius of any future sampling corruption to one token. 3. **Consider defaulting `SGLANG_SANITIZE_NAN_LOGITS=1`** (or at least recommending it in the K3 cookbook) — with the caveat that for a *fully*-NaN row it converts the failure into a uniform-random sample; a cheap boundary-id guard in the sampling kernels (like #32396 did for EAGLE) may be the better structural fix. 4. **Reconsider `allowed_special="all"` for untrusted chat text** (encode user content with special-token strings escaped), keeping structural tokens injectable only by the chat encoder itself. Happy to provide additional stream captures, decode-log excerpts, or run instrumented builds — and we'll report the post-#32477 A/B numbers here either way.

signal.title: [Feat][Multimodal] Add ViT patch-based admission control for multimodal requests
signal.text: ## Motivation **Note**: Given that PR https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/31788 has not yet been merged, this PR incorporates fixes for sequence length. Multimodal requests may contain images with significantly different resolutions and aspect ratios. Limiting only the number of images or the original pixel count is inflexible and does not accurately represent ViT memory consumption. A request containing many small images may be safe, while another request containing only a few large images may cause an NPU out-of-memory error. This PR introduces admission control based on the actual ViT patch count after image resizing and alignment. It allows mixed-resolution requests to be scheduled according to their real visual workload and prevents oversized requests or prefill batches from entering ViT forward. ## Modifications - Compute the raw ViT patch count of each image from `image_grid_thw` after image preprocessing. - Propagate image patch counts from the tokenizer manager to the scheduler. - Add `--max-mm-patch-tokens-per-request` to reject requests whose total visual patch count exceeds the configured per-request limit. - Add `--max-prefill-mm-patch-tokens` to limit the total visual patch count admitted into a single prefill batch. - Keep requests that exceed the current prefill budget in the waiting queue instead of rejecting them. - Leave text-only requests and decode scheduling unchanged. - Add unit tests covering: - Mixed image grids. - PyTorch tensor and NumPy inputs. - Patch-count calculation. - Multimodal-input merging. ## Test ### Test Environment | Item | Configuration | |---|---| | Hardware | Ascend 910B3 / signal.title: fix: skip singleton sampler token sync
signal.text: ## Summary - skip sampler token-ID synchronization when the selected TP sync group has world size one - preserve the existing `ReduceOp.MIN` synchronization for multi-rank groups - add CPU unit coverage for singleton and multi-rank behavior ## Motivation With DP attention, the sampler may select an attention TP group whose world size is one. Grammar sampling currently calls `torch.distributed.all_reduce` directly for that group. Although the collective is an identity, its first use can lazily initialize a singleton NCCL communicator and allocate a large NET shared P2P pool. The group membership is fixed, so skipping a singleton collective cannot suppress a future multi-rank operation. Fixes #35826. Related: #8400 and NVIDIA/nccl#2363. ## Testing ```text PYTHONPATH=python python -m pytest -q test/registered/unit/layers/test_sampler_tp_sync.py 2 passed ``` `pre-commit run --files python/sglang/srt/layers/sampler.py test/registered/unit/layers/test_sampler_tp_sync.py` also passes. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32463145686](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32463145686)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32463145834](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32463145834)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32463145638](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32463145638)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [Quant] SM120: opt-in NVFP4 (W4A4) serving for ModelOpt FP8 column-parallel projections
signal.text: # [Quant] SM120: opt-in NVFP4 (W4A4) serving for ModelOpt FP8 column-parallel projections ## Motivation On SM120 (RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell), bs=1 decode of a ModelOpt `MIXED_PRECISION` checkpoint (NVFP4 MLP + FP8 attention/linear-attention projections) is weight-bandwidth bound: in torch-profiler traces the FP8 projection GEMMs stream their weights at 1.18-1.35 TB/s, i.e. at this card's practical DRAM wall. At the wall, kernel selection cannot buy speed; halving the weight bytes can. This PR adds an **opt-in** that requantizes the FP8 **column-parallel** projections (qkv-style input projections) to NVFP4 at load time and serves them W4A4 through the existing FlashInfer FP4 GEMM path. **No new kernels** — it reuses `fp4_quantize` and the `fp4_gemm` custom op that the checkpoint's NVFP4 layers already use. Why only column-parallel: their inputs come out of layernorm and tolerate the extra quantization error, while converting the row-parallel output projections (which read heavy-tailed attention / linear-attention core outputs) collapses generation quality outright (GSM8K goes to ~0). The `isinstance(layer, ColumnParallelLinear)` gate encodes that boundary. ## Mechanism - Load time (`_maybe_convert_fp8_proj_to_nvfp4`): dequantize the fp8 weight, NVFP4-quantize with per-16 block scales (`weight_scale_2 = amax / (448*6)`), derive the activation global scale from the checkpoint's per-tensor `input_scale` (`input_scale_2 = input_scale / 6`), store `alpha = input_scale_2 * weight_scale_2`. - `apply()`: `fp4_quantize(x)` + `fp4_gemm(...)` — identical code path to the NVFP4 layers, backend autotuned. - Guards: SM120 + FlashInfer FP4 available, per-tensor `input_scale`, N % 128 == 0, K % 64 == 0, (K/16) % 4 == 0. Anything else keeps the FP8 path. - Off by default (`SGLANG_ENABLE_MODELOPT_FP8_PROJ_NVFP4`); accuracy is checkpoint-dependent, gate deployments on an eval. ## Benchmarks RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (SM120), single GPU, 27B hybrid (GDN + full attention) model with a ModelOpt mixed NVFP4/FP8 checkpoint; `bench_serving --dataset-name random --random-input-len 1024 --random-output-len 512 --num-prompts 10 --max-concurrency 1`, seed-paired lanes on the same GPU, this PR's branch. **Plain autoregressive decode (bs=1, fixed 512-token outputs — deterministic length, so the delta is pure speed):** | seed | baseline (FP8 proj) | this PR (NVFP4 proj) | speedup | |---|---|---|---| | 1234 | 66.99 tok/s (TPOT 14.71 ms) | 74.29 tok/s (TPOT 13.26 ms) | +10.9% | | 42 | 67.56 tok/s (TPOT 14.68 ms) | 74.65 tok/s (TPOT 13.26 ms) | +10.5% | **Accuracy (GSM8K, 1319 questions, `sglang.test.run_eval`):** baseline 0.964 vs this PR 0.962 (and 0.965 vs 0.968 in an earlier pre-rebase round) - within run-to-run noise in both directions. ## Limitations - SM120 only: the converted weights use the FlashInfer CUTLASS SM120 FP4 layout. Other Blackwell parts default to a different FP4 backend layout and are not covered here. - Requires per-tensor activation `input_scale` from the checkpoint. - Expert opt-in flag, not a default: whether the column-parallel projections tolerate W4A4 is a property of the checkpoint's calibration; validate with an eval before use. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add benchmarks in this PR description. - [x] Accuracy validated (GSM8K, both lanes). 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

signal.title: [Model Loader] Harden startup weight-load overlap and expand model coverage
signal.text: ## Summary This is the hardening and coverage follow-up to #32017. It keeps startup weight-load overlap opt-in, makes admission/fallback deterministic, and extends the path to hybrid, MoE/EP, and one narrowly validated FP8 model profile. - Replace implicit support checks with a structured admission plan and deterministic rejection report. - Add `--startup-weight-load-mode=auto`: admitted configurations use overlap; rejected configurations preserve serial startup. - Check resolved checkpoint capabilities before capture-safe mutation, so `auto` can fall back for PT or secondary weights without allocating the model twice. - Freeze graph-visible parameter, buffer, and explicitly registered derived-tensor storage across the real-weight commit, then reject stale capture sentinels or storage rebinding. - After graph capture, cooperatively cancel and drain checkpoint prefetch before the real commit. If the bounded drain times out, continue with the conservative commit-reader policy while the cancelled daemon worker exits, without waiting a second time. - Preserve serial post-load semantics for optional parameters that intentionally skip dummy-weight validation. - Report complete overlap phase timings and assign `ModelRunner.weight_load_time` only after the real commit. - Add exact profiles for Qwen hybrid/MoE models and GLM-5.2 FP8. The default remains `serial`. Explicit `overlap` fails during preflight with actionable reasons when unsupported; `auto` logs the same reasons and follows the serial path. ## Supported profiles | Profile | Admitted configuration | | --- | --- | | Native dense | Native `LlamaForCausalLM`, `Qwen2ForCausalLM`, or `Qwen3ForCausalLM`; FP16/BF16; TP1/TP2 | | Qwen3.5-family hybrid VLM | Native `Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration` (including Qwen3.6 dense checkpoints); BF16; TP2/TP4; Triton linear attention; breakable or disabled prefill CUDA graphs | | Qwen3.5 MoE hybrid VLM | Native `Qwen3_5MoeForConditionalGeneration`; BF16; TP2+EP2; Triton MoE and linear attention; standard EP path; breakable or disabled prefill CUDA graphs | | Qwen3 MoE EP | Native `Qwen3MoeForCausalLM`; BF16; TP2+EP2; Triton MoE runner; standard EP path (`moe_a2a_backend=none`) | | GLM-5.2 FP8 | Native `GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM` with the GLM-5.2 fingerprint; serialized dynamic E4M3 FP8 with 128x128 blocks; BF16 execution/KV cache; Hopper SM90; TP8/TP16 with EP1; DSA with FA3 prefill/decode; Triton FP8 GEMM and MoE; prefill graphs disabled; shared-expert fusion off | The GLM profile is keyed to the native GLM-5.2 IndexShare fingerprint (default `cli_factor`, no custom `index_topk_pattern`, `index_topk_freq=4`, and `index_skip_topk_offset=3`), not merely the architecture name. Other quantized/repacked-weight paths, speculative decoding, LoRA/offload, and parallel/backend combinations outside the rows above remain rejected. `auto` sends them through serial startup. The end-to-end GLM validation below covers TP16; TP8 is an admitted profile, not a performance result in this PR. ## Design details `StartupWeightLoadAdmission` separates side-effect-free config preflight from native model-class resolution. Cheap rules run first; implementation resolution/import only happens for a viable candidate. Checkpoint format and secondary weights are checked after source resolution but before sentinel initialization, which gives `auto` a final safe serial-fallback boundary. `ModelStorageManifest` records tensor identity, pointer, shape, stride, dtype, device, and storage offset after dummy post-load preparation. Finalization proves that real loading refreshed the same graph-visible storage. Models can enumerate derived tensors through a per-module hook without a recursive attribute scan; the GLM/DeepSeek path uses this for MLA-derived weights and scales. Checkpoint staging remains best-effort. After graph capture, the manager cooperatively stops and joins the worker before starting normal multithreaded commit. If the bounded stop times out, the handle remains active and the loader preserves its conservative concurrency policy. Worker failure, intentional cancellation, and full-file completion remain distinguishable, and no filesystem/path-specific policy is used. Real-weight commit failures after capture-safe preparation are terminal startup failures. `auto` intentionally does not retry serial loading after model mutation or graph capture. ## H100 validation ### Controlled Qwen3.6 startup benchmark `Qwen/Qwen3.6-27B@6a9e13bd6fc8f0983b9b99948120bc37f49c13e9`, BF16, TP2, FA3, Triton GDN/linear attention, prefill CUDA graph disabled, decode FullCG, local NVMe. Three interleaved trials per mode were run after separate JIT warmup. Before every trial, checkpoint pages were evicted with `POSIX_FADV_DONTNEED` and verified with `mincore` to have zero resident bytes. | Metric (median) | Serial | Overlap | Change | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | Process ready | 50.193 s | 46.122 s | **-8.11% / 1.088x** | | Scheduler startup | 30.03 s | 26.30 s | -12.4% | | `load_weight` | 11.66 s | 7.50 s | -35.7% | Every overlap trial exercised the active handoff rather than an already-complete prefetch: capture ended with only 8-9 of 15 shards fully staged, the worker stopped in about 3.8 s, and multithreaded commit then resumed. There were no fallback, timeout, manifest, or sentinel errors. The server requested decode graph BS 256, but the hybrid Mamba-state capacity resolved the maximum running/captured BS to 39. The actual capture shapes were `[1, 2, 4, 8, 12, 16, 24, 32, 39]`; this resolved limit was identical in both modes. Across all six startups, two fixed prompts produced bit-identical text, token IDs, input/output logprobs, and top-logprobs. The timing is an end-to-end `serial` versus `overlap` mode comparison; coordinated checkpoint staging and its handoff are part of the overlap path, not a claim about graph capture in isolation. ### Controlled GLM-5.2 FP8 TP16 startup benchmark `zai-org/GLM-5.2-FP8@ba978f7d347eaf65d22f1a86833408afdb953541`, BF16 execution/KV cache, TP16 on 16 H100s, DSA with FA3 prefill/decode, sgl-kernel top-k, DeepGEMM paged MQA, Triton FP8 GEMM/MoE, prefill CUDA graph disabled, decode FullCG up to BS 64, local NVMe. A serial pilot established the compilation-cache baseline. The overlap pilot, all six interleaved measured trials, and `auto` validation then started from cold checkpoint pages; across those eight cold-controlled arms, the maximum observed resident fraction was `2.71e-8`, and compilation-cache membership and size stayed unchanged. | Metric | Serial | Overlap | Change | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | Process ready (median) | 135.482 s | 125.709 s | **-7.21% / 1.078x** | | Process ready (mean) | 135.564 s | 125.464 s | -7.45% | | Cross-trial CV | 0.086% | 0.280% | — | The three paired speedups were `1.0777x`, `1.0777x`, and `1.0861x`. All five overlap-enabled starts (overlap pilot, three measured trials, and `auto`) exercised active prefetch drain on every rank, for 80 rank-level drain records total, before normal multithreaded commit resumed. There were no fallback, prefetch-timeout, storage-manifest, or sentinel-validation errors. The two pilots, six measured starts, and `auto` validation all served successfully and produced matching text, token IDs, and input/output logprobs for the fixed single and batched probes. The recorded cross-node coordination-window upper bounds ranged from 1.18 to 2.39 ms across all nine starts. ### Coverage and correctness probes - `Qwen/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B`, BF16, TP2+EP2, FA3, Triton MoE/linear attention: text, image, batched, and prefix-branching requests matched across `serial`, `overlap`, and `auto`. - `Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507`, BF16, TP2+EP2, FA3, Triton MoE: multi-route batched and prefix-branching requests matched exactly across startup modes. These additional probes establish model/topology correctness coverage; the controlled Qwen3.6 and GLM-5.2 experiments above are the performance results. ## Tests - Final focused startup/prefetch suite on the GPU development image: `84 passed, 98 subtests passed`. - Unit coverage includes deterministic admission/rejection, `auto` fallback boundaries, timing ownership, storage/sentinel validation, derived-tensor refresh, optional single/both-scale post-load behavior, prefetch EOF/cancel/crash races, bounded drain/timeout, and loader dispatch after handoff. - The registered one-GPU parity test compares both `overlap` and `auto` with default serial startup. - `black --check`, `isort --check-only`, `ruff check --select F401,F821,UP037`, `codespell`, `py_compile`, and `git diff --check` pass on the changed files. ## Follow-up This PR intentionally leaves `serial` as the default. Follow-up work can add separately validated DeepSeek V4 Flash and Kimi Linear/K3 profiles; define a two-phase, capture-stable contract for quantization methods that repack or replace weight storage; broaden backend/topology and storage evidence; isolate graph overlap with a serial-plus-coordinated-prefetch benchmark arm; and then consider making automatic overlap selection the default. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32357825842](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32357825842)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32357825733](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32357825733)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32357825862](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32357825862)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [MiniMax-M3-MXFP8] Fuse the ~20-kernel decode elementwise/fill/copy small-op tail
signal.text: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation On MiniMax-M3-MXFP8 (TP4/EP1, MI355X/gfx950) a long tail of elementwise/fill/copy kernels is 17.5% of decode compute (5.11 ms/step), ~1150 launches/step over 57 sparse layers, and is launch- and overhead-bound, which makes it the largest single decode kernel lever. The task is to shrink that tail: fewer launches per decode step, at no cost to model output. Most of those kernels do no useful work. One divides every K/V value by exactly 1.0. One clamps expert ids into a range they are already inside. One zeroes a buffer that the next GEMM overwrites in full. signal.title: [Tracking] Host allocator: page-aligned allocation with host-side bookkeeping
signal.text: ## Motivation The KV allocator keeps its source of truth on device. Freeing KV therefore reads device state back -- `torch.unique(free_index // page_size)` with a data-dependent output shape, and on the SWA side the `full_to_swa_index_mapping` gather plus its `> 0` liveness filter -- each forcing a stream synchronization on the scheduler's stream. Under the overlap scheduler these syncs queue behind the WAR barrier, so the CPU parks until the in-flight forward drains. On workloads where requests finish every step (e.g. PD decode), this is a measurable throughput loss. None of that information needs a device read: it is host-known at allocation time. Target design (validated end-to-end by the #31335 spike): - Allocation is planned host-side in whole pages; each request tracks a page-ceiled allocated extent (`req.kv.kv_allocated_len`) with a single writer. - `free()` receives whole pages by construction -- no dedup, no liveness filter, no data-dependent shapes. `torch.unique` survives only behind a legacy API for truly scattered index sets. - Device tables (`req_to_token`, `full_to_swa_index_mapping`, `free_pages`) become write-only projections consumed by kernels; the scheduler never reads them back. ## Prior work **Landed** - #29427 / #29429 / #29432 -- `req.kv` container: owned-KV lifecycle and bookkeeping coupled to real allocations - #32701 -- free KV pages by segment in the paged allocator without a device sync (non-SWA) - #33475 / #34067 -- free-group batching and aliasing fix (hardening the deferred-free machinery the sync-free path relies on) - #35265 -- page-align the DFLASH decode KV reservation (toward the invariant: every writer keeps `kv_allocated_len` page-aligned) - #35286 -- assert the page-aligned SWA evict floor at PD decode prealloc (I2: SWA liveness boundary invariant) - #35382 -- share the page-aligned decode alloc lens between EAGLE and DFLASH (dedup; the watermark loop becomes the single writer of kv_allocated_len) **Closed** - #31335 (with CI companion #31194) -- the original spike validating the full shape - #25500 -- early PoC: unify page allocation estimation on `kv_allocated_len` - #33907 / #34783 -- SWA free without a device sync via segment liveness contracts; closing in favor of the host-bookkeeping approach (the `swa_alive_from` contract only holds on the chunk-cache path; page-aligned extents remove the need for it) ## In flight - #35396 -- assert the page-aligned SWA evict floor on the second PD decode prealloc path, and drop the fixture that mocked an unaligned tail length - #35401 -- write the `req_to_token` page tail so a row stays valid over every page the allocator handed out; widen the row headroom to `page_size - 1` for every paged config. Prerequisite for page-ceiling `kv_allocated_len`: without it, anything slicing a row by a page-ceiled length reads the previous occupant's indices - #35592 -- decide SWA slot liveness on the host and drop the `> 0` filter in `free_swa`. Callers now declare whether a range's SWA peers are still live, from state they already keep (`node.swa_tombstone`, `req.kv.swa_evicted_seqlen`, the unified tree's `cd.value is None`); `free_full` completes the pool-specific pair so `free(x) == free_full(x) + free_swa(x)` holds for every allocator. Stacked on #35773 this makes the per-decode-step window eviction (`free_swa_out_of_window_slots`) sync-free outright at `page_size == 1`; measured on its own it moves nothing, because the mapping clear syncs independently of the filter. Paged configs still hit the `torch.unique` in `_expand_to_full_pages`, which needs the page-representative read to go with it -- blocked only by HiCache LOAD_BACK, which re-pairs a page-aligned full chunk with an arbitrarily offset SWA chunk - #35773 -- clear `full_to_swa_index_mapping` with `index_fill_` instead of a scalar assignment. The `= 0` form takes the zero from host memory, so the write is a blocking H2D copy ordered behind everything already queued on the stream -- a second sync in the same free path, independent of the `> 0` filter. Four call sites: `free_swa`, the PD decode prealloc path (`alloc_extend_swa_tail`), and tombstone recovery in both the legacy and the unified tree

signal.title: fix(sgl-model-gateway): parse prefilled Qwen3 reasoning
signal.text: ## Motivation Fixes #35148. When `qwen3` reasoning parsing is configured only in `sgl-model-gateway`, Qwen3.8 responses can contain a prefilled reasoning segment from the chat template. signal.title: [AMD] fix(rocm): support flydsl 0.3.0 in the FlyDSL fused norm kernel
signal.text: ## Summary `jit-kernel-unit-test-amd` fails on both ROCm 7.0 and ROCm 7.2 in AMD AITER Scout: ``` > from flydsl.expr import arith, buffer_ops, const_expr, range_constexpr E ImportError: cannot import name 'buffer_ops' from 'flydsl.expr' python/sglang/kernels/ops/diffusion/flydsl/fused_residual_norm.py:29 ``` The Scout installs AITER `main` instead of the Dockerfile pin, and [ROCm/aiter#4431](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/4431) bumped AITER's flydsl pin from 0.2.4 to 0.3.0. flydsl 0.3.0 removed `flydsl/expr/buffer_ops.py`, pushing the buffer-resource layer down to its consumers. AITER vendored its own copy in [ROCm/aiter#4402](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/4402) before making that bump; this kernel was never migrated. Fall back to AITER's copy, which exposes the same API. On flydsl 0.2.4 the original import still wins, so the currently pinned stack is untouched and `aiter` is not imported. Today this is CI-only, since `multimodal_gen/runtime/layers/layernorm.py` already catches `ImportError` and falls back to the native path. It will break regular PR CI as soon as `AITER_COMMIT_DEFAULT` moves past the flydsl bump. ## Test plan Run on MI300X with the ROCm 7.2 CI image: - [x] flydsl 0.2.4 + AITER `d9e5ef7ce` (the current pin): 8/8 pass, `buffer_ops` resolves to `flydsl.expr.buffer_ops`, `aiter` not imported - [x] flydsl 0.3.0 (what the Scout installs): 8/8 pass via AITER's copy - [x] Full `jit-kernel-unit-test-amd` suite: this was the only failing file of 28 before the change, clean after - [x] isort / black / ruff Made with [Cursor](https://cursor.com) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:no_entry_sign: [Run #32458854166](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32458854166)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32458853757](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32458853757)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:no_entry_sign: [Run #32458854269](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32458854269)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [Intel][XPU] Add NUMA node binding support for Intel XPU
signal.text: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation `numa_utils` (the `SGLANG_NUMA_BIND_V2` launcher path that binds each GPU worker's CPU/memory to the GPU's local NUMA node) only supported CUDA — it discovered the GPU→NUMA mapping via NVML. Intel XPU has no NVML, so NUMA binding was silently skipped, leaving XPU workers unbound on multi-socket hosts and paying cross-socket memory-access penalties. This extends the existing NUMA-bind-v2 path to Intel XPU so XPU deployments get the same automatic CPU/memory affinity as CUDA. CUDA behavior is unchanged. ## Modifications `python/sglang/srt/utils/numa_utils.py`: - Admit XPU in the availability gate: `_is_numa_available` now checks `(_is_cuda or _is_xpu)`. - Query the GPU→NUMA mapping from **sysfs PCI topology** for XPU (`_query_numa_node_for_xpu` / `_list_xpu_pci_addresses`) instead of NVML — reads `/sys/bus/pci/devices/*/numa_node`, filtering to Intel display controllers (vendor `0x8086`, PCI class `0x03xx`), sorted by BDF to match PyTorch XPU's device order. Runs purely from sysfs in the launcher parent, mirroring why the CUDA path uses NVML there (no XPU-runtime init needed). - Honor `ZE_AFFINITY_MASK` (the XPU analogue of `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES`) so a logical device index maps to the correct physical GPU; falls back to unmasked order for composite/unparseable masks. - Report `ZE_AFFINITY_MASK` (instead of `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES` / NVML index) in the numactl debug string. - All XPU logic is behind `_is_xpu` branches; the CUDA path is untouched. Tests: - New `test/registered/xpu/test_numa_utils_xpu.py` (`register_xpu_ci` + `register_cpu_ci`; mock-based, no XPU hardware required) covering the XPU availability gate, Intel-GPU sysfs filtering/sorting, `ZE_AFFINITY_MASK` logical→physical remap, `numa_node == -1 → []`, out-of-range and no-GPU handling, and `_query_numa_node_for_gpu` delegation to the XPU path. - `test/registered/utils/test_numa_utils.py`: pinned `_is_xpu=False` on the two CUDA/CPU cases that exercise the real `_is_numa_available` / pynvml path, so they stay hermetic when the file runs on an XPU host. Verified on an 8× Intel Arc Pro B60 host: the sysfs enumeration matched `torch.xpu.device_count()`, produced a coherent 4-NUMA-node mapping, and `ZE_AFFINITY_MASK` remapping resolved correctly. NUMA unit tests pass (48 passed, 2 skipped). > **Known assumption:** the sysfs BDF sort is assumed to match PyTorch XPU's device order (the standard Level Zero convention). This could not be cross-checked directly on the test host (torch XPU exposes no PCI BDF, and `sycl-ls`/`xpu-smi` were unavailable), though the resulting NUMA mapping was coherent. ## Accuracy Tests N/A — this only affects launcher-side CPU/memory affinity (process placement), not the kernel or model forward path, so it cannot change model outputs. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not included. NUMA binding is a locality optimization whose benefit is host- and topology-dependent (magnitude scales with cross-socket memory traffic on the specific machine), and it is opt-in via `SGLANG_NUMA_BIND_V2`. With the flag unset, behavior is unchanged; the CUDA path is untouched, so there is no regression risk to the default path. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. signal.title: [Bug] Grammar token sync initializes a singleton NCCL group under DP attention
signal.text: ### Checklist - [x] I searched related issues. This is a focused follow-up to #8400 with a confirmed singleton-group cause. - [x] The behavior is present on current `main`. - [x] A minimal configuration and environment are included below. - [x] This report is in English. ### Describe the bug `Sampler._sync_token_ids_across_tp()` calls `torch.distributed.all_reduce()` directly whenever grammar sampling is active (or `SYNC_TOKEN_IDS_ACROSS_TP=1`). With DP attention enabled, the sampler selects `attn_tp_group`. A valid configuration can have: ```text tp_size=8 attention_dp_size=8 attention_cp_size=1 attention_tp_size = 8 / 8 / 1 = 1 ``` The sampler still submits a token-ID all-reduce to this singleton group. The operation is mathematically an identity, but the first call lazily initializes a one-rank NCCL communicator. On our topology NCCL 2.28.9 allocated a 512 MiB NET shared P2P pool during that initialization: ```text ncclCommInitRankConfig ... rank 0 nranks 1 ... Init START P2P Chunksize set to 524288 transport/net.cc:656 Cuda Alloc Size 536870912 64 coll channels ... 64 p2p channels, 64 p2p channels per peer ncclCommInitRankConfig ... rank 0 nranks 1 ... Init COMPLETE AllReduce ... count 1 ... [nranks=1] ``` When serving-time GPU memory is constrained, communicator initialization fails with: ```text sampler.py::_sync_token_ids_across_tp torch.distributed.all_reduce ncclUnhandledCudaError Failed to CUDA calloc 536870912 bytes ``` This is not a 512 MiB token tensor. The NCCL allocation is `64 channels * 16 shared steps * 512 KiB`. The corresponding NCCL behavior is reported in NVIDIA/nccl#2363. SGLang's `GroupCoordinator.all_reduce()` already returns locally when `world_size == 1`, but this sampler path bypasses `GroupCoordinator` because it needs `ReduceOp.MIN`. ### Reproduction Start a server with DP attention where attention TP size is one: ```bash python -m sglang.launch_server \ --tp-size 8 \ --dp-size 8 \ --enable-dp-attention \ --grammar-backend xgrammar \ ... ``` Then send a request with constrained decoding, for example `response_format.type=json_schema`. Ordinary requests do not take this sampler branch when `SYNC_TOKEN_IDS_ACROSS_TP` is unset. For allocation visibility: ```bash NCCL_DEBUG=INFO NCCL_DEBUG_SUBSYS=INIT,GRAPH,COLL,ALLOC ``` A short JSON-schema request is sufficient to initialize the singleton communicator. It does not require a long prompt or high KV-cache usage. ### Expected behavior Skip token-ID synchronization when the selected sampler sync group has `world_size <= 1`. The communicator membership is fixed, so this cannot suppress a later multi-rank collective; a real multi-rank operation necessarily uses a different process group. The minimal change should preserve the existing `ReduceOp.MIN` behavior for groups with `world_size > 1`. ### Environment - SGLang current `main` (base SHA `26579d893e4a7405fcee43479cd0afbe8291d0af`) - PyTorch 2.11.0 + CUDA 13.0 - NCCL 2.28.9 - 8x NVIDIA B300, single node - `tp_size=8`, `dp_size=8`, `attention_cp_size=1`, DP attention enabled - xgrammar backend; request uses JSON-schema constrained decoding Related history: #8400 reported the same grammar-sampler allocation failure signature. #13947 previously guarded TP synchronization by group size but was later reverted by #16845 as part of a broader sampler change.

signal.title: Extend Qwen3-VL EAGLE3 draft support
signal.text: ## Motivation Extend Qwen3-VL EAGLE3 draft model support to include draft models that ship with `Eagle3LlamaForCausalLM` as their `architectures` field (vLLM-style class name; e.g. [AngelSlim/Qwen3-VL-30B-A3B-Instruct_eagle3](https://huggingface.co/AngelSlim/Qwen3-VL-30B-A3B-Instruct_eagle3) ). The canonical SGLang arch name for these drafts is `LlamaForCausalLMEagle3`, so currently any draft published with the `Eagle3LlamaForCausalLM` alias fails to load because the model registry has no entry for that name. ## Modifications - In `model_config._config_draft_model`, normalize the `Eagle3LlamaForCausalLM` alias to `LlamaForCausalLMEagle3` for draft models. This routes such drafts through the existing `LlamaForCausalLMEagle3` implementation without needing a registry alias or any new draft model code. ## Accuracy Tests Not done. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not done. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. signal.title: fix: manually register kv_b_proj to attn_mha so mla models can round-…
signal.text: ## Motivation address #35702. MLA models now cannot be saved then loaded with `ShardedModelLoader`. The error we get is : ``` File "python/sglang/srt/model_loader/loader.py", line 1796, in load_model param_data = state_dict[key].data ~~~~~~~~~~^^^^^ KeyError: 'model.layers.22.self_attn.attn_mha.kv_b_proj.weight' ``` and the reason is: 1. `DeepseekV2AttentionMLA.__init__` sets `self.attn_mha.kv_b_proj = None` and `forward_prepare` fills it in on first use. Assigning an `nn.Module` goes through `nn.Module.__setattr__`, which **registers `kv_b_proj` as a submodule of `attn_mha`** — so after one forward the same weight appears in `model.state_dict()` under two names sharing one storage. 2. `ShardedStateLoader.save_model` dumps `_filter_subtensors(model.state_dict())`, which dedups tensors sharing storage and keeps the lexicographically smaller key. `...attn_mha.kv_b_proj.weight` sorts before `...kv_b_proj.weight`, so the canonical name is dropped from the checkpoint. 3. On load, `load_model` iterates the checkpoint's keys and indexes a **fresh** model's state dict, which has never forwarded and therefore has no `attn_mha.kv_b_proj` — `KeyError`. ## Modifications We mannually register `kv_b_proj` as attribute of `self.attn_mha` without making it a module. This means, it will not be present in `model.state_dict()` and will not cause the eviction of our beloved `self.kv_b_proj`. ## Accuracy Tests Using DeepSeek-V2-Lite on GH200 node. ``` python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model-path '${model}' \ --trust-remote-code --attention-backend triton \ --host 127.0.0.1 --port ${PORT} python3 -m sglang.test.run_eval --host 127.0.0.1 --port ${PORT} \ --eval-name gsm8k --api completion --num-examples 200 ``` results: ``` Total latency: 21.807 s Score: 0.320 Output throughput: 1987.862 token/s [METRIC] gsm8k_score=0.32 labels={"model": "/iopsstor/scratch/cscs/yboughizane/.cache/huggingface/hub/models--deepseek-ai--DeepSeek-V2-Lite/snapshots/604d5664dddd88a0433dbae533b7fe9472482de0", "eval": "gsm8k"} [METRIC] gsm8k_latency=21.806841063982574 labels={"model": "/iopsstor/scratch/cscs/yboughizane/.cache/huggingface/hub/models--deepseek-ai--DeepSeek-V2-Lite/snapshots/604d5664dddd88a0433dbae533b7fe9472482de0", "eval": "gsm8k"} ``` ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not applicable, this PR does not involve performance-related changes. ## Validation The repro script from #35702 does not fail anymore. ## Checklist - signal.title: [RFC][Refactor] `mem_cache` pool / allocator restructure
signal.text: > **Roadmap v2.** Rewritten against `sglang/main` @ 2026-08-20; the original body is > in this issue's edit history. Hardware backends (`hardware_backend/npu/`, > `hardware_backend/mlx/`) are **out of scope** and are not covered by any item or > guard below. --- ## 1. TL;DR Reorganize `mem_cache/` from "a few catch-all files plus cross-feature pollution" into per-family one-module-per-family packages: - `allocator.py` → `allocator/` package — **done**, keep it closed - `memory_pool_host.py` → `pool_host/` package — **in progress**, 3 items left - `memory_pool.py` + 6 sibling files → `pool/` package — **not started**, and it is the only part of `mem_cache/` still actively getting worse - Untangle DSv4 ↔ HiSparse class misplacement - Naming rule: **remove role affixes that don't differentiate** - Add `mem_cache/README.md` (type × scope) index - Land a CI guard so the layout cannot regress once a target directory exists --- ## 2. Why v2: what changed since the RFC was opened The RFC was opened 2026-05-15. Three months of data: | File | 2026-05-15 | 2026-08-20 | Δ | |---|---|---|---| | `memory_pool.py` | 2257 lines / 11 classes | **5042 lines / 17 classes** | **+123%** | | `memory_pool_host.py` | 2105 lines / 8 classes | **1517 lines / 6 classes** | −28% | The layer that got a target directory shrank. The layer that did not got 2.8k lines and 6 new classes dumped into it: `PageMajorMHATokenToKVPool`, `MHATokenToKVPoolMXFP8`, `MHATokenToKOnlyPool`, `MiniMaxSparseKVPool`, `DSATokenToKVPool`, plus `KVWriteLoc` / `KvBufferDesc`. Two consequences drive v2: 1. **`pool/` moves from last to first.** It is the only remaining catch-all and the only one still growing. 2. **A directory alone is not a rule.** #29678 (2026-07-01) added `multi_ended_allocator.py` (2559 lines, 3 allocator classes) at top level *two months after* `allocator/` existed. Section 8 adds the guard. Additional drift the original body does not reflect: - `unified_cache_components/` was moved to `unified_cache/components/` in 60d6914f1 (2026-07-28), but the `_component` suffix was kept. The naming rule was silently dropped; the tree in the old §3.2 is contradicted by a landed PR. - `NSATokenToKVPool` → `DSATokenToKVPool`; `NSAIndexerPoolHost` → `DSAIndexerPoolHost`. All `nsa` names in the old tree are stale. - `allocator/mamba.py` holds `MambaSlotAllocator`, not `MambaTokenToKVPoolAllocator`. - `allocator/swa.py` gained `PureSWATokenToKVPoolAllocator` — filed correctly, which is the evidence that the rule works once the directory exists. - New, entirely uncovered by the old roadmap: `unified_memory_pool.py` (1691), `multi_ended_allocator.py` (2559), `kv_cache_configurator.py` (2190), `mamba_checkpoint_pool.py`, `index_key_cache.py`, `dsa_cache_layer_split.py`, `mamba_slot_fused.py`, `kv_vmm_backing.py`, `layout/`, `buffer_mode/`, `allocation.py`, `allocation_sizing.py`, `embedding_store.py`. --- ## 3. Rules for every PR under this issue 1. Title must carry the `[mem_cache][N/N]` prefix and state whether it is a **Mechanical Move**. 2. Mechanical Moves must satisfy the `mechanical-refactor-verify` skill. 3. Preserve git blame as far as possible; `git blame -C -C` is the accepted fallback. 4. **No compatibility shims.** Each move updates all importers in the same PR. This is the established precedent — `allocator.py` was deleted outright, not left as a re-export. `memory_pool.py` currently has 98 importers; they get updated, not forwarded. 5. Every PR must shrink the guard allowlist (§8) by exactly the classes it moved. 6. Adequate test coverage, and detailed review — no exceptions for "trivial" moves. --- ## 4. Naming rules 1. **Drop role affixes that do not differentiate.** If every file in a directory shares the role the directory already names, the affix carries no information: `pool_host/mha.py`, not `pool_host/mha_pool_host.py`. Keep `_backend` / `_controller` style only where same-directory siblings have *different* roles. 2. **A family is a module, and a module may be a file or a package.** One file per family is the default; a family over ~1500 lines becomes a package (`pool/deepseek_v4/` already does this, and `pool/mha/` must — see §5). 3. `Allocator` is overloaded and the two meanings must not be merged: - **slot allocator** — a `BaseTokenToKVPoolAllocator` subclass, answers "which slots are free". These belong in `allocator/`. - **host tensor allocator** — `HostTensorAllocator` and its subclasses (`ShmHostTensorAllocator`, `MooncakeHostTensorAllocator`, `UMBPHostTensorAllocator`), answers "give me pinned host memory". These stay in `pool_host/common.py` and `storage/`, and are **not** in scope for `allocator/`. --- ## 5. Target tree ``` mem_cache/ ├── README.md # (type × scope) index │ ├── allocator/ # slot indexing — CLOSED except for the two items in §6.1 │ ├── __init__.py │ ├── base.py # BaseTokenToKVPoolAllocator (abc only) │ ├── token.py # TokenToKVPoolAllocator (page_size=1) │ ├── paged.py # PagedTokenToKVPoolAllocator │ ├── mamba.py # MambaSlotAllocator │ ├── swa.py # SWATokenToKVPoolAllocator │ │ # PureSWATokenToKVPoolAllocator │ ├── hisparse.py # HiSparseTokenToKVPoolAllocator │ │ # DeepSeekV4HiSparseTokenToKVPoolAllocator │ └── multi_ended.py # MultiEndedAllocator │ # UnifiedMambaTokenToKVPoolAllocator │ # UnifiedSWATokenToKVPoolAllocator │ ├── pool/ # device physical storage │ ├── __init__.py │ ├── base.py # KVCache + BaseSWAKVPool + KVWriteLoc + KvBufferDesc │ ├── req_to_token.py # ReqToTokenPool + HybridReqToTokenPool │ ├── mha/ # 6 classes / ~1900 lines → package │ │ ├── __init__.py │ │ ├── base.py # MHATokenToKVPool │ │ ├── noop.py # NoOpMHATokenToKVPool │ │ ├── fp4.py # MHATokenToKVPoolFP4 │ │ ├── mxfp8.py # MHATokenToKVPoolMXFP8 │ │ ├── page_major.py # PageMajorMHATokenToKVPool │ │ └── k_only.py # UnifiedMambaPool + UnifiedMambaSlotAllocator │ │ ├── swa.py # UnifiedSWAKVPool │ │ └── hybrid.py # UnifiedHybridReqToTokenPool + UnifiedHybridLinearKVPool │ └── deepseek_v4/ │ ├── __init__.py │ ├── composite.py # The `_set_kv_buffer_*` helpers stay put: the moved region references none of them, so moving them would only widen the diff. - [ ] [Mechanical Move] `ReqToTokenPool` + `HybridReqToTokenPool` → `pool/req_to_token.py` - [ ] [Mechanical Move] `pool/mha/` package — one PR for `base.py` (`MHATokenToKVPool`, 1112 lines), then one PR per variant group: `noop` + `k_only`, `fp4` + `mxfp8`, `page_major` - [ ] [Mechanical Move] `MLATokenToKVPool` + `MLATokenToKVPoolFP4` → `pool/mla.py` - [ ] [Mechanical Move] `DSATokenToKVPool` + `HiSparseDSATokenToKVPool` → `pool/dsa.py`, delete `hisparse_memory_pool.py` - [ ] [Mechanical Move] `IndexKeyCache` → `pool/dsa.py`, delete `index_key_cache.py` *(same module as its sole owner `DSATokenToKVPool`, which removes the `TYPE_CHECKING` import cycle between the two)* - [ ] [Mechanical Move] `LayerSplitDSATokenToKVPool` + `LayerSplitIndexKeyCache` → `pool/dsa.py`, delete `dsa_cache_layer_split.py` - [ ] [Mechanical Move] `MambaPool` → `pool/mamba.py`; `tree_component.py` → `base.py` — #35644 *(this was missed by #32484, which moved the directory but kept the suffixes)* ### 6.5 Documentation and guard - [x] `mem_cache/README.md` — layer map, placement-by-base-class, §4 naming rules, §7 dependency invariants — #35643. Deliberately coarse: a per-class inventory would need updating by every remaining move, and it already has a rot-proof home in §8's shrink-only pins. - [x] `test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_mem_cache_layout_ratchet.py` (§8) — R1 (allocator + pool_host), R2, R3, R4 — #35638 (draft, stacked on #35306) - [ ] `.claude/skills/mem-cache-layout/SKILL.md` + trigger line in `.claude/rules/modify-component-must-read.md` - [ ] enable R1 for the `pool` role once `mem_cache/pool/` exists (first item of §6.3) --- ## 7. Layering and dependency invariants ``` scheduler / model_runner / attention backend │ ▼ ┌──────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ allocation.py │ per-batch allocation policy └──────────────────────────────────────────┘ │ ▼ ┌──────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ hybrid_cache/ │ multi-pool router └──────────────────────────────────────────┘ │ ▼ ┌──────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ allocator/ │ "give me N slots" └──────────────────────────────────────────┘ │ holds a reference to ↓ ▼ ┌────────────────────────┐ ┌──────────────────────────┐ │ pool/ (device, L1) │ ─ hicache ►│ pool_host/ (host, L2) │ └────────────────────────┘ offload └──────────────────────────┘ │ ▼ ┌──────────────────────────┐ │ storage/ (L3) │ └──────────────────────────┘ construction layer (cuts across all of the above, not a tier): kv_cache_configurator.py, kv_cache_builder.py, cache_init_params.py, allocation_sizing.py, kv_cache_dtype.py, kv_vmm_backing.py, hybrid_cache/pool_assembler.py ``` | Module | Cares about | In → Out | |---|---|---| | `allocation.py` | per-batch allocation policy | `batch` → `out_cache_loc` | | `hybrid_cache/` | per-layer routing across pools | `layer_id` → pool | | `allocator/` | which slots are free | `need_size` → `indices` | | `pool/` | physical KV / SSM state layout | `(layer_id, indices) ↔ tensor` | | `pool_host/` | host mirror + H2D/D2H | `device_indices ↔ host_indices` | **Dependency invariants** (machine-checkable, enforced by §8): - `pool/` must not import `allocator/`, `hybrid_cache/`, or `allocation.py`. - `pool_host/` must not import `allocator/` or `hybrid_cache/`. - `allocator/` may import `pool/` (it holds the pool it allocates into); the reverse is forbidden. - Nothing under `pool/`, `pool_host/`, or `allocator/` may import the construction layer. Construction depends on them, never the other way round. The original RFC declared per-layer responsibilities but no dependency direction. Without an enforced direction, the split only relocates files — the layers stop being layers the first time a pool reaches back up into an allocator. --- ## 8. Guard: `test_mem_cache_layout_ratchet.py` A directory is not a rule (see §2). The guard is a ratchet test in `test/registered/unit/mem_cache/`, modelled on the existing `test/registered/unit/test_module_state_ratchet.py` and registered into `base-a-test-cpu`. Four pins, each shrink-only, each covering one way the layout regressed after the restructure was agreed. ### R1 — a class lives where its base class says **Role is decided by base class, never by class name** — `HostTensorAllocator` is named `Allocator` but hands out pinned host memory, not KV slots (§4.3). Because inheritance crosses modules, the test builds a class graph over `mem_cache/` and takes its transitive closure. Class names do collide (three modules define `TreeNode`), so ancestry is unioned across same-named definitions: over-approximating turns a collision into a review conversation, where dropping all but one definition would turn it into a silent miss. | Transitive base | Required home | |---|---| | `BaseTokenToKVPoolAllocator` | `mem_cache/allocator/` | | `HostKVCache` | `mem_cache/pool_host/` | | `KVCache`, `BaseSWAKVPool`, `ReqToTokenPool`, `MambaPool` | `mem_cache/pool/` *(deferred)* | `_LEGACY_HOMES` pins the five classes still misfiled today (3 allocators in `multi_ended_allocator.py`, 2 host pools in `memory_pool_host.py`). **The pool role is enforced only once `mem_cache/pool/` exists.** An error telling someone to file a class into a package nobody has created is a trap, not a rule. R3 covers the device pools in the meantime; when the first `pool/` PR lands, `pool` joins the enforced roles and its 29 classes move from R3's pin into `_LEGACY_HOMES`. ### R2 — no new top-level modules `_TOP_LEVEL_MODULES` freezes the 40 `mem_cache/*.py` files that exist today. A new top-level module must go into a package, or grow the pin in the same PR — which forces the "why is this not in a package?" conversation into review instead of leaving it to be noticed three months later. ### R3 — modules slated for deletion only shrink R1 and R2 both miss the most damaging case: a class appended to a module that already exists. That is exactly how `memory_pool.py` gained `PageMajorMHATokenToKVPool`, `MHATokenToKVPoolMXFP8`, `MHATokenToKOnlyPool`, `MiniMaxSparseKVPool` and `DSATokenToKVPool` after the split was agreed. `_SHRINKING_MODULES` pins the class list of every module §5 marks for deletion. It needs no target package to exist, so it is what stands in for the pool role until R1 takes over. ### R4 — layers don't import upwards Asserts the §7 dependency invariants over the import graph. It passes on `main` today, so it locks in a property the code already has rather than demanding new work. ### Mechanics - Pins hold today's state, so the test is green on landing and never blocks unrelated work. - A violation that is not pinned → fail, with an error naming the correct target file and linking this roadmap. - **Every pin also fails when it rots**: a class that has moved, a module that is gone, a file that no longer exists. This makes every move PR shrink a pin (Rule 5 in §3) and turns the pins into the migration's progress ledger. - Scope is `python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/` only. `hardware_backend/` is explicitly excluded — its NPU/MLX pools and allocators are a separate device axis and are not governed by this issue. Each of the six failure paths (four violations, two rot cases) was verified to fire by injecting the violation into a scratch copy of the tree; a guard nobody has seen go red is not a guard. A skill (`.claude/skills/mem-cache-layout/SKILL.md`) covers the same rules for coding agents, but is *not* the guard: human PRs never read `.claude/skills/`. The ratchet blocks; the skill only teaches. --- ## 9. Resolved design decisions **D1 — `Unified*` shared-arena classes stay cohesive.** `unified_memory_pool.py` and `multi_ended_allocator.py` (both from #29678) are `Unified*` variants of every family, but they are coupled to a shared `UnifiedKVPool` arena rather than to their own families. Folding each into its family file would spread one concern across six files. They keep their cohesion in `pool/unified/` and `allocator/multi_ended.py`, as §5 shows. `pool/unified/` is the one place where the one-module-per-family rule (§4.2) is deliberately overridden by a one-module-per-arena split. **D2 — the construction layer is a follow-up issue, not part of this one.** `kv_cache_configurator.py` (2190) + `kv_cache_builder.py` + `cache_init_params.py` + `allocation_sizing.py` + `kv_cache_dtype.py` + `kv_vmm_backing.py` + `hybrid_cache/pool_assembler.py` (1960) is ~5.5k lines with no home in the tier diagram. §7 recognizes it as a cross-cutting layer; §5 deliberately leaves the files where they are. `mem_cache/build/` gets planned as its own issue **after §6.3 lands** — moving construction and storage in the same window would churn the same importers twice and make every Mechanical Move proof harder to review. **D3 — `IndexKeyCache` goes into `pool/dsa.py`, with no new base class.** Its only two importers are `DSATokenToKVPool` and `LayerSplitIndexKeyCache`, both of which land in `pool/dsa.py`; it holds a `self.pool` back-reference and reads ten pool attributes, so today the two sides only avoid an import cycle via `TYPE_CHECKING` and a string annotation. Same module removes the cycle. Its whole API (`move`, `get_buffer`, `store_quantized`, `cpu_copy`, `load_cpu_copy`, `state_buf_infos`) is the storage contract, and `DSATokenToKVPool` forwards to it one line at a time — it is simply DSA's second device buffer. It is **not** given a `KVCache` base just so the guard can classify it: inventing an abstraction to satisfy a linter is the wrong direction. Rule 2 of §8 covers it instead, by pinning the top-level module list.
