signal.text:
### Checklist - [x] I searched related issues but found no solution (see Related issues section below for adjacent reports). - [x] Reproduces on SGLang `v0.5.12` and `v0.5.12.post1` (current stable release at draft time); `dev` / `nightly-dev` not tested. - [x] Environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are included below. - [x] This is a bug report, not a general question. - [x] Posted in English. ### Summary On 8x NVIDIA B200 (SM100), the `flashinfer_trtllm` MoE runner shows two failure modes across the two MoE checkpoints I tested in SGLang `v0.5.12` and `v0.5.12.post1`: 1. **`nvidia/MiniMax-M2.7-NVFP4`**: the server starts successfully and returns HTTP 200, but generation is deterministic replacement-character-heavy corrupted text at `temperature=0`. This reproduces across the localization sweep below: FP4 GEMM backend, prompt shape, max_tokens, SGLang version, and both TP=8 and TP=1. 2. **`deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash`**: the server crashes at first forward pass with an `AssertionError` at `flashinfer_trtllm.py:686`. For comparison, the launch command shown on the NVIDIA model card for `nvidia/MiniMax-M2.7-NVFP4` uses `--moe-runner-backend flashinfer_cutlass`. On the same hardware, image, weights, and probes, that path produces clean expected output for M2.7-NVFP4, including `"What is 2+2?"` → `"4"` and 0% non-ASCII ratio across all four probes. The M2.7 failure narrows to the `flashinfer_trtllm` MoE runner path; I did not capture a server-side trace pinpointing the specific fused function reached on M2.7. The V4-Flash crash reaches the FP8 fused-experts path at `flashinfer_trtllm.py:686` (`fused_experts_none_to_flashinfer_trtllm_fp8`) per the stack trace below. **Maintainer note:** - **Scope:** I filed this as one issue because both failures occur through the `flashinfer_trtllm` MoE runner module. I have not verified that they share a root cause. I can split into separate issues if triage prefers. - **Terminology:** `flashinfer_trtllm` here refers to FlashInfer's TRT-LLM-derived MoE kernel path used through SGLang dispatch, not standalone TensorRT-LLM. ### Environment | Field | Value | | --- | --- | | Hardware | 8x NVIDIA B200 SXM (SM100) | | Driver | 580.126.09 | | CUDA in container | 13.0.1 (NVCC 13.0.88) | | Image | `lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.12.post1` | | Image digest | `sha256:b9079f568489b6620b580c2658e68e24791f02a212c4de23b8b5d42661de4b11` | | Image label | `ai.sglang.image.tag=lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.12.post1` | | SGLang commit | `5a15cde858ea09b77116212a39356f2fc51b8584` (per image labels) | | SGLang version (in-container) | `0.5.12.post1` | | FlashInfer | `0.6.11.post1` | | PyTorch | `2.11.0+cu130` (wheel built against CUDA 13.0; runs on container CUDA 13.0.1) | | Triton | `3.6.0` | | ModelOpt | `0.44.0` | | Transformers | `5.6.0` | | Python | `3.12` | | HF revision: `nvidia/MiniMax-M2.7-NVFP4` | `e79701cb1f9dce8fe5395b9ed2b20170beebecde` (uploaded 2026-04-24) | | HF revision: `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash` | `6976c7ff1b30a1b2cb7805021b8ba4684041f136` (uploaded 2026-05-06) | Also confirmed with base `lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.12` (the original V4 day-0 build before the `.post1` patch). Both versions exhibit the same failure mode (output reproduces under the base tag; see Cross-version evidence table below for the caveat that I captured `pip freeze` only inside the `.post1` container). This is not a `.post1`-only regression. > Note for maintainers: per FlashInfer release notes, DeepSeek-V4 sparse MLA TRTLLM-GEN kernels (PR flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#3269) landed in FlashInfer `v0.6.12rc1` (2026-05-22), which post-dates the FlashInfer `0.6.11.post1` shipped inside `lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.12.post1`. This may be relevant to Failure Mode 2 (V4-Flash assertion). I have not yet tested with FlashInfer `0.6.12+` and can do so on request.
python3 -m sglang.check_env output (captured inside lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.12.post1 on the test node) ``` ========== == CUDA == ========== CUDA Version 13.0.1 Python: 3.12.3 (main, Mar 23 2026, 19:04:32) [GCC 13.3.0] CUDA available: True GPU 0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7: NVIDIA B200 GPU 0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7 Compute Capability: 10.0 CUDA_HOME: /usr/local/cuda NVCC: Cuda compilation tools, release 13.0, V13.0.88 CUDA Driver Version: 580.126.09 PyTorch: 2.11.0+cu130 sglang: 0.5.12.post1 sglang-kernel: 0.4.2.post2 flashinfer_python: 0.6.11.post1 flashinfer_cubin: 0.6.11.post1 flashinfer_jit_cache: 0.6.11.post1+cu130 triton: 3.6.0 transformers: 5.6.0 torchao: 0.17.0+cu130 numpy: 2.3.5 aiohttp: 3.13.5 fastapi: 0.136.1 huggingface_hub: 1.16.1 interegular: 0.3.3 modelscope: 1.37.1 orjson: 3.11.9 outlines: 0.1.11 packaging: 26.2 psutil: 7.2.2 pydantic: 2.13.4 python-multipart: 0.0.29 pyzmq: 27.1.0 uvicorn: 0.47.0 uvloop: 0.22.1 vllm: Module Not Found xgrammar: 0.2.0 openai: 2.6.1 tiktoken: 0.13.0 anthropic: 0.104.1 litellm: Module Not Found torchcodec: 0.11.1+cu130 NVIDIA Topology: GPU0 GPU1 GPU2 GPU3 GPU4 GPU5 GPU6 GPU7 CPU Affinity NUMA Affinity GPU NUMA ID GPU0 X NV18 NV18 NV18 NV18 NV18 NV18 NV18 0-79 0 N/A GPU1 NV18 X NV18 NV18 NV18 NV18 NV18 NV18 0-79 0 N/A GPU2 NV18 NV18 X NV18 NV18 NV18 NV18 NV18 0-79 0 N/A GPU3 NV18 NV18 NV18 X NV18 NV18 NV18 NV18 0-79 0 N/A GPU4 NV18 NV18 NV18 NV18 X NV18 NV18 NV18 80-159 1 N/A GPU5 NV18 NV18 NV18 NV18 NV18 X NV18 NV18 80-159 1 N/A GPU6 NV18 NV18 NV18 NV18 NV18 NV18 X NV18 80-159 1 N/A GPU7 NV18 NV18 NV18 NV18 NV18 NV18 NV18 X 80-159 1 N/A Hypervisor vendor:: KVM ulimit soft: 1024 ```
### Failure Mode 1: M2.7-NVFP4 produces deterministic mojibake **Reproduction.** Launch: ```bash docker run --rm --gpus all --ipc=host --network=host --shm-size=32g \ --ulimit nofile=1048576:1048576 --ulimit memlock=-1 --ulimit stack=67108864 \ -v /path/to/m27-nvfp4:/models/m27-nvfp4:ro \ -e HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 \ lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.12.post1 \ python3 -m sglang.launch_server \ --model /models/m27-nvfp4 \ --served-model-name nvidia/MiniMax-M2.7-NVFP4 \ --tensor-parallel-size 8 \ --quantization modelopt_fp4 \ --trust-remote-code \ --reasoning-parser minimax-append-think \ --tool-call-parser minimax-m2 \ --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_trtllm \ --fp4-gemm-backend cutlass \ --attention-backend flashinfer \ --host 127.0.0.1 --port 30000 ``` Probe (temperature=0): ```bash curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:30000/v1/chat/completions \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"model":"nvidia/MiniMax-M2.7-NVFP4","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"What is 2+2? Reply with the number only."}],"temperature":0,"max_tokens":64}' \ | python3 -c 'import json,sys; print(repr(json.load(sys.stdin)["choices"][0]["message"]["content"]))' ``` **Expected**: clean answer content. With the `flashinfer_cutlass` MoE path, this probe returns `'... 4'`. **Observed** with `flashinfer_trtllm` MoE: `'�s000,�s,�s�l�l�s�l�l�s�l�n�s�l�s�l�s�l�i�s�l�i�s�l�i�s�l�i�s�l�'`. The output is deterministic across repeated `temperature=0` invocations and has a high non-ASCII/replacement-character ratio. **Localization sweep.** Failure reproduces under every combination I tested across these five axes: | Axis | Variants tested | All mojibake? | | --- | --- | --- | | FP4 GEMM backend | `auto`, `cutlass`, `flashinfer_cutedsl` | yes | | Prompt content / shape | 4 probes (2+2 short, 2+2 long max_tokens, reasoning, chat-shape long-context) | yes | | Prompt max_tokens | 64, 256, 512 | yes | | SGLang version | `v0.5.12`, `v0.5.12.post1` (byte-identical outputs) | yes | | Tensor parallelism | TP=8, TP=1 (single B200) | yes (TP=1 produces denser corruption than TP=8; see following table) | Sample per-probe statistics from the `cutlass` FP4 + `flashinfer_trtllm` MoE configuration at TP=8: | Probe | Probe description | max_tokens | Non-ASCII chars (code points) | Total chars (code points) | Non-ASCII ratio | | --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | | p1 | "What is 2+2?" | 64 | 30 | 71 | 42.25% | | p2 | Same prompt | 256 | 121 | 276 | 43.84% | | p3 | Reasoning ("trains meeting") | 256 | 203 | 279 | 72.76% | | p4 | Chat-shape long-context | 512 | 178 | 791 | 22.50% | Same probes at TP=1 (single B200), same model, same backend flags except `--tensor-parallel-size 1`: | Probe | Non-ASCII ratio (TP=1) | Non-ASCII ratio (TP=8) | | --- | ---: | ---: | | p1 | **88.73%** | 42.25% | | p2 | **96.96%** | 43.84% | | p3 | **96.20%** | 72.76% | | p4 | **75.72%** | 22.50% | TP=1 produces replacement-char-heavy output more densely than TP=8 across every probe. The failure reproduces on a single rank, so TP-distributed expert dispatch and all-to-all are not required to trigger it. This narrows the M2.7 repro to the single-rank `flashinfer_trtllm` runner/kernel path. **Cross-version evidence.** Identical config (`cutlass` FP4 + `flashinfer_trtllm` MoE), same hardware, same probes, only the SGLang image differs: | Image | Image digest | p1 first 200 chars | p2-p4 | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.12.post1` | `sha256:b9079f568489b6620b580c2658e68e24791f02a212c4de23b8b5d42661de4b11` | `�s000,�s,�s�l�l�s�l�l�s�l�n�s�l�s�l�s�l�i�s�l�i...` | replacement-char-heavy | | `lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.12` | `sha256:79d577610f5022e66b5bb618d434b23ab7121fc9f96d5dba3ee046d5eecfd4df` | byte-identical to row above | byte-identical | `v0.5.12.post1` is the post-release patch of the base `v0.5.12` release that introduced day-0 DeepSeek-V4 support. I observe the same output under the base tag; the in-container `pip freeze` was captured only for `.post1`, so I report this as "same output reproduces on base `v0.5.12`" rather than "byte-identical package set." This is not a `.post1`-only regression. **Reference comparison.** "Reference" throughout this draft means the NVIDIA model-card-recommended launch command (`--moe-runner-backend flashinfer_cutlass`); see . Same hardware, same image, same weights, same probes, only swapping `--moe-runner-backend flashinfer_trtllm` (the bug repro) back to `--moe-runner-backend flashinfer_cutlass`: | Probe | Non-ASCII ratio (`flashinfer_cutlass` MoE) | | --- | ---: | | p1 | 0% (cleanly returns "4") | | p2-p4 | 0% (clean prose) | ### Failure Mode 2: V4-Flash crashes at first forward pass Same image, same hardware, weights at `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash`. Launch command: ```bash docker run --rm --gpus all --ipc=host --network=host --shm-size=32g \ --ulimit nofile=1048576:1048576 --ulimit memlock=-1 --ulimit stack=67108864 \ -v /path/to/v4-flash:/models/v4-flash:ro \ -e HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 \ lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.12.post1 \ python3 -m sglang.launch_server \ --model /models/v4-flash \ --served-model-name deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash \ --tensor-parallel-size 8 \ --trust-remote-code \ --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_trtllm \ --attention-backend flashinfer \ --host 127.0.0.1 --port 30000 ``` This launch differs from Failure Mode 1 only in: model path and served-model-name swapped to V4-Flash; M2.7-specific `--reasoning-parser minimax-append-think`, `--tool-call-parser minimax-m2`, and `--quantization modelopt_fp4 --fp4-gemm-backend cutlass` flags dropped. V4-Flash carries its quantization in the model config. The server crashes during initial forward pass: ``` File "/sgl-workspace/sglang/python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/fused_moe_triton/layer.py", line 1062, in forward return self.forward_impl(hidden_states, topk_output) File "/sgl-workspace/sglang/python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/fused_moe_triton/layer.py", line 1072, in forward_impl combine_input = self.run_moe_core( File "/sgl-workspace/sglang/python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/fp8.py", line 1874, in apply return self.runner.run(dispatch_output, quant_info) File "/sgl-workspace/sglang/python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/runner.py", line 100, in run return self.fused_func(dispatch_output, quant_info, self.config) File "/sgl-workspace/sglang/python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/flashinfer_trtllm.py", line 1116, in fused_experts_none_to_flashinfer_trtllm return fused_experts_none_to_flashinfer_trtllm_fp8( File "/sgl-workspace/sglang/python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/flashinfer_trtllm.py", line 686, in fused_experts_none_to_flashinfer_trtllm_fp8 assert TopKOutputChecker.format_is_bypassed(topk_output) AssertionError ``` The same `flashinfer_trtllm.py` module that produces corrupted output on M2.7 fails an explicit format check on V4-Flash. The assertion suggests the FP8 fused path is receiving a `topk_output` format that does not satisfy `TopKOutputChecker.format_is_bypassed(topk_output)`. ### Localization summary The tested failures localize to the **`flashinfer_trtllm` MoE runner path**: - V4-Flash reaches the FP8 fused-experts code at `flashinfer_trtllm.py:686`. - M2.7 returns corrupted text through the same runner path, though I did not capture a trace identifying the exact fused function reached. The M2.7 sweep makes these less likely as primary triggers: - FP4 GEMM backend: varied `auto`, `cutlass`, and `flashinfer_cutedsl`; all reproduced. - Prompt content / shape: four probes reproduced. - Tensor parallelism: reproduced at both TP=8 and TP=1 (TP=1 produces denser corruption than TP=8 across all four probes; the bug is not TP-distribution-specific). - SGLang image: reproduced under both `v0.5.12` and `v0.5.12.post1`. - Weight loading / basic scheduler path: the `flashinfer_cutlass` MoE path on the same image, hardware, weights, and probes produced clean output. ### What this issue does NOT validate Untested axes (all orthogonal; I can run any on request): - FlashInfer `0.6.12rc1` or newer (only `0.6.11.post1` tested, as bundled in `lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.12.post1`). - SGLang `dev` / `nightly-dev` tags. - Different SM (only B200/SM100 tested; H100/H200 not tested). - Different attention backend (only `flashinfer` tested; `fa3`/`fa4`/`trtllm_mha`/`flashmla` not tested). - DeepEP / expert-parallelism enabled. - Speculative decoding enabled. - KV cache dtype other than default. - `--disable-flashinfer-autotune` (per the SGLang cookbook for DeepSeek-V4; not tested here). - Other NVFP4 MoE checkpoints beyond `nvidia/MiniMax-M2.7-NVFP4` and `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash`. - Direct FlashInfer-only repro (I observe the failure through SGLang's dispatch into FlashInfer). ### Repro artifacts Run directories on the test node, by purpose: - M2.7 isolation sweep manifest + per-probe smoke responses (A1 / X1 / TW configs at chat 2K/512 Poisson 4 rps): `track1-prepost-moe-isolation-20260525T180536Z/` - Cross-version probe artifacts (M2.7 on `v0.5.12.post1` + base `v0.5.12`, 4 probes per image, full analysis.txt): `mojibake-probe-20260525T182412Z/` - Localization probe artifacts (V4-Flash full crash log + M2.7 TP=1 single-rank probes): `localization-probes-20260525T184624Z/` - Reference (`flashinfer_cutlass` MoE) baseline + 3-run regimes: `track1-m27-reference-20260525T155755Z/` and `track1-reference-regimes-20260525T044957Z/` - Inside-container `pip freeze` (full 335-line capture from `lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.12.post1`): `env-capture-20260525T191232Z/env.txt` Available inline on request: full V4-Flash traceback, complete `pip freeze`, per-probe response JSONs, M2.7 server logs around the bad-output requests, raw response bytes (hex) for byte-level inspection. I can post a gist with any subset the maintainer wants to inspect. ### Potential next checks - Test whether FlashInfer `0.6.12rc1` or newer changes either failure mode. I can run this if useful. - Open a parallel issue in `flashinfer-ai/flashinfer` if maintainers believe the root cause is upstream of SGLang dispatch. - Consider replacing the V4-Flash assertion with a clearer error or fallback path if this topk format is currently unsupported by the FP8 `flashinfer_trtllm` path. ### Related issues Adjacent reports surfaced during issue search. I did not find an exact duplicate; these appear adjacent on the axes called out per bullet (let triage decide on duplication). None of them include an applicable fix or workaround for the failure modes reported here. Included for triage context in case they share a root cause or a tracking owner. - #19971 — `MiniMax-M2.5 FP8 produces garbage output on B200 with default trtllm gemm backend`. Same hardware (B200), same model family (M2 series), same "garbage output" symptom, different quantization (FP8 vs NVFP4) and different layer (trtllm GEMM vs trtllm MoE). May indicate a pattern in trtllm-derived kernels on B200 for this family. - #18989 (closed) — `[Bug] deepseek 3.2 nvfp4 moe-runner-backend=flashinfer_trtllm illegal memory access`. Same MoE runner, different NVFP4 MoE checkpoint, different failure mode (illegal memory access vs mojibake/assertion). Same kernel family. - #24502 — `[Bug] flashinfer_trtllm MoE runner has no DeepEP fused func registered — blocks EP+NVFP4 on Blackwell`. Same MoE runner, Blackwell-specific structural gap on a different code path. - #20022 — `[Tracking] Minimax-M2.5 (G)B200 Functional Support and Optimizations`. Cross-linking for the M2-family Blackwell tracking owners. Reporter context: independent benchmarking work on Nebius B200 hardware.

signal.title: RFC: Re-layer Draft SWA into Committed Sidecar KV and Verify Scratch
signal.text: ### Checklist - [ ] If this is not a feature request but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed. - [ ] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Summary This RFC proposes splitting draft Sliding Window Attention (SWA) KV in speculative decoding, such as DSV4 DSpark, into two explicitly modeled components: ```text Draft SWA ├── committed sidecar KV: content-scoped and reusable └── verify temporary: step-scoped scratch, never entering cache ``` Today, draft SWA is implicitly managed through the draft worker KV pool and coupled to target KV pool sizing. Its committed and in-flight states are not represented separately. This causes two problems: 1. Committed draft KV lacks explicit cache semantics. 2. Draft SWA memory is estimated as if draft layers had the same average structure as target layers. The proposal introduces: - A content-scoped draft SWA sidecar aligned with the target prefix cache. - Step-scoped scratch for speculative verification. - SWA-only draft memory accounting. - Correct stage-count derivation. - Radix cache, PD, and HiCache integration. - A draft-only compatibility path for `unified_kv`. This proposal does not change model numerics. It changes memory ownership, cache lifecycle, physical layout, and pool sizing. ## 2. Motivation ### 2.1 Memory ownership should follow data semantics Device memory in SGLang can be classified by ownership and lifetime: ```text Model-scoped: model weights and persistent model buffers Content-scoped: committed KV, Mamba checkpoints, compressed pages Request-scoped: active recurrent state and request-local runtime state Step-scoped: verification intermediates, logits, and temporary workspaces ``` The important distinction is: ```text Running / intermediate / in-flight state -> request-scoped or step-scoped Committed / reusable artifact -> content-scoped ``` Draft SWA currently mixes these two categories. ### 2.2 Semantics of committed draft SWA Taking DSV4 DSpark as an example, canonical draft KV is derived from injected target hidden states: ```text target hidden states -> canonical draft KV ``` For an already committed prefix: ```text same prefix + same target/draft weights -> same canonical draft KV ``` Therefore, committed draft SWA is a reusable artifact: ```text committed draft SWA = content-scoped sidecar KV ``` Its lifecycle should follow the committed target prefix rather than the lifetime of a request slot. ### 2.3 Semantics of verify temporary During speculative verification, temporary draft KV may represent tokens that are later rejected. Before acceptance is known, that data is not part of the committed sequence: ```text in-flight draft KV != committed prefix artifact ``` Verify temporary should therefore be: ```text step-scoped scratch ``` It must not become radix-visible, transferable, or reusable until the corresponding tokens have been accepted and canonical committed KV has been produced. ## 3. Problems with the Current Design ### 3.1 Committed draft SWA is not explicitly modeled The problem is not the target KV cache. The problem is that draft SWA is implicitly folded into the existing draft worker pool and target budget logic. There is no independent abstraction expressing: ```text this draft KV belongs to committed prefix content ``` Consequently: 1. Cache ownership is unclear. 2. Committed and speculative data share lifecycle assumptions. 3. Prefix reuse is difficult to express. 4. PD and HiCache integration is indirect. 5. Pool sizing is coupled to target-layer averages. ### 3.2 Draft SWA memory accounting is inaccurate The current DSV4 pool configurator approximately scales the target cost as follows: ```text bytes_per_full_token *= (target_layers + draft_layers) / target_layers ``` This treats each draft layer as one target average layer. However, DSV4 DSpark draft layers are SWA-only: ```text draft layer does not include C4 draft layer does not include C128 draft layer does not include the C4 indexer draft layer does not include C4/C128 compression state ``` Charging a draft layer as a target average layer therefore overestimates draft KV memory and reduces usable target KV capacity. A more accurate semantic term is: ```text draft_swa_committed_bytes_per_full_token = swa_full_tokens_ratio * draft_swa_bytes_per_token * draft_swa_stage_count ``` The physical `draft_swa_bytes_per_token` must come from the active backend layout: ```text paged backend: packed/padded SWA page bytes unified backend: unified row stride and storage dtype ``` Verify scratch is a separate fixed workspace term: ```text draft_swa_scratch_bytes = max_concurrent_requests * verify_scratch_width * scratch_bytes_per_row * draft_swa_stage_count ``` This separates content capacity from fixed speculative workspace. ### 3.3 DSpark stage count is ambiguous A DSpark bundle may expose: ```text num_nextn_predict_layers = 1 dspark_target_layer_ids = [40, 41, 42] ``` Although the model has one logical next-token prediction layer, the runtime captures and injects multiple target stages. The draft SWA sidecar stage count must therefore come from the actual capture/injection stages: ```text draft_swa_stage_count = len(dspark_target_layer_ids) ``` It must not be inferred only from `num_nextn_predict_layers`. ### 3.4 Rejected data can outlive its semantic scope A request-scoped ring may physically retain rejected draft rows until they are overwritten. Physical retention alone is acceptable for scratch, but those rows must never be interpreted as: - Committed KV. - Radix-cache content. - PD-transferable state. - HiCache-offloadable state. The current representation does not make this boundary explicit. ## 4. Relationship to `unified_kv` ### 4.1 Different architectural dimensions This RFC and `unified_kv` address different concerns. `unified_kv` primarily defines an execution-oriented physical layout: ```text request slot -> fixed SWA ring -> position modulo ring size ``` Its strengths include: - Predictable addresses. - Contiguous memory. - Low metadata overhead. - Efficient unified SWA/C4/C128 kernels. - Request-slot-oriented hot-path execution. The draft sidecar proposal defines ownership and cache lifecycle: ```text committed prefix artifact -> content-scoped sidecar in-flight verify state -> step-scoped scratch ``` The distinction is: ```text unified_kv: execution-oriented physical layout draft SWA sidecar: content-oriented ownership and lifecycle ``` ### 4.2 This RFC does not redesign target `unified_kv` The proposal does not convert target unified SWA into a content-addressed layout. The following target structures remain unchanged: ```text target unified SWA ring target C4/C128 layout target compression state target unified attention kernels target request-slot addressing ``` Compatibility is implemented as a draft-only extension. ### 4.3 Draft-only unified layout A compatible draft unified pool can use: ```text [ committed draft SWA rows ][ verify scratch rows ] ``` The draft attention metadata combines two address sources: ```text committed prefix: radix/content mapping -> committed sidecar rows current speculative step: request/step mapping -> scratch rows ``` The buffer can remain contiguous and compatible with a unified attention interface while preserving separate semantic lifecycles. ### 4.4 Transfer semantics under `unified_kv` Target and draft state may use different transfer semantics: ```text target unified SWA: request-scoped SWA_RING state draft committed sidecar: content-scoped SWA page state draft verify scratch: never transferred ``` This preserves the original target unified design while making committed draft SWA independently reusable. ## 5. Proposed Design ### 5.1 Overall structure ```text Draft SWA ├── committed sidecar KV │ ├── content-scoped │ ├── radix-visible │ ├── reusable │ └── transferable └── verify temporary ├── step-scoped ├── allocator-independent ├── radix-invisible └── non-transferable ``` This follows the same principle used by Mamba and compressed KV artifacts: ```text runtime temporary data is not shared only committed artifacts enter the cache ``` ### 5.2 Committed sidecar KV Committed sidecar KV represents canonical draft SWA KV belonging to an accepted prefix. Its properties are: 1. Content-scoped. 2. Determined by prefix content and model weights. 3. Reusable on radix-cache hits. 4. Coupled to target prefix lifecycle. 5. Eligible for PD transfer. 6. Eligible for HiCache offload/loadback. 7. Evicted consistently with the corresponding target prefix. It can be understood as: ```text the draft-side sidecar of the target prefix cache ``` The sidecar may use a separate pool or an additional physical region, but it must have explicit coverage and lifecycle semantics. ### 5.3 Verify temporary Verify temporary contains draft KV and attention inputs needed only by the active speculative step. Its properties are: 1. Step-scoped. 2. Never radix-visible. 3. Excluded from HiCache. 4. Excluded from PD transfer. 5. Excluded from long-lived allocator state. 6. Reusable as workspace after the step. 7. Incapable of producing cache artifacts for rejected tokens. Possible physical representations include: ```text temporary tensor workspace buffer step-local scratch range ``` It must not be treated as a long-lived committed request cache. ### 5.4 Accept-path data flow The numerically safe baseline is: ```text draft proposal / verify -> generate step-local temporary KV -> run verify attention -> compute accept/reject accepted -> derive canonical draft KV from target hidden states -> write canonical KV into committed sidecar -> mark sidecar coverage as committed rejected -> discard temporary KV ``` The invariant is: ```text only canonical, committed draft KV enters the sidecar ``` ### 5.5 Promotion optimization Promotion is valid only when verify temporary already contains the canonical target-hidden-derived KV representation: ```text canonical verify scratch -> select accepted rows -> promote/copy accepted rows into sidecar ``` Proposal KV produced from draft mask/noise hidden states is not necessarily numerically equivalent to canonical committed KV. Therefore: ```text proposal scratch must not be promoted directly ``` The first implementation should prefer direct canonical materialization. Promotion can be introduced later after numerical equivalence is demonstrated. ### 5.6 Prefix-cache-hit behavior When both target and draft sidecar coverage hit: ```text target committed KV hit draft committed sidecar KV hit -> reuse both directly ``` When target KV hits but draft sidecar coverage is missing: ```text target committed KV hit draft sidecar miss -> recompute/backfill draft sidecar ``` For SWA, the fallback should preserve the reusable prefix and recompute only the required trailing window where possible: ```text reuse prefix before trailing SWA window recompute trailing window commit reconstructed sidecar coverage ``` This fallback should be observable and should not become the normal path. ### 5.7 Eviction and consistency Sidecar coverage must never outlive its corresponding target prefix. The required invariant is: ```text valid draft sidecar coverage implies valid corresponding target prefix coverage ``` Insert, split, eviction, backup, and loadback must update sidecar coverage consistently. A stale sidecar must never be paired with a newly allocated target prefix using the same physical slots. ## 6. Backend Layouts ### 6.1 Paged backend The paged layout can use: ```text committed sidecar pages: indexed through content/SWA mapping verify scratch pages: indexed through request slot and step offset ``` Only committed pages are exposed to radix cache, PD, and HiCache. ### 6.2 `unified_kv` backend The target unified layout remains unchanged. The draft unified pool adds: ```text committed content-addressed rows verify scratch rows ``` The draft attention index stream is assembled from: ```text content indices for committed prefix scratch indices for current verify step ``` No target C4/C128 or target ring redesign is required. ### 6.3 Backend-independent semantics Physical layouts may differ, but all backends must satisfy: ```text committed rows: content-scoped and transferable scratch rows: step-scoped and non-transferable ``` Backend-specific row stride, padding, and dtype must be reflected in memory accounting. ## 7. Implementation Plan ### 7.1 Accounting fix Replace target-average-layer scaling with explicit draft SWA terms: ```text committed sidecar bytes per full token fixed verify scratch bytes ``` This step changes pool sizing only. ### 7.2 Stage-count correctness Derive `draft_swa_stage_count` from actual target capture/injection stages, such as `dspark_target_layer_ids`. ### 7.3 Sidecar abstraction Introduce an explicit draft SWA sidecar component with: - Content coverage. - Target-prefix coupling. - Insert, split, and eviction lifecycle. - Backup and loadback lifecycle. - Radix visibility. ### 7.4 Verify scratch separation Route speculative proposal and verify KV through step-local scratch. Scratch addresses must not be inserted into request-to-token mappings or radix nodes. ### 7.5 Accept path Materialize canonical accepted draft KV directly into committed sidecar rows. Rejected rows produce no sidecar coverage. ### 7.6 Prefix-hit and fallback path Reuse sidecar KV on a complete hit. On a target-hit/sidecar-miss case, recompute only the required trailing SWA region where possible. ### 7.7 PD and HiCache integration Expose committed sidecar pages as transferable state. Explicitly exclude verify scratch from all transfer descriptors. ### 7.8 `unified_kv` adapter Add a draft-only unified sidecar/scratch layout and mixed index generation. Do not modify the target unified ring or compressed-state kernels. ### 7.9 Rollout Gate the new layout behind a server argument during rollout. Unsupported backends must reject explicit enablement rather than silently falling back to incompatible semantics. ## 8. Compatibility and Risks ### 8.1 Numerical compatibility The design should not change model numerics. Canonical committed KV must continue to come from the target-hidden injection path unless a promotion path has proven numerical equivalence. ### 8.2 Cache consistency Sidecar and target prefix eviction must remain coupled. Incorrect coverage updates could pair stale sidecar KV with unrelated target content. ### 8.3 Fallback overhead A frequent sidecar-miss fallback would erase reuse benefits. The implementation should record sidecar hit rate and trailing-recompute frequency. ### 8.4 Accept-path overhead Extra materialization or copies may offset memory benefits. The baseline should use one canonical projection and direct committed scatter. Promotion should only be added when it reduces measured critical-path cost. ### 8.5 Backend complexity Paged and unified backends use different physical layouts. The abstraction must standardize semantics without forcing target unified kernels into the paged cache model. ### 8.6 Memory accounting drift Backend row padding, dtype, and page stride must be included in physical sizing. Semantic token counts alone are insufficient for exact allocation. ## 9. Validation Plan ### 9.1 Correctness Verify output parity and speculative accept-rate parity against main. ### 9.2 Cache-artifact invariant Confirm that: ```text rejected draft tokens produce no radix artifact verify scratch is unreachable after the step only accepted canonical KV gains sidecar coverage ``` ### 9.3 Accounting Compare calculated draft memory against allocated and measured memory. Expected results: - Lower draft over-reservation. - Larger usable target KV pool. - Fixed scratch overhead independent of cached token count. ### 9.4 Prefix reuse Measure: - Sidecar hit rate. - Target-hit/sidecar-miss rate. - Trailing-window recompute frequency. - Amount of reused committed draft KV. ### 9.5 PD and HiCache Verify that committed sidecar KV survives: - Prefill/decode transfer. - Offload. - Loadback. - Eviction and reallocation. Verify that scratch rows are never transferred. ### 9.6 `unified_kv` Validate that: - Target unified behavior is unchanged. - Draft committed rows use content indices. - Verify rows use scratch indices. - Mixed index streams produce numerical parity. - Target `SWA_RING` and draft `SWA` transfer states coexist correctly. ### 9.7 Performance Measure: - Per-step scratch overhead. - Canonical commit cost. - Optional promotion cost. - Attention metadata construction. - Prefix-hit latency. - End-to-end throughput and latency. ## 10. Alternatives Considered ### 10.1 Keep draft SWA request-scoped This preserves the current implementation shape but prevents committed draft KV from becoming a reusable prefix artifact. ### 10.2 Recompute draft SWA on every prefix hit This avoids sidecar memory but makes fallback the default and repeatedly pays the target-hidden projection cost. ### 10.3 Keep verify data in a long-lived request ring This simplifies addressing but retains rejected state longer than necessary and blurs committed versus in-flight ownership. ### 10.4 Convert target unified SWA to content-addressed storage This would unnecessarily redesign the target unified hot path and is outside the scope of this RFC. The preferred approach is a draft-only unified extension. ### 10.5 Promote proposal scratch directly This is invalid unless proposal scratch is numerically identical to canonical target-hidden-derived KV. The proposal does not assume this equivalence. ### Related resources _No response_

signal.title: [CPU] Update base image to Ubuntu 26.04
signal.text: ## Motivation Update CPU base image to Ubuntu 26.04, so that gcc/g++ 15.2.0 are default installed compilers. ## Modifications Other than image name change, `google-perftools` needs to be updated as `libgoogle-perftools-dev`. Ref: https://www.azerothcore.org/wiki/how-to-use-gperftool ## Checklist - [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process). 2. signal.title: [DSv4][DSpark] Split draft SWA into committed sidecar KV and verify scratch
signal.text: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Summary Fixes https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/35789 This PR re-layers DSV4 DSpark draft SWA into two explicitly managed regions: - **Committed sidecar KV**: content-scoped, radix-cache-visible, reusable, and transferable. - **Verify scratch**: step-scoped workspace that never enters the content cache. The change preserves model numerics and keeps the target `unified_kv` ring, C4/C128 layout, and target attention kernels unchanged. ## Motivation Committed draft SWA is deterministically derived from the committed prefix and model weights, so it should be reusable across prefix-cache hits. Speculative verify KV may contain rejected tokens and therefore must not become a cache artifact. The existing pool accounting also treats draft layers as target average layers, although DSpark draft stages are SWA-only and contain no C4, C128, indexer, or compression state. ## Design Draft SWA is split into: - `committed sidecar KV` - Content-scoped. - Coupled to target SWA allocation and prefix lifecycle. - Reused by radix cache. - Participates in PD and HiCache. - `verify scratch` - Request-slot-addressed but step-scoped. - Reused after each verify step. - Excluded from radix cache, PD, and HiCache. - Rejected tokens leave no cache artifact. Accepted canonical KV is produced from target hidden states and written directly to committed sidecar locations. Proposal scratch is not promoted because it is not guaranteed to be numerically equivalent to canonical target-hidden-derived KV. ## Main Changes - Replace target-average-layer draft accounting with SWA-only accounting. - Derive draft stage count from actual DSpark target capture layers. - Add explicit committed/scratch physical boundaries. - Add radix sidecar coverage tracking and lifecycle handling. - Recompute only the trailing SWA window on a sidecar miss. - Commit sidecar coverage after fallback recomputation. - Exclude scratch pages from PD and HiCache transfer. - Support HF3FS, Mooncake, NIXL, and UMBP sidecar hit semantics. - Add draft-only `unified_kv` support: - Target unified layout remains unchanged. - Draft unified storage uses committed rows plus scratch rows. - Attention reads committed prefix rows and the complete verify scratch block. - PD transfers draft sidecar as content-addressed `SWA`, while target remains `SWA_RING`. - HiCache attaches draft sidecar storage to the logical SWA component. - Add explicit draft stage IDs for PP-aware NIXL/Mooncake state transfer. - Fix scratch placement for non-page-aligned committed capacities. ## Compatibility - Model numerics are unchanged. - Existing target SWA, C4, C128, and target unified kernels are unchanged. - The feature is controlled by `--speculative-dspark-draft-swa-sidecar`. - `--no-speculative-dspark-draft-swa-sidecar` restores the legacy path. - NPU remains explicitly unsupported because it uses a separate DSV4 cache implementation. ## Accuracy Tests <!-- If this pull request affects model outputs (e.g., changes to the kernel or model forward code), provide accuracy test results. --> ## Speed Tests and Profiling <!-- If this pull request impacts inference speed, provide benchmarking and profiling results. --> ## Checklist - signal.title: [AMD]DSV4 Fix KV pool sizing for the unified_kv backend
signal.text: ## Motivation The DSV4 `unified_kv` backend has a different physical KV layout than the fp8 path, but `DSV4PoolConfigurator` sized both identically. Under `unified_kv` this over-allocates memory (and can OOM), because: - KV is stored in **bf16 over the full latent** (`attn_head_dim * 2` bytes), not the fp8(nope) + bf16(rope) + scale 584-byte cell. - SWA and the c4/c128 compress-states are **fixed per-request rings** (`num_req_slots * ring_size`), independent of `full_token`, so they must be fixed biases rather than per-token terms. ## Modifications All changes are gated on the same `is_unified_kv_triton()` / `_unified_kv` switch the pool itself uses, so sizing and allocation cannot drift apart. **No behavior change on the non-unified (fp8) path.** ### Pool sizing (`pool_configurator.py`) - Use bf16 full-latent bytes for the per-token coeff on the unified path (`_get_bytes_per_full_token`). - Exclude SWA from the per-token coeff and account for it as a fixed bias (`_fixed_swa_bytes`), inflated for the speculative draft worker the same way as the coeff. - Move the **c4 compress-state (attn + indexer)** off the per-token coeff and size it as a request-scoped fixed bias (`_fixed_c4_state_bytes` / `_unified_c4_state_pool_size`), finalized once `max_running_requests` is known — mirroring the c128 state pool. Subtract it from the token budget and log `c4_state_fixed`. - Factor the `max_running_requests`-per-worker resolution into a shared helper (`_resolve_max_running_requests_per_worker`) reused by the c128 state, SWA ring, and c4 state fixed-byte terms. - Log the SWA ring and c4-state fixed biases alongside the existing c128 fixed bias. ### Memory pool (`deepseek_v4_memory_pool.py`) - Clamp `c4_state_pool_size` up to `num_req_slots * c4_ring_size` as a safety net (mirrors the c128 clamp). ### SWA idle accounting on the unified ring - `model_runner`: reconcile `swa_max_total_num_tokens` down to the allocator ring capacity (`swa_available_size`) so the idle pool-leak invariant matches the fixed per-request SWA ring (gated on unified_kv; no real buffer is resized). - `invariant_checker`: skip the SWA token-pool leak invariant on the unified ring — its `available` is non-binding and cached radix prefixes report a spurious `swa_evictable`, so `available + evictable + protected == total` does not hold; ring slots are still covered by the `req_to_token` leak check. - `pool_stats_observer`: zero `swa_evictable` on the unified ring so `swa_num_used` / `swa_token_usage` stay coherent (cached prefixes hold no ring slot). ### Review-fix follow-ups - Detect unified-KV via the canonical `get_kvcache()._unified_kv` (the previous `getattr(alloc, "_unified", ...)` was always `False` on the wrapped allocators — thanks @amd-danli103). Applied consistently in `invariant_checker`, `pool_stats_observer`, and `schedule_batch`. - Unwrap `logical_attn_allocator` in the `_check_kv_page_invariants` sub-allocator probe so the DSV4-HiSparse wrapper reaches its inner full/swa allocators. - `schedule_policy`: align the `add_one_req` SWA admission gate (`>=` -> `>`) with `add_one_req_ignore_eos` so an exact-fit request is admitted. ## Accuracy / Validation Validated on **DeepSeek-V4-Pro, `unified_kv` + EAGLE MTP (speculative), TP8 / DP8, ROCm**. <details> <summary>Server launch command</summary> ```bash export SGLANG_DEFAULT_THINKING=1 export SGLANG_DSV4_REASONING_EFFORT=max export SGLANG_OPT_DEEPGEMM_HC_PRENORM=false export SGLANG_USE_AITER=1 export SGLANG_USE_ROCM700A=1 export SGLANG_OPT_USE_FUSED_COMPRESS=true export SGLANG_HACK_FLASHMLA_BACKEND=unified_kv_triton export SGLANG_OPT_FP8_WO_A_GEMM=false export SGLANG_OPT_USE_JIT_INDEXER_METADATA=false export SGLANG_OPT_USE_TOPK_V2=false export SGLANG_OPT_USE_AITER_INDEXER=true export SGLANG_OPT_USE_TILELANG_INDEXER=false export SGLANG_OPT_USE_TILELANG_MHC_PRE=false export SGLANG_OPT_USE_TILELANG_MHC_POST=false export SGLANG_FP8_PAGED_MQA_LOGITS_TORCH=1 export SGLANG_OPT_USE_FUSED_COMPRESS_TRITON=true export SGLANG_OPT_USE_MULTI_STREAM_OVERLAP=false export SGLANG_ROCM_USE_MULTI_STREAM=false export AITER_BF16_FP8_MOE_BOUND=0 export SGLANG_OPT_FP4_MOE_K_ALIGN=128 export SGLANG_DSV4_INDEXER_K_CACHE_PRESHUFFLE=1 export SGLANG_EAGER_INPUT_NO_COPY=false export SGLANG_DP_USE_GATHERV=1 python3 -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path /models/DeepSeek-V4-Pro \ --trust-remote-code \ --swa-full-tokens-ratio 0.10 \ --tp 8 \ --dp 8 \ --enable-dp-attention \ --enable-cache-report \ --attention-backend dsv4 \ --max-running-request 2048 \ --page-size 256 \ --chunked-prefill-size 32768 \ --mem-fraction-static 0.9 \ --port 30001 \ --disable-shared-experts-fusion \ --tool-call-parser deepseekv4 \ --reasoning-parser deepseek-v4 \ --speculative-algorithm EAGLE \ --speculative-num-steps 3 \ --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4 \ --speculative-eagle-topk 1 \ --enable-prefill-delayer ``` </details> <details> <summary>Client / bench_serving command</summary> ```bash NUM_PROMPT=2048 INPUT_LEN=50 python3 -m sglang.bench_serving \ --dataset-name random \ --random-range-ratio 1 \ --num-prompt ${NUM_PROMPT} \ --max-concurrency ${NUM_PROMPT} \ --random-input $((INPUT_LEN * 1024)) \ --random-output 1024 \ --port 30001 ``` </details> ### Pool sizing (startup) `unified=True`, `bytes_per_full_token=9064` (spec-inflated), `c128_state_fixed=7.83 GB`, `swa_ring_fixed=1.99 GB`, `c4_state_fixed=1.21 GB` — matches the bf16 layout + request-scoped fixed rings. Non-unified (fp8) path logs/sizes are unchanged. | full_token | before | after | | --- | --- | --- | | capacity | 8, 898, 560 | 12,047,104 | ### Stress (`bench_serving`, random) 1800 prompts × 51200-token input, 500-token output, concurrency 1800 (92.16M input tokens). - **1800 / 1800 requests completed, 0 crashes / 0 pool-leak errors** across the full run. - Peak `full token usage` 0.96 (previously the saturation zone that tripped idle/leak asserts). - Peak concurrent requests 1800. - MTP accept length 3.07; total token throughput 44,415 tok/s. ### Throughput (8k in / 1k out, concurrency 1024) | config | Total token throughput (tok/s) | Mean TTFT (ms) | Mean TPOT (ms) | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | before | 4523.21 | 89981.16 | 130.75 | | apply PR | 4559.63 | 90483.00 | 129.75 | ### GSM8K (5-shot,) **accuracy 0.950, invalid 0.000** — confirms the sizing / SWA-accounting changes do not affect correctness. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:no_entry_sign: [Run #32342868416](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32342868416)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32342868309](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32342868309)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32342868355](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32342868355)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [Scheduler] Reclaim committed KV without token IDs
signal.text: ## Why Overlap scheduling can commit a KV slot before its sampled token is accepted. If the result is rejected, `kv_committed_len` can be one greater than the request token sequence. A prefix cache has no token ID with which to key that tail slot, but common cleanup previously treated the full committed range as handled and could leave the unnamed slot allocated. ## Change - Bound the effective cacheable KV length by the request token sequence. - Keep the non-speculative allocation invariant based on physical committed KV rather than cacheable KV. - Let the existing common tail-release path return the unnamed allocation. The normal path is unchanged when committed KV and the token sequence have equal lengths. This complements #35204: that PR defines no-insert disposal from ownership, while this change defines what can enter a prefix cache. ## Validation - The focused regression test fails on current `main` with allocator capacity `12 != 13` and passes with this change. - 81 related tests and 61 subtests passed on one H200 with `lmsysorg/sglang:dev-cu13`, covering RadixCache, paged frees, no-insert cleanup, streaming sessions, and decode KV offload. - Repository pre-commit checks passed for all three changed files. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32451136321](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32451136321)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32451136123](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32451136123)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32451136368](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32451136368)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.text: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation As per the title. Add INT4 dense linear support for AWQ/GPTQ quantized models on Intel XPU, enabling INT4 inference on this backend. ## Modifications - New `python/sglang/srt/hardware_backend/xpu/quantization/: int4pack_utils.py, awq_kernels.py, gptq_kernels.py` — INT4 checkpoint conversion and native XPU packed-MM helpers. - Wire up scheme routing in `awq/awq.py, awq/schemes/awq_linear.py, gptq/gptq.py, gptq/schemes/gptq_linear.py, and layers/quantization/__init__.py` to dispatch dense INT4 linear to the XPU kernels. - Add unit tests: `test/registered/xpu/test_xpu_int4_dense.py`. ## Accuracy Tests Model: `hugging-quants/Meta-Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct-AWQ-INT4` / `hugging-quants/Meta-Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct-GPTQ-INT4` GSM8K: AWQ `~0.78`; GPTQ `~0.785`. ## Limitations GPTQ + TP>1 is only rejected when a row-parallel shard actually splits a quantization group — i.e. when `act_order` (`desc_act=true`) has permuted `g_idx` so the local channels no longer sort into whole `group_size` blocks. signal.title: [AMD] Fix gfx950 Triton compiler crash on fp8 KV-cache attention
signal.text: ## Motivation `test/registered/attention/test_verify_shared_kv.py::test_qwen3_5_fp8_kv_cache` has never passed on `stage-b-1-gpu-small-amd-mi35x` since it was added (#34517); it fails inside the Triton AMD backend, not in sglang code ([latest instance](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32166850277/job/95808413702)): ``` python3: llvm/ADT/SmallVector.h:292: Assertion `idx < size()' failed. extend_attention.py:305:0: error: Failures have been detected while processing an MLIR pass pipeline extend_attention.py:305:0: note: Pipeline failed while executing [`ConvertTritonAMDGPUToLLVM` ...] RuntimeError: PassManager::run failed ``` Only the fp8 variant fails; the bf16 variants of the same test pass. The crash is not test-specific — it is in the shared prefill kernel, so a model served on MI35x with `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3` **through the Triton attention backend** hits it, in decode as well as prefill. (Backends that do not route through these kernels, and the two ROCm Triton kernels that cannot take an fp8 pool at all, are out of scope; see Modifications.) **Scope: the ROCm 7.0 image only — 7.2 was never affected.** The dividing line is the Triton wheel, not ROCm. On the pre-fix ROCm 7.2 MI35x lane ([job 95705686213](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32135460766/job/95705686213), Aug 18, before any commit here) `test_verify_shared_kv.py` reported `"passed": true` with no `PassManager::run failed` or `idx < size()` in the log; that lane's only red was the unrelated `test_quark_mxfp4.py` near-miss. The 7.0 log carries aiter's `require triton>=3.6.0, found 3.4.0`, while 7.2 emits no such warning, so its Triton clears 3.6.0 (`docker/rocm.Dockerfile` installs aiter's pin over the base ROCm Torch `triton==3.5.1` when `BUILD_TRITON=1`). ### Root cause Every Triton attention kernel that reads a KV pool casts the wide operand *down* to the pool dtype before the dot (`tl.dot(q.to(k.dtype), k)`, `tl.dot(p.to(v.dtype), v)`), so an fp8 pool also feeds the fp8 matrix core. On gfx950 `AccelerateAMDMatmul` promotes an fp8 x fp8 `tl.dot` to the scaled `V_MFMA_*_F8F6F4` family, which is **16x16x128** under the `matrix_instr_nonkdim=16` launch hint all of these kernels pass. A dot whose reduction is narrower than 128 does not tile that instruction: `AMDMfmaEncodingAttr::getRepForOperand` clamps the resulting zero K-repetitions up to one, and `ScaledDotOpMFMAConversionHelper` then reads `kBase = 32` elements per lane from a register range that only holds `K / 4`. That is the out-of-bounds `SmallVector` access. `P @ V` reduces `BLOCK_N`, which is 64 (extend, verify) or 32 (decode, split-KV verify) — never 128 — so the fp8 path never compiles on gfx950. `Q @ Kpe` reduces `BLOCK_DPE` (32/64) and `Q @ K` reduces `BLOCK_DMODEL`, which is also below 128 at head_dim <= 64. Triton rejects the intrinsic instead of miscompiling it as of [triton-lang/triton#8278](https://github.com/triton-lang/triton/pull/8278), which dropped the `enforcedNonKDim == 0 &&` escape hatch that had let an explicit `matrix_instr_nonkdim` skip Triton's own "K is not a multiple of the intrinsic's kDim" check. That fix missed 3.5 and landed in 3.6: | Triton branch | guard in `chooseMfmaInstruction` | narrow fp8 dot | |---|---|---| | `release/3.4.x`, `release/3.5.x` | `enforcedNonKDim == 0 && inputKSize % kDim != 0` | promoted, then aborts | | `release/3.6.x` and later | `if (inputKSize % kDim != 0)` | rejected, falls back to non-scaled fp8 MFMA | So anything on 3.4 or 3.5 with `matrix_instr_nonkdim` set — which is every kernel here — crashes, and the ROCm 7.0 image ships 3.4.0. **The guard therefore carries a `triton.__version__ < 3.6` term, so it is inert on 7.2.** Without it the guard also fired on 7.2, where Triton already falls back to the non-scaled `V_MFMA_F32_16X16X32_FP8_FP8` and the narrow dot works — [the same pre-fix job](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32135460766/job/95705686213) ran `test_qwen3_5_fp8_kv_cache` green. That would have substituted a bf16 dot for a working fp8 one on the lane that gates PRs, trading unquantized `P` (more accurate) against fp8→bf16 converts and a 2-byte V tile in LDS, for a rate difference nobody has measured. Not a trade worth making on the primary lane. With the version term: - **7.0 / Triton 3.4** — guard active, replaces a hard compile abort. - **7.2 / Triton ≥3.6** — guard inert, codegen byte-identical to today. - When ROCm 7.0 is dropped the guard is permanently inert and the whole module can be deleted, so this does not become long-lived debt. `extend_attention.py` already gates gfx950 tile choices on `_is_triton_ge_37`, so a Triton-version term is an established idiom in this file rather than a new mechanism. A version string that will not parse keeps the guard on, which is the safe direction. ## Modifications - New `python/sglang/kernels/ops/attention/fp8_dot_support.py` with `dot_in_kv_dtype(kv_dtype, reduction_width)`: `True` for every non-fp8 pool and every arch other than gfx950, and on gfx950 only for reduction widths that tile the scaled MFMA instruction. - Each dot that casts an operand down to the tile it reads gets its own constexpr verdict (`QK_DOT_IN_KV_DTYPE`, `QK_PE_DOT_IN_KV_DTYPE`, `PV_DOT_IN_KV_DTYPE`, `PV_EXTEND_DOT_IN_V_DTYPE`). When it is `False` the KV tile is upcast to the query dtype instead of the query tile being cast down. This covers `_fwd_kernel` and `_fwd_kernel_unified` (extend), `_fwd_grouped_kernel_stage1` (decode), `_verify_mla_prefix_stage1`, and `_verify_prefix_stage1` — including `_fwd_kernel`'s extend-stage `P @ V`, whose V is the caller's current-chunk tensor rather than the pool. Every flag is `True` on non-gfx950 hardware and for bf16/fp16 pools, so those paths generate the same code as before. `matrix_instr_nonkdim`, tile sizes, warp counts, and the `#mma` layout are all untouched. **Non-AMD impact: none, verified rather than argued.** `is_gfx95_supported()` returns `False` for every non-HIP build without touching the device, so `dot_in_kv_dtype` short-circuits to `True` on NVIDIA and the guards select the pre-existing expression. To confirm that costs nothing, I compiled the original kernel body and the guarded one (flags `True`) for five targets with Triton 3.4.0 and diffed the emitted TTGIR and LLIR modulo debug locations: **identical on sm90 (bf16 and fp8), sm100 (fp8), gfx942 (fp8) and gfx950 (bf16)**. That check is what caught the one real difference — writing the guard as `tl.dot(p.to(v.dtype), v)` reorders the P cast against the `acc * re_scale` multiply, which on Hopper with an fp8 pool moved the async `warp_group_dot` relative to the accumulator scaling. Keeping `p = p.to(v.dtype)` as its own statement inside the guard restores exact equivalence, which is why it is written that way. NVIDIA fp8 KV keeps casting down to fp8 and keeps its fp8 tensor-core path. The residual cost off gfx950 is one extra Triton compile (the new constexpr parameters change the cache key) and three or four integer / `frozenset` comparisons per launch. Two other ROCm Triton kernels dot against a tile that could in principle be fp8, and deliberately get no verdict: - `prefill_attention.py` never reads a KV pool, its `Q @ K` is uncast (so its operands already share a dtype), and its gfx950 `BLOCK_N` is 128 — which tiles the scaled instruction even if `P @ V` ran in fp8. - `rocm_mla_decode_rope.py` does read the pool, but its `Q @ K` is uncast too, so a bf16 query against an fp8 pool fails Triton's frontend with `Unsupported rhs dtype fp8e4nv` well before the AMD backend. That is a separate pre-existing gap in that kernel, not this crash, and a per-dot verdict would not make it work. The verify combine kernels compute their draft-draft block with `tl.sum(q[:, None, :] * ke[None, :, :], 2)`, not `tl.dot`, so no matrix-core promotion applies there. **On unit tests:** I wrote and then dropped a CPU test for the predicate. Asserting `dot_in_kv_dtype(fp8, 64) is False` against a body of `width % 128 == 0` only restates the expression, and the one assertion with real coupling — that the gfx950 head_dim-256 config yields a `BLOCK_N` the guard rejects — would fail if someone legitimately retuned `BLOCK_N` to 128, which is the documented fallback here. Pinning that would block an improvement rather than catch a bug. The failure mode worth guarding is "a new narrow fp8 dot appears on gfx950", and what catches that is compiling the real kernel on real gfx950, i.e. the MI35x lane. Alternatives considered and rejected: dropping or raising `matrix_instr_nonkdim` for the fp8 path (Triton's own guard then rejects the intrinsic, but the 16x16 tile becomes 32x32, which changes `warpsPerTile` for the chain-dot tail from `[8, 1]` to `[4, 2]` and inserts a layout conversion between the two dots), and forcing `BLOCK_N = 128` (fixes only head_dim 256 and re-tunes the bf16 path with it). ## Accuracy Tests `stage-b-test-1-gpu-small-amd-mi35x` now passes on MI35x hardware. [Run 32217006660](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32217006660) is a targeted dispatch of just that stage against this PR's head (ROCm 7.0, since that lane is schedule-only and a PR event never runs it): **9/9 passed**, `test_verify_shared_kv.py` reports `"passed": true` with `test_qwen3_5_fp8_kv_cache` executing, and the log contains no `PassManager::run failed` or `idx < size()`. ([Run 32212523645](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32212523645) is the same result on the first commit.) The change only affects gfx950 with an fp8 KV pool, where nothing compiled before, so there is no prior behaviour to regress. Within that path `P` reaches the dot as bf16 rather than quantized to e4m3, which is strictly more accurate; `extend_attention_fwd` and `verify_shared_kv_fwd` widen the same dots, so `test_qwen3_5_fp8_kv_cache`'s parity check compares like with like. ## Speed Tests and Profiling @chuyeh benched the three #34517 kernels on MI355X at the Qwen3.5 TP4-local verify shape ([full tables](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/35428#issuecomment-5364623778)). fp8 pool versus bf16 pool at a 16k prefix: | Kernel | bf16 pool | fp8 pool | Δ | |---|---:|---:|---:| | grouped-head verify | 0.048 ms | 0.042 ms | **−12%** | | split-KV verify | 0.073 ms | 0.056 ms | **−23%** | | extend | 1.069 ms | 1.791 ms | **+68%** | The bandwidth-bound verify kernels gain from the halved KV traffic; extend regresses. Two caveats on reading that: 1. **Those numbers are from `780d4ab`, before the Triton-version term.** On ROCm 7.2 the guard was still firing there, so the fp8 extend row is the widened bf16 `P @ V`. At HEAD the guard is inert on 7.2, so that row should not reproduce on that image. 2. **The bench cannot attribute the +68%.** A pool that halves KV bytes made the other two kernels faster, so extend moving the other way is either the widened `P @ V` (fp8→bf16 V converts plus a 2-byte V tile in LDS, paid every iteration of a serial prefix loop at `BLOCK_M=128`/`BLOCK_N=64`/head_dim 256) or something inherent to fp8 extend that this PR neither causes nor cures. An extend-only rerun at HEAD on 7.2 separates them; requested, not blocking. What this does not change: on ROCm 7.0 the alternative to widening is a compile abort, so a slower extend is still the right trade there, and it is the only image that pays it. If the widening does own the regression, the follow-up lever is `BLOCK_N = 128` for the fp8 extend tile — it reaches the scaled 16x16x128 instruction on both dots and compiles today, at the cost of retuning the tile and doubling the K/V LDS footprint. That belongs in its own change with numbers behind it, not here. Independently useful from the same run: "the flags-`True` path does not move the bf16 numbers", which confirms the codegen-equivalence check above on hardware. ## Verification Triton 3.4.0's AMD backend compiles for `hip:gfx950` without a GPU, so the fix was checked by driving the ttir/ttgir/llir stages directly on the same tile shape and launch hints as `extend_attention` at head_dim 256 (`BLOCK_M=128`, `num_warps=8`, `matrix_instr_nonkdim=16`): | KV dtype | `PV_DOT_IN_KV_DTYPE` | `BLOCK_N` | Result | |---|---|---|---| | fp8_e4m3 | True (today) | 64 | **`RuntimeError: PassManager::run failed`** | | fp8_e4m3 | False (this PR) | 64 | compiles | | fp8_e4m3 | True | 32 | **`Assertion 'idx < size()' failed`** | | fp8_e4m3 | False | 32 | compiles | | fp8_e4m3 | True | 128 | compiles (128 tiles the instruction) | | bf16 | True | 64 | compiles (unchanged path) | The fixed variant's TTGIR keeps the fp8 fast path where it is legal and drops to bf16 only for `P @ V`, both under the same `#mma` layout as before: ``` %50 = tt.dot_scaled %28, %49, %cst_2 lhs = e4m3 rhs = e4m3 : tensor<128x256xf8E4M3FN, dot_op<{opIdx = 0, parent = #mma, kWidth = 16}>> * tensor<256x64xf8E4M3FN, ...> %77 = tt.dot %76, %75, %73 : tensor<128x64xbf16, dot_op<{opIdx = 0, parent = #mma, kWidth = 4}>> * tensor<64x256xbf16, dot_op<{opIdx = 1, parent = #mma, kWidth = 4}>> ``` The K3 MLA tile (`BLOCK_DMODEL=512`, `BLOCK_DPE=64`, `BLOCK_N=64`), where two of the three dots widen, behaves the same way: crashes today, compiles with the per-dot verdicts. Narrowing `BLOCK_DMODEL` to 64 crashes the `Q @ K` dot too, which is why the verdict is computed per dot rather than assuming `Q @ K` is always wide enough. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). The regression test is the existing `test_verify_shared_kv.py::test_qwen3_5_fp8_kv_cache` on `stage-b-test-1-gpu-small-amd-mi35x`, which this PR turns green; no new test file is added (see below). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

signal.title: [Bug] Qwen3-VL vision features diverge from Transformers/vLLM in v0.5.17 on fine-grained grounding
signal.text: ### Checklist - [x] I searched related issues but found no solution. - [x] The bug persists in the latest version. - [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback. - [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed. - [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Describe the bug ### Summary On the latest release, SGLang v0.5.17 (commit `29481685462732237d80d86076d6563e1f658102`), we observe a large accuracy discrepancy for fine-grained visual grounding with two Qwen3-VL-family checkpoints: `Tencent/UI-Mate-27B` and `Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B`. We replayed the same captured prompt contents and image bytes through SGLang, Hugging Face Transformers, and vLLM under greedy decoding (`temperature=0.0`, `top_p=1.0`). Only the engine changed. Transformers and vLLM agree closely, while SGLang produces systematically incorrect click coordinates. | Model | Engine | Dtype | Half-row hits | Median absolute y error / row pitch | |---|---|---:|---:|---:| | UI-Mate-27B | SGLang 0.5.17 | BF16 | 0/20 | 0.9748 | | UI-Mate-27B | Transformers | BF16 | 20/20 | 0.0636 | | UI-Mate-27B | vLLM (official-style TP2) | BF16 | 20/20 | 0.0649 | | Qwen3.8-27B | SGLang 0.5.17 | BF16 | 1/20 | 4.5964 | | Qwen3.8-27B | Transformers | BF16 | 20/20 | 0.0481 | | Qwen3.8-27B | vLLM | BF16 | 20/20 | 0.0559 | The criterion is whether the first click falls within half of one rendered row pitch. All arms use the same 20 fixed first-step inputs. This is intentionally a narrow fine-grained grounding test; we are not claiming that all Qwen3-VL tasks fail in SGLang. ### Evidence localizing the discrepancy For an aligned Qwen3.8 seed: - `input_ids` are identical between the Transformers replay and SGLang (same shape and hash). - `image_grid_thw` is identical: `[[1, 62, 100]]`. - The processor output shape is identical: `pixel_values=[6200, 1536]`, float32. - The default SGLang GPU processor differs slightly from the CPU processor (max absolute pixel delta `2/255`, mean absolute delta `1.56e-6`). Disabling the fast image processor remains 1/20, so this small preprocessing delta is not sufficient to explain the failure. - Text token embeddings before multimodal replacement are exactly equal elementwise in our probe. - Immediately after the vision merge, image-token relative L2 difference is approximately `0.0401`. - After the first GDN layer and the first full-attention layer, the relative L2 difference remains approximately `0.036`. This suggests the discrepancy is already present in the vision output and is then propagated by the language model. With an exact Transformers-generated prefix forced into both engines, both choose the same first action token and, after a prefix ending in `"y":`, the same leading coordinate digit with probability effectively 1. This argues against an action parser problem or a fixed coordinate-output-head bias. ### Controlled SGLang ablations (Qwen3.8 BF16, same 20 inputs) | Change from baseline | Half-row hits | Median error / row pitch | |---|---:|---:| | Baseline | 1/20 | 4.5964 | | Disable fast image processor | 1/20 | 4.5068 | | Disable prefill CUDA graph | 1/20 | 4.5516 | | Multimodal attention FA3 -> SDPA | 1/20 | 3.5061 | | Enable precise embedding interpolation | 1/20 | 4.5964 | | Compatibility-adapted v0.5.6.post2 `qwen3_vl.py` vision path | 0/20 | 4.5964 | ### Related issue This may be related to #19513, which reported incorrect Qwen3-VL vision output in older SGLang releases. However, we do not assume the same root cause: unlike that report, a compatibility-adapted v0.5.6.post2 vision-file rollback did **not** recover accuracy on our current v0.5.17 / Transformers 5.12 stack. We would appreciate guidance on the best supported way to compare the vision-encoder output against the Transformers reference, or on any known correctness flags/patches for this model family. ### Reproduction ### Minimal replay (Qwen3.8-27B, seed 8001) The attachment `qwen_seed8001_greedy_payload.json.txt` is a self-contained OpenAI chat-completions payload. It contains the exact prompt and the screenshot as a data URL. Compared with the captured benchmark request, only three fields were normalized: model ID → `Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B`, `temperature` → `0.0`, and `top_p` → `1.0`. The message contents and image bytes are unchanged. Start SGLang: ```bash python3 -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B \ --host 0.0.0.0 --port 30000 \ --tp-size 1 \ --dtype bfloat16 \ --trust-remote-code \ --context-length 131072 \ --chunked-prefill-size 4096 \ --reasoning-parser qwen3 ``` Download the attachment and replay it: ```python import json import requests payload = json.load(open("qwen_seed8001_greedy_payload.json.txt")) response = requests.post( "http://127.0.0.1:30000/v1/chat/completions", json=payload, timeout=600, ) response.raise_for_status() message = response.json()["choices"][0]["message"] print(message.get("reasoning_content")) print(message.get("content")) ``` Oracle row center for this screenshot: `y=277.1328125` in the declared 1000x1000 output space. Half-row acceptance interval: `[260.39453125, 293.87109375]`. Observed final actions under greedy decoding: ```text SGLang 0.5.17 BF16: {"type":"click","x":150,"y":125,"button":"left"} Transformers BF16: {"type":"click","x":150,"y":276,"button":"left"} vLLM BF16: {"type":"click","x":144,"y":275,"button":"left"} ``` Prompt-token counts are identical for this Qwen replay (2639). The same 20-input discrepancy was independently reproduced with UI-Mate-27B using its official-style vLLM TP2 serving configuration. SHA-256 of the proposed attachment: `d74eb21f628f4f9d172b916c2ec31e54162a954f15cc2f4bd0226ca3517287c2`. [qwen_seed8001_greedy_payload.json.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31285951/qwen_seed8001_greedy_payload.json.txt) ### Environment ```text Python: 3.12.3 (main, Jun 19 2026, 12:46:00) [GCC 13.3.0] CUDA available: True GPU 0,1,2,3: NVIDIA H200 NVL GPU 0,1,2,3 Compute Capability: 9.0 CUDA_HOME: /usr/local/cuda NVCC: Cuda compilation tools, release 12.9, V12.9.86 CUDA Driver Version: 580.105.08 PyTorch: 2.11.0+cu129 sglang: 0.5.17 sglang-kernel: 0.4.5+cu129 flashinfer_python: 0.6.15.post1 flashinfer_cubin: 0.6.15.post1 flashinfer_jit_cache: 0.6.15.post1+cu129 triton: 3.6.0 transformers: 5.12.1 torchao: 0.17.0+cu129 numpy: 2.4.4 aiohttp: 3.14.3 fastapi: 0.141.1 huggingface_hub: 1.27.0 interegular: 0.3.3 modelscope: 1.39.1 orjson: 3.11.9 outlines: 0.1.11 packaging: 26.3 psutil: 7.2.2 pydantic: 2.13.4 python-multipart: 0.0.32 pyzmq: 27.1.0 uvicorn: 0.52.1 uvloop: 0.22.1 vllm: Module Not Found xgrammar: 0.2.1 openai: 2.6.1 tiktoken: 0.13.0 anthropic: 0.121.0 litellm: Module Not Found torchcodec: 0.11.1+cu129 NVIDIA topology: GPU0 GPU1 GPU2 GPU3 NIC0 NIC1 CPU_Affinity NUMA GPU0 X NV6 NV6 NV6 SYS SYS 0-31,64-95 0 GPU1 NV6 X NV6 NV6 SYS SYS 0-31,64-95 0 GPU2 NV6 NV6 X NV6 SYS SYS 32-63,96-127 1 GPU3 NV6 NV6 NV6 X SYS SYS 32-63,96-127 1 ulimit soft: 131072 ``` SGLang source commit: `29481685462732237d80d86076d6563e1f658102` Container image: `sglang-0.5.17-cu129.sif` Primary SGLang launch settings: BF16, TP1 for Qwen3.8; BF16, TP2 for UI-Mate; FA3 default attention backend; chunked prefill size 4096. Exact Qwen command is included in Reproduction.

signal.title: [Bug] Qwen3.5 MTP weights silently dropped on compressed-tensors checkpoints (accept len pinned at 1.0)
signal.text: ### Checklist - [x] I searched related issues but found no solution. - [x] The bug persists in the latest version. - [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback. - [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed. - [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Describe the bug **This is the compressed-tensors counterpart of #23113.** That issue added a `quark` branch to `_mtp_quant_config()` in `python/sglang/srt/models/qwen3_5_mtp.py`; `compressed_tensors` still has no branch, and fails the same way. Serving a Qwen3.5-family model from a **compressed-tensors** checkpoint (AutoRound / llm-compressor) with MTP speculative decoding produces **`accept len: 1.000` exactly** — zero drafted tokens ever accepted — with zero variance across every prompt, seed and depth. Throughput collapses, since the full draft cost is paid for nothing: 30.7 tok/s at depth 8 against 248 tok/s for a working speculative path on the same server, model and prompts. **Root cause.** Such checkpoints list the MTP linears in `quantization_config.ignore` **individually**: ``` mtp.fc mtp.layers.0.self_attn.q_proj mtp.layers.0.mlp.gate_proj mtp.layers.0.self_attn.k_proj mtp.layers.0.mlp.up_proj mtp.layers.0.self_attn.v_proj mtp.layers.0.mlp.down_proj mtp.layers.0.self_attn.o_proj ``` but SGLang constructs them **fused**, as `qkv_proj` and `gate_up_proj`. The fused names match no `ignore` entry, so exactly those two linears are built quantized while the unfused ones correctly fall back to unquantized. Dumping the constructed module's parameters: ``` model.layers.0.qkv_proj.weight_packed (7168, 640) <- quantized model.layers.0.mlp.gate_up_proj.weight_packed (17408, 640) <- quantized model.layers.0.o_proj.weight (5120, 3072) <- correct model.layers.0.mlp.down_proj.weight (5120, 8704) <- correct ``` Every `mtp.*` tensor in the checkpoint is plain bf16 (15 tensors, none with `_scale`, none packed), so the five stacked ones find no matching parameter and are dropped in `load_weights()` by `logger.warning_once`: ``` Parameter model.layers.0.q_proj.weight not found in params_dict, skip loading Parameter model.layers.0.k_proj.weight not found in params_dict, skip loading Parameter model.layers.0.v_proj.weight not found in params_dict, skip loading Parameter model.layers.0.mlp.gate_proj.weight not found in params_dict, skip loading Parameter model.layers.0.mlp.up_proj.weight not found in params_dict, skip loading ``` The MTP attention and MLP therefore run **randomly initialized**. Because `o_proj` and `down_proj` load correctly, the module is only partly broken, weight loading reports success, and `warning_once` deduplicates the five lines into a single easily-missed warning. This is not a verification-side problem: the failure is identical under a greedy request and under `--speculative-use-rejection-sampling`, while a non-MTP speculative control on the same server, model and prompts reads `accept len` 5.43. ### Proposed fix Give `compressed_tensors` the same treatment as `quark`, in `_mtp_quant_config()`: ```python if quant_config and quant_config.get_name() == "compressed_tensors": ignore = getattr(quant_config, "ignore", None) or [] if any(isinstance(layer, str) and layer.startswith("mtp.") for layer in ignore): return None ``` Verified on the setup below — the fused parameters become plain `.weight` at full shape, `not found in params_dict` goes from 10 hits (5 tensors x 2 TP ranks) to 0, and acceptance comes alive: | | accept len | decode tok/s | |---|---:|---:| | before, `--speculative-num-draft-tokens 4` | 1.000 | 44.1 | | before, `--speculative-num-draft-tokens 8` | 1.000 | 30.7 | | **after, 4** | **3.262** | **141.7** | | **after, 8** | **5.132** | **153.1** | (mean over three prompt types, 2 seeds each, `--max-num-seqs 1`.) I am happy to open a PR with this if the approach looks right. A more general alternative would be to make the fused-name gate (`should_ignore_layer(..., fused_mapping=...)`) resolve MTP prefixes, but the narrow branch matches what #23113 already established for quark. ### Reproduction Any Qwen3.5-family compressed-tensors checkpoint whose `quantization_config.ignore` lists `mtp.*` layers. Used here: `Qwen3.8-27B-W4A16-AutoRound` (`quant_method: compressed-tensors`, `format: pack-quantized`), served on 2x RTX 3090: ```bash python3 -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path <qwen3.5-family-compressed-tensors-checkpoint> \ --tp-size 2 --dtype bfloat16 --trust-remote-code \ --context-length 98304 --mem-fraction-static 0.84 \ --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 --sampling-defaults model \ --speculative-algorithm EAGLE \ --speculative-draft-model-path <same checkpoint> \ --speculative-num-steps 3 --speculative-eagle-topk 1 \ --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4 ``` Send any request and watch the scheduler log: ``` Decode batch, ... accept len: 1.00, accept rate: 0.00, ... ``` `accept len` is pinned at exactly 1.00 for every batch. Grepping the boot log for `not found in params_dict` shows the five skipped MTP tensors. ### Environment ``` Python: 3.10.12 (main, Jun 22 2026, 18:55:27) [GCC 11.4.0] CUDA available: True GPU 0,1: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3090 GPU 0,1 Compute Capability: 8.6 CUDA_HOME: /usr/local/cuda NVCC: Cuda compilation tools, release 13.3, V13.3.73 CUDA Driver Version: 595.84 PyTorch: 2.13.0+cu130 sglang: 0.0.0.dev16855+g5f1283959 sglang-kernel: 0.4.6.post1+cu130 flashinfer_python: 0.6.17 flashinfer_cubin: 0.6.17 flashinfer_jit_cache: 0.6.17+cu130 triton: 3.7.1 transformers: 5.12.1 torchao: 0.17.0 numpy: 2.2.6 aiohttp: 3.14.3 fastapi: 0.141.1 huggingface_hub: 1.27.0 interegular: 0.3.3 modelscope: 1.39.1 orjson: 3.12.0 outlines: 0.1.11 packaging: 26.3 psutil: 7.2.2 pydantic: 2.13.4 python-multipart: 0.0.32 pyzmq: 27.1.0 uvicorn: 0.52.3 uvloop: 0.22.1 vllm: Module Not Found xgrammar: 0.2.1 openai: 2.6.1 tiktoken: 0.13.0 anthropic: 0.122.0 litellm: Module Not Found torchcodec: 0.15.0+cu130 NVIDIA Topology: [4mGPU0 GPU1 CPU Affinity NUMA Affinity GPU NUMA ID[0m ```
