signal.title: [AMD] DeepSeek-V4 MI355X: eliminate bpreshuffle fp8-scale copies at producer sites (MoE down, MLA o_proj bmm)
signal.text: ## Summary Follow-up to the dense-linear bpreshuffle scale no-copy. Several DeepSeek-V4 sites **pre-quantize** an activation and hand a `(fp8, scale)` tuple to a downstream Linear; those scales are emitted row-major and then relaid out with `materialize_bpreshuffle_fp8_scale` — a relayout **copy per site, per layer** on MI355X (gfx950). This PR eliminates those copies for the producer quant kernels that honor `transpose_scale`, via a zero-copy `torch.as_strided` reinterpret. ## What changed - **`python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/fp8_utils.py`** — one producer-neutral `view_aiter_fused_rms_transposed_fp8_scale` (+ `_tuple`) helper: the zero-copy stride reinterpret of a scale a quant kernel already emitted with `transpose_scale=True`. This **consolidates** the identical `view_aiter_fused_rms_transposed_fp8_scale` that landed on main in #31727 with this PR's producer helper (both were `as_strided(scale, scale.shape, (1, scale.shape[0]))`) into a single operation, keeping the established #31727 name for consistency. Also adds `emit_transposed_bpreshuffle_scale(m, on_bpreshuffle_gfx95=...)`, centralizing the shared `M >= 2` emit gate. - **`python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_v4.py`** — fused-RMS producer repointed to the consolidated helper. - **`python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_v2.py`** — MLP down-proj input producer (`fused_clamp_act_mul`): request `transpose_scale=True` and reinterpret instead of copy (gated `M>=2`). - **`python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_common/attention_forward_methods/forward_mla_rocm.py`** — o_proj bmm producers ×2 in `rocm_absorb_v_bmm` (`fused_flatten_fp8_group_quant`): same treatment. (ROCm MLA now dispatches here after the recent `forward_mla_rocm.py` split; the optimization was moved off `forward_mla.py`, which is back to matching upstream, so it lands on the actual MI355X call path.) Sites fed by `fused_rms_fp8_group_quant` follow the same helper now (the #31727 fix made that kernel honor `transpose_scale`). ## Tests - **CPU** (`test_fp8_bpreshuffle_scale.py`) — helper-level stride/no-copy contract, and the centralized `emit_transposed_bpreshuffle_scale` gate incl. the `M == 1` materialize fallback. - **MI35X GPU** (`test_fp8_bpreshuffle_producer_mi35x.py`, `stage-b-test-1-gpu-small-amd-mi35x`) — invokes **both real producers** (`fused_clamp_act_mul`, `fused_flatten_fp8_group_quant`) with `transpose_scale=True` + no-copy vs `transpose_scale=False` + materialize, asserting bit-identical quantized output, equal scale values, the `(1, M)` column-major stride, and zero-copy storage sharing (M ∈ {1, 2, 8, 16}; M==1 exercises the materialize fallback). This is the direct producer-level equivalence evidence — the invariant the optimization relies on, checked on the real kernels rather than a fabricated layout. ## Validation Model: `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro`. Hardware: MI355X (gfx950), TP8. Image: `rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.16-rocm720-mi35x-20260731`. Env: `SGLANG_USE_AITER=1 AITER_BF16_FP8_MOE_BOUND=0 SGLANG_HACK_FLASHMLA_BACKEND=unified_kv_triton`. ### Accuracy (GSM8K, 1319 questions × 2 runs) | run | baseline | patched | |----:|:--------:|:-------:| | 1 | 0.942 | 0.933 | | 2 | 0.939 | 0.931 | The patched runs sit ~0.8–0.9 pt below baseline. With only two runs per arm this is consistent with, but does not by itself establish, DeepSeek-V4 fp4-MoE run-to-run noise. The correctness guarantee for this PR comes instead from the **producer-level bit-exact test** above: the converted kernels emit identical quantized output and scale values on both paths, so the reroute cannot change the model result. (Happy to add more GSM8K reps if useful.) ### Perf (random 8k/1k, `--random-range-ratio 1.0`, seed 42) — preliminary **Single-shot, one run per arm — treat as preliminary, not an established speedup.** The Δ below (≈ ±0.4–0.8%) is within DeepSeek-V4 decode run-to-run noise at these concurrencies and is not backed by repeated A/B runs, so I'm not claiming it as a confirmed win. The correctness/no-regression guarantee for this PR is the **producer-level bit-exact test** above (identical quantized output + scale values on both paths); the value here is eliminating a per-site/per-layer relayout copy, which these numbers are consistent with but do not by themselves prove. I can add repeated-run A/B (mean/p50/variance) if a throughput claim is wanted. | conc | baseline TPOT (ms) | patched TPOT (ms) | ΔTPOT | baseline total tok/s | patched total tok/s | Δtot | |-----:|:------------------:|:-----------------:|:-----:|:--------------------:|:-------------------:|:----:| | 16 | 19.48 | 19.32 | −0.8% | 6500.2 | 6549.1 | +0.8% | | 32 | 24.63 | 24.50 | −0.5% | 9685.3 | 9728.3 | +0.4% | | 64 | 35.03 | 34.79 | −0.7% | 12819.0 | 12898.1 | +0.6% | Measured under pure TP8. (No DP-attention measurement yet — the earlier "larger under DP-attention" note is removed until that's actually measured.) Coherent, zero dropped requests. Applies on top of the dense-linear PR (different `fp8_utils` region) or standalone. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:no_entry_sign: [Run #32272019567](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32272019567)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32272018916](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32272018916)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32272019119](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32272019119)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [DO NOT MERGE][Test] Tighten the DCP HiCache KL threshold to 0.005
signal.text: ## Motivation `test_unified_radix_cache_kl_dcp.py` (Kimi Linear + DCP4 + HiCache L2 + UnifiedRadixCache) has gated at `kl_threshold = 0.01` since it landed in #33112. Every other fp8 hybrid cache-hit KL case in the same directory gates at 0.005: | case | threshold | | --- | --- | | `test_unified_radix_cache_kl_mamba.py` | 0.005 | | `test_unified_radix_cache_kl_cp.py` | 0.005 | | `test_unified_radix_cache_hicache_pp_kl.py` | 0.005 | | `test_unified_radix_cache_kl_dsv4.py` | 0.005 | | `test_unified_radix_cache_kl_dcp.py` | **0.01** | A looser threshold tolerates float noise and small state bugs alike, and the thing this case exists to catch — a missing DCP logical→physical translation handing back another rank's KV on a cache hit — is exactly what slack hides. This PR tries the house value so the DCP translation path is held to the same bar as the non-DCP ones. This is an experiment: the point is to find out whether the DCP path actually holds at 0.005 in CI. If it flakes, the measured headroom tells us either to keep 0.01 with a comment recording why (the way the mamba case documents its own 0.003 → 0.005 bump) or that there is real divergence worth chasing. ## Modifications One line: `kl_threshold` 0.01 → 0.005 in `test/registered/radix_cache/unified_radix_tree/test_unified_radix_cache_kl_dcp.py`. No source changes. ## Accuracy Tests No model-output changes. The case is registered as `stage="extra-b"`, `runner_config="4-gpu-b200"`, so it needs the extra CI stage to actually exercise the new threshold. ## Speed Tests and Profiling N/A — test threshold only. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32446478926](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32446478926)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32446478822](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32446478822)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32446478978](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32446478978)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [BugFix][DP] Prevent health checks from perturbing user request routing
signal.text: ## Motivation Generation health checks (`HEALTH_CHECK_*`) are intentionally skipped by the scheduler while normal inference is already making progress. Under DP serving, however, the request passes through `DataParallelController` before that scheduler-side skip. With `round_robin`, a generation health request currently advances the same dispatch state used by user requests. For load-aware methods, it can also participate in the user load-budget refresh/update path. This means a health request that is later discarded can still perturb user-request ownership across DP ranks. In a long-prefill DP-Attention workload, this produced a reproducible scheduling failure chain: ```text generation health request -> user LB state is mutated -> per-rank user ownership becomes uneven -> some DP ranks become idle while peers continue prefill -> PrefillDelayer sees persistent mixed states / timeout -> effective concurrency and throughput drop ``` The root-cause investigation is tracked in #35241. ## Modifications This PR isolates generation-health dispatch state from user load-balancing state in `DataParallelController`: - Detect generation health requests before normal user LB dispatch. - Use an independent round-robin counter for health requests. - Do not refresh or mutate the user `DPBudget` for health-only dispatches. - For batch generate, refresh the user load budget only when the batch contains a user request. - Preserve explicit `routed_dp_rank` behavior. - Preserve `FOLLOW_BOOTSTRAP_ROOM` semantics for PD/disaggregated serving, since that path uses request-specific routing rather than shared mutable user LB state. This PR does **not** change DP Attention, PrefillDelayer, scheduler busy-health skip behavior, or the health endpoint semantics. ## Regression Tests Added CPU unit coverage for: - independent user-RR and health-RR state; - health dispatch using only active workers; - explicit `routed_dp_rank` not advancing health RR state; - health dispatch bypassing user load-budget refresh; - health-only batch dispatch not refreshing user load state; - `FOLLOW_BOOTSTRAP_ROOM` health routing compatibility. ```text python3 -m pytest test/registered/unit/managers/test_data_parallel_controller.py -q 23 passed git diff --check clean pre-commit run --files \ python/sglang/srt/managers/data_parallel_controller.py \ test/registered/unit/managers/test_data_parallel_controller.py all passed ``` ## Runtime Validation Validated on 8x NVIDIA B300 with DeepSeek-V4-Pro, TP8/DP8, DP Attention, MegaMoE, PrefillDelayer, round-robin routing, 8k effective prefill chunk, C16/N160, 60k input / 1 output. The external watchdog continued issuing generation health checks during the patched runs. | Configuration | Input TPS | avg running | HEALTH at DPC | IDLE-while-EXTEND | Delayer timeout | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | Original + generation health ON (observed HIT) | 76,417 | 6.84 | 59 | 33 | 9 | | Original + generation health OFF | 94,720-94,974 | 8.55-8.76 | 0 | 0 | 0 | | Patched + generation health ON, 4/4 runs | 94,372-94,822 | 8.60-8.69 | 49-51 | 0 | 0 | All patched runs completed 160/160 requests with no fatal errors. Generation-health traffic remained present at DPC, while the user-ownership hole and associated concurrency collapse disappeared. This is a scoped validation for the tested failure family; it is not intended to claim that generation health is the cause of every low-throughput state. ## Scope The intended invariant is: > Generation health traffic must not mutate the load-balancing state used by user requests when it is routed through DP serving. This PR does not make round-robin load-aware and does not change the configured load-balancing policy. Related: #35241 <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32445999557](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32445999557)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32445998878](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32445998878)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32445999010](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32445999010)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [Bug] PrefillDelayer can enter a persistent mixed-state feedback loop and collapse prefill progress under DP Attention + chunked prefill
signal.text: ### Checklist - [x] I searched related issues / PRs and did not find one matching this exact failure mode. - [x] The issue is reproducible across repeated runs with the same server/client configuration. - [x] Requests complete successfully; this is primarily a scheduler / performance-stability issue rather than a model-correctness failure. - [x] I compared the behavior against `PrefillDelayer` disabled and inspected the relevant scheduler / delayer source code. - [x] I collected per-DP-rank scheduler metrics and prefill-progress counters. --- ## Summary Under a long-prefill workload with: - DeepSeek-V4-Pro - TP=8 - DP=8 - DP Attention enabled - chunked prefill enabled - PrefillDelayer enabled - one 8-GPU node an identical server configuration and deterministic workload can enter two qualitatively different runtime regimes: ### Healthy synchronized state - Input throughput: ~94.6–94.8k tok/s - DP ranks progress through prefill nearly in lockstep - `PrefillDelayer` converges to sustained `all / no_wait` - average running requests is ~8.5 ### Pathological LOW state - Input throughput: ~62–79k tok/s - within the first ~5 s of the formal workload, DP-rank prefill progress diverges by an integer number of effective prefill chunks - the first observed spread is typically exactly **16384 tokens**, i.e. one effective per-rank chunk - `PrefillDelayer` remains dominated by `mixed / delay` - average running requests collapses to ~0.15 - residual / under-filled prefill batches increase sharply This is not explained by persistent per-rank request-count imbalance. In one representative LOW run, the first 30 s admitted exactly the same number of sequences on all 8 DP ranks, yet rank-level prefill progress had already diverged by one full chunk within 5 s. Disabling `PrefillDelayer` does **not** recover the healthy state. Instead, the system enters a third regime with lower but more continuous concurrency: - throughput: ~48–68k tok/s - avg running requests: ~4.7–5.9 - residual batches: ~11–14% Therefore the LOW state with PrefillDelayer enabled is not equivalent to "PrefillDelayer disabled". It appears to be a distinct scheduler regime in which the delayer participates in suppressing prefill progress. The exact upstream trigger is still being localized. I am opening this issue because the observed `mixed/delay` feedback loop appears different from the already-known `all/slot_condition` starvation fixed in #29898. --- ## Environment ```text SGLang version : 0.5.14 commit : 49e384ce9d304648e9959666ecb8ce8cd98d0deb git log -1 : 49e384c [Cherry-pick to release/v0.5.14] Revert Gemma4 modelopt fp4 MoE backend change (#28347) (#29246) git describe : v0.5.14 remote : https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang.git local patches : no tracked-file modifications ``` The earlier scheduler-debug instrumentation was fully reverted before the measurements described here. The remaining untracked files were only local backup files / an empty accidental file; tracked scheduler source matched the clean release tree. Hardware / topology: ```text 1 node 8 × NVIDIA B30Z TP = 8 DP = 8 DP Attention = enabled MoE A2A backend = MegaMoE ``` Relevant server configuration: ```bash --tp 8 --dp 8 --enable-dp-attention --enable-prefill-delayer --chunked-prefill-size 131072 ``` With DP Attention, the effective per-rank prefill chunk is: ```text 131072 / 8 = 16384 tokens ``` Relevant MegaMoE cap: ```bash SGLANG_OPT_DEEPGEMM_MEGA_MOE_NUM_MAX_TOKENS_PER_RANK=16512 ``` Workload: ```text input length : 60000 output length : 1 max concurrency : 16 num prompts : 160 ignore_eos : true seed : 1 ``` The 60k prompt is therefore processed approximately as: ```text 16384 + 16384 + 16384 + remainder ``` The client workload is burst-style; no request-rate throttling or intentional staggering is used in the baseline. --- ## Reproduction behavior Representative post-reboot runs: | Run | Input TPS | Median TTFT | avg running | avg queue | residual batches | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | good | 94,634 | 9.66 s | 8.13 | 0.16 | 11.96% | | LOW | 72,923 | 12.38 s | 0.17 | 0.84 | 27.17% | | LOW | 62,379 | 13.81 s | 0.12 | 0.85 | 29.03% | | good | 94,690 | 9.65 s | 8.37 | 0.17 | 9.52% | | mid | 82,688 | 9.68 s | 5.90 | 0.29 | 12.81% | | LOW | 78,571 | 10.45 s | 0.24 | 0.84 | 28.41% | The healthy-state throughput is extremely stable (~94.6k tok/s, sub-percent variation), while LOW runs have a qualitatively different scheduler signature rather than ordinary run-to-run noise. A host reboot did not eliminate the problem. --- ## Observation 1: LOW starts as a rank-level prefill-progress divergence Using the per-rank counter: ```text sglang:realtime_tokens_total{dp_rank="...", mode="prefill_compute"} ``` I computed: ```text progress_spread(t) = max_i(prefill_tokens_i(t)) - min_i(prefill_tokens_i(t)) ``` Results: | Run | TPS | spread@5s | spread@10s | spread@15s | spread@20s | spread@30s | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | good | 94,634 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | | good | 94,690 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | | mid | 82,688 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | | LOW | 72,923 | 16k | 22k | 27k | 11k | 16k | | LOW | 62,379 | 16k | 16k | 60k | 60k | 60k | | LOW | 78,571 | 16k | 22k | 27k | 0 | 0 | The important feature is that the first LOW-state divergence is quantized at approximately: ```text 16384 tokens ``` which is exactly one effective prefill chunk. `realtime_tokens_total` is incremented from `report_prefill_stats()` after a prefill batch result is processed, so this metric represents completed/reported prefill progress. It does **not** by itself prove whether the original cause was scheduler suppression or slower GPU execution. ### Metric-cadence validation I separately validated the observable cadence of `realtime_tokens_total` using 0.2 s scrapes during a smaller N32/C16 run with the same 16k effective chunk. Across all ranks: ```text jump interval p50 = 1.397 s jump interval p95 = 1.535 s min interval = 0.401 s ``` Jump-size distribution: ```text 16384 ×112 (one full chunk) 11264 ×8 (tail chunks) 256 ×3 (small startup fragments) 32768 ×0 (no two-chunk merge observed) ``` Thus the progress-spread observation is not an artifact of multiple 16k completions being collapsed into one scrape sample in this validation run. --- ## Observation 2: persistent request-count imbalance is not required for LOW I counted per-rank `#new-seq` admissions during the first 30 s of the formal workload. | Run | r0 | r1 | r2 | r3 | r4 | r5 | r6 | r7 | range | CV | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | good | 26 | 26 | 26 | 26 | 26 | 27 | 26 | 26 | 1 | 1.4% | | good | 26 | 25 | 25 | 25 | 25 | 25 | 25 | 26 | 1 | 1.8% | | mid | 27 | 26 | 26 | 26 | 26 | 26 | 26 | 26 | 1 | 1.4% | | LOW | 18 | 18 | 18 | 18 | 18 | 18 | 18 | 18 | **0** | **0.0%** | | LOW | 18 | 18 | 18 | 18 | 17 | 17 | 18 | 18 | 1 | 2.6% | | LOW | 14 | 15 | 10 | 14 | 10 | 14 | 13 | 14 | 5 | 14.8% | The strongest case is the 72.9k TPS LOW run: ```text 18 18 18 18 18 18 18 18 ``` All eight ranks admitted exactly the same number of sequences during the first 30 s, yet prefill progress had already diverged by one 16k chunk at 5 s. Therefore persistent per-rank request-count imbalance is not a necessary condition for entering the LOW state. Sub-second request-arrival / dispatch timing skew is **not** ruled out by this measurement. Also, `#new-seq` is scheduler admission into a prefill batch, not a direct counter of the initial DataParallelController request dispatch. --- ## Observation 3: PrefillDelayer state strongly separates healthy and LOW runs From: ```text sglang:prefill_delayer_outcomes_total ``` healthy runs eventually converge to sustained: ```text input_estimation="all" output_reason="no_wait" ``` while LOW runs remain dominated by: ```text input_estimation="mixed" output_reason="delay" ``` In healthy runs, after an initial transient, `mixed/delay` can disappear for long intervals and all 8 ranks repeatedly observe an immediately releasable state. In LOW runs, `mixed/delay` remains persistent and the scheduler never establishes the same synchronized regime. I use: ```text all_no_wait / (all_no_wait + mixed_delay) ``` only as a diagnostic state index, not as a literal request-release probability, because `mixed/delay` may be counted repeatedly across multiple scheduler passes during one waiting episode. The observed behavior is best described as synchronization / phase-locking-like behavior; I am not claiming a formal oscillator model. --- ## Observation 4: LOW is not equivalent to disabling PrefillDelayer I ran a separate six-run experiment with the same 16k effective chunk but with PrefillDelayer disabled. | Run | Input TPS | avg running | residual batches | median TTFT | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 1 | 67,658 | 5.65 | 11.78% | 12.62 s | | 2 | 48,536 | 4.73 | 12.01% | 15.11 s | | 3 | 53,299 | 5.26 | 11.18% | 15.43 s | | 4 | 64,174 | 5.36 | 12.24% | 13.29 s | | 5 | 55,500 | 4.69 | 14.04% | 15.70 s | | 6 | 64,715 | 5.90 | 12.02% | 13.10 s | Mean throughput: ```text 58,980 tok/s CV = 12.88% ``` The important mechanism difference is: ```text PrefillDelayer ON, healthy : avg running ≈ 8.5 PrefillDelayer ON, deep LOW: avg running ≈ 0.15 PrefillDelayer OFF : avg running ≈ 4.7–5.9 ``` Thus the ON-LOW state is not simply the delayer becoming ineffective and behaving like OFF. The delayer-enabled LOW regime suppresses running concurrency far more aggressively than the OFF regime. This OFF experiment was not interleaved with the ON runs, so I do **not** use it to estimate relative state-entry probabilities. I also do not claim six samples prove a statistically unimodal OFF distribution. The robust observation is the mechanism-signature difference above. --- ## Observation 5: staggered arrivals make the failure worse As a diagnostic experiment, I changed the formal client traffic from a burst to: ```text 2 requests/s, fixed interval ``` while keeping concurrency=16. This was intentionally stopped after the direction was clearly harmful. Representative results: ```text burst: 94,630 tok/s ramp : 53,449 tok/s burst: 64,016 tok/s ramp : LOW again ``` The ramp sends approximately one new request every 0.5 s. With DP=8 this naturally exposes only a subset of ranks to new work at a time, increasing the probability that the delayer observes a `mixed` state. This is not presented as a production benchmark because the arrival process itself changed. It is included because the behavior is consistent with the delayer being highly sensitive to cross-rank arrival phase. Related newer work such as #35191 independently discusses trickle arrivals and persistent fragmented prefills, although that PR operates on a newer optional queue-trigger path that is not enabled in this configuration. --- ## Local source comparison against later upstream fixes I compared this exact `v0.5.14` tree against several later PrefillDelayer / scheduler fixes. ### 1. #29898 — missing locally The local `PrefillDelayer` has a bounded delay in the `mixed` branch: ```python prev_delayed_count = prev_state.delayed_count if prev_state else 0 if prev_delayed_count < self._max_delay_passes - 1: ... output_reason="delay" else: ... output_reason="wait_timeout" ``` but its `all` branch can still delay indefinitely when `slot_condition` or `queue_condition` remains true: ```python if slot_condition or queue_condition: ... next_state = next_state.bump_delayed_count() return _NegotiateOutput( output_allow=False, output_reason="delay", ... ) ``` with no equivalent `max_delay_passes` bound. This confirms that the local tree predates #29898. However, I do **not** claim #29898 is the direct cause here: in the collected workload, `all/delay` was not observed; the pathological state is dominated by `mixed/delay`. Its relevance is that upstream has independently confirmed that PrefillDelayer feedback can cause prefill starvation and running-batch collapse. --- ### 2. #31835 — current reproduction hits the older negotiation placement The local `schedule_policy.py` contains two paths: ```text add_one_req_ignore_eos() -> negotiation after budget/admission checks add_one_req() -> negotiation at the beginning of the function ``` The dispatch condition is: ```python if req.sampling_params.ignore_eos and getattr(self.tree_cache, "disable", True): return self.add_one_req_ignore_eos(req) ``` This reproduction has: ```text ignore_eos = true radix cache enabled -> tree_cache.disable = false ``` so the condition is false and the workload falls through to `add_one_req()`. In the local tree, `add_one_req()` begins with: ```python if (self.prefill_delayer_single_pass is not None) and ( not self.prefill_delayer_single_pass.negotiate_should_allow_prefill( local_prefillable=True, running_batch=self.running_batch.batch_size(), max_prefill_bs=self.max_prefill_bs, max_running_requests=self.max_running_requests, waiting_queue_len=self.waiting_queue_len, ) ): return AddReqResult.OTHER ``` before later request / chunk / admission checks. Therefore, on the actual reproduction path, `local_prefillable=True` is sampled before all subsequent admission checks. The alternate `add_one_req_ignore_eos()` path samples after budget checks, so the two paths have different semantics. This is directly relevant to interpretation of `all/mixed`: `local_prefillable` is a scheduler-side estimate whose meaning depends on where it is sampled, not a direct GPU-readiness signal. That said, I do **not** currently think this semantic issue alone explains the LOW state. In the failing workload, KV/SWA pressure is very low (observed full-pool usage ~0.55%, SWA usage ~2.74%), so most post-negotiation admission checks are unlikely to fail. The placement issue is therefore real in this path but not yet demonstrated to be the active trigger. --- ### 3. #30295 — key chunked-request double-count shape is still present The local scheduler already contains an early guard: ```python if ( self.get_num_allocatable_reqs(running_bs) <= 0 and self.chunked_req is None ... ): ``` but the later waiting-queue loop still contains: ```python if len(adder.can_run_list) >= self.get_num_allocatable_reqs(running_bs): self.running_batch.batch_is_full = True ``` while `add_chunked_req(...)` adds the in-flight chunked request to `self.can_run_list`, and `get_num_allocatable_reqs()` uses: ```python min( pp_max_micro_batch_size - running_bs, req_to_token_pool.available_size(), ) ``` where the in-flight request's slot is already reflected in `available_size()`. This preserves the shape of the later double-count fixed by #30295. I do not think this alone explains the reported collapse: #30295 causes a stable one-slot loss, whereas the LOW state here collapses avg running from approximately 8.5 to approximately 0.15. It may still be an adjacent bug or amplification factor. --- ### 4. #24768 — present locally, but current configuration uses CPU/Gloo negotiation The local tree contains the NCCL/device-group option for PrefillDelayer synchronization. With the current settings: ```text disable_overlap_schedule = false SGLANG_NCCL_ALL_GATHER_IN_OVERLAP_SCHEDULER_SYNC_BATCH = false ``` PrefillDelayer uses the CPU/Gloo negotiation path. Enabling the NCCL synchronization path in this MegaMoE configuration was not stable in my environment and led to an NVLink/barrier timeout, so it is not currently usable as a workaround. If the failure is ultimately localized to scheduler/readiness coordination, this cross-DP negotiation path is one area I plan to investigate further. --- ### 5. #35191 — not directly active, but relevant to the dynamics This newer work describes a separate PrefillDelayer problem where trickle arrivals can keep the observed batching target small and sustain fragmented prefills. The optional queue-trigger feature involved there is not enabled in this workload (`queue_min_ratio` unset), so this is not a direct code-path match. It is nevertheless consistent with the observation here that staggered arrivals strongly destabilize synchronized prefill behavior. --- ## Current interpretation The strongest evidence currently supports this descriptive sequence: ```text formal workload begins ↓ DP ranks initially receive approximately balanced request counts ↓ within the first few seconds, per-rank prefill progress diverges by an integer prefill-chunk amount ↓ PrefillDelayer repeatedly observes mixed states ↓ mixed/delay persists ↓ under-filled / residual batches increase ↓ running concurrency collapses ↓ LOW throughput state becomes self-sustaining ``` One causal distinction is still unresolved: ### Hypothesis B — execution-duration divergence One or more ranks receive comparable forward work but their GPU forward takes longer: ```text same/similar forward opportunity ↓ one rank completes later ↓ prefill progress diverges ↓ Delayer subsequently observes mixed ``` ### Hypothesis C — scheduler/readiness suppression The scheduler / delayer gives some ranks fewer forward opportunities: ```text scheduler readiness / negotiation diverges ↓ Delayer suppresses some prefill admissions ↓ those ranks do less forward work ↓ prefill progress diverges ``` I am instrumenting: ```text sglang:realtime_tokens_total{dp_rank,mode="prefill_compute"} ``` together with: ```text sglang:forward_execution_seconds_total{dp_rank,category} ``` using `SGLANG_ENABLE_METRICS_DEVICE_TIMER=1`. The DeviceTimer implementation uses CUDA events plus non-blocking `end_event.query()` rather than `synchronize()`, but I am first validating that enabling the timer itself does not perturb this timing-sensitive synchronization state. The intended discriminator is **not** event timestamp ordering, because Delayer negotiation necessarily precedes forward completion in the source code. Instead, the discriminator is the per-rank relationship between: ```text Δprefill_progress and Δcompleted_forward_execution_time ``` over a short window after the first rank-level progress divergence. Roughly: ```text ΔP lower and ΔF proportionally lower → rank likely completed less forward work → supports scheduler/readiness-side cause ΔP lower but ΔF similar or higher → rank spent comparable/more GPU time for less progress → supports execution-duration-side cause ``` This follow-up work is ongoing and is not required for the observations reported above. --- ## Why I think this deserves a separate issue I could not find an upstream issue matching all of these properties together: ```text DP Attention + PrefillDelayer + chunked long-prefill workload + same deterministic configuration + healthy ~94.8k state vs persistent LOW state + LOW dominated by mixed/delay + avg running collapsing near zero + rank progress diverging by exactly one effective prefill chunk + request-count admission remaining balanced in at least one LOW reproduction ``` #29898 is the closest known failure family, but it is specifically an `all / slot_condition` liveness bug. The behavior reported here appears to be a different `mixed`-branch feedback failure mode. --- ## Questions for maintainers 1. Is a persistent `mixed/delay` loop with very low `num_running_reqs` an expected / known failure mode of PrefillDelayer? 2. Are there known cases where the cross-DP `local_prefillable` negotiation can remain phase-shifted even when request counts are balanced across DP ranks? 3. Is there a known interaction between chunked prefill, an in-flight `chunked_req`, `can_run_list`, `batch_is_full`, and PrefillDelayer state that can create a self-reinforcing mixed state? 4. Would you expect #29898 / #31835 / #30295 to materially change this workload even though the observed state is primarily `mixed/delay` rather than `all/delay`? 5. Is there a recommended way to trace the first divergence between per-rank PrefillDelayer negotiation, prefill admission, and model-forward execution without materially perturbing scheduler timing? --- ## Additional data available I retained: - per-run server logs - per-rank Prefill batch logs - `#new-seq` / `#new-token` traces - 0.2 s Prometheus cadence captures - per-rank `realtime_tokens_total` - PrefillDelayer outcome counters - queue/running-request counters - host/GPU telemetry - good-state and LOW-state profiling artifacts I can provide a reduced reproduction package or additional per-rank timelines if useful.

signal.title: [XPU] Add diffusion server test config for Intel XPU B60
signal.text: ## Motivation **Let the `multimodal_gen` diffusion server tests run on Intel XPU with correct expectations.** The diffusion server tests compare generated images against committed ground-truth images and check stage timings against committed perf baselines. Both sets of reference values are CUDA-derived, and neither is reachable from XPU today: - `get_consistency_platform()` has no XPU branch, so an XPU run silently falls through to the `h100` thresholds. - `BASELINE_CONFIG` composes per-platform perf overrides for Ascend and MUSA, but there is no XPU entry. The image mismatch is not a correctness bug. XPU seeds its initial latent noise from a different RNG stream than CUDA, so the pixels cannot match bit-for-bit: the image stays semantically identical (CLIP remains high) while `ssim` / `psnr` / `mean_abs_diff` degrade. Comparing XPU output against CUDA thresholds therefore fails on a difference that carries no signal. This PR adds XPU as a first-class platform in both registries, following the existing Ascend and MUSA pattern. ## Modifications Purely additive: 4 files, 56 insertions, 0 deletions. - **`test/test_utils.py`** — register `intel_xpu_b60` in `CONSISTENCY_THRESHOLD_FILE_BY_PLATFORM`, add the `intelxpub60` alias, and add the `current_platform.is_xpu()` branch to `get_consistency_platform()`. - **`test/server/consistency_thresholds/intel_xpu_b60.json`** — XPU consistency thresholds for `qwen_image_t2i_2_gpus` and `fsdp-inference`. - **`test/server/xpu/perf_baselines_xpu.json`** — XPU perf baselines for `fsdp-inference`, measured on Intel Arc Pro B60 (22.71 GiB per card). - **`test/server/testcase_configs.py`** — chain the XPU baseline file into `BASELINE_CONFIG`, alongside the existing Ascend and MUSA `.update()` calls. No CUDA path changes: both new files are read only when the resolved platform is XPU, and the two registry additions are new keys. ## Thresholds | case | clip | ssim | psnr | mean_abs_diff | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `fsdp-inference` | 0.97 | 0.6 | 11.0 | 37.0 | | `qwen_image_t2i_2_gpus` | 0.98 | 0.79 | 15.7 | 17.2 | Only these two cases were measured on XPU hardware. signal.title: [PP + HiCache] HiCache Consistency Fix Plan
signal.text: # PP HiCache Consistency for Disaggregated Prefill — PR Plan ## Background ### Motivation In agentic and long-context reasoning scenarios, requests frequently share long prefixes (system prompts, tool definitions, multi-turn history) that can span tens of thousands of tokens. Recomputing these shared prefixes for every request is prohibitively expensive. SGLang's **HiCache** addresses this with a 3-level KV cache hierarchy — **L1** (GPU device memory) → **L2** (CPU host memory) → **L3** (external distributed storage, e.g. Mooncake) — enabling prefix reuse across requests and even across restarts via persistent storage. Meanwhile, large models (e.g. DeepSeek-V3 with 60 layers) require **Pipeline Parallelism (PP)** to split layers across multiple GPU groups, combined with **disaggregated prefill** where prefill and decode run on separate server pools. This PP + HiCache + disaggregated prefill stack is critical for production agentic workloads: it maximizes both throughput (via disaggregation) and cache hit rates (via L3 persistence) on large models. However, combining PP with L3 storage introduces a class of consistency bugs that do not exist in simpler configurations. Understanding why requires examining the cache hierarchy level by level. ### Why L3 Storage Breaks PP Consistency In PP mode, each rank runs an independent scheduler with its own radix tree. The key question is: why does adding L3 cause divergence when L1 and L2 alone do not? **L1-only + PP (no HiCache)**: Both ranks receive the same requests in the same order via P2P. `match_prefix` operates on the device radix tree, which is fully deterministic — insert and evict are driven by the same batch picks, and all operations are synchronous within each scheduler cycle. **No divergence possible.** **L1 + L2 + PP (HiCache without storage)**: Adding the host cache introduces `write-through` (GPU→CPU backup) and `load-back` (CPU→GPU restore). These are still **synchronous** operations within each cycle — `writing_check()` and `loading_check()` are called at deterministic points in the event loop, and the host tree mutations they produce are driven by the same batch sequence. ~~**No divergence possible.**~~ There is a small probability of matched_host mismatch!!! **L1 + L2 + L3 + PP (HiCache with storage)**: Adding L3 storage introduces the **prefetch thread** — an asynchronous background thread that queries external storage independently on each rank. This is where consistency breaks: 1. **Async completion timing**: PP0 and PP1's prefetch threads may complete at different wall-clock times. When PP0's prefetch finishes first, it inserts nodes into its host tree immediately, while PP1's tree has not yet been updated. The next `match_prefix` on each rank sees different host tree states → different `host_hit_length` → different `prefix_indices`. 2. **Anchor divergence**: The L3 query uses a hash chain starting from an anchor node in the host tree. If PP0 has already inserted nodes from a previous prefetch (giving it `host_hit=896`), its anchor and token range differ from PP1's (which has `host_hit=0`). The two ranks compute **completely different hash chains** for the same request → fetch different (or wrong) data from storage. 3. **Eviction divergence from wall-clock LRU**: Even after fixing async finalization (making PP1 event-driven), the eviction layer itself can diverge. LRU eviction uses `last_access_time = time.monotonic()`, which differs by microseconds between ranks → different victim node selection → different GPU→CPU demotion → different host memory pressure → different `evictable_host_leaves` candidate sets. In production (PP2 + NSA + disagg prefill), this caused: PP0 finalized a prefetch → inserted host node → immediately triggered `evict_host` (memory pressure) → evicted the node. PP1 replayed the same finalize event one cycle later → inserted the node → no eviction pressure → node remained. Result: PP0 `matched_host=0`, PP1 `matched_host=17664` → shape mismatch crash. 4. **Amplification cascade**: Once the host tree diverges (even by one node), all subsequent operations compound the difference — different eviction decisions, different write-through timing, different prefetch anchors for the next request — until a shape mismatch crash occurs. In essence: **L1 and L2 operations are synchronous and deterministic within each cycle, but L3 prefetch is asynchronous and state-dependent. The async completion timing, state-dependent query parameters, and wall-clock-dependent eviction ordering create a feedback loop where small divergences amplify into crashes.** ## Solution Architecture thanks @stepinto ### Three Communication Channels (Three Edge Types) ① PG1 — green bidirectional (between prefetch_thread) - Uses prefetch_sync_groups, gloo (CPU) backend, members = TP+CP+PP - Handles `#1` : global MIN over storage_hit_count - Bidirectional arrow = a truly symmetric all_reduce; all ranks participate equally and obtain the same hit count ② PG2 — purple bidirectional (between prefetch_sync_thread) - Uses prefetch_sync_groups2, also gloo, members = TP+CP+PP - Handles `#2`: global MIN over completed_tokens - Likewise a symmetric all_reduce ③ Scheduler-thread _all_reduce — directional (between Scheduler loops, PP0→PP1→PP2) - Handles `#3`/ `#4`/ `#5`/ `#6` (terminate MAX, qsize MIN, finish MIN) - Different mechanism: first reduces within the local stage's TP/CP group via GLOO, then uses _pp_sync point-to-point to overwrite downstream ranks with PP0's result - Directional arrow = not a symmetric reduce, but PP0 single-point decision + downstream broadcast ### Why Split It This Finely (Key Design Intent) 1. PG1 and PG2 have identical members, yet two sets are created — because `#1` and `#2` run on two different background threads. The same gloo communicator cannot be used for concurrent all_reduce from two threads (it would corrupt/deadlock), so each gets its own set. 2. Background uses gloo, while the scheduler-thread set mixes NCCL+P2P — gloo is CPU communication, isolated from the scheduler thread's CUDA collectives, preventing background all_reduce from blocking GPU computation. 3. The two categories have different semantics: - ①② are symmetric global MIN — pulling each rank's progress into alignment (whoever is slowest wins) - ③ is PP0 directional broadcast — termination timing / drain counts decided uniformly by the leader ## Work In Progress - [X] need cp sync https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/20460 - [x] https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/27285 FIx L2 - [ ] https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/27010 Fix L3 - [x] https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/29106 - [x] https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/25887 - [x] https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/29258 - [x] https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/30476 - [x] https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/28379 - [x] https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/31869 - [ ] A important debugging feature by @stepinto god : https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/34406 - [ ] https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/34815 Special thanks to @ShangmingCai @hzh0425 @stepinto for their guidance on the HiCache architecture, PP synchronization design, and code review throughout this effort. signal.title: Support deepseek v4 and kimi k3 on ssd
signal.text: # [Feature] Add SSD-backed Expert Pack inference for DeepSeek-V4-Flash and Kimi-K3 ## Summary This PR adds an opt-in SSD-backed inference path for **DeepSeek-V4-Flash** and **Kimi-K3**. It allows these MoE models to run when their complete weights are larger than GPU VRAM and host RAM combined. Routed expert weights are stored on SSD and loaded only when selected by the router. The implementation uses: - an expert-major **Expert Pack** layout for efficient random access; - direct I/O into aligned pinned host buffers; - asynchronous host-to-device transfers; and - a byte-budgeted LFU/LRU GPU cache for frequently used experts. The runtime does not prune, merge, skip, replace, or re-quantize experts, and does not reduce Expert Top-K. The default `auto`, `safetensors`, and `gguf` loading paths remain unchanged; SSD execution is enabled only through the explicit `expert_pack` path. ## Supported Scope `ExpertPackModelLoader` is selected only with `--load-format expert_pack`. Official checkpoints loaded through the standard `auto` or `safetensors` paths never enter this loader. The currently validated DeepSeek input is the single-file MXFP4 GGUF used by `frob/deepseek-v4-flash-0731:latest`. Its routed expert matrices use `MXFP4`; the large non-routed matrices are mostly `Q8_0`, router input weights are `BF16`, and the inventory also contains `F32` and `I32` normalization or auxiliary tensors. The inspected GGUF contains 129 `MXFP4`, 512 `Q8_0`, 43 `BF16`, 641 `F32`, and 3 `I32` tensors. It contains no FP8 tensors. The other validated input is the text-only 38-shard `KIMI-K3-MXP4-DERISKED-Q2_K-*.gguf`, whose routed experts use Q2_K for gate/up and Q3_K for down. The Kimi launcher extracts the official `text_config` into a flat `KimiLinearConfig`; the complete multimodal Kimi-K3 checkpoint is not supported by this loader. Other GGUF quantization variants have not been validated and are not currently claimed as supported. ## Usage Install this branch from source before running the examples: ```bash python3 -m pip install -e "python" ``` ### DeepSeek-V4-Flash The tested MXFP4 GGUF is available as [`frob/deepseek-v4-flash-0731:latest`](https://ollama.com/frob/deepseek-v4-flash-0731), which was imported from [`unsloth/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-GGUF`](https://huggingface.co/unsloth/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-GGUF). The benchmark used the immutable Ollama model blob with SHA-256 `947ac34c08c0e5c5752ac76398f934b3b6b4075cfe915ba43dd5ac754900a4cd`. ```bash python3 examples/runtime/deepseek_v4/benchmark_deepseek_5090.py \ --gguf /path/to/deepseek-v4-flash-0731-mxfp4.gguf \ --prompt "Explain why the sky appears blue." \ --max-new-tokens 200 ``` ### Kimi-K3 Download all 38 Q2_K GGUF shards from [`Blackfrost-AI/KIMI-K3-Q2_K-GGUF-ABLITERATED`](https://huggingface.co/Blackfrost-AI/KIMI-K3-Q2_K-GGUF-ABLITERATED). Also place the tokenizer/config files from [`moonshotai/Kimi-K3`](https://huggingface.co/moonshotai/Kimi-K3) in a sibling directory named `kimi-k3-tokenizer`. ```bash hf download Blackfrost-AI/KIMI-K3-Q2_K-GGUF-ABLITERATED \ --include "KIMI-K3-MXP4-DERISKED-Q2_K-*.gguf" \ --local-dir /path/to/kimi-k3 ``` ```bash python3 examples/runtime/kimi_k3/benchmark_kimi_k3_5090.py \ --gguf /path/to/kimi-k3/KIMI-K3-MXP4-DERISKED-Q2_K-00001-of-00038.gguf \ --prompt "Explain why the sky appears blue." \ --max-new-tokens 200 ``` The first shard is only the entrypoint. The launcher automatically discovers and uses all 38 shards in the same directory. Both launchers derive the remaining paths automatically. If the Expert Pack is missing, it is built on the first launch and reused afterward. | Model | First Expert Pack build | Approximate first-run readiness | | --- | ---: | ---: | | DeepSeek-V4-Flash | Estimated **5-10 minutes** on the benchmark NVMe SSD | **8-15 minutes** | | Kimi-K3 | **29 minutes 42 seconds measured** | **35-45 minutes** | The 38 Kimi-K3 source shards and generated Expert Pack occupy approximately 1.814 TiB in total, so a 4 TB SSD is recommended for practical headroom. ## Correctness - DeepSeek-V4-Flash produced semantically equivalent answers to Ollama across travel planning, science, history, programming, and mathematics prompts. - Kimi-K3 matched the 200-token SGLang reference output exactly. All 92 routed layers executed Top-16 experts with `fallback_count=0` and `io_errors=0`. ## Performance The target platform is one RTX 5090 with 32 GB VRAM, 32 GB host RAM, and NVMe SSD storage. The retained measurements were collected on RTX 5090 hosts; host RAM and SSD capacity differed between the two model runs. ### DeepSeek-V4-Flash vs Ollama Five prompts were measured with 200 generated tokens per prompt. | Metric | SGLang | Ollama | Result | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | Prefill | 3.265 token/s | 1.457 token/s | **2.24x faster** | | Decode | 2.020 token/s | 1.354 token/s | **1.49x faster** | ### Kimi-K3 vs llama.cpp The SGLang run used a 91-token prompt and generated 200 tokens. | Metric | SGLang | llama.cpp | Result | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | Prefill | 0.66412 token/s | 0.11289 token/s | **5.88x faster** | | Decode | 0.44830 token/s | 0.1810 token/s | **2.48x faster** | The llama.cpp decode baseline came from an earlier 50-token run, so the 2.48x decode figure is indicative rather than a strict equal-length comparison.

signal.title: fix(test): deflake zmq load-snapshot round-trip tests
signal.text: ## Motivation `test/registered/unit/managers/test_load_snapshot_backends.py` intermittently fails in CI, most visibly as: ``` ERROR: test_read_returns_latest (__main__.TestZmqRoundTrip) AssertionError: 8 != 9 ``` The `TestZmqRoundTrip` and `TestEndToEndZmqSimulation` cases each `write()` one or more snapshots and then wait a fixed `time.sleep(0.05)` before a single `read()` / `read_all()`. The zmq PUSH/PULL transport delivers asynchronously: once `write()` returns, the background IO thread may not yet have handed the message to the reader. Under CPU contention (e.g. the full CPU unit-test suite running on an 8‑vCPU agent), the last message can miss the 50 ms window, so the reader observes a stale value and the assertion fails. Because both sockets use `CONFLATE=1`, the latest message is guaranteed to arrive eventually — the fixed sleep is simply not a reliable synchronization point. ## Modifications Test-only change; no production code is touched. - Add a small `_read_until(read_fn, predicate, ...)` helper that polls the reader until the expected snapshot is observed or a bounded timeout elapses. This mirrors the existing `_warmup_zmq` polling idiom already used in this file. - Replace the fixed `time.sleep(0.05)` + single read in the four zmq round-trip tests (`test_single_rank_zmq_to_shm`, `test_multi_rank_zmq`, `test_read_returns_latest`, `test_full_flow_dp_size_2`) with `_read_until`. The assertions are unchanged and are not weakened: a backend that never surfaces the expected snapshot still fails — it just fails deterministically after the full timeout instead of flaking on a 50 ms race. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the Code Formatting with Pre-Commit (black clean; flake8 clean). - [x] Add unit tests as outlined in the Running Unit Tests (this PR fixes an existing unit test; no new behavior). - [ ] Update documentation / docstrings / example tutorials as needed (N/A — test-only). - [ ] Provide throughput / latency benchmark results (N/A — test-only). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32446302188](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32446302188)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32446302115](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32446302115)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32446302232](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32446302232)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [model-gateway] Add opt-in `fips` feature using the AWS-LC FIPS module
signal.text: ## Motivation Some deployments (government and other regulated environments) require all cryptography to come from a FIPS 140-3 validated module. This PR adds an opt-in `fips` cargo feature to sgl-model-gateway so those users can build a compliant gateway. Default builds are not affected. ## Modifications Behind the new `fips` feature (off by default): - rustls uses the AWS-LC FIPS provider instead of ring for all TLS (HTTPS server and the reqwest/kube outbound clients; tonic is built without TLS features and does no TLS itself). - JWT verification uses the jsonwebtoken AWS-LC backend. - The wasm module SHA-256 hash uses AWS-LC. - `aws-lc-fips-sys` uses a normal caret requirement (`0.14`) so builds pick up the latest AWS-LC FIPS release (currently 0.14.1, bundling AWS-LC FIPS 4.1.0). AWS-LC FIPS is a CMVP-validated module lineage (see [certificate #5314](https://csrc.nist.gov/projects/cryptographic-module-validation-program/certificate/5314) for the 3.x static module). The exact module version in any given build can be read from the binary with `strings <binary> | grep "AWS-LC FIPS"`. Deployments that need a version literally listed on an issued certificate can pin, for example `=0.13.11` (AWS-LC FIPS 3.1.0, the exact version on #5314). - At startup the gateway asserts the installed rustls provider is FIPS and that the AWS-LC JWT provider was installed. If not, it fails to start. - The Python and Go bindings expose the same `fips` feature. Changes that apply to all builds: - New `src/crypto.rs` with `ensure_crypto_provider_installed()`, which replaces the two previous ad-hoc `ring::default_provider().install_default()` call sites, and a `Sha256Hasher` wrapper used for wasm module hashing. Default builds keep ring and RustCrypto sha2. - `jsonwebtoken` upgraded 9.3 to 10.4 and `smg-auth` 1.0.0 to 1.2.2. jsonwebtoken 9 was hardwired to ring; version 10 has pluggable backends. Default builds use its `rust_crypto` backend. Not changed: blake3/xxhash (used for cache-aware routing and consistent hashing, not security relevant) and the openssl dependency (test cert generation and the optional `vendored-openssl` feature only). Build note: `--features fips` (and therefore `--all-features`, used by `make lint` and the rust CI lint job) needs cmake and Go to compile AWS-LC. The CI lint job passes since GitHub runners include both. <details> <summary>FIPS verification evidence</summary> - The fips binary embeds the AWS-LC FIPS module version string (checked with `strings`, currently `AWS-LC FIPS 4.1.0`); the default binary does not. - The fips binary starts cleanly and serves `/liveness` and `/health`. - TLS handshake against the fips build negotiates TLS 1.3 `TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384`. Forcing `TLS_CHACHA20_POLY1305_SHA256` (not FIPS approved) fails against the fips build and succeeds against the default build, showing the provider swap is active. - Known residual: ring and the jsonwebtoken RustCrypto backend remain linked (cargo features are additive) but are never selected at runtime, which the startup assertions enforce. smg-auth internally uses RustCrypto sha2 for API key fingerprinting; that code only runs when control plane API keys are configured. </details> ## Accuracy Tests N/A, no model or inference code touched. ## Speed Tests and Profiling N/A, default builds keep the same crypto stack. The fips path only affects opt-in builds. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). (`cargo test --test security_tests` passes 48/48 with and without `--features fips`, covering JWT auth, API keys, and mTLS. `cargo clippy --all-targets` is clean in both modes.) - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). (N/A, no model or inference code touched.) - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. signal.title: [Router] Add bounded consistent hashing with an absolute load gap
signal.text: Recommended review order: 1. Core policy and spill condition 2. HTTP active-load lifetime 3. Config and Python binding 4. Tests and documentation Fixes #33625 Supersedes #33791 This follow-up continues #33791 with permission from @waizuichougou. The original implementation commits are preserved with their authorship. Permission: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33791#issuecomment-5211652164 ## Summary - Keep `bounded_consistent_hashing` as an independent opt-in policy; strict `consistent_hashing` is completely unchanged. - Add the policy-specific configurable `min_load_gap`, measured in active requests. - Allow bounded spill only for an explicit `X-SMG-Routing-Key`, and only when both the absolute and relative load thresholds are exceeded. - Keep `X-SMG-Target-Worker` and implicit keys from `Authorization`, `X-Forwarded-For`, and `Cookie` strict. - In non-IGW mode, route over a cached aggregate ring containing both Regular and HTTP workers. - Rebuild that ring only when membership changes; the request hot path does not construct a ring. - Retain the preferred worker when no eligible spill candidate qualifies. - Track active load for the full streaming and non-streaming request lifecycle. ## Why existing policies do not cover this case This policy addresses a narrower contract than the existing alternatives: - `manual` with `assignment_mode=min_load` assigns a new routing key to the least-loaded worker and then stores that assignment in gateway-local mutable state. Separate gateway replicas cannot independently derive the same assignment without shared state. - `prefix_hash` hashes token prefixes and applies a ratio-only load factor. The regular Model Gateway HTTP path does not supply tokens, and its affinity key is not `X-SMG-Routing-Key`. - `cache_aware` detects fleet-wide max/min imbalance and switches to shortest-queue routing. It does not preserve deterministic routing-key placement or ring-order failover. - PR #31170 applies bounded affinity among native intra-instance DP ranks. It cannot select among independent backend workers behind Model Gateway. - Strict `consistent_hashing` remains unchanged for deployments where affinity is a correctness requirement rather than a cache-locality preference. ## Threshold rationale and limitations The two threshold terms intentionally use different references: - `preferred_load - min_healthy_load > min_load_gap` requires that moving the request can reduce active load by a meaningful absolute amount. - `preferred_load > mean_healthy_load * max_load_skew` requires that the preferred worker is an outlier relative to the healthy fleet. Using the minimum as the ratio denominator would be unstable whenever an idle worker has load zero. The parameter names are kept distinct from cache-aware `balance_abs_threshold` / `balance_rel_threshold` because the compared workers, selection behavior, and policy scope differ. Naming can be adjusted if the Model Gateway maintainers prefer a shared configuration vocabulary. **Limitations.** The load signal is local to each gateway process, so multiple gateway replicas may make different best-effort spill decisions. A spill also sacrifices worker-local KV locality and may require a cold prefill on the selected worker. This policy is therefore intended for cache-locality optimization only and must not be used when backend-local session state makes affinity a correctness requirement. ## Spill condition ```text preferred_load.saturating_sub(min_healthy_load) > min_load_gap && preferred_load > mean_healthy_load * max_load_skew ``` Both comparisons are strict. ## Two-worker HTTP A/B and default status The two-worker HTTP A/B comprised 5 repetitions, 20 cells, 400 groups, and 3,200 streaming requests. | Policy | Throughput vs strict | Mean TTFT | Placement | Spill | | ------ | -------------------------------: | ---------: | --------: | ----: | | strict | baseline | 3087.04 ms | 8:0 | N/A | | gap=1 | +2.330%, CI [1.016110, 1.035140] | 2684.51 ms | 6:2 | 25% | | gap=2 | +2.376%, CI [1.016512, 1.035208] | 2688.84 ms | 6:2 | 25% | | gap=4 | +2.099%, CI [1.012597, 1.031751] | 2694.72 ms | 6:2 | 25% | - All 3,200/3,200 requests returned HTTP 200 with matching output and no counter leakage. - Bounded routing changed the frozen eight-sibling placement from 8:0 to 6:2 and reduced mean TTFT by about 13%. - The cached-token fraction fell from 75.546% under strict routing to about 56.95%, while prefill compute increased by about 76%. - This explicitly trades cache reuse and prefill work for better load balance and latency. - Direct paired confidence intervals among gaps 1, 2, and 4 could not establish that any of the three settings differs from either of the others; all three converged to the same 25% spill and 6:2 placement. - The benchmark supports the bounded mechanism, but it does not support a claim that `min_load_gap=2` is optimal. The value 2 remains only a conservative, configurable middle default for this opt-in policy. The GPU A/B ran at SHA `10a3b95f510584174d8b8c661c7974b97d72291a`. The subsequent commits `75b73b0c5adc8c92b648caf984cd0cb28ab42877` and `356299712d1bc649efed655dc610838096b80d3a` contain only documentation/comment clarification and Black formatting; neither changes runtime semantics. ## Production signal and limitation hassellof reported successful affinity and a 3/2/1/2 placement during a storm drill: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/33625#issuecomment-5209076175 That drill did not record any diverts. It therefore did not exercise the gateway spill branch and is not a complete validation of spillover behavior. ## Validation - `cargo fmt --all -- --check` - `cargo check --locked --all-targets` - Bounded-policy Rust tests: 18 passed - Full Rust library: 414 passed - Load guard: 8 passed - Production Router→HTTP regression: 5 independent runs passed - Python: - 31 passed, 1 expected skip - 21 passed, 1 expected skip - 79 passed - Exact-SHA GPU A/B: 3,200/3,200 passed - Lint, Router, SMG benchmark, and current Base/platform CI passed - Any Draft-gated Extra workflow state reflects workflow gating or permissions, not a code failure - `git diff --check` - `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD` <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32352882706](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32352882706)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32352882467](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32352882467)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:heavy_minus_sign: **No AMD PR run found for this commit**.<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [Diffusion] Add MiniMax H3 cube sparse attention
signal.text: ## Summary - add a FlexAttention-based cube sparse attention backend for MiniMax H3's 3D visual streams - wire H3 packed-sequence metadata and denoise-step sparsity schedules into the native pipeline - keep text, audio, standalone reference images, and the text-only token refiner on dense attention - document the component-scoped command and add numerical, CUDA, admission, and parallelism coverage ## Behavior Select the backend only for the H3 transformer: ```bash --component-attention-backends transformer=cube_sparse_attn \ --attention-backend-config '{"local_cube_size":[4,4,4],"topk_ratio_list":[1.0,1.0,0.8,0.7,0.6,0.5,0.5]}' ``` A ratio of `1.0` uses H3's native FlashAttention path. Ratios below `1.0` use approximate cube sparsity. Ring parallelism is rejected because its attention exchange does not compose with this backend; Ulysses remains supported. ## Recommended `attention-backend-config` For `num_inference_steps=50` (49 denoise updates), use: ```json { "local_cube_size": [4, 4, 4], "topk_ratio_list": [ 1.0, 1.0, 0.55, 0.45, 0.35, 0.35, 0.30, 0.25, 0.25, 0.20, 0.20, 0.20, 0.15, 0.15, 0.15, 0.10, 0.10, 0.10, 0.10, 0.05, 0.05, 0.05, 0.05, 0.05, 0.05, 0.05, 0.05, 0.05, 0.05, 0.05, 0.05, 0.05, 0.05, 0.05, 0.05, 0.05, 0.05, 0.05, 0.05, 0.05, 0.05, 0.05, 0.05, 0.05, 0.05, 0.05, 0.05, 0.05, 0.05 ] } ``` Pass this JSON through `--attention-backend-config` alongside the component-scoped backend selection above. ## Implementation Note The Cube sparse attention backend in this PR is a reference implementation built with PyTorch FlexAttention. For higher performance on supported NVIDIA hardware, future work may explore replacing it with cuDNN Frontend's Block Sparse Attention ([cudnn-frontend/python/cudnn/block_sparse_attention at main · NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/tree/main/python/cudnn/block_sparse_attention)) operator. Broader hardware support and backend-specific optimizations are left to future community contributions. ## Performance On 2×H100 with the 1344×768, 4-second, 8-step TP2 workload: - dense FlashAttention denoise: 16.51s - aggressive all-`0.05` sparse schedule: 13.32s (19.3% faster) - mixed `[1.0, 1.0, 0.8, 0.7, 0.6, 0.5, 0.5]` schedule: 19.67s The mixed schedule is slower on this short sequence because FlexAttention routing overhead outweighs the sparse-kernel savings, so the feature remains opt-in and the cookbook calls out the tradeoff. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32444805483](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32444805483)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32444805371](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32444805371)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32444805340](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32444805340)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [UnifiedTree] feat: support runtime attach/detach for historage
signal.text: ## Motivation `UnifiedRadixCache.attach_storage_backend` / `detach_storage_backend` were stubs that always returned `False`, so the `/hicache/storage-backend` admin API only worked with `HiRadixCache`. This implements them for the unified tree. Preceding fix for #35081. Supersedes #35240 (same feature, developed in parallel). ## Modifications **`unified_cache/storage_attachment.py` (new).** `StorageAttachment` owns the storage backend lifecycle: policy validation, extra-config parsing, controller attach, the ordered teardown, and `apply_runtime_config()`. Keeping it beside the tree rather than inside it leaves `UnifiedRadixCache` on cache logic and gives the three entry points — startup, the admin API, and the atexit hook — one implementation. `UnifiedRadixCache` goes from 2764 to 2520 lines. `apply_runtime_config()` is the single point where storage turns on, which is why the hash backfill below lives there rather than in `attach()`. **Hash-chain backfill (correctness).** Page hashes chain off the parent's last hash, and `_add_new_node` only computes them when storage is enabled. A node built before attach therefore has no hash, and hashing its children against it restarts the chain mid-sequence — the resulting L3 keys claim to encode a full prefix but only encode a suffix, so an unrelated request starting with those tokens loads KV computed under a different prefix, silently. Reproduced end-to-end with `--page-size 64` and explicit `input_ids` (P, R, Q are 128 tokens each): request `P+R` with storage off, attach, request `P+R+Q`, flush, then request `Q+S`. | | L3 hit for the `Q`-prefixed request | |---|---| | without backfill | **128 tokens** — loaded KV computed after `P+R` | | with backfill | **0** — correctly misses | | control: same sequence after its own backup | 128 in both, so L3 itself is healthy | `UnifiedTreeCore.backfill_missing_hash_values()` walks parent-before-child so each node hashes against an already-filled parent. **`cache_controller.py`.** The storage control queues are now initialized to `None` in `__init__` instead of only existing after `_start_storage_threads()`, so a detach on a server that never attached is a clean no-op rather than an `AttributeError`. ## Accuracy Tests Output stability is asserted throughout: every scenario re-runs fixed prompts and compares them byte-for-byte against a baseline captured before any attach. ## Tests **15-scenario attach/detach state machine**, run in one server process, asserting per step that the HTTP result is as expected, the server stays healthy, output is unchanged, and `GET /hicache/storage-backend` reflects reality: - traffic → attach → traffic → detach → traffic - attach → traffic → detach - attach → attach (same backend → 200, policies updated; different backend → 400, state unchanged) - attach → detach → detach; detach before any attach - attach/detach cycled 5× with traffic in between - interleaved traffic/attach/traffic/attach/traffic/detach/traffic/detach/traffic - L3 actually used when attached (960 tokens) and unused when detached (0) - invalid policies rejected without changing state - attach onto a warm tree, then extend an existing prefix (the backfill path) - **attach/detach hammered under concurrent traffic**: 16 ops → `[200, 400×15]`, every 400 a `not idle` refusal, state never half-applied, no output drift - **8× attach + real L3 traffic + detach**: L3 hit count constant at 960 across rounds, which is the observable proof that host pages come back (the scheduler's invariant checker guards the device pool but not the host pool) Result: **157 PASS / 0 FAIL on 1 GPU and again under `--tp-size 2`** (48 attaches, repeatedly creating and destroying the prefetch gloo groups; no traceback, SIGQUIT, leak or NCCL/gloo anomaly after server ready). **Unit tests** — `TestUnifiedRadixCacheStorageAttachBackfill` pins the contract that a backfilled hash chain is identical to one hashed from the start. Verified by mutation: stubbing `backfill_missing_hash_values` to `return 0` turns two cases red; restoring it turns them green. Full file: 1046 passed, 0 failed. **Registered e2e** — `test_hicache_storage_runtime_attach_detach.py` now covers both implementations via a subclass, so the existing HiRadixCache coverage is retained rather than switched over. 2 passed. ## Notes `HiRadixCache` has the same unhashed-node issue and the same non-idempotent detach when no backend was ever attached. Both are left alone here to keep this PR scoped to the unified tree. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32210047237](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32210047237)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32444471781](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32444471781)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32210047280](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32210047280)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [diffusion] Forward multimodal token type IDs in image encoding
signal.text: ## Motivation Transformers 5.12 Qwen3-VL requires `mm_token_type_ids` when multimodal grid inputs are present. The JoyAI image-edit processor already returns this tensor, but `ImageEncodingStage` selected only the older processor outputs before calling the text encoder. As a result, JoyAI image editing failed before inference with the error reported in #34366. ## Modifications - Centralize the text-encoder input assembly for image encoding. - Forward `mm_token_type_ids` when the processor returns it, in both the positive and classifier-free-guidance negative paths. - Preserve the previous call shape when processors omit the optional field. - Add CPU unit coverage with a real `transformers.BatchFeature`, distinct positive/negative token-type IDs, dtype/device assertions, and a strict legacy encoder signature without `**kwargs`. The change is intentionally limited to stage plumbing; it does not alter model-side position-ID computation. ## Accuracy Tests - `TORCHDYNAMO_DISABLE=1 PYTHONPATH=python python -m pytest -q python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_image_encoding_stage.py` — 3 passed. - The existing `joyai_image_edit_ti2i` 1-GPU case is the focused end-to-end regression smoke test. It was not run locally because a compatible GPU and model weights were unavailable, so it is requested in CI. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not applicable. This only forwards an existing integer tensor and adds no model computation or tensor copy. ## Checklist - [x] Format the Python changes with the repository pre-commit hooks. All affected-file hooks passed; the repository-wide non-Rust hooks also passed (Rust-only hooks were skipped because this PR does not touch Rust). - [x] Add unit tests according to the contribution guide. - [x] Document the behavior and compatibility scope in this PR; no user-facing API documentation changes are needed. - [x] Provide the relevant accuracy/speed rationale above; the GPU smoke test is delegated to CI. - [x] Follow the SGLang code-style guidance. Fixes #34366 <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32337649348](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32337649348)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32337648995](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32337648995)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32337649598](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32337649598)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [Intel GPU] Route MXFP4 MoE to the sgl-kernel-xpu W4A16 grouped GEMM
signal.text: MXFP4 checkpoints (GPT-OSS) could not run on XPU: `mxfp4` was registered only for cpu/cuda/gfx95, and `Mxfp4MoEMethod` had no XPU branch, so it fell through to a bf16 upcast needing `triton_kernels` and ~42 GB for GPT-OSS-20B. `moe_grouped_mm_nt_xe20_w4a16` consumes the checkpoint layout as-is (packed e2m1 + N-outer ue8m0 g32 scales, interleaved gate/up rows), so add the XPU dispatch, skip the upcast, and keep the layout unpadded. Registration is gated on `use_intel_xpu_backend()`; without that backend the upcast would still be hit, so leaving it unregistered keeps the current clear error. Also forward activation/routed_scaling_factor/gemm1_alpha/gemm1_limit/ swiglu_limit through the existing `_use_sgl_xpu` redirect in triton_utils/fused_moe.py, which dropped them and so computed a plain silu*up instead of the GPT-OSS clamped swiglu. cpu/cuda/rocm unchanged. Verified on Arc Pro B60: gpt-oss-20b MXFP4 loads at 12.87 GB packed (not ~42 GB) and generates correctly. <!-- Thank you for your contribution! compiled-kernel cache moves under `SGLANG_CACHE_DIR`**, so the first launch after upgrading recompiles once. Copy or symlink the old directories if you pre-warm or volume-mount them (`deep_gemm` and `flashinfer` are the expensive ones): `~/.triton` to `{SGLANG_CACHE_DIR}/triton`, `~/.cache/flashinfer` to `{SGLANG_CACHE_DIR}/.cache/flashinfer`, `~/.cache/deep_gemm` to `{SGLANG_CACHE_DIR}/deep_gemm`, `/tmp/torchinductor_$USER` to `{SGLANG_CACHE_DIR}/inductor`, `~/.nv/ComputeCache` to `{SGLANG_CACHE_DIR}/nv`. Setting any of `TRITON_CACHE_DIR`, `FLASHINFER_WORKSPACE_BASE`, `SGLANG_DG_CACHE_DIR`, `TORCHINDUCTOR_CACHE_DIR`, or `CUDA_CACHE_PATH` keeps that one where it is: [#32434](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32434) * **The torchao integration is removed** (`--torchao-config` had raised ImportError for every accepted value since the torchao pin moved to 0.17.0): [#34304](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/34304) * **DeepEP now installs from released `sgl-deep-ep` wheels** instead of building from source: [#33932](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33932) * **MoE deferred finalize is on by default** on the NVFP4 + `flashinfer_trtllm` path with an unfused, non-TP1 shared expert (the DeepSeek-V3 family); set `SGLANG_ENABLE_MOE_DEFERRED_FINALIZE=False` to fall back: [#33618](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33618) * **Unified-cache out-of-window SWA slot freeing is on by default** for the unified radix cache; set `SGLANG_OPT_UNIFIED_CACHE_FREE_OUT_OF_WINDOW_SLOTS=False` to restore the old behavior: [#34653](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/34653) * **Remote media downloads are bounded to 64 MiB by default**, with redirect validation and opt-in exact-hostname allowlisting for image, video, and audio URLs: [#34892](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/34892) * **The DSV4 fused MHC post+pre path is on by default**, including on SM12x: [#35214](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/35214), [#34019](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/34019) * **torch.compile becomes opt-in for diffusion speed mode**: [#34173](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/34173) * **22 unmaintained benchmarks are removed**: [#34520](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/34520) ## Known Issues * **The Kimi K3 MLA gate-projection fusion into the QKV-A GEMM was landed and reverted** this cycle ([#33623](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33623), [#34642](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/34642)).
